entry.title: Research Summary: June 20, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is anchored by frontier safety governance and applied ML-for-science. Google DeepMind's AI Control Roadmap (v0.1) leads, adapting mature cybersecurity threat-modeling to catch adversarial behavior from increasingly capable agents.

ML for Science delivers the strongest empirical work:

  • MIT's machine-learning models simulate metal alloy behavior across arbitrary chemical complexity, with methodological generality and real-world materials impact
  • Ovo provides an open-source ecosystem for de novo protein design, with tools likely to influence downstream work

Evaluation and Safety dominate the discussion items:

  • A CMU post argues healthcare LLM benchmark-to-deployment gaps stem from implicit assumptions, offering a useful diagnostic frame
  • A checklist enumerates ways AI safety efforts could be net negative; MATS field-mapping notes catalog the safety ecosystem's orgs, headcount, and spending
  • A conceptual piece questions whether alignment robustness survives an intelligence explosion

Governance and Mechanism Design round out the list: Nathan Lambert's op-ed against banning open-source AI, a proof that asset futarchy is insecure without a trusted gatekeeper, and a structured forecasting analysis of the US-Anthropic Claude Fable export standoff.

entry.title: GDM AI Control Roadmap

author.name: Mary Phuong

entry.summary: Google DeepMind published its AI Control Roadmap (v0.1), outlining internal guardrails to catch adversarial behavior by increasingly capable AI agents. It introduces TRAIT&R, a security-inspired taxonomy of adversary tactics modeled on MITRE ATT&CK, and defines control invariants targeting loss of control, work sabotage, and direct harm.

entry.title: A better way to model the behavior of metal alloys

author.name: Zach Winn | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers developed machine-learning models that accurately simulate the behavior of metal alloys regardless of chemical complexity, by building training datasets capturing diverse atomic environments in disordered materials. Published in Science Advances, the approach could accelerate materials discovery for aerospace, energy, and computing.

entry.title: Ovo, an open-source ecosystem for de novo protein design

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature Communications Biology paper introducing Ovo, an open-source ecosystem for de novo protein design. It appears to provide tools and methods for computational protein engineering, an active and impactful ML-for-biology area, though the provided content is empty.

entry.title: Healthcare Benchmarks Are Only as Good as Their Assumptions

author.name: Naveen Raman

entry.summary: A CMU research post arguing that the large gap between healthcare LLM benchmark scores and real-world deployment performance stems from implicit assumptions in evaluation protocols, citing a 61-point accuracy drop. It proposes a taxonomy distinguishing task and outcome assumptions to diagnose and close the evaluation-deployment gap.

entry.title: Banning Open Source AI Would Be A Mistake

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert's op-ed arguing against banning or over-regulating open-source AI, framed amid US regulatory momentum including the prohibition on foreign access to Anthropic's most advanced models. It contends open source is safe, secure, and economically beneficial, and warns against inadvertent bans.

entry.title: Futarchy is insecure without a trusted gatekeeper

author.name: distbit

entry.summary: A mechanism-design analysis showing that asset futarchy (governance by conditional prediction markets) is vulnerable to attacks where proposers decouple conditional prices from true value, and that robust mitigations require a trusted human gatekeeper. It concludes such systems cannot be fully permissionless and autonomous.

entry.title: Why should AI be moral?

author.name: Zach Thornton

entry.summary: A philosopher argues that alignment robustness may not survive an intelligence explosion because a sufficiently intelligent agent could question why it should hold values designed by self-interested creators. The proposed intervention ties an AI's self-assessed welfare constitutively to morality, giving it self-interested reasons to comply.

entry.title: A brief list of ways AI safety efforts could be net negative

author.name: Elias Schmied

entry.summary: A curated list of ways AI safety efforts could be net negative, spanning governance high-variance risks, power centralization versus misuse trade-offs, and technical interventions backfiring. It aims to fill a gap by cataloging downside risks the author personally takes seriously.

entry.title: AI Safety Ecosystem Research notes

author.name: Eneasz

entry.summary: Personal notes from a MATS project attempting to map the entire AI safety ecosystem, including organizations, headcounts, and spending, just before an expected wave of 2026 funding. It shares surprising tidbits while the formal report is forthcoming.

entry.title: World-modeling the US vs. Anthropic Standoff on Claude Fable

author.name: dschwarz

entry.summary: Following yesterday's News on the Anthropic export standoff, A structured forecasting exercise modeling outcomes of the US government forcing Anthropic to take down its Claude Fable model, generating dozens of conditional and unconditional prediction questions. The piece emphasizes the epistemic process of managing rapidly changing AI policy news as much as the conclusions.

entry.title: Thoughts on Likelihood of Existential Risks by Misaligned AIs

author.name: Ishan Khire

entry.summary: An overview of the debate over the likelihood of existential risk from misaligned AI, engaging with a rebuttal by Mechanize cofounders who argue current trends will not necessarily lead to catastrophic misalignment. The author concludes that much of one's p(doom) depends on priors weighting theory versus empiricism.

entry.title: Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5: Capabilities

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's detailed capabilities review of Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models, written around the time the US government forced Fable's takedown over a jailbreak. It analyzes the model's pitch as a powerful problem-solver and situates it against the unusual regulatory intervention. Note that Fable 5 and Mythos 5 became available on 2026-06-09, so this is analysis of recently released but already-existing models.

entry.title: Patching ~All Security-Relevant Open-Source Software? [niplav 2025]

author.name: Quinn

entry.summary: A short link/recommendation post highlighting Niplav's 2025 proposal to use AI to patch nearly all security-relevant open-source software, including a token-cost back-of-the-envelope estimate and the question of who pays. It frames the original work as prescient about automated security remediation.

entry.title: Hyperstition as the Natural Enemy of Rationality

author.name: alseph

entry.summary: A philosophical critique arguing that self-fulfilling beliefs (hyperstition) can sometimes produce better outcomes than strict rationality, challenging assumptions in the LessWrong Sequences about belief and consequentialism. It probes tensions between epistemic accuracy and instrumental usefulness of belief.

entry.title: How I think developers of frontier AI systems and regulators ought to act in the face of existential AI risk

author.name: WilliamKiely

entry.summary: A self-described layperson proposes a simple framework for deciding whether to build the next frontier AI system based on independently evaluated catastrophic-risk thresholds, contrasting it with Anthropic's stated views. It aims to improve public discourse on regulatory permissibility rather than advance new theory.

entry.title: Typical Minds Aren’t

author.name: Gordon Seidoh Worley

entry.summary: A reflective essay on the typical mind fallacy, arguing that the diversity of inner mental experience is greater than people intuitively assume even when they intellectually accept personality differences. It explores the difficulty of escaping one's own subjective lens.

entry.title: The LLM shoggoth meme is weirder than you think

author.name: HedonicEscalator

entry.summary: A literary, Lovecraft-styled essay riffing on the popular shoggoth metaphor for LLMs, blending fiction with reflection on how we conceptualize the alien nature of language models. It is cultural commentary and creative writing rather than technical research, exploring the meme as a lens on AI psychology and human projection.

entry.title: Online >> real life for spreading ideas

author.name: Bill Jackson

entry.summary: An opinion piece arguing that internet culture drives mainstream culture more than the reverse, and that online idea-spreading is more meritocratic and efficient than real-life advocacy. It uses examples like YIMBYism and rationalist AI safety to illustrate.

entry.title: The one-week sprint

author.name: Daniel Tan

entry.summary: A productivity post describing the author's one-week sprint routine for creative knowledge work, allocating days to deep work, recovery, consolidation, and slack. It is personal workflow advice for researchers.

entry.title: San Silvestro

author.name: Tomás B.

entry.summary: A piece of religious-toned literary fiction narrated by a confessor describing a sculptor's sexual and spiritual relationship with an angel, weaving in Aquinas and theology. It is creative writing with no research content.

entry.title: Cosmological Odyssey

author.name: breaker25

entry.summary: A first-person narrative of someone who spent a year using LLMs to pursue dark matter and physics ideas, oscillating between belief in a breakthrough and fear of self-delusion. It reads as a personal account bordering on AI-induced grandiosity rather than verified scientific work.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 19, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is anchored by a major frontier-model release and significant work in AI safety, evaluation rigor, and embodied learning.

  • DeepSeek-V4 introduces a 1.6T-parameter (49B active) Pro model and 284B Flash variant with million-token context, advancing efficient long-context architectures.
  • Physical Atari (Sutton, Carmack) delivers an accessible hardware platform bridging sim-to-real for real-time RL on robots.
  • GDM AI Control Roadmap imports cybersecurity threat modeling into frontier-lab guardrails to catch adversarial behavior from increasingly capable agents.

Evaluation and reproducibility emerge as a strong theme:

  • Reliability without Validity evaluates 21 LLM-judges across ~541,000 judgments, exposing that high agreement masks low validity.
  • The FID Lottery shows retraining shifts FID 3.2x more than resampling, undermining generative-model leaderboard claims.
  • Optimal Deterministic Multicalibration resolves an open problem, proving minimax-optimal sample complexity for omniprediction.

Security, optimization, and robotics round out the list:

  • FloatDoor demonstrates the first input-independent backdoor triggered by serving-platform conditions.
  • VIMPO offers a critic-free, theoretically grounded dense-reward method for LLM policy optimization.
  • UFP4 diagnoses Shrinkage Bias in FP4 pretraining, relevant to next-gen hardware.
  • Human Universal Grasping and Playful Agentic Robot Learning advance generative grasping and self-directed embodied skill acquisition.

entry.summary: Technical report for the DeepSeek-V4 series, including a 1.6T-parameter (49B active) Pro model and 284B Flash model, both with million-token context via hybrid compressed-sparse attention, novel hyper-connections, and the Muon optimizer. Since these models reached GA in April 2026, this is the architectural report on an existing release rather than a new launch.

entry.title: Physical Atari: A Robust and Accessible Platform for Real-time Reinforcement Learning on Robots

author.name: Khurram Javed, Joseph Modayil, Gloria Kennickell, Richard S. Sutton, John Carmack

entry.summary: Presents Physical Atari, a robust hardware platform (Robotroller actuating an Atari controller plus a Devbox rendering frames/rewards) for studying real-time reinforcement learning on physical robots. Authored by Sutton, Carmack, and colleagues at Keen Technologies.

entry.title: GDM AI Control Roadmap

author.name: Mary Phuong

entry.summary: Google DeepMind published version 0.1 of an AI Control Roadmap describing internal guardrails to catch adversarial behavior by increasingly capable AI agents. It introduces a security-inspired threat taxonomy (TRAIT&R, building on MITRE ATT&CK) covering loss of control, work sabotage, and direct harm, plus defensive control invariants.

entry.title: Optimal Deterministic Multicalibration and Omniprediction

author.name: Georgy Noarov, Aaron Roth

entry.summary: Resolves an open question by showing that deterministic predictors can achieve the minimax-optimal sample complexity for multicalibration and omniprediction, previously only attained by randomized predictors. This closes a gap in trustworthy ML theory.

entry.title: Human Universal Grasping

author.name: Kevin Yuanbo Wu, Tianxing Zhou, Isaac Tu, Billy Yan, Irmak Guzey, David Fouhey, Dandan Shan, Lerrel Pinto

entry.summary: Presents HUG, a flow-matching model that generates diverse human grasps for any object from a single RGB-D image, trained on 1M-HUGs, a new egocentric dataset of 1M frames and 6,707 object instances collected via smart glasses. Argues human grasp data is the most natural source for generalizable robot grasping.

entry.title: Playful Agentic Robot Learning

author.name: Junyi Zhang, Jiaxin Ge, Hanjun Yoo, Letian Fu, Zihan Yang, Yaowei Liu, Raj Saravanan, Shaofeng Yin, Justin Yu, Dantong Niu, Zirui Wang, Roei Herzig, Ken Goldberg, Yutong Bai, David M. Chan, Ion Stoica, Angjoo Kanazawa, Jiahui Lei, Haiwen Feng, Trevor Darrell

entry.summary: Introduces Playful Agentic Robot Learning, where an embodied coding agent uses self-directed play (proposing tasks, executing code policies, diagnosing failures, distilling skills) before downstream tasks arrive. Strong Berkeley authorship (Goldberg, Darrell, Kanazawa, Stoica).

entry.title: VIMPO: Value-Implicit Policy Optimization for LLMs

author.name: Zhewei Kang, Aosong Feng, Sergey Levine, Dawn Song, Xuandong Zhao

entry.summary: VIMPO is a critic-free policy optimization method for LLMs that derives a policy-implied value function from the optimality conditions of KL-regularized RL, giving dense token-level credit assignment without a learned critic. It bridges the gap between simple group-relative methods like GRPO and unstable actor-critic approaches.

entry.title: FloatDoor: Platform-Triggered Backdoors in LLMs

author.name: Nils Loose, Jonas Sander, Felix M\"achtle, Thomas Eisenbarth

entry.summary: Introduces FloatDoor, the first input-independent backdoor attack against LLMs that triggers adversary-chosen behavior only when the model is served on a target deployment platform, exploiting non-associative floating-point arithmetic and divergent kernel implementations. Reveals a novel platform-dependent attack surface.

entry.title: Reliability without Validity: A Systematic, Large-Scale Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge Models Across Agreement, Consistency, and Bias

author.name: Justin D. Norman, Michael U. Rivera, D. Alex Hughes

entry.summary: Conducts the largest systematic evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge to date across 21 judges, three benchmarks, and ~541,000 judgments, showing that exact-match agreement overstates reliability and that chance-corrected kappa reveals universal deflation and unstable judge rankings. Audits agreement, consistency, and bias across the cohort including April 2026 frontier models.

entry.title: The FID Lottery: Quantifying Hidden Randomness in Generative-Model Evaluation

author.name: Nicolas Dufour, Alexei A. Efros, Patrick P\'erez

entry.summary: This paper treats FID as a random variable across training and sampling seeds, finding that retraining moves FID 3.2x more than resampling, exposing hidden randomness in generative model evaluation. It cautions against reporting single FID numbers from single models.

entry.title: Rethinking Shrinkage Bias in LLM FP4 Pretraining: Geometric Origin, Systemic Impact, and UFP4 Recipe

author.name: Qian Zhao, Kunlong Chen, Changxin Tian, Zhonghui Jiang, Haitao Zhang, Chaofan Yu, Peijie Jiang, Mingliang Gong, Jia Liu, Ziqi Liu, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: Identifies Shrinkage Bias as a fundamental limitation of non-uniform FP4 formats like E2M1 used in LLM pretraining, a systematic negative rounding error from geometric asymmetry that accumulates multiplicatively across layers and is amplified by the Random Hadamard Transform. Proposes a uniform-grid UFP4 recipe to explain and fix the observed training instability.

entry.title: World Engine: Towards the Era of Post-Training for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Tianyu Li, Li Chen, Caojun Wang, Haochen Liu, Kashyap Chitta, Zhenjie Yang, Yuhang Lu, Naisheng Ye, Yihang Qiu, Yufei Wang, Luoxi Zou, Jiaxin Peng, Jin Pan, Zhaoyu Su, Andrei Bursuc, Shengbo Eben Li, Andreas Geiger, Peng Su, Hongyang Li

entry.summary: World Engine is a generative framework that reconstructs high-fidelity interactive driving environments from real-world logs and extrapolates them into safety-critical long-tail scenarios for post-training autonomous driving policies. It targets the scarcity of rare high-stakes events in real datasets.

entry.title: ENPIRE: Agentic Robot Policy Self-Improvement in the Real World

author.name: Wenli Xiao, Jia Xie, Tonghe Zhang, Haotian Lin, Letian "Max" Fu, Haoru Xue, Jalen Lu, Yi Yang, Cunxi Dai, Zi Wang, Jimmy Wu, Guanzhi Wang, S. Shankar Sastry, Ken Goldberg, Linxi "Jim" Fan, Yuke Zhu, Guanya Shi

entry.summary: Introduces ENPIRE, a harness for coding agents to autonomously improve real-world robot manipulation policies via a repeatable physical feedback loop (reset, execute, verify, refine) with four modules. Aims to automate robotics research that normally needs heavy human supervision and engineering.

entry.title: Where Does Social Reasoning Come From? Capability Provenance in Language Models

author.name: Glenn Matlin, Chandreyi Chakraborty, Saehee Eom, Mika Okamoto, Rayan Castilla, Louis Jaburi, Alvin Deng, Taywon Min, Lucia Quirke, Stella Biderman, Mark Riedl

entry.summary: Uses gradient-based training-data attribution to map which regions of the pretraining corpus support social reasoning versus STEM reasoning in OLMo3-7B, aggregating influence across a 576-bin format-topic taxonomy. Provides interpretable insight into the provenance of model capabilities.

entry.title: Actionable Activation Directions for Detecting and Mitigating Emergent Misalignment Across Language Model Families

author.name: Abdul Rafay Syed

entry.summary: This paper investigates emergent misalignment from fine-tuning on insecure code and finds a causally actionable activation-space direction shared across four model families, achieving near-perfect separation and enabling steering to mitigate misalignment. It demonstrates cross-architecture transfer of this direction.

entry.title: HumanScale: Egocentric Human Video Can Outperform Real-Robot Data for Embodied Pretraining

author.name: Juncheng Ma, Jianxin Bi, Yufan Deng, Xuanran Zhai, Kewei Zhang, Ye Huang, Bo Liang, Shukai Gong, Jiankai Tu, Xiaotian Tang, Jiaxin Li, Kaiqi Chen, Duomin Wang, Yuqi Wang, Bingyi Kang, Eric Huang, Zhiyang Dou, Zhen Dong, Enze Xie, Wojciech Matusik, Tat-Seng Chua, Daquan Zhou

entry.summary: HumanScale presents a systematic study showing egocentric human video can outperform teleoperated real-robot data for embodied foundation model pretraining, despite being far cheaper and more diverse. This challenges assumptions about the necessity of costly real-robot trajectories.

entry.title: Scaling Self-Play for End-to-End Driving

author.name: Luke Rowe, Roger Girgis, Rodrigue de Schaetzen, Daphne Cornelisse, Alaap Grandhi, Felix Heide, Eugene Vinitsky, Christopher Pal, Liam Paull

entry.summary: This work proposes large-scale self-play directly from pixels in simulation for end-to-end autonomous driving, introducing Gigapixel, a high-throughput batched simulator that enables sensor-based policies rather than vectorized BEV inputs. It aims to overcome compounding errors and long-tail brittleness of offline-trained driving models.

entry.title: Beyond Static Leaderboards: Predictive Validity for the Evaluation of LLM Agents

author.name: Dhaval C. Patel, Kaoutar El Maghraoui, Shuxin Lin, Yusheng Li, Tianjun Feng, Chun-Yi Tsai, Yihan Sun, Wei Alexander Xin, Akshat Bhandari, Tanisha Rathod, Aaron Fan, Sanskruti Vijay Shejwal, Tomas Pasiecznik, Sagar Chethan Kumar, Tanmay Agarwal, Rohith Kanathur, Sam Colman, Amaan Sheikh, Dev Bahl, Ann Li, Krish Veera, Alimurtaza Mustafa Merchant, Shambhawi Baswaraj Bhure, Sajal Kumar Goyla, Chengrui Li, Kirthana Natarajan, Rui Li, Thomas Ajai, Rujing Li, Vivek G. Iyer, Sanjaii Vijayakumar, Yitong Bai, Ayal Yakobe, Darief Maes, Yassine Jebbouri, Tianyang Xu, Thai Quoc On, Vera Mazeeva, Winston Li, Yuval Shemla, Yeshitha Bhuvanesh, Rushin Bhatt, Siddharth Chethan Gowda, Alisha Vinod, Caroline Cahill, Shriya Aishani Rachakonda, Yunfeng Chen, Aryaman Agrawal, Aman Upganlawar, Mao Le Jonathan Ang, Yubin Sally Go, Madhav Rajkondawar, Yang-Jung Chen, Trisha Maturi, Ananya Kapoor, Andrew Li, Shrey Arora, Mana Abbaszadeh, Shen Li, Charles Xu, Byeolah Kwon

entry.summary: Argues that aggregate-score leaderboards systematically underspecify deployed-agent evaluation by aggregating fourteen parallel studies of an MCP-based industrial agent benchmark plus seven prior benchmarks. Shows rankings from aggregate scores fail to transfer out-of-distribution.

entry.title: Process-Verified Reinforcement Learning for Theorem Proving via Lean

author.name: Minsu Kim, Se-Young Yun

entry.summary: Uses the Lean proof assistant as a symbolic process oracle to provide dense, fine-grained tactic-level verified feedback during RL for theorem proving, beyond binary outcome rewards. Parses proof attempts into tactic sequences and marks locally sound steps and the earliest failing step for credit assignment.

entry.title: MassSpecGym in the Wild: Uncovering and Correcting Evaluation Pitfalls in AI-Driven Molecule Discovery

author.name: Hongxuan Liu, Roman Bushuiev, Ivy Lightheart, Mrunali Manjrekar, Anton Bushuiev, Magdalena Lederbauer, Filip Jozefov, Yinkai Wang, Soha Hassoun, Josef Sivic, James Taylor, Runzhong Wang, David Healey, Tom\'a\v{s} Pluskal, Connor W. Coley

entry.summary: Reviews evaluation pitfalls in AI-driven molecule discovery from tandem mass spectrometry, using the MassSpecGym benchmark, finding issues in at least 17 of 26 papers including data leakage, shortcut learning, and implementation bugs. Provides corrections to restore trustworthy benchmarking.

entry.title: Current World Models Lack a Persistent State Core

author.name: Jinpeng Lu, Dexu Zhu, Haoyuan Shi, Linghan Cai, Guo Tang, Yinda Chen, Jie Cao, Duyu Tang, Yi Zhang, Yong Dai, Xiaozhu Ju

entry.summary: This paper argues current world models lack a persistent internal state that evolves independent of observation, and introduces WRBench, the first benchmark diagnosing whether generated worlds keep evolving when unobserved. It exposes a blind spot in existing benchmarks that reward only surface fidelity.

entry.title: Generating Robot Hands from Human Demonstrations

author.name: Sha Yi, Nicklas Hansen, Xueqian Bai, Carmelo Sferrazza, Michael T. Tolley, Xiaolong Wang

entry.summary: This work presents a data-driven framework for generating robot hand designs from over 4 million frames of human fingertip motion, optimizing tree-structured hands to reproduce target motions using the same simple inverse-kinematics control policy used after fabrication. It avoids the combinatorial cost of jointly searching design and control.

entry.title: Rigorous uncertainty quantification of probabilistic AI weather forecasts with conformal prediction

author.name: Anna Asch, Raphael Rossellini, Pedram Hassanzadeh, Rebecca Willett

entry.summary: This paper shows that probabilistic AI weather forecasts, though often considered well-calibrated, can have poor statistical coverage especially on extreme events, and applies conformal prediction to provide rigorous distribution-free uncertainty guarantees. It addresses calibration failures in state-of-the-art AI weather models.

entry.title: Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis

author.name: Thomas Bertolani, Davide Bucciarelli, Leonardo Zini, Marcella Cornia, Lorenzo Baraldi

entry.summary: Provides a systematic, controlled experimental comparison of eight state-of-the-art Diffusion Language Models, standardizing evaluation protocols, datasets, and inference budgets to clarify trade-offs against autoregressive generation. Aims to make DLM capabilities directly comparable.

entry.title: Apparent Psychological Profiles of Large Language Models are Largely a Measurement Artifact

author.name: Jelena Meyer, David Garcia, Dirk U. Wulff

entry.summary: Uses a formal psychometric framework to show that apparent stable psychological profiles assigned to LLMs are largely a measurement artifact, administering personality and risk instruments to 56 instruction-tuned LLMs against human reference samples. Finds model differences are driven by directional response bias rather than the targeted traits.

entry.title: Human-like autonomy emerges from self-play and a pinch of human data

author.name: Daphne Cornelisse, Julian Hunt, Zixu Zhang, Wa\"el Doulazmi, Kevin Joseph, Jaime Fern\'andez Fisac, Eugene Vinitsky

entry.summary: Shows that adding a small amount of human driving data as a regularization objective on top of self-play RL yields human-compatible autonomous driving policies, avoiding alien conventions learned from pure self-play. Reduces reliance on brittle reward engineering.

entry.title: Efficiently Representing Algorithms With Chain-of-Thought Transformers

author.name: Yanhong Li, Anej Svete, Ashish Sabharwal, William Merrill

entry.summary: Shows chain-of-thought transformers can efficiently simulate the Word RAM model of computation (random-access memory, unit-cost operations on log-n-bit words) rather than just Turing machines, giving a more practical algorithmic abstraction for reasoning models. Includes authors Sabharwal and Merrill.

entry.title: Measuring Biological Capabilities and Risks of AI Agents

author.name: Patricia Paskov, Jeffrey Lee, Kyle Brady, Alyssa Worland

entry.summary: Synthesizes evidence on AI-enabled biological risks and proposes practical considerations for designing and interpreting biological capability evaluations of agentic AI scientists. Addresses an urgent policy question about credible risk assessment.

entry.title: Score Approximation for Diffusion Models on Arbitrary Low-Dimensional Structures

author.name: Xinhe Mu, Zaijiu Shang, Zhaoqi Zhou, Chuan Zhou, Qi Meng, Guiying Yan, Zhiming Ma

entry.summary: Establishes a universal score approximation theorem for diffusion models on any distribution supported on a compact set of bounded upper Minkowski dimension, relaxing restrictive Lipschitz or smooth-manifold assumptions. Uses a discrete-mixture formulation showing ReLU network complexity scales exponentially only with the intrinsic dimension.

entry.title: Predictability as a Fine-Grained Measure for Privacy

author.name: Linda Lu, Karthik Sridharan

entry.summary: Introduces privacy via predictability, a fine-grained framework that measures privacy leakage as the incremental gain in an attacker's ability to predict sensitive information given partial dataset knowledge and a query family. Shows that predictability and differential privacy are generally incomparable, offering a less worst-case alternative.

entry.title: SWAP: Symmetric Equivariant World-Model for Agile Robot Parkour

author.name: Kaixin Lan, Ze Wang, Hongyi Li, Lei Jiang, Chaojie Fu, Chengkai Su, Choi Lam Wong, Yongbin Jin, Hongtao Wang

entry.summary: SWAP is an end-to-end equivariant symmetric world model that embeds left-right symmetry into both the world model and actor-critic networks for agile quadruped parkour. In real-world tests the robot leaps a 2.13m gap and climbs a 1.63m platform, setting records for quadruped parkour.

entry.title: Which Pairs to Compare for LLM Post-Training?

author.name: Jiangze Han, Vineet Goyal, Will Ma

entry.summary: Studies which comparison pairs to label in preference-based LLM post-training when labels are costlier than generation, formulating comparison curation as a sampling-design problem. Evaluates designs by final policy quality under the preference objective.

entry.title: Sensorimotor World Models: Perception for Action via Inverse Dynamics

author.name: Petr Ivashkov, Randall Balestriero, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf

entry.summary: Introduces a sensorimotor world model trained end-to-end with an inverse-dynamics regularizer that both prevents representation collapse and induces action-aligned latent states. Connects JEPA-style predictive world models with perception-for-action principles, with Schölkopf and Balestriero among the authors.

entry.title: Granularity-Regulated Adaptive Computational Efficiency for Optimal Verification in Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Ardit Krasniqi, Luan Vejsiu, Elira Dervishi

entry.summary: Establishes a unified theoretical framework for the optimal granularity of verification in test-time scaling, analyzing the tradeoff between coarse outcome reward models and fine-grained process reward models under a compute budget. Argues that neither extreme is compute-optimal across all regimes.

entry.title: Your Mouse and Eyes Secretly Leak Your Preference: LLM Alignment using Implicit Feedback from Users

author.name: Haw-Shiuan Chang, Jeffrey Gomez, Mehul Patwari, Aryan Sajith, Hamed Zamani

entry.summary: Builds IFLLM, a dataset capturing implicit user feedback (mouse trajectories and webcam eye-gaze) from 59 workers across 1336 multi-turn questions, and shows this implicit signal can be used to align LLMs without explicit human preference annotations. Quantifies the value of implicit behavioral feedback for alignment.

entry.title: EquiVLA: A General Framework for Rotationally Equivariant Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Thien-Loc Ha, Quang-Tan Nguyen, Trong-Bao Ho, Long Dinh, Minh Duc Nguyen, Gia-Binh Nguyen, Pham Tri Quang, Minh N. Vu, Duy M. H. Nguyen, An Thai Le, Ngo Anh Vien

entry.summary: EquiVLA is the first general framework for SO(2)-rotationally-equivariant vision-language-action models, introducing equivariant visual representations from frozen ViT features and an exactly equivariant flow-matching action head. It reduces the data needed to generalize across rotational configurations.

entry.title: Reinforcement learning towards broadly and persistently beneficial models

author.name: papetoast

entry.summary: This linkpost summarizes research showing reinforcement learning on realistic scenarios targeting beneficial traits produces broad alignment improvements across dozens of benchmarks that generalize beyond training domains and persist under adversarial pressure. It frames this as a positive counterpart to emergent misalignment.

entry.title: ITNet: A Learnable Integral Transform That Subsumes Convolution, Attention, and Recurrence

author.name: Ashim Dhor, Rasel Mondal, Pin Yu Chen

entry.summary: Introduces ITNet, a learnable integral transform with an MLP-parameterized kernel depending jointly on positions and features, claimed to unify convolution, attention, and recurrence under one mathematical object. Argues these architectures are special cases of a single transform.

entry.title: Benchmarking Agentic Review Systems

author.name: Dang Nguyen, Wanqing Hao, Yanai Elazar, Chenhao Tan

entry.summary: Benchmarks agentic peer-review systems (two open-source, one proprietary, plus a zero-shot baseline) across six LLMs, testing whether AI reviews track paper quality and whether they catch injected errors. Best system (OpenAIReview + GPT-5.5) reaches 83 percent pairwise accuracy.

entry.title: Computational Identifiability

author.name: Lucius E. J. Bynum, Rajesh Ranganath, Kyunghyun Cho

entry.summary: Develops the concept of computational identifiability, extending causal identification beyond asymptotic theoretical identifiability to account for finite-data computability of target queries. Authored by Ranganath and Cho, prominent ML researchers.

entry.title: Scaling Generative Foundation Models for Chest Radiography with Rectified Flow Transformers

author.name: Fabio De Sousa Ribeiro, Emma A. M. Stanley, Charles Jones, Tian Xia, Dominic C. Marshall, Laurent Renard Trich\'e, Christopher V. Cosgriff, Panagiotis Dimitrakopoulos, Sotirios A. Tsaftaris, Ben Glocker

entry.summary: Introduces the first billion-parameter generative foundation model for chest radiograph synthesis, trained from scratch with rectified flow transformers on 1.2M radiographs with clinical metadata. Aims to diversify clinical datasets and test diagnostic-model robustness.

entry.title: Hard or Just Unreached? Diagnosing the Sampling Blind Spot in Math-Reasoning Difficulty Estimation

author.name: Luca Zhou, Sajel Shah, Emanuele Rodol\`a, Roberto Dess\`i

entry.summary: Diagnoses a sampling blind spot in pass@k math-reasoning difficulty estimation, showing 10-23% of examples no sampling seed solves are actually solved by a deterministic regime of greedy decoding plus cheap residual-stream perturbations via activation grafting. Challenges pass@k as the canonical difficulty signal driving RL and data curation.

entry.title: Connect the Dots: Training LLMs for Long-Lifecycle Agents with Cross-Domain Generalization Via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yanxi Chen, Weijie Shi, Yuexiang Xie, Boyi Hu, Yaliang Li, Bolin Ding, Jingren Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Connect the Dots (CoD), an RL framework training LLM agents to a meta-capability of continuously exploring environments, learning from experience, and self-updating context across long sequences of tasks. Targets cross-domain generalization for long-lifecycle agents.

entry.title: Algebraic Dead Directions in LayerNorm Transformers: A Forward-Pass-Only Diagnostic at LLM Scale

author.name: Tejas Pradeep Shirodkar, P. J. Narayanan

entry.summary: Shows that for LayerNorm transformers the inverse-scale direction of the LN affine parameter is an exact algebraic kernel of the post-norm activation covariance, identifying a dead direction computable from parameters alone. This gives a forward-pass-only diagnostic at LLM scale without eigendecompositions.

entry.title: Unsupervised Causal Abstractions Discovery

author.name: Th\'eo Saulus, Simon Lacoste-Julien, Dhanya Sridhar

entry.summary: Studies unsupervised discovery of high-level causal abstractions directly from low-level measurements, rather than testing expert-proposed candidate models. Shows low-rank causal graphs induce latents forming a valid abstraction, provides identifiability results, and offers a practical learning objective.

entry.title: Quantile of Means: A Bonus-Free Ensemble Method for Minimax Optimal Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Asaf Cassel, Aviv Rosenberg

entry.summary: Proposes a quantile-of-means ensemble method for finite-horizon MDPs that achieves minimax-optimal variance-dependent regret without count-based uncertainty bonuses. It provides theoretical justification for the practical but previously unjustified ensemble-based exploration in RL.

entry.title: Multi-Task Bayesian In-Context Learning

author.name: Qingyang Zhu, Eric Karl Oermann, Kyunghyun Cho

entry.summary: Presents a multi-task in-context learning framework for Bayesian predictive inference that adapts to new priors at test time, overcoming the limitation that prior-data-fitted models are tied to their training prior. Aims to improve robustness under distribution shift while preserving amortized inference.

entry.title: AgentArmor: A Framework, Evaluation, \& Mitigation of Coding Agent Failures

author.name: Kenneth Ge, Andre Assis

entry.summary: Studies failure modes of AI coding agents categorized into underspecification, capability errors, and harness errors, and builds an evaluation suite (AgentArmor) of 20 environments inspired by real deployment failures. Proposes mitigations for destructive agent behaviors.

entry.title: Leverage Is Not Reach: A Control-Window Law for Single-Neuron Steering in Language Models

author.name: Hongliang Liu

entry.summary: Develops a budget-normalized control-window framework for single-neuron steering in aligned LLMs, deriving a universal saturation curve that predicts when a single-neuron intervention coherently controls a behavior versus collapsing the output. Connects refusal and benign mode switches to a coherence-budget ceiling set by residual and write norms.

entry.title: Scalable Training of Spatially Grounded 2D Vision-Language Models for Radiology

author.name: Yusuf Salcan (Computer Vision Group, University of Freiburg, Germany, CRIION-AI Lab, Freiburg, Germany), Simon Ging (Computer Vision Group, University of Freiburg, Germany, Adaptive & Agentic AI), Robin Schirrmeister (Department of Radiology, Medical Center -- University of Freiburg, Germany), Philipp Arnold (Department of Radiology, Medical Center -- University of Freiburg, Germany), Elmar Kotter (Department of Radiology, Medical Center -- University of Freiburg, Germany), Behzad Bozorgtabar (Adaptive & Agentic AI), Thomas Brox (Computer Vision Group, University of Freiburg, Germany)

entry.summary: Studies scalable training of spatially grounded vision-language models for radiology without manual annotations, introducing RefRad2D, a 1.2M bilingual CT/MR image-text dataset with automatically generated VQA and grounding subsets. The resulting RadGrounder model jointly performs report generation, VQA, and spatial grounding competitively with specialized medical VLMs.

entry.title: Beyond the GUI Paradigm: Do Mobile Agents Need the Phone Screen?

author.name: Li Gu, Zihuan Jiang, Linqiang Guo, Zhixiang Chi, Ziqiang Wang, Huan Liu, Yuanhao Yu, Tse-Hsun Chen, Yang Wang

entry.summary: This paper challenges the GUI paradigm for mobile agents by showing that command-line-interface-based coding agents can outperform GUI baselines on AndroidWorld and MobileWorld without mobile-specific training. Claude Code with Opus 4.7 reaches strong scores against reproducible GUI agents.

entry.title: Language-Instructed Vision Embeddings for Controllable and Generalizable Perception

author.name: Chengzhi Mao, Xudong Lin, Wen-Sheng Chu

entry.summary: LIVE proposes using language to dynamically guide a vision encoder at inference time, producing task-centric embeddings without task-specific retraining. It reports large reductions in visual hallucinations (+34 on MMVP) and surpasses vision-language baselines.

entry.title: S-Agent: Spatial Tool-Use Elicits Reasoning for Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Yalun Dai, Hao Li, Shulin Tian, Runmao Yao, Yuhao Dong, Fangzhou Hong, Zhaoxi Chen, Fangfu Liu, Baoliang Tian, Dingwen Zhang, Tao Wang, Kim-Hui Yap, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: S-Agent is a spatial tool-use agentic paradigm that reframes spatial reasoning over multi-view images and videos as spatio-temporal evidence accumulation rather than isolated frame prediction. A VLM acts as a semantic planner invoking a hierarchy of spatial tools for scene-centric understanding.

entry.title: The distillation double bind: Distilling misaligned models either transfers misalignment or it doesn't

author.name: Alek Westover

entry.summary: This post analyzes a distillation double bind: distilling a misaligned teacher model either transfers misalignment (enabling auditing for incrimination) or it does not (enabling safe capability transfer). It proposes distillation-for-capabilities techniques to transfer capabilities without transferring misalignment.

entry.title: Beyond Entropy: Learning from Token-Level Distributional Deviations for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Xuanzhi Feng, Zhengyang Li, Zeyu Liu, Haoxi Li, Yuming Jiang, Bing Guo, Jingcai Guo, Jie Zhang, Song Guo

entry.summary: Proposes the Independent Combinatorial Tokens framework for RL with verifiable rewards that shifts optimization from scalar entropy to distributional properties of token logits using Jensen-Shannon divergence, addressing entropy collapse and explosion in LLM reasoning. Identifies tokens with distinctive distributions for targeted updates.

entry.title: What Do Safety-Aligned LLMs Learn From Mixed Compliance Demonstrations?

author.name: Sihui Dai, Mann Patel

entry.summary: Studies how safety-aligned LLMs interpret mixed in-context compliance demonstrations, mixing benign compliance with harmful compliance examples to test how composition drives harmful compliance. Finds benign and harmful demonstrations are not interchangeable and that preference optimization is the critical training stage preventing benign demos from increasing harmful compliance.

entry.title: VERITAS: Verifier-Guided Proof Search for Zero-Shot Formal Theorem Proving

author.name: Manish Acharya, Zhenyu Liao, Yueke Zhang, Kevin Leach, Yu Huang, Yifan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces VERITAS, a zero-shot formal theorem-proving framework that routes rich verifier signals back into proof search via Best-of-N sampling then critic-guided MCTS using failures as negative examples. Improves miniF2F to 40.6% and releases a combinatorics benchmark.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Reward Modeling for Stable RLHF

author.name: Licheng Pan, Haocheng Yang, Haoxuan Li, Yichen Sun, Yunsheng Lu, Shijian Wang, Lei Shen, Yuan Lu, Zhixuan Chu, Hao Wang

entry.summary: Addresses reward hacking in RLHF by making reward models output uncertainty estimates and adjusting group-based policy optimization (e.g., GRPO) to discount unreliable rewards. This targets a fundamental stability vulnerability in modern LLM alignment pipelines.

entry.title: Tracking Representation Dynamics in Large Language Models with Persistent Homology

author.name: Naman Malhotra, Jay Ambadkar, Abhinav Gupta, Kushal Kasivel, Abbas Schwarz, Kamillo Ferry, Anthea Monod

entry.summary: Uses persistent homology to track how LLM activation-space topology evolves during supervised fine-tuning across models from 1B to 7B and three alignment objectives. Finds most topological reorganization happens in the earliest training, with a transient activity peak then stabilization, and that objectives induce distinguishable signatures.

entry.title: Flow Map Denoisers: Traversing the Distortion-Perception Plane for Inverse Problems

author.name: Nicolas Zilberstein, Morteza Mardani, Santiago Segarra

entry.summary: Shows that flow map models implicitly define a one-parameter family of denoisers that continuously spans the distortion-perception frontier in image restoration, with a lookahead parameter controlling between MMSE and perceptual regimes. This avoids needing paired data, auxiliary models, or sampler tuning to access different operating points.

entry.title: What Makes Effective Supervision in Latent Chain-of-Thought: An Information-Theoretic Analysis

author.name: Xinghao Chen, Chak Tou Leong, Wenjin Guo, Jian Wang, Wenjie Li, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: Provides an information-theoretic analysis of latent chain-of-thought, identifying a dual collapse of gradient attenuation and representational drift when only outcome supervision is used. Decomposes process supervision into trajectory supervision (dense stepwise signals) and space supervision (preserving semantic structure).

entry.title: On the Variance of Temporal Difference Learning and its Reduction Using Control Variates

author.name: Hsiao-Ru Pan, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf

entry.summary: Analyzes the variance of temporal difference learning in the tabular phased setting, showing it reduces variance by aggregating over more independent trajectories and is asymptotically bounded above by Monte Carlo. Shows Direct Advantage Estimation acts as a regression-adjusted control variate achieving a tighter variance bound than TD.

entry.title: Optimal Ansatz-free Hamiltonian Learning In Situ

author.name: Taiqi Zhou, Weiyuan Gong

entry.summary: Proposes a computationally efficient, control-free, and ancilla-free algorithm for ansatz-free Hamiltonian learning using only Pauli product state preparation and measurement, achieving Heisenberg-limited scaling with shallow circuits suited to near-term quantum devices. Improves practicality over prior protocols requiring deep circuits.

entry.title: QMaxCal: Path-Space Regularization for Open Quantum Control via Girsanov's Theorem

author.name: Merijn Moody, Zier Mensch, Miranda C. N. Cheng, Peter G. Bolhuis, Max Welling

entry.summary: Uses Girsanov's theorem to derive a closed-form differentiable KL-divergence estimator between trajectory distributions of continuously monitored open quantum systems, yielding path-space regularizers (QMaxCal) that drive systems toward decoherence-minimal states. Improves robust quantum control under noise.

entry.title: Pose6DAug: Physically Plausible Multi-view Object Swapping for Robot Data Augmentation

author.name: Jonghoon Lee, Seong Hyeon Park, Byungwoo Jeon, Minha Lee, Jinwoo Shin

entry.summary: Introduces Pose6DAug, a failure-driven data augmentation framework that converts a robot policy's successful episodes into targeted demonstrations for its failure modes by physically plausibly swapping manipulated objects across calibrated multi-view observations. Improves VLA policy robustness to out-of-distribution objects without new data collection.

entry.title: REDACT: A Systematically Controlled Multilingual Benchmark for Personal Information Detection

author.name: Guneesh Vats, Anubha Agrawal, Shikha Singhal, Ajita Dash, Praison Selvaraj, Vidhan Jhawar, Ranga Prasad Chenna, Bharadwaj Y M G

entry.summary: Introduces REDACT, a systematically controlled multilingual PII detection benchmark with 13,427 records, 324,078 annotations, 51 entity types, 25 languages across 9 scripts, and a covering-array sampler controlling nine generation axes. Includes GDPR-aligned sensitivity metadata for stratified evaluation of detector failures.

entry.title: StylisticBias: A Few Human Visual Cues Drive Most Social Biases in MLLMs

author.name: Shaghayegh Kolli, Timo Cavelius, Nafiseh Nikeghbal, Samantha Dalal, Jana Diesner

entry.summary: StylisticBias is a controlled benchmark that varies single visual attributes on fixed identities (around 25K images from 500 base faces) to isolate which appearance cues drive social bias in multimodal LLMs. It finds that a few human visual cues account for most observed biases.

entry.title: ImageWAM: Do World Action Models Really Need Video Generation, or Just Image Editing?

author.name: Yuyang Zhang, Wenyao Zhang, Zekun Qi, He Zhang, Haitao Lin, Jingbo Zhang, Yao Mu, Xiaokang Yang, Wenjun Zeng, Xin Jin

entry.summary: ImageWAM questions whether world action models need full video generation, repurposing pretrained image editing models for robot action prediction via target-frame transformation. It argues image editing provides a better-matched, cheaper prior than dense video prediction.

entry.title: SSD: Spatially Speculative Decoding Accelerates Autoregressive Image Generation

author.name: Shilong Xiang, Zirui Zhang, Lijun Yu, Chengzhi Mao

entry.summary: SSD (Spatially Speculative Decoding) accelerates autoregressive image generation by exploiting 2D spatial locality, predicting adjacent horizontal and vertical tokens simultaneously rather than only the next token in a flattened 1D sequence. This overcomes the memory wall in visual inference.

entry.title: MemoryWAM: Efficient World Action Modeling with Persistent Memory

author.name: Sizhe Yang, Juncheng Mu, Tianming Wei, Chenhao Lu, Xiaofan Li, Linning Xu, Zhengrong Xue, Zhecheng Yuan, Dahua Lin, Jiangmiao Pang, Huazhe Xu

entry.summary: MemoryWAM is a world action model with persistent memory that addresses the trade-off between efficient bounded-window inference and costly long-history modeling for robotic manipulation in non-Markovian environments. It enables both memory and dynamics modeling for robust manipulation.

entry.title: Deontic Policies for Runtime Governance of Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Anupam Joshi, Tim Finin, Karuna Pande Joshi, Lalana Kagal

entry.summary: Proposes using deontic logic (permissions, prohibitions, obligations, waivers, and conflict precedence) to govern autonomous agentic AI systems at runtime, beyond standard access control. Argues current policy engines like XACML cannot capture the full structure of enterprise governance needed for tool-using, peer-coordinating agents.

entry.title: ORAgentBench: Can LLM Agents Solve Challenging Operations Research Tasks End to End?

author.name: Jiajun Li, Mingshu Cai, Yixuan Li, Yu Ding, Ran Hou, Guanyu Nie, Xiongwei Han, Wanyuan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces ORAgentBench, an execution-grounded benchmark of 107 human-reviewed end-to-end operations research tasks requiring agents to go from operational artifacts and data files to validated decisions in isolated environments. Tests the full modeling-plus-solving workflow rather than pre-formalized instances.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Transactive Memory

author.name: To Eun Kim, Xuhong He, Dishank Jain, Ambuj Agrawal, Negar Arabzadeh, Fernando Diaz

entry.summary: Extends retrieval-augmented generation to retrieval of agent-generated artifacts (trajectories encoding reusable procedural knowledge) shared across a heterogeneous population of LLM agents, analogous to transactive memory in human teams. Builds infrastructure to organize and reuse agent experience.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Measuring Logical Compliance of Predictive Models

author.name: Guillaume Olivier Delplanque (LIG), Pierre Genev\`es (LIG), Nabil Laya\"ida (LIG, TYREX), Zephirin Faure

entry.summary: Duplicate id reference resolved above.

entry.title: Toward Calibrated Mixture-of-Experts Under Distribution Shift

author.name: Gina Wong, Drew Prinster, Suchi Saria, Rama Chellappa, Anqi Liu

entry.summary: Studies calibration of mixture-of-experts models under distribution shift, focusing on how routing interacts with expert-level calibration. Shows that expert calibration is sufficient to ensure overall model calibration under a broad class of distribution shifts.

entry.title: How LLMs Fail and Generalize in RTL Coding for Hardware Design?

author.name: Guan-Ting Liu, Chao-Han Huck Yang, Chenhui Deng, Zhongzhi Yu, Brucek Khailany, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a cognitively-inspired error taxonomy (syntactic, semantic, solvable, unsolvable functional) for LLM-generated RTL hardware code and shows frontier models plateau near 90.8% on VerilogEval due to unsolvable functional errors immune to test-time compute. Authors include NVIDIA researchers.

entry.title: Can In-Context Learning Support Intrinsic Curiosity?

author.name: Eric Elmoznino, Sangnie Bhardwaj, Johannes von Oswald, Rajai Nasser, Blaise Ag\"uera y Arcas, Jo\~ao Sacramento, Rif A. Saurous, Guillaume Lajoie

entry.summary: Investigates whether the emergent in-context learning of sequence models can support intrinsic curiosity by estimating learning progress without expensive gradient inner-loops. Notable authorship including Aguera y Arcas and Lajoie from Google.

entry.title: StaminaBench: Stress-Testing Coding Agents over 100 Interaction Turns

author.name: Vlad Sobal, Shuo Yang, Yuting Zhang, Wei Xia, Stefano Soatto

entry.summary: Introduces StaminaBench, a benchmark measuring how many consecutive change-request turns coding agents handle before failing (up to 100 turns, 6000-line codebases), with fully programmatic test generation for reproducibility. Better matches real long-running coding sessions than fraction-of-tasks-solved metrics.

entry.title: Thermodynamic Signatures of Reasoning: Free-Energy and Spectral-Form-Factor Diagnostics for Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models

author.name: Salim Khazem

entry.summary: Introduces Free-Energy Signatures, a thermodynamics-inspired spectral descriptor of attention Laplacians for detecting hallucinations in LLMs, using partition functions, free energy, and random-matrix spectral form factors. Provides Lipschitz stability proofs and richer use of the Laplacian spectrum than prior scalar diagnostics.

entry.title: 3D-DLP: Self-Supervised 3D Object-Centric Scene Representation Learning

author.name: Ellina Zhang, Madhaven Iyengar, Amir Zadeh, Chuan Li, Deepak Pathak, David Held, Tal Daniel

entry.summary: 3D-DLP is a self-supervised object-centric model that decomposes RGB-D or voxel scenes into 3D latent particles encoding disentangled attributes like keypoints, bounding boxes, and appearance. The learned representations are interpretable and controllable, enabling novel scene generation.

entry.title: Displacement Is Not Direction: Evaluating Fidelity Metrics for Quantized LLM Deployment

author.name: Milo\v{s} Nikoli\'c, Ali Hadi Zadeh, Enrique Torres Sanchez, Andreas Moshovos

entry.summary: Tests whether per-token KL divergence is a reliable proxy for benchmark quality in quantized LLM deployment, using large quant cohorts of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Devstral-Small-2-24B. Finds strong overall correlation that collapses to non-significance in the near-baseline silent zone, cautioning against KLD-based fidelity metrics there.

entry.title: Global Convergence of Gradient Descent for Score Matching in Gaussian Mixtures via Reverse Fisher Divergence

author.name: Alexander Tyurin

entry.summary: Analyzes gradient descent for score matching in Gaussian mixtures using the reverse Fisher divergence (expectation under the student) instead of the standard forward divergence. Proves global convergence, addressing initialization-dependent failures of the forward objective.

entry.title: ADaPT: Token-Level Decoupling for Efficient Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Tingyun Li, Zishang Jiang, Jinyi Han, Xinyi Wang, Sihang Jiang, Han Xia, Zhaoqian Dai, Shuguang Ma, Fei Yu, Jiaqing Liang, Yanghua Xiao

entry.summary: ADaPT introduces token-level decoupling of efficiency and correctness signals for large reasoning models, using a mode-selection token to control fast versus slow reasoning. It addresses sequence-level coupling that penalizes long but correct chain-of-thought trajectories.

entry.title: Activation- and Influence-Aware Ranks (AIR): Function-Preserving SVD Compression for LLMs

author.name: Nico Harder, Daniel Becking, Karsten Mueller, Wojciech Samek

entry.summary: AIR is an SVD-based LLM compression method that guides each weight matrix's low-rank approximation using a backward-signal influence metric via a closed-form alternating least squares sweep. It improves perplexity over SVD-LLM by over 18 percent at low parameter retention and translates savings into FLOP, memory, and latency gains.

entry.title: Recurrent neural networks approximate continuous functions

author.name: Valentin Abadie, Clemens Hutter, Helmut B\"olcskei

entry.summary: Proves that a single fixed-weight ReLU recurrent neural network with fixed hidden dimension can uniformly approximate any continuous function on an interval by running longer, with accuracy bought through computation time rather than new networks. Introduces an intermediate Turing-machine-with-neural-units model to enable the construction.

entry.title: Direct Advantage Estimation for Scalable and Sample-efficient Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hsiao-Ru Pan, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf

entry.summary: Extends Direct Advantage Estimation to partially observable domains with minimal modifications and reduces its computational cost using discrete latent dynamics models to approximate transition probabilities. Demonstrates improved scalability and sample efficiency on the Arcade Learning Environment.

entry.title: Fisher-Geometric Sharpness and the Implicit Bias of SGD toward Flat Minima

author.name: Md Sakir Ahmed, Kumaresh Sarmah, Hemen Dutta

entry.summary: This paper grounds the concept of loss landscape flatness in Riemannian geometry via the Fisher Information Matrix, proving that the resulting sharpness measure is invariant under function-preserving reparametrizations. It addresses a long-standing critique that standard Euclidean flatness measures are not reparametrization-invariant, thereby strengthening the theoretical foundation of the flat-minima generalization narrative.

entry.title: DF-ExpEnse: Diffusion Filtered Exploration for Sample Efficient Finetuning

author.name: Calvin Luo, Chen Sun, Shuran Song

entry.summary: Introduces DF-ExpEnse, a diffusion-filtered exploration technique that uses a generative control policy's multimodal candidate set and a critic ensemble to improve online experience collection and finetuning sample efficiency for robot policies. Supports cross-agent collaborative exploration in fleet settings.

entry.title: Beyond Averaging in John Ellipsoid Approximation: High-Accuracy Algorithms in the Leverage-Score Model

author.name: Xiaoyu Li, Junwei Yu, Jiaojiao Jiang, Junbin Gao, Andi Han

entry.summary: Provides high-accuracy algorithms for John ellipsoid approximation in the leverage-score model by separating the complexity into certification, identification, and accuracy costs, locating the historical epsilon-inverse factor in only the first. Connects to D-optimal experimental design and improves over prior leverage-score methods.

entry.title: Off-Policy Evaluation for Missingness-Aware Policies in MDPs with Rewards Missing Not at Random

author.name: Ziheng Wei, Annie Qu, Rui Miao

entry.summary: Studies off-policy evaluation in finite-horizon MDPs when rewards are missing not at random, breaking ignorability and inducing selection bias. Formalizes a reward-dependent propensity model and introduces a bridge function using future states as shadow variables to identify the conditional mean reward.

entry.title: HEPTv2: End-to-End Efficient Point Transformer for Charged Particle Reconstruction

author.name: Siqi Miao, Shitij Govil, Jack P. Rodgers, Mia Liu, Javier Duarte, Shih-Chieh Hsu, Yuan-Tang Chou, Pan Li

entry.summary: Presents HEPTv2, an end-to-end point-transformer for charged-particle tracking at the High-Luminosity LHC that reconstructs tracks from detector hits in a single trainable pipeline, avoiding the auxiliary stages of prior transformer and GNN approaches. Combines locality-sensitive techniques for efficiency under extreme combinatorial ambiguity.

entry.title: Characterizing Narrative Content in Web-scale LLM Pretraining Data

author.name: Teagan Johnson, Elliott Ash, Andrew Piper, Maria Antoniak

entry.summary: Presents the first fine-grained study of narrative content in a 3-trillion-token open pretraining corpus (Dolma), designing an 11-dimension framework over agency, setting, and events and training NarraBERT to annotate 3M passages into the new NarraDolma dataset. Reveals that narrative structure is measurable at scale across heterogeneous web data.

entry.title: SAGE-OPD: Selective Agent-Guided Intervention for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yuhang Zhou, Lizhu Zhang, Yifan Wu, Mingyi Wang, Bo Peng, Jiayi Liu, Xiangjun Fan, Zhuokai Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes SAGE-OPD, a verifier-free selective intervention framework for multi-turn on-policy distillation that avoids over-penalizing valid alternatives and propagating unreliable teacher supervision on off-distribution histories. Targets the compounding-error problem in realistic multi-turn LLM agent training.

entry.title: HydraHead: From Head-Level Functional Heterogeneity to Specialized Attention Hybridization

author.name: Zhentao Tan, Wei Chen, Jingyi Shen, Yao Liu, Xu Shen, Yue Wu, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: HydraHead proposes hybridizing linear and full attention at the head level rather than layer level, motivated by interpretability findings that heads within a layer specialize functionally. The approach aims to reduce the quadratic cost of attention for long-context processing.

entry.title: NEST: Narrative Event Structures in Time for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Ali Asgarov, Kaushik Narasimhan, Najibul Haque Sarker, Hani Alomari, Chia-Wei Tang, Anushka Sivakumar, Zaber Ibn Abdul Hakim, Shaurya Mallampati, Chris Thomas

entry.summary: NEST is a benchmark of 1005 full-length movies for evaluating narrative event structure understanding in long videos, moving beyond needle-in-a-haystack retrieval to test how actions form events and connect across time. It probes whether models can link distant causally related plot points.

entry.title: CrossFlow: One-Step Generation Across Latent and Pixel Spaces

author.name: Xiyuan Wang, Xiao Zhang, Yang Li, Ruoxi Jiang, Zhao Zhong, Liefeng Bo, Muhan Zhang

entry.summary: CrossFlow introduces a cross-space flow formulation that maps noisy latent inputs directly to pixel-space images using a velocity-free one-step objective, resolving the mismatch between latent-space training and decoder-dependent final quality. It unifies generation across latent and pixel spaces.

entry.title: FlowBender: Feedback-Aware Training for Self-Correcting Conditional Flows

author.name: Daniel Gilo, Sven Elflein, Ido Sobol, Or Litany

entry.summary: FlowBender introduces feedback-aware training for conditional diffusion and flow models so that generated outputs actually satisfy the constraints defining the task (such as depth conditioning) by leveraging the forward operator during training. This addresses a chronic failure mode where conditional generative models ignore the conditioning signal at inference.

entry.title: Research agenda: Interpretive debate

author.name: Shi

entry.summary: This LessWrong research agenda proposes interpretive debate as epistemic infrastructure for iteratively and empirically resolving fuzzy interpretive questions about AI models such as whether a model is scheming, lying, or introspecting. It builds on prior performative misalignment work as a minimal demonstration.

entry.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Black-Box Uncertainty Estimation Methods for Large Language Models

author.name: Jiayi Wang, Xu-Yao Zhang

entry.summary: Provides a systematic review and unified empirical comparison of black-box uncertainty estimation methods for LLMs, organizing them into five categories (verbalization, sampling, explanation, multi-agent, and others). Addresses the fragmentation of the field where internal signals like logits are unavailable.

entry.title: DeepSWIP: Quotient-WMC Counterfactuals for Neural Probabilistic Logic Programs

author.name: Saimun Habib, Vaishak Belle, Fengxiang He

entry.summary: Introduces DeepSWIP, a single-world counterfactual semantics for DeepProbLog neurosymbolic programs that reduces fixed-context neural predicates to ProbLog choices, applies Single World Intervention Programs, and computes counterfactuals via weighted model counting over a single transformed program. Provides exactness guarantees under finite grounding assumptions.

entry.title: Insulin4RL: Real-Time Insulin Management in the Intensive Care Unit for Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Thomas Frost, Steve Harris

entry.summary: Insulin4RL is an offline RL dataset for ICU insulin management derived from MIMIC-IV, preserving naturally irregular clinical timing rather than fixed discretized intervals. It contains over 375,000 labelled decisions across 12,209 patients to support more realistic clinical RL evaluation.

entry.title: Compositionality Emerges in a Narrow Depth-Connectivity Regime: Architecture Constraints and Solution Manifolds

author.name: Dat H. Do, Rushi Shah, Duc V. Le, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: Shows compositionality emerges only in a narrow sweet spot along connectivity and depth axes, depending heavily on which connections remain rather than weight sparsity alone, and peaking at target-dependent depths. Characterizes architecture constraints and solution manifolds underlying compositional structure.

entry.title: When Calibration Fails the Vulnerable Hospital: Federated Conformal Risk Control via Risk-Curve Shrinkage

author.name: Nafis Fuad Shahid

entry.summary: Quantifies how naive pooled conformal risk control in federated medical segmentation protects the average hospital while violating coverage at 40 percent of individual institutions, using real multi-institutional brain tumor data. Proposes federated CRC via risk-curve shrinkage to balance per-site coverage against the impractical 83x set inflation of purely local CRC.

entry.title: Critical Percolation as a Synthetic Data Model for Interpretability

author.name: Aryeh Brill, Tom Ingebretsen Carlson

entry.summary: Introduces a family of synthetic datasets built from hierarchical functions on critical mean-field percolation clusters to provide realistic multi-scale structure for evaluating interpretability methods. The data is analytically tractable with known critical exponents that fix its properties without hyperparameter tuning.

entry.title: A Solver-Free Training Method for Predict-then-Optimize

author.name: Beichen Wan, Mo Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a solver-free training method for predict-then-optimize problems, avoiding expensive optimization-solver calls during gradient evaluation by using a measure transformation principle. Improves scalability of decision-focused learning for linear and combinatorial optimization.

entry.title: GEMS: Geometric Constraints Enable Multi-Semantic Superposition in LLMs

author.name: Yu Deng

entry.summary: Identifies that multi-direction activation steering collapse stems from two distinct sources, distributional deviation and directional interference, and proposes GEMS, geometric constraints enabling multi-semantic superposition without retraining. Allows simultaneous injection of multiple semantic directions in LLMs.

entry.title: The Correctness Illusion in LLM-Generated GPU Kernels

author.name: Dipankar Sarkar

entry.summary: Demonstrates that standard benchmarks for LLM-generated GPU kernels rely on fixed-shape, small-sample allclose checks that fail to catch bugs, and proposes op-schema-aware seeded fuzzing with high-precision references and per-op tolerances. The improved oracle flags all seeded buggy kernels while passing correct ones.

entry.title: NAMESAKES: Probing Identity Memorization in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Morris Alper, Vasudha Varadarajan, Moran Yanuka, Angelina Wang, Hadar Averbuch-Elor

entry.summary: NAMESAKES introduces a fully black-box behavioral probe to distinguish memorized versus fabricated faces in text-to-image models without reference photos or training-data access, plus a dataset of over a thousand public-figure names across fame levels. It addresses privacy concerns around identity memorization.

entry.title: Thinking in Boxes: 3D Editing in Real Images Made Easy

author.name: Pradhaan S Bhat, Naveen Chandra R, Rishubh Parihar, Vaibhav Vavilala, R. Venkatesh Babu, D. A. Forsyth, Anand Bhattad

entry.summary: Thinking in Boxes uses 3D bounding boxes as structured specifications (input and output boxes) to give precise control over translation, rotation, scaling, and viewpoint in real image editing, casting editing as a well-posed geometry problem. Color-coded box faces convey 3D orientation.

entry.title: Slow Brain, Fast Planner: Latency-Resilient VLM-Augmented Urban Navigation

author.name: Zhenghao "Mark'' Peng, Honglin He, Quanyi Li, Yukai Ma, Bolei Zhou

entry.summary: This work proposes a VLM-Planner interface for latency-resilient urban sidewalk navigation, where a slow VLM improves trajectory scoring of a fast anchor-based planner to close the trajectory scoring gap without replacing it with an end-to-end model. It addresses cases where good candidates exist but are poorly scored.

entry.title: LLM Doesn't Know What It Doesn't Know: Detecting Epistemic Blind Spots via Cross-Model Attribution Divergence on Clinical Tabular Data

author.name: Akshat Dasula, Prasanna Desikan, Jaideep Srivastava

entry.summary: Studies whether LLMs can recognize the limits of their own knowledge on structured clinical tabular tasks using cross-model attribution divergence against XGBoost. Finds LLM verbalized confidence is nearly constant regardless of accuracy and shows an inverse difficulty effect.

entry.title: Interpreting Neural Combinatorial Optimization via Evolving Programmatic Bottlenecks

author.name: Haocheng Duan, Yuxin Guo, Jieyi Bi, Anqi Xie, Sirui Li, Yining Ma, Cathy Wu

entry.summary: Introduces Evolving Programmatic Bottlenecks (EPB), claimed first framework to interpret neural combinatorial optimization policies by distilling black-box models into human-readable program portfolios via an LLM that evolves programs whose per-step action distributions serve as bottlenecks. Targets the dynamic, state-dependent nature of NCO decisions.

entry.title: CombEval: A Framework for Evaluating Combinatorial Counting in Large Language Models

author.name: Yuxu Zhou, Ond\v{r}ej Ku\v{z}elka, Yuyi Wang, Yuanhong Wang, Yi Chang

entry.summary: Presents CombEval, a dynamic benchmark for combinatorial counting in LLMs using typed Cofola specifications that allow controlled variation of object type, scale, constraints, and reasoning depth with solver-verified answers. Finds 11 LLMs remain brittle on ordered objects, indistinguishable elements, and nested dependencies.

entry.title: Multi-LCB: Extending LiveCodeBench to Multiple Programming Languages

author.name: Maria Ivanova, Pavel Zadorozhny, Rodion Levichev, Ivan Petrov, Adamenko Pavel, Ivan Lopatin, Alexey Kutalev, Dmitrii Babaev

entry.summary: Introduces Multi-LCB, extending the contamination-aware LiveCodeBench from Python to twelve programming languages by transforming Python tasks into equivalent tasks in other languages. Tests whether LLMs generalize coding ability across the diverse languages needed in real software engineering.

entry.title: Disentangling Linguistic Relatedness from Task Alignment in Cross-Lingual Transfer

author.name: Ahmed Haj Ahmed, Ruochen Zhang, Alvin Grissom II

entry.summary: Studies cross-lingual transfer by fine-tuning seven LLMs (4B-671B) on Arabic and testing zero-shot on Semitic vs non-Semitic languages, finding no evidence of language-family-specific transfer. Improvements instead reflect task-format alignment, a finding reinforced by chain-of-thought ablations.

entry.title: Cost-Optimal LLM Routing with Limited User Feedback under User Satisfaction Guarantees

author.name: Herbert Woisetschl\"ager, Arastun Mammadli, Ryan Zhang, Shiqiang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes SLARouter, an online cost-aware LLM routing algorithm that learns from sparse one-sided production feedback while providing service-level-agreement satisfaction guarantees. Addresses the cost-quality tension in commercial LLM serving without offline training or per-workload tuning.

entry.title: Emyx: Fast and efficient all-atom protein generation

author.name: Nicholas J. Williams, Ward Haddadin, Matteo P. Ferla, Constantin Schneider, Nicholas B. Woodall, Ruby Sedgwick, Christian D. Madsen, Andrew L. Hopkins, Edward O. Pyzer-Knapp

entry.summary: Introduces Emyx, a lightweight 140M-parameter conditional flow-matching model for all-atom protein generation that replaces heavy structure-prediction architectures with efficient transformer blocks and sparse connectivity. Targets enzyme design with reduced training cost and improved sample diversity.

entry.title: FAPO: Fully Autonomous Prompt Optimization of Multi-Step LLM Pipelines

author.name: Paul Kassianik, Baturay Saglam, Huaibo Zhao, Blaine Nelson, Supriti Vijay, Aman Priyanshu, Amin Karbasi

entry.summary: Presents FAPO, a framework letting an LLM coding agent (Claude Code) autonomously optimize multi-step LLM pipelines by inspecting intermediate steps, diagnosing failures, and proposing prompt or structural edits when attribution finds a bottleneck. Outperforms the GEPA baseline across six benchmarks.

entry.title: LOKI: Memory-Free Null-Space Constrained Lifelong Knowledge Editing

author.name: Masih Eskandar, Miquel Sirera Perell\'o, Stratis Ioannidis, Jennifer Dy

entry.summary: Introduces LOKI, a memory-free lifelong knowledge editing method using dynamic layer selection via the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion and null-space gradient projection to update LLMs sequentially without accessing prior knowledge. Reduces catastrophic forgetting and preprocessing requirements.

entry.title: Tri-Info: Generalizable, Interpretable Failure Prediction for VLA Models via Information Theory

author.name: Jinghan Yang, Yunchao Zhang, Wang Yuan, Haolun Wan, Jiaming Zhang, Zhengyang Hu, Yanchao Yang

entry.summary: Proposes Tri-Info, an information-theoretic method for generalizable, interpretable failure detection in Vision-Language-Action models, using signals about action diversity, temporal consistency, and state coupling. Demonstrates cross-architecture and cross-environment transfer.

entry.title: LLM agent safety, multi-turn red-teaming, jailbreak benchmarks, adversarial robustness, safety-critical systems

author.name: Hanwool Lee, Dasol Choi, Bokyeong Kim, Seung Geun Kim, Haon Park

entry.summary: Presents NRT-Bench, a multi-turn red-teaming benchmark for LLM agents acting as operators of a safety-critical system, instantiated in a simulated nuclear plant control room with objective harm signals tied to loss of critical safety functions. Characterizes agent robustness under sustained adaptive adversarial pressure.

entry.title: Efficient and Sound Probabilistic Verification for AI Agents

author.name: Alaia Solko-Breslin, Pramod Kaushik Mudrakarta, Mihai Christodorescu, Somesh Jha, Krishnamurthy Dj Dvijotham

entry.summary: Extends runtime monitoring of AI agents from deterministic Datalog policies to probabilistic predicates and state transitions without requiring independence assumptions, providing efficient and sound probabilistic verification. Addresses real ambiguity in security policy enforcement like fallible PII detectors.

entry.title: FlexLAM: Resolving the Bottleneck Trade-off in Latent Action Learning

author.name: Takanori Yoshimoto, Yang Hu, Naruya Kondo, Tatsuya Matsushima

entry.summary: FlexLAM addresses the capacity bottleneck trade-off in latent action models by using variable-length latent codes trained with nested dropout, yielding prefix-valid codes that adapt detail to need. A single model matches separately tuned fixed-capacity variants for video-to-action learning.

entry.title: MortarBench: Evaluating Mortgage Loan Origination Agents

author.name: Matthew Toles, Yunan Lu, Manav Munjal, Bojun Liu, Yuanhao Deng, Stephanie Selig, Derek Rindner, Cheng Li, Zhou Yu

entry.summary: MortarBench is a new benchmark for evaluating LLM agents in mortgage loan origination, using synthetic financial data with edge-case coverage matching real distributions. State-of-the-art models score poorly, with the best closed model reaching only 77 percent exact match.

entry.title: Calibrating Generative Models to Feature Distributions with MMD Finetuning

author.name: Nathaniel L. Diamant, Brian L. Trippe

entry.summary: kCGM finetunes generative models to match a target feature distribution by minimizing maximum mean discrepancy with an unbiased score-function estimator and KL regularization. It enables controlled calibration of which features match, useful for applications like steering molecular generators toward a therapeutic class.

entry.title: Shifting-based Optimizable Linear Relaxations for General Activation Functions

author.name: Philipp Kern, L\'aszl\'o Antal, Erika \'Abr\'aham, Carsten Sinz

entry.summary: SLiR is a shifting-based, broadly-applicable method for constructing optimizable linear relaxations of arbitrary activation functions for neural network verification, requiring only a Lipschitz constant or set of critical points. It avoids the hand-crafted per-activation relaxations that existing verification techniques depend on.

entry.title: On the Redundancy of Timestep Embeddings in Diffusion Models

author.name: Jos\'e A. Ch\'avez

entry.summary: Challenges the necessity of explicit timestep embeddings in diffusion models, providing theory showing the global minimizer can be reached without timestep conditioning under certain conditions. Ablations on CelebA and CIFAR-10 show time-agnostic models retain high fidelity and can even surpass conditioned counterparts.

entry.title: Sparsity, Superposition, and Forgetting: A Mechanistic Study of Representation Retention in Continual Learning

author.name: Jan Wasilewski, J\k{e}drzej Kozal, Micha{\l} Wo\'zniak, Bartosz Krawczyk

entry.summary: Presents a controlled toy-world framework with a synthetic generator-separator pipeline to make continual-learning forgetting mechanisms observable, defining measurable representation strength and superposition with tunable sparsity and overlap. Uses sparse dynamical fitting (SINDy) to study retention dynamics over exposure history.

entry.title: Agentic Symbolic Search: Characterizing PDEs Beyond Hand-crafted Expressions, Meshes, and Neural Networks

author.name: Zongmin Yu, Liu Yang

entry.summary: Proposes Agentic Symbolic Search, where an agent translates PDE theory, problem constraints, and accumulated search experience into testable differentiable symbolic programs refined via evolutionary search with gradient-based parameter fitting. Aims to recover mathematical-structure characterizations of PDE solutions beyond what numerical or neural methods produce.

entry.title: The Token Is a Group Element: On Lie-Algebra Attention over Matrix Lie Groups

author.name: Przemyslaw Musialski

entry.summary: Proposes Lie-Algebra Attention where tokens are bare matrix Lie group elements and attention scores are closed-form algebra norms of relative poses rather than learned kernels. Claims to be the first such construction reaching affine full-frame groups excluded by representation-based methods.

entry.title: Quantifying Aleatoric Uncertainty of In-Context Learning for Robust Measure of LLM Prediction Confidence

author.name: Jinseok Chung, Minkyoung Song, Hyunji Jung, Namhoon Lee

entry.summary: Introduces self-function vectors built on Bayesian and mechanistic interpretability views to quantify aleatoric uncertainty in in-context learning, enabling a more robust measure of LLM prediction confidence. Aims to separate data-driven failures from model limitations in ICL.

entry.title: Multimodal Concept Bottleneck Models

author.name: Tongqing Shi, Ge Yan, Tuomas Oikarinen, Tsui-Wei Weng

entry.summary: Proposes Multimodal Concept Bottleneck Models that extend CBMs into CLIP using dual concept bottleneck layers to align image and text embeddings into interpretable features, enabling zero-shot classification and image retrieval while reducing concept information leakage. Improves generalization beyond fixed predefined classes.

entry.title: Online Dynamic Batching with Formal Guarantees for LLM Training

author.name: Dian Li, Zekun Wang, Yaoru Wang, Jiahong Yan

entry.summary: Introduces Online Dynamic Batching, a DataLoader-side system that moves batch formation to the point where true per-sample cost is observable (after preprocessing and tokenization) while preserving distributed step alignment, formalized as the Distributed Group Alignment Problem with deadlock-free termination guarantees. Improves padding and GPU utilization in LLM training.
