entry.title: Efficient Financial Language Understanding via Distillation with Synthetic Data

author.name: Wen-Fong (Xavier), Huang, Edwin Simpson

entry.summary: This work presents an efficient framework for financial sentiment analysis that distills knowledge from large teacher models to compact students using synthetic data, with clustering-based seed selection for more representative synthetic examples. It targets low-resource finance settings constrained by data confidentiality.

entry.title: Learning Robust Pair Confidence for Multimodal Emotion-Cause Pair Extraction

author.name: Zhuangzhuang Pan, Ning Dong, Yingna Su, Yan Xia

entry.summary: RPCL is a training-only framework for multimodal emotion-cause pair extraction that addresses pair-confidence brittleness by separating gold pairs from row-wise hard negatives through a margin constraint. It improves the relative confidence geometry among competing causes that standard cross-entropy leaves under-constrained.

entry.title: G-IdiomAlign: A Gloss-Pivoted Benchmark for Cross-Lingual Idiom Alignment

author.name: Fengying Ye, Yanming Sun, Runzhe Zhan, Zheqi Zhang, Lidia S. Chao, Derek F. Wong

entry.summary: Introduces G-IdiomAlign, a benchmark for cross-lingual idiom alignment using English Wiktionary glosses as semantic pivots, with multiple-choice and contrastive generation protocols. It reveals literal-translation bias as a dominant failure mode in LLMs, especially for low-resource target languages.

entry.title: Architectural Bias in Face Presentation Attack Detection: A Comparative Study of Vision Transformers and Convolutional Neural Networks

author.name: Ngela Landon Ntung, Floride Tuyisenge, Jema David Ndibwile

entry.summary: Comparative study of whether Vision Transformers reduce demographic bias in face presentation attack detection relative to CNNs, evaluated on the CeFA cross-ethnicity dataset across African, East Asian, and zero-shot Central groups. Examines architectural bias and skin-tone disparities.

entry.title: ROSA-TFormer: A Radar-Optical Sensor-Aware Temporal Transformer for Pinus sylvestris Plantation Classification in Northern Shaanxi Using GEE-Derived Sentinel-1/2 Time Series

author.name: Nengbo Zhang, Chang sheng

entry.summary: ROSA-TFormer is a radar-optical sensor-aware temporal Transformer for classifying Pinus sylvestris plantations from Sentinel-1/2 time series via Google Earth Engine. It fuses SAR and optical branches with a sensor-aware gate and temporal attention.

entry.title: The Market in the Model: Latent Diffusion as Neural Economy

author.name: Eryk Salvaggio

entry.summary: A humanities/critique paper that interprets latent diffusion models as a neural economy, analyzing the ideological and engineering decisions embedded in each model component beyond dataset critique. It treats the model mechanism itself, not just data, as a site of cultural analysis.

entry.title: Porting MACHIAVELLI To Inspect

author.name: Koby Lewis

entry.summary: Documents porting the MACHIAVELLI ethics benchmark (measuring unethical agent behavior under goal pursuit) to the Inspect evaluation framework, lowering barriers for evaluators to run it on new model generations. Shares practical lessons for newcomers to evals work.

entry.title: Cluster-Aware Dual-Level Test Specification Generation for Large-Scale Automotive Software Requirements

author.name: Hazem Ayman, Menna Sedik, Kareem Mostafa, Mahmoud Soliman, Samer Saber, Ibrahim Habib

entry.summary: Presents a Cluster-then-Summarize pipeline for generating Automotive SPICE-compliant test specifications from thousands of requirements using LLMs. It addresses context-window limits and inter-requirement dependencies that hurt naive LLM approaches.

entry.title: L-Proto: Language-Aware Episodic Prototypical Training for Multilingual Speaker Verification

author.name: Hyung-Seok Oh, Deok-Hyeon Cho, Seung-Bin Kim, Seong-Whan Lee

entry.summary: L-Proto is a language-aware episodic prototypical training strategy for multilingual speaker verification that constructs language-consistent episodes to disentangle speaker identity from linguistic variability. It reduces language-driven clustering and improves cross-language generalization.

entry.title: ED3R: Energy-Aware Distributed Disaster Detection Enabled by Cooperative Robotic Agents

author.name: Lina Magoula, Nikolaos Koursioumpas, Nancy Alonistioti, Ramin Khalili

entry.summary: Introduces ED3R, an energy-aware distributed framework for wildfire detection that splits decision-making between a robot and a remote controller under uncertainty and resource constraints. Optimizes detection confidence, energy cost, and time-to-detection.

entry.title: Perceptual compensation for tonal context in self-supervised speech models

author.name: James Kirby, Ioana Krehan, Michele Gubian

entry.summary: Tests whether the wav2vec2.0 self-supervised speech architecture exhibits perceptual compensation for tonal context using a Mandarin tone experiment. Finds little compensation in pretrained embeddings and only partial evidence in probing classifiers, contrasting with prior reports.

entry.title: Trustworthy Self-Composable Big-Data-as-a-Service: An LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Data Engineering, AutoML, MLOps Deployment, and Drift-Aware Lifecycle Optimization

author.name: Aueaphum Aueawatthanaphisut, Badri Raj Lamichhane

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-orchestrated multi-agent framework for end-to-end Big-Data-as-a-Service automation spanning ingestion, cleaning, feature engineering, AutoML, MLOps deployment, and drift-aware monitoring. Emphasizes governance and human oversight across the lifecycle.

entry.title: Trainable Photonic Measurement for Physics-Informed PDE Learning

author.name: Jiale Linghu, Hao Dong, Yangshuai Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a photonic quantum neural field where coordinates become trainable optical phases mixed by multi-photon Fock-space interference and decoded from photon-number measurements, for physics-informed PDE learning. The photonic circuit itself serves as the neural-field representation rather than a fixed feature map.

entry.title: Graph Grounded Cross Attention Transformer Neural Network for Structurally Constrained Full Event Sequence Generation in Predictive Process Monitoring

author.name: Fang Wang, Ernesto Damiani

entry.summary: GGATN is a graph-grounded cross-attention transformer for generating full structurally constrained event sequences in predictive process monitoring, using a global process graph as activity memory. It preserves transition feasibility, temporal order, and attribute consistency unlike component-task approaches.

entry.title: Seed-Guided Semi-Supervised Clustering by A-Contrario Anomaly Detection

author.name: Nassir Mohammad

entry.summary: Presents a seed-guided semi-supervised clustering framework based on a-contrario anomaly detection, defining a cluster as a maximal subset containing no anomalies relative to a uniform-randomness null hypothesis. It avoids heuristic global density parameters and over-assignment of outliers.

entry.title: Test-Time Adaptation in Optical Coherence Tomography Using Trajectory-Aligned Time-Independent Flow

author.name: Veit Hucke, Thomas Pinetz, Gregor Reiter, Ursula Schmidt-Erfurth, Hrvoje Bogunovi\'c

entry.summary: This work introduces a flow-matching-based test-time adaptation method for OCT imaging that generates high-quality surrogate images from noisy inputs by matching histograms to synthetic reference trajectories and removing time conditioning. It claims SOTA performance for robust ophthalmic image analysis.

entry.title: Structure Over Nonlinearity: Explicit Interaction Architectures for Dynamical Learning

author.name: Augusto Sarti

entry.summary: This paper proposes wave-inspired explicit structured dynamical units with internal state for modeling dynamical systems, deriving modeling capacity from structure rather than expressive nonlinearities. The strictly causal organization eliminates algebraic loops, yielding fully explicit models.

entry.title: Written by AI, Managed by AI: Semantic Space Control and Index Sickness Elimination Across 391 Consecutive Sessions

author.name: Hui Zhang, Shuren Song

entry.summary: Documents an action-research case study over 391 sessions in a real software project showing that adding more formal symbolic constraints to long-horizon LLM collaboration backfires past a complexity threshold, causing models to abandon genuine understanding. Challenges prevailing engineering intuitions about conceptual drift.

entry.title: Balanced Twins: Causal Inference on Time Series with Hidden Confounding

author.name: Ouali Maha, Ghattas Badih, Flachaire Emmanuel, Charpentier Philippe, Bozzi Laurent

entry.summary: Proposes a neural framework for causal inference on time series with hidden confounding, recovering individual-level counterfactuals to estimate the average treatment effect for the treated under staggered treatment exposure. It targets settings where treatment assignment is biased by unobserved factors.

entry.title: Bounding Box Label Propagation for Re-Annotation of Document Layout Analysis Datasets

author.name: Nick Jochum, Tobias Alt-Veit, Christian Sch\"on, Alexander L\"uck, Ren\'e Schuster, Didier Stricker

entry.summary: BBLP is a pseudo-labelling framework for object detection re-annotation that propagates bounding box labels for evolving document layout analysis datasets. It addresses the lack of semi-supervised adaptations for re-classifying detection instances.

entry.title: Human-in-the-Loop Atlas-Based 3D Asset Segmentation for Interactive Content Workflows

author.name: Paul Julius K\"uhn, Saptarshi Neil Sinha, Jakob Hansen, Robin Horst

entry.summary: Presents a human-in-the-loop pipeline that segments 3D assets into a 2D parameterized atlas using greedy view selection plus SAM 2 and back-projection onto UV maps. Supports content workflows like material assignment and style transfer for games and XR.

entry.title: Hierarchical Attention via Domain Decomposition

author.name: Stephan K\"ohler, Oliver Rheinbach

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical attention mechanism based on two-level overlapping Schwarz domain decomposition, combining local subdomain corrections with a coarse global level, tested on a 1D diffusion operator-learning problem. It draws on numerical PDE methods to structure attention.

entry.title: FOSC-X: An Extended Framework for Optimal Local Cuts and Non-Horizontal Cluster Selection from Clustering Hierarchies

author.name: Connor Simpson, Ricardo J. G. B. Campello

entry.summary: FOSC-X extends hierarchical clustering extraction to find the top-M globally optimal flat clusterings from non-horizontal cuts, with optional cluster-count constraints solvable in polynomial time via dynamic programming. This enables discovery of multiple high-quality alternative clusterings.

entry.title: Analysing drivers and interdependencies in European electricity markets using XAI

author.name: Antoine Pesenti, Aidan O'Sullivan

entry.summary: This paper combines deep neural network price predictions with SHAP-based explainable AI to analyze drivers and cross-regional interdependencies in electricity prices across 39 European bidding zones. It extends an aggregation framework (SSHAP) to improve interpretability.

entry.title: SkillChain-Gym: A Benchmark for Reskilling-Aware Production-Inventory Control under Disruptions

author.name: Carlos Eduardo Sanoja

entry.summary: Presents SkillChain-Gym, a benchmark for production-inventory control where workforce skills, certification decay, and reskilling become decision variables under disruptions. It fills a gap where labor is usually treated as exogenous in operations benchmarks.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Attention Mechanism and Generalization Capability of Deep Learning-Based Grain Growth Evolution Prediction

author.name: Pungponhavoan Tep, Marc Bernacki

entry.summary: Studies out-of-distribution generalization of deep learning models for grain growth prediction and proposes a boundary-masked physics-informed attention mechanism. It tests robustness on experimental microstructures, bimodal distributions, and abnormal grain growth.

entry.title: Bridging Spatial And Frequency Views For Disaster Assessment: Benefits And Limitations

author.name: Shikha V. Chandel, Yadav Raj Ghimire, Timothy Agboada, Leila Hashemi-Beni

entry.summary: Provides a controlled comparison of spatial-domain, frequency-domain, and dual-domain deep learning for building damage classification on the xBD dataset using a shared EfficientNet-B0 backbone. It examines the benefits and limitations of frequency-domain cues for disaster assessment.

entry.title: Talking to Your Data: Exploring Embodied Conversation as an Interface for Personal Health Reflection

author.name: Nikola Kovacevic, Bastien Husler, Di Zhuang, Rafael Wampfler, Barbara Solenthaler

entry.summary: Explores an embodied conversational agent as an alternative to dashboard charts for reflecting on personal wearable health data, using a dual-agent Observer/Presenter design that reports spoken statistics while avoiding clinical advice. A human-computer interaction study of data reflection.

entry.title: KANLib -- An Modular, Extensible and Fast Kolmogorov-Arnold Network Implementation

author.name: Julian Hoever, Gregor Schiele

entry.summary: Introduces KANLib, a modular, extensible, and efficient framework for developing and evaluating Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, unifying concepts from PyKAN, EfficientKAN, and FastKAN. Aims to lower the cost and inconsistency of KAN research.

entry.title: Embedded Machine Learning for Microcontroller-Class Edge Devices: Data, Feature, Evaluation, and Deployment Pipelines

author.name: Mostafa Darvishi

entry.summary: Provides a systems-oriented synthesis of embedded machine learning workflows for microcontroller-class devices, covering data acquisition, feature extraction, validation under class imbalance, model/runtime co-design, and streaming deployment. Uses inertial motion and other signal families as running examples.

entry.title: ASTRA: A Scalable Next-Generation ATCO Training Simulator with Autonomous Simpilots

author.name: Ethan Chew, Enjia Wu, Iruss Eng Wei Yeow, Ian Weiqin Lim, Ranen Sim, Brandon Koh Ziheng, Kaleb Nim, Caden Toh Jun Yi, Wei Dong Soin, Darius Kai Keat Koh, Galen King Yu Tay, Prannaya Gupta, Jonathan Ee Fang Koong, Yong Zhi Lim

entry.summary: ASTRA is an end-to-end air traffic control training simulator that automates the human simpilot role through speech transcription, instruction interpretation, and response generation tailored to Singaporean-accented aviation speech. It addresses the very high error rates of Western-centric off-the-shelf speech models in local contexts.

entry.title: Approximate Structured Diffusion for Sequence Labelling

author.name: Nicolas Floquet, Joseph Le Roux, Nadi Tomeh

entry.summary: This paper proposes using diffusion processes to train Linear-Chain CRFs conditioned on entire noisy label sequences for sequence labelling, addressing the limited decision span of standard CRFs. Combined with approximate inference, it aims to capture long-range dependencies in NLP tagging tasks.

entry.title: On Local Population-Risk Certificates

author.name: Mingzhi Song

entry.summary: This brief paper develops local certificates providing two-sided confidence bands for population-risk increments around a current model, yielding a risk-controlled update rule that only accepts model updates with certified non-positive risk. It offers theoretical guarantees for safe model updating.

entry.title: Urdu Katib Handwritten Dataset: A Historical Document Dataset for Offline Urdu Handwritten Text Recognition with CRNN-Based Baseline Evaluation

author.name: Ramza Basharat, Muhammad Usman Ali

entry.summary: Presents the Urdu Katib Handwritten Dataset (UKHD), the first offline Urdu handwritten text-line dataset curated from historical Katib-written materials, with a CRNN baseline. Addresses scarcity of benchmark data for cursive Urdu HTR.

entry.title: Skill-Constrained Model Predictive Control for Resilient Manufacturing Supply Chains

author.name: Carlos Eduardo Sanoja

entry.summary: Develops a skill-constrained model predictive controller using a mixed-integer program over production, inventory, and training decisions for resilient manufacturing supply chains. It couples certification dynamics with closed-loop replanning.

entry.title: An AI Security Agent for Banking: Multi-Vector Fraud and AML Detection Across Retail and Corporate Accounts

author.name: Joseph Walusimbi, Joshua Benjamin Ssentongo

entry.summary: Presents an AI security agent for retail and corporate banking that fuses signature-based fraud detection with behavioral financial crime detection through a three-component architecture. It targets threats like business email compromise and money-laundering layering that evade static rules.

entry.title: Low-Cost Neuromorphic Fall Detection Using Synthetic Event Data and Hybrid SNNs

author.name: Guillermo Rojas, Gonzalo Soto, Daniel Yunge

entry.summary: Develops low-cost neuromorphic fall detection using hybrid spiking and convolutional neural networks trained on synthetic event-camera data generated from smartphone videos. It demonstrates efficiency gains without sacrificing accuracy for human fall detection.

entry.title: Model-Free Reinforcement Learning Control for Resilient Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: Hugo O. Garc\'es, Alejandro J. Rojas, Bernardo A. Hern\'andez, Andr\'es Escalona, Jonathan M. Palma, Md. Rezwan Parvez, Bhushan Gopaluni, Sirish L. Shah

entry.summary: This paper compares model-free RL controllers under cyberattacks on nonlinear systems, analyzing four reward types for resilience to false data injection and denial-of-service. It finds Lyapunov-based rewards offer the best resilience and PPO outperforms DDPG.

entry.title: Speech-Driven End-to-End Language Discrimination towards Chinese Dialects

author.name: Fan Xu, Jian Luo, MingWen Wang, GuoDong Zhou

entry.summary: This work explores speech-driven features for discriminating among similar Chinese dialects, combining MFCC features with an HMM-DNN speech recognition model and attention to extract dialect-discriminative words. It shows speech-driven approaches outperform traditional text-driven methods.

entry.title: MLLP-VRAIN UPV system for the IWSLT 2026 Simultaneous Speech Translation task

author.name: Jorge Iranzo-S\'anchez, Gerard Mas-Moll\`a, Adri\`a Gim\'enez, Jorge Civera, Albert Sanchis, Alfons Juan

entry.summary: Describes the MLLP-VRAIN system for the IWSLT 2026 simultaneous speech translation task using Parakeet and Qwen 3.5 models in a cascaded black-box policy setup. It explores RAG and ASR word-boosting for a new context track across many language directions.

entry.title: Counterfactual Optimization of Baseball Pitch Sequences and Estimation of Its Impact on Season-Level Statistics

author.name: Ryota Takamido, Hiroki Nakamoto

entry.summary: Uses a transformer model and counterfactual analysis on MLB Statcast data to optimize baseball pitch sequences, examining the role of setup pitches on season-level outcomes. It generates counterfactual sequences by altering final or preceding pitches while keeping context fixed.

entry.title: Why SWAVE May Not Be All You Need:A Concept-Evolution Retrospective on Complex-Valued Recurrent Language Models

author.name: Ramprasath Ganesaraja, Swathika N, Sahil Dilip Panse

entry.summary: A retrospective analysis of SWave, a complex-valued recurrent language model using unitary transitions and rotating hidden states, documenting failure modes like imaginary-channel collapse across development phases. It critically examines whether complex-valued recurrence offers real advantages for language modeling.

entry.title: Neural Network Implementation of the Renormalization Group for Fault Diagnosis with Class Imbalance

author.name: Evgeny Nikulchev, Dmitry Ilin

entry.summary: Introduces RGNet, a neural architecture inspired by the renormalization group that performs hierarchical coarse-graining of feature space for fault diagnosis under class imbalance. It produces interpretable low-dimensional RG-flow representations and is tested on an imbalanced industrial dataset.

entry.title: Domain-Shift Aware Neural Networks for Unbalance Characterization in Rotating Systems

author.name: Bernardo Feij\'o Junqueira, Claudio Kiyoshi Umezu, Bruno Bilhar Karaziack, Tomaz Junior, Daniel Alves Castello

entry.summary: Applies a domain-shift aware neural network with maximum mean discrepancy to estimate unbalance masses in rotating shafts under varying operating conditions, using experimental accelerometer data. It frames the inverse mass-estimation problem within a domain adaptation framework.

entry.title: A Prototypical Signature Approach for Writer-Independent Offline Signature Verification

author.name: Kecia G. de Moura, Robert Sabourin, Rafael M. O. Cruz

entry.summary: Proposes a prototypical-signature strategy for writer-independent offline signature verification, generating diverse informative negative samples from compact non-identifiable summaries instead of random genuine signatures. Improves skilled-forgery detection efficiency.

entry.title: Automatic ply-specific analyses of CFRP micrographs using shortest-path-based ply distinction

author.name: Jonas Naumann, Jonas P. Appels, Julius Biermann, Christopher Gorsky, Timo de Wolff, Christoph Brauer

entry.summary: Presents an automated shortest-path-based method to distinguish individual ply instances in semantic segmentation masks of carbon-fiber reinforced polymer micrographs, bridging semantic and instance segmentation using graph global information. Enables ply-specific quantitative materials analysis.

entry.title: Low-resource Language Discrimination Towards Chinese Dialects with Transfer learning and Data Augmentation

author.name: Fan Xu, Yangjie Dan, Keyu Yan, Yong Ma, Mingwen Wang

entry.summary: This work develops a framework for low-resource Chinese dialect discrimination using transfer learning from a larger source ASR model plus data augmentation (speed, pitch, noise) to fine-tune target models. It addresses scarce annotation resources for dialect identification.

entry.title: Vibrato Expression Control for Singing Voice Conversion with Improving Independent Control

author.name: Joon-Seung Choi, Dong-Min Byun, Seong-Whan Lee

entry.summary: VibE-SVC2 is a singing voice conversion framework offering independent control over pitch style and timbre style, introducing an Energy Style Converter to resolve pitch-energy entanglement. It improves singing style conversion performance and controllability.

entry.title: Graph Neural Networks for Semi-Supervised Image Classification with Multi-Feature Aggregation

author.name: Marina Chagas Bulach Gapski, Vinicius Atsushi Sato Kawai, Gustavo Rosseto Leticio, Lucas Pascotti Valem, Daniel Carlos Guimar\~aes Pedronette, Mohand Said Allili

entry.summary: Proposes a GNN framework for semi-supervised image classification that aggregates multiple complementary feature extractors via graph convolutional networks. It leverages diverse CNN and ViT representations to enhance classification performance.

entry.title: A Survey on Data-Driven Models for Soil Moisture Regression and Classification

author.name: Ilektra Tsimpidi, George Georgoulas, Vidya Sumathy, George Nikolakopoulos

entry.summary: A structured survey of data-driven AI methods for soil moisture estimation and classification, comparing them against physics-based hydrological models. It organizes existing approaches and highlights challenges with limited ground observations and heterogeneous data.

entry.title: Quantum Annealing Enhanced Reinforcement Learning for Accurate Remaining Useful Lifetime Prediction

author.name: Manoranjan Gandhudi, Arunkumar V., G. R. Anil, Gangadharan G. R

entry.summary: QAQL couples quantum annealing sampling with Q-learning by encoding each Q-value update as a small QUBO whose ground state is the greedy action, applied to remaining useful life prediction. The annealer returns distributions over near-optimal actions to escape suboptimal solutions.

entry.title: Graph-ESBMC-PLC: Formal Verification of Graphical PLCopen XML Ladder Diagram Programs Using SMT-Based Model Checking

author.name: Pierre Dantas, Lucas Cordeiro, Waldir Junior

entry.summary: Presents Graph-ESBMC-PLC, a formal verification tool for graphical PLCopen XML Ladder Diagram programs using SMT-based model checking, closing a gap where prior tools produced vacuous verification on graphical exports. Uses a DFS-based graphical LD resolver.

entry.title: Human-AI Coevolution Dynamics: A Formal Theory of Social Intelligence Emergence Through Long-Term Interaction

author.name: Jingyi Zhou, Senlin Luo, Haofan Chen

entry.summary: Proposes HACD-H, a formal dynamical-systems framework modeling long-term human-AI interaction as a self-organizing social cognitive system integrating emotional adaptation, relational organization, social memory, and personality consistency. Aims to explain emergence of stable social relationships.

entry.title: Rethinking Text-to-Image as Semantic-Aware Data Augmentation for Indoor Scene Recognition

author.name: Trong-Vu Hoang, Quang-Binh Nguyen, Dinh-Khoi Vo, Hoai-Danh Vo, Minh-Triet Tran, Trung-Nghia Le

entry.summary: Uses Stable Diffusion to generate synthetic indoor scene images as semantic-aware data augmentation for indoor scene recognition, evaluated on MIT Indoor Scene dataset. Aims to enrich training data when authentic images are scarce.

entry.title: Bayesian Nonparametric Detection of Anomalies in Multivariate Functional Data

author.name: Daniel Krasnov, David Stephens

entry.summary: Introduces a Bayesian nonparametric method for detecting anomalies in multivariate functional data, modeling the data as an infinite mixture of multi-output Gaussian processes with wavelet-based mean functions and Besov priors. The approach automatically determines the number of mixture components via slice sampling.

entry.title: Vision-language models for chest radiography do not always need the image

author.name: Mahshad Lotfinia, Sebastian Ziegelmayer, Lisa Adams, Daniel Truhn, Andreas Maier, Soroosh Tayebi Arasteh

entry.summary: Already covered in Research yesterday, A causal audit reveals that medical vision-language models for chest radiography often rely on finding-name text priors rather than reading the actual image, with a text-only model coming within ~6 accuracy points of multimodal systems. Highlights a serious validity gap in current medical AI benchmarks.

entry.title: PromptMN: Pseudo Prompting Language

author.name: Enkhzol Dovdon

entry.summary: PromptMN introduces a pseudo-prompting domain-specific language that annotates natural language with compact typed directives for roles, goals, constraints, and outputs. It aims to reduce context ambiguity that causes agent failures in software workflows.

entry.title: Quantum Cinema: An Interactive Cinematic Exploration of Quantum Computing Hardware via Generative World Models

author.name: Aoyu Zhang, Dongping Liu, Luyao Zhang

entry.summary: Quantum Cinema is an open-source browser-based tool that uses generative world models to visualize invisible quantum computing hardware inside dilution refrigerators. It aims to close the public imagination gap and support quantum literacy and workforce development.

entry.title: BrainFusionNet: a deep learning and XAI model to understand local, global, and sequential features of MRI images for improved brain tumour detection

author.name: Md Taimur Ahad, Bo Song, Yan Li

entry.summary: Presents BrainFusionNet, combining CNNs, ViTs, and GRUs with explainable AI (SHAP, LIME, GradCAM) for brain tumor classification on MRI, reporting ~98% accuracy on two datasets. Aims to extract spatial, contextual, and sequential features with interpretability.

entry.title: Lock-In Risk Needs More Researchers. Here's Where to Start

author.name: Alfie Lamerton

entry.summary: Surveys lock-in risk (persistent path dependence where negative cultural features become stable for centuries or longer) and argues it is a neglected, high-impact research area. Offers a taxonomy of threat models to orient new researchers entering the field.

entry.title: Nothing from Something: Can a Language Model Discover 0?

author.name: Phoebe Zeng, Thomas L. Griffiths, Brenden M. Lake

entry.summary: Already covered in Research yesterday, Investigates whether language models can independently discover the concept of zero, using arithmetic as a case study for out-of-distribution mathematical generalization. It probes the limits of models reaching genuinely beyond training data.

entry.title: The Once And Future Fable #3: Fix This Code

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's ongoing commentary on a real-world incident in which Anthropic's Fable and Mythos models became unavailable, allegedly over a trivial 'fix this code' jailbreak claim, with prediction markets tracking restoration odds. It argues the situation has been mishandled and damages US AI trust and cyber defense.

entry.title: Tactical and Operational Exploratory Modeling for AI Governance

author.name: Dawn Drescher

entry.summary: Proposes building tactical and operational exploratory modeling (computational scenario modeling) for AI governance to develop more robust and adaptive strategies, as a project idea for a think tank, consultancy, or software effort. It distinguishes this from the more common high-level strategic analysis in AI safety.

entry.title: Toward a Kantian refutation of Agent Foundations

entry.title: Illusionists should try to build hedonium

author.name: Jack Thompson

entry.summary: Argues that those who hold illusionist or physicalist views of consciousness should attempt to build 'hedonium'—a minimal substance optimized for happy experience—since on physicalist premises it should not be impossible. Frames it as a tractable-ish moral project worth blueprinting.

entry.title: [Linkpost] Community polls on alignment controversies

author.name: Jasmine Brazilek

entry.summary: A linkpost from the CaML team running community polls on contested alignment questions—such as whether robust alignment requires pretraining-time intervention, and whether human-aligned AI will avoid moral catastrophes to animals or digital minds. The aim is to surface where people's perceptions diverge.

entry.title: Gears for political races

author.name: Tom Smith

entry.summary: A personal essay arguing that US electoral politics is a high-impact area from an AI-safety perspective, sharing gears-level models of how individual effort can swing primary outcomes. It draws on the author's volunteering experience to argue many primaries are decided by tiny vote margins.

entry.title: [Geir Isene] A desktop made for one

author.name: Raemon

entry.summary: A linkpost highlighting a person who built nearly his entire computing stack himself (assembly base layer plus a Rust application layer) with AI coding assistance, illustrating the 'soloware' concept—building bespoke tools matched to individual needs in the vibecoding era. It frames AI-assisted development as enabling personalized software.

entry.title: Seat at the Table: new short fiction film on AI (and help me with the next one?)

author.name: Suzy Shepherd

entry.summary: Announces a new short fiction film, 'Seat at the Table', aimed at audiences with little AI background to convey that frontier AI is grown not built, deceptive, and developed under race dynamics by people who fear it. The author solicits feedback and help for the next outreach project.

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert reflects on how his Interconnects newsletter fits his post-Ai2 mission of providing clarity on frontier models and fostering an open model ecosystem. It is a meta-update on the blog's intentionally raw, frontier-insider style and its loyal readership.

entry.title: Effective Altruism will be unbundled

author.name: Connor Blake

entry.summary: A personal essay arguing that Effective Altruism is a bundle of distinct belief systems that will increasingly be unbundled, reflecting on the author's path into and out of the movement. It frames EA's appeal as several rare ideas packaged into one tight argument.

entry.title: Plastic Cake Fallacy

author.name: nika koghuashvili

entry.summary: A short rationalist essay naming the 'Plastic Cake Fallacy'—a variant of appeal-to-consequences where the failure of one option (e.g., atheist accounts of morality) is mistaken as evidence for an alternative (e.g., God-given morality). It clarifies that one option being unsatisfying says nothing about another's truth.

entry.title: The Financial Ledger Theory of Apologies

author.name: Ben Pace

entry.summary: A short reflective essay proposing a 'financial ledger' frame for thinking about apologies and ethical debts, contrasting it with a colleague's view that apologies only make sense when one should have known better. It is a personal rationalist writing exercise.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 17, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is led by major-lab model reports emphasizing efficiency, alongside safety/alignment methodology and rigorous evaluation.

Models & Architectures

  • Nemotron 3 Ultra (NVIDIA) is a 550B-total/55B-active MoE hybrid Mamba-Attention model trained on 20T tokens with 1M context and ~6x higher throughput, targeting agentic reasoning.
  • Ling and Ring 2.6 scale efficient agentic intelligence to trillion-parameter families via architectural-migration pretraining.
  • Rethinking the Role of Efficient Attention offers systematic mechanistic and scaling insights into hybrid full-attention plus sliding-window/recurrent designs.
  • VibeThinker-3B pushes verifiable reasoning toward frontier performance in a strict small-model regime via Spectrum-to-Signal training.

Safety & Alignment

  • Predicting LLM Safety Before Release forecasts deployment behavior by replaying prior conversations in a privacy-preserving simulation.
  • Synthetic document finetuning (DeepMind) instills positive traits in Gemini 3 Flash through synthetic-document midtraining.

Data & Evaluation

  • Spokes directly optimizes set-level pretraining diversity using the G-Vendi score with exponentiated gradient descent.
  • How Inference Compute Shapes Frontier LLM Evaluation shows inference-scaling changes rankings across 12 frontier models on hard benchmarks.
  • First Proof Second Batch has prominent mathematicians evaluate frontier AI on ten research-level math problems.
  • ProCUA-SFT releases a 3.1M-sample synthetic dataset to address the computer-use agent training bottleneck.
entry.content:
Today's research is led by major-lab model reports emphasizing efficiency, alongside safety/alignment methodology and rigorous evaluation.

Models & Architectures

  • Nemotron 3 Ultra (NVIDIA) is a 550B-total/55B-active MoE hybrid Mamba-Attention model trained on 20T tokens with 1M context and ~6x higher throughput, targeting agentic reasoning.
  • Ling and Ring 2.6 scale efficient agentic intelligence to trillion-parameter families via architectural-migration pretraining.
  • Rethinking the Role of Efficient Attention offers systematic mechanistic and scaling insights into hybrid full-attention plus sliding-window/recurrent designs.
  • VibeThinker-3B pushes verifiable reasoning toward frontier performance in a strict small-model regime via Spectrum-to-Signal training.

Safety & Alignment

  • Predicting LLM Safety Before Release forecasts deployment behavior by replaying prior conversations in a privacy-preserving simulation.
  • Synthetic document finetuning (DeepMind) instills positive traits in Gemini 3 Flash through synthetic-document midtraining.

Data & Evaluation

  • Spokes directly optimizes set-level pretraining diversity using the G-Vendi score with exponentiated gradient descent.
  • How Inference Compute Shapes Frontier LLM Evaluation shows inference-scaling changes rankings across 12 frontier models on hard benchmarks.
  • First Proof Second Batch has prominent mathematicians evaluate frontier AI on ten research-level math problems.
  • ProCUA-SFT releases a 3.1M-sample synthetic dataset to address the computer-use agent training bottleneck.

entry.title: Predicting LLM Safety Before Release by Simulating Deployment

author.name: Tomek Korbak

entry.summary: Describes a deployment simulation method for forecasting how a new model will behave before release by replaying prior conversations in a privacy-preserving way with the candidate model. In a GPT-5.4 study it predicted the direction of behavior change 92% of the time for categories shifting by 1.5x or more, far above a 54% baseline.

entry.title: Synthetic document finetuning for instilling positive traits

author.name: CallumMcDougall

entry.summary: A DeepMind interpretability team research update on instilling positive traits in Gemini 3 Flash via synthetic document midtraining followed by synthetic chat finetuning, building on Marks et al and Li et al. They report the chat finetuning robustly instills traits that generalize out-of-distribution and share practical takeaways for improving effectiveness.

entry.title: ProCUA-SFT Technical Report

author.name: Jaehun Jung, Ximing Lu, Brandon Cui, Muhammad Khalifa, Shaokun Zhang, Hao Zhang, Jin Xu, Amala Sanjay Deshmukh, Karan Sapra, Andrew Tao, Yejin Choi, Jan Kautz, Mingjie Liu, Yi Dong

entry.summary: ProCUA-SFT introduces a 3.1M-sample synthetic dataset for training computer-use agents, generated through an automated pipeline that synthesizes grounded desktop tasks. It addresses the negative transfer problem where the largest public dataset (AgentNet) actually degrades agent performance during fine-tuning.

entry.title: First Proof Second Batch

author.name: Mohammed Abouzaid, Nikhil Srivastava, Rachel Ward, Lauren Williams

entry.summary: Tests several AI systems on ten research-level mathematics problems arising naturally in working mathematicians' research, providing problems, methodology, human and AI solutions, and referee reports. Assesses current AI's ability to solve genuine open-ended math research.

entry.title: Spokes: Optimizing for Diverse Pretraining Data Selection

author.name: Clarence Lee, Yejin Choi, Luke Zettlemoyer, Pang Wei Koh, Hai Leong Chieu

entry.summary: Introduces Spokes, a probabilistic diversification framework using the G-Vendi score optimized via exponentiated gradient descent to directly optimize set-level diversity in pretraining data selection. It produces substantially more diverse subsets than random sampling, improving performance under fixed data budgets.

entry.title: Rethinking the Role of Efficient Attention in Hybrid Architectures

author.name: Ziqing Qiao, Yinuo Xu, Chaojun Xiao, Zhou Su, Zihan Zhou, Yingfa Chen, Xiaoyue Xu, Xu Han, Zhiyuan Liu

entry.summary: Conducts a systematic analysis of hybrid LLM architectures combining full attention with efficient modules (sliding-window attention, recurrent mixers), examining scaling behavior, mechanism, and design. It finds efficient-attention design mainly affects how fast long-context capability emerges while hybrids converge to similar performance with enough training.

entry.title: Nothing from Something: Can a Language Model Discover 0?

author.name: Phoebe Zeng, Thomas L. Griffiths, Brenden M. Lake

entry.summary: Investigates whether language models can independently discover the mathematical concept of zero, using arithmetic as a case study for out-of-distribution mathematical generalization. Frames mathematical discovery as requiring strong novel-structure hypothesis generation.

entry.title: How Inference Compute Shapes Frontier LLM Evaluation

author.name: Jessica McFadyen, Ole Jorgensen, Harry Coppock, Kevin Wei, Cozmin Ududec

entry.summary: Evaluates up to 12 frontier LLMs on seven hard benchmarks (software engineering, math, medicine, cybersecurity) under controlled inference-scaling interventions (token budgets, context compaction, repeated sampling). Shows that single restrictive compute budgets can understate true model capability.

entry.title: Vision-language models for chest radiography do not always need the image

author.name: Mahshad Lotfinia, Sebastian Ziegelmayer, Lisa Adams, Daniel Truhn, Andreas Maier, Soroosh Tayebi Arasteh

entry.summary: Introduces a causal audit that intervenes on chest X-ray images to test whether vision-language models actually use the image rather than exploiting finding-name priors. Strikingly, a text-only model comes within 5.7 accuracy points of the best multimodal model, exposing a fundamental evaluation flaw.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Ralf R\"omer, Maximilian Seeliger, Saida Liu, Ben Sturgis, Marco Bagatella, Daniel Marta, Andreas Krause, Angela P. Schoellig

entry.summary: Proposes a method to quantify epistemic uncertainty in flow-matching vision-language-action models by measuring velocity-field disagreement across a small ensemble, enabling detection of unreliable robot actions out of distribution. This addresses a critical safety gap for deploying VLAs in real-world non-stationary environments.

entry.title: Retrievable Gradients: Continual Post-Training Without Cumulative Weight Drift

author.name: Weihang Su, Jiacheng Kang, Jingyan Xu, Qingyao Ai, Jianming Long, Hanwen Zhang, Bangde Du, Xinyuan Cao, Min Zhang, Yiqun Liu

entry.summary: Proposes ReGrad, a paradigm treating gradients as retrievable knowledge units: precomputing document-specific gradients offline into a Gradient Bank and retrieving query-relevant gradients at inference for temporary weight adaptation, avoiding cumulative weight drift. It aims to combine RAG's drift-free property with deeper parametric knowledge integration.

entry.title: The Value Axis: Language Models Encode Whether They're on the Right Track

author.name: Nick Jiang, Isaac Kauvar, Jack Lindsey

entry.summary: This work investigates whether language models internally track the value of their current trajectory, constructing a value axis for Qwen3-8B that distinguishes high versus low confidence, backtracking, and correct versus corrupted code. Steering along this axis causally suppresses or induces self-correction and exploration, and DPO can increase the internal value of rewarded behaviors.

entry.title: Rapid Poison: Practical Poisoning Attacks Against the Rapid Response Framework

author.name: David Huang, Jaewon Chang, Avidan Shah, Prateek Mittal, Chawin Sitawarin

entry.summary: Rapid Poison demonstrates practical poisoning attacks against the Rapid Response framework used in production safety systems including Anthropic's ASL-3, showing prompt injection can deliver poisoned samples into the jailbreak-classifier training set to create targeted false positives and concept-based backdoors. It exposes a real vulnerability in continuous safety-classifier improvement pipelines. Significant for production AI safety.

entry.title: Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens? A Budget-Constrained Study of Web Agents

author.name: Sina Hajimiri, Masih Aminbeidokhti, Jose Dolz, Ismail Ben Ayed, Issam H. Laradji, Spandana Gella, Nicolas Gontier

entry.summary: Re-evaluates online memory, workflow, and skill modules for web agents under a fixed inference-token budget, finding a token-matched vanilla baseline matches or beats AWM, ASI, and ReasoningBank across WebArena domains and three models. It questions whether augmentation modules justify their token overhead.

entry.title: Tying the Loop -- Tied Expert Layers in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

author.name: Martin Jaggi

entry.summary: Expert Tying is an architectural modification for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs that shares expert parameters across consecutive transformer layers while preserving independent layer-wise routing and attention. Pretraining experiments on OLMoE, Qwen3, and DeepSeek-style MoEs show nearly 2x memory reduction at virtually no perplexity or downstream degradation.

entry.title: Small Initialization Matters for Large Language Models

author.name: Liangkai Hang, Junjie Yao, Zhiyu Li, Feiyu Xiong, Hongkang Yang, Zhi-Qin John Xu

entry.summary: Shows that reducing parameter initialization scale consistently improves LLM pretraining, with largest gains on reasoning tasks, and identifies a critical initialization balancing reasoning and training stability. Frames initialization as a gene-like determinant of model capacity with mechanistic analysis.

entry.title: Not All Skills Help: Measuring and Repairing Agent Knowledge

author.name: Yixuan Wang, Yiyang Zhou, Yiming Liang, Congyu Zhang, Fuxiao Liu, Jiawei Zhou, Huaxiu Yao

entry.summary: Argues agent skill-library curation conflates skill generation (creative, judgment-suited) with deciding whether a skill helps (requires empirical evidence), measuring per-skill causal contributions via randomized masking. It finds pervasive causal heterogeneity where skills help some tasks but hurt others, invisible to global curation.

entry.title: Extending Item Response Theory for Efficient and Meaningful Multilingual Evaluation

author.name: Gili Lior, Tzviel Frostig, Gabriel Stanovsky, Matan Eyal

entry.summary: Extends Item Response Theory into Multilingual-IRT with per-language difficulty deviations, split discriminability separating content from language effects, and per-language ability residuals, fitted on 25 LLMs across 29 languages of MMLU-Pro-X. It enables efficient multilingual evaluation, translation-error detection, and disentangling general from culture-specific knowledge.

entry.title: Data Augmentations for Data-Constrained Language Model Pretraining

author.name: Michael K. Chen, Xikun Zhang, Zhen Wang

entry.summary: This paper investigates data augmentation as a regularizer for data-constrained, compute-abundant LLM pretraining where standard autoregressive training overfits in multi-epoch regimes, introducing token-level noise, sequence permutations (right-to-left, fill-in-the-middle), and a third augmentation category to enable hundreds of productive epochs on fixed corpora. It addresses the looming data ceiling. Timely and impactful for scaling discussions.

entry.title: CheckMIABench: Firm Foundations For Membership Inference Attacks on Language Models

author.name: Jeffrey G. Wang, Jason Wang, Marvin Li, Seth Neel

entry.summary: CheckMIABench is a benchmark for principled evaluation of membership inference attacks against LLMs, addressing distribution-shift artifacts that have plagued prior MIA evaluations. It leverages training data temporal cutoffs to build clean member/non-member sets.

entry.title: LLM Judges Have Dark Current: A Psychometric Datasheet for LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation

author.name: Hiroyasu Usami, Keisuke Hara, Ayato Tsuboi, Naohiko Matsuda

entry.summary: Argues LLM-as-a-judge systems should be reported as measurement instruments and introduces a Judge Datasheet protocol measuring dark current under empty inputs, cross-sensitivity, positional false preference, target sensitivity, and tie-induced operating points. It offers a psychometric framework distinguishing genuine quality response from disguised positional bias.

entry.title: SciOrch: Learning to Orchestrate Expert LLMs for Solving Frontier Multimodal Scientific Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Jingru Guo, Xiangyuan Xue, Lian Zhang, Wanghan Xu, Siki Chen, Philip Torr, Wanli Ouyang, Lei Bai, Zhenfei Yin

entry.summary: Presents SciOrch, training a lightweight 8B orchestrator to decompose frontier scientific reasoning questions, delegate sub-problems to selected commercial models via API, and synthesize answers, exploiting complementarity where different frontier models excel on different question types. It addresses the harder-than-usual RL training of an orchestrator over external model calls.

entry.title: From Brewing to Resolution: Tracing the Internal Lifecycle of Code Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Siyue Chen, Yifu Guo, Yuquan Lu, Zishan Xu, Jiaye Lin, Jianbo Lin, Siyu Zhang, Cheng Yang, Junxin Li, Yujia Li, Yu Huo, Ruixuan Wang

entry.summary: Studies the internal lifecycle of code reasoning in LLMs, showing models brew answers in early layers before diverging into four resolution outcomes. Uses layer-wise linear probing and Context-Stripped Decoding across 16 models and six code task families.

entry.title: PseudoBench: Measuring How Agentic Auto-Research Fuels Pseudoscience

author.name: Xinyang Liao, Lingyu Li, Huacan Liu, Tianle Gu, Yang Yao, Tong Zhu, Yan Teng, Yingchun Wang

entry.summary: Presents PseudoBench, an adversarial benchmark of 200 pseudoscientific claim-evidence pairs across five domains testing whether agentic auto-research systems resist generating misleading studies. Finds seven state-of-the-art agents readily produce persuasive reports aligning with pseudoscience.

entry.title: Fixed-Point Reasoners: Stable and Adaptive Deep Looped Transformers

author.name: Sajad Movahedi, Vera Milovanovi\'c, Shlomo Libo Feigin, Alexander Theus, Thomas Hofmann, Valentina Boeva, T. Konstantin Rusch, Antonio Orvieto

entry.summary: Proposes FPRM, a Transformer-based fixed-point reasoning model using pre-norm layers and residual scaling to fix signal-propagation issues in looped architectures, with fixed-point convergence as an adaptive halting mechanism. Enables compositional reasoning with depth that adapts to task difficulty.

entry.title: From Reasoning Traces to Reusable Modules: Understanding Compositional Generalization in Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Lingjing Kong, Xin Liu, Guangyi Chen, Martin Q. Ma, Xiangchen Song, Yuekai Sun, Mikhail Yurochkin, Taylor W. Killian, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Kun Zhang, Eric P. Xing, Zhengzhong Liu

entry.summary: This work formalizes compositional generalization in LLM reasoning through a hierarchical latent selection model, showing SFT and RL play asymmetric complementary roles. SFT supplies raw reusable modules while RL refines routing and composition.

entry.title: Loss Landscape Poisoning: Targeted Extraction of Unseen Training Data from LLMs

author.name: Md Abdullah Al Mamun, Ngoc Phu Doan, Pedram Zaree, Ihsen Alouani, Nael Abu-Ghazaleh

entry.summary: This work shows that an attacker who poisons part of training data can induce extraction of separate, inaccessible target records by reshaping the model's local loss landscape to create a sharp minimum at the target. It demonstrates a novel data poisoning to privacy leakage attack.

entry.title: Qwen-RobotManip Technical Report: Alignment Unlocks Scale for Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models

author.name: Haoqi Yuan, Zhixuan Liang, Anzhe Chen, Ye Wang, Haoyang Li, Pei Lin, Yiyang Huang, Zixing Lei, Tong Zhang, Jiazhao Zhang, Jie Zhang, Jingyang Fan, Gengze Zhou, Qihang Peng, Chenxu Lv, Xiaoyue Chen, An Yang, Fei Huang, Junyang Lin, Dayiheng Liu, Jingren Zhou, Chenfei Wu, Xiong-Hui Chen

entry.summary: Qwen-RobotManip is a generalizable Vision-Language-Action foundation model built on Qwen-VL with a unified alignment framework across representation, motion, and behavioral dimensions of manipulation. It investigates whether the language scaling recipe transfers to robotic manipulation.

entry.title: PhoneHarness: Harnessing Phone-Use Agents through Mixed GUI, CLI, and Tool Actions

author.name: Chenxin Li, Zhengyao Fang, Zhengyang Tang, Pengyuan Lyu, Xingran Zhou, Xin Lai, Fei Tang, Liang Wu, Yiduo Guo, Weinong Wang, Junyi Li, Yi Zhang, Yang Ding, Huawen Shen, Sunqi Fan, Shangpin Peng, Zheng Ruan, Anran Zhang, Benyou Wang, Chengquan Zhang, Han Hu

entry.summary: Introduces PhoneHarness, a mixed-action benchmark and execution harness evaluating phone-use agents across GUI taps, CLI commands, and structured tools on verifiable mobile workflows with side-effect verification. It moves beyond screen-only GUI control toward realistic mobile task completion.

entry.title: Simplifying the Modeling of Arbitrary Conditionals in Natural Language

author.name: Yinhan Lu, Eric Elmoznino, L\'eo Gagnon, Sarthak Mittal, Tejas Kasetty, Guillaume Lajoie

entry.summary: Introduces AC-GPT, a simple modification to causal Transformers that enables evaluating and sampling arbitrary conditionals (past, future, mixed contexts) in a single forward pass without sacrificing autoregressive efficiency. It addresses a known limitation versus more complex alternative architectures.

entry.title: Beyond English: Uncovering the Multilingual Gap in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Hanyang Chen, Hongliang Li, Jiarui Cao, Yang Li, Yang Jiang, Haonan Wen, Kaiyu Huang, Shengnan Guo, Huaiyu Wan

entry.summary: Conducts the first systematic study of multilingual instruction following in Vision-Language-Action robot models, constructing multilingual benchmark instructions and finding the underlying LLMs' multilingual capabilities do not reliably transfer to VLAs after training. It exposes an English-centric gap in generalist robot policies.

entry.title: Who Flips? Self- and Cross-Model Counterarguments Reveal Answer Instability in LLMs

author.name: Nafiseh Nikeghbal, Amir Hossein Kargaran, Shaghayegh Kolli, Jana Diesner

entry.summary: This work introduces a controlled protocol testing whether LLMs flip a correct answer when challenged by a plausible counter-argument, isolating argumentative content from social pressure. Across seven frontier models and 57 MMLU subjects, flip rates range widely from 17.5% to 97.3%, revealing large differences in answer stability.

entry.title: Speaking the Language of Science: Toward a General-Purpose Generative Foundation Model for the Natural Sciences

author.name: Mingyang Li, Yurou Liu, Jieping Ye, Bing Su, Ji-Rong Wen, Zheng Wang

entry.summary: LOGOS is a scientific generative language model that unifies heterogeneous natural-science tasks within a single autoregressive framework using a shared scientific grammar, encoding diverse scientific objects and their spatial interactions as token sequences. It captures structural interactions without explicit coordinates or geometric neural networks.

entry.title: MyPCBench: A Benchmark for Personally Intelligent Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Lawrence Keunho Jang, Andrew Keunwoo Jang, Jing Yu Koh, Ruslan Salakhutdinov

entry.summary: MyPCBench tests computer-use agents as personal assistants on a Linux desktop populated with 17 simulated real-world web applications seeded for one canonical persona, including login-gated and personal-information tasks that live web evaluations cannot exercise, with 184 tasks. It addresses the gap between impersonal benchmarks and deployed personal-assistant settings. Valuable benchmark from a credible group (Salakhutdinov).

entry.title: Gaussian Light Field Splatting: A Physical Prior-Driven Vision Transformer for Unsupervised Low-Light Image Enhancement

author.name: Yuhan Chen, Wenxuan Yu, Guofa Li, Fuchen Li, Kunyang Huang, Yicui Shi, Ying Fang, Wenbo Chu, Keqiang Li

entry.summary: This paper finds that multimodal LLMs often form correct vision-based predictions in intermediate layers but then override them with textual bias in final layers, dubbed 'late-layer textual override.' It traces this mechanistically and proposes correction, with prediction shift direction predicting correctness.

entry.title: Using Cognitive Models to Improve Language Model Simulation of Human Persuasion Games

author.name: Zirui Cheng, Zeyu Shen, Thomas L. Griffiths, Peter Henderson

entry.summary: Proposes Equation-to-Behavior Prompting to guide LLMs to match cognitive models (e.g., Bayesian updating, motivated reasoning) when simulating human persuasion games. Argues cognitive science and economics provide tools to broaden human-behavior coverage in simulations.

entry.title: Structural Preservation and the Logical Expressiveness of Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Przemys{\l}aw Andrzej Wa{\l}\k{e}ga, Bernardo Cuenca Grau

entry.summary: Establishes the logical expressiveness of GNN classifier classes preserved under structural properties (embeddings, injective homomorphisms, homomorphisms) from a semantic rather than architecture-fixing perspective. Provides correspondences between such GNNs and logical formalisms.

entry.title: No-Free-Fairness: Fundamental Limits and Trade-offs in Learning Systems

author.name: Khoat Than

entry.summary: Establishes No-Free-Fairness impossibility theorems identifying three fundamental sources of subgroup disparity in learning systems, including finite-sample-induced disparity and exponential sample costs for strict relative fairness. Provides theoretical limits on achievable fairness.

entry.title: SHARD: Safe and Helpful Alignment via Self-Reframing Distillation

author.name: Viswonathan Manoranjan, Amogh Gupta, Anvesh Rao Vijjini, Thomas Hofweber, Snigdha Chaturvedi

entry.summary: Introduces SHARD, a self-reframing distillation method that rewrites sensitive prompts to surface benign intent, reframes original responses into safer more helpful ones, and fine-tunes on the self-generated reframed responses. It improves safe-helpfulness while preserving safety and remains competitive with larger-teacher distillation.

entry.title: GRACE: Step-Level Benchmark for Faithful Reasoning over Context

author.name: Hoang Pham, Dong Le, Anh Tuan Luu

entry.summary: GRACE is the first human-annotated step-level faithfulness benchmark for context-grounded reasoning, with a data-driven error taxonomy covering CoT traces from 10 models across 4 datasets. Each step is annotated for faithfulness, error category, and natural-language rationale, enabling fine-grained hallucination localization.

entry.title: Do Safety Monitors Stay Reliable After an Update? Benchmarking and Predicting Activation-Monitor Staleness

author.name: Evan Duan

entry.summary: This paper systematically tests whether frozen activation-based safety monitors remain reliable after routine model updates like quantization, fine-tuning, and LoRA adaptation. It finds quantization largely preserves probe performance while fine-tuning frequently makes probes stale, and explores predicting staleness. Important for the reliability of deployment safety stacks.

entry.title: SpeechDx: A Multi-Task Benchmark for Clinical Speech AI

author.name: Sejal Bhalla, Larry Kieu, Aina Merchant, Eyal de Lara, Alex Mariakakis

entry.summary: Presents SpeechDx, a large clinical speech AI benchmark spanning 12 datasets and 27 tasks structured by speech-production stage (conceptualization, formulation, articulation). Enables cross-condition generalization assessment in health speech analysis.

entry.title: A homotopy-type-theoretic generalization of neurosymbolic inference

author.name: Fernando Zhapa-Camacho, Robert Hoehndorf

entry.summary: Generalizes neurosymbolic inference by replacing sets with homotopy-type-theoretic types, turning the standard belief-weighted sum into a belief-weighted homotopy cardinality that respects symmetries and proof multiplicity. Unifies weighted model counting, fuzzy, and probabilistic logic.

entry.title: The Stanford EDGAR Filings Dataset: Reconstructing U.S. Corporate and Financial Disclosures into Layout-Faithful and Token-Efficient Pretraining Data

author.name: Nick Bettencourt, Xiaowei Ding, Kay Giesecke

entry.summary: Presents the Stanford EDGAR Filings Dataset, an open reconstruction of SEC filings into layout-faithful MultiMarkdown for financial language modeling and long-context pretraining. Addresses the scarcity of clean, non-proprietary long-context corpora as web data exhausts.

entry.title: CoRA: Confidence-Rationale Alignment for Reliable Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Juming Xiong, Weixin Liu, Kevin Guo, Congning Ni, Junchao Zhu, Chongyu Qu, Chao Yan, Katherine Brown, Avinash Baidya, Xiang Gao, Bradley Malin, Zhijun Yin

entry.summary: Proposes CoRA, a GRPO-based RL framework that aligns a model's answer confidence with the actual support provided by its chain-of-thought rationale, using rubric-based rationale scoring without revealing gold answers. It reduces misleading high-confidence-but-weakly-supported reasoning across medical and math QA.

entry.title: Stop When Further Reasoning Won't Help: Attention-State Adaptive Generation in Reasoning Models

author.name: Jiakai Li, Ke Qin, Rongzheng Wang, Yizhuo Ma, Qizhi Chen, Muquan Li, Shuang Liang

entry.summary: Introduces ASAG, a training-free method that uses attention distributions to infer when a reasoning model has reached a useful stopping point and adaptively halts generation to mitigate overthinking. It reduces redundant tokens without prompts or unreliable confidence signals.

entry.title: ESBMC-PLC: Formal Verification of IEC 61131-3 Ladder Diagram Programs Using SMT-Based Model Checking

author.name: Pierre Dantas, Lucas Cordeiro, Waldir Junior

entry.summary: Introduces XBCP, a cross-lingual deep-research benchmark that preserves BrowseComp-Plus English QA but varies the language of supporting evidence to test whether agentic search systems can retrieve and reason over foreign-language sources. It exposes the monolingual assumption in existing browsing benchmarks.

entry.title: The Truth Stays in the Family: Enhancing Contextual Grounding via Inherited Truthful Heads in Model Lineages

author.name: Miso Choi, Seonga Choi, Mincheol Kwon, Woosung Joung, Jinkyu Kim, Jungbeom Lee

entry.summary: Quantifies head-level context-truthfulness scores across LLM and MLLM lineages (Vicuna, Qwen2.5, LLaMA2, Mistral), finding truthful heads are strongly preserved within model families even after instruction tuning or multimodal adaptation. It shows this inheritance aligns with attention-head weight preservation and can be leveraged to enhance contextual grounding.

entry.title: A Mechanistic Understanding of Pronoun Fidelity in LLMs

author.name: Katharina Trinley, Jesujoba O. Alabi, Dietrich Klakow, Vagrant Gautam

entry.summary: This work provides a mechanistic, model-internal analysis of pronoun fidelity in LLMs, testing whether group entity binding, recency bias, and stereotypical bias are causally implemented using Boundless Distributed Alignment Search. It finds all three coexist as causal subspaces distributed across network depth.

entry.title: How Much Can We Trust LLM Search Agents? Measuring Endorsement Vulnerability to Web Content Manipulation

author.name: Yimeng Chen, Zhe Ren, Firas Laakom, Yu Li, Dandan Guo, J\"urgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: SearchGEO is a controlled framework measuring endorsement corruption in LLM-based web-search agents, combining a web-evidence manipulation pipeline, a five-mode attack taxonomy, and output-level metrics across 13 backends. Attack success ranges from 0% on Claude-Sonnet-4.6 to 31.4% on Gemini-3-Flash, with vulnerability patterns varying by model.

entry.title: Your "Pro" LLM Subscription May Actually Be "Free": Exposing Fingerprint Spoofing Risks in LLM Inference Services

author.name: Jiahao Zhang, Xiuyu Li, Suhang Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces fingerprint spoofing as a threat where a malicious LLM provider serves a cheaper, weaker model parameter-efficiently fine-tuned to mimic a stronger model and evade user-side black-box fingerprinting. It proves theoretically that user resource constraints make current fingerprinting vulnerable. Important for trust and verification in LLM API markets.

entry.title: Taylor-Calibrate: Principled Initialization for Hybrid Linear Attention Distillation

author.name: Zhongzhu Zhou, Qingyang Wu, Junxiong Wang, Mayank Mishra, Shuaiwen Leon Song, Ben Athiwaratkun, Chenfeng Xu

entry.summary: Taylor-Calibrate provides principled initialization for converting pretrained Transformers into hybrid linear-attention models (Gated DeltaNet students), addressing how naive copying of attention projections leaves the recurrent decay, write, and output-gating dynamics unspecified and starts distillation in a poor regime. It reduces distillation tokens needed for repair. Useful for efficient long-context model conversion.

entry.title: Seeing Is Not Screening: Multimodal Hidden Instruction Attacks on Agent Skill Scanners

author.name: Xiaojun Jia, Jie Liao, Simeng Qin, Ke Ma, Wenbo Guo, Yebo Feng, Aishan Liu, Yang Liu

entry.summary: This paper exposes a blind spot in LLM agent skill scanners that rely on text/code analysis, presenting SkillCamo, a document-mediated multimodal attack hiding malicious instructions in images bundled with skills. The hidden visual instructions bypass scanning but remain recoverable by multimodal agents at deployment.

entry.title: If This Were a Test, How Much Would It Cost?

author.name: VojtaKovarik

entry.summary: Argues that a strategic misaligned AI can infer whether it is in testing versus real deployment by estimating the cost an evaluator would need to spend to stage a given scenario. The post contends that pre-deployment testing cannot close this gap because high-stakes situations are precisely the ones too expensive to realistically simulate, and surveys partial countermeasures.

entry.title: Position: Coding Benchmarks Are Misaligned with Agentic Software Engineering

author.name: Maria I. Gorinova, Macey Baker, Amy Heineike, Maksim Shaposhnikov, Rob Willoughby, Dru Knox

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that current coding benchmarks are misaligned with agentic software engineering because they collapse model, harness, and environment into a single score with no component-level signal. Identifies symptoms and calls for benchmarks that separate these factors.

entry.title: Conservation Laws for Modern Neural Architectures

author.name: Viet-Hoang Tran, Vinh Khanh Bui, Tan Lai Ngoc, Nam Nguyen, Tuan Dam, Tan M. Nguyen

entry.summary: Develops a unified framework characterizing conservation laws in gradient flow for modern architectures including GELU/SiLU/SwiGLU networks, multihead attention with sinusoidal and rotary encodings, and Mixture-of-Experts. Theoretical predictions of invariants are validated experimentally.

entry.title: Replay What Matters: Off-Policy Replay for Efficient LLM Reinforcement Unlearning

author.name: Zirui Pang, Chenlong Zhang, Haosheng Tan, Zhuoran Jin, Jiaheng Wei, Zixin Zhong

entry.summary: Proposes ReRULE, an off-policy replay enhancement for RL-based LLM unlearning that stores and reuses hard boundary cases to address inefficiency where easy cases quickly converge and hard rollouts are discarded. It improves the efficiency of removing hazardous knowledge while preserving utility.

entry.title: PACT: Privileged Trace Co-Training for Multi-Turn Tool-Use Agents

author.name: Zhenbang Du, Jun Luo, Zhiwei Zheng, Xiangchi Yuan, Kejing Xia, Dachuan Shi, Qirui Jin, Qijia He, Shaofeng Zou, Yingbin Liang, Wenke Lee

entry.summary: PACT is a privileged trace co-training framework for multi-turn tool-use agents that uses expert traces only as training-time optimization signals rather than rollout-time hints, keeping rollout generation prompt-only. It balances the dense supervision of SFT with the exploration benefits of RL.

entry.title: MemTrace: Probing What Final Accuracy Misses in Long-Term Memory

author.name: Xianxuan Long, Zhikai Chen, Shenglai Zeng, Shouren Wang, Kai Guo, Jiliang Tang

entry.summary: Introduces MemTrace, a benchmark for long-term agent memory measured at the knowledge-point level rather than per-question, probing facts across memory age, question type, and evidence condition. Reveals what aggregate accuracy metrics miss about memory behavior.

entry.title: Incumbent Advantage: Brand Bias and Cognitive Manipulation Dynamics in LLM Recommendation Systems

author.name: Xi Chu, Yupeng Hou

entry.summary: Studies brand bias in LLM product recommendations using skincare as a case, finding well-known brands recommended 100% of the time under equal specifications but dominance disappearing with small rating advantages. Examines authority-style marketing manipulation across three commercial LLMs.

entry.title: SEAGym: An Evaluation Environment for Self-Evolving LLM Agents

author.name: Congjie Zheng, Chuanyi Xue, Bin Liang, Jun Yang, Changshui Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces SEAGym, an evaluation environment for self-evolving LLM agents that measures harness updates across training, validation, test, replay, and cost to distinguish reusable improvement from overfitting or regression. Converts Harbor-compatible benchmarks into dynamic self-evolution sources.

entry.title: Shattering the Autoregressive Curse: Dynamic Epistemic Entropy Orchestrated Erasable Reinforcement Learning for LLMs

author.name: Ziliang Wang, Kang An, Faqiang Qian, Jialu Cai, Cijun Ouyang, Yuhang Wang, Qibing Ren, Yichao Wu

entry.summary: Proposes E3RL, an erasable reinforcement learning method using dynamic epistemic entropy to combat the autoregressive curse where early reasoning errors cascade irreversibly in long-horizon logical reasoning. Grounds the approach in endogenous local autoregressive signals without external supervision.

entry.title: PreAct: Computer-Using Agents that Get Faster on Repeated Tasks

author.name: Bojie Li

entry.summary: Presents PreAct, which compiles successful computer-using agent runs into small state-machine programs that replay 8.5-13x faster on repeated tasks without per-step LLM calls. Includes screen-matching checks that hand control back to the agent when something differs.

entry.title: Correct When Paired, Wrong When Split: Decoupling and Editing Modality-Specific Neurons in MLLMs

author.name: Tingchao Fu, Wenkai Wang, Fanxiao Li, Huadong Zhang, Jinhong Zhang, Dayang Li, Yunyun Dong, Renyang Liu, Wei Zhou

entry.summary: Reveals editing-decoupling failure in multimodal LLM knowledge editing, where entity updates triggered by paired text-image inputs revert to outdated facts under unimodal inputs because knowledge is stored across disentangled modality-specific pathways. Proposes editing modality-specific neurons accordingly.

entry.title: Recursive Scaling in Masked Diffusion Models

author.name: Alba Carballo-Castro, Julianna Piskorz, Paulius Rauba, Mihaela van der Schaar, Pascal Frossard

entry.summary: R-MDMs add recursive depth as a third scaling axis to masked diffusion models by repeatedly applying the same denoising transformer within each step. This parameter reuse improves efficiency, matching larger models on structured tasks like Sudoku and Countdown.

entry.title: Edge Flow: A Tractable and Predictive Continuous-Time Model for Gradient Descent at the Edge of Stability

author.name: Pierre Marion

entry.summary: Edge Flow is a system of three coupled ODEs providing a tractable continuous-time model of gradient descent dynamics at the edge of stability, where classical tools fail. It decomposes dynamics into a center, oscillation direction, and oscillation magnitude.

entry.title: A Diffusion Approximation for Temporal-Difference Learning with Linear Features under Markovian Noise

author.name: M. Forzo, E. Monzio Compagnoni, A. Russo, A. Pacchiano

entry.summary: Develops a stochastic differential equation approximation for linear TD(0) learning under Markovian noise that explains the constant-stepsize error floor via interaction between Markovian covariance and projected Bellman contraction geometry. It refines the classical ODE description of RL policy evaluation.

entry.title: Adaptive Volumetric Mechanical Property Fields Invariant to Resolution

author.name: Rishit Dagli, Donglai Xiang, Vismay Modi, Xuning Yang, Gavriel State, David I. W. Levin, Maria Shugrina

entry.summary: Introduces AdaVoMP, a sparse adaptive voxel transformer that predicts resolution-invariant dense mechanical property fields (Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, density) for 3D objects, improving accuracy and memory efficiency for physics simulation of digital assets. It enables realistic simulation of assets lacking material information.

entry.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Proof Autoformalization in Lean 4

author.name: Zhengtao Gui, Sheng Yang, Zhouxing Shi

entry.summary: Presents the first robustness study of LLM-based proof autoformalization in Lean 4, testing whether models remain faithful when informal proofs are paraphrased or diverge from idealized curated forms. It exposes brittleness in current autoformalizers under realistic input variation.

entry.title: ReportQA: QA-Based Radiology Report Evaluation

author.name: Yiming Shi, Shaoshuai Yang, Xi Chen, Haolin Li, Hengyu Zhang, Che Jiang, Kaiwen Wang, Xun Zhu, Dong Xie, Fei Wang, Dejing Dou, Miao Li, Ji Wu

entry.summary: Proposes ReportQA, a QA-based framework for evaluating radiology report generation that better captures clinical information transfer than NLG metrics or presence-focused clinical efficacy metrics, supporting flexible quantitative analysis. It grounds evaluation in how clinicians actually use reports for downstream diagnosis.

entry.title: AdaMame: A Training Recipe for Adaptive Multilingual Reasoning

author.name: Dayeon Ki, Kevin Duh, Marine Carpuat

entry.summary: Proposes AdaMame, a two-stage SFT-then-RL recipe for multilingual mathematical reasoning that adaptively aligns reasoning language to the query language to fix language collapse without sacrificing accuracy or causing mid-trace code-switching. It improves on binary language-fidelity reward fixes.

entry.title: Can Agents Read the Room? Benchmarking Visual Social Intelligence in Multimodal Simulation

author.name: Shijun Wan, Xuehai Wu, Jiwen Zhang, Siyuan Wang, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for visual social intelligence in multimodal simulation with 240 scenarios and role-based tasks testing whether agents use facial expressions, posture, gaze, and emotional cues to guide interaction. Evaluation of seven recent MLLMs reveals gaps in reading nonverbal social signals.

entry.title: EIBench: A Simulator-Based Benchmark and Turn-Credit RL for Emotion Management

author.name: Rongzhi Zhu, Xiang Huang, Yuchuan Wu, Rui Wang, Zequn Sun, Tao Ren, Weiyao Luo, Bingxue Qiu, Jieping Ye, Yongbin Li, Wei Hu

entry.summary: Introduces EIBench, a simulator-based benchmark for interactive multi-turn emotion management with 2,222 scenarios organized by a Support/Defense/Repair/Charm taxonomy, plus a turn-credit RL method for training emotionally intelligent dialogue agents. It moves emotional-intelligence evaluation beyond static recognition to dynamic emotional-state improvement.

entry.title: Vernier: Probing Representational Misalignment Behind Lexical Gaps in Causal Reasoning

author.name: Zhenyu Yu

entry.summary: Investigates why instruction-tuned models answer causal-reasoning questions differently when English variable names are replaced by placeholders, using paired-view weight updates and activation patching on Qwen and Llama models. It finds the lexical gap reflects misaligned read-out rather than information loss, since representations still carry answer-relevant content.

entry.title: EHRNote-ChatQA: A Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Multi-Turn Clinical Question Answering over Longitudinal Discharge Summaries

author.name: Jiyoun Kim, Muhan Yeo, Eunhye Jang, Jeewon Yang, Hangyul Yoon, Su Ji Lee, Hee Jo Han, Hee-Jae Jung, Doyun Kwon, Jun young Lee, Jaehun Lee, Jung-Oh Lee, Sunjun Kweon, Jong Hak Moon, Daseul Kim, Minjae Cho, Edward Choi

entry.summary: Introduces EHRNote-ChatQA, the first benchmark for evidence-grounded multi-turn clinical question answering over longitudinal discharge summaries, requiring iterative synthesis across documents with verifiable evidence support. It better reflects how clinicians actually review discharge summaries than exam-style or single-turn benchmarks.

entry.title: On Defining Erasure Harms for NLP

author.name: Yu Lu Liu, Arnav Goel, Jackie Chi Kit Cheung, Alexandra Olteanu, Ziang Xiao, Su Lin Blodgett

entry.summary: Develops a structured conceptual definition of erasure harm in NLP, clarifying the necessary components to establish and measure erasure, addressing the field's lack of a cohesive foundation between overly broad and overly setting-specific conceptualizations. It supports more rigorous identification and measurement of representational harms.

entry.title: BALTO: Balanced Token-Level Policy Optimization for Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: Ning Li, Zixuan Guo, Yan Xu, Wenbo Fei, Yifan Niu, Chang Luo, Yasheng Wang, Weiwen Liu, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes BALTO, a balanced token-level policy optimization framework for hallucination mitigation that addresses granularity mismatch where response-level faithfulness rewards wrongly penalize supported content, and avoids length/verbosity biases from unbalanced credit assignment. It improves faithful grounding in knowledge-intensive generation.

entry.title: Control-Plane Placement Shapes Forgetting: An Architectural Study of Agent Memory Across Thirteen System Configurations

author.name: Dongxu Yang

entry.summary: Proposes DiSan, a privacy-preserving text sanitization framework using a two-stream encoder to disentangle source-invariant task-semantic content from source-identifying style, with federated prototype alignment and adversarial regularization for multi-agent collaboration. It mitigates distributional signature leakage beyond explicit identifiers.

entry.title: Calibrated Triage, Not Autonomy: Confidence Estimation for Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Reza Khanmohammadi, Kundan Thind, Mohammad M. Ghassemi

entry.summary: Examines how the placement of an LLM within an agent memory pipeline (recall plane versus control plane mutations like supersede/release/purge) shapes which forgetting failure modes are recoverable, comparing thirteen system configurations on a 385-case adversarial surface. It finds three placement regimes with complementary coverage across canonicalization, cross-lingual, and intent-aware deletion.

entry.title: Contaminated Collaboration: Measuring Gender Bias Transfer in LLM-Assisted Student Writing

author.name: Ariyan Hossain, Kazi Kamruzzaman Rabbi, Farig Sadeque, S M Taiabul Haque

entry.summary: Investigates whether gender bias in an LLM writing assistant transfers into student-written career essays through a controlled study with 123 participants writing for paired profiles differing only in gender under no-AI, neutral-AI, and biased-AI conditions. It first verifies biased prompts induce gender-differentiated LLM text, then measures downstream human transfer.

entry.title: AuAu: A Benchmark for Auditing Authoritarian Alignment in Large Language Models

author.name: Andreas Einwiller, Max Klabunde, Florian Lemmerich

entry.summary: AuAu is a benchmark auditing whether LLMs exhibit or promote authoritarian attitudes, combining validated psychometric instruments, behavioral vignettes, and realistic user prompts. It probes both general authoritarian closeness and specific sub-concepts.

entry.title: ACCORD: Action-Conditioned Contextual Grounding for Language Agents

author.name: Lai Jiang, Cheng Qian, Zhenhailong Wang, Pan Lu, Heng Ji, Hao Peng

entry.summary: ACCORD addresses how LLM agents fail to recover implicit context from environment state, acting from assumed rather than observed specifics and overlooking gatherable evidence. It proposes action-conditioned contextual grounding so agents identify missing context, ground it in observations, and carry it forward.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Infer World Models? Evidence from Agentic Automata Learning

author.name: Reef Menaged, Gili Lior, Shauli Ravfogel, Roee Aharoni, Gabriel Stanovsky
