author.name: Kathrin Korte, Christian Medeiros Adriano, Joachim Winther Pedersen, Eleni Nisioti, Sebastian Risi

entry.summary: Investigates how modular architecture, task similarity, and representational dimensionality jointly shape compositional continual learning in an A-B-A paradigm. Finds that explicit modularity helps little in high-dimensional lazy regimes but matters in low-dimensional ones.

entry.title: MGUP: A Momentum-Gradient Alignment Update Policy for Stochastic Optimization

author.name: Da Chang, Ganzhao Yuan

entry.summary: MGUP is a momentum-gradient alignment update policy that applies larger step-sizes to a selected proportion of parameters while keeping smaller steps for others, integrating with AdamW, Lion, and Muon. It offers fine-grained selective updates with convergence guarantees.

entry.title: Sign-Rank, Index, and List Replicability: Connections and Separations

author.name: Ari Blondal, Hamed Hatami, Pooya Hatami, Chavdar Lalov, Sivan Tretiak

entry.summary: This paper establishes connections and separations between sign rank, the Z2-index, and list replicability in learning theory. It resolves an open question by showing a strong separation between sign rank and Z2-index.

entry.title: Turning music identification into a neural forward pass

author.name: Muhammad Taimoor Haseeb, Ahmad Hammoudeh, Gus Xia

entry.summary: This work turns music identification from a System-2 rule-based search pipeline into a single neural feed-forward pass by a generative transformer that predicts track identifiers directly from audio excerpts. It mimics associative human recognition rather than explicit candidate enumeration.

entry.title: Damage Adaptation in Seconds for Architected Materials

author.name: James Avtges, Jake Ketchum, Helena Young, Taekyoung Kim, Ryan Truby, Todd Murphey

entry.summary: This work enables proprioceptive adaptation to catastrophic damage in soft-actuated architected materials in under one minute, using latent damage representations and a simple ensemble method. It identifies conditions where exponential sample complexity collapses to linear.

entry.title: Differential Privacy of Gaussian Process Posterior Sampling

author.name: Tomasz Maciazek

entry.summary: This work studies the differential privacy of releasing Gaussian process posterior sample paths, showing the intrinsic randomness of posterior sampling yields Renyi-DP guarantees without external noise. It separates posterior-mean leakage from covariance leakage and validates with membership inference attacks.

entry.title: Let LLMs Judge Each Other: Multi-Agent Peer-Reviewed Reasoning for Medical Question Answering

author.name: Zaifu Zhan, Shuang Zhou, Rui Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-agent peer-reviewed reasoning method where multiple LLM agents generate chain-of-thought answers then review each other's reasoning for factual correctness and logic, selecting the highest-rated chain. It improves accuracy and interpretability on medical QA benchmarks over single-model CoT.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Stance Detection in Scientific Discourse: A Test Case in Bayesian Cognitive Science

author.name: Eyup Engin Kucuk, Tarik Kelestemur, \"Omer Da\u{g}lar Tanrikulu

entry.summary: Studies LLM-assisted stance detection in scientific discourse, using a theory-driven codebook and diagnostic-gated prompt optimization to classify whether authors treat Bayesian cognitive models as realist or instrumentalist across three frontier LLMs. It validates LLMs for interpretive qualitative coding with multi-rater reliability analysis.

entry.title: Distilling Examples into Task Instructions: Enhanced In-Context Learning for Real-World B2B Conversations

author.name: Guy Rotman, Adi Kopilov, Danit Berger Zalmanson, Omri Allouche

entry.summary: Introduces the Call Playbook dataset of five classification tasks from real B2B sales conversations and proposes knowledge-extraction methods that distill verbose few-shot examples into compact interpretable task instructions for in-context learning. It addresses ICL limitations as context length grows with concatenated examples.

entry.title: A Large-Scale Multi-Dimensional Empirical Study of LLMs for Conversation Summarization

author.name: Weixiao Zhou, Gengyao Li, Xianfu Cheng, Junnan Zhu, Feifei Zhai, Zhoujun Li

entry.summary: OmniCSEval is a large-scale benchmark for conversation summarization spanning 1,800 conversations across six scenarios with context lengths up to 32k tokens, using a bidirectional fact-checking framework to assess completeness, conciseness, and faithfulness. It includes frontier reasoning systems and small models.

entry.title: FraudSMSWalker: Benchmarking Agentic Large Language Models for SMS-to-Webpage Fraud Detection

author.name: Y. H. Zhou, Z. M. Ma, Y. J. Zhou, Y. T. Li, H. X. Xiang, Y. M. Cheng, T. L. Chen, K. J. Zhang, Z. H. Nan, J. H. Ni, Z. Wu, Q. Y. Pan, S. Zhang, S. Cheng, M. Y. Luo

entry.summary: FraudSMSWalker is a controlled benchmark for URL-masked SMS-to-webpage fraud detection requiring models to judge how SMS claims align with sanitized webpage content and requested actions, avoiding reputation shortcuts. It contains 699 bilingual chains across ten service scenarios.

entry.title: The Art of Mixology: Mixup-based Obfuscation for Privacy-Preserving Split Learning in Large Language Models

author.name: Chen Chen, Xiang Gao, Xianshun Wang, Chengran Li, Shengyu Xia, Xueluan Gong, Linru Zhang, Qian Wang, Kwok-Yan Lam

entry.summary: MIXGUARD is a mixup-based privacy-preserving split learning framework for LLMs introducing token-level obfuscation to defend against data reconstruction attacks while balancing utility, efficiency, and stability. It targets the difficult tradeoff among these factors in resource-constrained split training.

entry.title: MAGE-RAG: Multigranular Adaptive Graph Evidence for Agentic Multimodal RAG in Long-Document QA

author.name: Yilong Zuo, Xunkai Li, Jing Yuan, Qiangqiang Dai, Hongchao Qin, Ronghua Li

entry.summary: MAGE-RAG is a multigranular adaptive graph evidence framework for long-document multimodal QA that uses page retrieval as an entry point and builds query-time graph evidence to balance coverage, noise, and inference cost across text, tables, images, and charts. It improves on fixed top-k retrieval. Relevant for multimodal RAG.

entry.title: SierpinskiCam: Camera-Controlled Video Retaking with Sierpinski Triangle Pattern Cues

author.name: Suttisak Wizadwongsa, Hyelin Nam, Supasorn Suwajanakorn, Jeong Joon Park

entry.summary: SierpinskiCam tackles single-video camera-controlled video retaking by augmenting geometry-based guidance with Sierpinski dome texture cues that provide rich trackable features even under large viewpoint changes, addressing the degradation of geometry guidance when the target camera departs from the source trajectory. It improves rendering of newly revealed regions. A creative video diffusion guidance technique.

entry.title: StereoFactory: A Unified Merging Framework for Robust Stereo Matching

author.name: Xianda Guo, Pinhan Fu, Ruilin Wang, Wenke Huang, Mang Ye, Qin Zou

entry.summary: StereoFactory is a coarse-to-fine evolutionary framework for adaptive model merging in stereo matching, using a genetic algorithm to search which specialized models should participate then resolving module-level interference, offering a scalable post-hoc alternative to costly joint retraining. It addresses harmful task-vector interference in existing merging methods. Relevant for scalable stereo foundation models.

entry.title: Universal Image Restoration via Internalized Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Yu Guo, Zhengru Fang, Shengfeng He, Senkang Hu, Yihang Tao, Phone Lin, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: CoTIR is a universal image restoration framework that internalizes chain-of-thought reasoning within a single model by viewing restoration as a specialized subtask of image editing, avoiding the high computational cost and weak degradation-interaction modeling of multi-round CoT with specialized modules. It targets complex mixed degradations. Relevant for all-in-one restoration.

entry.title: The Slop Paradox: How Synthetic Standardization Erodes Clinical Uncertainty and Cross-Modal Alignment in AI-Rewritten Radiology Reports

author.name: Samar Ansari

entry.summary: This single-author study measures information degradation when LLMs rewrite radiology reports, quantifying entity erosion, hedging collapse (loss of clinical uncertainty), and cross-modal alignment changes across three rewriting tasks. It finds a dissociation between information loss and cross-modal fidelity.

entry.title: DexLink Hand: A Compact, Affordable, 16-DOF Linkage-Driven Hand with Human-Like Dexterity

author.name: Hao Wu, Yanzhe Wang, Yu Feng, Jian Liu, Jihao Li, Jianshu Zhou, Huixu Dong

entry.summary: DexLink Hand is a compact, low-cost (under USD 400, 320g) 16-actuator, 20-joint linkage-driven anthropomorphic hand achieving human-like dexterity within a human-sized form. It addresses the dexterity-compactness-affordability trade-off in robotic hands.

entry.title: LLM-as-Judge in Education: A Curriculum-Grounded Marking Pipeline

author.name: Xiwei Xu, Chen Wang, Jacky Jiang, Phil Yang, Qian Fu, Mohan Dhall, Wenjie Zhang, Liming Zhu

entry.summary: Presents a curriculum-grounded LLM-as-Judge pipeline for question-level exam marking that grounds outputs in authorized curriculum artifacts and marking guidelines, co-developed with an industry partner. Targets high-stakes exam preparation for university admission.

entry.title: Memory as a Wasting Asset: Pricing Flash Endurance for Embodied Agents, and the Limits of Doing So

author.name: Josef Liyanjun Chen

entry.summary: Treats embodied-agent flash memory as depreciating non-renewable capital, pricing write endurance with a single shadow price to make cost-optimal memory placement across RAM/NVM/cloud a threshold rule. Measures the value-write association on real robot logs and identifies limits of the approach.

entry.title: ParkingTransformer: LLM-Enhanced End-to-End Trajectory Planning for Autonomous Parking

author.name: Hauteng Wu, Xu Li, Dong Kong, Zihang Wang, Xieyuanli Chen, Benwu Wang, Wenkai Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes ParkingTransformer, an end-to-end autonomous parking trajectory planner that combines multi-view perception with LLM scene-understanding, interacting directly with historical and raw sensor data to output trajectories without dense bird's-eye-view representations. Adds interpretability and semantic understanding to black-box parking.

entry.title: Amortized Probabilistic Retrieval of Atmospheric CO2 from OCO-2 Spectra Using Deep Learning with Laplace Approximations and Normalizing Flows

author.name: Alejandro Calle-Saldarriaga, Felix Jimenez, Jack Grosskreuz, Jiazheng Wang, Jonathan Hobbs, Matthias Katzfuss

entry.summary: A deep learning framework for retrieving atmospheric CO2 from satellite spectra using Laplace approximations and normalizing flows for uncertainty quantification. It offers a faster alternative to expensive operational retrieval algorithms validated on high-fidelity simulations.

entry.title: When the Next Step Is Not One Step: Distribution-Aware Execution Modeling for Concurrent Go Programs

author.name: Kaviru Hapuarachchi

entry.summary: This work uses scheduler nondeterminism in concurrent Go programs as a training signal, fine-tuning a 7B model to match empirical distributions of next-events via KL objective. It improves prediction accuracy on real production bugs from CockroachDB, Kubernetes, and others.

entry.title: An expressivity analysis of hierarchical modelling in deep transformers via bounded-depth grammars

author.name: Vinoth Nandakumar, Qiang Qu, Pramod Thebe, Sakshi Khachariya, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: This work analyzes the expressiveness of deep transformers in representing hierarchical structures through the lens of bounded-depth, non-recursive context-free grammars. It provides rigorous theory for how depth enables hierarchical representations in language modeling.

entry.title: Fast Nonparametric Conditional Independence Testing via Two-Stage Regression

author.name: Eric V. Strobl

entry.summary: BLITZ is a fast nonparametric conditional independence test designed for constraint-based causal discovery, running under a second while maintaining calibration. It uses two-stage residualization combining low-order polynomial regression with shallow tree regressions.

entry.title: Evaluating Open-Source LLMs for Multi-Label ATT&CK Technique Classification on CTI Reports

author.name: Ahmed Ryan, Saad Sakib Noor, Md Erfan, Shaswata Mitra, Sudip Mittal, Md Rayhanur Rahman

entry.summary: Evaluates open-source LLMs on multi-label MITRE ATT&CK technique classification from realistic unstructured cyber threat intelligence reports, showing prior single-technique evaluations inflate performance. It establishes more honest baselines for complex, multi-step attack pattern recognition.

entry.title: CoCoGEC: Counterfactual Generation for Robust Grammatical Error Correction

author.name: Qianyu Wang, Xiaoman Wang, Yuanyuan Liang, Xinyuan Li, Yunshi Lan

entry.summary: Proposes CoCoGEC, a counterfactual generation framework for grammatical error correction that alters error-irrelevant context to improve robustness against context perturbations and label-flipping. It targets GEC models' tendency to fail when surrounding context shifts.

entry.title: DYNA : Dynamic Episodic Memory Networks for Augmenting Large Language Models with Temporal Knowledge Graphs in Continuous Learning

author.name: Ali Sarabadani, Mahtab Tajvidiyan

entry.summary: Proposes DYNA, a lightweight framework augmenting a frozen LLM with a temporal knowledge graph as updatable external memory, retrieving relevant nodes via random walks and centrality, reducing catastrophic forgetting by ~7% versus fine-tuning and improving temporal ordering ~5% over standard RAG. It links graph clustering structure to retrieval quality.

entry.title: Interactor: Agentic RL oriented Iterative Creation for Ad Description Generation in Sponsored Search

author.name: Penghui Wei, Jiayu Wu, Chao Ye, Zhi Guo, Shuanglong Li, Lin Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Interactor, a multi-turn iterative creation framework optimized with agentic RL for generating informative ad descriptions in sponsored search, where the generation policy interacts with an environment of multiple generative reward models evaluating knowledge capacity and selling points. It targets longer-span descriptions that incorporate world knowledge to address search intent.

entry.title: FinBalance: A Multi-Document Accounting Reconciliation Benchmark

author.name: Sasank Tumpati, Devansh Agarwal, Ayush Kedia, Arjun Neekhra, Murari Mandal, Krishna Garg, Yash Sinha, Suman Gupta, Dhruv Kumar

entry.summary: FinBalance is a multi-document accounting reconciliation benchmark built from synthetic source-document bundles across industries and difficulty levels, requiring models to produce journal entries, balance sheets, and detect inconsistencies. It targets realistic earlier-stage accounting workflows rather than prepared financial artifacts.

entry.title: In-Domain Supervised Pathology Report Classification: A Reproducible Pipeline from Data Curation to Production-Matched Evaluation

author.name: Isaac Hands, Bin Huang, Adam Spannaus, John Gounley, Heidi Hanson, Eric Durbin, Sally R. Ellingson

entry.summary: This paper presents a reproducible in-domain supervised pipeline for pathology report classification that counters out-of-distribution performance drops across cancer registries, emphasizing low false-negative rates and manageable reviewer workload. It standardizes data curation with facility-stratified sampling and production-matched holdouts.

entry.title: Does Traversal Order Matter? A Systematic Study of Tree Traversal Methods in Transformer Grammars

author.name: Zongru Liu, Pengyu Ji, Pengcheng Wang, Kewei Tu

entry.summary: This work systematically studies tree traversal methods in Transformer Grammars, introducing Breadth-First Traversal and a hybrid Production-Rule Traversal that combines structural lookahead with early lexical generation, beyond the standard Depth-First Traversal. It evaluates these across language modeling, syntactic generalization, and summarization.

entry.title: Cloze: An Open Research Platform for Studying Human-AI Conversations in Mental Health Contexts

author.name: Matthew Flathers, Francesco Cipriani, John Torous

entry.summary: Cloze is an open-source platform for running controlled, monitored studies of human-AI conversation in mental health research, offering configurable models, prompts, scheduling, and unconditional safety constraints with full provenance logging. It addresses the lack of experimental control in consumer LLM products for researchers. Valuable infrastructure for responsible mental-health AI study.

entry.title: Focus When Necessary: Adaptive Routing and Collaborative Grounding for Training-Free Visual Grounding

author.name: Yifan Wang, Peiming Li, Shiyu Li, Zhiyuan Hu, Xiaochen Yang, Wenming Yang, Yang Tang, Zheng Wei

entry.summary: LazyMCoT is a training-free framework that adaptively allocates visual grounding effort based on sample difficulty using an uncertainty-based adaptive routing mechanism from first-token statistics, avoiding indiscriminate image scaling and cropping. It targets fine-grained perception in high-resolution images by MLLMs. A practical efficiency-accuracy improvement for visual grounding.

entry.title: LLM-Powered Virtual Population for Demand Simulation and Pricing

author.name: Chengpiao Huang, Kaizheng Wang

entry.summary: This work develops an LLM-powered virtual population model that simulates demand for pricing decisions by representing customers as a finite mixture of personas, eliciting persona-level purchase probabilities from rich product text and images, and aggregating through calibrated mixture weights to yield demand distributions with uncertainty. It supports counterfactual pricing. An interesting LLM-for-economics application.

entry.title: Selection Without Signal, Recovery Through Expression: A Measurement Study of Post-Hoc Falsification Operators for Frozen Small Code Models

author.name: Mehmet Iscan

entry.summary: This measurement study evaluates 26 semantic post-hoc operators (selection, verification, repair, elimination, portfolios, sound vetoes) against Best-of-N for frozen small code models under a leakage-free matched-compute protocol, finding that none improve held-out accuracy on the tested benchmarks. It provides a sobering negative result for post-hoc remedies. Useful methodological caution.

entry.title: FATE: Pillar Encoding and Frequency-Aware Training for Event-Based Object Detection

author.name: Md Tawheedul Islam Bhuian, Kyoung-Don Kang

entry.summary: FATE proposes a unified framework for event-based object detection built on a novel Pillar Encoding that preserves fine-grained temporal structure rather than discarding it through fixed temporal sub-binning, enabling frequency-aware training beyond the low temporal frequencies imposed by training supervision. It addresses the sparse, asynchronous nature of event streams. Relevant for event-camera perception.

entry.title: RAVA: Retrieval-Augmented Viewpoint Alignment for Subject-Driven Image Generation

author.name: Qiwei Yan, Zhiqiang Yuan, Chongyang Li, Jiapei Zhang, Ying Deng, Jinchao Zhang, Jie Zhou

entry.summary: RAVA addresses cross-subject viewpoint alignment in subject-driven image generation, where a model must infer one subject's implicit viewpoint and transfer it to another using only image-level evidence without camera poses or depth, using a retrieval-augmented approach to avoid spurious semantic correlations that cause viewpoint drift and structural mismatches. It targets reliable viewpoint control. Relevant for controllable generation.

entry.title: MaineCoon: Pursuing A Real-Time Audio-Visual Social World Model

author.name: Lichen Bai, Tianhao Zhang, Shitong Shao, Dingwei Tan, Qiyu Zhong, Zhengpeng Xie, Haopeng Li, Qinghao Huang, Dandan Shen, Tengjiao Ji, Wei Wang, Peicheng Wu, Yuxuan Zhao, Xiangyu Zhu, Welly Luo, Shurui Yang, Zeke Xie

entry.summary: MaineCoon presents a 22B-parameter real-time audio-visual autoregressive world model targeting human-centric social dynamics rather than physical or gaming worlds. It claims sub-second interaction latency as a prototype social world model.

entry.title: AnnotateAnything: Automatic Annotation of 3D Assets for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Haoran Lu, Mutian Shen, Shuyang Yu, Yu Xiao, Songling Liu, Jianshu Zhang, Shang Wu, Yue Chen, Guo Ye, Jiayi Wang, Zhaoran Wang, Han Liu

entry.summary: AnnotateAnything automatically converts passive 3D assets into manipulation-ready assets by inferring semantics, interaction constraints, and 3D-grounded cues via vision-language reasoning, plus a fully automatic annotation pipeline. It addresses the gap between raw geometry and actionable robot manipulation labels.

entry.title: Structured Adversarial Camouflage via Voronoi Diagrams

author.name: Jens Bayer, Stefan Becker, David M\"unch, Michael Arens, J\"urgen Beyerer

entry.summary: Proposes adversarial camouflage using Voronoi diagrams that optimizes only seed-point locations under fixed printable palettes, producing structured patterns that fool person detectors. The attack transfers across detector families and backgrounds in black-box settings.

entry.title: A Neuromorphic Trigger for Efficient Audio Event Detection

author.name: Benjamin Hatton, Oliver Rhodes, Luca Peres

entry.summary: Introduces a spiking neural network trigger that gates audio input, forwarding only salient segments to heavier downstream models for event detection. Achieves strong F1 scores while reducing computation for resource-constrained systems.

entry.title: Non-negative Elastic Net Decoding for Information Retrieval

author.name: Koki Okajima, Yasutoshi Ida, Tsukasa Yoshida, Yasuaki Nakamura

entry.summary: Reformulates dense retrieval as a joint decoding problem using non-negative elastic net optimization to select documents with awareness of the entire corpus, reducing redundancy. Aims to produce more diverse, less redundant retrieved sets than score-independent top-k.

entry.title: Expanding SPHERE-JEPA: A Family of Statistical Regularizers for the Hypersphere

author.name: L\'eo Nicollier (CB, ATT), Enric Meinhardt-Llopis (CB), Max Dunitz (ATT), Marc Pic (ATT), Pablo Mus\'e (CB, IFUMI), Gabriele Facciolo (CB)

entry.summary: This paper expands the SPHERE-JEPA family of self-supervised learning regularizers by analytically integrating out random projections to yield a deterministic Maximum Mean Discrepancy, avoiding the variance of sliced methods. It targets representation collapse prevention on the hypersphere.

entry.title: Where Should Action Generation Begin? A Learnable Source Prior for Generative Robot Policies

author.name: Meipo Dai, Qiyuan Zhuang, He-Yang Xu, Ying-Jie Shuai, Yijun Wang, Qi Dou, Xiu-Shen Wei

entry.summary: LeaP replaces the standard Gaussian source distribution in generative robot policies with a proprioception-conditioned diagonal Gaussian over action chunks. This observation-informed yet stochastic initialization lets the generator focus on precise action refinement.

entry.title: GRACE-DS: a Guarded Reward-guided Agent Correction Environment in Data Science

author.name: Aleksandr Tsymbalov, Danis Zaripov, Artem Epifanov, Anastasya Palienko

entry.summary: GRACE-DS is a guarded reward-guided evaluation environment for LLM-powered AutoML agents on tabular ML tasks, with hidden validators measuring not only predictive performance but also leakage avoidance, reproducibility, protocol validity, and correction behavior. It supports pre-deployment evaluation across realistic data science workflow stages.

entry.title: XAI-Grounded Explanation Generation for Speech Deepfake Detection with Training-Free Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Yupei Li, Qiyang Sun, Xiaoliang Wu, Chenxi Wang, Berrak Sisman, Bj\"orn W. Schuller

entry.summary: This work proposes a training-free framework integrating XAI attribution evidence with multimodal LLMs to generate grounded natural-language explanations for speech deepfake detection. It bridges low-level attribution signals and human-understandable explanations without task-specific supervision.

entry.title: SkillWiki: A Living Knowledge Infrastructure for Agent Skills

author.name: Dingcheng Huang, Yuda Ding, Bingshuo Liu, Qingbin Liu, Xi Chen, Jiang Bian, Hongliang Sun, Zhiying Tu, Dianhui Chu, Xiaoyan Yu, Dianbo Sui

entry.summary: SkillWiki is a living knowledge infrastructure for agent skills supporting large-scale production, governance, and evolution by transforming heterogeneous knowledge into reusable skill assets linked to originating evidence. It presents a complete skill lifecycle from ingestion through provenance-aware exploration and execution-driven evolution.

entry.title: Fast When, Careful Who: Dual-Process Multiparty Turn-Taking with Diffusion Augmentation

author.name: Rutherford A. Patamia, Ming Liu, Wei Luo, Favour Ekong, Akan Cosgun

entry.summary: This work proposes an audio-only two-stage pipeline for multiparty turn-taking that separates when to trigger a turn boundary from whether the floor is actually transferring, with a fast trigger and lightweight verifier plus diffusion augmentation. It targets realistic multiparty audio with overlap and rapid speaker changes.

entry.title: Robust Dual-Signal Fusion: Hybrid Neuro-Symbolic Gating with Compressed Chain-of-Thought Refinement for Irony Detection in Social Media Texts

author.name: Ankit Bhattacharjee, Krityapriya Bhaumik

entry.summary: The RDS Fusion framework is a hybrid neuro-symbolic architecture for zero-shot irony detection that compresses chain-of-thought reasoning without supervised fine-tuning, achieving 78.1% accuracy on TweetEval and filtering out-of-distribution hallucinations on iSarcasm. It matches fine-tuned BERTweet performance while remaining zero-shot.

entry.title: IMPACTeen: Intentions, Manipulation, Persuasion, Annotations, and Consequences in Teen Communication Dataset

author.name: Aleksander Szcz\k{e}sny, Wiktoria Mieleszczenko-Kowszewicz, Maciej Markiewicz, Beata Bajcar, Tomasz Adamczyk, Jolanta Babiak, Grzegorz Chodak, Przemys{\l}aw Kazienko

entry.summary: IMPACTeen is a dataset of 1,021 social influence scenarios in adolescent contexts with 5,100 annotation records labeled from five perspectives (teens, parents, psychologists, communication experts, teachers). It supports research on social influence, manipulation, and persuasion detection in teen communication.

entry.title: Whose hotel does the AI recommend? An algorithm audit of reputation signals in LLM-assisted hotel selection

author.name: Mirza Samad Ahmed Baig, Syeda Anshrah Gillani, Asher Ali

entry.summary: This algorithm audit uses a pre-registered randomized conjoint design across personas, prompts, and twelve open and proprietary models to measure which reputation signals drive LLM hotel recommendations. It finds guest rating and price dominate, with a top rating raising selection by 31.6 percentage points. Relevant for understanding LLMs as commercial gatekeepers and bias.

entry.title: Reasoning Text-to-Video Retrieval for Operating Room Clips via Action-Driven Digital Twins

author.name: Yiqing Shen, Hao Ding, Mathias Unberath

entry.summary: OR3 is a reasoning-capable text-to-video retrieval method for operating-room clips that converts clips into action-driven digital twins by grouping concurrent subject-action-object triplets under non-overlapping temporal intervals, enabling implicit queries requiring reasoning rather than relying on global embeddings. It supports OR safety event retrieval. A focused medical video retrieval contribution.

entry.title: EventDrive: Event Cameras for Vision-Language Driving Intelligence

author.name: Dongyue Lu, Rong Li, Ao Liang, Lingdong Kong, Wei Yin, Lai Xing Ng, Benoit R. Cottereau, Camille Simon Chane, Wei Tsang Ooi

entry.summary: EventDrive is a benchmark and model suite unifying event-camera streams, RGB frames, and language supervision for vision-language driving intelligence. It examines how high-dynamic-range, low-latency event sensing aids reasoning and decision-making across the driving loop.

entry.title: HumanoidArena: Benchmarking Egocentric Hierarchical Whole-body Learning

author.name: Taowen Wang, Zikang Xie, Bin Yang, Yunheng Wang, Zizhao Yuan, Yuetong Fang, Yixiao Feng, Yichi Wang, Xingyu Chen, Haodong Chen, Qiwei Wu, Weisheng Xu, Lihan Chen, Lusong Li, Zecui Zeng, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: HumanoidArena is a simulation-first benchmark for egocentric hierarchical whole-body humanoid learning that specifically evaluates the high-level-policy-to-low-level-tracker interface for executability, robustness, and transferability. It addresses a gap where benchmarks rarely test the policy-tracker interface itself.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction Intervals with Tail-Specific Guarantees

author.name: Simone Cuonzo, Nina Deliu

entry.summary: This paper extends split conformal prediction to provide explicitly calibrated tail-specific coverage guarantees for upper and lower tails separately, then derives a two-sided interval by intersection with proven tail and global marginal coverage. It covers both exchangeable (finite-sample) and non-exchangeable (asymptotic) settings.

entry.title: Distributed General-Purpose Agent Networks: Architecture, Key Mechanisms, and Prototypes

author.name: Shengli Zhang, Deen Ma, Zibin Lin, Taotao Wang

entry.summary: Studies distributed peer-to-peer networks of heterogeneous LLM agents that discover one another, establish trust, and negotiate cooperation across devices and governance boundaries. Argues such networks need new mechanisms beyond combining existing P2P overlays with agents.

entry.title: SegTME-UNI2: A Foundation Model-Based Framework for Generalisable Multiclass Cell Segmentation and LLM-Driven Tumour Microenvironment Characterisation in Histopathology

author.name: Wan Siti Halimatul Munirah Wan Ahmad, Faris Syahmi Samidi, Mohammad Badal Ahmmed, Vimal Angela Thiviyanathan, Selvam James Thavaraj, Anwar P. P. Abdul Majeed

entry.summary: Presents a unified histopathology framework combining a pathology foundation model with dual UperNet decoders for multiclass cell segmentation and LLM-driven tumour microenvironment reporting. It addresses the lack of pixel-level annotations via progressive pseudo-labeling.

entry.title: Performance-Driven Environment Abstraction with Multi-Timescale Learning

author.name: Yue Guan, Dipankar Maity, Panagiotis Tsiotras

entry.summary: This paper develops performance-driven environment abstraction for large MDPs, aggregating states to directly optimize decision quality rather than preserving structure. It pairs this with a multi-timescale RL framework with theoretical performance guarantees.

entry.title: Toward Controllable Catalyst Inverse Design via Large-Scale Autoregressive Pretraining

author.name: Dong Hyeon Mok, Jonggeol Na, Seoin Back

entry.summary: This work presents a GPT-based conditional generative model for inverse design of heterogeneous catalysts, using a numerical embedding layer to generate structures with target properties. It aims to overcome screening inefficiencies in catalyst discovery.

entry.title: Physics-Constrained Neural Networks for Improved Short-Term Weather Forecasting: A Case Study over the South Pacific

author.name: Egor Bugaev, Fedor Buzaev, Dmitry Efremenko, Denis Derkach, Fedor Ratnikov

entry.summary: This study enhances physics-constrained neural networks for short-term weather forecasting over the South Pacific, building on WeatherGFT with an upgraded WENO-5 solver, a unified autoregressive hybrid block, and integration with foundation models. It achieves up to 26% MSE reduction.

entry.title: Monotonic Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks: A Theoretical and Empirical Study of Monotonicity as an Inductive Bias

author.name: Mikhail Krasnov, Carolina Fortuna, Bla\v{z} Bertalani\v{c}

entry.summary: MKAN is a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network with hard monotonicity guaranteed for all parameter values via exponential reparameterization of B-spline coefficients. It enables standard unconstrained training while ensuring monotonicity, unlike prior projection-based methods.

entry.title: RadSEM: A Finding-by-Finding Metric for Clinical Consistency in Radiology Reports

author.name: Zhenhong Yang, Zhuoyun Liu, Jintao Fei, Wen Tang, Shichao Quan, Jun Zhao, Jun Xu

entry.summary: RadSEM is a finding-by-finding metric for evaluating radiology reports that distinguishes clinical compatibility from surface similarity, handling negation, laterality, and polarity. It performs contradiction-constrained matching of atomic finding sentences.

entry.title: Root-Selecting Fixed-Point Inversion for Rectified Flows via Trajectory Straightness

author.name: Semin Kim, Jihwan Yoon, Seunghoon Hong

entry.summary: SelFix is a root-selecting fixed-point inversion method for rectified flows that uses trajectory straightness as a principled criterion for selecting among multiple fixed-point solutions. It improves reconstruction and editing quality for training-free image editing.

entry.title: Beyond Visual Cues: CoT-Enhanced Reasoning for Semi-supervised Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Yuming Chen, Yuxin Xie, Tao Zhou, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: CERS integrates Chain-of-Thought reasoning into semi-supervised medical image segmentation to move beyond pixel-level visual pattern matching. It aims to capture the diagnostic logic experts use when visually similar lesions warrant distinct conclusions.

entry.title: AmchiBias: Measuring Stereotypical Bias in Goan Identity Groups with a Minimal Pair Dataset in English and Konkani

author.name: Michelle Barbosa, Sebastian Pad\'o, Franziska Weeber

entry.summary: Presents AmchiBias, the first subnational stereotype-bias benchmark for the Indian state of Goa with 313 minimal pairs across eight sociodemographic dimensions in English and Konkani, evaluating five multilingual encoders. It highlights near-chance performance in Konkani revealing low-resource language incompetence.

entry.title: Few-Shot Biomedical Relation Extraction with Large Language Models: A Viable Alternative to Supervised Learning?

author.name: Jakob Mraz, Toma\v{z} Curk, Bla\v{z} Zupan

entry.summary: Investigates few-shot biomedical relation extraction with prompt-based LLMs, comparing pairwise classification (higher recall) versus joint generation (higher precision) on BioREDirect as an alternative to costly supervised models. It assesses scalability and adaptability across relation types.

entry.title: AthDGC: An Open Diachronic Greek Treebank with Indo-European Parallels

author.name: Nikolaos Lavidas, Kiki Nikiforidou, Dag Haug, Leonid Kulikov, Vassiliki Geka, Vassileios Symeonidis, Theodoros Michalareas, Sofia Chionidi, Anastasia Tsiropina, Eleni Plakoutsi, Evangelos Argyropoulos

entry.summary: Introduces AthDGC, the first openly licensed dependency-parsed treebank of Greek spanning eight diachronic periods under a unified PROIEL schema, with verse-level New Testament alignment to Latin, Gothic, Old Church Slavonic, and Armenian. It provides a resource for diachronic and Indo-European comparative linguistics.

entry.title: SAG: SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation with Query-Time Dynamic Hyperedges

author.name: Yuchao Wu, Junqin Li, XingCheng Liang, Yongjie Chen, Yinghao Liang, Linyuan Mo, Guanxian Li

entry.summary: SAG proposes a SQL-based retrieval augmentation approach that converts text chunks into semantically complete events with indexing entities, then uses dynamic SQL join queries instead of pre-built static knowledge graphs. It aims to address structured constraints and multi-hop reasoning limits in dense retrieval RAG.

entry.title: Scaling Human and G2P Supervision for Robust Phonetic Transcription

author.name: Alexander Metzger, Aruna Srivastava, Ruslan Mukhamedvaleev

entry.summary: This study examines how automatic phonetic transcription performance scales with human versus G2P supervision in English, finding a quality threshold where G2P helps only with fewer than 20-30 hours of human annotation. Beyond it, ASR pretraining drives substantial error reduction across native, non-native, and post-stroke speech.

entry.title: PVminerLLM2: Improving Structured Extraction of Patient Voice via Preference Optimization

author.name: Samah Fodeh, Linhai Ma, Ganesh Puthiaraju, Srivani Talakokkul, Afshan Khan, Elyas Irankhah, Sreeraj Ramachandran, Ashley Hagaman, Sarah Lowe, Aimee Roundtree

entry.summary: PVminerLLM2 applies preference optimization to improve structured extraction of patient voice from unstructured patient-generated text, targeting token-critical errors that supervised fine-tuning struggles with. It introduces a token-aware preference objective for rare, fine-grained extraction errors.

entry.title: Surpassing Scale by Efficiency: A Compact 135M Parameter Foundational LLM Natively Adapted for the Bangla Language

author.name: Rabindra Nath Nandi

entry.summary: This paper presents bangla-smollm-135m, a compact 135M-parameter decoder model natively adapted for Bangla via a deterministic token-merging strategy between TituLLMs and SmolLM2, overcoming subword script fragmentation. It targets efficient deployment on edge and mobile hardware for a low-resource non-Latin script.

entry.title: P3B3: A Multi-Turn Conversational Benchmark for Measuring European and Brazilian Portuguese Variety Bias in LLMs

author.name: Rafael Ferreira, In\^es Vieira, In\^es Calvo, James Furtado, Iago Paulo, Diogo Tavares, Diogo Gl\'oria-Silva, David Semedo, Jo\~ao Magalh\~aes

entry.summary: P3B3 is a multi-turn conversational benchmark for measuring European versus Brazilian Portuguese variety bias in LLMs, with an evaluation framework for bias and controllability. Experiments show most LLMs strongly favor pt-BR with varying controllability across models.

entry.title: SCAR: Semantic Continuity-Aware Retrieval for Efficient Context Expansion in RAG

author.name: Nathana\"el Langlois

entry.summary: SCAR is an adaptive RAG retrieval policy that selectively expands neighboring chunks by weighing query-neighbor relevance against a structural continuity penalty, using a relative expansion threshold tied to each chunk's own relevance to achieve approximately scale-invariant decisions transferable across embedding models. It mitigates boundary fragmentation without heavy token overhead. A practical RAG improvement.

entry.title: Flux-Guard: Facial Identity Protection using diffusion models

author.name: Jie Wang, Tao Wang, Ru Zhang, Jianyi Liu

entry.summary: Flux-Guard is a privacy-preserving face editing framework based on adversarial attacks that protects facial identity from unauthorized face recognition systems while remaining compatible with generative face editing, addressing that current editing tools preserve identity features still trackable by malicious FR. It uses diffusion models for personalized portrait protection. Relevant to privacy in generative editing.

entry.title: HLS-GPT: A Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT) for Continental-Scale NASA Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) Reflectance Reconstruction Across All Bands on Arbitrary Dates

author.name: Junjie Li, Hankui K. Zhang, David P. Roy

entry.summary: HLS-GPT is a large generative pretrained Transformer reconstructing NASA Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel-2 surface reflectance across all bands, any date, and any pixel, trained on nine years of continental-scale time series. It overcomes spectral coverage and geographic scalability limits of prior methods.

entry.title: EgoCS-400K: An Egocentric Gameplay Dataset for World Models

author.name: Rongjin Guo, Dong Liang, Yuhao Liu, Fang Liu, Tianyu Huang, Gerhard P. Hancke, Rynson W. H. Lau

entry.summary: EgoCS-400K is a large-scale replay-grounded egocentric Counter-Strike dataset providing temporally aligned video-action-language trajectories for training world models. It addresses the scarcity of executable action and state supervision in existing video datasets.

entry.title: ERQA-Plus: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Reasoning in Embodied AI

author.name: Hong Yang, Basura Fernando

entry.summary: ERQA-Plus is a diagnostic benchmark of 1,766 QA instances over 711 robot-centric images, organized by a reasoning taxonomy to isolate grounded embodied reasoning from shortcut pattern matching. It enables controlled evaluation of spatial, action, and commonsense reasoning in embodied AI.

entry.title: LAGO Policy: Latency-Aware Asynchronous Diffusion Policies with Goal-Directed Collision-Free Planning for Smooth Manipulation

author.name: Guowei Shi, Xupeng Xie, Yiming Luo, Jian Guo, Jun Ma, Boyu Zhou

entry.summary: LAGO Policy is a latency-aware asynchronous diffusion-policy framework that improves inter-chunk consistency via classifier-free guidance on future actions and enables goal-directed collision-free planning by predicting interaction goals from demonstrations. It addresses jerky motions and collisions in asynchronous diffusion-policy deployment.

entry.title: Anytime-valid Optimal Policy Identification

author.name: Daniel Molitor

entry.summary: This paper develops an anytime-valid framework for optimal policy identification from logged contextual bandit data, constructing a time-indexed set that retains the true optimal policy uniformly over time with high probability. It enables continuous monitoring and early stopping without fixed sample sizes.

entry.title: Proximal Mediation Analysis with Hidden Recanting Witnesses

author.name: Sihan Wu, Yang Bai, Yifan Cui

entry.summary: This work uses proximal causal inference to develop three identification strategies for path-specific mediation effects when recanting witnesses (treatment-induced confounders) are unobserved, plus a semiparametric inference framework. It relaxes the stringent assumption that such confounders are absent or fully known.

entry.title: A Test Suite for Concepts

author.name: Gretta Duleba

entry.summary: Argues for a test suite of concrete, varied example concepts to ground the mathematical study of natural latents and natural abstractions, criticizing existing literature for hand-waving in tying math to examples. Proposes a typology distinguishing abstract from physics-grounded concepts.

entry.title: When Multiple Scripts Matter: Evaluating ASR in Clinical Settings

author.name: Jean Seo, Minkyu Kim, Jeonguk Lee, Jisoo Jung, Wooseok Han, Eunho Yang

entry.summary: Introduces MultiClin, a clinical ASR benchmark designed to evaluate robustness to multiscript orthographic variability in non-English settings, showing that conventional string-matching metrics underestimate performance. Also investigates training-time script consistency effects.

entry.title: Plug-and-Adapt: Multimodal Coreference Resolution at First Sight with a Pretrained Alignment Model

author.name: Jinghan Wu, Jing Li, Ivor W. Tsang, Xuetao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a plug-and-adapt method that adapts a pre-trained alignment model for immediate use in multimodal coreference resolution without target-dataset training, enabling zero-shot deployment. Avoids reliance on inaccessible large vision-language models.

entry.title: When Dynamics Models Read the Wrong Time Steps: Label-Free Event Credit Re-Anchoring for Robust Global Readouts

author.name: Yifan Wang

entry.summary: This work identifies temporal credit dilution, where learned dynamics models read from smooth correlates rather than the brief physical events that determine global targets. It introduces Credit-in-Event, a label-free probe for measuring and correcting where readouts assign functional credit.

entry.title: VISTA: Scale-Aware Visual Navigation via Action History Conditioning

author.name: Maeva Guerrier, Koki Kobayashi, Simon Roy, Jana Pavlasek, Giovanni Beltrame

entry.summary: VISTA addresses a deployment vulnerability in vision navigation foundation models that predict normalized actions, where scaling factors distort physical geometry. It conditions the model on normalized action histories to provide context on prediction-displacement relationships.

entry.title: A Bayesian Boolean Matrix Factorization with Application to Copy Number Analysis in Cancer

author.name: Adolphus Wagala, Mehmet Samur, Giovanni Parmigiani

entry.summary: Bayesian Boolean Matrix Factorization (BBMF) is a fully conjugate generative model with sparsity for decomposing binary matrices into interpretable logical patterns, applied to cancer copy number analysis. It supports principled model selection and uncertainty quantification unlike heuristic methods.

entry.title: From Argument Components to Graphs: A Multi-Agent Debate with Confidence Gating for Argument Relations

author.name: Jakub B\k{a}ba, Jaros{\l}aw A. Chudziak

entry.summary: This work proposes a training-free multi-agent debate framework with confidence gating for argument relation classification, extending a Proponent-Opponent-Judge architecture to address contextual analysis weaknesses without expensive fine-tuning. It targets argument mining tasks where two text parts must be jointly analyzed.

entry.title: Lect\=uraAgents: A Multi-Agent Framework for Adaptive Personalized AI-Assisted Learning and Embodied Teaching

author.name: Jaward Sesay, Yue Yu, Siwei Dong, Yemin Shi, Guangyao Chen, B\"orje F. Karlsson

entry.summary: LecturaAgents is a multi-agent framework for personalized AI-assisted learning that mirrors a professor-student relationship, with a ProfessorAgent leading specialized subordinate agents through research and adaptive embodied teaching. It targets multimodal, learner-tailored instruction beyond lecture content automation.

entry.title: The BD-LSC Dataset: Facilitating the Benchmarking of Models for Lexical Semantic Change Detection in Slang and Standard Usage

author.name: Afnan Aloraini, Viktor Schlegel, Goran Nenadic, Riza Batista-Navarro

entry.summary: BD-LSC introduces benchmark datasets for bi-directional lexical semantic change capturing sense gain, sense loss, and stability across time periods, with a complementary SlangTrack dataset for words with both slang and standard meanings. It addresses gaps in modeling complex semantic trajectories.

entry.title: Data-Driven Decoding of Russell's Circumplex Model of Affect

author.name: Amdjed Belaref, Samir Sadok, Zineb Noumir, Renaud Seguier

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether Transformer text and speech embeddings recover the geometric regularities of Russell's circumplex model of affect, unifying experiments with RoBERTa, wav2vec 2.0, and a multimodal fusion architecture. It tests whether latent spaces encode valence-arousal topology and human-like neighborhood relations.

entry.title: Understanding Scam Trends and Rail Paths from Reddit Self-Disclosure Narratives

author.name: Yangjun Zhang, Mirko Bottarelli, Mark Hooper, Carsten Maple

entry.summary: This work builds a dataset of 21,304 Reddit self-disclosure scam narratives from 2023 to 2025 to analyze yearly trends in scam characteristics and rail paths across identity, communication, platform, and payment dimensions. It tracks temporally ordered scam lifecycles rather than isolated signals.

entry.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Continuous Edge Inference for Fine-Grained Roadside Perception

author.name: Aditya Mishra, Haroon Lone

entry.summary: Edge-TSR is a deployment-oriented continuous edge inference system for sustained roadside perception on Jetson Orin Nano, integrating detection, tracking, fine-grained classification, and lightweight track-aware temporal stabilization, with the central finding that benchmark-centric evaluation systematically overstates deployed performance due to thermal throttling and temporal instability. It surfaces real deployment effects. Useful for edge AI practitioners.

entry.title: Test-Time Training for Robust Text-Guided Open-Vocabulary Object Counting

author.name: Hao-Yuan Ma, Yuda Zou, Li Zhang, Yongchao Xu

entry.summary: This work introduces Robust-TOOC, the first benchmark for evaluating text-guided open-vocabulary object counting under six corruption types (rain, fog, darkness, Gaussian noise, salt-and-pepper, mixed), and proposes test-time training to improve robustness since existing methods are developed on ideal images. It bridges the gap to real-world adverse conditions. Useful for robust counting.

entry.title: Blended Chart Surfaces: A Seamless Explicit Representation for Smooth Surface Fitting

author.name: Romy Williamson, Niloy Mitra

entry.summary: Blended Chart Surfaces introduces a compact, network-free explicit surface representation that is smooth by construction, blending local charts to avoid seam artifacts while supporting differentiable optimization. It targets geometry processing needs for smooth surface fitting.

entry.title: RICH-SLAM: Radar SLAM with Incremental and Continuous Hilbert Mapping

author.name: Bingbing Zhang, Huan Yin, Yang Xu, Shuo Liu, Shaojie Shen, Fumin Zhang, Wen Xu

entry.summary: RICH-SLAM is a radar SLAM framework using a Rao-Blackwellized particle filter backend and an incremental Hilbert-space reduced-rank Gaussian process mapping strategy for continuous, uncertainty-aware dense maps from sparse noisy radar. It targets robustness to adverse weather and lighting.

entry.title: A Hybrid Optimization Framework for Grasp Synthesis under Partial Observations

author.name: Wenzheng Zhang, Fahira Afzal Maken, Tin Lai, Fabio Ramos

entry.summary: This hybrid grasp synthesis framework combines a learned energy-based model prior with analytical ICP refinement via Stein variational gradient descent to generate robust grasps from partial point clouds. It outperforms AnyGrasp and GPD on 67 objects across 5,360 grasp attempts.

entry.title: On Response-Adaptive Targeting Strategies for Multi-Treatment Experiments

author.name: Redouane Yagouti, R\'emy Degenne, Emilie Kaufmann

entry.summary: This paper introduces alpha-Rebalancing Targeting Strategies, a unified response-adaptive randomization framework for multi-treatment (K>=2) experiments generalizing the two-armed ERADE strategy, and proves shared asymptotic properties. It unifies a previously fragmented theory for multi-arm adaptive clinical trials.

entry.title: When Rules Learn: A Self-Evolving Agent for Legal Case Retrieval

author.name: Mingxu Tao, Jiawei Hu, Xian Zhou, Wenpeng Hu, Jiajun Cheng, Yunbo Cao, Zhunchen Luo, Guotong Geng

entry.summary: Introduces a self-evolving framework where an LLM agent iteratively learns query-rewriting rules to enhance BM25 for Chinese legal case retrieval without parameter training. Demonstrates that rule-driven query rewriting can boost a strong lexical baseline.

entry.title: Brick-DICL: Dynamic In-Context Learning for Automated Brick Schema Classification

author.name: Yiyue Qian, Shinan Zhang, Huan Song, Negin Sokhandan, Hannah Marlowe, Diego Socolinsky

entry.summary: Proposes Brick-DICL, a two-stage dynamic in-context learning framework for mapping building management system points to the Brick schema's 936 classes. Addresses class count, limited LLM domain knowledge, and verification effort in building automation.

entry.title: Surveying GenAI-based Automation in Printed Circuit Board Design and Test

author.name: Sahana Srinivasan, Benjamin Turnbull, Hammond Pearce

entry.summary: Surveys generative AI applications across the entire printed circuit board design lifecycle, from supply chains and specification through layout, validation, test, and assembly. Presents a taxonomy distinguishing PCB automation from the more common integrated-circuit design focus.

entry.title: Comprehensive pKa Data Augmentation from Limited Real Data through an Engineered Models-Quantum Framework

author.name: Wang Rui, Liu Dinghao

entry.summary: Performs large-scale regression-based pKa prediction on unlabeled molecular datasets using optimized machine-learning models combined with quantum energy calculations, aiming to augment scarce high-quality experimental pKa data from the iBonD database. Addresses the fundamental constraint on rapid pKa data growth.

entry.title: AI Adoption Across a Multinational Workforce: Sociotechnical Conditions for GenAI Acceptance in Human Resources

author.name: Dalia Ali, Maria Jos\'e Rodr\'iguez Vel\'azquez, Manoel Horta Ribeiro, Vera Liao, Orestis Papakyriakopoulos

entry.summary: Studies GenAI adoption in a multinational company's transition to a GenAI-supported HR search system, using search logs, surveys, and interviews. Finds adoption depends on fit between system assumptions and employees' work positionalities like role, language, and tenure.

entry.title: Trustworthy Self-Composable Big-Data-as-a-Service: An LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Data Engineering, AutoML, MLOps Deployment, and Drift-Aware Lifecycle Optimization

author.name: Aueaphum Aueawatthanaphisut, Badri Raj Lamichhane

entry.summary: Provides a quantitative analysis of cross-modal relationships among tau-PET, structural MRI, cognitive scores, and APOE4 data in Alzheimer's research using 789 ADNI subjects, quantifying mutual information and explained variance. Aims to identify redundant assessments and reduce patient burden.

entry.title: Generalization Guarantees for Multi-Input Neural Operator Learning in Sobolev Spaces

author.name: Yahong Yang, Zecheng Zhang, Wei Zhu, Wenjing Liao, Hao Liu

entry.summary: This paper derives approximation and generalization error bounds for multi-input neural operators with outputs measured in Sobolev norms. It extends operator learning theory to handle multiple input functions on different domains with varied regularities.

entry.title: Operator Boosting Produces Pareto-Efficient PDE Surrogates

author.name: Lennon J. Shikhman

entry.summary: Operator Boosting is a stagewise residual-learning framework that builds compact neural operator surrogates for PDEs directly, rather than training large models and compressing them. It trains a sequence of tiny operators on residuals with validation-selected shrinkage.

entry.title: Another Look at Log-PCA for Probability Measures: A Dynamical Formulation and Statistical Convergence

author.name: Peng Xu, Changbo Zhu, Young-Heon Kim, Xiaohui Chen

entry.summary: This paper provides a dynamical formulation of log-PCA for probability measures under Wasserstein geometry, termed Wasserstein Tangential PCA. It derives statistical convergence rates for the empirical estimator using parallel transport structure.

entry.title: OmniPlan: An Adaptive Framework for Timely and Near-Optimal Network Planning Optimization

author.name: Longlong Zhu, Jiashuo Yu, Zedi Chen, Yuhan Wu, Zhifan Jiang, Yuchen Xian, Yimeng Liu, Jiajie Su, Shaopeng Zhou, Xingyuan Li, Hongyan Liu, Xuan Liu, Dong Zhang, Chunming Wu, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: Presents OmniPlan, an adaptive framework for network planning optimization that balances execution time and near-optimality across diverse user intents, applicable to transportation, communication, and power-grid domains. It aims to overcome the time-optimality tradeoff in existing MIP/DRL approaches.

entry.title: When Cognitive Graphs Meet LLMs: BDEI Cognitive Pathways for Panic Emotional Arousal Prediction

author.name: Mengzhu Liu, Long Qin, Chuan Ai, Zhengqiu Zhu, Hongru Liang, Chen Gao, Yong Li, Xin Lu, Quanjun Yin

entry.summary: Combines cognitive graphs with LLMs grounded in appraisal emotion theory to predict the timing of individual panic emotional arousal before it manifests, introducing a BDEI cognitive-pathway model with an explicit emotion node. It targets proactive emergency intervention.

entry.title: ROMPAR: Morphological Completion and Demographic Unlearning for Romanian-Accented Speech Recognition

author.name: Andrei-Marius Avram, Aureliu-Valentin Antonie, \c{S}tefan-Bogdan Badea, Andrei Florea, Robert-Nicolae Zaharoiu, Dumitru-Clementin Cercel

entry.summary: ROMPAR introduces a 17.8-hour Romanian and Moldavian parliamentary speech corpus with double annotation and reconstructed word-fragment labels, plus a multi-task adversarial training framework enforcing demographic invariance across age, gender, and dialect. It addresses bias and dialectal variation in ASR.

entry.title: Creative Collision: Directorial Persona Steering and Competition in Large Language Models

author.name: Subramanyam Sahoo, Justin Shenk

entry.summary: Creative Collision studies activation steering when two semantically opposing persona vectors (Spielberg vs. Scorsese) are superimposed and interpolated, examining moral valence and other creative axes. It explores a richer multi-direction steering regime beyond single-vector injection.

entry.title: Islamic Large Language Models: From Knowledge Acquisition to Trustworthy and Hallucination-Resistant AI

author.name: Mohammed Amine Mouhoub

entry.summary: This survey reviews the emerging field of Islamic LLMs and trustworthy Islamic AI, organizing literature around Arabic NLP, Qur'anic QA, Islamic knowledge benchmarks, RAG, and legal reasoning with attention to citation exactness and jurisprudential disagreement. It highlights the demanding requirements of grounded religious and legal QA.

entry.title: LLM-based Visual Code Completion for Aerospace Geometric Design

author.name: Hau Kit Yong, Robert Marsh, Edmar A. Silva, Andr\'as S\'obester, Stuart E. Middleton

entry.summary: This paper presents an LLM-based visual programming copilot for aerospace geometric design using a visual ReAct variant and GPT-5.4, plus Wingbuilder, a Grasshopper plugin with aerospace-specific geometry components. It addresses the lack of LLM design copilots in the safety-prioritizing aerospace industry.

entry.title: Rhythm of the Deep: A Computational-Linguistic Test of Duality of Patterning in Sperm Whale Codas

author.name: Mudit Sinha, Sanika Chavan

entry.summary: This paper applies computational-linguistic structure discovery to 1,483 sperm whale codas to test for duality of patterning, treating it as structure discovery from continuous audio rather than a direct language claim. Using frozen audio encoders and rigorous statistical nulls, it finds support for a narrow two-tier architecture. An interesting interdisciplinary application of ML to animal communication.

entry.title: Measuring Whether LLM Tutors Teach or Solve: A Diagnostic for Educational Impact

author.name: Junyi Yao, Zihao Zheng, Baichuan Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes a lightweight diagnostic measuring the gap between solving-oriented and pedagogy-oriented benchmark performance to assess whether LLM tutors actually teach rather than just solve. Using MathTutorBench leaderboard results, it shows the two dimensions are only partially aligned (correlation 0.421). Relevant for evaluating educational LLM impact.

entry.title: Symbolic Informalization: Fluent, Productive, Multilingual

author.name: Aarne Ranta

entry.summary: Symbolic informalization aims to reliably convert formal mathematics to fluent natural language without loss of precision, generalizing syntactic sugar into ordinary mathematical language and explaining AI-constructed proofs across multiple formal and natural languages via the Informath project. It targets human-readable machine-checked content. Relevant to autoformalization and proof assistants.

entry.title: RT-Counter: Real-Time Text-Guided Open-Vocabulary Object Counting

author.name: Hao-Yuan Ma, Li Zhang, Zhiwei Zhu, Jie Gao

entry.summary: RT-Counter is a real-time text-guided open-vocabulary object counting framework featuring a Visual Prototype Textualization module that projects visual features into text space, achieving both good counting accuracy and high computational efficiency. It addresses fine-grained spatial understanding and real-time requirements that vision-language models struggle with. Relevant for efficient open-vocabulary counting.

entry.title: BrainWorld: A Structural-Prior-Conditioned Generative Model for Whole-Brain 4D fMRI Dynamics

author.name: Junfeng Xia, Wenhao Ye, Junxiang Zhang, Xuanye Pan, Mo Wang, Quanying Liu

entry.summary: BrainWorld is a structural-prior-conditioned generative model for whole-brain 4D fMRI dynamics, using sMRI anatomical context to guide future fMRI generation. Evaluated across 22 datasets, it generates stable trajectories up to 400 frames and improves downstream tasks.

entry.title: PhaseWin: An Efficient Search Algorithm for Faithful Visual Attribution

author.name: Zihan Gu, Ruoyu Chen, Junchi Zhang, Li Liu, Xiaochun Cao, Hua Zhang

entry.summary: PhaseWin proposes an efficient search algorithm for faithful visual attribution, casting attribution as an ordered subset-search problem and reducing the quadratic cost of greedy search. It improves interpretability auditing of vision and vision-language models.

entry.title: Continual Online Personalization of Exoskeleton Control via Manifold-Aware Experience Replay

author.name: Changseob Song, Inseung Kang

entry.summary: This work develops a manifold-aware experience replay framework for continual online personalization of exoskeleton control, preserving user-specific representations across tasks to avoid catastrophic forgetting during real-time adaptation. It targets clinical users with gait disabilities.

entry.title: WireCraft: A Simulation Benchmark for Industrial DLO Manipulation

author.name: Chongyu Zhu, Ramy ElMallah, Hyegang Kim, Zachary Tang, Jiachen Rao, Artem Arutyunov, Seungyeon Ha, Chi-Guhn Lee

entry.summary: WireCraft is a simulation benchmark for industrial deformable linear object (wire/cable) manipulation, offering modular customizable task assets with fixtures relevant to real-world wire assembly and aligning simulation, real data, and shared evaluation protocols. It addresses the lack of standardized DLO manipulation benchmarks.

entry.title: Kernel-Based Functional Balancing for Causal Inference with Compositional Treatments

author.name: Sungbum Kim, Jiayi Wang

entry.summary: This work develops a kernel-based functional balancing approach for causal effect estimation with compositional treatments on a simplex, constructing weights by minimizing worst-case RKHS balancing error and building an augmented weighted estimator. It addresses estimands defined over compositions rather than scalar treatments.

entry.title: Two Classical Answers to "What do Two Variables Share?"

author.name: Haru

entry.summary: First post in a series connecting classical information theory results to John Wentworth's natural latents framework, examining what two random variables share. It aims to provide exact theoretical results underpinning natural abstraction theory.

entry.title: MoCo-AIS: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Similarity Computation of Vessel Trajectories

author.name: Ruixin Song, Md Mahbub Alam, Zahra Sadeghi, Amilcar Soares, Jos\'e F. Rodrigues-Jr, Gabriel Spadon

entry.summary: Presents MoCo-AIS, a unified momentum-contrast self-supervised framework for computing vessel trajectory similarity from AIS data, avoiding reliance on labels from traditional distance measures. Aims for consistent, generalizable trajectory representations.

entry.title: Continuous-time Optimal Stopping through Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Cosmin Borsa, Michael Ludkovski

entry.summary: CARLOS is a reinforcement-learning algorithm for continuous-time optimal stopping that learns exercise rules at arbitrarily fine time resolution using an aggregate deep network. It addresses discretization errors in classical dynamic programming solvers.

entry.title: Blind Recovery of Latent Domains via Unsupervised Symmetry Discovery

author.name: Onur Efe, Arkadas Ozakin

entry.summary: This work proposes an unsupervised framework for recovering latent domains and signals in blind inverse problems by discovering symmetries of the data distribution. It uses group-convolutional networks with stationarity and locality regularization.

entry.title: Tight $L_\infty$ Sample Complexity for Low-Degree and Sparse Boolean Polynomials

author.name: Jasper van Doornmalen, Mathieu Molina, Victor Verdugo, Jos\'e Verschae

entry.summary: This paper characterizes minimax sample complexity for learning bounded Boolean polynomials under L-infinity error guarantees rather than L2. It derives tight rates for low-degree and sparse Fourier-Walsh polynomials under subgaussian noise.

entry.title: Beyond IGO-Flow: Toward Convergence Analysis of IGO in Continuous Spaces

author.name: Ryosuke Kimura, Youhei Akimoto

entry.summary: This paper studies discrete-time Information-Geometric Optimization in continuous spaces with non-infinitesimal learning rates, analyzing IGO over multivariate Gaussian families on strongly convex quadratics. It advances convergence theory beyond continuous-time IGO flow idealizations.

entry.title: Domain-Validity-Gated Metamorphic Testing of Scientific ML Surrogates

author.name: Meng Li, Xiaohua Yang, Jie Liu, Shiyu Yan

entry.summary: This work proposes a domain-validity-gated metamorphic testing framework for scientific ML surrogates, addressing the oracle problem by screening candidate metamorphic relations for validity. It introduces a domain-validity rubric and executable MR-cards as oracle-free test assets.

entry.title: INI-VPINN: A Variational Physics-Informed Neural Network with Implicit Neumann and Interface Handling for Multi-Material Domains with Geometric Singularities

author.name: Shayan Dodge (DESTeC, University of Pisa, Pisa, Italy), Alessandro Formisano (Department of Engineering, University of Campania Luigi Vanvitelli, Aversa, Italy), Sami Barmada (DESTeC, University of Pisa, Pisa, Italy)

entry.summary: INI-VPINN is a weak-form physics-informed neural network that naturally incorporates Neumann boundary and interface conditions into its variational formulation without extra loss terms or subdomain networks. It uses compact support weighting functions for multi-material domains with geometric singularities.

entry.title: Bridging the Usability Gap: Lessons from Interpreting Studies for Machine Interpreting Design

author.name: Claudio Fantinuoli

entry.summary: This position paper argues that machine interpreting should be treated as a distinct subfield of speech translation requiring evaluation grounded in communicative effectiveness rather than textual fidelity, coining the term accuracy illusion. It draws on interpreting studies to identify usability dimensions missing from current benchmarks.

entry.title: LiFT: Local Search via Linear Programming for Overfitting-Controlled Transformers

author.name: Abhishek Shukla, Anikeit Khanna, Ankur Sinha, Faiz Hamid

entry.summary: LiFT proposes a linear-programming-based local search framework for fine-tuning pretrained transformers with explicit overfitting control, formulating it as bilevel optimization that jointly updates parameters and regularization hyperparameters using validation gradients and training Hessian information. It builds validation-aware descent directions. A novel optimization angle on fine-tuning.

entry.title: GASE: Gaussian Splatting-Based Automated System for Reconstructing Embodied-Simulation Environments

author.name: Jiawei Zhang, Yiming Yan, Chao Liang, Nuo Xu, Seson Sun, Qichen Zhang, Yuhao Xu, Yantai Yang, Yingqiao Wang, Qin Jin, Zhipeng Zhang

entry.summary: GASE is a highly automated Gaussian-Splatting-based system for reconstructing embodied-simulation environments from panoramic multi-view video, improving data acquisition speed and foreground object extraction. It targets low sim-to-real gap scene construction for robot learning.

entry.title: Abstention-Aware Personalized Object Rearrangement via Uncertainty-Guided LLM Assistance

author.name: Sam Collin, Ali Ayub

entry.summary: APOLLO is an abstention-aware personalized object rearrangement framework combining a lightweight personalized embedding model with selective LLM assistance, deciding not only where to place objects but when to abstain. It targets realistic cluttered settings with partial errors.

entry.title: Bayesian Poisson-Randomized Gamma Tensor Factorization with Application to International Trade Flows

author.name: Jie Jian, Aaron Schein

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Bayesian hierarchical tensor factorization with low-rank CP structure on a latent Poisson rate tensor coupled with a conditional Gamma model for positive outcomes, handling sparse semi-continuous data with excess zeros and heavy tails. It is applied to international trade flows.

entry.title: Martingale Doppelg\"anger-Eval: An Identification Framework for Auditing Candlestick Understanding in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ziyao Wang

entry.summary: Martingale Doppelganger-Eval is a benchmark for auditing whether vision-language models genuinely use candlestick chart evidence versus extrapolating trends, proving that observational scores cannot distinguish grounded from trend-shortcut responders under strong coupling and that interventions can. It provides an identification framework via matched evidence interventions.

entry.title: Extracting Semantics: LLM-Guided Automatic Population of Robot Ontology from URDF

author.name: Bastien Dussard (LAAS-RIS, LAAS), Guillaume Sarthou (LAAS-RIS, LAAS)

entry.summary: Presents a preliminary approach for automatically generating robot semantic ontologies by transforming URDF robot description files into populated ontologies, using LLMs to commonsense-interpret identifiers. Aims to reduce the manual bottleneck in cognitive robotics knowledge construction.

entry.title: ED3R: Energy-Aware Distributed Disaster Detection Enabled by Cooperative Robotic Agents

author.name: Lina Magoula, Nikolaos Koursioumpas, Nancy Alonistioti, Ramin Khalili

entry.summary: Presents an energy-aware distributed framework for wildfire detection using cooperative decision-making between robots and a remote controller under uncertainty and resource constraints. It balances detection confidence with energy and time costs.

entry.title: Talking to Your Data: Exploring Embodied Conversation as an Interface for Personal Health Reflection

author.name: Nikola Kovacevic, Bastien Husler, Di Zhuang, Rafael Wampfler, Barbara Solenthaler

entry.summary: Explores an embodied conversational agent as an alternative to dashboards for reflecting on personal wearable health data, using a dual-agent design that extracts statistics and communicates them while avoiding clinical advice. Aimed at supporting objective self-reflection.

entry.title: High-Fidelity 3D Geometric Reconstruction of Pelvic Organs from MRI: A Hybrid Deep Learning and Iterative Optimization Approach

author.name: Hui Wang, Xiaowei Li, Chenxin Zhang, Yifan Feng, Jianwei Zuo, Yumeng Tang, Xiuli Sun, Jianliu Wang, Bing Xie, Jiajia Luo

entry.summary: Introduces a hybrid deformable shape modeling framework combining deep learning prediction with iterative optimization to reconstruct high-fidelity 3D geometry of bladder, uterus, and rectum from MRI. Aims at standardized patient-specific pelvic floor modeling.

entry.title: ReRAM-aware Model Finetuning addressing I-V Non-linearity and Retention Errors

author.name: Ching-Yi Lin, Shamik Kundu, Arnab Raha, Sahil Shah

entry.summary: This work proposes a finetuning-based hardware-aware training algorithm for deploying neural networks on ReRAM in-memory computing crossbars. It mitigates I-V non-linearity via a sinh transformation and incorporates retention errors as a regularization loss.

entry.title: Reducing Learner Redundancy in Boosting via Residual Orthogonalization

author.name: Ye Su, Jipeng Guo, Yong Liu, Xin Xu, Gangchun Zhang, Jinxin Chen, Di Wu, Longlong Zhao

entry.summary: SCBoost shifts boosting from residual fitting to residual orthogonalization, projecting residuals onto the orthogonal complement of historical predictions to reduce learner redundancy. It pairs this with covariance-regularized ensemble weighting.

entry.title: ConTex: Reformulating Counterfactual Generation For Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Jan Voets, Hasan Tercan, Tobias Meisen, Sebastian Baum

entry.summary: ConTex reformulates counterfactual generation for time-series forecasting to provide actionable insights on how inputs must change to reach desired outcomes. It moves beyond costly instance-wise optimization toward a more consistent and real-time approach.

entry.title: Theoretical Grounding of Out-Of-Distribution Detection With Reinforcement Learning Optimizer

author.name: Salimeh Sekeh, Xin Zhang

entry.summary: This work establishes theoretical grounding for dynamic OOD detection using a reinforcement learning-guided optimizer that explicitly favors updates reducing semantic OOD false positives over time. It adds an RL correction term on top of standard gradient descent.

entry.title: Koshur Diacritizer: A Byte-Level Sequence-to-Sequence Model for Kashmiri Diacritic Restoration

author.name: Haq Nawaz Malik, Nahfid Nissar, Faizan Iqbal

entry.summary: Presents Koshur Diacritizer, a ByT5-small byte-level sequence-to-sequence model for restoring diacritics in Kashmiri Perso-Arabic text, releasing a 23.7k aligned undiacritized-diacritized sentence-pair dataset with script-aware normalization and skeleton-preserving inference. It achieves a diacritic error rate of about 0.20.

entry.title: PaperJury: Due-Process Review for Bounded LaTeX Revision

author.name: Yiran Wang, Ruixuan An, Biao Wu, Wenhao Wang

entry.summary: PaperJury is a closed-loop review-revise-verify system for pre-submission hardening of LaTeX papers, using a deterministic-versus-semantic split where deterministic orchestration manages decomposition, claim tracking, and patch application while semantic components handle critique. It supports adversarial whole-paper review with explicit no-fix outcomes.

entry.title: Neural Tree Reconstruction for the Open Forest Observatory

author.name: Marissa Ramirez de Chanlatte, Arjun Rewari, Trevor Darrell, Derek J. N. Young

entry.summary: This work from the Open Forest Observatory introduces neural tree reconstruction to replace classical structure-from-motion for 3D forest mapping from drone imagery, improving detail and reducing artifacts. It supports climate applications like reforestation, wildfire reduction, and carbon monitoring.

entry.title: Directing Open-Ended Evolution in Artificial Life via Multi-Scale Path Divergence

author.name: Mikhail Akhtyrchenko, Mikhail I. Katsnelson, Andrey Ustyuzhanin

entry.summary: This work introduces MSPD, a renormalization-group-inspired scalar quantifying multiscale temporal organization in artificial-life systems, serving both as a gradient-free fitness function and a post-hoc analytical lens. It aims to connect open-ended evolution to physical complexity theory rather than black-box metrics.

entry.title: FLAP: FOV-Constrained Active Perception Planning for Prior-Map-Free 3D Navigation

author.name: Mengke Zhang, Sitong Li, Tiancheng Lai, Ruitian Pang, Mingxuan Zhang, Qingcheng Chen, Fei Gao, Chao Xu, Yanjun Cao

entry.summary: FLAP is a FOV-constrained active perception planning framework that integrates perception constraints directly into trajectory optimization for prior-map-free 3D UAV navigation. It improves safety while preserving efficiency without conservative heuristics.

entry.title: Beyond Failure Recovery: An Engagement-Aware Human-in-the-loop Framework for Robotic Systems

author.name: Jiaying Fang, Joyce Yang, Zhanxin Wu, Bohan Yang, Tapomayukh Bhattacharjee

entry.summary: This work proposes an engagement-aware human-in-the-loop framework that keeps users involved in decision-making rather than only intervening on failures, especially for physical caregiving where mobility limitations reduce in-the-moment intervention. It reframes human involvement around engagement instead of failure recovery.

entry.title: Simpler User Interfaces in an AI Future

author.name: Adam Chlipala

entry.summary: Argues that as the economy shifts toward AI agents interacting directly with each other, user interfaces—historically hard to formally verify due to human modeling—may become far more amenable to formal specification and verification. Suggests cybersecurity benefits follow from such verification.

entry.title: Learn to Quantify Social Interaction with Constraints for Pedestrian Walking

author.name: Xiaodan Shi

entry.summary: Proposes Learn to Cluster, a probabilistic method to quantify and interpret the types of social interactions among pedestrians for long-term path forecasting in crowds. Aims to reveal which interactions occur and how they affect pedestrian decision-making.

entry.title: Confusion-Aware Transfer Teacher Curriculum Learning Framework: Disentangling Scoring and Pacing Effects

author.name: Savini Kommalage, Sanka Mohottala, Asiri Gawesha, Dulara Madhusanka, Menan Velayuthan, Dharshana Kasthurirathna, Mahima Milinda Alwis Weerasinghe, Charith Abhayaratne

entry.summary: Disentangles the two coupled components of curriculum learning, difficulty scoring and pacing, using dedicated evaluation protocols and a confusion-aware difficulty score. Demonstrated on CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18 and VGG-16.

entry.title: Perceptual compensation for tonal context in self-supervised speech models

author.name: James Kirby, Ioana Krehan, Michele Gubian

entry.summary: Examines whether wav2vec2.0 exhibits perceptual compensation for tonal context, replicating a Mandarin tone experiment and comparing pre-trained versus ASR-fine-tuned models. Finds little compensation in pre-trained embeddings and only partial evidence in probing classifiers.

entry.title: KANLib -- An Modular, Extensible and Fast Kolmogorov-Arnold Network Implementation

author.name: Julian Hoever, Gregor Schiele

entry.summary: Introduces KANLib, a modular and efficient framework unifying PyKAN, EfficientKAN, and FastKAN implementations for developing and benchmarking Kolmogorov-Arnold Network architectures. Addresses computational cost and inconsistent feature support across existing frameworks.

entry.title: MM++: Unsupervised Scale-Invariant Multilayer OOD Detection via Top-K Gated Feature Fusion

author.name: Rahim Hossain, Md Tawheedul Islam Bhuian, Md Farhan Shadiq, Kyoung-Don Kang

entry.summary: MM++ is an unsupervised, post-hoc framework for out-of-distribution detection that fuses discriminative intermediate layers using entropy-based selection and a regularized covariance estimate. It aims for scale invariance and hierarchical expressivity without requiring auxiliary OOD data.

entry.title: QueryMarket: Cost-Aware Online Active Learning in Data Markets

author.name: Xiwen Huang, Pierre Pinson

entry.summary: QueryMarket is a market-inspired framework for cost-aware online active learning that unifies pricing, information gain, and rolling budget constraints under concept drift. Its OVBAL method selects samples via a D-optimality criterion with exponential forgetting.

entry.title: Geometrical fairness in graph neural networks

author.name: Arturo P\'erez-Peralta, Sandra Ben\'itez-Pe\~na, Blas Kolic, Rosa E. Lillo

entry.summary: This work introduces a fairness-aware adaptation of graph-based diffusion methods by modifying the underlying Laplacian operator with subspace projections and spectral adjustments. It aims to prevent graph neural networks from propagating or amplifying data biases.

entry.title: Entity Labels Are Not Entity Signals: A Framework for Observable Relevance in Document Re-Ranking

author.name: Utshab Kumar Ghosh, Shubham Chatterjee
