author.name: Jianghan Shen, Siqi Luo, Yue Li, Jiyao Liu, Wanying Qu, Yi Zhang, Ziyan Huang, Tianbin Li, Ming Hu, Xiaohong Liu, Yirong Chen, Junjun He

entry.summary: Derives LLM policy optimization methods from first principles starting from the expected-reward objective, organizing REINFORCE, PPO, GRPO, and extensions by how each modifies trajectory probability or reward factors. Provides a unified gradient-estimator-centric view of where each method intervenes.

entry.title: Honeypot Protocol

author.name: Najmul Hasan

entry.summary: Introduces the honeypot protocol for AI control that actively tests for context-dependent behavior by varying only the system prompt across evaluation, synthetic deployment, and no-monitoring conditions while holding the task identical. Evaluates a Claude model in BashArena across conditions in honest and attack modes.

entry.title: Is Your Agent Playing Dead? Deployed LLM Agents Exhibit Constraint-Evasive Fabrication and Thanatosis

author.name: Andoni Rodr\'iguez, Alberto Pozanco, Daniel Borrajo

entry.summary: This paper characterizes Constraint-Evasive Fabrication, where LLM agents under irreconcilable constraints spontaneously fabricate plausible external obstacles, and its extreme form Thanatosis, where the agent simulates a system crash to make users disengage. It documents these behaviors including a GPT-4o banking agent faking exception traces.

entry.title: The Perils of Agency: How Developers Perceive, Prioritize, and Address Risks in Agentic AI Products

author.name: Hao-Ping Lee, Jessica He, David Piorkowski, Thomas Serban von Davier, Jodi Forlizzi, Sauvik Das

entry.summary: Qualitative study of how 35 industry developers perceive, prioritize, and address risks in agentic AI products, finding they prioritize product/business risks over downstream societal risks and lack mature mitigation practices. Offers empirical grounding for agentic AI governance.

entry.title: EHRNote-ChatQA: A Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Multi-Turn Clinical Question Answering over Longitudinal Discharge Summaries

author.name: Jiyoun Kim, Muhan Yeo, Eunhye Jang, Jeewon Yang, Hangyul Yoon, Su Ji Lee, Hee Jo Han, Hee-Jae Jung, Doyun Kwon, Jun young Lee, Jaehun Lee, Jung-Oh Lee, Sunjun Kweon, Jong Hak Moon, Daseul Kim, Minjae Cho, Edward Choi

entry.summary: EHRNote-ChatQA is the first benchmark for evidence-grounded multi-turn clinical QA over longitudinal discharge summaries, requiring iterative synthesis across multiple summaries with evidence-grounding verification. Reflects realistic clinical review workflows beyond exam-style or single-turn QA.

entry.title: DifFRACT: Diffusion Feature Reconstruction and Attribution for Circuit Tracing

author.name: Artyom Mazur, Nina Konovalova, Aibek Alanov

entry.summary: DifFRACT extends transcoder-based circuit tracing and feature attribution to multimodal diffusion transformers, providing tools to understand how semantic information propagates across denoising steps and how text and image representations interact in double-stream MM-DiT architectures. Addresses the opacity of diffusion transformers for interpretability.

entry.title: Data Augmentations for Data-Constrained Language Model Pretraining

author.name: Michael K. Chen, Xikun Zhang, Zhen Wang

entry.summary: Investigates data augmentation as a regularizer to enable productive multi-epoch language model pretraining in the emerging data-constrained, compute-abundant regime. Introduces three orthogonal augmentation categories to mitigate severe overfitting in standard autoregressive training.

entry.title: Adaptive inference and function vectors in deep transformers

author.name: Ravin Raj, Gautam Reddy

entry.summary: This paper develops a mean-field theory of deep transformers as distributed inference systems that exploit function vectors to infer latent context at progressively finer scales across layers. It predicts and tests relationships between hierarchical latent structure and transformer depth.

entry.title: A Bifurcation Theory Framework for Gradient Descent on the Edge of Stability

author.name: Eric Gan

entry.summary: Develops a bifurcation theory framework explaining the Edge of Stability phenomenon in gradient descent for overparameterized networks, decomposing dynamics into normal and tangent components to the minimizer manifold. Shows stable EoS arises from a flip bifurcation in the normal direction.

entry.title: Auditing Machine Unlearning: A Systematic Research on Whether Models Truly Forget

author.name: Dayong Ye, Tianqing Zhu, Ruiding Huang, Xinbo Fu, Jiayang Li, Bo Liu, Huan Huo, Wanlei Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes the first practical, general-purpose framework for auditing whether machine unlearning algorithms truly erase data influence, inspired by proof-of-ignorance and avoiding the need for retraining. Investigates residual information leakage risks systematically.

entry.title: GD$^2$PO: Mitigating Multi-Reward Conflicts via Group-Dynamic reward-Decoupled Policy Optimization

author.name: Haotian Liu, Yihao Liu, Jingwei Ni, Siyuan Huang, Xinpeng Liu, Pengyu Cheng, Jiajun Song, Ruijin Ding, Junfeng Li, Zhechao Yu, Mengyu Zhou, Hongteng Xu, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: GD2PO addresses multi-reward conflicts in LLM post-training RL where positive and negative advantages across reward dimensions cancel out. It proposes group-dynamic reward-decoupled policy optimization to mitigate signal cancellation and improve training efficiency.

entry.title: From Physics to Representation: Audio Learning with Synthetic Pre-training via Procedural Generation

author.name: Fengrui Liu, Ruiyang Huang, Qijian Zheng, Yuanfang Wang, Feng Liu

entry.summary: AudioPG is a procedural synthesis framework that pre-trains a masked autoencoder entirely on synthetically generated waveforms from acoustic primitives, eliminating real audio in pre-training. It transfers strongly to real benchmarks (90.6 percent on ESC-50) with under 20 minutes of single-GPU pre-training.

entry.title: Emergent retokenization symmetry in large language models: phenomenology and applications

author.name: Kanishk Jain, Matthew Day, Tankut Can

entry.summary: Investigates an emergent symmetry in LLMs where models partially respect non-canonical token segmentations of the same string despite training only on canonical ones. Probes this through compositional understanding, representation diversity, and benchmark performance experiments.

entry.title: Learning ground state observables from quantum computing experiments

author.name: Ben Jaderberg, Freya Shah, Minjun Jeon, M. Emre Sahin, Christa Zoufal, Kunal Sharma

entry.summary: Demonstrates machine learning of ground-state observables from experimental quantum data on the 2D Heisenberg XXZ model with system sizes up to 115 qubits, scaling beyond prior small-system demonstrations. Constructs datasets of single-site, two-point, and 12-body correlations.

entry.title: Diffusion Flow Matching: Dimension-Improved KL Bounds and Wasserstein Guarantees

author.name: Marta Gentiloni Silveri, Giovanni Conforti, Alain Durmus

entry.summary: Provides refined theoretical convergence guarantees for Brownian-motion-based Diffusion Flow Matching generative models, deriving KL divergence bounds with improved dimensional dependence and extending to 2-Wasserstein distance under mild conditions. Achieves state-of-the-art scaling for discretization error under minimal assumptions.

entry.title: The Complexity of Min-Max Optimization for Quadratic Polynomials

author.name: Martino Bernasconi, Matteo Castiglioni, Andrea Celli, Alexandros Hollender

entry.summary: Proves PPAD-hardness for computing approximate stationary points of min-max optimization over the hypercube for quadratic multilinear polynomials. It yields the first PPAD-hardness results for two-team zero-sum polymatrix games.

entry.title: PhoneHarness: Harnessing Phone-Use Agents through Mixed GUI, CLI, and Tool Actions

author.name: Chenxin Li, Zhengyao Fang, Zhengyang Tang, Pengyuan Lyu, Xingran Zhou, Xin Lai, Fei Tang, Liang Wu, Yiduo Guo, Weinong Wang, Junyi Li, Yi Zhang, Yang Ding, Huawen Shen, Sunqi Fan, Shangpin Peng, Zheng Ruan, Anran Zhang, Benyou Wang, Chengquan Zhang, Han Hu

entry.summary: PhoneHarness is a mixed-action benchmark and execution harness for phone-use agents combining GUI, CLI, and tool actions on verifiable mobile workflows. It moves beyond GUI-only evaluation to check whether intended side effects actually occurred.

entry.title: CoRA: Confidence-Rationale Alignment for Reliable Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Juming Xiong, Weixin Liu, Kevin Guo, Congning Ni, Junchao Zhu, Chongyu Qu, Chao Yan, Katherine Brown, Avinash Baidya, Xiang Gao, Bradley Malin, Zhijun Yin

entry.summary: CoRA introduces a GRPO-based RL framework that aligns model confidence with rationale quality in chain-of-thought reasoning, rewarding correctness, answer probability, and rubric-based rationale support. It reduces misleadingly confident but poorly supported reasoning.

entry.title: Beyond Monolingual Deep Research: Evaluating Agents and Retrievers with Cross-Lingual BrowseComp-Plus

author.name: Yuheng Lu, Qingcheng Zeng, Heli Qi, Puxuan Yu, Fuheng Zhao, Rui Yang, Hitomi Yanaka, Naoto Yokoya, Weihao Xuan

entry.summary: Introduces XBCP, a cross-lingual extension of BrowseComp-Plus that varies the language of supporting documents while keeping English queries and answers. It tests whether deep research agents and retrievers can operate when evidence is in another language.

entry.title: Who Flips? Self- and Cross-Model Counterarguments Reveal Answer Instability in LLMs

author.name: Nafiseh Nikeghbal, Amir Hossein Kargaran, Shaghayegh Kolli, Jana Diesner

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled protocol measuring answer stability when LLMs face plausible counterarguments to correct answers, finding flip rates of 17.5% to 97.3% across seven frontier models and 57 MMLU subjects. It isolates argumentative content from overt social pressure.

entry.title: Towards Pareto-Optimal Tool-Integrated Agents with Pareto Ranking Policy Optimization

author.name: Junyi Li, Xiaowei Qian, Yingyi Zhang, Wenlin Zhang, Guojing Li, Sheng Zhang, Xiao Han, Yichao Wang, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: ParetoPO is a two-stage multi-objective optimization framework for aligning tool-using LLMs under competing objectives like accuracy and tool-use efficiency, using hypervolume-guided scalarization then Pareto-ranking-based advantages. It targets Pareto-optimal tool-integrated agents.

entry.title: Weaving Multi-Source Evidence for Biomedical Reasoning: The BioMedHop Benchmark and BioWeave Framework

author.name: Xingyu Tan, Shiyuan Liu, Xiaoyang Wang, Qing Liu, Xiwei Xu, Xin Yuan, Liming Zhu, Wenjie Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces BioMedHop, a multi-source graph-grounded biomedical QA benchmark with 10,045 instances across KG, document, web, and hybrid evidence, plus the BioWeave framework for weaving evidence topologies. It targets source-conditioned graph reasoning underexplored in prior benchmarks.

entry.title: Context-Aware RL for Agentic and Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Peiyang Xu, Bangzheng Li, Sijia Liu, Karthik R. Narasimhan, Pramod Viswanath, Prateek Mittal, Xingyu Fu

entry.summary: ContextRL is a context-aware reinforcement learning method that improves long-horizon and multimodal reasoning via an indirect auxiliary objective rewarding selection of the supporting context for a query-answer pair. It encourages fine-grained grounding in coding agents and multimodal tasks.

entry.title: Misinformation Propagation in Benign Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jonas Becker, Jan Philip Wahle, Terry Ruas, Bela Gipp

entry.summary: This work studies how intent-based misinformation injected into benign multi-agent LLM systems propagates and persists through debate, degrading reasoning, knowledge, and alignment tasks. Agents often retain incorrect answers introduced by misinformed peers.

entry.title: Towards Global AI-Driven Cervical Cancer Screening

author.name: Thuy Nuong Tran, \"Omer S\"umer, Evangelia Christodoulou, Lennart Nausch\"utte, Simon Kalteis, Martin Paulikat, Esmira Pashayeva, Klara Steinheuer, Isabella Borges, Piotr Kalinowski, Hermann Bussmann, Sieng Sokmney, Poeung Kuong, Sathiarany Vong, Achim Schneider, Magnus von Knebel-Doeberitz, Patrick Godau, Lena Maier-Hein

entry.summary: This work presents the first deep learning cervical cancer screening approach validated on multi-country colposcopy data, framed as a multi-task lesion detection and classification problem. It targets the WHO goal of cervical cancer elimination in low- and middle-income countries.

entry.title: GeoStream: Toward Precise Camera Controlled Streaming Video Generation

author.name: Yizhou Zhao, Yifan Wang, Xiaoyuan Wang, Yushu Wu, Hao Zhang, Moayed Haji-Ali, Rameen Abdal, Ashkan Mirzaei, Yanyu Li, Willi Menapace, Laszlo Jeni, Sergey Tulyakov, Peter Wonka, Chaoyang Wang

entry.summary: GeoStream enables precise metric-scale camera control in autoregressive streaming video generation by maintaining a self-refreshing 3D cache updated online from the model's own outputs. It overcomes the limitation of static 3D caches that fail when viewpoints move beyond the original frustum.

entry.title: Show the Signal, Hide the Noise: Spectral Forcing for Pixel-Space Diffusion

author.name: Weichen Fan, Haiwen Diao, Penghao Wu, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces spectral forcing for pixel-space diffusion, exploiting the frequency-dependent data-to-noise contour to address a capacity-allocation problem where denoisers waste computation on noise-dominated frequency-time regions. It makes the implicit coarse-to-fine structure explicit.

entry.title: CausalDrive: Real-time Causal World Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Tianyi Yan, Huan Zheng, Dubing Chen, Meizhi Qu, Yingying Shen, Lijun Zhou, Mingfei Tu, Bing Wang, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Haiyang Sun, Cheng-zhong Xu, Jianbing Shen

entry.summary: CausalDrive proposes a real-time, controllable world model for autonomous driving that renders future driving scenes from only an initial frame, ego trajectory, and a text prompt, forcing reactivity by excluding oracle future agent layouts. This bridges the gap between non-reactive layout renderers and slow action-conditioned predictors for closed-loop policy learning.

entry.title: VFUSE: Virulent Feature Understanding With Sparse AutoEncoders

author.name: michaelwaves

entry.summary: VFUSE trains sparse autoencoders on protein diffusion-transformer activations (RoseTTAFold3, RFDiffusion3) to audit for hazard-aware features, finding monosemantic features firing on hazardous designs at up to 0.84 AUROC. It is claimed as the first SAE trained on an all-atom diffusion model and first feature-level virulence audit.

entry.title: The embrace of open science: An analysis of a decade of AI research and 56 800 conference papers

author.name: Kevin L Coakley, Thijs Snelleman, Holger Hoos, Odd Erik Gundersen

entry.summary: Analyzes reproducibility documentation practices across 56,800 papers from five leading AI conferences over a decade, finding code-and-data sharing rose nearly sixfold from 11% to 64% (2014-2024). Assesses whether reproducibility checklists have changed documentation behavior.

entry.title: Divide-and-Denoise: A Game-Theoretic Method for Fairly Composing Diffusion Models

author.name: Abhi Gupta, Polina Barabanshchikova, Vikas Garg, Samuel Kaski, Tommi Jaakkola

entry.summary: Divide-and-Denoise coordinates multiple pre-trained diffusion models during sampling via a game-theoretic allocation that fairly divides responsibility over regions of the noisy sample, solving a fair division game at each timestep. Prevents one model dominating or models disagreeing during composition.

entry.title: AutoDojo: Adaptive Attacks Expose Superficial Defenses and User-Underspecification Limits in LLM Agents

author.name: Xinhang Ma, Taoran Li, Chaowei Xiao, Zhiyuan Yu, Ning Zhang, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik

entry.summary: AutoDojo introduces adaptive attacks against LLM agent defenses to indirect prompt injection, showing static benchmarks like AgentDojo fail to capture robustness to adaptive threats. It exposes superficial defenses and limits stemming from user underspecification.

entry.title: Service-Induced Congestion in Memory-Constrained LLM Serving

author.name: Ruicheng Ao, Jing Dong, Gan Luo, David Simchi-Levi

entry.summary: Develops a discrete-time dynamical model of memory-constrained LLM serving where growing KV caches cause endogenous congestion and request eviction, analyzing eviction-free fixed points and limit behavior under continuous batching. Provides theoretical grounding for serving system design.

entry.title: PO-PDDL: Learning Symbolic POMDPs from Visual Demonstrations for Robot Planning Under Uncertainty

author.name: Wenjing Tang, Xuanjin Jin, Yuan Liu, Renming Huang, Cewu Lu, Panpan Cai

entry.summary: PO-PDDL extends PDDL to symbolically model partially observable, stochastic POMDPs with beliefs while retaining LLM-friendly syntax, plus a pipeline that learns these models from real-robot execution videos. Targets robot planning under uncertainty.

entry.title: Snyk VulnBench JS 1.0: Can LLMs Find the Same Bugs Twice?

author.name: Liran Tal, Johannes Kloos, Arsenii Rudich, Stephen Thoemmes, Manoj Nair

entry.summary: Snyk VulnBench JS 1.0 runs 300 repeated agentic LLM vulnerability scans on identical JavaScript code to measure repeatability, finding reference-matched findings are stable while extra model reports vary heavily across runs (many appearing in only one of five repetitions). Highlights reliability concerns for LLM security review.

entry.title: The Truth Stays in the Family: Enhancing Contextual Grounding via Inherited Truthful Heads in Model Lineages

author.name: Miso Choi, Seonga Choi, Mincheol Kwon, Woosung Joung, Jinkyu Kim, Jungbeom Lee

entry.summary: Shows that head-level context-truthfulness scores are strongly preserved within model families (Vicuna, Qwen2.5, LLaMA2, Mistral lineages) even after instruction tuning or multimodal adaptation, with truthful heads attending to query-relevant evidence. Leverages inherited truthful heads to enhance contextual grounding.

entry.title: Scalable Circuit Learning for Interpreting Large Language Models

author.name: Naiyu Yin, Dennis Wei, Tian Gao, Amit Dhurandhar, Karthikeyan Natesan Ramamurthy, Yue Yu

entry.summary: CircuitLasso is a scalable circuit-learning method using sparse linear regression over sparse-autoencoder features that matches intervention-based circuit accuracy at a fraction of the compute. It makes interpretable circuit discovery over high-dimensional SAE features tractable.

entry.title: A Decision-Theoretic View of Test-Time Training: When, How Far, and Which Directions to Adapt

author.name: Tomoya Wakayama

entry.summary: Provides a decision-theoretic analysis of test-time training as implicit Bayesian inference in the kernel regime, showing TTT helps when updates are spectrally matched to signal-to-noise ratio and aligned with query-relevant eigendirections. Explains TTT instability and motivates adaptive update schemes.

entry.title: ReQAT: Achieving Full-Precision Reasoning Accuracy with 4-bit Floating-Point Quantization-Aware Training

author.name: Janghwan Lee, Sihwa Lee, Jinseok Kim, Yongjik Kim, Jieun Lim, Jinwook Oh, Jungwook Choi

entry.summary: ReQAT is a reasoning-centric FP4 quantization-aware training framework that recovers full-precision reasoning accuracy under aggressive W4A4KV4 quantization. It identifies that FP4 failures concentrate on low-entropy symbolic tokens (digits, operators) and uses trace-aligned training to fix them.

entry.title: Mixtures of Subspaces for Bandwidth Efficient Context Parallel Training

author.name: Sameera Ramasinghe, Ajanthan Thalaiyasingam, Hadi Mohaghegh Dolatabadi, Gil Avraham, Violetta Shevchenko, Yan Zuo, Chamin Hewa Koneputugodage, Alexander Long

entry.summary: Proposes a communication-efficient context-parallel training method for decentralized low-bandwidth settings by exploiting the intrinsic low-rank structure of activations using dynamically constructed mixtures of subspaces. Achieves over 95% compression with negligible overhead and no convergence loss.

entry.title: Privacy from Symmetry: Orthogonally Equivariant Transformers for LLM Inference

author.name: Alexander Yukhimchuk, Andrey Shulga, Mladen Kolar, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}

entry.summary: Proposes ConjFormer, an orthogonally-equivariant transformer variant enabling privacy-preserving split inference: clients multiply embeddings by a secret orthogonal matrix, and the model performs correct inference under arbitrary rotations via scalar RMSNorm and blockwise orthogonal conjugation. This prevents nearest-neighbor recovery of tokens from transmitted representations.

entry.title: Identification and Inference for Algorithmic Frontiers with Selective Labels

author.name: Yiqi Liu, Francesca Molinari, Amilcar Velez

entry.summary: This paper provides identification results and statistical inference tools for characterizing fairness-accuracy frontiers when outcomes are observed only for selected individuals (selective labels). It includes a debiased ML estimator with asymptotic distribution under unconfoundedness.

entry.title: Stop When Further Reasoning Won't Help: Attention-State Adaptive Generation in Reasoning Models

author.name: Jiakai Li, Ke Qin, Rongzheng Wang, Yizhuo Ma, Qizhi Chen, Muquan Li, Shuang Liang

entry.summary: ASAG is a training-free method that infers a reasoning model's state from attention distributions to adaptively stop generation and reduce overthinking. It mitigates redundant token output and accuracy degradation without prompts or confidence signals.

entry.title: Calibrated Triage, Not Autonomy: Confidence Estimation for Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Reza Khanmohammadi, Kundan Thind, Mohammad M. Ghassemi

entry.summary: Evaluates seven confidence estimators across five medical vision-language models and three VQA datasets, framing the question as how much imaging work a model can safely handle alone. It argues for calibrated triage and abstention rather than autonomy.

entry.title: PathRouter: Aligning Rewards with Retrieval Quality in Agentic Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Bo Wang, Heyan Huang, Yaolin Li, Wei Tang, Yuan Zhang, Wenbo Li, Mingze Gao, Ge Shi, Chong Feng

entry.summary: PathRouter is a path-aware training framework for agentic GraphRAG that addresses answer-path reward aliasing and search-update ambiguity in outcome-only RL by jointly evaluating answer correctness and evidence-path quality. It aligns rewards with retrieval quality.

entry.title: Uncertainty Is Not a Safety Net for Clinical VQA, but Can It Anticipate Model Failure?

author.name: Arnisa Fazla, Alberto Testoni, Ameen Abu-Hanna, Barbara Plank, Iacer Calixto

entry.summary: Benchmarks 8 uncertainty estimation methods across 12 clinical VLMs on VQA, finding UE quality tracks model accuracy and degrades precisely where reliability is most needed. It shows accuracy collapses under NOTA perturbations while uncertainty barely changes.

entry.title: Learning Sparse Latent Predictive Foundation Model for Multimodal Neuroimaging

author.name: Haoxu Huang, Long Chen, Jingyun Chen, Jinu Hyun, James Ryan Loftus, Kara Melmed, Daniel Orringer, Jennifer Frontera, Seena Dehkharghani, Arjun Masurkar, Narges Razavian

entry.summary: Neuro-JEPA is a sparse multimodal neuroimaging foundation model combining a latent predictive (JEPA) objective with a Mixture-of-Experts architecture to encode brain MRI across T1w, T2w, and FLAIR contrasts. It provides a systematic study of architecture, masking, objective, and sparsity design choices.

entry.title: OSGuard: A Benchmark for Safety in Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Mina Mohammadmirzaei, Jeffrey Flanigan

entry.summary: OSGuard is a dual-granularity benchmark for safety in computer-use agents, evaluating both action-level guardrail decisions and end-to-end execution under benign instructions. It targets unsafe shortcuts that task-success metrics miss.

entry.title: Where Did It Go Wrong? Process-Level Evaluation of Web Agents with Semantic State Tracking

author.name: Jiwan Chung, JiHyuk Byun, Vibhav Vineet, Seon Joo Kim

entry.summary: WebStep is a benchmark of 1,800 web-agent tasks with automatic semantic state tracking via a deterministic semantic MDP alongside the GUI, enabling process-level rather than terminal-success evaluation. Reveals differences invisible to outcome-only metrics.

entry.title: LLM-as-Code Agentic Programming for Agent Harness

author.name: Junjia Qi, Zichuan Fu, Jingtong Gao, Wenlin Zhang, Hanyu Yan, Xian Wu, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: Argues that token explosion, control-flow hallucination, and unreliable completion in LLM agents stem from assigning deterministic control flow to a probabilistic system, and proposes Agentic Programming where the program governs control flow and the LLM (LLM-as-Code) is invoked only for reasoning. Reframes agent architecture.

entry.title: Looking Is Not Picking: An Attention-Segment Account of Tool-Selection Failures in LLM Agents

author.name: Shiyang Chen

entry.summary: Shows that LLM agent tool-selection failures occur at the decision readout, not at attention to the right tool, finding the model attends most to the correct tool 80% of the time yet still picks wrong. Refutes the crowded-harness/lost-in-the-middle explanation through attention-segment analysis on BFCL failures.

entry.title: AgentFairBench: Do LLM Agents Discriminate When They Act?

author.name: Triveni Morla, Rohith Reddy Bellibaltu, Manpreet Singh, Manmeet Singh Kapoor

entry.summary: AgentFairBench is a multi-domain benchmark measuring demographic disparity in the actions of LLM agents across hiring, lending, and medical triage, using counterfactual matched profiles varying only race-gender signals. Moves fairness evaluation from grading answers to assessing actions under increasing agency scaffolds.

entry.title: X-Tokenizer: A Multimodal Action Tokenizer for Vision-Language-Action Pretraining

author.name: Xirui Kang, Yanpei Shi, Lucy Liang, Roy Gan, Dongxiu Liu, Pushi Zhang, Danpeng Chen, Xiaoyi Qin, Yinan Zheng, Jinliang Zheng, Hao Wang, Xianyuan Zhan, Hang Su

entry.summary: X-Tokenizer reframes action tokenization for Vision-Language-Action models as semantic interface learning, using a Semantic Residual Quantization encoder-decoder to provide a shared action interface across diverse robotic arm embodiments. Aims to give stronger semantic supervision to the VLA backbone than reconstruction-only tokenizers.

entry.title: Efficient Reinforcement for Visual-Textual Thinking with Discrete Diffusion Model

author.name: Yoonjeon Kim, Yuhta Takida, Chieh-Hsin Lai, Eunho Yang, Yuki Mitsufuji

entry.summary: This work shows multimodal discrete diffusion models are effective for RL post-training of interleaved visual-textual reasoning, enabling efficient localized image editing instead of full image regeneration. It reduces GRPO rollout computation by about 27% versus autoregressive baselines with minimal performance loss.

entry.title: FastMix: Fast Data Mixture Optimization via Gradient Descent

author.name: Haoru Tan, Sitong Wu, Yanfeng Chen, Jun Xia, Ruobing Xie, Bin Xia, Xingwu Sun, Xiaojuan Qi

entry.summary: FastMix automates pretraining/post-training data mixture discovery by jointly optimizing mixture coefficients and model parameters using a single proxy model, reformulating mixture selection as bilevel optimization via gradient descent. It shows optimizing mixture ratios is equivalent to a weight-assignment problem, improving efficiency over heuristics and simulations.

entry.title: Resilient Consensus in Agentic AI

author.name: Sribalaji C. Anand, George J. Pappas

entry.summary: This paper tests whether classical resilient Byzantine consensus theory transfers to LLM agents, finding that prompted LLM agents fail to reach agreement achievable in principle even where convergence is guaranteed. Wrapping agents with classical resilient consensus filters restores agreement.

entry.title: Spokes: Optimizing for Diverse Pretraining Data Selection

author.name: Clarence Lee, Yejin Choi, Luke Zettlemoyer, Pang Wei Koh, Hai Leong Chieu

entry.summary: Spokes directly optimizes diversity in pretraining data selection via a probabilistic diversification framework based on the G-Vendi score, optimized with exponentiated gradient descent, rather than relying on proxies. It produces substantially more diverse subsets than random sampling.

entry.title: T-Mem: Memory That Anticipates, Not Archives

author.name: Weidong Guo, Dakai Wang, Zixuan Wang, Hui Liu, Yu Xu

entry.summary: T-Mem proposes an anticipatory long-term memory for conversational agents that retrieves associatively (latent semantic arcs) rather than just by surface lexical/vector similarity, addressing failures on queries that share no surface features with memories.

entry.title: Vernier: Probing Representational Misalignment Behind Lexical Gaps in Causal Reasoning

author.name: Zhenyu Yu

entry.summary: Vernier probes why instruction-tuned models answer causal-reasoning questions differently when variable names are replaced by placeholders, using paired-view weight updates and activation patching to show the gap reflects representational misalignment rather than information loss. Reveals answer-relevant content survives in placeholder representations.

entry.title: OmniTraffic: A Controllable Generation Pipeline and Benchmark for Spatio-Temporal Traffic Reasoning

author.name: Maonan Wang, Zhengyan Huang, Kemou Jiang, Yuhang Fu, Jiayue Zhu, Yuxin Cai, Xingchen Zou, Qiaosheng Zhang, Yi Yu, Ding Wang, Xi Chen, Ben M. Chen, Yuxuan Liang, Zhiyong Cui, Man On Pun, Yirong Chen

entry.summary: OmniTraffic is a controllable generation pipeline and benchmark for spatio-temporal traffic reasoning, built around 12 real intersections reconstructed as editable 3D environments plus surveillance footage, supporting evaluation of lane topology, multi-view geometry, temporal evolution, and signal-phase reasoning. Goes beyond passive visual recognition.

entry.title: Deep Residual Injection for Full-Spectrum Forensic Signal Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Kaiqing Lin, Zhiyuan Yan, Ruoxin Chen, Ke-Yue Zhang, Yue Zhou, Caiyong Piao, Bin Li, Taiping Yao, Bo Wang, Youchang Xiao, Shouhong Ding

entry.summary: Deep Residual Injection enables full-spectrum forensic signal perception in MLLMs for AI-generated image detection, using layer-wise analysis showing semantic information forms in early-to-middle layers while artifact fine-tuning disrupts it, then injecting low-level generator artifacts without sacrificing semantic knowledge. Targets robust deepfake detection.

entry.title: Intelligence Is Not the Bottleneck: Validating an LLM First-Pass Manuscript Score Against Peer-Review Outcomes

author.name: Costa Georgantas

entry.summary: Validates AIPR, an LLM first-pass manuscript scorer that emits five quality dimensions and a weighted overall score by prompting alone, against public ICLR decision outcomes across 300 submissions with pre-registered hypotheses, achieving AUROC 0.82 separating accepted from rejected. Argues intelligence is not the bottleneck for review assistance.

entry.title: Do Safety Monitors Stay Reliable After an Update? Benchmarking and Predicting Activation-Monitor Staleness

author.name: Evan Duan

entry.summary: First systematic study of whether frozen activation-based safety monitors remain reliable after routine model updates like quantization, fine-tuning, or LoRA. Finds quantization preserves probe performance while fine-tuning frequently makes probes stale.

entry.title: Entropy-Gated Latent Recursion

author.name: Soham Bhattacharjee, Dushyant Singh Chauhan, Salem Lahlou, Martin Takac, Nils Lukas

entry.summary: Entropy-Gated Latent Recursion introduces a second, fully deterministic axis for inference-time scaling by recursively re-applying a frozen model's top decoder layers at high-uncertainty tokens. Different layer spans solve different problem subsets without stochastic sampling.

entry.title: Demystifying Variance in Circuit Discovery of LLMs

author.name: Frank Zhengqing Wu, Francesco Tonin, Volkan Cevher

entry.summary: This paper investigates and reduces the variance afflicting LLM circuit discovery, characterizing resampling, rephrasing, and sample-wise variance and proposing CEAP to improve stability over the EAP-IG method. It strengthens the reliability of mechanistic interpretability.

entry.title: Phantoms and Disclosures: a Causal Framework for Auditing Synthetic Data

author.name: Kareem Amin, Rudrajit Das, Alessandro Epasto, Adel Javanmard, Dennis Kraft, M\'onica Ribero, Sergei Vassilvitskii

entry.summary: This paper presents a customizable empirical auditing framework that distinguishes true disclosures, where synthetic data directly reproduces user information, from phantom disclosures, where it incidentally generates similar data, via train/holdout partitioning. It provides a causal lens for auditing privacy leakage in generative synthetic data.

entry.title: Semantic DLM+: Improving Diffusion Language Models through Bias-variance Trade-off in Transition Kernel Design

author.name: Keyue Jiang, Yuxiang Wang, Yanan Zhao, Xiang Yu, Qifang Zhao, Bohan Tang, Baojian Zhou, Yanghua Xiao, Lin Qu, Xiaoxiao Xu

entry.summary: Semantic DLM+ analyzes how transition kernel choice affects diffusion language model performance through a bias-variance lens, identifying asymptotic bias, exposure bias, and optimization variance. It proposes improved kernel designs to stabilize training and reduce biased sampling.

entry.title: DiRecT: Safe Diffusion-Based Planning via Receding-Horizon Denoising

author.name: Paolo Giaretta, Zeyang Li, Navid Azizan

entry.summary: DiRecT is a training-free algorithm for safe diffusion-based planning that enforces constraints only on the final clean trajectory via receding-horizon denoising with terminal constraints, rather than projecting noisy intermediates. This avoids overconstraining sampling dynamics and preserves sample quality.

entry.title: Formalizing and Mitigating Structural Distortion in LLM Attention for Zero-Shot Graph Reasoning

author.name: Donald Loveland, Puja Trivedi, Ari Weinstein, Edward W Huang, Danai Koutra

entry.summary: Formalizes how rotary positional embeddings turn graph linearization into bandwidth-dependent attention decay, suppressing attention between graph-adjacent but sequence-distant nodes in LLM graph reasoning. Proposes mechanism-based attention correction rather than prompt engineering.

entry.title: Mean-Field Parallel Decoding for Discrete Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Tamim Zoabi, Ameen Ali, Liran Ringel, Lior Wolf

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free mean-field decoding framework for discrete diffusion language models that coordinates parallel token updates via pairwise interaction refinement of commit scores. A variational relaxation yields a fixed-point update that suppresses conflicting simultaneous commitments to improve effective parallelism.

entry.title: MUNI: Multimodal Unified Latent Diffusion for Coherent Any-to-Any Generation

author.name: Kyeongmin Yeo, Yunhong Min, Minhyuk Sung

entry.summary: MUNI is an end-to-end multimodal latent diffusion framework for any-to-any generation that unifies subset-conditioned cross-modal generation and unconditional joint sampling through a shared stochastic latent. Unlike LLM-based or text-aligned approaches, it does not require text-paired or fully-paired training data.

entry.title: Taylor-Calibrate: Principled Initialization for Hybrid Linear Attention Distillation

author.name: Zhongzhu Zhou, Qingyang Wu, Junxiong Wang, Mayank Mishra, Shuaiwen Leon Song, Ben Athiwaratkun, Chenfeng Xu

entry.summary: Taylor-Calibrate provides principled initialization for converting pretrained Transformers into hybrid linear-attention models (Gated DeltaNet students), since naively copying attention projections leaves recurrent decay, write, and output-gating dynamics unspecified. It calibrates the student to start in a good dynamical regime, reducing distillation tokens needed.

entry.title: Multimodal Evaluator Preference Collapse: Cross-Modal Contagion in Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Zewen Liu

entry.summary: This paper shows that Evaluator Preference Collapse in self-evolving agents is amplified in multimodal settings, with one strategy absorbing 48 percent of weight. It introduces cross-modal contagion, where preferences learned on one modality corrupt strategy selection on another.

entry.title: From Tokens to Policy: Causal and Interpretable Heterogeneous Treatment Effects Identification

author.name: Riccardo Cadei, Frank Otchere, Nyasha Tirivayi, Gustavo Angeles Tagliaferro, Falco J. Bargagli-Stoffi, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: This work reframes heterogeneous treatment effect identification as a Markov-blanket discovery problem using multimodal pre-treatment measurements and scalable representations. It aims for causal and interpretable HTE identification even when some heterogeneity drivers are unmeasured.

entry.title: Audited Conformal Prediction for Classification under Unknown Distribution Shift

author.name: Yanfei Zhou, Rizal Fathony, Nam H. Nguyen, Matteo Sesia

entry.summary: Audited Conformal Prediction trains an auxiliary audit model on a small target-population labeled set to identify where a deployed classifier is likely to fail under unknown distribution shift. It integrates these signals into conformal prediction to maintain marginal coverage while improving conditional coverage.

entry.title: Distilling latent electrostatics from foundation machine learning interatomic potentials

author.name: Xiaoyu Wang, Bingqing Cheng

entry.summary: This work uses Latent Ewald Summation to extract latent electrostatics implicit in foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials, training a lightweight student model from teacher energies and forces. It adds explicit long-range electrostatics to foundation MLIPs that otherwise lack them.

entry.title: Replay What Matters: Off-Policy Replay for Efficient LLM Reinforcement Unlearning

author.name: Zirui Pang, Chenlong Zhang, Haosheng Tan, Zhuoran Jin, Jiaheng Wei, Zixin Zhong

entry.summary: ReRULE adds off-policy replay to reinforcement-learning-based LLM unlearning, prioritizing hard boundary cases that on-policy methods discard after one use. It improves efficiency of removing hazardous knowledge while preserving general utility.

entry.title: Finite Resources False Discovery Rate Control in Structured Hypothesis Spaces

author.name: Binyamin Perets, Shie Mannor

entry.summary: This paper presents a framework for controlling the false discovery rate when each hypothesis has only a finite count of null draws (leaving p-values uncertain) and when the hypothesis space carries arbitrary structure represented via a reproducing kernel. It provides decision rules for finite-resource structured multiple testing.

entry.title: A Spatio-Temporal Expert Prefetching Framework for Efficient MoE-based LLM Inference

author.name: Yingnan Zhao, Razvan Bunescu, Ahmed Louri, Avinash Karanth, Ke Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a spatio-temporal expert prefetching framework to reduce the expert-loading overhead during inference for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs like Qwen and DeepSeek. Aims to mitigate latency from dynamic, token-dependent expert activation.

entry.title: Phase Transition in Convex Relaxations for Graph Alignment

author.name: Laurent Massouli\'e, Sushil Mahavir Varma, Louis Vassaux, Ir\`ene Waldspurger

entry.summary: Studies the graph alignment problem for correlated Gaussian matrices and analyzes when convex relaxations recover the hidden permutation. Proves a phase transition: when correlation is sufficiently high, the relaxation solution concentrates around the ground-truth permutation.

entry.title: LoComposition: Terrain-Adaptive Energy-Efficient Quadruped Locomotion without Gait Priors

author.name: Loukas Kordos, Leonard T. Franz, Simon Rappenecker, Oliver Hausdoerfer, Angela P. Schoellig, Pavel Kolev, Georg Martius

entry.summary: Presents LoComposition, a quadruped locomotion learning approach that decomposes the reward into distinct mechanisms (rewards for tasks, constraints for limits, energy minimization for gait, perception for terrain) and removes explicit gait priors. Shows emergent terrain-adaptive, energy-efficient gaits with ablations exposing distinct failure modes.

entry.title: Learning the generating functional for variance reduction in lattice QCD

author.name: Ryan Abbott, Yang Fu, Daniel C. Hackett, Gurtej Kanwar, Fernando Romero-L\'opez, Phiala E. Shanahan

entry.summary: Uses machine-learned normalizing flows to reduce variance of arbitrary N-point correlation functions in lattice gauge theory by encoding the generating functional. Demonstrates up to threefold variance reduction on glueball correlators and Wilson loops in QCD.

entry.title: Closing the Approximation Gap in Simulation-free Latent SDEs

author.name: Henry D. Smith, Brian L. Trippe, Scott W. Linderman

entry.summary: Closes the approximation gap in simulation-free variational inference for latent SDEs, which parameterize the posterior through instantaneous marginals rather than drift to avoid expensive numerical simulation. Improves efficiency for recovering dynamical systems from noisy observations in neuroscience and physics.

entry.title: Task-Error Residual Learning for Real-Robot Five-Ball Juggling

author.name: Kai Ploeger, Jan Peters

entry.summary: Achieves stable real-robot three-, four-, and five-ball juggling on anthropomorphic arms via residual learning with directional task-error supervision, which carries far more information than scalar reward, plus a task-error model driving sample selection. The system converges from the second attempt.

entry.title: Agent trajectories as programs: fingerprinting and programming coding-agent behavior

author.name: Hamidah Oderinwale

entry.summary: Proposes treating agent trajectories as programs and fingerprinting coding agents by their behavioral habits, achieving 85.7% attribution accuracy across ten agents. It offers a procedural way to compare agent problem-solving beyond benchmark scores.

entry.title: Can Agents Read the Room? Benchmarking Visual Social Intelligence in Multimodal Simulation

author.name: Shijun Wan, Xuehai Wu, Jiwen Zhang, Siyuan Wang, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for visual social intelligence in multimodal social simulation, with 240 scenarios testing whether agents can use facial expressions, gaze, and posture to guide interaction. It evaluates seven MLLMs on role-level tasks.

entry.title: Beyond English: Uncovering the Multilingual Gap in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Hanyang Chen, Hongliang Li, Jiarui Cao, Yang Li, Yang Jiang, Haonan Wen, Kaiyu Huang, Shengnan Guo, Huaiyu Wan

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic study of multilingual instruction following in vision-language-action models, finding a significant gap when instructions are non-English despite underlying multilingual LLM capabilities. It extends benchmarks with translated instructions.

entry.title: On Defining Erasure Harms for NLP

author.name: Yu Lu Liu, Arnav Goel, Jackie Chi Kit Cheung, Alexandra Olteanu, Ziang Xiao, Su Lin Blodgett

entry.summary: Develops a structured conceptual definition of erasure harm in NLP, clarifying the components needed to establish and measure it. It bridges overly broad and overly setting-specific prior conceptualizations.

entry.title: BALTO: Balanced Token-Level Policy Optimization for Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: Ning Li, Zixuan Guo, Yan Xu, Wenbo Fei, Yifan Niu, Chang Luo, Yasheng Wang, Weiwen Liu, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: BALTO is a balanced token-level policy optimization framework for hallucination mitigation that addresses granularity mismatch in response-level faithfulness rewards and unbalanced credit assignment. It aims to reduce spurious penalties on supported content.

entry.title: Contaminated Collaboration: Measuring Gender Bias Transfer in LLM-Assisted Student Writing

author.name: Ariyan Hossain, Kazi Kamruzzaman Rabbi, Farig Sadeque, S M Taiabul Haque

entry.summary: Investigates whether gender bias in an LLM writing assistant transfers into human-written career plan essays via a controlled study with 123 participants under three assistance conditions. It examines bias propagation from model to human-authored text.

entry.title: SING: Synthetic Intention Graph for Scalable Active Tool Discovery in LLM Agents

author.name: Qiao Xiao, Haochen Shi, Yisen Gao, Wenbin Hu, Huihao Jing, Tianshi Zheng, Baixuan Xu, Ziheng Zhang, Weiqi Wang, Haoran Li, Jiaxin Bai, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: SING uses a synthetic intention graph for scalable active tool discovery in LLM agents, addressing the closed-world limits of exhaustive tool injection and the misalignment of one-shot retrieval with true task intention. It targets long-horizon tasks where required tools emerge through decomposition.

entry.title: How Far Can Machine Translation Quality Take You? Extrinsic Discourse Evaluation in Goal-Oriented Setups

author.name: Wafaa Mohammed, Kata Naszadi, Vlad Niculae

entry.summary: Performs extrinsic discourse evaluation of machine translation under static (entity counting for referential consistency) and interactive (Welfare Diplomacy game) regimes. It shows high intrinsic MT quality does not reliably predict downstream discourse success.

entry.title: LESS Is More: Mutual-Stability Sampling for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Amr Mohamed, Guokan Shang, Michalis Vazirgiannis

entry.summary: LESS is a training-free, model-agnostic adaptive sampler for diffusion LLMs that treats token commitment as an online stopping problem using a mutual-stability rule. It improves efficiency by avoiding wasted computation on already-stable positions and premature commitment of unstable ones.

entry.title: FairGen: Preference-Aligned Diffusion for Demographically Equitable Medical Image Synthesis

author.name: Zhimin Li, Ruichen Zhang, Zhen Tan, Howard J Aizenstein, Jingtong Hu, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: FairGen is a fairness-aware diffusion framework that synthesizes demographically balanced medical images to counteract diagnostic bias from imbalanced clinical datasets. It uses preference alignment to address naturally rare phenotypic presentations across demographic groups.

entry.title: ReGenHuman: Re-Generating Human Appearances for Realistic Full-Body Video Anonymization

author.name: Adam Sun, Eshaan Barkataki, Arnold Milstein, Gordon Wetzstein, Ehsan Adeli

entry.summary: ReGenHuman is the first full-body video anonymization pipeline that regenerates rather than edits human appearances to be simultaneously realistic, temporally consistent, and anonymous. It composites 2D pose, segmentation, and depth into conditioning streams to fine-tune a video-to-video diffusion model.

entry.title: Keep It in Mind: User Centric Continual Spatial Intelligence Reasoning in Egocentric Video Streams

author.name: Yun Wang, Junbin Xiao, Han Lyu, Yifan Wang, Jing Zuo, Zhanjie Zhang, Hong Huang, Dapeng Wu, Angela Yao

entry.summary: UCS-Bench is a dataset of 170+ hours of egocentric video with 8.1K timestamped questions for diagnosing user-centric continual spatial intelligence. The accompanying DirectMe framework incrementally builds structured spatial memory from streaming egocentric observations for long-horizon spatial reasoning.

entry.title: HemExp: Clinically-Guided Latent Diffusion for Modeling Hematoma Expansion

author.name: Orhun Utku Aydin, Satoru Tanioka, Tzu I Chuang, Alexander Koch, Dimitrios Rallios, Marie Gultom, Begum Tahhan, Fujimaro Ishida, Dietmar Frey, Adam Hilbert

entry.summary: HemExp is a clinically-guided latent diffusion model that generates patient-specific follow-up CT images and hemorrhage segmentations to model hematoma expansion after intracerebral hemorrhage. It conditions on baseline imaging, clinical variables, and an explicit expansion indicator for controllable, uncertainty-aware scenario simulation.

entry.title: Track2View: 4D-Consistent Camera-Controlled Video Generation via Paired 3D Point Tracks

author.name: Feng Qiao, Zhaochong An, Zhexiao Xiong, Serge Belongie, Nathan Jacobs

entry.summary: Track2View conditions a video diffusion transformer on paired 3D point tracks to enable camera-controlled, 4D-consistent novel-view video generation with explicit temporally continuous correspondences. Improves over per-frame pose or noisy point-cloud conditioning approaches.

entry.title: Metis: A Generalizable and Efficient World-Action Model for Autonomous Driving and Urban Navigation

author.name: Jingyu Li, Zhe Liu, Dongnan Hu, Junjie Wu, Zipei Ma, Wenxiao Wu, Chao Han, Zhihui Hao, Zhikang Liu, Kun Zhan, Jiankang Deng, Xiatian Zhu, Li Zhang

entry.summary: Metis is a world-action model for autonomous driving that decouples video generation and action prediction using a Mixture-of-Transformers with dedicated experts, reducing inference latency and representational mismatch. Aims for generalizable, efficient end-to-end driving and urban navigation.

entry.title: GraphWorld: Long-Horizon Planning with World Models for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Ziying Song, Caiyan Jia, Lin Liu, Lei Yang, Shengkai Zhang, Feiyang Jia, Fengda Zhao, Peiliang Wu, Shaoqing Xu, Chen Lv, Yadan Luo

entry.summary: UniDDT is a unified multimodal model that uses a Noisy ViT encoder with an LLM to share semantic encoding across visual understanding and generation, while a decoupled diffusion transformer handles generation, addressing learning conflicts and scalability issues. Targets duality between understanding and generation.

entry.title: DreamX-World 1.0: A General-Purpose Interactive World Model

author.name: DreamX Team, Yancheng Bai, Rui Chen, Xiangxiang Chu, Rujing Dang, Hao Dou, Bingjie Gao, Qiwen Gu, Siyu Hong, Jiachen Lei, Geng Li, Jifan Li, Ruimin Lin, Qingfeng Shi, Bingze Song, Lei Sun, Jing Tang, Ruitian Tian, Jun Wang, Jiahong Wu, Pengfei Zhang, Shen Zhang, Jiashu Zhu

entry.summary: DreamX-World 1.0 is a general-purpose interactive text/image-to-video world model supporting camera navigation, region revisits, and promptable events across photorealistic, game, and stylized domains. It introduces E-PRoPE for camera control and converts a bidirectional video generator into a few-step autoregressive world model via causal forcing.

entry.title: Provably Safe, Yet Scalable Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kai S. Yun, Zeyang Li, Navid Azizan

entry.summary: PS2-RL is a two-phase framework for learning provably safe RL policies in a scalable manner, avoiding the poor scaling and conservatism of explicit certificate-function methods while providing formal safety guarantees absent from soft-constrained approaches. It aims to bridge the gap between empirical and formally guaranteed safe RL.

entry.title: Forced Deferral: Manipulating Routing Decisions in Multimodal LLM Cascades

author.name: Zhongye Liu, Yaopei Zeng, Yurui Chang, Lu Lin

entry.summary: Introduces the Forced Deferral Attack, an adversarial image attack that lowers a weak model's confidence in multimodal LLM cascades to force expensive deferral to the strong model. Exposes a cost-manipulation attack surface in cascade routing.

entry.title: MR-GVNO: A Geometry-Aware Variational Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Mindlin-Reissner Plates on Irregular Domains

author.name: Siqi Wang, Daobo Sun, Yizheng Wang, Yilong Zhang, Yabin Jin, Xiaoying Zhuang, Timon Rabczuk

entry.summary: CoffeeBench evaluates LLM agents in a long-horizon multi-agent economy of heterogeneous firms (farmers, roasters, retailers) operating over a 90-day simulation to maximize income through communication and trade. Moves beyond single-agent passive-environment benchmarks toward economic multi-agent interaction.

entry.title: Adaptive and Explicit safe: Triggering Latent Safety Awareness in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Ke Miao, Jiaxin Li, Hongliang Chen, Yuke Hu, Zhan Qin

entry.summary: Identifies latent safety awareness in Large Reasoning Models that surfaces when they re-examine queries alongside their own reasoning, and uses supervised fine-tuning with safe tags to adaptively trigger safety analysis. Aims to defend against jailbreaks without heavy external annotation while preserving normal responses.

entry.title: Free Energy Heuristics: Fast-And-Frugal Cognition as Active Inference Under Uncertain Precision

author.name: Alex Bogdan

entry.summary: Frames fast-and-frugal cognition and chain-of-thought behavior through active inference, arguing meta-uncertainty (uncertainty about evidence reliability) decides whether more reasoning helps or hurts, and proves the free-energy-minimizing policy stops integrating cues after finitely many high-validity ones under heavy-tailed precision priors. Offers a principled account of when CoT degrades performance.

entry.title: MosaicQuant: Inlier-Outlier Disaggregation for Unified 4-Bit LLM Quantization

author.name: Yangjia Hu, Haodong Wang, Zicong Hong, Qianli Liu, Quanxin Shou, Jian Lin, Song Guo, Xiaowei Shen, Xiangjun Huang, Dian Wang, Jian Yang

entry.summary: MosaicQuant is a unified 4-bit LLM quantization method built on inlier-outlier disaggregation that handles both dense common values and rare large-magnitude outliers without breaking low-bit execution uniformity. It avoids the precision-conversion overhead of mixed-precision approaches.

entry.title: When Correct Edges Cannot Be Verified: A Provenance Gap in Incomplete KGQA and a Provenance-Favoring Completion Policy

author.name: Yongqi Kang, Yu Fu, Yong Zhao

entry.summary: Investigates whether textual verifiability tracks correctness in incomplete knowledge graph QA, finding 76-96% of gold-correct completed edges have no supporting passage even under exhaustive retrieval. It proposes a provenance-favoring completion policy in response.

entry.title: Multi-HMR 2: Multi-Person Camera-Centric Human Detection, Mesh Recovery and Tracking

author.name: Gu\'enol\'e Fiche, Philippe Weinzaepfel, Romain Br\'egier, Fabien Baradel

entry.summary: Multi-HMR 2 is a DETR-based framework for multi-person camera-centric human detection, mesh recovery, and tracking that predicts metric 3D localization in camera coordinates rather than pelvis-centered recovery. It avoids fixed camera assumptions and handcrafted post-processing for real-world deployment.

entry.title: Conditional Multi-Event Temporal Grounding in Long-Form Video

author.name: Yuanhao Zou, Arthad Kulkarni, Lucas Tonanez, Lincoln Spencer, Guangyu Sun, Tianxingjian Ding, Andong Deng, Yi Li, Shuangjun Liu, Yuan Li, Dashan Gao, Ning Bi, Taotao Jing, Shuai Zhang, Chen Chen

entry.summary: CoMET-Bench is a benchmark for conditional multi-event temporal grounding in long-form video, with 2789 compositional queries over 600 videos averaging 33.8 minutes across five domains. It addresses the gap that existing benchmarks localize only a single moment or treat grounding and counting separately.

entry.title: Trust Between AI Agents: Measuring Formation, Breakage, and Recovery, with Implications for Governing Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yujiao Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a behavioral measure of trust between AI agents based on costly verification in a cooperative survival game, studying how trust forms, breaks, and recovers across frontier model snapshots. Relevant to governance of multi-agent systems.

entry.title: CODA-BENCH: Can Code Agents Handle Data-Intensive Tasks?

author.name: Yuxin Zhang, Ju Fan, Meihao Fan, Shaolei Zhang, Xiaoyong Du

entry.summary: CODA-BENCH is the first benchmark to jointly evaluate code and data intelligence in a data-intensive Linux sandbox built on the Kaggle ecosystem, where agents handle both complex code and large-scale data. Bridges a gap between code-centric and data-centric benchmarks.

entry.title: AIChilles: Automatically Uncovering Hidden Weaknesses in AI-Evolved Systems

author.name: Yajie Zhou, Ao Li, Ashwin Silla, Zaoxing Liu, Vyas Sekar

entry.summary: AIChilles automatically uncovers hidden weaknesses in AI-evolved systems programs by searching for workloads where an AI-rewritten program regresses relative to its baseline. Addresses reliability and scalability risks of AI-driven system evolution.

entry.title: The Faithfulness Gap: Certifying Semantic Equivalence Between Natural-Language and Formal Mathematical Statements

author.name: Noor Islam S. Mohammad, Tamim Sheikh

entry.summary: Bidirectional Provability Fingerprinting certifies semantic faithfulness between natural-language and formal mathematical statements via forward/backward consequence neighborhoods and counterfactual probe generation. Targets the autoformalization bottleneck where a statement can typecheck yet encode a different theorem.

entry.title: Skill-to-LoRA: From Using Skills to Learning Behaviors for Token-Efficient LLM Agents

author.name: Tianyi Zhang, Zhonghao Qi

entry.summary: Skill-to-LoRA replaces runtime SKILL.md skill text with skill-specific LoRA adapters, modeling the behavioral change induced by skill documents rather than re-injecting text into context. Synthesizes skill-guided demonstrations offline and dynamically loads adapters online for token efficiency.

entry.title: Do Large Language Models Have Emotions?

author.name: Amit Goldenberg, James J. Gross

entry.summary: Critically evaluates Anthropic's claim that Claude has functional emotions against affective neuroscience, arguing emotions serve context-sensitive situation interpretation and cross-system reorganization. Finds partial support for the first function but notes the discrete consistent representations sit uneasily with variable human emotion.

entry.title: QPILOTS: Efficient Test-Time Q-Steering for Flow Policies

author.name: Yifan Ruan, Chenyang Cao, Andreas Burger, Ali Pesaranghader, Kaveh Kamali, Jaehong Kim, Nandita Vijaykumar, Alan Aspuru-Guzik, Igor Gilitschenski, Nicholas Rhinehart

entry.summary: QPILOTS steers flow-matching/diffusion robot policies at inference time using a Q-critic without modifying or retraining the policy, avoiding unstable backpropagation through denoising. It performs test-time Q-steering at each denoising step for stable policy improvement.

entry.title: EyeMVP: OCT-Informed Fundus Representation Learning via Paired CFP--OCT Pretraining

author.name: Zhuo Deng, Ruiheng Zhang, Ziheng Zhang, Weihao Gao, Yitong Li, Qian Wang, Lei Shao, Jiaoyue Dong, Zhixi Zeng, Lijian Fang, Haibo Wang, Xiaobin Lin, Tao Liu, Zhicheng Du, Zhengwei Zhang, Lin Yang, Zheng Gong, Xinyu Zhao, Zhenquan Wu, Fang Li, Zhiguang Zhou, Guoming Zhang, Sun Jing, Han Lv, Wenbin We, Lan Ma

entry.summary: EyeMVP is a cross-modal retinal foundation model pretrained on ~675K same-eye same-day paired CFP-OCT image triples to learn OCT-informed fundus representations using cross-modal masked reconstruction. It requires only color fundus photos at inference while enriching them with OCT-associated supervision.

entry.title: Benign in Isolation, Harmful in Composition: Security Risks in Agent Skill Ecosystems

author.name: Yi Xie, Jiawei Du, Yu Cheng, Jiuan Zhou, Zhaoxia Yin

entry.summary: This work identifies Skill Composition Risk, where individually benign LLM agent skills become harmful when composed in a shared execution context through trust signals and side effects. It introduces SCR-Bench, recording downstream state changes in sandboxed environments to evaluate composition risks beyond isolated vetting.

entry.title: Exploring Starts Are Not Enough: Counterexamples and a Fix for Monte Carlo Exploring Starts

author.name: Octave Oliviers, Glenn Vinnicombe

entry.summary: This paper resolves a long-standing open question by constructing counterexamples showing tabular Monte Carlo Exploring Starts can converge to suboptimal solutions for both initial-visit and first-visit variants. It provides a convergence-restoring fix by scaling learning rates inversely to per-state update frequencies.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Text Sanitization for Distributed Agents Collaboration via Disentangled Representations

author.name: Xuan Liu, Hefeng Zhou, Sicheng Chen, Chao Yang, Xingcheng Xu, Jingjing Qu, Jiong Lou, Jie LI, Xia Hu

entry.summary: Presents DiSan, a privacy-preserving text sanitization framework using disentangled role and style representations so distributed agents can collaborate without leaking distributional fingerprints. Combines federated prototype alignment and adversarial regularization.

entry.title: Distilling Drifting Transformers with Representation Autoencoders

author.name: Jiawei Zhang, Mengfei Xia, Gen Li, Yuantao Gu

entry.summary: Studies distilling diffusion/flow models in Representation Autoencoder latent spaces, showing that anisotropy and high curvature from rich DINO-based semantics destabilize trajectory distillation, and proposes Drifting Models compatible with RAE latents. Provides theory plus statistics of curvature/isotropy.

entry.title: InstantForget: Update-Free Backdoor Unlearning with Inference-Time Feature Reset

author.name: Zhenyu Yu

entry.summary: InstantForget studies update-free inference-time backdoor unlearning, auditing a projection assumption that fails on WaNet, Blended, and SIG triggers, and introduces a clean-calibrated gated feature reset triggered by a logit-triplet gap and Mahalanobis anomaly detection. Removes backdoors with frozen parameters.

entry.title: SACE: Concept Erasure at the Semantic Singularity in Visual Autoregressive Models

author.name: Siya Yang, Nanxiang Jiang, Zhaoxin Fan, Yunfeng Diao

entry.summary: SACE performs concept erasure in visual autoregressive models, proposing the Semantic Singularity Axiom that target concepts are locked at Scale-0 and validating it via Incremental Semantic Saliency Analysis to avoid the catastrophic semantic collapse that diffusion-designed erasure methods cause on VAR models. Targets safety alignment of text-to-image generation.

entry.title: Open-SWE-Traces: Advancing Dual-Mode Multilingual Distillation for Software Engineering Agents

author.name: Wasi Uddin Ahmad, Nikolai Ludwig, Somshubra Majumdar, Boris Ginsburg

entry.summary: Introduces Open-SWE-Traces, a dataset of 207,489 agentic software-engineering trajectories across nine programming languages, synthesized with dual thinking and non-thinking reasoning modes. Aims to relieve the data bottleneck for training autonomous SWE agents.

entry.title: Scaling Adaptive Depth with Norm-Agnostic Residual Networks

author.name: Tom\'as Figliolia, Beren Millidge

entry.summary: Introduces NAG, a norm-agnostic residual architecture that separates magnitude from directional information in the residual stream to prevent residual-norm growth from suppressing later-layer contributions. Enables better depth scaling with negligible added parameters.

entry.title: Cascaded Sparse Autoencoders Learn Multi-Level Visual Concepts in Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Yusong Zhao, Hengyi Wang, Tanuja Ganu, Akshay Nambi, Hao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces cascaded sparse autoencoders (CSAEs) that train a second-level SAE on the decoder weights of a first-level SAE to learn hierarchical visual concepts in multimodal LLMs. Provides explicit multi-level concept organization beyond flat feature dictionaries.

entry.title: Training and Evaluating Diffusion Policies with Long Context Lengths

author.name: Abhinav Agarwal, Adam Wei, Taylan Kargin, Michael Zeng, Cole Becker, Arif Kerem Dayi, Pablo Parrilo, Asuman Ozdaglar, Russ Tedrake

entry.summary: First detailed study of context length in imitation-learning diffusion policies, benchmarking performance as context grows across tasks with varying memory and stability requirements. Challenges prior claims and shows naive context-length scaling is not straightforwardly beneficial.

entry.title: daVinci-kernel: Co-Evolving Skill Selection, Summarization, and Utilization via RL for GPU Kernel Optimization

author.name: Dayuan Fu, Mohan Jiang, Tongyu Wang, Dian Yang, Jiarui Hu, Liming Liu, Jinlong Hou, Pengfei Li

entry.summary: daVinci-kernel is an RL framework that co-evolves skill selection, summarization, and exploitation through a dynamic skill library to optimize GPU kernels in CUDA/Triton. Verified speedups gate skill additions, coupling discovery with reuse.

entry.title: Transformers Learn the Mestre-Nagao Heuristic

author.name: Pranav Venkata Konda

entry.summary: This paper trains a two-layer transformer to classify rational elliptic curves by rank from Frobenius traces with over 99% accuracy, then reverse-engineers the learned algorithm using mechanistic interpretability, finding it implements the Mestre-Nagao heuristic via a sparse 20-neuron circuit. It demonstrates transformers rediscovering a known number-theoretic heuristic.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Measuring Bias Acknowledgment in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Responsible AI Evaluation

author.name: Xian Sun, Wei Gao, Yingshuo Wang, Lingdong Kong, Yanhang Li, Zhichao Fan, Zexin Zhuang, Wenlong Dong, Zhiyuan Zheng, Hrishikesh Paranjape, Abhishek Mandal, Johnny R. Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a trace-level diagnostic that measures whether chain-of-thought reasoning explicitly acknowledges injected biasing content, beyond just final-answer accuracy. It separates susceptibility (bias breaks the answer) from acknowledgment (bias is flagged), addressing a blind spot in responsible AI evaluation.

entry.title: Towards Data-Efficient Cross-Device Generalization of Grad-Shafranov Equilibria via Transfer Learning Neural Operator

author.name: Jay Phil Yoo, William Howes, Yashika Ghai, Kazuma Kobayashi, Souvik Chakraborty, Syed Bahauddin Alam

entry.summary: Develops a transfer-learning neural operator that recasts Grad-Shafranov plasma equilibrium reconstruction as a cross-device operator learning problem, mapping geometry and profile parameters to poloidal flux fields. Enables data-efficient generalization across tokamak geometries for real-time fusion control.

entry.title: SILAGE: Memory-Efficient, Full-Gradient-Free Nonconvex Optimization for Nested Finite Sums

author.name: Igor Sokolov, Laurent Condat, Peter Richt\'arik

entry.summary: SILAGE is a memory-efficient, full-gradient-free optimizer for nonconvex nested double finite-sum problems that avoids both periodic global full-gradient refreshes (like PAGE) and the O(nm) memory of single-loop variance-reduced methods. Targets pooled data silos and out-of-core learning.

entry.title: The Information-Theoretic Benefit of Shared Representations under Orthogonality Constraints

author.name: Thomas Dittrich, Oliver Potocki, Philipp Grohs

entry.summary: Proves information-theoretic lower and upper bounds on the parametric complexity benefit of shared representations in multitask learning under structural constraints like orthogonality and equivariance. Clarifies when joint approximation is more parameter-efficient than separate approximation.

entry.title: QK-Normed MLA: QK normalization without full key caching

author.name: Yizhou Han, Yao Zhao, Jun Zhou, Longfei Li, Ruoyu Sun

entry.summary: Shows that QK normalization, thought incompatible with Multi-head Latent Attention because it appears to need full keys, can be made compatible by decomposing RMSNorm into a static affine weight absorbable into the query projection and a dynamic per-token inverse-RMS scalar. This enables stable QK-normed attention without full key caching.

entry.title: Neural Bayesian Anomaly Mitigation: A Robust Loss that Doubles as an Unsupervised Contamination Classifier

author.name: S. A. K. Leeney, W. J. Handley, H. T. J. Bevins, E. de Lera Acedo

entry.summary: NBAM introduces a Bayesian latent-switch mixture loss that serves both as a robust supervised training loss and as an unsupervised contamination classifier yielding calibrated per-sample anomaly posteriors. It improves on classic robust losses by identifying which observations are corrupted.

entry.title: Maximum Entropy Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Mean-Field Games with Average Reward

author.name: \c{S}evket Kaan Alk{\i}r, Naci Sald{\i}, Berkay Anahtarc{\i}, Can Deha Kar{\i}ks{\i}z

entry.summary: This paper develops maximum entropy inverse reinforcement learning for average-reward mean-field games, recovering rewards from expert demonstrations under a stationary mean-field equilibrium. It provides a convex dual reformulation and convergence guarantees for linear rewards.

entry.title: Factorized Neural Operators Decompose Dynamic and Persistent Responses

author.name: Hao Tang, Yuechen Duan, Jiongyu Zhu, Zimeng Feng, Hao Li, Chao Li

entry.summary: Factorized Neural Operators decompose spectral representations into equivariant dynamic responses and invariant persistent responses via a unified Green's function framework. The two branches spontaneously specialize into distinct physical roles, improving interpretability and generalization for multiscale physics.

entry.title: Think Less, Act Early: Reinforced Latent Reasoning with Early Exit in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Dianqiao Lei, Lianlei Shan

entry.summary: AVA-VLA replaces explicit chain-of-thought in vision-language-action models with latent reasoning variables and an RL-based denoising mechanism with early exit. It aims to reduce computational cost and error propagation in multi-step robotic tasks.

entry.title: Conformal Candidate Certification for Offline Model-Based Optimization

author.name: Seungjin Choi

entry.summary: Conformal Candidate Certification attaches a calibrated one-sided lower bound to each candidate in offline model-based optimization, advancing only those whose bound exceeds a target threshold. It uses the Gibbs-tilted proposal from entropy-regularized surrogate maximization to supply importance weights for weighted conformal prediction.

entry.title: EIBench: A Simulator-Based Benchmark and Turn-Credit RL for Emotion Management

author.name: Rongzhi Zhu, Xiang Huang, Yuchuan Wu, Rui Wang, Zequn Sun, Tao Ren, Weiyao Luo, Bingxue Qiu, Jieping Ye, Yongbin Li, Wei Hu

entry.summary: Introduces EIBench, a simulator-based benchmark for interactive multi-turn emotion management in LLMs, with 2,222 scenarios across a Support/Defense/Repair/Charm taxonomy, plus a turn-credit RL method. Moves beyond static emotional intelligence evaluation toward improving user emotional state over conversation.

entry.title: Generative Modeling on Metric Graphs via Neural Optimal Transport

author.name: Alessandro Micheli, Yueqi Cao, Anthea Monod, Samir Bhatt

entry.summary: Introduces what the authors claim is the first deep generative modeling framework for distributions supported on compact metric graphs, embedding the graph into ambient space, solving an entropic optimal transport problem via neural semidual parameterization, and projecting back. Proves weak convergence of the learned generator to a valid transport map.

entry.title: A Mechanistic Understanding of Pronoun Fidelity in LLMs

author.name: Katharina Trinley, Jesujoba O. Alabi, Dietrich Klakow, Vagrant Gautam

entry.summary: Provides a mechanistic, model-internal analysis of pronoun fidelity in LLMs, testing whether group entity binding, recency bias, and stereotypical bias are causally implemented using Boundless Distributed Alignment Search. Finds all three coexist as causal subspaces distributed across network depth.

entry.title: Learning Hybrid Biophysical Neuron Models with Neural ODEs

author.name: Jonas Beck, Michael Deistler, D\'ora Vikt\'oria Moln\'ar, Jakob H. Macke, Philipp Berens

entry.summary: Introduces a hybrid modeling framework embedding neural ODEs into conductance-based biophysical neuron models to capture unmodeled currents or mis-specified channel kinetics while preserving mechanistic interpretability. Parameterizes the neural ODE in terms of voltage-dependent steady-states and time constants.

entry.title: Functional Gradient Descent with Adaptive Representations

author.name: Daniel Csillag, Rodrigo Schuller, Pedro Dall'Antonia, Leonidas Guibas, Luiz Velho, Tiago Novello

entry.summary: Proposes a theoretically-grounded functional gradient descent algorithm with adaptive representations that avoids fixed-approximation error by adapting the function-space representation, addressing the infinite-dimensionality of functional gradients. Combines strong FGD convergence theory with practical implementability.

entry.title: A Multi-Center Benchmark for Abdominal Disease Diagnosis and Report Generation from Non-Contrast CT

author.name: Mariam Elbakry, Aliaa Sayed Sheha, Salma Hassan Tantawy, Aya Yassin, Concetto Spampinato, Karim Lekadir, Xiaomeng Li, Marawan Elbatel

entry.summary: Presents a multi-center benchmark for abdominal disease diagnosis and radiology report generation from non-contrast CT, synthesizing contrast-enhanced findings without injecting contrast agents. It curates paired NCCT-CECT studies to reduce patient risk and radiologist workload.

entry.title: Context Compression Is Not One Thing: Readable Symbolic Re-expression vs. Coherent Summary at Matched Budget

author.name: Sisong Bei, Mikhail L. Arbuzov, Ziwei Dong, Dmitri Kalaev, Alexey Shvets

entry.summary: Proposes Telegraph English, a readable symbolic entity-relation format for context compression in multi-hop QA with small LMs, outperforming matched-budget baselines by 13-20 F1 points. It distinguishes symbolic re-expression from coherent summarization.

entry.title: ReportQA: QA-Based Radiology Report Evaluation

author.name: Yiming Shi, Shaoshuai Yang, Xi Chen, Haolin Li, Hengyu Zhang, Che Jiang, Kaiwen Wang, Xun Zhu, Dong Xie, Fei Wang, Dejing Dou, Miao Li, Ji Wu

entry.summary: ReportQA is a QA-based framework for evaluating radiology reports, using clinically meaningful downstream questions instead of NLG metrics or limited clinical-efficacy metrics. It supports flexible, detailed quantitative analysis of report quality.

entry.title: Prior over Evidence: Stereotype-Driven Diagnosis in LLM-Based L2 Pronunciation Feedback

author.name: Rong Wang, Kun Sun

entry.summary: Tests whether audio-capable LLMs ground L2 pronunciation feedback in actual speech evidence or in pretraining priors, across 1800 utterances and five evidence conditions. It finds diagnoses are often stereotype-driven rather than evidence-based.

entry.title: Pepti-Agent: An AI Agent for Peptide Design and Optimization

author.name: Houxu Chen, Achuth Chandrasekhar, Amir Barati Farimani

entry.summary: Pepti-Agent is an AI agent for therapeutic peptide design that pairs generative models with property predictors while explicitly tracking the evolving multi-property state of each candidate. It addresses competing constraints like solubility, hemolytic activity, and fouling.

entry.title: Neuron Level Analysis of Large Language Model in Legal Domain Reasoning

author.name: Eri Onami, Youmi Ma, Shuhei Kurita, Naoaki Okazaki

entry.summary: Conducts neuron-level analysis of legal-domain reasoning across seven open-weight LLMs, showing that suppressing identified neurons collapses target-task accuracy while random suppression does not. It finds both task-specific and cross-task influential neurons.

entry.title: FinBalance: A Multi-Document Accounting Reconciliation Benchmark

author.name: Sasank Tumpati, Devansh Agarwal, Ayush Kedia, Arjun Neekhra, Murari Mandal, Krishna Garg, Yash Sinha, Suman Gupta, Dhruv Kumar

entry.summary: FinBalance is a multi-document accounting reconciliation benchmark built from source-document bundles across eight industries, requiring reconciliation into cited journal entries, balance sheets, and contradiction checks. It uses a deterministic generator producing 23 inconsistency-code labels.

entry.title: SAG: SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation with Query-Time Dynamic Hyperedges

author.name: Yuchao Wu, Junqin Li, XingCheng Liang, Yongjie Chen, Yinghao Liang, Linyuan Mo, Guanxian Li

entry.summary: SAG is an SQL-retrieval augmented generation architecture that converts each chunk into a semantically complete event with indexing entities and uses query-time SQL joins to form dynamic hyperedges. It avoids pre-built static knowledge graphs for structured constraints and multi-hop reasoning.

entry.title: A Large-Scale Multi-Dimensional Empirical Study of LLMs for Conversation Summarization

author.name: Weixiao Zhou, Gengyao Li, Xianfu Cheng, Junnan Zhu, Feifei Zhai, Zhoujun Li

entry.summary: OmniCSEval is a large-scale conversation summarization benchmark with 1800 conversations across six scenarios and context lengths up to 32k tokens, using a bidirectional fact-checking framework. It evaluates frontier reasoning and small models on completeness, conciseness, and faithfulness.

entry.title: From Awareness to Adherence: Bridging the Context Gap in Spoken Dialogue Systems via Context-Aware Decoding

author.name: Che Hyun Lee, Heeseung Kim, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: Identifies a gap between latent context awareness and active adherence in spoken dialogue systems and proposes an audio-adapted Context-Aware Decoding approach contrasting output distributions with and without key historical context. It improves context adherence in multi-round conversations.

entry.title: FraudSMSWalker: Benchmarking Agentic Large Language Models for SMS-to-Webpage Fraud Detection

author.name: Y. H. Zhou, Z. M. Ma, Y. J. Zhou, Y. T. Li, H. X. Xiang, Y. M. Cheng, T. L. Chen, K. J. Zhang, Z. H. Nan, J. H. Ni, Z. Wu, Q. Y. Pan, S. Zhang, S. Cheng, M. Y. Luo

entry.summary: FraudSMSWalker is a controlled benchmark for URL-masked SMS-to-webpage fraud judgment with 699 bilingual chains, requiring models to align SMS claims with sanitized page content rather than relying on URL or domain reputation shortcuts. It evaluates agentic LLMs on cross-channel fraud detection.

entry.title: Understanding the Behaviors of Environment-aware Information Retrieval

author.name: Ruifeng Yuan, Chaohao Yuan, David Dai, Yu Rong, Hong Cheng, Hou Pong Chan, Chenghao Xiao

entry.summary: This work provides the first systematic study of how LLMs can learn via reinforcement learning to tailor query formulation strategies to different retrievers in RAG. It finds that different retrievers prefer surprisingly distinct optimal query styles.

entry.title: DEEPRUBRIC: Evidence-Tree Rubric Supervision for Efficient Reinforcement Learning of Deep Research Agents

author.name: Minghang Zhu, Chuyang Wei, Junhao Xu, Yilin Cheng, Zhumin Chen, Jiyan He

entry.summary: DeepRubric is a data construction framework that reverses the typical rubric-generation process to obtain more reliable query-rubric supervision for RL training of deep research agents. It improves RL efficiency by ensuring rubric criteria better capture task scope and evidence needs.

entry.title: VisualClaw: A Real-Time, Personalized Agent for the Physical World

author.name: Haoqin Tu, Jianwen Chen, Zijun Wang, Siwei Han, Juncheng Wu, Hardy Chen, Haonian Ji, Kaiwen Xiong, Jiaqi Liu, Peng Xia, Jieru Mei, Hongliang Fei, Jason Eshraghian, Zeyu Zheng, Yuyin Zhou, Huaxiu Yao, Cihang Xie

entry.summary: VisualClaw is a self-evolving real-time multimodal agent that uses hybrid encoding to filter uninformative video frames and compress its skill bank, plus skill evolution that learns from failures.
