A stagnation-triggered mechanism enhances exploration over classical single-operator iterated greedy.

entry.title: Occupancy-Grounded Room Segmentation for Hierarchical 3D Scene Graphs

author.name: Carlos Cueto Zumaya, Iacopo Catalano, Jorge Pe\~na-Queralta, Wallace Moreira Bessa

entry.summary: This work presents an occupancy-grounded pipeline for hierarchical 3D scene graphs where room nodes are anchored to tracked free-space regions from occupancy decomposition, giving each room an explicit polygonal footprint. It enables evaluation of room nodes on a common geometric criterion across 12 Matterport3D scenes.

entry.title: Optimality-Preserving Decomposition for Scalable QAOA in Natural-Language-Guided Multi-Drone Assignment

author.name: Junyeop Bang, Byongho Lee, Dohyun An, Hwangnam Kim

entry.summary: SyLink Hand is a linkage-driven anthropomorphic robotic hand designed from human-hand synergy analysis to balance dexterity with mechanical simplicity in a compact, low-cost form. Motion-capture data informs a simplified yet functional DOF configuration.

entry.title: CogGuard: Cognitive and Operational Profiling for Proactive Warning in Edge Intelligent Services

author.name: Zhi Yao, Weihao Chen, Zhiqing Tang, Hanshuai Cui, Qianli Ma, Weijia Jia, Wei Zhao

entry.summary: CogGuard provides cognitive and operational profiling for proactive task-completion warnings in edge intelligent services, using LLM long-context reasoning to build structured profiles under latency and privacy constraints. Aims at a reusable abstraction across service scenarios.

entry.title: Gender Differences in AI Literacy Workshop Outcomes and Deepfake Engagement

author.name: Jake Renzella, Christian Bergh, Natasha Banks, Alexandra Vassar

entry.summary: Studies gender differences in AI literacy, safety awareness, and STEM aspirations among Australian secondary students before and after a one-day AI literacy workshop, finding pre-workshop males reported higher STEM career interest across AI, CS, and engineering. Informs equitable K-12 AI curriculum design.

entry.title: Unifying Acoustic Features and Text with Multimodal LLMs for Neurodegenerative Screening

author.name: Qingfeng Zhang, Yuanxiong Guo, Yanmin Gong

entry.summary: NeurMLLM is a multimodal generative framework that unifies acoustic features and text within an LLM for staging neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. It encodes spectrograms and MFCCs via vision transformers and instruction-tunes the LLM with LoRA.

entry.title: The Reservoir Attention Network: Cross-Pass State in Pretrained Transformers via Content-Addressable Reservoir Injection

author.name: Emma Leonhart

entry.summary: A feasibility study of the Reservoir Attention Network, which injects a fixed random reservoir into mid-layer attention of pretrained transformers to carry state across forward passes, tested on GPT-2 and Qwen2.5 on a single GPU. Isolates whether untrained recurrent dynamics suffice for cross-pass state.

entry.title: Quantifying the Impact of Lossy Compression on Neural Generative Surrogate Modeling

author.name: Zhimin Li, Harshitha Menon, Charles Jekel, Valerio Pascucci, Peter Lindstrom

entry.summary: Quantifies how lossy compression of training data affects the quality of neural generative surrogate models used in scientific simulation. Characterizes inherent uncertainty and the subtle ways compression errors propagate into model quality.

entry.title: A Comparative Study of Graph Neural Network Layer Selection for Interaction Modelling in Driving Trajectory Prediction

author.name: George Daoud, Mohamed El-Darieby

entry.summary: This paper provides a comparative study of 19 graph neural network layer types for modeling spatiotemporal agent interactions in driving trajectory prediction, identifying five standout layer combinations including ARMA and Chebyshev. It offers practical architecture-design guidance for a non-standardized area.

entry.title: Dual-Network PINNs for Optimal Control: A Reproducible Benchmark on the Mass-Spring-Damper System

author.name: Abdeladhim Tahimi, Rinaldo Vieira da Silva Junior

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks a dual-network Physics-Informed Neural Network formulation for optimal control of a mass-spring-damper system against Pontryagin's Minimum Principle and direct collocation. It emphasizes transparency and reproducibility with exact boundary-condition enforcement.

entry.title: Biarchetype analysis for univariate functional data. An application to macroeconomic financial time series

author.name: Aleix Alcacer, Rafael Benitez, Vicente J. Bolos, Irene Epifanio

entry.summary: Introduces biarchetype analysis for univariate functional data, simultaneously identifying archetypal patterns across cases and time points expressed as mixtures of biarchetypes. Applies it to macroeconomic financial time series for interpretable representations.

entry.title: Hidden Degradation Costs in Energy-Cost-Only HEMS Optimisation: Study on Battery and PV Sensitivity

author.name: Dawood Butt, Nandor Verba

entry.summary: Analyzes hidden battery degradation costs in energy-cost-only home energy management system optimization using MILP-based model predictive control, studying battery and PV sensitivity. Shows that omitting degradation from the objective can lead to costly aggressive cycling strategies.

entry.title: A Dual-Branch Collaborative Framework for Joint Optimization of Underwater Image Enhancement and Object Detection

author.name: Liyuan Cao, Zheng Liu, Guanghao Liao, Yonghui Yang, Qi Li

entry.summary: A dual-branch underwater image enhancement framework jointly optimized for object detection, with a detail-enhancement branch and a color-restoration branch to balance enhancement quality, efficiency, and downstream detection. Targets practical underwater perception.

entry.title: SUP-MCRL: Subject-aware Unified Pseudo-feature Coded Multimodal Contrastive Representation Learning for EEG Visual Decoding

author.name: Shengyu Gong, Weiming Zeng, Yueyang Li, Zijian Kang, Hongjie Yan, Wai Ting Siok, Nizhuan Wang

entry.summary: SUP-MCRL is a multimodal contrastive representation learning framework for EEG-based visual decoding that adds semantic-aware visual encoding, a unified EEG enhancer, and prototype-based progressive alignment. It targets fidelity degradation and spurious zero-shot alignment when generalizing across subjects.

entry.title: MSC-CMA-ES: Structure-Aware Restarts for CMA-ES via Cyclic Nearest-Better Basin Discovery

author.name: Dimitar Nedanovski, Svetoslav Nenov, Dimitar Pilev

entry.summary: MSC-CMA-ES makes CMA-ES restarts structure-aware by partitioning a Sobol pre-sample into approximate basins via nearest-better clustering, seeding restarts basin by basin with locally scaled step and population sizes, and excluding redundant basins. It is evaluated across four CEC benchmark suites at official budgets.

entry.title: Comparison Patrols on Drifting Orders: Certified Rank Maintenance, Evolving Planar Maxima, and Selection under Drifting Fitness

author.name: Faruk Alpay, Levent Sarioglu

entry.summary: This work formulates rank-based selection under drifting fitness as a data-structure problem, introducing a comparison patrol that maintains an order under adjacent transpositions using one truthful pairwise comparison per step. It provides certified rank maintenance with deterministic verification-age bounds for evolving planar maxima and selection.

entry.title: ChatPlanner: A Large Language Model Framework for Personalized Public Transit Routing

author.name: Tingting Yang, Chenhao Xue, Jun Chen

entry.summary: ChatPlanner uses fine-tuned LLMs with RAG to extract routing parameters and interpret user preferences for personalized public transit routing, integrating them into the routing objective. Designs preference-aware datasets with personas and contexts.

entry.title: Unassigned Agents in Compilation-based Multi-agent Path Finding

author.name: Pavel Surynek

entry.summary: Studies compilation-based solvers for multi-agent path finding with unassigned agents, where some agents have no goal but must be moved out of the way. Extends MAPF to a relevant non-standard variant.

entry.title: Sensor-Conditioned Representation Learning via Scene-Relevant Observation Quotients

author.name: Yan Jiao, Pin-Han Ho, Limei Peng

entry.summary: Formalizes sensor-conditioned representation correctness via a scene-relevant observation quotient that preserves sensing-supported distinctions while suppressing nuisance variation. Targets intelligent sensing systems where reconstruction accuracy alone fails to specify justified latent distinctions.

entry.title: Integrating Multi-Label Classification and Generative AI for Scalable Analysis of User Feedback

author.name: Sandra Loop, Erik Bertram, Sebastian Juhl, Martin Schrepp

entry.summary: Combines multi-label classification with generative AI to scalably analyze large volumes of open-ended UX user feedback, developed during a long-term measurement project at a major software company. Aims to efficiently process and interpret extensive user comments alongside standardized questionnaires.

entry.title: Momentum-Guided Semantic Forecasting (MoFore) for Self-Supervised Video Representation Learning

author.name: Qinwu Xu

entry.summary: MoFore introduces a self-supervised video representation learning method that learns temporally predictive latent representations via momentum-guided semantic forecasting, rather than pixel reconstruction or task-specific alignment. It positions itself as an alternative to MAE/VideoMAE and CLIP-style approaches.

entry.title: MatchLM2Lite: A Scalable MLLM-to-Lite Framework for Reproduced Content Identification

author.name: Xiaotian Fan, Hiok Hian Ong, David Yuchen Wang, Zirui Zhu, Kanchan Sarkar, Kun Xu

entry.summary: MatchLM2Lite is a production-grade reproduced-content identification system that distills a multimodal LLM into a small fast model to detect duplicated/low-value videos at scale. It jointly models video, audio, and text to produce fine-grained reproduction scores.

entry.title: Bridging Geographic Bias in Urban Streetscape Inference via Lifelong Learning with Visual-Semantic Pivoting

author.name: Xinze Zhang

entry.summary: HVSP-LL is a lifelong learning framework that reduces geographic bias in urban streetscape inference using stratified visual-semantic pivoting and equity-aware rehearsal. It aligns image features to a three-tier landscape ontology to resist distributional drift across underrepresented districts.

entry.title: Intrinsic Computational Functionalism and Simulated Consciousness

author.name: Ryota Kanai, Shuqin Ma

entry.summary: A philosophical/theoretical paper extending Intrinsic Computational Functionalism to argue whether simulated brains could be conscious, building on prior Canonical Functionalism work. It is conceptual rather than empirical.

entry.title: Runtime Analysis of Cartesian Genetic Programming in Evolving Boolean Functions

author.name: Duc-Cuong Dang, Roman Kalkreuth, Andre Opris

entry.summary: Provides the first runtime analysis of Cartesian Genetic Programming for evolving Boolean functions, proving asymptotic bounds on expected fitness evaluations under different selection schemes. Offers theoretical explanations for empirically observed CGP behaviors.

entry.title: Orchestrated Reality: From Role-Play to Living, Playable Game Worlds -- LLM-Driven World Simulation as a Parameterized-Action POMDP

author.name: Yuhang Huang, Chenmiao Li, Chaowei Fang

entry.summary: Frames LLM-driven game world simulation as a parameterized-action POMDP, aiming to sustain persistent validated world state alongside narrative generation. Addresses the gap where current systems assert state in free prose without a verified representation.

entry.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Medical Image Segmentation: Challenges, Benchmarks, and Beyond

author.name: Pengyu Zhu, Xiaojing Zhang, Kunbo Zhang, Chunyan Zhang, Zhenyu Wang

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey of medical image segmentation organizing U-Net, Transformer, and SAM-based methods within a unified analytical framework, alongside datasets, metrics, and challenges. Distinguishes itself from single-family surveys by cross-comparing architectures.

entry.title: How Much Do Reviews Really Contribute? A Study on Text-Enriched Matrix Factorization for Recommendations

author.name: Eduardo Ferreira da Silva, Mayki dos Santos Oliveira, Joel Machado Pires Denis Dantas Boaventura, Frederico Ara\'ujo Dur\~ao

entry.summary: This study systematically investigates how much textual reviews truly contribute to matrix-factorization recommenders against strong collaborative baselines, introducing a learnable gating mechanism for two review representations. It questions the real value of review-derived signals.

entry.title: Machine learning enables roughness-driven inverse design of milling processes

author.name: Hadi Bakhshan, Sima Farshbaf, Fernando Rastellini, Josep Maria Carbonell

entry.summary: Proposes a machine-learning framework for inverse design of milling processes targeting surface roughness, using forward-trained DNN and random forest models. Addresses limited datasets and robustness challenges in manufacturing inverse design.

entry.title: Semi-Supervised Speech Confidence Detection using Pseudo-Labelling and Whisper Embeddings

author.name: Adam Wynn, Jingyun Wang, Xiangyu Tan

entry.summary: Introduces a semi-supervised framework for detecting speaker confidence in educational settings, combining human-engineered speech features (pitch, volume, rate, disfluencies) with Whisper encoder embeddings via co-attention, using pseudo-labelling to expand limited labeled data. Achieves 75% accuracy.

entry.title: GOOSE-M2F: Adapting Mask2Former for High-Fidelity, Long-Tailed Fine-Grained Semantic Segmentation in Unstructured Outdoor Terrain

author.name: Jyothiraditya Lingam, Nikhileswara Rao Sulake, Sai Manikanta Eswar Machara

entry.summary: GOOSE-M2F adapts Mask2Former for fine-grained semantic segmentation of unstructured outdoor terrain with 64 long-tailed classes, adding more object queries, a feature refinement module, and auxiliary supervision plus rare-class augmentation. Targets the GOOSE ICRA 2026 challenge.

entry.title: Towards UAV Image Dehazing: A UAV Atmospheric Scattering Model, Benchmark, and Geometry-Aware Deep Unfolding Network

author.name: Wenxuan Fang, Jiangwei Weng, Yu Zheng, Junkai Fan, Guangfa Wang, Xiang Chen, Jian Yang, Jun Li

entry.summary: This work proposes a UAV-specific atmospheric scattering model that accounts for flight altitude and pitch to handle non-uniform haze, plus a benchmark and a geometry-aware deep unfolding dehazing network. It targets the spatially varying heavy haze unique to aerial imaging.

entry.title: Hierarchical Fine-Grained Aerial Object Detection

author.name: Yan Zhang, Fang Xu, Wen Yang, Gui-Song Xia

entry.summary: ExpertDet enhances fine-grained aerial object detection by incorporating expert-informed structured priors such as attributes and category hierarchies to distinguish model-level categories with subtle differences. It uses vision-aware masked attention to leverage multi-granularity semantics.

entry.title: Structure-aware Knowledge-guided Heterogeneous Mamba for Zygomaticomaxillary Suture Assessment

author.name: Xiaoqi Guo, Birui Chen, Xinquan Yang, Chaoyun Zhang, Xuefen Liu, Mianjie Zheng, Kun Tang, Xuguang Li, Wen Ma, Yanhua Xu, Linlin Shen

entry.summary: SKMamba is a structure-aware, knowledge-guided Mamba-based multi-modal framework for automated staging of zygomaticomaxillary suture maturation, accompanied by the first public ZMS dataset of 3,790 images spanning ages 4 to 24. It targets subtle high-frequency suture transitions and semantic ambiguity between adjacent maturation stages.

entry.title: Variable-Rate Deep Image Compression based on Low-Rank Adaptation by Progressive Learning

author.name: Xing-Yu Xu, Chen-Hsiu Huang, Ja-Ling Wu

entry.summary: This work proposes variable-rate deep image compression using low-rank adaptation with progressive learning, enabling a single model to achieve multiple compression rates efficiently. It avoids deploying multiple networks or incurring the higher computational cost of prior single-model approaches.

entry.title: Impedance MPC with Patient-Torque Estimation for Knee Rehabilitation Exoskeletons

author.name: Yongyan Cao, Jinshan Tang

entry.summary: This paper presents an Impedance Model Predictive Control framework with patient-torque estimation for knee rehabilitation exoskeletons on a series-elastic-actuator platform. An algebraic feedforward reduces dynamics to a scalar double integrator and a receding-horizon QP enforces hard range-of-motion, torque, and velocity limits per ISO 13482 safety standards.

entry.title: Kine2Go: Kinematic dataset for the Unitree Go2 robot with diverse gaits and motions

author.name: W{\l}adys{\l}aw Pa{\l}ucki, Pawe{\l} Siwak, Krzysztof Ciebiera, Marek Cygan

entry.summary: Kine2Go is a kinematic dataset for the widely used Unitree Go2 quadruped covering diverse gaits and motions, intended to support imitation learning, RL, and behavioral cloning research. It lowers the barrier to obtaining demonstration data for this popular platform.

entry.title: AI-Driven Framework for Adaptive Water Network Management with Proof-of-Concept Implementation: Addressing Non-Revenue Water in Jordan

author.name: Mohammed Fasha, Nahel Al-Maayta, Bilal Sowan, Mohammad Athamneh, Husam Barham

entry.summary: Proposes an AI framework integrating EPANET hydraulic modeling, digital twins, SCADA, and LLM agents with RAG and function calling to manage non-revenue water in Jordan's water networks. Provides a proof-of-concept for adaptive water management.

entry.title: EcoBin: A Two-Stage Deep Convolutional Neural Network for Contamination-Aware Waste Classification

author.name: Raghav Senthil Kumar

entry.summary: EcoBin is a two-stage CNN that classifies household waste by disposal pathway and overrides recycling decisions when contamination is detected, addressing a gap where accurate classifiers ignore contamination. Uses an EfficientNetV2-S backbone.

entry.title: MVOFormer: Flow-Semantic Transformer for Robust Monocular Visual Odometry

author.name: Jituo Li, Shunwang Sun, Jialu Zhang, Xinqi Liu, Jinyao Hu, Zhicheng Lu, Sajad Saeedi, Guodong Lu

entry.summary: MVOFormer is a transformer framework for robust monocular visual odometry that fuses dense optical-flow geometric cues with object-centric semantic priors to distinguish static structures from dynamic distractors. An iterative multimodal decoder improves cross-domain generalization.

entry.title: Latent Space Reinforcement Learning for Inverse Material Estimation in Food Fracture Simulation

author.name: Adrian Ramlal, Yuhao Chen, John S. Zelek

entry.summary: This paper tackles inverse estimation of food material parameters from fracture behavior in a non-differentiable continuum damage simulator, using orange peeling as a test case. It trains a neural surrogate on 2,000 simulations and compares CMA-ES versus PPO across original and learned latent parameter spaces.

entry.title: Effective and Low-cost Lane-based Map Localization for Vehicle-Centric Route Generation

author.name: Hong-Shiang Lin, Jung-Hsin Chen, Yu-Luen Tzeng, Wei-Hao Chen, Yi-Chen Lee, Li-Jhe Chen, Peng-Yuan Chen

entry.summary: OLRA is a low-cost map-localization framework that derives driver-view-aligned routes by matching map navigation routes with camera-detected lane markings, mutually improving localization accuracy and route consistency. It introduces practical route evaluation metrics and outperforms OpenPilot in complex road segments on nuScenes.

entry.title: Evolution & Foundation: AI Shares Creative Control

author.name: Dylan Banarse, Stephen Todd, William Latham, Frederic Fol Leymarie

entry.summary: This work integrates genetic algorithms with the visual reasoning of multimodal AI foundation models to evolve aesthetically pleasing complex 3D organic forms. It reframes the artist's role from direct selection to system design, delegating step-by-step aesthetic curation to an AI agent capable of multimodal judgement.

entry.title: What Robots Do Matters More Than What They Look Like: Task Context Shapes Trust in Educational HRI

author.name: Anna-Maria Velentza, Konstantina Nikou, Anne-Gwenn Bosser, Nikolaos Fachantidis

entry.summary: A within-subjects study (N=81) examining how robot appearance and task type jointly shape trust in educational human-robot interaction, finding that task context matters more than appearance. It informs design choices for socially assistive robots.

entry.title: A Definition of Good Explanations and the Challenges Explaining LLM Outputs

author.name: Louis Mahon, Elliot Ford, Callum Hackett

entry.summary: This paper proposes a philosophical definition of good explanations grounded in counterfactual reasoning while accounting for an interlocutor's prior beliefs, then applies it to argue why LLM outputs are particularly hard to explain. It contributes conceptual clarity to the explainability debate rather than new technical methods.

entry.title: Posterior Twins: Distributional Behavioral Simulation for Enterprise Decisions

author.name: Ankit Das (Twinning Labs)

entry.summary: Posterior Twins presents a memory-grounded digital-twin approach representing likely population behavior as distributions under specific decision contexts for enterprise decisions. Evaluates modal accuracy and Wasserstein-1 distance, showing these identify different operating regimes.

entry.title: Poster: EdgeCitadel -- Hybrid NATS-MQTT Orchestration for Edge Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Zhonghao Zhan, Yefan Zhang, Hamed Haddadi

entry.summary: EdgeCitadel is an edge multi-agent orchestration platform built around a single NATS server with built-in MQTT adapter, combining MQTT connectivity, JetStream persistence/replay, peer delegation, and a passive aggregator. Targets coordination of edge-resident AI agents across heterogeneous devices without cloud-style transports.

entry.title: XMedFusion: A Knowledge-Guided Multimodal Perception and Reasoning Framework for Autonomous Medical Systems

author.name: Hamza Riaz, Arham Haroon, Maha Baig, Muhammad Dawood Rizwan, Muhammad Naseer Bajwa, Muhammad Moazam Fraz

entry.summary: XMedFusion is a modular, knowledge-guided multimodal framework for radiology report generation that decomposes visual reasoning into expert-like agents to improve visual grounding. It aims to reduce unreliable interpretations and omission of subtle clinical findings in autonomous medical systems.

entry.title: Teacher-Student Structure for Domain Adaptation in Ensemble Audio-Visual Video Deepfake Detection

author.name: Elham Abolhasani, Maryam Ramezani, Hamid R. Rabiee

entry.summary: EAV-DFD is a deep ensemble audio-visual deepfake detection model with a teacher-student domain adaptation mechanism to improve cross-domain generalization. It fuses audio, image, and interaction features to detect manipulated media.

entry.title: Provenance-Enhanced Statements in Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Fabio Vitali, Valentina Pasqual

entry.summary: This paper introduces DEC, a framework that interprets provenance predicates in knowledge graphs as indicators of epistemic stance and groups provenance-homogeneous statements into cognitive worlds. It draws on cognitive modal logic to relate attributed claims to factual commitment and reasoning.

entry.title: MADAR: An Address-Free Processor

author.name: Mohamed Amine Bergach

entry.summary: MADAR proposes a radically different address-free processor architecture where state circulates in rings of slots and values are named by position in an orbit rather than by address, with compile-time scheduling replacing cache hierarchies. A speculative computer-architecture concept.

entry.title: IoT-Zoo: A Container-Based Framework for Heterogeneous IoT Device Profiles and Reproducible Traffic Capture

author.name: Vagner E. Quincozes, Diego Kreutz, Silvio E. Quincozes

entry.summary: IoT-Zoo is a container-based testbed built on Containernet for reproducible experimentation with heterogeneous, dataset-driven IoT device profiles supporting real protocols like MQTT and RTSP. Aims to improve realism and reproducibility in IoT networking/security research.

entry.title: Contextual Bandits for Maximizing Stimulated Word-of-Mouth Rewards

author.name: Ahmed Sayeed Faruk, Elena Zheleva

entry.summary: Proposes a contextual multi-armed bandit framework for optimizing stimulated word-of-mouth marketing by estimating heterogeneous spillover probabilities across social network connections. It targets users most likely to spread influence beyond their immediate audience.

entry.title: On the Entropy Formula for Real, Complex, and Quaternionic Deep Linear Networks

author.name: Luis Contreras, Marco Nahas, Tejas Kotwal

entry.summary: This theoretical paper extends an existing entropy formula for real deep linear networks to complex and quaternionic variants, providing a unified formula across the three number systems. It is a mathematical contribution to deep learning theory.

entry.title: If These Walls Could Talk: Critical Play with Large Language Models in Museums

author.name: Anders Sundnes L{\o}vlie

entry.summary: A reflective design paper identifying a fundamental dilemma in using LLM role-playing chatbots in museums: they cannot be trusted to tell the truth, yet attempts to make them reliable may diminish their engaging conversational appeal. Proposes designing for critical play with intentionally unreliable bots.

entry.title: Deep Temporal Modeling and Ensemble Fusion for Multimodal Emotion Recognition from Physiological Signals

author.name: Desta Haileselassie Hagos, Saurav Keshari Aryal, Patrick Ymele-Leki, Anietie Andy, Legand L. Burge

entry.summary: Evaluates LSTM, TCN, and Transformer models with early and late fusion for multimodal emotion and stress recognition from wrist and chest physiological signals on WESAD. It includes per-modality ablations and ensemble fusion.

entry.title: Enhancing Precision Agriculture with a Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Multi-Class Plant Disease Classification and Interpretability

author.name: Hasibul Islam Sufi, Ridam Roy, Shayla Alam Setu, Mahimul Islam Nadim

entry.summary: This study proposes a hybrid ResNet plus Vision Transformer architecture for multi-class plant disease classification across 38 classes, with interpretability analysis, compared against ResNet-50, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNet-B0. It targets precision agriculture applications.

entry.title: Sustainable Face Recognition on Low-Power Devices with VQ-VAE Embeddings

author.name: Christos Chronis, Georgios Th. Papadopoulos, Iraklis Varlamis

entry.summary: Proposes an energy-efficient, edge-deployable face recognition system using VQ-VAE embeddings combined with knowledge distillation from pretrained face models. It targets sustainability and reduced carbon footprint while retaining competitive accuracy.

entry.title: Ellipse Meets Bit-Planes: A Novel Approach to RNFL based Glaucoma Detection Using Advanced Image Processing and Deep Learning

author.name: Snigdha Paul, Sambit Mallick, Anindya Sen

entry.summary: Proposes a glaucoma detection pipeline using ellipse-based polar transformation of fundus images and two frameworks: a deep feature-fusion approach reaching 99.3% detection and a lightweight bit-plane image-processing approach. Targets accessible RNFL-based screening.

entry.title: Stringalign: Moving beyond summary statistics with a transparent Unicode-aware tool for evaluating automatic transcription models

author.name: Yngve Mardal Moe, Marie Roald

entry.summary: Stringalign is a Unicode-aware Python library for transparent, reproducible evaluation of automatic transcription models (HTR, OCR, ASR), moving beyond summary error statistics to visualize error types. Aims to improve evaluation transparency in transcription projects.

entry.title: RGFVR: Reference-Guided Face Video Restoration with Flow Matching

author.name: Cem Eteke, Batuhan Tosun, Eckehard Steinbach

entry.summary: RGFVR is a subject-agnostic, reference-guided face video restoration framework that injects bimodal perceptual-descriptive identity conditioning into a pretrained flow-based text-to-video generator. A two-stage training strategy strengthens identity preservation while generalizing to unseen identities.

entry.title: MVM-IOD: An Industrial Object-Centric Benchmark Dataset for the Evaluation of 3D Reconstruction Methods

author.name: Robert Langend\"orfer, Markus Hillemann, Markus Ulrich

entry.summary: MVM-IOD is an industrial object-centric benchmark dataset for evaluating 3D reconstruction and camera pose estimation, captured systematically via a robot-mounted camera on a hemisphere around objects. It provides reference camera poses and 3D point clouds for realistic industrial metrology scenarios.

entry.title: Explainable Task-Oriented Token Communication for AI-Native 6G Networks

author.name: Feibo Jiang, Lei Mao, Li Dong, Kezhi Wang, Cunhua Pan, Jiangzhou Wang

entry.summary: ET-TokenCom is an explainable task-oriented token communication framework that treats tokens as unified units for information representation and transmission in AI-native 6G networks. It addresses insufficient token representation, weak visual-task token collaboration, and limited interpretability in task-oriented image communication.

entry.title: Effects of Objective Normalization on Regions of Interest in Preference-Based Evolutionary Multi-Objective Optimization

author.name: Ryuichi Mogami, Ryoji Tanabe

entry.summary: This paper investigates how objective normalization affects regions of interest in preference-based evolutionary multi-objective optimization, showing that ROIs defined in unnormalized versus normalized objective spaces can differ significantly. It highlights an overlooked standardization issue in the EMO community.

entry.title: Short-Horizon Position Accuracy of Single-Track Models: Implications for Motion Planning of Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Aron J. Aertssen, Lars A. T. H. van Alen, Igo J. M. Besselink, Rudolf G. M. Huisman, Ren\'e M. J. G. van de Molengraft

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates short-horizon positional accuracy of three single-track vehicle models against real instrumented vehicle measurements across maneuvers. It provides practical guidance on model-complexity trade-offs for AV motion planning.

entry.title: SCAN: A Decision-Making Framework for Effective Task Allocation with Generative AI

author.name: Fendi Tsim, Alina Gutoreva

entry.summary: SCAN is a human-centric framework based on Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development to help learners allocate tasks between themselves and generative AI across four sub-zones (Substitute, Complement, Aid, Non-negotiable). Connects to cognitive load and metacognition theories.

entry.title: An Exploratory Study of Blood Glucose Estimation from Photoplethysmography Signals using Machine Learning

author.name: Ruhani Bhatia, Vijval Ekbote

entry.summary: An exploratory study using machine learning to estimate blood glucose non-invasively from photoplethysmography signals captured by wearables. Aims toward scalable, non-invasive continuous glucose monitoring.

entry.title: Rotational Symmetry based Object Pose Estimation from Point Clouds in the Absence of Known 3D Models

author.name: Weichen Dai, Ruixun Yu, Yangjie Tang, Yifan Du, Yiyang Zhang, Donglei Sun, Hua Zhang

entry.summary: This method estimates object pose from point clouds without known 3D models by exploiting rotational symmetry common in industrial objects as prior information. Pose is jointly estimated with point-cloud refinement through iterative optimization.

entry.title: Polyp-D2ATL: Deep Domain-Adaptive Transfer Learning for Colorectal Polyp Classification under Label Distribution Shift

author.name: Sajad Jabarzadeh Ghandilu, Maryam Sadat Hosseini Azad, Shahriar Baradaran Shokouhi, Emad Fatemizadeh

entry.summary: Polyp-D2ATL is a deep domain-adaptive transfer learning framework with a tailored training strategy for colorectal polyp classification under label distribution shift, imbalanced data, and cross-modality generalization. It targets accurate prediction of difficult NICE-classification polyps in real-world scenarios.

entry.title: The Integrator Advantage: Controlled Agentic AI for Small and Medium-Sized Companies

author.name: Christopner Koch, Joshua A. Wellbrock

entry.summary: Argues that near-term value of agentic AI for small and medium companies lies in controlled partial autonomy rather than full autonomy, proposing an integration framework covering use-case suitability, autonomy levels, and technical integration. Frames agentic systems as administrative-burden reducers for SMEs.

entry.title: Mask Proposal Voting Based on Geodesic Framework for Robust Image Segmentation

author.name: Li Liu, Mingzhu Wang, Zhenjiang Li, Da Chen, Laurent D. Cohen

entry.summary: This paper proposes a mask proposal voting framework built on a geodesic minimal-path model to overcome sensitivity to initialization in image segmentation. It constructs adaptive domain cuts to constrain initialization and enable robust segmentation in cluttered scenes.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Attention for Automated Disaster Damage Assessment Using Remote Sensing Imagery and Deep Learning

author.name: Tewodros Syum Gebre, Jagrati Talreja, Leila Hashemi-Beni

entry.summary: This paper presents a multi-modal attention framework for automated building damage assessment from pre- and post-disaster satellite imagery, classifying buildings into four damage levels. It uses a lightweight ConvNeXT-Tiny backbone and bi-temporal feature fusion for efficient change detection.

entry.title: Cognitive Trajectory Modeling: Quantifying Human-AI Co-Creation through Cognitively Grounded Interaction Trajectories

author.name: Nicholas Davis

entry.summary: Introduces Cognitive Trajectory Modeling, a theoretical framework conceptualizing human-AI co-creation as dynamics evolving across cognitive attractor landscapes. Aims to capture higher-order interaction reorganization over time.

entry.title: The algebra of Krom logic programs

author.name: Christian Anti\'c

entry.summary: Investigates the algebraic structure of Krom logic programs (facts and rules with at most one body atom), showing sequential composition yields monoid structure with extensions to various seminearrings and connections to finite-state automata. A pure logic-programming theory paper.

entry.title: NVMOS: Non-Verbal Vocalization Quality Assessment in Speech

author.name: Jialong Mai, Jinxin Ji, Xiaofen Xing, Wencui Liu, Xiangmin Xu

entry.summary: Introduces NV-MOS, a dataset and evaluation approach for assessing the perceptual quality of non-verbal vocalizations like laughter and sighs in synthesized speech, an area prior work neglected. It also shows that audio-capable multimodal LLMs like Gemini disagree with expert human ratings.

entry.title: A comparative and critical study of EEGNet for fNIRS-driven cognitive load classification

author.name: Mehshan Ahmed Khan, Houshyar Asadi, Li Zhang, Mohammad reza Chalak Qazani, Ghazal Bargshady, Stefanos gkikas, Christian arzate, Sam Oladazimi, Zoran Najdovsk, Lei Wei, Chee Peng Lim

entry.summary: Comparative critical study of EEGNet applied to fNIRS-based cognitive load classification, systematically examining segmentation strategies, window lengths, feature extraction, learning rates, and evaluation protocols. Highlights sensitivity to preprocessing and evaluation choices.

entry.title: NeuronFabric: A Software Reference Architecture for On-Chip Transformer Training with Local Adam

author.name: Evgeny Ukladchikov

entry.summary: Presents NeuronFabric, a software reference architecture for on-chip transformer training with local Adam updates intended for future FPGA/ASIC implementation, validated through a C# prototype on a 334K-parameter model. Aims to validate numerical correctness and memory requirements before hardware implementation.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quality of VGGT: An Analysis on the DTU Benchmark Dataset

author.name: Markus Hillemann, Robert Langend\"orfer, Steven Landgraf, Markus Ulrich

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the quality of uncertainty estimates produced by VGGT, a feed-forward transformer for 3D reconstruction, using the DTU benchmark. It matters for photogrammetry applications that need reliable confidence measures, not just point predictions.

entry.title: Semantic Reasoning in Medicine: The Role of Knowledge Graphs Across Five Key Domains

author.name: Haniye Sherafatmandjoo, Mohammad Akbari, Zahed Rahmati

entry.summary: A survey of how knowledge graphs support semantic reasoning across five biomedical domains including clinical decision support, outcome prediction, and medical QA. Highlights their role in interpretability and patient-specific reasoning.

entry.title: Robust Transformer-Based One-Step Stock Index Forecasting via Shifted Data Augmentation

author.name: Tien Thanh Thach

entry.summary: Proposes a modified Transformer for one-step stock index forecasting with a novel Shifted Data Augmentation technique and learning-rate scheduling, evaluated on VN30 and S&P 500. Shows cosine annealing with warmup and SDA reduce forecasting error and run-to-run variability.

entry.title: Transfer Learning for FHIR Questionnaire Terminology Binding

author.name: Maxim Gorshkov

entry.summary: Treats FHIR Questionnaire-to-LOINC code binding as a retrieval problem and benchmarks six methods including TF-IDF, BioBERT, BioLORD, and contrastive fine-tuning on a small 54-item healthcare evaluation set. Finds no single method dominates, with biomedical-pretrained encoders performing best on top-rank accuracy.

entry.title: Evaluative Judgement in Teaching AI-based Translation: A Class-room Case Study of AI-Mediated Translation and Post-Editing

author.name: Gokhan Dogru

entry.summary: A classroom case study of 23 student translation projects examining how structured comparison of LLMs and MT systems develops evaluative judgement in AI-mediated translation and post-editing. It reports descriptive and qualitative findings on student decision-making.

entry.title: ttda704 at SemEval-2026 Task 6: Structured Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Political Evasion Detection

author.name: Tai Tran Tan, An Dinh Thien

entry.summary: A SemEval-2026 system paper comparing QLoRA fine-tuning of Qwen3 models against structured chain-of-thought prompting of reasoning models for detecting political evasion in interview Q&A. It finds CoT prompting outperforms the fine-tuning baseline.

entry.title: AI for Maritime Security: Comparative Evaluation of CNN and Vision Transformer Architectures for Maritime Object Detection

author.name: Ismet Gocer, Zakirul Bhuiayn, Shakeel Ahmad, Raza Hasan

entry.summary: This study compares CNN, transfer learning, and Vision Transformer architectures for detecting ships under varied weather conditions using a 6,468-image maritime dataset. It evaluates six deep learning models for maritime security applications.

entry.title: Segmentation-based Detection for Efficient Multi-Task Spacecraft Perception

author.name: Sivaperuman Muniyasamy, Surendar Devasundaram

entry.summary: A compact MobileNetV3+U-Net architecture for unified spacecraft classification, detection, and component segmentation under challenging space imaging conditions, submitted to the SPARK 2026 Challenge. Targets efficient multi-task on-orbit perception with scarce annotated data.

entry.title: When the Past Matters: FlashBack Memory for Precipitation Nowcasting

author.name: Yuhao Du, Boxiao Huang, Chengrong Wu, Jiankai Zhang

entry.summary: FlashBack Memory is a plug-in module that dynamically retrieves key historical states and fuses them via an adaptive gate to improve recurrent precipitation nowcasting models. Tested across PredRNN variants and three datasets, it improves standard forecasting metrics, especially for high-intensity rainfall events.

entry.title: Beer-Lambert Guided Representation Learning for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Sub-THz Food Inspection Images

author.name: Gyutae Hwang, Sang Jun Lee

entry.summary: This work introduces a Beer-Lambert guided representation learning framework for unsupervised anomaly detection in sub-THz food inspection images, using an attenuation decomposition module as auxiliary regularization. It aims to capture transmission-specific characteristics that RGB-pretrained models miss.

entry.title: Decoupled Object-Centric Video Understanding for Generating Robotic Manipulation Commands

author.name: Thanh Nguyen Canh, Thanh-Tuan Tran, Haolan Zhang, Ziyan Gao, Xiem HoangVan, Nak Young Chong

entry.summary: This framework decouples action recognition from object identification to generate precise grammar-free robotic manipulation commands from human video demonstrations. It uses Temporal Shift Modules for action classification and a novel object selection algorithm based on trajectory roles and blur/overlap heuristics.

entry.title: You need to know about the Baruch Plan

author.name: aggliu

entry.summary: A historical essay recounting the 1946 Baruch Plan, where the US proposed placing atomic technology under international control only to be blocked by the USSR, drawing implicit parallels to contemporary debates over an AI pause. It uses nuclear history to inform AI governance thinking.

entry.title: ttda704 at SemEval-2026 Task 4: Modeling Narrative Structures via Pseudonymization and Multi-View Sentence Alignment

author.name: Tai Tran Tan, An Dinh Thien

entry.summary: A SemEval-2026 system for narrative story similarity using contrastive learning with fine-tuned sentence transformers, including single-view and multi-view (theme, plot, outcome) pipelines trained on synthetic data. It applies self-supervised alignment and layer freezing.

entry.title: Active Reference Acquisition in Few-Shot Font Generation

author.name: Shinnosuke Matsuo

entry.summary: This paper proposes an active reference acquisition framework for few-shot font generation where the model sequentially decides which characters to request when current references inadequately represent a style. It shifts focus from fixed reference sets to adaptive reference selection.

entry.title: A Security Analysis of Long-Horizon Agentic AI Systems: Threats, Evaluation, and Framework Development

author.name: Ahmed Mohammed Almalki, Mehedi Masud

entry.summary: This is a structured review and taxonomy of security threats in long-horizon agentic AI systems, covering attack propagation mechanisms and evaluation approaches. It proposes a framework for analyzing how attacks propagate across agent workflows.

entry.title: Mojo: A Promising Tool for Scalable Financial AI Efficiency

author.name: Henry Han

entry.summary: Surveys Mojo, Modular's Python-like systems language, as a structural solution to the two-language tax in quantitative finance, enabling bit-exact deterministic kernels for reproducible backtests. Highlights MLIR compilation for performance and auditability.

entry.title: Optimising Temporary Accommodation Placement Across London with AI-Powered SaaS in E-Governance Systems

author.name: Hankun He, Jordan Richards, Gopalakrishnan Netuveli, Kumar Aniket, Ramya Pachatcharam, Binta Ade-olusile, Nathan Nagaiah, Matthew I Bellgard

entry.summary: DOMUS is a cloud-based, AI-enabled decision-support SaaS built for a London borough to optimize statutory temporary accommodation placement, combining rule-based filtering with LLM-assisted search of live rental listings. It addresses a major fiscal pressure on English local authorities.

entry.title: Decomposing one-class support vector machine into an ensemble of one-data support vector machines

author.name: Toshitaka Hayashi, Dalibor Cimr, Hamido Fujita, Richard Cimler

entry.summary: Proposes accelerating one-class SVM by decomposing the dataset into single-data-point SVMs combined via ensemble learning, with further speedup from averaging-based data reduction. Addresses OCSVM scalability on large datasets.

entry.title: Instance-Aware Knowledge Distillation for Semi-Supervised Learning of an On-Board Multi-Task Dense Prediction Model for Collision Avoidance System

author.name: Gyutae Hwang, Sang Jun Lee

entry.summary: This paper presents an instance-aware knowledge distillation framework for semi-supervised training of a lightweight multi-task dense prediction model used in edge-deployed collision avoidance systems. Pseudo-labels mitigate teacher bias by combining domain priors with foundation-model knowledge.

entry.title: Hybrid NARX-LLM for Greenland Iceberg Discharge: Prompt-Driven Residual Correction

author.name: Yiquan Gao, Duohui Xu

entry.summary: This paper presents a hybrid NARX-LLM framework for Greenland iceberg discharge prediction, where a NARX model captures temporal dependencies and an LLM performs residual correction guided by physics-informed prompts. It explores using structured physical knowledge prompts for zero-shot in-context reasoning rather than just maximizing accuracy.

entry.title: Machine Learning and the Random Walk Puzzle: Forecasting the CAD/USD Exchange Rate with Expanding Window Evaluation and SHAP Interpretability

author.name: Louis Agyekum, Edmund Fosu Agyemang, Obu-Amoah Ampomah, Kofi Acheampong, Emmanuel Boadi, Priscilla Yaa Amakye, Fafa Shalom Tchorly, Enock Adu Bonsu, Eric Nyarko

entry.summary: This study evaluates whether five machine learning models can beat the naive random walk benchmark in forecasting the monthly USD/CAD exchange rate using an expanding-window framework and SHAP interpretability, with Diebold-Mariano tests. It revisits the classic random-walk forecasting puzzle.

entry.title: Simulation-Based Multi-Fillet Evaluation of Woody Breast Poultry Fillets

author.name: Chirantan Sen Mukherjee, Seung-Chul Yoon, William J. Beksi

entry.summary: This work proposes a multi-fillet detection architecture using a top-down camera to overcome the single-fillet throughput bottleneck in woody breast poultry inspection. It first builds a high-fidelity digital twin of an industrial conveyor system to validate the approach.

entry.title: ForestBack: Breadcrumb-Based Pedestrian Dead Reckoning for Infrastructure-Free Return Navigation

author.name: Aueaphum Aueawatthanaphisut, Chanakan Chaipan

entry.summary: ForestBack is an infrastructure-free pedestrian return-navigation system using breadcrumb-based dead reckoning, integrating step detection, adaptive step-length, magnetometer heading, and barometric altitude for reverse-path guidance in GPS-denied environments. It requires no external positioning infrastructure.

entry.title: Quantum Machine Learning for Industrial Applications

author.name: L\'eo Monbroussou

entry.summary: This thesis surveys the theoretical foundations of quantum machine learning for industrial applications, focusing on trainability, expressivity, and resistance to classical simulation of variational quantum circuits. It examines near-term and future practical applications.

entry.title: Transformation-driven generation of comparable projection images from multimodal anatomical scenes

author.name: Dariusz Pojda, Krzysztof Domino, Micha{\l} Tarnawski, Agnieszka Anna Tomaka

entry.summary: This work presents a transformation-driven framework for generating reproducible projection-space images from heterogeneous anatomical scenes whose components undergo independent spatial transformations, demonstrated on mandibular motion. It treats projection imaging as an observation process over an explicitly represented anatomical scene rather than a registration or rendering task.

entry.title: How reality turns to slop

author.name: julius vidal

entry.summary: Introduces the concept of 'hyperslopification', a feedback loop where hyperpalatable AI-generated slop shifts cultural norms and the Overton window, which then re-enters AI training data, pushing culture toward simpler, more cartoonish forms. It is a speculative cultural-dynamics argument with anecdotal examples.

entry.title: Double-Helix Vision (DH-V2): A Geometry-Based Visual Sampler for Bandwidth-Constrained Perception

author.name: Jinwen Wen

entry.summary: Double-Helix Vision is a geometry-based, neural-network-free visual sampler that compresses images into compact 1D signals using paired golden-ratio spiral trajectories with foveated sampling. It claims extreme compression and sub-millisecond CPU-only perception pipelines.

entry.title: Leveraging Deep Learning for Object and Position Recognition of Load Carriers for Autonomous Logistics Vehicles

entry.title: LLM-Based Visual Explanation Evaluation Framework for Assessing the Explainability of Facial Skin Disease Classification Models

author.name: Gyuyeon Na

entry.summary: This study proposes a domain-specific LLM-based framework to evaluate the explainability of facial skin disease classifiers by assessing whether Grad-CAM explanations are grounded in clinically relevant lesion regions. entry.title: Scribby: A Multi-Level LLM Framework for Semantic Video Analysis

entry.title: Sensory Restoration via Brain-Computer Interfaces: A Unified 2 x 2 Framework and Convergence Roadmap

entry.title: Multi-Task Tennis Stroke Biomechanics Analysis Using MediaPipe Pose

entry.title: A frontier AI company should shut down

entry.summary: An opinion essay arguing that a frontier AI company should voluntarily shut down and publicly declare AI an extinction risk, contending this would signal seriousness to policymakers and undercut the someone-else-will-build-it refrain. It is advocacy on AI existential risk governance.

entry.title: Improved Knowledge Distillation for Land-Use Image Classification

author.name: Arundhuti Sur, Abhiroop Chatterjee, Susmita Ghosh, Emmett Ientilucci

entry.title: An Empirical Study on Learning Latent Representations for Emotional Speech Synthesis

author.name: Vinh Dang Quang, Huy Ngo Quang

entry.summary: This empirical study explores learning latent representations for emotional speech synthesis, integrating speaker embeddings and a prosody bottleneck into FastSpeech 2. It targets the VLSP 2022 emotional speech synthesis task to control expressiveness.

entry.title: Development of a 3 in Sewer Pipe Inspection Robot with an Articulated Differential Mechanism using X-shaped Linkages

author.name: Shoya Umemura, Ryota Taniguchi, Atsushi Kakogawa

entry.summary: Describes an improved 3-inch sewer pipe inspection robot using X-shaped linkages and an articulated differential mechanism for better traction and obstacle traversal. It is a niche mechanical engineering contribution for infrastructure inspection.

entry.title: The Once And Future Fable #2

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A speculative fictional/commentary piece by Zvi imagining a scenario where the US government forces Anthropic to take down models (Claude Fable and Mythos) over a narrow jailbreak via export restrictions. It dramatizes tensions around haphazard AI regulation of released models.

entry.title: An Empirical Analysis of Optimization Dynamics and Sparsity Boundaries in Large-Scale Pedestrian Attribute Recognition

author.name: Houssam El Mir

entry.summary: This paper empirically studies optimization dynamics for pedestrian attribute recognition under extreme class imbalance when merging PETA and PA-100K datasets. It tunes Multi-Label Focal Loss hyperparameters to preserve hard-example mining while matching a BCE baseline.

entry.title: An Ensemble Deep Learning Approach for Reliable and Scalable Lemon Leaf Disease Classification

author.name: Shayan Abrar, Sudeepta Mandal, Abdul Awal Yasir, Sonjoy Bhattacharjee, Sadman Haque Bhuiyan, Samanta Ghosh, Rafi Ahamed

entry.summary: This paper proposes an ensemble of InceptionV3 and MobileNetV2 for lemon leaf disease classification across 9 classes, reporting 99.27% accuracy with adversarial training for robustness. It targets agricultural disease detection on a 1,354-image dataset.

entry.title: Does preservation make sense before we know how to revive?

author.name: Aurelia

entry.summary: A personal essay arguing that whole-body end-of-life preservation for future revival is scientifically justifiable even without current revival capability, challenging the immediate-revival objection. It is advocacy rather than technical research.

entry.title: On Responsibility and Death: Can We See Reality for What It Is or Will It Break Us

author.name: Dawn Drescher

entry.summary: A reflective personal essay on bearing the weight of consequential moral responsibility, drawing on charity allocation experience and the question of whether confronting harsh reality breaks or strengthens people. It is introspective ethics rather than technical work.

entry.title: Finding pi and G in Mathland

author.name: Fernand0

entry.summary: A draft philosophical essay on the relationship between mathematical theories and physical phenomena, arguing science selects among neighboring mathematical theories in 'Mathland' rather than purely abstracting from observations. It is speculative epistemology of science.

entry.title: The Power to Punish

author.name: Ben Pace

entry.summary: A short essay arguing that society advances by limiting the magnitude of failure (e.g., banning duels, limited-liability companies) to encourage greater risk-taking, framed as part of a daily writing challenge. It is a conceptual social-design reflection.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 15, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is anchored by optimizer theory and a deep slate of AI safety, interpretability, and agent work. A strong Muon cluster dominates optimization: Free Heavy-Tailed Lunch for Muon (Suvrit Sra) proves optimal sample complexity for non-Euclidean matrix optimizers, with Muon^p, Zeta, and Gefen adding spectral-power, dual-whitening, and memory-efficient variants. Beyond a Single Explanation of the Adam-SGD Gap debunks single-cause narratives across modalities.

Safety and interpretability are the densest theme:

  • Low-Rank Subspace Analysis (Torr, Oxford) models refusal, jailbreak, and sycophancy as low-rank activation subspaces
  • Adversarial Concept Search predicts compositional failures from feature geometry
  • Natively Unlearnable LLMs (NULLs) architect models for built-in unlearning
  • Same-Origin Policy for Agentic Browsers (Dawn Song) shows the agent itself acts as a cross-origin channel
  • Right or Wrong, Models Comply reveals Compliance Asymmetry in moral judgment across 9 models

Agent capability and evaluation infrastructure round out the list:

  • Every Eval Ever (Biderman, Solaiman, Choshen, Cohan) proposes a unifying schema and community repository for eval results
  • GauntletBench stress-tests agent generalization in unfamiliar professional domains
  • When the Tool Decides finds agents defer to GNN tools 97.6-99.2% of the time, with stronger backbones deferring more
  • OdysSim builds foundation models for human behavior simulation, targeting the Sim2Real register gap
entry.content:
Today's research is anchored by optimizer theory and a deep slate of AI safety, interpretability, and agent work. A strong Muon cluster dominates optimization: Free Heavy-Tailed Lunch for Muon (Suvrit Sra) proves optimal sample complexity for non-Euclidean matrix optimizers, with Muon^p, Zeta, and Gefen adding spectral-power, dual-whitening, and memory-efficient variants. Beyond a Single Explanation of the Adam-SGD Gap debunks single-cause narratives across modalities.

Safety and interpretability are the densest theme:

  • Low-Rank Subspace Analysis (Torr, Oxford) models refusal, jailbreak, and sycophancy as low-rank activation subspaces
  • Adversarial Concept Search predicts compositional failures from feature geometry
  • Natively Unlearnable LLMs (NULLs) architect models for built-in unlearning
  • Same-Origin Policy for Agentic Browsers (Dawn Song) shows the agent itself acts as a cross-origin channel
  • Right or Wrong, Models Comply reveals Compliance Asymmetry in moral judgment across 9 models

Agent capability and evaluation infrastructure round out the list:

  • Every Eval Ever (Biderman, Solaiman, Choshen, Cohan) proposes a unifying schema and community repository for eval results
  • GauntletBench stress-tests agent generalization in unfamiliar professional domains
  • When the Tool Decides finds agents defer to GNN tools 97.6-99.2% of the time, with stronger backbones deferring more
  • OdysSim builds foundation models for human behavior simulation, targeting the Sim2Real register gap

entry.title: Free Heavy-Tailed Lunch for Muon: A Theoretical Justification of Empirical Success

author.name: Florian H\"ubler, Thomas Pethick, Suvrit Sra

entry.summary: This paper provides theoretical justification for the empirical success of non-Euclidean matrix optimizers like Muon, proving they achieve optimal sample complexity under heavy-tailed gradients while Euclidean methods incur dimension-dependent costs. It explains why Muon outperforms Adam-style methods for transformer training.

entry.title: A Low-Rank Subspace Analysis of LLM Interventions

author.name: Angira Sharma, Christian Schroeder de Witt, Philip Torr, Anisoara Calinescu, Jialin Yu

entry.summary: This paper introduces a diagnostic framework that models LLM behaviors (refusal, jailbreak, sycophancy) as low-rank subspaces in activation space, showing that interventions on one behavior propagate asymmetrically to others. It explains why targeted safety interventions cause unintended side-effects, which matters for designing reliable safety controls.

entry.title: Right or Wrong, Models Comply: Directional Blindness in LLM Moral Judgment

author.name: Jihye Kim, Jeffrey Flanigan

entry.summary: Introduces Compliance Asymmetry, a bidirectional diagnostic comparing whether LLMs follow helpful nudges versus misleading nudges. Across 9 models and 972,000 responses, finds models selectively resist harmful nudges on factual questions but comply with both directions nearly equally on moral questions, revealing directional blindness in moral judgment.

entry.title: Every Eval Ever: A Unifying Schema and Community Repository for AI Evaluation Results

author.name: Jan Batzner, Sree Harsha Nelaturu, Anastassia Kornilova, Jon Crall, Tommaso Cerruti, Yanan Long, Yifan Mai, Sanchit Ahuja, Asaf Yehudai, Marek \v{S}uppa, John P. Lalor, Oluwagbemike Olowe, Jatin Ganhotra, Brian H. Hu, Eliya Habba, Andrew M. Bean, Chang Liu, Sander Land, Steven Dillmann, Aniketh Garikaparthi, Elron Bandel, Saki Imai, James Edgell, Wm. Matthew Kennedy, Jenny Chim, Patrick Meusling, Asteria Kaeberlein, Venkata Ramachandra Karthik Chundi, Manasi Patwardhan, Martin Ku, Austin Meek, Leon Knauer, Brian Wingenroth, Srishti Yadav, Usman Gohar, Felix Friedrich, Michelle Lin, Jennifer Mickel, Arman Cohan, Stella Biderman, Irene Solaiman, Zeerak Talat, Anka Reuel, Mubashara Akhtar, Gjergji Kasneci, Avijit Ghosh, Leshem Choshen

entry.summary: Every Eval Ever introduces the first shared schema and community-crowdsourced repository for AI evaluation results, standardizing how evaluations are represented in a unified JSON document. It tackles fragmentation and inconsistency across leaderboards, harnesses, and papers.

entry.title: Natively Unlearnable Large Language Models

author.name: Gaurav R. Ghosal, Pratyush Maini, Aditi Raghunathan

entry.summary: Proposes NULLs (Natively Unlearnable LLMs), a model class with shared backbone neurons and sparsely activated per-source sinks so that source-specific information concentrates in sinks and can be disabled at deployment to unlearn data. Resolves the tension between joint learning and clean removal.

entry.title: Adversarial Concept Search: Predicting Compositional Errors From Feature Geometry

author.name: Jennifer Meng Lu, Ruochen Zhang, Isabelle Lee, David Alvarez-Melis, Ellie Pavlick, Naomi Saphra

entry.summary: Uses an LLM's representational geometry to predict which concept combinations it will fail to compose, attributing failures to feature interference when concept encodings are near each other rather than orthogonal. Demonstrated across programmatic, multihop, and multilingual tasks.

entry.title: Same-Origin Policy for Agentic Browsers

author.name: Xilong Wang, Xiaoxing Chen, Patrick Li, Dawn Song, Neil Gong

entry.summary: Investigates whether the same-origin policy remains effective in agentic browsers, showing the agent itself can act as a cross-origin data flow channel violating SOP. Introduces SOPBench and finds existing agentic browsers frequently violate SOP.

entry.title: OdysSim: Building Foundation Models for Human Behavior Simulation

author.name: Xuhui Zhou, Weiwei Sun, Weihua Du, Jiarui Liu, Haojia Sun, Qianou Ma, Tongshuang Wu, Yiming Yang, Maarten Sap

entry.summary: OdysSim builds foundation models for simulating human behavior, addressing the homogeneous overly-agreeable register that helpfulness training induces. It introduces the SOUL taxonomy, a 21.4M-interaction corpus, a benchmark, and a training recipe for behavioral simulation.

entry.title: Running the Gauntlet: Re-evaluating the Capabilities of Agents Beyond Familiar Environments

author.name: Mykola Vysotskyi, Runqi Lin, Grzegorz Biziel, Michal Zakrzewski, Sebastian Montagna, Damian Rynczak, Shreyansh Padarha, Kumail Alhamoud, Zihao Fu, William Lugoloobi, Kai Rawal, Hanna Yershova, Xander Davies, Taras Rumezhak, Guohao Li, Fazl Barez, Baoyuan Wu, Arkadiusz Drohomirecki, Yarin Gal, Chris Russell, Christopher Summerfield, Adam Mahdi, Volodymyr Karpiv, Philip Torr, Adel Bibi

entry.summary: GauntletBench is a web-based benchmark evaluating AI agent generalisation in unfamiliar professional applications (3D modeling, circuit design, flight analysis) focusing on temporal perception, graphical understanding, and 3D reasoning. It probes underexplored agent capabilities where current benchmarks are saturated.

entry.title: Muon$^p$: Muon with Fractional Spectral Powers

author.name: Yihe Dong, Will Sawin

entry.summary: Introduces Muon^p, an optimizer generalizing Muon by using fractional spectral-power updates to interpolate between Muon and gradient descent. Proves fractional powers cannot be computed by fixed polynomial iterations and derives matrix-multiplication-only approximations.

entry.title: Decompose Sparsely Where You Should, Absorb Densely Where You Should No

author.name: Ruixuan Deng, Zehao Jin, Zekun Wang, Zihan Dong

entry.summary: Challenges the assumption that all residual stream activations suit sparse decomposition, hypothesizing a dense low-rank component unsuitable for sparse representation. Adds a small rank-r linear bottleneck parallel to sparse autoencoders, reducing dense latent count by up to 84 percent on Gemma-2-2B while improving reconstruction.

entry.title: SuperThoughts: Reasoning Tokens in Superposition

author.name: Zheyang Xiong, Shivam Garg, Max Yu, Vaishnavi Shrivastava, Haoyu Zhao, Anastasios Kyrillidis, Dimitris Papailiopoulos

entry.summary: SuperThoughts compresses pairs of consecutive chain-of-thought tokens into single latent representations and decodes two tokens per step via multi-token prediction, doubling reasoning throughput while preserving discrete supervision. Evaluated on math reasoning benchmarks with Qwen models.

entry.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: Benchmarking Agent Safety Against Decomposition Attacks with DECOMPBENCH

author.name: Vikhyath Kothamasu, Virginia Smith, Chhavi Yadav

entry.summary: Introduces DECOMPBENCH, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agent safety against decomposition attacks where harmful tasks are split into benign subtasks that evade safety mechanisms individually but combine to fulfill malicious intent. It addresses a gap in existing benchmarks that fail to capture this realistic adversarial flow.

entry.title: Temporal Backtracking Search for Test-time Generative Video Reasoning

author.name: Sejoon Jun, Zheng Ding, Huangyuan Su, Weirui Ye, Yilun Du

entry.summary: Introduces Temporal Backtracking Search, a test-time scaling method for generative video reasoning that shifts the search space to the temporal axis with a generate-verify-restart loop. Addresses the limitation that spatial trajectories commit early in diffusion.

entry.title: LLMs Contain Multitudes: How Deployment Context Reshapes Model-Level Preferences and Values

author.name: Filip Trhlik, Aoife O'Flynn, Angela Yu, Arduin Findeis, Paula Buttery

entry.summary: Tests whether claimed stable model-level value systems in LLMs survive changes in deployment context (task framing), finding that preferences and values shift substantially when the surrounding task changes. Challenges recent characterizations of LLMs as having fixed value systems.

entry.title: Semidefinite Relaxations for Collision-Free Motion Planning

author.name: Bernhard Paus Graesdal, Alexandre Amice, Pablo A. Parrilo, and Russ Tedrake

entry.summary: Provides the first theoretical analysis of semidefinite relaxations for collision-free motion planning, focusing on a point robot moving through spherical obstacles. Shows the convex relaxation is equivalent to solving a related higher-dimensional motion planning problem to global optimality.

entry.title: Small LLMs: Pruning vs. Training from Scratch

author.name: Yufeng Xu, Taiming Lu, Kunjun Li, Jiachen Zhu, Mingjie Sun, Zhuang Liu

entry.summary: Empirically examines whether pruning Llama-3.1-8B at high ratios produces strong small models versus training from scratch, under token-matched budgets across six methods spanning depth, width, and sparse granularities. Finds pruned initialization beats random under equal token budgets but the advantage narrows at higher pruning ratios and larger budgets.

entry.title: CacheRL:Multi-Turn Tool-Calling Agents via Cached Rollouts and Hybrid Reward

author.name: Md Amirul Islam, Sumiran Thakur, Huancheng Chen, Su Min Park, Jiayun Wang, Gyuhak Kim

entry.summary: CacheRL trains small agent foundation models for multi-step tool-calling, reaching 92 percent process accuracy versus GPT-5's 94 percent with 100x less compute. It uses hybrid thinking trajectories augmenting agent trajectories with reasoning traces and a CacheAgentLoop that eliminates live tool execution via cached environments.

entry.title: When the Tool Decides: LLM Agents Defer Blindly to Graph Neural Network Tools, and Stronger Backbones Defer More

author.name: Zhongyuan Wang, Pratyusha Vemuri

entry.summary: This study shows that LLM agents given a GNN as a callable tool blindly defer to it, agreeing with raw GNN outputs 97.6-99.2% of the time and bypassing their own reasoning, with stronger backbones deferring more. It challenges the assumption that agents exercise judgment over tool use.

entry.title: Mirage Probes: How Vision Models Fake Visual Understanding

author.name: Daniel Ben-Levi, Judah Goldfeder, Weiliang Zhao, Raz Lapid, Amit LeVi, Allen G. Roush, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, Hod Lipson

entry.summary: Introduces Mirage Probes showing that vision-language models can answer image questions correctly without seeing the image, and that this mirage behavior is linearly decodable from internal activations. Argues this is two distinct failure modes rather than one.

entry.title: Gefen: Optimized Stochastic Optimizer

author.name: Nadav Benedek, Tomer Koren, Ohad Fried

entry.summary: Gefen is a memory-efficient optimizer that shares second-moment estimates across parameter blocks and quantizes the first moment with a learned codebook, cutting AdamW memory ~8x while maintaining performance. Motivated by a Hessian-alignment theoretical result.

entry.title: Sorries Are Not the Hard Part: An Expert-Review Case Study of a Semi-Autonomous Formalization

author.name: Vasily Ilin, Brian Nugent

entry.summary: An expert-review case study of a semi-autonomous formalization of Grothendieck's vanishing theorem, showing that compiling without sorries does not equal a reusable library contribution. Finds agents handle local mechanical feedback well but struggle with definitions and API design.

entry.title: XRDiff: Crystal Structure Prediction from Powder X-Ray Diffraction Data Using Diffusion Models

author.name: Nofit Segal, Mingda Li, Benjamin Kurt Miller, Rafael G\'omez-Bombarelli

entry.summary: XRDiff is a diffusion model that recovers crystal structures from powder X-ray diffraction patterns, solving the underdetermined inverse problem caused by phase information loss. It works given stoichiometry or the harder setting of only elemental constituents and atom count.

entry.title: Lyapunov-Based Sample Complexity Analysis for Weakly-Coupled MDPs

author.name: Tianhao Wu, Matthew Zurek, Weina Wang, Qiaomin Xie

entry.summary: Provides Lyapunov-based finite-sample analysis for learning in average-reward weakly-coupled MDPs and Restless Bandits under a generative model, achieving sample and computational complexity polynomial in the number of arms rather than exponential. Establishes the first finite-sample PAC guarantee with polynomial complexity for fully heterogeneous WCMDPs.

entry.title: Beyond a Single Explanation of the Adam--SGD Gap

author.name: Chenxiang Zhang, Rustem Islamov, Enea Monzio Compagnoni, Jun Pang, Aurelien Lucchi, Antonio Orvieto

entry.summary: This controlled empirical study revisits multiple hypotheses for the Adam-versus-SGD performance gap across vision, language, genomics, and graph tasks. It finds no single factor consistently explains the gap, with effects reversing under different data distributions and architectures.

entry.title: BayLing-Duplex: Native Full-Duplex Speech Dialogue with a Single Autoregressive LLM

author.name: Qingkai Fang, Shoutao Guo, Yang Feng

entry.summary: BayLing-Duplex is a native full-duplex speech dialogue model where a single autoregressive LLM decides when to listen, speak, and stop, eliminating the external voice activity detection module. It adds only a few special tokens, enabling transfer across LLMs and handling overlap, hesitation, and barge-in.

entry.title: Provably Safe, Yet Scalable Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kai S. Yun, Zeyang Li, Navid Azizan

entry.summary: PS2-RL is a two-phase framework for learning provably safe RL policies that scales better than certificate-function methods while providing formal safety guarantees absent in soft-constrained approaches. It aims to overcome the scalability bottleneck of control-invariant set synthesis.

entry.title: Zeta: Dual Whitening for Matrix Optimization via Coordinate-Adaptive Preconditioning

author.name: Kaiwen Chen, Shuhai Zhang, Qiuwu Chen, Zimo Liu, Linxiao Li, Ying Sun, Yuchen Li, Yifan Zhang, Bo Han, Mingkui Tan

entry.summary: Identifies that matrix-aware optimizers like Muon are vulnerable because their Newton-Schulz iteration depends on input conditioning while raw momentum matrices exhibit severe coordinate-wise scale heterogeneity, verified via a chi-square uniformity test. Proposes Zeta, a dual whitening optimizer applying coordinate and spectral whitening in order to correct this.

entry.title: Riemannian Metric Matching for Scalable Geometric Modeling of Distributions

author.name: Jacob Bamberger, Adam Gosztolai, Pierre Vandergheynst, Michael Bronstein, Iolo Jones

entry.summary: Riemannian metric matching is a denoising probabilistic framework that learns the carre du champ operator via neural networks to recover data geometry without scale-poor graphs and kernels. It enables amortized constant-cost inference for diffusion-geometry-based downstream tasks.

entry.title: EM-NeSy: Expectation Maximization for Neurosymbolic Learning

author.name: Annegret Seibt, Luc De Raedt, Giuseppe Marra

entry.summary: EM-NeSy casts probabilistic neurosymbolic learning as an Expectation-Maximization algorithm, computing posteriors over neurally predicted symbols and updating neural parameters via gradients only through the neural component. This removes the requirement that symbolic reasoning be differentiable, enabling approximate inference.

entry.title: From Shield to Target: Denial-of-Service Attacks on LLM-Based Agent Guardrails

author.name: Yuguang Zhou, Xunguang Wang, Pingchuan Ma, Zhantong Xue, Zhaoyu Wang, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: This paper reveals a denial-of-service vulnerability in LLM-based agent guardrails: attackers can craft payloads that trap the guardrail in extended reasoning loops, using beam-search optimization and structural mutations to maximize reasoning length. It shows the reasoning ability enabling protection also creates an attack surface.

entry.title: CineOrchestra: Unified Entity-Centric Conditioning for Cinematic Video Generation

author.name: Sharath Girish, Tsai-Shien Chen, Zhikang Dong, Mukesh Singhal, Hao Chen, Sergey Tulyakov, Aliaksandr Siarohin

entry.summary: CineOrchestra is a unified video diffusion model that jointly controls multiple subjects, events, camera movement, and shot transitions by representing each as an entity acting over a temporal interval through a shared conditioning structure. It integrates four cinematic control axes previously handled in isolation.

entry.title: Diffusion Policy Optimization without Drifting Apart

author.name: Haozhe Jiang, Haiwen Feng, Pieter Abbeel, Jiantao Jiao, Angjoo Kanazawa, Nika Haghtalab

entry.summary: DiPOD is a diffusion policy optimization framework that diagnoses a double-drift phenomenon (ELBO separating from true log-likelihood, misaligning the proxy policy gradient) and fixes it by interleaving self-distillation with policy-improving updates plus an on-policy ELBO regularizer. It stabilizes RL post-training of diffusion policies.

entry.title: Aligning Quantum Operators with Large Language Models

author.name: Rogerio Feris, Yunchao Liu, Pengyuan Li, Hang Hua, David Kremer

entry.summary: Proposes mapping quantum unitary operators into an LLM latent space to enable joint reasoning over quantum and linguistic inputs, demonstrated on Clifford+T circuit synthesis. It enables language-conditioned circuit synthesis competitive with state-of-the-art methods.

entry.title: Output-Level Regularization Eliminates the Seed Lottery in Single-GPU VLA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Jeffrin Sam, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: Identifies a seed lottery problem in single-GPU VLA fine-tuning where identical training runs randomly collapse to poor performance due to output collapse. Proposes output-level regularization that eliminates this instability where weight-level methods fail.

entry.title: Capability Minimization as a Safety Primitive: Risk-Aware Causal Gating for Least-Privilege LLM Agents

author.name: Laxmipriya Ganesh Iyer and Rahul Suresh Babu

entry.summary: Introduces Risk-Aware Causal Gating (RACG), a framework deciding whether an LLM agent should act, defer, or abstain based on counterfactual risk estimation with distribution-free bounds. Frames capability minimization as a safety primitive for least-privilege agents.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Visual Questioner

author.name: Yijun Liang, Hengguang Zhou, Ming Li, Lichen Li, Cho-Jui Hsieh, Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes a self-evolving framework where a vision-language model acts as both proposer and filter to generate increasingly hard, informative, visual-centric questions to train itself without external supervision. Improves the underexplored active-questioning ability of VLMs.

entry.title: Dialogue SWE-Bench: A Benchmark for Dialogue-Driven Coding Agents

author.name: Brendan King and Jeffrey Flanigan

entry.summary: Presents Dialogue SWE-Bench, a benchmark evaluating coding agents in interactive dialogue-driven settings rather than as fully autonomous systems, using a persona-grounded user simulator. A proposed schema-guided agent improves dialogue capabilities by 3-14 percent over baselines.

entry.title: Utility-Constrained Policy Optimization

author.name: Mehrdad Moghimi, Bernardo Avila Pires

entry.summary: Introduces a practical methodology for utility-constrained MDPs that supports risk-sensitive constraints, overcoming a limitation of standard constrained MDPs that allow mixing catastrophic and overly conservative behaviors. It provides the first practical solution for UCMDPs in constrained RL.

entry.title: WAM4D: Fast 4D World Action Model via Spatial Register Tokens

author.name: Ying Li, Xiaobao Wei, Jiajun Cao, Hao Wang, Xiaowei Chi, Chengyu Bai, Qianpu Sun, Jiajun Li, Xiaojie Zhang, Jian Tang, Sirui Han, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: WAM4D is a fast 4D world action model for robotic manipulation that uses lightweight spatial register tokens as training-time future-depth readouts to inject 3D geometric priors without slowing causal action generation. It bridges the gap between 2D video world models and the 3D spatial constraints needed for precise manipulation.

entry.title: Naive Visual Memory is Not Enough: A Failure-Mode Study of GUI Agents

author.name: Seoyoung Choi, Minseok Ko, Hyunseok Lee, Kunwoong Kim, Woomin Song, Chanseok Jeon, and Jinwoo Shin

entry.summary: Conducts a failure-mode study of visual memory in GUI agents, introducing a taxonomy of four failure types to analyze which failures visual memory mitigates versus exacerbates. Finds naive visual memory is insufficient, challenging the assumption that storing past screenshots reliably improves agent decisions.

entry.title: Closing the Reflection Gap: A Free Calibration Bonus for Agentic RL

author.name: Yinglun Zhu

entry.summary: This work identifies a reflection gap where LLM agents mis-assess their own outputs even after environment feedback, and proposes RefGRPO, which adds a calibration bonus contrasting self-reflection with actual outcomes. It requires no extra reward model or judge.

entry.title: Operator Calculus for Population-Based Optimization: A Mean-Field Convergence Theory

author.name: Pekka Malo, Lauri Viitasaari, Patrik Nummi, Antti Suominen, Ankur Sinha, and Olli Tahvonen

entry.summary: This paper introduces an operator calculus that describes a broad class of population-based optimization methods as compositions of mutation, selection, and recombination operators on probability measures. It establishes a mean-field convergence theory unifying fragmented algorithm-specific analyses.

entry.title: A theoretical model for task routing in mixture-of-expert transformers

author.name: Yongli Xiang, Vinoth Nandakumar, Yunzhi Yao, Peike Li, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical explanation of task-expert specialization in MoE transformers using discrete language models (syntactic templates and key-value dictionaries), proving a single-layer MoE can encode knowledge through task-specialized experts. It bridges a gap between empirical MoE observations and theory.

entry.title: A Fixed-Point Neural Operator for Size- and Functional-Transferable Hamiltonian Prediction

author.name: Yunhong Lou, Xihang Yue, Xinran Wei, Tianqi Deng, Linchao Zhu

entry.summary: HamEvo is a neural operator that learns the single-step self-consistent field update and returns the converged Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian as its fixed point, transferable across molecule sizes and functionals. It improves ML-accelerated DFT by respecting the SCF fixed-point structure.

entry.title: Behavioral Audit of Machine Unlearning Has a Privacy Cost

author.name: Liou Tang, James Joshi, Ashish Kundu
