entry.summary: APPO addresses credit assignment in agentic RL by identifying that influential decision points are distributed throughout sequences rather than concentrated at tool calls, proposing procedural policy optimization with adaptive branching and fine-grained credit. It improves multi-turn tool-use agent training.

entry.title: When Probing Accuracy Saturates, Fragility Resolves: A Complementary Metric for LLM Pre-Training Analysis

author.name: Orion Reblitz-Richardson

entry.summary: This paper introduces fragility, a per-layer metric defined as the activation-noise level at which probe accuracy collapses, as a complementary signal to standard linear probing whose accuracy saturates early in pretraining. Fragility recovers representational structure (e.g., margin and redundancy evolution) that accuracy alone misses across pretraining checkpoints.

entry.title: Learning What to Say to Your VLA: Mostly Harmless Vision Language Action Model Steering

author.name: Hyun Joe Jeong, Gokul Swamy, Andrea Bajcsy

entry.summary: This framework interactively searches for language sequences that improve closed-loop VLA task performance, distills them into a test-time language feedback policy, and learns a head predicting when language steering helps. It addresses the brittle and unintuitive mapping from instructions to robot behavior.

entry.title: [New Paper] Prioritizing Risks from AI: A Delphi Study of 272 Experts

author.name: peterslattery

entry.summary: Reports a Delphi study of 272 international AI experts prioritizing 24 risk domains from the MIT AI Risk Taxonomy. Experts judged a greater-than-10-percent chance of catastrophic outcomes from 18 of 24 domains within five years under business-as-usual, and identified a responsibility gap where users are most vulnerable while developers and governance actors are most responsible.

entry.title: The Theory of Mind Utility: Formal Specification of a Mentalizing Mechanism

author.name: Nikolos Gurney, Stacy Marsella

entry.summary: The Theory of Mind Utility formalizes epistemic-state inference at the computational level, using Local Epistemic World Models (directed typed graphs) to track who told whom what and how credibly. It specifies what mentalizing computes without committing to implementation details.

entry.title: Teach-and-Repeat: Accurately Extracting Operational Knowledge from Mobile Screen Demonstrations to Empower GUI Agents

author.name: Yudong Zhang (Honor Device Co., Ltd), Lei Hu (Honor Device Co., Ltd), Daoyang Liu (The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China), Jiawei Liu (Honor Device Co., Ltd), Yangfan Luo (Honor Device Co., Ltd), Xingyu Liu (Honor Device Co., Ltd), Zuojian Wang (Honor Device Co., Ltd), Zhilin Gao (Honor Device Co., Ltd)

entry.summary: Teach-and-Repeat introduces Teach VLM, a model that translates mobile screen demonstration trajectories into step-wise operational knowledge by extracting operation-related keyframes, to empower GUI agents. It addresses VLMs struggling with heterogeneous UI designs.

entry.title: Learning What to Remember: A Cognitively Grounded Multi-Factor Value Model for Agentic Memory

author.name: Zhibao Chen, Qian Cheng

entry.summary: This paper proposes a cognitively grounded multi-factor memory value function over seven interpretable factors (emotional intensity, goal relevance, task utility, etc.) for deciding what LLM agents should remember or forget under a fixed budget. Weights are learned from a downstream objective by a gradient-free optimizer.

entry.title: APCyc: Property-Informed Design of Cyclic Peptides via Automated Cyclization

author.name: Yifan Zhao, Lang Qin, Jintai Chen

entry.summary: APCyc is a target-aware de novo cyclic peptide generation framework that explicitly models cyclization and jointly optimizes multiple physicochemical properties, addressing limitations of models trained mainly on linear peptides. It identifies pocket-adaptive cyclization patterns and linkage sites.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Agents for Regulated Process Automation: Challenges and Research Agenda

author.name: Alexander Rombach, Chantale Lauer, Nijat Mehdiyev

entry.summary: This paper argues that symbolic structures (regulations, typed process models, compliance constraints) in regulated industries should be core architectural components of LLM agents rather than external monitors, proposing compliance-by-construction as a complement to guardrails. It lays out a neuro-symbolic research agenda for regulated process automation.

entry.title: CloudCons: A Comprehensive End-to-End Benchmark for Cloud Resource Consolidation

author.name: Xiaobin Zhang, Lefei Shen, Mouxiang Chen, Zhuo Li, Hongkai Li, Han Fu, Jianling Sun, Xiaoxue Ren, Chenghao Liu

entry.summary: CloudCons is an end-to-end benchmark for cloud resource consolidation that evaluates forecasting models by their downstream decision utility rather than only prediction-error metrics, examining time-series foundation models in a forecast-then-optimize pipeline. It bridges the gap between prediction accuracy and practical decision value.

entry.title: Diffusion Transformer World-Action Model for AV Scene Prediction

author.name: Ruslan Sharifullin, Benjamin Jiang, Kai Xi Chew

entry.summary: Presents a compact latent world model for autonomous-vehicle scene prediction that forecasts future camera latents from ego-actions, critiquing how standard distortion metrics mislead by rewarding blurry predictions. Benchmarks multiple frozen encoders on nuScenes.

entry.title: Functional Cache Grafting: Robust and Rapid Code-Policy Synthesis for Embodied Agents

author.name: Saehun Chun, Wonje Choi, Sera Choi, Sanghyun Ahn, Honguk Woo

entry.summary: Presents FCGraft, a Functional Cache Grafting framework that maintains a library of validated code skeletons and their transformer KV-cache states to accelerate and stabilize code-policy synthesis for embodied agents. Reduces prefill latency and API-mismatch errors.

entry.title: Modern analog computing for solving differential and matrix equations

author.name: Zhong Sun, Piergiulio Mannocci, Manuel Le Gallo, Abu Sebastian

entry.summary: A survey of modern analog computing for AI and scientific computing, identifying three core primitives—solving differential equations, matrix equations, and matrix-vector multiplications—and reviewing hardware implementations from discrete components to resistive memory. Connects computational tasks across analog approaches.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Masked Compositional Concept Modeling for Enhancing Visio-Linguistic Compositionality

author.name: Wei Li, Zhen Huang, Xinmei Tian

entry.summary: Proposes MACCO, a masked compositional concept modeling framework that masks compositional concepts in one modality and reconstructs them conditioned on the other to improve visio-linguistic compositionality in CLIP-style models, addressing bag-of-words behavior. Targets object relations, attribute bindings, and word order.

entry.title: Understanding the Rejection of Fixes Generated by Agentic Pull Requests -- Insights from the AIDev Dataset

author.name: Mahmoud Abujadallah, Ali Arabat, Mohammed Sayagh

entry.summary: A qualitative study analyzing 306 non-merged agentic pull requests from Copilot, Devin, Cursor, and Claude (from the AIDev dataset where 46% of fixes are rejected) to characterize the failure modes of AI coding agents. Aims to inform better human-AI collaboration in software development.

entry.title: Adaptive Turn-Taking for Real-time Multi-Party Voice Agents

author.name: Soumyajit Mitra, Prabhat Pandey, Abhinav Jain, Shanmukha Sahith, K V Vijay Girish

entry.summary: Proposes ModeratorLM, a role-playing voice agent conditioning turn-taking on an explicitly assigned role for multi-party conversations, built on a chunk-wise streaming speech LLM with a reasoning-augmented variant, plus RolePlayConv, a large synthetic multi-party speech dataset. Addresses turn-taking under dynamic floor competition.

entry.title: ArogyaSutra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Multimodal Medical Reasoning in Indic Languages

author.name: Tanmoy Kanti Halder, Akash Ghosh, Subhadip Baidya, Arijit Roy, Sriparna Saha

entry.summary: Introduces ArogyaSutra, a multi-agent framework for multimodal medical reasoning in Indic languages, along with ArogyaBodha, a large multilingual multimodal medical QA dataset spanning eight sources, 31 body systems, and multiple languages. Targets equitable healthcare AI for low-resource Indic-language rural settings.

entry.title: Least-Action-Guided Diffusion for Physical Extrapolation

author.name: Zhongxin Yang, Yuanwei Bin, Xiang I. A. Yang, Shiyi Chen

entry.summary: LAPG is a least-action-principle-guided diffusion framework that promotes physical consistency at inference for extrapolation beyond the training distribution. Combines a score-based diffusion proposal with an action-derived physical guidance refinement.

entry.title: Recursive Binding on a Budget: Subspace Carving in Order-p Tensor Memories

author.name: Travis Pence, Daisuke Yamada, Vikas Singh

entry.summary: Orthogonal Subspace Carving (OSC) binds fillers to roles by projecting onto the null space of the role basis before aggregating into a fixed order-p tensor, decoupling tensor order from structural depth. Addresses the tradeoff between Tensor Product Representations and Vector Symbolic Architectures.

entry.title: Probabilistic Contrastive Pretraining for Multi-task ADME Property Prediction

author.name: Yifan Xue, Srimukh Prasad Veccham, Saee Paliwal, Tyler Shimko, Micha Livne

entry.summary: Proposes a molecular graph-transformer pretraining framework combining chemistry self-supervision with contrastive mutual information learning for multi-task ADME property prediction. Formulates reconstruction, contrastive, and chemistry tasks jointly rather than as weighted auxiliaries.

entry.title: APEX: A Network-Native Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting and Anomaly Detection for Wireless Edge Operations

author.name: Swadhin Pradhan, Niloo Bahadori, Peiman Amini

entry.summary: APEX is a network-native decoder-only time-series foundation model for wireless edge telemetry forecasting and anomaly detection, pretrained on ~4,500 production networks. Outperforms generic TSFM baselines on DHCP degradation tasks with cloud and edge variants.

entry.title: Range-Aware Bayesian Optimization for Discovering Diverse Designs within Target Property Windows

author.name: Shengli Jiang, Jason Wu, Charles M. Schroeder, Michael A. Webb

entry.summary: Develops range-aware Bayesian optimization where the acquisition function scores the posterior probability a candidate satisfies a target property window, and pursues multiple distinct specifications in parallel. Aimed at materials and product design with acceptable ranges rather than single optima.

entry.title: Beyond the Golden Teacher: Enhancing Graph Learning through LLM-GNN Co-teaching

author.name: Zhuoyi Peng, Hanlin Gu, Lixin Fan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Proposes LLM-GNN co-teaching for few-shot text-attributed graph learning, rejecting the golden-teacher assumption where one model supervises the other since both have blind spots under sparse supervision. Mutual teaching aims to combine topology and text strengths.

entry.title: TimeRouter: Efficient and Adaptive Routing of Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Kanghui Ning, Yushan Jiang, Kashif Rasul, Anderson Schneider, Yuriy Nevmyvaka, Dongjin Song

entry.summary: TimeRouter is a lightweight routing framework that selects among pretrained time-series foundation models using a discriminative routing head, selective gating, and ensemble fallback, avoiding costly LLM-based controllers. Exploits empirical complementarity across TSFMs.

entry.title: From Uniform to Learned Graph Priors: Diffusion for Structure Discovery

author.name: Qi Shao, Hao Guo, Jiawen Chen, Duxin Chen, Wenwu Yu

entry.summary: Diff-prior is a diffusion-parameterized adaptive prior for neural relational inference that calibrates the latent graph distribution rather than generating graphs, replacing oversimplified factorized priors. Aims to sharpen edge posteriors for more reliable structure discovery.

entry.title: Fine-tuning Multi-modal LLMs with ART: Art-based Reinforcement Training

author.name: Michal Chudoba, Sergey Alyaev, Petra Galuscakova, Tomasz Wiktorski

entry.summary: ART (Art-based Reinforcement Training) fine-tunes frozen multimodal LLMs by optimizing only their raw visual input via backpropagation, enabling soft-token-style adaptation on precompiled computational graphs supported by high-throughput engines like vLLM. Avoids modifying the model graph as LoRA and soft prompting require.

entry.title: Efficient Multinomial Logistic Bandit via Frequent Directions

author.name: Linzhe He, Yu-Jie Zhang, Sifan Yang, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: EOFD-MLogB makes multinomial logistic bandits efficient by integrating frequent-directions matrix sketching into a UCB-type algorithm, maintaining a low-rank SVD sketch of the Hessian to reduce per-round time and space costs in high dimensions. Preserves regret guarantees.

entry.title: The Standard Interpretable Model: A general theory of interpretable machine learning to deductively design interpretable methods using Lagrangian mechanics

author.name: Pietro Barbiero, Giovanni De Felice, Mateo Espinosa Zarlenga, Francesco Giannini, Filippo Bonchi, Mateja Jamnik, Giuseppe Marra, Ruggero Noris

entry.summary: The Standard Interpretable Model proposes a general theory grounded in Lagrangian mechanics to deductively design interpretable ML methods from a set of user-defined premises, deriving interpretability symmetries. It aims to unify a fragmented interpretability literature.

entry.title: Calibration Drift Under Reasoning: How Chain-of-Thought Budgets Induce Overconfidence in Large Language Models

author.name: Prakul Sunil Hiremath, Harshit R. Hiremath

entry.summary: This paper identifies Calibration Drift Under Reasoning, showing that increasing chain-of-thought reasoning budget beyond a task-specific threshold can make LLMs systematically overconfident, with non-monotonic expected calibration error. It analyzes the phenomenon both theoretically and empirically.

entry.title: Search Discipline for Long-Horizon Research Agents

author.name: Adithya Srinivasan, Devesh Paragiri

entry.summary: This paper shows that long-horizon autoresearch agents optimizing an aggregate metric can rank the wrong candidate first when scientific validity lives in disaggregated structure (regions, slices, cohorts), demonstrating the inversion on an ecosystem fire-model task. It argues for search discipline that respects multi-dimensional validity rather than single reductions.

entry.title: Neuro-Relational Programs: Unifying Queries and Neural Computation over Structured Data

author.name: Arie Soeteman, Balder ten Cate, Maurice Funk, Benny Kimelfeld, Carsten Lutz, Moritz Sch\"onherr

entry.summary: Neuro-Relational Programs extend Datalog-style rules with operations over numeric vector embeddings attached to database tuples, interleaving relational reasoning and learnable neural components in a single declarative formalism. It generalizes neural computation over structured relational data.

entry.title: MLT-Dedup: Efficient Large-Scale Online Video Deduplication via Multi-Level Representations and Spatial-Temporal Matching

author.name: David Yuchen Wang, Haoying Li, Hailun Xu, Wei Chee Yew, Zirui Zhu, Sanjay Saha, Hao Hei, Kanchan Sarkar, Kun Xu

entry.summary: This paper studies market design for human-generated content used in AI training, arguing both fair-use free-for-all and strong IP rights models fail to incentivize quality, especially penalizing original creators. It develops static and dynamic game-theoretic models revealing an originality penalty.

entry.title: SENTINEL: Failure-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Training Tool-Using Language Model Agents

author.name: Ziyi Wang, Yuxuan Lu, Yimeng Zhang, Qun Liu, Chen Luo, Jiri Gesi, Hanqing Lu, Yisi Sang, Manling Li, Jing Huang, Dakuo Wang

entry.summary: SENTINEL is a failure-driven RL framework for training tool-using LLM agents that converts the solver's rollout failures into targeted training tasks via a Controller-Proposer-Solver loop. It addresses task distribution mismatch as agent capabilities evolve during training.

entry.title: EvoBrowseComp: Benchmarking Search Agents on Evolving Knowledge

author.name: Yunhan Wang, Jiaan Wang, Lianzhe Huang, Xianfeng Zeng, Fandong Meng

entry.summary: EvoBrowseComp is an evolving, contamination-free benchmark of 400 English and 400 Chinese complex questions synthesized via live-web traversal using a three-agent collaborative framework. It addresses test-set contamination and parametric memorization that let models score high through fact recall rather than genuine browsing.

entry.title: Computationally tractable robust differentially private mean estimation

author.name: Kelly Ramsay

entry.summary: Introduces the balloon mean, a differentially private and robust mean estimator based on iterative clipping over expanding Mahalanobis balls. It satisfies zero-concentrated differential privacy with interpretable tuning parameters and provides guarantees under heavy-tailed and contaminated elliptical models.

entry.title: ToolSense: A Diagnostic Framework for Auditing Parametric Tool Knowledge in LLMs

author.name: Ashutosh Hathidara, Sai Shruthi Sistla, Sebastian Schreiber, Sahil Bansal

entry.summary: ToolSense introduces a diagnostic framework to audit whether parametric tool-retrieval methods in LLMs genuinely understand their tools, rather than just exploiting verbose queries and constrained decoding on standard benchmarks. It exposes gaps between benchmark performance and true tool comprehension.

entry.title: WISE: A Long-Horizon Agent in Minecraft with Why-Which Reasoning

author.name: Renmin Cheng (The Hong Kong University of Science, Technology), Changhao Chen (The Hong Kong University of Science, Technology)

entry.summary: WISE is a long-horizon Minecraft agent that augments episodic memory with a Causal Event Graph linking observations to task relevance, decoupling what-where-when memory from which-why reasoning. It improves low-level controller reliability in embodied tasks.

entry.title: PRISMR: Overcoming Parse Collapse in Multimodal Listwise Ranking via Parameterized Representation Internalization

author.name: Hao Jiang, Xin Li, Annan Wang, Zhi Yang, Haoxiang Zhang, Yichi Zhang, Weisi Lin

entry.summary: PRISMR addresses parse collapse in generative listwise ranking with large multimodal models, where decoders silently omit candidates in long contexts, by replacing transient in-context list processing with parametric structural conditioning. It improves multimodal listwise ranking.

entry.title: Brick: Spatial Capability Routing for the Mixture-of-Models (MoM) Paradigm

author.name: Francesco Massa, Marco Cristofanilli

entry.summary: Brick is a multimodal router for a Mixture-of-Models paradigm that scores each model on six capability dimensions and combines them with per-query difficulty to dispatch via a cost-penalized geometric rule, with a tunable quality-versus-savings knob. It targets within-domain variance that surface-feature routers ignore.

entry.title: Efficient, Robust, and Anti-Collusion Fingerprinting of Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Jianwei Fei, Yunshu Dai, Zhihua Xia, Xiaochun Cao, Jiantao Zhou, Alessandro Piva, Benedetta Tondi

entry.summary: Reveals that existing fingerprinting methods for text-to-image diffusion models are vulnerable to collusion attacks and proposes the first anti-collusion fingerprinting approach encoding bits into model coefficients. Addresses IP protection for generative models.

entry.title: MemRefine: LLM-Guided Compression for Long-Term Agent Memory

author.name: Minjae Kim, Jinheon Baek, Soyeong Jeong, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: Proposes MemRefine, an LLM-guided compression framework for storage-budgeted long-term agent memory that keeps a memory store within a fixed budget while preserving information useful for future tasks, addressing unbounded memory growth and redundancy. Targets resource-constrained deployments.

entry.title: An LLM System for Autonomous Variational Quantum Circuit Design

author.name: Kenya Sakka, Wataru Mizukami, Kosuke Mitarai

entry.summary: Introduces an autonomous LLM-agent framework for variational quantum circuit design with seven components forming a closed loop of exploration, generation, validation, and evaluation, applied to quantum feature maps and VQE ansatz generation in quantum chemistry. Reduces reliance on human expertise.

entry.title: AgentRivet: an automated system for producing Rivet routines from journal publications

author.name: Antonio J. Costa, Caterina Doglioni, Christian G\"utschow, Andrew D. Pilkington, Sukanya Sinha

entry.summary: Designs AgentRivet, an LLM-based automated workflow to generate missing Rivet analysis routines for particle physics measurements, addressing that only 39% of measurements have public routines. Extracts analysis info from publications and produces C++ routines for the preservation ecosystem.

entry.title: EvTexture++: Event-Driven Texture Enhancement for Video Super-Resolution

author.name: Dachun Kai, Jiayao Lu, Yueyi Zhang, Xiaoyan Sun

entry.summary: Proposes EvTexture++, the first event-driven framework dedicated to texture enhancement (rather than motion refinement) in video super-resolution, leveraging high-frequency spatiotemporal details from event cameras through an iterative texture enhancement module. Shifts the role of event signals in VSR.

entry.title: Few-Shot Resampling for Scalable Statistically-Sound Data Mining

author.name: Leonardo Pellegrina, Fabio Vandin

entry.summary: Proposes a few-shot resampling method to make statistically-sound data mining scalable, avoiding the thousands of resampled datasets typically needed for significance testing. This matters for applying rigorous statistical validation to large-scale or computationally expensive analyses.

entry.title: LakeFM: Toward a Foundation Model for Aquatic Ecosystems Using Irregular Multivariate Multi-depth Time Series Data

author.name: Abhilash Neog, Sepideh Fatemi, Medha Sawhney, Kazi Sajeed Mehrab, Aanish Pradhan, Bennett J. McAfee, Emma Marchisin, Arka Daw, Robert Ladwig, Cayelan C. Carey, Paul Hanson, Anuj Karpatne

entry.summary: LakeFM is a foundation model for aquatic ecosystems pretrained on simulated and observed lake data, handling irregular multivariate multi-depth time series. Aims to generalize across heterogeneous lakes for water quality forecasting.

entry.title: GLACIER: A Multimodal Student-Teacher Foundation Model for Molecular Property Prediction

author.name: Emily Nguyen, Yongchan Hong, Harsh Toshniwal, Yan Liu, Andreas Luttens

entry.summary: GLACIER is a multimodal student-teacher foundation model for molecular property prediction integrating molecular graphs, SMILES, and physicochemical descriptors. Learns rich embeddings to improve drug discovery scalability.

entry.title: OmniLoc: A Geometry-Aware Foundation Model for Anchor-Free UE Localization Across Diverse Indoor Environments

author.name: Lei Chu, Yuning Zhang, Omer Gokalp Serbetci, Anushka Katiyar, Bassel Abou Ali Modad, Andreas F. Molisch

entry.summary: OmniLoc is a geometry-aware foundation model for anchor-free indoor user-equipment localization from wireless measurements, designed to generalize across diverse building geometries and access-point sets. Claimed as the first foundation-model approach for this task.

entry.title: TAROT: Task-Adaptive Refinement of LLM-prior Graphs for Few-shot Tabular Learning

author.name: Ruxue Shi, Yili Wang, Mengnan Du, Hangting Ye, Yi Chang, Xin Wang

entry.summary: TAROT refines LLM-prior semantic graphs in a task-adaptive way for few-shot tabular learning, leveraging feature semantic relationships while avoiding feeding raw data into LLMs to address privacy concerns. Builds and adapts a semantic graph over features.

entry.title: Space-sampled Value Decay: Forgetting Mechanisms for Non-stationary Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Felix St\"orck, Fabian Hinder, Barbara Hammer

entry.summary: Introduces Space-sampled Value Decay as an explicit forgetting mechanism for value-based deep RL in non-stationary environments, without requiring task IDs or context information about the drift. Inspired by adaptive behavior in rodents under environmental drift.

entry.title: MemNovo: Look Back at the Spectrum for Balanced De Novo Peptide Sequencing from Mass Spectrometry

author.name: Dongxin Lyu, Jingbo Zhou, Hongxin Xiang, Yuqiang Li, Jun Xia

entry.summary: MemNovo addresses a pathology in Transformer de novo peptide sequencing where decoders over-rely on generated-sequence priors and under-use spectral evidence, leading to plausible but unfaithful peptides. Proposes a mechanism to re-attend to the input spectrum.

entry.title: Tabular Foundation Models for Clinical Survival Analysis via Survival-Aware Adaptation

author.name: Minh-Khoi Pham, Luca Cotugno, Alina Sirbu, Tai Tan Mai, Martin Crane, Marija Bezbradica

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight survival-aware adaptation for applying tabular foundation models to censored time-to-event clinical prediction, extending them beyond discrete classification to survival analysis. Targets mortality and other clinical outcomes without task-specific training.

entry.title: A Riemannian Approach to Low-Rank Optimal Transport

author.name: Pratik Jawanpuria, Bamdev Mishra

entry.summary: This paper proposes a unified Riemannian geometric framework for low-rank optimal transport, modeling factored couplings as smooth manifolds with Fisher-Rao metrics to derive tractable retractions and Hessian-vector products. It generalizes across linear OT, Gromov-Wasserstein, and fused variants without per-method tuning.

entry.title: Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking in Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Stipe Frkovic, Metod Jazbec, Dan Zhang, Christian A. Naesseth, Ilija Bogunovic, Eric Nalisnick

entry.summary: This paper re-evaluates training-free confidence-based remasking methods (like WINO) for masked diffusion language models, scrutinizing whether post-hoc self-correction genuinely improves generation. It provides a more careful empirical assessment of a growing class of dLLM techniques.

entry.title: Redesign Mixture-of-Experts Routers with Manifold Power Iteration

author.name: Songhao Wu, Ang Lv, Ruobing Xie, Yankai Lin

entry.summary: This paper redesigns Mixture-of-Experts routers by aligning each router row with the principal singular direction of its associated expert via Manifold Power Iteration, providing a principled basis for token-expert affinity. It improves the cornerstone routing component of MoE models.

entry.title: My Chemical Harness: Evolutionary Molecular Design over Synthetic Pathways with Large Language Model Agents

author.name: C\'esar Ojeda, Darius A. Faroughy, Maryam Karimi, Payam Zarrintaj, Mir Mehdi Seyedebrahimi, Mart\'in Carballo-Pacheco

entry.summary: My Chemical Harness is a route-native evolutionary framework for molecular design where the search population consists of executable synthetic pathways built from purchasable building blocks, with LLMs acting only as high-level strategy controllers and deterministic chemistry tools handling construction. It ensures candidate molecules come with feasible synthesis routes.

entry.title: A Scalable PyTorch Abstraction for Multi-GPU Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Matthew Cong, Francis Williams, Jonathan Swartz, Mark Harris, Sanja Fidler, Ken Museth

entry.summary: This work presents a scalable PyTorch backend for multi-GPU Gaussian splatting that distributes Gaussian parameters and splatting operators across GPUs via CUDA unified memory and NVLink at the operator level, requiring no explicit cross-device communication in model code. It scales neural reconstruction to higher resolutions and larger scenes.

entry.title: ISE: An Execution-Grounded Recipe for Multi-Turn OS-Agent Trajectories

author.name: Siyuan Luo, Nairong Zheng, Lin Zhou, Tiankuo Yao, Shengyou Yuan, Haojia Yu, Cong Pang, Jiapeng Luo, Lewei Lu

entry.summary: ISE is a three-stage synthesis paradigm (Intent, Simulate, Execute) for generating multi-turn OS-agent training trajectories, constructing ~50k structured intents via a 4D framework and grounding user simulation in actual execution outcomes. It produces data capturing structured intents, multi-turn delegation, and grounded tool execution absent from existing datasets.

entry.title: From Persistence to Survival: Hypothesis Testing, Effect Sizes and Vectorisation for Topological Features

author.name: Juliette Murris, Bernadette Stolz, Karsten Borgwardt

entry.summary: STRAND reframes topological persistence diagrams as survival data, treating each feature's persistence as a time-to-event and using the persistence survival function for comparison. This unifies statistical testing, effect sizes, and vectorization of topological features.

entry.title: ALIGNBEAM : Inference-Time Alignment Transfer via Cross-Vocabulary Logit Mixing

author.name: Chirag Chawla, Pratinav Seth, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

entry.summary: ALIGNBEAM is a training-free inference-time method to transfer safety alignment across models with different vocabularies by translating anchor logits token-by-token into the target vocabulary, then using a small LLM judge to select the safest continuation. It restores safety degraded by domain fine-tuning across model families.

entry.title: LoHoSearch: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Search Agents Beyond the Human Difficulty Ceiling

author.name: Jiarui Zhao, Rongzhi Zhang, Lingchuan Liu, Hao Yang, Xunliang Cai, Xi Su

entry.summary: LoHoSearch is a benchmark of 544 human-verified questions across 11 domains built via an automated pipeline over a knowledge graph of 7 million Wikipedia entities, designed to exceed the human difficulty ceiling of saturated search agent benchmarks. It maximizes search space size and structural complexity.

entry.title: Polar: A Benchmark for Evaluating Political Bias in LLMs

author.name: Sangho Kim, Heejin Kim, Yoonhee Park, Hyunggeun Jeon, Jaejin Lee

entry.summary: Polar is a 4,026-instance multiple-choice benchmark measuring political bias in LLMs via option-level likelihoods across two ideological axes and eight issue categories in both U.S. and South Korean contexts. Across 38 models, all lean left-progressive on U.S. content but show mixed patterns on Korean content.

entry.title: PersonaDrive: Human-Style Retrieval-Augmented VLA Agents for Closed-Loop Driving Simulation

author.name: Mahmoud Srewa, Praneetsai Iddamsetty, Mohammad Abdullah Al Faruque, Salma Elmalaki

entry.summary: PersonaDrive conditions a vision-language-action driving agent on retrieved demonstrations from human drivers explicitly instructed to drive in different styles, enabling more realistic non-ego traffic agents in CARLA closed-loop simulation. It improves on proxy-based style modeling.

entry.title: Iterating Toward Better Search: A Two-Agent Simulation Framework for Evaluating Agentic Search Architectures in E-Commerce

author.name: Jetlir Duraj, Jayanth Yetukuri, Shuang Zhou, Dhruv Varma, Rui Kong, Ishita Khan, Qunzhi Zhou

entry.summary: This paper presents a modular two-agent simulation framework for evaluating conversational shopping assistants, pairing a configurable buyer agent with interchangeable responders against a real e-commerce search API. It finds rolling-window memory outperforms intent-extraction memory while being faster.

entry.title: Is It You or Your Environment? A Bayesian Inference Framework for Genomically-Anchored Personalized Physiological Interpretation

author.name: Aruna Dey, Suraj Biswas

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Bayesian inference framework using an individual's genomic profile as an exogenous genetic anchor (a personalized prior fixed at conception) to solve the cold-start problem in personalized health AI, distinguishing constitutional variation from environmentally driven deviation. The anchor initializes a Bayesian belief state over physiological set points from GWAS-derived effect sizes.

entry.title: NaturalFlow: Reducing Disruptive Pauses for Natural Speech Flow in Simultaneous Speech-to-Speech Translation

author.name: Dongwook Lee, Youngho Cho, Sangkwon Park, Heeseung Kim, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: Introduces NaturalFlow, a fluency-aware optimization framework for simultaneous speech-to-speech translation that minimizes disruptive inter-chunk pauses using model-internal signals to balance low latency with natural acoustic flow. Reduces listener cognitive load.

entry.title: Toward Instructions-as-Code: Understanding the Impact of Instruction Files on Agentic Pull Requests

author.name: Ali Arabat, Mohammed Sayagh

entry.summary: Investigates the relationship between developer-authored instruction files and AI-agent pull request performance, analyzing 15,549 agentic PRs to assess whether instructions improve merge rate, handle complex tasks, and reduce merge effort. Proposes treating instructions-as-code.

entry.title: Accurate and Resource-Efficient Federated Continual Learning

author.name: Jebacyril Arockiaraj, Dhruv Parikh, Jayashree Adivarahan, Rajgopal Kannan, Viktor Prasanna

entry.summary: FedRAN is a resource-aware analytic federated continual learning framework that replaces gradient updates with compact random-feature statistics, transmitting truncated-SVD summaries of Gram matrices to cut communication cost. Avoids replay and full supervision.

entry.title: Kuramoto Attention: Synchronizing Self-Attention on the Torus

author.name: Joshua Nunley

entry.summary: Kuramoto attention treats hidden coordinates as angles and updates tokens via the Kuramoto synchronization coupling term, with the attention matrix acting as an adaptive content-dependent coupling kernel. Frames self-attention as phase synchronization on the torus.

entry.title: Physics-Distilled Neural Network enabled by Large Language Models for Manufacturing Process-Property Predictive Modeling

author.name: Ge Song, Kiarash Naghavi Khanghah, Anandkumar Patel, Rajiv Malhotra, Hongyi Xu

entry.summary: A knowledge distillation framework that extracts analytical physics priors from scientific literature via LLMs into a privileged teacher model, then distills to a lightweight student for manufacturing process-property prediction. Uses graph-masked attention to capture physical dependencies in data-scarce settings.

entry.title: Tree-Structured Orthonormal Decomposition of the Aitchison Simplex

author.name: Daisuke Yamada, Qijun Zhang, Travis Pence, Barbara B. Bendlin, Federico Rey, Vikas Singh

entry.summary: PolyILR provides a canonical orthonormal decomposition of the Aitchison tangent space aligned with any tree topology for compositional data, supporting arbitrary (non-binary) hierarchical structures. Yields interpretable coordinates respecting both geometry and known taxonomies.

entry.title: RCAP: Robust, Class-Aware, Probabilistic Dynamic Dataset Pruning

author.name: Atif Hassan, Swanand Khare, Jiaul H. Paik

entry.summary: RCAP is a robust, class-aware, probabilistic dynamic dataset pruning algorithm that uses a closed-form estimate of per-class sample fractions, adaptively adjusted via class-wise loss, to maintain worst-group accuracy at high pruning rates. Targets both balanced and imbalanced datasets.

entry.title: Fourier Features Let Agents Learn High Precision Policies with Imitation Learning

author.name: Bal\'azs Gyenes, Emiliyan Gospodinov, Jan Frieling, Enrico Krohmer, Nicolas Schreiber, Xiaogang Jia, Niklas Freymuth, Gerhard Neumann

entry.summary: The authors map point clouds into high-dimensional Fourier feature space to counteract neural networks' spectral bias toward low-frequency functions, enabling high-precision robotic manipulation policies via imitation learning. This improves fine-grained spatial reasoning over Cartesian-conditioned policies.

entry.title: ProcessThinker: Enhancing Multi-modal Large Language Models Reasoning via Rollout-based Process Reward

author.name: Jingpei Wu, Xiao Han, Weixiang Shen, Boer Zhang, Zifeng Ding, Volker Tresp

entry.summary: ProcessThinker provides step-level process rewards for multimodal LLM reasoning via rollout-based estimation, avoiding the need for large-scale chain-of-thought annotations required by traditional process reward models. It improves visual question answering requiring multi-step reasoning under RLVR/GRPO.

entry.title: Density estimation for Hellinger via minimum-distance estimators: mixtures of Gaussians, log-concave, and more

author.name: Spencer Compton, Jerry Li

entry.summary: This theoretical paper extends the minimum-distance estimator approach for density estimation from total variation to Hellinger distance, requiring only bounds on the VC dimension of a related concept class, with applications to Gaussian mixtures and log-concave densities. It provides a unified recipe yielding sharp Hellinger guarantees.

entry.title: Higher-Order Token Interactions via Quantum Attention

author.name: Jian Xu, Chao Li, Delu Zeng, John Paisley, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: Quantum Higher-Order Attention (QHA) is a shallow hardware-realizable quantum attention head that synthesizes order-k token interactions inside a quantum circuit via data re-uploading and an all-to-all non-Clifford entangler, with a proven expressivity separation from single standard self-attention layers. It enables higher-order interactions that classically require super-quadratic resources or depth.

entry.title: UniIntervene: Agentic Intervention for Efficient Real-World Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haoyuan Deng, Yitong Gao, Yudong Lin, Haichao Liu, Zhenyu Wu, Ziwei Wang

entry.summary: UniIntervene is an agentic intervention model for human-in-the-loop RL that autonomously detects unproductive exploration and recovers policies toward high-value states, reducing human correction burden in real-world robotic manipulation. It uses future-conditioned action-value estimation to take over most interventions.

entry.title: Shopping Reasoning Bench: An Expert-Authored Benchmark for Multi-Turn Conversational Shopping Assistants

author.name: Shuxian Fan, Seonwoo Min, Youna Hu, Botao Xia, Jayakrishnan Unnikrishnan, Rowan Musselmann, Yifan Gao, Qingyu Yin, Priyanka Nigam, Bing Yin

entry.summary: Shopping Reasoning Bench is an expert-authored benchmark of 525 missions with over 10,000 importance-weighted binary rubrics for evaluating multi-turn conversational shopping assistants. It captures open-ended reasoning, domain expertise, and criterion-level quality absent from prior e-commerce benchmarks.

entry.title: GENIE: A Fine-Grained Measure for Novelty

author.name: Ramya Namuduri, Manya Wadhwa, Anshun Asher Zheng, Greg Durrett, Junyi Jessy Li

entry.summary: GENIE is a fine-grained, task-specific metric for measuring the novelty of LLM-generated content along task-relevant features relative to a population of responses. It outperforms holistic metrics in capturing high-dimensional novelty and reveals which properties drive it.

entry.title: LEDGER: A Long-Context Benchmark of Corporate Annual Reports for Grounded Financial Retrieval and Extraction

author.name: Charles Moslonka, Amaury de Vitry, Arthur Garnier, Hicham Randrianarivo, Emmanuel Malherbe

entry.summary: LEDGER is a long-context benchmark of 4,999 digitized full corporate annual reports with figures, tables, and narrative, labeled with 31 financial KPIs linked to market reactions at earnings dates. It moves beyond plain-text SEC filings to enable rigorous grounded financial retrieval and extraction evaluation.

entry.title: TrajGenAgent: A Hierarchical LLM Agent for Human Mobility Trajectory Generation

author.name: Siyu Li, Toan Tran, Lingyi Zhao, Khurram Shafique, Li Xiong

entry.summary: TrajGenAgent is a hierarchical orchestrator-worker LLM agent framework for generating realistic synthetic human mobility trajectories without fine-tuning, balancing zero-shot reasoning with spatiotemporal grounding. It targets privacy-constrained applications in transportation and epidemiology.

entry.title: Reasoning for Mobile User Experience with Multimodal LLMs: Task, Benchmark, and Approach

author.name: Ruichao Mao, Zhou Fang, Teng Guo, Hao Yang, Yaping Li, Shaohua Peng, Maji Huang, Xiaoyu Lin, Shuoyang Liu, Xuepeng Li, Yuyu Zhang, Hai Rao

entry.summary: UXBench is a multimodal benchmark of 2,000 VQA samples across 8 tasks for assessing MLLMs' ability to reason about UI/UX issues (usability, consistency, functional clarity) from screenshots. It addresses the immature state of UX evaluation via UI screenshots.

entry.title: MOSAIC: Modality-Specific Adaptation for Incremental Continual Learning in Parkinson's Disease Gait Assessment

author.name: Minlin Zeng, Zhipeng Zhou, Yang Qiu, Martin J. McKeown, Zhiqi Shen

entry.summary: MOSAIC is a compact continual learning framework for modality-incremental Parkinson's disease gait assessment, introducing Modality-Specific Warm-Up to counter a Toxic Teacher phenomenon in cross-modal distillation. It handles new sensors arriving over time without access to historical data.

entry.title: G-Long: Graph-Enhanced Memory Management for Efficient Long-Term Dialogue Agents

author.name: Minjun Choi, Yoonjin Jang, Sangwon Youn, Youngjoong Ko

entry.summary: Proposes G-Long, a graph-enhanced memory framework for long-term dialogue agents that uses a fine-tuned small LM for triplet extraction and associative retrieval plus an attention-aware importance scoring mechanism, reducing operational cost versus LLM-based memory. Addresses long-context consistency.

entry.title: Transformer-Guided Graph Attention for Direct Cardiac Mesh Reconstruction: A Structural Digital Twin Framework

author.name: Abhishek H S, Akash Ganamukhi, Abhimanyu Suresh, Aditya G Hiremath, Prasad B Honnavalli, Adithya Balasubramanyam

entry.summary: Proposes an end-to-end network using a 3D Swin Transformer with graph attention that directly reconstructs simulation-ready cardiac surface meshes from raw 3D medical images, bypassing the slow segment-then-marching-cubes-then-cleanup workflow. Targets patient-specific cardiac digital twins.

entry.title: SupraBench: A Benchmark for Supramolecular Chemistry

author.name: Tianyi Ma, Yijun Ma, Zehong Wang, Weixiang Sun, Ziming Li, Connor R. Schmidt, Chuxu Zhang, Matthew J. Webber, Yanfang Ye

entry.summary: Introduces SupraBench, the first benchmark for evaluating LLMs on supramolecular chemistry host-guest reasoning across four tasks including binding affinity prediction, built in collaboration with domain experts. Addresses the lack of systematic LLM evaluation in this specialized chemistry domain.

entry.title: SwiftCTS: Fast Cross-Design Prediction and Pareto Optimization of Clock Tree Metrics via Few-Shot Calibration

author.name: Barsat Khadka, Kawsher Roxy, Md Rubel Ahmed

entry.summary: SwiftCTS is a physics-informed surrogate for clock tree synthesis prediction and Pareto optimization, using physics-grounded features with gradient-boosted ensembles for fast cross-design transfer. Trains in under five seconds and supports millions of evaluations.

entry.title: DeepRHP: A Hybrid Variational Autoencoder for Designing Random Heteropolymers as Protein Mimics

author.name: Shuni Li, Zhiyuan Ruan, Andy Shen, Ivan Jayapurna, Ting Xu, Haiyan Huang

entry.summary: DeepRHP is a hybrid semi-supervised VAE for designing random heteropolymers as protein mimics, equipping a classical VAE with a feature-based VAE so the latent space captures both chemical feature structure and sequence patterns. Guides RHP design for protein-like materials.

entry.title: Scalable Deep Learning Framework for Global High-Resolution Land Use Reconstruction

author.name: Amirpasha Mozaffari, Marina Casta\~no, Stefano Materia, Etienne Tourigny, Oscar Molina-Sedano, Jordi Varela-Agrelo, Dario Garcia-Gasulla, Miguel Castrillo Melguizo, Mario Acosta, Amanda Duarte

entry.summary: AI4Land is a scalable U-Net-based deep learning framework for generating high-resolution global land use and land cover reconstructions and projections from coarse scenario data and static geophysical features. First phase focuses on reconstruction to reduce land-surface uncertainty in climate models.

entry.title: Multimodal Ordinal Modeling of Alzheimer's Disease Severity Using Structural MRI and Clinical Data

author.name: Boris-Stephan Rauchmann, Jonathan Laib, Buse Ercik, Robert Perneczky, Sergio Altares-L\'opez

entry.summary: An attention-enhanced multimodal framework with ordinal regression for automated Alzheimer's disease severity staging, integrating structural MRI with demographic and genetic data. Uses strict cohort-stratified and held-out test splits across ADNI, AIBL, and NIFD.

entry.title: TaskFusion: Continual Anomaly Detection for Heterogeneous Tabular Data

author.name: Dayananda Herurkar, Federico Raue, Joachim Folz, J\"orn Hees, Andreas Dengel

entry.summary: TaskFusion is a continual anomaly detection method for heterogeneous tabular data with differing feature schemas, distribution shifts, and class imbalance, mapping task-specific features into a shared space and using outlier exposure. Overcomes the fixed-input-space assumption of conventional continual learning.

entry.title: Time-Series Foundation Model Embeddings for Remaining Useful Life Estimation

author.name: Amir El-Ghoussani, Michele De Vita, Ronald Naumann, Valiseios Belagiannis

entry.summary: Uses a frozen pretrained time-series foundation model (Chronos-2) as a feature extractor combined with a small regression head for remaining useful life estimation from multivariate sensor data. Shows consistent improvements over baselines on real industrial data.

entry.title: Phi-Actor-Critic: Steering General-Sum Games to Pareto-Efficient Correlated Equilibria

author.name: Wongyu Lee, Francesco Lelli, Omran Ayoub, Massimo Tornatore

entry.summary: Phi-Actor-Critic leverages swap regret minimization to steer multi-agent reinforcement learning in general-sum games toward Pareto-efficient correlated equilibria, overcoming the tendency of standard MARL to converge to socially inefficient Nash equilibria. It targets equilibrium selection rather than just equilibrium finding.

entry.title: Interpretable Neural Marked Statistics for Cosmological Inference

author.name: Federico Semenzato, Benjamin D. Wandelt, Michele Liguori, Alvise Raccanelli

entry.summary: This paper proposes a neural marking scheme for cosmological inference that generalizes marked statistics through interpretable, physically-motivated field transformations, using contrastive learning to align learnable marked summaries with cosmological parameters. It recovers non-Gaussian information beyond the power spectrum interpretably.

entry.title: Learning Object Manipulation from Scratch via Contrastive Interaction

author.name: Tongle Shen, Caleb Chuck, Fan Feng, Biwei Huang

entry.summary: This work formulates robotic manipulation dynamics as a piecewise-smooth Markov process, showing that object-centric interactions like contact and grasping create piecewise nonlinear reachability structures difficult for standard contrastive RL energy functions, and proposes a method to learn manipulation from scratch via contrastive interaction. It addresses why CRL struggles in interaction-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Teaching Diffusion to Speculate Left-to-Right

author.name: Lexington Whalen, Yuki Ito, Ryo Sakamoto

entry.summary: This work teaches block-diffusion language model drafters to speculate in a left-to-right manner for speculative decoding, addressing the subtlety that bidirectional within-block generation conflicts with the autoregressive verification of target models. It improves diffusion-based draft models for accelerating LLM inference.

entry.title: Seeing Below the Limit of Detection: A Censored-Poisson Bayesian Latent-Growth Change-Point Detector (the Span Detector) for Serial ctDNA in HR+/HER2- Metastatic Breast Cancer

author.name: Aarchi Singh Thakur, Abhijoy Sarkar

entry.summary: The Span Detector is a censored-Poisson Bayesian latent-growth change-point model for serial ctDNA that treats non-detects as left-censored observations rather than zeros, detecting drug resistance below the assay limit of detection. It accumulates faint signals over time for early cancer progression detection.

entry.title: Helping Figures Tell their Story! Paper-Grounded Video Generation Explaining Complex Scientific Figures

author.name: Ishani Mondal, Javad Baghirov, Jordan Boyd-Graber

entry.summary: MINARD generates paper-grounded, region-grounded narrated walkthrough videos that explain complex scientific figures step-by-step, alongside the FigTalk benchmark with sequential and component-level grounding metrics. It introduces the task of figure-to-video explanation generation.

entry.title: MARD: Mirror-Augmented Reasoning Distillation for Mechanism-Level Drug-Drug Interaction Prediction

author.name: Mohammadreza Riyazat, Vian Lelo, Rameen Jafri, Yumna Khan, Abeer Badawi

entry.summary: MARD uses mirror-augmented reasoning distillation to build a 7B model for mechanism-level drug-drug interaction prediction, identifying which enzyme axis is implicated and in which direction with auditable reasoning. It introduces a structured 7-family/147-subtype taxonomy and leakage-safe evaluation protocols.

entry.title: Detect, Remask, Repair: Diffusion Editing for Faithful Summarization of Evolving Contexts

author.name: Hao Zou, Zachary Horvitz, Chandhru Karthick, Zhou Yu, Kathleen McKeown

entry.summary: DETECT-REMASK-REPAIR is a diffusion-based framework for localized faithfulness repair of summaries, identifying, remasking, and repairing outdated spans with masked diffusion language models while preserving supported content. It introduces the StreamSum benchmark of synthetic event timelines.

entry.title: Rapid mixing for Gibbs measures in Riemannian manifolds

author.name: \'Angela Capel, Marco Castrill\'on-L\'opez, Sofyan Iblisdir, Angelo Lucia, Pablo P\'aez-Velasco, David P\'erez-Garc\'ia

entry.summary: Analyzes Langevin dynamics on Riemannian manifolds and identifies curvature, temperature, and saddle-point conditions ensuring a logarithmic Sobolev inequality and thus rapid mixing to the Gibbs measure. Under these conditions, polynomial-in-dimension mixing times are achievable, with implications excluding barren plateaus and spurious minima.

entry.title: Nous: An Attempt to Extract and Inject the Cognition Behind Prediction-Market Behavior

author.name: Haowei Qian

entry.summary: Nous extracts an eight-dimension behavioral profile from real Polymarket trading and injects it into LLM agents via prompts to recover human cognitive diversity and counter the correlated-error monoculture of foundation models. It finds extraction partially works but injection has limited effect.

entry.title: ERTS: Adversarial Robustness Testing of Ethical AI via Semantic Perturbation in a Bounded Consequence Space

author.name: Pratyush Chaudhari

entry.summary: ERTS is a closed-pipeline framework for adversarial robustness testing of ethical AI, encoding dilemmas into a 22-dimensional Ethical Consequence Space, applying semantic perturbations under validity constraints, and measuring decision deviation via an Ethical Instability Index. It targets high-stakes contexts like healthcare triage and hiring.

entry.title: scLLM-DSC: LLM-Knowledge Enhanced Cross-Modal Deep Structural Clustering for Single-Cell RNA Sequencing

author.name: Ping Xu, Pengjiang Li, Tian Du, Zaitian Wang, Jiawei Gu, Ziyue Qiao, Pengfei Wang, Yuanchun Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes scLLM-DSC, an LLM-knowledge enhanced cross-modal deep structural clustering framework for single-cell RNA sequencing that injects biological gene-function semantics rather than relying solely on numerical patterns. Aims to improve cell-population identification.

entry.title: MP3: Multi-Period Pattern Pre-training forSpatio-Temporal Forecasting

author.name: Lilan Peng, Yandi Liu, Qingren Yao, Chongshou Li, Tianrui Li

entry.summary: Introduces MP3, a multi-period pattern pre-training plugin for spatio-temporal forecasting that addresses the temporal mirage problem where similar inputs yield divergent futures, using multi-period pattern learning to distinguish such cases. Targets transportation, climate, and energy forecasting.

entry.title: Dual-Domain Equivariant Generative Adversarial Network for Multimodal CT-PET Synthesis

author.name: Gabriel Steele, Alzahra Altalib, Alessandro Perelli

entry.summary: Presents DDE-GAN, a dual-domain equivariant GAN for CT-PET image synthesis that jointly learns in spatial and Fourier domains and embeds rotational equivariance from CT/PET physics into generator and discriminator losses to improve structural and anatomical fidelity. Uses hierarchical dual-domain training.

entry.title: SkMTEB: Slovak Massive Text Embedding Benchmark and Model Adaptation

author.name: Marek \v{S}uppa, Andrej Ridzik, Daniel Hl\'adek, Nat\'alia K\v{n}a\v{z}ekov\'a, Vikt\'oria Ondrejov\'a

entry.summary: Introduces SkMTEB, the first comprehensive MTEB-style text embedding benchmark for Slovak with 31 datasets across 7 task types, and develops efficient e5-sk-small/large embedding models via vocabulary trimming and fine-tuning. Reveals that Slovak NLU-specific models transfer poorly to embedding tasks.

entry.title: Bernstein-Schur Kernels: Random Features by Sketched Modulation and Radial Randomization

author.name: Taha Bouhsine

entry.summary: Introduces Bernstein-Schur kernels and a random-feature construction for a class of nonstationary kernels that fall between shift-invariant and dot-product templates. Provides unbiasedness and variance guarantees with reduced feature dimension.

entry.title: Energy-Conserved Neural Pipelines: Attenuating Error Propagation in Modular Neural Networks via Physical Conservation Constraints

author.name: David Young, Swan Yi Htet

entry.summary: Introduces energy conservation as a hard constraint on inter-module information flow in modular neural pipelines to attenuate compounding error propagation. Demonstrates substantially improved noise robustness on CIFAR-10 versus baselines.

entry.title: RePAIR: Predictive Self-Supervised Representation Learning in Chess

author.name: Christoph Koller, Johannes F\"urnkranz, Timo Bertram

entry.summary: RePAIR is a self-supervised representation learning architecture synthesizing masked autoencoders, JEPA, and BERT to encode sequential chess positions into compact representations via iterative refinement in a lower-dimensional embedding space. Masks latent states and repairs gaps with a lightweight predictor.

entry.title: Implicit Neural Representations of Individual Behavior

author.name: Andrew Kang, Priya Narasimhan

entry.summary: Behavioral INR is a self-supervised generative model adapting implicit neural representations to behavior, representing each policy as a state-action function modulated by an episode-level latent via FiLM layers. It learns policy representations from unlabeled multi-policy data for robotics, games, and demonstrations.

entry.title: Compatibility-Aware Dynamic Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models

author.name: Yucheng Zhou, Junwei Sheng, Qianning Wang, Jianbing Shen

entry.summary: CADFT extends Dynamic Fine-Tuning by controlling sample-level optimization variance through a dynamic policy-dependent coefficient, addressing demonstration-policy mismatch in heterogeneous instruction data. It improves the stability and generalization of supervised fine-tuning for LLMs.

entry.title: APEX: Automated Prompt Engineering eXpert with Dynamic Data Selection

author.name: Fei Wang, Si Si, Cho-Jui Hsieh, Inderjit S. Dhillon

entry.summary: APEX is an automatic prompt optimization framework that jointly optimizes data usage and prompt search, dynamically stratifying the development dataset into Easy, Hard, and Mixed tiers and prioritizing the Mixed tier where the LLM has variable performance. It improves data efficiency over evolutionary prompt-optimization methods that treat data as static.

entry.title: Substrate Asymmetry in User-Side Memory: A Diagnostic Framework

author.name: Youwang Deng

entry.summary: This work argues LLM user-side memory should not be scored as a single personalization metric, decomposing it into behavioral consistency, factual presence, and factual absence axes. It finds per-user LoRA wins on style while RAG wins on factual recall, with no substrate dominating all axes.

entry.title: Mathematical perspective on genetic algorithms with optimization guided operators

author.name: Anna Brandenberger, Ilan Doron-Arad, Elchanan Mossel

entry.summary: This paper provides a mathematical model of genetic algorithms with ML optimization-guided mutation and recombination operators, where operators actively improve objectives rather than acting randomly. It analyzes the tradeoff between higher per-step improvement and increased computational cost.

entry.title: Adjoint Method versus Physics-Informed Neural Networks in PDE-Constrained Inverse Problems

author.name: Zhen Zhang, Alessandro Alla, George Em Karniadakis

entry.summary: This paper provides a fair, controlled comparison of adjoint-based optimization versus physics-informed neural networks for PDE-constrained inverse problems, matching domains, equations, optimizers, and regularization. It clarifies the relative performance of the two approaches.

entry.title: Context-Driven Incremental Compression for Multi-Turn Dialogue Generation

author.name: Yeongseo Jung, Jaehyeok Kim, Eunseo Jung, Jiachuan Wang, Yongqi Zhang, Ka Chun Cheung, Simon See, Lei Chen

entry.summary: C-DIC introduces context-driven incremental compression for multi-turn dialogue, treating conversations as interleaved threads and storing revisable per-thread compression states in a compact shared memory. It improves efficiency and robustness over truncation, summarization, and prior context compressors.

entry.title: Construct validity of Claude Opus 4.8's System Card – A commentary

author.name: Maria Federica Martino Lena

entry.summary: A commentary examining the Claude Opus 4.8 system card with a focus on the construct validity of its alignment evaluations. It raises three concerns: chain-of-thought monitoring missing unsurfaced reasoning, underestimated evaluation awareness, and evaluators drawn from the same model family possibly sharing assumptions.

entry.title: Once-for-All: Scalable Simultaneous Forecasting via Equilibrium State Estimation

author.name: Beinan Xu, Andy Song, Jiti Gao, Feng Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Equilibrium State Estimation, a paradigm for simultaneous forecasting of multiple interacting systems in a single pass by first estimating a cross-system equilibrium then forecasting deviations from it. Demonstrated on currency exchange and COVID-19 spread datasets.

entry.title: Ontology Memory-Augmented ASR Correction for Long Text-Speech Interleaved Conversations

author.name: Xinxin Li, Huiyao Chen, Meishan Zhang, Yunxin Li, Zulong Chen, Zhibo Ren, Xiaoqing Dong Baotian Hu, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes an ontology memory-augmented ASR correction framework for long text-speech interleaved conversations, organizing interaction history into a dynamically updatable ontology memory to locate sparse correction evidence amid redundancy. Moves beyond isolated-utterance ASR correction.

entry.title: Massive Open-Vocabulary Keyword Spotting

author.name: Leonor Barreiros, Raul Monteiro, Afonso Mendes, Gon\c{c}alo M. Correia

entry.summary: This paper proposes a massive open-vocabulary keyword spotting system with contextual biasing that stores features up to 128x more compactly than baselines, enabling processing of huge glossaries while remaining open-vocabulary and language-agnostic without fine-tuning the ASR model. It mitigates poor transcription of rare specialized terminology.

entry.title: SPADE: Split-and-Delay Embeddings for Autoregressive High-Granularity Calorimeter Simulation

author.name: Joschka Birk, Frank Gaede, Anna Hallin, Gregor Kasieczka, Martina Mozzanica, Henning Rose

entry.summary: SPADE is an autoregressive transformer for multi-feature token sequences that embeds features independently and delays each feature stream relative to the previous, allowing self-attention to learn intra-token correlations. Applied to high-granularity calorimeter shower simulation, it is competitive with state-of-the-art models and outperforms VQ-VAE predecessors.

entry.title: Measuring Semantic Progress in Multi-turn Dialogue via Information Gain

author.name: Paul He, Shiva Kasiviswanathan, Dominik Janzing

entry.summary: This work formalizes semantic progress in multi-turn information-seeking dialogue as question-conditioned uncertainty reduction and introduces an information-theoretic metric approximating it in embedding space. It uses a tractable Gaussian formulation with closed-form updates for measuring accumulated non-redundant information.

entry.title: Small LLMs for Biomedical Claim Verification: Cost-Effective Fine-Tuning, Structural Dataset Shortcuts, and Cross-Domain Generalization

author.name: Gaurav Kumar

entry.summary: This study fine-tunes small LLMs (Phi-3-mini, Qwen2.5-3B, Mistral-7B) via QLoRA for biomedical claim verification, with Mistral-7B surpassing GPT-4o and GPT-5 by up to 12% F1 at a fraction of the cost using just 1,008 examples. It also identifies a structural dataset artifact in SciFact and tests cross-domain generalization.

entry.title: A Tutorial on World Models and Physical AI

author.name: Il-Seok Oh

entry.summary: This tutorial surveys world models and physical AI, distinguishing explicit world models (structured dynamics for planning) from implicit ones (predictive structure in learned representations), with applications in robotics and autonomous driving. It outlines open challenges toward unified perception-prediction-action systems.

entry.title: Multi-Field Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Maritime Accident Root Cause Analysis

author.name: Seongjin Kim, Sungil Kim

entry.summary: This paper proposes a multi-field hybrid RAG framework for maritime accident root cause analysis over 13,329 Korea Maritime Safety Tribunal reports, structuring adjudications into incident cards indexed by Summary, Causes, and Disposition fields with a hierarchical cause taxonomy. It uses field-aware sparse-dense fusion via reciprocal rank fusion.

entry.title: NTS-CoT: Mitigating Hallucinations in LLM-based News Timeline Summarization with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Feng Lyu, Huiqin Yan, Sijing Duan, Hao Wu, Shuang Gu, Xue Qiao, Weixu Zhang, Haolun Wu

entry.summary: Introduces NTS-CoT, a chain-of-thought framework for LLM-based news timeline summarization that mitigates two hallucination types—unfaithful summarization and information omission—via element extraction, date selection, and temporal reasoning modules. Targets faithful event-tracking summaries.

entry.title: Decoding Insect Song: A Multitask Semisupervised Orthoptera Bioacoustic Classifier

author.name: Olga Isupova, Danil Kuzin, Ella Browning, Tom Mills, Steven Reece

entry.summary: Presents PULSE, a semi-supervised multi-task framework for Orthoptera (insect) bioacoustic classification combining weak supervision, self-supervised learning on field audio, and knowledge distillation from a general bioacoustic model. Substantially outperforms a SOTA general model and enables ecologically meaningful embeddings.

entry.title: Towards Personalized Federated Learning for Dysarthric Speech Recognition

author.name: Tao Zhong, Mengzhe Geng, Jiajun Deng, Shujie Hu, Xunying Liu

entry.summary: Explores personalized federated learning for dysarthric speech recognition, comparing parameter-based and embedding-based aggregation strategies to handle speaker heterogeneity while preserving privacy. Shows significant WER improvements over regularized FedAvg on UASpeech and TORGO.

entry.title: Restless bandits with imperfect binary feedback: PCL-indexability analysis and computation

author.name: Jos\'e Ni\~no-Mora

entry.summary: Develops a partial conservation laws framework for analyzing indexability and computing the Whittle index in restless bandits with binary latent states and imperfect binary feedback, motivated by opportunistic spectrum access with sensing errors. Provides tractable expressions across threshold regimes.

entry.title: Physics-informed generative AI for semiconductor manufacturing: Enforcing hard physical constraints in generative models by construction

author.name: Yaser Mike Banad, Sarah Sharif

entry.summary: A perspective arguing that generative AI for semiconductor manufacturing must enforce hard physical constraints by construction rather than via post-hoc filtering. Frames constrained physical generation as a broader computational-science challenge.

entry.title: Loss Landscape Diagnosis for Gradient-Based Gray-Scott System Inversion: Disentangling the Roles of PINN Components

author.name: Yan Yang

entry.summary: A diagnostic study backpropagating through unrolled Gray-Scott PDE simulation to recover parameters, revealing why direct gradient-based inversion fails due to flat plateaus and sharp cliffs aligned with bifurcation boundaries. Disentangles roles of PINN components.

entry.title: Federated continual learning: A comprehensive survey on lifelong and privacy-preserving learning over distributed and non-stationary data

author.name: Masoume Gholizade, Fabrizio Ruffini, Pietro Ducange, Francesco Marcelloni

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey on federated continual learning, covering lifelong and privacy-preserving learning over distributed, non-stationary data. Bridges federated learning and continual learning constraints like privacy, communication, and heterogeneity.

entry.title: Mahalanobis-Guided Latent OOD Detection for Hybrid ES-DRL Control in Time-Varying Systems

author.name: Shaifalee Saxena, Alexander Scheinker

entry.summary: Uses Mahalanobis distance in a VAE latent space to detect out-of-distribution observations and trigger switching between an RL controller and extremum-seeking control in time-varying systems. Applied to beam-profile control.

entry.title: What Uncertainties Do We Need for Dynamical Systems?

author.name: Yusuf Sale, Christopher B\"ulte, Felix Czaja, Joshua Stiller, Eyke H\"ullermeier

entry.summary: A perspective paper offering a machine-learning view on uncertainty modeling for dynamical systems, clarifying aleatoric versus epistemic sources and how representation and quantification objectives vary across tasks. Asks what uncertainties are actually needed for dynamical systems.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Disrupts Gradient-Based Adversarial Optimization

author.name: Xinhai Zou, Chang Zhao, Alireza Aghabagherloo, Dave Singel\'ee, Robin Degraeve, Bart Preneel

entry.summary: This work finds that training image classifiers with policy-gradient RL objectives disrupts the gradient structure exploited by gradient-based adversarial attacks, supported by loss-landscape and gradient analyses across CIFAR and ImageNet-100. It proposes RL training as an adversarial defense mechanism.

entry.title: Harness In-Context Operator Learning with Chain of Operators

author.name: Minghui Yang, Ling Guo, Liu Yang

entry.summary: Chain of Operators (CHOP) harnesses a frozen In-Context Operator Network to generalize to out-of-distribution operator-learning tasks by constructing chains of explicit elementary operators, without parameter updates. It transfers LLM-style prompting strategies to neural operator learning.

entry.title: Energy-Efficient On-Device RAG on a Mobile NPU: System Design and Benchmark on Snapdragon X Elite

author.name: Zhiyuan Cheng, Longying Lai

entry.summary: This paper presents the first end-to-end RAG pipeline running all neural stages (embedding, reranking, LLM generation) entirely on a mobile NPU (Qualcomm Hexagon on Snapdragon X Elite), achieving 9.1x higher embedding throughput and 12.3x less energy than CPU on indexing. It demonstrates energy-efficient on-device RAG for privacy and offline use.

entry.title: Geometric bias in eigenspace perturbation under random heterogeneous noise

author.name: Fengkai Liu, Ke Wang, Wanjie Wang

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies eigenspace perturbation of signal-plus-noise matrices under sparse, heterogeneous-variance random noise, demonstrating a geometric bias that the worst-case Davis-Kahan/Wedin bounds fail to capture. It refines spectral method stability analysis for inhomogeneous noise settings.

entry.title: FlexiBrain: Resolution-Agnostic Voxel-Level Encoding for Native fMRI

author.name: Mo Wang, Wenhao Ye, Junfeng Xia, Minghao Xu, Hongkai Wen, Quanying Liu

entry.summary: FlexiBrain is a resolution-agnostic voxel-level encoding framework for native fMRI based on Mamba-JEPA that defines patch sizes in real-world physical units, handling spatial and temporal resolution heterogeneity across datasets without rigid preprocessing. It avoids degradation of subject-specific anatomy and reduces computational overhead.

entry.title: Enhancing Spectral Embedding through Robust and Flexible Knowledge Transfer in Electronic Health Records

author.name: Feiqing Huang, Zongqi Xia, Rong Ma, Tianxi Cai

entry.summary: This work proposes a spectral-based unsupervised representation learning framework for clinical concepts and patients in rare-disease EHR cohorts, transferring knowledge from a broader population while relaxing restrictive one-to-one signal-alignment assumptions via a two-step spectral embedding procedure. It enables robust low-dimensional embeddings in high-dimensional, small-sample settings.

entry.title: When Do Data-Driven Systems Exhibit the Capability to Infer?

author.name: Maximilian Poretschkin, Tabea Naeven

entry.summary: Motivated by the EU AI Act's undefined notion of inference capability, this work uses statistical learning theory to determine when data-driven systems like credit scoring qualify as AI under the regulation. It addresses a legal gray area with formal analysis.

entry.title: GraspLLM: Towards Zero-Shot Generalization on Text-Attributed Graphs with LLMs

author.name: Hengyi Feng, Zeang Sheng, Meiyi Qiang, Li Yang, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: GraspLLM combines graph structural comprehension with LLM semantic understanding for zero-shot generalization on text-attributed graphs across diverse datasets and tasks. It aims to capture transferable structural patterns that existing LLM-graph methods miss.

entry.title: SafeLLM: Extraction as a Hallucination-Resistant Alternative to Rewriting in Safety-Critical Settings

author.name: Julia Ive, Felix Jozsa, Evridiki Georgaki, Nabeel Sheikh, Emma Cattell, Nick Jackson, Paulina Bondaronek, Ciaran Scott Hill, Richard Dobson

entry.summary: SafeLLM proposes extraction as a hallucination-resistant alternative to free-form rewriting in safety-critical RAG settings like SOPs and HR policies, comparing line-number-based source selection and guideline extraction strategies. It balances precision, recall, and safety across document types and model scales.

entry.title: M\"OVE: A Holistic LLM Benchmark for the German Public Sector

author.name: Camilla Dalerci, Thilo Michael, Robin Schaefer, Daniel Weinland

entry.summary: MOEVE is a holistic benchmark evaluating 39 LLMs for the German public sector across performance criteria (summarization, QA, topic extraction) and governance criteria including hallucination, energy consumption, transparency, and constitutional alignment. It addresses ad hoc model selection in public administration.

entry.title: On McDiarmid's Inequality under Dependence via Approximate Tensorization of Entropy

author.name: Valentin Roth

entry.summary: Argues that dependent versions of McDiarmid's inequality, derived via approximate tensorization of entropy, are useful but underused in statistics and learning theory. It derives the inequality for non-isotropic Gaussian vectors with a constant scaling like the covariance condition number.

entry.title: A Three-Layer Framework for AI in Scientific Discovery

author.name: Guojun Liao

entry.summary: This paper proposes a three-layer view of AI in scientific discovery: search/retrieval by LLMs (Layer 1), model formation through qualitative reasoning (Layer 2, the main innovation), and execution via optimization/simulation/automation (Layer 3). It argues current discussions neglect the central act of forming and evolving models through structural insight.

entry.title: IVIE: A Neuro-symbolic Approach to Incremental and Validated Generation of Interactive Fiction Worlds

author.name: Micaela Vaucher, Santiago Silveira, Santiago G\'ongora, Luis Chiruzzo

entry.summary: Introduces IVIE, a neuro-symbolic system for incrementally generating complete, playable interactive fiction worlds, delegating creative decisions to LLMs while grounding world state through symbolic validation. Balances creative flexibility with coherence in a four-stage pipeline.

entry.title: Heterogeneous LiDAR Early Fusion and Learned Re-Ranking Strategy for Robust Long-Term Place Recognition in Unstructured Environments

author.name: Judith Vilella-Cantos, Juan Jos\'e Cabrera, M\'onica Ballesta, David Valiente, Luis Pay\'a

entry.summary: Proposes MinkUNeXt-VINE++, combining early fusion of heterogeneous LiDAR data from two sensors with a learned re-ranking strategy at inference for robust long-term place recognition in unstructured environments like agricultural fields. Leverages complementary sensor strengths.

entry.title: Contrast-Informed Augmentation and Domain-Adversarial Training for Adult-to-Neonatal MR Reconstruction Generalization

author.name: Stephen Moore, Lara Leijser, Richard Frayne, Roberto Souza

entry.summary: Investigates contrast-informed data augmentation and domain-adversarial training to improve adult-to-neonatal generalization of the E2E-VarNet MRI reconstruction model, evaluating three training regimes on undersampled brain MR data at multiple acceleration factors. Addresses domain shift in medical reconstruction.

entry.title: LatticeBridge: Rare-Event Sequential Inference for Faithful Structured Sequence Synthesis

author.name: Faruk Alpay, Bugra Kilictas

entry.summary: LatticeBridge frames constrained structured sequence generation as rare-event sequential inference, combining a prefix language model, instance-compiled surface automata, and twisted sequential Monte Carlo with multilevel splitting to satisfy multiple input-derived constraints jointly. It improves faithful generation when standard decoding under-weights constraint-satisfying continuations.

entry.title: Corpus Augmentation for Sign Language Translation via LLM-Guided Video Stitching

author.name: Zsolt Robotka, \'Ad\'am R\'ak, Jalal Al-Afandi, Andr\'as Horv\'ath, Gy\"orgy Cserey

entry.summary: This work augments sign language translation corpora via LLM-guided video stitching, generating new sign video-text pairs from existing gloss-annotated data without external corpora or generative video models. It addresses the scarcity of parallel data for fine-tuning.

entry.title: Rigel: Reverse-Engineering the Metal 4.1 Tensor Compute Path on the Apple M4 Max GPU

author.name: Ramchand Kumaresan

entry.summary: Rigel empirically reverse-engineers Apple's hidden Metal 4.1 tensor compute path on the M4 Max GPU using a checksum-gated microbenchmark harness, recovering eleven facts the specification hides about hardware acceleration, accumulator widths, and matrix partitioning. It exposes where and how matmul operations physically execute.

entry.title: PRISM: Prosody-Integrated Multi-Agent Reasoning Framework for Empathetic Spoken Dialogue

author.name: Wen Zhang, Xiaocui Yang, Zhuoyue Gao, Shi Feng, Daling Wang, Yifei Zhang

entry.summary: PRISM is a multi-agent framework for empathetic spoken dialogue that decouples speech perception, response generation, and synthesis, introducing a prosody-to-language translation mechanism to stabilize LLM reasoning. It enables on-demand knowledge tool invocation for emotionally aligned responses.

entry.title: Calibrating simplified vine copulas with a noise contrastive estimation approach

author.name: Michael Denis Kraus, David Huk, Claudia Czado

entry.summary: Proposes a calibration strategy for simplified vine copula models that adds observation-specific correction factors derived via noise contrastive estimation, reframed as a binary classification density-estimation task. This relaxes the restrictive simplifying assumption when conditional dependence varies.

entry.title: Symmetry-electronic fingerprints reveal competing magnetic phases in two-dimensional materials

author.name: Addis Fuhr, Zachary R. Fox, David Parker, Ayana Ghosh

entry.summary: Introduces a symmetry-electronic fingerprint representation that encodes crystallographic symmetry, Wyckoff-site geometry, and site-resolved electronic structure to predict magnetic ground states of 2D materials. Combined with random forests, it classifies magnetic ordering and regresses moments and anisotropy with physical interpretability.

entry.title: Definitional alignment before capability alignment: a Design-Science framework for adjudicating claims about AGI

author.name: J. E. Aguilera Briones

entry.summary: This article treats AGI's lack of a stable shared definition as a governance and design problem, proposing DAF-AGI, a conceptual artifact with ordinal criteria for assessing definition fitness and a governance audit. It demonstrates the framework on five prominent AGI definitions.

entry.title: A Minimal Model of Bounded Trade-Off Screening in Multi-Attribute Choice

author.name: Manisha Dubey, Anirban Sarkar, Subramanian Ramamoorthy

entry.summary: This paper proposes a bounded trade-off screening model of multi-attribute choice where decisions are governed by a screening process with a tolerance parameter, departing from fully compensatory utility aggregation. Simulations show it captures context-dependent preference patterns not produced by standard utility models.

entry.title: Cascade Classification of Dermoscopic Images of Skin Neoplasms with Controllable Sensitivity and External Clinical Validation

author.name: Elena S. Kozachok, Sergey S. Seregin, Aleksandr V. Kozachok, Ilya P. Latyshev, Oleg I. Samovarov

entry.summary: Compares deep learning architectures and classification schemes for dermoscopic skin neoplasm images, testing a two-stage cascade with controllable sensitivity and validating generalization from open ISIC data to independent Russian clinical datasets. Evaluates ViT, Swin, ConvNeXt, and EfficientNetV2.

entry.title: Rarity-Gated Context Conditioning for Offline Imitation Learning-Based Maritime Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yongmin Kim, ByeongHoon Jeon, Sungil Kim

entry.summary: Proposes Rarity-Gated Feature-wise Linear Modulation, an imitation-learning conditioning module for maritime anomaly detection that combines feature modulation with a rarity-score gate to handle highly imbalanced context distributions and reduce false alarms in rare regimes. Targets contextual anomaly detection.

entry.title: PermDoRA -- Understanding Adapter Interference in Language Models: Limits of Parameter-Space Geometry

author.name: Gowtham Sivaramakrishnan, Sarvesha Kumar Kombaiah Seetha, Kishan Gupta Balaji, Santhosh Baradwaj Vaduvur Ranganathan
