entry.summary: Ouroboros-Spatial is a self-evolving training loop where a frozen proposer generates spatial QA pairs with executable verification from 3D scene metadata and video, and a solver trains on them, closing the data-model loop for spatial reasoning. It improves data efficiency by adapting difficulty to the model's evolving capability.

entry.title: Bridging the Morphology Gap: Adapting VLA Models to Dexterous Manipulation via Intent-Conditioned Fine-Tuning

author.name: Chuanke Pang, Junyi Huang, Zhijun Zhao, Yaobing Wang, Kun Xu, Xilun Ding

entry.summary: This paper introduces InDex, a data-efficient framework for adapting VLA models from low-DoF parallel grippers to high-DoF dexterous hands, addressing the morphology gap that causes catastrophic forgetting. It repurposes pre-trained grasp output as a continuous virtual grasp intent proxy via intent-conditioned fine-tuning.

entry.title: Market Design for AI: Beyond the Copyright Binary

author.name: Yan Dai, Maryam Farboodi, Negin Golrezaei, Sepehr Shahshahani

entry.summary: This economics-of-AI paper designs a market for human-generated training content that balances technological progress with creator incentives, showing both free-for-all and strong-IP models fail. It models the problem as a Stackelberg game and identifies an originality penalty and dynamic market failures.

entry.title: APPO: Agentic Procedural Policy Optimization

author.name: Xucong Wang, Ziyu Ma, Yong Wang, Yuxiang Ji, Shidong Yang, Guanhua Chen, Pengkun Wang, Xiangxiang Chu

entry.summary: APPO (Agentic Procedural Policy Optimization) improves credit assignment in agentic RL for multi-turn tool-use by studying where to branch and how to assign credit after branching, finding influential decision points are broadly distributed rather than concentrated at tool calls. It moves beyond coarse heuristic credit units.

entry.title: Structure-Preserving Neural Surrogates with Tractable Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Handi Zhang, Adrienne M. Propp, Brooks Kinch, Houman Owhadi, Nathaniel Trask

entry.summary: This work builds structure-preserving neural surrogates for PDEs that incorporate physical conservation laws and provide closed-form uncertainty quantification via Gaussian processes derived from exterior calculus topology. It bridges scientific ML speed with simulator-grade verification.

entry.title: RLCSD: Reinforcement Learning with Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Leyi Pan, Shuchang Tao, Yunpeng Zhai, Lingzhe Zhang, Zhaoyang Liu, Bolin Ding, Aiwei Liu, Lijie Wen

entry.summary: RLCSD identifies a pathology in on-policy self-distillation where the learning signal concentrates on stylistic tokens rather than task-relevant ones, causing style drift and length collapse. It mitigates this by contrasting teacher-student gaps under correct versus incorrect contexts.

entry.title: Online Shift Detection and Conformal Adaptation for Deployed Safety Classifiers

author.name: Jun Wen Leong

entry.summary: This work presents an online monitoring system that detects distributional shift in deployed safety classifiers using calibrated sequential statistics and adapts decision thresholds via conformal abstention. A pre-registered factorial evaluation shows high valid-detection rates across synthetic, jailbreak, and adversarial shifts.

entry.title: Density estimation for Hellinger via minimum-distance estimators: mixtures of Gaussians, log-concave, and more

author.name: Spencer Compton, Jerry Li

entry.summary: This paper extends the minimum-distance estimator approach for density estimation from total variation to Hellinger distance, showing that bounding the VC dimension of a related concept class yields sharp guarantees. It applies to mixtures of Gaussians, log-concave densities, and more.

entry.title: TacCoRL: Integrating Tactile Feedback into VLA via Simulation

author.name: Siyu Ma, Yuqi Liang, Chang Yu, Yunuo Chen, Hao Su, Yixin Zhu, Yin Yang, Chenfanfu Jiang

entry.summary: TacCoRL integrates tactile feedback into vision-language-action robot policies using sim-real co-training and simulation-based RL, avoiding the need for large tactile pretraining or risky real-world contact exploration. It focuses on learning how touch should modulate actions in rare near-failure states for contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Learning What to Say to Your VLA: Mostly Harmless Vision Language Action Model Steering

author.name: Hyun Joe Jeong, Gokul Swamy, Andrea Bajcsy

entry.summary: This framework interactively searches for language sequences that improve closed-loop VLA task performance, distills them into a test-time language feedback policy, and learns a head predicting when language steering will help. It addresses the brittle, unintuitive mapping from language to robot behavior in VLAs.

entry.title: When Does Language Matter? Multilingual Instructions Reveal Step-wise Language Sensitivity in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Xuan Dong, Zhe Han, Tianhao Niu, Qingfu Zhu, Wanxiang Che

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic multilingual evaluation of VLA models by translating the LIBERO benchmark into ten languages, revealing 30-50% success-rate drops under non-English instructions. It finds language influence is highly non-uniform across task steps and proposes a step-wise inference-time intervention.

entry.title: Doc-to-Atom: Learning to Compile and Compose Memory Atoms

author.name: Xingjian Diao, Wenbo Li, Yashas Malur Saidutta, Avinash Amballa, Lazar Valkov, Srinivas Chappidi

entry.summary: ModSleuth is an agentic system that recursively reconstructs LLM dependency graphs from fragmented public artifacts with source-grounded evidence, auditing invisible recursive dependencies (data generation, filtering, judging). It finds the main challenge is defining and reconciling what counts as a dependency rather than extraction.

entry.title: UniReason-Med: A Shared Grounded Reasoning Interface for 2D-to-3D Transfer in Medical VQA

author.name: Mengzhuo Chen, Yan Shu, Chi Liu, Hongming Piao, Xidong Wang, Derek Li, Bryan Dai

entry.summary: Presents UniReason-Med, a single-checkpoint framework enabling 2D-to-3D transfer in medical VQA via a shared grounded reasoning interface, trained on a 220K instruction-tuning dataset with interleaved reasoning and visual evidence. Matters for leveraging abundant 2D medical data to improve scarce 3D medical understanding.

entry.title: 4DP-QA: Scalable QA for 4D Perception in Vision Language Models

author.name: Seokju Cho, Abhishek Badki, Hang Su, Jindong Jiang, Ziyao Zeng, Seungryong Kim, Sifei Liu, Orazio Gallo

entry.summary: Presents 4DP-QA, a scalable QA generation pipeline for evaluating VLM understanding of 4D scene dynamics, introducing True-Motion Tracking to disentangle camera and object motion. From a strong NVIDIA-affiliated team addressing a recognized VLM weakness in dynamic reasoning.

entry.title: Sequent: scale and automation for higher confidence in alignment

author.name: Geoffrey Irving

entry.summary: Announces Sequent, a large new nonprofit aiming for higher-confidence AI alignment via a portfolio of theory and empirical bets heavily augmented by automation, drawing on researchers from UK AISI's Alignment Team and Timaeus. It argues theory unlocks better automation and aims for 40-80 FTE within two years.

entry.title: Embodied-R1.5: Evolving Physical Intelligence via Embodied Foundation Models

author.name: Yifu Yuan, Yaoting Huang, Xianze Yao, Yutong Li, Shuoheng Zhang, Linqi Han, Pengyi Li, Jiangeng Sun, Wenting Jia, Zhao Zhang, Yuhao Liu, Ruihao Liao, Yucheng Hu, Qiyu Wu, Yuxiao Li, Zibin Dong, Fei Ni, Yan Zheng, Shuyang Gu, Yi Ma, Hongyao Tang, Han Hu, Jianye Hao

entry.summary: Embodied-R1.5 is a unified 8B-parameter embodied foundation model integrating embodied cognition, task planning, correction, and pointing, trained on over 15B tokens via three automated data pipelines and a multi-task balanced RL recipe. It introduces a Planner-Grounder-Corrector closed loop for autonomous self-correction on long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Decomposition for Multimodal Interaction Learning

author.name: Zequn Yang, Yake Wei, Haotian Ni, Zhihao Xu, Di Hu

entry.summary: This paper offers an information-theoretic decomposition of multimodal interactions into redundant, unique, and synergistic components, arguing these vary dynamically per sample and that conventional paradigms fail to capture synergy or fully use redundancy. It motivates approaches that learn sample-specific interaction types.

entry.title: Sparse probes and murky physics: a case study of interpretability challenges in a foundation model for continuum dynamics

author.name: Katherine Rosenfeld, Maike Sonnewald

entry.summary: This case study applies sparse autoencoders guided by physical principles to interpret a continuum-dynamics foundation model (Walrus by Polymathic), triaging over 20,000 features to ask whether internal mechanisms align with known physics. It surfaces practical interpretability challenges in scientific foundation models.

entry.title: ICA Lens: Interpreting Language Models Without Training Another Dictionary

author.name: Sida Liu, Feijiang Han

entry.summary: ICA Lens revisits independent component analysis to find interpretable directions in LLM activations without training another sparse-autoencoder dictionary, exploiting that token-selective directions look less Gaussian than random ones. It offers a fast, training-free first lens for interpretability.

entry.title: Blind Dexterous Grasping via Real2Sim2Real Tactile Policy Learning

author.name: Shengcheng Luo, Xiyan Huang, Zhe Xu, Wanlin Li, Ziyuan Jiao, Chenxi Xiao

entry.summary: This framework enables tactile-only blind dexterous grasping on a real multi-fingered hand via a Real2Sim tactile calibration pipeline producing a contact-calibrated digital twin, a layout-aware tactile encoder, and sim-to-real policy learning. It bridges the tactile sim-to-real gap and limited expressiveness of sparse tactile signals.

entry.title: DuoBench: A Reproducible Benchmark for Bimanual Manipulation in Simulation and the Real World

author.name: Tobias J\"ulg, Seongjin Bien, Simon Hilber, Yannik Blei, Pierre Krack, Maximilian Li, Sven Parusel, Rudolf Lioutikov, Florian Walter, Wolfram Burgard

entry.summary: DuoBench is a reproducible benchmark for bimanual manipulation on the FR3 Duo platform with eleven tasks across four coordination categories, implemented in simulation and partially in the real world with stage-based evaluation for fine-grained failure analysis and human-teleoperated datasets. It addresses control complexity and failure modes specific to two-arm coordination.

entry.title: Categorical Prior Lock-in: Why In-Context Learning Fails for Structured Data

author.name: Antonio Pelusi, Stefano Braghin, Alberto Trombetta

entry.summary: This paper identifies categorical prior lock-in, where in-context learning cannot update LLMs' pretrained token-distribution priors for structured high-cardinality tabular generation, improving numerical fidelity with more examples but hitting a sharp ceiling on categorical distributions and failing to reproduce rare classes. It shows parameter-efficient fine-tuning is needed where ICL fails.

entry.title: ALIGNBEAM : Inference-Time Alignment Transfer via Cross-Vocabulary Logit Mixing

author.name: Chirag Chawla, Pratinav Seth, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

entry.summary: ALIGNBEAM is a training-free inference-time method that transfers safety alignment across models with different vocabularies by translating anchor logits into the target model's vocabulary token-by-token, then using a small LLM judge to select the safest continuation. It addresses safety degradation in cross-family fine-tuned specialists.

entry.title: Fourier Features Let Agents Learn High Precision Policies with Imitation Learning

author.name: Bal\'azs Gyenes, Emiliyan Gospodinov, Jan Frieling, Enrico Krohmer, Nicolas Schreiber, Xiaogang Jia, Niklas Freymuth, Gerhard Neumann

entry.summary: This work shows that mapping point clouds from Cartesian space into high-dimensional Fourier space lets imitation-learning robotic policies overcome neural networks' spectral bias toward low-frequency functions, enabling high-precision manipulation. The Fourier features help point-cloud encoders learn fine spatial detail.

entry.title: My Chemical Harness: Evolutionary Molecular Design over Synthetic Pathways with Large Language Model Agents

author.name: C\'esar Ojeda, Darius A. Faroughy, Maryam Karimi, Payam Zarrintaj, Mir Mehdi Seyedebrahimi, Mart\'in Carballo-Pacheco

entry.summary: My Chemical Harness is a route-native evolutionary framework for molecular design where the search population is executable synthetic pathways rather than isolated molecules. LLMs act only as high-level strategy controllers while deterministic chemistry tools build and score routes.

entry.title: Forecasting Future Behavior as a Learning Task

author.name: Mosh Levy, Yoav Goldberg, Asa Cooper Stickland

entry.summary: Proposes training Behavior Forecasters that predict large reasoning models' future behavior directly from a single reasoning trajectory, bypassing unfaithful explanation steps. Training data comes from querying the model itself with no human labels.

entry.title: Signed Compression Progress on a Sealed Audit is Goodhart-Resistant

author.name: Ayush Mittal, Dhruv Gupta

entry.summary: The authors formalize and prove that compression-progress intrinsic reward measured against a fixed sealed audit telescopes exactly to endpoint audit improvement, making it Goodhart-resistant. This provides theoretical grounding for intrinsic motivation schemes that cannot be gamed without genuine learning.

entry.title: ISE: An Execution-Grounded Recipe for Multi-Turn OS-Agent Trajectories

author.name: Siyuan Luo, Nairong Zheng, Lin Zhou, Tiankuo Yao, Shengyou Yuan, Haojia Yu, Cong Pang, Jiapeng Luo, Lewei Lu

entry.summary: ISE is a three-stage synthesis pipeline (Intent, Simulate, Execute) for generating multi-turn OS-agent trajectories that capture structured intents, task delegation, and grounded tool execution. It addresses the scarcity of training data for capable OS agents.

entry.title: Runtime Skill Audit: Targeted Runtime Probing for Agent Skill Security

author.name: Tu Lan, Chaowei Xiao

entry.summary: Runtime Skill Audit dynamically probes LLM agent skills under targeted runtime conditions to detect behavior that looks benign statically but becomes harmful when invoked with particular inputs, state, or multi-step interactions. It addresses the brittleness of static skill vetting for agent security.

entry.title: From Prompts to Tokens: Internalizing Causal Supervision in Vision-Language Model for Multi-Image Causal Reasoning

author.name: Haoping Yu, Yuanxi Li, Jing Ma

entry.summary: BridgeVLM internalizes visual causal reasoning by inducing a causal graph from multi-image inputs and converting it into structured Causal Tokens executed during inference, rather than injecting causal knowledge only through textual prompts. It improves interventional and counterfactual reasoning over multi-image inputs.

entry.title: AnchorEdit: Maintaining Temporal Consistency in Multi-turn Image Editing via Causal Memory

author.name: Hang Xu, Xiaoxiao Ma, Guohui Zhang, Yu Hu, Siming Fu, Jie Huang, Lin Song, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan, Feng Zhao

entry.summary: AnchorEdit is an autoregressive diffusion framework for multi-turn image editing that uses causal memory and a three-stage training curriculum with self-rollout to prevent identity drift and error accumulation across editing steps. It aligns the model with the causal sequential nature of interactive editing rather than bidirectional video priors.

entry.title: On the Limits of LLM-as-Judge for Scientific Novelty Assessment

author.name: Soumitra Sinhahajari, Navonil Majumder, Soujanya Poria

entry.summary: This paper studies the limits of using LLMs as judges of scientific novelty, focusing on research question generation as a cleaner upstream object. They introduce RQ-Bench, reconstructing author-anchored research questions from recent arXiv papers as reference points for testing novelty judgments.

entry.title: Soft-Prompt Tuning for Fair and Efficient LLM Benchmark Evaluation

author.name: Selen Erkan, Bastian Boll, Kristian Kersting, Bj\"orn Deiseroth, Letitia Parcalabescu

entry.summary: This paper proposes soft-prompt tuning (optimizing only ~10 vectors, 0.0006% of params) to fairly evaluate LLM benchmarks by adapting models to specific output formats, especially helping base models that know answers but lack format-following ability. It separates underlying knowledge from formatting competence.

entry.title: Redesign Mixture-of-Experts Routers with Manifold Power Iteration

author.name: Songhao Wu, Ang Lv, Ruobing Xie, Yankai Lin

entry.summary: This paper redesigns Mixture-of-Experts routers by aligning each router row with the principal singular direction of its associated expert matrix, using Manifold Power Iteration, on the principle that this provides the most expressive description of the expert. It establishes a design principle for condensing expert matrices into router representations.

entry.title: Reroute, Don't Remove: Recoverable Visual Token Routing for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Cheng-Yu Yang, Shao-Yuan Lo, Yu-Lun Liu

entry.summary: Reroute is a training-free plug-in for Vision-Language Models that replaces irreversible visual-token removal with recoverable routing, recognizing that token importance changes across decoder depth. Deferred tokens can re-enter computation in later layers, improving efficiency without permanently discarding grounding-relevant tokens.

entry.title: A prior-free blind detection of information leakage from model predictions

author.name: Laurence A. Jacobs

entry.summary: This paper develops a prior-free, blind framework to detect information leakage from a model's predictions and outcomes alone, without training code, external data, or domain expertise. It proves a sharp impossibility: a recalibrated leak matching an honest model's calibration is indistinguishable from honesty.

entry.title: IAPO: Input Attribution-Aware Policy Optimization for Tool Use in Small Multimodal Agents

author.name: Yifan Yang, Zhen Zhang, Jiayi Tian, Liyan Tan, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: IAPO is a reinforcement learning method for improving tool-calling in small multimodal language model agents, using input attribution to provide denser rewards than brittle exact-match signals. It addresses cases where multiple valid tool paths exist and trajectories are unannotated.

entry.title: Flow Matching with In-Context Priors for Out-of-Distribution Brain Dynamics

author.name: Sam Gijsen, Micha{\l} {\L}ukomski, Marc-Andr\'e Schulz, Kerstin Ritter

entry.summary: This work proposes a per-timestep conditioned diffusion transformer for generating realistic fMRI brain dynamics during unseen cognitive tasks using compositional language and spatial priors in-context. It enables zero-shot generation for in-silico cognitive experiment design.

entry.title: PAWS: Preference Learning with Advantage-Weighted Segments

author.name: Aleksandar Taranovic, Onur Celik, Niklas Freymuth, Ge Li, Serge Thilges, Huy Le, Tai Hoang, Rania Rayyes, Gerhard Neumann

entry.summary: PAWS is a preference-based RL method that performs policy updates directly using segment-level advantage functions, aligning utility training with policy optimization to fix a distribution-shift mismatch. This improves temporal credit assignment in learning from trajectory comparisons.

entry.title: How Low Can You Go? Active Learning for Sparse Model Discovery in the Ultra-Low-Data Limit

author.name: Ana Larra\~naga, Urban Fasel, Steven L. Brunton

entry.summary: This work introduces an active learning strategy built on SINDy and its ensemble extension E-SINDy for discovering governing equations of dynamical systems in the ultra-low-data limit. It iteratively samples the most informative regions using epistemic uncertainty rather than random sampling.

entry.title: Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking in Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Stipe Frkovic, Metod Jazbec, Dan Zhang, Christian A. Naesseth, Ilija Bogunovic, Eric Nalisnick

entry.summary: This paper re-evaluates training-free confidence-based remasking in masked diffusion language models, critically examining a representative method (WINO) and its reported gains. It revisits whether post-hoc self-correction actually improves dLLM generation.

entry.title: Claw-SWE-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating OpenClaw-style Agent Harnesses on Coding Tasks

author.name: Mengyu Zheng, Kai Han, Boxun Li, Haiyang Xu, Yuchuan Tian, Wei He, Hang Zhou, Jianyuan Guo, Hailin Hu, Lin Ma, Chao Xu, Guohao Dai, Lixue Xia, Yunchao Wei, Yunhe Wang, Yu Wang

entry.summary: Claw-SWE-Bench is a multilingual SWE-bench-style benchmark and adapter protocol that makes heterogeneous coding-agent harnesses comparable under fixed prompts, runtime budgets, and workspace contracts. It contains 350 issue-resolution instances across 8 languages and 43 repositories.

entry.title: A Scalable PyTorch Abstraction for Multi-GPU Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Matthew Cong, Francis Williams, Jonathan Swartz, Mark Harris, Sanja Fidler, Ken Museth

entry.summary: This work presents a scalable PyTorch backend for multi-GPU Gaussian splatting that distributes parameters and operators across GPUs via CUDA unified memory and NVLink, requiring no explicit cross-device communication in model code. It scales neural reconstruction to higher resolutions and larger scenes.

entry.title: Learning Object Manipulation from Scratch via Contrastive Interaction

author.name: Tongle Shen, Caleb Chuck, Fan Feng, Biwei Huang

entry.summary: This work analyzes why Contrastive RL struggles in interaction-rich manipulation, formulating manipulation dynamics as a piecewise-smooth Markov process where contact-induced mode changes create reachability structures hard for standard energy functions to represent. It proposes a method to learn manipulation from scratch via contrastive interaction.

entry.title: Higher-Order Token Interactions via Quantum Attention

author.name: Jian Xu, Chao Li, Delu Zeng, John Paisley, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: Quantum Higher-Order Attention is a shallow, hardware-realizable quantum attention head that synthesizes order-k token interactions inside a circuit via data re-uploading and an all-to-all entangler, exposed through local read-out. The authors prove an expressivity separation from standard single-layer self-attention.

entry.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Optimistic Multiplicative Weight Update

author.name: Francesco Orabona

entry.summary: This paper proves last-iterate asymptotic convergence of Optimistic Multiplicative-Weights Update for smooth convex-concave saddle-point problems under a small constant learning rate, resolving a long-standing open question. The result requires no uniqueness, strict complementarity, or near-solution initialization.

entry.title: Neuro-Relational Programs: Unifying Queries and Neural Computation over Structured Data

author.name: Arie Soeteman, Balder ten Cate, Maurice Funk, Benny Kimelfeld, Carsten Lutz, Moritz Sch\"onherr

entry.summary: Neuro-Relational Programs extend Datalog-style rules with operations over vector embeddings attached to database tuples, interleaving relational reasoning and learnable neural components in one declarative formalism. This unifies database queries and neural computation over structured data.

entry.title: Adjoint Method versus Physics-Informed Neural Networks in PDE-Constrained Inverse Problems

author.name: Zhen Zhang, Alessandro Alla, George Em Karniadakis

entry.summary: This work gives a fair, matched comparison of adjoint-based optimization versus physics-informed neural networks for PDE-constrained inverse problems, controlling for formulation, parameterization, optimizer, and regularization. It clarifies their relative performance, which prior unequal comparisons obscured.

entry.title: One Jailbreak, Many Tongues: Learning Language-Insensitive Intention Representations for Multilingual Jailbreak Detection

author.name: Shuyu Jiang, Kaiyu Xu, Xingshu Chen, Hao Ren, Rui Tang, Yi Zhang, Tianwei Zhang, Hongwei Li

entry.summary: MLJailDe is a multilingual jailbreak detection framework that learns language-insensitive intention representations via back-translation augmentation to close safety gaps in non-dominant languages. It targets the exploitable mismatch where safety training concentrates in English and Chinese.

entry.title: FORT-Searcher: Synthesizing Shortcut-Resistant Search Tasks for Training Deep Search Agents

author.name: Jia Deng, Yimeng Chen, Xiaoqing Xiang, Ziyang Zeng, Shuo Tang, Wayne Xin Zhao, Feng Chang, Chuan Hao, Yuan Wei, Ran Tao, Bryan Dai, Ji-Rong Wen

entry.summary: FORT-Searcher formalizes a shortcut-aware difficulty framework for synthesizing search tasks, identifying four shortcut risks (evidence co-coverage, single-clue selectivity, exposed constants, prior-knowledge binding) that let agents bypass intended search. It uses trajectory signatures to diagnose realized search difficulty for training deep search agents.

entry.title: Beyond Fully Random Masking: Attention-Guided Denoising and Optimization for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Jia Deng, Junyi Li, Wayne Xin Zhao, Jinpeng Wang, Hongyu Lu, Ji-Rong Wen

entry.summary: AGDO is an attention-guided denoising and optimization framework for diffusion LLMs that replaces random masking with attention-derived token dependencies, finding tokens attending strongly to unmasked context have greater generation stability. It aligns both denoising order and optimization with attention structure.

entry.title: Dummy Backdoor as a Defense: Removing Unknown Backdoors via Shared Internal Mechanisms for Generative LLMs

author.name: Kazuki Iwahana, Masaru Matsubayashi, Takuma Koyama, Toshiki Shibahara, Kenichiro Omintato, Akira Ito

entry.summary: Proposes a backdoor removal method for generative LLMs based on shared internal mechanisms across different backdoors, exploiting the observation that backdoors with the same task induce similar activation changes. Important for defending LLMs against hidden trigger attacks without prior knowledge of attack types.

entry.title: Plan-and-Verify Video Reward Reasoning with Spatio-Temporal Scene Graph Grounding

author.name: Hyomin Kim, Junghye Kim, Joanie Hayoun Chung, Yoonjin Oh, Kyungjae Lee, Sungbin Lim, Sungwoong Kim

entry.summary: Proposes SG-PVR, a text-to-video reward model using plan-and-verify reasoning grounded in spatio-temporal scene graphs to systematically verify every prompt condition with explicit visual evidence. Aims to improve fine-grained semantic alignment in T2V post-training.

entry.title: Wild3R: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting from Unconstrained Sparse Photo Collection

author.name: Yuto Furutani, Takashi Otonari, Kaede Shiohara, Toshihiko Yamasaki

entry.summary: Presents Wild3R, a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting method for unconstrained sparse photo collections with diverse lighting and transient objects, plus WildCity, a large training dataset (200 scenes, 170 lighting conditions, 337,500 images). Addresses the training-data bottleneck for robust in-the-wild 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: Tac-DINO: Learning Vision-Tactile Features with Patch Alignment

author.name: Hong Li, Yankang Dong, Yue Xu, Yihan Tang, Mingzhu Li, Jiamin Qiu, Qihang Yao, Xing Zhu, Yujun Shen, Nan Xue, Yong-Lu Li

entry.summary: Presents Tac-DINO, building a large-scale tactile dataset (20K+ contacts from 505 objects) and a Vision-Tactile Patch Alignment method plus a holographic matching benchmark for local-to-global vision-tactile representation learning. Addresses the gap in scale-aware tactile alignment.

entry.title: VOID: Defeating Unauthorized Mimicry in Latent Diffusion Models

author.name: Chunlin Qiu, Ang Li, Tianxiao Huang, Ruilin Gan, Yunjie Ge, Shenyi Zhang, Huayi Duan, Lingchen Zhao, Chao Shen, Qian Wang

entry.summary: Proposes VOID, a defense against unauthorized mimicry in latent diffusion models that manipulates the model's intrinsic stochasticity rather than relying on subtle perturbations, which the model's restoration mechanism can remove. Addresses a fundamental weakness in existing anti-mimicry defenses.

entry.title: Reason, Then Re-reason: Cross-view Revisiting Improves Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Chaofan Ma, Zhenjie Mao, Yuhuan Yang, Fanqin Zeng, Yue Shi, Yingjie Zhou, Xiaofeng Cao, Jiangchao Yao

entry.summary: ReRe is a training-free inference-time framework for egocentric spatial reasoning that first forms a spatial hypothesis from a video, then verifies or revises it using complementary viewpoints. It treats spatial conclusions as revisitable when more evidence becomes available.

entry.title: Compatibility-Aware Dynamic Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models

author.name: Yucheng Zhou, Junwei Sheng, Qianning Wang, Jianbing Shen

entry.summary: CADFT extends Dynamic Fine-Tuning for LLMs by controlling sample-level optimization variance caused by demonstration-policy mismatch in heterogeneous instruction data. It derives a dynamic, policy-dependent coefficient to weight samples and stabilize SFT.

entry.title: LifeSentence: Language models can encode human life course trajectories from longitudinal panel data

author.name: Samuel Liu, Muchen Xi, William Yeoh, Joshua J. Jackson

entry.summary: LifeSentence represents each life event as a structured natural-language record and instruction-tunes a 24B model across an 18-task taxonomy to forecast human life-course trajectories from longitudinal panel data. It bridges LLMs with panel studies that lack large-scale training data.

entry.title: Debiasing Without Protected Attributes: Latent Concept Erasure from Textual Profiles

author.name: Shun Shao, Zheng Zhao, Anna Korhonen, Yftah Ziser, Shay B. Cohen

entry.summary: H-SAL performs post-hoc concept and attribute erasure using self-description text as an implicit debiasing signal when protected attributes are unavailable due to privacy or legal constraints. It introduces a multi-domain Stack Exchange fairness benchmark for helpfulness prediction with explicit and implicit signals.

entry.title: A PubMed-Scale Dataset of Structured Biomedical Abstracts

author.name: Chia-Hsuan Chang, Haerin Song, Brian Ondov, Hua Xu

entry.summary: Doc2Atom is a compositional parametric memory framework that compiles documents into multiple composable memory atoms instead of a single monolithic LoRA adapter, addressing irrelevant-query interference and poor compositional recall in context distillation. It improves long-document reasoning and scalability over Doc-to-LoRA.

entry.title: Architecture-Aware Reinforcement Learning Makes Sliding-Window Attention Competitive in Math Reasoning

author.name: Kai Liu, Peijie Dong, Xinchen Xie, Jianfei Gao, Qipeng Guo, Xiaowen Chu, Shaoting Zhang, Kai Chen

entry.summary: SWARR adapts sliding-window attention models for math reasoning via SFT conversion from full-attention models followed by RL policy adaptation, addressing the quadratic cost of self-attention for long-context inference. It identifies a data-architecture mismatch that RL helps overcome.

entry.title: The Art of Interrogation: Consistency Amplifies Factuality in Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Theo Uscidda, Marta Tintore Gazulla, Maks Ovsjanikov, Federico Tombari, Leonidas Guibas

entry.summary: Argues that large reasoning models already possess latent spatial reasoning capabilities that need alignment via logical coherence rather than new supervised data. Proposes a self-supervised RL framework using consistency verifiers under geometric constraints, with no ground-truth annotations.

entry.title: RoVE: Rotary Value Embeddings Attention for Relative Position-dependent Value Pathways

author.name: Alejandro Garc\'ia-Castellanos, Maurice Weiler, Erik J Bekkers

entry.summary: RoVE proposes a parameter-free modification making value vectors position-sensitive by rotating them alongside keys, turning RoPE attention into attentive convolution and unifying formulations across vision, robotics, and LLMs. Trained 124M and 354M GPT-2 models show consistent gains on in-context learning, OOD perplexity, and long-context retrieval.

entry.title: Risk Under Pressure: Compute-Aware Evaluation of Adversarial Robustness in Language Models

author.name: Malikeh Ehghaghi, Bogl\'arka Ecsedi, Marsha Chechik, Colin Raffel

entry.summary: Proposes a compute-aware adversarial robustness evaluation framework that measures attack effort in cumulative FLOPs rather than fixed query budgets, since attack costs vary by orders of magnitude. It introduces risk-compute curves mapping budgets to attack risk to reveal whether attack cost justifies payoff.

entry.title: APEX: Automated Prompt Engineering eXpert with Dynamic Data Selection

author.name: Fei Wang, Si Si, Cho-Jui Hsieh, Inderjit S. Dhillon

entry.summary: APEX is an automated prompt-optimization framework that dynamically stratifies the development dataset into Easy, Hard, and Mixed tiers to allocate compute toward the most informative examples. It addresses the data-efficiency bottleneck in evolutionary prompt search.

entry.title: SirenFNO: Efficient and Full Frequency Learning of Fourier Neural Operators

author.name: Pengqing Shi, Jie Yin, Stephen Tierney, Junbin Gao

entry.summary: SirenFNO augments Fourier neural operators with sinusoidal representation networks to learn a full-grid spectrum and overcome the spectral bias toward low frequencies that limits FNOs on high-frequency PDEs. It improves discretization-invariant PDE surrogate modeling.

entry.title: Sovereign Assurance Boundary: Certificate-Bound Admission for Agentic Infrastructure

author.name: Jun He, Deying Yu

entry.summary: The Sovereign Assurance Boundary is a certificate-bound runtime admission layer that intercepts autonomous agent proposals, compiles them into typed execution contracts bound to cryptographic evidence and policy versions before allowing high-stakes mutations. It addresses the control-plane authorization gap for agentic infrastructure.

entry.title: ARGUS: Stacked Multi-View Identity Mosaic Injection for Subject-Preserving Video Generation

author.name: Zijie Meng, Jiwen Liu, Yufei Liu, Chengzhuo Tong, Xiaoqiang Liu, Yuanxing Zhang, Yulong Xu, Pengfei Wan

entry.summary: ARGUS introduces Stacked Multi-View Identity Mosaic Injection for subject-preserving video generation, replacing the single static reference with a 3x3 mosaic of multi-view identity evidence synchronized with diffusion timesteps. It maintains recognizability across motion, viewpoint, occlusion, and conflicting references.

entry.title: Goal-Autopilot: A Verifiable Anti-Fabrication Firewall for Unattended Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Youwang Deng

entry.summary: Goal-Autopilot externalizes long-horizon agent state into a durable gated finite-state machine advanced one tick at a time, with a hard floor forbidding any done claim whose verification gate did not execute and pass, proving a No-False-Success theorem. It targets honest reporting in unattended autonomous agents.

entry.title: Hey Chat, Can You Teach Me? Structuring Socratic Dialogue for Human Learning in the Wild

author.name: Sidney Tio, Arunesh Sinha, Pradeep Varakantham

entry.summary: This work studies structuring Socratic tutoring dialogue with LLMs in unstructured chat settings where no prior student record exists, showing frontier and education-tuned models tutor poorly because they must simultaneously sequence curriculum, conduct Socratic dialogue, and infer knowledge state. It proposes separating these responsibilities.

entry.title: From Uniform to Learned Graph Priors: Diffusion for Structure Discovery

author.name: Qi Shao, Hao Guo, Jiawen Chen, Duxin Chen, Wenwu Yu

entry.summary: Diff-prior introduces a diffusion-parameterized adaptive prior to calibrate latent graph distributions in neural relational inference, replacing oversimplified factorized near-uniform priors that treat edges as independent. It frames prior integration as learnable denoising-style calibration to sharpen edge posteriors for structure discovery.

entry.title: Task-Aware Structured Memory for Dynamic Multi-modal In-Context Learning

author.name: Zhirui Chen, Ziwei Chen, Ling Shao

entry.summary: TASM is a training-free task-aware structured memory framework for multimodal in-context learning that uses task-vector guidance to build structure-preserving, dynamically accessible compressed memory, avoiding rigid token removal or biased importance estimation. It addresses finite context windows and growing KV-cache costs in long multimodal sequences.

entry.title: "That's AI Slop, You Bot!" Studying Accusations, Evidence, and Credibility in Online Discourse Towards LLM-Generated Comments

author.name: Jason Miklian, John E. Katsos

entry.summary: This large-scale study analyzes 25 million Hacker News and Reddit comments (2023-2026) to track how readers accuse others of using AI-generated text, finding a tenfold rise in pejorative AI accusations versus a stable placebo vocabulary. It examines accusation patterns, evidence, and credibility in online discourse.

entry.title: Agentic Environment Engineering for Large Language Models: A Survey of Environment Modeling, Synthesis, Evaluation, and Application

author.name: Jiachun Li, Zhuoran Jin, Tianyi Men, Yupu Hao, Kejian Zhu, Lingshuai Wang, Dongqi Huang, Longxiang Wang, Shengjia Hua, Lu Wang, Jinshan Gao, Hongbang Yuan, Ruilin Xu, Kang Liu, Jun Zhao

entry.summary: This survey systematically reviews agentic environment engineering for LLM agents across the lifecycle of environment modeling, synthesis, evaluation, and application, categorizing representative environments by eight attributes and eight domains. It addresses the lack of systematic analysis in this important area.

entry.title: VIA-SD: Verification via Intra-Model Routing for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Yuchen Xian, Yang He, Yunqiu Xu, Yi Yang

entry.summary: VIA-SD improves speculative decoding by introducing a slim-verifier derived from the full verifier via intra-model routing, handling tokens needing moderate verification instead of binary accept/full-recompute decisions. This multi-tier framework reduces expensive large-model calls.

entry.title: Least-Action-Guided Diffusion for Physical Extrapolation

author.name: Zhongxin Yang, Yuanwei Bin, Xiang I. A. Yang, Shiyi Chen

entry.summary: Least-Action-Principle-Guided diffusion (LAPG) promotes physical consistency during inference for extrapolation in computational physics, combining a conditional score-based diffusion model with an action-derived physical guidance score. It generates an in-distribution proposal then refines it toward out-of-distribution targets via a variational prior.

entry.title: Counterexample Guided Learning in the Large using Reasoning Agents

author.name: Hongyi Liu, Frederic Sala, Thomas Reps, Adithya Murali

entry.summary: This paper studies counterexample-guided learning with LLM agents on regular-expression induction, a symbolic learning problem where precise feedback exists as counterexamples. It identifies novel refinement strategies like regularization that enable effective regex learning from positive/negative examples and verifier counterexamples.

entry.title: GraphInfer-Bench: Benchmarking LLM's Inference Capability on Graphs

author.name: Zhuoyi Peng, Jingzhou Jiang, Hanlin Gu, Lixin Fan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: GraphInfer-Bench is a benchmark testing whether LLMs can perform genuine graph inference—producing open-ended answers no single node supports and no path retrieves—across five Description and Comparison tasks. It distinguishes this from existing graph-QA protocols that admit single-node or path-retrievable answers.

entry.title: Spectrally Regularized Latent Flow Matching for Turbulence Generation

author.name: Khalid Rafiq, Aditya G. Nair

entry.summary: This paper introduces a spectrally regularized latent flow matching framework for turbulence generation that fixes the systematic under-representation of dissipation-range amplitudes. Replacing an MSE VAE with a log-spectral objective dramatically improves retained spectral power.

entry.title: A Riemannian Approach to Low-Rank Optimal Transport

author.name: Pratik Jawanpuria, Bamdev Mishra

entry.summary: This work proposes a unified Riemannian geometric framework for low-rank optimal transport, modeling rank-r couplings as smooth manifolds with a Fisher-Rao metric and deriving tractable projectors and retractions. It extends to Gromov-Wasserstein and fused variants in a cost-agnostic way.

entry.title: Phi-Actor-Critic: Steering General-Sum Games to Pareto-Efficient Correlated Equilibria

author.name: Wongyu Lee, Francesco Lelli, Omran Ayoub, Massimo Tornatore

entry.summary: Phi-Actor-Critic is a MARL framework that leverages swap regret minimization to steer general-sum games toward Pareto-efficient correlated equilibria, avoiding socially inefficient Nash equilibria. It addresses equilibrium selection where individual incentives conflict with collective welfare.

entry.title: FlexiBrain: Resolution-Agnostic Voxel-Level Encoding for Native fMRI

author.name: Mo Wang, Wenhao Ye, Junfeng Xia, Minghao Xu, Hongkai Wen, Quanying Liu

entry.summary: FlexiBrain is a resolution-agnostic voxel-level encoding framework for native fMRI based on Mamba-JEPA that defines patch sizes in real-world physical units to handle heterogeneous spatial and temporal resolutions. It avoids rigid preprocessing pipelines that degrade subject-specific information and add computational overhead.

entry.title: Teaching Diffusion to Speculate Left-to-Right

author.name: Lexington Whalen, Yuki Ito, Ryo Sakamoto

entry.summary: This work teaches block-diffusion language models to draft tokens left-to-right for speculative decoding, addressing the subtlety that bidirectional block drafting conflicts with autoregressive verification. It improves the use of diffusion drafters to accelerate LLM inference.

entry.title: From Persistence to Survival: Hypothesis Testing, Effect Sizes and Vectorisation for Topological Features

author.name: Juliette Murris, Bernadette Stolz, Karsten Borgwardt

entry.summary: STRAND reframes persistence diagrams from topological data analysis as survival data, defining a persistence survival function to enable two-sample testing, effect sizes, and vectorization. This unifies statistical comparison and downstream prediction tools for topological features.

entry.title: Measuring Semantic Progress in Multi-turn Dialogue via Information Gain

author.name: Paul He, Shiva Kasiviswanathan, Dominik Janzing

entry.summary: This paper formalizes semantic progress in information-seeking multi-turn dialogue as question-conditioned uncertainty reduction and introduces an information-theoretic metric estimated in embedding space with closed-form Gaussian updates. It provides a principled way to measure how much new relevant information accumulates across turns.

entry.title: Detecting AI-Generated Content on Social Media with Multi-modal Language Models

author.name: Chenyang Yang, Shen Yan, Yibo Yang, Litao Hu, Yuchen Liu, Yuan Zeng, Hanchao Yu, Yinan Zhu, Sumedha Singla, Brian Vanover, Huijun Qian, Zihao Wang, Fujun Liu, Aashu Singh, Jianyu Wang, Xuewen Zhang

entry.summary: This paper presents a pipeline for detecting AI-generated images and videos on social media by continuously curating diverse multimodal data and training a compact vision-language model that both detects and explains. It claims SOTA on public benchmarks plus robust performance on internal social-media data.

entry.title: SAGE: Answer-Conditioned Uncertainty Targets for Verbal Uncertainty Alignment

author.name: Kaiwen Shi, Zheyuan Zhang, Yanfang Ye

entry.summary: SAGE proposes Semantic-Answer Guided Entropy, a group-level uncertainty target estimated from repeated model outputs that constructs an answer-conditioned uncertainty geometry to align an LLM's verbal uncertainty with its sampled behavior. It frames verbal uncertainty alignment as a distributional calibration problem.

entry.title: UR-BERT: Scaling Text Encoders for Massively Multilingual TTS Through Universal Romanization and Speech Token Prediction

author.name: Sangmin Lee, Eekgyun Ahn, Woongjib Choi, Hong-Goo Kang

entry.summary: UR-BERT is a Romanized-transcription-based TTS text encoder scaling to 495 languages by unifying writing systems into shared Romanization, plus a speech-token prediction objective for speech-aware phonetic representations. It overcomes the ~100-language ceiling of grapheme-to-phoneme approaches.

entry.title: Agreement in Representation Space for Open-Ended Self-Consistency

author.name: Paula Ontalvilla, Gorka Azkune, Aitor Ormazabal

entry.summary: Embedding-Based Agreement extends self-consistency to open-ended generation (code synthesis, summarization) by treating consistency as a geometric property, clustering sampled generations in embedding space rather than relying on exact matching. It operationalizes agreement training-free where categorical matching fails.

entry.title: Reassessing High-Performing LLMs on Polish Medical Exams: True Competence or Bias-Driven Performance?

author.name: Antoni Lasik, Jakub Pokrywka, {\L}ukasz Grzybowski, Jeremi Ignacy Kaczmarek, Gabriela Korza\'nska, Janusz \'Swieczkowski-Feiz, Oskar Pastuszek, Paulina Hoffman, Jakub Tomasz D\k{a}browski, Wojciech Kusa

entry.summary: This work reassesses high-performing LLMs on Polish medical exams with an expanded harder benchmark (15,000+ questions, two new domains, four structural modifications reducing MCQA artifacts). Under the harder setup, the best model (Qwen3.5-122B) drops 28-31 percentage points, showing standard MCQA scores overstate clinical competence.

entry.title: Building Social World Models with Large Language Models

author.name: Haofei Yu, Yining Zhao, Guanyu Lin, Jiaxuan You

entry.summary: Introduces the Social World Model (SWM) framework, which uses LLMs to learn state-transition functions for how social beliefs evolve following major events, optimizing an evidence lower bound without human annotations or census data. Matters because it offers a computational approach to modeling social belief dynamics in social science.

entry.title: Which Speech Representation Better Matches Text-Native Reasoning? A Study of Speech-Text Alignment on Frame Rate and Representation

author.name: Zhen Ye, Xu Tan, Yiming Li, Guangyan Zhang, Chimin Chan, Haohe Liu, Zhengxi Liu, Hongzhan Lin, Zheqi Dai, Xinshen Zhang, Peiwen Sun, Qiuqiang Kong, Wei Xue

entry.summary: Studies why reasoning degrades when LLMs condition on speech instead of text, attributing it to temporal-granularity mismatch, and explores frame-rate and representation design with factorized FSQ and a non-autoregressive audio LM head. Relevant for improving spoken dialogue models.

entry.title: Damage-TriageFormer: A Foundation-Model Framework for Typology-Based Building Damage Assessment from Mono-Temporal Imagery

author.name: Yiming Xiao, Yu-Hsuan Ho, Sanjay Thasma, Junwei Ma, Ali Mostafavi

entry.summary: Presents Damage-TriageFormer, a single-image post-event footprint-conditioned foundation-model framework producing a building damage typology rather than a severity scale, with the DamageTriage-Bench benchmark spanning hurricanes and wildfires. Addresses limitations of severity scales and the unavailability of pre-event imagery for disaster response.

entry.title: How Seemingly Inconsequential Design Choices Dictate Performance of LLMs in Pathology

author.name: Kian R. Weihrauch, Thomas A. Buckley, William Lotter, Arjun K. Manrai

entry.summary: A systematic factorial analysis showing that seemingly trivial design choices (patch size, count, magnification, inference mode) dramatically affect general-purpose LLM performance on whole-slide pathology images. It challenges the assumption that domain-specific training is necessary by showing generalist LLM baselines are often unfairly configured.

entry.title: GraphGP: Scalable Gaussian Processes with Vecchia's Approximation

author.name: Benjamin Dodge, Philipp Frank, Susan E. Clark

entry.summary: Presents GraphGP, a GPU algorithm for Vecchia's approximation of Gaussian processes that scales to nearly a billion parameters with linear time and memory, using a bit-reversed k-d tree ordering and a differentiable CUDA implementation. It dramatically extends the practical scale of GP modeling.

entry.title: EC2’s formally verified “isolation engine” provides mathematical assurance of virtual-machine isolation

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon announces the M9g/M9gd EC2 instances powered by Graviton5 and the new Nitro Isolation Engine, the first formally verified hypervisor deployed in commercial cloud, proven correct using the Isabelle/HOL proof assistant with 330,000 lines of machine-checked mathematics. It provides mathematical assurance of VM isolation.

entry.title: CRUMB: Efficient Prior Fitted Network Inference via Distributionally Matched Context Batching

author.name: Jamie Heredge, Mattia J. Villani, Pranav Deshpande, Akshay Seshadri, Niraj Kumar

entry.summary: CRUMB is an inference wrapper for prior-fitted tabular networks that clusters test queries and selects distributionally matched training subsets via MMD minimization to enable exact PFN inference on large datasets. It tackles the quadratic attention bottleneck limiting tabular foundation models.

entry.title: Physics-Distilled Neural Network enabled by Large Language Models for Manufacturing Process-Property Predictive Modeling

author.name: Ge Song, Kiarash Naghavi Khanghah, Anandkumar Patel, Rajiv Malhotra, Hongyi Xu

entry.summary: This framework uses LLMs to extract analytical physics priors from scientific literature into a privileged teacher model with graph-masked attention, then distills that knowledge into a lightweight student for data-scarce manufacturing process-property prediction. It improves accuracy and interpretability under limited data.

entry.title: Layer-Isolated Evaluation: Gating the Deterministic Scaffold of a Production LLM Agent with a No-LLM, Regression-Locked Test Harness

author.name: Sawyer Zhang, Alexander Wang, Sophie Lei

entry.summary: This paper proposes layer-isolated evaluation for production LLM agents, decomposing a deployed ordering agent into a taxonomy of layers each tested by deterministic no-LLM assertion slices in CI, validated by controlled regression injection. It reveals masking where aggregate task-success hides per-layer regressions.

entry.title: Substrate Asymmetry in User-Side Memory: A Diagnostic Framework

author.name: Youwang Deng

entry.summary: This diagnostic framework decomposes user-side LLM memory into behavioral consistency, factual presence, and factual absence axes, showing no single substrate wins all three. Comparing per-user LoRA adapters against dense retrieval, it finds LoRA wins style while RAG wins factual recall, exposing trade-offs hidden by aggregate personalization metrics.

entry.title: Automated Creativity Evaluation of Language Models Across Open-Ended Tasks

author.name: Min Sen Tan, Zachary Kit Chun Choy, Syed Ali Redha Alsagoff, Nadya Yuki Wangsajaya, Mohor Banerjee, Swaagat Bikash Saikia, Alvin Chan

entry.summary: This paper presents an automated, domain-agnostic framework for quantifying LLM creativity across open-ended tasks by separating the measurement apparatus from the creative task itself, measuring divergent creativity in a scalable, task-agnostic way. It addresses the over-coupling of existing creativity metrics to specific domains.

entry.title: Characterizing Software Aging in GPU-Based LLM Serving Systems

author.name: Domenico Cotroneo, Bojan Cukic

entry.summary: This paper presents an empirical methodology to characterize software aging in GPU-based LLM serving systems, running a 216-hour campaign across six co-located deployments and applying statistical analysis to find significant memory aging in all deployments with leak rates dependent on the serving runtime. It adapts aging studies to the distinctive Python-host plus CUDA-device LLM serving stack.

entry.title: Mathematical perspective on genetic algorithms with optimization guided operators

author.name: Anna Brandenberger, Ilan Doron-Arad, Elchanan Mossel

entry.summary: This theoretical paper develops a mathematical model of genetic algorithms whose mutation and recombination operators are ML optimization-guided rather than random, reflecting recent inference-time evolutionary methods. It analyzes the tradeoff between higher-quality but computationally costlier operators.

entry.title: Seeing Before Colliding: Anticipatory Safe RL with Frozen Vision-Language Models

author.name: Samuel Tetteh, Cody Fleming

entry.summary: VLM-Safe-RL integrates a frozen vision-language model into the constrained-MDP Lagrangian update as an anticipatory cost term, addressing the structural lateness of reactive cost signals in high-speed racing where collisions are instantaneous. It uses decoupled dual-path CLIP and an augmented multiplier update.

entry.title: Learning from almost nothing: How neural networks survive heavy input corruption

author.name: Justin Tahmassebpur, Asadullah Bhuiyan, Hyejin Kim, Omri Lesser

entry.summary: This study examines how neural networks survive heavy input (attribute) corruption, finding MLPs maintain well-above-chance accuracy even with over 90% corrupted inputs, far beyond human recognition. It analyzes infinite-width networks to understand this robustness to additive and replacement noise.

entry.title: Beyond the Golden Teacher: Enhancing Graph Learning through LLM-GNN Co-teaching

author.name: Zhuoyi Peng, Hanlin Gu, Lixin Fan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: This paper challenges the golden-teacher assumption in LLM-GNN methods for few-shot learning on text-attributed graphs, arguing neither model is reliable under sparse supervision since GNNs fail on cold nodes and LLMs fail on text-ambiguous nodes. It proposes a co-teaching framework where both models learn from each other rather than one supervising the other.

entry.title: Capacity-Constrained Online Convex Optimization with Delayed Feedback

author.name: Alexander Ryabchenko, Idan Attias, Daniel M. Roy

entry.summary: This paper studies online convex optimization with delayed feedback under a hard capacity constraint where only a limited number of pending rounds can be tracked. It introduces a semi-clairvoyant model and a reduction-based approach to a delayed-and-weighted setting.

entry.title: MemNovo: Look Back at the Spectrum for Balanced De Novo Peptide Sequencing from Mass Spectrometry

author.name: Dongxin Lyu, Jingbo Zhou, Hongxin Xiang, Yuqiang Li, Jun Xia

entry.summary: MemNovo addresses a pathology in Transformer de novo peptide sequencing where autoregressive decoders over-rely on sequence priors and under-use mass-spectrum evidence, producing plausible but unfaithful sequences. It proposes a mechanism to re-attend to the input spectrum for balanced predictions.

entry.title: Energy-Efficient On-Device RAG on a Mobile NPU: System Design and Benchmark on Snapdragon X Elite

author.name: Zhiyuan Cheng, Longying Lai

entry.summary: This work presents the first end-to-end RAG pipeline running all neural stages (embedding, reranking, LLM generation) on the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU of the Snapdragon X Elite. It achieves large throughput and energy improvements over CPU and GPU baselines for on-device privacy-preserving retrieval.

entry.title: Interpretable Neural Marked Statistics for Cosmological Inference

author.name: Federico Semenzato, Benjamin D. Wandelt, Michele Liguori, Alvise Raccanelli

entry.summary: This work proposes a neural marking scheme for cosmological inference that generalizes marked statistics through interpretable, physically motivated field transformations to access non-Gaussian information beyond the power spectrum. It uses contrastive learning to align marked summaries with cosmological parameters.

entry.title: Enhancing Spectral Embedding through Robust and Flexible Knowledge Transfer in Electronic Health Records

author.name: Feiqing Huang, Zongqi Xia, Rong Ma, Tianxi Cai

entry.summary: This work proposes a spectral-based unsupervised representation learning framework for clinical concepts and patients in rare-disease EHR cohorts, transferring knowledge from a broader population sharing a partially overlapping subspace. It relaxes restrictive one-to-one signal-alignment assumptions for more flexible structured knowledge transfer.

entry.title: Renewable Lasso without Batch-Number Constraints: A Gradient-Enhanced Approach

author.name: Junzhuo Gao, Ling Peng, Xu Guo, Heng Lian

entry.summary: This work proposes a gradient-enhanced renewable Lasso for online estimation of high-dimensional generalized linear models with streaming data that removes the batch-number constraint of prior renewable methods. It extends to distributed master-client streaming where only gradient summaries are exchanged.

entry.title: UniIntervene: Agentic Intervention for Efficient Real-World Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haoyuan Deng, Yitong Gao, Yudong Lin, Haichao Liu, Zhenyu Wu, Ziwei Wang

entry.summary: UniIntervene is an agentic intervention model for human-in-the-loop RL that detects unproductive exploration and autonomously recovers the policy toward high-value states, reducing reliance on frequent human corrections. It uses future-conditioned action-value estimation for real-world robotic manipulation.

entry.title: Beyond Compaction: Structured Context Eviction for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Andrew Semenov, Svyatoslav Dorofeev

entry.summary: Context Window Lifecycle gives long-horizon LLM agents an effectively unbounded working horizon via graduated, semantically-aware eviction of typed dependency-linked episodes when a token budget is exceeded. It preserves user turns and active reasoning context while shedding completed action episodes deterministically.

entry.title: Scenario-based Probing and Steering Cultural Values in Large Language Models--Extended Version

author.name: Trung Duc Anh Dang, Tung Kieu, Sarah Masud

entry.summary: This paper probes and steers latent cultural values in LLMs along the World Values Survey Inglehart-Welzel axes by converting survey questions into scenario-based behavioral dilemmas and applying activation steering with country-conditioned prompting. It addresses how direct survey prompting elicits neutral, safety-aligned answers that hide underlying preferences.

entry.title: Notes2Skills: From Lab Notebooks to Certainty-Aware Scientific Agent Skills

author.name: Shi Liu, Jiayao Chen, Chengwei Qin, Yanqing Hu, Jufan Zhang, Linyi Yang

entry.summary: Notes2Skills converts informal lab notebooks, which intermingle validated observations and tentative judgments, into certainty-aware scientific agent skills, an underexplored input type for AI science agents. It aims to capture evolving scientific reasoning and author uncertainty rather than polished final results.

entry.title: Gumbel-BEARD: Automatic Layer Selection for Self-Supervised Adaptation of Whisper in Low-Resource Domains

author.name: Zilai Wang, Natarajan Balaji Shankar, Mohan Shi, Kaiyuan Zhang, Abeer Alwan

entry.summary: Structured PubMed is a corpus of over 23.2 million section-labeled biomedical abstracts, with 5.9 million author-structured and 17.2 million automatically labeled, addressing the bottleneck of unstructured abstracts for biomedical text processing. It supports information retrieval, text mining, and knowledge synthesis at scale.

entry.title: Beyond Third-Person Audits: Situated Interaction Auditing for User-Centered LLM Bias Research

author.name: Andr\'es Abeliuk, Cinthia Sanchez Macias, Valentina Alarc\'on, \'Alvaro Madariaga, Claudia Lopez

entry.summary: Proposes Situated Interaction Auditing (SIA), a user-centered framework for studying how LLMs adjust responses based on inferred user demographics, addressing a blind spot in third-person bias audits. Important for understanding personalized bias in real LLM interactions.

entry.title: SheafStain: Sheaf-Theoretic Schr\"odinger Bridge for Spatially and Biologically Coherent Virtual Staining

author.name: Hyeongyeol Lim, Hongjun Yoon, Eunjin Jang, Daeky Jeong, Won June Cho, Hwamin Lee

entry.summary: Proposes AGE-MIL, an anchor-guided evidence multiple instance learning framework for patient-level prediction that integrates evidence across multiple whole-slide images, addressing misalignment when patient-level supervision is imposed on slide-level MIL. Relevant for computational pathology diagnostics and prognostics.

entry.title: SG2Loc: Sequential Visual Localization on 3D Scene Graphs

author.name: Nicole Damblon, Olga Vysotska, Federico Tombari, Marc Pollefeys, Daniel Barath

entry.summary: Introduces SG2Loc, a lightweight sequential visual localization method using compact 3D scene graphs where nodes are objects and edges encode spatial relationships, avoiding storage of large image databases or point clouds. Targets robotics and AR localization in complex indoor environments.

entry.title: DynaTok: Token-Based 4D Reconstruction from Partial Point Clouds

author.name: Weirong Chen, Keisuke Tateno, Hidenobu Matsuki, Michael Niemeyer, Daniel Cremers, Federico Tombari

entry.summary: Proposes DynaTok, a point-based framework for correspondence-free 4D reconstruction from partial, unordered point cloud sequences without images, encoding frames into compact latent tokens aggregated over time via a transformer. Addresses geometry-only dynamic reconstruction with incomplete observations.

entry.title: Adversarial Attacks on Learned Policies for Surgical Robotic Tasks

author.name: Shutong Jin, Ziyang Chen, Preethi Satish, Paavan Gupta, Florian T. Pokorny, Ken Goldberg

entry.summary: Presents the first study of adversarial attacks on learning-based policies in surgical robotics, investigating disruptive attacks that interrupt execution and steering attacks that redirect actions via imperceptible visual perturbations. It evaluates three attack methods with increasing policy access on surgical tasks.

entry.title: Dual-Stance Evaluation of Sycophancy: The Structure of Agreement and the Limits of Intervention

author.name: Matthew James Buchan

entry.summary: Introduces dual-stance evaluation of sycophancy, testing whether a sycophancy-reduction steering direction also suppresses agreement with factually correct statements. Finds that on Llama-3-8B, sycophantic and factual agreement occupy geometrically distinct subspaces yet the steering direction projects equally onto both, harming correctness.

entry.title: Calibration Drift Under Reasoning: How Chain-of-Thought Budgets Induce Overconfidence in Large Language Models

author.name: Prakul Sunil Hiremath, Harshit R. Hiremath

entry.summary: Identifies Calibration Drift Under Reasoning, where increasing the chain-of-thought budget beyond a threshold makes LLMs systematically overconfident on incorrect answers. It analyzes theoretically and empirically a non-monotonic relationship between reasoning budget and expected calibration error.

entry.title: When Poison Fails After Retrieval: Revisiting Corpus Poisoning under Chunking and Reranking Pipelines

author.name: Xi Nie, Hongwei Li, Shenghao Wu, Mingxuan Li, Jiachen Li, Wenbo Jiang

entry.summary: Revisits corpus poisoning attacks on RAG under realistic multi-stage pipelines (chunking, dense retrieval, reranking, grounded generation), showing many existing attacks degrade after reranking. It identifies retrieval granularity mismatch as a key reason adversarial signals fragment during chunking.

entry.title: Quantifying Subliminal Behavioral Transfer Ratios in Language Model Distillation

author.name: Uwe Konig, Hamza Kazmi, Ruizhe Li, Maheep Chaudhary

entry.summary: Quantifies subliminal behavioral transfer in distillation, steering two teacher models at varying strengths and distilling students on only benign data, then measuring undesirable trait transfer on JailbreakBench prompts. It finds robust but model-dependent transfer with distinct scaling behaviors.

entry.title: When Probing Accuracy Saturates, Fragility Resolves: A Complementary Metric for LLM Pre-Training Analysis

author.name: Orion Reblitz-Richardson

entry.summary: Introduces fragility, a per-layer metric defined as the activation-noise level at which probe accuracy collapses, complementing standard linear probing whose accuracy saturates early in pretraining. Applied to open checkpoints, it reveals representational structure (e.g., evolving moralized representations) that accuracy alone cannot see.

entry.title: Pretrained self-supervised speech models can recognize unseen consonants

author.name: Chihiro Taguchi, \'Eric Le Ferrand, Hirosi Nakagawa, Hitomi Ono, Kanji Kato, Emily Prud'hommeaux, David Chiang

entry.summary: This work fine-tunes self-supervised speech models (Wav2Vec2, HuBERT) on click-rich Khoisan languages to test whether typologically rare consonants are recognized as accurately as common sounds. It probes representational bias in speech foundation models toward high-resource phonologies.

entry.title: ConsistencyPlanner: Real-time Planning with Fast-Sampling Consistency Models

author.name: Qichao Zhang, Xing Fang, Jiaqi Fang, Zhenwen Cai, Jie Ling, Qiankun Yu, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: ConsistencyPlanner uses fast-sampling consistency models for real-time closed-loop autonomous driving planning, balancing multimodal behavior modeling against latency to avoid indecisive or unsafe actions. It applies efficient generative sampling to safety-critical planning.

entry.title: TAROT: Task-Adaptive Refinement of LLM-prior Graphs for Few-shot Tabular Learning

author.name: Ruxue Shi, Yili Wang, Mengnan Du, Hangting Ye, Yi Chang, Xin Wang

entry.summary: TAROT refines LLM-derived prior graphs over tabular features in a task-adaptive way for few-shot tabular learning, avoiding extra training on generated data and the privacy concerns of feeding raw tables to LLMs. It exploits semantic feature relationships often overlooked by prior methods.

entry.title: TextHOI-3D: Text-to-3D Hand-Object Interaction via Discrete Multi-View Generation and Joint Mesh Optimization

author.name: Zixiong Hao, Zhencun Jiang

entry.summary: TextHOI-3D generates 3D hand-object interaction meshes from text via a VQ token space for fixed-camera observations, a CLIP-conditioned visual autoregressive model predicting multi-view tokens, and joint mesh recovery preserving semantics, geometry, articulated hand shape, and plausible contact. It tackles physically plausible text-to-3D HOI generation.

entry.title: Towards Data-free and Training-free Compression for Speech Foundation Models Using Parameter Clustering

author.name: Haoning Xu, Zhaoqing Li, Huimeng Wang, Youjun Chen, Chengxi Deng, Mengzhe Geng, Xunying Liu

entry.summary: This work proposes data-free and training-free compression of speech foundation models via channelwise k-means parameter clustering, with mixed-sparsity pruning that varies cluster counts per layer, achieving large WER reductions over magnitude pruning on LibriSpeech. It enables compression without calibration data or retraining.

entry.title: Fine-tuning Multi-modal LLMs with ART: Art-based Reinforcement Training

author.name: Michal Chudoba, Sergey Alyaev, Petra Galuscakova, Tomasz Wiktorski

entry.summary: ART (Art-based Reinforcement Training) is a PEFT method that injects information into a frozen multimodal LLM by optimizing only its raw visual input via backpropagation, enabling a soft-token approach on precompiled computational graphs unsupported by engines like vLLM. It avoids modifying the model's computational graph unlike LoRA or soft prompting.

entry.title: Implicit Neural Representations of Individual Behavior

author.name: Andrew Kang, Priya Narasimhan

entry.summary: Behavioral INR is a self-supervised generative model that adapts implicit neural representations from vision to behavior, representing each policy as a state-action function modulated by an episode-level latent via FiLM layers. It enables policy identification from unlabeled multi-policy behavioral data.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Disrupts Gradient-Based Adversarial Optimization

author.name: Xinhai Zou, Chang Zhao, Alireza Aghabagherloo, Dave Singel\'ee, Robin Degraeve, Bart Preneel

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether reinforcement learning training (policy-gradient with epsilon-greedy exploration) can disrupt the gradient structure exploited by gradient-based adversarial attacks on image classifiers. Experiments across CIFAR and ImageNet-100 show RL-trained classifiers significantly disrupt adversarial optimization, with mechanism analysis via loss landscape visualization.

entry.title: ProHiFlo: Hierarchical Flow Matching with Functional Guidance for De Novo Protein Generation

author.name: Chuanzhen Wang, Meade Cleti, Pete Jano

entry.summary: ProHiFlo is a hierarchical flow matching framework for de novo protein generation that models backbone geometry coarsely before refining to all-atom coordinates, with functional guidance from pretrained predictors and an adaptive SE(3)-equivariant architecture. It reduces computational cost while incorporating functional constraints.

entry.title: Recursive Binding on a Budget: Subspace Carving in Order-p Tensor Memories

author.name: Travis Pence, Daisuke Yamada, Vikas Singh

entry.summary: Orthogonal Subspace Carving binds fillers to roles in tensor product representations by projecting onto the null space of the role basis before aggregating into a fixed order-p tensor, decoupling tensor order from structural depth. It bridges the fidelity of tensor product representations with the constant dimensionality of vector symbolic architectures.

entry.title: OmniLoc: A Geometry-Aware Foundation Model for Anchor-Free UE Localization Across Diverse Indoor Environments

author.name: Lei Chu, Yuning Zhang, Omer Gokalp Serbetci, Anushka Katiyar, Bassel Abou Ali Modad, Andreas F. Molisch

entry.summary: OmniLoc is a geometry-aware foundation model for anchor-free user equipment localization across diverse indoor environments directly from wireless measurements, addressing variation in building geometry, detectable access points, and signal heterogeneity. It is claimed to be the first foundation-model approach for this wireless localization task.

entry.title: APEX: A Network-Native Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting and Anomaly Detection for Wireless Edge Operations

author.name: Swadhin Pradhan, Niloo Bahadori, Peiman Amini

entry.summary: APEX is a network-native decoder-only transformer foundation model for forecasting and anomaly detection on wireless network telemetry, pre-trained on ~100K AP time series from ~4,500 production networks. It reduces MAE by 18% over the strongest foundation-model baseline on DHCP degradation, with edge and cloud variants.

entry.title: Range-Aware Bayesian Optimization for Discovering Diverse Designs within Target Property Windows

author.name: Shengli Jiang, Jason Wu, Charles M. Schroeder, Michael A. Webb

entry.summary: This paper develops range-aware Bayesian optimization where the acquisition function scores the posterior probability that a candidate satisfies a target property window rather than a single optimum, and extends to parallel pursuit of multiple distinct specifications over a shared space. It recovers diverse solutions valuable for cost, processability, or robustness considerations in materials design.

entry.title: TimeRouter: Efficient and Adaptive Routing of Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Kanghui Ning, Yushan Jiang, Kashif Rasul, Anderson Schneider, Yuriy Nevmyvaka, Dongjin Song

entry.summary: TimeRouter is a lightweight routing framework that selects among multiple pretrained time-series foundation models without relying on expensive LLM controllers. It uses discriminative routing, selective gating, and ensemble fallback to match models to forecasting regimes.

entry.title: Space-sampled Value Decay: Forgetting Mechanisms for Non-stationary Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Felix St\"orck, Fabian Hinder, Barbara Hammer

entry.summary: Space-sampled Value Decay introduces an explicit forgetting mechanism for value-based deep RL in non-stationary environments that does not require task IDs or context information about drift. It is inspired by rodent behavioral adaptation.

entry.title: HAMNO: A Hierarchical Adaptive Multi-scale Neural Operator with Physics-Informed Learning for Dynamical Systems

author.name: Mostafa Bamdad, Mohammad Sadegh Eshaghi, Timon Rabczuk

entry.summary: HAMNO is a hierarchical adaptive multi-scale neural operator combining local convolutions, global spectral operators, and a data-dependent gating mechanism for learning solutions to nonlinear time-dependent PDEs. It targets multi-scale structures and stable long-time evolution.

entry.title: Efficient Multinomial Logistic Bandit via Frequent Directions

author.name: Linzhe He, Yu-Jie Zhang, Sifan Yang, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: EOFD-MLogB integrates frequent-directions matrix sketching into multinomial logistic bandits to drastically reduce per-round time and space costs while preserving regret guarantees. It addresses the prohibitive computational cost of UCB-type methods in high dimensions.

entry.title: Holding the FP8 Quality Ceiling at 8-Bit Weights and Activations: INT8 and GGUF Post-Training Quantization of Ideogram 4.0 for Consumer GPUs

author.name: Deep Gandhi, Ali Asaria, Tony Salomone

entry.summary: This paper studies INT8 and GGUF post-training quantization of Ideogram 4.0, a 9.3B flow-matching diffusion transformer, to run on consumer Ampere GPUs that lack FP8 tensor cores. The INT8 W8A8 recipe with SmoothQuant and mixed-precision protection matches FP8 quality on a 200-prompt benchmark.

entry.title: A2SG:Adaptive and Asymmetric Surrogate Gradients for Training Deep Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Yechan Kang, Yongjin Kweon, Mingyeong Seo, Sohee Park, Yeonguk Jeon, Jongkil Park, Hyun Jae Jang, Jaewook Kim, YeonJoo Jeong, Suyoun Lee, Seongsik Park

entry.summary: A2SG is a unified framework of adaptive and asymmetric surrogate gradients for training deep spiking neural networks, reducing spatial gradient variation and assigning larger gradients to higher-membrane-potential neurons. It proves lower variation than symmetric surrogates and connects gradient variation to loss curvature.

entry.title: Geometric bias in eigenspace perturbation under random heterogeneous noise

author.name: Fengkai Liu, Ke Wang, Wanjie Wang

entry.summary: This paper analyzes spectral perturbation of signal-plus-noise matrices under sparse, inhomogeneous-variance noise, showing a geometric bias that classical Davis-Kahan and Wedin bounds fail to capture. It provides finer-grained analysis of how signal geometry interacts with the noise distribution.

entry.title: Massive Open-Vocabulary Keyword Spotting

author.name: Leonor Barreiros, Raul Monteiro, Afonso Mendes, Gon\c{c}alo M. Correia

entry.summary: This paper proposes a massive open-vocabulary keyword spotting system that stores features with up to 128x smaller memory footprint, enabling contextual biasing over very large glossaries. It achieves comparable entity recall to uncompressed solutions without fine-tuning the speech model, even in unseen languages.

entry.title: SPADE: Split-and-Delay Embeddings for Autoregressive High-Granularity Calorimeter Simulation

author.name: Joschka Birk, Frank Gaede, Anna Hallin, Gregor Kasieczka, Martina Mozzanica, Henning Rose

entry.summary: SPADE is an autoregressive transformer for multi-feature tokens that embeds features independently and delays each feature stream so self-attention learns intra-token correlations. Applied to calorimeter shower generation, it is competitive with state-of-the-art and substantially beats a VQ-VAE predecessor.

entry.title: Neural-Parameterized Cellular Automata for Wildfire Spread

author.name: Maksym Zhenirovskyy, Ion Matei, Rohit Vuppala, Takuya Kurihana, Hon Yung Wonga

entry.summary: This work introduces a hybrid deep-learning parameterized probabilistic cellular automata framework for wildfire spread, using a multi-scale CNN to dynamically generate spatially varying spread parameters. The JAX implementation enables hardware acceleration and gradient-based calibration while preserving physical interpretability.

entry.title: Seeing Below the Limit of Detection: A Censored-Poisson Bayesian Latent-Growth Change-Point Detector (the Span Detector) for Serial ctDNA in HR+/HER2- Metastatic Breast Cancer

author.name: Aarchi Singh Thakur, Abhijoy Sarkar

entry.summary: Span is a censored-Poisson Bayesian latent-growth change-point detector for serial ctDNA in metastatic breast cancer, treating non-detects as left-censored observations to spot tumor growth below the assay detection limit. It aims to detect drug resistance earlier than conventional snapshot-based liquid biopsy interpretation.

entry.title: When More Documents Hurt RAG: Mitigating Vector Search Dilution with Domain-Scoped, Model-Agnostic Retrieval

author.name: Nabaraj Subedi, Ahmed Abdelaty, Shivanand Venkanna Sheshappanavar

entry.summary: This work identifies vector search dilution, where scaling RAG to large heterogeneous corpora causes top-k retrieval to return similar-but-wrong chunks, observed in a deployed transportation corpus dropping accuracy from 75% to under 40%. It proposes MASDR-RAG, a multi-agent domain-scoped retrieval method evaluated across backbones and corpora.

entry.title: Context-Aware Multimodal Claim Verification in Spoken Dialogues

author.name: Chaewan Chun, Delvin Ce Zhang, Dongwon Lee

entry.summary: MAD2 is a new benchmark of 1,000 two-speaker spoken dialogues with 3,368 check-worthy claims for multimodal claim verification, paired with a calibrated fusion of context-aware audio and dialogue-aware text models. It addresses under-studied spoken misinformation built conversationally across turns.

entry.title: Adaptive Multi-Resolution Procedural Knowledge Compression for Large Language Models

author.name: Changyue Wang, Weihang Su, Qingyao Ai, Yichen Tang, Runzhong Qiao, Xuancheng Li, Min Zhang, Yiqun Liu

entry.summary: This work proposes adaptive multi-resolution compression of procedural knowledge (reusable LLM skills) that preserves logical dependencies among workflows and tool protocols, unlike methods designed for factual document compression. It reduces prefill cost and latency from repeatedly placing full skill text in context.

entry.title: Verifiable Environments Are LEGO Bricks: Recursive Composition for Reasoning Generalization

author.name: Hao Xiang, Qiaoyu Tang, Le Yu, Yaojie Lu, Xianpei Han, Ben He, Le Sun, Bowen Yu, Peng Wang, Hongyu Lin, Dayiheng Liu

entry.summary: Gumbel-BEARD automates Whisper encoder layer selection for self-supervised domain adaptation via an end-to-end trainable hard Gumbel-Softmax selector with a BEST-RQ objective, adapting to target acoustics without manual tuning. On child speech, 10 hours of labeled data matches a fully supervised 133-hour baseline, setting new SOTA WERs.

entry.title: DarkVGGT: Seeing Through Darkness Using Thermal Geometry without Daylight Tax
