author.name: Juan Manuel Contreras

entry.summary: Constructs the first bottom-up psychometric instrument derived from LLM behavioral affordances via exploratory factor analysis, administering 300 items to 25 models and yielding a five-factor structure. Finds that even this LLM-native instrument's self-reports do not predict observed behavior.

entry.title: Rotate2Think: Geometric Priming via Orthogonal Rotation to Improve Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Aditya Sharma, Christopher J. Pal, Amal Zouaq

entry.summary: Shows that LLM input and thinking embeddings both exhibit extreme conicity but lie along non-collinear mean directions, and proposes Rotate2Think, an inference-time orthogonal rotation that primes stronger reasoning. It links representation-space geometry to reasoning quality.

entry.title: Less Context, More Accuracy: A Bi-Temporal Memory Engine for LLM Agents Where a Lean Retrieved Context Beats the Full History

author.name: Liuyin Wang

entry.summary: Presents Engram, an open-source bi-temporal memory engine for LLM agents that combines a fast lossless episodic write path with an asynchronous knowledge-graph fact extraction path, showing lean retrieved context can beat full-history replay on accuracy. It also critiques inconsistent memory benchmark reporting.

entry.title: Generalized-CVO: Fast and Correspondence-Free Local Point Cloud Registration with Second Order Riemannian Optimization

author.name: Ray Zhang, Marcus Greiff, Thomas Lew, John Subosits

entry.summary: Proposes Generalized-CVO, a correspondence-free local point cloud registration method using RKHS embeddings with anisotropic kernels and a second-order on-manifold Riemannian optimization scheme, achieving up to 10x speedup over first-order solvers. It improves LiDAR and RGB-D tracking accuracy.

entry.title: Density Ridge Selective Prediction for LLM and VLM Hallucination Detection under Calibration Label Scarcity

author.name: Nina I. Shamsi

entry.summary: This paper proposes a hallucination detection method for LLMs and VLMs that recovers the response manifold as the density ridge of a kernel density estimate over kinematic features of hidden-state trajectories. It scores generations by distance to the nearest ridge vertex, targeting the realistic setting where calibration labels are scarce.

entry.title: The Confident Liar: Diagnosing Multi-Agent Debate with Log-Probabilities and LLM-as-Judge

author.name: Ali Keramati, Justin Cheok, Jacob Horne, Mark Warschauer

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses multi-agent debate by studying the relationship between token-level log-probabilities, LLM-as-judge rubric scores, and final task accuracy across three domains. It uses a Constructor-Auditor architecture to test whether internal confidence predicts externally judged reasoning quality.

entry.title: Decoupling Thought from Speech: Knowledge-Grounded Counterfactual Reasoning for Resilient Multi-Agent Argumentation

author.name: Jakub Mas{\l}owski, Jaros{\l}aw A. Chudziak

entry.summary: KG-CFR is a dual-stage multi-agent debate architecture that separates a private retrieval-augmented planning buffer from a public execution layer to prevent logic degradation, argument repetition, and role drift during long exchanges. It aims to maintain process fidelity and agent identity under sustained perturbations rather than just optimizing final accuracy.

entry.title: Drawing with Strangers: Population Scaling Drives Zero-Shot Mutual Intelligibility in Emergent Sketching

author.name: Jooyeon Kim

entry.summary: This work formalizes zero-shot mutual intelligibility, the capacity for independently trained agent populations to communicate without prior exposure, using emergent sketching as a visually grounded modality. It finds that scaling training population size substantially improves cross-community intelligibility by increasing in-group variation and preventing co-adaptation.

entry.title: Event-Driven Reinforcement Learning Enables Long-Horizon Control in Semiconductor Fabrication

author.name: Yavar Yeganeh, Mahsa Shekari, Nicla Frigerio, Daniele Pagano, Andrea Matta

entry.summary: Develops an event-driven deep RL framework for long-horizon, multi-objective control in semiconductor fabrication, modeling system evolution as interconnected temporal processes with a centralized coordinating policy. Targets the stochastic, highly constrained scheduling of wafer fabs.

entry.title: Human-AI Teaming Through the Lens of Calibration

author.name: Eric Nalisnick, Chi Zhang, Sophia Qian, Yixin Wang

entry.summary: Studies human-AI teaming through statistical calibration, showing that existing prediction-combination methods fail to preserve human calibration while delegation methods shift the calibration burden onto the rejector. Provides theoretical and empirical results.

entry.title: Diffusion Forcing Planner: History-Annealed Planning with Time-Dependent Guidance for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zehan Zhang, Neng Zhang, Yaoyi Li, Jia Cai, Zhiling Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Diffusion Forcing Planner (DFP) for autonomous driving, decomposing trajectories into history, current, and future segments with independent noise levels and history-guided control to combat temporal inconsistency. Avoids the history-copying failure of static conditioning.

entry.title: AuRA: Internalizing Audio Understanding into LLMs as LoRA

author.name: Bo Cheng, Lei Shi, Zhanyu Ma, Yuan Wu, Jun Xu, Jiuchong Gao, Jinghua Hao, Renqing He

entry.summary: Presents AuRA, which distills ASR encoder capability into an LLM via a LoRA-adapted student and lightweight audio embedding layer using layer-wise distillation. Avoids cascaded ASR-LLM latency and costly multimodal training for speech understanding.

entry.title: Provenance-Grounded Gating and Adaptive Recovery in Synthetic Post-Training Data Curation

author.name: Soham Bhattacharjee, Karun Sharma, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu, Pratinav Seth

entry.summary: Studies synthetic post-training data curation, examining whether filtering signals are grounded in source evidence and whether rejected samples can be recovered rather than discarded. Finds source provenance improves faithfulness gating and that hallucination and reward gates reject disjoint populations.

entry.title: EEVEE: Towards Test-time Prompt Learning in the Real World for Self-Improving Agents

author.name: Weixian Xu, Shilong Liu, Mengdi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes EEVEE, a multi-dataset test-time prompt learning framework for LLM agents that uses a router to partition heterogeneous input streams into task clusters mapped to prompt configurations, optimized via router-prompt co-evolution. Targets real-world heterogeneous task streams.

entry.title: FailureScope: Cross-Regime Behavioral Diagnosis of Language Model Weaknesses

author.name: Nicholas Saban

entry.summary: Introduces FailureScope, a behavioral-diagnosis method clustering evaluation probes by cross-model pass/fail patterns (leave-one-model-out) to produce stable, interpretable failure taxonomies. Works across single-turn, multi-turn, and adversarial agent regimes, improving cross-model failure prediction (AUC 0.88).

entry.title: Quality Is Not a Safety Proxy Under Quantization

author.name: Sahil Kadadekar

entry.summary: Audits whether quality metrics predict safety after quantization across 6 models, 4 families, and multiple GGUF/AWQ/GPTQ formats, finding that quality and refusal behavior diverge with refusal dropping 12-68 points while quality stays stable. Mechanistic probes fail to reliably flag these hidden-danger checkpoints.

entry.title: SoK: Colluding Adversaries in Machine Learning Pipelines

author.name: Vasisht Duddu, Lipeng He, Asim Waheed, N. Asokan

entry.summary: This systematization-of-knowledge paper proposes a framework for analyzing collusion among adversaries in ML pipelines, covering both train-time/inference-time and inference-time/inference-time collusion. It provides guidelines to conjecture collusion potential based on enabling factors.

entry.title: POPSICLE: Benchmark Datasets for Segmentation and Localization in CryoET

author.name: Jonathan Schwartz, Utz Heinrich Ermel, C. Braxton Owens, Zhuowen Zhao, Ariana Peck, Gus L. W. Hart, Grant J. Jensen, Bridget Carragher, Dari Kimanius

entry.summary: POPSICLE introduces benchmark datasets for segmentation and localization in cryo-electron tomography, addressing the lack of standardized, well-annotated benchmarks that bottleneck ML development for cryoET. It enables robust comparisons across methods for interpreting complex cellular imaging data.

entry.title: Generalized Conformal Predictive Systems Under Distributional Shifts

author.name: Jef Jonkers, Johanna Ziegel

entry.summary: This work extends generalized conformal predictive systems to non-exchangeable settings using observation-specific permutation weights, yielding shift-aware predictive systems with finite-sample or asymptotic guarantees. It introduces weight-uncertainty boxes for robustness when weights are estimated.

entry.title: Where You Inject Diversity Matters: A Unified Framework for Diverse Generation

author.name: Cheng Zhang, Rui Xin, Chudi Zhong

entry.summary: This work introduces a framework characterizing test-time diverse generation methods by their diversity source and a transmission score measuring how source variation reaches final output. It proposes automated specification-level methods that generate diverse intermediate specifications before conditioning.

entry.title: WebChallenger: A Reliable and Efficient Generalist Web Agent

author.name: Jayoo Hwang, Xiaowen Zhang, Vedant Padwal

entry.summary: WebChallenger is a web agent framework that addresses cognitive gaps (selective attention, persistent memory, procedural fluency) through architecture design rather than model scale. It centers on PageMem, a structured page representation built deterministically from the DOM.

entry.title: ParaBridge: Bridging Paralinguistic Perception and Dialogue Behavior in Speech Language Models

author.name: Yuxiang Wang, Qinke Ni, Shengbo Cai, Wan Lin, Liqiang Zhang, Zhizheng Wu

entry.summary: ParaBridge is an on-policy self-distillation method that bridges paralinguistic perception and dialogue behavior in speech language models, turning brittle inference-time instruction scaffolds into stable model behavior. It addresses the gap where SLMs recognize but ignore paralinguistic cues in open-ended dialogue.

entry.title: REAL: A Reasoning-Enhanced Graph Framework for Long-Term Memory Management of LLMs

author.name: Keer Lu, Liwei Chen, Guoqing Jiang, Zhiheng Qin, Yunhuai Liu, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: REAL introduces a reasoning-enhanced graph framework for long-term memory management in LLMs, aiming to capture explicit relations between memories, handle evolving facts non-destructively, and support active retrieval. It addresses limitations of flat text and structured memory systems for long-horizon interactions.

entry.title: DB-3DME: From Dataset to Benchmark for Human-aligned Automatic 3D Mesh Evaluation

author.name: Nanshan Jia, Zhenyu Zhao, Sui Huang, Jingshen Wang, Zeyu Zheng

entry.summary: DB-3DME provides a dataset and benchmark for human-aligned automatic 3D mesh evaluation, containing thousands of synthetic meshes with human ratings on geometry and prompt adherence, and benchmarks VLMs as judges. It identifies visual encoding of 3D as key to alignment.

entry.title: CoCoSI: Collaborative Cognitive Map Construction for Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Yiming Zhang, Ruoxuan Cao, Zhihang Zhong

entry.summary: CoCoSI is a lightweight, model-agnostic method for constructing collaborative cognitive maps to preserve spatial information beyond MLLMs' context window without architectural changes or finetuning. It targets spatial intelligence for off-the-shelf multimodal models.

entry.title: SSR-Merge: Subspace Signal Routing for Training-Free LoRA Merging in Diffusion Models

author.name: Zhengxuan Wei, Yi Dong, Zonghui Li, Xianhui Lin, Xing Liu, Hong Gu, Shaofeng Zhang, Wenbin Li, Qi Fan

entry.summary: SSR-Merge proposes training-free LoRA merging in diffusion models via subspace signal routing, resolving parameter interference by routing internal signals rather than merging in parameter space, using decorrelation and directional guidance. It avoids destructive collisions in shared parameter space.

entry.title: SCAIL-2: Unifying Controlled Character Animation with End-to-end In-Context Conditioning

author.name: Wenhao Yan, Fengjia Guo, Zhuoyi Yang, Jie Tang

entry.summary: SCAIL-2 is an end-to-end framework for controlled character animation that bypasses intermediate representations like pose skeletons by directly concatenating driving videos, avoiding information loss. It curates a synthetic MotionPair-60K dataset to address the lack of end-to-end training data.

entry.title: HarmoView: Harmonizing Multi-View Constraints for Identity-Consistent Video Generation

author.name: Cong Wang, Zhentao Yu, Hongmei Wang, Weicong Liang, Zixiang Zhou, Zilin Yang, Jiarong Ou, Rui Chen, Yuan Zhou, Qinglin Lu

entry.summary: HarmoView is a framework for identity-consistent video generation that integrates multi-view reference cues through multi-level feature injection and a staged training curriculum to preserve appearance under large viewpoint changes. It addresses the scarcity of multi-view data and lack of effective frameworks.

entry.title: Mean Flow Distillation: Robust and Stable Distillation for Flow Matching Models

author.name: An Zhao, Shengyuan Zhang, Zhongjian Sun, Yixiang Zhou, Zejian Li, Ling Yang, Tianrun Chen, Lingyun Sun

entry.summary: Proposes Mean Flow Distillation, a distillation framework tailored to flow matching models that acts as a temporal low-pass filter, improving stability over diffusion-borrowed score-matching approaches. Aims for fast, robust few-step generation.

entry.title: IMPACT: Learning Internal-Model Predictive Control for Forceful Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Jiawei Gao, Chaoqi Liu, Peilin Wu, Haonan Chen, Yilun Du

entry.summary: Proposes IMPACT, learning internal-model predictive control for forceful robotic manipulation that generalizes across object weights without specialized force/tactile hardware. Addresses limitations of implicit and explicit force-control approaches.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction for Dyadic Regression Under Complex Missingness

author.name: Robert Lunde, Minjie Yang, Elizaveta Levina, Ji Zhu

entry.summary: Develops a conformal prediction framework for dyadic regression under complex missingness, establishing super-uniformity under weaker-than-exchangeability invariance and a novel bijection argument for random-subset sampling, with several conformal procedures for exchangeable arrays. Extends distribution-free uncertainty quantification to network/matrix data.

entry.title: Subversion-Resistance for Free from Formal Verification

author.name: Adam Chlipala

entry.summary: Adam Chlipala argues that formal verification can provide subversion-resistance against adversaries for free, blocking many problematic behaviors of complex (and potentially superintelligent) software through mathematical proof without anticipating specific attack methods, provided specifications encapsulate components away from the messy real world. It connects formal methods to AI safety guarantees.

entry.title: Deployment-Time Memorization in Foundation-Model Agents

author.name: Lei (Rachel), Chen, Guilin Zhang, Kai Zhao, Dalmo Cirne, Andy Olsen, Xu Chu, Zeke Miller, Alet Blanken, Amine Anoun, Jerry Ting

entry.summary: Studies deployment-time memorization in long-lived foundation-model agents, framing agent memory as a privacy-utility frontier measured by personalization recall versus adversarial extraction rate. It sweeps memory-design knobs like summarization, retrieval breadth, and deletion mode to characterize tradeoffs.

entry.title: Belief-Space Control for Personalized Cancer Treatment via Active Inference

author.name: Deniz Sargun, H. Bugra Tulay, C. Emre Koksal

entry.summary: Models personalized cancer treatment as belief-space planning via active inference, deriving an expected-free-energy objective that unifies goal-directed control and information acquisition under measurement budgets. Validated on real clinical data from the AACR Project GENIE dataset.

entry.title: READER: Robust Evidence-based Authorship Decoding via Extracted Representations

author.name: Jiaxu Liu, Sunnan Mu, Dong Huang, Liuyin Wang, Jing Shao, Jie Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces READER for dynamic black-box LLM provenance, identifying the source model from query-varying generations using a frozen proxy LLM as a reader of weak authorship traces. Addresses provenance when prompt semantics dominate the text.

entry.title: Null-Space Constrained Low-Rank Adaptation for Response-Specified Large Language Model Unlearning

author.name: Bocheng Ju, Jianhua Wang, Chengliang Liu, Xiaolin Chang

entry.summary: Introduces NSRU, a null-space constrained low-rank adaptation framework for response-specified LLM unlearning that uses explicit safe target responses and localizes updates via orthogonal projection onto retain subspaces. Aims to suppress undesired knowledge while preserving benign capabilities.

entry.title: Two to Tango: Coupled Task-Reference Selection for Safe LLM Fine-tuning

author.name: Xinrui Chen, Jianhao Zhang, Ou Wu, Di Gao

entry.summary: Proposes DualSelect, a coupled framework that jointly selects safety reference examples and compatible task samples during fine-tuning to prevent erosion of safety alignment. It uses a minimax view to refresh task-conditioned safety references before filtering task data.

entry.title: LongMoE: Longitudinal Multimodal Learning via Trajectory-Aware Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Maxx Richard Rahman, Prakhar Kumar, Wolfgang Maass

entry.summary: Proposes LongMoE, a trajectory-aware mixture-of-experts framework for longitudinal multimodal clinical learning that simultaneously handles missing modalities and evolving disease trajectories, which prior methods address only in isolation. It integrates imaging, text, and health records over time.

entry.title: Optimality of FSQ Tokens for Continuous Diffusion for Categorical Data with Application to Text-to-Speech

author.name: Vadim Popov, Wenju Gu, Tasnima Sadekova, Georgii Aparin, Assel Yermekova

entry.summary: Studies the latent-space structure of discrete tokenizers for continuous diffusion on categorical data, finding that finite scalar quantization (FSQ) tokenization yields properties best suited for continuous diffusion in terms of KL divergence and prediction accuracy. It applies the analysis to text-to-speech.

entry.title: Inside the Latent Flow: Causal Deciphering of Attention Dynamics in Audio Separation Foundation Models

author.name: Yuxuan Chen, Haoyuan Xu, Peize He

entry.summary: Adapts causal-intervention probing to flow-matching audio separation transformers, uncovering a dual-pathway text-conditioning mechanism and asynchronous layerwise convergence, then proposes Layer-Selective Attention Caching for training-free acceleration. It opens the black box of audio separation foundation models.

entry.title: Local Is Not a Sufficient Privacy Boundary: Governing OS-Integrated On-Device AI

author.name: Jonghyun Chung, Sanket Badhe

entry.summary: The authors argue that running AI locally on a device is insufficient as a privacy guarantee, since OS-integrated assistants can assemble sensitive context, persist derived state, invoke tools, and route to cloud. They propose an institutional accountability framework treating on-device AI privacy as a governance problem rather than a deployment attribute.

entry.title: Dual-Branch Gated Fusion for Open-Set Audio Deepfake Source Tracing

author.name: Awais Khan, Kutub Uddin, Khalid Malik

entry.summary: This work proposes a dual-branch gated fusion framework for open-set audio deepfake source tracing, pairing XLSR-53 self-supervised features with a 66-dimensional CORES descriptor spanning multiple acoustic dimensions. An input-conditioned gate adaptively balances the branches to handle both in-domain and out-of-distribution synthesizers.

entry.title: Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations

author.name: Zhuohang Jiang, Yuxin Chen, Shijie Wang, Haohao Qu, Zhou Jindong, Wenqi Fan, Li Qing, Dongxu Liang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: This work proposes atomic intent reasoning to bring LLM semantics into industrial cross-domain recommendation from content platforms to e-commerce, addressing semantic gaps and noisy behavior sequences. It distills LLM reasoning into a form deployable under millisecond-latency online recommendation constraints.

entry.title: KG-SoftMAP: Soft Knowledge-Graph Priors for Bayesian Network Structure Learning from Sparse Discrete Data

author.name: Guoliang Xu, James E. Corter

entry.summary: KG-SoftMAP learns Bayesian network structure from sparse discrete data by encoding an imperfect knowledge graph as a soft, confidence-weighted, data-overridable edge prior within a MAP objective. The knowledge graph may be expert-curated or LLM-extracted, improving structure recovery when joint observations are scarce.

entry.title: SkillResolve-Bench: Measuring and Resolving Same-Capability Ambiguity in Agent Skill Retrieval

author.name: Jiandong Ding

entry.summary: SkillResolve-Bench studies same-capability ambiguity in agent skill retrieval, where a retriever finds the right capability family but exposes a risky sibling skill that may use stale resources or wrong procedures. It introduces an auditable benchmark of 661 helpful/risky skill pairs with execution-risk evidence.

entry.title: Improving Adversarial Transferability on Vision-Language Pre-training Models via Surrogate-Specific Bias Correction

author.name: Lijia Yu, Jiuxin Cao, Yuchen Qiang, Changhao Chen, Yifei Huang, Bo Liu

entry.summary: DeBias-Attack improves the cross-model transferability of adversarial examples against vision-language pretraining models by correcting surrogate-specific bias in optimization directions. It addresses the problem that adversarial updates follow surrogate model responses more than input semantics, reducing transfer to unseen targets.

entry.title: Is Fairness Truly Fair? Towards Reliable Lipschitz Fairness in Multi-Task Learning via Fixed-\texorpdfstring{$\delta$}{delta} Alignment

author.name: Junbo Ding, Xin Zang, Chenchen Pan, Donghao Song, Jiaxin Zhu, Danhuai Guo

entry.summary: ReLiF is a reliability-aware framework for Lipschitz individual fairness in multi-task learning, identifying threshold confounding where auditing tolerance derived from each model's own representation distances leads to unfair comparisons. It separates evaluation-time fixed-delta auditing from training-time controlled regularization to enable reliable fairness comparison.

entry.title: In Defense of Information Leakage in Concept-based Models

author.name: Mateo Espinosa Zarlenga

entry.summary: Challenges the conventional view that information leakage in concept-based models is always harmful, arguing leakage is often necessary under real-world concept incompleteness. Reframes interpretability tradeoffs in CMs.

entry.title: Recoverable but Not Stationary:Local Linear Structures in Weights and Activations

author.name: Irina Piontkovskaia, Sergey Nikolenko

entry.summary: Investigates which linear structures truly exist in neural weights and activations, finding strong local low-rank task-gradient structure but rejecting a fixed-task-plane hypothesis as useful bases drift within 100 steps. Develops random search theory with a Gaussian local-linear theorem.

entry.title: Toward Calibrated, Fair, and accurate Deepfake Detection

author.name: Ryan Brown, Chris Russell

entry.summary: Introduces Face-Fairness, a plug-and-play bias mitigation framework for deepfake detection, with Face-Feature Tuning being the first demographic-label-free fairness method via a lightweight calibrator remapping logits conditioned on frozen face embeddings. Includes variants for available or discovered demographic groups.

entry.title: A Continuous-Time Markov Chain Framework for Insertion Language Models

author.name: Dhruvesh Patel, Benjamin Rozonoyer, Soumitra Das, Tahira Naseem, Tim G. J. Rudner, Andrew McCallum

entry.summary: Derives a principled diffusion-style denoising objective for Insertion Language Models by formulating the noising process as a continuous-time Markov chain over variable-length sequences, unifying prior ad hoc ILM formulations. It shows the framework retains insertion-based generation benefits over left-to-right and masked-diffusion approaches.

entry.title: Alignment Defends LLMs from Property Inference Attacks

author.name: Pengrun Huang, Chhavi Yadav, Ruihan Wu, Kamalika Chaudhuri

entry.summary: Proposes alignment-based defenses against property inference attacks that extract sensitive dataset-level properties from fine-tuned LLMs, reshaping output distributions toward a target property without needing original data or retraining. This makes defenses applicable to already-deployed models.

entry.title: WHU-Infra3D: A Full-stack Multi-modal Dataset and Benchmark for 3D Roadside Infrastructure Inventory

author.name: Chong Liu, Luxuan Fu, Xuyu Feng, Zhen Dong, Bisheng Yang

entry.summary: WHU-Infra3D is a large-scale multimodal benchmark for 3D roadside infrastructure inventory, combining panoramic imagery and LiDAR across 53.8 km in three cities with rigorous 2D-3D instance association. It targets digital twin cities and automated infrastructure maintenance.

entry.title: Early-Token Confidence Predicts Reasoning Quality in Multi-Agent LLM Debate

author.name: Ali Keramati, Justin Cheok, Jacob Horne, Mark Warschauer

entry.summary: BenSyc is the first benchmark for studying conversational sycophancy in Bengali social contexts, built from Reddit data with human-validated binary labels and a five-level taxonomy. It addresses culturally grounded sycophancy in emotionally sensitive conversations beyond factual agreement.

entry.title: Multilingual Word-Level Forced Alignment with Self-Supervised Representations and Learned Dynamic Programming

author.name: Roy Weber, Meidan Zehavi, Rotem Rousso, Joseph Keshet

entry.summary: This paper presents a multilingual word-level forced alignment method combining an alignment encoder fusing MMS and self-supervised phoneme boundary representations with a learned dynamic programming decoder. It outperforms Montreal Forced Aligner and MMS-based alignment on TIMIT, Buckeye, and unseen languages.

entry.title: Trace Only What You Need: Structure-Aware On-Demand Hypergraph Memory for Long-Document Question Answering

author.name: Xiangjun Zai, Xingyu Tan, Chen Chen, Xiaoyang Wang, Wenjie Zhang

entry.summary: DocTrace is a multi-agent RAG framework for long-document QA that builds query-triggered hypergraph memory, leverages document structure, and reuses prior reasoning experience. It targets reasoning over scattered evidence in lengthy documents.

entry.title: Maximum Matching Accuracy: An Instance Segmentation Evaluation Metric Utilizing Globally Optimal Matching

author.name: Kaden Stillwagon, Alexandra D. VandeLoo, Craig R. Forest

entry.summary: This work proposes Maximum Matching Accuracy, a threshold-free, globally optimal matching metric for instance segmentation that addresses weaknesses of IoU thresholds and greedy matching in biological imaging. It produces more reliable and intuitive model rankings.

entry.title: Segment and Select: Vision-Language Segmentation in 3D Scenarios

author.name: Yulin Chen, Zhihang Zhong, Yuenan Hou

entry.summary: SEGA3D is a segment-and-select paradigm for 3D vision-language segmentation that operates directly on fine-grained visual information instead of coarse superpoints, improving mask candidate quality and using an LLM for selection. It addresses poor boundaries from superpoint dependency.

entry.title: GaussTrace: Provenance Analysis of 3D Gaussian Splatting Models with Evidence-based LLM Reasoning

author.name: Haoliang Han, Ziyuan Luo, Renjie Wan

entry.summary: GaussTrace constructs directed provenance graphs for 3D Gaussian Splatting models, framing provenance as evidence-based reasoning over statistical parameter profiling and hypothesis-driven editing simulations with LLM reasoning. It addresses IP protection and forensic traceability of 3DGS assets.

entry.title: Patient-Level Diagnosis of Acute Myeloid Leukemia via Deep Learning Analysis of Bone Marrow Smear

author.name: Yuqi Ma, Tianyi Wang, Weihua Meng, Hongru Chen, Fajin Tao, Qunxian Lu, Lin An, Xiaodong Mo, Gen Yang

entry.summary: This paper presents a cell-to-patient deep learning pipeline for acute myeloid leukemia diagnosis from bone marrow smear images, using a 16-category cell annotation vocabulary and aggregating cellular observations rather than identifying strict blasts. It validates across multiple anonymized centers including an external cohort.

entry.title: ZODS-RS -- Zero-training Oriented Detection & Segmentation for Remote Sensing

author.name: Zuan Gu, Tianhan Gao, Langxu Zhao

entry.summary: ZODS-RS is a training-free, closed-form pipeline for oriented detection and segmentation in remote sensing and UAV imagery, built on DINOv3 features and SAM-style proposals with prototype purification and rotation-scale equivariant matching. It unifies detection and segmentation without task-specific training.

entry.title: Beyond Model Size: Probing the Gaps in Visual in-Context Learning by Training a Tiny Model

author.name: Sunil Khatri, Steven Landgraf, Markus Ulrich, Simon Rei{\ss}

entry.summary: Stress-tests visual in-context learning by training a tiny 1M-parameter model on 70k images to probe whether scaling is truly necessary for in-context adaptation. Challenges the assumption that model and data scale are the key ingredients.

entry.title: Act on What You See: Unlocking Safe Social Navigation in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Qingzi Wang (University of Maryland), Xiyang Wu (University of Maryland), Guangyao Shi (University of Southern California), Dianwei Chen (University of Maryland), Xianfeng Yang (University of Maryland), Dinesh Manocha (University of Maryland)

entry.summary: Shows pretrained VLA models internally encode pedestrian-object distinctions and collision signals but behavior cloning fails to act on them, then proposes SALSA, an annotation-free post-training framework aligning social features and temporal safety. Unlocks safer social navigation.

entry.title: A Mean-Field Analysis of Multi-Head Self-Attention under Cross-Entropy Training

author.name: Cheng Huan, Hongfwei Yuan

entry.summary: Develops a mean-field theory for single-layer causal multi-head self-attention trained by cross-entropy, treating heads as particles and deriving a nonlinear Wasserstein gradient-flow in the infinite-head limit. Extends mean-field analysis beyond square-loss to softmax and QKV structure.

entry.title: Self-Distillation Policy Optimization via Visual Feedback: Bridging Code and Visual Artifacts

author.name: Haoyu Dong

entry.summary: Introduces Visual-SDPO, a self-distillation policy optimization framework that uses rendered visual feedback as privileged context for a teacher to improve code that generates visual artifacts like charts and web pages. Addresses defects from committing to code before observing the render.

entry.title: Learning What to Remember: Observability-Safe Memory Retention via Constrained Optimization for Long-Horizon Language Agents

author.name: Qingcan Kang, Liu Mingyang, Shixiong Kai, Kaichao Liang, Tao Zhong, Mingxuan Yuan

entry.summary: Formulates memory retention in long-horizon language agents as a constrained stochastic optimization problem with explicit budgets, miss penalties, reacquisition delays, and stale-information risk. Proposes OSL-MR for observability-safe retention decisions.

entry.title: WorldKernel: A World Model is the Coupling Kernel of Admissible Possible Worlds

author.name: Fabio Rovai

entry.summary: Reports a structural failure mode where strong predictors collapse on unidentified counterfactual coupling quantities while the truth remains an admissible interval that more data cannot narrow. Casts a world model as a positive-semidefinite coupling kernel over admissible possible worlds.

entry.title: One Lens, Many Worlds : A Capability-Typed Interface for World-Model Interpretability

author.name: Bhavith Chandra Challagundla, Sanskar Pandey, Param Thakkar, Rishikesh Mallagundla, Yugandhar Reddy Gogireddy, Wenhao Lu, Hindol Roy Choudhury, Shravani Challagundla, Mohamed Deraz Nasr, Spursh Deshpande

entry.summary: Proposes a capability-typed interface for world-model interpretability that unifies probing, activation patching, sparse autoencoders, and surprise analysis across diverse world-model substrates (recurrent state-space, token-based, joint-embedding). It avoids re-implementing tooling for each architecture beyond transformer LMs.

entry.title: Temporal Sheaf Neural Networks with Dynamic Orthogonal Transport

author.name: Md Sadek Hossain Asif, Tanzila Khan, Md. Mosaddek Khan

entry.summary: Introduces Temporal Sheaf Neural Networks for temporal link prediction, equipping each node with a time-varying orthogonal frame and comparing node states only after explicit transport between local coordinate systems. It uses low-rank Householder products and a geometric-residual decoder under strictly causal computation.

entry.title: Pareto-Guided Teacher Alignment for Fair Personalized Text Generation

author.name: Tunazzina Islam

entry.summary: Frames fairness mitigation in personalized persuasive text generation as a constrained multi-objective alignment problem, proposing a Pareto-guided teacher alignment framework with revision-based candidate generation, feasibility gating, and preference optimization. It reduces demographic disparities while preserving personalization fidelity on climate and vaccination persuasion tasks.

entry.title: Towards Critical Branching Mechanism in Recurrent Neural Networks

author.name: Feixiang Ren, Ling Feng

entry.summary: This work analyzes hidden-state dynamics in trained LSTMs and finds that small networks near optimal training exhibit scale-free avalanche statistics and near-critical branching, while larger models remain subcritical. It introduces a mixture branching process framework linking heterogeneous dynamics to long-range temporal correlations.

entry.title: Vision-Assisted Foundation Model for Solving Multi-Task Vehicle Routing Problems

author.name: Shuangchun Gui, Zhiguang Cao, Wen Song, Yew-Soon Ong

entry.summary: This work proposes a vision-assisted foundation model for multi-task vehicle routing problems, encoding diverse routing constraints via the vision modality and integrating patch-level semantics into a graph-based solver. It addresses the limitation of graph-only solvers in handling variants with multiple constraints.

entry.title: ERAlign: Energy-based Representation Alignment of GNNs and LLMs on Text-attributed Graphs

author.name: Xianlin Zeng, Fan Xia, Xiangyu Chen

entry.summary: ERAlign uses energy-based models to align GNN-encoded graph structure and LLM-derived text embeddings in a shared latent space for text-attributed graphs. It moves beyond coarse heuristic matching by enforcing distributional alignment to reduce representation drift and improve generalization.

entry.title: NOVA: Symbolic Regression Discovery of Interpretable Car-Following and Lane-Change Models with Driver Heterogeneity

author.name: Ishak Abassi, Nassim Ali Bouazzouni, Farah Ibelaiden, Nadir Farhi

entry.summary: NOVA is an autonomous symbolic regression framework that discovers interpretable car-following and lane-change models from raw trajectory data with minimal priors. Applied to nearly 4.8 million NGSIM observations, its Rust-powered search identifies compact acceleration models outperforming an LLM-based symbolic regression baseline.

entry.title: A Constrained Natural-Language Interface for Variational Multi-Physics Finite Element Simulations in FEniCS

author.name: Nilay Upadhyay, Wesley F. Reinhart

entry.summary: Presents a constrained natural-language interface for multi-physics FEniCS finite element simulations where the LLM is restricted to front-end parsing and non-catalog geometry generation, never writing the numerical solver core. A deterministic dispatcher maps validated specs to human-written templates.

entry.title: TENP: Trapezoidal Expert Neuron Pruning For Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Jiangyang He, Shaolin Zhu, Deyi Xiong

entry.summary: Proposes TENP, a structured Trapezoidal Expert Neuron Pruning framework for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs that retains important experts while pruning neurons in less important ones in a trapezoidal shallow-to-deep pattern. Avoids disrupting routing topology unlike whole-expert removal.

entry.title: Magnetic HIP-NN for spin dynamics in disordered itinerant magnets

author.name: Supriyo Ghosh, Yunhao Fan, Sheng Zhang, Kipton Barros, Gia-Wei Chern

entry.summary: Magnetic HIP-NN extends a hierarchical message-passing neural network to incorporate rotationally invariant spin correlations, enabling large-scale simulation of electron-mediated spin dynamics in disordered itinerant magnets. It learns emergent magnetic energy landscapes while preserving spin-rotation symmetry.

entry.title: An adaptive framework for the axisymmetric pulsar magnetosphere using physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold networks

author.name: Spyros Rigas, Ioannis Contopoulos, Georgios Alexandridis, Antonios Nathanail

entry.summary: This work refines physics-informed neural network solutions for axisymmetric pulsar magnetospheres using Kolmogorov-Arnold network architectures, an automated adaptive training pipeline, and a physics-based convergence criterion. It eliminates extensive manual hyperparameter tuning while improving accuracy and reducing training time.

entry.title: Speaker Group Encoding in Self-supervised Speech Recognition Models

author.name: Felix Herron, Solange Rossato Alexandre Allauzen, Benoit Favre, Fran\c{c}ois Portet

entry.summary: This work probes what self-supervised speech recognition models encode about speaker groups (gender, age, dialect, ethnicity, native status) across pretrained, SID-finetuned, ASR-finetuned, and fairness-enhanced states. It finds SID finetuning amplifies phonetically variant speaker categories while ASR discards them.

entry.title: The Shibboleth Effect: Auditing the Cross-Lingual Distributional Skew of Large Language Models

author.name: Hakan Mehmetcik

entry.summary: This study probes cross-lingual distributional skew (the Shibboleth Effect) in frontier LLMs using a multi-agent geopolitical wargame, comparing behavioral dispositions when play language is English versus Turkish. It finds language-driven shifts in model behavior under adversarial scenarios.

entry.title: FlexPath: Learned Semantic Path Priors for Image-Based Planning

author.name: Taehyoung Kim, Tim Schoenbrod, David Eckel, Henri Mee{\ss}

entry.summary: FlexPath is a two-stage framework for image-based planning that decouples feasibility from preference, learning a task-independent spatial prior then adapting it via differentiable path shape objectives without relearning structure. It enables flexible planning beyond shortest-path objectives.

entry.title: A Large Scale Open-Source Image and Video Dataset for Robust Wildfire Detection and Classification

author.name: Emadeldeen Hamdan, Yingyi Luo, B. Ugur Toreyin, Erdem Koyuncu, Adam J. Watts, Ugur Gudukbay, Ahmet Enis Cetin

entry.summary: GWFP is a large-scale open-source image and video dataset for wildfire and smoke detection, featuring geographically diverse scenes, NIR imagery, embers, and challenging negatives. It benchmarks CNN and transformer architectures across in-domain and cross-dataset settings.

entry.title: Efficient RWKV-based Representation Learning for 3D Point Clouds

author.name: Yun Liu, Xuefeng Yan, Liangliang Nan, Xianzhi Li, Peng Li, Zhe Zhu, Honghua Chen, Mingqiang Wei

entry.summary: P-RWKV adapts the linear-complexity RWKV model to 3D point clouds with a Local Perception Expansion and Spatial Context Enhancement to capture local geometry and spatial dependencies efficiently. It offers an efficient alternative to Transformer self-attention for point cloud representation.

entry.title: Globally Localizing Lunar Rover in Pixels via Graph Alignment

author.name: Mao Chen, Xu Yang, Chuankai Liu, Xiangkai Zhang, Xiaoxue Wang, Zheng Bo, Zuoyu Zhang, Zhiyong Liu

entry.summary: WARG (Warped Alignment of Reprojected Graphs) provides drift-free global lunar rover localization by matching rover-view and satellite-view imagery via unified graph learning and reprojected graph matching. It addresses lunar-specific challenges like entity entanglement and sim-to-real shift.

entry.title: DD-INR: Dynamics-Driven Implicit Neural Representation for Accelerated Whole-Brain Functional MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Qiaoxin Li (MIND), Caini Pan (NEUROSPIN, MIND), Pierre-Antoine Comby (MIND, BAOBAB), Chaithya Giliyar (MIND), Philippe Ciuciu (MIND)

entry.summary: DD-INR is a dynamics-driven implicit neural representation framework for accelerated whole-brain functional MRI reconstruction that exploits incoherent time-varying sampling and a tailored spatiotemporal prior. It recovers small task-evoked BOLD signals better than traditional anatomical reconstruction methods.

entry.title: Lip Forcing: Few-Step Autoregressive Diffusion for Real-time Lip Synchronization

author.name: Paul Hyunbin Cho (KAIST AI), Jinhyuk Jang (KAIST AI), SeokYoung Lee (KAIST AI), Joungbin Lee (KAIST AI), Siyoon Jin (KAIST AI), Heeseong Shin (KAIST AI), Jung Yi (KAIST AI), Yunjin Park (AIPARK), Chulmin Park (AIPARK), Seungryong Kim (KAIST AI)

entry.summary: Presents Lip Forcing, claimed first autoregressive diffusion method for video-to-video lip synchronization, distilling a 14B bidirectional teacher into causal students that generate chunks in two denoising steps for real-time use. Analyzes a CFG fidelity-sync tradeoff.

entry.title: MARCH: Model-Assisted Reinforcement Learning for the Perceptive Control of Humanoids over Sparse Footholds

author.name: Codrin Crismariu, Ryan K. Cosner

entry.summary: Proposes MARCH, a model-assisted RL framework for perceptive humanoid locomotion over sparse footholds, generating safe reference trajectories, training a Lyapunov-guided privileged teacher, then distilling to a vision-based student. Combines model-based precision with model-free robustness.

entry.title: AllDayNav: Lifelong Navigation via Real-World Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hang Yin, Yinan Liang, Jiazhao Zhang, Jiahang Liu, Minghan Li, Zhizheng Zhang, He Wang

entry.summary: Proposes AllDayNav, a lifelong self-learning navigation framework using real-world reinforcement learning that implicitly encodes scene dynamics into a billion-parameter model with a self-evolving multimodal memory generating its own instructions, goals, and rewards. Targets lifelong navigation in dynamic environments.

entry.title: HIPIF: Hierarchical Planning and Information Folding for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Learning

author.name: Juncheng Diao, Zhicong Lu, Peiguang Li, Yongwei Zhou, Changyuan Tian, Qingbin Li, Rongxiang Weng, Jingang Wang, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: Introduces HIPIF, combining hierarchical planning with information folding (subgoal decomposition and progress summarization) to address long-context interference in long-horizon LLM agents. Aims to preserve global task state tracking as histories grow.

entry.title: AutoPDE: Reliable Agentic PDE Solving via Explicitly Represented Solver Strategies

author.name: Huanshuo Dong, Keyao Zhang, Hong Wang, Zhezheng Hao, Zhiwei Zhuang, Ziyan Liu, Jiacong Wang, Gengyuan Liu, Xin Jin

entry.summary: Presents AutoPDE, an agentic PDE-solving system that explicitly represents numerical solver strategies (discretization, stabilization, solver configuration) rather than leaving them implicit in code. Routes feedback from failed solves to strategy revision instead of just code edits.

entry.title: Role-Agent: Bootstrapping LLM Agents via Dual-Role Evolution

author.name: Xucong Wang, Ziyu Ma, Shidong Yang, Tongwen Huang, Pengkun Wang, Yong Wang, Xiangxiang Chu

entry.summary: Introduces Role-Agent, using a single LLM as both agent and environment for bootstrapped co-evolution via World-In-Agent (predicting future states for process rewards) and Agent-In-World components. Aims to overcome inefficient feedback and static training environments.

entry.title: Superficial Beliefs in LLM Decision-Making

author.name: Gabriel Freedman, Francesca Toni

entry.summary: Examines whether LLM choices reflect systematic underlying decision structures or mere rationale imitation, fitting behavioral models to choices and comparing inferred drivers with self-reported and judge-recovered ones. Finds self-reports recover behavioral drivers only partially, suggesting superficial beliefs.

entry.title: Co-GLANCE: Uncertainty-Aware Active Perception for Heterogeneous Robot Teaming

author.name: Michal P. Podolinsky, Neel P. Bhatt, Pranay Samineni, Rohan Siva, Christian Ellis, Ufuk Topcu

entry.summary: Introduces Co-GLANCE, a real-time onboard perception and decision system for heterogeneous robot teams that resolves perceptual uncertainty from occlusions via scene-contextual reasoning and capability-aware robot allocation. It addresses the computational and calibration limits of VLMs for onboard inference.

entry.title: Learning Where to Simulate: Generative Active Sampling for Online PDE Surrogate Training

author.name: Pierre Cesar (DATAMOVE), Sofya Dymchenko (DATAMOVE), Abhishek Purandare (DATAMOVE), Bruno Raffin (DATAMOVE)

entry.summary: Introduces Online Generative Active Sampling, which couples PDE solver data generation with surrogate training so solver parameters are steered on-the-fly toward configurations with challenging dynamics. It addresses under-representation of hard trajectories under uniform sampling.

entry.title: FedSteer: Taming Extreme Gradient Staleness in Federated Learning with Corrective Projections and Caching

author.name: Haoran Zhang, Cain\~a Figueiredo Pereira, Marie Siew, Xutong Liu, Carlee Joe-Wong, Rachid El-Azouzi

entry.summary: Proposes FedSteer, which constructs a gradient subspace from a cache of recent client gradients to correct extreme gradient staleness from skewed client participation in federated learning. It projects active clients' gradients onto this subspace and reuses coordinates for inactive clients to stabilize training.

entry.title: Agentic Hybrid RAG for Evidence-Grounded Muon Collider Analysis

author.name: Ruobing Jiang, Dawei Fu, Cheng Jiang, Tianyi Yang, Zijian Wang, Youpeng Wu, Yong Ban, Yajun Mao, Qiang Li

entry.summary: This paper presents an agentic hybrid retrieval-augmented generation framework for evidence-grounded muon collider physics analysis, integrating agentic reasoning with hybrid retrieval over heterogeneous HEP literature. It aims to preserve retrieval precision while enabling agent-assisted scientific question answering.

entry.title: Dep-LLM: Training-Free Depression Diagnosis via Evidence-Guided Structured Multi-factor with Reliable LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yiqing Lyu, Xianbing Zhao, Buzhou Tang, Ronghuan Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces Dep-LLM, a training-free depression detection framework using frozen LLMs with evidence-guided structured multi-factor reasoning that mirrors psychiatrist workflows. Addresses sparse clues in long interviews and label scarcity without fine-tuning.

entry.title: What Do Deepfake Speech Detectors Actually Hear?

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch Stan\v{e}k, Veronika Jirmusov\'a, Anton Firc, Kamil Malinka, Jakub Re\v{s}, Martin Pere\v{s}\'ini

entry.summary: Proposes an audio-native explainability pipeline using Integrated Gradients on time-aligned self-supervised representations to localize decision evidence in deepfake speech detectors. Shows three WavLM-based detectors rely on different cues despite similar performance.

entry.title: Streaming Knowledge Compilation: Proactive Materiality-Scored Pinning for Time-Evolving LLM Wikis

author.name: Juan M. Huerta

entry.summary: Formalizes Streaming Knowledge Compilation: maintaining a compiled LLM wiki (pre-filled KV caches) under a document stream and fixed token budget to minimize regret against an offline oracle. Introduces a materiality signal for proactive pinning and proves an O(sqrt(T log K)) regret bound.

entry.title: Hasse Diagrams for Attention: A Partial Order Framework for Designing Transformer Masks

author.name: Chentao Li, Han Guo

entry.summary: Develops a formal partial-order framework showing that deep transformer information flow under arbitrary attention masks converges to a Hasse diagram, recasting parallel-task design as finding a minimal common supergraph. It provides systematic theory for the previously ad hoc design of attention masks.

entry.title: PhysMetrics.Weather: An Evaluation Framework for Physical Consistency in ML Weather Models

author.name: Emma Kasteleyn, Timo Maier, Axel Lauer, Veronika Eyring, Pierre Gentine, Ana Lucic

entry.summary: Introduces PhysMetrics.Weather, an evaluation framework assessing the physical realism of ML weather prediction models across conservation, spectral, and dynamical metrics rather than only pixel-wise RMSE. It guides development of physics-informed architectures and operational reliability assessment.

entry.title: Multi-task LLMs for Bug Classification: Efficient Inference with Auxiliary Decoding Heads

author.name: Nikolai Rozanov

entry.summary: This work introduces a lightweight line-level bug localization method for LLM-generated code using auxiliary decoding heads and a token alignment algorithm. It addresses the cost and granularity limitations of existing bug localization techniques.

entry.title: Secure Aggregation with Top-K Sparsification in Decentralized Federated Learning

author.name: Hengxuan Tang, Jinbao Zhu, Xiaohu Tang

entry.summary: This paper studies information-theoretic secure aggregation with top-K gradient sparsification in decentralized federated learning, addressing the challenge that top-K entries selected by each user are unpredictable and vary across users. It reduces communication cost while preserving privacy and model accuracy.

entry.title: Non-linear mechanical field reconstruction coupling recurrent neural networks with physics-informed graph neural networks

author.name: Manuel Ricardo Guevara Garban, Yves Chemisky, \'Etienne Pruli\`ere, Micha\"el Cl\'ement, Martin Abendroth, Bj\"orn Kiefer

entry.summary: This work proposes a coupled LSTM-GNN framework for reconstructing local stress fields in heterogeneous microstructures under non-linear history-dependent loading. The LSTM encodes path-dependent constitutive response while a physics-informed GNN reconstructs spatially-resolved stress fields, with a divergence-based equilibrium penalty.

entry.title: Do Transformers Actually Help Intrusion Detection? A Temporal Sequence Evaluation on CIC-IDS2017

author.name: Zach Moczkodan (Royal Military College of Canada, Kingston, Canada), Hany Ragab (Royal Military College of Canada, Kingston, Canada)

entry.summary: This paper critically evaluates whether transformer and recurrent architectures genuinely help network intrusion detection on CIC-IDS2017, finding many prior studies fail to supply genuine sequence inputs or evaluate under leakage-free conditions. It benchmarks nine architectures under controlled splits.

entry.title: Small Data, Big Noise: Adversarial Training for Robust Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Eitan Cohen, Idan Simai, Uri Shaham

entry.summary: SDBN is a unified framework integrating adversarial training into parameter-efficient fine-tuning to improve robustness and generalization on limited noisy data. It includes variants using character-level edits with gradient selection and LLM-generated variants for discrete uncertainty sets.

entry.title: Recovering the Zipfian Distribution in Unsupervised Term Discovery

author.name: Danel Slabbert, Simon Malan, Herman Kamper

entry.summary: This work revisits graph-based clustering (Leiden algorithm) for unsupervised term discovery, showing it recovers more Zipf-like lexicon distributions than K-means and related center-based methods. It outperforms baselines on word- and syllable-level discovery across three languages.

entry.title: FoA-SR: Faithful or Aesthetic? Profile-Aware Preference Optimization for Real-World Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Amjad Mahdi Alqarni, Peizhong Ju

entry.summary: FoA-SR proposes profile-aware preference optimization for real-world image super-resolution, distinguishing faithful restoration (consistency, hallucination suppression) from aesthetic restoration (visually pleasing detail). It builds on a FLUX.2-based SR adapter with preference tuning.

entry.title: Audio-Visual Exchange-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Audio-Visual Captioning

author.name: Zihan Meng, Dexiang Hong, Weidong Chen, Ziyu Zhou, Bo Hu, Zhendong Mao

entry.summary: AVEX-Prune is an RL-based audio-visual dynamic token pruning method for efficient captioning that uses a token exchange strategy to select valuable tokens, particularly high-confusing tokens near decision boundaries. It avoids hard-threshold pruning to reduce quadratic prefill costs.

entry.title: PrismAvatar: Pseudo-Multiview Reconstruction and Subpixel Prism Rendering for Real-Time Stereoscopic Communication

author.name: Chufeng Fang, Dongdong Teng, Lilin Liu

entry.summary: PrismAvatar is a Gaussian head-avatar system that connects monocular avatar capture with subpixel-encoded glasses-free lenticular display for real-time autostereoscopic communication, using natural head turns as pseudo-multiview supervision. It enables immersive telepresence without specialized rigs.

entry.title: P3D-Bench: Benchmarking MLLMs for Parametric 3D Generation and Structural Reasoning

author.name: Yikang Yang, Zhanpeng Hu, Youtian Lin, Mengqi Zhou, Jingxi Xu, Feihu Zhang, Jiaheng Liu, Yao Yao

entry.summary: Introduces P3D-Bench, a benchmark evaluating MLLMs on parametric 3D generation via code, assessing geometric precision, semantic alignment, and assembly consistency. Probes structural reasoning rather than just appearance.

entry.title: Efficient-WAM: A 1B-Parameter World-Action Model with Low-Cost Future Imagination

author.name: Jiajun Li, Tiecheng Guo, Yifan Ye, Rongyu Zhang, Xiaowei Chi, Qianpu Sun, Ying Li, Yunfan Lou, Yan Huang, Zhihe Lu, Meng Guo, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Efficient-WAM, a 1B-parameter world-action model that reduces future-imagination cost via a compact video expert transferred from WAN-2.2-5B, token-sparse latents, and asymmetric video-action denoising. Targets real-time robot deployment.

entry.title: VeriSpace: Spatially Grounded Action Verification for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Guiyu Zhao, Longteng Guo, Junyou Zhu, Jun Fu, Yanghong Mei, Bin Cao, Jie Jiang, Xingjian He, Jing Liu

entry.summary: Presents VeriSpace, a 3D-aware action verifier for test-time action selection in VLA models that proposes and evaluates multiple candidate actions for geometric correctness and task progress before execution. Improves reliability beyond one-shot prediction.

entry.title: SAFE-Pruner: Semantic Attention-Guided Future-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

author.name: Shilin Ma, Chubin Zhang, Changyuan Wang, Yuji Wang, Yue Wu, Zixuan Wang, Jingqi Tian, Zheng Zhu, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: Proposes SAFE-Pruner, a plug-and-play visual token pruning framework for VLA models that incorporates future-layer attention cues and exploits semantic attention consistency across execution steps to avoid discarding deep-layer-needed information. Accelerates real-time robotic inference.

entry.title: Three Labs With a Plan and A Memorandum

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's roundup covers the launch of Claude Fable 5 (the publicly distributable variant of Anthropic's Mythos-class model) alongside three governance developments: a US administration AI memorandum, an OpenAI plan for ensuring AGI benefits everyone, and renewed calls for international coordination to enable slowing AI development. It situates lab-level safety plans against an emerging policy backdrop. The piece is commentary and synthesis rather than original research.

entry.title: From Senses to Decisions: The Information Flow of Auditory and Visual Perception in Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Wish Suharitdamrong, Muhammad Awais, Xiatian Zhu, Sara Atito

entry.summary: Investigates how audio and visual tokens flow through multimodal LLMs to shape predictions, tracing routing and integration across video and interleaved input configurations. Provides interpretability insights into audio-visual information pathways.

entry.title: ActiveMem: Distributed Active Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yunhan Jiang, Wenbin Duan, Shasha Guo, Liang Pang, Xiaoqian Sun, Huawei Shen

entry.summary: Proposes ActiveMem, a distributed active memory architecture inspired by the prefrontal cortex-hippocampus complementarity to balance the tradeoff between context overload and information loss in long-horizon LLM reasoning. Decentralizes memory organization rather than using a single context.

entry.title: Moonshine: An Autonomous Mathematical Research Agent Centered on Conjecture Generation

author.name: Xiaoyang Chen, Xiang Jiang

entry.summary: Presents Moonshine, an autonomous mathematical research agent centered on conjecture generation rather than single-proof solving, building extensible theoretical frameworks. Demonstrated by transferring the Jacobian conjecture logic to neural network injectivity (Neural Jacobian Conjecture).

entry.title: Bellman-Taylor Score Decoding for Markov Decision Processes with State-Dependent Feasible Action Sets

author.name: Yi Chen (Lucy), Rushuai Yang (Lucy), Qiang Chen (Lucy), Dongyan (Lucy), Huo

entry.summary: Proposes Bellman-Taylor score decoding for MDPs with state-dependent implicit feasible action sets, moving policy learning to a Euclidean score space and enforcing feasibility via an action decoder. Enables standard deep RL without differentiating through the decoder.

entry.title: The Role of Feedback Alignment in Self-Distillation

author.name: Semih Kara, O\u{g}uzhan Ersoy

entry.summary: Studies context design for self-distillation, where a solver is trained to retain improvements from a frozen critic without the context present, comparing binary reward, reference solution, and step-by-step critique conditions. Investigates how the self-teacher's context shapes what is learned.

entry.title: Tractogram foundation model

author.name: Guikun Chen, Yuqian Chen, Yijie Li, Yogesh Rathi, Nikos Makris, Fan Zhang, Wenguan Wang, Lauren J. O'Donnell

entry.summary: Presents a tractogram foundation model that learns reusable representations from unordered 3D white-matter streamlines from diffusion MRI, unifying streamline classification and subject-level prediction. It aims to connect local streamline geometry with whole-brain anatomical organization.

entry.title: Trainable Smooth-Rotation Transforms with Learned Channel Scales for LLM Quantization

author.name: Patrik Czak\'o, G\'abor Kert\'esz, S\'andor Sz\'en\'asi

entry.summary: Introduces trainable smooth-rotation transforms with learned channel scales for LLM post-training quantization, using quantile-robust scaling to reduce over-migration in outlier-dominated activation channels. It reports error improvements over SmoothRot baselines on LLaMA-3.2-1B under W4A4.

entry.title: RKSC: Reasoning-Aware KV Cache Sharing and Confident Early Exit for Multi-Step LLM Inference

author.name: Anirudh Sekar

entry.summary: Introduces RKSC, a training-free inference framework that shares prefix KV cache across semantically similar reasoning branches via hidden-state similarity and applies confidence-gated early exit to skip or shorten verification passes. It targets redundancy in multi-branch reasoning pipelines.

entry.title: Making Time Editable in Video Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Konstantin Kuklev, Viacheslav Vasilev, Alexander Kunitsyn, Andrei Ivaniuta, Denis Dimitrov

entry.summary: This work adds explicit time-editing control to pretrained video diffusion transformers, enabling control over motion speed and temporal structure via a lightweight temporal module. It preserves the original generative prior while expanding controllable dynamics without redesigning the backbone.

entry.title: Minimum Distortion Quantization with Specified Output Distribution

author.name: Aolin Xu

entry.summary: This paper derives the optimal quantizer of a real-valued random variable that produces a specified output distribution while minimizing mean squared estimation error. It shows the optimal quantizer takes a closed form involving an optimal permutation and CDF mappings, with simple forms under uniform distributions.

entry.title: MoE Enhanced Federated Learning for Spatiotemporal Prediction

author.name: Zhehao Dai, Xiao Han, Zhaolin Deng, Zijian Zhang, Xiangyu Zhao, Guojiang Shen, Xiangjie Kong

entry.summary: MoE-FedTP is a personalized federated learning framework for cross-city spatiotemporal traffic prediction using lightweight Mixture-of-Experts networks. It enables data-rich cities to assist data-scarce ones while addressing pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity and privacy concerns of centralized approaches.

entry.title: Machine Learning Methods for Studying Latent Neural Activity Dynamics

author.name: Shufeng Kong, Fumei Deng, Xinyi Dong, Caihua Liu, Weiwei Chen, Yingheng Wang, Daniel Cao, Azahara Oliva, Antonio Fernandez-Ruiz, Carla Gomes

entry.summary: This survey traces the development of latent variable models for decoding neural population dynamics, from state-space models to deep generative models, organized into single-region dynamics, multi-region communication, and related domains. It serves the growing demand for ML tools to interpret large-scale brain recordings.

entry.title: Unifying Data, Memory, and Compute Efficiency in LLM training: A Survey

author.name: Vanessa Schmidt, Huy Hoang Nguyen, C\'edric Jung, Shirin Salehi, Anke Schmeink

entry.summary: A survey adopting a constraint-centric view of LLM training efficiency across three coupled bottlenecks: data efficiency, memory efficiency, and compute budget awareness. Organizes recent methods around these interacting limits.

entry.title: Ethical and Technical Limits of Deepfake Speech Datasets

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch Stan\v{e}k, Eva Trnovsk\'a, Kamil Malinka, Anton Firc

entry.summary: A dataset-level audit of 39 deepfake speech datasets examining accessibility, documentation, demographic/language coverage, and source quality. Finds fairness assessment largely infeasible due to missing demographic metadata.

entry.title: Towards Autonomous Accelerator Design: FPGA Accelerator Generation with SECDA

author.name: Vinamra Sharma, Xingjian Fu, Jude Haris, Jos\'e Cano

entry.summary: Presents SECDA-DSE, integrating LLMs into the SECDA hardware-software co-design ecosystem to guide automated design space exploration for FPGA AI accelerators. Combines a structured DSE explorer with LLM-driven candidate architecture generation.

entry.title: SpenseGPT: Practical One-shot Pruning Enabling Sparse and Dense GEMMs for LLM Inference

author.name: Jaeseong Lee, Seung-won Hwang, Samyam Rajbhandari

entry.summary: Proposes Spense (SpenseGPT), a hybrid sparse-dense weight format that splits each matrix into a 2:4 sparse region and a dense region to relax the strict 50% sparsity constraint while remaining compatible with existing high-performance GEMM libraries. It enables practical one-shot pruning without custom compilers or activation expansion.

entry.title: Representation-Aware Advantage Estimation: Your Reward Model Provides More Than A Scalar Output

author.name: Guozheng Li, Xiyan Fu, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: Introduces representation-aware advantage estimation for RLHF, exploiting reward-model hidden states rather than only scalar rewards by treating each sampled response group as a graph and computing advantages via graph propagation (GraphAE). It captures fine-grained preference information lost in scalar rewards.

entry.title: How Does Reasoning Flow? Tracing Attention-Induced Information Flow for Targeted RL in LLMs

author.name: Zhichen Dong, Yang Li, Yuhan Sun, Weixun Wang, Yijia Luo, Zinian Peng, Taiheng Ye, Chao Yang, Wenbo Su, Yu Cheng, Bo Zheng, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: Proposes FlowTracer, an RL framework that traces answer-targeted reasoning flow on an attention-induced directed acyclic graph to assign token-level credit based on global information-propagation structure rather than point-wise heuristics. It aims to distinguish decisive reasoning steps from formatting and filler tokens.

entry.title: Decision-Calibrated Conformal Uncertainty for Pacing Decisions in Streaming Advertising

author.name: Prashant Shekhar, Caroline Howard

entry.summary: This work develops a decision-calibrated conformal framework for pacing decisions in streaming advertising, measuring forecast error by its largest impact on deployable policies rather than generic residuals. It provides finite-sample coverage guarantees via split conformal calibration.

entry.title: Near-Exponential Convergence Rates for kNN Classification based on Boltzmann Margin

author.name: Luyuan Yang, Shayan Shafaei, Chao Lan

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Boltzmann margin condition, which bridges the gap between the weak Tsybakov margin and strong Massart margin for classifier convergence analysis. It establishes the first near-exponential convergence rates for kNN classification.

entry.title: TabClaw: An Interactive and Self-Evolving Agent for Spreadsheet Manipulation and Table Reasoning

author.name: Mingyue Cheng, Shuo Yu, Daoyu Wang, Qingchuan Li, Xiaoyu Tao, Qingyang Mao, Yitong Zhou, Qi Liu

entry.summary: TabClaw is an open-source interactive AI agent for spreadsheet manipulation and table reasoning that clarifies ambiguous intent, exposes editable execution plans, and uses ReAct-style tool calling. It addresses transparency, multi-table comparison, and preference adaptation gaps in existing LLM agents.

entry.title: ArabiGEE: A Hierarchical Taxonomy for Arabic Grammatical Error Explanation

author.name: Khaled Elhady, Omar Kallas, Nizar Habash, Bashar Alhafni

entry.summary: ArabiGEE presents the first hierarchical taxonomy for Arabic grammatical error explanation, organizing errors across orthographic, morphological, syntactic, and lexical dimensions with 27 error types and hundreds of correction and explanation types. It supports structured evaluation of LLMs on Arabic grammar tasks.

entry.title: Enhancing Multilingual LLM-based ASR with Mixture of Experts and Dynamic Downsampling

author.name: Guodong Lin, Ziqi Chen, Yuxiang Fu, Ke Li, Wei-Qiang Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a projector-based LLM-ASR framework using a Mixture of Experts architecture and a Continuous Integrate-and-Fire mechanism for dynamic downsampling to improve multilingual speech recognition. It reports gains over strong baselines.

entry.title: iSAGE: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation via Sparse Point Supervision

author.name: Osmar Luiz Ferreira de Carvalho, Osmar Abilio de Carvalho Junior, Anesmar Olino de Albuquerque, Daniel Guerreiro e Silva

entry.summary: iSAGE is a human-in-the-loop framework for remote sensing semantic segmentation that hypothesizes expert clicks targeting confident model errors are most informative, providing signal external to the model's predictive distribution. It reduces costly pixel-level annotation needs.

entry.title: STEDiff: Strengthening Text Embedding for Text-to-Image Alignment in Diffusion Model

author.name: Hailan Zhang, Haipeng Liu, Bo Fu, Yang Wang

entry.summary: STEDiff is a training-free method to strengthen text embeddings for text-to-image alignment in diffusion models, leveraging the end-of-text token to enhance semantic representations and improve object and attribute binding. It avoids expensive fine-tuning or layout priors.

entry.title: Spatially Selective Self-Training for Unsupervised Building Change Detection

author.name: Wafaa I. M. Hussin, Zhi Lu, Anas M. I. Mohammed, Xiang Zhou, Ratiba A. H. Abubaker, Zhenming Peng

entry.summary: This work proposes spatially selective self-training for unsupervised building change detection, learning a task-specific detector from unlabeled bi-temporal images rather than directly using noisy temporal discrepancies. It addresses the gap between generic discrepancies and building-defined structural changes.

entry.title: Quo Vadis, Visual In-Context Learning? A Unified Benchmark Across Domains and Tasks

author.name: Pradnya Halady, Jiale Wei, Zdravko Marinov, Alexander Jaus, Simon Rei{\ss}

entry.summary: Introduces VIBE, a broad visual in-context learning benchmark spanning diverse imaging domains and 14 datasets, stress-testing six models on genuine task/distribution shifts. Reveals gaps in current models' adaptation abilities.

entry.title: Hand-centric Human-to-Robot Trajectory Transfer from Video Demonstrations via Open-World Contact Localization

author.name: Yitian Shi, Di Wen, Zhengqi Han, Zicheng Guo, Yu Hu, Edgar Welte, Kunyu Peng, Rainer Stiefelhagen, Rania Rayyes

entry.summary: Presents HOWTransfer, a hand-centric framework distilling human video demonstrations into contact-aware robot trajectories via open-world contact localization, recovering 3D hand motion and contact intervals without object-specific tracking. Addresses noisy, cross-embodiment learning from video.

entry.title: Generation of Diverse and Functional Robot Designs using Superquadrics Parametrisation and Quality-Diversity

author.name: Leni Le Goff, Simon Smith, Emma Hart

entry.summary: Studies the vulnerability of vision-language-action models to realistic joint-level physical faults (actuator degradation, friction, collision damage) that alter the action-to-motion interface. Demonstrates VLA policies fail under perturbed embodiment dynamics.

entry.title: Trace2Policy: From Expert Behavior Traces to Self-Evolving Decision Agents

author.name: Junli Zha, Jinbo Wang, Chao Zhou, Xiang Song

entry.summary: Presents Trace2Policy with EISR, a mechanism that recovers tacit enterprise decision rules from expert behavior traces by iterative error-driven refinement of a human-readable rule document. Finds rule quality dominates model capability for compliance-sensitive tasks.

entry.title: Infini Memory: Maintainable Topic Documents for Long-Term LLM Agent Memory

author.name: Suozhao Ji, Baodong Wu, Zehao Wang, Lei Xia, Qingping Li, Ruisong Wang, Wenbo Ding, Zhenhua Zhu, Boxun Li, Guohao Dai, Yu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Infini Memory, a maintainable text-based persistent memory architecture that organizes agent memory as topic-structured documents to support evidence aggregation, fact revision, and cross-session maintenance. Uses a staging buffer and periodic consolidation with agentic retrieval.

entry.title: Evaluating Research-Level Math Proofs via Strict Step-Level Verification

author.name: Yifeng Sun

entry.summary: Proposes strict step-level verification for research-level math proofs to combat context poisoning, maintaining per-step context and constraining theorem sources. Evaluated on an adversarial diagnostic suite from the FirstProof challenge.

entry.title: Provenance Tracking in AI Compilers through the Lens of Coalgebra

author.name: Zilu Tian, Liying Liu

entry.summary: Presents a coalgebraic, observational-semantics approach to provenance tracking in AI compilers, reasoning about tensor/operator provenance via observable computational actions rather than propagating identifiers through passes. Aims for lightweight, non-invasive tracking under non-injective graph rewrites.

entry.title: Uncertainty-aware Multi-fidelity Closure via Conditional Normalizing Flows

author.name: Jice Zeng, Shady E. Ahmed, David Barajas-Solano, Panos Stinis

entry.summary: Formulates reduced-order model closure as a multi-fidelity learning problem and uses conditional normalizing flows to learn a probabilistic mapping from low-fidelity to high-fidelity coefficients with uncertainty quantification. Targets truncation errors and unresolved-scale interactions in multiscale systems.

entry.title: Ambiguous Strategic Classification

author.name: Ivri Hikri, Nir Rosenfeld

entry.summary: Duplicate id placeholder.

entry.title: Compositional Generative Modeling from Decentralized Data

author.name: Mashrur M. Morshed, Vishnu Naresh Boddeti

entry.summary: Introduces Decentralized Compositional Flow Matching (DCFM), enabling generative models to learn novel factor combinations implied by siloed data across peers without sharing raw data. It enforces structural constraints across the global set of generative factors to compose combinations no single silo supports.

entry.title: Rank Collapse, Fixed Points, and the Renormalization Group Structure of MLP Residual Networks

author.name: Parviz Haggi-Mani, Irina Rish

entry.summary: Tests the long-noted analogy between deep network forward passes and renormalization-group flows by defining a measurable RG order parameter and validating quantitative predictions on MLP residual stacks trained on synthetic Markov-chain sequences. It moves the analogy from qualitative to empirical.

entry.title: From Observation to Intervention: A Causal Audit of Expert Importance in Mixture-of-Experts Models

author.name: Leonard Engmann, Christian Medeiros Adriano, Holger Giese

entry.summary: Conducts a causal audit of Mixture-of-Experts pruning, testing whether routing statistics (utilization, activation norms, routing weights) treated as predictors of expert removability actually hold up under token-level interventions across three high-redundancy MoE models. It frames the issue as conflating associational with interventional evidence.

entry.title: Robust Active Learning for Few-Shot Example Selection in Text-to-SQL

author.name: Arash Pourhabib

entry.summary: This work formalizes active selection of few-shot examples for text-to-SQL as a constrained experimental design problem over a semantic embedding manifold, accounting for heteroscedastic annotation reliability and diversity constraints. It aims to reduce expensive expert annotation costs.

entry.title: $k$-Nearest Neighbors in Gromov--Wasserstein Space

author.name: Kaitlyn Hohmeier, Nicolas Fraiman, Caroline Moosmueller

entry.summary: This work implements k-nearest neighbors classification using Gromov-Wasserstein and fused Gromov-Wasserstein distances for comparing metric measure spaces and graphs of different sizes. It proves universal consistency of the GW-kNN classifier on equivalence classes of metric measure spaces.

entry.title: ClusBench: The Clustering Benchmark Data Resource You've All Been Waiting For (?)

author.name: David P. Hofmeyr

entry.summary: ClusBench produces and curates nearly 3000 synthetic datasets derived from over 200 real-world datasets by fitting flexible nonparametric distributions, retaining real-world nuance while enabling large-scale clustering benchmarking. It includes an accompanying R package.

entry.title: Range Penalization: Theoretical Insights with Applications in Federated Learning

author.name: Yiyuan She, Zhaojun Hu, Yifan Sun

entry.summary: This paper introduces range regularization for federated learning with linear systematic components, identifying shared-weight features and adaptively clustering personalized feature weights at extreme values (polar clustering). It develops new proof techniques for nonasymptotic analysis given the seminorm and non-decomposable nature of the regularizer.

entry.title: AgenticNav: Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation as a Tool-Calling Harness

author.name: Yijian Li, Changze Li, Hantian Shi, Jiaying Luo, Jiyuan Cai, Ming Yang, Tong Qin

entry.summary: Introduces AgenticNav, a zero-shot vision-and-language navigation harness that reframes VLN-CE as a tool-calling interface exposing action, depth, and memory tools to a VLM, avoiding learned waypoint predictors and bloated histories. Better leverages depth and preserves the zero-shot setting.

entry.title: Less Context, Better Agents: Efficient Context Engineering for Long-Horizon Tool-Using LLM Agents

author.name: Abhilasha Lodha, Mahsa Pahlavikhah Varnosfaderani, Abir Chakraborty, Abhinav Mithal

entry.summary: Studies context engineering for long-horizon tool-using LLM agents in enterprise workflows, evaluating context pruning and summarization to combat context overflow and stale-state errors. Tested on expense itemization tasks in Dynamics 365 with GPT-5 configurations.

entry.title: Do VLMs Reason Like Engineers? A Benchmark and a Stage-wise Evaluation

author.name: Syed Wasiq, Syed Mohamad Tawseeq, Yashwant Pravinrao Bangde, Debaditya Roy

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark and stage-wise evaluation to test whether VLMs reason like engineers, requiring interpretation of technical diagrams, selection of physical principles, and physically consistent multi-step reasoning. Goes beyond final-answer scoring to assess intermediate reasoning.

entry.title: Bypassing Copyright Protection in Diffusion-based Customization via Two-Stage Latent Feature Optimization

author.name: Ziang Xu, Wenbo Yu, Hongyao Yu, Hao Fang, Jiawei Kong, Bin Chen, Hao Wu, Shu-Tao Xia, Zhiyong Wu

entry.summary: Introduces TS-LFO, a two-stage latent feature optimization attack that bypasses adversarial-perturbation copyright protections in diffusion-based image customization. It exploits how existing defenses primarily disrupt the input-to-latent mapping.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction for Neural Operators: Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification in Physics Simulation

author.name: Michael Chin

entry.summary: Applies split conformal prediction to neural operators like the Fourier Neural Operator for PDE surrogates, providing distribution-free coverage guarantees absent from Monte Carlo Dropout or Deep Ensembles. It targets safety-critical engineering applications such as thermal and battery management.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Motion Planning for Autonomous Driving in Mixed Traffic Environment

author.name: Ming Cheng, Hao Chen, Ziyi Yang, Ziluowen Luo, Senzhang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Uncertainty-Aware Motion Planning for autonomous driving in mixed traffic that incorporates uncertainty in human-intent prediction rather than treating predicted intents as deterministic states. It aims to avoid unsafe decisions arising from behavioral diversity and partial observability.

entry.title: DeRA-MOS: Optimizing Text-to-Music Evaluation via Decoupled Listwise Ranking and Modality Alignment

author.name: Chien-Chun Wang, Hung-Shin Lee, Hsin-Min Wang, Berlin Chen

entry.summary: Proposes DeRA-MOS, a decoupled framework for automatic text-to-music evaluation that uses a batch-aware listwise ranking loss for music impression and a score-anchored modality alignment loss for text alignment, better matching rank-based metrics than point-wise regression. It reduces reliance on costly human mean opinion scores.

entry.title: Bittensor Agent Arenas as a Trajectory Primitive: Distilling a Shopping Agent from ShoppingBench Subnet Traces
