entry.title: Beyond Neural Collapse: Task-Intrinsic Geometry Governs Neural Representations in Modular Arithmetic

author.name: Hu Tan, Kuo Gai, Shihua Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that in modular arithmetic tasks, neural networks deviate from neural collapse and instead compress to a two-dimensional cyclic geometry, explained by layerwise non-uniform training dynamics. Refines understanding of task-intrinsic representation geometry. Contributes to mechanistic understanding of grokking-like phenomena.

entry.title: Stabilizing On-Policy Distillation for MLLM Reasoning with Global Normalization

author.name: Dongze Hao, Zhiwei Jin, Chen Chen, Haonan Lu

entry.summary: Proposes GNDPO to stabilize on-policy distillation for multimodal LLM reasoning by transforming raw KL scores into batch-level relative advantages, mitigating gradient instability from outlier states. Improves over naive token-level distillation. Relevant to MLLM post-training.

entry.title: Distilling Safe LLM Systems via Soft Prompts for On Device Settings

author.name: Motasem Alfarra, Cristina Pinneri, Dana Kianfar, Mohammed Almousa, Christos Louizos

entry.summary: Studies parameter-efficient safety alignment for on-device LLMs, finding that soft prompts combined with distillation outperform alternatives for distilling dual-model guard systems into resource-constrained settings. Enables safe LLMs on edge devices. Relevant to deployable safety.

entry.title: AutoMegaKernel: A Statically-Checked Agent Harness for Self-Retargeting Megakernel Synthesis

author.name: Jaber Jaber, Osama Jaber

entry.summary: AutoMegaKernel compiles HuggingFace Llama-family models into a single persistent CUDA megakernel running the whole forward pass in one launch, with a static schedule-IR validator certifying deadlock- and race-freedom across thousands of adversarial schedules. Systems contribution for safe kernel synthesis. Matters for inference systems.

entry.title: Steer Where It Matters: Token-Level Visual-Sensitivity Steering for LVLMs Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: Ruipeng Zhang, Zhihao Li, C. L. Philip Chen, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes token-level visual-sensitivity steering to reduce hallucinations in large vision-language models, observing that visual conditioning affects token prediction sparsely during decoding rather than uniformly. By targeting steering only at critical tokens and adapting strength, it improves signal-to-noise ratio over fixed-strength activation steering methods.

entry.title: Inverse design of bespoke interatomic potentials via active learning by information-matching

author.name: Yonatan Kurniawan (Department of Physics and Astronomy, Brigham Young University, Provo, UT, USA), Logan D. Williams (Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Livermore, CA, USA), Amit Samanta (Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Livermore, CA, USA), Ilia Nikiforov (Department of Aerospace Engineering and Mechanics, University of Minnesota, Minneapolis, MN, USA), Daniel Schwalbe-Koda (Department of Materials Science and Engineering, University of California, Los Angeles, CA, USA), Mark K. Transtrum (Cross Stream Consulting, Springville, UT, USA), Ellad B. Tadmor (Department of Aerospace Engineering and Mechanics, University of Minnesota, Minneapolis, MN, USA), Vincenzo Lordi (Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Livermore, CA, USA), Vasily V. Bulatov (Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Livermore, CA, USA)

entry.summary: Presents an active learning approach using information-matching to inverse-design bespoke interatomic potentials, selecting training data that provides sufficient parameter-space information for targeted material properties. Combines national-lab and academic expertise to make IP construction more efficient and reliable.

entry.title: Stable and Scalable Probabilistic Numerical Solvers for Stiff and High-Dimensional ODEs

author.name: Nathanael Bosch

entry.summary: Develops probabilistic numerical ODE solvers that are both stable and scalable for stiff, high-dimensional problems, using a matrix-free update with Jacobian-vector products and iterative solvers for linear scaling while retaining stability. Closes a gap where prior methods were either stable but cubic-cost or scalable but unstable.

entry.title: Learning to Solve Generative ODEs Beyond the Linear Span

author.name: Sihyeon Kim, Seunghun Lee, Vikas Singh, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: Identifies that scalar-coefficient solver learning for diffusion/flow ODEs is span-limited, fitting only in-span components of buffered velocity evaluations while leaving out-of-span residuals unreachable. Proposes SpanLift, a lightweight neural solver adding a spatial residual operator to break this bottleneck.

entry.title: Rank Intervals for Leaderboards: A Hierarchical Framework for Model Evaluation

author.name: Bitya Neuhof, Yuval Benjamini

entry.summary: Introduces a hierarchical framework for constructing model rank confidence intervals on multi-task leaderboards, providing statistical guarantees at both task and leaderboard levels via pairwise comparisons. Addresses the neglected uncertainty and cross-task variability obscured by current aggregate rankings.

entry.title: Discovering and decoding latent mean-field structure with variational autoencoders

author.name: Marco Biroli, Max Welling, Vincenzo Vitelli

entry.summary: Establishes a criterion quantifying a variational autoencoder's capacity to faithfully reconstruct the joint distribution of many-body systems, bounding capacity by comparing latent channel rate to bipartite mutual information. Shows successful VAE reconstruction implies the conditionally independent decoder is structurally a mean-field factorization.

entry.title: Fourier Neural Operators with rank-1 lattice points and hyperbolic cross

author.name: Jakob Dilen, Alexander Keller, Frances Y. Kuo, Dirk Nuyens

entry.summary: Improves Fourier Neural Operators by replacing spatial tensor-product grids with rank-1 lattice points and using a second lattice in parametric space, deriving regularity bounds that prove improved generalization. Achieves more accurate, efficient approximations from fewer parameters, spatial points, and training samples.

entry.title: What the Eyes See, the LLMs Miss: Exploiting Human Perception for Adversarial Text Attacks

author.name: Qin Yang, Lu Malloy, Joshua Lee, Xiaohan Chang, Meisam Mohammady, Doowon Kim, Yuan Hong

entry.summary: Introduces Human-Perceptible Adversarial Attacks that embed harmful content via typographic manipulations readable by humans but invisible to tokenized LLM moderation. Exposes a perceptual mismatch in content-moderation defenses.

entry.title: Discovering Functionally Selective Brain Regions with a Deep Topographic Multimodal Model

author.name: Badr AlKhamissi, Johannes Mehrer, Lara Marinov, Ahmed Abdelaal, Abdulkadir Gokce, Martin Schrimpf

entry.summary: Introduces Topo-Omni, a multimodal topographic model where vision, audio, and language share a single contiguous in-silico cortical sheet trained with spatial smoothness, reproducing functionally selective brain regions consistent with human neuroimaging. Bridges deep learning and computational neuroscience.

entry.title: Unlocking Latent Value: Taxonomy-Guided Recovery of High-Performing Data from Low-Tier Web Corpora

author.name: Neeraj Varshney, Sanket Lokegaonkar, Nasser Zalmout, Qingyu Yin, Priyanka Nigam, Bing Yin

entry.summary: Proposes a taxonomy-driven web data curation framework that recovers high-value pretraining content along semantic dimensions like timeliness and cultural specificity missed by composite quality scores. Distills annotations into lightweight models for 50x faster corpus-wide filtering.

entry.title: Forward-Free Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Haotian Sun, Rushi Qiang, Yuqian Zheng, Bo Dai

entry.summary: Proposes FReDA, a forward-free diffusion language model that eliminates hand-designed corruption forward processes by formulating diffusion as recursive distribution refinement. Aligns the process with actual generation errors to improve sample quality.

entry.title: Back on Track: Aligning Rewards and States for Reasoning in Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Yawen Shao, Jie Xiao, Kai Zhu, Yu Liu, Hongchen Luo, Xueyang Fu, Yang Cao, Wei Zhai, Zheng-Jun Zha

entry.summary: Introduces PAPO, a reinforcement learning framework for diffusion LLM reasoning that addresses process-reward and state-trajectory misalignment by aligning rewards to intermediate steps and keeping updates on authentic trajectories. Improves credit assignment and gradient efficiency for dLLM reasoning.

entry.title: Is Text All You Need? Text as a Universal Information Bottleneck for Speech LLMs

author.name: Ming-Hao Hsu, Yuxuan Hu, Shujie Liu, Jinyu Li, Yan Lu, Zhizheng Wu

entry.summary: Proposes Convex Gate, a speech-to-LLM bridge that constrains all speech representations to lie within the LLM input embedding manifold via an architectural convex-hull constraint, balancing transcription accuracy and paralinguistic retention. It addresses drift in continuous speech-to-LLM interfaces.

entry.title: Reasoning without Gold Standards: A Proxy-Judge Theory of Autoformalization

author.name: Lei Xu, Xin Quan, Andr\'e Freitas

entry.summary: Introduces a reference-free proxy-judge framework for autoformalization that replaces gold-standard matching with per-axis property checks organized along structural scopes. It addresses the problem that one informal argument admits many valid formal renderings.

entry.title: Detecting Differences Is Not Understanding Structure: Large Language Models Fail at Graph Isomorphism

author.name: Kumar Thushalika, Sukumar Kishanthan, Asela Hevapathige

entry.summary: Demonstrates that LLMs achieve near-perfect graph isomorphism detection but fail when identical graphs are presented with permuted node labels, revealing they exploit patterns rather than reasoning about abstract structure. It argues permutation invariance is a fundamental requirement that LLMs lack.

entry.title: PsychoSafe: Eliciting Psychologically-Informed Refusals in Large Language Models

author.name: Gianluca Barmina, Federico Torrielli, Sven Harms, Jacob Nielsen, Felix M\"achtle, Stine Lyngs{\o} Beltoft, Peter Schneider-Kamp, Thomas Eisenbarth, Lukas Galke Poech, Anne Lauscher

entry.summary: PsychoSafe is a psychologically-informed refusal framework that reframes refusal as structured supportive communication grounded in evidence-based intervention strategies, built from 8,019 prompt-response pairs across five risk domains. It targets high-risk interactions involving crisis or coercion.

entry.title: Harnessing Streaming Video in the Wild

author.name: Dingyu Yao, Shuhuan Gu, Qingyi Si, Junhao Zhou, Chenxu Yang, Chuanyu Qin, Naibin Gu, Zheng Lin, Weiping Wang, Nan Duan, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: Addresses streaming video understanding for VLMs by constructing a 248K streaming training dataset with a novel training objective for proactive interaction, long-horizon memory, and real-time processing. It targets the gap where existing VLMs excel offline but fail at streaming deployment.

entry.title: Struct-Searcher: Agentic Structural Thinking Advances Multimodal Deep Information Seeking

author.name: Fan Zhang, Vireo Zhang, Shengju Qian, Haoxuan Li, Zheng Lian, Hao Wu, Yuan Gao, Xinyu Geng, Xin Wang, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: Struct-Searcher is a structural agentic workflow for multimodal deep information seeking grounded in belief revision theory, maintaining an evolving multimodal structural graph to handle contradictory information across modalities. It moves beyond linear evidence accumulation models.

entry.title: One Stone, Three Birds: Self-adaptive Optimal Transport for Multi-VLM Selection, Adaptation, and Ensembling

author.name: Qiyu Xu, Zhanxuan Hu, Yu Duan, Yonghang Tai, Huafeng Li, Quanxue Gao, Xiangyong Cao

entry.summary: This work jointly tackles VLM selection, target adaptation, and ensembling using self-adaptive optimal transport when no target labels are available across multiple candidate models. It reframes single-backbone deployment assumptions for cross-domain settings.

entry.title: HDSL: A Hierarchical Domain-Specific Language for Structured 3D Indoor Scene Generation and Localized Editing with LLM Agents

author.name: Letian Li, Chao Shen, Shuzhao Xie, Chenghao Gu, ZhengXiao He, Yu Meng, Xin Yang, Wenyuan Jiang, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: HDSL is a hierarchical XML/CSS-style domain-specific language for structured 3D indoor scene generation and localized editing with LLM agents, representing rooms, regions, and objects as a tree with local coordinates. It frames the task as structured program generation and local program repair.

entry.title: EgoPriMo: Egocentric Motion Generation for Interactive Humanoid Control

author.name: Haoyang Ge, Peng Ren, Yukun Shi, Cong Huang, Kun Li, Kai Chen

entry.summary: EgoPriMo learns egocentric motion priors for humanoid robots from human demonstrations, using a triple-stream DiT to reconstruct, generate, and forecast SMPL full-body motion conditioned on text and egocentric observations. Language serves as high-level control rather than full specification.

entry.title: iMaC: Translating Actions into Motion and Contact Images for Embodied World Models

author.name: Zhenyu Wu, Xiuwei Xu, Yukun Zhou, Yifan Li, Qiuping Deng, Xiaofeng Wang, Zheng Zhu, Bingyao Yu, Ziwei Wang, Jiwen Lu, Haibin Yan

entry.summary: iMaC proposes treating raw visual images as native action representations for embodied world models, translating actions into motion and contact images rather than low-dimensional structured action vectors. It aims for greater expressiveness and cross-embodiment generalization.

entry.title: Perceptive Behavior Foundation Model: Adapting Human Motion Priors to Robot-Centric Terrain

author.name: Zifan Wang, Yizhao Li, Teli Ma, Qiang Zhang, Yudong Fan, Hao Xu, Shuo Yang, Junwei Liang

entry.summary: Perceptive Behavior Foundation Model is a terrain-aware humanoid control framework that adapts human motion priors to robot-specific terrain conditions like footholds and clearance. It addresses the gap where reference motions assume environmental compatibility that does not hold for the robot's actual surroundings.

entry.title: OASIS: From Simulation Data Collection to Real-World Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Zehao Yu, Jiakun Zheng, Weiji Xie, Jiyuan Shi, Chenyun Zhang, Chenjia Bai, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: OASIS is a simulation-data-driven framework for humanoid loco-manipulation that reconstructs realistic object assets from real images via a 3D generative model and generates scalable embodiment-aligned training data without physical hardware. It bridges simulation data collection to real-world deployment.

entry.title: FAWAM: Force-Aware World Action Models for Closed-Loop Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Haotian He, Zeyu Yan, Qipeng Liu, Ning Guo, Wenzhao Lian

entry.summary: FAWAM is a force-aware world action model that incorporates force/torque signals at perception, prediction, and closed-loop execution levels for contact-rich manipulation. It jointly predicts future actions and end-effector wrenches with a residual correction module.

entry.title: Dream-Tac: A Unified Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yunfan Lou, Yifan Ye, Yankai Fu, Jun Cen, Xiaowei Chi, Yaoxu Lyu, Peidong Jia, Sirui Han, Zhihe Lu, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: Dream-Tac is a unified tactile world action model that jointly models actions, future visual observations, and tactile dynamics with contact-gated visuotactile fusion and a contact-aware attention bias. It includes a dual-level acceleration strategy for real-time deployment.

entry.title: Guided Discovery of New Behaviors using Diffusion Policies

author.name: Dian Yu, Sebastian Sanokowski, Majid Khadiv

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework combining Feynman-Kac correctors with a novel guiding potential to systematically discover diverse and rare behaviors in diffusion policies, overcoming the tendency to reproduce dominant modes from limited demonstrations. It avoids pushing samples into infeasible regions.

entry.title: Back to the Familiar Future: Failure Recovery for VLA Policies via Pre-Imagined Milestone Selection

author.name: Suyeon Shin, Juwon Kim, Hyeonbin Park, Hyunseo Kim, Hyundo Lee, Hyung-Sin Kim, Byoung-Tak Zhang

entry.summary: B2FF is a failure recovery framework for vision-language-action policies that pre-generates a milestone bank of familiar future states from the clean initial observation, then selects a recovery milestone as a fixed visual goal when deviations occur. It avoids destabilizing re-planning in unfamiliar state spaces.

entry.title: TORL-VLA: Tactile Guided Online Reinforcement Learning for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Huaihang Zheng, Yi Yang, Kai Ma, Shenglin Xu, Tian Xie, Guozheng Li, Xiangyu Wang, Yiren Ma, Si Liu, Yinian Mao, Baoxu Liu

entry.summary: TORL-VLA is a tactile-guided online reinforcement learning framework that couples tactile feedback with policy refinement for contact-rich manipulation, enabling online adaptation when contact conditions shift from training distribution. It uses a wrench-aware VLA predicting reference actions and future wrench sequences.

entry.title: Nonparametric undirected graphical model selection using diffusion models

author.name: Hyeok Kyu Kwon, Myeonggu Kang, Minwoo Chae, Wanjie Wang

entry.summary: This paper develops a nonparametric approach to undirected graphical model selection using diffusion models, leveraging their ability to adapt to unknown graph structure for explicit graph estimation beyond parametric settings. It bridges generative diffusion models and conditional independence structure recovery.

entry.title: Why Limit the Residual Stream to Layers and Not Tokens? Persistent Memory for Continuous Latent Reasoning

author.name: Mujtaba Farhan, Maheep Chaudhary

entry.summary: This paper identifies a concept bottleneck in continuous latent reasoning (CoCoNuT) where intermediate hidden states get overwritten, and proposes persistent memory across tokens to retain earlier facts during multi-hop reasoning. It addresses a concrete limitation in latent-space reasoning architectures.

entry.title: Contract2Tool: Learning Preconditions and Effects for Reliable Tool-Augmented LLM Agents

author.name: Rahul Suresh Babu, Laxmipriya Ganesh Iyer

entry.summary: Contract2Tool infers tool contracts (preconditions, effects, risk, cost) from metadata, schemas, docs, and execution traces so tool-augmented agents know when a tool is causally appropriate, not just how to call it. It addresses scalability of causal tool filtering in large changing tool ecosystems.

entry.title: Efficient Skill Grounding via Code Refactoring with Small Language Models

author.name: Sera Choi, Wonje Choi, Saehun Chun, Daehee Lee, Jooyoung Kim, Chaeun Lee, Honguk Woo

entry.summary: RECENT is a refactoring-centric framework enabling efficient skill grounding for embodied agents using small language models by decoupling skill semantics from embodiment-specific execution binding. It targets reliable long-horizon control without reliance on large LLMs.

entry.title: Beyond Agent Architecture: Execution Assumptions and Reproducibility in LLM-Based Trading Systems

author.name: Junyi Yao, Zihao Zheng

entry.summary: This reproducibility audit reviews 30 LLM-based trading studies using a coded evidence matrix to assess execution realism, point-in-time controls, cost/turnover treatment, and artifact release. It finds architecture reporting is clearer than evaluation rigor, undermining performance comparability.

entry.title: Towards Long-Horizon Vessel Trajectory and Destination Forecasting with Reasoning Large Language Models

author.name: Hongwei Wang, Miao Zhou, Fengde Wang, Yuting Wang, Jiewen Yu, Jun-Yan He, Bohao Qu, Wanbing Zhang, Xiuju Fu, Qing Guo, Zipei Fan, Yingying Xing, Yi Yuan

entry.summary: This work tackles long-horizon (month-level) vessel trajectory and destination forecasting using reasoning LLMs post-trained with RLVR, building an AIS benchmark with 60-day histories and 30-day horizons. It targets route feasibility and destination correctness over extended horizons that existing methods struggle with.

entry.title: ConMem: Structured Memory-Guided Adaptation in Training-Free Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Zhixun Tan, Qiang Chen, Tairan Huang, Xiu Su, Yi Chen

entry.summary: ConMem is a relation-aware, training-free framework for multi-agent adaptation that distills historical trajectories into structured memory cards organized in a relation-aware memory graph and retrieves them per task need. It addresses noisy trajectories and memory-skill relation modeling without extra training.

entry.title: Oversight Has a Capacity: Calibrating Agent Guards to a Subjective, Fatiguing Human

author.name: Emre Turan

entry.summary: This work argues that human-in-the-loop approval gates for LLM agents face two false assumptions—a ground-truth notion of risk and a perfect always-available reviewer—and frames the guard as selective classification under asymmetric cost and reviewer fatigue. It uses a hand-labeled set of 125 adversarial agent actions showing only moderate reviewer agreement.

entry.title: Capacity, Not Format: Rethinking Structured Reasoning Failures

author.name: Hengxin Fan

entry.summary: This work argues that the cost of structured output formats (like JSON) on reasoning is capacity-dependent rather than a fixed reasoning tax, using information-matched controls and a schema-complexity gradient across 4 models and 5 benchmarks. Models with spare capacity absorb constraints while those near their limits degrade through distinct mechanisms.

entry.title: SIFT: Selective-Index For Fast Compute of RAG Prefill by Exploiting Attention Invariance

author.name: Rya Sanovar, Srikant Bharadwaj, Hritvik Taneja, Moinuddin Qureshi

entry.summary: SIFT accelerates RAG prefill by exploiting attention invariance and a selective index for fine-grained KV reuse, addressing how prior coarse KV-reuse methods can be slower than full recomputation due to disk-transfer latency and degrade accuracy. It targets reduced time-to-first-token with preserved quality.

entry.title: Next-Token Prediction Learns Generalisable Representations of Sleep Physiology

author.name: Jonathan F. Carter, Lionel Tarassenko

entry.summary: This paper shows next-token prediction yields generalisable representations of sleep physiology, presenting Hypnos, a multi-modal sleep foundation model trained across eight sensing modalities, as a simple scalable alternative to masked-reconstruction and contrastive objectives. It argues NTP suits the stochastic nature of physiological signals.

entry.title: Multi-Turn Evaluation of Deep Research Agents Under Process-Level Feedback

author.name: Rishabh Sabharwal, Hongru Wang, Amos Storkey, Jeff Z. Pan

entry.summary: This work conducts a multi-turn evaluation of deep research agents under self-reflection versus process-level feedback, introducing Research Gap Inference to infer research-process gaps from satisfied and unsatisfied rubric criteria. It finds agents can regress under self-reflection but benefit from targeted process feedback.

entry.title: Enabling KV Caching of Shared Prefix for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Younghun Go, Jaehoon Han, Changyong Shin, Chuk Yoo, Gyeongsik Yang

entry.summary: Identifies that standard KV caching corrupts shared prefixes in diffusion language models due to bidirectional attention and proposes bicache, the first KV caching technique for shared prefixes in DLMs. Restores high-throughput serving where naive caching collapses accuracy to near zero.

entry.title: Large Language Models Should Learn Personalized Rather Than Aggregated Human Preferences

author.name: Cristina Garbacea

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that LLMs should learn personalized individual preferences rather than aggregated ones, since aggregation optimizes for a nonexistent average user and masks preference diversity. Grounds the argument in social choice theory and demographic evidence and surveys personalization approaches.

entry.title: Semantic Cache Distillation: Efficient State Transfer via Reuse and Selective Patching

author.name: Qianli Ma, Zhiqing Tang, Hanshuai Cui, Zhi Yao, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: Semantic Cache Distillation replaces raw KV-cache transmission in disaggregated LLM serving with compact semantic codes, reconstructing most layers from low-rank subspaces and selectively patching key layers. This reduces the communication bottleneck that dominates time-to-first-token.

entry.title: TianJi-Environ: An Autonomous AI Scientist for Atmospheric Environmental Research

author.name: Haoluo Zhao, Hongchun Zhang, Nan Li, Jing-Jia Luo, Kaikai Zhang, Mengyang Yu, Nan Chen, Tao Song, Fan Meng

entry.summary: TianJi-Environ is an auditable AI scientist for atmospheric chemistry that uses a WRF-Chem-based multi-agent framework to autonomously convert mechanistic hypotheses into executable simulations and traceable evidence. It targets interpretable validation of pollution mechanisms.

entry.title: Beyond Pass/Fail: Using Process Mining to Understand How LLMs Resist (and Fail) Red Team Attacks

author.name: Zvi Topol

entry.summary: This work applies process mining to red-teaming traces to reveal sequential defense structures invisible to attack-success-rate alone, analyzing 8,575 scored events across GPT-OSS 120B and Llama 3.3 70B. It extracts directly-follows graphs showing structurally distinct defense profiles.

entry.title: PRISM: PRior-guided Imagination Sampling in world Models

author.name: Yuhai Wang, Jiawei Xia, Rongxuan Zhou, Xiao Hu, Yongliang Shi, Jing Du, Yang Ye

entry.summary: PRISM proposes prior-guided imagination sampling in world models for continuous control, deriving a robust action prior from the world model itself rather than separate visual encoders or large VLMs. It focuses planning search on candidate actions worth evaluating using state-conditioned expert confidence.

entry.title: Semantic Quorum Assurance: Collective Certification for Non-Deterministic AI Infrastructure

author.name: Jun He, Deying Yu

entry.summary: Semantic Quorum Assurance is a control-plane primitive that governs non-deterministic LLM-agent cloud operations by evaluating the safety of proposed intent, not just deterministic state replication, using declarative execution contracts bound to cryptographic evidence. It addresses operationally unsafe but syntactically valid agent mutations.

entry.title: "I understand your perspective": LLM Persuasion and Sycophancy through the Lens of Communicative Action Theory

author.name: Esra D\"onmez, Agnieszka Falenska

entry.summary: This work analyzes LLM persuasion and sycophancy through Habermas' Theory of Communicative Action, examining whether LLMs express illocutionary intents like building trust or signaling similarity compared to humans. It uses ChangeMyView discussions to compare human and LLM counter-arguments.

entry.title: RAPID: Layer-Wise Redundancy-Aware Pruning and Importance-Driven Token Merging for Efficient ViT

author.name: Kyumin Choi, Ikbeom Jang

entry.summary: RAPID is a depth-aware token reduction framework for Vision Transformers that uses redundancy-aware pruning in shallow layers and importance-driven merging in deeper layers. It adapts strategies to how token representations evolve across network depth to cut ViT computational cost.

entry.title: Auditable Graph-Guided Root Cause Analysis for Kubernetes Incidents

author.name: Anastasiia Kuvshinova, Seungmin Jin

entry.summary: Graph Traversal Agent is a graph-guided root cause analysis agent for Kubernetes incidents combining LLM reasoning with deterministic graph and tool operations over a typed evidence graph. It maps operational constraints to a LangGraph traversal state machine with a separate validation stage for auditable, evidence-based verdicts.

entry.title: A multi-agent system for spine MRI report generation from multi-sequence imaging

author.name: Zhiping Xiao, Junwei Yang, Gongbo Sun, Han Zhang, Hanwen Xu, Yi Yao, Zachary D. Miller, William E. King III, Mohammed M. Kanani, Jalal B. Andre, Sammy Chu, Ming Zhang, Paul E. Kinahan, Nathan M. Cross, Sheng Wang

entry.summary: SpineAgent is a multi-agent framework for spine MRI report generation built on a multi-sequence foundation model trained on data from 32,000 patients and over 13 million slices. It integrates multi-sequence imaging while preserving sequence-specific diagnostic information.

entry.title: Culturally-Adapted Red-Teaming Across East and Southeast Asian Contexts: A Methodological and Comparative Analysis

author.name: Hyeji Choi, Yongtaek Lim, Minwoo Kim

entry.summary: Constructs paired direct-translation and culturally-adapted red-teaming datasets for Korean, Japanese, Thai, and Khmer, showing culturally-adapted prompts raise attack success rates and that direct translation underestimates risk. Provides comparative cross-cultural safety analysis.

entry.title: Emergence of Context Characteristics Sensitivity in Large Language Models

author.name: Nadya Yuki Wangsajaya, Haeun Yu, Isabelle Augenstein

entry.summary: Investigates how LLM sensitivity to context characteristics is acquired across instruction fine-tuning stages (SFT, DPO, RLVR), finding SFT increases reliance on easy-to-understand contexts. It traces how context-usage relationships emerge during training rather than only at inference.

entry.title: Position: Genomic Model Research Must Move Beyond Anecdotal Evaluation of Interpretability Methods

author.name: Shasha Zhou, Mingyu Huang, Ke Li

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that genomic model research must move beyond anecdotal evaluation of interpretability methods, showing via a transcription-factor-binding benchmark that different IML methods yield contradictory explanations and fail to localize known motifs. It calls for systematic IML benchmarking in genomics.

entry.title: Mitigating the Contractivity Trap in Diffusion ODEs via Stein Stabilization

author.name: Shigui Li, Delu Zeng

entry.summary: Identifies a contractivity trap in large-step diffusion ODE inference and proposes SteinDiff, a training-free, step-wise stabilization using closed-form Stein corrections. It regularizes large solver updates without reference samples or retraining.

entry.title: Beyond Homophily: Towards Generalized Graph Reconstruction Attack and Defense

author.name: Zhanke Zhou, Bo Han, Xuan Li, Jiangchao Yao, Sanmi Koyejo, Michael K. Ng

entry.summary: Provides a systematic characterization of when GNN training-graph adjacency becomes recoverable via graph reconstruction attacks, modulated by homophily and inductive bias, and views inference through a Markov chain lens. It develops generalized attack and defense beyond homophilous settings.

entry.title: A Joint Finite-Sample Certificate for Adaptive Selective Conformal Risk Control

author.name: Xiaoli Yu, Jiamiao Liu

entry.summary: Provides a joint finite-sample certificate for adaptive selective conformal risk control that simultaneously bounds selected risk, acceptance probability, and utility under adaptive threshold selection. It uses empirical-Bernstein, Clopper-Pearson, and union bounds for non-monotone losses.

entry.title: Improved Convergence Analysis of Topology Dependence in Decentralized SGD

author.name: Yuki Takezawa, Anastasia Koloskova, Sebastian U. Stich

entry.summary: Provides a tighter convergence analysis of Decentralized SGD that better explains why network topology has large empirical impact in heterogeneous settings but little in homogeneous ones, resolving a gap between theory and observation. Theoretical contribution to distributed optimization.

entry.title: The Injection Paradox: Brand-Level Suppression in Safety-Trained LLM Recommendations via RAG Context Injection

author.name: Hyunseok Paeng

entry.summary: Documents the Injection Paradox in RAG-based LLM recommendations, where prompt injections in retrieved documents backfire under safety-trained models, suppressing the target brand below baseline and propagating to other documents of the same brand. Studied on Claude models. Matters for understanding RAG safety dynamics.

entry.title: Graph Mamba Operator: A Latent Simulator for Interacting Particle Systems

author.name: Karn Tiwari, Niladri Dutta, N M Anoop Krishnan, Prathosh A P

entry.summary: Introduces Graph Mamba Operator (GraMO), a latent-space simulator integrating state-space models with graph-based interaction learning to capture both spatial interactions and long-range temporal dependencies in particle systems, reducing rollout error accumulation. Matters for physical simulation.

entry.title: BUDDY: BUdget-Driven DYnamic Depth Routing for Adaptive Large Language Model Inference

author.name: Yuhua Zhou, Shaoqi Yu, Shichao Weng, Changhai Zhou, Mingze Yin, Fei Yang, Aimin Pan

entry.summary: Buddy is a budget-driven dynamic depth-routing framework for LLM inference that scores and skips Transformer layers under user compute budgets and adapts routing as context grows during decoding by reusing first-layer KV cache. Improves controllable inference efficiency. Relevant to deployable LLMs.

entry.title: When Do Local Score Models Extrapolate Across Size? A Diagnostic Theory and Benchmark

author.name: Wenjie Xi

entry.summary: Develops a diagnostic theory for when local score-based generative models extrapolate across system size, showing that stable size transfer depends on quasi-locality of the Gaussian-smoothed score rather than architectural locality alone, and proves a size-uniform comparison theorem. Provides benchmark. Matters for scientific generative modeling.

entry.title: Priors Persist Through Suppression: A Stroop Paradigm for Lexical Override

author.name: Han-yu Wang

entry.summary: Uses a Stroop-style paradigm to show that lexical priors persist through instruction-based overrides in LLMs (a remapping rule like doctor means forest), with prior strength predicting interference across 11 open-weight models. Provides mechanistic insight into how rules suppress rather than replace meanings. Relevant to prompt/glossary reliability and interpretability.

entry.title: Disentangling Latent Risk Pathways via Bayesian Hypergraph Inference

author.name: Shengxian Ding, Haonan Gao, Pangpang Liu, Xinyuan Tian, Yize Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces a Bayesian hypergraph inference framework for multi-disease modeling from EHR data, representing risk factors as acting on hyperedges (latent disease pathways) to enable interpretable, higher-order, uncertainty-aware predictions. Aims to overcome the limitations of black-box and independent-disease models.

entry.title: GNSS-FM: A Self-Supervised Foundation Model for Daily GNSS Displacement Time Series

author.name: Nick Teutschmann (Institute of Geodesy and Photogrammetry, ETH Zurich, Switzerland), Laura Crocetti (Institute of Geodesy and Photogrammetry, ETH Zurich, Switzerland), Fanny Lehmann (ETH AI Center, Switzerland), Leonardo Trentini (Institute of Geodesy and Photogrammetry, ETH Zurich, Switzerland), Benedikt Soja (Institute of Geodesy and Photogrammetry, ETH Zurich, Switzerland)

entry.summary: Presents GNSS-FM, a self-supervised foundation model for daily GNSS displacement time series pretrained with masked latent prediction and vector-quantized targets adapted from speech modeling. Addresses the scarcity of labeled GNSS data despite abundant unlabeled data for monitoring crustal deformation and earthquakes.

entry.title: Mind Your Steps: A General Learning Framework for Accurate Humanoid Foothold Tracking

author.name: Alessandro Montenegro, Shihao Li, Puze Liu, Alberto Maria Metelli, Jan Peters

entry.summary: Proposes a general learning framework for accurate humanoid foothold tracking, combining the robustness of velocity-commanded RL with explicit control over foot placement to avoid unsafe stepping and enable precise navigation. Targets real-world deployment by relaxing unrealistic state assumptions of prior foothold-tracking policies.

entry.title: Querying Counterfactuals on Tissue Graphs with Supervised Disentanglement

author.name: Abdul Moeed, Stefan Schrod, Martin Rohbeck, Marc Jan Bonder, Pavlo Lutsik, Oliver Stegle, Daniel Dimitrov

entry.summary: Formalizes tissue graph counterfactuals as spatial interventions (edge rewiring or neighbor expression modification) and introduces Cellina, a supervised-disentanglement framework to query how a cell's expression would change under altered spatial neighbor contexts. Unifies previously fragmented intervention-specific methods in spatial biology.

entry.title: SAEExplainer: Interpreting SAE Features with Activation-Guided Preference Optimization

author.name: Jingyi He, Haiyan Zhao, Ruxue Shi, Yanguang Liu, Xin Wang, Fei Sun, Mengnan Du

entry.summary: Proposes SAEExplainer, a closed-loop training framework that uses sparse-autoencoder activation scores as a reward signal to iteratively self-correct and refine feature explanations. Moves beyond open-loop explanation methods that ignore mechanistic feedback.

entry.title: Parameter Tuning with Generalization Guarantees for GPU-Accelerated Linear Programming

author.name: Siddharth Prasad, Dravyansh Sharma

entry.summary: Derives generalization guarantees for hyperparameter tuning in cuPDLP, a GPU-accelerated first-order linear programming solver, by characterizing PDHG behavior as a function of step size and primal weight to obtain linear sample complexity. Conducts structural analysis covering preconditioning, adaptive steps, restarts, and smoothing.

entry.title: Compositional Approximation Can Strictly Outperform Superpositional Approximation

author.name: Dennis Elbr\"achter, Philipp Petersen

entry.summary: Proves that compositional approximation methods (like neural networks) can strictly outperform superpositional (linear-combination) methods on certain function classes, even when bit-encoding constraints make their parameter counts comparable. Provides a theoretical separation result demonstrating an advantage of compositional structure.

entry.title: OptMuon: Closed-Loop Orthogonalized Momentum Methods for Stochastic Optimization with Zero-Noise Optimality

author.name: Ganzhao Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes OptMuon, a family of adaptive orthogonalized momentum optimizers that calibrate update magnitudes from the observed trajectory via an AdaGrad-Norm-type coefficient schedule, rather than constant or open-loop rules. Combines Muon-style polar-factor directions with closed-loop, noise-adaptive control and proves zero-noise optimality.

entry.title: Echo-Memory: A Controlled Study of Memory in Action World Models

author.name: Wayne King, Zeyue Xue, Yuxuan Bian, Jie Huang, Haoran Li, Yaowei Li, Yaofeng Su, Yuming Li, Haoyu Wang, Shiyi Zhang, Songchun Zhang, Yuwei Niu, Sihan Xu, Junhao Zhuang, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan

entry.summary: Presents Echo-Memory, a controlled study isolating memory mechanisms in action-conditioned world models by fixing the backbone and varying only how history is stored and read. Identifies memory rather than image synthesis as the central failure when scenes change after camera returns.

entry.title: From Player to Master: Enhancing Test-Time Learning of LLM Agents via Reinforcement Learning over Memory

author.name: Yishuo Cai, Xingyu Guo, Xuancheng Huang, Jinhua Du, Can Huang, Wenxuan Huang, Wenhan Ma, Yuyang Hu, Aohan Zeng, Jie Tang, Xu Sun

entry.summary: Proposes MemoPilot, a plug-in memory copilot that trains the memory-update process of a frozen LLM agent end-to-end via multi-turn GRPO to improve test-time learning across sequential interactions. Replaces hand-designed prompting rules with learned memory management.

entry.title: The Amplifying Mirror: Locating and Steering the Partisan Direction inside a Large Language Model

author.name: Wendy K. Tam

entry.summary: Trains linear probes on Llama 3.1 8B activations using 190K congressional tweets to locate a single layer-18 axis separating Republican from Democratic text with AUC 0.945, then uses sparse autoencoders to decompose and steer partisan generation. Shows political identity is encoded and steerable in activation space. References existing Llama 3.1 8B Instruct as the study model.

entry.title: What Should a Skill Remember? Quality-Cost Trade-offs in Cost-Aware Skill Rewriting for Language Model Agents

author.name: Qinghua Xing, Yinda Chen, Yaping Jin, Zhenhe Wu, Bohan Lin, Hang Zhou, Xinghao Chen, Hanting Chen, Zhiwei Xiong

entry.summary: Studies skill rewriting for LLM agents through an economic lens, showing that shorter skills can make agents more expensive by removing sparse operational anchors needed for debugging and recovery. It profiles quality-cost trade-offs across information-preservation strategies on SkillsBench.

entry.title: Friend or Foe? Language as an ideological switch in open-weight LLMs under Russian disinformation stress

author.name: Anna Ma{\l}gorzata Kami\'nska, Tetiana Klynina

entry.summary: Audits four open-weight LLMs sharing a base model but fine-tuned for different post-Soviet linguistic communities, disconfirming the assumption that culturally aligned adaptation encodes political orientation against Russian disinformation. It queries them across ten contested wartime narratives in three languages.

entry.title: VisualFLIP: Do Predictions Depend on Task-Critical Visual Evidence in Multimodal Reasoning?

author.name: Didi Zhu, Changrui Chen, Stefanos Zafeiriou, Jiankang Deng

entry.summary: VisualFLIP is a paired benchmark of 1,374 images arranged as same-question perturbation pairs across cardinality, attribute, spatial, and logic tasks, where minimal evidence changes deterministically flip the gold answer. It uses pair accuracy and a Collapse Rate metric to test whether predictions depend on task-critical visual evidence.

entry.title: LiteVSR: Lightweight Adaptation of Frozen Diffusion Transformers for Video Super-Resolution

author.name: Yu Cao, Ziquan Liu, Zhensong Zhang, Jiankang Deng, Shaogang Gong, Jifei Song

entry.summary: LiteVSR adapts frozen diffusion transformers for video super-resolution using flow matching, reducing the task to learning a fixed injection pattern rather than full fine-tuning. This offers efficient cross-domain adaptation without duplicating the backbone.

entry.title: ContextShift: A Controlled Benchmark for Context Dependence in Object Detection

author.name: Dan Zlotnikov, Alex Lazarovich, Ohad Ben-Shahar

entry.summary: ContextShift is a controlled benchmark built on COCO that systematically manipulates object-context relationships while preserving object appearance, isolating context as an independent variable to probe detector robustness. It uses a continuous compatibility axis based on pointwise mutual information.

entry.title: GraspFoM: Towards Reconstruction-Driven Robotic Grasping with 3D Foundation Priors

author.name: Dongli Wu, Xiaobao Wei, Hao Wang, Qiaochu Dong, Ying Li, Qingpo Wuwu, Ming Lu, Wufan Zhao

entry.summary: GraspFoM is a reconstruction-driven robotic grasping framework that uses 3D foundation priors (SAM3D) to build a shared 3D object latent reused for both reconstruction and grasp pose prediction. It introduces an anchor-initialized truncated pose-reasoning diffuser for multimodal grasp poses.

entry.title: PhysGraph: A Physics-aware 3D Scene Graph for Perception and Reasoning

author.name: Haoyu Li, Aaron Thomas, Shuyan Zhou, Xianyi Cheng

entry.summary: PhysGraph is a physics-aware 3D scene graph that unifies symbolic reasoning with structured geometry to model kinematic and physical properties in cluttered scenes from RGB-D observations. It supports task planning and affordance prediction beyond semantic-only retrieval.

entry.title: RGB-S: Image-Aligned Tactile Saliency for Robust Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Shengcheng Luo, Kefei Wu, Xiaoying Zhou, Wanlin Li, Ziyuan Jiao, Chenxi Xiao

entry.summary: This work proposes RGB-S, an image-aligned tactile saliency that projects sparse tactile sensor contacts into the image domain using forward kinematics and camera calibration, explicitly grounding physical contacts visually. It improves visuo-tactile integration for dexterous manipulation under occlusion.

entry.title: DexPIE: Stable Dexterous Policy Improvement from Real-World Experience

author.name: Ruizhe Liao, Wenrui Chen, Liangji Zeng, Haoran Lin, Fan Yang, Kailun Yang, Yaonan Wang

entry.summary: DexPIE is a post-training framework that improves dexterous manipulation policies from real-world deployment experience using a dexterous-hand-adapted intervention system and multi-stage DAgger-style data collection. It moves beyond pure imitation learning's compounding errors and data demands.

entry.title: Real-IKEA: Physical Fidelity is the Prerequisite for Robust Manipulation

author.name: Kunqi Xu, Zhenhao Huang, Siyuan Luo, Ziqiu Zeng, Fan Shi

entry.summary: Real-IKEA is a dataset and simulation framework prioritizing physical fidelity for articulated manipulation, providing over 1000 asset configurations from real IKEA handles with calibrated contact geometry and resistance dynamics. It argues physical realism is a prerequisite for robust policy learning.

entry.title: ReGIL: Retrieval-Guided Imitation Learning from a Single Demonstration

author.name: Yuying Zhang, Francesco Verdoja, Wenyan Yang, Ville Kyrki

entry.summary: ReGIL is a retrieval-guided imitation learning framework that treats a single demonstration as external memory, repeatedly querying it to guide exploration, build a regularization buffer, and construct rewards through local temporal alignment. It enables learning manipulation policies from one demonstration with limited online interaction.

entry.title: Goal Sets, Not Goal States: Queryable Robot Goals through Goal-Set Hindsight Relabeling

author.name: Carlos V\'elez Garc\'ia, Miguel Cazorla, Jorge Pomares

entry.summary: GS-HER generalizes hindsight relabeling to certify query-defined goal sets rather than singleton goal states, making the goal predicate an inference-time input and improving offline goal-conditioned RL when full-state goals are bottlenecked by nuisance dimensions. It turns hindsight relabeling into a reusable goal interface.

entry.title: Physics-Aware Sparse Learning and Selective Online Adaptation for Euler-Lagrange Robot Dynamics

author.name: Rishabh Dev Yadav, Samaksh Ujjawal, Sihao Sun, Spandan Roy, Wei Pan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a structure-preserving residual learning method for Euler-Lagrange robot dynamics that corrects nominal models while preserving symmetry, positive-definiteness, and inertia-velocity coupling, plus selective online adaptation. It addresses physically inconsistent predictions from naive additive residuals.

entry.title: Syll: Open-Source Personal Automation with Cross-Surface Execution

author.name: Bo Zhang, Borui Zhang, Chenghao Jiang, Minglei Shi, Xiaofeng Wang, Zheng Zhu, Jie Zhou, Jiwen Lu

entry.summary: Syll is an open-source self-hosted multimodal agent harness unifying API/MCP tools, CLI, and GUI control with a bidirectional user-agent teaching layer that compiles demonstrations into reusable skills. It is notable for emphasizing auditability and cross-surface execution in personal automation.

entry.title: How Small Can You Go? LoRA Fine-Tuning 270M-8B Models for Merchant Information Extraction in Financial Transactions

author.name: Donghao Huang, Tomas Drietomsky, Benjamin Barrett, Zhaoxia Wang

entry.summary: This deployment-focused study fine-tunes 24 model variants (270M-8B across Gemma 3, Qwen 3.5, Aya, LLaMA) with LoRA for merchant information extraction from noisy financial transaction strings, comparing accuracy, throughput, and cost. It identifies how small models can match an 8B production system at far lower cost.

entry.title: InA-Probe: Instruction-Aware Active Probing for Time Series Forecasting with LLMs

author.name: Peiliang Gong, Emadeldeen Eldele, Chenyu Liu, Ziyu Jia, Yi Ding, Xinliang Zhou, Lianchao Gu, Qi Zhu, Yang Liu, Daoqiang Zhang, Xiaoli Li

entry.summary: InA-Probe shifts LLM time-series forecasting from passive modality alignment toward active instruction-driven probing, using multi-level instruction injection and adaptive query generation to capture fine-grained non-stationary patterns and task intent. It improves adaptation to nuanced forecasting tasks.

entry.title: RAILS: Verification-Native Clearing For Agentic Commerce

author.name: Adrian de Valois-Franklin, Alex Bogdan

entry.summary: RAILS proposes verification-native clearing for agentic commerce, defining the agentic clearing problem of determining whether an agent met its delegated obligation, who is responsible, and which settlement follows, distinct from payment, authorization, or LLM-as-judge. It introduces a real-time agent integrity and ledger settlement primitive.

entry.title: STAR: Rethinking MoE Routing as Structure-Aware Subspace Learning

author.name: Sumin Park, Noseong Park

entry.summary: STAR reframes Mixture-of-Experts routing as subspace learning, augmenting linear routers with an evolving principal subspace tracked via the Generalized Hebbian Algorithm to align routing with input structure. This aims to reduce unstable routing and improve expert specialization.

entry.title: Diverse Thinking Schemata Elicit Better Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Xinyue Liang, Yizhe Yang, Yu Bai, Bin Xu, Jiawei Li, Yang Gao

entry.summary: DiScO observes a correlation between the diversity of reasoning transitions and answer candidates (thinking schemata) and model performance, then proposes Diverse Schemata Policy Optimization to enhance reasoning by increasing this diversity. It targets large reasoning models on math problems.

entry.title: ComplexConstraints and Beyond: Expert Rubrics for RLVR

author.name: Sushant Mehta, Liudas Panavas, Edwin Chen

entry.summary: This paper systematically analyzes expert-curated rubric-based evaluation for RLVR as an alternative to programmatic verification, articulating five design principles for high-quality rubrics across complex instruction-following and enterprise agentic tasks. It addresses nuanced behaviors that resist scripted checks.

entry.title: Reliable to Expressive: A Curriculum for Rubric-Following Safety Judges

author.name: Yongtaek Lim, Hyeji Choi, Minwoo Kim

entry.summary: This paper frames safety judging as a rubric-following problem and proposes training combining instance-conditioned dynamic rubrics with a reliable-to-expressive curriculum to make judges robust to prompt and rubric variation. It addresses documented brittleness with large false-negative-rate swings.

entry.title: Optical Reasoning: Rethinking Images as an Expressive Reasoning Medium Beyond Text

author.name: Yutong Bian, Dongjie Cheng, Heming Xia, Yongqi Li, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: This work proposes optical reasoning, treating images as a standalone reasoning medium for both language and multimodal tasks, with typographic and graphical variants that render rationales as optimized visual layouts. It pushes beyond text and interleaved-modal chain-of-thought.

entry.title: SearchSwarm: Towards Delegation Intelligence in Agentic LLMs for Long-Horizon Deep Research

author.name: Pu Ning, Quan Chen, Kun Tao, Xinyu Tang, Tianshu Wang, Qianggang Cao, Xinyu Kong, Zujie Wen, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: SearchSwarm targets delegation intelligence in agentic LLMs for long-horizon deep research, where a main agent decomposes tasks and dispatches subtasks to subagents that return summarized results to conserve context budget. It addresses the scarcity of training data for learning when and what to delegate.

entry.title: SIGA: Self-Evolving Coding-Agent Adapters for Scientific Simulation

author.name: Matthew Ho, Brian Liu, Jixuan Chen, Audrey Wang, Lianhui Qin

entry.summary: SIGA is a self-evolving Simulator-Interface Grounding Adapter that supplies off-the-shelf coding agents with a simulator's executable contract—vocabulary, structural constraints, validation rules, termination conditions—via retrieval and learned procedures. It frames simulator setup as agent-tool interface grounding for scientific software.

entry.title: Liberating LLM Capabilities in Full-Duplex Speech Models

author.name: Luoyuan Zhang, Bokai Xu, Junbo Cui, Weiyue Sun, Yingjing Xu, Hanyu Liu, Yuan Yao

entry.summary: Proposes Listen-Write-Speak, a text-first tri-channel paradigm for full-duplex speech LLMs where a single model continuously listens, writes visible text as primary output, and speaks, unlocking text-native capabilities like code generation in realtime interaction. Treats text as a first-class output rather than hidden intermediate.

entry.title: The Montparnasse Algorithm for RNA Design

author.name: Tristan Cazenave

entry.summary: Introduces the Montparnasse Monte Carlo search algorithm for RNA design that solves all 100 Eterna100 puzzles faster than the prior state-of-the-art DesiRNA and improves mRNA secondary-structure optimization. Advances computational design for synthetic biology and medicine.

entry.title: HARP: Efficient Data Selection for Finetuning Large Language Models

author.name: Ning Wang, Zhengxin Zhang, Maosen Tang, Yitang Gao, Claire Cardie, Sainyam Galhotra

entry.summary: HARP is an efficient train-based data selector for LLM finetuning that organizes the training pool into a node-leaf hierarchy and evaluates only representative leaves to preserve downstream alignment at reduced cost. It seeks the accuracy of gradient-based selection without the expense of repeated finetuning.

entry.title: FunctionEvolve: Structure-Guided Symbolic Regression with LLMs

author.name: Zeyu Xia, Jun Zhu, Dong Yan

entry.summary: FunctionEvolve is an LLM-driven symbolic regression framework that uses explicit expression trees to organize evolutionary search, combining structural summaries for diverse parent selection with local tree mutation. It addresses the structure-blindness of prior LLM-guided symbolic regression.

entry.title: Beyond Point Estimates: Benchmarking Uncertainty Quantification Methods on the AION-1 Astronomical Foundation Model

author.name: Karla Tame-Narvaez, Aleksandra \'Ciprijanovi\'c, Shubhendu Trivedi

entry.summary: This work benchmarks seven uncertainty quantification methods on frozen AION-1 astronomical foundation model embeddings for galaxy property regression, finding distribution-free conformal methods achieve near-nominal coverage. It emphasizes reliable UQ over point estimates for scientific inference.

entry.title: LogNEO: A GPT-Neo Reinforcement Learning Framework for Accurate Real-Time Log Anomaly Detection

author.name: David Eje, Tanmay Sharma, Khush Patel, Manuel Mazzara, Leonard Johard

entry.summary: LogNEO is a log anomaly detector built on GPT-Neo 1.3B fine-tuned with a novel position-aware partial-credit reward via PPO, achieving strong F1 scores on HDFS, BGL, and Thunderbird benchmarks. The reward models prediction difficulty by position to improve real-time detection.

entry.title: The Governance of Human-LLM Interaction: Safety Gating, Civility Steering, and Affective Default Lock-In

author.name: Manuele Reani, Hongjian Zhang, Hongyu Tian

entry.summary: This paper frames LLM interaction style as a governance object, introducing a deterministic multi-agent pipeline to measure prompt steerability and style drift in long-horizon dialogue across personas and domains. It examines how provider-side alignment locks in communicative defaults that shape user epistemic distance and ability to opt out.

entry.title: More Yap Less Meaning: Uncovering Self-Improvement Behavior in SLMs

author.name: Marina Igitkhanian, Erik Arakelyan

entry.summary: This study constructs a sufficiency test to examine self-correction in small language models via a minimal three-step pipeline collecting initial answers, generating hints for wrong responses given ground truth, and refining. It evaluates instruction-tuned and reasoning SLMs, finding self-improvement behavior dubious.

entry.title: Knowledge Graphs and Reasoning LLMs for Finding Simple Yet Effective Transcriptomic Perturbation Predictors

author.name: Jake Fawkes, Liam Hodgson, Jason Hartford

entry.summary: Shows that a simple K-nearest-neighbor over biological knowledge graphs is highly competitive for predicting transcriptomic perturbation effects, and that RL-optimized LLMs can improve it further. Challenges the need for complex virtual cell models.

entry.title: From Statute to Control Flow: Span-Grounded Deontic Trees for Defeasible Scope Parsing

author.name: Jian Chen, Siyuan Li, Chucheng Wan, Zixuan Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces NormBench and span-grounded deontic trees to diagnose Silent Scope Omission, where rule-following agents drop nested exceptions while appearing compliant. Spans Chinese, English, and other statutory texts to test structural understanding.

entry.title: Unveiling Privacy Risks in Multi-modal Large Language Models: Task-specific Vulnerabilities and Mitigation Challenges

author.name: Tiejin Chen, Pingzhi Li, Kaixiong Zhou, Tianlong Chen, Hua Wei

entry.summary: Reveals task-specific privacy risks in multimodal LLMs that can extract and expose sensitive information embedded in images, introducing MM-Privacy dataset to assess disclosure and inference risks. Highlights mitigation challenges unique to image-text models.

entry.title: Pretrained, Frozen, Still Leaking: Auditing Cross-Encoder Attribute Transfer in EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Jianwei Tai

entry.summary: Audits EEG foundation models (BIOT, LaBraM, EEGPT) jointly across four privacy endpoints, showing single-endpoint audits miss spectral attribute leakage detectable via cross-encoder transfer. Demonstrates an attribute decoder transfers across frozen encoders via a linear bridge with provable sufficient conditions.

entry.title: Conan-embedding-v3: Fusing Modality-Specific Models for Omni-Modal Embedding

author.name: Shiyu Li, Zhiyuan Hu, Yifan Wang, Peiming Li, Zheng Wei, Yang Tang

entry.summary: Conan-embedding-v3 builds an omni-modal retrieval embedding by training modality specialists and fusing their task vectors into a shared backbone (Decoupled Specialist Fusion). It identifies and addresses a failure mode for projector-based audio attachment in unified retrieval.

entry.title: Do Video Foundation Models Understand Intuitive Physics? A Layerwise Probing Analysis

author.name: Samuele Punzo, Niccol\`o Caselli, Ippokratis Pantelidis, Francesco Massafra, Salvatore Lo Sardo, Mohammadreza Salehi

entry.summary: Probes whether video foundation models encode intuitive physics in frozen representations across V-JEPA, VideoMAE, and a diffusion video generator using IntPhys2 and MVP benchmarks. Finds V-JEPA strongest and that physics-relevant information is weakest in early layers and most accessible in intermediate layers.

entry.title: Difference-Aware Retrieval Policies for Imitation Learning

author.name: Quinn Pfeifer, Ethan Pronovost, Paarth Shah, Khimya Khetarpal, Siddhartha Srinivasa, Abhishek Gupta

entry.summary: Presents DARP, a semi-parametric retrieval-based imitation learning method that reparameterizes the problem in terms of local neighborhood structure rather than direct state-to-action mappings to reduce compounding errors. It reuses training data at inference via k-nearest-neighbor expert demonstrations.

entry.title: Byzantine Cheap Talk: Adversarial Resilience and Topology Effects in LLM Coordination Games

author.name: Aya El Mir, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}, Salem Lahlou

entry.summary: Studies adversarial (Byzantine) and topology-related vulnerabilities in multi-agent LLM coordination via a 4-player Stag Hunt game across six model families. It finds agents detect betrayal but fail to collectively adapt, and that restricting communication topology collapses cooperation.

entry.title: Teacher-Free Self-Training Amplifies but Does Not Compound: A Pass@$K$ Crossover on a Free-Verifier Domain

author.name: Igor Lima Strozzi

entry.summary: Investigates whether teacher-free self-training on verified outputs grants new capability or just amplifies existing ability, using a verifiable DSL setup on a 4-bit Qwen3-4B. It finds critic-guided selection beats best-of-k filtering, with gains localized to disagreement cases, suggesting amplification without compounding.

entry.title: ConSteer-RL: Steering Reasoning Capabilities in Large Language Models via Confidence-Aware Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Qing Miao, Yiming Zhao, Jing Yang, Chenxi Liu, Yuehai Chen, Yuewen Liu, Shaoyi Du, Badong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes ConSteer-RL, integrating token-level confidence signals from log-probabilities into RLVR via GRPO to shape rewards that penalize overconfident errors and reinforce confident correctness. It addresses sparse binary rewards and ignored model uncertainty in reasoning RL.

entry.title: Neural Field Tokenizations with Hierarchy and Spatial Locality Priors

author.name: Alonso Urbano, David W. Romero, Max Zimmer, Sebastian Pokutta

entry.summary: Proposes LH-NeF, a feed-forward neural field tokenization framework injecting locality and hierarchy priors to learn general-purpose tokenized representations of continuous signals without modality-specific assumptions. It avoids expensive per-sample meta-learning.

entry.title: OrderDP: A Theoretically Guaranteed Lossless Dynamic Data Pruning Framework

author.name: Chenhan Jin, Shengze Xu, Qingsong Wang, Fan Jia, Dingshuo Chen, Tieyong Zeng

entry.summary: Proposes OrderDP, a plug-and-play dynamic data pruning framework that randomly selects a subset then picks top-q samples to obtain stable, unbiased, near-lossless training acceleration with theoretical guarantees. It addresses biased gradient estimation from informativeness-based pruning.

entry.title: A spectral audit framework reveals task-dependent aperiodic reliance across EEG and ECG deep learning

author.name: Jasmeet Singh Bindra, Siddharth Panwar, Shubhajit Roy Chowdhury

entry.summary: Introduces a spectral audit framework decomposing physiological signals into aperiodic 1/f and periodic components with phase-preserving Fourier interventions to reveal task-dependent reliance of EEG/ECG deep models on broadband activity. It finds aperiodic reliance varies strongly by task and is architecture-general.

entry.title: Claw-R1: A Step-Level Data Middleware System for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Daoyu Wang, Mingyue Cheng, Qingchuan Li, Shuo Yu, Jie Ouyang, Qi Liu

entry.summary: Claw-R1 is a step-level data middleware system for agentic RL that connects heterogeneous agent runtimes with RL training backends via a Gateway Server and Data Pool, addressing the full data lifecycle of agent-environment interactions. Infrastructure contribution for training LLM agents. Matters for scaling agentic RL.

entry.title: Toward Compiler World Models: Learning Latent Dynamics for Efficient Tensor Program Search

author.name: Haolin Pan, Lianghong Huang, Xvlin Zhou, Mingjie Xing, Yanjun Wu

entry.summary: Proposes a world-model-inspired evaluator for tensor program optimization that models schedule evaluation as action-conditioned latent dynamics over program states, avoiding expensive AST mutation and capturing schedule trajectories. Aims to improve compiler auto-scheduling. Matters for ML compiler efficiency.

entry.title: Data-driven discovery of governing differential equations across physical systems

author.name: Siyu Lou, Hao Xu, Wenguan Wang, Lu Lu, Hao Sun, Yang Liu, Linfeng Zhang, Dongxiao Zhang, Yuntian Chen

entry.summary: A review proposing a problem-oriented perspective on data-driven differential equation discovery, organizing the rapidly expanding field including AI-based approaches. Provides structure and synthesis for scientific discovery via governing equations. Useful survey for the SciML community.

entry.title: Evaluating the Representation Space of Diffusion Models via Self-Supervised Principles

author.name: Xiao Li, Yixuan Jia, Zekai Zhang, Xiang Li, Lianghe Shi, Jinxin Zhou, Zhihui Zhu, Liyue Shen, Qing Qu

entry.summary: Proposes a framework jointly evaluating diffusion models' generation and representation abilities by decomposing features into invariant and residual components and deriving the Fisher-based Invariant Contamination Ratio. Connects self-supervised learning principles to diffusion analysis. Matters for understanding diffusion representations.

entry.title: Perturbative Contrastive Physical Learning

author.name: Kyungeun Kim, Amanuel Anteneh, Israel Klich, Olivier Pfister, J. M. Schwarz

entry.summary: Introduces Perturbative Contrastive Physical Learning (PCPL), a general framework where learning emerges from measurable contrasts between physical states under controlled perturbations, unifying Equilibrium Propagation and Frequency Propagation. Relevant to physical/analog learning systems. Theoretical synthesis with physics grounding.

entry.title: Need We Teach Foundation Models What is a Generative Image? Gradient-Free Generative Artifact Detection via Analytic Spectral Adaptation

author.name: Qiaoyu Chen, Bing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a gradient-free method for detecting AI-generated images by reframing detection as out-of-distribution anomaly measurement on a frozen foundation model, avoiding fine-tuning that causes anchor drift in feature space. Uses analytic spectral adaptation to preserve intrinsic representations.

entry.title: Variational Proximal Policy Optimization

author.name: Ousmane Amadou Dia

entry.summary: Introduces Variational Proximal Policy Optimization, a particle-based variational inference framework mapping RLHF policy optimization to Stein Variational Gradient Descent within a Mixture-of-Experts architecture. Aims to reduce mode collapse and reliance on fixed clipping or KL schedules, tested on a 33B/4B sparse MoE model.

entry.title: Biological Reasoning-Informed Regression for Interpretable Regulatory DNA Activity Prediction

author.name: Yi Duan, Zhao Yang, Jiwei Zhu, Ying Ba, Chuan Cao, Bing Su

entry.summary: Introduces R3LM, a framework that teaches LLMs reasoning-informed regression for predicting regulatory DNA activity by injecting structured biological knowledge. Aims to improve both interpretability and regression accuracy over black-box sequence-to-activity models.

entry.title: SegmentAnyTreeV2: Scaling Transformer-Based Tree Instance Segmentation Across Sensors, Platforms, and Forests

author.name: Maciej Wielgosz, Stefano Puliti, Rasmus Astrup

entry.summary: Presents SegmentAnyTreeV2, a sensor- and platform-agnostic Point Transformer v3 framework for semantic and instance segmentation of forest point clouds, plus an expanded FOR-instance v3 benchmark with 427 scenes and 26k+ annotated trees. Improves tree separation in dense, structurally complex stands across diverse LiDAR platforms.

entry.title: CATPO: Critique-Augmented Tree Policy Optimization

author.name: Ayush Singh, Umang Goyal, Ankur Dahiya

entry.summary: Introduces CATPO, a critique-augmented tree policy optimization for RLVR that diagnoses uninformative rollout trees (all-success, all-fail, or already-predicted) via a tree informativeness score and addresses wasted compute. Builds on tree-based methods like TreeRPO to obtain dense step-level rewards more efficiently.

entry.title: Tensorizing Engram: Sharing Latents Across N-Gram Embeddings is Beneficial in LLMs

author.name: Wuyang Zhou, Yuxuan Gu, Giorgos Iacovides, Yuning Qiu, Qibin Zhao, Danilo Mandic

entry.summary: Proposes Tensorized Engram (TN-gram), a compact memory module representing multi-token n-gram embeddings via shared Canonical Polyadic factors instead of separate hash tables. Avoids hash collisions and enables nested n-grams to share latent structure, improving over Engram and over-tokenized Transformers.

entry.title: RAM: Reachability Across Morphologies

author.name: Tim Walter, Xinyu Chen, Jonathan K\"ulz, Matthias Althoff

entry.summary: Introduces RAM, a morphology-conditioned implicit neural representation acting as a fast differentiable surrogate for robot pose reachability that generalizes to unseen morphologies and accounts for self-collisions. Trains on a large 3e10-sample dataset from forward kinematics, achieving 86% F1 at nanosecond inference.

entry.title: Code Is More Than Text: Uncertainty Estimation for Code Generation

author.name: Yuling Shi, Caiqi Zhang, Yuexian Li, Haopeng Wang, Yeheng Chen, Nigel Collier, Xiaodong Gu

entry.summary: Argues code generation needs uncertainty estimation distinct from natural language, defining three axes (token fragility, intent-code gap, executability) for reliable selective prediction. Tailors UE to code-specific properties for safer agentic decisions.

entry.title: TRADE: Transducer-Augmented Decoder for Speech LLM

author.name: Yun Tang, Shanil Puri, Shinji Watanabe, Subhabrata Mukherjee

entry.title: Inside the LLM Word Factory

author.name: Benzi Busigin, Yuval Pinter

entry.summary: Uses activation patching in controlled paired experiments to localize English detokenization in Llama2-7B to a two-stage process at Layer 1, where attention transmits token-specific signals from nonfinal subwords. Pins down the mechanics of how transformers aggregate subwords into words.

entry.title: Precision Is Not Faithfulness: Coverage-Aware Evaluation of Grounded Generation with a Complete Oracle

author.name: Juan S. Santillana

entry.summary: Shows that reference-free faithfulness metrics measure only precision and reward abstention, using Formula 1 telemetry where complete ground truth allows exact recall measurement. It argues for coverage-aware evaluation of grounded generation.

entry.title: H2HMem: A Multimodal Memory Benchmark for Agents in Human-Human Interactions

author.name: Shiping Zhu, Yibo Yang, Zhengyang Wang, Tiancheng Shen, Dandan Guo, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: H2HMem is a multimodal memory benchmark for agents observing human-human interactions like meetings and clinical documentation, capturing anaphora, deixis, and conflicting multi-participant information. It addresses the gap in existing single-user text-only memory benchmarks.

entry.title: UXBench: Benchmarking User Experience in AI Assistants

author.name: Mengze Hong, Xia Zeng, Zeyang Lei, Sheng Wang, Chen Jason Zhang, Di Jiang, Taiming Fu, Jinfeng Huang, Mengqiao Liu, Qinghe Chang, Haosheng Zou, Qiongyi Zhou, Sijun He, Chen Xiaoshuai, Simon Deng, Haojing Huang, Zijian Li, Lucas Mu Li, Fubao Zhang, Mona Zhou, Wei Ma, Chenxuan Ma, Yuanmeng Zhang, Jian Song, Minlong Peng, Di Liang, Davey Chen

entry.summary: UXBench is a user-centric benchmark grounded in real feedback signals for evaluating AI assistant user experience, with three tasks and 7,400 instances extracted from over 70,000 interaction logs of a Chinese AI assistant. It evaluates 26 frontier models on preference alignment and dialogue quality.

entry.title: Are Reasoning Vision-Language Models Robust to Semantic Visual Distractions?

author.name: Yizheng Sun, Mochuan Zhan, Yanan Ma, Jia Tong See, Yifan Wang, Ziyi Wang, Hao Li, Yang Cui, Wenhao Cai, Jingyu Sun, Chenghua Lin, Riza Batista-Navarro, Jingyuan Sun

entry.summary: Distract-Bench evaluates reasoning vision-language models' robustness to semantic visual distractions, where a model perceives evidence correctly but reasons from plausible but irrelevant distracting evidence. It targets an underexplored reliability failure mode beyond input corruptions.

entry.title: Document-Authored Control-Signal Impersonation: A Low-Cost Indirect Prompt Attack on RAG Safety Boundaries

author.name: Jianguo Zhu

entry.summary: Identifies Document-Authored Control-Signal Impersonation (DACSI), a low-cost indirect prompt injection where attacker-authored retrieved text impersonates metadata, provenance, or policy signals in RAG systems. It frames the core lesson that document-authored labels are data, not policy.

entry.title: DALE-CT: Depth-Aware Foundation Models for Computed Tomography

author.name: Evan W. Damron, Mahmut S. Gokmen, Mitchell A. Klusty, Caroline N. Leach, Emily B. Collier, V. K. Cody Bumgardner

entry.summary: DALE-CT is a depth-aware foundation model for computed tomography built from scratch using 2D slice-based architectures and the LeJEPA self-supervised approach, with a novel 3D depth-aware pretraining objective. It is compared against a continually pre-trained DINOv2 baseline on CT-RATE.

entry.title: ChronoPhyBench: Do MLLMs Truly Understand the World or Merely Exploit Language Priors?

author.name: Bin Zhu, Yanhao Jia, Kexin Zhao, Jie Wang, Munan Ning, Hao Li, Yuwei Niu, Tanqing Sun, Huangchong Yan, Mingjun Pan, Xinyi Wu, Qishen Yin, Yunyang Ge, Shuai Zhao, Li Yuan

entry.summary: ChronoPhyBench is a chronological physical dynamics reasoning benchmark that unifies next-state prediction with VQA to test whether MLLMs synthesize cross-modal information or merely exploit language priors. It is designed to mitigate language modality bias and shortcuts.

entry.title: EditSSC: Toward Editable Semantic Occupancy Scenes with Unconditional Diffusion Models

author.name: Fatima Balde, Raoul de Charette, Alexandre Boulch

entry.summary: EditSSC generates editable 3D semantic occupancy scenes by reshaping occupancy grids into multi-channel BEV images and using off-the-shelf Stable Diffusion components with minimal modification. This enables training-free editing for autonomous driving scene generation.

entry.title: SwiftVR: Real-Time One-Step Generative Video Restoration

author.name: Jiaqi Yan, Xiangyu Chen, Xinlin Zhong, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, Jie Liu, Jiantao Zhou, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: SwiftVR is a streaming one-step generative video restoration framework that reduces high-resolution attention cost via mask-free shifted-window self-attention and addresses autoencoder latency under a causal chunk-wise protocol. It targets real-time deployment on consumer GPUs.

entry.title: Beyond Spherical Harmonics: Rethinking Appearance Models for Radiance Reconstruction

author.name: Ewa Miazga, Jorge Condor, Piotr Didyk

entry.summary: This work systematically evaluates spherical function alternatives to spherical harmonics for view-dependent appearance modeling in radiance reconstruction, aiming to capture high-frequency specular effects with lower memory and compute. It rethinks appearance models for novel-view synthesis.

entry.title: Revisiting Articulated Parts Perception in Robot Manipulation

author.name: Xiaoqian Wu, Yejie Guo, Xiaoyang Chen, Lixin Yang, Cewu Lu, Yong-Lu Li

entry.summary: This work proposes Geometric Primary Structure, an abstraction of articulated part geometry balancing scalability and quality, to improve articulated parts perception for robotic manipulation. It contrasts with costly pose-based and low-quality affordance-based representations.

entry.title: PhysAgent: Automating Physics-Based 4D Synthesis via Trajectory-Grounded Multi-Agent Feedback

author.name: Chunji Lv, Jiaxi Ye, Yuchen Jiang, Rexar Lin, Changsheng Li

entry.summary: PhysAgent automates physics-based 4D synthesis by using trajectory-grounded multi-agent feedback to optimize complex environmental force fields, addressing the manual bottleneck and the failures of naive LLMs and SDS in force-field optimization. It targets scalable physically plausible motion synthesis.

entry.title: Vision-Guided Dual-Arm Humanoid Robotic Disassembly of End-of-Life 18650 Lithium-ion Battery Packs

author.name: Yile Chen, Zhihao Liu, Xi Vincent Wang, Lihui Wang

entry.summary: A vision-guided dual-arm pipeline disassembles end-of-life 18650 lithium-ion battery packs from arbitrary poses using only general-purpose grippers, RGB-D sensing, and a pre-trained grasp detector. It targets fixture-free cell-level disassembly under pose uncertainty, an unsolved recycling problem.

entry.title: Deterministic Execution of ROS~2 Applications via Lingua Franca

author.name: Harun Teper, Shaokai Lin, Shulu Li, Edward A. Lee, Jian-Jia Chen

entry.summary: This paper presents a framework to convert unmodified ROS 2 applications to deterministic execution via Lingua Franca, addressing the inherent nondeterminism of ROS 2's publish-subscribe callback dispatching. Deterministic execution enables safety analysis and guarantees.

entry.title: VAIC: Vision-Guided Humanoid Agile Object Interaction Control via Decoupled Commands

author.name: Dongting Li, Qianyang Wu, Xingyu Chen, Liang Li, Yuhang Lin, Sikai Wu, Guoyao Zhang, Mingliang Zhou, Diyun Xiang, Qiang Zhang, Renjing Xu, Jianzhu Ma

entry.summary: VAIC is a vision-guided humanoid framework for agile object interaction using a decoupled command interface, relying only on onboard depth and proprioception via a two-stage teacher-student distillation. It bridges the deployment gap from dense reference trajectories and perfect state observability.

entry.title: Motion planning for hundreds of floating robots

author.name: Jan Kamm, Antonio Terpin, Raffaello D'Andrea, Aswin Ramachandran

entry.summary: This work presents a scalable motion planning pipeline for hundreds of omnidirectional floating robots on water, decomposing the strongly coupled collision-avoidance problem into interaction clusters solved independently in parallel with robustness mechanisms. It validates up to 500 robots generating choreographies within seconds.

entry.title: AetheRock: An Arm-Worn Robot Teaching System for Force-Guided Vision-Tactile Learning

author.name: Hong Li, Yue Xu, Yihan Tang, Yankang Dong, Chenyuan Liu, Chenyang Yu, Xuyang Li, Siyuan Huang, Yujun Shen, Nan Xue, Yong-Lu Li

entry.summary: AetheRock is an arm-worn robot teaching device integrating gripper force, vision, and modular visuo-tactile sensing for force-aware data collection, paired with ForceVT, a representation learning framework using force and vision to guide fidelity-agnostic tactile learning. It addresses incompatible assembly of tactile and force sensors in wearable devices.

entry.title: SynManDex: Synthesizing Human-like Dexterous Grasps from Synthetic Human Pre-Grasps

author.name: Yanming Shao, Zanxin Chen, Wenwei Lin, Mingjie Zhou, Tianxing Chen, Xiaokang Yang, Yichen Chi, Yao Mu

entry.summary: SynManDex is a synthetic pipeline that uses generated human pre-grasps as affordance-aware proposals, retargets them to dexterous robot hands, and optimizes force-closure contacts on the target embodiment to synthesize human-like grasps. It supports diverse prehensile tasks designed via VLM agents.

entry.title: CP-factorization for high dimensional tensor time series and double projection iterations

author.name: Jinyuan Chang, Guanglin Huang, Qiwei Yao, Long Yu

entry.summary: This work adopts canonical polyadic decomposition to model high-dimensional tensor time series, proposing a one-pass eigen-analysis estimator for factor loadings with established asymptotic properties under general conditions including correlated factors and weak factors. It uses double projection iterations for refinement.

entry.title: PathoSage: Towards Multi-Source Evidence Adjudication in Pathology via Experience-Aware Agentic Workflow

author.name: Chengyang Zhang, Wenchuan Zhang, Bo Li, Mengran Li, Bob Zhang, Yuhao Yi, Hong Bu, Jiancheng Lv

entry.summary: PathoSage is a three-stage agentic framework for computational pathology that separates knowledge retrieval, evidence collection, and adjudication to reduce hallucination and context contamination in patch-level multimodal reasoning.
