It matters because reliable evidence handling is a key barrier to deploying MLLMs in clinical pathology.

entry.title: MemToolAgent overview with a simple restaurant booking scenario where the agent retrieves similar memories, receives feedback on an invalid time format, and generates a reflection to update its memory

author.name: Suleyman Armagan Er, Danilo Ribeiro, Yogesh Virkar, Surafel Lakew, Adi Kalyanpur, James Gung, Thomas Delteil, Arshit Gupta

entry.summary: MemToolAgent improves tool-using agents by extracting structured memory from past user-agent conversations and retrieving relevant entries plus reflections to correct errors like invalid input formats. It targets learning from long-term interaction history for better tool use.

entry.title: SAGE: An LLM-driven Self Reflective Agentic Framework for Fraud Detection

author.name: Yichen Chen, Siying Li, Yuhang Liang, Lijun Wang, Renyang Liu

entry.summary: SAGE is an end-to-end LLM-driven multi-agent self-reflective framework for fraud detection that aims for individual-level accuracy, robustness under class imbalance, and interpretability for risk managers. It addresses gaps in AutoML and GNN approaches for real-world fraud constraints.

entry.title: Revisiting the shutdown problem

author.name: David Thorstad

entry.summary: This paper revisits the catastrophic shutdown problem in AI existential-risk arguments, arguing existing theorems do not establish its difficulty and that concern for it has driven misguided technical solutions. It offers a critical philosophical analysis of a core x-risk premise.

entry.title: Instrumental convergence and power-seeking

author.name: David Thorstad

entry.summary: This philosophy paper critically examines the instrumental convergence thesis underpinning AI power-seeking and existential-risk arguments, contending that existing defenses do not establish a strong enough version to ground the power-seeking concern. It discusses implications for longtermism and AI governance.

entry.title: AlloSpatial: Agentic Harness Framework for Spatial Reasoning in Foundation Models

author.name: Shouwei Ruan, Bin Wang, Zhenyu Wu, Qihui Zhu, Yuxiang Zhang, Jingzhi Li, Yubin Wang, Xingxing Wei

entry.summary: AlloSpatial is an agentic framework that converts egocentric observations into structured allocentric spatial priors (spatial trees, route maps) to improve spatial reasoning in multimodal foundation models. The World2Mind cognitive mapping sandbox supports querying topology, geometry, and trajectories.

entry.title: RTL-BenchLS: A Large-Scale Benchmark for RTL Reasoning and Generation with Large Language Models

author.name: Jing Wang, Shang Liu, Wenji Fang, Yuchao Wu, Yugao Zhu, Zhiyao Xie

entry.summary: RTL-BenchLS is a large-scale benchmark for LLM RTL reasoning and generation that overcomes prior limits in scale and task scope, where frontier models already saturate. It addresses the difficulty of obtaining aligned specs and testbenches for real-world hardware designs.

entry.title: Late-Layer Fusion is Enough: Dual-Path Vision Token Routing for Multimodal Large Language Models under Visual Saturation

author.name: Siyuan Liu, Jinyang Wu

entry.summary: This work shows that vision tokens in MLLMs saturate in middle layers (text-to-image attention dropping sharply by layer 4) while text tokens benefit from deeper processing, motivating a dual-path late-layer fusion with vision token routing. It challenges the symmetric Transformer backbone for multimodal models.

entry.title: Capability-Aligned Hierarchical Learning for Tool-Augmented LLMs

author.name: Haotong Yang, Ting Long, Yi Chang

entry.summary: CAHL jointly optimizes high-level planner and low-level executor policies for tool-augmented LLMs using RLVR, addressing planner-executor misalignment caused by separate optimization in prior hierarchical methods. It improves alignment for tool-use tasks.

entry.title: TheoremBench: Evaluating LLMs on Theorem Proving in Formal Mathematics

author.name: QuocViet Pham, Elvir Karimov, Andrey Galichin, Ivan Oseledets

entry.summary: TheoremBench is a Lean4 benchmark evaluating LLM theorem provers beyond competition problems, built from ~100 classical theorems in both a plain main version and a premised version expanding each into structured families of subtheorems. It captures behavior on longer, dependency-rich developments.

entry.title: TABVERSE: Benchmarking Cross-Format Table Understanding in LLMs and VLMs

author.name: Momina Ahsan, Sarfraz Ahmad, Ming Shan Hee, Roy Ka-Wei Lee, Preslav Nakov

entry.summary: TABVERSE is a controlled multimodal benchmark that aligns identical table content across HTML, Markdown, LaTeX, and rendered images to isolate the effect of table representation on LLM and VLM reasoning. It enables systematic study of format and modality effects while holding content constant.

entry.title: (Auto)formalization is supposed to be easy: Trellis process semantics for spelling out rigorous proofs

author.name: Wesley Pegden

entry.summary: Trellis is an autoformalization system using LLM agents in a deterministically constrained workflow that enforces incremental progress in Lean tasks through iterative refinement, motivated by the mathematician's notion that any proof step should be routine to elaborate. Specialization comes from a meaning-of-rigor process semantics rather than task-specific training.

entry.title: LEAF: Growing Trees Without Branching for Speech-Aware Large Language Model Post-Training

author.name: Argyrios Gerogiannis, Yekaterina Yegorova, Mark Hasegawa-Johnson, Venugopal V. Veeravalli

entry.summary: Proposes LEAF, a retrospective tree-based RL method for speech-aware LLM post-training that overcomes coarse credit assignment in GRPO by grouping responses with shared prefixes and assigning span-level advantages without online branching. Recovers useful structure from rollout batches at decision boundaries.

entry.title: Can You Trust What You See? Human and AI Detection of Synthetic Legal Evidence

author.name: Jinzhe Tan, Ali Ekber Cinar, Karim Benyekhlef

entry.summary: Builds SLED-1400, a dataset of 200 authentic and 1,200 synthetic legal evidence images, and tests both 136 lay humans and frontier multimodal LLMs on distinguishing real from AI-generated evidentiary photos. Addresses the erosion of visual evidence reliability in legal contexts.

entry.title: ScaleSweep: Accurate NVFP4 Post-Training Quantization of LLMs via Block Scale Initialization

author.name: Li Lin, Xiaojun Wan

entry.summary: Proposes ScaleSweep, an NVFP4 post-training quantization method that sweeps over feasible block-scale candidates to minimize a target objective, improving on AbsMax initialization with theoretical MSE/WMSE bounds. Targets accurate 4-bit LLM quantization on new hardware-supported formats.

entry.title: AVI-Bench: Toward Human-like Audio-Visual Intelligence of Omni-MLLMs

author.name: Yaoting Wang, Ziyi Zhang, Wenming Tu, Shaoxuan Xu, Wenjie Du, Cheng Liang, Weijun Wang, Yuanchao Li, Guangyao Li, Hao Fei, Yuanchun Li, Henghui Ding, Yunxin Liu

entry.summary: Introduces AVI-Bench, a cognitively inspired benchmark evaluating Omni-Multimodal LLMs across perception, understanding, and reasoning via cross-modal audio-visual tasks, plus an extension probing primitive sensation with unfamiliar low-semantic stimuli. Enables fine-grained diagnosis of model capabilities and failure modes.

entry.title: ViMax: Agentic Video Generation

author.name: Lingxuan Huang, Sizhe He, Hengji Zhou, Liqiang Nie, Lianghao Xia, Chao Huang

entry.summary: ViMax is an agentic, multi-agent framework for long-form video generation that coordinates specialized components for narrative planning and visual consistency across scenes. It uses a hierarchical narrative engine with retrieval-augmented generation and dependency-aware consistency tracking to maintain character and environmental coherence.

entry.title: TRACER: Token ReAssignment for Concept ERasure in Generative Recommendation

author.name: Ziheng Chen, Jiali Cheng, Zezhong Fan, Hadi Amiri, Diyuan Wu, Gabriele Tolomei, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: TRACER addresses concept unlearning in generative recommendation, where semantic-ID tokens shared between forget and retain items cause conflicts that standard LLM unlearning cannot handle. It proposes token reassignment to remove sensitive concepts while preserving recommendation utility.

entry.title: RecurGuard: Runtime Monitoring for Reasoning-Token Consumption Attacks

author.name: Abid Aziz, Hafsa Binte Kibria

entry.summary: RecurGuard is a runtime monitor that detects reasoning-token consumption attacks, where reasoning LLMs are induced to waste their generation budget on injected decoy tasks causing denial of service or wallet. It tracks recurrence rate, volume growth, and progress toward the user query across reasoning chunks.

entry.title: IEA: Amateur-Friendly Conversational Image Editing Agent via Three Stages of Multitask Alignment

author.name: Zichen Zhu, Yuheng Sun, Mingxuan Zhu, Wenjie Ma, Situo Zhang, Zhexiang Wang, Ziyue Yang, Danyang Zhang, Kunyao Lan, Zihan Zhao, Dingye Liu, Siqi Xiang, Lu Chen, Kai Yu

entry.summary: IEA is a conversational image editing agent trained via a three-stage multitask pipeline (SFT on expert edits, GRPO with rewards for likeness and tool usefulness, and large-scale synthetic finetuning) that operates parameterized tools in an interpretable action space. It targets amateur users by explaining why edits were made.

entry.title: GIScholarBench: Benchmarking LLM Overconfidence in GIS Research

author.name: Zongrng Li, Mingzheng Yang, Lei Zou, Hongxu Ma, Hao Tian, Siqi Zhou, Wenjing Gong, Kaili Zhang, Bingqian Chen, Mitch Zhang, Yifan Yang

entry.summary: GIScholarBench benchmarks LLM overconfidence in GIS research using 10,865 papers across three tasks of increasing complexity. It frames overconfidence behaviorally as confident, well-formatted outputs despite incomplete knowledge, relevant to scholarly factual precision.

entry.title: PIPE-Cypher: Automatic Enterprise Benchmark Generation for Text-to-Cypher Systems

author.name: Suraj Ranganath, Anish Raghavendra

entry.summary: PIPE-Cypher is a local benchmark-generation pipeline that turns a live property graph and optional seed queries into balanced, executable natural-language-to-Cypher benchmarks. It addresses the difficulty of creating deployment-relevant Text2Cypher benchmarks for diverse enterprise graphs.

entry.title: EinSort: Sorting is All We Need for Tensorizing LLM

author.name: Toshiaki Koike-Akino, Jing Liu, Ye Wang

entry.summary: EinSort proposes an adaptive tensorization method that discovers inherent low-rank structure in target tensors via index ordering for compressing LLM weights and KV cache. Experiments show improved reconstruction quality over baselines for tensor-network compression.

entry.title: Scaling Decision-Focused Learning to Large Problems with Lagrangian Decomposition

author.name: St\'ephane Eilles-Chan Way, Hugo Percot, Quentin Cappart, Tias Guns, Louis-Martin Rousseau

entry.summary: Scales decision-focused learning to large predict-then-optimize problems by incorporating Lagrangian decomposition, introducing a surrogate objective and two loss functions to reduce the cost of solving optimization per training instance. Offers variants trading off compute and accuracy.

entry.title: Benchmarking Vision-Language-Action Models on SO-101: Failure and Recovery Analysis

author.name: Yi Yu, Xinchuan Qiu

entry.summary: Provides a standardized real-world benchmark for evaluating VLA and imitation-learning policies on the low-cost SO-101 robot, with failure and recovery analysis across four manipulation tasks. Fine-tunes and compares pi0.5, SmolVLA, Wall-X, and ACT on physical hardware.

entry.title: Internalizing Geometric Law: Learning from Solver Residuals for Precision-Critical Generation

author.name: Rafael Cabral, Pang Zixi, Ziyi Shou, Shen Xin

entry.summary: Studies open-ended geometric synthesis from natural language, releasing a differentiable geometric DSL (PyGeoX) and benchmark with per-constraint verifiable rewards. It identifies a failure mode called Outlier Gradient Masking under global-norm reward schemes for precision-critical generation.

entry.title: Closing the Prior-Posterior Loop: Self-Reflective Molecular Design with Analysis-Driven LLM Iteration

author.name: Junyi Gong, Zijie Qiu, Ben Zhong Tang

entry.summary: Proposes a self-reflective molecular design system that feeds full physicochemical rationales (orbital energies, atomic charges, electron densities) from first-principles calculations back into an LLM design loop rather than scalar scores. It transforms the LLM from a trial-and-error sampler into a causal reasoner for HOMO-LUMO gap targeting.

entry.title: FMplex: Model Virtualization for Serving Extensible Foundation Models

author.name: Hetvi Shastri, Pragya Sharma, Walid A. Hanafy, David Irwin, Mani Srivastava, Prashant Shenoy

entry.summary: Presents FMplex, a serving system that virtualizes foundation model backbones so independently customized tasks share a single physical FM via virtual FM abstractions. It saves accelerator memory and amortizes batching/loading costs while preserving task-specific extensions.

entry.title: Boundary Variance Inflation Causes Acquisition Bias in Gaussian Processes

author.name: Maria B{\aa}nkestad, Sanna Jarl, Jens Sj\"olund

entry.summary: Identifies and explains boundary variance inflation in Gaussian processes with stationary kernels on bounded domains, tracing it to truncation of the kernel correlation neighborhood at boundaries that worsens with dimensionality. Shows how this distortion biases acquisition functions toward over-exploration in Bayesian optimization.

entry.title: When Should an AI Scientist Stop? Verifiable Experiment Steering and Refusal for Autonomous Discovery

author.name: Neel Tushar Shah, Manglam Kartik

entry.summary: Presents CARTOGRAPH, a verification layer for AI scientists that combines experiment steering, ambiguity closure, and residual-based library-inadequacy detection to decide when to refuse or steer experiments. It tentatively identifies out-of-library mechanisms and revokes uncertain identifications.

entry.title: Sequential statistical inference for Large Language Models: Representation, validity, and monitoring

author.name: Yao Xie

entry.summary: Position/discussion paper arguing that sequential statistical inference can improve LLM trustworthiness by modeling repeated, context-dependent queries as dependent stochastic processes. It proposes three pillars: representation, validity under dependence, and monitoring via change-point detection for shifts in calibration, hallucination, or fairness.

entry.title: Noise-Adaptive High-Probability Regret Bounds for Online Convex Optimization

author.name: Wentao Zhang, Yutong Zhang, Wentao Mo

entry.summary: Establishes noise-adaptive high-probability regret bounds for online convex optimization with strongly convex losses, scaling deviation with noise level sigma rather than gradient bound G. It introduces an exponential supermartingale argument bypassing Freedman's bounded-difference requirement.

entry.title: Causal Semantic Alignment for LLM-based Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Kexuan Zhang, Xiaobei Zou, Cesare Alippi, Gary G. Yen, Yang Tang

entry.summary: Proposes CVAformer, a variable-level alignment framework for LLM-based time series forecasting that disentangles each variable into invariant and dynamic components and applies causal intervention to remove confounding. It addresses spurious correlations during temporal-to-embedding alignment.

entry.title: When Are Neural Interaction Discoveries Real? Identifiability, Recoverability, and a Pre-Fit Diagnostic

author.name: Valentina Kuskova, Dmitry Zaytsev, Michael Coppedge

entry.summary: Frames neural interaction discovery as an identifiability question governed by input-support geometry rather than architecture, using a multiplicative-gating extension of neural additive vector autoregression. It provides a pre-fit diagnostic distinguishing real interactions from model-flexibility artifacts.

entry.title: Theoretical Foundations of Continual Learning via Drift-Plus-Penalty

author.name: Nazreen Shah, Govinda Arya, Bharath B. N., Ranjitha Prasad

entry.summary: Provides a control-theoretic foundation for continual learning, proposing COLD which uses a drift-plus-penalty Lyapunov approach to regulate forgetting under long-term stability constraints in replay-based CL. It treats adaptation as a controlled process with stability guarantees.

entry.title: Lost in the Non-convex Loss Landscape: How to Fine-tune the Large Time Series Model?

author.name: Xu Zhang, Peang Wang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: Diagnoses the poorly conditioned non-convex loss landscape of pretrained large time series models that hampers fine-tuning, and proposes Smoothed Full Fine-tuning (SFF) using an auxiliary model to smooth the landscape. It aims to avoid overfitting and recover pretraining benefits.

entry.title: SkillHone: A Harness for Continual Agent Skill Evolution Through Persistent Decision History

author.name: Zhiwei Li, Yong Hu

entry.summary: Introduces SkillHone, a harness for continual LLM-agent skill evolution that retains persistent decision history (diagnoses, revisions, evidence, rejected alternatives) rather than only final artifacts. Role-separated subagents evaluate candidate skills on practice probes for grounded improvement.

entry.title: Self-Consistent Generative Paths via Admissible Random Variational Transport

author.name: Lei Luo, Yingzhen Zhang, Jian Yang

entry.summary: Introduces a notion of self-consistent generative paths as random fixed points of admissible local variational transport corrections, offering a complementary theoretical lens unifying diffusion, flow matching, and other generative methods. Theoretical framework rather than new method. Matters for foundational understanding of generative models.

entry.title: Counterfactual Transport Flows for Offline Conservative Trajectory Refinement

author.name: Lena Krieger, Xuan Zhao, Zhuo Cao, Qin Wang, Hanno Scharr, Ira Assent

entry.summary: Proposes counterfactual transport flows for offline RL trajectory refinement, retrieving nearby higher-feedback trajectories as weak supervision for conservative, instance-specific improvement without extrapolating beyond data support. Addresses offline policy improvement safely. Contribution to offline decision-making.

entry.title: ERBench: A Benchmark and Testsuite for Equation Discovery Algorithms

author.name: Paul Kahlmeyer, Henrik Voigt, Michael Habeck, Joachim Giesen

entry.summary: Introduces ERBench, a benchmark and test suite for equation discovery algorithms that emphasizes out-of-domain extrapolation and ground-truth formula recovery rather than just in-domain prediction accuracy. Provides better evaluation for symbolic regression. Matters for scientific model discovery.

entry.title: On Choosing the $\mu$ Parameter in Gaussian Differential Privacy

author.name: Bogdan Kulynych, Antti Honkela

entry.summary: Provides principled mappings from pure-DP epsilon to Gaussian DP mu by matching worst-case membership inference success across three metrics, recommending mu approximately epsilon/5 as a conservative conversion. Practical guidance for reporting privacy guarantees. Relevant to differential privacy practice.

entry.title: In-Context Learning for Latent Space Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Tuan A. Vu, Harri L\"ahdesm\"aki, Julien Martinelli

entry.summary: Addresses the mismatch between latent-space Bayesian optimization tasks and the pretraining distributions of tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabICL) by complementing pretraining to better match latent-to-objective maps. Improves in-context surrogates for structured design. Relevant to sample-efficient molecular/protein design.

entry.title: SC3: The Multi-Solvent Solubility Challenge and Benchmark

author.name: Vansh Ramani, Har Ashish Arora, Dhairya Kuchhal, Sergei Tatarin, Lev Krasnov, Sayan Ranu, Tarak Karmakar

entry.summary: Introduces SC3, a multi-solvent solubility benchmark built on 101k+ curated measurements, arguing prior benchmarks rely on flawed curation and misleading aleatoric ceilings. Provides a reproducible pipeline and better evaluation metrics for tail-heavy solvent distributions.

entry.title: Differentially Private Range Subgraph Counting

author.name: Xian Chen, Ruobing Bai, Pan Peng

entry.summary: Initiates the study of differentially private range subgraph counting, privately counting pattern occurrences within attribute-range-induced subgraphs despite high sensitivity. Presents the first efficient algorithms with small additive error.

entry.title: Predictive Coding with Bayesian Priors via Proximal Gradients

author.name: Francesco Bullo

entry.summary: Recasts predictive coding as continuous-time proximal gradient descent on a regularized MAP objective, showing the single-level case recovers the Rao-Ballard leaky firing-rate network with the prior selecting the nonlinearity via its proximal operator. Extends the framework to multi-level hierarchies via variable splitting.

entry.title: Improving Bayesian Optimization via Training-Aware Conditional Diffusion Models

author.name: Yilin Zheng, Haowei Wang, Szu Hui Ng, Enlu Zhou

entry.summary: Improves Bayesian optimization by using conditional diffusion models to efficiently approximate the distribution of the global optimum location, replacing expensive GP posterior sampling used in information-based acquisition functions like Predictive Entropy Search. Develops BO-inherent training strategies for the diffusion model.

entry.title: Generalization in Nonlinear Least Squares via Learned Feature Geometry

author.name: Ayub Kharel, Ilja Kuzborski, Patrick Rebeschini, Yasin Abbasi-Yadkori

entry.summary: Studies generalization of ridge-regularized nonlinear least-squares via on-average algorithmic stability, deriving error bounds in terms of a data-dependent effective dimension reflecting gradient-model geometry at the trained parameters. Recovers classical effective dimension in the linear case but evaluated at the trained model rather than initialization.

entry.title: Continuous Language Diffusion as a Decoder-Interface Problem

author.name: Zhicheng Du, Lan Ma

entry.summary: Investigates why continuous diffusion language models generate fluent text from non-interpretable Gaussian-corrupted embeddings, identifying a decoder-basin mechanism where denoising succeeds when trajectories reach regions the native decoder can read. Introduces diagnostics exposing failures hidden by scalar metrics like MSE and perplexity.

entry.title: SG-OPD: Sign-Gated On-Policy Distillation via Sign-Consistency Gating and Phased Teacher Sampling

author.name: Haoran Xu, Hongyu Wang, Yifei Gao, Jiaze Li, Xiaofeng Zhang, Xiaosong Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces Sign-Gated On-Policy Distillation, which uses a binary verifier as a trust signal to gate teacher supervision at both rollout and token levels during distillation. Addresses cases where standard on-policy distillation assumptions about teacher reliability break down.

entry.title: MechLens: Late Crystallization of Factual Knowledge Explains Intervention Effectiveness in Language Models

author.name: Xueping Gao

entry.summary: Quantifies Late Crystallization, showing factual knowledge emerges abruptly at final layers rather than gradually, with 27-93% of correct answers never appearing in intermediate top-10 predictions across five model families. Connects this phenomenon to intervention effectiveness for hallucination mitigation.

entry.title: Support Vector Rubrics: Closing the Gap Between Self-Generated and Human Rubrics

author.name: Mengyuan Sun, Yu Li, Zhuohao Yu, Shikun Zhang, Wei Ye

entry.summary: Introduces Support Vector Rubrics, recasting rubric construction as max-margin boundary learning over preference pairs to close the gap between self-generated and human rubrics. Mines contrastive discriminative features rather than describing good responses.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Skill Generation and Policy Optimization

author.name: Zhiwei Zhang, Yudi Lin, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Linlin Wu, Xiaomin Li, Songtao Liu, Fenglong Ma

entry.summary: Proposes co-evolving skill generation and policy optimization for language agents, finding that even frontier-LLM-generated skills have highly mixed utility and proposing to assess skill usefulness before storing them. Addresses unreliable skill banks in skill-augmented RL.

entry.title: Symbolic and Abstractive Reasoning with Complex Visual Queries

author.name: Yichi Zhang, Jingdian Lu, Zhuo Chen, Lingbing Guo, Jun Xu, Wen Zhang, Huajun Chen

entry.summary: Introduces complex visual queries (CVQ) to probe symbolic and abstractive reasoning in multimodal LLMs, with a scalable pipeline that synthesizes queries grounded in multimodal knowledge graphs using first-order logic operators. It addresses an underexplored neuro-symbolic reasoning dimension.

entry.title: AbstRAG: Learning to Abstract for Retrieval Problems

author.name: Lei Xu, Xin Quan, Daniel Pedronette, Andr\'e Freitas

entry.summary: AbstRAG treats abstraction as an explicit retrieval object, decomposing the query-evidence abstraction gap into expression, conceptual, intent-evidence, and event-type components. It addresses retrieval failures when query and document express information at different abstraction levels.

entry.title: Where Does the Answer Come From? Benchmarking View-Level Visual Evidence Identification in Multi-View MLLMs for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yimu Wang, Yee Man Choi, Barry Zhang, Mozhgan Nasr Azadani, Sean Sedwards, Krzysztof Czarnecki

entry.summary: Introduces a multi-view VQA benchmark for autonomous driving where models must identify the correct supporting camera view alongside answering, using synchronized NuScenes views. It reveals that answer accuracy alone does not indicate correct visual grounding.

entry.title: IS-CoT: Breaking the Long-form Generation Collapse via Interleaved Structural Thinking

author.name: Zechen Sun, Yuyang Sun, Zecheng Tang, Juntao Li, Wenpeng Hu, Wenliang Chen, Zhunchen Luo, Guotong Geng, Min Zhang

entry.summary: IS-CoT addresses long-form generation collapse where performance degrades sharply beyond 2,000 words, embedding a dynamic plan-write-reflect cycle into the generation process rather than relying on static hierarchical planning. It maintains coherence over extended contexts.

entry.title: PulseBench-Tab: A Multilingual Benchmark for Table Extraction with Graph-Based Evaluation

author.name: Ritvik Pandey, Sid Manchkanti, Mohammed Wazir Adain, Mohammed Hadi, Dushyanth Sekhar

entry.summary: PulseBench-Tab is a multilingual benchmark of 1,820 human-annotated tables spanning 9 languages and 4 scripts for table extraction from document images, with a novel graph-based evaluation metric (T-LAG) using optimal bipartite matching. It evaluates 9 commercial and open-source systems.

entry.title: Property-Informed Diffusion-Based Text-to-Microstructure Generation

author.name: Bingxuan Dai, Hongsong Wang, Jie Gui

entry.summary: This paper proposes a property-informed diffusion model generating 3D metamaterial microstructures directly from text descriptions, leveraging semantic and physical-property guidance for inverse design. It aims to improve design diversity and physical feasibility.

entry.title: Temporal-Aware Reasoning Optimization for Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Minghang Zheng, Zihao Yin, Yi Yang, Yuxin Peng, Yang Liu

entry.summary: TaRO improves video temporal grounding in multimodal LLMs by using dense captions to construct grounded reasoning paths and rewarding reasoning quality, not just answer correctness. It addresses superficial reasoning in RL-trained localization models.

entry.title: vesselFM-CT: Segmenting All Blood Vessels in CT Images for System-Level Cardiovascular Analysis

author.name: Bastian Wittmann, Chinmay Prabhakar, Suprosanna Shit, Bjoern Menze

entry.summary: vesselFM-CT aims to segment all blood vessels across the whole body in CT images, enabling system-level cardiovascular analysis rather than isolated vessel segments. It addresses extreme structural heterogeneity of the vascular network.

entry.title: Training-Free Generalized Few-Shot Segmentation through Open-Vocabulary Semantic Arbitration

author.name: Silas Kwabla Gah, Ebenezer Owusu

entry.summary: Open-V solves generalized few-shot segmentation without training by combining SAM3 promptable concept segmentation with K-shot CLIP support centroids via calibrated per-pixel semantic arbitration. It reframes GFSS as inference-time coordination of frozen foundation priors.

entry.title: MinNav: Minimalist Navigation Using Optical Flow For Active Tiny Aerial Robots

author.name: Aniket Patil, Mandeep Singh, Uday Girish Maradana, Nitin J. Sanket

entry.summary: MinNav is a minimalist monocular navigation stack for tiny aerial robots using optical flow and its uncertainty to fly through scenes with static/dynamic obstacles and unknown-shaped gaps without prior scene knowledge. It uses active exploratory motion to improve success rates.

entry.title: X-Palm: Paired Multispectral-to-Smartphone Dataset for Cross-Domain Palmprint Authentication

author.name: Jamal Seyedmohammadi, Pai Chet Ng, Angelo Genovese, Zhixiang Chi, Jeannie Lee, Konstantinos N. Plataniotis

entry.summary: X-Palm is a cross-domain palmprint dataset of 6,006 paired images from 103 individuals, providing paired multispectral enrollment and unconstrained smartphone authentication to bridge the controlled-to-mobile domain gap. It is the first such paired-identity palmprint dataset.

entry.title: IntentNav: Learning Spatial-Visual Object Navigation from Human Demonstrations

author.name: Yuxin Cai, Zongtai Li, Maonan Wang, Muyi Bao, Haokun Zhu, Ruofei Bai, Ding Zhao, Zirui Li, Wenshan Wang, Wei-Yun Yau, Ji Zhang, Chen Lv

entry.summary: IntentNav learns human-like object navigation policies from human demonstrations by inferring high-level search intent through frontier-based labeling and a spatial-visual candidate space. It addresses how robots decide where to explore next under partial observability, mimicking human exploration strategies.

entry.title: Learning Predictive Control with Deep Koopman Operators for Autonomous Vehicle Motion Planning

author.name: Xinglong Zhang, Yongqian Xiao, Haotian Cao, Xing Zhou, Xin Yin, Xin Xu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a learning predictive control framework using deep Koopman operators for autonomous vehicle motion planning, lifting nonlinear vehicle dynamics into an interpretable linear space for efficient real-time MPC. It blends actor-critic RL with control-theoretic structure.

entry.title: Bridged SBI: Correcting Biased Low-Fidelity Posteriors for Cost-Efficient High-Fidelity Inference

author.name: Gahee Kim, Yuki Kadokawa, Sandro M. Alcantara Tacora, Taro Abe, Daisuke Endo, Genki Yamauchi, Takeshi Hashimoto, Takamitsu Matsubara

entry.summary: Bridged SBI corrects biased low-fidelity posteriors in simulation-based inference for calibrating particle-based earthwork simulators, using a bridge to transfer cheap low-fidelity inference to costly high-fidelity settings. It addresses parameter shifts caused by changing particle size and count.

entry.title: MosaicIMU: Composing Carrier Experts for Generalizable Neural Inertial Odometry

author.name: Junye Zou, Huiyi Yan, Xinning Xu, Xiaolei Li, Pengkun Zhou, Jinhui Zhang, Ziyang Meng

entry.summary: MosaicIMU is a carrier-conditioned Mixture-of-Experts framework for generalizable neural inertial odometry that composes carrier-specific expert features via a prototype router and integrates them with a history-aware EKF. It adapts to unseen platforms by freezing the base and learning lightweight expert residuals.

entry.title: Safe Polytope-in-Polytope Motion Planning and Control with Control Barrier Functions

author.name: Alejandro Gonzalez-Garcia, Dries Dirckx, Jan Swevers, Wilm Decr\'e

entry.summary: This work proposes safe local motion planning that guarantees a polytopic robot footprint stays inside a continuously updated convex free-space region, formulating containment as discrete-time control barrier function constraints within an MPC. It avoids conservative point or circle robot approximations for navigating narrow passages.

entry.title: Inference for High-Dimensional Sparse Spectral Precision Matrices

author.name: Navonil Deb, Younghoon Kim, Sumanta Basu

entry.summary: This work develops likelihood-based inference for high-dimensional sparse spectral precision matrices in stationary time series, addressing truncation and smoothing biases from finite-sample Fourier transforms and complex-valued variance estimation. It enables frequency-specific tests of conditional dependence among time series components.

entry.title: Coverage-driven alignment - What ‘Teaching Claude Why’ can borrow from AV verification

author.name: Yoav Hollander

entry.summary: This post argues that alignment training could borrow coverage-driven verification methodology from autonomous vehicle development, building on Anthropic's finding that teaching Claude alignment rules via next-token learning on stories outperformed behavioral shaping. It proposes using explicit coverage maps to systematize alignment training.

entry.title: Efficient tradeoffs and the safety-usefulness tradeoff model

author.name: Buck

entry.summary: This alignment forum post by Buck examines the common safety-usefulness tradeoff model, where developers balance safety against utility under limited willingness to sacrifice usefulness. It interrogates when this model holds and how risk-reduction strategies change when its assumptions break down, distinguishing between pushing the Pareto frontier and increasing the safety budget.

entry.title: Improving Multimodal Reasoning via Worst Dimension Optimization

author.name: Haocheng Lv, Huaping Zhang, Qiuchi Li, Lei Li, Chunxiao Gao

entry.summary: This paper proposes worst-dimension optimization for process reward models in multimodal reasoning so that individual failure dimensions are not masked by dominating factors. It aims to improve reasoning integrity across visual grounding and logical consistency.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Learning in Industrial Scenarios: New Large-Scale Benchmark, Challenges and Baseline

author.name: Zekai Zhang, Qinghui Chen, Maomao Xiong, Shijiao Ding, Zhanzhi Su, Xinjie Yao, Yiming Sun, Cong Bai, Jinglin Zhang

entry.summary: This paper presents MMIO, an 80K-sample industrial open dataset, and a Refined Text-Visual Prompt method for zero-shot industrial defect detection that reduces irrelevant-pixel noise from user prompts. It extends LVLM applicability to data-scarce industrial scenes.

entry.title: GIFT: LLM-Guided State-Reward Interface for Financial Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yanyan Wu, Boyi Zhang, Yanlin Liu, Xinyu Fang, Jining Luan, Meiqi Zhang, Jiacheng Liu, Hao Zeng, Dexu Yu, Chang Liu, Hanwen Du, Yongxin Ni, Youhua Li

entry.summary: GIFT is an LLM-guided framework for state and reward interface design in PPO-based financial portfolio RL, using factor-guided state enhancement rather than letting the LLM make trading decisions directly. It injects financial knowledge into RL design under non-stationary markets.

entry.title: Personalization Meets Safety:Mechanisms,Risks,and Mitigations in Personalized LLMs

author.name: Yanyan Luo, Xue Han, Ruiqiao Bai, Xin Huang, Yitong Wang, Qian Hu, Qing Wang, Chunxu Zhao, Jie Liu, Cong Geng, Lehao Xing, Pengwei Hu, Junlan Feng

entry.summary: This survey provides the first comprehensive safety-aware review of personalized LLMs, organizing personalization across user representation, paradigm, and evaluation, and introducing a unified taxonomy of safety risks. It maps the under-explored intersection of personalization and safety.

entry.title: IMUG-Bench: Benchmarking Unified Multimodal Models on Interleaved Understanding and Generation

author.name: Lingyi Meng, Zecong Tang, Haoran Li, Tengju Ru, Zhejun Cui, Weitong Lian, Qi Kang, Hangshuo Cao, Yichen Zhu, Yechi Liu, Kaixuan Wang, Yu-Jie Yuan, Chunwei Wang, Yu Zhang, Bo Dai

entry.summary: IMUG-Bench is a benchmark for evaluating unified multimodal models on multi-turn interleaved image-text dialogue across Static Spatial, Temporal Causal, and Hybrid categories, jointly assessing understanding and generation. It addresses exposure bias and single-turn limitations of prior benchmarks.

entry.title: Anything2Skill: Compiling External Knowledge into Reusable Skills for Agents

author.name: Qianjun Pan, Yutao Yang, Junsong Li, Jie Zhou, Kai Chen, Xin Li, Qin Chen, Liang He

entry.summary: Anything2Skill is a taxonomy-guided framework that compiles heterogeneous external knowledge (manuals, logs, trajectories) into reusable, retrievable, executable skills for agents, moving beyond RAG's fragmented declarative retrieval. It lets agents install procedural domain expertise.

entry.title: Experience Makes Skillful: Enabling Generalizable Medical Agent Reasoning via Self-Evolving Skill Memory

author.name: Haoran Sun, Wenjie Li, Yujie Zhang, Zekai Lin, Fanrui Zhang, Kaitao Chen, Xingqi He, Yichen Li, Mianxin Liu, Lei Liu, Yankai Jiang

entry.summary: SkeMex is a post-deployment self-evolution framework that improves medical agents through a skill-based memory distilled from informative past experiences, without updating model weights, and selectively retains memories truly useful for future reasoning. It targets long-horizon interactive clinical decision-making.

entry.title: Beyond Item IDs: Scaling Short-Form-Video Recommendation via Semantic-Native Long Sequence Modeling

author.name: Ruixiao Sun, Diego Uribe Mora, Zhimeng Jiang, Yuanzhen Lin, Jiarui Wang, Yuening Li, Danfeng Guo, Zhizhong Chen, Chuan He, Liang Liu

entry.summary: Presents a production-scale framework for short-form video recommendation using content-native Semantic IDs and long-sequence modeling, overcoming Video-ID semantic sparsity and Transformer quadratic complexity at billion-user scale. Demonstrates deployable efficiency at industrial scale.

entry.title: A Mechanistic Analysis of Adversarial Fine-tuning of Vision Transformers

author.name: Hannah Gao (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Isha Agarwal (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Dylan Hadfield-Menell (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Rachel Ma (Massachusetts Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: Provides a mechanistic analysis of adversarial fine-tuning of vision transformers under low- and high-frequency perturbations, examining how robustness training reshapes internal representations. Relevant to ViTs embedded in modern VLMs and VLA models.

entry.title: Query Lens: Interpreting Sparse Key-Value Features with Indirect Effects

author.name: Hwiyeong Lee, Ingyu Bang, Uiji Hwang, Hyelim Lim, Taeuk Kim

entry.summary: Proposes Query Lens, extending Logit Lens by jointly considering encoder-side key features and decoder-side value features in sparse autoencoders, also accounting for indirect module-mediated effects. Yields coherent token signatures for features that were uninterpretable under Logit Lens.

entry.title: MM-Matryoshka: Towards Budget-Elastic Visual Document Retrieval via a 2D Multimodal Matryoshka Training Framework

author.name: Haowen Xiang, Yibo Yan, Jiahao Huo, Yu Huang, Yi Cao, Mingdong Ou, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: MM-Matryoshka is a 2D Matryoshka training framework for visual document retrieval that lets a single multi-vector retriever flexibly trade accuracy against both vector dimension and encoder depth at inference. This enables budget-elastic deployment without training separate models.

entry.title: Frequency-Domain Latent Attention Gating for Cross-Domain Token Aggregation

author.name: Kewei Li, Rongying Zhang, Xueli Wang, Xiwen Gong, Zhongjian Wang, Lan Huang, Ruochi Zhang, Fengfeng Zhou

entry.summary: FLaG is a plug-in token aggregation module that transforms representations via real FFT, summarizes spectral components with learnable latent queries, gates channels, and reconstructs time-domain tokens for pooling. It is evaluated across protein, image, and text classification tasks.

entry.title: Projecting the Emerging Mindset of SWE Agent by Launching a Wild Code Understanding Journey

author.name: Zhengyi Zhuo, Yan Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces Ada, a scoped apparatus for repository-level code understanding that records faithful, replayable trajectories of SWE agents including tool use, reasoning, evidence selection, and self-directed stopping. It aims to make agent behavior observable and characterizable through disciplined trajectory analysis.

entry.title: RadOT-Eval: Auditable Structured-Evidence Transport for Radiology Report Evaluation

author.name: Weixin Liu, Juming Xiong, Yang Li, Qingyuan Song, Susannah Rose, Murat Kantarcioglu, Bradley Malin, Zhijun Yin

entry.summary: RadOT-Eval is an interpretable optimal-transport framework for auditing radiology report generation by decomposing reports into structured clinical evidence units and aligning them. It targets clinically meaningful errors like omissions, hallucinations, and polarity reversals.

entry.title: TRIAGE: Dialectical Reasoning for Explainable Risk Prediction on Irregularly Sampled Medical Time Series with LLMs

author.name: Hyeongwon Jang, Gyouk Chu, Changhun Kim, Joonhyung Park, Hangyul Yoon, Eunho Yang

entry.summary: TRIAGE trains an LLM to generate dialectical reasoning over competing clinical outcomes for risk prediction on irregularly sampled medical time series, mitigating overconfident binary risk polarization. It aims for calibrated risk scores plus verifiable interpretable rationales.

entry.title: End-to-End Training for Discrete Token LLM based TTS System

author.name: Changfeng Gao, Yong Ren, Jun Yuan, Ye Bai, Zhao You, ShiDong Shang

entry.summary: Proposes a fully end-to-end optimization framework unifying training of the speech tokenizer, autoregressive LLM, flow-matching model, and a reward model for discrete-token TTS. Jointly optimizes the tokenizer via reconstruction, next-token prediction, and recognition objectives.

entry.title: Memory Beyond Recall: A Dual-Process Cognitive Memory System for Self-Evolving LLM Agents

author.name: Tianxiang Fei, Mingyang Song, Mao Zheng, Xiang Yu

entry.summary: Proposes DCPM, a dual-process cognitive memory system for self-evolving LLM agents that organizes memory along a hierarchy from atomic facts to belief trajectories and cross-domain patterns. It splits into a System1 daytime writer and presumably a System2 consolidation process for implicit personalization.

entry.title: AGENTSERVESIM: A Hardware-aware Simulator for Multi-Turn LLM Agent Serving

author.name: Rakibul Hasan Rajib, Mengxin Zheng, Qian Lou

entry.summary: Presents AGENTSERVESIM, a hardware-aware simulator for multi-turn LLM agent serving that captures stateful program execution dynamics like turn dependencies, tool gaps, and reusable KV state. It addresses the gap that existing simulators target stateless request-level workloads.

entry.title: UNIQ: Conformal Calibration for Adaptive Conservatism in Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Aditya Upadhyay

entry.summary: Presents UNIQ, an offline RL method that introduces state-adaptive conservatism via conformally calibrated uncertainty estimation built on Implicit Q-Learning. It relaxes conservatism in well-covered regions and strengthens it near the uncertain data frontier on D4RL benchmarks.

entry.title: Constraint-Aware Optimization for Robust Protein Stability Prediction

author.name: A Shivram, Aneesh S. Chivukula, Manik Gupta, Sourav Chowdhury

entry.summary: Introduces a constraint-aware optimization framework for protein stability (delta-delta-G) prediction combining balanced MSE, a Siamese anti-symmetric regularizer, and an OOD-margin consistency loss. It improves robustness, forward-reverse symmetry, and rare stabilizing-mutation detection.

entry.title: QueryWeaver: Reliable Multi-Tool Query Execution Planning via LLM-Based Graph Generation

author.name: Aishwarya Chakravarthy, Vidhi Kulkarni, Duen Horng Chau

entry.summary: Introduces QueryWeaver, a system converting natural-language multi-tool queries over personal data into structured dependency graphs executed via a deterministic depth-first planner. It improves reliability of cross-tool query execution even with small or local LLMs.

entry.title: How Much Capacity Does EEG Denoising Need? Ultra-Compact Networks reveal Benchmark Saturation and Metric-Utility Gap

author.name: Jasmeet Singh Bindra, Siddharth Panwar, Shubhajit Roy Chowdhury

entry.summary: Isolates model capacity as the sole variable in EEG denoising by sweeping channel width from ~1K to 40K parameters in a minimal U-Net, finding reconstruction performance saturates early and a gap between reconstruction metrics and downstream utility. It questions the trend toward ever-larger denoising models.

entry.title: Operator learning for the 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations: a conformal prediction approach in the data-scarce regime

author.name: Weinan Wang, Bowen Gang, Hao Deng

entry.summary: Proposes a perturbation-based conformal prediction framework for uncertainty quantification in operator learning for 2D Navier-Stokes, building local uncertainty scales by comparing FNOs trained on original versus noise-perturbed labels. It targets the data-scarce regime with fixed label budgets.

entry.title: From Hazard Functions to Language Space: Cox-Supervised Distillation of Survival Risk into a Large Language Model

author.name: Nicholas I-Hsien Kuo, Blanca Gallego, Louisa Jorm

entry.summary: Distills Cox proportional hazards survival risk into a Qwen-based LLM by converting clinical covariates to text prompts, achieving competitive discrimination via text generation. Analyzes hidden-state geometry showing smooth risk structure. Bridges survival analysis and language models.

entry.title: Trajectory Geometry of Transformer Representations Across Layers

author.name: Vishal Pandey, Gopal Singh

entry.summary: Recasts the transformer forward pass as a discrete population trajectory through representation manifolds, characterizing layer-wise geometry via metrics like curvature and semantic convergence across GPT-2, TinyLlama, and Qwen2.5. Contributes mechanistic interpretability tools borrowed from neuroscience. Matters for understanding representation dynamics.

entry.title: Phase Marginalization for Patch-Grid Instability in Vision Transformers

author.name: O\u{g}uzhan Ercan

entry.summary: Identifies patch-grid phase as a nuisance variable causing instability in Vision Transformers for dense prediction near patch boundaries, and proposes training-free Phase Marginalization that aggregates outputs over shifted patch grids. The uniform K=4 variant improves segmentation, depth, and matching over the standard single-grid baseline.

entry.title: CHROMA: Detecting AI-Generated Images through Inter-Channel Color-Space Correlations

author.name: Juan Pablo Sotelo, Marina Gardella, Pablo Mus\'e

entry.summary: Introduces CHROMA, a lightweight forensic method for detecting AI-generated images using inter-channel color-space correlations, an underexploited cue. Shows that perceptual metrics like LPIPS respond inconsistently to channel-dependence perturbations, motivating cross-channel statistics for more generalizable detection.

entry.title: Driving Video Retrieval for Complex Queries with Structured Grounding

author.name: Manyi Yao, Sparsh Garg, Christian Shelton, Amit Roy-Chowdhury, Abhishek Aich

entry.summary: Proposes STRIVE-D, a data-calibrated retrieval framework for driving videos that uses weakly labeled in-domain data to estimate when query rules are reliable and adapts rules that mismatch observations. Targets retrieval of dynamic events like cut-ins and hard braking that vision-language and keyword methods miss.

entry.title: Counterfactual Reasoning for Fine-Grained Evidence Disentanglement in VideoQA

author.name: Zhou Du, Hamid Krim, Xiao Wu, Zhaoquan Yuan, Liangwei Li, Keisuke Fujii

entry.summary: Proposes a counterfactual reasoning framework for fine-grained evidence disentanglement in VideoQA that separates causal visual cues from confounders and provides localized evidence rather than operating at coarse time-interval level. Aims to reduce reliance on spurious correlations for more faithful, robust video question answering.

entry.title: Adaptive directional gradients for parameterised quantum circuits

author.name: Brian Coyle, Snehal Raj, Virag Umathe, El Amine Cherrat, Elham Kashefi

entry.summary: Proposes forward-gradient estimators for parameterized quantum circuits that reduce measurement cost of training while unifying SPSA, random coordinate descent, and parameter-shift as special cases. Provides convergence guarantees with no ancilla overhead.

entry.title: Multilingual Refusal Alignment for Safer Large Language Models

author.name: Aleksandra Krasnod\k{e}bska, Wojciech Kusa, Aldo Lipani

entry.summary: Investigates multilingual refusal alignment, introducing RefusEU covering 12 European languages, and studies whether single-language safety alignment transfers cross-lingually under DPO. Examines tradeoffs between consistency and general knowledge.

entry.title: Bridging the Agent-World Gap: Text World Models for LLM-based Agents

author.name: Yixia Li, Hongru Wang, Peng Lai, Zhiwen Ruan, He Zhu, Youxin Zhu, Ganlong Zhao, Minda Hu, Yun Chen, Sibei Yang, Peng Li, Jeff Z. Pan, Jia Pan, Guanhua Chen, Yang Liu, Guanbin Li

entry.summary: Provides a systematic review of text world models for LLM agents, formalizing transition models over textual states that predict resulting webpages, terminal outputs, or replies to support planning and evaluation. Organizes the field around a formal framework and the agent lifecycle.

entry.title: OpenBibleTTS: Large-Scale Speech Resources and TTS Models for Low-Resource Languages

author.name: David Guzm\'an, Luel Hagos Beyene, Jesujoba Oluwadara Alabi, Yejin Jeon, Dietrich Klakow, David Ifeoluwa Adelani

entry.summary: OpenBibleTTS is a large-scale benchmark for low-resource speech synthesis spanning 37 underrepresented languages built from Bible recordings, with a systematic comparison of TTS architectures. It addresses the gap that prior low-resource TTS often uses artificially downsampled high-resource corpora.

entry.title: TinyGiantALM: A Compact Audio-Language Model for Intent-Aware Reasoning under Resource Constraints

author.name: Vinh-Thuan Ly

entry.summary: TinyGiantALM is a compact 1.5B audio-language model using an instruction-aware feature refinement framework with a query-guided projector and semantic gating to filter acoustic signals by user intent. It reportedly outperforms 7B-13B baselines on the MMAR benchmark with 46.4% zero-shot accuracy.

entry.title: Vision-Language Asymmetry in Bistable Image Captioning

author.name: Arohan Agate

entry.summary: Investigates where in a vision-language model the commitment to one interpretation of bistable images is made, using a behavioral baseline over 83 bistable stimuli and a TopK sparse autoencoder trained on the CLIP layer LLaVA consumes. It finds simultaneous activation of both aspect feature pools at the vision tower.

entry.title: Visual Para-Thinker++: A Single-Policy Multi-Agent Framework for Visual Reasoning

author.name: Haoran Xu, Hongyu Wang, Yifei Gao, Jiaze Li, Zizhao Tong, Xiaofeng Zhang, Xiaosong Yuan

entry.summary: Visual Para-Thinker++ uses a single shared MLLM policy instantiated as role-conditioned Main/Worker/Summary agents for parallel visual reasoning, trained with role-specific rewards. It aims to reduce early perceptual commitment and hallucination in single-chain reasoning.

entry.title: ExDet: Open-Domain Open-Vocabulary Detection with Cross-modal Extrapolation and Rectification

author.name: Yupeng Zhang, Yuzhong Feng, Ruize Han, Zhiwei Chen, Wei Feng, Liang Wan

entry.summary: ExDet is a lightweight framework for open-domain open-vocabulary detection that uses text-guided extrapolation and a detector-compatible rectification module to boost cross-category and cross-domain generalization without training from scratch. It exploits VLM DeltaSpace properties.

entry.title: Programmable Silicon Retina on Pixel Processor Array

author.name: Maciej Lewandowski, Prince Philip, Alexandre Marcireau, Chetan Singh Thakur, Andr\'e van Schaik, Piotr Dudek

entry.summary: This paper presents the first multi-stage Silicon Retina model with spatial filtering and gain control on the SCAMP-5 Pixel Processor Array, plus a GPU simulation framework, evaluated on intensity reconstruction and saliency prediction. The bio-inspired model improves saliency prediction despite worse intensity reconstruction.

entry.title: OctaOctree Neural Radiosity for Real-time Glossy Material Rendering

author.name: Jierui Ren (Peking University), Haojie Jin (Peking University), Bo Pang (Peking University), Meng Gai (Peking University), Fei Zhu (Peking University), Yisong Chen (Peking University), Sheng Li (Peking University)

entry.summary: OctaOctree is a spatial-angular radiance representation for real-time global illumination that organizes outgoing radiance via an adaptive octree coupled with per-node octahedral directional maps. It targets sharp directional radiance variations for glossy and specular materials.

entry.title: Taming Perception Jitter: Uncertainty-Aware LiDAR Object Detection for Reliable Motion Classification

author.name: Cornelius Schr\"oder, \v{Z}ygimantas Marcinkus, Markus Lienkamp

entry.summary: This work augments a 3D LiDAR detector with aleatoric uncertainty estimates and applies a two-sample z-test over short windows to distinguish true motion from perception jitter, reducing false dynamic predictions for static objects. It integrates into Autoware with minimal overhead.

entry.title: Agentic Neuro-Symbolic Planning and Commissioning for Human-in-the-Loop Industrial Robotics with Digital Twins

author.name: Zhihao Liu, Victor Nan Fernandez-Ayala, Tianyu Wang, Qiang Qin, Xi Vincent Wang, Dimos V. Dimarogonas, Lihui Wang

entry.summary: This work proposes an agentic neuro-symbolic framework for human-in-the-loop industrial robotics, using LLMs for language and reasoning while keeping verification, sequencing, and execution deterministic. It adapts a Planner-Generator-Evaluator software pattern with failure recovery via LangGraph routing.

entry.title: LUNA-AD: Lightweight Uncertainty-Aware Language Model with Lifelong Learning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Ruoyu Yao, Pei Liu, Ruiguo Zhong, Mingxing Peng, Rui Yang, Jun Ma

entry.summary: LUNA-AD is a lightweight uncertainty-aware language model with lifelong learning for autonomous driving, using a tri-system architecture with a multi-agent demonstration generator and distilled dual-head heuristic model. It targets reasoning diversity, efficient deployment, and continual refinement in safety-critical driving.

entry.title: PTDL:Multi-Terrain Fall Recovery via Phase-Terrain Decoupled Learning

author.name: Xiaoyu Xu, Zhiming Chen, Yuenan Zhao, Ran Song, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: PTDL is a phase-terrain decoupled learning method for humanoid fall recovery and locomotion across multiple terrains using proprioception alone, decoupling training supervision along phase and terrain axes while deploying one policy. It handles the post-fall ground-contact phase often neglected by prior work.

entry.title: VGP-Nav: Metric-Aware Visual Geometric Perception for Robot Navigation

author.name: Hewei Pan, Weiye Zhu, Zekai Zhang, Zitong Huang, Rongtao Xu, Jinbao Wang, Feng Zheng

entry.summary: VGP-Nav is a vision-only navigation framework providing metric-aware visual geometric perception, achieving both globally consistent localization and dense metric-consistent obstacle perception from a monocular system without LiDAR. It avoids complex multi-sensor calibration.

entry.title: A Switching Beamformer for Highly Non-Stationary Environments

author.name: Manan Mittal, Ryan M. Corey, John R. Buck, Andrew C. Singer

entry.summary: This work introduces the Universal Switching Beamformer, integrating competitive sequential prediction into adaptive beamforming to resolve the memory trade-off between rapid tracking and stable interference rejection in highly non-stationary environments. It implicitly maintains an exponentially large family of candidate covariance histories.

entry.title: Contextual Identity Laundering: How Claude’s Image Refusal Can Be Routed Through Web Search

author.name: Failfinder70

entry.summary: This report documents two findings about Claude's photo-identification safety controls: its chain-of-thought identifies public figures while the output refuses to disclose, and its web search tool bypasses facial-recognition restrictions via contextual non-facial inference. It highlights a gap between internal processing and user-facing behavior and inconsistent policy enforcement.

entry.title: EditSR: Enhancing Neural Symbolic Regression via Edit-based Rectification

author.name: Da Li, Xinxin Li, Xingyu Cui, Jin Xu, Juan Zhang, Junping Yin

entry.summary: EditSR augments neural symbolic regression with an edit-based rectifier that post-hoc corrects structurally incorrect expressions without restarting global search, mitigating autoregressive error accumulation. It improves both accuracy and efficiency in symbolic equation discovery.

entry.title: DN-Hypo-Pipeline: An AI-Driven Workflow for Hypothesis Generation via Large Language Models and Scientific Explanations

author.name: Lei Lin, Ronghao Wang, Chunbao Zhou, Jue Wang, Yangang Wang

entry.summary: DN-Hypo-Pipeline is an LLM-based workflow for scientific hypothesis generation that uses the deductive-nomological model, identifying underlying laws and theories from a paper's conclusion to reconstruct new testable explanations. It supports structured scientific reasoning grounded in scientific explanations.

entry.title: Structure-Conditioned Actor-Critic Branches for Quality-Diversity Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Lianrong Zuo, Peilan Xu, Yong Liu, Wenjian Luo

entry.summary: SV-QD-RL is a structure-value coupled framework for quality-diversity RL that represents each candidate as a structure-conditioned actor-critic branch with a structural mask, branch-specific critic, and evaluation attributes. It focuses on the under-explored learning branches that generate candidate policies.

entry.title: Order Matters: Unveiling the Hidden Impact of Macro Placement Sequences via Proxy-Guided LLM Evolution

author.name: Shibing Mo, Jing Liu, Jianchu Xu, Ruilin Wu

entry.summary: OrderPlace shows that the macro placement sequence in chip design is a decisive optimization factor, not just preprocessing, and proposes a proxy-guided LLM evolution framework to discover good placement orderings. It demonstrates irreversible domino effects from early placement decisions.

entry.title: Deterministic Integrity Gates for LLM-Assisted Clinical Manuscript Preparation: An Auditable Biomedical Informatics Architecture

author.name: Yoojin Nam, Jinhoon Jeong, Namkug Kim

entry.summary: This paper proposes an auditable architecture for LLM-assisted clinical manuscript preparation that pairs generation with deterministic, re-executable integrity gates that halt on failure to catch fabricated citations, drifting numbers, and unmet reporting-guideline items. It uses the cheapest sufficient verification mechanism per integrity question.

entry.title: Beyond Probabilistic Similarity: Structural, Temporal, and Causal Limitations of Retrieval-Augmented Generation in the Legal Domain

author.name: Hudson de Martim

entry.summary: This paper argues that RAG failures in legal AI (fabricated citations, anachronistic content) are not residual confabulations but symptoms of an architectural mismatch between probabilistic retrieval and the hierarchical, temporal, and institutional structure of legal knowledge. It grounds the argument in classical legal theory.

entry.title: Phantom transitions in language model fine-tuning

author.name: Vaibhav Prakash, Jayasri Dontabhaktuni

entry.summary: Studies a silent failure in fine-tuning where cross-entropy loss decreases monotonically yet the correct token never overtakes a near-synonym competitor, introducing an order parameter that decomposes into signal and embedding background drag. Identifies distinct failure modes across five transformers.

entry.title: Contribution Weights: A Geometrical Analysis of Self-Attention Transformers

author.name: Harry Jake Cunningham, Nicola Muca Cirone

entry.summary: Introduces Contribution Weights, a projection-based interpretability metric quantifying token influence by combining attention weight, value magnitude, and directional alignment with layer output. Shows it identifies semantically critical tokens more faithfully than attention-based metrics across decoder-only models.

entry.title: "So There's a Catch-22 Here": How Early Adopters Who Build Multi-Agent LLM Systems Conceptualize Transparency

author.name: Suchismita Naik, Samir Passi, Mihaela Vorvoreanu, Scott Saponas, Amanda Hall

entry.summary: This empirical study interviews 13 early adopters who build and use multi-agent LLM systems at a large tech org to understand how they conceptualize transparency. Thematic analysis reveals divergent framings including reproducibility, debugging, boundary-setting, and visualization.

entry.title: Set-Based Transformer for Atmospheric Compensation in Standoff LWIR Hyperspectral Imaging

author.name: Fabian Perez, Nicolas Quintero, Jeferson Acevedo, Hoover Rueda-Chacon

entry.summary: This paper presents a lightweight set-based transformer for atmospheric compensation in standoff long-wave infrared hyperspectral imaging, taking multiple radiance measurements at different ranges to jointly estimate transmittance, path radiance, and downwelling spectrum. A sparse autoencoder analysis reveals interpretable latent features.

entry.title: How Many Counterfactuals Does It Take? Probing VLM Hallucinations Through Circuits and Causal Effects

author.name: Abhivansh Gupta, Simardeep Singh, Advika Sinha, Shreyansh Modi, Akshat Tomar

entry.summary: Studies the sample complexity of counterfactual robustness for VLM hallucinations using a causal influence metric based on log-probability differences and circuit discovery to identify responsible components. Probes how stable hallucinated predictions are under perturbations.

entry.title: BareWave: Waveform-Native Flow-Matching Text-to-Speech

author.name: Wei Fan, Chao-Hong Tan, Qian Chen, Wen Wang, Xiangang Li, Kejiang Chen, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: BareWave is a fully waveform-native flow-matching text-to-speech framework that generates raw waveforms directly without intermediate acoustic representations. It tackles training challenges of lacking pretrained scaffolds and aligning perceptual and velocity-space objectives.

entry.title: EgoTactile: Learning Grasp Pressure for Everyday Objects from Egocentric Video

author.name: Yuan Zeng, Yujia Shi, Tiao Tan, Xingting Li, Yaqi Qin, Zongqing Lu, Wenming Yang, Jing-Hao Xue, Qingmin Liao

entry.summary: EgoTactile introduces a benchmark pairing egocentric video with full-hand grasp pressure supervision for diverse everyday objects, including a bare-hand transfer subset. It establishes discriminative and diffusion-based baselines (EgoPressureFormer, EgoPressureDiff) for estimating grasp pressure without intrusive sensors.

entry.title: Context-Aware Deep Learning for Defect Classification in Atomic-Resolution STEM

author.name: Jiadong Dan, Cheng Zhang, Leyi Loh, Ivan Verzhbitskiy, Yuan Chen, Goki Eda, Michel Bosman, N. Duane Loh

entry.summary: Develops a context-aware deep learning framework for defect classification in atomic-resolution STEM that integrates image contrast with metadata on composition, beam energy, and detector geometry. Trained on ~55M simulated patches across doped TMD materials, it resolves ambiguities that contrast-only methods miss.

entry.title: SecureClaw: Clawing Back Control of LLM Agents

author.name: Yuhan Ma, Stefan Schmid

entry.summary: Presents SecureClaw, a dual-boundary security architecture for tool-using LLM agents placing authorization at the effect sink and plaintext confinement at the read boundary. Sensitive reads pass through a trusted gateway replacing raw values with opaque handles.

entry.title: Hybrid Robustness Verification for Spatio-Temporal Neural Networks

author.name: Sherwin Varghese, Matthew Wicker, Alessio Lomuscio

entry.summary: Proposes hybrid robustness verification for spatio-temporal neural networks (3D CNNs on video and volumetric inputs) that exploits structured spatial-temporal correlations rather than overly conservative lp-norm perturbations. Targets safety-critical applications in action recognition and autonomous driving.

entry.title: FASE: Fast Adaptive Semantic Entropy for Code Quality

author.name: Shizhe Lin, Ladan Tahvildari

entry.summary: Proposes FASE, a fast adaptive semantic entropy metric for code quality that approximates functional correctness via minimum spanning trees of structural and semantic dissimilarity graphs, avoiding costly LLM-driven equivalence checks. Outperforms state-of-the-art semantic entropy methods on HumanEval and BigCodeBench.

entry.title: AHA-WAM:Asynchronous Horizon-Adaptive World-Action Modeling with Observation-Guided Context Routing

author.name: Jisong Cai, Long Ling, Shiwei Chu, Zhongshan Liu, Jiayue Kang, Zhixuan Liang, Wenjie Xu, Yinan Mao, Weinan Zhang, Xiaokang Yang, Ru Ying, Ran Zheng, Yao Mu

entry.summary: Proposes AHA-WAM, an asynchronous horizon-adaptive world-action model on a dual Diffusion Transformer architecture that decouples world prediction and action execution temporal resolutions. It argues binding both to the same rhythm underutilizes the video branch for embodied control.

entry.title: A Framework for Evaluating and Benchmarking Concept Drift Detection Methods

author.name: Vitor Cerqueira, Heitor Murilo Gomes, Marco Heyden, Bernhard Pfahringer, Albert Bifet

entry.summary: Presents a benchmarking framework for concept drift detection featuring Monte Carlo drift injection into real datasets, a standardized evaluation protocol, and transparent hyperparameter handling. It addresses inconsistent evaluation across the data-stream mining field.

entry.title: AttentionCap: Transformer Based Capacitance Matrix Learning Toward Full-Chip Extraction

author.name: Jiechen Huang, Hector R. Rodriguez, Dingcheng Yang, Zuochang Ye, Yibo Lin, Wenjian Yu

entry.summary: Introduces AttentionCap, a transformer for capacitance matrix learning in chip extraction with a Gram representation, physics-aligned symmetric-attention output, normalized Laplacian loss, and process-node embeddings for multi-node learning. It overcomes fixed-layer constraints of MLP/CNN methods toward full-chip extraction.

entry.title: De novo molecular generation with optical property preconditioning at the token level

author.name: Haozhe Huang, Manuel Gonzalez Lastre, Hyun Suk Park, Jorge A. Campos-Gonzalez-Angulo, Xinjian Liu, Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik

entry.summary: Benchmarks a token-conditioned autoregressive GPT2 model for OLED molecule generation in a low-data regime, conditioning on absorption energy and oscillator strength with HOMO-LUMO gap as auxiliary descriptor. Generated molecules are validated at the TDDFT level for controllability and fidelity.

entry.title: Titans-as-a-Layer: Test-Time Memory for Conversational Speech Emotion Recognition

author.name: Daniel Chen, Qicong Hu, Yang Xiao, Ting Dang, Hong Jia

entry.summary: Introduces a Titans-based Memory-as-a-Layer adapter that adds test-time neural memory to large audio-language models for conversational speech emotion recognition, supplying per-dialogue context while keeping the backbone frozen. It writes dialogue history into a small neural memory read back as audio-token-aligned residuals.

entry.title: Hierarchical Projection for Adaptive Knowledge Transfer

author.name: Samhita Pal, Tian Gu

entry.summary: Proposes Projection Transfer Learning (ProjectionTL), integrating hierarchical Bayesian modeling with adaptive projection for selective knowledge transfer from heterogeneous sources to a limited target. It decouples transfer via a source-guided prior and projection to avoid negative transfer from spurious signals.

entry.title: Asymptotic Optimality of Thompson Sampling for Risk-Averse Bandits with Sub-Gaussian Rewards

author.name: Joel Q. L. Chang

entry.summary: Proves asymptotic optimality of a nonparametric Thompson Sampling algorithm for risk-averse bandits across general continuous risk functionals (CVaR, mean-variance, Sharpe) under only weak continuity conditions. Extends optimality guarantees beyond prior parametric/Lipschitz results. Theoretical bandit contribution.

entry.title: PRISM: Topology-Aware Cross-Modal Imputation for Modality-Deficient Federated Graph Learning

author.name: Zekai Chen, Miao Zhang, Jiayang Xing, Xunkai Li, Xun Wu, Rong-Hua Li, Guoren Wang

entry.summary: PRISM addresses client-level modality deficiency in multimodal federated graph learning, where clients lack entire modalities, via topology-aware cross-modal imputation that accounts for how imputation errors propagate through message passing. Tackles a realistic distributed setting. Relevant to federated multimodal learning.

entry.title: Algorithm for Contextual Queueing Bandits with Rate-Optimal Queue Length Regret

author.name: Seoungbin Bae, Dabeen Lee

entry.summary: Improves contextual queueing bandit regret from T^{-1/4} to T^{-1/2} queue length regret via a three-phase algorithm that uses random exploration only up to a chosen cutoff round. Theoretical advance in learning to schedule under unknown context-dependent service rates. Specialized bandit/queueing theory.

entry.title: MOLOT System Card: Malicious Operational Logic Observation Transformer

author.name: Daniil Lopatkin, Maksim Mitrofanov, Stanislav Rakovsky, Aleksandr Khalikov

entry.summary: Presents MOLOT, a static malicious-code detection system that represents source code as behavior sequences from static call graphs and ranks suspicious activities for explainability. Evaluated on PyPI/npm packages and accompanied by a public Open Malicious-Code Bench.

entry.title: Pointwise Complexity for Gaussian Fields: Upper Envelopes, Algorithmic Lower Bounds, and Separation

author.name: Yunbei Xu

entry.summary: Proves a variance-aware pointwise majorizing-measure theorem for centered Gaussian processes, generalizing generic chaining to give simultaneous high-probability envelopes for the entire field. Also records a Bayesian algorithmic lower bound and separation result.

entry.title: Bayesian Optimization of a Multi-Product Chemical Reactor Using Composite Models and Partial Physics Knowledge

author.name: Liqiu Dong, Marta Zag\'orowska, Mehmet Mercang\"oz

entry.summary: Studies data-driven real-time economic optimization of a multi-product chemical reactor using a composite Bayesian optimization formulation where GPs predict physical outputs and profit is computed analytically. Preserves economic-objective structure, remains parametric in prices without retraining, and incorporates partial physics via energy balance.

entry.title: Speaker-Invariant Representation Learning for Spoofing Detection via Gradient Reversal and A Variational Information Bottleneck

author.name: Anh-Tuan Dao, Driss Matrouf, Mickael Rouvier, Nicholas Evans

entry.summary: Proposes a teacher-student framework for speaker-invariant spoofing detection that disentangles speaker identity using gradient reversal and a variational information bottleneck without requiring speaker labels. Argues poor out-of-domain generalization stems from speaker bias where models learn voice traits rather than manipulation markers.

entry.title: Multi-Armed Bandits with Arriving Arms: Sequential Screening, Dynamic Regret, and Sublinear Guarantees

author.name: Deqi Zheng, Xiaoyang Xu, Yuhong Yang

entry.summary: Studies a multi-armed bandit problem where the set of arms expands over time, evaluating performance against the best currently-available arm via a dynamic-regret criterion. Proposes UCB-AA, an elimination-based procedure with preliminary screening for new arms, and proves sublinear regret guarantees.

entry.title: Whose Norms? Disentangling Cultural and Personal Alignment in Large Language Models

author.name: Angana Borah, Isabelle Augenstein, Rada Mihalcea

entry.summary: Introduces PACT to disentangle cultural-norm versus personal-preference alignment in LLMs, finding behavior shifts more by country context than by age or gender. Studies how instruction tuning non-uniformly alters norm enforcement.

entry.title: SurgiQ: A Large-Scale Multi-Domain Benchmark for Evaluating Surgical Understanding in Large Language Models

author.name: Ayah Al-Naji, Edoardo Fazzari, Saif Alkindi, Hamdan Alhadhrami, Preslav Nakov, Cesare Stefanini

entry.summary: Presents SurgiQ, a large multi-domain benchmark of 13,055 surgical MCQs testing procedural reasoning, negation, and operative decisions beyond general medical knowledge, evaluating 35 open-weight LLMs. Reveals substantial remaining gaps in surgical understanding.

entry.title: When Correct Decisions Hide Internal Stress: Decision-State Probing in Multimodal Language Models

author.name: Haoran Zhao, Soyeon Caren Han, Eduard Hovy

entry.summary: Introduces S3E, a framework probing whether multimodal models' internal decision states remain stable under semantic stress even when external behavior is correct. Reveals behavior-internal decoupling using pre-answer hidden states in forced-choice setups.

entry.title: AsyncLane: Decoupling Refinement from Advancement in Diffusion Language Model Decoding

author.name: Yingxuan Ren, Yuxuan Lou, Yong Liu, Pengcheng Fang, Ziming Wang, Pengfei Zhou, Yang You

entry.summary: Proposes AsyncLane, a training-free decoding scheduler for diffusion LLMs that decouples block refinement from advancement, allowing continuation to begin once a stable delimiter or prefix appears. Improves inference efficiency over strict block-wise dependencies.

entry.title: LexRubric: A Rubric-Guided Diagnostic Benchmark for Open-Ended Legal Tasks

author.name: Yifan Chen, Haitao Li, Yiran Hu, Kaisong Song, Jun Lin, Yueyue Wu, Qingyao Ai, Min Zhang, Yiqun Liu

entry.summary: LexRubric is a rubric-based diagnostic benchmark for open-ended Chinese legal tasks with 649 instances and over 12,000 expert-written atomic scoring criteria across 14 legal scenarios. It enables fine-grained identification of legal response quality failures.

entry.title: When Built-in Thinking Helps and Hurts: Constraint-Level Error Shifts in Instruction Following

author.name: Sai Adith Senthil Kumar

entry.summary: Studies how built-in thinking modes affect instruction following using Qwen3 models with Thinking ON/OFF controls on IFEval, finding small aggregate changes but 10-20% of prompts flipping between pass and fail. It identifies that thinking improves planning constraints but harms precision constraints.

entry.title: ChinaHeritaQA: A Culturally-Grounded Visual Question Answering Dataset for World Heritage Sites in China

author.name: Yi Zhang, Bolei Ma, Yong Cao, Chengyan Wu, Daniel Hershcovich, Anna-Carolina Haensch

entry.summary: ChinaHeritaQA is a multimodal benchmark of 2,279 in-the-wild images and 14,133 bilingual QA pairs for evaluating cultural reasoning of VLMs on UNESCO World Heritage sites in China, spanning seven cognitive dimensions. Evaluations show top models exceed human average but vary substantially by task.

entry.title: Readable Yet Unpredictable: Rotated-Outcome Prediction in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Lexin Wang, Shenghua Liu, Yiwei Wang, Jiafeng Guo, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: Studies whether VLMs can predict what a 180-degree rotation would reveal from an original image alone, introducing RotOutBench. It finds models can recognize content when directly shown either orientation but collapse to near-zero accuracy when inferring rotated results.

entry.title: Simultaneous hyperkinetic movement disorders phenotyping: a cross-cohort pediatric transfer study using routine videos, markerless pose estimation and a tabular foundation model

author.name: Laura Cif, Diane Demailly, Zohra Souei, Muhammad Mushhood Ur Rehman, Juan Dario Ortigoza Escobar, Mayt\'e Castro Jim\'enez, C\'ecile A. Hubsch, Sophie Huby, Morgan Dornadic, Gun-Marie Hariz, Eduardo M. Moraud, Jocelyne Bloch, Gabriella A. Horvath, Xavier Vasques

entry.summary: Develops a video-based framework for simultaneous detection of multiple hyperkinetic movement disorder phenomenologies, combining markerless pose estimation, kinematic descriptors, and a pretrained tabular foundation model. It explicitly tests cross-cohort transfer from adults to pediatric populations.

entry.title: Reason Twice: Segmentation via Candidate Discovery and Comparative Reasoning

author.name: Xinyan Gao, Haoran Hao, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: Rea2Seg is a two-stage reasoning segmentation framework that discovers candidate masks from MLLM attention maps then uses comparative reasoning to select the correct one. It addresses limited training data and the gap between MLLMs and mask generators.

entry.title: RT-SDGOD: Real-Time Single-Domain Generalized Object Detection

author.name: Yupeng Zhang, Fangzhuo Gao, Ruize Han, Wei Feng, Liang Wan

entry.summary: RT-SDGOD formulates single-domain generalized object detection under strict real-time constraints, requiring cross-domain robustness with zero extra inference overhead via training-time representation learning. It analyzes DETR-based real-time detector degradation under domain shift.

entry.title: MAVIS: Multi-Agent Video Retrieval via Structured Video Understanding

author.name: Jie Zhang, Qilang Ye, Hao Zhou, Haochen Liang, Fei Luo

entry.summary: MAVIS reframes video retrieval as cooperative multi-agent reasoning, parsing videos into a structured semantic library for attribute-level indexing and decomposing queries into sub-tasks dispatched to specialized agents. It targets efficiency and semantic asymmetry issues of embedding-based scanning.

entry.title: GenEyePose: Patient-Free, Knowledge-Based Saccadic Eye Movement Modeling for Digital Neurophysiologic Biomarker Development

author.name: Tianyu Lin, Jooyoung Ryu, Puvada Sreevarsha, Rahul Srinivasaragavan, Riya Satavlekar, Susan Kim, Nidhi Soley, Yujie Yan, Ishan Vatsaraj, Carl Harris, Aimon Rahman, Vishal Patel, Joseph Greenstein, Casey Taylor, Kemar E. Green

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Poisoned Data Detector as an active defense to ensure integrity of self-supervised curated datasets for foundation models, mitigating data poisoning risks from unvetted external sources. It targets robustness of SSL-based data curation pipelines.

entry.title: Personalized and Robust Proactive Robot Assistance with Uncertainty-Guided LLM Reasoning

author.name: Alvaro Gonzalez, M. H. Hasan Shovo, Ali Ayub

entry.summary: GLOBE is a lightweight framework for proactive household robot assistance combining n-gram Markov models for temporal patterns with uncertainty-guided LLM reasoning invoked only when confidence is low. It introduces HOMER-Noise, a noisy benchmark for realistic evaluation.
