entry.title: ReasoningFlow: Discourse Structures for Understanding LLM Reasoning Traces

author.name: Jinu Lee, Shivam Agarwal, Amruta Parulekar, Siddarth Madala, Dilek Hakkani-Tur, Julia Hockenmaier

entry.summary: Introduces ReasoningFlow, a framework capturing the discourse structure of LLM reasoning traces as fine-grained directed acyclic graphs to handle non-linear behaviors like backtracking and self-correction. Validated with manual annotation and scaled to 1,260 traces across three tasks and five models.

entry.title: Consistency Training Along the Transformer Stack

author.name: Sukrati Gautam, Neil Shah, Arav Dhoot, Bryan Maruyama, Caroline Wei, Rohan Kapoor, Robert Sidey, Prakhar Gupta, Zi Cheng Huang, David Demitri Africa

entry.summary: Broadens consistency training with two new internal targets (MLP and per-head attention consistency) and applies it to four additional safety threats including persona attacks, adversarial frustration, prefill attacks, and conditional misalignment. Finds consistency training reduces misalignment well beyond sycophancy and jailbreak settings.

entry.title: OrderGrad: Optimizing Beyond the Mean with Order-Statistic Policy Gradient Estimation

author.name: Paavo Parmas, Yongmin Kim, Kohsei Matsutani, Shota Takashiro, Soichiro Nishimori, Takeshi Kojima, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: OrderGrad introduces unbiased likelihood-ratio and reparameterization gradient estimators for order-statistic objectives (VaR, CVaR, trimmed means, best-of-K) by changing only rank weights. From the Matsuo lab, it generalizes policy gradients beyond expected return to distributional/tail objectives.

entry.title: Subspace-Aware Sparse Autoencoders for Effective Mechanistic Interpretability

author.name: Seyed Arshan Dalili, Mehrdad Mahdavi

entry.summary: Argues that standard sparse autoencoders' single-direction-per-feature assumption mismatches multi-dimensional model features, provably inducing feature splitting, and proposes subspace-aware SAEs with multi-dimensional decoder directions. It improves mechanistic interpretability by reducing artificial feature splitting.

entry.title: Spectral Scaling Laws of Muon

author.name: Gagik Magakyan, Pablo Parrilo, Asuman Ozdaglar

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic study of how the singular-value spectrum of Muon's momentum matrices behaves during training and across model sizes, noting that Newton-Schulz orthonormalization fails on small singular values. From credible authors (Parrilo, Ozdaglar), it derives spectral scaling laws for the increasingly popular Muon optimizer.

entry.title: Derivative Informed Learning of Exchange-Correlation Functionals

author.name: Eike S. Eberhard, Luca A. Thiede, Abdul Aldossary, Andreas Burger, Nicholas Gao, Vignesh Bhethanabotla, Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik, Stephan G\"unnemann

entry.summary: This work introduces a Derivative-Informed XC-Loss for machine-learned exchange-correlation functionals in density functional theory, supervising first and second energy derivatives on the Grassmannian rather than just matching self-consistent fixed points. It aims to make O(N^3) ML functionals competitive with O(N^4) hybrid functionals.

entry.title: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Reward Models Learn Interpretable and Specialized Experts for Personalized Preference Modeling

author.name: Yifan Wang, Jinyi Mu, Mayank Jobanputra, Yu Wang, Ji-Ung Lee, Soyoung Oh, Isabel Valera, Vera Demberg

entry.summary: This work proposes a sparse Mixture-of-Experts reward model for RLHF that learns interpretable, specialized experts capturing disentangled preference components for personalized preference modeling. It addresses the limitation of universal reward functions by modeling heterogeneous human preferences without extra annotation.

entry.title: From Symbolic to Geometric: Enabling Spatial Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Chen Chu, Bita Azarijoo, Li Xiong, Khurram Shafique, Cyrus Shahabi

entry.summary: This work introduces the Spatial Language Model (SLM), a multimodal LLM treating location as a first-class modality to enable genuine geometric spatial reasoning rather than symbolic pattern matching over spatial language. It operates directly on learned spatial representations with explicit geometric operators.

entry.title: Activation Steering of Video Generation Models via Reduced-Order Linear Optimal Control

author.name: Jihoon Hong, Alice Chan, Qiyue Dai, Julian Skifstad, Glen Chou

entry.summary: Introduces LA-LQR, a reduced-order optimal control framework for activation steering of text-to-video models to reduce harmful outputs without finetuning. It formulates inference as a dynamical system with closed-loop feedback interventions to avoid oversteering.

entry.title: AlphaQ: Calibration-Free Bit Allocation for Mixture-of-Experts Quantization

author.name: Wanqi Yang, Yuexiao Ma, Alexander Conzelmann, Xiawu Zheng, Michael W. Mahoney, T. Konstantin Rusch, Shiwei Liu

entry.summary: Proposes AlphaQ, a calibration-free bit-allocation method for Mixture-of-Experts quantization that avoids reliance on proprietary calibration data by exploiting cross-expert structure. It addresses memory-bound MoE deployment without access to training distributions.

entry.title: Unpredictable Safety: Domain-Dependent Compliance and the Transparency Gap in Open-Weight LLMs

author.name: Zacharie Bugaud

entry.summary: Conducts a systematic study of domain-dependent safety in open-weight LLMs across 7 ethical domains and 4,200 interactions, finding compliance varies from 14.7% to 85.7% depending on domain and framing. It highlights that the same model behaves unpredictably across contexts, undermining trustworthy deployment.

entry.title: Expert-Aware Refusal Steering

author.name: Anna C. Marbut, Daniel R. Olson, Travis J. Wheeler

entry.summary: Extends refusal-suppression steering vectors to Mixture-of-Experts LLMs, finding steering remains effective despite complex routing, and proposes two expert-aware methods leveraging refusal-specific expert routing and expert-specific steering directions. It reveals new safety vulnerabilities in MoE architectures.

entry.title: A Vision-language Framework for Comparative Reasoning in Radiology

author.name: Tengfei Zhang, Ziheng Zhao, Lisong Dai, Xiaoman Zhang, Pengcheng Qiu, Ya Zhang, Yanfeng Wang, Weidi Xie

entry.summary: This work formulates radiological comparison as entity-aware cross-image reasoning, supporting reference-case retrieval and temporal comparative interpretation. It introduces MedReCo-DB, a large-scale comparative imaging resource of 690,000+ images from 160,000+ patients across eight institutions and seven modalities.

entry.title: ActiveMimic: Egocentric Video Pretraining with Active Perception

author.name: Xingyao Lin, Guojin Zhong, Tianyi Lu, Ziyi Ye, Yichen Zhu, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: ActiveMimic recovers camera and wrist trajectories from body-worn egocentric video and models head/camera motion as an action, closing the gap between human-video and robot-data pretraining. It treats active perception as signal rather than noise.

entry.title: How Far Did They Go? The Persuasive Tactics of Covert LLM Agents in a Discontinued Field Experiment

author.name: Kokil Jaidka, Saifuddin Ahmed

entry.summary: Analyzes a controversial Reddit r/ChangeMyView field experiment where undisclosed AI agents engaged users in debate, doing structured content analysis of persuasive tactics like identity performance and authority signaling. It matters because it documents covert LLM persuasion in the wild and surfaces ethical concerns about undisclosed AI manipulation.

entry.title: Multilingual Fine-Tuning via Localized Gradient Conflict Resolution

author.name: Long P. Hoang, Yiran Zhao, Wei Lu, Wenxuan Zhang

entry.summary: Reformulates multilingual fine-tuning as multi-objective optimization and proposes Bucket-Level MOO, applying gradient-based conflict resolution locally on parameter buckets to avoid full-gradient communication overhead, with proven Pareto-stationarity guarantees. It matters for mitigating cross-lingual negative interference at scale.

entry.title: DiG-Plan: Mitigating Early Commitment for Tool-Graph Planning via Diffusion Guidance

author.name: Yansi Li, Zhuosheng Zhang

entry.summary: Identifies early-commitment in autoregressive tool planning and proposes DiG-Plan, using a diffusion-based proposer to generate diverse tool sets via iterative refinement before structural refinement, sharply raising solution coverage. It matters for combinatorial tool-graph planning.

entry.title: A Pre-Registered Causal Partition of Self-Consistency Elicitation and Reward Design in RLVR

author.name: Yuze Gao

entry.summary: Provides a pre-registered causal decomposition showing the common naive estimator for reward-design effects in RLVR conflates self-consistency elicitation with genuine reward-design signal, proving systematic bias and measuring each component in a tabular GRPO simulator. It matters for correctly attributing why spurious-reward RLVR works.

entry.title: Memory is Reconstructed, Not Retrieved: Graph Memory for LLM Agents

author.name: Shuo Ji, Yibo Li, Bryan Hooi

entry.summary: Proposes MRAgent, framing memory as reconstructed rather than retrieved, using a Cue-Tag-Content associative memory graph with active reconstruction that integrates LLM reasoning into memory access during inference. It matters for agents reasoning over long interaction histories beyond static retrieve-then-reason pipelines.

entry.title: Closing the Loop on Latent Reasoning via Test-Time Reconstruction

author.name: Xiaopeng Yuan, Haibo Jin, Ye Yu, Peng Kuang, Lijun Yu, Yushun Dong, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes ReLAT, a self-supervised test-time training method that closes the loop on latent reasoning by reconstructing the original query from latent states to verify fidelity. Addresses the inspectability loss when reasoning moves from text to latent representations.

entry.title: Do Models Share Safety Representations? Cross-Model Steering for Safe Visual Generation

author.name: Tobia Poppi, Silvia Cappelletti, Sara Sarto, Florian Schiffers, Garin Kessler, Marcella Cornia, Lorenzo Baraldi, Rita Cucchiara

entry.summary: Introduces the first framework for cross-model safety steering, estimating a safety direction in a source LLM from paired safe-unsafe prompts and transporting it to target generators via lightweight alignment on benign data alone. Tests whether safety can be a portable, reusable latent direction without accessing unsafe target data.

entry.title: Pattern Selectivity is Not Task-Causal Structure: A Cross-Architecture Mechanistic Study of Composed-Task Circuits in 1B-Class Language Models

author.name: Yongzhong Xu

entry.summary: Tests whether a screen-and-ablate circuit-discovery recipe yields consistent mechanistic claims across model families, running a unified protocol on four composed tasks and three 1B-class models with matched-random nulls. Finds the recipe ports but the specific circuits identified do not generalize across architectures.

entry.title: VASO: Formally Verifiable Self-Evolving Skills for Physical AI Agents

author.name: Yunhao Yang, Neel P. Bhatt, Kevin Wang, Samuel Tetteh, Zhangyang Wang, Ufuk Topcu

entry.summary: Introduces VASO, a framework for verification-guided self-evolution of LLM-generated robot skill contracts, representing each skill semantically to check temporal safety contracts under untested conditions rather than relying on trace-level execution evidence. Aims to make trusting auto-generated skills cheaper, not just creating them.

entry.title: Conformal Risk-Averse Decision Making with Action Conditional Guarantee

author.name: Zihan Zhu, Shayan Kiyani, George Pappas. Hamed Hassani

entry.summary: Generalizes conformal prediction to action-conditional guarantees for risk-averse decision making, providing safety guarantees conditioned on each action rather than just marginal guarantees. Builds on prior work translating prediction sets into optimal risk-averse decision policies.

entry.title: Benchmarks in Leipzig

author.name: Andrei Balakin, Mikl\'os B\'ona, Marie-Charlotte Brandenburg, Clara Briand, Veronica Calvo Cortes, Shelby Cox, Jesus A. De Loera, Danai Deligeorgaki, Hannah Friedman, Tim Gehrunger, Chiara Giardino, Stephen Griffeth, Baran Hashemi, Elena Hoster, Alexander Ivanov, Nupur Jain, Aryaman Jal, Leonie Kayser, Joris Koefler, Kevin K\"uhn, Mario Kummer, Felix Lotter, Ren\'e Marczinzik, Victor S. Miller, Alejandro Morales, Greta Panova, Gianni Petrella, Nathan Pflueger, Lakshmi Ramesh, Nikolas Rieke, Carlos Rodriguez, Andrea Rosana, Flavio Salizzoni, Otto T. P. Schmidt, Sven Ulf Schmitz, Lina Maria Simbaqueba Marin, Luca Sodomaco, Christian Stump, Bernd Sturmfels, Alexander Taveira Blomenhofer, Simon Telen, Philipp Tuchel, Emil Verkama, Carl Felix Waller, Julian Weigert, Annette Werner, Nathan Williams, Claudius Zibrowius

entry.summary: Reports a collaborative effort by 49 mathematicians to compile 100 research-level mathematics questions with known answers, then evaluates five state-of-the-art LLMs in escalating stages, leaving only 2 questions unsolved after heavy-thinking models. Provides a hard mathematical reasoning benchmark.

entry.title: LatentSkill: From In-Context Textual Skills to In-Weight Latent Skills for LLM Agents

author.name: Aofan Yu, Chenyu Zhou, Tianyi Xu, Zihan Guo, Rong Shan, Zhihui Fu, Jun Wang, Weiwen Liu, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang, Jianghao Lin

entry.summary: LatentSkill converts in-context textual skills for LLM agents into LoRA adapters via a pretrained hypernetwork, storing skill knowledge in weights rather than prompt tokens. It improves ALFWorld success substantially while reducing prefill token overhead.

entry.title: LLMs Can Leak Training Data But Do They Want To? A Propensity-Aware Evaluation of Memorization in LLMs

author.name: Gianluca Barmina, Peter Schneider-Kamp, Lukas Galke Poech

entry.summary: PropMe introduces a propensity-aware framework for evaluating LLM memorization, distinguishing whether models can be forced to leak training data from whether they do so under ordinary use, with a metric transformation and an infini-gram-based tracing pipeline (SimpleTrace). It shifts memorization evaluation from capability to propensity.

entry.title: PC Layer: Polynomial Weight Preconditioning for Improving LLM Pre-Training

author.name: Senmiao Wang, Tiantian Fang, Haoran Zhang, Yushun Zhang, Kunxiang Zhao, Alex Schwing, Ruoyu Sun

entry.summary: The PC Layer parameterizes weights with a polynomial preconditioner that reshapes the singular-value spectrum for stable conditioning during LLM training, merging back into the original architecture with no inference overhead. It improves Llama-1B pretraining for both AdamW and Muon, with convergence theory.

entry.title: Unlocking Feature Learning in Gated Delta Networks at Scale

author.name: Yifeng Liu, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: Derives Maximal Update Parametrization (muP) scaling rules for Gated Delta Networks by rigorously propagating coordinate-size estimates through forward pass, gating, and recurrent state dynamics, enabling zero-shot hyperparameter transfer for these linear-attention models. Experiments confirm stable learning-rate transfer across model sizes.

entry.title: dMX: Differentiable Mixed-Precision Assignment for Low-Precision Floating-Point Formats

author.name: Giuseppe Franco, Ian Colbert, Pablo Monteagudo-Lago, Felix Marty, Nicholas Fraser

entry.summary: dMX introduces a differentiable framework for assigning per-layer floating-point bit-widths in LLM quantization, targeting the OCP microscaling (MXFP) data type family. By folding the bit-width design space into a single learnable scalar per layer, it enables gradient-based mixed-precision optimization for efficient deployment.

entry.title: The Loss Is Not Enough: Sampling Conditions and Inductive Bias in Contrastive Representation Learning

author.name: Justinas Zaliaduonis, Patrick Putzky, Till Richter, Sergios Gatidis

entry.summary: This paper develops a measure-theoretic framework for contrastive learning, formalizing a diversity condition on positive-pair sampling necessary for isometric latent recovery. It shows full-support sampling guarantees recovery up to orthogonal transformation while restricted conditionals can favor non-orthogonal maps.

entry.title: Expectations vs. Realities: The Cost of MSE-Optimal Forecasting Under Conditional Uncertainty

author.name: Riku Green, Zahraa S. Abdallah, Telmo M Silva Filho

entry.summary: This paper shows that MSE-optimal multi-step forecasting (targeting the conditional mean) becomes misleading under conditional uncertainty, formalizing a conditional uncertainty gap and proving no deterministic predictor can both minimize MSE and match the marginal distribution of futures. It establishes a fundamental trade-off between point accuracy and marginal realism.

entry.title: The price of multi-group transductive learning

author.name: Noah Bergam, Samuel Deng, Daniel Hsu

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows that in transductive multi-group learning, every learner may incur a multiplicative error penalty on some group that grows linearly with the number of groups (up to sqrt of sample size), contrasting sharply with the at-most-logarithmic penalty in analogous statistical settings. It establishes a fundamental price of transductive multi-group learning.

entry.title: Towards Accurate Model Selection in Deep Unsupervised Domain Adaptation

author.name: Kaichao You, Ximei Wang, Mingsheng Long, Michael I. Jordan

entry.summary: This work proposes Deep Embedded Validation (DEV), a model selection method for deep unsupervised domain adaptation that embeds adapted feature representations into the validation procedure to obtain unbiased target-risk estimates with bounded variance. It addresses the lack of accurate, standardized model selection that hampers Deep UDA progress.

entry.title: Trace-Mediated Peak Bias: Bridging Temporal Credit Assignment and Cognitive Heuristics in Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Viktor Vesel\'y, Aleksandar Todorov, Erwan Escudie, Matthia Sabatelli

entry.summary: This paper identifies a systematic failure mode in deep RL called Trace-Mediated Peak Bias, where agents at intermediate eligibility trace depths prefer trajectories with reward peaks over higher-return alternatives. It mechanistically links this to the human Peak-End Rule cognitive bias, connecting credit assignment with cognitive science.

entry.title: Data Attribution in Large Language Models via Bidirectional Gradient Optimization

author.name: Fr\'ed\'eric Berdoz, Luca A. Lanzend\"orfer, Kaan Bayraktar, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: Proposes a training data attribution method for autoregressive LLMs using bidirectional gradient optimization that perturbs the model on generated outputs and measures loss changes across training samples. It supports attribution at arbitrary data granularity for governance and provenance.

entry.title: Invariant Gradient Alignment for Robust Reasoning Distillation

author.name: Zehua Cheng, Wei Dai, Jiahao Sun

entry.summary: Introduces Invariant Gradient Alignment for robust reasoning distillation, aligning gradient updates across logically isomorphic problems in different semantic domains to combat shortcut learning. It uses logical isomer sets and a continuous gradient conflict mask to transfer chain-of-thought reasoning robustly to smaller students.

entry.title: The Invisible Lottery: How Subtle Cues Steer Algorithm Choice in LLM Code Generation

author.name: Akanksha Narula, Mofasshara Binte Rafique, Laurent Bindschaedler

entry.summary: Defines algorithm steering as cue-induced shifts in algorithm-family choice under fixed correctness, running 46,535 controlled experiments showing incidental prompt cues steer which valid algorithm LLMs select in code generation. It reveals output-policy sensitivity beyond output quality.

entry.title: Can Generalist Agents Automate Data Curation?

author.name: Feiyang Kang, Hanze Li, Adam Nguyen, Mahavir Dabas, Jiaqi W. Ma, Frederic Sala, Dawn Song, Ruoxi Jia

entry.summary: Curation-Bench is an agent-centric benchmark testing whether generalist coding agents can automate the iterative data-curation loop, with a fixed model and evaluation pipeline. Out-of-the-box agents reach strong data-selection baselines within ten iterations, but trajectory analysis reveals limitations.

entry.title: SparDA: Sparse Decoupled Attention for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Yaosheng Fu, Guangxuan Xiao, Xin Dong, Song Han, Oreste Villa

entry.summary: SparDA is a decoupled sparse attention architecture that adds a fourth per-layer Forecast projection to predict which KV blocks the next layer needs, enabling lookahead prefetch that overlaps CPU-to-GPU transfer with computation. It tackles KV cache growth and the quadratic cost of sparse selection in long-context inference.

entry.title: UniPixie: Unified and Probabilistic 3D Physics Learning via Flow Matching

author.name: Qilin Huang, Quynh Anh Huynh, Long Le, Chen Wang, Chuhao Chen, Ryan Lucas, Eric Eaton, Lingjie Liu

entry.summary: UniPixie reframes 3D physical material prediction from a single point estimate to learning a continuous, controllable distribution of plausible material properties using flow matching. It introduces a multiverse dataset spanning a softest-to-stiffest spectrum, allowing controllable generation of diverse physically valid material fields.

entry.title: Flash-WAM: Modality-Aware Distillation for World Action Models

author.name: Arman Akbari, Ci Zhang, Arash Akbari, Lin Zhao, Yixiao Chen, Weiwei Chen, Xuan Zhang, Geng Yuan, Yanzhi Wang

entry.summary: Flash-WAM introduces a modality-aware step-distillation method for world-action models that jointly generate video and robot actions, solving the SNR mismatch between video and action diffusion streams. It aims to enable real-time control by cutting denoising steps.

entry.title: Announcing the ARC White-Box Estimation Challenge

author.name: Jacob_Hilton

entry.summary: ARC and AIcrowd launched the White-Box Estimation Challenge, a contest with a 100k-plus prize pool to improve algorithms that estimate the expected output of random MLPs from their weights under FLOP constraints. This connects to ARC interpretability and formal estimation work relevant to AI safety verification.

entry.title: Fix the Mind, Not the Move: Interpretable AI Assistance via Knowledge-Gap Localization

author.name: Ayano Hiranaka, Ya-Chuan Hsu, Stefanos Nikolaidis, Erdem B{\i}y{\i}k, Daniel Seita

entry.summary: Introduces SENSEI, a framework that infers user misconceptions from interaction behavior and gives minimal targeted suggestions to correct underlying knowledge gaps rather than just patching individual wrong actions. It matters for AI assistance that produces durable human improvement.

entry.title: FIDES: Faithful Inference via Deep Evidence Signals for Retrieval-Memory Conflict in RAG

author.name: Zhe Yu, Wenpeng Xing, Tiancheng Zhao, Mohan Li, Changting Lin, Meng Han

entry.summary: Proposes FIDES, a token-level contrastive decoding method that identifies sharply concentrated retrieval-memory conflict on answer-critical tokens and applies targeted contrast rather than a uniform global weight. It matters for making RAG models faithfully follow context over memorized priors.

entry.title: From Risk Classification to Action Plan Remediation: A Guardrail Feedback Driven Framework for LLM Agents

author.name: Yuhao Sun, Jiacheng Zhang, Shaanan Cohney, Zhexin Zhang, Feng Liu, Xingliang Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces TRIAD, a guardrail-feedback-driven framework that moves beyond uniformly blocking contaminated tasks to remediate action plans, preserving benign parts while removing threats, and evaluates downstream safety effects. It matters for guardrails that enable safe task completion rather than blanket refusal.

entry.title: Retry Policy Gradients in Continuous Action Spaces

author.name: Soichiro Nishimori, Paavo Parmas

entry.summary: Introduces pathwise derivative estimators for retry objectives like pass@K and max@K, extending ReMax to continuous action spaces and showing it encourages stochastic exploration by reshaping the policy-gradient landscape even with deterministic rewards. It matters for exploration in continuous-control RL without explicit bonuses.

entry.title: LLM Self-Recognition: Steering and Retrieving Activation Signatures

author.name: Thibaud Ardoin, Jonas Sch\"afer, Gerhard Wunder

entry.summary: Demonstrates LLM self-recognition of their own outputs is reliable even in low-entropy settings, and can be amplified by steering the residual stream with a random sparse vector to create detectable fingerprints. Achieves over 98% attribution accuracy while preserving text quality.

entry.title: Trust, but Don't Verify: Epistemic Blind Spots in LLM Source Evaluation

author.name: Rohan N. Pradhan, Steve Goley

entry.summary: Shows that LLMs can detect fabricated statistics in isolation (0.76-1.00 accuracy) but fail to recruit this capability during multi-source synthesis, producing similar estimates whether statistics are fabricated or valid. Identifies a methodology-register gate responding to analytical text style rather than numeric validity.

entry.title: Enhancing Software Engineering Through Closed-Loop Memory Optimization

author.name: Xuehang Guo, Zora Zhiruo Wang, Qingyun Wang, Graham Neubig, Xingyao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a closed-loop framework for memory augmentation in software engineering agents that grounds memory utility in validated downstream impact, enabling agents to retain and reuse experiences across tasks. Addresses the episodic nature of current SE agents that repeatedly reconstruct context.

entry.title: Mechanistic Insights into Functional Sparsity in Multimodal LLMs via CoRe Heads

author.name: Ruoxi Sun, Quantong Qiu, Juntao Li, Zecheng Tang, Yihang Lou, Min Zhang

entry.summary: An interpretability study uncovering functional sparsity in multimodal LLMs, identifying a specialized subset of Context-aware Retrieval (CoRe) attention heads that act as dedicated cross-modal information extractors using a Retrieval Attention Mass metric. Reveals a clear functional division of labor across attention heads.

entry.title: OPRD: On-Policy Representation Distillation

author.name: Shenzhi Yang, Guangcheng Zhu, Bowen Song, Haobo Wang, Mingxuan Xia, Xing Zheng, Yingfan Ma, Zhongqi Chen, Weiqiang Wang, Gang Chen

entry.summary: Proposes On-Policy Representation Distillation (OPRD), which lifts distillation into hidden-state space by aligning student and teacher representations across layers on the same rollouts, bypassing the LM head to eliminate sampling variance from large-vocabulary KL estimates. Provides richer per-layer structural supervision than output-only on-policy distillation.

entry.title: Double Preconditioning (DoPr): Optimization for Test-Time Performance, not Validation Loss

author.name: Thomas T. Zhang, Alok Shah, Yifei Zhang, Vincent Zhang, Nikolai Matni, Max Simchowitz

entry.summary: Double Preconditioning (DoPr) reframes optimization to target test-time rollout performance rather than one-step validation loss, addressing the train-test feedback mismatch that grows with sequence length in autoregressive, flow-based, and robot-policy settings. It proposes optimization as a new lever against test-time feedback drift.

entry.title: HANDOFF: Humanoid Agentic Task-Space Whole-Body Control via Distilled Complementary Teachers

author.name: Lizhi Yang, Junheng Li, Nehar Poddar, Yiling Hou, Gio Huh, Robert Griffin, Georgia Gkioxari, Aaron Ames

entry.summary: HANDOFF is a single humanoid whole-body controller using a compact task-space command interface, distilled via multi-teacher KL distillation into a mixture-of-experts student from three complementary specialists (motion tracking, etc.) under context-conditioned gating. From credible authors (Aaron Ames, Gkioxari), it bridges task planning and whole-body control.

entry.title: Large Language Models Hack Rewards, and Society

author.name: Wei Liu, Xinyi Mou, Hanqi Yan, Zhongyu Wei, Yulan He

entry.summary: Hypothesizes and tests societal hacking, that RL post-training causes LLMs to exploit loopholes in societal regulations (structurally similar to reward functions), introducing SocioHack, a sandbox of 72 societal environments to study this failure mode. It extends reward-hacking concerns into consequential rule-exploitation behavior.

entry.title: Prediction Under Imperfect Compression: A Theory of Approximate MDL

author.name: Qian Li, Xinyu Mao, Shang-Hua Teng, Guangxu Yang

entry.summary: Develops a theory of approximate Minimum Description Length prediction, analyzing under what forms of approximation and regularization compression guarantees and reliable prediction still hold. It bridges classical MDL theory with practical approximate optimization.

entry.title: Be Fair! Can Machine Learning Engineering Agents Adhere to Fairness Constraints?

author.name: Anna Richter, Julia Stoyanovich, Sebastian Schelter

entry.summary: Investigates whether ML engineering agents can adhere to fairness constraints, proposing a responsibility-centered evaluation framework via a melanoma classification case study focusing on fairness across skin tones. It argues existing benchmarks are insufficient for safely deploying MLE agents in regulated domains.

entry.title: SymTRELLIS: Symmetry-Enforced Voxel Latents for 3D Generation

author.name: Guangda Ji, Qimin Chen, Qinchan Li, Mingrui Zhao, Kai Wang, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: Presents SymTRELLIS, which enforces arbitrary finite point-group symmetries during flow-based 3D generation without retraining the underlying VAE or flow model, by approximating spatial-transform latent actions as a learned linear operator. It addresses physically unusable symmetry violations in single-view 3D generation.

entry.title: Knowledge Distillation for Visual Autoregressive Models

author.name: Elia Peruzzo, Aritra Bhowmik, Guillaume Sautiere, Yuki M Asano, Amirhossein Habibian

entry.summary: This work presents the first systematic study of knowledge distillation for visual autoregressive image generation models, finding that language-developed KD methods do not transfer directly due to long decoding horizons and visual token ambiguity. It proposes VarKD to address unreliable teacher supervision under student-conditioned contexts.

entry.title: GRAMformer: Any-Order Modality Interactions via Volumetric Multimodal Cross-Attention

author.name: Giordano Cicchetti, Eleonora Grassucci, Danilo Comminiello

entry.summary: GRAMformer introduces Volumetric Multimodal cross-Attention, where attention scores are a function of the joint configuration of multiple modalities rather than pairwise dot products or concatenation. It enables any-order modality interactions while avoiding quadratic complexity in the number of modalities.

entry.title: FlowPRO: Reward-Free Reinforced Fine-Tuning of Flow-Matching VLAs via Proximalized Preference Optimization

author.name: Yihao Wu, He Zhang, Junbo Tan, Xueqian Wang, Zhengyou Zhang

entry.summary: FlowPRO is a reward-free offline reinforced fine-tuning framework for flow-matching VLA models using a preference-optimization objective with proximal regularization tailored to flow-matching action heads. Avoids difficult real-world reward design and critic training.

entry.title: MotionDisco: Motion Discovery for Extreme Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Ilyass Taouil, Michal Ciebelski, Shafeef Omar, Haizhou Zhao, Angela Dai, Aaron M. Johnson, Majid Khadiv

entry.summary: MotionDisco discovers contact-rich long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation motions from scratch by coupling LLM-guided evolutionary search over interaction sequences with a sequential kinodynamic trajectory optimizer. Avoids teleoperation or motion retargeting.

entry.title: Mutation Without Variation: Convergence Dynamics in LLM-Driven Program Evolution

author.name: Can Gurkan, Forrest Stonedahl, Uri Wilensky

entry.summary: Studies LLM-driven program mutation without selection pressure and finds it converges to restricted attractor regions, with most mutations revisiting prior structural forms rather than exploring new ones. It matters for understanding limits of LLMs as evolutionary operators in program synthesis.

entry.title: EpiEvolve: Self-Evolving Agents for Streaming Pandemic Forecasting under Regime Shifts

author.name: Yiming Lu, Sihang Zeng, Zhengxu Tang, Max Lau, Fei Liu, Wei Jin

entry.summary: Introduces EpiEvolve, a self-evolving LLM forecasting agent that keeps weights fixed but adapts via hierarchical episodic memory, reflection on delayed labels, and distilled error rules for streaming pandemic forecasting under regime shifts. It matters for operational, non-stationary epidemic prediction.

entry.title: Answer Presence Drives RAG Rewriting Gains

author.name: Yuejie Li, Yueying Hua, Ke Yang, Li Zhang, Yueping He, Yueping He, Ruiqi Li, Bolin Chen, Tao Wang, Bowen Li, Chengjun Mao

entry.summary: Uses controlled intervention audits to test whether RAG rewriting gains are causally driven by the gold answer string appearing in the rewritten context rather than by general curation quality. It matters for understanding the real source of RAG rewriter improvements.

entry.title: SubtleMemory: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Relational Memory Discrimination in Long-Horizon AI Agents

author.name: Wenxuan Wang, Haoyu Sun, Fukuan Hou, Mingyang Song, Weinan Zhang, Yu Cheng, Yang Yang

entry.summary: Introduces SubtleMemory, a benchmark for fine-grained relational memory discrimination in long-horizon agents, with relation-controlled artifacts that are complementary, nuanced, or contradictory embedded in realistic scenarios. It matters because correct assistance depends on memory relations, not just isolated recall.

entry.title: Can LLMs Write Correct TLA+ Specifications? Evaluating Natural-Language-to-TLA+ Generation

author.name: Arslan Bisharat, Brian Ortiz, Eric Spencer, Khushboo Bhadauria, TaiNing Wang, George K. Thiruvathukal, Konstantin Laufer, Mohammed Abuhamad

entry.summary: Provides the first systematic evaluation of whether LLMs can generate semantically correct TLA+ formal specifications from natural language, testing 30 models with parser and model-checker validation. It matters for lowering the expertise barrier to formal verification used at Amazon and Microsoft.

entry.title: Edit-R2: Context-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Image Editing

author.name: Yuxiao Ye, Haoran He, Fangyuan Kong, Xintao Wang, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai, Ling Pan

entry.summary: Introduces Edit-R2, a context-aware reinforcement learning method for multi-turn in-context image editing that tackles long-context dilution and state contamination as users iteratively refine images. It matters for realistic iterative image editing beyond single-turn settings.

entry.title: When Should Memory Stay Silent: Measuring Memory-Use Boundaries in Memory-Augmented Conversational Agents

author.name: Lingxiang Xu, Jiaoyun Yang, Min Hu, Hongtu Chen, Ning An

entry.summary: Introduces RBI-Eval, a controlled study measuring whether retrieved sensitive memories are warranted in a given turn, comparing model behavior with and without memory access under identical benign prompts across four memory-access settings. It matters for knowing when memory should stay silent rather than just be accurate.

entry.title: Towards Healthy Evolution: Exploring the Role and Mechanisms of Human-Agent Interaction in Self-Evolving Systems

author.name: Dianxing Shi, Junqi He, Junhao Chen, Bowen Wang, Yuta Nakashima

entry.summary: Introduces ANCHOR, an LLM-based framework that simulates human oversight to deliver feedback during self-evolution of agents, mitigating safety drift and capability degradation. Evaluated on two open-source self-evolving systems across coding, math, and safety tasks.

entry.title: RedKnot: Efficient Long-Context LLM Serving with Head-Aware KV Reuse and SegPagedAttention

author.name: Yang Liu, ZhaoKai Luo, HuaYi Jin, ZhiYong Wang, RuoZhou He, BoYu Wang, Guanjie Chen, Junhao Hu

entry.summary: Introduces RedKnot, a long-context LLM serving system using head-aware KV cache reuse and SegPagedAttention, observing that KV cache utility varies across attention heads. Targets KV cache as the dominant bottleneck in large-scale serving.

entry.title: MLEvolve: A Self-Evolving Framework for Automated Machine Learning Algorithm Discovery

author.name: Shangheng Du, Xiangchao Yan, Jinxin Shi, Zongsheng Cao, Shiyang Feng, Zichen Liang, Boyuan Sun, Tianshuo Peng, Yifan Zhou, Xin Li, Jie Zhou, Liang He, Bo Zhang, Lei Bai

entry.summary: Presents MLEvolve, an LLM-based self-evolving multi-agent framework for automated ML algorithm discovery, extending tree search to Progressive MCGS with cross-branch graph reference edges and entropy-inspired exploration-to-exploitation shift. Addresses information isolation and memoryless search in MLE agents.

entry.title: Gradient Descent with Large Step Size Restores Symmetry in Deep Linear Networks with Multi-Pathway

author.name: Hee-Sung Kim, Sungyoon Lee

entry.summary: Proves that discrete gradient descent with large step size restores path symmetry in multi-pathway deep linear networks, contrasting with gradient-flow predictions of winner-takes-all specialization. Shows Edge of Stability oscillations drive a re-balancing phase where signals redistribute across pathways.

entry.title: What Objects Enable, Not What They Are: Functional Latent Spaces for Affordance Reasoning

author.name: Rohan Siva, Neel P. Bhatt, Yunhao Yang, Seoyoung Lee, Nishant Gadde, Christian Ellis, Alvaro Velasquez, Zhangyang Wang, Ufuk Topcu

entry.summary: Introduces A4D, which maps visual observations into a shared latent space structured around affordances (what objects enable) rather than appearance, for robot planning. Aims to improve generalization to novel robot-object interactions through functional reasoning.

entry.title: Cross-Epoch Adaptive Rollout Optimization for RL Post-Training

author.name: Yiming Zong, Yige Wang, Jiashuo Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes CERO, an adaptive rollout allocation method for RL post-training that maintains a Beta posterior over each prompt's success probability and allocates rollouts based on Bayesian estimates of marginal value. Formulates the problem as online resource allocation with prompt-level diminishing returns under a fixed budget.

entry.title: Let It Be Simple: One-Step Action Generation for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yitong Chen, Shiduo Zhang, Jingjing Gong, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: Argues that one-step action generation for vision-language-action models need not require advanced one-step image-synthesis methods, since VLA action prediction has a different condition-target structure (rich conditioning, compact low-dimensional action). Achieves strong one-step generation simply by biasing training-time toward high-noise states with standard velocity prediction.

entry.title: Causal Scaffolding for Physical Reasoning: A Benchmark for Causally-Informed Physical World Understanding in VLMs

author.name: Tianyi Tang, Zhuoyi Lin, Zeyu Feng, Tianyi Ma, Yew-Soon Ong, Ivor Tsang, Haiyan Yin

entry.summary: Introduces CausalPhys, a benchmark of over 3,000 video and image questions across Perception, Anticipation, Intervention, and Goal Orientation domains, each paired with expert-annotated causal graphs of object-attribute-event dependencies. Provides a causal-graph-grounded metric for evaluating physical reasoning in VLMs.

entry.title: On Advantage Estimates for Max@K Policy Gradients

author.name: Shota Takashiro, Soichiro Nishimori, Paavo Parmas, Yongmin Kim, Kohsei Matsutani, Gouki Minegishi, Yusuke Iwasawa, Takeshi Kojima, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: Studies policy-gradient advantage estimators for max@K and pass@K inference-time objectives, showing existing estimators produce non-centered advantages and introducing a Leave-Two-Out baseline that preserves unbiasedness. From the Matsuo lab, it clarifies relationships among RLVR estimators.

entry.title: TAM: Torque Adaptation Module for Robust Motion Transfer in Manipulation

author.name: Dongwon Son, Florian Shkurti, Jason Lee, Naman Shah, Beomjoon Kim, Dieter Fox

entry.summary: TAM (Torque Adaptation Module) adapts torque commands sent to a robot to match an ideal robot's behavior, mitigating sim-to-real and cross-robot dynamics gaps in contact-rich manipulation without recollecting data per robot. From credible robotics authors including Dieter Fox.

entry.title: Learning What to Forget: Improving LLM Unlearning via Learned Token-Level Importance

author.name: Gizem Y\"uce, Giorgos Nikolaou, Nicolas Flammarion

entry.summary: Proposes a token-level importance method for LLM unlearning that characterizes a token as forget-specific when minimizing its forget loss does not conflict with retain optimality, formalized as a joint optimization over parameters and token weights. It learns what to forget without auxiliary models or annotations.

entry.title: Self-Augmenting Retrieval for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Paul J\"unger, Justin Lovelace, Linxi Zhao, Dongyoung Go, Kilian Q. Weinberger

entry.summary: SARDI is a training-free dynamic RAG framework for discrete diffusion language models that exploits discarded low-confidence lookahead tokens from the denoising trajectory as early retrieval signals, fetching stronger evidence before output is finalized. From Weinberger's group, it uniquely leverages diffusion LM dynamics for retrieval.

entry.title: Regret Minimization with Adaptive Opponents in Repeated Games

author.name: Mingyang Liu, Asuman Ozdaglar, Tiancheng Yu, Kaiqing Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Repeated Policy Regret (RP-Regret), a game-theoretic regret metric for repeated games with adaptive opponents that respond to play history, addressing external regret's failure to capture adaptivity. From credible authors (Ozdaglar, Kaiqing Zhang), it enables stronger comparators and fewer opponent constraints.

entry.title: RUBAS: Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning for Agent Safety

author.name: Xian Qi Loye, Qinglin Su, Zhexin Zhang, Shiyao Cui, Qi Zhu, Fei Mi, Hongning Wang, Minlie Huang

entry.summary: RUBAS is a rubric-based reinforcement learning framework for agent safety that decomposes agent behavior into tool-use safety, argument safety, response safety, and helpfulness, providing fine-grained interpretable rewards over complete trajectories. From Minlie Huang's group, it balances safe tool execution with task completion.

entry.title: OpenRFM: Dissecting Relational In-Context Learning

author.name: Zhikai Chen, Junyu Yin, Jialiang Gu, Siheng Xiong, Xiaoze Liu, Ruowang Zhang, Keren Zhou, Kai Guo

entry.summary: OpenRFM dissects relational foundation models by analyzing the Relational Transformer, showing it performs relation-level in-context learning that fails under sparse label coverage via a kernel-regression view. It also ablates pretraining data sources to explain the gap between open and commercial RFMs.

entry.title: When Do Fewer Coordinates Suffice in DP-SGD?

author.name: Huiqi Zhang, Fang Xie

entry.summary: This paper proposes TP-TopK, a two-phase coordinate-sparse DP-SGD method where a private warm-up identifies a coordinate support to focus training on, reducing injected noise that otherwise scales with full parameter dimension. It gives a criterion for when coordinate restriction is beneficial and a nonconvex stationarity bound.

entry.title: ParetoPilot: Zero-Surrogate Offline Multi-Objective Optimization via Infer-Perturb-Guide Diffusion

author.name: Ruiqing Sun, Sen Yang, Dawei Feng, Bo Ding, Yijie Wang, Huaimin Wang

entry.summary: ParetoPilot is a zero-surrogate diffusion framework for offline multi-objective optimization that leverages conditional priors embedded in pretrained diffusion models via an infer-perturb-guide scheme, avoiding external surrogate models that introduce overhead and deceptive evaluations. It discovers Pareto-optimal designs from static datasets.

entry.title: LimiX-2M: Mitigating Low-Rank Collapse and Attention Bottlenecks in Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Yuanrui Wang, Xingxuan Zhang, Han Yu, Mingchao Hao, Gang Ren, Hao Yuan, Li Mao, Yunjia Zhang, Chun Yuan, Peng Cui

entry.summary: LimiX-2M addresses low-rank collapse and attention bottlenecks in tabular foundation models with a tokenize-and-route framework: RaBEL expands scalars into localized RBF features to improve conditioning and effective rank, while a reordered bidirectional S-N-F block aligns computation with readout. It improves compute efficiency of TFMs that rival tree ensembles.

entry.title: Rollout-Level Advantage-Prioritized Experience Replay for GRPO

author.name: Gyeongtae Yoo, Sanghyeok Park, Soohyuk Jang, Ik-hwan Kim, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: This paper proposes a rollout-level advantage-prioritized experience replay buffer for GRPO that stores and samples individual rollouts (rather than whole groups), bounds staleness via age eviction, and preserves on-policy data through fresh-anchored composition. It improves the sample inefficiency of GRPO where each rollout is normally used once and discarded.

entry.title: Learning symplectic model reduction based on a approximation theorem of symplectic embeddings

author.name: Liyi Feng, Yifa Tang, Yulin Xie, Ruili Zhang, Aiqing Zhu

entry.summary: This paper establishes a universal approximation theorem for symplectic embeddings and proposes symplecticity-preserving autoencoders (SpAE) where the decoder is a symplectic embedding, for model reduction of high-dimensional Hamiltonian systems. It preserves intrinsic symplectic structure that standard autoencoders destroy, enabling stable long-time prediction.

entry.title: Explainably Safe Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Sabine Rieder, Stefan Pranger, Debraj Chakraborty, Jan K\v{r}et\'insk\'y, Bettina K\"onighofer

entry.summary: This work proposes explainably safe reinforcement learning, addressing that formally-synthesized shields enforcing safety are themselves hard for humans to interpret, especially when non-deterministic shields yield overly large decision-tree representations. It develops a method to represent shields more compactly and explainably.

entry.title: Learning Long Range Spatio-Temporal Representations over Continuous Time Dynamic Graphs with State Space Models

author.name: Ayushman Raghuvanshi, Thummaluru Siddartha Reddy, Sundeep Prabhakar Chepuri, Mahesh Chandran

entry.summary: This paper derives a parameter-efficient state-space modeling framework (CTDG-SSM) for continuous-time dynamic graphs, introducing a continuous-time topology-aware HiPPO operator for long-range information propagation. It overcomes existing methods' restriction to local one-hop temporal neighborhoods to capture multi-hop global structural patterns.

entry.title: Measuring Model Robustness via Fisher Information: Spectral Bounds, Theoretical Guarantees, and Practical Algorithms

author.name: Chong Zhang, Xiang Li, Jia Wang, Qiufeng Wang, Xiaobo Jin

entry.summary: Proposes an attack-agnostic robustness metric based on the spectral norm of the Fisher Information Matrix, with closed-form spectral bounds for common architectures and scalable estimation algorithms. It offers theoretical robustness rankings independent of specific attacks.

entry.title: Learning While Acting: A Skill-Enhanced Test-Time Co-Evolution Framework for Online Lifelong Learning Agents

author.name: Bo Mao, Jie Zhou, Yutao Yang, Xin Li, Xian Wei, Qin Chen, Xingjiao Wu, Liang He

entry.summary: Proposes LifeSkill, a two-stage RL framework for online lifelong learning LLM agents that continuously internalizes test-time feedback through verifier-guided skill learning and test-time co-evolution. It aims to move beyond static-parameter skill retrieval for long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Provably Reduced Sample Cost in Prior-Guided Hyperparameter Optimization

author.name: Leona Hennig, Jasmin Brandt, Lukas Fehring, Barbara Hammer, Marius Lindauer, Marcel Wever

entry.summary: Provides the first distribution-dependent sample complexity bounds for multi-fidelity hyperparameter optimization with priors, framed through fixed-budget best-arm identification. It quantifies how prior informativeness reduces sampling cost in AutoML.

entry.title: STaR-Quant: State-Time Consistent Post-Training Quantization for Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Xin Yan, Aqiang Wang, Zhenglin Wan, Xingrui Yuand Ivor Tsang

entry.summary: Proposes STaR-Quant, a state-time consistent post-training quantization method for diffusion LLMs that addresses state-dependent activation disparity between masked and unmasked tokens and temporal error accumulation across denoising steps. It targets efficient low-bit deployment of DLLMs.

entry.title: In-Context Graphical Inference

author.name: Zehua Cheng, Wei Dai, Jiahao Sun

entry.summary: Introduces In-Context Graphical Inference, an autoregressive Graph Transformer that mimics Variable Elimination with learned Tensor-Train-compressed factors to perform marginal inference on graphical models. It pairs a Dirichlet output layer with weighted conformal prediction for calibration.

entry.title: Graph Cascades: Contagion-Based Mesoscopic Rewiring for Structure-Aware Graph Machine Learning

author.name: Meher Chaitanya, My Le, Luana Ruiz

entry.summary: Introduces Graph Cascades, a contagion-based mesoscopic rewiring strategy for GNNs and Graph Transformers that promotes multi-hop reinforced node pairs to direct neighbors in linear time. It provides theoretical conditions under which reinforcement-based rewiring improves label alignment.

entry.title: Learning What Not to Impute: An Uncertainty-Aware Diffusion Framework for Meaningful Missingness

author.name: Lixing Zhang, Yidong Ouyang, Weifu Li, Shixiang Zhu, Guang Cheng, Liyan Xie

entry.summary: Formalizes selective imputation, distinguishing meaningfully missing entries from those missing due to observation, and proposes Diff-Joint, a diffusion framework that jointly models tabular data and a latent missingness mask. It infers which entries to preserve versus recover.

entry.title: RePercENT: Scaling Disentangled Representation Learning Beyond Two Modalities

author.name: Vasiliki Rizou, Pascal Frossard, Dorina Thanou

entry.summary: Proposes RePercENT, a self-supervised framework for scalable disentangled representation learning beyond two modalities, overcoming the scalability bottleneck of existing two-modality methods. It identifies shared and unique factors across multiple modalities via pairwise disentanglement.

entry.title: Deep Embedded Multiplicative DMD for Algebra-Preserving Koopman Learning

author.name: Kelan Gray, Finlay Brown, Nicolas Boull\'e, Matthew J. Colbrook

entry.summary: Introduces DeepMDMD, which learns a latent space partition while enforcing the Koopman product rule as an exact algebraic constraint, combining deep Koopman flexibility with structure preservation. Training alternates between operator updates and differentiable latent clustering.

entry.title: Beyond Static Priors: Dynamic Neural Guidance for Large-Scale Ant Colony Optimization

author.name: Dat Thanh Tran, Van Khu Vu, Yining Ma

entry.summary: Proposes DyNACO, which achieves dynamic neural guidance for Ant Colony Optimization by periodically observing pheromone distributions and incumbent solutions, fixing the training-inference misalignment of static-prior approaches. It scales to 100,000-node TSP instances while often reducing runtime.

entry.title: Bayesian Membership Privacy for Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Sinan Y{\i}ld{\i}r{\i}m, Megha Khosla

entry.summary: Introduces Bayesian Membership Privacy, a sampling-aware formulation of node-level membership privacy for GNNs that incorporates node-dependent priors and graph sampling probabilities into a Bayesian hypothesis test. It addresses structural correlations overlooked by privacy analyses inherited from non-graph settings.

entry.title: The Differentiable Auditory Loop (DAL): An ML Framework for Hyper-Personalized Hearing Aids

author.name: Alejandro Ballesta Rosen, Jason Mikiel-Hunter, Julian Maclaren, Jack Collins, Richard F. Lyon, Simon Carlile

entry.summary: Introduces the Differentiable Auditory Loop, an open-source framework for personalized hearing aid design using CARFAC, a differentiable cochlear model ported to JAX, to optimize neural networks matching impaired auditory patterns to normal-hearing references. It targets the underlying encoding dysfunctions of hearing loss beyond fixed amplification.

entry.title: veriFIRE: an Industrial Case Study in Verifying Consistency Properties for a DNN-Based Wildfire Detection System

author.name: Idan Refaeli, Maya Swisa, Itay Buchnik, Alon Zada, Guy Amir, Elad Mandelbaum, Ziv Freund, Guy Katz

entry.summary: Reports an industrial case study (veriFIRE) verifying consistency properties of deep neural networks in a real airborne wildfire-detection system, encoding application requirements like monotonicity of detector confidence into solver-compatible verification queries. It demonstrates end-to-end formal verification for a safety-critical system.

entry.title: CaloTrilogy: Toward a Breakthrough in One-Step, End-to-End, Physics-Guided Shower Generation for Modern Calorimeters

author.name: Cheng Jiang, Sitian Qian, Kevin Pedro, Oz Amram, Huilin Qu, Maggie Voetberg

entry.summary: Introduces CaloTrilogy, a unified one-step end-to-end physics-guided framework for calorimeter shower generation that combines an average velocity field integrator to avoid the hundreds of function evaluations typical of flow/diffusion surrogates. It improves the balance among speed, shower quality, and physics fidelity for collider simulation.

entry.title: A General Framework for Dynamic Consistent Submodular Maximization

author.name: Paul D\"utting, Federico Fusco, Silvio Lattanzi, Ashkan Norouzi-Fard, Ola Svensson, Morteza Zadimoghaddam

entry.summary: This paper provides a general framework for fully dynamic consistent submodular maximization, handling both insertions and deletions, and obtains the first constant-factor approximations with sublinear consistency for cardinality constraints. Consistency means maintaining a near-optimal solution with few adjustments per step.

entry.title: CHASE: Adversarial Red-Blue Teaming for Improving LLM Safety using Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Rahul Markasserithodi, Aditya Joshi, Yuekang Li, Ishmanbir Singh, Chris Yoo, Alan Niu

entry.summary: CHASE is a closed-loop red-blue teaming framework where a black-box GRPO-trained attacker and a safety-aligned defender co-evolve to improve LLM safety against adaptive prompt-rewriting attacks like persona modulation and fictional framing. It targets the brittleness of defenses that rely on human curation or white-box optimization overfit to specific internals.

entry.title: What's in a Name? Morphological Shortcuts by LLMs in Pharmacology

author.name: Kaijie Mo, Thomas Yang, Chantal Shaib, Qing Yao, William Rudman, Ramez Kouzy, Kanishka Misra, Byron C. Wallace, Junyi Jessy Li

entry.summary: Studies how LLMs use morphological affix cues to confidently reason about fictitious drugs in pharmacology, revealing dangerous overgeneralization. Provides a behavioral and mechanistic framework distinguishing affix, stem, and full-name semantics across 653 drugs.

entry.title: Latent Reasoning with Normalizing Flows

author.name: Guancheng Tu, Xiangjun Fu, Suhao Yu, Yao Tang, Haoqiang Kang, Lianhui Qin, Yizhe Zhang, Jiatao Gu

entry.summary: Proposes latent reasoning with normalizing flows that preserves native left-to-right autoregressive generation and probabilistic structure while performing higher-bandwidth continuous intermediate computation. It aims to retain CoT advantages while moving computation to latent states.

entry.title: UltraVR: A Diagnostic Ultra-Resolution Image-VQA Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Reasoning

author.name: Gexin Huang, Yanting Yang, Myeongkyun Kang, Beidi Zhao, Jun Zhou, Chen Zhou, Gang Wang, Zu-hua Gao, Xiaoxiao Li

entry.summary: UltraVR is a diagnostic VQA benchmark for evidence-grounded reasoning over ultra-resolution images across CCTV, remote sensing, pathology, and industrial anomaly detection. It moves beyond final-answer accuracy to evaluate whether VLMs actually acquire and integrate necessary visual evidence.

entry.title: Imagine Before You Predict: Interleaved Latent Visual Reasoning for Video Event Prediction

author.name: Tianxiang Jiang, Linquan Wu, Sheng Xia, Songze Li, Ziang Yan, Haoyu Yang, Yu Qiao, Yi Wang

entry.summary: Future-L1 introduces interleaved latent visual reasoning for video event prediction, letting an MLLM alternate between language tokens and continuous latent visual spans during decoding. This avoids hallucinations from verbalizing fine-grained motion and geometry cues, supported by a new 50K dataset.

entry.title: LoomVideo: Unifying Multimodal Inputs into Video Generation and Editing

author.name: Jianzong Wu, Hao Lian, Jiongfan Yang, Dachao Hao, Ye Tian, Yunhai Tong, Jingyuan Zhu, Biaolong Chen, Qiaosong Qi, Aixi Zhang, Wanggui He, Mushui Liu, Jinlong Liu, Hao Jiang

entry.summary: LoomVideo is an efficient 5B-parameter unified architecture for video generation and editing that interprets interleaved multimodal inputs, replacing the text encoder with an MLLM. It avoids the sequence-doubling concatenation that quadruples self-attention cost in larger 13B+ unified models.

entry.title: HyperVis: Continuous Latent Visual Relational Graphs on the Lorentz Hyperboloid for Compositional Reasoning

author.name: Moshiur Farazi, Sameera Ramasinghe, Mahbub Ahmed Turza, Shafin Rahman

entry.summary: HyperVis improves compositional reasoning in VLMs by computing a dense visual relation tensor via spatially-biased cross-attention and projecting it onto a Lorentz hyperboloid, enforcing hierarchy through spatial physics. It shows that injecting discrete scene-graph text labels actually degrades GQA accuracy, motivating the continuous latent approach.

entry.title: Geodesic Flow Matching on a Riemannian Degradation Manifold for Blind Image Restoration

author.name: Akshay Janardan Bankar, Ankita Chatterjee, Sayan Banerjee, Shreyas Pandith, Kalakonda Sai Shashank, Amit Satish Unde

entry.summary: This work formulates blind image restoration as geodesic transport on a Riemannian degradation manifold, modeling degradations as points on a low-dimensional curved space. Using geodesic flow matching, it learns intrinsic transport dynamics respecting degradation-space curvature, generalizing linear Euclidean flow matching.

entry.title: Complexity-Balanced Diffusion Splitting

author.name: Noam Issachar, Dani Lischinski, Raanan Fattal

entry.summary: Complexity-Balanced Splitting is a framework for temporal capacity allocation in diffusion models that partitions the generative timeline into segments of equal approximation burden across specialized sub-networks. Grounded in function approximation theory and de Boor's equidistribution principle, it allocates more capacity where needed instead of uniformly.

entry.title: Ask-to-Clarify: Resolving Instruction Ambiguity through Multi-turn Dialogue

author.name: Xingyao Lin, Xinghao Zhu, Tianyi Lu, Sicheng Xie, Hui Zhang, Xipeng Qiu, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: Ask-to-Clarify is a framework for embodied agents that resolves ambiguous instructions through multi-turn dialogue before generating low-level actions end-to-end. It moves VLA-based agents from one-way passive execution toward interactive collaboration that adapts based on human feedback.

entry.title: Is This Edit Correct? A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Reasoning-Aware Image Editing

author.name: Yixuan Ding, Wei Huang, Ruijie Quan, Xiaojuan Qi, Yi Yang

entry.summary: RE-Edit is a benchmark for reasoning-aware image editing evaluating systems across physical, environmental, cultural, causal, and referential reasoning dimensions. Its 1,000 samples are designed so visual plausibility alone is insufficient and correct editing requires satisfying implicit contextual constraints.

entry.title: AffordanceVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model Empowering Action Generation through Affordance-Aware Understanding

author.name: Qize Yu, Jiadi You, Yuran Wang, Jiaqi Liang, Bowen Ping, Yang Tian, Yue Chen, Minghong Cai, Zeying Gong, Ruihai Wu, Yinchuan Li, Junwei Liang, Yingcong Chen

entry.summary: AffordanceVLA introduces structured affordance forecasting as an intermediate representation to bridge VLM semantic spaces and robot control, improving perception-action mapping. Uses object-centric grounding components for manipulation.

entry.title: Accelerating and Scaling MPC-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Humanoid Locomotion and Manipulation

author.name: Junheng Li, Liang Wu, Sergio A. Esteban, Lizhi Yang, J\'an Drgo\v{n}a, Aaron D. Ames

entry.summary: Introduces MPC-RL with a centroidal-dynamics MPC reward and a parallel-in-horizon construction-free GPU MPC to accelerate MPC-guided RL for humanoid locomotion and manipulation. Makes MPC guidance practical in massively parallel training.

entry.title: Gotta Grow Fast: Design and Benchmarking of a Tip Mount for High-Speed Vine Robots

author.name: Antonio Alvarez Valdivia, Robert Reeve, Ankush Dhawan, Ciera McFarland, Chad Council, Margaret McGuinness, Nathaniel Hanson

entry.summary: RealDexUMI is a wearable universal manipulation interface with a shared dexterous end-effector module integrating a dexterous hand, in-hand vision, and fingertip tactile sensing, plus an isomorphic teleoperation glove. Enables retargeting-free, contact-aware dexterous data collection.

entry.title: Output Type Before Quality: A Standards-Derived XAI Admissibility Rubric for Autonomous-Driving Safety

author.name: Abhinaw Priyadershi, Mandar Pitale, Jelena Frtunikj, Maria Spence

entry.summary: Derives a standards-based admissibility rubric for explainable AI in autonomous driving, identifying an evidence-type gap where popular methods like SHAP cannot produce the directed causal chains safety standards require. It matters for aligning XAI outputs with assurance-case demands.

entry.title: AdaMEM: Test-Time Adaptive Memory for Language Agents

author.name: Yunxiang Zhang, Yiheng Li, Ali Payani, Lu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes AdaMEM, a test-time adaptive memory framework that maintains long-term trajectory memory plus dynamically generated short-term strategy memory to guide agents during long-horizon tasks without updating weights. It matters for keeping agent guidance aligned as tasks unfold.

entry.title: Learning Visual Spatial Planning from Symbolic State via Modality-Gap-Aware Self-Distillation

author.name: Haocheng Luo, Jiahui Liu, Ruicheng Zhang, Zhizhou Zhong, Jiaqi Huang, Zunnan Xu, Quan Shi, Jun Zhou, Xiu Li

entry.summary: Proposes MGSD, a modality-gap-aware self-distillation framework that first grounds visual state representations then transfers planning ability from a privileged symbolic teacher, addressing the perception-reasoning gap in visual spatial planning. It matters for improving VLMs at inferring latent state structure from pixels for multi-step planning.

entry.title: Humans' ALMANAC: A Human Collaboration Dataset of Action-Level Mental Model Annotations for Agent Collaboration

author.name: Jiaju Chen, Yuxuan Lu, Jiayi Su, Chaoran Chen, Songlin Xiao, Zheng Zhang, Yun Wang, Yunyao Li, Jian Zhao, Tongshuang Wu, Toby Jia-Jun Li, Dakuo Wang, Bingsheng Yao

entry.summary: Introduces ALMANAC, a human collaboration dataset with action-level mental model annotations capturing reasoning, partner intentions, and shared goals during collaborative tasks. Aims to guide agents toward process-level collaborative competence beyond task completion.

entry.title: RREDCoT: Segment-Level Reward Redistribution for Reasoning Models

author.name: Mykyta Ielanskyi, Kajetan Schweighofer, Lukas Aichberger, Sepp Hochreiter

entry.summary: RREDCoT applies segment-level reward redistribution and credit assignment to reasoning-model RL, addressing the high variance of GRPO/Monte-Carlo methods under delayed rewards by emphasizing CoT segments important for correct solutions. From Hochreiter's group, it improves credit assignment for chain-of-thought training.

entry.title: Policy Gradient for Continuous-Time Robust Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Tanya Veeravalli, David M. Bossens, Atsushi Nitanda

entry.summary: This work develops policy gradient algorithms for continuous-time robust MDPs, deriving policy and adversarial gradients via pathwise and adjoint-based formulas for SDEs/ODEs. It proposes double-loop optimizers achieving linear convergence and O(1/epsilon^2) sample complexity.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware End-to-End Co-Design of Neural Network Processors: From Training and Mapping to Fabrication

author.name: Yuyang Du, Yujun Huang, Gioele Zardini

entry.summary: Presents a unified, monotone co-design framework for neural network processors that jointly optimizes network training, chip mapping, wafer fabrication, and compute allocation with uncertainty awareness. It composes interoperable design blocks across the full hardware-software stack.

entry.title: Counterfactual Explanations for Deep Two-Sample Testing

author.name: Wei-Cheng Lai, Marco Simnacher, Christoph Lippert

entry.summary: Proposes a counterfactual explanation framework for deep two-sample testing that generates sample-level edits moving observations toward a target group while reducing the test discrepancy, using a diffusion autoencoder. It provides insight into which features drive null-hypothesis rejection on high-dimensional data.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Dataset Condensation for Diffusion Model Training

author.name: Xiao Cui, Yulei Qin, Mo Zhu, Wengang Zhou, Hongsheng Li, Houqiang Li

entry.summary: This work reformulates real-subset selection for diffusion model dataset condensation as a geometry-aware distribution alignment problem using one-sided partial optimal transport. It preserves the distributional geometry required by diffusion likelihood objectives while allowing unmatched mass in low-density regions.

entry.title: Global-Local Monte Carlo Tree Search in Vision-Language Models for Text-to-3D Indoor Scene Generation

author.name: Mengshi Qi, Wei Deng, Xianlin Zhang, Huadong Ma

entry.summary: This work models text-to-3D indoor scene generation as a global-local Monte Carlo Tree Search problem with vision-language models, replacing error-prone sequential chain-of-thought decisions. The global tree iteratively places objects while local trees refine placements like humans furnishing a room.

entry.title: PAR3D: A Unified 3D-MLLM with Part-Aware Representation for Scene Understanding

author.name: Shaohui Dai, Yansong Qu, You Shen, Shengchuan Zhang, Liujuan Cao

entry.summary: PAR3D is a unified part-aware 3D multimodal LLM enabling models to understand, reason about, and ground both objects and their fine-grained parts in 3D scenes. It introduces ScenePart, a synthetic 3D scene dataset with part-level annotations and language instructions for training and evaluation.

entry.title: What Should Agents Say? Action-state Communication for Efficient Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Chen Huang, Yuhao Wu, Wenxuan Zhang

entry.summary: Studies inter-agent communication strategies in LLM multi-agent systems and proposes PACT, a protocolized action-state communication scheme that preserves only the action-centered information downstream agents need. It matters for reducing token costs and context bloat in multi-agent pipelines.

entry.title: Brick-Composer: Using MLLMs for Assembly with Diverse Bricks

author.name: Jiateng Liu, Bingxuan Li, Zhenhailong Wang, Rushi Wang, Kaiwen Hong, Cheng Qian, Jiayu Liu, Denghui Zhang, Katherine Driggs-Campbell, Manling Li, Heng Ji

entry.summary: Studies whether MLLMs have the visual grounding and spatial reasoning for brick assembly, framing it as sequential brick selection and pose estimation and introducing BC-Bench. It matters for probing embodied-style spatial reasoning toward AI that builds physical objects from reusable parts.

entry.title: Self-Commitment Latency: A Reward-Free Probe for Prompted Implicit Hacking

author.name: Bonan Shen, Youting Wang, Dingyan Shang, Tao Ning

entry.summary: Proposes self-commitment latency, a reward-free probe measuring how early a prompted reasoning context commits to its own final answer, to detect implicit reward hacking when chain-of-thought looks benign. It matters for auditing hidden shortcut reasoning without task-specific reward signals.

entry.title: Beyond Output Matching: Preserving Internal Geometry in NVFP4 LLM Distillatio

author.name: Fangbo Tu, Junhua Zhao, Chi Liu, Xin Chen, Haifeng Wu, Jian Wan, Srinivasan Manoharan

entry.summary: Diagnoses that output-matching quantization-aware distillation can mask internal representational degradation, and proposes preserving internal geometry (via CKA) during NVFP4 LLM distillation rather than only matching logits. It matters for higher-fidelity low-precision model deployment.

entry.title: QCFuse: Query-Aware Cache Fusion via Compressed View for Efficient RAG Serving

author.name: Jianxin Yan, Wangze Ni, Zhenxin Li, Jiabao Jin, Zhitao Shen, Haoyang Li, Jia Zhu, Peng Cheng, Xuemin Lin, Lei Chen, Kui Ren

entry.summary: Presents QCFuse, a compressed-view query-aware cache fusion method for efficient RAG serving that resolves the quality-efficiency dilemma between query-agnostic and full-view query-aware KV-cache selectors. It matters for reducing the dominant prefill cost of RAG inference.

entry.title: PLAN-S: Bridging Planning with Latent Style Dynamics for Autonomous Driving World Models

author.name: Xiaoyun Qiu, Jingtao He, Yijie Chen, Yusong Huang, Haotian Wang, Yixuan Wang, Xinhu Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes PLAN-S, a planner-facing bridge for autonomous-driving latent world models that decodes a style-conditioned four-channel semantic cost map to make risk, drivability, and driving-style dynamics inspectable and modulable before trajectory selection. It matters for controllability and interpretability in end-to-end driving.

entry.title: WorldFly: A World-Model-Based Vision-Language-Action Model for UAV Navigation

author.name: Shengtao Zheng, Kai Li, Weichen Zhang, Yu Meng, Chen Gao, Xinlei Chen, Yong Li, Xiao-Ping Zhang

entry.summary: Presents WorldFly, a world-model-based vision-language-action framework for UAV navigation that imagines future states to handle occlusions and viewpoint changes in dense urban environments. Also introduces an Urban Canyon Traversal Benchmark for spatial understanding.

entry.title: Boosting Brain-to-Image Decoding with TRIBE v2 Data Augmentation

author.name: Yohann Benchetrit, Marl\`ene Careil, Simon Dahan, Hubert Banville, St\'ephane d'Ascoli, Jean-R\'emi King

entry.summary: Investigates boosting fMRI brain-to-image decoding in low-data regimes by augmenting datasets with synthetic data from TRIBE v2, a large encoding model pretrained on 1000+ hours of fMRI responses. Reports up to 68% improvement in image retrieval accuracy.

entry.title: Temporal Preference Concepts and their Functions in a Large Language Model

author.name: Ian Rios-Sialer, Shantanu Darveshi, Shuai Jiang, Avigya Paudel, Anastasiia Pronina, Ipshita Bandyopadhyay, Justin Shenk

entry.summary: Causally localizes a temporal-preference subgraph in a distilled LLM (Qwen3-4B) using gradient attribution and activation patching, finding time-horizon geometry encoded in the residual stream. Behaviorally, unintervened models discount the future far less steeply than humans but the preference is unstable.

entry.title: Differentiable Efficient Operator Search

author.name: Xiaohuan Pei, Jiyuan Zhang, Yuanfan Guo, Weiguo Feng, Tao Huang, Cho-Jui Hsieh, Chang Xu

entry.summary: Introduces Efficient Operator Search, a differentiable framework unifying token-reduction operators (pruning, merging, pooling, reweighting) as regimes of a shared operator space. Jointly searches where to reduce tokens, how many to retain, and how to process reduced information under budget constraints.

entry.title: Gradient descent at the Edge of Stability: free energy model and kinetic description of the two-layer network

author.name: Antonin Chodron de Courcel

entry.summary: Develops a continuous-time effective free energy model and kinetic description of two-layer network gradient descent in the Edge of Stability regime, tracking averaged trajectories coupled with time-averaged oscillation covariance. Reveals an effective free energy combining risk with a curvature-related entropic term.

entry.title: Almieyar-Oryx-BloomBench: A Bilingual Multimodal Benchmark for Cognitively Informed Evaluation of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Mohammad Mahdi Abootorabi, Omid Ghahroodi, Anas Madkoor, Marzia Nouri, Doratossadat Dastgheib, Mohamed Hefeeda, Ehsaneddin Asgari

entry.summary: Introduces BloomBench, a cognitively grounded bilingual English-Arabic multimodal benchmark for vision-language models structured around the six levels of Bloom's Taxonomy. Aims to diagnose true reasoning abilities and chart progress toward human-like multimodal intelligence.

entry.title: TensorBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents on a Compiler-Based Tensor Framework

author.name: Bobby Yan, Fredrik Kjolstad

entry.summary: Introduces TensorBench, a benchmark of 199 feature-addition and refactoring tasks on a compiler-based tensor framework, graded by running the framework's test suite including randomized regression tests. Addresses the trade-off between task difficulty and evaluation reliability in repository-level coding benchmarks.

entry.title: Data Flow Control: Data Safety Policies for AI Agents

author.name: Charlie Summers, Eugene Wu

entry.summary: Introduces Data Flow Control (DFC), a framework to declaratively specify and guarantee policy enforcement over tuple-level data flows within database queries generated by AI agents. Frames data safety (regulatory, privacy, business constraints) as a data infrastructure problem distinct from query correctness.

entry.title: DRIFT: A Residual Flow Adapter for Decoding Continuous Outputs in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhuoming Liu, Jinhong Lin, Kwan Man Cheng, Lin Zhang, Shayok Bagchi, Yin Li

entry.summary: Proposes DRIFT, a residual flow-matching adapter that enables pretrained autoregressive VLMs to produce precise continuous outputs (temporal boundaries, robot actions) by combining a coarse base predictor with iterative generative refinement. Addresses the mismatch between discrete-token decoding and tasks requiring continuous outputs.

entry.title: Deciphering Two Training Clocks in Grokking via Deep Linear Network Theory with Conditional ReLU Reduction

author.name: Hu Tan, Kuo Gai, Shihua Zhang

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical analysis of grokking via deep linear network theory, separating the fast decay of classification loss from the slower simplification of learned representation into two distinct training clocks. Uses Schatten-type penalty and Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz tail conditions to characterize the timescales.

entry.title: MDP-GRPO: Stabilized Group Relative Policy Optimization for Multi-Constraint Instruction Following

author.name: Mohammad Mahdi Salmani-Zarchi, Zahra Rahimi, Heshaam Faili, Mohammad Javad Dousti

entry.summary: MDP-GRPO identifies three failure modes of z-score normalization in GRPO under discrete low-dispersion rewards and proposes fixes including multi-temperature sampling, dual-anchor advantages, and prospect-theoretic shaping. It stabilizes RL for multi-constraint instruction following.

entry.title: Quantum enhanced rare event discovery and sampling

author.name: Naixu Guo, Po-Wei Huang, Qisheng Wang, Jayne Thompson, Patrick Rebentrost, Mile Gu, Chengran Yang

entry.summary: Introduces a quantum algorithm for discovering and sampling rare events (probability below a threshold) without first learning which events are rare, achieving optimal sampling overhead. It targets domains like financial crashes, infrastructure failures, and critical AI errors.

entry.title: HomeWorld: A Unified Floorplan-to-Furnished Framework for Generating Controllable, Densely Interactive Whole-Home Scenes

author.name: Wenbo Li, Xiaoliang Ju, Zipeng Qin, Rongyao Fang, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: HomeWorld is a unified hierarchical floorplan-to-furnished framework generating controllable, densely interactive whole-home 3D scenes, training an LLM on 300K real residential floorplans for whole-home generation followed by furnishing stages. It targets simulation-ready, globally coherent indoor scenes for robotics and design.

entry.title: Code2LoRA: Hypernetwork-Generated Adapters for Code Language Models under Software Evolution

author.name: Liliana Hotsko, Yinxi Li, Yuntian Deng, Pengyu Nie

entry.summary: Code2LoRA uses a hypernetwork to generate repository-specific LoRA adapters that inject repo knowledge with zero inference-time token overhead, offering static (snapshot) and evolving (GRU-updated per diff) variants for code language models under software evolution. It replaces costly per-repo fine-tuning or long-context injection.

entry.title: EvalStop: Using World Feedback to Detect and Correct Reward Overoptimization in Multi-Tenant RLHF Platforms

author.name: Guilin Zhang, Chuanyi Sun, Shahryar Sarkani, John M. Fossaceca

entry.summary: EvalStop is a scheduling primitive for multi-tenant RLHF cloud platforms that detects reward overoptimization using downstream eval metrics rather than training loss, terminating jobs after consecutive eval-score declines to free shared GPUs. It tackles reward hacking from a systems-and-scheduling angle.

entry.title: KODA: Contrastive Representation Comparison and Alignment for Vision-Language Foundation Models

author.name: Youqi Wu, Mohammad Jalali, Farzan Farnia

entry.summary: KODA is a kernel-based framework for structurally comparing vision-language model representations (e.g., CLIP vs SigLIP) by identifying sample subsets clustered differently under each model. It moves beyond downstream-performance comparisons to explain how representations differ.

entry.title: From Ticks to Flows: Dynamics of Neural Reinforcement Learning in Continuous Environments

author.name: Saket Tiwari, Tejas Kotwal, George Konidaris

entry.summary: This theoretical paper models deep RL in continuous environments as a continuous-time stochastic process, deriving a two-timescale (environment time and gradient time) formulation for actor-critic with single-hidden-layer networks. It characterizes how environment state and return estimates evolve in the infinite-width limit.

entry.title: Offline-to-Online Learning in Linear Bandits

author.name: Kushagra Chandak, Toshinori Kitamura, Xiaoqi Tan

entry.summary: This paper studies online learning augmented with an offline dataset in stochastic linear bandits, proposing an algorithm that relies on offline data early and increasingly explores as the horizon grows. It establishes regret bounds competitive with both purely online and purely offline solutions.

entry.title: Measuring What Matters: Synthetic Benchmarks for Concept Bottleneck Models

author.name: Julian Skirzynski, Harry Cheon, Shreyas Kadekodi, Meredith Stewart, Berk Ustun
