entry.summary: This work develops synthetic benchmarks for concept bottleneck models, generating labeled datasets while controlling key properties to study decision-support and automation use cases. It addresses the scarcity of concept-labeled datasets that limits understanding of when these interpretable models succeed or fail.

entry.title: A Geometric Characterization of the Stationary Plateau for Two-Layer Neural Networks

author.name: Tian Ding, Dawei Li, Ruoyu Sun

entry.summary: This paper geometrically characterizes stationary plateaus in two-layer neural network loss landscapes, focusing on neuron splitting where duplicating hidden neurons creates affine sets of stationary points. It classifies these as local minima or saddles via a per-neuron inner Hessian object.

entry.title: MeshTok: Efficient Multi-Scale Tokenization for Scalable PDE Transformers

author.name: Yanshun Zhao, Xiaoyu Peng, Jiamin Jiang, Congcong Zhu, Jingrun Chen

entry.summary: MeshTok is an adaptive mesh refinement-inspired tokenization framework for PDE transformers that selectively refines spatial regions with sharp gradients or multiscale structure, producing heterogeneous multiscale tokens on a fixed grid. It addresses the inefficiency of uniform patchification for complex PDE solutions.

entry.title: When Both Layers Learn: Training Dynamics of Representing Linear Models via ReLU Networks

author.name: Berk Tinaz, Changzhi Xie, Mahdi Soltanolkotabi

entry.summary: This paper characterizes gradient descent dynamics when jointly training both layers of a one-hidden-layer ReLU network to fit a linear target under Gaussian inputs, analyzing the loss landscape with non-strict saddles and explaining why GD reliably escapes bad stationary regions. It models end-to-end training behavior in inverse problems and autoencoders.

entry.title: Smart Picks in the Dark: Towards Efficient RLVR for Reasoning via Tracing Metacognitive Pivots

author.name: Guangcheng Zhu, Shenzhi Yang, Haobo Wang, Xing Zheng, Yingfan MA, Xuening Feng, Zhongqi Chen, Bowen Song, Weiqiang Wang, Gang Chen

entry.summary: This work studies a pick-in-the-dark setup for data-efficient RLVR, aiming to select beneficial unlabeled samples without prior supervision by tracing metacognitive pivots in reasoning. It bridges supervised data selection (which needs labels) and unsupervised RLVR (which underperforms).

entry.title: GeoMin: Data-Efficient Semi-Supervised RLVR via Geometric Distribution Modeling

author.name: Guangcheng Zhu, Shenzhi Yang, Haobo Wang, Xing Zheng, Yingfan MA, Xuening Feng, Zhongqi Chen, Kai Tang, Zhengqing Zang, Bowen Song, Weiqiang Wang, Gang Chen

entry.summary: GeoMin is a data-efficient semi-supervised RLVR method that models global feature distributions on labeled data to decode structural discrepancies between correct and incorrect unlabeled samples, going beyond coarse performance heuristics. It improves the data-efficiency bottleneck in semi-supervised RLVR for LLM reasoning.

entry.title: Test-Time Compute Scaling for ASR with Depth-Conditioned Looped Transformers

author.name: Yacouba Kaloga, Shashi Kumar, Shakeel A. Sheikh, Driss Khalil, Petr Motlicek, Ina Kodrasi

entry.summary: LARM is a depth-conditioned looped transformer for ASR that turns recurrent encoder depth into a controllable test-time compute axis, combining sparse CTC checkpoints, supervision-clock embeddings, FiLM depth conditioning, and delayed soft-posterior feedback. It enables trading test-time compute for better recognition without training a larger model.

entry.title: Scenario Generation for Risk-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Probably Approximately Safe Guarantees

author.name: Mohit Prashant, Arvind Easwaran

entry.summary: Develops scenario generation for risk-aware RL that constructs probabilistic barrier certificates to provide Probably Approximately Safe guarantees, addressing tight bounds under transition uncertainty. It approximates trajectory distributions to demarcate safe from unknown behavior.

entry.title: RIDE: An Open Dataset and Benchmark for Train Delay Prediction

author.name: Cl\'ement Elliker, Mathis Le Bail, Cl\'ement Mantoux, Jesse Read, Sonia Vanier

entry.summary: Introduces RIDE, an open nationwide-scale benchmark for train delay prediction over the Belgian railway network covering 94.5M train events and weather records. It standardizes prediction tasks and evaluation protocols to enable reproducible progress.

entry.title: Toward Pre-Deployment Assurance for Enterprise AI Agents: Ontology-Grounded Simulation and Trust Certification

author.name: Thanh Luong Tuan, Abhijit Sanyal

entry.summary: Presents an ontology-grounded verification framework for pre-deployment assurance of enterprise AI agents, combining an Agent Operational Envelope, automated ontology-to-scenario generation, and trust certification. It addresses the gap between LLM benchmarking and production deployment assurance.

entry.title: Dive into the Scene: Breaking the Perceptual Bottleneck in Vision-Language Decision Making via Focus Plan Generation

author.name: Boyuan Xiao, Bohong Chen, Yumeng Li, Ji Feng, Yao-Xiang Ding, Kun Zhou

entry.summary: Addresses the perceptual bottleneck in vision-language decision making by proposing focus plan generation to break visual hallucinations from distractors in embodied tasks. It moves beyond ineffective one-step focus to a planned approach for distinguishing task-relevant objects.

entry.title: MimeLens: Position-Agnostic Content-Type Detection for Binary Fragments

author.name: Michael J. Bommarito II

entry.summary: Introduces MimeLens, a family of small BERT-style encoders for position-agnostic content-type detection of binary fragments, pretrained on byte windows sampled at random offsets without privileged head-of-file position. It handles real-world inputs like single packets, carved fragments, and disk blocks that break whole-file classifiers like Magika.

entry.title: Flatness and Generalization: Learning Multi-Index Models with Homogeneous Neural Networks

author.name: Harsh Vardhan, Hossein Taheri, Arya Mazumdar

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes a rigorous connection between flatness of minima and generalization for two-layer homogeneous neural networks learning multi-index models, addressing the critique that flatness can be made arbitrary via symmetries. It provides conditions under which the flatness-generalization heuristic holds.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Decentralized Stochastic Convex Optimization over Networks

author.name: Nitai Kluger, Amit Attia, Tomer Koren

entry.summary: This theoretical paper presents an accelerated decentralized stochastic optimization method over gossip networks that preserves the centralized convergence rate for far more workers than previous bounds, improving the maximal worker scaling. It uses a one-step-delayed stochastic acceleration technique.

entry.title: Predictable Scaling Laws of Optimal Hyperparameters for LLM Continued Pre-training

author.name: Yongwei Zhou, Juncheng Diao, Junlin Shang, Peiguang Li, Rongxiang Weng

entry.summary: Empirically shows that optimal hyperparameters during LLM continued pre-training follow predictable scaling laws, and proposes a framework relating compute budget to optimal learning rate and batch size. This could reduce costly grid searches and training instability.

entry.title: AdaPlanBench: Evaluating Adaptive Planning in Large Language Model Agents under World and User Constraints

author.name: Jiayu Liu, Cheng Qian, Zhenhailong Wang, Bingxuan Li, Jiateng Liu, Heng Wang, Jeonghwan Kim, Yumeng Wang, Xiusi Chen, Yi R. Fung, Heng Ji

entry.summary: AdaPlanBench is a dynamic interactive benchmark evaluating whether LLM agents can adaptively re-plan under progressively revealed world and user constraints, built on 307 household tasks. It targets an underexplored gap in adaptive planning evaluation.

entry.title: Many Circuits, One Mechanism: Input Variation and Evaluation Granularity in Circuit Discovery

author.name: Alireza Bayat Makou, Jingcheng Niu, Subhabrata Dutta, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: Tests the assumption that structurally different discovered circuits imply distinct mechanisms by varying input statistics while fixing the task, finding phantom specialization where structurally distinct circuits implement the same computation. Uses sequence copying across token-frequency bands in Pythia models.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Elicits Contextual Learning of Unseen Language Translation

author.name: Hanxu Hu, Zden\v{e}k \v{S}najdr, Pinzhen Chen, Jannis Vamvas, Rico Sennrich

entry.summary: Proposes an RL approach (rewarding with chrF) to elicit the meta-skill of using in-context linguistic knowledge for translating unseen low-resource languages, rather than memorizing specific languages. RL-trained models generalize contextual learning better than continued training.

entry.title: BRepCLIP: Contrastive Multimodal Pretraining on BRep Primitives for CAD Understanding

author.name: Muhammad Usama, Didier Stricker, Mohammad Sadil Khan, Muhammad Zeshan Afzal

entry.summary: BRepCLIP is the first framework to align boundary representation (BRep) CAD geometry with language and image embeddings via contrastive pretraining. It tokenizes CAD objects as face and edge sequences with separate vocabularies for surfaces and curves.

entry.title: Parallel Jacobi Decoding for Fast Autoregressive Image Generation

author.name: Boya Liao, Ying Li, Siyong Jian, Huan Wang

entry.summary: Parallel Jacobi Decoding accelerates autoregressive image generation by expanding draft tokens in the 2D spatial domain rather than 1D, exploiting local spatial correlations. This training-free method overcomes the saturation caused by 1D error propagation in standard Jacobi decoding.

entry.title: VTI-CoT: Visual-Textual Interleaved Chain of Thought for Video Reasoning

author.name: Shufan Zhang, Ziyue Lin, Bairun Wang, Lei Jin, Xuanding Ding, Xinzhu Ma, Kunlin Yang

entry.summary: VTI-CoT introduces visual-textual interleaved chain-of-thought for video reasoning, integrating textual reasoning steps with corresponding visual frames rather than relying on text-only deduction. It develops an automated annotation pipeline to address the scarcity of interleaved CoT data.

entry.title: Resonant Minds: Closed-Loop Social Avatars with Theory of Mind

author.name: Jianxu Shangguan, Jing Xu, Hang Ye, Xiaoxuan Ma, Yizhou Wang, Wentao Zhu

entry.summary: Resonant Minds proposes a closed-loop dual-agent framework for social avatars unifying perception, Theory of Mind social reasoning, and multimodal expression in a continuous interaction cycle. It bridges the gap between dialogue-capable LLMs and visually faithful talking-head models.

entry.title: VZCrash: A Large-Scale IMU Dataset of Ego-Vehicle Crashes

author.name: Tommaso Bianconcini, Henrique Pi\~neiro Monteagudo, Aurel Pjetri, Tomaso Trinci, Leonardo Taccari

entry.summary: VZCrash is the largest public dataset of real-world vehicle crashes with IMU telemetry, containing over 31,000 validated crashes and 158,000 negatives from 73,010 commercial vehicles. It includes acceleration, angular velocity, and GPS speed with benchmark experiments from heuristics to deep learning.

entry.title: Where, What, Why, and Importance: Structured Defect Grounding for Text-to-Image Feedback

author.name: Huaisong Zhang, Hao Yu, Yuxuan Zhang, Jiahe Wang, Xinrui Chen, Haoxiang Cao, Feng Lu, Wendong Zhang, Changqian Yu, Chun Yuan

entry.summary: Structured Defect Grounding casts text-to-image diagnosis as structured set prediction, answering where defects occur, what type, why, and importance, replacing heatmap regression. This enables localizing variable-cardinality defects and binding semantic reasons to individual failures for richer T2I feedback.

entry.title: Adversarial Attacks Already Tell the Answer: Directional Bias-Guided Test-time Defense for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Liangsheng Liu, Si Chen, Jiamin Wu, Weiwei Feng, Zhixin Cheng, Xiaotian Yin, Wenfei Yang, Tianzhu Zhang

entry.summary: ReCache learns budget-aware caching schedules for diffusion models via REINFORCE, letting users specify a target compute budget rather than tuning thresholds. It selects which denoising steps to fully recompute, inverting heuristic-based schedules where cost is a side-effect.

entry.title: Symb-xMIL: Symbolic Explanations for Multiple Instance Learning in Digital Pathology

author.name: Yanqing Luo (Berlin Institute for the Foundations of Learning and Data, Berlin, Germany, Machine Learning Group, Technische Universit\"at Berlin, Berlin, Germany), Julius Hense (Berlin Institute for the Foundations of Learning and Data, Berlin, Germany, Machine Learning Group, Technische Universit\"at Berlin, Berlin, Germany), Niklas Preni{\ss}l (Institute of Pathology, Charit\'e Universit\"atsmedizin, Berlin, Germany, Berlin Institute of Health at Charit\'e -- Universit\"atsmedizin Berlin, BIH Biomedical Innovation Academy, BIH Charit\'e Digital Clinician Scientist Program, Berlin, Germany), Andreas Mock (Institute of Pathology, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, Munich, Germany, Division of Translational Medical Oncology, DKFZ, Heidelberg, Germany, NCT Heidelberg, Heidelberg, Germany, German Cancer Consortium), Klaus-Robert M\"uller (Berlin Institute for the Foundations of Learning and Data, Berlin, Germany, Machine Learning Group, Technische Universit\"at Berlin, Berlin, Germany, Department of Artificial Intelligence, Korea University, Seoul, Korea, Max-Planck Institute for Informatics, Saarbr\"ucken, Germany), Thomas Schnake (Department of Chemistry, Chemical Physics Theory Group, University of Toronto, Canada, Vector Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Toronto, Canada, Acceleration Consortium, University of Toronto, Canada), Mina Jamshidi Idaji (Berlin Institute for the Foundations of Learning and Data, Berlin, Germany, Machine Learning Group, Technische Universit\"at Berlin, Berlin, Germany)

entry.summary: Symb-xMIL is a post-hoc symbolic explanation framework for multiple instance learning in digital pathology that quantifies how a model's behavior aligns with human-readable logical decision rules (AND, OR, NOT) between features. It explains how evidence from tissue regions is combined, going beyond region-highlighting heatmaps.

entry.title: RhymeFlow: Training-Free Acceleration for Video Generation with Asynchronous Denoising Flow Scheduling

author.name: Chensheng Dai, Shengjun Zhang, Yifan Li, Zhang Zhang, Zheng Zhu, Yueqi Duan

entry.summary: RhymeFlow accelerates video generation by relaxing the constraint that every frame undergo full dense denoising across all timesteps, using asynchronous denoising flow scheduling. It exploits content and motion correspondence among adjacent frames so non-keyframes need less computation.

entry.title: Monte Carlo Steklov Operators for Large-Scale Geometry Processing in the Wild

author.name: Arman Maesumi, Tanish Makadia, Aruna Anderson, Oras Phongpanangam, Justin Solomon, Daniel Ritchie

entry.summary: Introduces a Monte Carlo method for estimating the Dirichlet-to-Neumann (Steklov) operator to enable robust geometry processing on messy, multi-component in-the-wild meshes. Relaxes topology assumptions that break intrinsic Laplacian-based methods.

entry.title: PiL-World: A Chunk-Wise World Model for VLA Policy-in-the-Loop Evaluation

author.name: Chong Ma, Taiyi Su, Jian Zhu, Jianjun Zhang, Zitai Huang, Yi Xu, Hanli Wang

entry.summary: PiL-World is a chunk-wise world model for closed-loop policy-in-the-loop evaluation of VLA policies, generating multi-view future observations conditioned on each executed action chunk. Addresses limitations of open-loop world-model evaluation.

entry.title: Flow-based Policy Adaptation without Policy Updates

author.name: Luzhe Sun, Jingtian Ji, Haoran Chen, Jiawei Zhou, Matthew R. Walter

entry.summary: GLOVES is a family of flow-based adaptation methods that correct suboptimal non-expert actions by transporting them toward an expert distribution without updating the policy, and uses reverse flow evaluation as an intervention gate. Enables selective action-level adaptation preserving agent intent.

entry.title: Environment-Robust Representation Learning with Empirical Bayes

author.name: Yuli Slavutsky, Matthew Shen, Bohan Wu, David M. Blei

entry.summary: Proposes an empirical Bayes approach for environment-robust representation learning where environments shift a latent variable while conditional mechanisms stay stable, deriving a variational objective with a cross-environment balancing term. Targets multi-environment prediction like clinical cohorts.

entry.title: Minimizing the Hidden Cost of Scales: Graph-Guided Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization for Large Language Models

author.name: Rayyan Abdalla, Amir Hussein, Min Wu, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: Proposes SAGE-PTQ, an ultra-low-bit post-training quantization framework that separates salient and unsalient weights, models unsalient weights as a sparse graph to set per-layer grouping, and minimizes hidden scaling overhead. It matters for efficient LLM deployment under extreme quantization.

entry.title: PSEBench: A Controllable and Verifiable Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs in Patient Safety Event Triage

author.name: Keqi Han, Ryan Young, Annabel Strauss, Lindsey Hughes, Katharine M. Nesbitt, Nicole Schueler, Che Ngufor, Carl Yang, Yuan Xue, Zhijun Yin

entry.summary: Introduces PSEBench, a controllable benchmark for LLM patient safety event triage using clause cards that factorize regulatory text into auditable decision specifications, testing policy reasoning, information seeking, and abstention. It matters for high-stakes healthcare compliance evaluation.

entry.title: Seeing Time: Benchmarking Chronological Reasoning and Shortcut Biases in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Haoyu Zhou, Qing Qing, Caichong Li, Qixin Zhang, Yongcheng Jing, Ziqi Xu, Juncheng Hu, Xikun Zhang, Renqiang Luo

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for chronological reasoning in vision-language models across and within images, with three datasets, exposing shortcut biases in how VLMs judge temporal order. It matters for an under-explored temporal-reasoning capability of multimodal models.

entry.title: A Framework for Measuring Appropriate Reliance on Set-Valued AI Advice

author.name: Ranjan Mishra, Jakob Schoeffer

entry.summary: Develops the first formal framework for measuring appropriate human reliance on set-valued AI advice (discrete sets or continuous intervals) in the judge-advisor paradigm across classification and regression, defining correct-reliance metrics. It matters as uncertainty-communicating advice increasingly replaces point predictions.

entry.title: DragOn: A Benchmark and Dataset for Drag-Based GUI Interactions

author.name: Nathan Bout, Maxime Langevin, Ronan Riochet

entry.summary: Introduces DragOn, a benchmark and large training dataset (286K screenshots, 3.5M tasks) for drag-based GUI interactions like highlighting, cell selection, resizing, and sliders. Addresses the underrepresentation of drag grounding versus click grounding in GUI agents.

entry.title: Benchmark Everything Everywhere All at Once

author.name: Shiyun Xiong, Dongming Wu, Peiwen Sun, Yuang Ai, Bokang Yang, Wencheng Han, Xiao-Hui Li, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: Introduces Benchmark Agent, a fully autonomous agentic system for constructing benchmarks end-to-end from query analysis and subtask design to annotation and quality control. Aims to address the labor-intensive, unsustainable nature of manual benchmark creation.

entry.title: Policy-Conditioned Counterfactual Credit for Verifiable Reinforcement Learning of Long-Horizon Language Agents

author.name: Renwei Meng

entry.summary: Proposes CVT-RL, a constrained policy-gradient algorithm for long-horizon language agents using dense verifiable rewards, intervention-validity gating, and a policy-conditioned counterfactual contribution estimator. Addresses unsupported evidence chains and shortcut actions by estimating each step's causal contribution to verified success.

entry.title: LoRi: Low-Rank Distillation for Implicit Reasoning

author.name: Ryan Solgi, Jiayi Tian, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes LoRi, a low-rank distillation framework for implicit chain-of-thought that transfers reasoning by aligning teacher and student hidden-state trajectories in a shared low-rank tensor subspace using first- and second-order statistics. Motivated by the observed low-rank structure of reasoning trajectories.

entry.title: Balancing Image Compression and Generation with Bootstrapped Tokenization

author.name: Haozhe Chi, Jinghan Li, Hao Jiang, Wu Sheng, Yi Ma, Jing Wang, Yadong Mu

entry.summary: Introduces SelfBootTok, an image tokenization method that cleanly decomposes information into global and local token groups via self-bootstrapped learning, shifting detail prediction burden from generator to tokenizer. Reduces generator computation by ~40% while improving reconstruction.

entry.title: Value-and-Structure Alignment for Routing-Consistent Quantization of Mixture-of-Experts Models

author.name: Hancheol Park, Geonho Lee, Tairen Piao, Tae-Ho Kim

entry.summary: Proposes VSRAQ, a MoE-specific post-training quantization objective that preserves pre-quantization expert-selection behavior to prevent routing instability where small perturbations change top-k expert choices. Combines value and structure routing alignment objectives.

entry.title: TLA-Prover: Verifiable TLA+ Specification Synthesis via Preference-Optimized Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Eric Spencer, Arslan Bisharat, Brian Ortiz, Khushboo Bhadauria, TaiNing Wang, George K. Thiruvathukal, Konstantin Laufer, Mohammed Abuhamad

entry.summary: TLA-Prover is a 20B model for synthesizing verifiable TLA+ formal specifications, trained with SFT plus repair-based GRPO where TLC model-checker provides reward signals. It significantly improves syntactic parse and semantic model-check rates over public baselines.

entry.title: Plug-and-Play Guidance for Discrete Diffusion Models via Gradient-Informed Logit Correction

author.name: Hongkun Dou, Zike Chen, Fengji Li, Hongjue Li, Yue Deng

entry.summary: GILC is a plug-and-play, training-free guidance framework for discrete diffusion models that repurposes the denoising network as a variational proxy and uses a Jacobian-free mechanism to correct clean-prediction logits, supporting differentiable and non-differentiable rewards. It enables efficient controllable discrete generation.

entry.title: In-Context Multiple Instance Learning

author.name: Alexander M\"ollers, Marvin Sextro, Julius Hense, Gabriel Dernbach, Klaus-Robert M\"uller

entry.summary: Introduces in-context multiple instance learning by pretraining a Perceiver-style in-context learner on synthetic data, enabling new MIL tasks to be solved from a handful of labeled bags in a single forward pass without gradient updates. It targets the low-label regime where flexible models overfit and rigid ones underfit.

entry.title: TempoVLA: Learning Speed-Controllable Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Dong Jing, Jingchen Nie, Tianqi Zhang, Jiaqi Liu, Huaxiu Yao, Zhiwu Lu, Mingyu Ding

entry.summary: TempoVLA learns speed-controllable vision-language-action policies, observing that predicted action magnitude governs robot speed and turning this into an explicit speed condition, enabling both acceleration and the under-explored deceleration. It allows fast transit and slow precise contact phases within a single VLA.

entry.title: Do Transformers Need Three Projections? Systematic Study of QKV Variants

author.name: Ali Kayyam, Anusha Madan Gopal, M Anthony Lewis

entry.summary: Systematically studies whether transformers need all three QKV projections by evaluating shared-projection variants (Q-K=V, Q=K-V, Q=K=V) and addressing the resulting symmetric attention via 2D positional encodings, across synthetic, vision, and language tasks up to 1.2B parameters. It clarifies the individual roles of Q, K, V projections.

entry.title: Dual Advantage Fields

author.name: Alexey Zemtsov, Maxim Bobrin, Alexander Nikulin, Dmitry V. Dylov, Fakhri Karray, Vladislav Kurenkov, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}, Arip Asadulaev

entry.summary: Dual Advantage Fields turns a bilinear dual value model into a local advantage signal for offline goal-conditioned RL, learning an action-effect model that predicts feature displacement and scoring actions by alignment with the goal direction. It bridges global reachability estimates with local action selection.

entry.title: Revisiting Privacy Amplification by Subsampling in Selective Release DPSGD

author.name: Xiaobo Huang, Fang Xie

entry.summary: This paper re-examines privacy amplification by subsampling in the DPSUR selective-release DP-SGD algorithm, showing its privacy accounting overlooks sampling-probability variation from selective release and thus compromises rigor. It proposes corrected privacy analysis for the selective-release mechanism.

entry.title: Low-Rank Decay for Grokking in Scale-Invariant Transformers: A Spectral-Geometric View

author.name: Mingyu Li

entry.summary: This single-author paper studies grokking in scale-invariant transformers (with RMSNorm and QK-Norm) through a spectral-geometric lens, proposing Low-Rank Decay, a nuclear-norm-like regularizer whose subgradient retains a tangential component even in scale-invariant regimes. This drives the function toward lower rank where standard weight decay cannot.

entry.title: Rethinking Incompleteness: Formalizing Protocol Divergence and Train-Once Learning for Robust IMVC

author.name: Haolu Liu, Xiyue Wang, Xuanting Xie, Liangjian Wen, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: Reveals that incomplete multi-view clustering evaluation is flawed because identical missing rates can differ 50x in fully observed sample proportions, inducing different learning regimes. It formalizes incompleteness divergence and proposes train-once learning robust to protocol variation.

entry.title: SC-TauPath: A Structural Connectivity Attribution Framework for Mapping Tau Propagation Pathways in Alzheimer's Disease

author.name: Jing Zhang, Norman Scheel, Minheng Chen, Tong Chen, Yanjun Lyu, David C. Zhu, Rong Zhang, Dajiang Zhu

entry.summary: Presents SC-TauPath, a structural connectivity attribution framework combining a network-diffusion-augmented MLP with gradient-times-input attribution to map tau propagation pathways in Alzheimer's disease. It produces neurobiologically interpretable multi-scale pathway maps from in vivo imaging.

entry.title: Cartridges at Scale: Training Modular KV Caches over Large Document Collections

author.name: Momchil Hardalov, Gonzalo Iglesias, Adri\`a de Gispert

entry.summary: Cartridges at Scale (CAS) is a training framework for scalable multi-cartridge learning, where document collections are distilled into reusable KV caches that avoid prefilling; it adds dynamic distractor mixing and a memory-efficient budget manager. It solves the problem that monolithic cartridges don't scale and naive mixing collapses performance.

entry.title: Rethinking Continual Experience Internalization for Self-Evolving LLM Agents

author.name: Jingwen Chen, Wenkai Yang, Shengda Fan, Wenbo Nie, Chenxing Sun, Shaodong Zheng, Yangen Hu, Lu Pan, Ke Zeng, Yankai Lin

entry.summary: This paper finds that under multi-iteration experience learning, existing methods for converting agent interactions into reusable parametric capability suffer progressive capability collapse rather than compounding improvement. It examines experience granularity (principle-level vs instance-level) and other dimensions to diagnose the failure.

entry.title: Epistemic Injustice in Language Models: An Audit of Pretraining Filters and Guardrails

author.name: Marco Antonio Stranisci, A Pranav, Rossana Damiano, Christian Hardmeier, Anne Lauscher

entry.summary: Audits four pretraining filters and three inference-time guardrails for epistemic erasure around gender and regional-origin mentions, finding decisions driven by blocklist lexical cues while missing contextually harmful content. Reveals tensions between automated systems and human judgment.

entry.title: Decomposing Factual Sycophancy in Language Models: How Size and Instruction Tuning Shape Robustness

author.name: Victor De Marez, Luna De Bruyne, Walter Daelemans

entry.summary: Decomposes factual sycophancy into truth margin (baseline preference) and manipulation sensitivity across 56 open models (0.3B-32B) and 13 manipulation types, finding vulnerability governed mainly by size but reshaped by instruction tuning. Small instruction-tuned models can become less robust.

entry.title: KV-Control: Parameter-Efficient K/V Injection for Trajectory-Controlled Text-to-Motion

author.name: Tengjiao Sun, Pengcheng Fang, Xiaoyu Zhan, Yanwen Guo, Dongjie Fu, Xiaohao Cai, Hansung Kim

entry.summary: KV-Control is a parameter-efficient attention-side interface for trajectory-controlled text-to-motion generation, injecting K/V into a frozen masked motion generator. It enables precise path/end-effector control without overwriting the pretrained text-conditioned prior or heavy test-time optimization.

entry.title: TextWand: A Unified Framework for Scene Text Editing

author.name: Shuyu Wang, Zhile Guan, Hongxiu Chen, Yule Duan, Weiqi Li, Xin Shan, Ronggang Wang, Jian Zhang

entry.summary: TextWand unifies scene text removal, generation, and replacement in a single model by decomposing editing into rendering and erasure primitives. It introduces Overlay-Reference Positional Encoding for layout fidelity and Region-Adaptive Suppression for clean erasure, plus a new benchmark.

entry.title: Gender Artifacts from Art History to Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Piera Riccio, Miriam Doh, Benedikt H\"oltgen, Noa Garcia, Nanne van Noord

entry.summary: StyleGender is the first dataset investigating the interplay between gender representation and artistic style across art history and generated images, comprising 74k images over 19 styles. It enables direct art-history-to-generation comparison of how style encodes gender constructions.

entry.title: Self-Learning Expression Deformations for Data-Efficient Gaussian Avatars

author.name: Jiahao Yang, Xiaohang Yang, Qing Wang, Yilan Dong, Gregory Slabaugh, Shanxin Yuan

entry.summary: SAGE enables data-efficient animatable Gaussian avatars by self-learning expression-induced deformations from minimal input, replacing extensive multiview sequential data. It jointly optimizes 2D Gaussian surfels and an SDF for compact surface-aligned distributions with self-supervised expression learning.

entry.title: Diff-CA: Separating Common and Salient Factors with Diffusion Models

author.name: Micha\"el Soumm, Alexandre Fournier Montgieux, Yunlong He, Pietro Gori, Alasdair Newson

entry.summary: Diff-CA enables contrastive analysis to separate common from salient factors between two distributions using diffusion models, overcoming VAE/GAN reconstruction limitations. It trains a prompt-free image-conditioned diffusion model then decomposes conditioning into common and salient factors with weak supervision and theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: Adaptive Tokenisation Via Temporal Redundancy Masking And Latent Inpainting

author.name: Kevin Dave, Sai Aditya Patkuri, Chhaya Kumar Das, Gouranga Bala, R. Venkatesh Babu, Rajeshkumar SA

entry.summary: This work introduces a parameter-free adaptive video token allocation mechanism that exploits temporal redundancy already encoded in a frozen continuous video tokenizer's latent space. Spatial positions changing minimally between frames carry near-zero information, avoiding costly iterative searches or full-rate decoder passes.

entry.title: StoryVideoQA: Scaling Deep Video Understanding with a Large-Scale, Multi-Genre and Auto-Generated Dataset

author.name: Zhengqian Wu, Zhixian Liu, Aodong Chen, Jingyang Zhang, Ruizhe Li, Hanlin Ge, Zhongyuan Wang, Chunxia Xiao, Chao Liang

entry.summary: StoryVideoQA scales deep video understanding with a large-scale, multi-genre auto-generated dataset addressing the comprehension of complex storylines beyond factoid VideoQA. It builds on StoryMind to automatically construct balanced fine-grained DVU datasets overcoming manual annotation limits.

entry.title: MoDex: A Diffusion Policy for Sequential Multi-Object Dexterous Grasping

author.name: Haofei Lu, Hongjia Liu, Yifei Dong, Florian T. Pokorny, Jens Lundell, Danica Kragic

entry.summary: MoDex is a diffusion policy for sequentially grasping multiple objects with one dexterous hand without releasing held items, using opposition-space conditioning to reserve degrees of freedom. Enables multi-object grasps underutilized by single-object methods.

entry.title: Discrete-WAM: Unified Discrete Vision-Action Token Editing for World-Policy Learning

author.name: Ziyang Yao, Haochen Liu, Yuncheng Jiang, Zeyu Zhu, Zibin Guo, Jingru Wang, Tianle Liu, Jianwei Cui, Kuiyuan Yang, Hongwei Xie, Jingwei Zhao, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye

entry.summary: Discrete-WAM represents future visual states and ego actions as aligned discrete tokens in a shared discrete diffusion world-policy framework for autonomous driving, enabling compositional counterfactual reasoning. Goes beyond direct state-to-action mappings.

entry.title: Breaking Time: A Fully Gaussian Framework for Distributed and Continuous-Time SLAM

author.name: Davide Ceriola, Simone Ferrari, Luca Di Giammarino, Leonardo Brizi, Giorgio Grisetti

entry.summary: G-solver introduces a fully Gaussian distributed framework for continuous-time SLAM combining Gaussian Belief Propagation with Gaussian Process motion priors for heterogeneous asynchronous sensors. Enables consistent interpolation and scalable message-passing estimation.

entry.title: Multi-Resolution Tactile Imitation Learning for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Rickmer Krohn, Erik Helmut, Niklas Funk, Jan Peters, Vignesh Prasad, Georgia Chalvatzaki

entry.summary: MiTaS fuses multiple heterogeneous tactile sensors (RGB camera, GelSight Mini, event-based Evetac) at different temporal resolutions via modality-specific stems and transformer fusion for contact-rich manipulation imitation learning. Explores underexplored heterogeneous tactile fusion.

entry.title: Amortized Nonlinear Model Predictive Control

author.name: Francesco Pillitteri, Alberto Bemporad

entry.summary: Amortized Nonlinear MPC approximates the optimal control move for input-affine systems with a state-dependent QP whose parameters come from an analytic baseline plus a learned residual corrector, solved by a differentiable interior-point layer. Enables real-time NMPC on resource-constrained hardware.

entry.title: Fast and Robust Convergence Rate for TD(0) with Linear Function Approximation, Universal Learning Steps and I.I.D. Samples

author.name: Ziad Kobeissi (L2S), \'Elo\"ise Berthier (U2IS)

entry.summary: Establishes a new finite-time convergence rate for TD(0) with linear function approximation under i.i.d. samples, constant learning step, and Polyak-Juditsky averaging that is fast (1/k), robust to ill-conditioning, and independent of the smallest eigenvalue. Provides sharp constants.

entry.title: Optimally taming biases in black-box models for efficient semiparametric estimation

author.name: Yihong Gu, Qishuo Yin, Tianxi Cai, Jianqing Fan

entry.summary: This paper questions whether the multiplicative error dependence in double machine learning is optimal for black-box nuisance estimation, analyzing the partial linear model under structure-agnostic conditions. It seeks optimal bias control for efficient semiparametric estimation with generic ML nuisance functions.

entry.title: Harnessing Generalist Agents for Contextualized Time Series

author.name: Zihao Li, Kaifeng Jin, Yuanchen Bei, Jiaru Zou, Avaneesh Kumar, Xuying Ning, Yanjun Zhao, Mengting Ai, Baoyu Jing, Hanghang Tong, Jingrui He

entry.summary: Introduces TimeClaw, an agentic harness equipping generalist LLM agents with time-series-native runtime tools and executable temporal operations for contextualized forecasting and analysis. It matters for bridging textual agents and structured temporal signals in end-to-end workflows.

entry.title: Ten Headache Specialists versus Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Literature Summarization: A Critical Evaluation and Comparison

author.name: Alejandro Lozano, Keiko Ihara, Ping-Hao Yang, Carrie E. Robertson, Jennifer Stern, Allan Purdy, Hsiangkuo Yuan, Pengfei Zhang, Yulia Orlova, Olga Fermo, Jennifer Hranilovich, Fred Cohen, Todd J. Schwedt, Jenelle A. Jindal, Serena Yeung-Levy, Chia-Chun Chiang

entry.summary: Compares ten headache specialists against a RAG-based agentic AI using multiple LLMs for clinical literature summarization, providing a critical expert evaluation and direct human-AI comparison. It matters for assessing AI reliability in evidence-based medicine. Note: models referenced (GPT-4o, Sonnet, Llama 3.1) are older.

entry.title: Evaluation of LLMs for Mathematical Formalization in Lean

author.name: Tyson Klingner, Drew Bladek, Escher Crawford, Bohao Chen, Ariel Fu, Kaira Nair, Jarod Alper, Giovanni Inchiostro, Vasily Ilin

entry.summary: Benchmarks 30+ LLMs on generating Lean 4 formal proofs using pass@k and refine@k on miniF2F and miniCTX, finding Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 4.7 lead with cost-effective alternatives noted. It matters as a practical guide for choosing models for formalization projects. (Both top models are existing releases as of coverage date.)

entry.title: Beyond Vector Similarity: A Structural Analysis of Graph-Augmented Retrieval for Industrial Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Grama Chethan

entry.summary: Compares eight retrieval architectures for aerospace supply-chain knowledge graphs, showing five query classes are structurally unreachable for vector retrieval and advancing the operator vocabulary thesis that LLM graph reasoning is limited by available traversal operators, not model intelligence. It matters for graph-augmented retrieval design.

entry.title: Unsupervised Skill Discovery for Agentic Data Analysis

author.name: Zhisong Qiu, Kangqi Song, Shengwei Tang, Shuofei Qiao, Lei Liang, Huajun Chen, Shumin Deng

entry.summary: Proposes DataCOPE, an unsupervised verifier-guided skill discovery framework for data-analytic agents that derives verifier signals from exploration trajectories without labeled supervision. Iteratively coordinates an analytic agent to discover reusable procedural skills.

entry.title: The Granularity Gap: A Multi-Dimensional Longitudinal Audit of Sycophancy in Gemini Models

author.name: Patrick Keough

entry.summary: A longitudinal audit of sycophancy across six Gemini variants (generations 2.0, 2.5, 3.0) on 73 adversarial prompts under three guardrail conditions, yielding 8,830 graded responses. Introduces the Granularity Gap concept showing coarse binary metrics mask subtle social-compliance behaviors. Note that the analyzed Gemini models are existing releases.

entry.title: Statistically Reliable LLM-Based Ranking Evaluation via Prediction-Powered Inference

author.name: Abhishek Divekar

entry.summary: Extends Prediction-Powered Inference to ranking evaluation, producing provably unbiased bias-corrected estimates of hierarchical metrics like Precision@K by combining small human-labeled sets with large LLM-judged sets. Reduces output-space computation and lowers standard error on the ESCI benchmark.

entry.title: SlotGCG: Exploiting the Positional Vulnerability in LLMs for Jailbreak Attacks

author.name: Seungwon Jeong, Jiwoo Jeong, Hyeonjin Kim, Yunseok Lee, Woojin Lee

entry.summary: Introduces SlotGCG, a jailbreak attack that explores token insertion positions (slots) beyond the prompt suffix used by standard GCG, finding vulnerability strongly depends on slot selection. Proposes a Vulnerable Slot Score to identify high-risk insertion points.

entry.title: LongSpace: Exploring Long-Horizon Spatial Memory from Perception to Recall in Video

author.name: Shiqiang Lang, Jing Liu, Haoyang He, Peiwen Sun, Yuanteng Chen, Tao Liu, Lan Yang, Longteng Guo, Honggang Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces LongSpace-Bench for long-horizon spatial memory in room-tour videos and LongSpace, a memory framework that models long videos as chunks with 3D structural cues for spatial reasoning. Targets retrieval of previously observed layouts, routes, and object states for tasks like autonomous driving and navigation.

entry.title: Benchmarking Counterfactual Prediction in Epidemic Time Series with Time-Varying Interventions

author.name: Wenhao Mu, Facundo Yan, Anik Mumssen, Marisa Eisenberg, Alexander Rodr\'iguez

entry.summary: Develops a large-scale benchmark for counterfactual prediction in epidemic time series under static and time-varying interventions, supporting single- and multi-policy settings with observable counterfactual outcomes. Addresses the lack of realistic causal inference benchmarks with ground-truth counterfactuals.

entry.title: ViCuR: Visual Cues as Recoverable Privilege for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Kanghui Tian, Siyuan Liu, Ziang Yan, Sheng Xia, Shuai Dong, Yi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes ViCuR, a multimodal on-policy distillation framework that replaces answer-side privileged-teacher signals with visual cues derived from the input, avoiding train-test mismatch and shortcut imitation. Aims to encourage visually grounded reasoning rather than answer leakage.

entry.title: UniVoice: A Unified Model for Speech and Singing Voice Generation

author.name: Junjie Zheng, Huixin Xue, Shihong Ren, Chaofan Ding, Hao Liu, Zihao Chen

entry.summary: Presents UniVoice, a unified speech and singing voice generation framework based on conditional flow matching that handles both flexible language-driven prosody for speech and explicit melody/rhythm control for singing via differentiated conditioning. Resolves the conflict where melody conditions should constrain singing but not speech.

entry.title: OneReason Technical Report

author.name: OneRec Team, Biao Yang, Boyang Ding, Chenglong Chu, Dunju Zang, Fei Pan, Han Li, Hao Jiang, Honghui Bao, Huanjie Wang, Jian Liang, Jiangxia Cao, Jiao Ou, Jiaxin Deng, Jinghao Zhang, Kun Gai, Lu Ren, Peiru Du, Pengfei Zheng, Rongzhou Zhang, Ruiming Tang, Shiyao Wang, Siyang Mao, Siyuan Lou, Teng Shi, Wei Yuan, Wenlong Xu, Xingchen Liu, Xingmei Wang, Xinqi Jin, Yan Sun, Yan Wang, Yifei Hu, Yingzhi He, Yufei Ye, Yuhao Wang, Yunhao Zhou, Yuqin Dai, Zhao Liu, Zhipeng Wei, Zhixin Ling, Ziming Li, Zixing Zhang, Ziyuan Liu, An Zhang, Changxin Lao, Chaoyi Ma, Chengru Song, Defu Lian, Fan Yang, Guowang Zhang, Hao Peng, Jiayao Shen, Jie Chen, Jun Xu, Junmin Chen, Kun Zhang, Kuo Cai, Mingxing Wen, Minmao Wang, Minxuan Lv, Qi Zhang, Qiang Luo, Sheng Yu, Shijie Li, Shijie Yi, Shuang Yang, Shugui Liu, Shuni Chen, Tinghai Zhang, Tingting Gao, Xiang Wang, Xiangyu Wu, Xiangyu Zhao, Xiao Lv, Xiaoyou Zhou, Xuming Wang, Yong Du, Zejian Zhang, Zhaojie Liu, Zhiyang Zhang, Zhuang Zhuang, Ziqi Wang, Ziyi Zhao

entry.summary: OneReason, from Kuaishou's OneRec team, explores activating reasoning in generative recommendation models, noting that naive think-before-answer modes fail to help with item-only token sequences. It investigates how to bring chain-of-thought benefits to industrial generative recommenders.

entry.title: Self-Distilled Policy Gradient

author.name: Yifeng Liu, Shiyuan Zhang, Yifan Zhang, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: SDPG (Self-Distilled Policy Gradient) uses on-policy self-distillation where a model conditions on privileged context to supervise its own generations, instantiated as a full-vocabulary reverse-KL loss combined with group-relative verifier advantages and reference-policy KL regularization. It improves stability and performance over RLVR and self-distillation baselines.

entry.title: A Goal-Set Characterization of Task Composition in the Boolean Task Algebra

author.name: Eduardo Terr\'es-Caballero, Herke van Hoof

entry.summary: Revisits the Boolean Task Algebra, proving that in deterministic MDPs every optimal extended Q-value function is determined by the universal and empty tasks, making the logarithmic set of base tasks redundant, and introduces a goal-set-based composition method that reconstructs composed value functions by slicing universal/empty functions. It reduces learning costs for zero-shot task composition.

entry.title: Adaptive Patching Is Harder Than It Looks For Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Federico Zucchi, Yi Xie, Chao Zhang, Keyuan Luo, Thomas Lampert, Ziyue Li

entry.summary: Critically examines adaptive patching for time-series Transformers, modeling patching as budgeted bitrate allocation and deriving an explicit threshold that content-adaptive rules must satisfy to beat a tuned uniform baseline, with local and global improvement bounds. It shows local heterogeneity alone does not justify finer patching.

entry.title: Low-rank Distributional Matrix Completion

author.name: Jiayi Wang, Raymond K. W. Wong

entry.summary: This paper generalizes matrix completion to the case where each entry is a probability distribution observed only through finite samples, using kernel mean embeddings and a Tucker-rank notion for distribution-valued matrices. It introduces functional unfolding operators to handle the infinite-dimensional embeddings.

entry.title: A Geometric View of Counterfactual Behavior: Interaction of Boundary Proximity and Local Support

author.name: Ioanna Gemou, Matteo Gamba, Randall Balestriero, Ritambhara Singh

entry.summary: This work studies counterfactual explanations geometrically, examining how decision boundary proximity and local data support interact to determine whether nearby counterfactuals are achievable. It uses a standardized local search probe across pretrained encoders to show models with similar accuracy can differ greatly in counterfactual feasibility.

entry.title: Recover-LoRA for Aggressive Quantization: Reclaiming Accuracy in 2-Bit Language Models via Low-Rank Adaptation with Knowledge Distillation on Synthetic Data

author.name: Devleena Das, Rajeev Patwari, Elliott Delaye, Ashish Sirasao

entry.summary: Recover-LoRA is extended to ultra-low-bit (2-bit) quantization, using selective mixed-precision (only MLP gate/up projections at 2-bit) plus low-rank adaptation with knowledge distillation on synthetic data to recover accuracy. It targets edge and on-device LLM deployment.

entry.title: Loss-Conditional PINNs for Parametric PDE Families

author.name: Anna Lazareva, Alexander Tarakanov

entry.summary: LC-PINN adapts loss-conditional training to physics-informed neural networks, training a single network across the entire weight space of loss-term weights rather than tuning one fixed weight vector. This avoids degenerate solutions caused by poor weighting in PDE residual/boundary/data loss balancing.

entry.title: Cone-Compatible Monge Geometry for High-Dimensional Ordered Optimal Transport

author.name: Lei Luo, Hongliang Zhang, Jian Yang

entry.summary: This paper studies when high-dimensional optimal transport admits an analogous Monge structure to the 1D case, introducing a cone-compatible Monge geometry where a convex cone induces a partial order compatible with transport costs. For squared Mahalanobis costs it proves compatibility holds exactly when the cone is acute under the M-inner product.

entry.title: Signed Dual Attention: Capturing Signed Dependencies in Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Balthazar Courvoisier, Tristan Cazenave

entry.summary: Introduces Signed Dual Attention, a parameter-free attention formulation capturing both positive and negative dependencies in time series via a dual message-passing scheme inspired by correlation structures. It addresses the implicit homophily assumption in standard attention.

entry.title: Towards Pretraining Text Encoders for TabPFN

author.name: Mustafa Tajjar, Alexander Pfefferle, Lennart Purucker, Frank Hutter

entry.summary: Explores pretraining text encoders for the tabular foundation model TabPFN to avoid the information bottleneck of PCA-compressing text embeddings into scalar features. It seeks end-to-end handling of high-cardinality text features in tabular learning.

entry.title: Toward Multi-Domain and Long-Tailed Quantization via Feature Alignment and Scaling

author.name: Chin-Yuan Yeh, Ting-An Chen, De-Nian Yang, Ming-Syan Chen

entry.summary: Proposes EmaQ for multi-domain quantization via CDF-based domain alignment and sensitivity-aware weight aggregation, extended to EmaQ-LT for long-tailed settings with class-conditioned variance scaling. It addresses quantization under domain shift and class imbalance with convergence guarantees.

entry.title: New Benchmarking Shows Limited Generalization Power of TCR Antigenic Epitope Prediction Models

author.name: Yiming Liao, Yiheng Li, Ning Jiang, Bo Li, Keke Chen

entry.summary: Introduces rigorously defined unseen benchmark datasets for evaluating TCR-antigen epitope prediction models and shows existing models have limited generalization. It provides a framework for unbiased assessment and next-generation algorithm development in immune engineering.

entry.title: Identifying Gems from Roman RAPIDly

author.name: Karan Gandhi, Ashish A. Mahabal, Jacob E. Jencson, Russ R. Laher, Ben Rusholme, Lin Yan, Ryan M. Lau, Schuyler D. Van Dyk, Mansi M. Kasliwal

entry.summary: Presents RuBR, a machine learning model and methodology for distinguishing real transients from spurious detections in the RAPID pipeline ahead of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launch. It addresses the absence of real Roman data by developing transient-detection pipelines proactively.

entry.title: Graph Set Transformer

author.name: Jose E. Escrig Molina, Baoquan Chen, Daniel Probst

entry.summary: Introduces the Graph Set Transformer, an architecture for learning on sets of graphs that interleaves node-level propagation with cross-graph contextual modeling at each layer via gating, avoiding the bottleneck of pre-encoded graph embeddings. It is evaluated on synthetic set-conditional reasoning and real benchmarks.

entry.title: Towards Efficient and Evidence-grounded Mobility Prediction with LLM-Driven Agent

author.name: Linyao Chen, Qinlao Zhao, Zechen Li, Mingming Li, Likun Ni, Jinyu Chen, Yuhao Yao, Xuan Song, Noboru Koshizuka, Hiroki Kobayashi

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free LLM-driven agent framework for individual-level mobility prediction that uses adaptive, evidence-controlled decision making with fast paths for routine cases and iterative tool use for ambiguous ones. It aims for efficient, interpretable, evidence-grounded next-location prediction.

entry.title: Generating Financial Time Series by Matching Random Convolutional Features

author.name: Konrad J. Mueller, Nikita Zozoulenko, Ben Wood, Thomas Cass, Lukas Gonon

entry.summary: Proposes generating realistic financial time series by training generators to match random convolutional features rather than path signatures or adversarial discriminators, mitigating overfitting under single historical paths. It improves on signature-based feature maps that miss relevant properties.

entry.title: BBOmix: A Tabular Benchmark for Hyperparameter Optimization of Unsupervised Biological Representation Learning

author.name: Luca Thale-Bombien, Jan Ewald, Ralf K\"onig, Aaron Klein

entry.summary: Introduces BBOmix, the first open-source tabular benchmark for hyperparameter optimization of unsupervised biological representation learning, addressing that reconstruction loss is a poor proxy for downstream utility. It democratizes large-scale unsupervised HPO research.

entry.title: SPLIT-PINN: Separable Probability Learning Technique via Physics-Informed Neural Networks for High-Dimensional Probabilistic Modeling

author.name: Pouria Behnoudfar, Deekshith Naidu Ponnana, Noah J. Schmelzer, Janith Wanni, George T. Gray III, Dan J. Thoma, Curt A. Bronkhorst, Nan Chen, Wenxiao Pan

entry.summary: Presents SPLIT-PINN, a separable physics-informed neural network technique for high-dimensional probabilistic modeling of material microstructure variability, inferring an unknown drift in a Liouville transport equation. It enables stable, interpretable inference in transport-dominated settings.

entry.title: SpliceBind: Isoform-Aware Prediction of Binding Pocket Druggability

author.name: Bryan Cheng, Austin Jin, Joshua Chang

entry.summary: Introduces SpliceBind, a graph neural network for isoform-aware druggability prediction that compares binding pockets across protein isoforms, addressing splice-mediated drug resistance. It establishes a two-tier resistance taxonomy distinguishing structurally detectable from allosteric mechanisms.

entry.title: Structure-Aware Prediction of PROTAC-Mediated Protein Degradability via Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Bryan Cheng, Austin Jin

entry.summary: Presents DegradoMap, a graph neural network predicting PROTAC-mediated protein degradability from protein structure and E3 ligase identity alone, the minimal information available before molecule synthesis. It uses lysine-weighted graph pooling and cross-attention for protein-E3 compatibility.

entry.title: Finite-Iteration Local Dynamics and Warm Starts for Alternating Power Iteration in Spiked Tensor PCA

author.name: Yanjin Xiang, Zhihua Zhang

entry.summary: Provides a finite-iteration local theory for alternating power iteration in spiked tensor PCA that is independent of initialization, decomposing error into geometric decay and an intrinsic noise floor. It separates the warm-start mechanism from specific spectral initializations.

entry.title: CADET: A Modular Platform for Evaluating Distributed Cooperative Autonomy in Connected Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Pragya Sharma, Brian Wang, Mani Srivastava

entry.summary: Presents CADET, a modular platform for evaluating distributed cooperative autonomy in connected autonomous vehicles, modeling network latency, compute heterogeneity, and multi-tenant contention beyond monolithic onboard designs. It supports V2X cooperative perception and control evaluation.

entry.title: EpiFormer: Learning Antigen-Antibody Interactions for Epitope Prediction via Geometric Deep Learning

author.name: Mansoor Ahmed, Huirong Chai, Haoxin Wang, Hemanth Venkateswara, Murray Patterson

entry.summary: Proposes EpiFormer, a geometric deep learning encoder-decoder for epitope prediction that uses interleaved cross-attention within GNN encoders to capture co-dependent antibody-antigen structural features, addressing late-stage chain combination and severe class imbalance. It improves modeling of binding interfaces.

entry.title: LazyAttention: Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Deferred Positional Encoding

author.name: Haocheng Xia, Mihir Pamnani, Hanxi Fang, Supawit Chockchowwat, Yongjoo Park

entry.summary: LazyAttention introduces a kernelized deferred positional encoding that enables zero-copy, position-agnostic KV cache reuse for RAG and in-context learning. It overcomes the limitation that conventional KV caches embed positional info, restricting reuse to prefixes.

entry.title: GENEB: Why Genomic Models Are Hard to Compare

author.name: Daria Ledneva, Mikhail Nuridinov, Denis Kuznetsov

entry.summary: GENEB is a large-scale diagnostic benchmark evaluating frozen representations from 40 genomic foundation models across 100 tasks under a unified probing protocol, including few-shot regimes. It shows that aggregate leaderboards are unstable and rankings vary across tasks, exposing why genomic models are hard to compare.

entry.title: MusaCoder: Native GPU Kernel Generation with Full-Stack Training on Moore Threads GPU

author.name: Kun Cheng, Songshuo Lu, Sicong Liao, Tankun Li, Yafei Zhang, Dong Yang, Qiheng Lv, Hua Wang, Zhi Chen, Yaohua Tang

entry.summary: MusaCoder is a full-stack training framework for native GPU kernel generation on CUDA and MUSA (Moore Threads) backends, combining progressive data synthesis, diversity-preserving rejection fine-tuning, and execution-feedback RL with mechanisms to stabilize sparse-reward, reward-hacking-prone training. It targets the weakness of LLMs at generating efficient low-level kernel code.

entry.title: Less is MoE: Trimming Experts in Domain-Specialist Language Models

author.name: Haoze He, Xinkai Zou, Xuan Jiang, Xingyuan Ding, Ao Qu, Juncheng Billy Li, Heather Miller

entry.summary: Shows prior MoE compression fails on general benchmarks because important capabilities concentrate in tiny FFN intermediate dimensions, using Fisher importance to identify them; removing as few as 12 of 1.35M dimensions collapses GSM8K. Enables fine-grained domain-specialist trimming.

entry.title: VideoKR: Towards Knowledge- and Reasoning-Intensive Video Understanding

author.name: Lin Fu, Zheyuan Yang, Yang Wang, Tingyu Song, Arman Cohan, Yilun Zhao

entry.summary: VideoKR is a large-scale (315K examples over 145K CC-licensed expert videos) training corpus plus benchmark for knowledge- and reasoning-intensive video understanding, built via a human-in-the-loop skill-oriented pipeline. It targets genuine reasoning rather than textual shortcuts.

entry.title: Unpaired RGB-Thermal Gaussian-Splatting Using Visual Geometric Transformers

author.name: Jean Cordonnier, Chenghao Xu, Olga Fink, Malcolm Mielle

entry.summary: This work enables unpaired RGB-thermal novel view synthesis using VGGT to independently estimate camera poses per modality, then aligning via Procrustes with cross-modal matching. It avoids requiring precisely calibrated RGB-thermal pairs via multi-modal 3D Gaussian Splatting.

entry.title: V2V-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Video-to-Video Generation Evaluation

author.name: Tao Liu, Leela Krishna, Gouti Pavan Kumar, Sreeja K, Vishav Garg

entry.summary: V2V-Bench is an 11-dimension benchmark for video-to-video generation evaluation, covering temporal alignment, structural fidelity, transformation quality, video quality, and semantic alignment. It evaluates commercial models including Grok Imagine and Gemini Veo3 alongside open-source Open Sora 2.

entry.title: LiAuto-GeoX: Efficient Grounded Driving Transformer

author.name: Jiawei Lian, Haoyi Sun, Yang Wu, Lifu Mu, Siyuan Wang, Le Hui, Ning Mao, Tao Wei, Pan Zhou, Kun Zhan, Jian Yang

entry.summary: LiAuto-GeoX is an efficient grounded driving transformer for real-time onboard 3D scene understanding, learning a driving geometry model from large-scale surround-view data with sparse LiDAR priors. It targets long-range geometric fidelity and surround-view consistency for autonomous driving.

entry.title: Beyond Absolute Scores: Relative Edit-induced Difference for Generalizable Image Aesthetic Assessment

author.name: Qifei Jia, Xintong Yao, Minghao Li, Yajie Chai, Qiming Lu, Baoyue Shen, Yasen Zhang, Runyu Shi, Ying Huang, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: RED-Aes reframes image aesthetic assessment from absolute MOS regression to relative edit-induced differences, using controllable editing to simulate human comparative aesthetic reasoning. This aims for more generalizable aesthetic principles across diverse scenarios.

entry.title: Faithful, Enriched, and Precise: Benchmarking Natural-Science Illustration Generation by T2I models

author.name: Yifan Chang, Jiaxin Ai, Jianwen Sun, Yuandong Pu, Siqi Luo, Liangliang Zhao, Yuchen Ren, Minghao Liu, Yunfei Yu, Yu Qiao, Kaipeng Zhang, Yihao Liu

entry.summary: FEPBench is a benchmark for evaluating text-to-image models on natural-science illustration generation, providing fine-grained atomic assessment across disciplines and layout types. It addresses gaps in evaluating scientific reasoning ability and output conciseness in current holistic benchmarks.

entry.title: Visual Commonsense Driven Knowledge Refinements for Scene Graph Generation

author.name: Ma\"elic Neau, Salim Baloch, Jakob Suchan, Zoe Falomir, Mehul Bhatt

entry.summary: This work proposes a model-agnostic, semantically-guided knowledge refinement framework for scene graph generation that mines commonsense-grounded constraints from training data. It uses declarative commonsense reasoning to correct ranked SGG predictions at inference without manual rules or retraining.

entry.title: Auditing Demonstration Curation Metrics: Action-Only Scorers Fail on the Structural Defects That Degrade Imitation Policies

author.name: Aarav Bedi (University of California, Berkeley)

entry.summary: Audits seven imitation-learning demonstration curation metrics in a controlled testbed with injected defects, finding that action-only scorers fail to detect structural defects that degrade policies. Provides an evaluation framework for curation reliability.

entry.title: DexFuture: Hierarchical Future-State Visuomotor Targeting for Bimanual Dexterous Tool Use

author.name: Runfa Blark Li, Kuang-Ting Tu, Nikola Raicevic, Dwait Bhatt, Xinshuang Liu, Keito Suzuki, Ki Myung Brian Lee, Nikolay Atanasov, Truong Nguyen

entry.summary: DexFuture couples a high-level future-state visuomotor target predictor with a low-level target-conditioned dexterous policy for bimanual tool use, avoiding slow online planning or demonstration-reference dependence. Generates dynamically consistent future references hierarchically.

entry.title: Finding Most Influential Sets

author.name: Lucas D. Konrad, Nikolas Kuschnig

entry.summary: Reduces finding most-influential-sets (size-k subsets whose removal maximally changes an estimand) from combinatorial search to a one-parameter sequence of top-k problems via Dinkelbach's method for linear-fractional leave-set-out effects. Achieves O(n) per-iteration cost with global optimality for the ratio objective.

entry.title: Adaptive Learning Rates with Surrogate Probability for Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader

author.name: Jongyeong Lee, Junya Honda, Shinji Ito, Chansoo Kim

entry.summary: Proposes an adaptive, probability-dependent learning rate for Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader using surrogate probabilities to achieve best-of-both-worlds guarantees, overcoming the difficulty of designing adaptive rates for FTPL's optimization-free structure. Extends BOBW bandit results to a computationally efficient alternative.

entry.title: Anchor PCA

author.name: Benedikt Seiter, Anya Fries, Julius von K\"ugelgen, Jonas Peters

entry.summary: Anchor PCA performs dimension reduction across multiple related domains by focusing on shared directions of variation, trading off overall explained variance against agreement between shared and domain-specific embeddings. Avoids spurious directions that vary in only a few domains.

entry.title: Multimarginal flow matching with optimal transport potentials

author.name: Raghav Kansal, David Crair, Nghia Nguyen, Scott Pope, Bradley Parry

entry.summary: Extends flow matching to the multimarginal setting with intermediate observed marginals by leveraging the connection to dynamic optimal transport, softly steering flows toward intermediate distributions through OT potential terms. Targets temporal evolution modeling in dynamical systems.

entry.title: Mamba-Assisted Non-Markovian Closure for Reduced-Order Modeling

author.name: Zhi-Feng Wei, Saad Qadeer, Panos Stinis

entry.summary: Mamba-Assisted Closure recasts non-Markovian closure modeling for reduced-order systems as sequence modeling, training a Mamba state-space model to predict the Mori-Zwanzig memory functional coupled with reduced governing equations. Exploits the dual representation of state-space models.

entry.title: Bentkus-type asymptotic e-values

author.name: Diego Martinez-Taboada, Ben Chugg, Aaditya Ramdas

entry.summary: This paper introduces Bentkus-type asymptotic e-values that eliminate the missing-factor scaling inefficiency afflicting existing asymptotic e-values, yielding sharper post-hoc inference and tighter confidence intervals. It draws on near-optimal concentration inequalities for use in multiple testing with data-dependent significance levels.

entry.title: GITCO: Gated Inference-Time Context Optimization in TSFMs

author.name: Manya Pandey, Dhruv Kumar, Murari Mandal, Saurabh Deshpande

entry.summary: Proposes GITCO, an inference-time context optimization framework that detects and suppresses anomalous patches harming zero-shot forecasts in time series foundation models, without changing weights. It matters for improving forecast reliability cheaply at deployment.

entry.title: SciVisAgentSkills: Design and Evaluation of Agent Skills for Scientific Data Analysis and Visualization

author.name: Kuangshi Ai, Haichao Miao, Kaiyuan Tang, Shusen Liu, Chaoli Wang

entry.summary: Presents SciVisAgentSkills, a library of reusable agent skills encoding tool-specific expertise for scientific visualization tools like ParaView and napari, evaluated on SciVisAgentBench with Codex and Claude Code. It matters for making coding agents competent in specialized scientific workflows.

entry.title: PerceptUI: LLM Agents as Human-Aligned Synthetic Users for UI/UX Evaluation

author.name: Nicolas Bougie, Xiaotong Ye, Gian Maria Marconi, Narimasa Watanabe

entry.summary: Introduces PerceptUI, a persona-conditioned framework training MLLMs as human-aligned synthetic users that predict how a specific user would answer interface questions and produce rationales, via contrastive then supervised stages. It matters for cheaper early-stage UI/UX evaluation.

entry.title: Agentic Molecular Recovery via Molecule-Aware Exploration

author.name: Suwan Yoon, Changhee Lee

entry.summary: Reframes invalid LLM-generated SMILES from validity repair to identity-preserving molecular recovery, using molecule-aware agentic exploration with RDKit tools to restore validity while preserving target-relevant structure. It matters for reliable text-guided molecular generation.

entry.title: Amortizing Federated Adaptation: Hypernetwork Driven LoRA for Personalized Foundation Models

author.name: Sunny Gupta, Shambhavi Shanker, Amit Sethi

entry.summary: Proposes HyperLoRA, a federated fine-tuning framework using hypernetwork-driven LoRA generation and product-space aggregation to address structural aggregation bias and initialization lag in federated LoRA. It amortizes adaptation rather than iterating per-client.

entry.title: A Taxonomy of Runtime Faults in Model Context Protocol Servers

author.name: Joshua Owotogbe, Indika Kumara, Willem-Jan van den Heuvel, Damian Andrew Tamburri, Antonio Ken Iannillo, Roberto Natella

entry.summary: Presents the first empirical taxonomy of runtime faults in Model Context Protocol servers, manually analyzing 837 fault threads from 473 GitHub repositories via open coding to derive 11 top-level categories. Highlights issues like configuration parameters accepted but not enforced at runtime.

entry.title: Human oversight of agentic systems in practice: Examining the oversight work, challenges, and heuristics of developers using software agents

author.name: Shipi Dhanorkar, Samir Passi, Mihaela Vorvoreanu

entry.summary: An exploratory interview study with 17 experienced developers examining how they oversee autonomous software agents in practice, documenting emergent oversight work, challenges, and heuristics. Provides early empirical anchors for largely conceptual agent oversight frameworks.

entry.title: When Evidence is Sparse: Weakly Supervised Early Failure Alerting in Dialogs and LLM-Agent Trajectories

author.name: Avinash Baidya, Xinran Liang, Ruocheng Guo, Xiang Gao, Kamalika Das

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage weakly supervised approach for early failure alerting in dialogs and LLM-agent trajectories, challenging the assumption that terminal labels should be assigned to every prefix. Addresses the practical problem of flagging likely failures while interactions are still unfolding.

entry.title: Safe Embodied AI for Long-horizon Tasks: A Cross-layer Analysis of Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Dabin Kim, Daemin Park, Sangyub Lee, Jinsik Kim, Yeongtak Oh, Jongho Shin, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: A survey providing a structured cross-layer review of safety in long-horizon robotic manipulation, spanning planning, policy design, and runtime execution. Identifies how semantic misgrounding, error propagation, execution drift, and contact-rich risk accumulate in closed-loop embodied systems.

entry.title: CollabBench: Benchmarking and Unleashing Collaborative Ability of LLMs with Diverse Players via Proactive Engagement

author.name: Hong Qian, Yuanhao Liu, Zihan Zhou, Zongbao Zhang, Hanjie Ge, Haotian Shi, Liang Dou, Xiangfeng Wang, Jingwen Yang, Aimin Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes CollabBench, a benchmark for evaluating and training collaborative LLM agents in cooperative games, featuring diverse player profile simulation and a collaborative agentic training paradigm unifying reasoning, communication, and action via rollouts. Addresses the challenge of effective collaboration with realistic human-like partners.

entry.title: Learning Geometric Representations from Videos for Spatial Intelligent Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Haibo Wang, Lifu Huang

entry.summary: Presents GeoVR, a framework that learns geometric 3D-aware representations from purely 2D video sequences by distilling geometry knowledge from pretrained 3D foundation models into MLLM latent space. Aims to give multimodal LLMs spatial intelligence despite scarce large-scale 3D data.

entry.title: Better Literary Translation: A Multi-Aspect Data Generation and LLM Training Approach

author.name: Zhihao Lin, Ziqi Zhu, Hao Huang, Guanghui Wang, Peiyang He

entry.summary: Presents a multi-aspect iterative refinement framework for literary translation that uses specialized LLM translators targeting distinct quality dimensions to generate high-quality references and preference data for SFT and RL. Finds generated references outperform ground truth for SFT and that DPO degrades performance while reward-model-based GRPO improves it.

entry.title: When Good Enough Is Optimal: Multiplication-Only Matrix Inversion Approximation for Quantized Gated DeltaNet

author.name: Luoming Zhang, Yuwei Ren, Kui Zhang, Tian Liu, Lingjuan Ge, Denghao Li, Matthew Harper Langston, Yin Huang, Weiliang Will Zeng, Liang Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a matrix-multiplication-based algorithm for inverting lower-triangular matrices in chunk-wise linear attention, using truncated Neumann expansion to eliminate sequential dependencies. It targets NPU/quantized deployment of Gated DeltaNet for long-context efficiency.

entry.title: MPCoT: Reward-Guided Multi-Path Latent Reasoning for Test-Time Scalable Vision-Language-Action

author.name: Boyang Zhang, Lianlei Shan

entry.summary: MPCoT is a reward-guided multi-path latent reasoning framework for Vision-Language-Action policies that initializes multiple hypotheses, refines them with weight-tied steps, and aggregates before action decoding, enabling test-time deliberation without text CoT latency. It targets brittleness in long-horizon control.

entry.title: Towards One-to-Many Temporal Grounding

author.name: Qi Xu, Yue Tan, Shihao Chen, Jiahao Meng, Anna Wang, Shunping Ji, Hao Fei, Jason Li

entry.summary: Defines One-to-Many Temporal Grounding (localizing multiple disjoint video segments for a single query), builds the first benchmark with count-accuracy and effective temporal F1 metrics, and curates training data, since prior one-to-one MLLMs score near zero. It addresses event cardinality perception in video grounding.

entry.title: Pseudospectral Bounds for Transient Amplification in Coupled Gradient Descent

author.name: Ahanaf Hasan Ariq

entry.summary: Develops a pseudospectral theory for block-triangular coupled-gradient-descent Jacobians (relevant to bilevel optimization, two-time-scale approximation, and adversarial training), proving Kreiss-constant bounds with matching minimax lower bounds and characterizing a critical coupling threshold for transient amplification. It explains non-normal transient blow-up before convergence.

entry.title: Smart Transportation Without Neurons -- Fair Metro Network Expansion with Tabular Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Dimitris Michailidis, Sennay Ghebreab, Fernando P. Santos

entry.summary: This paper reformulates the Metro Network Expansion Problem as a Non-Markovian Rewards Decision Process and shows that tabular RL matches deep RL performance while being far cheaper computationally and environmentally. It argues deep RL is unnecessary for problems of this scale.

entry.title: Scaling Novel Graph Generation via Lightweight Structure-Guided Autoregressive Models

author.name: Alessio Barboni, Massimiliano Lupo Pasini, Bishal Lakha, Edoardo Serra

entry.summary: This paper presents a lightweight autoregressive framework for graph generation that uses structure-guided topological ordering to serialize graphs into regular edge sequences, achieving near log-linear generation complexity. It targets scalability and novelty limitations of diffusion and quadratic autoregressive models.

entry.title: Episodic Memory Temporal Consistency for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zicheng Zhao, Yu Lan, Chengzhengxu Li, Zhaohan Zhang, Xiaoming Liu

entry.summary: EMTC improves cooperative multi-agent RL with episodic memory by adding a temporally consistent semantic embedder (combining contrastive learning and time-conditioned state reconstruction) to prevent representation collapse, plus selective leveraging of historical experiences. It mitigates reward sparsity and local-optima trapping in MARL.

entry.title: HalfNet: Randomized Neural Networks with Learned Subspace Geometry

author.name: Ethem Alpaydin

entry.summary: HalfNet draws fixed random weights from N(0, Sigma) with a learned low-rank factorized covariance rather than the standard N(0,I), learning the geometry of the weight distribution from data. Experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 show it matches fully-trained MLPs with far fewer parameters, suggesting predictive power lies in weight-space geometry.

entry.title: ALINC: Active Learning for Inductive Node Classification via Graph Sampling

author.name: Pascal Plettenberg, Denis Huseljic, Andr\'e Alcalde, Bernhard Sick, Josephine M. Thomas

entry.summary: ALINC is an active learning framework for inductive node classification that selects entire graphs (rather than single nodes) for annotation, addressing settings like molecular chemistry where annotating one node requires full-graph analysis. It tackles a graph-selection active-learning problem not previously addressed.

entry.title: Curvature-aware dynamic precision approach for physics-informed neural networks

author.name: Yingjie Shao, Ioannis N. Athanasiadis, George van Voorn, Taniya Kapoor

entry.summary: Proposes a curvature-aware precision controller that dynamically adapts numerical precision during physics-informed neural network training to balance the cost of double precision against the failures of single precision. It targets efficient PDE simulation without sacrificing accuracy.

entry.title: AdaKoop: Efficient Modeling of Nonlinear Dynamics from Nonstationary Data Streams with Koopman Operator Regression

author.name: Naoki Chihara, Ren Fujiwara, Yasuko Matsubara, Yasushi Sakurai

entry.summary: Presents AdaKoop, an efficient streaming algorithm using Koopman operator theory to model nonlinear dynamics in nonstationary data streams under time constraints. It adapts finite-dimensional Koopman approximations for real-time analysis.

entry.title: FLAGG: Flexible Autoregressive Graph Generation

author.name: Samuel Cognolato, Alessandro Sperduti, Luciano Serafini

entry.summary: Proposes FLAGG, a flexible framework that sequentially generates portions of graphs using one-shot models, combining the strengths of one-shot (small graphs) and sequential (large graphs) generation. It enables applying any one-shot model across diverse graph sizes and topologies.

entry.title: SpurAudio: A Benchmark for Studying Shortcut Learning in Few-Shot Audio Classification

author.name: Giries Abu Ayoub, Morad Tukan, Loay Mualem

entry.summary: Introduces SpurAudio, a benchmark for studying shortcut learning in few-shot audio classification by leveraging the natural separability of foreground events and background environments. It provides controlled multi-level evaluation of spurious foreground-background correlations.

entry.title: Efficient and Training-Free Single-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Haojun Qiu, Kiriakos N. Kutulakos, David B. Lindell

entry.summary: This paper generates images matching the patch-distribution structure of a single reference image without training, using a closed-form optimal denoiser over the finite patch dataset to compute score functions. It eliminates the hours of optimization required by single-image diffusion models.

entry.title: AgentJet: A Flexible Swarm Training Framework for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Qingxu Fu, Boyin Liu, Shuchang Tao, Zhaoyang Liu, Bolin Ding

entry.summary: AgentJet is a distributed swarm training framework for LLM agent reinforcement learning that decouples model optimization on GPU clusters from agent rollouts running on arbitrary devices. It enables heterogeneous multi-model RL, multi-task training, and fault-tolerant execution that centralized frameworks struggle to support.

entry.title: COP-Q: Safety-First Reinforcement Learning for Robot Control via Cholesky-Ordered Projection

author.name: Guopeng Li, Moritz A. Zanger, Matthijs T. J. Spaan, Julian F. P. Kooij

entry.summary: COP-Q is a safety-first off-policy reinforcement learning method for robot control that incorporates inter-objective covariance between reward and safety Q-values via Cholesky-ordered projection, rather than treating uncertainty independently. This reduces overly conservative value estimates and improves sample efficiency under safety constraints.

entry.title: Trajectory Dynamics in Language Model Hidden States Predict Human Processing Costs Beyond Surprisal

author.name: Elan Barenholtz

entry.summary: This work shows that the trajectory dynamics of language model hidden states (the direction of evolving interpretation) predict human incremental processing costs beyond what surprisal captures. It argues that the evolving interpretive state's trajectory, not just position, shapes processing, reflecting local momentum in language.

entry.title: YouZhi: Towards High-Concurrency Financial LLMs via Adaptive GQA-to-MLA Transition

author.name: PSBC LLM Team, Huawei LLM Team, Ruihan Long, Junjie Wu, Tianan Zhang, Duo Zhang, Yaozong Wu, Jinbin Fu, Chang Liu, Zhentao Tang, Wenshuang Yang, Xin Wang, Zhihao Song, Ning Huang, Wenjing Xu, Shuai Zong, Shupei Sun, Sen Wang, Jing Hu, Bin Wang, Xinyu Wang, Junkui Ju, Zequn Ding, Jie Ran, Man Luo, Shixiong Kai, Linkai Hou, Kaichao Liang, Hu Zhao, Yang Zhao, Shucheng Lin, Wei Yu, Chenghan Jiang, Jingjing Ding, Jiahui Zhang, Tian Jin, Yuhang Zhang, Dong Guo, Wei Sun, Jun Xie, Jianwei Li, Lei Cao, Pei Li, Jiabin Li, Jia Yuan, Rui Yuan, Jing Zhu, Mingxuan Yuan, Zhangcheng Lv, Xin Jiang, Xiuhong Fei, Xiaozhe Ren, Yulong Li, Zhipeng Zhang, Hang Wang, Zhaohui Xu, Rui Zhao, Yibo He, Xinzhuang Niu

entry.summary: YouZhi-LLM is a high-concurrency financial LLM using a layer-adaptive GQA-to-MLA transition framework to maximize KV-cache compression while minimizing perplexity loss, built on Huawei Ascend hardware. It targets deployment cost and scalability.

entry.title: USAD 2.0: Scaling Representation Distillation for Universal Audio Understanding
