entry.summary: This paper addresses multi-view clustering under both incomplete views and noisy correspondences, arguing both arise from imperfect cross-view counterpart information. It proposes a unified method robust to absent and unreliable counterparts simultaneously.

entry.title: IRIS-GAN: Staged Specialist Detection of Deepfake Faces

author.name: Jaume M. Trenchs, Veronica Sanz

entry.summary: IRIS-GAN is a specialist forensic detector for GAN-generated deepfake faces using staged training across increasingly difficult GAN families, achieving over 99% detection. Grad-CAM analysis reveals generator-dependent spatial signatures useful for secondary classification.

entry.title: TGSD: Topology-Guided State-Space Diffusion for EEG Spatial Super-Resolution

author.name: Zijian Kang, Weiming Zeng, Yueyang Li, Shengyu Gong, Hongjie Yan, Wai Ting Siok, Nizhuan Wang

entry.summary: TGSD is a topology-guided state-space diffusion framework that recovers dense-channel EEG from sparse low-density recordings for spatial super-resolution. It uses a hierarchical spatial prior encoder to incorporate electrode topology and address whole-channel missingness.

entry.title: Teaching Robots to Say 'I Don't Know' : SENTINEL for Uncertainty-Aware SLAM

author.name: Abhishek S, Badrikanath Praharaj, Sreeram MV

entry.summary: SENTINEL is a training-free, label-free reliability estimation framework giving low-cost range-only 2D LiDAR a diagnostic signal by combining scan geometry statistics with cross-modal LiDAR-RGB-D depth consistency. Below-threshold scans are rejected and the robot falls back to wheel odometry to prevent silent SLAM corruption.

entry.title: Plan First, Judge Later, Run Better: A DMAIC-Inspired Agentic System for Industrial Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yongzi Yu, Ao Li, Le Wang, Ziyue Li, Fugee Tsung, Yuxuan Liang, Man Li

entry.summary: Presents DMAIC-IAD, a Plan First, Judge Later multi-agent system for industrial anomaly detection inspired by the DMAIC quality-management framework. It emphasizes strategy formulation over pure execution to handle heterogeneous modalities cost-effectively.

entry.title: What Type of Inference is Active Inference?

author.name: Wouter W. L. Nuijten, Mykola Lukashchuk, Thijs van de Laar, Bert de Vries

entry.summary: Provides a variational analysis clarifying that Expected Free Energy minimization in active inference can be rewritten as predictive-model VFE plus explicit entropy-correction and planning-correction terms. It characterizes which corrections are required for proper EFE-based planning.

entry.title: Optical-Guided Neural Collapse for SAR Few-Shot Class Incremental Learning

author.name: Fan Zhang, Sijin Zheng, Fei Ma, Qiang Yin, Yongsheng Zhou, Fei Gao, Xian Sun

entry.summary: Proposes an optical-guided SAR few-shot class-incremental learning framework inspired by neural collapse, deriving orthogonal feature subspaces from a data-rich optical ATR dataset as geometric priors and projecting SAR features onto them via principal-angle constraints to transfer discriminative structure. It addresses SAR data scarcity, azimuth sensitivity, and catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: TIDE: Proactive Multi-Problem Discovery via Template-Guided Iteration

author.name: Soyeong Jeong, Jinheon Baek, Minki Kang, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: TIDE is a template-guided iterative framework enabling agents to proactively discover multiple hidden problems from user context, grounded in evidence and paired with actions, rather than only acting on explicit requests. It counters the tendency of single-pass prediction to anchor on the most salient cases.

entry.title: From Agent Traces to Trust: Evidence Tracing and Execution Provenance in LLM Agents

author.name: Yiqi Wang, Jiaqi Zhang, Taotao Cai, Zirui Liu, Qingqiang Sun, Zequn Sun, Zhangkai Wu, Mingkai Zhang, Yanming Zhu

entry.summary: This paper addresses evidence tracing and execution provenance in LLM agents, modeling how retrieved evidence, tool outputs, memory, and intermediate claims connect throughout execution to support verification, debugging, and auditing. It argues final-answer accuracy alone cannot explain agent behavior.

entry.title: KODA: Contrastive Representation Comparison and Alignment for Vision-Language Foundation Models

author.name: Youqi Wu, Mohammad Jalali, Farzan Farnia

entry.summary: KODA is a kernel-based framework for contrastive comparison and alignment of vision-language foundation models (CLIP, SigLIP) via a Contrastive Embedding Clustering task that finds subsets weakly clustered under one representation but strongly under another. It constructs unified multimodal kernels and formulates discrepancy analysis to explain structural differences.

entry.title: Learning What to Learn: Stage-Specific Data Sets for SFT-then-RL in Small Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Chongyang He, Rui Zhang, Zixuan Wang, Xin Li

entry.summary: This paper argues data strategy should match the distinct roles of SFT and RL in small language model reasoning, using SFT for not-yet-mastered skills and RL to consolidate partially accessible ones, with a Bridge mechanism transforming teacher traces into learnable supervision. It organizes training into difficulty-aware stage-specific sets.

entry.title: Entity Binding Failures in Speech LLM Reasoning: Diagnosis and Chain-of-Thought Intervention

author.name: Ming-Hao Hsu, Xiaohai Tian, Jun Zhang, Zhizheng Wu

entry.summary: This work diagnoses that speech LLMs collapse to chance on logical entity-tracking tasks due to entity binding failure, where continuous speech features lose precise entity-property associations, while matching text models on spatial, syntactic, and factual tasks. It proposes Entity-Aware Chain-of-Thought forcing explicit entity enumeration before reasoning.

entry.title: GARL: Game-Theoretic Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Agent Strategic Prioritisation

author.name: Yuxiao Ye, Yiwen Zhang, Huiyuan Xie, Yuqin Huang, Zhiyuan Liu

entry.summary: GARL is a game-theoretic RL framework for multi-agent strategic prioritisation, formalizing the task as a two-stage game where agents allocate resources and an arbiter produces final rankings. It grounds reward design in interaction structure rather than task-specific heuristics.

entry.title: Reflection Separation from a Single Image via Joint Latent Diffusion

author.name: Zheng-Hui Huang, Zhixiang Wang, Yu-Lun Liu, Yung-Yu Chuang

entry.summary: This paper fine-tunes a diffusion model for single-image reflection separation, jointly generating transmission and reflection layers with a cross-layer self-attention mechanism and disjoint sampling to reduce interference. It targets hard cases like glare and weak reflections.

entry.title: XSSR: Cross-Domain Self-Supervised Representative Selection for Efficient Annotation in Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Byunghyun Ko, Aleksei Anisimov, Kobe Ke, Suhas Bharthepude, Jeongkyu Lee

entry.summary: XSSR minimizes target-domain annotation in cross-domain medical image segmentation via a masked autoencoder for shared embeddings, a greedy density/novelty/diversity selection algorithm, and a U-Net segmentation stage. It addresses costly labeling under domain shift.

entry.title: COMBINER: Composed Image Retrieval Guided by Attribute-based Neighbor Relations

author.name: Zixu Li, Yupeng Hu, Zhiwei Chen, Haokun Wen, Xuemeng Song, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: COMBINER improves composed image retrieval by representing cross-modal features through attribute prototypes and neighbor relations, addressing cases where images look alike but differ in attributes. It tackles attribute-semantic entanglement, cross-modal inconsistency, and missing supervision.

entry.title: CDPM-Align: Multi-Scale Guidance-Aligned Diffusion Pretraining for Robust Few-Shot Anatomical Landmark Detection

author.name: Roberto Di Via, Irina Voiculescu, Francesca Odone, Vito Paolo Pastore

entry.summary: CDPM-Align introduces a multi-scale guidance-aligned conditional diffusion pretraining approach for few-shot anatomical landmark detection in medical images. It explores representation learning to improve reliability and robustness under limited annotation regimes.

entry.title: Drift-Augmented Scoring: Text-Derived Noise Robustness for Zero-Shot Audio-Language Classification

author.name: Tu Vo, Sheir Zaheer, Chan Y. Park

entry.summary: Drift-Augmented Scoring adds a small text-derived per-class bonus to zero-shot audio-language classification scores to improve robustness under acoustic noise. The bonus rewards classes when noisy embeddings drift in directions predicted by noise-conditioned text prompts, computed once with no gradients.

entry.title: CADENCE: Predicting Realized MAPF Execution Time Beyond Sum of Costs

author.name: Abhishek S, Badrikanath Praharaj, Sreeram MV

entry.summary: CADENCE is a hardware study examining which pre-execution features best predict realized wall-clock completion time for multi-agent path finding, beyond standard metrics like sum-of-costs and makespan. Experiments on a 7x7 workcell with seven differential-drive robots compare planned travel cost, primitive motion burden, and other predictors.

entry.title: Tree-Based Formalization of Multi-Agent Complementarity in Human-AI Interactions

author.name: Andrea Ferrario

entry.summary: Provides a tree-based formalization of complementarity in multi-agent human-AI interaction, modeling how agent predictions compose into workflow-sensitive protocols via rooted binary trees. It closes a gap in formal treatment of when human-AI teams beat the best member.

entry.title: SpurAudio: A Benchmark for Studying Shortcut Learning in Few-Shot Audio Classification

author.name: Giries Abu Ayoub, Morad Tukan, Loay Mualem

entry.summary: Introduces SpurAudio, a benchmark for studying shortcut learning and spurious foreground-background correlations in few-shot audio classification. It enables controlled multi-level evaluation of contextual exploitation in audio, an under-studied modality.

entry.title: Bayes-Sufficient Representations in Supervised Learning

author.name: Vasileios Sevetlidis

entry.summary: Defines Bayes-sufficiency for supervised representations as the property that a prediction head can implement a Bayes-optimal action rule, making target information loss-dependent. It introduces the Bayes quotient and connects the framework to property elicitation.

entry.title: AgenticDiffusion: Agentic Diffusion-based Path Planning for Vision-Based UAV Navigation

author.name: Faryal Batool, Muhammad Ahsan Mustafa, Fawad Mehboob, Valerii Serpiva, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: Introduces AgenticDiffusion, a multi-view UAV indoor navigation framework combining language-guided reasoning, open-vocabulary grounding, diffusion-based planning, and NMPC control over synchronized first-person and top-view observations. It improves reasoning about occlusions and global scene structure.

entry.title: ChessMimic: Per-Rating Transformer Models for Human Move, Clock, and Outcome Prediction in Online Blitz Chess

author.name: Thomas Johnson

entry.summary: Presents ChessMimic, three small encoder-only transformers for human move, thinking-time, and outcome prediction in online blitz chess, fitted separately per 100-Elo rating band to sharpen per-skill calibration. It outperforms Maia-2 on human move prediction across all Elo bands and matches Maia-3 efficiency tiers.

entry.title: Treat Traffic Like Trees: A Semantic-Preserving Hierarchical Graph-Based Expert Framework for Encrypted Traffic Analysis

author.name: Yuantu Luo, Jun Tao, Linxiao Yu, Guang Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes PTGAMoE, a semantic-preserving hierarchical graph-based mixture-of-experts framework for encrypted traffic analysis that represents traffic as protocol trees mirroring protocol-layer/field hierarchy, avoiding the obscuring of protocol semantics by complex preprocessing. It exploits protocol-specification structure underused in prior learning frameworks.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware End-to-End Co-Design of Neural Network Processors: From Training and Mapping to Fabrication

author.name: Yuyang Du, Yujun Huang, Gioele Zardini

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified, monotone co-design framework composing four interoperable blocks spanning neural network training, chip mapping, wafer fabrication, and compute allocation for neural network processors. It addresses uncertainty across the end-to-end hardware-software pipeline.

entry.title: SharedRequest: Privacy-Preserving Model-Agnostic Inference for Large Language Models

author.name: Peihua Mai, Xuanrong Gao, Youlong Ding, Xianglong Du, Wei Liu, Yan Pang

entry.summary: SharedRequest is a model-agnostic framework for privacy-preserving LLM inference that obscures sensitive prompts by mixing them with noisy variants and batching semantically equivalent instructions to amortize cost. It aims to protect prompt privacy without sacrificing much utility or efficiency.

entry.title: Query-based Cross-Modal Projector Bolstering Mamba Multimodal LLM

author.name: SooHwan Eom, Jay Shim, Gwanhyeong Koo, Haebin Na, Mark A. Hasegawa-Johnson, Sungwoong Kim, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: This paper proposes a query-based cross-modal projector to improve Mamba-based multimodal LLMs by compressing visual tokens via cross-attention, avoiding manual 2D scan-order design. It targets the efficiency advantages of state-space models for vision-language tasks.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Incremental Segmentation via Semantic Anchors and Spatial Arbitration

author.name: Zhonggai Wang, Kai Fang, Guangyu Gao

entry.summary: SASA tackles weakly incremental semantic segmentation by using learnable semantic anchors as rigid class references plus elastic residual adaptation and spatial arbitration to resist feature drift. It aims to prevent newly learned classes from overwriting old ones under noisy supervision.

entry.title: SBP-Net: Learning Thin Structure Reconstruction with Sliding-Box Projections

author.name: Ofir Gilad, Andrei Sharf

entry.summary: SBP-Net reconstructs thin 3D structures (e.g., vasculature, pipes) using local orthographic depth projections from a sliding box, processed by a network to recover missing 2D thin geometry then fused into 3D. It targets failures of dense-surface neural methods on sparse thin structures.

entry.title: VT-3DAD: Cross-Category 3D Anomaly Detection via Visual-Text Normal Space Alignment

author.name: Zi Wang, Katsuya Hotta, Yawen Zou, Koichiro Kamide, Yijin Wei, Chao Zhang, Jun Yu

entry.summary: VT-3DAD is a training-free framework for few-shot cross-category 3D anomaly detection that aligns multi-view CLIP visual features with text in a normal space to avoid confusion among geometrically similar categories. It uses depth maps from frozen CLIP encoders for visual-text alignment.

entry.title: Multi-Camera AR Guidance System for Surgical Instrument Handling and Assembly: Investigating Workload and Efficiency

author.name: Shiyu Li, Julian Kreimeier, Hannah Schieber, Dirk M\"uller, Bernhard Kainz, R\"udiger von Eisenhart-Rothe, Daniel Roth

entry.summary: This work presents a marker-free multi-camera AR guidance system using 6D pose estimation and head-mounted display visualization to assist scrub nurses with surgical instrument handling and assembly. A user study investigates workload and efficiency, with the pose network trained purely on synthetic data.

entry.title: Cooperative Circumnavigation for Multiple Unmanned Surface Vehicles Without External Localization

author.name: Xueming Liu, Lin Li, Xiang Zhou, Tianjiang Hu, Qingrui Zhang

entry.summary: This paper presents a cooperative target circumnavigation framework for multiple unmanned surface vehicles operating without external localization, using only onboard range, displacement, and bearing measurements. A heterogeneous perception strategy and relative position estimation maintain uniform circular formation around a non-cooperative target.

entry.title: Trivium: Temporal Regret as a First-Class Objective for Causal-Memory Controllers

author.name: Edward Y. Chang

entry.summary: Introduces Trivium, proposing long-horizon temporal regret and epistemic regret as first-class objectives alongside outcome regret for causal-memory controllers. It targets why and when failures persist rather than only what failed.

entry.title: HighTide: An Agent-Curated Open-Source VLSI Benchmark Suite

author.name: Benjamin Goldblatt, Paolo Pedroso, Farhad Modaresi, Ethan Sifferman, Matthew R. Guthaus

entry.summary: Introduces HighTide, an evolving AI-assisted open-source VLSI benchmark suite spanning multiple design languages and technology nodes with Bazel-based incremental RTL-to-GDS compilation and agent-curated design skills with decision logs. It supports the open hardware ecosystem.

entry.title: ADAPTOOD: Uncertainty-Aware Fine-Tuning for Out-of-Distribution ECG Time Series Models

author.name: Sotirios Vavaroutas, Yu Yvonne Wu, Ali Etemad, Cecilia Mascolo

entry.summary: Introduces ADAPTOOD, an uncertainty-aware fine-tuning method for out-of-distribution ECG time-series models that accounts for shift severity rather than assuming fixed distribution shifts. It targets robustness degradation across diverse sensors, populations, and settings.

entry.title: DSIRM: Learning Query-Bridged Discrete Semantic Identifiers for E-commerce Relevance Modeling

author.name: Bokang Wang, Xing Fang, Mingmin Jin, Jing Wang, Zhentao Song, Guangxin Song, Jianbo Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes DSIRM, a Discrete Semantic Identifier Relevance Model for e-commerce search that explicitly models discrete relevance features via a query-bridged supervised approach rather than unsupervised quantization, addressing difficulty in capturing fine-grained attribute distinctions. It improves query-dependent ranking.

entry.title: QO-Bench: Diagnosing Query-Operator-Preserving Retrieval over Typed Event Tuples

author.name: Mengao Zhang, Xiang Yang, Chang Liu, Tianhui Tan, Ke-wei Huang

entry.summary: QO-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark for query-operator question answering over typed event tuples extracted from text, testing whether RAG systems can execute database-style queries rather than just retrieve relevant passages. Answers are deterministically computed and exact-matched, avoiding LLM-judge ambiguity.

entry.title: Scenario Generation for Risk-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Probably Approximately Safe Guarantees

author.name: Mohit Prashant, Arvind Easwaran

entry.summary: This work develops scenario generation for risk-aware RL with probably-approximately-safe guarantees, constructing probabilistic barrier certificates by sampling trajectories and approximating violation distributions under transition perturbations. It tightens bounds in insufficiently explored states.

entry.title: Self-Reflective APIs: Structure Beats Verbosity for AI Agent Recovery

author.name: Arquimedes Canedo, Grama Chethan

entry.summary: This paper shows that self-reflective APIs returning machine-readable recovery suggestions on validation failure substantially improve AI agent task completion versus plain-English error messages. A leak-audited pilot finds large gains on Anthropic models but not on gpt-4o-mini, with better token efficiency.

entry.title: GeM-NR: Geometry-Aware Multi-View Editing for Nonrigid Scene Changes

author.name: Josef Bengtson, Yaroslava Lochman, Fredrik Kahl

entry.summary: GeM-NR is a fast, training-free approach for general multi-view consistent image editing that handles nonrigid edits substantially changing scene geometry, unlike methods restricted to rigid or appearance-only edits. It is geometry-aware to maintain cross-view consistency.

entry.title: Variance Reduction for Heavy-Tailed Monetization Metrics in Ranking Experiments via Post-Stratification

author.name: Neeti Pokharna, Olivier Jeunen, Yatharth Saraf, Aleksei Ustimenko

entry.summary: This paper presents a practical variance-reduction framework for online ranking experiments with heavy-tailed monetization metrics, combining post-stratification with CUPED using pre-experiment covariates. Deployed at ShareChat, it substantially reduces variance and improves experiment sensitivity without extra traffic.

entry.title: Offline-to-Online Learning in Linear Bandits

author.name: Kushagra Chandak, Toshinori Kitamura, Xiaoqi Tan

entry.summary: This paper studies offline-to-online learning in stochastic linear bandits, proposing an algorithm that relies on offline data early and increasingly favors exploration as the horizon grows. It establishes regret bounds competitive with both purely online and purely offline solutions.

entry.title: PointAction: 3D Points as Universal Action Representations for Robot Control

author.name: Mutian Tong, Han Jiang, Qiao Feng, Lingjie Liu, Jiatao Gu

entry.summary: Presents PointAction, a framework that bridges video-prediction models to robot actions by fine-tuning a video generation foundation model to jointly predict future RGB frames and dynamic 3D pointmaps, using points as universal action representations. It resolves the ambiguity of grounding actions from RGB-only video rollouts.

entry.title: Toward a Generalized Defense Across Sparse, Continuous, and Structured Parameter Attacks

author.name: Bin Duan, Zeyu Bai, Guowei Yang

entry.summary: ParDef proposes a generalized defense against sparse, continuous, and structured parameter (weight tampering) attacks on deployed models, aiming to handle unpredictable attack forms without retraining. It targets integrity risks across cloud, CI/CD, and edge deployment pipelines.

entry.title: Spatially Grounded Concept Bottleneck Models via Part-Factorized Attention

author.name: Dhanesh Ramachandram

entry.summary: This work introduces a part-factorized concept bottleneck model on a frozen DINOv3 backbone that uses a foreground gate and fixed concept-to-part routing so each attribute reads only from its anatomical region. It improves spatial faithfulness and auditability of concept-based decisions.

entry.title: Hyper-ICL: Attention Calibration with Hyperbolic Anchor Distillation for Multimodal In-Context Learning

author.name: Niloufar Alipour Talemi, Hossein Kashiani, Fatemeh Afghah

entry.summary: Hyper-ICL is a demonstration-free multimodal in-context learning framework that learns a low-rank logit-level adapter using hyperbolic anchor distillation to reconstruct demonstration effects without including examples at inference. It reduces latency and instability from demonstration sensitivity.

entry.title: Distributional Approximate Nearest Neighbour Search for Uncertainty-Aware Retrieval

author.name: Olivier Jeunen

entry.summary: This paper extends approximate nearest neighbor search to operate over distributions rather than point embeddings, incorporating embedding uncertainty to counter retrieval bias toward popular head items. It aims for fairer long-tail recommendation retrieval.

entry.title: Beyond Symmetric Alignment: Spectral Diagnostics of Modality Imbalance in Vision-Language Models in the Medical Domain

author.name: Alessandro Gambetti, Qiwei Han, Cl\'audia Soares, Hong Shen

entry.summary: This work introduces the Spectral Alignment Score, an asymmetric metric projecting modalities onto an anchor eigenbasis to reveal which modality drives cross-modal degradation in medical vision-language models. It diagnoses modality information imbalance hidden by symmetric metrics.

entry.title: CRAFT: Cost-aware Refinement And Front-aware Tuning of Prompts

author.name: Shanu Kumar, Shubhanshu Khandelwal, Akhila Yesantarao Venkata, Parag Agrawal, Yova Kementchedjhieva, Manish Gupta

entry.summary: CRAFT is a Pareto-front prompt optimizer that treats target-LLM validation calls as a scarce resource and allocates them near the candidate frontier, avoiding scalarization collapse from fixed weighted objectives. It jointly optimizes prompt accuracy and token cost.

entry.title: FoeGlass: Simple In-Context Learning Is Enough for Red Teaming Audio Deepfake Detectors

author.name: Sepehr Dehdashtian, Jacob H Seidman, Vishnu N Boddeti, Gaurav Bharaj

entry.summary: FoeGlass is a black-box automated red-teaming method for audio deepfake detectors that uses LLM in-context learning to explore the TTS-generated audio space and discover detector blind spots. It surfaces high-error regions underexplored by existing benchmarks.

entry.title: Preserving Data Privacy in Learning Causal Structure with Fully Homomorphic Encryption

author.name: Jian Yang, Yuan Tong, Qinbin Li, Zeyi Wen, Xiaofang Zhou

entry.summary: This work enables privacy-preserving distributed causal structure learning using fully homomorphic encryption, with circuit simplification and techniques to handle FHE limitations on division and logarithms. It keeps data encrypted during transmission and computation.

entry.title: Long Live Fine-Tuning: Task-Specific Transformers Outperform Zero-Shot LLMs for Misinformation Response Classification on Reddit

author.name: JooYoung Lee, Lin Tian, Angela Brillantes, Adriana-Simona Mih\u{a}i\c{t}\u{a}, Marian-Andrei Rizoiu

entry.summary: This study compares nine models across paradigms on 900 Reddit comments for misinformation response classification and finds fine-tuned task-specific transformers outperform zero-shot frontier LLMs (Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini Flash Lite, Claude Sonnet 4.6). It challenges the assumption that scale alone suffices for nuanced misinformation discourse classification.

entry.title: Noisy memory encoding explains negative polarity illusions

author.name: Yuhan Zhang, Edward Gibson

entry.summary: This psycholinguistics paper proposes that lossy context surprisal (imperfect memory encoding) explains negative polarity illusions, where ungrammatical sentences are rated acceptable because readers entertain determiner exchanges that license polarity items. It links memory representation similarity to the illusion strength.

entry.title: When Clients Stop Following: A Cognitive Conceptualization Diagram-driven Framework for Strategic Counseling

author.name: Yihao Qin, Junyi Zhao, Changsheng Ma, Yongfeng Tao, Minqiang Yang, Chang Liu, Bin Hu

entry.summary: This work identifies a counselor-following phenomenon where simulated counseling clients rapidly shift from resistance to compliance, inflating benchmark scores, and proposes a CBT-grounded resistance-aware simulator (CARS) and a strategic counseling framework (STREAMS). It improves realism in evaluating LLM psychological counseling.

entry.title: LDARNet: DNA Adaptive Representation Network with Learnable Tokenization for Genomic Modeling

author.name: Daria Ledneva, Denis Kuznetsov

entry.summary: LDARNet is a 120M-parameter genomic foundation model that adapts H-Net dynamic chunking to masked language modeling, combining BiMamba-2 state-space layers with local attention and a ratio-based regularizer to learn adaptive token boundaries without supervision. It challenges fixed k-mer or BPE tokenization in genomics.

entry.title: SMADE-IE: Sparse Multi-Agent Framework with Evidence-Driven Debate for Zero-Shot Information Extraction

author.name: Kenfeng Huang, Yi Cai, Xin Wu, Zikun Deng, Li Yuan

entry.summary: SMADE-IE is a sparse, evidence-driven multi-agent framework for zero-shot information extraction that uses adaptive routing to reduce token overhead and cross-type conflicts. It addresses inefficiencies in monolithic prompting and standard multi-agent debate.

entry.title: Disentangling Answer Engine Optimization from Platform Growth: A Log-Based Natural Experiment on ChatGPT Referral Traffic

author.name: Keisuke Watanabe, Kazuki Nakayashiki

entry.summary: This log-based natural experiment on a single high-traffic domain disentangles answer-engine-optimization effects from platform-level growth in ChatGPT referral traffic. It uses an untreated site subset as a control to isolate causal AEO impact.

entry.title: A Cookbook of 3D Vision: Data, Learning Paradigms, and Application

author.name: Hongyang Du, Zongxia Li, Dawei Liu, Runhao Li, Haoyuan Song, Qingyu Zhang, Yubo Wang, Jingcheng Ni, Shihang Gui, Congchao Dong, Tao Hu

entry.summary: This survey provides a data-centric taxonomy of 3D vision connecting geometric representations (point clouds, meshes, voxels, 3D Gaussians), datasets, learning paradigms, and applications in a unified conceptual map. It aims to reduce fragmentation across 3D vision subfields.

entry.title: Implicit Fuzzification via Bounded Noise Injection for Robust Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Bisheng Tang, Zhangfeng Ma, Chuchu Zhai, Feng Dong, Yaoqun Wu, Ammar Oad, Yifei Peng

entry.summary: NoiseUNet injects bounded perturbations into U-Net skip connections to regularize cross-scale feature fusion, inducing an implicit fuzzification effect that yields soft boundary memberships. It addresses overconfident predictions in ambiguous transition regions for medical segmentation.

entry.title: A New Angle on Bones: Robust Pose Estimation in X-Ray and Ultrasound

author.name: Ron Keuth, Christoph Gro{\ss}br\"ohmer, Franziska Halm, Miriam Johann, Anne-Nele Schr\"oder, Ludger T\"ushaus, Mattias P. Heinrich, Lasse Hansen

entry.summary: This work performs automatic bone pose and angle estimation in X-ray and ultrasound using learning-based point candidate proposals followed by robust line fitting (RANSAC, Hough) with false-positive reduction. It targets reproducible paediatric angle measurements across three clinical tasks.

entry.title: 3D Temporal Analysis for Autism Spectrum Disorder Screening During Attention Tasks

author.name: Inam Qadir, Elizabeth B Varghese, Dena Al-Thani, Marwa Qaraqe

entry.summary: This work presents a 3D temporal analysis framework using DECA-derived head pose and pose-independent facial expressions to screen for Autism Spectrum Disorder in school-age children during attention tasks. It aims to replace subjective 2D assessments with quantifiable spatial-temporal features.

entry.title: SoftPINCH: EMG-Driven Soft Exoskeleton Assistance for Finger Flexion and Grasping

author.name: Nicklas Nikolaj Gr{\o}nvall, Magnus Malthe Sigsgaard Nielsen, Xiaofeng Xiong, Saravana Prashanth Murali Babu

entry.summary: SoftPINCH is an EMG-driven soft wearable exoskeleton for thumb-index finger flexion and pinch grasp assistance, combining a tendon-driven soft design, fingertip magnetic contact sensing, and neural EMG decoding for intention-based control. It addresses the noise, fatigue, and inter-subject variability challenges of EMG-driven hand assistance while keeping the device comfortable.

entry.title: LCSHBench: A Multilingual, Consensus-Grounded Benchmark for Library of Congress Subject Heading Assignment

author.name: Kwok Leong Tang

entry.summary: Introduces LCSHBench, a multilingual consensus-grounded benchmark of 22,346 books in 15 languages for Library of Congress Subject Heading assignment, including records where at least two cataloging agencies agreed, scoring both exact and concept-level matches. A concordance study shows libraries usually agree on topic but differ in exact expression.

entry.title: SFMambaNet: Spectral-Frequency Enhanced Selective State Space Model for Correspondence Pruning

author.name: Zhihua Wang, Yanping Li, Yizhang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes SFMambaNet, a spectral-frequency enhanced Mamba-based network for two-view correspondence pruning that integrates frequency-domain perception to better capture subtle geometric consistencies of inliers and reduce inconsistent hidden-state feature accumulation. It addresses limitations of GNN- and Mamba-based pruning methods.

entry.title: DeliChess: A Multi-party Dialogue Dataset for Deliberation in Chess Puzzle Solving

author.name: Xiaochen Zhu, Georgi Karadzhov, Tom Stafford, Andreas Vlachos

entry.summary: DeliChess is a multi-party dialogue dataset of group deliberations solving chess puzzles, with pre- and post-discussion choices and chess-engine-based evaluation metrics. It studies collaborative reasoning, finding that deliberation significantly improves group decisions.

entry.title: BEATS: Bootstrapping E-commerce Attribute Taxonomies for Search through Iterative Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Yung-Yu Shih, Shang-Yu Su, Tzu-I Ho, Dongzhe Wang, Yun-Nung Chen

entry.summary: BEATS is a human-in-the-loop LLM framework for bootstrapping e-commerce product attribute taxonomies from scratch, adding production stages for quality checking and domain-expert annotation. It targets underdeveloped catalogs in emerging markets to improve search.

entry.title: IMPose: Interactive Multi-person Pose Estimation with Dynamic Correction Propagation

author.name: Haoyang Ge, Jian Ma, Ziwen Wang, Qihe Wang, Jianqi Fan, Hongzhi Yu, Xingyu Chen, Kun Li

entry.summary: IMPose is an interactive tool for multi-person dynamic pose annotation that propagates one-frame corrections across entire videos via dual-level keypoint and instance tracking. It reduces manual intervention in multi-person scenarios where existing tools fail.

entry.title: Consensus is Strategically Insufficient: Reasoning-Trace Disagreement as a Knowledge-Representation Signal

author.name: Micha{\l} Wawer, Jaros{\l}aw A. Chudziak

entry.summary: Argues that consensus-seeking in multi-agent systems is insufficient for value-laden tasks, proposing a symbolic knowledge layer that treats reasoning-trace disagreement as a meaningful signal rather than error. It distinguishes four disagreement states by reasoning similarity and conclusion agreement.

entry.title: The Digital Apprentice: A Framework for Human-Directed Agentic AI Development

author.name: Travis Weber, Rohit Taneja

entry.summary: Presents the Digital Apprentice framework where agent autonomy is earned per-skill through empirical evidence rather than assumed, capturing a director's tacit methodology. It aims to balance scalability with accountability via developmental autonomy tiers.

entry.title: A Normative Intermediate Representation for ASP-Based Compliance Reasoning

author.name: Yangfan Wu, Huanyu Yang, Jianmin Ji

entry.summary: Proposes MONIR, a modalized-output normative intermediate representation for ASP-based compliance reasoning with staged operational semantics and an executable compilation. It is instantiated on Chinese ADAS regulations via an LLM-assisted extraction pipeline.

entry.title: Gravity-Aware Hierarchical Routing for Lightweight SensorLLM on Human Activity Recognition

author.name: Hao Li, Mingrui Zheng, Yasuyuki Tahara, Yuichi Sei

entry.summary: Identifies that compressing SensorLLM backbones to tiny models degrades recognition of low-motion static activities, and proposes a gravity-aware hierarchical routing head as a lightweight post-alignment adaptation. It improves static-class discrimination for wearable human activity recognition.

entry.title: StandardE2E: A Unified Framework for End-to-End Autonomous Driving Datasets

author.name: Stepan Konev

entry.summary: Presents StandardE2E, a framework providing a single unified interface over end-to-end autonomous driving datasets, standardizing preprocessing, file formats, coordinate conventions, and modality coverage to enable cross-dataset experimentation. It addresses fragmentation in the driving-dataset ecosystem.

entry.title: Generalizable Multi-Task Learning for Wireless Networks Using Prompt Decision Transformers

author.name: Fatih Temiz, Shavbo Salehi, Melike Erol-Kantarci

entry.summary: Proposes using prompt decision transformers for generalizable multi-task learning in wireless networks, targeting AI-driven radio resource management and coordinated multipoint transmission selection across heterogeneous, dynamic conditions. It enables rapid adaptation to diverse network and task configurations.

entry.title: Rethinking Sales Lead Scoring with LLM-based Hierarchical Preference Ranking

author.name: Chenyu Zhang, Yiwen Liu, Yin Sun, Xinyuan Zhang, Yuji Cao, Junming Jiao, Juyi Qiao

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-based discriminative framework using hierarchical preference ranking for sales lead scoring in high-stakes domains with prolonged decision cycles, addressing sparse supervision, semantic gaps in CRM logs, and the need to capture relative lead priority. It adapts LLMs to produce comparable scores aligned with sales-funnel hierarchies.

entry.title: Learning Long Range Spatio-Temporal Representations over Continuous Time Dynamic Graphs with State Space Models

author.name: Ayushman Raghuvanshi, Thummaluru Siddartha Readdy, Sundeep Prabhakar Chepuri, Mahesh Chandran

entry.summary: CTDG-SSM derives a state-space modeling framework for continuous-time dynamic graphs, introducing a topology-aware HiPPO operator to capture long-range multi-hop temporal patterns. It addresses the locality limitation of existing dynamic graph methods.

entry.title: CoRe-MoE: Contrastive Reweighted Mixture of Experts for Multi-Terrain Humanoid Locomotion with Gait Adaptation

author.name: Kailun Huang (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Zikang Xie (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Yanzhe Xie (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Panpan Liao (Guangdong University of Technology), Fanghai Zhang (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Yanheng Mai (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Wenhao Xu (South China Agricultural University), Yunheng Wang (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Renjing Xu (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Haohui Huang (Guangdong University of Technology)

entry.summary: CoRe-MoE is a two-stage RL framework using a contrastive reweighted mixture-of-experts to unify gait transitions and multi-terrain adaptation for humanoid locomotion. It addresses gradient interference and weak expert specialization in naive MoE training.

entry.title: Signed Dual Attention: Capturing Signed Dependencies in Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Balthazar Courvoisier, Tristan Cazenave

entry.summary: Signed Dual Attention introduces a parameter-free attention formulation capturing both positive and negative dependencies in time series via a dual message-passing scheme, overcoming the homophily assumption of standard attention. It propagates supportive and contrastive information jointly.

entry.title: Arithmetic Pedagogy for Language Models

author.name: Andhika Bernard Lumbantobing, Hokky Situngkir

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether human math pedagogy (the Indonesian GASING left-to-right method) can guide LLM arithmetic training by serializing computation traces into chain-of-thought supervision. A small 86M GPT-2 trained from scratch with next-token prediction reveals distinct learning phases.

entry.title: Low-rank Distributional Matrix Completion

author.name: Jiayi Wang, Raymond K. W. Wong

entry.summary: This work studies low-rank distributional matrix completion, where each matrix entry is a probability distribution observed only via finite samples, using kernel mean embeddings and a Tucker-rank notion for distribution-valued matrices. It introduces functional unfolding operators to handle the infinite-dimensional structure.

entry.title: Reconciling Causality and Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics with Hamiltonian Causal Models

author.name: Dario Rancati, Max Welling, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: Introduces Hamiltonian Causal Models, a trajectory-level causal framework where interventions act as controls of Hamiltonian mechanisms, handling path-dependent effects and dynamics-mediated feedback. It connects causal modeling to non-equilibrium thermodynamics via entropy production.

entry.title: Optimal Transport Flow Matching by Design

author.name: Shimon Malnick, Matan Rusanovsky, Ohad Fried, Shai Avidan

entry.summary: Reformulates optimal-transport flow matching by treating the prior as a design choice rather than a fixed input, since many priors admit an OT-optimal identity coupling to the data. This avoids the intractable high-dimensional OT computation while enabling straight non-crossing trajectories for fast generation.

entry.title: Long-Term and Short-Term Transistor Aging in Deep Neural Networks: Impact and Mitigation

author.name: Alireza Sarmadi, Virinchi Roy Surabhi, Prashanth Krishnamurthy, Hussam Amrouch, Ramesh Karri, Farshad Khorrami

entry.summary: This chapter analyzes how long-term and short-term transistor aging degrades DNN inference accuracy through timing violations and discusses mitigation strategies that avoid large performance-costly guardbands. It connects hardware reliability physics to model deployment.

entry.title: Knockoffs-based False Discovery Rate Control and Simplification for Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Huiqi Zhang, Wenyu Liao, Yiqing Shi, Xiaobo Huang, Fang Xie

entry.summary: This paper proposes knockoff-based variable screening methods for deep neural networks that control false discovery rate while simplifying inputs and parameters. It extends knockoff FDR control from high-dimensional regression to regularized neural networks.

entry.title: Crafting Your Evolving Dreams: Concept-Incremental Versatile Customization

author.name: Jiahua Dong, Wenqi Liang, Hongliu Li, Yang Cong, Duzhen Zhang, Hanbin Zhao, Henghui Ding, Yulun Zhang, Salman Khan, Fahad Shahbaz Khan

entry.summary: This paper develops a continually customizable diffusion model enabling concept-incremental personalization via attribute-decoupled LoRA and relevance-guided aggregation, mitigating catastrophic forgetting and concept neglect. It supports growing collections of user concepts over time.

entry.title: Bayesian learning for the stochastic shortest path problem

author.name: Chon Wai Ho, Sumeetpal S. Singh, Jiaqi Guo

entry.summary: This paper develops a Bayesian framework for the stochastic shortest path problem that constructs posterior beliefs over the optimal action-value function directly through Bellman optimality equations, avoiding unrealistic modeling assumptions. It characterizes the posterior as a manifold density for deterministic rewards.

entry.title: Stepwise Reasoning Enhancement for LLMs via External Subgraph Generation

author.name: Xin Zhang, Yang Cao, Baoxing Wu, Kai Song, Siying Li

entry.summary: SGR is a stepwise reasoning framework that integrates LLMs with external knowledge graphs by extracting a structured schema, retrieving compact query-relevant subgraphs, and using them as explicit relational evidence. It aims to improve logical consistency, factual grounding, and interpretability in multi-step reasoning.

entry.title: Large Language Models in K-12 Education: Alignment with State Curriculum Standards and Student Personas

author.name: Lisa Korver, Tomo Lazovich, Sherief Reda

entry.summary: This work builds an LLM pipeline to evaluate whether LLM responses align with U.S. state-level K-12 curriculum standards, focusing on variations in U.S. History curricula. It raises ethical questions about educational use of chatbots by students.

entry.title: Hierarchical Space Partition for Surface Reconstruction

author.name: Minjie Tang, Xiangfei Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes a hierarchical space partition with a plane-assembling strategy for surface reconstruction that recovers missing geometry from incomplete LiDAR point clouds. Planes are categorized by visibility and grown with priorities to produce compact polygonal models.

entry.title: MaCo-GAN: Manifold-Contrastive Adversarial Learning for Single Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Daeyoung Han, Seongmin Hwang, Moongu Jeon

entry.summary: MaCo-GAN replaces standard adversarial loss with a supervised contrastive objective for single image super-resolution, using a dynamic fake-sample synthesizer to enforce conditional realism. It aims to reduce hallucinated artifacts common in GAN-based SISR.

entry.title: Fog of Love: Engineering Virtuous Agent Behavior with Affinity-based Reinforcement Learning in a Game Environment

author.name: Ajay Vishwanath, Christian Omlin

entry.summary: Introduces a two-player multi-agent environment based on the board game Fog of Love to study affinity-based reinforcement learning for instilling virtuous agent behavior. It extends prior grid-world demonstrations to richer cooperative-competitive settings.

entry.title: Revisiting Vul-RAG: Reproducibility and Replicability of RAG-based Vulnerability Detection with Open-Weight Models

author.name: Sabrina Kaniewski, Fabian Schmidt, Tobias Heer

entry.summary: This reproducibility study replicates Vul-RAG, a RAG-based vulnerability detection framework, in a fully local open-weights setting and extends evaluation across diverse models. It examines whether reported results depend on specific proprietary model choices.

entry.title: OA-CutMix: Correcting the Label Bias of CutMix

author.name: Tobias Christian Nauen, Stanislav Frolov, Federico Raue, Brian B. Moser, Andreas Dengel

entry.summary: OA-CutMix corrects a label-assignment bias in CutMix, where area-based weights misattribute label credit to background patches, by deriving weights from segmentation masks proportional to visible object area. It documents that mean label-area discrepancy is over 21 percent.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Distillation for Prompt Tuning Biomedical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Tran Dinh Tien, Zhiqiang Shen

entry.summary: OGKD is a geometry-aware knowledge distillation framework for prompt-tuning biomedical vision-language models that injects inter-class relation structure into the teacher to produce directional targets, rather than treating all non-target classes as equally wrong. It develops global and local geometry-aware distillation losses for limited-supervision medical settings.

entry.title: Towards Efficient and Evidence-grounded Mobility Prediction with LLM-Driven Agent

author.name: Linyao Chen, Qinlao Zhao, Zechen Li, Mingming Li, Likun Ni, Jinyu Chen, Yuhao Yao, Xuan Song, Noboru Koshizuka, Hiroki Kobayashi

entry.summary: This paper presents a training-free LLM-driven agent for individual mobility prediction that frames next-location prediction as adaptive evidence-controlled decision making, using a fast path for routine cases and iterative tool use for ambiguous ones. It aims for efficient, evidence-grounded, interpretable predictions.

entry.title: Training-Free Lexical-Dense Fusion for Conversational-Memory Retrieval

author.name: Christian Lysenst{\o}en

entry.summary: This paper proposes a training-free, CPU-only lexical-dense fusion stage for long-term conversational memory retrieval, combining late-interaction dense scoring with BM25 under a single leave-one-conversation-out weight. It reports substantial Hit@1 gains on LoCoMo across six encoders.

entry.title: PE-MHL: Physics-Encoded Modular Hybrid Layers for Scalable Learning of Complex Systems

author.name: Ismail Hassaballa, Mircea Lazar

entry.summary: PE-MHL is a physics-encoded modular hybrid layer framework that incrementally refines a baseline physics model by adding sub-models, each increasing complexity while preserving prior learning, with a theoretical training guarantee under least-squares initialization. It targets scalable, noise-robust, interpretable learning of complex systems for control.

entry.title: STRIDE: Training Data Attribution via Sparse Recovery from Subset Perturbations

author.name: Rishit Dagli, Abir Harrasse, Luke Zhang, Florent Draye, Amirali Abdullah, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Zhijing Jin

entry.summary: Proposes STRIDE, a training data attribution method that models the functional effect of training data in activation space via steering rather than estimating parameter changes through gradients. It uses sparse recovery from subset perturbations to avoid expensive retraining and gradient tracking for LLMs.

entry.title: Neetyabhas: A Framework for Uncertainty-Aware Public Policy Optimization in Rational Agent-Based Models

author.name: Janani Venugopalan, Gaurav Deshkar, Rishabh Gaur, Harshal Hayatnagarkar, Jayanta Kshirsagar

entry.summary: Proposes Neetyabhas, a framework for uncertainty-aware public policy optimization in rational agent-based models, incorporating uncertainties in epidemic measurement and policy execution. It simulates 1,000 individuals making real-time choices under imperfect tracking for COVID-19 interventions.

entry.title: Neural Radiated-Noise Fields for Unmanned Underwater Vehicle Noise Spectrum Prediction in Three-Dimensional Scenes

author.name: Yan Wu, Yang Yang, Jun Fan, Bin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a neural radiated-noise field (NRNF) representing UUV radiated-noise spectra as a continuous function of position, hydrophone location, yaw, and frequency for 3D query-based prediction. It overcomes the dependence of physics-based methods on structural and boundary information.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Short-Term Flood Prediction

author.name: Tewodros Syum Gebre, Jagrati Talreja, Leila Hashemi-Beni

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-informed ML framework embedding hydrological knowledge (a trend-alignment constraint between precipitation and discharge) into an LSTM loss for short-term flood prediction, improving robustness in data-scarce and extreme conditions. It addresses physically inconsistent predictions from purely data-driven models.

entry.title: HYolo: An Intelligent IoT-Based Object Detection System Using Hypergraph Learning

author.name: Isha Abid, Fawad Khan, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad

entry.summary: Presents HYolo, an IoT-based object detection framework integrating hypergraph learning into the YOLO architecture to capture high-order relationships among objects and contextual features beyond pairwise interactions, reporting ~12% mAP@50 improvement on COCO. It targets richer contextual dependency modeling.

entry.title: RowNet: A Memory Transformer for Tabular Regression

author.name: Askat Rakhymbekov, Gulshat Muhametjanova

entry.summary: Presents RowNet, a retrieval-based memory transformer for tabular regression (real estate price-per-square-meter) that represents a query property through pairwise similarity to historical observations, explicitly modeling comparable-property retrieval missing in MLPs and GBDTs. It targets structured regression with heterogeneous features.

entry.title: Synthetic Personalities: How Well Can LLMs Mimic Individual Respondents Using Socio-Economic Microdata?

author.name: Leonard Kinzinger, Jochen Hartmann

entry.summary: This study builds detailed individual-level LLM digital twins from pre-existing heterogeneous panel data (German SOEP) rather than purpose-collected surveys, evaluating across a grid of open-weight models and construction methods. It addresses the operationally relevant case for market research using CRM and loyalty data firms already hold.

entry.title: Coarse-to-fine Hierarchical Architecture with Sequential Mamba for Brain Reconstruction

author.name: Hoang-Son Vo, Van-Hung Bui, Minh-Huy Mai-Duc, Tien-Dung Mai, Soo-Hyung Kim

entry.summary: CHASMBrain is a hierarchical two-stage image-to-fMRI encoding framework using a dual-stream Mamba design to separately process global semantic tokens and local spatial patches, motivated by visual cortex organization. It uses a coarse-to-fine strategy predicting ROI activations then refining.

entry.title: Learning Empirically Admissible Neural Heuristics for Combinatorial Search

author.name: Siddharth Sahay

entry.summary: This work introduces a framework for learning validation-calibrated admissible neural heuristics for combinatorial search puzzles, ensuring heuristics do not overestimate cost-to-go and thus preserve A* optimality. It addresses the overestimation problem of standard MSE-trained value networks like DeepCubeA.

entry.title: Pseudospectral Bounds for Transient Amplification in Coupled Gradient Descent

author.name: Ahanaf Hasan Ariq

entry.summary: This work develops a pseudospectral theory for block-triangular coupled gradient descent Jacobians, proving bounds on the Kreiss constant that govern transient amplification from non-normality, with matching minimax lower bounds. It characterizes a critical coupling threshold relevant to bilevel optimization and adversarial training.

entry.title: When Offline Selectors Cannot Beat the Best Single Model: A Diagnostic Study on edX Dropout Prediction

author.name: Tyler Crosse, Alan Nadelsticher Ruvalcaba, Dustin Khang LeDuc, Thomas Trask, Nicholas Lytle, David Joyner

entry.summary: This diagnostic study examines why offline model selectors fail to beat the best single predictor on edX dropout prediction, separating three causes: mismatched learner, uninformative state, and label shift. It proposes a three-stage diagnostic using k-NN label-consistency ceilings, BC/offline-RL learners, and state ablation.

entry.title: Data Attribution in Large Language Models via Bidirectional Gradient Optimization

author.name: Fr\'ed\'eric Berdoz, Luca A. Lanzend\"orfer, Kaan Bayraktar, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: Proposes a training data attribution method for autoregressive LLMs via bidirectional gradient optimization, perturbing the model with gradient ascent and descent on a generated sample and measuring loss changes across training data. It supports attribution at arbitrary granularity for governance and provenance.

entry.title: Representation Matters in Randomized Smoothing for Audio Classification

author.name: Jong-Ik Park, Shreyas Chaudhari, Jos\'e M. F. Moura, Carlee Joe-Wong

entry.summary: This paper shows that randomized smoothing for audio classification is under-specified unless preprocessing and the certified object are made explicit, since waveform-to-spectral pipelines change the noise space. It provides diagnostics arguing for representation-aware robustness reporting.

entry.title: REGAIN: REconciliation GAIN-driven Auxiliary Direction Learning

author.name: Weijia Li, Shun Hu, Yanfei Kang

entry.summary: REGAIN is a forecast-reconciliation framework that learns which additional linear measurements to forecast and include, selecting auxiliary directions by their downstream reconciliation gain. It departs from variance- or predictability-based selection by optimizing the final reconciled forecast.

entry.title: Scaling Datasets for Multi-Sensor, Multi-Agent, and Multi-Domain Learning in Autonomous Systems

author.name: R. Spencer Hallyburton, David Hunt, Miroslav Pajic

entry.summary: This paper presents a modular pipeline generating terabyte-scale, ground-truth-labeled multi-agent, multi-sensor, multi-domain datasets for autonomy using AVstack and CARLA. It enables controllable experimentation for collaborative perception and fusion.

entry.title: ReSGA: A Large Tail Risk Model for Learning Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall

author.name: Yichi Zhang, Ke Zhu, Zhoufan Zhu

entry.summary: ReSGA is a million-parameter retrieval-enhanced self-grouping autoencoder for learning Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall from firm characteristics, outperforming twelve econometric and ML baselines on US equity returns. It scales tail-risk modeling beyond limited-parameter approaches.

entry.title: U-Net-Accelerated Quality-Diversity Optimization for Climate-Adaptive Urban Layouts

author.name: Alexander Hagg, Tania Guerrero, Dirk Reith

entry.summary: This paper replaces a slow regulatory climate simulator with a U-Net spatial surrogate inside an offline MAP-Elites quality-diversity loop to optimize climate-adaptive urban layouts. It compares spatial deep-learning versus Gaussian-process surrogates across data strategies.

entry.title: NLLog: Lightweight, Explainable SOC Anomaly Detection via Log-to-Language Rewriting

author.name: Samuel Ndichu, Tao Ban, Seiichi Ozawa, Takeshi Takahashi, Daisuke Inoue

entry.summary: NLLog is a lightweight SOC anomaly detection pipeline that deterministically rewrites parsed log templates into WHO-WHAT-SEVERITY natural-language sentences, classifies sessions with tree ensembles, and provides TreeSHAP explanations. It sustains low false-positive rates at commodity-hardware latency.

entry.title: Activation-Based Active Learning for In-Context Learning: Challenges and Insights

author.name: Yaseen M. Osman, Geoff V. Merrett, Stuart E. Middleton

entry.summary: This paper tests whether transformer MLP activations can guide active selection of in-context examples and reports a negative result: massive-activation and similar lenses do not yield useful selection signal across classification and generative tasks. It is a careful study using Llama-3.2-3B and Qwen2.5-3B.

entry.title: Using Text-Based Causal Inference to Disentangle Factors Influencing Online Review Ratings

author.name: Linsen Li, Aron Culotta, Nicholas Mattei

entry.summary: This paper applies text-based causal inference (an enhanced CausalBERT with temperature scaling and hyperparameter tuning) to disentangle how individual aspects causally affect overall online review ratings amid correlated facets. It isolates per-aspect effects beyond standard aspect-based sentiment analysis.

entry.title: Multilingual Long-Form Speech Instruction Following: KIT's Submission to IWSLT 2026

author.name: Enes Yavuz Ugan, Maike Z\"ufle, Yuka Ko, Supriti Sinhamahapatra, Fabian Retkowski, Seymanur Akti, Jan Niehues, Alexander Waibel

entry.summary: KIT's IWSLT 2026 submission tackles multilingual long-form speech instruction following, using data augmentation to convert short corpora into over 1M long-form instruction examples. It addresses overfitting to known tasks via an unknown surprise task.

entry.title: Fast Cubical Persistent Homology on 2D and 3D Images via Union-Find, Pruning, and Lookup Tables

author.name: Titouan Le Breton, Karol Szustakowski, Marie Piraud

entry.summary: Flash Cubical presents a highly efficient computation of cubical persistent homology for 2D/3D images using union-find, edge pruning, and lookup tables. It claims state-of-the-art speed for topological data analysis on images.

entry.title: What Can Eye Gaze Teach Us About Real-World Cycling? Insights From the Oxford RobotCycle Project

author.name: Benjamin Hardin, Efimia Panagiotaki, Daniele De Martini, Lars Kunze

entry.summary: This study uses wearable eye-tracking glasses in the Oxford RobotCycle project to investigate the perceived (subconscious) danger of real-world cycling across bike lanes, car lanes, and shared bus lanes. It finds that gaze patterns differ across environments, revealing distinct cognitive challenges that self-report may miss.

entry.title: Incremental Sheaf Cohomology on Cellular Complexes: O(1)-in-n Lazy Edit Processing under Bounded Local Geometry

author.name: Jason L. Volk

entry.summary: Presents an algorithmic framework for incremental maintenance of first sheaf cohomology on dynamically evolving 1D cellular complexes, achieving O(1)-in-n lazy edit processing under bounded local geometry instead of O(n^3) full recomputation. It is a theoretical contribution in computational topology.

entry.title: TITAN-FedAnil+: Trust-Based Adaptive Blockchain Federated Learning for Resource-Constrained Intelligent Enterprises

author.name: Muhammad Hadi, Muhammad Jahangir, Talha Shafique, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad

entry.summary: Presents TITAN-FedAnil+, a trust-based adaptive blockchain federated learning framework for resource-constrained enterprises, using affinity-propagation-based clustered aggregation to filter malicious updates without knowing the attacker count, plus GPU-accelerated vectorization for efficiency. It addresses non-IID heterogeneity and decentralized security threats.

entry.title: QuBLAST: A Framework for Quantizing Large Language Models with Block-Level Compression Approach and Activation Scaling Strategy

author.name: Pasindu Wickramasinghe, Achyuta Muthuvelan, Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Minghao Shao, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: QuBLAST proposes block-level quantization for LLMs with non-uniform precision across attention blocks plus an activation scaling strategy to handle outliers cheaply. It also evaluates on non-conventional architectures like state-space models.

entry.title: Curvature-aware dynamic precision approach for physics-informed neural networks

author.name: Yingjie Shao, Ioannis N. Athanasiadis, George van Voorn, Taniya Kapoor

entry.summary: This work proposes a curvature-aware precision controller for physics-informed neural networks that adapts numerical precision between FP32 and FP64 during training. It aims to retain FP64 accuracy at reduced computational cost for PDE simulation.

entry.title: AdaKoop: Efficient Modeling of Nonlinear Dynamics from Nonstationary Data Streams with Koopman Operator Regression

author.name: Naoki Chihara, Ren Fujiwara, Yasuko Matsubara, Yasushi Sakurai

entry.summary: AdaKoop is an efficient streaming algorithm applying Koopman operator theory to model nonlinear dynamics in nonstationary data streams via finite-dimensional linear approximations. It adapts to changing nonlinear patterns under strict time constraints.

entry.title: Inverse Critical Experiment Design via Gradient Optimization and a Multigroup Attention-Based Neural Network Architecture

author.name: Will Savage, Logan Burnett, Dean Price

entry.summary: This paper presents inverse design of nuclear critical experiments using a multigroup attention-based neural network surrogate and gradient optimization to maximize neutronic similarity (correlation coefficient ck) to target reactor technologies. The surrogate is trained on OpenMC-calculated sensitivity vectors.

entry.title: SurvPFN: Towards Foundation Models for Survival Predictions

author.name: Samuel B\"ohm (Institute of Epidemiology and Prevention, Medical Center - University of Freiburg, Faculty of Medicine, University of Freiburg, Freiburg, Germany), Lennart Purucker (Department of Computer Science, University of Freiburg, Freiburg, Germany, PriorLabs, Freiburg, Germany), Frank Hutter (Department of Computer Science, University of Freiburg, Freiburg, Germany, PriorLabs, Freiburg, Germany), Pascal Schlosser (Institute of Epidemiology and Prevention, Medical Center - University of Freiburg, Faculty of Medicine, University of Freiburg, Freiburg, Germany, Department of Epidemiology, Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, Baltimore, Maryland, US, CIBSS - Centre for Integrative Biological Signalling Studies, University of Freiburg, Freiburg, Germany)

entry.summary: Introduces SurvPFN, a prior-data fitted network for time-to-event survival prediction that natively handles censored data, pretrained on millions of synthetic survival tasks via distributional regression. It extends tabular foundation models to the previously untouched survival domain.

entry.title: Answer Self-Consistency with Margin-Triggered Question Re-Arbitration for the CVPR 2026 VidLLMs Challenge

author.name: Tomoya Miyazawa, Hiroyasu Okuno

entry.summary: ASC-MQRA is a training-free test-time reasoning framework for video relational reasoning that aggregates multiple stochastic VQA runs via answer-level self-consistency, with conditional re-arbitration for low-margin cases. It was the authors' CVPR 2026 VidLLMs Challenge Track 2 solution.

entry.title: HD-DinoMoE: A Class-Aware Hierarchical Dual Mixture-of-Experts Network for Scleral Anomaly Segmentation in Complex Acquisition Scenarios

author.name: Yinxiang Yu, Maoxiang Chu, Qi Niu, Guanghu Liu, Wei Xu, Haotian Wang, Zhi Chen, Yutian Zhu, Yuelong Fan, Guanghao Liao

entry.summary: HD-DinoMoE is a class-aware hierarchical dual mixture-of-experts network for scleral surface anomaly segmentation in Traditional Chinese Medicine ocular inspection. It combines dual-stream DINOv3 features with class-specific experts to handle distribution shifts and specular reflections.

entry.title: Instance-Level Post Hoc Uncertainty Quantification in Object Detection

author.name: Chongzhe Zhang, Zifan Zeng, Qunli Zhang, Feng Liu, Zheng Hu

entry.summary: This paper proposes MC-GLM, a Monte-Carlo generalized linearized model for instance-level, approximately post-hoc uncertainty quantification in object detection, using Laplace approximation with a constant number of samples. It targets safety-critical autonomous driving where retraining is impractical.

entry.title: Abduction Prover in Isabelle/HOL

author.name: Yutaka Nagashima, Daniel Sebastian Goc

entry.summary: This paper introduces an Abduction Prover for Isabelle/HOL that constructs proof scripts by identifying useful conjectures through abductive reasoning, aiming to improve automation in expressive proof assistants. It targets reducing the cost of formal verification.

entry.title: AlphaQ: Calibration-Free Bit Allocation for Mixture-of-Experts Quantization

author.name: Wanqi Yang, Yuexiao Ma, Alexander Conzelmann, Xiawu Zheng, Michael W. Mahoney, T. Konstantin Rusch, Shiwei Liu

entry.summary: Proposes AlphaQ, a calibration-free mixed-precision bit allocation method for Mixture-of-Experts quantization that does not require proprietary training data to estimate expert importance. It addresses memory-bound MoE deployment where calibration sets are imperfect surrogates.

entry.title: SANE Schema-aware Natural-language Evaluation of Biological Data

author.name: Rolf Gattung, Martin Krueger, Markus Reischl

entry.summary: SANE is a schema-grounded, automatically generated benchmark paradigm for domain-specific text-to-SQL evaluation on high-throughput microscopy biological data, addressing reliability concerns from LLM hallucination. It enables scalable, systematic, reproducible evaluation under constrained schemas.

entry.title: Light or Full Verb? A Minimal-Pair Dataset for Probing Phraseological Competence in Language Models

author.name: Francesca Franzon, Nicolas Ros\`as G\'omez, Leo Wanner

entry.summary: This work introduces a minimal-pair dataset probing whether language models distinguish light-verb constructions from full lexical predicates (e.g., make a decision vs make a cake). Probing experiments show models differentiate these uses even in minimal contexts.

entry.title: Towards Estimating Normal and Shear Interface Pressures in Prosthetic Sockets via Least Squares and Mechanics Modeling

author.name: Axel Gonz\'alez Cornejo, Tianhao Yu, Chi Hwan Lee, Edgar Bol\'ivar-Nieto

entry.summary: This work develops a least-squares mechanics-modeling approach and testbed to estimate both normal and shear interface pressures in prosthetic sockets from sparse sensor measurements. It addresses sensor drift and crosstalk that complicate decoupling normal and shear stresses for socket fit.

entry.title: Thinking Through Signs: PEEL as a Semiotic Scaffolding for Epistemically Accountable AI-Enabled Research

author.name: Clarisse de Souza, Gabriel Barbosa, Simone Diniz Junqueira Barbosa, B\'arbara Betts, Renato Cerqueira, Juliana Jansen Ferreira

entry.summary: Introduces PEEL, a semiotic scaffolding combining deterministic distant-reading tools with LLM interpretation to preserve epistemic accountability in research. It shows LLM summaries systematically distort quantity, term frequency, and voice in ways invisible without non-AI measurement.

entry.title: Constraint-Enhanced Physical Search through Correlation Matching

author.name: Song-Ju Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a principle of constraint-enhanced physical search where temporal exploration correlations are matched to constraint-induced spatial correlations, demonstrated on a tug-of-war bandit model. It shows search efficiency improves by matching correlations to the physical update scale rather than maximizing randomness.

entry.title: Overview of the EReL@MIR 2025 Multimodal Document Retrieval Challenge (Track 1)

author.name: Jingbiao Mei

entry.summary: Provides an overview of Track 1 of the EReL@MIR 2025 Multimodal Document Retrieval Challenge, which asks for a single retrieval system handling closed-set page retrieval and open-domain image-query retrieval over visually-rich documents. It motivates retaining the visual channel in retrievers.

entry.title: An Ensembled Latent Factor Model via Differential Evolution and Gradient Descent Optimization

author.name: Rui Zhang, Jinhang Liu, Wenbo Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes ELFM-DEGDO, an ensembled latent factor model for high-dimensional incomplete data that independently trains two models via differential evolution and gradient descent respectively, then ensembles them to mitigate insufficient and biased representations from gradient-only optimization. It targets heterogeneous HDI data.

entry.title: Multi-SPIN: Multi-Access Speculative Inference for Cooperative Token Generation at the Edge

author.name: Haotian Zheng, Zhanwei Wang, Mingyao Cui, Chang Cai, Hongyang Du, Kaibin Huang

entry.summary: Multi-SPIN extends speculative inference to distributed edge systems, where on-device small models draft tokens and an edge server LLM verifies them in batches. It treats draft length as a control variable to balance heterogeneous device/server loads, targeting cooperative token generation at the network edge.

entry.title: From Prompt to Process: a Process Taxonomy and Comparative Assessment of Frameworks Supporting AI Software Development Agents

author.name: Sanderson Oliveira de Macedo

entry.summary: This survey proposes a process taxonomy and comparative assessment of six operational frameworks (e.g., GitHub Spec Kit, BMAD Method) that turn AI coding capabilities into structured development processes with roles, artifacts, and verification. It fills a gap left by surveys focused on agents and LLMs rather than operational frameworks.

entry.title: TANDEM: Bi-Level Data Mixture Optimization with Twin Networks

author.name: Jiaxing Wang, Deping Xiang, Jin Xu, Mingyang Yi, Guoqiang Gong, Zicheng Zhang, Haoran Li, Pengzhang Liu, Zhen Chen, Ke Zhang, Ju Fan, Qixiang Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces TANDEM, a bi-level data mixture optimization method for LLM pretraining that uses twin networks (a proxy and a dynamically updated reference) to measure data efficacy and up-weight beneficial domains. It simplifies the bi-level problem into a penalized single-level form with theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: Be Fair! Can Machine Learning Engineering Agents Adhere to Fairness Constraints?

author.name: Anna Richter, Julia Stoyanovich, Sebastian Schelter

entry.summary: Investigates whether machine learning engineering agents can adhere to fairness constraints, arguing existing benchmarks are insufficient for sensitive regulated domains. It proposes responsibility-centered evaluation desiderata and conducts an exploratory study on melanoma classification across skin tones.

entry.title: Cross-Prompt Generalization in Detecting AI-Generated Fake News Using Interpretable Linguistic Features

author.name: Aya Vera-Jimenez, Samuel Jaeger, Calvin Ibenye, Dhrubajyoti Ghosh

entry.summary: This study examines cross-prompt generalization in detecting AI-generated fake news using interpretable linguistic features (lexical diversity, readability, emotion) with a random forest classifier. It tests whether detectors trained on one prompting strategy transfer to unseen prompts.

entry.title: Radiomic Feature Selection Using Gradient Loss of Deep Neural Network for Lung Cancer Stage Detection

author.name: Hina Shakir, Mohammad Mohatram, Javeed Hussain, Syed Rizwan Ali, Muhammad Irfan Memon

entry.summary: This study proposes Gradient-Loss Recursive Feature Elimination, integrating DNN gradient sensitivity to select the most influential radiomic features from CT scans for lung cancer stage detection. It addresses high-dimensional, small-sample radiomics challenges.

entry.title: Reconstructing Unobservable Temperature Fields via Simulation-Aided Intelligent Sensing

author.name: Monika Stipsitz, H\`elios Sanchis-Alepuz, Jacob Reynvaan, Silvester Sabathiel

entry.summary: This work reconstructs unobservable internal temperature fields from sparse embedded sensors using a neural network trained solely on randomized physics-based simulation data. It demonstrates a proof-of-concept synthetic-to-real thermal monitoring pipeline.

entry.title: Learning Control-Affine Reduced-Order Models via Autoencoders

author.name: Ali Mjalled, Martin M\"onnigmann

entry.summary: This work learns control-affine reduced-order models using autoencoders that jointly transform high-dimensional states and inputs into latent control-affine dynamics, extended to sequence-based history-aware prediction. It enables feedback linearization on the derived models.

entry.title: Computational conceptual history of scientific concepts: From early digital methods to LLMs

author.name: Michael Zichert, Arno Simons

entry.summary: This article situates LLMs within the longer history of computational concept analysis in history, philosophy, and sociology of science, reviewing early digital methods, distributional approaches, and lexical semantic change detection. It examines what LLMs add and what longstanding problems they inherit.

entry.title: DLLG: Dynamic Logit-Level Gating of LLM Experts

author.name: Bingnan Li, Zhaoyang Zhang, Xiaoze Liu, Yantao Shen, Shuli Jiang, Shuo Yang, Wei Xia, Zhuowen Tu, Stefano Soatto

entry.summary: GlossAssist is an interactive interlinear glossing tool built on a retrieval-based CWoMP architecture grounding predictions in a mutable lexicon, designed for field linguists to correct and feed expertise back into model behavior. It targets adoption in low-resource language documentation.

entry.title: Data Efficient Complex Feature Fusion Network For Hyperspectral Image Classification

author.name: Maitreya Shelare, Atharva Satam, Poonam Sonar, Sneha Burnase

entry.summary: DE-CFFN is a data-efficient dual-branch complex-feature-fusion network for hyperspectral image classification, using real-valued and complex-valued (Fourier) streams with factor analysis for dimensionality reduction. It enhances latent feature representation over PCA-based approaches.

entry.title: Selecting haptic guidance models in teleoperation: guidelines from a comparative user study

author.name: Alexis Boulay (AUCTUS), Margot Vulliez (AUCTUS), David Daney (AUCTUS)

entry.summary: This user study compares three classical haptic guidance models (spring-damper, potential field, guiding tube) for teleoperation across six scenarios in a vertical farming task and provides selection guidelines. It finds no universally superior model, with each excelling under different environmental conditions.

entry.title: Early Detection of Alzheimer's Disease Using Explainable Machine Learning on Clinical Biomarkers: A Multi-Class Classification Study Using the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) Dataset

author.name: Afshan Hashmi

entry.summary: Develops an XGBoost classifier with SHAP explanations for three-class Alzheimer's detection (NC/MCI/AD) using eight routine clinical features from the ADNI dataset, with SMOTE and bootstrap confidence intervals. It targets interpretable early detection from accessible assessments.

entry.title: Enhancing MedSAM with a Lightweight Box Predictor for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Amirhossein Movahedisefat, Amirreza Fateh, Mohammad Reza Mohammadi

entry.summary: This paper enhances MedSAM with a lightweight Box Predictor that estimates a bounding box from a single user click, providing richer spatial context than point prompts for medical image segmentation. It improves reliability for irregular or low-contrast structures.

entry.title: DiverAge: Reliable Pluralistic Face Aging with Cross-Age Identity Relation Guidance

author.name: Yueying Zou, Peipei Li, Qianrui Teng, Dianyan Xu, Zekun Li

entry.summary: DiverAge is a face aging framework that provides appearance-level candidate diversity within each age group while maintaining sequence-level ordinal reliability across ordered age groups, using cross-age identity relation guidance. It addresses the one-to-many nature of face aging for biometric and forensic applications.

entry.title: The price of multi-group transductive learning

author.name: Noah Bergam, Samuel Deng, Daniel Hsu

entry.summary: Proves that multi-group learners in the transductive setting can suffer a multiplicative error penalty on some group that grows linearly with the number of groups, up to roughly the square root of the sample size. This contrasts sharply with statistical settings where the penalty is only logarithmic and group-independent.

entry.title: Handwriting Extraction and Analysis of Signature Lists in Swiss Popular Initiatives

author.name: Marco Peer, Thomas Gorges, Mathias Seuret, Vincent Christlein, Andreas Fischer

entry.summary: This paper investigates automated handwriting extraction and writer retrieval for validating Swiss popular-initiative signature lists, combining template-based segmentation, OCR, and AI handwriting analysis. Writer retrieval (50.6% mAP) proved more robust than OCR (29.6% CER) on out-of-vocabulary handwriting.

entry.title: The Biomimetic Architecture of Software 4.0

author.name: Philip Sheldrake, Dirk Scheffler

entry.summary: Proposes Software 4.0, an autopoietic biomimetic architecture intended to replace the static code-assembly execution model that mismatches probabilistic connectionist intelligence. It critiques current LLM-harness approaches as compounding architectural complexity.

entry.title: Metric-Aware Hybrid Forecasting for the CTF4Science Lorenz Challenge

author.name: Cen Lu

entry.summary: Describes a metric-aware hybrid system for the CTF4Science Lorenz challenge, assigning different predictors (synthetic-pretrained denoisers, ODE fitting/shooting, histogram-tail substitution) to different metric families since no single model dominated all metrics. It scored well on the public leaderboard.

entry.title: An Empirical Audit of Input Encoders for Multi-Channel Signal Transformers

author.name: Ossi Lehtinen

entry.summary: This empirical audit compares eight input encoders for embedding multi-channel scalar signals into transformer inputs, on synthetic and ETTh1 benchmarks measured by next-step NLL. The key finding is that many encoders, including the standard per-channel linear projection, perform near-equivalently within a top tier.

entry.title: LimiX-2M: Mitigating Low-Rank Collapse and Attention Bottlenecks in Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Yuanrui Wang, Xingxuan Zhang, Han Yu, Mingchao Ming, Gang Ren, Hao Yuan, Li Mao, Yunjia Zhang, Chun Yuan, Peng Cui

entry.summary: Presents LimiX-2M, a tabular foundation model that mitigates low-rank collapse and attention bottlenecks via RBF-based feature tokenization and a reordered bidirectional block routing computation. It aims to make tabular foundation models more compute-efficient and competitive with tree ensembles.

entry.title: Prediction Under Imperfect Compression: A Theory of Approximate MDL

author.name: Qian Li, Xinyu Mao, Shang-Hua Teng, Guangxu Yang

entry.summary: Develops a theory of approximate Minimum Description Length prediction, characterizing what forms of approximation and regularization preserve the compression and prediction guarantees of exact MDL. It bridges the gap between classical MDL theory and practical approximate optimization.

entry.title: STaR-Quant: State-Time Consistent Post-Training Quantization for Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Xin Yan, Aqiang Wang, Zhenglin Wan, Xingrui Yuand Ivor Tsang

entry.summary: Proposes STaR-Quant, a state-time consistent post-training quantization method for diffusion large language models, addressing state-dependent activation disparity between masked and unmasked tokens and temporal error accumulation across denoising steps. It enables efficient low-bit deployment of DLLMs.

entry.title: Modeling and Interpreting Teamwork Dynamics in Cancer Care Outcome Prediction
