author.name: Yuhua Huang, Hsiao-Ying Lu, Kwan-Liu Ma

entry.summary: This work models and interprets team coordination among healthcare professionals during cancer care delivery to predict patient outcomes, addressing an understudied delivery-phase human factor. It uses interpretable modeling of collaborative practice.

entry.title: Fitting scattered data with optional monotonicity constraints on GPU: LipFit package

author.name: Gleb Beliakov

entry.summary: LipFit is a GPU-friendly package for multivariate scattered data interpolation and approximation that produces optimal Lipschitz-continuous fits with optional monotonicity constraints, without a training phase. It avoids the discontinuities of nearest-neighbor approximation.

entry.title: QPredSGG: Hybrid Quantum Predicate Learning for Long-Tailed Scene Graph Generation

author.name: Prerana Ramkumar, Nouhaila Innan, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: QPredSGG replaces the classical predicate head of a scene graph generation network with a hybrid quantum predicate head to address long-tail predicate imbalance with reduced parameters. It explores quantum components for relational reasoning.

entry.title: An Open-Source Two-Stage Computer Vision Pipeline for Fine-Grained Vehicle Classification using Vision Transformers

author.name: Gandhimathi Padmanaban, Fred Feng

entry.summary: This work presents an open-source two-stage pipeline combining an RT-DETR detector with a fine-tuned Vision Transformer for fine-grained six-category vehicle body-type classification relevant to cyclist injury risk. It fills a gap in deployment-robust automated classification from roadway video.

entry.title: Listening to the Workforce: Measuring Construction Worker Safety Attitudes from Social Media Discourse Using LLMs

author.name: Farouq Sammour, Yuxin Zhang, Zhenyu Zhang

entry.summary: This study builds and validates the Construction Safety Attitude Framework with eight dimensions and an LLM-assisted codebook to measure worker safety attitudes from Reddit discourse at scale. Trained coders reached strong agreement on 250 posts.

entry.title: When Both Layers Learn: Training Dynamics of Representing Linear Models via ReLU Networks

author.name: Berk Tinaz, Changzhi Xie, Mahdi Soltanolkotabi

entry.summary: Analyzes gradient descent dynamics when jointly training both layers of a one-hidden-layer ReLU network to fit a linear target under Gaussian inputs. It characterizes the loss landscape with non-strict saddles and explains why GD reliably escapes bad stationary regions.

entry.title: In-Context Graphical Inference

author.name: Zehua Cheng, Wei Dai, Jiahao Sun

entry.summary: Introduces In-Context Graphical Inference, an autoregressive Graph Transformer that mimics Variable Elimination with Tensor-Train-compressed factors to perform marginal inference on discrete graphical models. It pairs this with a Dirichlet output and conformal prediction for calibration, restoring sequential elimination structure.

entry.title: Learning What Not to Impute: An Uncertainty-Aware Diffusion Framework for Meaningful Missingness

author.name: Lixing Zhang, Yidong Ouyang, Weifu Li, Shixiang Zhu, Guang Cheng, Liyan Xie

entry.summary: Formalizes a selective imputation problem distinguishing meaningfully missing entries from those missing due to observation, proposing Diff-Joint, a diffusion framework that jointly models tabular data and a latent missingness mask. It infers which entries to preserve versus recover.

entry.title: RePercENT: Scaling Disentangled Representation Learning Beyond Two Modalities

author.name: Vasiliki Rizou, Pascal Frossard, Dorina Thanou

entry.summary: Proposes RePercENT, a self-supervised framework for disentangled representation learning that scales beyond the two-modality regime to identify shared and unique factors across many modalities. It uses pairwise disentanglement to overcome the scalability bottleneck of existing multimodal methods.

entry.title: Bayesian Membership Privacy for Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Sinan Y{\i}ld{\i}r{\i}m, Megha Khosla

entry.summary: Introduces Bayesian Membership Privacy for graph neural networks, a sampling-aware formulation that incorporates node-dependent priors and treats graph sampling probabilities as part of the adversary's knowledge. It casts membership inference as a Bayesian hypothesis test, addressing structural correlations overlooked by non-graph privacy analyses.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Data Scale, Model Complexity, and Input Modalities in Visual Generalization

author.name: Luoyidi Zhou

entry.summary: Empirically analyzes how data scale, model complexity, and input modalities influence visual generalization, using controlled experiments such as fitting one-dimensional nonlinear functions with varying sample counts and polynomial degrees. It aims to clarify sources of deep network generalization beyond classical statistical learning theory.

entry.title: Policy Gradient for Continuous-Time Robust Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Tanya Veeravalli, David M. Bossens, Atsushi Nitanda

entry.summary: Derives policy gradient and adversarial gradient algorithms for continuous-time robust Markov decision processes using pathwise and adjoint methods, with double-loop optimizers achieving linear convergence and explicit sample complexity bounds. It extends robust RL guarantees from discrete to continuous time.

entry.title: Provably Reduced Sample Cost in Prior-Guided Hyperparameter Optimization

author.name: Leona Hennig, Jasmin Brandt, Lukas Fehring, Barbara Hammer, Marius Lindauer, Marcel Wever

entry.summary: Provides the first distribution-dependent sample complexity bounds for multi-fidelity hyperparameter optimization with priors, framed through fixed-budget best-arm identification. It quantifies how prior informativeness reduces sampling cost in AutoML.

entry.title: Towards Pretraining Text Encoders for TabPFN

author.name: Mustafa Tajjar, Alexander Pfefferle, Lennart Purucker, Frank Hutter

entry.summary: Proposes pretraining text encoders specifically for TabPFN to handle high-cardinality text features, avoiding the information bottleneck of compressing language-model embeddings via PCA before input. It seeks end-to-end handling of text cells without large text-heavy pretraining data.

entry.title: Graph Cascades: Contagion-Based Mesoscopic Rewiring for Structure-Aware Graph Machine Learning

author.name: Meher Chaitanya, My Le, Luana Ruiz

entry.summary: Introduces Graph Cascades, a contagion-based mesoscopic rewiring strategy that promotes node pairs supported by repeated multi-hop reinforcement to direct neighbors in linear time, capturing intermediate-scale structure for GNNs and Graph Transformers. It provides theoretical conditions for when reinforcement-based rewiring improves label alignment.

entry.title: Deep Embedded Multiplicative DMD for Algebra-Preserving Koopman Learning

author.name: Kelan Gray, Finlay Brown, Nicolas Boull\'e, Matthew J. Colbrook

entry.summary: Introduces DeepMDMD, which learns a latent space and partition while enforcing the Koopman product rule as an exact algebraic constraint, combining flexible deep coordinates with structure-preserving operator identities. Training alternates between exact multiplicative operator updates and differentiable latent clustering.

entry.title: ACAT: A Collaborative Platform for Efficient Aspect-Based Sentiment Dataset Annotation

author.name: Ana-Maria Luisa Mocanu, Ciprian-Octavian Truica, Elena-Simona Apostol

entry.summary: ACAT is a web-based collaborative annotation platform natively supporting four aspect-based sentiment analysis workflows with automated multi-annotator consolidation, relational reconstruction, and reliability metrics. It reduces the manual ETL burden of ABSA dataset creation.

entry.title: When Do Fewer Coordinates Suffice in DP-SGD?

author.name: Huiqi Zhang, Fang Xie

entry.summary: Introduces TP-TopK, a two-phase coordinate-sparse DP-SGD method where a private warm-up identifies a coordinate support to guide main training, reducing noise scaling from the ambient dimension to the active dimension. It gives a criterion for when coordinate restriction benefits private training.

entry.title: Learning symplectic model reduction based on a approximation theorem of symplectic embeddings

author.name: Liyi Feng, Yifa Tang, Yulin Xie, Ruili Zhang, Aiqing Zhu

entry.summary: Establishes a universal approximation theorem for symplectic embeddings and uses it to build symplecticity-preserving autoencoders where the decoder is a symplectic embedding, ensuring reduced models support a valid Hamiltonian flow. This improves long-time stability of model reduction for high-dimensional Hamiltonian systems.

entry.title: Graph Set Transformer

author.name: Jose E. Escrig Molina, Baoquan Chen, Daniel Probst

entry.summary: Introduces the Graph Set Transformer, an architecture for learning on sets of graphs that interleaves node-level feature propagation and cross-graph contextual modeling at every layer, fusing them via gating. It avoids the bottleneck of relying on pre-encoded graph embeddings from a separate GNN.

entry.title: AI from concrete to abstract: demystifying artificial intelligence to the general public

author.name: Rubens Lacerda Queiroz, F\'abio Ferrentini Sampaio, Cabral Lima, Priscila Machado Vieira Lima

entry.summary: Presents AIcon2abs, a methodology using visual programming and WiSARD weightless neural networks to teach general audiences, including children, how machine learning works through hands-on demystification. It targets broad AI literacy.

entry.title: How do machines learn? Evaluating the AIcon2abs method

author.name: Rubens Lacerda Queiroz, Cabral Lima, Fabio Ferrentini Sampaio, Priscila Machado Vieira Lima

entry.summary: Evaluates the effectiveness of the AIcon2abs AI-literacy method using the WiSARD weightless neural network across diverse age groups including K-12 students. It demonstrates accessible, internet-free hands-on ML education.

entry.title: Anycast Performance in Context

author.name: Eric Liang

entry.summary: Compares IP anycast latency across two settings, root DNS where recursive caching amortizes delay and CDNs where each round trip directly affects user-visible latency, finding root DNS tolerates substantial path inflation while CDN anycast needs active peering engineering. It is a networking systems synthesis.

entry.title: MeshTok: Efficient Multi-Scale Tokenization for Scalable PDE Transformers

author.name: Yanshun Zhao, Xiaoyu Peng, Jiamin Jiang, Congcong Zhu, Jingrun Chen

entry.summary: Proposes MeshTok, an adaptive-mesh-refinement-inspired tokenization scheme for PDE Transformers that allocates more tokens to regions with sharp gradients or multiscale features rather than uniform patches. It aims to make PDE surrogate modeling more compute-efficient and scalable.

entry.title: HalfNet: Randomized Neural Networks with Learned Subspace Geometry

author.name: Ethem Alpaydin

entry.summary: Proposes HalfNet, networks with random weights drawn from a learned low-rank covariance rather than the standard isotropic Gaussian, matching fully trained MLPs with far fewer parameters on MNIST and CIFAR-10. Spectral analysis suggests much predictive power lies in weight-space geometry rather than precise weights.

entry.title: Rethinking Incompleteness: Formalizing Protocol Divergence and Train-Once Learning for Robust IMVC

author.name: Haolu Liu, Xiyue Wang, Xuanting Xie, Liangjian Wen, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: Argues that missing rate alone fails to characterize data incompleteness in incomplete multi-view clustering, formalizing incompleteness divergence where identical missing rates can differ 50x in fully observed samples. It proves reconstruction-based objectives become ill-posed below a critical fraction of complete samples and proposes a train-once approach.

entry.title: RIDE: An Open Dataset and Benchmark for Train Delay Prediction

author.name: Cl\'ement Elliker, Mathis Le Bail, Cl\'ement Mantoux, Jesse Read, Sonia Vanier

entry.summary: Introduces RIDE, an open nationwide-scale benchmark for train delay prediction over the Belgian railway network covering 94.5M train events and weather data, with standardized prediction targets and evaluation protocols. It addresses the lack of common datasets hindering progress in the field.

entry.title: Generating Financial Time Series by Matching Random Convolutional Features

author.name: Konrad J. Mueller, Nikita Zozoulenko, Ben Wood, Thomas Cass, Lukas Gonon

entry.summary: Generates realistic financial time series by training generators to match random convolutional features of real and synthetic data, avoiding overfitting from limited single-path historical data and the discriminator memorization of adversarial training. It improves on path-signature feature approaches that miss relevant properties.

entry.title: Revisiting Privacy Amplification by Subsampling in Selective Release DPSGD

author.name: Xiaobo Huang, Fang Xie

entry.summary: Re-examines privacy amplification by subsampling in the DPSUR selective-release algorithm, identifying that prior accounting overlooked sampling-probability variation introduced by selective release. It proposes a corrected privacy analysis to restore rigorous guarantees.

entry.title: Loss-Conditional PINNs for Parametric PDE Families

author.name: Anna Lazareva, Alexander Tarakanov

entry.summary: Introduces LC-PINN, which adapts loss-conditional training so a single PINN explores the entire space of loss-weight combinations rather than tuning one weight vector. This addresses the brittleness of PINNs to loss-weight choices for parametric PDE families.

entry.title: Episodic Memory Temporal Consistency for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zicheng Zhao, Yu Lan, Chengzhengxu Li, Zhaohan Zhang, Xiaoming Liu

entry.summary: Proposes EMTC for cooperative multi-agent RL, combining a temporally consistent semantic embedder (contrastive learning plus time-conditioned reconstruction) with constrained episodic memory to avoid representation collapse and local optima under reward sparsity. It improves memory retrieval and incentive distribution.

entry.title: New Benchmarking Shows Limited Generalization Power of TCR Antigenic Epitope Prediction Models

author.name: Yiming Liao, Yiheng Li, Ning Jiang, Bo Li, Keke Chen

entry.summary: Introduces two rigorously defined unseen benchmark dataset classes for evaluating TCR antigen specificity prediction models, showing existing models have limited generalization. It provides a framework for unbiased model assessment and future algorithm development.

entry.title: BBOmix: A Tabular Benchmark for Hyperparameter Optimization of Unsupervised Biological Representation Learning

author.name: Luca Thale-Bombien, Jan Ewald, Ralf K\"onig, Aaron Klein

entry.summary: Introduces BBOmix, the first open-source tabular benchmark for hyperparameter optimization of unsupervised biological representation learning with autoencoders, where reconstruction loss may poorly proxy downstream utility. It democratizes large-scale unsupervised HPO research in omics.

entry.title: SpliceBind: Isoform-Aware Prediction of Binding Pocket Druggability

author.name: Bryan Cheng, Austin Jin, Joshua Chang

entry.summary: Introduces SpliceBind, a graph neural network for isoform-aware druggability prediction that compares binding pockets across protein isoforms, improving accuracy over P2Rank and characterizing when structural methods succeed or must fail. It addresses splice-mediated drug resistance affecting many kinase-inhibitor patients.

entry.title: Structure-Aware Prediction of PROTAC-Mediated Protein Degradability via Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Bryan Cheng, Austin Jin

entry.summary: Presents DegradoMap, a graph neural network predicting PROTAC-mediated protein degradability from protein structure and E3 ligase identity alone, the minimal information available before synthesis. It encodes biophysical priors via lysine-weighted pooling and models protein-E3 compatibility with cross-attention.

entry.title: SC-TauPath: A Structural Connectivity Attribution Framework for Mapping Tau Propagation Pathways in Alzheimer's Disease

author.name: Jing Zhang, Norman Scheel, Minheng Chen, Tong Chen, Yanjun Lyu, David C. Zhu, Rong Zhang, Dajiang Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces SC-TauPath, a structural-connectivity attribution framework mapping tau propagation pathways in Alzheimer's disease by combining a network-diffusion-augmented MLP with gradient-times-input attribution. It produces multi-scale neurobiologically interpretable pathway maps from neuroimaging.

entry.title: Literature-Guided Minimax Optimization of Virtual Epilepsy Neurostimulation

author.name: Cathy Liu

entry.summary: Presents a literature-guided minimax optimization pipeline coupling PubMed-scale hypothesis extraction, virtual brain epilepsy simulations, and LLM-guided black-box optimization to design neurostimulation protocols robust to worst-case patients. It moves beyond average-case optimization for safer patient-specific treatment.

entry.title: Toward Multi-Domain and Long-Tailed Quantization via Feature Alignment and Scaling

author.name: Chin-Yuan Yeh, Ting-An Chen, De-Nian Yang, Ming-Syan Chen

entry.summary: Presents EmaQ, a quantization method for multi-domain and long-tailed settings that aligns domain distributions via CDF projection and uses sensitivity-aware weight aggregation, extended with class-conditioned variance scaling for long-tailed data. It targets robust low-bit inference under domain shift and class imbalance.

entry.title: FLAGG: Flexible Autoregressive Graph Generation

author.name: Samuel Cognolato, Alessandro Sperduti, Luciano Serafini

entry.summary: Proposes FLAGG, a flexible framework that sequentially generates portions of graphs using one-shot models, combining the strengths of one-shot and autoregressive graph generation. It aims to handle graphs of varying size and topology where neither extreme alone works well.

entry.title: Identifying Gems from Roman RAPIDly

author.name: Karan Gandhi, Ashish A. Mahabal, Jacob E. Jencson, Russ R. Laher, Ben Rusholme, Lin Yan, Ryan M. Lau, Schuyler D. Van Dyk, Mansi M. Kasliwal

entry.summary: Presents RuBR, a machine learning model and methodology for distinguishing genuine transients from spurious detections in the RAPID pipeline for the upcoming Roman Space Telescope, developed without real Roman data. It prepares automated alert generation for the telescope's launch.

entry.title: Neural Galerkin Normalizing Flows for Bayesian Inference of Diffusions with Inaccessible Boundaries

author.name: Riccardo Saporiti, Fabio Nobile

entry.summary: Develops a normalizing-flow architecture trained in a Neural Galerkin framework to learn diffusion transition densities by solving the associated Fokker-Planck equation, enabling Bayesian inference of diffusion parameters when likelihoods are analytically intractable. It targets diffusions with inaccessible boundaries.

entry.title: DPDL: Towards Differential Privacy Preservation in Decentralized Stochastic Learning on Non-IID Data

author.name: Yunsheng Yuan, Xue Xiao, Lina Wang, Feng Li

entry.summary: Proposes DPDL, a differentially private decentralized stochastic learning algorithm designed for non-IID data across collaborating agents without a central server. It addresses both privacy leakage from gradient exchange and the challenge of heterogeneous data distributions.

entry.title: SPLIT-PINN: Separable Probability Learning Technique via Physics-Informed Neural Networks for High-Dimensional Probabilistic Modeling

author.name: Pouria Behnoudfar, Deekshith Naidu Ponnana, Noah J. Schmelzer, Janith Wanni, George T. Gray III, Dan J. Thoma, Curt A. Bronkhorst, Nan Chen, Wenxiao Pan

entry.summary: Presents SPLIT-PINN, a separable physics-informed neural network for high-dimensional probabilistic modeling of material spatial heterogeneity, inferring an unknown drift in a Liouville-equation transport model. It enables stable interpretable inference in transport-dominated settings for polycrystalline metals.

entry.title: Finite-Iteration Local Dynamics and Warm Starts for Alternating Power Iteration in Spiked Tensor PCA

author.name: Yanjin Xiang, Zhihua Zhang

entry.summary: Provides a finite-iteration local convergence theory for simultaneous alternating power iteration on asymmetric rank-one spiked tensor models, decomposing error into a decaying transient and an intrinsic noise floor. It separates the warm-start mechanism from any specific spectral initialization.

entry.title: A French Corpus Annotated for Multiword Expressions with Adverbial Function

author.name: Eric Laporte, Takuya Nakamura, Stavroula Voyatzi

entry.summary: This paper presents a French corpus annotated for multiword expressions with adverbial function, intended for information retrieval, extraction, and syntactic parsing research. The annotated resource is released under an open license.

entry.title: On Out-of-sample Embedding in UMAP

author.name: Mohammad Tariqul Islam, Jason W. Fleischer

entry.summary: Addresses UMAP's repulsion effect that places out-of-sample points on cluster peripheries by optimizing pairwise interactions within the original k-nearest-neighbor graph. It improves placement of new points into the interiors of their correct clusters.

entry.title: Mean-based algorithms: A lower bound and regret

author.name: Julius Durmann, Amelie Kleber

entry.summary: Studies mean-based online learning algorithms under unknown time horizons and bandit feedback, providing the first lower bound on the algorithm-defining sequence and proposing two new algorithms. It clarifies fundamental limits on how fast these algorithms can learn.

entry.title: CADET: A Modular Platform for Evaluating Distributed Cooperative Autonomy in Connected Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Pragya Sharma, Brian Wang, Mani Srivastava

entry.summary: Presents CADET, a modular platform for evaluating distributed cooperative autonomy in connected autonomous vehicles, accounting for systems-level challenges like network latency, compute heterogeneity, and multi-tenant contention beyond monolithic onboard designs. It supports cooperative perception and control with V2X connectivity.

entry.title: Graph-Guided Universum Learning in Generalized Eigenvalue Proximal SVMs for Alzheimer's Disease Classification

author.name: Yogesh Kumar, Vrushank Ahire, Mudasir Ganaie

entry.summary: This work proposes graph-guided Universum learning variants of GEPSVM for Alzheimer's classification, using MCI subjects as Universum data and incorporating geometric relationships among them via a graph. It targets AD-versus-normal classification from structural MRI.

entry.title: Latent Anchor-Driven Test Generation for Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Bin Duan, Matthew B. Dwyer, Guowei Yang

entry.summary: Proposes Latte, a black-box DNN testing framework that generates semantically proximate, diverse, fault-revealing test cases by anchoring exploration in the latent space. It aims to balance controllability, failure diversity, and semantic drift better than prior methods.

entry.title: Testing Neural Networks via Bayesian-Guided Exploration of Decision Landscapes

author.name: Bin Duan, Meiru Che, Guowei Yang

entry.summary: Presents BayesWarp, a neural network testing framework that mutates decision-critical input regions identified via saliency and uses uncertainty-aware Bayesian optimization to find diverse failures while preserving the data distribution. It targets efficient discovery of reliability issues in safety-critical models.

entry.title: Folded Transport MCMC: Certifiable Quotient Posterior Computation for Symmetric Bayesian Models

author.name: Jun Hu

entry.summary: Introduces Folded Transport MCMC, a method for Bayesian inference on symmetric models by sampling directly on the quotient posterior using a symmetrized normalizing flow, avoiding redundant multimodality from label permutations. It extends a certification framework to provide convergence guarantees on the quotient metric.

author.name: Xinyue Huang, Xiaochun Cao, Wenyuan Yang

author.name: Xiancheng Wang, Zhibo Zhang, Ran Li, Rui Wang, Minghang Zhao, Shisheng Zhong, Lin Wang

entry.title: Adaptive Patching Is Harder Than It Looks For Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Federico Zucchi, Yi Xie, Chao Zhang, Keyuan Luo, Thomas Lampert, Ziyue Li

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.04074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adaptive patching is a recent and compelling proposal for time-series Transformers: allocate finer patches where the sequence looks locally informati...

author.name: Pritam Dash, Tongyu Ge, Aditi Jain, Tanmay Shah, Zhiwei Shang

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.04329v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Memory is a core component of AI agents, enabling them to accumulate knowledge across interactions and improve performance. However, persistent memor...

entry.title: Smart Picks in the Dark: Towards Efficient RLVR for Reasoning via Tracing Metacognitive Pivots

author.name: Guangcheng Zhu, Shenzhi Yang, Haobo Wang, Xing Zheng, Yingfan MA, Xuening Feng, Zhongqi Chen, Bowen Song, Weiqiang Wang, Gang Chen

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.04503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has greatly advanced large reasoning models (LRMs), but it requires timely training on a huge f...

entry.title: Automatic Generation of Titles for Research Papers Using Language Models

author.name: Tohida Rehman, Debarshi Kumar Sanyal, Samiran Chattopadhyay

entry.summary: This work generates research paper titles from abstracts using open-weight pre-trained and large language models, introducing a new SpringerSSAT dataset and evaluating with metrics like ROUGE, BERTScore, and SciBERTScore. It compares fine-tuned models against zero-shot GPT-3.5-turbo.

entry.title: Multi-Column RBF Neural Network Using Adaptive and Non-Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization

author.name: Ammar Hoori, Yuichi Motai

entry.summary: This work proposes a multi-column RBF neural network trained with adaptive and non-adaptive particle swarm optimization, comparing PSO/APSO global search against gradient-based error-correction training. It targets improved accuracy and robustness to local minima.

entry.title: Stationarity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Shiqiao Zhou, Holger Sch\"oner, Zipeng Wu, Edouard Fouch\'e, IAG Wilson, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.04135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time series forecasting relies on historical patterns, but real-world series often exhibit non-stationarity and regime shifts that challenge fully para...

entry.title: Shortcomings and capacities of real-constrained neural networks in complex spaces

author.name: Andrew Gracyk

entry.summary: Computes the asymptotic ratio of storage capacities between real-constrained and complex pre-activations within a complex hypothesis class using Gardner volume and the Harish-Chandra-Itzykson-Zuber formula. It applies tools from random matrix theory to neural network capacity.

entry.title: VentAgent: When LLMs Learn to Breathe -- Multi-Objective Arbitration for ARDS Ventilation

author.name: Teqi Hao, Yuxuan Fu, Xiaoyu Tan, Shaojie Shi, Bohao Lv, Yinghui Xu, Xihe Qiu

author.name: Mirza Muhammad Mobeen

entry.summary: This paper presents a five-stage real-time ALPR pipeline using YOLOv8 detection, SORT tracking, and temporal data interpolation to handle illumination, speed, and occlusion challenges. It aims to improve OCR rates and tracking continuity in dynamic traffic.

entry.title: Federated Learning for Multi-Center Sepsis Early Prediction with Privacy-Preserving

author.name: Xixi Tian, Di Wu, Xiang Liu, Yiziting Zhu, Yujie Li, Xin Shu, Bin Yi

entry.summary: Empirically evaluates federated learning for privacy-preserving multi-center sepsis prediction using a small real clinical dataset of 648 samples. It assesses practical performance, robustness, and privacy tradeoffs across institutions.

entry.title: Dynamic Multi-Pair Trading Strategy in Cryptocurrency Markets with Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Damian Lebied\'z, Robert \'Slepaczuk

entry.summary: Applies deep reinforcement learning (PPO with an LSTM layer) as an execution overlay for cryptocurrency pair trading, using a hierarchical filter-then-rank pair selection and a fixed-risk adaptive-mean execution model. It investigates whether DRL improves robustness in high-volatility markets.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Network Modeling of Biodegradable Contaminant Transport through GCL/SL Composite Liners

author.name: Dong Li, Yapeng Cao, Haiping Zhao, Shutong Han

entry.summary: Develops a two-domain physics-informed neural network for biodegradable contaminant transport through composite landfill liners, comparing soft and hard constraint enforcement against analytical and finite-element references. The hard-constrained variant better captures early transient behavior.

entry.title: Tod Machover receives George Peabody Medal for contributions to music and technology

author.name: Media Lab

entry.title: Research Summary: June 03, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
NVIDIA dominates with two major world-model contributions: Cosmos 3 introduces an omnimodal architecture unifying multiple modalities for physical AI, while OmniDreams demonstrates real-time closed-loop AV simulation built on the Cosmos diffusion backbone.

  • LEAP from Google DeepMind achieves SOTA on formal theorem proving in Lean via agentic decomposition, introducing an IMO-level benchmark
  • WUSH derives closed-form transforms for joint weight-activation LLM quantization, advancing practical deployment efficiency
  • Reasoning Primitive Induction distills reusable reasoning moves from agent traces, surprisingly outperforming the source agent across tasks
  • TRAP exposes a novel attack surface on Vision-Language-Action robotic models by hijacking Chain-of-Thought reasoning via adversarial patches

Safety and alignment research features prominently: a principled cybersecurity refusal framework (Kolter et al.) addresses agent deployment boundaries, while a position paper argues solipsistic superintelligence is unlikely to be cooperative. Interpretability advances include a graph-based reasoning structure benchmark and a causal geometric decomposition of how prompting steers internal LLM representations.
entry.content:
NVIDIA dominates with two major world-model contributions: Cosmos 3 introduces an omnimodal architecture unifying multiple modalities for physical AI, while OmniDreams demonstrates real-time closed-loop AV simulation built on the Cosmos diffusion backbone.

  • LEAP from Google DeepMind achieves SOTA on formal theorem proving in Lean via agentic decomposition, introducing an IMO-level benchmark
  • WUSH derives closed-form transforms for joint weight-activation LLM quantization, advancing practical deployment efficiency
  • Reasoning Primitive Induction distills reusable reasoning moves from agent traces, surprisingly outperforming the source agent across tasks
  • TRAP exposes a novel attack surface on Vision-Language-Action robotic models by hijacking Chain-of-Thought reasoning via adversarial patches

Safety and alignment research features prominently: a principled cybersecurity refusal framework (Kolter et al.) addresses agent deployment boundaries, while a position paper argues solipsistic superintelligence is unlikely to be cooperative. Interpretability advances include a graph-based reasoning structure benchmark and a causal geometric decomposition of how prompting steers internal LLM representations.

It claims state-of-the-art across understanding and generation tasks for Physical AI.

entry.title: NVIDIA OmniDreams: Real-Time Generative World Model for Closed-Loop Autonomous Vehicle Simulation

author.name: NVIDIA, :, Aarti Basant, Amlan Kar, Despoina Paschalidou, Fangyin Wei, Francesco Ferroni, Guillermo Garcia Cobo, Haithem Turki, Huan Ling, Jaewoo Seo, James Lucas, Jay Zhangjie Wu, Jialiang Wang, Jonathan Lorraine, Jun Gao, Kai He, Katarina Tothova, Kevin Xie, Micha{\l} Tyszkiewicz, Qi Wu, Riccardo de Lutio, Ruilong Li, Sanja Fidler, Seung Wook Kim, Tianchang Shen, Tianshi Cao, Tobias Pfaff, William Lew, Xindi Wu, Xuanchi Ren, Yifan Lu, Yuxuan Zhang, Zan Gojcic, Zian Wang

entry.summary: NVIDIA's OmniDreams is a foundation generative world model, post-trained from the Cosmos diffusion model, for real-time closed-loop autonomous vehicle simulation that autoregressively generates action-conditioned sensor observations. Addresses long-tail scenario evaluation beyond reconstruction-based simulators.

entry.title: LEAP: Supercharging LLMs for Formal Mathematics with Agentic Frameworks

author.name: Po-Nien Kung, Linfeng Song, Dawsen Hwang, Jinsung Yoon, Chun-Liang Li, Simone Severini, Mirek Ol\v{s}\'ak, Edward Lockhart, Quoc V Le, Burak Gokturk, Thang Luong, Tomas Pfister, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: LEAP is an agentic framework enabling general-purpose foundation models to achieve state-of-the-art automated formal theorem proving in Lean by decomposing problems and iterating with the Lean compiler. It introduces Lean-IMO-Bench for rigorous evaluation.

entry.title: WUSH: Near-Optimal Adaptive Transforms for LLM Quantization

author.name: Jiale Chen, Vage Egiazarian, Roberto L. Castro, Torsten Hoefler, Dan Alistarh

entry.summary: Derives closed-form near-optimal linear blockwise transforms for joint weight-activation LLM quantization, called WUSH, combining a Hadamard backbone with a data-dependent second-moment component. It provides provable near-optimality for both integer and floating-point quantizers.

entry.title: A New Framework for Cybersecurity Refusals in AI Agents

author.name: Eliot Krzysztof Jones, Mateusz Dziemian, Matt Fredrikson, J Zico Kolter

entry.summary: This paper presents the first framework for establishing refusal boundaries for AI agents in offensive cybersecurity contexts, defining principled refusal criteria, task categories warranting refusal, and an evaluation methodology under benign and adversarial conditions. It complements proficiency-focused cyber benchmarks with a safety-refusal dimension.

entry.title: Inducing Reasoning Primitives from Agent Traces

author.name: Zhihan Lei, Jiarui Yan, Joshua Momo, William W. Cohen

entry.summary: Reasoning Primitive Induction mines successful ReAct agent traces, clusters recurrent reasoning moves, and converts them into a library of reusable typed pseudo-tools. The induced libraries notably outperform the agents that generated their traces.

entry.title: Solipsistic Superintelligence is Unlikely to be Cooperative

author.name: Rakshit S Trivedi, Natasha Jaques, Logan Cross, Alexander Sasha Vezhnevets, Joel Z Leibo

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that superintelligence developed via solipsistic unilateral optimization is unlikely to be cooperative, because deploying AI induces endogenous non-stationarity and a self-undermining train-test-deploy gap. It advocates for AI designed to participate in cooperative equilibrium selection.

entry.title: Reasoning Structure of Large Language Models

author.name: Fr\'ed\'eric Berdoz, Luca A. Lanzend\"orfer, Fabian Farestam, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark of logic puzzles plus a pipeline that converts reasoning traces into verifiable graphs of claims and dependencies, allowing reasoning to be measured structurally rather than only by accuracy or token count. It defines a reasoning efficiency metric capturing how concentrated a model's logical flow is, revealing behaviors hidden by standard metrics.

entry.title: Economy of Minds: Emerging Multi-Agent Intelligence with Economic Interactions

author.name: Zhenting Qi, Huangyuan Su, Ao Qu, Chenyu Wang, Yu Yao, Han Zheng, Kushal Chattopadhyay, Guowei Xu, Zihan Wang, Weirui Ye, Vijay Janapa Reddi, Ju Li, Paul Pu Liang, Himabindu Lakkaraju, Sham Kakade, Yilun Du

entry.summary: Economy of Minds studies how a population of LLM agents can self-organize into stronger collective intelligence through economic interactions—auctions for the right to act, payments, and wealth accumulation—inspired by Hayekian decentralized coordination. Economic signals induce decentralized credit assignment and evolutionary selection without central control.

entry.title: Backdoor Unlearning Generalization: A Path Toward the Removal of Unknown Triggers in LLMs

author.name: Lisa Bouger, Th\'eo Lasnier, Philippe Looubet Moundi, Yannick Teglia, Djam\'e Seddah

entry.summary: Shows that backdoor neutralization via unlearning generalizes, where training a model to ignore one trigger can also suppress other never-targeted backdoors across three model families. This offers a path to removing unknown backdoors without knowing triggers.

entry.title: Decomposing how prompting steers behavior

author.name: Fan L. Cheng, Nikolaus Kriegeskorte

entry.summary: Introduces a nested geometric decomposition framework analyzing how prompting reshapes internal representations of LLMs and VLMs, using increasingly expressive stimulus-invariant alignment maps and causal layer interventions. It seeks to explain mechanistically how instructions steer behavior.

entry.title: TRAP: Hijacking VLA CoT-Reasoning via Adversarial Patches

author.name: Zhengxian Huang, Wenjun Zhu, Haoxuan Qiu, Xiaoyu Ji, Wenyuan Xu

entry.summary: TRAP demonstrates the first targeted behavior-hijacking attack on Vision-Language-Action robotic models by exploiting their Chain-of-Thought reasoning via adversarial patches, e.g., causing a robot to deliver a knife instead of an apple. It shows CoT strongly governs action even when misaligned with instructions.

entry.title: What Benchmarks Don't Measure: The Case for Evaluating Abstention Competence in Autonomous Agents

author.name: Victor Ojewale, Suresh Venkatasubramanian

entry.summary: Argues that autonomous agent benchmarks ignore abstention competence, the ability to know when not to proceed, and identifies compliance bias arising from human-feedback reward hacking. It calls for evaluating when agents should pause rather than act.

entry.title: Entropy Is Not Enough: Unlocking Effective Reinforcement Learning for Visual Reasoning via Vision-Anchored Token Selection

author.name: Senjie Jin, Peixin Wang, Boyang Liu, Xiaoran Fan, Shuo Li, Zhiheng Xi, Jiazheng Zhang, Yuhao Zhou, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: The paper shows that token-level entropy, useful for credit assignment in text-only RL, collapses in visual reasoning because vision-sensitive tokens naturally have low entropy. It proposes VEPO, a vision-anchored token selection method that better interleaves perceptual grounding with semantic reasoning.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Molecular Design with Calibrated Deference

author.name: Newman Cheng, Gordon Broadbent IV, Jason Dong, Syed Mohammed Ali Hussaini, Farman Ullah, Morris Sharp, Gabrielle Barnes, Nanlin Guo, Deyu Zou, Karin Strauss, William Chappell, David G. Kwabi, Bichlien H. Nguyen, Jake A. Smith

entry.summary: CLIO is an agent for closed-loop molecular design that couples a belief-state graph with a recursive plan-then-act loop, introducing calibrated deference—recognizing when tools or assumptions fail and adapting strategy. It was tested in a human-AI campaign to design redox flow battery components.

entry.title: Are we really tilting? The mechanics of reward guidance in flow and diffusion models

author.name: Sanjit Dandapanthula, Nicholas M. Boffi

entry.summary: This work analyzes the mechanics of reward guidance in flow and diffusion models, showing that reward hacking arises from finite-particle plug-in estimation of the Doob h-function even in simple Gaussian settings, rather than from neural reward complexity. It clarifies the fundamental origins of over-optimization in reward-guided generation.

entry.title: Learning to Solve, Forgetting to Retain: Correct-Set Turnover in RLVR

author.name: Chuanyu Qin, Chenxu Yang, Qingyi Si, Naibin Gu, Peng Fu, Zheng Lin

entry.summary: Identifies correct-set turnover in RLVR training, where previously solved problems become unsolvable as training proceeds, hiding behind headline accuracy gains. Establishes a repair-window principle (cost of fixing regressions grows with delay) and proposes a method to exploit the low-cost window.

entry.title: Neuron Populations Exhibit Divergent Selectivity with Scale

author.name: Amil Dravid, Yasaman Bahri, Alexei A. Efros, Yossi Gandelsman

entry.summary: Studies whether neuron populations evolve predictably with model scale, finding that Rosetta Neurons (neurons with similar activations across independently trained models) follow a sublinear power law, growing in number but shrinking as a fraction of total neurons. Observes a Neuron Polarization Effect where they become more selective and monosemantic with scale.

entry.title: Coherence Maximization Improves Pluralistic Alignment

author.name: Taslim Mahbub, Yiding Pei, Shi Feng

entry.summary: Uses Internal Coherence Maximization to generate persona-specific in-context examples for pluralistic alignment without human supervision, matching gold-label performance. It finds that example coherence improves steering beyond mere label accuracy.

entry.title: Large Language Models Are Overconfident in Their Own Responses

author.name: Mario Sanz-Guerrero, Manuel Mager, Katharina von der Wense

entry.summary: Investigates miscalibration in chat-tuned LLMs, decoupling effects of post-training from the chat template, and finds an ownership bias where models trust their own answers more than identical user-provided ones. Tested across six open-weight models and three benchmarks.

entry.title: EvoTrainer: Co-Evolving LLM Policies and Training Harnesses for Autonomous Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Guhong Chen, Yingcheng Shi, Yongbin Li, Binhua Li, Xander Xu, Hu Wei, Shiwen Ni, Min Yang, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: EvoTrainer co-evolves LLM policies and their training harnesses through empirical feedback, diagnosing rollout failures, revising diagnostics, backtesting interventions, and accumulating reusable skills. It matches or exceeds human-engineered RL references on math, code, and software engineering.

entry.title: What Makes Interaction Trajectories Effective for Training Terminal Agents?

author.name: Sidi Yang, Chaofan Tao, Jierun Chen, Tiezheng Yu, Ruoyu Wang, Yuxin Jiang, Yiming Du, Wendong Xu, Jing Xiong, Taiqiang Wu, Lifeng Shang, Xiaohui Li, Ngai Wong, Haoli Bai

entry.summary: Investigates what makes interaction trajectories effective for training terminal/code agents, finding that a teacher agent's standalone performance does not dictate teaching efficacy. Trajectories from a lower-scoring agent (DeepSeek-V3.2) produced better-generalizing students than higher-scoring Claude Opus 4.6, attributed to environment-grounded supervision.

entry.title: Imaginative Perception Tokens Enhance Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Language Models

author.name: Mahtab Bigverdi, Lindsey Li, Weikai Huang, Yiming Liu, Jaemin Cho, Jieyu Zhang, Tuhin Kundu, Chris Dangjoo Kim, Zelun Luo, Linda Shapiro, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: Imaginative Perception Tokens (IPT) are intermediate representations that externalize what a VLM would perceive from unseen viewpoints, helping with spatial reasoning under occlusion or perspective shifts. The work introduces three tasks (perspective taking, path tracing, multiview counting) with datasets.

entry.title: The Ringelmann Effect in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Scaling Law for Effective Team Size

author.name: Bla\v{z} Bertalani\v{c}, Carolina Fortuna

entry.summary: This work derives a two-parameter scaling law for multi-agent LLM systems analogous to the Ringelmann effect, classifying configurations into hard-ceiling, sublinear, or linear regimes for effective team size. It shows peer count and debate rounds enter dynamics only through their product across 44 experimental cells.

entry.title: Linear Probes Detect Task Format, Not Reasoning Mode in Language Model Hidden States

author.name: Subramanyam Sahoo, Vinija Jain, Aman Chadha, Divya Chaudhary

entry.summary: This paper tests the common claim that linear probes detect distinct reasoning representations in LLM hidden states, achieving 100% probe accuracy on deductive, inductive, and abductive benchmarks. However, after residualizing format confounds like source identity and response length, accuracy drops to chance—indicating probes detect task format, not reasoning mode.

entry.title: ASymPO: Asymmetric-Scale Policy Optimization for Asynchronous LLM Post-Training Without Behavior Information

author.name: Zehua Liu, Yuxuan Yao, Xiaojin Fu, Tao Zhong, Mingxuan Yuan

entry.summary: ASymPO stabilizes asynchronous LLM RL post-training using only current-policy probabilities, avoiding the need for token-aligned behavior log-probabilities. Identifies a scale-imbalance failure mode from stale responses and corrects it with asymmetric scaling.

entry.title: GFFMERGE: Efficient Merging of Graph Neural Force Fields and Beyond

author.name: Parth Verma, Parv P. Singh, Vipul Garg, Ishita Thakre, N. M. Anoop Krishnan, Sayan Ranu

entry.summary: GFFMERGE is the first principled closed-form model merging framework for graph neural force fields, formulating merging as a convex embedding-alignment problem with analytical solution. Shows existing vision/language merging methods catastrophically fail on force-field regression.

entry.title: Neural Networks Provably Learn Spectral Representations for Group Composition

author.name: Jianliang He, Leda Wang, Fengzhuo Zhang, Siyu Chen, Zhuoran Yang

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis showing two-layer networks trained on group composition tasks provably learn spectral (Fourier/representation-theoretic) features, with each neuron converging to a single irreducible representation. Frames training dynamics as Riemannian gradient ascent on a representation-theoretic energy functional.

entry.title: Thinking Past the Answer: Evaluating Harmful Overthinking in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Simone Caldarella, Davide Talon, Rahaf Aljundi, Elisa Ricci, Massimiliano Mancini

entry.summary: This work studies harmful overthinking in large reasoning models by introducing a prefix-level trajectory evaluation protocol that defines the minimum reasoning budget needed for correctness. It examines whether reasoning after reaching the correct answer refines or degrades solutions.

entry.title: Gender-Dependent Diagnostic Substitution in LLM Medical Triage: Same Symptoms, Unequal Urgency

author.name: Qi Han Wong

entry.summary: Investigates gender-dependent diagnostic substitution in LLM medical triage, finding young women receive significantly lower emergency referral rates than age-matched men for identical neurological symptoms. It tests three frontier model families across demographic conditions. (Analyzes existing models like Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.4-mini, not release news.)

entry.title: Hedge-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks Pertaining to Financial Reasoning

author.name: Eric Cho, Shawn Huang, Alice Lu, Andy Lyu

entry.summary: Hedge-Bench presents 102 real hedge-fund analyst tasks grounded in expert reasoning traces, enabling deterministic grading against verified steps rather than noisy model-judged outputs. Frontier models score below 16%, exposing a large gap in open-ended financial reasoning.

entry.title: Samudra 2: Scaling Ocean Emulators across Resolutions

author.name: Yuan Yuan, Jesse Rusak, Alexander Merose, Adam Subel, Pavel Perezhogin, Alistair Adcroft, Carlos Fernandez-Granda, Laure Zanna

entry.summary: Samudra 2 scales neural ocean emulators to finer resolution with a wider U-Net backbone and ConvNeXt-style blocks, addressing long-horizon failure modes like variance collapse and imprinting artifacts. It enables faster multi-year autoregressive ocean simulations than traditional general circulation models.

entry.title: MultiTurnPSB: Evaluating Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks an dClassifier-Based Defenses for Medical AI Safety

author.name: Anushka Sheoran, Yiduo Hao

entry.summary: MultiTurnPSB extends a medical safety benchmark to four-turn adversarial conversations, showing unsafe responses rise from 35% to nearly 80% by turn 4 against GPT-4.1-mini under live attack. It reveals model safety divergences invisible to single-turn evaluation and identifies key attack patterns.

entry.title: Aligning Data-Driven Predictors with Allocation: A Decision-Focused Approach to Survival Analysis

author.name: Itai Zilberstein, Ioannis Anagnostides, Tuomas Sandholm

entry.summary: This work demonstrates that survival predictors optimized for standard metrics like the C-index can yield arbitrarily poor organ-allocation outcomes, and introduces a decision-focused learning approach aligning prediction with allocation policy. It bridges survival analysis and policy optimization in high-stakes settings.

entry.title: Fixing FOLIO and MALLS: Verified Annotations and an LLM-assisted Framework to Focus Human Relabeling

author.name: Andrea Brunello, Cristian Curaba, Luca Geatti, Michele Mignani, Angelo Montanari, Nicola Saccomanno

entry.summary: This paper audits the FOLIO and MALLS natural-language-to-first-order-logic benchmarks, finding roughly 39% and 36% of entries contain incorrect formalizations plus high rates of ambiguity. It releases corrected ground truths and an LLM-assisted framework to focus human relabeling efforts.

entry.title: MUSE: A Unified Agentic Harness for MLLMs

author.name: Jianglin Lu, Hailing Wang, Xu Ma, Qihua Dong, Mingyuan Zhang, Yizhou Wang, Yun Fu

entry.summary: MUSE is an agentic harness that wraps frozen MLLMs with composable modules for perception, parsing, verification, and repair to solve spatial tasks they normally fail. Shows how much capability can be elicited through scaffolding without retraining.

entry.title: Rethinking Molecular Text Representations for LLMs: An Empirical Study

author.name: Arun Raja, Garrett M. Morris, Kian Ming A. Chai

entry.summary: Systematic benchmark of nine molecular text representations across eight chemical tasks using 16 LLMs. Finds performance is strongly representation-dependent, with structured formats (CML, MolJSON) best for structural tasks and IUPAC best for semantic retrieval.

entry.title: SynCred-Bench: Benchmarking Synthetic Credibility in AI-Generated Visual Misinformation

author.name: Junxiao Yang, Minghao Zhang, Xiaoce Wang, Haoran Liu, Shiyao Cui, Hongning Wang, Minlie Huang

entry.summary: SynCred-Bench is a benchmark of 600 AI-generated misinformation images with realistic embedded text and layouts, addressing the new threat of synthetic credibility. Shows current MLLMs, AIGC detectors, and humans all perform poorly at detection.

entry.title: Local Guidance, Global Impact: Gaussian-Reshaped Trust Region Unlocks Behavior Transitions

author.name: Bingxu Liu, Jiashun Liu, Johan Obando-Ceron, Hao Wang, Runze Liu, Pablo Samuel Castro, Aaron Courville, Ling Pan

entry.summary: Shows standard PPO struggles in continual and non-stationary environments due to directionally inefficient local updates lacking geometry-aware guidance. Proposes a Gaussian-reshaped trust region to unlock behavior transitions where divergence regularization fails.

entry.title: Right Makes Might: Aligning Verified Hidden States Empowers RL Reasoning

author.name: Ziyue Wang, Aomufei Yuan, Yongfu Zhu, Shuai Dong, Wenpu Liu, Yiran Yao, Weichu Xie, Yuqi Xu, Caoyuan Ma, Wenqi Shao, Xiaoying Zhang, Nan Duan, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: Finds that correct RLVR rollouts converge geometrically at the anchor token before the answer marker, and proposes aligning these verified hidden states to extract a unified correct-decision representation that reduces sensitivity to reasoning path. Aims to improve RL reasoning by leveraging shared hidden-state structure beyond a single reward bit.

entry.title: Denoise First, Orthogonalize Later: Understanding Momentum in Muon via Spectral Filtering

author.name: Xianliang Li, Zihan Zhang, Weiyang Liu, Han Bao

entry.summary: Shows momentum in the Muon optimizer acts as a spectral filter, suppressing perturbations while preserving the dominant signal under a structured signal-plus-perturbation gradient model, thereby enlarging the spectral gap and stabilizing the orthogonalization step. Bridges the gap between analyses that remove or retain momentum without explaining its benefit.

entry.title: Small RL Controller, Large Language Model: RL-Guided Adaptive Sampling for Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Runpeng Dai, Tong Zheng, Rui Liu, Chengsong Huang, Hongtu Zhu

entry.summary: Frames adaptive sampling for test-time scaling as an MDP and trains a lightweight RL controller to decide when to stop sampling, balancing accuracy, latency, and compute. The controller relies only on answer statistics, making it cheap and broadly applicable.

entry.title: ARBOR: Online Process Rewards via a Reusable Rubric Buffer for Search Agents

author.name: Zheng Liu, Longxiang Zhang, Xintong Wang, Zhiang Xu, Shaoxiong Zhan, Xin Shan, Wen Huang, Tao Dai, Shu-Tao Xia, Chengfu Huo, Liang Ding

entry.summary: Proposes ARBOR, a reusable cross-query rubric buffer providing online process rewards for search agents, addressing zero-gradient cases when all sampled trajectories share correctness. Rubrics are consolidated across queries rather than discarded after one use.

entry.title: Don't Forget Your Embeddings: Robust Knowledge Erasure via Precise Editing of Embeddings

author.name: Clara Haya Suslik, Or Shafran, Mor Geva

entry.summary: Proposes EMBER, a plug-and-play knowledge erasure module that uses sparse matrix factorization to precisely remove concept-related features from token embeddings, an overlooked layer in prior unlearning. It aims for robustness against adversarial recovery and relearning.

entry.title: Exploring Adversarial Robustness and Safety Alignment in Multilingual Multi-Modal Large Language Models

author.name: Hashmat Shadab Malik, Muzammal Naseer, Salman Khan

entry.summary: Systematically studies adversarial robustness and safety alignment of multilingual multimodal LLMs across 12 languages, revealing transferable cross-lingual adversarial image vulnerabilities. Safety varies with how multilingual capability is acquired.

entry.title: Language Models Compare Quantities Using Number-specific and Unit-specific Heuristics

author.name: Mutsumi Sasaki, Go kamoda, Ryosuke Takahashi, Kosuke Sato, Kentaro Inui, Keisuke Sakaguchi, Benjamin Heinzerling

entry.summary: Studies how language models compare quantities with units, finding accuracy degrades near comparison boundaries and that models use number-specific and unit-specific heuristics rather than exact conversion. Causal interventions on aligned subspaces shift outputs.

entry.title: World Models Meet Language Models: On the Complementarity of Concrete and Abstract Reasoning

author.name: Yucheng Zhou, Wei Tao, Yiwen Guo, Jianbing Shen

entry.summary: Explores complementarity of world models (concrete visual rollouts) and MLLMs (abstract reasoning), formulating controlled concrete reasoning where a model invokes, verifies, and integrates visual simulation. It builds datasets to study when visual simulation helps.

entry.title: Consistent Yet Wrong: Evidence Insensitivity in Spatial Vision-Language Models

author.name: S Divakar Bhat, Toshihiko Yamasaki

entry.summary: Tests whether view-consistent VLM predictions reflect geometric grounding and finds the opposite: leading models give view-invariant but incorrect metric distance answers, showing evidence insensitivity. Introduces ViewDiag, a controlled multi-view evaluation protocol.

entry.title: $A^2$: Smaller Self-Supervised ViTs Localize Better than Larger Ones

author.name: Sreehari Rammohan, Huy Ha, Carl Vondrick

entry.summary: Finds that smaller self-supervised ViTs localize foreground objects better than larger ones, and proposes A2, decoupling where to look (small attention model) from what to extract (large embedding model) by cropping around attention peaks. It uses entirely pretrained components without retraining.

entry.title: Revisiting Embodied Chain-of-Thought for Generalizable Robot Manipulation

author.name: Nan Sun, Yuan Zhang, Yongkun Yang, Wentao Zhao, Peiyan Li, Jun Guo, Wenxuan Song, Pengxiang Ding, Runze Suo, Yifei Su, Xin Xiao, Xinghang Li, Huaping Liu

entry.summary: This paper revisits embodied chain-of-thought for VLA models at large scale, building the largest such corpus to date (nearly 1M trajectories, 226M samples). It finds that effective embodied CoT must ground high-level reasoning into concrete action cues like end-effector movements and image-space trajectories, while abstract reasoning alone yields marginal gains and explicit CoT does not scale reliably autoregressively.

entry.title: LURE: Alignment Evaluations to Reduce Evaluation Awareness

author.name: Igor Ivanov

entry.summary: LURE constructs alignment evaluations by replaying realistic deployment-like conversations and appending a safety-relevant test at the end, to reduce models' evaluation awareness compared to scenarios built from scratch. Measured against three black-box eval-awareness metrics, LURE-Scheming is hard for models to distinguish from real deployment, with scheming, sabotage, and sycophancy instantiations beating existing baselines.

entry.title: Do Real-World Datasets Contain Natural Experiments? An Empirical Study Using Causal Feature Selection

author.name: Gautam Gare, John Galeotti, Michael Mozer, Deva Ramanan, Nan Rosemary Ke

entry.summary: An empirical study asking whether real-world datasets contain natural experiments (implicit interventions affecting some groups but not others) using causal discovery and causal feature selection. Treating such data as interventional rather than observational improves downstream performance.

entry.title: ThoughtFold: Folding Reasoning Chains via Introspective Preference Learning

author.name: Ziyan Liu, Xueda Shen, Yuzhe Gu, Songyang Gao, Kuikun Liu, Guangran Cheng, Chengqi Lyu, Dahua Lin, Wenwei Zhang, Kai Chen

entry.summary: ThoughtFold uses fine-grained introspective preference learning to fold reasoning chains and mitigate overthinking in large reasoning models, targeting the reinforcement of redundant explorations by outcome-based RLVR. It reduces memorization of redundant exploration in long chains-of-thought.

entry.title: Building Better Activation Oracles

author.name: Jan Bauer, Celeste De Schamphelaere, Adam Karvonen, Niclas Luick, Neel Nanda

entry.summary: This work improves Activation Oracles for interpreting residual stream activations through on-policy training, better datasets, more layers, and an improved injection formula, while releasing AObench, the first comprehensive AO evaluation suite. Capability gains are marginal but quality and evaluation improvements are substantial.

entry.title: Large Byte Model: Teaching Language Models About Compiled Code

author.name: Florian St\"ortz, Catalin-Andrei Stan, Alexandru Dinu, Sandra Servia-Rodr\'iguez, Mihaela Gaman, Calin Miron, Edward Raff

entry.summary: This work presents the first byte-native LLM that can answer complex questions about malware binaries directly from raw bytes, using vocabulary expansion with a bespoke byte tokenizer. It achieves 69% to 98% accuracy across malware classification tasks, showing domain training is essential.

entry.title: Constitutional On-Policy Safe Distillation

author.name: Ming Wen, Yuxuan Liu, Kun Yang, Yunhao Feng, Zhuoer Xu, Yuhao Sun, Shiwen Cui, Xiang Zheng, Xingjun Ma, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: Studies safety on-policy self-distillation and finds it suffers from severe collapse, where constitutional conditioning contracts the teacher toward short conservative responses amplified by reverse KL. Formalizes this as geometric leakage and proposes a fix.

entry.title: WebRISE: Requirement-Induced State Evaluation for MLLM-Generated Web Artifacts

author.name: Yuxin Meng, Yuhan Suo, Junjie Wang, Yuhan Sun, Yiyao Yu, Ruixu Zhang, Ruining Hu, Yubin Wang, Shouwei Ruan, Bin Wang, Yuxiang Zhang, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: WebRISE compiles task requirements into Interaction Contract Graphs of observable states and transitions to evaluate MLLM-generated web artifacts, spanning 442 tasks across five input modalities. Reveals even the strongest model reaches only ~66% requirement coverage.

entry.title: Calibration Data Trade-offs Across Capability Dimensions: Why Multi-Source Mixing Matters for High-Sparsity LLM Pruning

author.name: Hu Xu, Zhaolong Xing, Congcong Liu, Jiaxing Wang, Zhida Jiang, Junshi Huang, Zhen Chen, Jianfeng Xu

entry.summary: Shows that calibration data source for high-sparsity LLM pruning has opposite-sign trade-offs across capability dimensions: low calibration perplexity helps general retention but hurts math. Argues multi-source calibration mixing matters, challenging prior averaged-accuracy conclusions.

entry.title: When Model Merging Breaks Routing: Training-Free Calibration for MoE

author.name: Canbin Huang, Tianyuan Shi, Xiaojun Quan, Jingang Wang, Jianfei Zhang, Qifan Wang

entry.summary: Identifies routing breakdown as a critical failure mode when merging Mixture-of-Experts LLMs, where the merged router fails to dispatch tokens to appropriate experts due to softmax/Top-k sensitivity. Proposes a training-free calibration to fix routing after merging.

entry.title: Scalable On-Hardware Training of Quantum Neural Networks and Application to Clinical Data Imputation

author.name: Natansh Mathur, Panagiotis Kl. Barkoutsos, Masako Yamada, Martin Roetteler, Iordanis Kerenidis

entry.summary: Introduces a quantum neural network training framework that reduces gradient-estimation cost from quadratic to logarithmic in the number of qubits using a Butterfly circuit architecture and layer-wise training. Applied to clinical data imputation, making hardware-based QNN optimization feasible at larger scales.

entry.title: Fast Organic Crystal Structure Prediction with Unit Cell Flow Matching

author.name: Alston Lo, Luka Mucko, Austin H. Cheng, Andy Cai, Alastair J. A. Price, Wojciech Matusik, Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik

entry.summary: Introduces Clari, a large-scale flow matching model for organic crystal structure prediction that generates redundancy-free unit cells using pure pair-bias attention instead of expensive triangle layers, reducing prediction time from minutes to seconds. Requires only atom types and bonds as input.

entry.title: Demystifying Pipeline Parallelism: First Theory for PipeDream

author.name: Ivan Ilin, Peter Richt\'arik

entry.summary: Provides the first theoretical convergence analysis for PipeDream-style pipeline parallelism via Randomized PipeDream, a stale block-SGD abstraction with a nonconvex convergence guarantee. Also delivers a scaling diagnosis of steady-state delay effects.

entry.title: HyperPatch: Sequential Knowledge Editing Under n-ary Structural Drift

author.name: Yu-Kai Chan, Wen-Sheng Lien, Dong-Ting Yao, Bo-Kai Ruan, Kwan-Yeung Lin, Hong-Han Shuai, Meng-Fen Chiang

entry.summary: Identifies N-ary Structural Drift, a failure mode where sequential knowledge editing fractures n-ary relations reified into triples, causing retriever mis-grounding mistaken for hallucination. Proposes HyperPatch, a parameter-preserving hypergraph-based editing framework to maintain event integrity.

entry.title: Benchmarking Speech-to-Speech Translation Models

author.name: Alkis Koudounas, Hayato Futami, Quentin Jodelet, Osamu Take, Shinji Watanabe, Emiru Tsunoo

entry.summary: Introduces COMPASS, a unified speech-to-speech translation benchmark integrating 46 metrics across eight dimensions over 1,248 model-language configurations. It shows single-metric rankings misrepresent quality and reduces metrics to a compact reproducible set.

entry.title: Multilingual Unlearning in LLMs: Transfer, Dynamics, and Reversibility

author.name: Chaoyi Xiang, Olga Ohrimenko, Benjamin I. P. Rubinstein, Lea Frermann

entry.summary: Studies multilingual unlearning by extending TOFU to five languages, finding that unlearning transfer across languages is highly variable and strongest among languages sharing scripts and families. It analyzes dynamics, reversibility, and layer-wise effects.

entry.title: Knowledge Editing in Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Haewon Park, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: Transfers locate-then-edit knowledge editing from autoregressive models to masked diffusion language models, comparing where edits apply across paradigms. It finds edit localization transfers but with paradigm-specific differences between MDMs and ARMs.

entry.title: Bootstrap Your Generator: Unpaired Visual Editing with Flow Matching

author.name: Yoad Tewel, Yuval Atzmon, Gal Chechik, Lior Wolf

entry.summary: Bootstrap Your Generator enables unpaired training of flow-matching image/video editing models by pairing instruction cues from the frozen base model with cycle-consistency, avoiding massive paired datasets. It routes gradients over clean predictions to make training tractable, from NVIDIA/Wolf-affiliated authors.

entry.title: When Helping Hurts and How to Fix It: Multi-Agent Debate for Data Cleaning

author.name: Chirag Parmar, Akshat Mehta, Henglin Wu, Jagadish Ramamurthy, Shweta Medhekar

entry.summary: An empirical study of when multi-agent debate helps versus hurts data cleaning, finding debate degrades generation through critique-induced confusion but improves error detection. It derives a condition predicting when debate is beneficial.

entry.title: The Shadow Price of Reasoning: Economic Perspective on Optimal Budget Allocation for LLMs

author.name: Xu Wan, Speed Zhu, Jianwei Cai, Guang Chen, XiMing Huang, Wiggin Zhou, Mingyang Sun

entry.summary: This paper formulates LLM inference budget allocation as a constrained optimization problem governed by economic shadow-price principles, deriving an optimal policy that reallocates compute from unsolvable to solvable queries. The CLEAR method performs rational abandonment near solvability thresholds.

entry.title: The Reliability Gap in Benchmark Auditing: Distribution Shift and Scale as Failure Modes of Contamination Detection

author.name: Wojciech Zarzecki, Jan Dubi\'nski, Sebastian Cygert

entry.summary: Investigates reliability failures of benchmark contamination detection methods under distribution shift and scale constraints, finding that methods validated in controlled academic regimes break in realistic auditing scenarios. It evaluates three leading membership-inference paradigms.

entry.title: The DeepSpeak-Agentic Dataset

author.name: Sarah Barrington, Maty Bohacek, Hany Farid

entry.summary: DeepSpeak-Agentic is a dataset of over 37 hours of semi-structured conversations between humans and embodied AI agents, used to evaluate forensic identification of AI agents across audio, video, and text. It includes a scalable data-capture system pairing agents with crowd workers.

entry.title: Unveiling the Structure of Do-Calculus Reasoning via Derivation Graphs

author.name: Cl\'ement Yvernes, Emilie Devijver, Marianne Clausel, Eric Gaussier

entry.summary: Introduces derivation graphs to represent how do-calculus rules are applied and combined, characterizing the full space of equivalent observational and interventional probability expressions. The structure yields a procedure using at most four rule applications.

entry.title: Oscillatory State-Space Models as Inductive Biases for Physics-Informed Neural PDE Solvers

author.name: Abhishek Chandra, Taniya Kapoor

entry.summary: TadA-Bench is a million-variant wet-lab replay benchmark from 31 directed-evolution rounds, designed to test whether models can prioritize future experiments rather than just fit static data. It provides aligned DNA/RNA/protein views and a graph-based label-unification pipeline for agentic protein engineering.

entry.title: Anomalies in Multivariate Time Series Benchmarks Are Mostly Univariate

author.name: Marc Pinet (LIG), Julien Cumin (LIG), Samuel Berlemont (LIG), Dominique Vaufreydaz (LIG)

entry.summary: This paper shows that anomalies in eight widely-used multivariate time series benchmarks are mostly univariate—no cross-channel rupture occurs without an accompanying single-channel deviation. It questions the value of cross-channel modeling assumptions in popular anomaly detection benchmarks.

entry.title: GRZO: Group-Relative Zeroth-Order Optimization for Large Language Model Fine-Tuning

author.name: Liyan Tan, Yequan Zhao, Yifan Yang, Ruijie Zhang, Xinling Yu, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: GRZO is a group-relative zeroth-order optimizer for memory-efficient LLM fine-tuning that draws per-example perturbations and aggregates losses via group-relative normalization, raising effective gradient-direction count to the batch size at no extra forward cost. It is proven directionally unbiased with variance shrinking proportionally to batch size, beating MeZO.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Reranking to Operationalize Nuanced Objectives in Recommender Systems

author.name: Amir Ghasemian, Homa Hosseinmardi, Upasana Dutta, Duncan J. Watts

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether LLM-assisted reranking in recommender systems, while improving personalization, inadvertently amplifies exposure to ideologically extreme or conspiratorial political content. It connects recommender system design to broader social concerns like polarization and filter bubbles.

entry.title: Patcher: Post-Hoc Patching of Backdoored Large Language Models

author.name: Anjun Gao, Yueyang Quan, Yufei Xia, Zhuqing Liu, Minghong Fang

entry.summary: Patcher repairs backdoored LLMs using only a single reported failure case and model parameters, localizing triggers via gradient-based saliency. It addresses the practical scenario where defenders cannot distinguish a backdoor attack from a natural alignment bug.

entry.title: Libra: Efficient Resource Management for Agentic RL Post-Training

author.name: Kaiwen Chen, Xin Tan, Jingzong Li, Hong Xu

entry.summary: Libra is a resource-management system for agentic RL post-training that handles long-tailed, non-stationary rollout workloads and asymmetric compute between rollout and training phases. Targets efficiency bottlenecks specific to tool-invoking agent trajectories.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning from Cross-domain Videos with Video Prediction Model

author.name: Zhao Yang, Xinrui Zu, Jacob E. Kooi, Thomas Delliaux, He Liu, Shujian Yu, Kevin Sebastian Luck, Vincent Fran\c{c}ois-Lavet

entry.summary: XIPER learns rewards from expert videos in visually distinct domains by training a cross-domain video prediction model that maps agent observations into the expert domain and uses prediction likelihood as reward. Outperforms baselines on DMC color and body suites despite domain gaps.

entry.title: EqGINO: Equivariant Geometry-Informed Fourier Neural Operators for 3D PDEs

author.name: Sungwon Kim, Juho Song, Seungmin Shin, Guimok Cho, Sangkook Kim, Chanyoung Park

entry.summary: EqGINO is an equivariant geometry-informed Fourier Neural Operator for 3D PDEs that enforces isotropy in the spectral domain to achieve equivariance affordably, avoiding costly spectral group convolutions. Improves generalization across geometric transformations.

entry.title: The Unsampled Truth: Psychometrics in SLMs Measure Prompt Artifacts, Not Psychological Constructs

author.name: Nils Schwager, Christoph Hau, Simon M\"unker, Achim Rettinger

entry.summary: Demonstrates across 13 open-weight small language models that psychometric assessments largely measure prompt artifacts (personas, instructions, item ordering, option symbols) rather than psychological constructs. Provides a diagnostic framework to separate semantic signal from artifacts.

entry.title: PRISM: Synergizing Vision Foundation Models via Self-organized Expert Specialization

author.name: Ying Tang, Dong Li, Youjia Zhang, Zikai Song, Junqing Yu, Wei Yang

entry.summary: PRISM is a dual-stream Mixture-of-Experts framework that distills multiple vision foundation models into one efficient model via teacher-conditional routing and dynamic recomposition, mitigating negative transfer in monolithic distillation. Synergizes complementary VFM strengths through modular specialization.

entry.title: Rethinking the Role of Tensor Decompositions in Post-Training LLM Compression

author.name: Artur Zagitov, Alexander Miasnikov, Maxim Krutikov, Vladimir Aletov, Gleb Molodtsov, Nail Bashirov, Artem Tsedenov, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates tensor decompositions for post-training LLM compression across dense and MoE architectures, identifying a fundamental mismatch between the shared subspaces tensor methods assume and the heterogeneous representations modern LLMs learn. Provides empirical and theoretical trade-off analysis.

entry.title: From Non-Convex to Strongly Convex: Curvature-Adaptive FTPL for Online Optimization

author.name: Moses Charikar, Chirag Pabbaraju, Ambuj Tewari

entry.summary: Shows that Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader can be made curvature-adaptive in the online non-convex setting without knowing in advance how curvature accumulates, using a time-varying perturbation scale. Interpolates between optimal regret bounds for convex and strongly convex losses.

entry.title: Dynamic Short Convolutions Improve Transformers

author.name: Oliver Sieberling, Bharat Runwal, Rameswar Panda, Yoon Kim

entry.summary: Introduces dynamic short convolutions with input-dependent filters as an additional Transformer primitive, applied to query/key/value representations to improve associative recall and language modeling. Preserves convolution's locality bias while increasing expressivity over static variants.

entry.title: Online Learning with Gradient-Variation Interval Regret

author.name: Yan-Feng Xie, Shuche Wang, Peng Zhao, Zhi-Hua Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes the first online learning algorithm achieving an interval regret bound that scales with gradient variation, performing well over every time interval in non-stationary settings. Uses a two-layer online ensemble structure with strong theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: An Asymptotic Theory of Chain-of-Thought in In-Context Learning

author.name: Kaito Takanami, Cengiz Pehlevan

entry.summary: Develops an asymptotic theory of chain-of-thought reasoning in in-context learning, modeling CoT as iterative weight refinement in linear regression and deriving exact generalization error formulas via random matrix theory. Reveals phase transitions in how reasoning depth affects generalization.

entry.title: Can Factual Opinions Be Edited (Manipulated) in Large Language Models?

author.name: Yuanpu Cao, Ziyi Yin, Fenglong Ma, Jinghui Chen

entry.summary: Introduces the FOE benchmark to study whether knowledge editing can manipulate documented opinions of public figures, exposing a societal risk beyond editing atomic facts. It shows current editing methods struggle with factual opinions while highlighting potential for image reshaping and election influence.

entry.title: MemTrain: Self-Supervised Context Memory Training

author.name: Ziheng Li, Xingrun Xing, Haoqing Wang, Zhi-Hong Deng, Yehui Tang

entry.summary: Introduces MemTrain, a self-supervised framework using masked-recovery proxy tasks over Wikipedia to enhance context-memory capability of long-horizon LLM agents before downstream post-training. It avoids costly annotated memory-intensive data.

entry.title: RealClawBench: Live OpenClaw Benchmarks from Real Developer-Agent Sessions

author.name: Zongwei Lv, Zhewen Tan, Yaoming Li, Yilun Yao, Yuxuan Tian, Lin Sun, Xiangzheng Zhang, Weihong Lin, Tong Yang, Guangxiang Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces RealClawBench, a live agent benchmark built from real developer-agent sessions with reconstructed execution environments and deterministic verifiable scorers. It captures realistic distribution, diversity, and difficulty of deployed agent use.

entry.title: PsychoPass: Geometric Profiling of Multi-Turn Adversarial LLM Conversations

author.name: Muberra Ozmen, Subhabrata Majumdar

entry.summary: Introduces PsychoPass, which models multi-turn jailbreak conversations as trajectories in embedding space to predict attacks before harmful content appears. It shows naive geometric classifiers are confounded by turn count and isolates a smaller genuine signal after correction.

entry.title: CAPER: Clause-Aligned Process Supervision for Text-to-SQL

author.name: Lujie Ban, Jiasheng Shi, Jinyang Li, Xiaolin Han, Tsz Nam Chan, Chenhao Ma

entry.summary: Proposes CAPER, which derives clause-level process supervision for text-to-SQL via counterfactual intervention on the SQL abstract syntax tree, enabling root-cause error localization. The resulting clause-level reward model trains a 9B PRM for policy optimization and candidate verification.

entry.title: Disentangling Visual and Factual Correctness in LVLMs' Visualization Literacy

author.name: Soohyun Lee, Jaeyoung Kim, Seokhyeon Park, Sihyeon Lee, Jiwon Song, Bohyoung Kim, Hyunjoo Song, Jinwook Seo

entry.summary: Presents a framework disentangling visual correctness from factual correctness in LVLMs' visualization literacy, showing some models reach human-level scores via memorized facts rather than genuine visual reasoning. It exposes validity limitations in existing visualization literacy tests.

entry.title: Diffusing in the Right Space: A Systematic Study of Latent Diffusability

author.name: Tianxiong Zhong, Xingye Tian, Xuebo Wang, Xin Tao, Pengfei Wan

entry.summary: This systematic study examines which properties make a latent space diffusion-friendly, testing factors like semantic separability, spectral smoothness, and manifold continuity across many tokenizers. It clarifies which factors best predict downstream generation quality.

entry.title: DyaPlex: Full-Duplex Speech-Motion Model for Dyadic Interaction

author.name: Koki Nagano, Hongyu Liu, Seonwook Park, Tianye Li, Amrita Mazumdar, Christian Jacobsen, Shengze Wang, Michael Stengel, Rajarshi Roy, Ka Chun Cheung, Simon See, Shalini De Mello

entry.summary: DyaPlex is a streaming full-duplex speech-and-motion model for dyadic interaction that simultaneously perceives and generates speech and physical motion in real time. It uses a dual-tower Transformer preserving a frozen full-duplex speech model while adding a coupled motion pathway, from NVIDIA-affiliated authors.

entry.title: Let the Dynamics Flow: Stable Flow Matching Dynamical Systems

author.name: Rodrigo P\'erez-Dattari, Francisco Leiva, Andrea Testa, Leonel Rozo, Javier Ruiz del Solar, No\'emie Jaquier

entry.summary: Stable Flow Matching Dynamical Systems (SFMDS) integrates formal Lyapunov stability guarantees into flow-matching imitation policies, parametrizing dynamical systems that retain expressive, multimodal action distributions while ensuring convergence. It bridges high-capacity generative motion modeling with provable stability for safe robot behavior.

entry.title: Handoff Debt: The Rediscovery Cost When Coding Agents Take Over Interrupted Tasks

author.name: Dipesh KC, Anjila Budathoki

entry.summary: Introduces handoff debt, the rediscovery cost when a coding agent takes over an interrupted task from another agent. A takeover protocol evaluates successor agents across four handoff views to measure this overlooked dimension.
