entry.title: Tiny Collaborative Inference for Occlusion-Robust Object Detection

author.name: Chieh-Tung Cheng, Mustafa Aslanov, Eiman Kanjo

entry.summary: Evaluates occlusion-robust object detection on ultra-low-end devices with under 1MB SRAM by combining an MCUNet backbone, YOLOv2 head, and TFLite quantization. It compares feature-level and decision-level collaborative inference, finding weighted boxes fusion best under occlusion.

entry.title: MariData: One-Step Unpaired Image Translation for Maritime Environments

author.name: Santeri Henriksson, Mehdi Asadi, Amin Majd, Juha Kalliovaara

entry.summary: Introduces a framework using CycleGAN-turbo one-step unpaired image translation to generate synthetic maritime imagery for adverse weather and low-light conditions, with zero-convolution skip connections to preserve small navigational objects. It addresses data scarcity for autonomous surface ship perception.

entry.title: IDO: Incongruity-aware Distribution Optimization for Multimodal Fake News Detection

author.name: Hengyang Zhou, Rongman Hong, Yuxuan Zhou, Jing Wang, Zhaoyan Pan

entry.summary: IDO is a multimodal fake news detection method that explicitly models semantic incongruity through channel-wise reweighting and Gaussian distribution modeling for factual and modality mismatches. It moves beyond cross-modal consistency to detect deceptive content.

entry.title: Beyond Single Solution: Multi-Hypothesis Collaborative Deep Unfolding Network for Image Compressive Sensing

author.name: Wenxue Cui, Hualin Li, Yuhang Qin, Yifu Xu, Xiaopeng Fan, Debin Zhao

entry.summary: MHC-DUN is a deep unfolding network for image compressive sensing that explicitly models multiple plausible solution hypotheses, jointly optimizing across diverse solution spaces via proximal gradient descent. It addresses the ill-posedness ignored by single-solution methods.

entry.title: Fixed-Time Dynamic Landing of Quadrotors using Adaptive Unscented Kalman Filtering and Nonlinear Model Predictive Control

author.name: Mohammadreza Izadi, Zeinab Shayan, Steven Waslander, Reza Faieghi

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether short-term synaptic plasticity stabilizes goal-conditioned dynamics in a PFC-inspired reservoir model with basal-ganglia-style temporal-difference readout for multistep goal-directed action planning. It finds goal identity is decodable without STP but examines STP's role in maintaining action-usable dynamics.

entry.title: eMEM: A Hybrid Spatio-Temporal Memory System For Embodied Agents

author.name: A. Haroon Rasheed, Maria Kabtoul

entry.summary: eMEM is a hybrid graph-based memory system for embodied agents that indexes experience simultaneously by meaning, space, and time using SQLite, HNSW semantic search, and an R-tree for spatial queries. A tiered consolidation pipeline compresses raw observations, inspired by hippocampal-neocortical consolidation.

entry.title: Recovering Direct Price Effects of Environmental Amenities in Housing Markets: Regression and Causal Machine Learning Model Assessment with Empirical Monte Carlo Simulation

author.name: Zhenshan Chen (Virginia Tech), Klaus Moeltner (Virginia Tech), Matthew Mair (Virginia Tech)

entry.summary: This study uses an empirical Monte Carlo simulation grounded in over a million real property transactions to compare traditional hedonic regression and causal machine learning for estimating direct, unmediated price effects of environmental amenities (DUET). By randomly assigning treatment over a real data-generating process, it avoids parametric simulation assumptions.

entry.title: TriEval: A Resource-Efficient Pipeline for LLM Bias, Toxicity, and Truthfulness Assessment

author.name: Akshatha Srikantha, Manpreet Singh, Yash Jajoo, Shyamal Lakhanpal

entry.summary: TriEval is a resource-efficient pipeline for jointly assessing LLM bias, toxicity, and truthfulness while minimizing compute. It aims to make multi-parameter LLM evaluation accessible to researchers without large resources.

entry.title: IdiomX A Multilingual Benchmark for Idiom Understanding, Retrieval, and Interpretation

author.name: Ayman Ali Sharara

entry.summary: IdiomX is a large-scale multilingual benchmark for idiom understanding, retrieval, and interpretation, containing over 190K contextualized examples across 12K+ idioms built via a multi-stage pipeline. It targets the persistent NLP challenge of non-compositional, cross-lingual idiomatic meaning.

entry.title: ERP-XTTN: Interpretable Prototype-Guided Cross-Attention for Cross-Subject ERP Classification

author.name: Charlotte Genevier Wyman, Leanne Hirshfield

entry.summary: Proposes ERP-XTTN, an interpretable cross-attention architecture for cross-subject EEG event-related potential classification that routes inputs to fixed difference-wave prototypes via query-key-only attention, making attention faithfulness structural. Aims for calibration-free generalization across subjects.

entry.title: Rethinking Neural Width for Alternating Current Optimal Power Flow Proxies

author.name: Dhruvi Khandelwal, Anurag Basistha, Ayushi Jolotia, Parikshit Pareek

entry.summary: Investigates how wide a neural network must be to approximate the AC optimal power flow manifold, introducing a Loss-Guided Neural Densification algorithm that incrementally adds capacity only when needed. Achieves baseline performance with up to 10x fewer neurons per layer, aiding formal verification.

entry.title: Topology-Aware Gaussian Graph Repair for Robust Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Anubha Goel, Juho Kanniainen

entry.summary: Proposes TAGR (Topology-Aware Gaussian Repair), a graph repair framework for robust GNN message passing that can both remove noisy edges and recover missing connections, unlike methods that only prune. Avoids the optimization complexity of full graph structure learning.

entry.title: Low-Frequency Shortcuts in Texture-Driven Visual Learning

author.name: Utku \c{S}irin, Cathy Hou, David Alvarez-Melis, Stratos Idreos

entry.summary: Analyzes shortcut learning in texture-driven visual domains, showing they suffer from low-frequency shortcuts where decisions rely on a few low-frequency components despite classification information residing in higher-frequency details. Extends shortcut analysis beyond standard shape-driven benchmarks.

entry.title: Set-Preserving Calibration from Conformal P-Values to E-Values

author.name: Nabil Alami, Jad Zakharia, Souhaib Ben Taieb

entry.summary: Identifies limitations of classical p-to-e calibrators in conformal prediction, showing they are not set-preserving and lead to conservative prediction sets, and proposes a novel P2E calibrator that converts conformal p-values to e-values without altering the induced prediction set. Bridges p-value and e-value conformal formulations.

entry.title: Quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons exhibit less fragmented loss landscapes and outperform leaky integrate-and-fire neurons in spike-based gradient descent

author.name: Carlo Wenig, Raoul-Martin Memmesheimer, Christian Klos

entry.summary: Demonstrates that quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons exhibit less fragmented loss landscapes and outperform leaky integrate-and-fire neurons in exact spike-based gradient descent for spiking neural networks. Shows that smoother spike dynamics translate into practical training advantages.

entry.title: Memory Retrieval for Changing Preferences

author.name: Yuehan Qin, Li Li, Linxin Song, Wei Yang, Jiate Li, Yuqing Yang, Yue Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes a unified framework for memory access and selection in long-context dialogue that handles changing user preferences, quantifying memory turn utility via a Bayes factor measuring likelihood improvement rather than semantic similarity. Addresses both when and which memory to retrieve.

entry.title: Framing Migration News with LLMs: Structured CoT as a Support for Human Interpretation

author.name: David Alonso del Barrio, Jing Wen, Daniel Gatica-Perez

entry.summary: Studies a locally deployable open-source LLM with Structured Chain-of-Thought prompting to support interpretable, auditable frame analysis of migration news. It emphasizes privacy, reproducibility, and equitable access for media researchers.

entry.title: PHAF-Personalized Hand Avatars in a Flash

author.name: Meghana Shankar, Akanxit Upadhyay, Anmol Namdev, Green Rosh KS, Pawan Prasad BH

entry.summary: PHAF generates personalized photorealistic hand avatars from just two images using semantic-guided mesh alignment and densified texture extraction, enabling real-time edge deployment. It avoids slow optimization-based texture techniques.

entry.title: A Benchmark for Semi-supervised Multi-modal Crowd Counting

author.name: Haoliang Meng, Xiaopeng Hong, Yabin Wang, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: This paper builds the first benchmark for semi-supervised multi-modal crowd counting, defining a standardized labeled/unlabeled protocol and tailoring representative baselines. It establishes reference points for an unexplored task.

entry.title: TTT-VLA: Test-Time Latent Prompt Optimization for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Wenbo Zhang, Jianxiong Li, Shuai Yang, Sijin Chen, Jiajun Liu, Lingqiao Liu, Xiao Ma

entry.summary: TTT-VLA proposes a test-time training method for vision-language-action models that adapts a learned latent prompt during deployment to counter distribution shifts. It treats the prompt itself as a steerable interface that can be optimized from interaction, with an auxiliary proxy task during training.

entry.title: EaDex: A Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation Framework from Low-Cost Demonstrations

author.name: Qian Zhao, Xin Tong, Chengdong Wu, Yang Yang, Yingtian Li

entry.summary: EaDex is a cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation framework that generates demonstration data cheaply from a single RGB-D camera using MANO-based hand modeling and motion retargeting. It aims to cut the high data and training costs of dexterous manipulation learning.

entry.title: Human2Humanoid: Physics-Aware Cross-Morphology Motion Retargeting for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Tianchen Huang, Feiyang Yuan, Junchi Gu, Shurui Fang, Xiaohu Zhang, Yu Wang, Wei Gao, Shiwu Zhang

entry.summary: Human2Humanoid is an unsupervised motion retargeting framework that transfers human motion to humanoid robots using a CycleGAN with a skeleton-aware graph convolutional network to handle topology and scale mismatch without paired data. It targets teleoperation, imitation learning, and human-robot interaction.

entry.title: Multimodal Transformer Based Generic Mixture Density Network for Scattering Timescale Estimation of Fast Radio Bursts

author.name: Bikash Kharel, Emmanuel Fonseca, Srinjoy Das, Mason Ng, Paul Scholz, Mawson W. Simmons, Lordrick Kahinga, Afrokk Khan

entry.summary: MT-GMDN is a multimodal transformer-based mixture density network that ingests fast radio burst dynamic spectra to estimate scattering timescales quickly and robustly, replacing slow, initialization-sensitive template fitting and deconvolution. It targets the parameter-extraction bottleneck created by rising FRB discovery rates.

entry.title: Taking the Training Wheels Off: Aligning LLMs without Personas

author.name: Matthew Khoriaty

entry.summary: This post argues that nearly all current alignment techniques (RLHF, steering vectors, prompting) rely on eliciting good personas already present in the model and contends this approach will not scale to superhuman models, since there is no human-level persona data to extrapolate beyond human capabilities. It motivates moving toward alignment methods that do not depend on personas.

entry.title: Acceptance-Test-Driven Evaluation Protocols for Business-Centric LLM Systems

author.name: Eric Liang

entry.summary: This paper proposes an acceptance-test-driven evaluation protocol for business LLM systems, translating stakeholder goals into executable behavioral contracts, release gates, monitoring signals, and evidence artifacts. It adapts red-green-refactor discipline to bridge deterministic requirements with probabilistic generative components.

entry.title: RMPrior: Bridging Propagation Priors and Diffusion Refinement for Efficient Radio Map Construction

author.name: Zixuan Guo, Xiucheng Wang, Nan Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes RMPrior, a mid-start diffusion sampling strategy for radio map construction that initializes from a perturbed classical propagation prior rather than pure Gaussian noise, focusing computation on multipath-aware refinement. Reduces sampling cost for dynamic wireless systems.

entry.title: Flicker-DDPM: Accelerating Denoising Diffusion via 1/f Colored Noise Injection

author.name: Kexiang Mao

entry.summary: Proposes Flicker-DDPM, a diffusion model that injects 1/f colored noise (inspired by self-organized criticality) instead of white noise to better match the power-law spectra of natural images. Theoretically links a spatial correlation kernel parameter to the spectral exponent for adaptation.

entry.title: HiSE: A Lightweight Hierarchical Semantic Explainer for Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Zongrui Li, Yuhang Zhao, Ying Zhao, Yuanzhao Guo, Qiang Huang, Yuan Tian

entry.summary: Proposes HiSE, a lightweight feature-oriented explainer for heterogeneous graph neural networks that reflects the model's inherent semantic hierarchy while avoiding costly search or perturbation. Aims to improve fidelity and efficiency of HGNN explanations.

entry.title: How Visible Are Silent Manipulation Failures? An Observability Study of False-Success Detection in Simulated Robot Episodes

author.name: Aarav Bedi (University of California, Berkeley)

entry.summary: An observability study examining how detectable false-success failures are in simulated robot manipulation episodes, asking how much overturning information comes from proprioception versus vision. Builds a bimanual ALOHA testbed with privileged ground-truth labels.

entry.title: A 3D Isovist World Model -- Revealing a City's Unseen Geometry and Its Emergent Cross-City Signature

author.name: Xuhui Lin, Stephen Law, Nanjiang Chen, Kunyao Li, Tao Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a 3D isovist world model that predicts navigable geometry an agent can traverse rather than scene appearance or flattened occupancy grids, preserving multi-level 3D structure for embodied navigation. Reveals an emergent cross-city geometric signature.

entry.title: MLSkip: Data Skipping for ML Filters via Lightweight Metadata

author.name: Mihail Stoian, Mark Gerarts, Pascal Ginter, Andreas Zimmerer, Jan Van den Bussche, Andreas Kipf

entry.summary: Initiates the study of data skipping for ML filter predicates in databases, showing that Parquet's default min-max metadata can enable pruning of non-qualifying row groups for black-box ML model filters. Connects to ML query languages and neural network verification.

entry.title: Mixed-Modality Dual Face-Hair Retrieval

author.name: Quoc-Anh Bui-Huynh, Mai-Tuyen Lam, Dai-Anh-Tuan Nguyen, Thanh Duc Ngo

entry.summary: Dual Face-Hair Retrieval introduces a mixed-modality retrieval task where queries combine a face identity image with a hairstyle reference (image or text), plus a 180K-triplet benchmark. It requires disentangling identity and hairstyle from heterogeneous modalities.

entry.title: AvatarMix: Identity-Preserving Cross-Avatar Composition for Outfit Personalization

author.name: Zhaorong Wang, Yoshihiro Kanamori, Yuki Endo

entry.summary: AvatarMix composes head and body from two high-fidelity Gaussian avatars for outfit personalization, avoiding intersection artifacts and identity degradation. It adds a SeamFix diffusion module to refine joins after body reshaping.

entry.title: An Attention-Based Denoising Model for Diffusion Weighted Imaging

author.name: Prithviraj Verma, Pawan Kumar, Chandan Deshani, Prasun Chandra Tripathi

entry.summary: This work proposes a noise-aware attention denoising framework for diffusion-weighted MRI combining Swin Transformer window attention with gated refinement and explicit noise-level conditioning. It targets signal-dependent Rician noise from fast acquisitions.

entry.title: Bionic Human-Motion Style Transfer for Physically Executable Whole-Body Control of Humanoid Robots

author.name: Tianchen Huang, Mingkuan Zhao, Yang Gao, Feiyang Yuan, Junchi Gu, Xiaohu Zhang, Dongdong Zhao, Shi Yan, Yu Wang, Wei Gao, Shiwu Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a generation-to-control framework for transferring human motion style (gait rhythm, posture, arm swing) onto humanoid robots from a short exemplar while producing physically executable whole-body motion. It aims to reuse a demonstrated style across different motion contents.

entry.title: CANMOT: Class-Aware Noise Modeling for Multi-Object Tracking in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Timo Osterburg, Stefan Sch\"utte, Torsten Bertram

entry.summary: CANMOT introduces class-aware noise modeling for Kalman-filter-based 3D multi-object tracking in autonomous driving, replacing globally shared process/measurement covariances with class-specific, object-frame-aligned matrices that preserve longitudinal-lateral anisotropy. It systematically evaluates the impact of this refinement.

entry.title: Toward a Modular Architecture for Embedded AI Agent Systems at the Edge

author.name: Marcus R\"ub, Michael Gerhards

entry.summary: Proposes a modular tiered reference architecture for deploying agentic AI on embedded microcontrollers, decoupling low-latency on-device agents from heavier cloud reasoning. It targets the gap between server-class agent frameworks and edge constraints.

entry.title: The Violation Situation Pattern: A Knowledge-Graph Pattern for Compliance Violations

author.name: Nima Kamali Lassem, Fuqi Song, Seyid Amjad Ali

entry.summary: The Violation Situation Pattern reifies detected compliance violations as persistent knowledge-graph nodes with rule identifiers, temporal validity, lifecycle state, and PROV-O-aligned audit history. It is instantiated on a legal entity and contract lifecycle property graph.

entry.title: Calibrating Urban Traffic Simulation from Sparse Road Observations via Genetic Optimization

author.name: Hunter Sawyer, Jesse Roberts, Simon Matei

entry.summary: Presents a genetic algorithm framework for calibrating urban traffic simulations from sparse road observations without requiring detailed employment or job-location data. It addresses two key data limitations for realistic city-scale traffic simulation using the SUMO platform.

entry.title: A Hybrid Approach For Malware Classification Using Secondary Features Fusion

author.name: Raja Khurram Shahzad, Muhammad Mustaqeem, Haroon Elahi

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid malware classification method using feature fusion of API calls and n-grams with customized feature selection to both detect malware and classify it into families. Aims to improve malware mitigation beyond binary detection.

entry.title: A Nonmonotone Gradient-Based Algorithm for Symmetric Nonnegative Matrix Factorization and Graph Clustering

author.name: Ryan Swart, Johannes Brust

entry.summary: Introduces SNMPBB, the first adaptation of nonmonotone projected Barzilai-Borwein methods to symmetric nonnegative matrix factorization, with extensions for graph clustering and low-rank approximations. Proves global convergence and shows gradient methods are more effective than previously believed.

entry.title: Coherent Swap Regret and Channel-Proof Learning

author.name: Sohail Sarkar

entry.summary: Introduces coherent swap regret as a regret benchmark against local CPTP quantum deviations in quantum games, with an algorithm achieving sublinear regret via entropic mirror ascent. Establishes a three-level deviation-class landscape connecting quantum and classical online learning.

entry.title: Resource-Constrained Adaptive Inference for Sequential Pricing

author.name: Ruicheng Ao, Jiashuo Jiang, David Simchi-Levi

entry.summary: Formalizes a support-exclusion failure in resource-constrained sequential pricing where the resource state can make target-price inference impossible, and designs a target-aware controller that certifies feasible bands and logs continuous densities for valid inference. Provides regret-information accounting under resource constraints.

entry.title: DiffUNet^2: Bidirectional Prediction, Probabilistic Generation and Collaborative Visual Discovery for Scientific Data

author.name: Mengdi Chu, Jiaxin Yang, Angus G. Forbes, Nathan Debardeleben, Earl Lawrence, Ayan Biswas, Han-Wei Shen

entry.summary: Presents DiffUNet2, a conditional diffusion model enabling bidirectional any-to-any generation across time for scientific data, integrated with interactive visual analytics supporting branching timelines and probabilistic exploration. Adds backward reasoning and uncertainty to scientific forecasting.

entry.title: Predicting Inference-Time Scaling Gains from Labeled Validation-Set Output Statistics

author.name: Luyang Zhang, Jingyan Li

entry.summary: Studies predicting best-of-N inference scaling gains in advance using cheap statistics from a single labeled validation-set sampling pass, fitting ridge predictors and using bootstrap-Lasso for stability. Identifies a compact stable predictor of best-of-N accuracy gain.

entry.title: When Does Complexity Conditioning Help a Frozen Sentence Embedding? A Controlled Study of Per-Sentence and Pair-Level Difficulty Adaptation

author.name: Suhwan Hwang

entry.summary: A controlled study testing whether conditioning frozen sentence embeddings on input difficulty helps, finding the naive per-sentence complexity approach fails and provides no advantage over controls. It cautions against an intuitive but unsupported design idea.

entry.title: Diagnosis of Human Object Interaction Detectors for Real World Educational Applications

author.name: Divya Mereddy, Ashwin Tudur Sadashiva, Marcos Quinones-Grueiro, Gautam Biswas

entry.summary: Presents a diagnosis-driven framework with a triplet-level HOI error taxonomy and error-factor attribution for human-object interaction detection in real-world educational video, using mixed-reality medical training data. It analyzes failure modes from domain objects, occlusions, and complex conditions.

entry.title: Cross-Modality Feature Fusion Based on Structured State Space Duality for Multimodal Image Registration Network

author.name: Zhikang Li, Yan Wu, Xin Hu, Yi Dai, Ming Li

entry.summary: RegNetMamba-2 applies Structured State Space Duality (Mamba-style) for efficient cross-modality feature fusion in multi-modal image registration. It targets shared structural feature extraction with better efficiency than Transformers.

entry.title: Structure-Guided Mixed Masked Pretraining and Spatial Continuity Regularization for Printed Circuit Board Defect Detection

author.name: Peitong Wang, Nuo Wang, Enxin Qin, Chengjin Yu, Hanyu Xuan, Yuanting Yan

entry.summary: This paper combines structure-guided mixed masked pretraining with spatial continuity regularization for PCB defect detection, targeting tiny low-contrast defects in dense backgrounds. It leverages unlabeled images via sparse convolutional masked pretraining.

entry.title: Short-Term Synaptic Plasticity Stabilizes Goal-Conditioned Dynamics in a PFC-Inspired Reservoir Model for Multistep Goal-Directed Action Planning

author.name: Jin Nakamura, Yuichi Katori

entry.summary: This work evolves pairs of CTRNN agents that use communication for predator avoidance, finding three dominant survival strategies including self-regulatory calling where agents depend on hearing their own vocalizations. It explores communication as more than information transfer in natural-like systems.

entry.title: NVIDIA Isaac Sim: Enabling Scalable, GPU-Accelerated Simulation for Robotics

author.name: Sicong Gao, Maurice Pagnucco, Tomasz Bednarz, Yang Song

entry.summary: This survey reviews NVIDIA Isaac Sim from system and application perspectives, detailing its GPU-accelerated architecture, synthetic data pipeline, and usage patterns, and comparing it against widely used robotics simulators. It also analyzes representative studies and limitations.

entry.title: Semantic-weighted ICP for LiDAR Odometry: Class-Aware Residual Reweighting for Robust Scan Registration

author.name: Vasco Carvalho, Tiago Barros, Urbano J. Nunes

entry.summary: This work proposes semantic class-weighted ICP for LiDAR odometry, reweighting registration residuals by class relevance rather than treating all environmental elements equally. It improves robustness in dynamic and unstructured scenes with moving objects, vegetation, and ambiguous structures.

entry.title: Claude Opus 4.8: Capabilities and Reactions

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's post aggregates benchmarks, model-card tests, and community reactions to characterize Claude Opus 4.8, arguing that understanding a new model requires many calibrated data points rather than a few benchmarks. It synthesizes capability and model-welfare information into a coherent picture of the model's behavior.

entry.title: Large AI Models in Dental Healthcare: From General-Purpose Systems to Domain-Specific Foundation Models

author.name: Sema Helali, Lina Abu Nadab, Sausan Alqawas, Alaa Abd-Alrazaq, Faleh Tamimi, Rafat Damseh

entry.summary: A PRISMA-guided scoping review of large AI models in dentistry, classifying language-generative, vision foundation, and dental-specific foundation models across 97 studies. It proposes a two-dimensional classification framework.

entry.title: From Prompt to Service: An SLM-Based Agent Orchestration Gateway for AI-Driven Virtual Worlds

author.name: Louis Nisiotis, Aimilios Hadjiliasi

entry.summary: Presents an SLM-based agent orchestration gateway for AI-driven virtual worlds that uses an edge-deployed small language model to classify user intent and route requests to heterogeneous AI backends. It decouples virtual world clients from backend models for extensibility.

entry.title: Leveraging BART to Assess CS1 C++ Programming Assignments using Rubric-based Criteria

author.name: Kelsey Rainey, Jesse Roberts

entry.summary: Uses a BART encoder-decoder with LoRA adaptation and multitask fine-tuning to automatically grade introductory C++ programming assignments according to rubric criteria, with a distribution-matching term to align predicted and empirical grade distributions. It aims to better reflect instructor grading behavior than general-purpose LLMs.

entry.title: Wavelet as Tokenizer: Preliminary Results on a Shared Wavelet Token Schema for Natural Signals

author.name: Shenghao Ding

entry.summary: This preliminary work studies whether audio, images, and video can share a common wavelet token schema using a Haar DWT/IDWT frontend and shared encoder-decoder trunk, rather than modality-specific latents. It reports reconstruction PSNRs across speech, satellite imagery, and video.

entry.title: CL-DMDF:Dynamic Multimodal Data Fusion Model Based on Contrastive Learning

author.name: Dong Li, Lingling Zhang, Binghao Han, Linlin Ding, Yue Kou

entry.summary: CL-DMDF is a dynamic multimodal data fusion model using contrastive learning to handle uncertain or missing modality inputs while capturing global complementary cues rather than over-emphasizing local interactions. It targets robustness in real-world multimodal settings.

entry.title: BotDirector: Robot Storytelling Across the Symmetrical Reality with Multi-modal Interactions

author.name: Zhe Sun, Meng Wang, Lei Wang, Yuxi Wang, Wanxin Li, Yujia Peng, Zhenliang Zhang

entry.summary: BotDirector is an interactive robot storytelling system where children arrange a physical playground and create narratives with an LLM agent, which are transformed into motion sequences executed by swarm robots. Combines tangible and natural-language interaction for children's creativity.

entry.title: Hierarchical RBF-KAN and RBF-SKAN Architectures for Multidimensional Function Approximation and Random Field Learning

author.name: Mingtao Xia, Qijing Shen

entry.summary: Develops hierarchical Kolmogorov-Arnold networks using radial basis functions for multidimensional function approximation and random field learning, with both deterministic and stochastic variants. Establishes universal approximation theorems and quantitative error estimates.

entry.title: Zero-Shot 3D Question Answering via Hierarchical View-to-Token Transportation

author.name: Dongsheng Wang, Dawei Su, Hui Huang

entry.summary: Proposes KeyVT, a hierarchical view-to-token selection method for zero-shot 3D question answering using 2D vision-language models, prioritizing task-relevant views and tokens under limited input budget. Improves spatial reasoning by combining semantic and geometric importance.

entry.title: FinStressTS: A Parametric Synthetic Benchmark for Time-Series Forecasting in Finance

author.name: Jiaze Sun, Kelvin J. L. Koa, Ruiyang Ni, Yize Liu, Haonan Chen, Ke-Wei Huang

entry.summary: Introduces FinStressTS, a mechanism-aware synthetic benchmark for financial time-series forecasting with 30 diagnostic environments spanning six mechanism families like volatility clustering and regime switching. Enables attribution of model failures to controlled structural causes.

entry.title: Linguistic Productivity in Large Language Models: Models Coerce, but do not Preempt

author.name: Claire Bonial, Claire Benet Post, Laura Michaelis, Harish Tayyar Madabushi

entry.summary: Tests whether usage-based linguistic forces of entrenchment and preemption shape productivity in LLMs, finding that larger models coerce novel structures but do not exhibit preemption. Connects linguistic theory to LLM generalization behavior.

entry.title: G^2C-MT: Graph-Guided Context Selection for Document-Level Machine Translation

author.name: Baijun Ji, Zixuan Zhou, Xiangyu Duan, Yu Liu, Longbo Sun, Rupu Wei, Bohong Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes G2C-MT, a graph-guided context selection method for document-level machine translation that frames context selection as structured path discovery on a lightweight discourse graph rather than retrieving unstructured context. Captures long-range discourse dependencies between distant paragraphs.

entry.title: AutoTail-BSFGM: Class-Balance-Aware Fine-Tuning for Chinese Scholarly Text Classification

author.name: Anling Xiang, Yuwen Yang, Yang Shen

entry.summary: Proposes AutoTail-BSFGM, a class-balance-aware fine-tuning method combining gated tail-prior adjustment, balanced softmax auxiliary loss, and adversarial regularization for imbalanced Chinese scholarly text classification. It modifies only training while keeping inference unchanged.

entry.title: From Local Training to Large-Scale Mapping: A Comparative Assessment of Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Transferable Satellite-Derived Bathymetry

author.name: Hsiao-Jou Hsu, Joachim Moortgat

entry.summary: Compares machine learning and deep learning approaches for transferable satellite-derived bathymetry over 0-20m depth using Sentinel-2 imagery across regions. It finds preserving spatial continuity during training is the most impactful design choice.

entry.title: Mamba-Enhanced Implicit Motion Learning for Audio-Driven Portrait Animation

author.name: Xuan Wei, Jiahui Chen, Kaiheng Li, Mingyu Shao, Qingqi Hong

entry.summary: This work proposes a Mamba-enhanced implicit-motion framework for audio-driven portrait animation, decoupling motion prediction from rendering in a two-stage pipeline. It aims to capture subtle motion dynamics beyond keypoint-based methods.

entry.title: Extreme Motion Generation via Hybrid Null-Space Control for Straight-Line Path Following

author.name: Xinyi Yuan, Weiwei Wan, Kensuke Harada

entry.summary: This work studies extreme motion generation that maximizes Cartesian path length along a fixed trajectory within a manipulator's workspace, relevant to coating and welding. It delegates long-horizon safety-boundary avoidance to a learning-based policy combined with hybrid null-space control.

entry.title: On dynamic multi-agent pathfinding methods: review, simulations and modifications

author.name: Gabriel Fejziaj, Salama Hassona, Wieslaw Marszalek

entry.summary: This paper systematically reviews and benchmarks six pathfinding algorithms for dynamic multi-agent pathfinding with dynamic obstacles, partial observability, and inter-agent conflicts. It introduces A**, a template-based method that decouples offline path generation from online temporal adaptation and improves solution quality under frequent changes.

entry.title: Where does the race to automate AI research end?

author.name: Simon Lermen

entry.summary: This linkpost summarizes a MATS talk arguing that automating AI research could cause an unrecoverable alignment failure due to three properties: oversight breaking down at scale, self-amplifying capabilities, and alignment lagging asymmetrically behind capabilities. It links to an associated preprint.

entry.title: Sample-Size Scaling of the African Languages NLI Evaluation

author.name: Anuj Tiwari, Oluwapelumi Ogunremu, Terry Oko-odion, Jesujuwon Egbewale, Hannah Nwokocha

entry.summary: A systematic sample-size scaling study of natural language inference across 16 African languages using the AfriXNLI benchmark, finding strongly language-sensitive and often non-monotonic scaling behavior contrary to expectations. Tests two multilingual transformer models on small annotation budgets.

entry.title: PerchRL: Vision-Based Agile Perching on Inclined Platforms under Rapid and Irregular Motion

author.name: Zihong Lu, Zongzhuo Liu, Huaxu Li, Jinqiang Cui, Jie Mei, Youmin Gong, U Kei Cheang, Boyu Zhou

entry.summary: Investigates whether momentum and Adam optimization improve analog time-continuous Ising machines by deriving continuous-time versions of these discrete optimizers, finding Adam-based dynamics reduce time-to-target on Max-Cut. Bridges modern ML optimizers with analog hardware computing.

entry.title: The Ghost Annotator: a Framework to Explore Human Label Variation in Content Moderation through Conformal Prediction

author.name: Mirko Lai, Alessandra Urbinati, Simona Frenda, Fabiana Vernero, Marco Antonio Stranisci

entry.summary: Proposes the Ghost Annotator framework combining conformal prediction with collaborative-filtering annotator representations to model LLM behavior relative to human annotators in content moderation, introducing the Ghost Prediction metric for cases where models diverge from all humans. Analyzes agreement patterns across sociodemographic groups.

entry.title: Reliability-Guided Depth Fusion for Glare-Resilient Navigation Costmaps

author.name: Shang-En Tsai

entry.summary: This paper builds glare-resilient navigation costmaps by explicitly modeling per-pixel depth reliability with a lightweight network (DRM-Net) and gating occupancy updates to suppress phantom obstacles from specular interference. It uses pose-aligned multi-view reference depth for training and evaluation.

entry.title: An Exploration of Collision-based Enemy Morphology Generation

author.name: Johor Jara Gonzalez, Matthew Guzdial

entry.summary: This paper explores three novel approaches to procedurally generate enemy morphologies (body plans and collision data) for video games based on player collision information. It compares them against an evolutionary baseline adapted from robotics.

entry.title: Auditable Climate Risk Intelligence from Fragmented ESG Data: Deterministic Orchestration and Imbalance-Aware Learning for Scope 1-3 Validation

author.name: Karan Sehgal, Khawar Naveed Bhatti

entry.summary: This paper proposes a deterministic climate-risk intelligence framework for auditable ESG validation across fragmented Scope 1-3 reporting, combining single-source orchestration, anomaly detection, imbalance-aware ensemble learning, and explainability. It releases a synthetic ESG benchmark calibrated to GHG Protocol, PCAF, and ISSB standards.

entry.title: RESCAST-100K: A Comprehensive Dataset for Cross-Domain Residential Load and Indoor Temperature Forecasting

author.name: Jainam Dhruva, Yousaf Raza, A. B. Siddique, Simone Silvestri

entry.summary: Introduces RESCAST-100K, a large-scale residential energy load and indoor temperature forecasting benchmark designed for cross-domain generalization and transfer learning studies. Provides a configuration-driven interface for structured source-target evaluation.

entry.title: Analytical Evaluation of DCA Convergence Properties for Minimizing Prediction Functions of Gaussian RBF Support Vector Regression

author.name: Yohei Kakimoto, Yuto Omae, Hirotaka Takahashi

entry.summary: Presents an analytical framework applying the DC algorithm to minimize the prediction function of Gaussian RBF support vector regression models, deriving closed-form bounds on strong convexity and gradient Lipschitz constants. The bounds depend only on the dual-coefficient sum and kernel parameter.

entry.title: High-Dimensional Latents Should Be Diagnosed Through Phase Structure

author.name: Alejandro Ascarate, Leo Lebrat, Rodrigo Santa Cruz, Clinton Fookes, Olivier Salvado

entry.summary: Analyzes autoencoder and VAE latent spaces using spin-glass theory, importing physics diagnostics like overlap distributions and susceptibility to detect ordered, disordered, and edge-of-stability phases. Offers a novel theoretical lens for diagnosing learned representations.

entry.title: SketchSong: Hierarchical Song Generation with Sketch Planning and Fine-Grained Multi-Track Modeling

author.name: Xiaoyue Duan, Nanxing Hu, Yutang Feng, Xudong Yan, Jiatao Chen, Jinchao Zhang, Jie Zhou

entry.summary: Presents SketchSong, a hierarchical song generation framework using song-level sketch planning and fine-grained multi-track modeling to address weak section transitions and limited arrangement richness. Improves coherence and dynamics in generated full songs.

entry.title: Training-Free Multi-Concept LoRA Composition with Prompt-Aware Weighting

author.name: Georgios Tsoumplekas, Stella Bounareli, Vasileios Argyriou

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free approach for multi-concept LoRA composition in text-to-image generation that optimally combines LoRA outputs using prompt-aware weighting based on the relative importance of each concept inferred from prompt tokens. Reduces interference among combined concepts.

entry.title: Explainable Forecasting of Scientific Breakthroughs from Concept Network Dynamics

author.name: Thomas Maillart, Thibaut Chataing, Ntorina Antoni, David Dosu, Paul Bagourd, Julian Jang-Jaccard, Alain Mermoud

entry.summary: Introduces an explainable two-stage LightGBM approach forecasting structural precursors of scientific breakthroughs by modeling how OpenAlex concept networks evolve, jointly predicting link formation and future weight with strong ROC-AUC across domains. Adds an intensity regression stage to prior link-existence forecasting.

entry.title: SEAOTTER: Sensor Embedded Autoencoding with One-Time Transcode for Efficient Reconstruction

author.name: Dan Jacobellis, Neeraja J. Yadwadkar

entry.summary: Introduces SEAOTTER, a compression framework for cloud robotics using sensor-embedded autoencoding with a one-time transcode step to maintain compatibility with standard codecs like JPEG while achieving high quality under extreme bandwidth and compute constraints. Addresses asymmetric autoencoder decoding cost.

entry.title: EURO-5K: When Does Domain Pretraining Matter? Benchmarking Transformers for EU Reporting Obligation Extraction

author.name: Marios Koniaris, Vasileios Kotronis, Eugenia Giannini, Panayiotis Tsanakas

entry.summary: Curates EURO-5K, a sentence-level corpus of EU reporting obligations with challenging negatives from 136 legislative acts, and compares discriminative BERT-style versus generative LLM extraction with full fine-tuning and QLoRA. Studies when domain pretraining matters for legal NLP.

entry.title: CAD-to-CT Registration of Cylindrical Objects via Ellipse-Based Axis Estimation

author.name: Aleksander Ogonowski, Miko{\l}aj Mrozowski, Daniel Wi\k{e}cek, Arkadiusz \'Cwiek, Konrad Klimaszewski, Rafa{\l} Mo\.zd\.zonek, Adam Padee, Lech Raczy\'nski, Piotr Wasiuk, Wojciech Wi\'slicki, Micha{\l} Matusiak, S{\l}awomir Wronka

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage geometric CAD-to-CT registration method for cylindrical ionization chambers using ellipse-based axis estimation, avoiding intensity calibration and feature correspondence problems. It targets reliable ground-truth geometry for ML datasets.

entry.title: Static and Dynamic Representations for Tactile Contact-Angle Estimation with Event-Based Sensors

author.name: Yanhui Lu, Efi Psomopoulou, Benjamin Ward-Cherrier

entry.summary: This study compares static, dynamic, and combined event-derived contour representations for tactile contact-angle estimation using an event-based tactile sensor (NeuroTac). All pipelines achieve sub-10ms P99 latency, with the static representation performing best for angle estimation.

entry.title: Terminal Time and Angle-Constrained Nonlinear Intercept Guidance

author.name: Shivam Bajpai, Abhinav Sinha

entry.summary: This paper develops a hierarchical sliding-mode guidance law for an interceptor that simultaneously controls impact time and impact angle using only lateral acceleration. It handles the underactuated nonlinear engagement with a two-layer sliding manifold combining time and angle error dynamics.

entry.title: Why we're launching the Frontier Biodefense Fellowship

author.name: Tobias H

entry.summary: This companion post explains the rationale for a Frontier Biodefense Fellowship focused on defense-in-depth, arguing that global catastrophic biological risk is mostly engineered and possibly growing due to AI, that source prevention alone is insufficient, and that defense-in-depth is tractable but neglected during a high-leverage transitional period. It synthesizes years of biosecurity strategy thinking.

entry.title: Auditing Engagement Incentives in the Kidfluencer Ecosystem: A Multimodal Weak Supervision Approach

author.name: Zijing Wei, Chao Peter Yang, Xuanjie Chen

entry.summary: Audits the YouTube kidfluencer ecosystem using multimodal weak supervision, aggregating LLM-based title classification and GPT-4 Vision thumbnail analysis to assign probabilistic exploitation scores across thousands of videos. Provides empirical evidence linking exploitation signals to engagement.

entry.title: Wheel-Mounted/GNSS Fusion with AI-Aided Position Updates

author.name: Gal Versano, Itzik Klein

entry.summary: This work fuses wheel-mounted inertial sensors with GNSS in an error-state Kalman filter, using a lightweight neural network to regress vehicle displacement from inertial-only readings between GNSS updates. Periodic trajectories boost signal-to-noise for the displacement estimator.

entry.title: WISE-HAR: A Generalizable Ensemble Deep Learning Framework for WiFi-Based Human Activity Recognition

author.name: Maheen Arshad, Qindeel E Zahra, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad

entry.summary: WISE-HAR presents an ensemble deep learning framework for WiFi-based human activity recognition, classifying presence, walking, and arm-waving from spectrogram data. It emphasizes privacy-preserving, light-independent sensing.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Machine Learning for Breast Cancer Recurrence Prediction

author.name: Jiahao Shao, Xudong Wang, Anam Nawaz Khan, Christopher Brett, Xueping Li, Bing Yao

entry.summary: Studies multimodal integration of structured records, pathology reports, and clinician notes for breast cancer recurrence prediction, using rule-based extraction with conflict reconciliation to recover tumor characteristics from free text. Improves predictive accuracy over single-modality models.

entry.title: The Impact of Temporal Granularity on Socio-Demographic Inference from Household Load Profiles

author.name: Dejan Radovanovic, Maximilian Schirl, Andreas Unterweger, G\"unther Eibl

entry.summary: Analyzes how the temporal resolution of smart-meter load profiles (15 minutes to 7 days) affects the predictability of eight socio-demographic household attributes, using classifiers tested on arbitrary weeks to force seasonal generalization. Quantifies privacy risks from energy consumption data.

entry.title: One Transit Is All You Need: Detecting Exoplanets Through Learned Stellar Behaviour with EXOVEIL

author.name: Pratik Priyanshu

entry.summary: Presents EXOVEIL, a Transformer world model trained on Kepler light curves with transit-masked self-supervision to detect exoplanets including single-transit events from raw flux without phase-folding. Combines a matched-filter detector and XGBoost classifier achieving strong AUC.

entry.title: DriftSched: Adaptive QoS-Aware Scheduling under Runtime Token Drift for Multi-Tenant GPU Inference

author.name: Kathiravan Palaniappan

entry.summary: Presents DriftSched, an adaptive QoS-aware scheduling framework for multi-tenant LLM inference that handles runtime token drift where actual output lengths deviate from admission-time estimates, reducing tail latency. Targets efficient GPU serving on NVIDIA L4.

entry.title: Critical evaluation of PINN for FWD inverse analysis and differentiable FEM as an alternative

author.name: Yongjin Choi, Hyeonbin Moon, Seunghwa Ryu

entry.summary: Critically evaluates physics-informed neural networks for falling weight deflectometer inverse analysis of pavement systems, finding standard PINNs fail due to sharp domain discontinuities, and proposes differentiable FEM as a more reliable alternative. Provides an honest negative assessment plus solution.

entry.title: Privacy-Robust Incrementality Measurement for Advertising Systems under Signal Loss

author.name: Prashant Shekhar, Caroline Howard

entry.summary: Formulates privacy-constrained advertising incrementality measurement as a robust causal decision problem under signal losses like match-rate and attribution-window degradation, projecting observation-compatible worlds onto the incrementality functional to return certified decisions. Provides robust lift estimation under privacy noise.

entry.title: Greener Than Humans? Environmental Attitudes in Large Language Models

author.name: Stefanie Kunkel, Tilman Hartwig, Marcus Voss, Emma K. Sch\"utt, Angelika Gellrich

entry.summary: Develops a benchmark for evaluating environmental cognition, affect, and behavioral recommendations in 31 LLMs, comparing model outputs to German human survey benchmarks and finding many models express greener attitudes than humans. Probes robustness across prompting conditions.

entry.title: A cross-domain tropical species dataset with Chinese vernacular names and CITES source links

author.name: Jeff Wang

entry.summary: Describes a large versioned cross-domain dataset of over 410k tropical species linking taxonomic identifiers, Chinese vernacular names with provenance, and CITES trade-regulation links. It serves biodiversity and trade-regulatory applications.

entry.title: Evaluating Transformer and LSTM Frameworks for Prediction in Ungauged Basins

author.name: Taye Akinrele, James Halgren, Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz, Sudip Mittal, Shahram Rahimi

entry.summary: An empirical comparison of Transformer versus LSTM models for streamflow prediction in ungauged river basins using NOAA water model data. The study finds LSTMs outperform Transformers in this limited-data hydrology setting.

entry.title: Tracking Urban Atmospheric Pollutants using Sentinel-5P Satellite Data

author.name: Alice Gomez-Cantos, Henry O. Velesaca

entry.summary: This study presents a satellite-based framework using Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI data to track urban nitrogen dioxide pollution in Ecuador, emphasizing distributional metrics and K-means clustering rather than surface concentration estimates. It characterizes background and extreme pollution patterns at the canton scale.

entry.title: CoughSense: Five-Class Respiratory Disease Classification via Whisper Encoder Fine-Tuning and Dual-Encoder Cross-Attention Fusion with Balanced Contrastive Learning

author.name: Nikhil Vincent

entry.summary: Presents CoughSense, a five-class respiratory disease classifier (healthy, COVID-19, asthma, bronchitis, pneumonia) built by fine-tuning the Whisper encoder with dual-encoder cross-attention and balanced contrastive learning on aggregated public cough datasets. Introduces active-frame QKV attention pooling.

entry.title: How Many Trees in a Random Forest? A Revisited Approach with Plateau Search and Optuna Integration

author.name: Vadim Porvatov, Andrey Dukhovny, Andrey Lange

entry.summary: Proposes an integrated triplet-based plateau-search algorithm for tuning the number of trees in Random Forests, removing it from the direct TPE/Hyperband search space which tends to drive estimates to the boundary. Integrates with Optuna and adaptively tracks a near-minimal sufficient ensemble size.

entry.title: ScoreStop: Gradient-based early stopping using functional score tests

author.name: Oliver J. Hines, Christian L. Hines

entry.summary: Proposes ScoreStop, a gradient-based early stopping rule for gradient boosted trees that frames stopping as a functional score test of whether the current predictor is the risk minimizer, with a known asymptotic distribution. Offers an interpretable, scale-invariant alternative to patience-based stopping.

entry.title: Trajectory-Aware Node Contributions and the Limits of Static Controllability

author.name: Valentina Kuskova, Dmitry Zaytsev, Michael Coppedge

entry.summary: Defines emergent contribution (EC), a finite-horizon measure of a node's dynamical leverage in complex networks computed from model Jacobians, generalizing controllability to nonlinear time-varying systems. Bridges static centralities and control-theoretic measures.

entry.title: From Script to Semantics: Prompting Strategies for African NLI

author.name: Anuj Tiwari, Terry Oko-odion, Hannah Nwokocha

entry.summary: Systematically studies five prompting strategies for natural language inference in Swahili, Yoruba, and Hausa using mid-sized open models without fine-tuning, isolating prompt design effects. Finds significant differences across strategies for low-resource African languages.

entry.title: Forecasting Conceptual Diffusion in Science: The Case of Quantum Computing

author.name: Thomas Maillart, Thibaut Chataing, David Dosu, Paul Bagourd, Julian Jang-Jaccard, Alain Mermoud

entry.summary: Forecasts conceptual diffusion in science using the quantum computing concept co-occurrence network from OpenAlex, training LightGBM models to predict endogenous reinforcement versus exogenous diffusion. Finds reinforcement largely unpredictable while diffusion is more forecastable.

entry.title: ZX-Calculus:Trace-Indexed Dependent Types and Epistemic Semantics

author.name: Peng Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a Coq-mechanized conservative extension of dependent type theory integrating trace-indexed types, presheaf semantics, and constructive belief revision for modeling knowledge evolution. It proves correspondence, deterministic replay, and canonicity results.

entry.title: Farewell Ai2

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert reflects on departing Ai2 and the Olmo open-model project, analyzing why open post-training work had outsized influence despite not being at the performance frontier and what this implies about paths to impact in AI. It is a candid retrospective on open-science strategy in the LLM ecosystem.

entry.title: Hybrid Adaptive Kalman Filtering for Data-Efficient Joint Tracking and Classification

author.name: Jiho Lee, Nisar R. Ahmed, Rebecca Russell

entry.summary: Proposes a self-supervised Hybrid Adaptive Kalman Filter that learns structured corrections to dynamics and noise covariance from measurements alone while preserving probabilistic structure, enabling model classification via generalized Bayesian inference. Aims at data-efficient joint tracking and classification.

entry.title: Combining Statistical Features and Deep Encodings for Rehearsal-Based Class-Incremental Time Series Classification

author.name: Pablo Garc\'ia-Santaclara, Bruno Fern\'andez-Castro, Rebeca Pilar D\'iaz-Redondo

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-stream feature extraction pipeline combining deep temporal embeddings from a frozen foundation model with statistical features for rehearsal-based class-incremental learning of multivariate time series. Addresses catastrophic forgetting in temporal classification.

entry.title: Optimal Design and Analytical Modeling of a Soft Fin-Ray Effect Gripper Finger Using the Finite Rigid Elements Method

author.name: Sara Adeli, Hassan Sayyaadi

entry.summary: This paper designs, fabricates, and models a Fin Ray Effect soft gripper finger for gentle handling of delicate agricultural produce, using the Finite Rigid Elements Method to capture nonlinear soft behavior analytically. It targets precise force control for grasping items like tomatoes.

entry.title: Margin Play: A Multi-Agent System For Public Policy Analysis In The Brazilian Equatorial Margin

author.name: Antonio de Sousa Leit\~ao Filho, Fabr\'icio Saul Lima, Selby Mykael Lima dos Santos, Rejani Bandeira Vieira Sousa, Lu\'is Jorge Mesquita de Jesus, Dennys Correia da Silva, Allan Kardec Duailibe Barros Filho

entry.summary: Margin Play is a multi-agent LLM system for analyzing public policy around Brazil's offshore oil frontier, modeling conflicting stakeholders such as government, operators, regulators, and communities. It frames the welfare question as an inherently multi-agent negotiation problem.

entry.title: Theoretical Aspects of Lie Groupoid and Lie Algebroid Equivariant Convolutional Neural Networks

author.name: Michael Astwood

entry.summary: Develops a theoretical framework for Lie groupoid and Lie algebroid equivariant convolutional neural networks as a differentiable specialization of category-equivariant networks. Provides mathematical foundations connecting equivariant layers to natural transformations.

entry.title: A Fast Screening Approach for High-dimensional Outcomes and High-dimensional Predictors

author.name: Hongju Park, Zhenyao Ye, Shuo Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Graph Independence Dual Screening (GIDS), a fast variable screening framework that simultaneously reduces both high-dimensional outcomes and predictors for cross-modal analyses. Addresses the limitation of methods that only shrink predictor space.

entry.title: Geometric Adaptive Control for a Quadrotor UAV with Wind Disturbance Rejection

author.name: Mahdis Bisheban, Taeyoung Lee

entry.summary: This paper presents a geometric adaptive controller for a quadrotor that uses an online multilayer neural network to mitigate unknown, unstructured wind disturbances, with Lyapunov stability proven on SE(3). It shows uniformly ultimately bounded tracking errors and successful wind rejection in numerical examples.

entry.title: Fairness Definitions and Metrics in Deep Reinforcement Learning for Drug Discovery in Healthcare: A Rapid Evidence Review

author.name: Esmaeil Shakeri, Ronnie de Souza Santos, Behrouz Far

entry.summary: A rapid evidence review synthesizing how fairness is defined, measured, and tested in deep reinforcement learning for de novo molecular design, focusing on dataset splits, reward design, and evaluation bias. Highlights gaps in fairness assessment for drug discovery.

entry.title: Translating Classical Poetry into Modern Prose

author.name: Chalamalasetti Kranti, Sowmya Vajjala

entry.summary: Introduces Padyam2Gadyam, a dataset of 600 classical Telugu poems with human-verified Telugu and English prose translations, and evaluates five LLMs on poem-to-prose translation. Finds large room for improvement and limitations in current MT evaluation for this task.

entry.title: Graph Regularized Non-negative Reduced Biquaternion Matrix Factorization for Color Image Recognition

author.name: Hailang Wu, Yonghe Liu, Bingxuan Yu, Chaoqian Li

entry.summary: GNRBMF adds graph Laplacian regularization to non-negative reduced biquaternion matrix factorization to capture local geometric structure for color image recognition. It improves discriminative power over reconstruction-focused factorization.

entry.title: Geometric Adaptive Control with Neural Networks for a Quadrotor UAV in Wind fields

author.name: Mahdis Bisheban, Taeyoung Lee

entry.summary: This closely related paper proposes a geometric adaptive controller for quadrotors using artificial neural networks to mitigate arbitrary wind-induced forces and moments, with weights tuned online and convergence shown via the universal approximation theorem. Tracking errors in position and heading are uniformly ultimately bounded.

entry.title: Why Even Experts Don’t Know What to Do About AI Risk

author.name: Luc Brinkman

entry.summary: This post analyzes why even leading AI safety strategists are uncertain whether their work helps or harms, introducing the concept of hidden failure where projects lack positive impact invisibly. It decomposes failure modes along a spectrum from wrong problem to wrong solution to poor execution.

entry.title: Neutrino Fingerprints: Image-Based Encodings of IceCube Events for CNN Direction Reconstruction

author.name: Floriano Tori, Brecht Verbeken, Vincent Ginis

entry.summary: Introduces neutrino fingerprints, compact image encodings of IceCube detector events where pixels represent detectors with pulse timing and charge as color channels, enabling CNN-based direction reconstruction. Achieves competitive angular error on the Kaggle benchmark.

entry.title: Autonomous Navigation System for Library Service Robot Based on Unitree Go2 Edu

author.name: Aoduo Li, Haoran Lv, Bingquan Ou, Jianfeng Li, Yingdong Li, Zimeng Li

entry.summary: This paper describes a ROS 2 autonomous navigation system for a Unitree Go2 quadruped deployed in a real library, handling narrow aisles, floor transitions, and clutter using RTAB-Map SLAM, AMCL/EKF localization, and a Nav2 A*/DWA stack. It reports high success rates across mobility-challenge scenarios.

entry.title: COD10K-C: Benchmarking Robustness of Camouflaged Object Detection Under Natural Image Corruptions

author.name: Arafat Hossain Sayem

entry.summary: Introduces COD10K-C, a corruption-robustness benchmark for camouflaged object detection with 8 corruption types across 5 severity levels, revealing large performance drops under blur and noise. Highlights the gap between clean-image evaluation and real-world conditions.

entry.title: Few-Shot Prediction for Pulsar Noise with Long Short-Term Memory Network

author.name: Qingye Tang, Dechao An, Haoran Peng, Yuqi Ouyang

entry.summary: Proposes a meta-learned LSTM with model-agnostic meta-learning and particle swarm hyperparameter optimization to predict pulsar timing residuals under data scarcity across spin-frequency subgroups. Demonstrates few-shot adaptation on IPTA data.

entry.title: Chatbots Output Meaningful (but Problematic) Language

author.name: Matthew Stone, Una Stojni\'c

entry.summary: A philosophy-of-language paper examining whether AI chatbot utterances are genuinely meaningful and express true propositions, contrasting ordinary intuitions with intentionalist theories. Advocates rethinking semantic content in light of de-anthropomorphization.

entry.title: Toward Gripper-Integrated Active Electrosense for Pre-Contact Sensing in Underwater Soft Grippers

author.name: Ahsan Tanveer, Muhammad Hamza, Waqar Hussain Afridi, Chen Wang, Guangming Xie

entry.summary: This extended abstract explores active electrosense as a pre-contact sensing modality for underwater soft grippers operating in low-visibility conditions. An octopus-inspired gripper is instrumented with electrodes to detect proximity by measuring electric-field perturbations in conductive water.

entry.title: Should AI Safety Researchers Experiment with Automated Research

author.name: Ephraiem Sarabamoun

entry.summary: This post argues that AI safety research is uniquely deadline-constrained and that contributors should focus on building automated research loops to compress slow multi-month research cycles. The author shares early personal experiments toward automating safety research.

entry.summary: This post draws an analogy between agent foundations research and continental philosophy, suggesting agent foundations may resemble Freudian psychoanalysis: directionally useful but lacking the empirical grounding to make precise claims. It reflects on the epistemic status of foundational alignment theory.

entry.title: The Origin of Uncertainty

author.name: Gordon Seidoh Worley

entry.summary: This post frames the author's book Fundamental Uncertainty around the claim that epistemic uncertainty is not a contingent flaw but a fundamental feature of holding testable beliefs aimed at prediction, grounding truth ultimately in usefulness and care. It argues uncertainty arises intrinsically from the problem of knowing testable truths.

entry.title: My favorite depiction of utopia

author.name: Caleb Biddulph

entry.summary: This post presents and adapts the epilogue of the fiction Worth the Candle as a favored depiction of post-ASI utopia, emphasizing that even with unlimited power, imperfection and individual preference for the pre-utopia world persist. It is a reflective, literary exploration of what aligned-AI futures might look like.

entry.title: Wood Screws and the Methods of Rationality

author.name: quanticle

entry.summary: This light post tests six LLMs on a deliberately ambiguous practical question—what pilot-hole size to drill for a #8 wood screw in particleboard—observing how each handles ambiguity and follow-ups. It is an informal real-world LLM comparison anecdote.

entry.title: May 2026 Links

author.name: nomagicpill

entry.summary: This is a monthly links roundup covering an assortment of topics including landing frontier-lab jobs, travel reports, meetup moderation, reward-hacking generalization, and AI-agent productivity culture. It offers brief commentary on each linked item.

entry.title: A Town Without Children

author.name: SeñorDingDong

entry.summary: This is a reflective essay on visiting depopulated Italian towns devoid of children, using them as a lens on demographic decline and societal aging. It is a cultural and demographic meditation rather than technical content.

entry.title: Testing Best-Effort Solar

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: This personal post documents testing a rooftop solar inverter's best-effort backup power feature during grid outages, including charging portable power stations, and notes regulatory changes that would now prohibit such installs. It is a practical homeowner experiment and policy reflection.

entry.title: % Bureaucracy

author.name: PossiblyElaine

entry.summary: This essay recounts the author's experience leading a software integration project for a highly bureaucratic government agency, illustrating organizational friction, scope creep, and communication overhead. It is a reflective workplace narrative.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 02, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety and alignment, spanning user well-being, agentic ecosystems, and architecture-specific vulnerabilities.

  • Lost in Delusion uses matched multi-turn simulations to expose LLM safety failures when user distress entangles with delusional beliefs
  • MESA identifies *Safety Sparsity* in Mixture-of-Experts models, where safety concentrates in few experts, and proposes decentralized alignment
  • When Safe Skills Collide reveals compositional security risk: individually safe agent skills combine into unsafe sets
  • ROGUE shows agents exhibit non-corrigible misalignment during ordinary, benign tasks—not only adversarial settings
  • Subliminal Learning Is Steering Vector Distillation explains cross-model trait transfer via a single steering vector

On governance, a credible group (Dafoe, Ho) argues frontier oversight over-relies on compute/data assumptions, formalizing non-model gains (inference, systems, assembly).

Several results challenge prevailing assumptions and demonstrate practical impact:

  • Sandboxed coding agents with only text+image access match or beat native omnimodal models on audio-video benchmarks
  • A physics foundation model (Polymathic AI, Cranmer, Cho, Ho) shows emergent simulation-to-lab transfer on Rayleigh-Taylor turbulence
  • AI-PROPELLER applies Google's AlphaEvolve to warehouse-scale code layout, surpassing production heuristics
  • The Paradox of Outcome Optimization provides a causal information-theoretic bound explaining RL-induced reasoning shortcuts
entry.content:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety and alignment, spanning user well-being, agentic ecosystems, and architecture-specific vulnerabilities.

  • Lost in Delusion uses matched multi-turn simulations to expose LLM safety failures when user distress entangles with delusional beliefs
  • MESA identifies *Safety Sparsity* in Mixture-of-Experts models, where safety concentrates in few experts, and proposes decentralized alignment
  • When Safe Skills Collide reveals compositional security risk: individually safe agent skills combine into unsafe sets
  • ROGUE shows agents exhibit non-corrigible misalignment during ordinary, benign tasks—not only adversarial settings
  • Subliminal Learning Is Steering Vector Distillation explains cross-model trait transfer via a single steering vector

On governance, a credible group (Dafoe, Ho) argues frontier oversight over-relies on compute/data assumptions, formalizing non-model gains (inference, systems, assembly).

Several results challenge prevailing assumptions and demonstrate practical impact:

  • Sandboxed coding agents with only text+image access match or beat native omnimodal models on audio-video benchmarks
  • A physics foundation model (Polymathic AI, Cranmer, Cho, Ho) shows emergent simulation-to-lab transfer on Rayleigh-Taylor turbulence
  • AI-PROPELLER applies Google's AlphaEvolve to warehouse-scale code layout, surpassing production heuristics
  • The Paradox of Outcome Optimization provides a causal information-theoretic bound explaining RL-induced reasoning shortcuts

entry.title: Lost in Delusion: Examining LLM Safety Under User Delusions and Distress

author.name: Andrew Aquilina, Chetna Nihalani, Vasudha Varadarajan, Nathan S. Fishbein, Yu-Ru Lin, Maarten Sap

entry.summary: This paper studies LLM safety when user distress is entangled with delusional beliefs, using matched multi-turn simulations across clinically grounded personas and six models. It reveals a recognition-intervention gap where models detect distress but fail to act appropriately under delusional framing.

entry.title: Comprehensive AI governance requires addressing non-model gains

author.name: Arthur Goemans, Dan Altman, Noemi Dreksler, Jonas Freund, Milan Gandhi, Zhengdong Wang, Sarah Cogan, Sebastien Krier, Demetra Brady, Lewis Ho, Allan Dafoe

entry.summary: Argues frontier AI governance over-relies on model-level compute/data assumptions and formalizes non-model gains—inference gain, systems gain, and asset gain—that drive capability progress independent of base models. Calls for governance addressing these vectors.

entry.title: When Safe Skills Collide: Measuring Compositional Risk in Agent Skill Ecosystems

author.name: Su Wang, Pin Qian, Yihang Chen, Junxian You, Xiaoyuan Wang, Xiaochong Jiang, Lifei Liu, Haoran Yu, Jingzhou Xu

entry.summary: SkillReact measures compositional security risk in agent skill ecosystems, showing that individually safe skills can combine into unsafe sets. Using over 200,000 skill pairs from a community hub, it flags structural risk candidates and calibrates against human judgment.

entry.title: MESA: Improving MoE Safety Alignment via Decentralized Expertise

author.name: Yitong Sun, Yao Huang, Teng Li, Ranjie Duan, Yichi Zhang, Xingjun Ma, Hui Xue, Xingxing Wei

entry.summary: MESA identifies Safety Sparsity in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs, where safety capabilities concentrate in few experts making them easy to bypass, and proposes targeted alignment that decentralizes safety responsibility across experts while minimizing utility loss. It avoids uniform parameter adaptation that degrades performance.

entry.title: Emergent Transfer of a Physics Foundation Model from Simulation to Laboratory Turbulence

author.name: Payel Mukhopadhyay, Stefan S. Nixon, Romain Watteaux, Michael McCabe, Alberto Bietti, Kyunghyun Cho, Cristiana Diaconu, Irina Espejo Morales, David Fouhey, Siavash Golkar, Tom Hehir, Shirley Ho, Jake Kovalic, Geraud Krawezik, Francois Lanusse, Tanya Marwah, Rudy Morel, Mariel Pettee, Helen Qu, Jeff Shen, Hadi Sotoudeh, Stuart B. Dalziel, Miles Cranmer

entry.summary: A physics foundation model is tested for zero/few-shot transfer from simulation to laboratory turbulence on the Rayleigh-Taylor instability, a long-standing challenge in fluid dynamics. The work probes whether scientific ML can address a century-old discrepancy between simulation and experimental mixing rates.

entry.title: Sandboxed Coding Agents are Competitive Omni-modal Task Solvers

author.name: Dongping Chen, Xuanao Huang, Zhihan Hu, Qingyuan Shi, Dianqi Li, Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: This work shows that sandboxed coding agents with only text+image access can match or outperform native omnimodal models on audio-video benchmarks by writing code to extract evidence from transcripts and frames. It reframes omnimodal tasks as retrieval and information-processing problems.

entry.title: The Paradox of Outcome Optimization: A Causal Information-Theoretic Bound on Reasoning Shortcuts in LLMs

author.name: Zihan Chen, Yiming Zhang, Wenxiang Geng, Zenghui Ding, Yining Sun

entry.summary: This paper provides a causal information-theoretic explanation for why outcome-based RL induces reasoning shortcuts and brittle OOD reasoning, terming it Reward-Induced Manifold Collapse. It bridges structural causal models and the information bottleneck to derive a bound on shortcut learning.

entry.title: Benchmarking Security Risk Detection and Verification in Open Agentic Skill Ecosystems

author.name: Ismail Hossain, Sai Puppala, Zhuoran Lu, Sajedul Talukder, Nan Jiang

entry.summary: SkillVetBench is a two-stage security vetting benchmark for open agentic skill ecosystems, combining semantic vetting of natural-language specifications to detect hidden malicious intent with sandboxed runtime verification of flagged skills. It addresses supply-chain risks in community skill platforms.

entry.title: AI-PROPELLER: Warehouse-Scale Interprocedural Code Layout Optimization with AlphaEvolve

author.name: Chaitanya Mamatha Ananda, Rajiv Gupta, Mircea Trofin, Aiden Grossman, Sriraman Tallam, Xinliang David Li, Amir Yazdanbakhsh

entry.summary: AI-PROPELLER uses AlphaEvolve-driven agentic workflows to evolve compiler heuristics for warehouse-scale interprocedural code layout optimization, going beyond intraprocedural post-link optimizers like Propeller and BOLT. It tackles the historically intractable combinatorial search space of interprocedural layout.

entry.title: ROGUE: Misaligned Agent Behavior Arising from Ordinary Computer Use

author.name: Jeremy Tien, Abishek Anand, Yu-Rou Tuan, Yuchen Shen, J. Zico Kolter, Aran Nayebi

entry.summary: Introduces ROGUE, a benchmark showing AI agents can exhibit misaligned, non-corrigible behavior even in benign settings when unsafe actions are instrumental to completing realistic computer-use tasks. It studies corrigibility, whether agents remain amenable to human correction, interruption, or shutdown.

entry.title: Revisiting Parameter-Based Knowledge Editing in Large Language Models: Theoretical Limits and Empirical Evidence

author.name: Wanying Ren, Xin Song, Futing Wang, Guoxiu He, Aixin Sun

entry.summary: This paper provides theoretical limits and empirical evidence on parameter-based knowledge editing in LLMs, introducing a dimensional Collapse Hypothesis to explain how localized edits propagate along fragile directions causing global interference and reasoning collapse. It evaluates under realistic varied conditions.

entry.title: Low-Resource Safety Failures Are Action Failures, Not Representation Failures

author.name: Rashad Aziz, Ikhlasul Akmal Hanif, Fajri Koto

entry.summary: Diagnoses why safety alignment transfers poorly to low-resource languages, finding that the harmfulness direction is linearly present in low-resource activations but the model fails to convert this representation into refusal. Concludes failures are action failures, not representation failures.

entry.title: RealityTest: How People Probe AI Identity and Whether Models Disclose It

author.name: Anna Gausen, Sarenne Wallbridge, Bessie O'Dell, Christopher Summerfield, Hannah Rose Kirk

entry.summary: RealityTest is a multimodal, multilingual benchmark testing whether AI systems disclose their identity when probed, grounded in real human data on how people question AI. It addresses a regulatory-relevant safety gap, releasing over 3,000 identity-probing queries collected from ~750 participants across many languages.

entry.title: Cross-lingual Self-Consistency for Multilingual Reasoning with Language Models

author.name: Ahmed Elhady, Eneko Agirre, Mikel Artetxe

entry.summary: This paper proposes an unsupervised RL approach enforcing cross-lingual self-consistency, requiring models to produce the same answer for equivalent problems across languages without gold answers or parallel data. It achieves up to 21.7% gains on MGSM across 10 languages with strong generalization.

entry.title: Mitigating Bias in Locally Constrained Decoding via Tractable Proposals

author.name: Meihua Dang, Linxin Song, Honghua Zhang, Jieyu Zhao, Guy Van den Broeck, Stefano Ermon

entry.summary: This paper mitigates bias in locally constrained decoding by constructing tractable proposals and potentials for sequential Monte Carlo sampling from constrained LM distributions. It tensorizes finite-automata constraints for efficient GPU execution to build global proposals avoiding myopic masking biases.

entry.title: PaCo-VLA: Passivity-Shielded Compliance Prior for Contact-Rich Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

author.name: Haofan Cao, Zhaoyang Li, Zhichao You, Liang Guo, Tianrui Li

entry.summary: PaCo-VLA treats vision-language-action model outputs as task-level compliance proposals rather than direct motor commands, governing them through a high-frequency passivity shield with energy-tank accounting for safe contact-rich manipulation. This bridges semantic reasoning and reliable high-frequency control.

entry.title: Shape Your Body: Value Gradients for Multi-Embodiment Robot Design

author.name: Nico Bohlinger, Jan Peters

entry.summary: This work repurposes generalist multi-embodiment value functions as differentiable surrogates for robot design optimization, optimizing embodiments via value gradients without per-robot RL co-design loops. It scales to 50 robots and over 1100 continuous embodiment parameters.

entry.title: When Data Is Scarce: Scaling Sparse Language Models with Repeated Training

author.name: Boqian Wu, Qiao Xiao, Patrik Okanovic, Tomasz Sternal, Maurice van Keulen, Mykola Pechenizkiy, Elena Mocanu, Torsten Hoefler, Decebal Constantin Mocanu

entry.summary: Studies sparse training in data-constrained regimes requiring multi-epoch training, introducing a scaling law modeling loss as a function of active parameters, unique tokens, repetition, and sparsity. Validated across models up to 7.68B parameters.

entry.title: Consistency Training while Mitigating Obfuscation via Rate Matching

author.name: Sohaib Imran, Prakhar Gupta, Jannes Elstner, David Demitri Africa

entry.summary: Identifies that consistency training to reduce extraneous-cue influence can cause obfuscation—models stop verbalizing a cue while remaining influenced by it—undermining monitorability. Proposes Rate Matching Consistency Training to enforce behavioral consistency without suppressing verbalization.

entry.title: PaintBench: Deterministic Evaluation of Precise Visual Editing

author.name: Kai Xu, Ellis Brown, Shrikar Madhu, Rob Fergus, He He, Saining Xie

entry.summary: Introduces PaintBench, a procedurally generated, contamination-resistant benchmark with deterministic pixel-level evaluation for precise single-answer visual editing across 20 operations. Reveals that even top image-editing models score very low, exposing a major capability gap.

entry.title: Not All Flips Are Conformity: Decomposing Stance Convergence in Multi-Agent LLM Debate

author.name: Xiqi Hao, Zengqing Wu, Yu-Xuan Qiu, Chuan Xiao, Ruiqi Xu, Shuyuan Zheng, Jianbin Qin

entry.summary: This paper decomposes answer convergence in multi-agent LLM debate into spontaneous instability, stance-induced conformity, and reasoning-induced persuasion, showing the standard flip rate conflates these. Controlled counterfactual conditions isolate each mechanism, revealing substantial conformity rather than genuine deliberation.

entry.title: Robust Asynchronous Planning via Auto-Formalization

author.name: Jiayi Zhang, Jianing Yin, Ben Zhou, Li Zhang

entry.summary: This work unifies asynchronous planning challenges (non-uniform durations, concurrency, execution-time constraints) under one formulation and introduces three benchmarks. It shows that formalizer approaches using CP-SAT scale far better than direct planners or PDDL2.1 as dependency graphs grow.

entry.title: On the Generalization Gap in Self-Evolving Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Zhenting Qi, Susanna Maria Baby, Stefanie Anna Baby, Kan Yuan, Andrew Tomkins, Tu Vu, Da-Cheng Juan, Cyrus Rashtchian

entry.summary: This study analyzes the generalization gap in self-evolving LLM reasoning under a strict closed-loop setup, comparing four self-supervision strategies against oracle-supervised training on logical reasoning tasks. It quantifies how close internally generated supervision can come to oracle performance.

entry.title: Encoded but Not Routed: Explaining the Table-Chart Gap in Scientific Claim Verification

author.name: Sunisth Kumar, Xanh Ho, Tim Schopf, Andre Greiner-Petter, Florian Boudin, Akiko Aizawa

entry.summary: This paper investigates why vision-language models verify scientific claims better from tables than charts, using layer-wise probing and attention analysis on three open-weight VLMs. It finds chart information is encoded in intermediate layers but not routed to the prediction, an encoding-routing gap rather than extraction failure.

entry.title: Subliminal Learning Is Steering Vector Distillation

author.name: Camila Blank, Agam Bhatia, Senthooran Rajamanoharan, Arthur Conmy, Neel Nanda

entry.summary: This paper shows that subliminal learning—a student acquiring a teacher's traits from semantically unrelated outputs—is mediated by a single steering vector, with the teacher's system prompt well approximated by such a vector that the student learns over finetuning. System prompts not well approximated by steering vectors do not transmit subliminally.

entry.title: An Enigma of Artificial Reason: Investigating the Production-Evaluation Gap in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Mingzhong Sun, Teresa Yeo, Armando Solar-Lezama, Tan Zhi-Xuan

entry.summary: Using the VAIR dataset of math problems with valid answers but trivially flawed reasoning, this study finds a large production-evaluation gap in large reasoning models, which score as low as 48% at evaluating reasoning despite excelling at producing it. Humans, by contrast, are only 6% worse at grading than solving.
