author.name: Mingxuan Zhang, Jiahui Han, Dadi Guo, Songze Li, Guanchu Wang, Na Zou, Dongrui Liu, Xia Hu

entry.summary: Introduces PrivacyPeek, a benchmark auditing what LLM agents acquire into their context (not just what they disclose) across 1,182 cases, 7 acquisition behaviors, and 16 domains. It highlights over-acquisition of sensitive data as a precursor to leakage.

entry.title: InfoAtlas: A Foundation Model for Zero-Shot Statistical Dependence Estimate

author.name: Zhengyang Hu, Yanzhi Chen, Hanxiang Ren, Qunsong Zeng, Youyi Zheng, Adrian Weller, Kaibin Huang, Yanchao Yang

entry.summary: Introduces InfoAtlas, a foundation-model architecture for zero-shot mutual information estimation that infers statistical dependence in a single forward pass after pretraining on large-scale synthetic data. It eliminates the costly per-dataset iterative optimization of neural MI estimators.

entry.title: PR2: Predictive Routing Replay for MoE-Based LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Daize Dong, Junlin Chen, Haolong Jia, Jiawei Wu, Huanwei Di, Jiang Liu, Jialian Wu, Zhengzhong Liu, Zicheng Liu, Emad Barsoum, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Hongyi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Predictive Routing Replay (PR2) to stabilize RL training of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs by addressing router drift and staleness that cause rollout-training mismatch. It predicts how the router evolves under off-policy updates rather than simply freezing the replay route.

entry.title: GeoSAM-3D: Geodesic Prompt Propagation for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Segmentation from Monocular Video

author.name: Arun Sharma

entry.summary: GeoSAM-3D enables open-vocabulary 3D scene segmentation from a single monocular video by propagating user prompts via heat-kernel geodesic distance over a Gaussian-splat scene graph. The geodesic propagation preserves continuity on curved surfaces and reduces leakage across disconnected regions.

entry.title: Skill or Skip? Learning Selective Skill Invocation in Agentic Tasks via Dual-Granularity Preference Learning

author.name: Chishui Chen, Jiaye Lin, Te Sun, Junxi Wang, Yi Yang, Cong Qin, Yangen Hu, Lu Pan, Ke Zeng

entry.summary: SelSkill is a dual-granularity preference-learning framework that teaches agents whether a relevant skill should actually be invoked at a given decision point, not just which skill is relevant. It uses predictive uncertainty to prioritize decision points and builds invoke-skip preference pairs.

entry.title: On the Difficulty of Learning a Meta-network for Training Data Selection

author.name: Zilin Du, Junqi Zhao, Boyang Albert Li

entry.summary: This work analyzes why meta-learning for training-data selection often underperforms, identifying poor gradient signal-to-noise ratio and lack of quality-correlated features as core obstacles. It provides mathematical analysis of normalized data-weight dynamics.

entry.title: Pause and Think: A Dataset and Benchmark for Video-Grounded Assistive Action Suggestion

author.name: Shivam Singh, Saptarshi Majumdar, Pratik Prabhanjan, Zicheng Liu, Emad Barsoum

entry.summary: This work introduces a reasoning-centric video dataset and benchmark for assistive action suggestion that encourages models to pause and reason over visual evidence before answering. A fine-tuned 4B model matches much larger models like Qwen3-VL-235B and GPT-5.2 on certain tasks.

entry.title: EPIC: Efficient and Parallel Inference under CFG Constraints for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Hyundong Jin, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: EPIC is an efficient framework for context-free grammar constrained decoding in diffusion language models that preserves parallel decoding, overcoming prior methods that were up to four times slower and sacrificed parallelism. It avoids sequential validity-check overhead.

entry.title: WaveFilter: Enhancing the Long-Context Capability of Diffusion LLMs via Wavelet-Guided KV Cache Filtering

author.name: Jinnan Yang, Yan Wang, Zhen Bi, Kehao Wu, Xiaojie Li, Jungang Lou, Zechao Li, Jing Liu

entry.summary: WaveFilter is a training-free KV-cache filtering framework for diffusion LLMs that uses wavelet transforms to precisely identify critical tokens in ultra-long contexts, addressing quality degradation in long-context generation. It mitigates the computational bottleneck of multi-step diffusion inference.

entry.title: Quantum Tunneling-Aware Machine Learning: Physics-Derived Noise Models for Robust Deployment

author.name: Uiwon Hwang, Jaeho Hwang

entry.summary: QTAML derives a physics-based weight-error distribution from the WKB quantum tunneling approximation for transistors, revealing structure that generic Gaussian noise models miss, such as affine mean drift and per-bit variance hierarchy. It packages these for robust ML deployment as scaling nears quantum limits.

entry.title: Behavior-Invariant Task Representation Learning with Transformer-based World Models for Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Fuyuan Qian, Menglong Zhang, Song Wang, Quanying Liu

entry.summary: This work proposes behavior-invariant task representation learning combined with a Transformer-based stochastic world model for offline meta-reinforcement learning, extracting task latents invariant to behavior policy. It addresses context and policy distribution shifts under sparse rewards.

entry.title: Beyond Independent Manipulation: Individual Fairness-aware Strategic Classification with Peer Imitation

author.name: Xinpeng Lv, Chunyuan Zheng, Yunxin Mao, Renzhe Xu, Jinxuan Yang, Yuanlong Chen, Wangrong Huang, Shaowu Yang, Wenjing Yang, Xinwang Liu, Peng Cui, Haotian Wang

entry.summary: This work extends strategic classification to individual fairness settings where agents' feature manipulations are interdependent through peer imitation, unlike prior assumptions of independent responses. It reformulates fairness-aware strategic classification under these coupled dynamics.

entry.title: FVSpec: Real-World Property-Based Tests as Lean Challenges

author.name: Quinn Dougherty, Max von Hippel, Hazel Shackleton, Mike Dodds

entry.summary: Builds a benchmark for formal software verification by scraping 11K Python property-based tests and translating thousands into Lean 4 specifications with placeholders. Uses a three-agent LLM pipeline to transpile imperative tests into dependently-typed Lean specs.

entry.title: PolySpeech-100: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Speech Understanding Across 100+ Languages and Dialects

author.name: Sicheng Yang, Shulan Ruan, Shiwei Wu, Yu Liu, Lu Fan, Zhi Li, You He

entry.summary: Introduces a large-scale speech understanding benchmark covering 110+ languages and dialects, including 19 Chinese dialects and 80+ low-resource languages, with focus on semantic reasoning beyond ASR. Uses a hybrid pipeline of human recordings and synthetic speech.

entry.title: MENTIS: What Belief Changes Under Alignment? Measuring Multi-Scale Latent Torsion in Language Models

author.name: Partha Pratim Saha, Samarth Raina, Mayur Parvatikar, Amit Dhanda, Vinija Jain, Aman Chadha, Amitava Das

entry.summary: Introduces MENTIS, a geometry-first framework measuring internal representational reorganization when an instruction-tuned model becomes preference-aligned. Aims to characterize where and how selectively alignment changes internal computation across concepts and model families.

entry.title: DiscourseFlip: An Oblique Discourse-Level Opinion Manipulation Attack against Black-box Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Yuyang Gong, Miaokun Chen, Jiawei Liu, Zhuo Chen, Guoxiu He, Wei Lu, XiaoFeng Wang, Xiaozhong Liu

entry.summary: Introduces DiscourseFlip, a black-box opinion-manipulation attack against RAG systems that coordinates poisoning across a semantic query network to induce opinion shifts over a multi-topic query space. Formalizes discourse-level manipulation as a new threat model.

entry.title: TukaBench: A Culturally Grounded Jailbreak Benchmark for African Languages

author.name: Victor Akinode, Senyu Li, Wassim Hamidouche, Waqas Zamir, Inbal Becker-Reshef, David Ifeoluwa Adelani

entry.summary: Introduces TukaBench, a culturally-grounded jailbreak benchmark for seven African languages extending JailbreakBench beyond direct translation with code-switched and culturally-adapted prompts. Finds prompting in African languages reduces model refusal rates.

entry.title: Dr. DocBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Expert-Level and Difficult Document Parsing

author.name: Minglai Yang, Xinyan Velocity Yu, Pengyuan Li, Xinyu Guo, Zhenting Qi, Konwoo Kim, Longtian Ye, Xiaolong Luo, Jinhe Bi, Henry Zhang, Haris Riaz, Xuan Zhang, Yunze Xiao, Bangya Liu, Tom Tang, Yunfei Zhao, Qunshu Lin, Zihan Wang, Minghao Liu, Michael Lingzhi Li, Yilun Du, Jesse Thomason, Rogerio Feris, Alex Pentland, Zexue He

entry.summary: Introduces Dr. DocBench, a difficulty-aware multilingual benchmark for expert-level document parsing covering 52 subject domains and challenging structures like chemical formulas, music notation, complex tables, and cross-page layouts. Targets gaps in OCR and document-parsing evaluation.

entry.title: ClawHub Security Signals: When VirusTotal, Static Analysis, and SkillSpector Disagree

author.name: Vincent Koc, Patrick Erichsen, Jacob Tomlinson, Agustin Rivera, Michael Appel, Nir Paz

entry.summary: ClawHub Security Signals releases a sanitized dataset of 67,453 public agent-skill versions and studies disagreement among three security scanners (VirusTotal, static analysis, SkillSpector). It reveals scanners rarely flag the same skills, highlighting gaps in agent-skill security detection.

entry.title: TimeSage-MT: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Evaluating Agentic Time Series Reasoning

author.name: Yaxuan Kong, Qingren Yao, Yuqi Nie, Yichen Li, Yilei Shao, Stefan Zohren, Anna Vettoruzzo, Joaquin Vanschoren, Ming Jin, Qingsong Wen

entry.summary: TimeSage-MT is a multi-turn benchmark for agentic time series reasoning with 240 tasks and 2,680 dialogue turns across 8 domains, moving beyond single-step forecasting tasks. It evaluates whether LLM agents can sustain reliable analysis as user goals evolve.

entry.title: Demystifying Multimodal Biomolecular Co-design With Intrinsic Geodesic Coupling

author.name: Keyue Qiu, Xintong Wang, Zhilong Zhang, Hao Zhou, Wei-Ying Ma

entry.summary: This work introduces intrinsic geodesic coupling for multimodal biomolecular co-design, arguing that temporal coupling between sequence and structure generative processes is an overlooked degree of freedom. It addresses high-variance supervision from fixed synchronous coupling.

entry.title: MINTS: Minimalist Thompson Sampling

author.name: Kaizheng Wang

entry.summary: MINTS introduces a minimalist Bayesian framework placing a prior only on the optimum's location and eliminating nuisance parameters via profile likelihood, instantiated as Minimalist Thompson Sampling. It establishes near-optimal regret guarantees for constrained multi-armed bandits.

entry.title: DOT-MoE: Differentiable Optimal Transport for MoEfication

author.name: Udbhav Bamba, Arnav Chavan, Aryamaan Thakur, Steve Teig, Deepak Gupta

entry.summary: DOT-MoE formulates the conversion of dense models into sparse MoEs as a differentiable optimal transport problem, replacing heuristic neuron clustering or random splitting. It aims for stable, efficient MoEfication of pretrained dense LLMs.

entry.title: Off-the-Shelf LLMs as Process Scorers: Training-Free Alternative to PRMs for Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Atoosa Chegini, Soheil Feizi

entry.summary: This work proposes Chunk-Level Guided Generation, a training-free alternative to process reward models that uses an off-the-shelf large LLM to score candidate chunks via likelihoods without generating text. It steers small-model math reasoning before errors propagate.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Pretrained Models for Instance Segmentation Tasks

author.name: Nermeen Abou Baker, David Rohrschneider, Uwe Handmann

entry.summary: Adaptive Auto-Harness extends auto-harness systems (which optimize agent prompts, skills, tools, and memory) from fixed offline benchmarks to open-ended task streams with shifting distributions. It enables sustained self-improvement with task-wise adaptation to prevent performance degradation.

entry.title: MMG2Skill: Can Agents Distill In-the-Wild Guides into Self-Evolving Skills?

author.name: Xinyu Che, Junqi Xiong, Yunfei Ge, Xinping Lei, Shihao Li, Hang Yan, Han Li, Yuanxing Zhang, Zhiqi Bai, Jinhua Hao, Ming Sun, Han Li, Jiaheng Liu

entry.summary: MMG2Skill formalizes guide-to-skill learning, converting noisy multimodal in-the-wild web guides into agent-executable, self-evolving skills, and introduces MMG2Skill-Bench. It proposes a closed-loop framework that compiles and continuously improves skills from agent trajectories.

entry.title: PlanarBench: Evaluating LLM Spatial Reasoning via Planar Graph Drawing

author.name: Oleksandr Nikitin

entry.summary: This work proposes a render-free framework for 3D-aware human motion control in video diffusion models, conditioning on compressed 3D human mesh tokens rather than rendered 2D guidance videos. It investigates whether diffusion models truly understand 3D structure versus reproducing 2D projections.

entry.title: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models using Multi-Clip Video

author.name: Choongwon Kang, Seungjong Sun, Hyunmin Jun, Jang Hyun Kim

entry.summary: Introduces Multi-Clip Video SafetyBench, a 2,920-video dataset showing that multimodal LLMs become more vulnerable to jailbreaks as video inputs contain more diverse clips related to a harmful query. Identifies clip diversity as a key driver of safety alignment failures in video MLLMs.

entry.title: Faster Synchronous On-Policy RL via Straggler-Aware Group Sizing

author.name: Azal Ahmad Khan, Ammar Ahmed, Zeshan Fayyaz, Sheng Di, Mingyi Hong, Ali Anwar

entry.summary: Proposes SAGC, a straggler-aware dynamic group-size controller for synchronous on-policy RL methods like GRPO, framing group sizing as online constrained optimization to reduce wall-clock stalls from slow rollouts. Targets the tension between larger groups and synchronization cost.

entry.title: SeClaw: Spec-Driven Security Task Synthesis for Evaluating Autonomous Agents

author.name: Hao Cheng, Changtao Miao, Tianle Song, Yin Wu, He Liu, Erjia Xiao, Junchi Chen, Xiaoyu Shi, Yichi Wang, Jing Yang, Taowen Wang, Jinhao Duan, Mengshu Sun, Peiyan Dong, Xuan Shen, Yang Cao, Renjing Xu, Kaidi Xu, Jindong Gu, Bo Zhang, Jize Zhang, Chenhao Lin, Philip Torr, Chao Shen

entry.summary: Introduces SeClaw, a framework combining specification-driven security task synthesis with execution-based evaluation for autonomous LLM agents in stateful environments. Enables scalable construction of security scenarios and assesses unsafe execution processes, not just final outcomes.

entry.title: A Pre-Training Analogue of Grokking in Language Models: Tracing Delayed Grammatical Generalization

author.name: Sherin Muckatira, Namrata Shivagunde, Vijeta Deshpande, Anna Rumshisky

entry.summary: Proposes an exposure-based framework to study grokking-like delayed generalization during LLM pre-training, grounding evaluation in BLiMP minimal pairs and tracking when grammatical generalization emerges relative to exposure. Adapts grokking analysis from supervised epochs to next-token pre-training.

entry.title: Adaptive Order Policies for Masked Diffusion

author.name: Jama Hussein Mohamud, Mohsin Hasan, Mirco Ravanelli, Yoshua Bengio

entry.summary: Proposes learning the token-unmasking order in masked diffusion models via a lightweight policy network that reweights diffusion loss terms toward positions where the denoiser is likely correct. Studies training the policy alone and jointly with the diffusion model.

entry.title: Auditing Near-Optimal Policies Can Be Exponentially Hard: Conditional Query Lower Bounds via Occupancy Rashomon Capacity

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Sanjeda Akter, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical framework formalizing how hard it is to audit near-optimal RL policies, introducing an occupancy-measure version of Rashomon capacity and proving conditional exponential query lower bounds. It matters for AI safety and policy verification under the reality that many distinct behaviors achieve similar returns.

entry.title: EST-PRM: Stress-Testing Process Reward Models Before They Become Load-Bearing

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Fariya Afrin, Sanjeda Akter, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces EST-PRM, a stress-testing framework that probes whether process reward models give stable scores under label-preserving transformations like step inflation and reordering. Reveals that PRM scores may not be robust proxies for step correctness.

entry.title: GNMR: Runtime Stability Control for Low-Precision Large Language Model Training

author.name: Boao Kong, Weichen Jia, Engao Zhang, Guohong Li, Yonghan Dong, Yao Wang, Yaoyuan Wang, Yunke Peng, Kun Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes GNMR, a lightweight runtime controller for low-precision LLM training that monitors gradient-norm-to-mean ratios to detect and recover from numerical instabilities without changing formats or kernels. Tested on DeepSeek-style recipes and LLaMA-2 fine-tuning.

entry.title: On the Recoverability of Causal Relations from Bulk Gene Expression Data

author.name: Gongxu Luo, Boyang Sun, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: Studies whether causal relations among genes are recoverable from bulk (aggregated) gene expression data, formalizing recoverability via functional-form and conditional-independence consistency. From Kun Zhang's causal-inference group.

entry.title: How Neural Losses Shape VAE Latents

author.name: Giorgio Strano, Luca Cerovaz, Michele Mancusi, Tommaso Mencattini, Emanuele Rodol\`a

entry.summary: Shows that perceptual and adversarial reconstruction losses in VAEs reshape the rate-distortion problem, reducing latent information content and altering latent geometry in ways invisible from reconstructions. Provides theory and empirical verification.

entry.title: Task Structure Reverses Layerwise State Encoding in Sequence Models

author.name: Yuhang Jiang

entry.summary: Shows that the same sequence model architecture reverses its layerwise state-encoding profile depending on task structure, comparing Transformers, Mamba, Mamba-2, LSTMs, and GRUs on Parity and Dyck-k. Disentangles algebraic versus computational structure as drivers.

entry.title: Non-Vacuous Certification of Transport MCMC via Oscillation-Controlled Normalizing Flows

author.name: Jun Hu

entry.summary: Establishes the first numerically non-vacuous, rigorous spectral-gap bounds for transport MCMC samplers that use normalizing flows to precondition Metropolis-Hastings, via oscillation-controlled flows with spectral normalization. Provides certified mixing guarantees on benchmark posteriors.

entry.title: Trust Region On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Xingrun Xing, Haoqing Wang, Boyan Gao, Ziheng Li, Yehui Tang

entry.summary: Proposes Trust Region On-Policy Distillation (TrOPD), which applies on-policy distillation only in regions where the teacher gives reliable supervision, stabilizing training when teacher and student distributions diverge. Improves credit assignment for LLM post-training, compression, and agent learning.

entry.title: Truthful AI Advisors: A Pre-Specified Benchmark for Large Language Model Honesty Under Preference Misalignment

author.name: Hamidreza Hasani Balyani, Seyed Pouyan Mousavi Davoudi, Alireza Amiri-Margavi, Amin Gholami Davodi, Arshia Gharagozlou

entry.summary: This paper turns the Crawford-Sobel cheap-talk economic model into a pre-specified benchmark for LLM honesty when advisor incentives misalign with users. It tests whether LLMs reveal information or strategically partition, an important alignment-evaluation question.

entry.title: OmniOPD: Logit-Free On-Policy Distillation via Speculative Verification

author.name: Yuhang Zhou, Lizhu Zhang, Yifan Wu, Mingyi Wang, Peng Bo, Jiayi Liu, Xiangjun Fan, Zhuokai Zhao

entry.summary: OmniOPD enables on-policy distillation without access to teacher logits by using speculative verification, allowing proprietary models to serve as teachers. It addresses the brittleness of token-level logit signals and degenerate repetition patterns.

entry.title: ContinuousBench: Can Differentially Private Synthetic Text Improve Capabilities?

author.name: Peihan Liu, Lucas Rosenblatt, Weiwei Kong, Natalia Ponomareva, Gautam Kamath, Rachel Cummings, Roxana Geambasu, Yu Gan, Lillian Tsai, Alex Bie

entry.summary: ContinuousBench is a continuously regenerated benchmark measuring whether differentially private synthetic text transmits genuinely new knowledge, with quarterly never-before-seen corpora paired with derived QA sets. It is designed to be unsolvable without the corpus yet learnable under DP.

entry.title: Minimax-Optimal Policy Regret in Partially Observable Markov Games

author.name: Raman Arora

entry.summary: Provides theoretical regret bounds for sequential decision-making in partially observable Markov games against adaptive adversaries, proving near-optimal policy regret with an epoch-based optimistic maximum-likelihood algorithm. Important for theoretical foundations of multi-agent learning under partial observability.

entry.title: Drifting Preference Optimization for One-Step Generative Models

author.name: Zhou Jiang, Yandong Wen, Zhen Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Drifting Preference Optimization for aligning deterministic one-step text-to-image generators using a non-parametric preference field and reference drift, avoiding reliance on policy likelihoods or trajectories. Addresses a real gap in finetuning fast single-pass generators.

entry.title: Parameter-Free and Group Conditional Online Conformal Prediction

author.name: Beepul Bharti, Ambar Pal, Jacopo Teneggi, Jeremias Sulam

entry.summary: Proposes a parameter-free algorithm for group-conditional online conformal prediction, achieving group-wise coverage guarantees robust to distribution shift without learning-rate tuning. Improves fairness and uncertainty quantification under non-exchangeable data.

entry.title: ViBE: Co-Optimizing Workload Skew and Hardware Variability for MoE Serving

author.name: Seokjin Go, Marko Scrbak, Ephrem Wu, Srilatha Manne, Divya Mahajan

entry.summary: Presents ViBE, a system co-optimizing workload skew and hardware variability for distributed Mixture-of-Experts inference, addressing stragglers caused by interaction of uneven expert loads and GPU performance variation. Targets serving latency in MoE deployments.

entry.title: Quality-Diversity Evolution for Discovering Diverse Vulnerabilities in LLM Safety

author.name: Subhadip Mitra

entry.summary: Introduces a quality-diversity evolutionary red-teaming framework using MAP-Elites to discover diverse interpretable LLM attack strategies at the semantic level, avoiding mode collapse and gibberish outputs. Reveals distinct vulnerability profiles across GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3.5, Gemini 2.0, and an open coding model.

entry.title: Coarse-to-Fine Compositional Diffusion for Long-Horizon Planning

author.name: Byoungwoo Park, Utkarsh A. Mishra, Jaemoo Choi, Juho Lee, Yongxin Chen

entry.summary: Proposes coarse-to-fine compositional diffusion for long-horizon planning, composing short-horizon priors into globally coherent long-horizon outputs beyond enforcing only local neighbor consistency. Addresses implausible global structure in standard compositional generation.

entry.title: Don't Read Everything: A Curvature-Conditioned Query for Linear Attention

author.name: Dong Le, Thong Nguyen, Cong-Duy Nguyen, Anh Tuan Luu

entry.summary: Introduces a curvature-conditioned query mechanism for linear attention, borrowing a second-order Taylor expansion of softmax's log-partition to contract queries at read time. It aims to fix linear attention's weakness on in-context retrieval and long-context tasks.

entry.title: Don't Let a Few Network Failures Slow the Entire AllReduce

author.name: Peiqing Chen, Jiedong Jiang, Nengneng Yu, Yuefeng Wang, Sixian Xiong, Wei Wang, Zaoxing Liu

entry.summary: Provides the first information-theoretic lower bound on AllReduce completion time under asymmetric network bandwidth from NIC failures, showing overhead is only O(1/p) when stragglers retain half bandwidth. It addresses how network failures slow distributed GPU training.

entry.title: Investigating and Alleviating Harm Amplification in LLM Interactions

author.name: Ruohao Guo, Wei Xu, Alan Ritter

entry.summary: Introduces HarmAmp, a benchmark for multi-turn harm amplification across twelve risk categories, studying how LLMs compound harm over extended interactions by democratizing expertise and scaling operations. It investigates and proposes mitigations for harm amplification missed by single-turn evaluations.

entry.title: How Far Do Auto-Interpretation Labels Generalize: A Controlled Study Across Languages, Scripts, and Rewordings

author.name: Sripad Karne

entry.summary: This study tests whether sparse autoencoder feature labels generalize across languages, scripts, and rewordings, using Serbian Latin/Cyrillic digraphia as a controlled testbed. It finds substantial cross-lingual feature overlap suggesting genuine semantic features but probes the limits of auto-interpretation labels.

entry.title: LaSR: Context-Aware Speech Recognition via Latent Reasoning

author.name: Heyang Liu, Ziyang Cheng, Jiayi Huang, Wenyang Xiao, Ronghua Wu, Qunshan Gu, Yanfeng Wang, Yu Wang

entry.summary: LaSR is a training paradigm for context-aware speech recognition that uses latent reasoning aligned to acoustic feature regions rather than explicit chain-of-thought tokens. It aims to make speech LLMs better reflect speaker intent and topical context.

entry.title: Robust Reasoning via Dynamic Token Selection for Distribution-Aligned Self-Distillation

author.name: Ruiqi Zhang, Lingxiang Wang, Hainan Zhang Zhiming Zheng

entry.summary: This paper proposes distribution-aligned self-distillation with dynamic token selection to separate beneficial logical corrections from harmful stylistic drift in rewritten training data. It targets high-perplexity tokens to preserve reasoning while avoiding surface-form imitation.

entry.title: OCC-RAG: Optimal Cognitive Core for Faithful Question Answering

author.name: Maksim Savkin, Mikhail Goncharov, Alexander Gambashidze, Alla Chepurova, Dmitrii Tarasov, Nikita Andriianov, Daria Pugacheva, Vasily Konovalov, Andrey Galichin, Ivan Oseledets

entry.summary: OCC introduces a family of task-specialized small language models, with OCC-RAG optimized for faithful context-grounded question answering through multi-hop reasoning while ignoring parametric knowledge. It argues that robust reasoning matters more than extensive memorized knowledge for many applications.

entry.title: Child-directed speech facilitates production, not comprehension, in BabyLMs

author.name: Bastian Bunzeck, Sina Zarrie{\ss}

entry.summary: This paper introduces a generation-based frame-completion evaluation for BabyLMs and finds child-directed speech facilitates production but not comprehension, dissociating the two capabilities. It supports usage-based language acquisition theories about constructional frames.

entry.title: PMC-InterCPT: Rethinking Biomedical Interleaved Data for Multimodal Continued Pretraining

author.name: Guanghao Zhu, Zeyu Liu, Zhitian Hou, Pengkai Wang, Zhijie Sang, Minheng Ni, Wenjun Wang, Yanggan Gu, Shuo Cai, Congkai Xie, Jianmin Wu, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: PMC-InterCPT is a context-grounded biomedical interleaved corpus that adds figure-referencing body text to image-caption pairs, addressing the brevity and structural noise of literature-extracted medical datasets. It rethinks data construction for medical multimodal continued pretraining.

entry.title: Not All Explanations Simulate Equally: Comparing Verbalized Feature Attributions and Self-Generated Rationales

author.name: Pingjun Hong, Benjamin Roth

entry.summary: This paper compares verbalized feature attributions against self-generated rationales for question answering models under a shared counterfactual simulation setting using an LLM judge as predictor. It analyzes how explanation source, verbalization strategy, and granularity affect simulatability.

entry.title: Med-HEAL: Analyzing and Mitigating Hallucinations in Medical LLMs with Hallucination-Aware In-Context Learning

author.name: Yiming Liao, Zeno Franco, Jose Eduardo Lizarraga Mazaba, Keke Chen

entry.summary: Med-HEAL is a framework for identifying, analyzing, and mitigating hallucinations in medical LLMs using clinically grounded EHR data, building a hallucination dataset from BioMistral-7B outputs on open-ended clinical QA. It introduces hallucination-aware in-context learning for mitigation.

entry.title: UniD$^3$: A Knowledge Graph-Enhanced RAG Framework for Drug-Disease Discovery and Reasoning

author.name: Qing Wang, Tianshi Liu, Minghao Zhou, Jialu Liang, Sen Guo, Guangyu Wang, Jing Su, Qianqian Song

entry.summary: UniD3 integrates LLMs with knowledge-graph-enhanced RAG to extract, organize, and validate drug-disease relationships across matching, effectiveness, and target analysis tasks. It processes nearly 158K PubMed articles with Llama 3.3-70B to construct a knowledge graph reducing hallucination.

entry.title: RCEM: Embedder Equipped with Query Rewriting Skill for Robust Conversational Search in Distributional Shift

author.name: Kilho Son, Paul Hsu, Cha Zhang, Dinei Florencio

entry.summary: RCEM is a conversational dense retrieval model that distills LLM query reformulation into the embedding model, enabling context-aware retrieval without explicit query rewriting at inference. It aligns conversational-query embeddings with rewritten-query embeddings for robustness under distributional shift.

entry.title: Geometric Latent Reasoning Induces Shorter Generations in LLMs

author.name: Shashi Kumar, Yacouba Kaloga, Petr Motlicek, Ina Kodrasi, Andrea Cavallaro

entry.summary: Geometric Latent Reasoning formulates latent reasoning as a geometric path-approximation problem in token-embedding space, using a lightweight transition head to predict iterative direction updates anchored by chain-of-thought traces. The approach induces shorter generations while reasoning continuously.

entry.title: WAXAL-NET: Finetuned Edge ASR Across 19 African Languages

author.name: Victor Tolulope Olufemi, Oreoluwa Babatunde, Ramsey Njema, Bolarinwa Gbotemi, Wanchi Lucia Yen, John Uzodinma, Sunday Ajayi, Oluwademilade Williams, Kausar Moshood, Innocent Elendu Anyaele, Akebert Arefaine, Candace Hunzwi, Wongel Dawit Daniel, Emmilly Namuganga, Cleophas Kadima, Athanase Bahizire, Onitsiky Ranaivoson, Emmanuel Aaron, Nicholaus Ladislaus, Idris Muhammed, Jonathan Enoch Simenya, Martin Koome, Matewos Tegete Endaylalu, Peter Ifeoluwa Adeyemo, Hondi Prisca Birindwa, Ukachi Agnes Eze-Mbey, Yacoba Oduro-Yeboah, Pericles Adjovi, Mikel K. Ngueajio, Toluwani Aremu, Prasenjit Mitra

entry.summary: WAXAL-NET fine-tunes compact edge ASR models for 19 African languages, achieving a macro WER of 38% versus 64.9% for the best zero-shot baseline using models 3-40x smaller. It demonstrates that domain specialization beats scale for spontaneous African speech.

entry.title: Decomposed On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Reasoning: Steering Gradients for Visual Grounding

author.name: Hee Suk Yoon, Eunseop Yoon, Jaehyun Jang, SooHwan Eom, Ji Woo Hong, Mark Hasegawa-Johnson, Qi Dai, Chong Luo, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: This paper mathematically decomposes on-policy VLM distillation loss into language-prior and visual-grounding components, showing their gradients are nearly orthogonal so standard optimization follows a suboptimal compromise. It proposes steering gradients to improve visual grounding in small reasoning models.

entry.title: BraveGuard: From Open-World Threats to Safer Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Yunhao Feng, Yifan Ding, Xiaohu Du, Ming Wen, Xinhao Deng, Yanming Guo, Yuxiang Xie, Baihui Zheng, Yingshui Tan, Yige Li, Yutao Wu, Yixu Wang, Kerui Cao, Wenke Huang, Xingjun Ma, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: BraveGuard is a self-evolving defense framework that trains guard models for computer-use agents by mining recent research for emerging threats, instantiating them as executable tasks, and deriving trajectory-level supervision. It targets multi-step harms that appear locally benign.

entry.title: MBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark on Memory Capability for Video World Models

author.name: Shengjun Zhang, Zhang Zhang, Simin Huang, Zhenyu Tang, Hanyang Wang, Chensheng Dai, Min Chen, Yifan Li, Yuxin Li, Yingjie Chen, Hao Liu, Chen Li, Yueqi Duan

entry.summary: MBench is a benchmark dedicated to evaluating memory capability in video world models, focusing on long-term consistency and complex interactions rather than just visual quality or motion coherence. It fills a gap left by existing benchmarks.

entry.title: SuperMemory-VQA: An Egocentric Visual Question-Answering Benchmark for Long-Horizon Memory

author.name: Samiul Alam, Shakhrul Iman Siam, Michael J. Proulx, James Fort, Richard Newcombe, Hyo Jin Kim, Mi Zhang

entry.summary: SuperMemory-VQA is an egocentric VQA dataset (52.9 hours from AI glasses) for evaluating long-horizon memory assistants on practical, personal memory tasks rather than short-clip action recognition. Authors include Meta Reality Labs researchers.

entry.title: PlatonicNav: Unveiling Semantic Correspondence in Navigation with Platonic Topological Maps

author.name: Junlin Long, Zeyu Zhang, Xu Deng, Yiran Wang, Yue Yang, Luke Borgnolo, Maxwell Twelftree, Yang Zhao

entry.summary: Presents PlatonicNav, exploring whether independently trained vision and language encoders already share a common semantic structure for embodied navigation, using Platonic topological maps to unify VLN and ObjNav without explicit cross-modal supervision. Challenges the architectural-fusion paradigm.

entry.title: RescueBench: Can Embodied Agents Save Lives in the Wild ?

author.name: Kui Wu, Beiyu Guo, Hao Chen, ShuHang Xu, Yuling Li, Yongdan Zeng, Zhoujun Li, Yizhou Wang, Fangwei Zhong

entry.summary: Introduces RescueBench, a photo-realistic diagnostic benchmark instantiating search-and-rescue as a four-stage pipeline (exploration, rescue, memory-guided return, handoff) to study how failures compound across embodied workflows. Combines sequential task composition with stage-level evaluation.

entry.title: SCAPO: Self-Supervised Category-Level Articulated Pose Estimation from a Single 3D Observation

author.name: Can Zhang, Gim Hee Lee

entry.summary: Proposes SCAPO, a self-supervised framework for category-level articulated pose estimation from a single RGB-D observation, estimating canonical geometry, part segmentation, and joint parameters without ground-truth labels or CAD templates. Uses SE(3)-equivariant autoencoding and joint-aware blend skinning.

entry.title: MT-EditFlow: Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Image Editing with Flow Matching

author.name: Jiahui Huang, Yasi Zhang, Tianyu Chen, Shu Wang, Jianwen Xie, Oscar Leong, Mingyuan Zhou, Nanzhu Wang, Ying Nian Wu

entry.summary: Introduces MT-EditFlow, a flow-matching reinforcement learning framework for multi-turn image editing that addresses error propagation and the all-or-nothing failure when single-turn editing models are applied iteratively. Optimizes robustness across editing sequences.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Implicit Memory for Video World Models

author.name: Zhengxuan Wei, Xu Guo, Xinghui Li, Xunzhi Xiang, Min Wei, Yiran Zhu, Qiulin Wang, Xintao Wang, Pengfei Wan, Xiangwang Hou, Qi Fan

entry.summary: Proposes GIM-World, a geometry-aware implicit memory framework for video world models that compresses variable-length history into fixed-size memory tokens with a camera-queryable geometry head distilling 3D scene structure. Addresses memory limitations in long-horizon rollouts.

entry.title: Active Exploring like a Pigeon: Reinforcing Spatial Reasoning via Agentic Vision-Language Models

author.name: Wei Deng, Xianlin Zhang, Mengshi Qi

entry.summary: Proposes an agentic pipeline reinforcing spatial reasoning in vision-language models, inspired by pigeon navigation, introducing a dynamic cognitive map of object positions/orientations as persistent memory and Spatial Assertion Codes as Python expressions describing spatial relationships. Moves VLMs from passive observers to active explorers.

entry.title: VISReg: Variance-Invariance-Sketching Regularization for JEPA training

author.name: Haiyu Wu, Randall Balestriero, Morgan Levine

entry.summary: Proposes VISReg, a JEPA self-supervised regularizer that replaces covariance with a Sliced-Wasserstein sketching objective to better enforce distributional shape and avoid embedding collapse. Improves training stability over VICReg and SIGReg.

entry.title: Safe2Drive: Evaluating Safe Driving Behaviors of E2E Autonomous Driving Models

author.name: Nishad Sahu, Kalpana Panda, Congyuan Yu, Changzhong Qian, Shounak Sural, Ragunathan Rajkumar

entry.summary: Safe2Drive adds 100 safety-critical scenarios (work zones, jaywalking, occluded VRUs) and a SafeDriving Score to benchmark end-to-end driving policies, revealing that high driving scores hide poor safety behavior. Tests LEAD and SimLingo.

entry.title: SKIP: Sparse Keyframe Interpolation Paradigm for Efficient Embodied World Models

author.name: Ziheng He, Yixiang Chen, Ning Yang, Zhanqian Wu, Qisen Ma, Yuan Xu, Jiabing Yang, Peiyan Li, Xiangnan Wu, Xiaofeng Wang, Zheng Zhu, Jing Liu, Nianfeng Liu, Yan Huang

entry.summary: SKIP is an event-preserving sparse keyframe interpolation framework for embodied world models that identifies task-relevant keyframes to avoid expensive frame-by-frame video generation. Reduces inference cost while preserving sparse task events like grasp and release.

entry.title: AlbedoEdit: Unified Instance-Level Video Editing with Albedo Guidance

author.name: Xilong Zhou, Bao-Huy Nguyen, Zheng Zeng, Jacob Munkberg, Jon Hasselgren, Thomas Leimk\"uhler, Nima Kalantari, Milo\v{s} Ha\v{s}an, Christian Theobalt

entry.summary: AlbedoEdit is a unified video editing framework using albedo guidance to support instance-level object insertion, removal, and texture editing with fine-grained control. Addresses limitations of coarse semantic control in existing methods.

entry.title: WALL-WM: Carving World Action Modeling at the Event Joints

author.name: Shalfun Li, Victor Yao, Charles Yang, Truth Qu, Regis Cheng, Ryan Yu, Howard Lu, Newton Von, Vincent Chen, Yohann Tang, Maeve Zhang, Ellie Ma, Gody Li, Sage Yang, Lorien Shu, J. W. Gao, Ethan Chen, Colin Ye, Yu Sun, Elise Mon, PS Zhang, Neo Li, Lily Li, James Wang, Ping Yang, Chris Pan, Lucy Liang, Hang Su, Roy Gan, Hao Wang, Qian Wang

entry.summary: WALL-WM shifts vision-language-action pretraining from fixed-length action chunks to semantically coherent action events as the atomic learning unit, addressing granularity mismatch between language, vision, and control. A world-action model for robotics.

entry.title: AFUN: Towards an Affordance Foundation Model for Functionality Understanding

author.name: Zhaoning Wang, Yi Zhong, Jiawei Fu, Henrik I. Christensen, Jun Gao

entry.summary: AFUN is a step toward an affordance foundation model that, from single RGB-D input, both localizes where interaction should happen and predicts executable motion, generalizing across objects and tasks. Aims to bridge perception and physical action.

entry.title: World Models for Robotic Manipulation: A Survey

author.name: Fangyuan Wang, Ziyuan Wang, Guorui Pei, Mengshi Zhang, Canxi Liang, Jun Hu, Zhongxuan Li, Jinsong Wu, Ning Han, Zeqing Zhang, Jiaming Qi, Hongmin Wu, Shiyao Zhang, Pai Zheng, Jia Pan, David Navarro-Alarcon, Sichao Liu, Peng Zhou

entry.summary: A survey of world models for robotic manipulation organized around three questions: what future representation is predicted, how prediction connects to action, and when prediction is used. Unifies fragmented literature spanning latent dynamics, video generators, and VLA modules.

entry.title: Constrained Whole-Body Tracking for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Daniel Morton, Pranit Mohnot, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: ConstrainedMimic enforces arbitrary runtime constraints on RL whole-body tracking policies for humanoids by combining operational space control and control barrier functions, validated on a simulated Unitree G1. Ensures safety for constraints specified after training.

entry.title: Make Your VLA More Robust Without More Data By Interleaving Motion Planning

author.name: Dan BW Choe, Sundhar Vinodh Sangeetha, Samuel Coogan, Shreyas Kousik

entry.summary: MPVI interleaves model-based motion planning with VLA models to improve robustness on long-horizon mobile manipulation without additional training, addressing compounding errors and maintaining progress across spatially distributed subtasks. Argues more data alone does not solve these challenges.

entry.title: OneVLA: A Unified Framework for Embodied Tasks

author.name: Lingfeng Zhang, Xiaoshuai Hao, Yingbo Tang, Lei Zhou, Shuyi Zhang, Jinkun Liu, Hongsheng Li, Chenhao Zhang, Qiang Zhang, Hangjun Ye, Xiaojun Liang, Long Chen, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: OneVLA is a unified architecture integrating navigation and manipulation into a single framework with a unified action head that generates both action types without task-specific variants, trained via multi-stage progressive training. Targets general-purpose robotic agents.

entry.title: [Linkpost] Prefixing names with 'secure_' makes agents write more secure code

author.name: Jack

entry.summary: An empirical study showing that prefixing function names with secure_ reliably caused coding agents to add unrequested security measures like password hashing, with different prefixes seeding distinct conceptual worlds that persisted across independently prompted steps. It demonstrates surprising priming effects in agentic code generation.

entry.title: Does Compression Preserve Uncertainty? A Unified Benchmark for Quantized and Sparse LLMs via Conformal Prediction

author.name: Yujia Tong, Yuxi Wang, Yunyang Wan, Tian Zhang, Junhao Dong, Jingling Yuan

entry.summary: This work benchmarks 12 LLMs under quantization and pruning across five NLP tasks using conformal prediction to rigorously measure uncertainty preservation, finding that compression frequently decouples accuracy from uncertainty and that larger models absorb compression-induced uncertainty better. It highlights overlooked uncertainty risks in compressed models for safety-critical use.

entry.title: Learning When Not to Act: Mitigating Tool Abuse in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Liuji Chen, Dianxing Tang, Xing Shi, Dingshuo Chen, Qiang Liu, Shu Wu, Liang Wang

entry.summary: EAPO is an efficient agentic policy optimization framework that learns selective tool use to mitigate tool abuse, introducing tool-free trajectories per rollout group, difficulty-aware reward shaping to penalize redundant calls on easy queries, and confidence-aware token reweighting. It improves accuracy across nine reasoning benchmarks while reducing unnecessary tool calls.

entry.title: TrustLDM: Benchmarking Trustworthiness in Language Diffusion Models

author.name: Yichuan Mo, Yukun Jiang, Yanbo Shi, Mingjie Li, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang, Yisen Wang

entry.summary: TrustLDM is a comprehensive trustworthiness benchmark for Language Diffusion Models evaluating safety, privacy, and fairness across architectures, finding alignment degrades notably under malicious post-context despite strong baseline trustworthiness. Probes risks of flexible any-order decoding.

entry.title: When Softmax Fails at the Top: Extreme Value Corrections for InfoNCE

author.name: Melihcan Erol, Suat Evren, Oktay Ozel, Alexander Morgan, Jongha Jon Ryu, Lizhong Zheng

entry.summary: Uses extreme value theory to show InfoNCE's softmax form encodes a statistical assumption about top-example selection that is misaligned with normalized embedding settings. Proposes WEINCE, a parameter-free correction blending softmax logits with an endpoint shortfall term, improving frozen-feature evaluation across five vision benchmarks.

entry.title: SkyShield: Occupancy as a Safety Interface for Low-Altitude UAV Autonomy

author.name: Jie Gao, Jie Ma, Kaihui Lin, Kai Ye, Miaohui Zhang, Pingyang Dai, Liujuan Cao

entry.summary: SkyShield frames 3D occupancy prediction as a safety interface for low-altitude UAV autonomy, addressing the gap where existing datasets lack front-facing monocular occupancy under changing 6-DoF aerial pose. It targets safe navigation in cluttered sub-20-meter urban airspace.

entry.title: When Do Attention Circuits Form? Developmental Trajectories of Capability and Attention-Sink Emergence Across Three 1B-ClassArchitectures

author.name: Yongzhong Xu

entry.summary: Tracks the developmental emergence of attention-head circuits (induction, previous-token, BOS-attractor) across three 1B-class models spanning dense and MoE architectures and two corpora. Finds layers 0-1 never produce BOS heads, identifying an architectural floor rather than learned outcome.

entry.title: Limits of Resolution Equivariance in Fourier Neural Operators

author.name: Alex Colagrande, Paul Caillon, Eva Feillet, Alexandre Allauzen

entry.summary: Empirically tests the assumed resolution-equivariance of Fourier Neural Operators, finding that direct fine-grid inference can underperform low-grid inference plus Fourier upsampling on Darcy flow. Analyzes spectral concentration in intermediate layers.

entry.title: MedGym:A Unified Continuous-Time Benchmark for Dynamic Medical Treatment Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuepeng Wang, Ken Kawano, Yongqi Zhou, Yoshihiko Fujisawa, Richard Weiss, Akifumi Wachi, Katsuki Fujisawa, Ying Chen, Mehrshad Sadria, Xin Liu, Kyoung-Sook Kim, Xiao Hu, Sebastien Gros, Xun Shen

entry.summary: Introduces MedGym, a continuous-time benchmark for dynamic medical treatment reinforcement learning that models irregular measurements, personalized response, and inter-decision safety, unlike prior discrete-time MDP/POMDP formulations. Provides a realistic evaluation environment.

entry.title: Interaction-Limited Safe Continuous-Time RL for Dynamical Medical Treatment

author.name: Xun Shen, Yuepeng Wang, Akifumi Wachi, Yongqi Zhou, Richard Weiss, Yoshihiko Fujisawa, Ken Kawano, Mehrshad Sadria, Ying Chen, Xin Liu, Sebastien Gros, Xiao Hu, Kyoung-Sook Kim, Mengmou Li, Katsuki Fujisawa, Kenji Wakabayashi

entry.summary: Proposes Interaction-Limited Safe Continuous-Time RL that jointly optimizes treatment intensity and intervention timing under trajectory-level safety constraints, reformulating the problem as an option-based semi-MDP. Enforces safety between clinical interactions rather than only at decision points.

entry.title: Lagrangian Perturbation Diffusion Steering: Latent Reinforcement Learning for Generative Policies

author.name: Hikmet Simsir, Ozgur S. Oguz

entry.summary: Proposes LP-DS, a lightweight RL adaptation method that improves a frozen generative imitation policy by learning a compact noise-space perturbation before decoding, optimized with a Lagrangian trust-region objective. Avoids unstable fine-tuning of large action decoders across robotics and locomotion tasks.

entry.title: Unveiling the Entropy Dynamics of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Ting Xu, Xu He, Yupu Lu, Jiankai Sun, Dong Li, Wai Lam, Jianye Hao

entry.summary: Uncovers a consistent two-phase entropy structure in chain-of-thought reasoning, an exploratory Uncertainty Region transitioning to a high-reliability, high-redundancy Confidence Region. It exploits this for efficient inference via early exit and confidence-signal test-time scaling.

entry.title: I-WebGenBench : Evaluating Interactivity in LLM-Generated Scientific Web Applications

author.name: Dasen Dai, Biao Wu, Meng Fang, Shuoqi Li, Wenhao Wang

entry.summary: I-WebGenBench evaluates whether LLM agents can convert research papers into executable interactive web systems with manipulable inputs and dynamic behaviors, beyond static summaries or slides. It introduces a Paper-to-Interactive-System Agent for end-to-end processing.

entry.title: Worlds Within Words: Translating Culture in Ancient Chinese Texts with Multi-Agent Coordination

author.name: Xiaoqi He, Kaixin Lan, Mu You, Tao Fang, Lidia S. Chao, Derek F. Wong

entry.summary: MACAT is a multi-agent culture-aware translation framework that formulates culture-loaded word translation in ancient Chinese as a selective explicitation task, dynamically deciding when and how to explicate culture-dependent knowledge. It balances literal preservation against over-explicitation for readability.

entry.title: Why Do Self-Harm Prediction Models Struggle to Generalise? Lexical and Semantic Variations in Emergency Department Triage Notes

author.name: Liuliu Chen, Mike Conway, Jo Robinson, Vlada Rozova

entry.summary: This paper investigates why self-harm prediction models fail to generalize across hospitals by analyzing lexical and semantic variations in emergency department triage notes from two institutions. It finds documentation differences in lexical expression and feature importance associated with reduced cross-site performance.

entry.title: Eyettention II: A Dual-Sequence Architecture for Modeling Fixation Location, Within-Word Landing Position, and Fixation Duration in Reading

author.name: Shuwen Deng, Cui Ding, David R. Reich, Paul Prasse, Lena A. J\"ager

entry.summary: Eyettention II is a dual-sequence deep-learning model generating realistic reading scanpaths including fixation location, within-word landing position, and fixation duration. It addresses eye-tracking data scarcity by synthesizing complete fixation sequences for downstream applications.

entry.title: TIDES: Time-Derivative Event Simulation via Deformable Reconstruction

author.name: Christopher Thirgood, Dipon Kumar Ghosh, Simon Hadfield

entry.summary: Presents TIDES, a continuous-time event camera simulator built on dynamic Gaussian splatting that derives per-pixel intensity dynamics from an explicit 3D scene representation rather than frame differencing, eliminating timestamp batching artifacts. Improves simulation accuracy under fast motion and occlusion.

entry.title: Ego-METAS: Egocentric online Multimodal Energy-efficient Temporal Action Segmentation benchmark

author.name: Maria Santos-Villafranca, Jesus Bermudez-cameo, Alejandro Perez-Yus, Giovanni Maria Farinella, Antonino Furnari

entry.summary: Introduces Ego-METAS, the first egocentric online multimodal energy-efficient temporal action segmentation benchmark with 100+ hours of untrimmed video across five modalities, formulating energy-aware sensor selection for resource-constrained embodied perception. Addresses under-explored energy-accuracy tradeoffs.

entry.title: From Extrinsic to Intrinsic: Geodesic-Guided Representation Learning for 3D Geometric Data

author.name: Yuming Zhao, Junhui Hou, Qijian Zhang, Jia Qin, Ying He

entry.summary: Proposes PRISM, a 3D representation learning paradigm that learns isometric embeddings by recovering intrinsic surface geodesic metrics, with a topology-enforcing objective constraining latent space and a two-stage training recipe. Bridges extrinsic and intrinsic geometric perspectives.

entry.title: Retrieve What's Missing: Coverage-Maximizing Retrieval for Consistent Long Video Generation

author.name: Minseok Joo, Dogyun Park, Taehoon Lee, Kyujin Lee, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: Proposes COVRAG, a coverage-maximizing depth-based memory retrieval framework for consistent long-horizon autoregressive video generation that reasons about pixel-wise visibility without costly explicit 3D reconstruction. Improves long-term geometric consistency in memory-augmented generation.

entry.title: X-Stream: Exploring MLLMs as Multiplexers for Multi-Stream Understanding

author.name: Peiwen Sun, Xudong Lu, Huadai Liu, Yang Bo, Dongming Wu, Huankang Guan, Minghong Cai, Jinpeng Chen, Xintong Guo, Shuhan Li, Rui Liu, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: Introduces X-Stream, the first benchmark for multi-stream streaming video understanding with 4,220 QA pairs across 932 videos spanning multi-window, multi-view, and multi-device scenarios, using a dual-verification pipeline. Addresses the gap left by single-stream benchmarks for cross-stream reasoning.

entry.title: Capability Self-Assessment: Teaching LLMs to Know Their Limits

author.name: Haoyan Yang, Reza Shirkavand, Yukai Jin, Jiawei Zhou, Shangqian Gao, Heng Huang

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Capability Self-Assessment, the ability of an LLM to know when to solve versus delegate a problem, and shows that models systematically overestimate competence. It demonstrates that reinforcement learning teaches this skill effectively while supervised fine-tuning degrades original capabilities.

entry.title: Expected Value Alignment for Generative Reward Modeling in Formal Mathematics Verification

author.name: Shihao Ji, Haotao Tan, Zihui Song, Mingyu Li

entry.summary: Expected Value Alignment (EVA) is a reward-modeling method for formal math verification with Lean 4 that keeps discrete textual outputs while extracting continuous scores from token distributions, resolving the trade-off between value-head and generative reward models. It targets scaling theorem proving with RL and search.

entry.title: Emergent Ordinal Geometry in Transformers Trained on Local Comparisons

author.name: Nishit Singh

entry.summary: This single-author study trains small Transformers only on adjacent comparisons from a hidden total order and finds emergent transitive inference generalization to distant pairs, accompanied by entity embeddings collapsing onto a one-dimensional manifold that recovers the rank. This mirrors the symbolic distance effect seen in humans and animals.

entry.title: ReSkill: Reconciling Skill Creation with Policy Optimization in Agentic RL

author.name: Zelin He, Haotian Lin, Boran Han, Wei Zhu, Haoyang Fang, Bernie Wang, Xuan Zhu, Runze Li, Matthew Reimherr

entry.summary: ReSkill is an RL-in-the-loop skill creation framework that reconciles skill evolution with policy optimization in agentic RL by exploiting GRPO's group-wise structure to embed assertion-driven skill creation with low overhead. It addresses the risk of adopting skills that conflict with an evolving policy.

entry.title: AutoMedBench: Towards Medical AutoResearch with Agentic AI Models

author.name: Junqi Liu, Salena Song, Yuhan Wang, Jiawei Mao, Hardy Chen, Xiaoke Huang, Tianhao Qi, Pengfei Guo, Yucheng Tang, Yufan He, Can Zhao, Andriy Myronenko, Dong Yang, Daguang Xu, Yuyin Zhou

entry.summary: AutoMedBench is a workflow-aware benchmark for autonomous medical-AI research organizing agent execution into a five-stage workflow (Plan, Setup, Validate, Inference, Submit) across imaging and multimodal tasks, with long-horizon runs averaging 33 turns. It evaluates agent behavior within the research process rather than only final outputs.

entry.title: Where Do Deep-Research Agents Go Wrong? Span-Level Error Localization in Agent Trajectories

author.name: Jiaming Wang, Ziteng Feng, Jiangtao Wu, Ruihao Li, Qianqian Xie, Yuxiang Ren, He Zhu, Xueming Han, Fanyu Meng, Junlan Feng, Jiaheng Liu

entry.summary: This work studies span-level error localization for deep-research agents, collecting 2,790 real trajectories and building TELBench, a 1,000-instance benchmark for identifying harmful error spans among normal exploration, failed searches, and harmless noise. It proposes DRIFT, a claim-based localization method.

entry.title: Harness-1: Reinforcement Learning for Search Agents with State-Externalizing Harnesses

author.name: Pengcheng Jiang, Zhiyi Shi, Kelly Hong, Xueqiang Xu, Jiashuo Sun, Jimeng Sun, Hammad Bashir, Jiawei Han

entry.summary: Harness-1 is a 20B search agent trained with RL inside a stateful harness that offloads routine bookkeeping (candidate pools, curated evidence sets) to the environment, freeing the policy to focus on semantic search decisions. This separation improves reliability of state management.

entry.title: HLL: Can Agents Cross Humanity's Last Line of Verification?

author.name: Xinhao Song, Su Su, Sirui Song, Hongliang Wu, Wen Shen, Zhihua Wei, Gongshen Liu, Linfeng Zhang, Dongrui Liu

entry.summary: Introduces HLL, a benchmark testing whether multimodal agents can cross human-verification boundaries (CAPTCHAs) through grounded interaction rather than recognition alone, raising deployment and security questions about agents bypassing anti-automation safeguards. Covers diverse interactive CAPTCHA types.

entry.title: Make Mechanistic Interpretability Auditable: A Call to Develop Guidelines via Continuous Collaborative Reviewing

author.name: Michael Lan, Narmeen Fatimah Oozeer, Chaithanya Bandi, Philip Quirke, Austin Meek, Fazl Barez, Amirali Abdullah

entry.summary: A position paper calling for standardized auditing guidelines in mechanistic interpretability via continuous collaborative reviewing, motivated by cases where papers reached conflicting or incomparable conclusions on the same behavior. Argues this is needed for safety-critical adoption.

entry.title: A Shared Valence Axis Across Modern LLMs and Human EEG: The Saturation Regularity

author.name: Yousef A. Radwan, Xuhui Liu, Kilichbek Haydarov, Yuqian Fu, Mohamed Elhoseiny

entry.summary: Builds a one-dimensional valence axis from LLM representations using only nine emotion-evocative sentences and shows it maps onto human EEG neural activity across 123 subjects. Reveals a saturation regularity shared between LLM features and human emotional valence encoding.

entry.title: Learning to Construct Practical Agentic Systems

author.name: Aditya Kumar, Zhihan Lei, Jerry Yan, Joshua W. Momo, Lauhitya Reddy, Rafael Enrique Cabrera Jimenez, Cassandra A. Cohen, Arthur Kajiyama, William W. Cohen

entry.summary: Proposes principled approaches for designing practical agentic LLM systems prioritizing simplicity, controllability, and predictable inference costs over pure quality optimization. Introduces pseudo-tools enabling modular recursive LLM calls on restricted contexts.

entry.title: Continuous Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action

author.name: Yueh-Hua Wu, Tatsuya Matsushima, Kei Ota

entry.summary: Argues natural language is mismatched to the fine temporal granularity of continuous control and proposes Continuous Reasoning for vision-language-action policies, where the reasoning medium is shareable, verifiable via action improvement, and aligned with temporal control structure. It rethinks what should play the role of language in VLA reasoning.

entry.title: Rethinking the Role of Temperature in Large Language Model Distillation

author.name: Hoang-Chau Luong, Lingwei Chen

entry.summary: Revisits the role of temperature in LLM distillation, showing it asymmetrically affects forward vs reverse KL: temperature enriches FKL with non-dominant token signals while mainly rescaling RKL gradients. This overturns the standard preference for RKL over FKL when temperature is properly accounted for.

entry.title: Finer Parameter Steps for Low-Rank PEFT: A Controlled Study with CP Tensor Adapters

author.name: Xinjue Wang, Xiuheng Wang, Yejun Zhang, Sergiy A. Vorobyov, Esa Ollila, Zhi-Yong Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces CP tensor adapters that offer much finer parameter-budget increments than LoRA's rank steps, studying whether finer capacity resolution improves the accuracy-budget trade-off in PEFT. It runs a controlled comparison on OPT models.

entry.title: Improving Visual Representation Alignment Generation with GRPO

author.name: Shentong Mo, Sukmin Yun

entry.summary: VRPO uses GRPO-style reinforcement learning to make representation alignment in diffusion transformers adaptive, replacing static cosine or contrastive alignment losses with task-adaptive optimization. It aims to improve convergence and generation quality.

entry.title: MemGraphRAG: Memory-based Multi-Agent System for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Chuanjie Wu, Zhishang Xiang, Yunbo Tang, Zerui Chen, Qinggang Zhang, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: MemGraphRAG is a memory-based multi-agent system for graph retrieval-augmented generation that addresses fragmented, thematically inconsistent knowledge graphs produced by isolated extraction. It introduces a more global corpus perspective during graph construction.

entry.title: Collaborative Few-Step Distillation and Low-Bit Quantization for Wan2.2 Dual-Expert Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Jinyang Du, Shenghao Jin, Ziqian Xu, Ruihao Gong, Shiqiao Gu, Yang Yong, Jinyang Guo, Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a deployment-oriented compression pipeline for the Wan2.2 dual-expert video diffusion model combining few-step distillation with low-bit quantization, calibrating high- and low-noise branches separately. Quantizing on the distilled student reduces activation-distribution mismatch.

entry.title: DASH: Dual-Branch Score Distillation for Guidance-Calibrated Compact Diffusion Models

author.name: Abdullah Al Shafi, Kazi Saeed Alam, Sk Imran Hossain, Engelbert Mephu Nguifo

entry.summary: DASH is a dual-branch score distillation framework that independently supervises both conditional and unconditional score branches in compressed diffusion models, fixing the underdetermined classifier-free guidance gap left by output-level distillation. It prevents degenerate branch-collapse solutions.

entry.title: SkillPager: Query-Adaptive Intra-Skill Navigation via Semantic Node Retrieval

author.name: Zicai Cui, Zihan Guo, Weiwen Liu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: SkillPager performs query-adaptive intra-skill retrieval by parsing skill documents into typed semantic nodes offline and using Maximal Marginal Relevance for query-conditioned node selection online. It achieves near full-document sufficiency while cutting prompt tokens by about 47 percent.

entry.title: From Cues to Horizons: Dynamic Risk Horizon Profiling for Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Xinyi Ning, Zilin Bian, Dachuan Zuo, Semiha Ergan, Kaan Ozbay

entry.summary: This paper introduces a risk horizon profiling module with a continuous learnable potential field that models the future evolution and uncertainty of safety risk for trajectory prediction in autonomous driving. It moves beyond using past risk as a secondary signal.

entry.title: Beyond Task-Agnostic: Task-Aware Grouping for Communication-Efficient Multi-Task MoE Inference

author.name: Zhiyao Xu, Aoxue Liu, Zhanjie Ding, Dan Zhao, Yong Jiang, Qing Li

entry.summary: Proposes task-aware grouping of MoE experts for communication-efficient distributed inference, observing that expert co-activation is task-conditioned rather than global. This reduces cross-GPU communication and load imbalance in multi-task serving.

entry.title: Hybrid Verified Decoding: Learning to Allocate Verification in Speculative Decoding

author.name: Xin Su, Dawid Majchrowski, Fangyuan Yu, Vanshil Atul Shah, Sebastian Rogawski, Pawel Morkisz, Anahita Bhiwandiwalla, Phillip Howard

entry.summary: Proposes Hybrid Verified Decoding for speculative decoding that predicts accepted length of a cache draft before verification to choose between cache and model-based drafting. Improves efficiency in structured and agentic workloads.

entry.title: Implicit Drifting Policy: One-Step Action Generation via Conditional Expert Geometry

author.name: Zemin Yang, Yaoyu He, Yiming Zhong, Yuhao Zhang, Xinge Zhu, Yao Mu, Qingqiu Huang, Yuexin Ma

entry.summary: Proposes Implicit Drifting Policy, a one-step imitation learning framework that recovers training-time trajectory correction without explicit vector field estimation, addressing latency of iterative diffusion/flow policies for high-frequency robot control. Extracts conditional expert geometry implicitly.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models for Molecular Generation via Reinforcement Learning and Fast Sampling

author.name: Guang Lin, Shikui Tu, Lei Xu

entry.summary: Proposes FTDiff, an RL fine-tuning framework for diffusion-based molecular generation under 3D structural constraints in structure-based drug design, using group-based optimization for stable multi-objective training. Avoids costly post-hoc processing and curated datasets.

entry.title: Connecting the Dots: Benchmarking Reflective Memory in Long-Horizon Dialogue

author.name: Jingjie Lin, Bingbing Wang, Zihan Wang, Zhengda Jin, Weiming Qiao, Jing Li, Ruifeng Xu

entry.summary: Introduces RefMem-Bench, a 26K-instance benchmark for reflective memory in long-horizon dialogue that requires synthesizing fragmented multimodal cues into high-level interpretations rather than factual recall. Proposes REMIND, a hierarchical reflective-memory induction framework.

entry.title: Knowledge-Intensive Video Generation

author.name: Chenxu Wang, Mingda Chen

entry.summary: Introduces knowledge-intensive video generation, where models produce videos from information-seeking prompts asking for explanations or procedures, with a 1080-prompt benchmark and factuality/helpfulness metrics. Finds current video models lag behind humans, especially on procedural content.

entry.title: Crazyflow: An Accurate, GPU-Accelerated, Differentiable Drone Simulator in JAX

author.name: Martin Schuck, Marcel P. Rath, Yufei Hua, AbhisheK Goudar, SiQi Zhou, Angela P. Schoellig

entry.summary: Crazyflow is a GPU-accelerated, differentiable drone simulator in JAX that unifies single-agent and multi-agent, model-based and data-driven simulation in one platform. It achieves over an order-of-magnitude speedup over existing drone simulators.

entry.title: EvoPool: Evolutionary Programmatic Annotation for Label-Efficient Specialized Supervision

author.name: Tianyi Xu, Yaolun Zhang, Xuan Ouyang, Huazheng Wang

entry.summary: EvoPool is an evolutionary multi-agent framework that generates executable annotator code via three specialized agents with viability and diversity gates, producing soft labels for label-efficient supervision. It runs orders of magnitude faster than direct LLM annotation in specialized domains.

entry.title: Easier to Mislead Than to Correct: Harmful and Beneficial Revision in LLM Conformity

author.name: Jiaming Qu, Lucheng fu, Yibo Hu

entry.summary: This controlled study examines LLM conformity in multi-agent settings, finding that models are easier to mislead than to correct when shown peer answers. It manipulates consensus structure and authority labels to measure beneficial versus harmful revisions across four open-weight LLMs.

entry.title: Two-Fidelity Best-Action Identification for Stochastic Minimax Tree

author.name: Peter Chen, Xi Chen

entry.summary: This paper studies fixed-confidence best-action identification in stochastic minimax trees, proposing 2FFS, a two-fidelity tree search that adaptively chooses between cheap biased and expensive accurate evaluations. It is motivated by MCTS with LLM rollouts facing cost-accuracy trade-offs.

entry.title: Post-Deterministic Distributed Systems: A New Foundation for Trustworthy Autonomous Infrastructure

author.name: Jun He, Deying Yu

entry.summary: This paper defines Deep Spurious Regression, extending the study of spurious correlations from classification to continuous-target settings without discrete groups. It investigates how regression models exploit unreliable shortcut attributes that fail under deployment shifts.

entry.title: THRD: A Training-Free Multi-Turn Defense Framework for Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models

author.name: Zhiqing Ma, Zhonghao Xu, Dong Yu, Chen Kang, Changliang Li, Pengyuan Liu

entry.summary: THRD is a training-free multi-turn jailbreak defense that explicitly models temporal risk accumulation along conversation trajectories rather than evaluating each turn in isolation. It addresses gradual-escalation and cross-turn coordination attacks.

entry.title: STaR-KV: Spatio-Temporal Adaptive Re-weighting for KV Cache Compression in GUI Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yuhang Han, Wenzheng Yang, Yujie Chen, Xiangqi Jin, Yaojie Zhang, Siteng Huang, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: STaR-KV proposes spatio-temporal adaptive re-weighting for KV cache compression in GUI vision-language agents, where caches grow linearly with interaction steps. It refutes assumptions of shared saliency maps and fixed cutoffs, exploiting attention-subspace spatial specialization.

entry.title: "I've Seen How This Goes": Characterizing Diversity via Progressive Conditional Surprise

author.name: Matthew Khoriaty, David Williams-King, Shi Feng

entry.summary: This paper proposes the Decan metric for measuring output diversity via progressive conditional surprise, using in-context learning and per-token log-probabilities in a single forward pass with no embedding model or reference corpus. It targets evaluation of mode collapse and creative diversity.

entry.title: Learning Implicit Bias in Generative Spaces for Accelerating Protein Dynamics Emulation

author.name: Kaihui Cheng, Zhiqiang Cai, Wenkai Xiang, Zhihang Hu, Siyu Zhu, Tzuhsiung Yang, Yuan Qi

entry.summary: This work introduces a history-dependent implicit bias in the generative space of pretrained protein dynamics emulators to steer sampling toward rare states, inspired by enhanced sampling. A score-based refinement step re-projects drifted samples onto the data manifold for long-horizon validity.

entry.title: Why Do Time Series Models Need Long Context Windows?

author.name: Luca Butera, Giovanni De Felice, Andrea Cini, Cesare Alippi

entry.summary: This paper argues that forecasting groups of time series involves two objectives, generative process identification and conditional forecasting, explaining why models benefit from long context windows beyond just capturing long-range dependencies. It reframes optimal predictions as averages over plausible data-generating processes.

entry.title: The Role of Ambiguity in Error Prediction via Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Ieva Raminta Stali\=unait\.e, James Bishop, Andreas Vlachos

entry.summary: Studies error prediction for LLMs by disentangling inherent input ambiguity (aleatoric uncertainty) from uncertainty quantification signals. Shows UQ metrics predict errors better on unambiguous questions and uses Gated Experts and Selective Prediction to improve calibration.

entry.title: Who Annotates in NLP? A Large-scale Assessment of Human Annotation Reporting between 2018 and 2025

author.name: Maria Kunilovskaya, Gagan Bhatia, Lisa Sophie Albertelli, Yanran Chen, Christian Greisinger, Lotta Kiefer, Christoph Leiter, Subhadeep Roy, Tewodros Achamaleh, Muhammad Arslan Manzoor, Sebastian Pohl, Yufang Hou, Steffen Eger

entry.summary: Conducts the first large-scale, task-level audit of human annotation reporting practices across NLP venues from 2018-2025, introducing a taxonomy and an LLM-assisted extraction pipeline validated against a human gold standard. Documents which annotation details are routinely missing.

entry.title: PaSBench-Video: A Streaming Video Benchmark for Proactive Safety Warning

author.name: Yusong Zhao, Yuejin Xie, Youliang Yuan, Junjie Hu, Jitian Guo, Yujiu Yang, Pinjia He

entry.summary: Presents PaSBench-Video, a 740-video benchmark for proactive safety warning where streaming video MLLMs must causally detect risk onset and issue timely warnings while avoiding false positives on safe scenes. Covers driving, healthcare, daily life, and industrial domains with frame-level annotations.

entry.title: Mitigating Perceptual Judgment Bias in Multimodal LLM-as-a-Judge via Perceptual Perturbation and Reward Modeling

author.name: Seojeong Park, Jiho Choi, Junyong Kang, Seonho Lee, Jaeyo Shin, Hyunjung Shim

entry.summary: Identifies Perceptual Judgment Bias in multimodal LLM judges, where they reward plausible text narratives over perceptually correct answers when visual and textual cues conflict. Introduces a perturbed counterfactual judgment dataset and reward modeling to mitigate it.

entry.title: LithoGRPO: Fast Inverse Lithography via GRPO Reinforced Flow Matching

author.name: Yao Lai, Xuyuan Xiong, Zeyue Xue, Guojin Chen, Jing Wang, Xihui Liu, Rui Zhang, Robert Mullins, Bei Yu, Ping Luo

entry.summary: Introduces LithoGRPO, an inverse lithography framework integrating flow matching with GRPO reinforcement learning fine-tuning to generate optimized photomasks that respect explicit physical evaluation metrics. Enables efficient exploration where standard generative models fall short.

entry.title: Adversarially Robust Control of Conditional Value-at-Risk via Rockafellar-Uryasev Conformal Inference

author.name: Catherine Chen, Jingyan Shen, Zhun Deng, Lihua Lei

entry.summary: Presents an online, distribution-free framework for controlling Conditional Value-at-Risk under non-stationary and adversarial environments, extending conformal tail risk control via the Rockafellar-Uryasev variational representation of CVaR. Provides provable adversarial regret guarantees.

entry.title: Grounded Decoding: Retrieval-Anchored Probability Fusion for Faithful RAG

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Fariya Afrin, Sanjeda Akter, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: Proposes Grounded Decoding, a training-free decoding method for RAG that fuses a full RAG distribution with a retrieval-only distribution at each generation step to improve faithfulness to retrieved evidence. Aims to stop models from over-relying on parametric knowledge.

entry.title: ProjQ: Project-and-Quantize for Adapter-Aware LLM Compression

author.name: Wneya Yu, Chao Zhang, Li Wang, Samson Lasaulce, Merouane Debbah

entry.summary: Proposes ProjQ, which constrains post-training quantization noise to a low-rank manifold via orthogonal subspace projection so that subsequent LoRA can effectively correct it. Improves the standard PTQ+LoRA deployment pipeline for LLMs.

entry.title: DREAM-S: Speculative Decoding with Searchable Drafting and Target-Aware Refinement for Multimodal Generation

author.name: Zining Liu, Yunhai Hu, Tianhua Xia, Bo Bao, Eric Sather, Vithursan Thangarasa, Sai Qian Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces DREAM-S, a speculative decoding framework tailored for vision-language models using neural architecture search to find optimal draft architectures and adaptive feature distillation. Accelerates autoregressive VLM generation.

entry.title: Score $\times$ Decoder: A Unified View of Unsupervised Inference-Time Scaling for Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: Yun-Chen Cheng, Che-Yu Lin, Cheng-Lin Yang

entry.summary: Provides a unified score-times-decoder view of unsupervised inference-time scaling for hallucination mitigation, pairing four intrinsic scores with three decoding families and evaluating on MATH500 with Qwen3 models. Identifies which base-model signals best surface correct answers without supervision.

entry.title: OmniEEG-Bench: A Standardized Evaluation Benchmark for EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Ziling Lu, Zongsheng Li, Xinke Shen, Kexin Lou, Yingyue Xin, Xiaoqi Chen, Shinan Wang, Xiang Chen, Jiahao Fan, Chenyu Huang, Xin Xu, Zhoujie Hou, Chen Wei, Quanying Liu

entry.summary: Introduces OmniEEG-Bench, a unified benchmark and task roadmap organizing EEG foundation model evaluation into six task families, addressing fragmented protocols. Provides standardized comparison for emerging EEG foundation models.

entry.title: Cellular Sheaf Neural Operators for Structure-Preserving Surrogate Modeling of Constrained PDEs

author.name: Lennon J. Shikhman, Shane Gilbertie

entry.summary: Proposes Cellular Sheaf Neural Operators, a discretization-aware framework that represents PDE states on oriented cell complexes with learned restriction maps and Hodge-informed message passing for structure-preserving surrogate modeling of constrained PDEs. Respects where physical quantities naturally live (vertices, edges, faces).

entry.title: Optimal-Point Variance Reduction For Bayesian Optimization With Regret Guarantee

author.name: Shion Takeno

entry.summary: Proposes Optimal-point Variance Reduction, a one-step lookahead Bayesian optimization method requiring only posterior sampling and Monte Carlo approximation, with a uniform Monte Carlo error bound and a regularized variant achieving vanishing Bayesian regret. Provides theoretical guarantees often missing from entropy-search-style methods.

entry.title: Decision-Focused On-Policy Learning for Contextual Linear Optimization with Partial Feedback

author.name: Wyame Benslimane, Tinghan Ye, Pascal Van Hentenryck, Paul Grigas

entry.summary: Develops an on-policy decision-focused learning method for contextual linear optimization under partial (bandit-like) feedback, learning a stochastic predict-then-optimize policy with a hybrid gradient estimator. Generalizes standard bandit feedback for decision-quality optimization.

entry.title: From Reward-Free Representations to Preferences: Rethinking Offline Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jun-Jie Yang, Chia-Heng Hsu, Kui-Yuan Chen, Ping-Chun Hsieh

entry.summary: Rethinks offline preference-based RL through reward-free representation learning, first learning latent successor-measure representations from reward-free data then using contrastive search and fine-tuning on preferences. Improves preference efficiency over two-stage reward-model pipelines.

entry.title: Beyond Sinusoids: A Morlet Wavelet Framework for Transformer Positional Encoding

author.name: Athanasios Zeris

entry.summary: Proposes Morlet Positional Encoding, where each transformer embedding dimension learns its own frequency and locality bandwidth, unifying sinusoidal and RoPE encodings as limiting cases when locality is switched off. Adds adaptive positional locality beyond standard schemes.

entry.title: GPTQ-intrinsic LoRA: A Near-optimal Algorithm for Low-precision Quantization with Low-rank Adaptation

author.name: Shihao Zhang, Rayan Saab

entry.summary: GPTQ-intrinsic LoRA is a training-free quantization algorithm that integrates low-rank correction directly into the GPTQ process, with the first information-theoretic lower bounds for low-precision-plus-low-rank weight representations. It targets aggressive low-bit compression of large networks.

entry.title: Rethinking the Role of Positional Encoding: Sliding-Window Transformers without PE Remain Turing Complete

author.name: Qian Li, Xinyu Mao, Shang-Hua Teng

entry.summary: This paper proves that sliding-window transformers without positional encoding remain Turing complete, showing the window mechanism itself breaks permutation symmetry. It challenges the belief that positional encoding is necessary for ordered sequence processing.

entry.title: Model Multiplicity and Predictive Arbitrariness in Recidivism Risk Assessment

author.name: Ashwin Singh, Carlos Castillo

entry.summary: This study examines model multiplicity and predictive arbitrariness in a recidivism risk assessment system in use for over 15 years, constructing a dataset from inmate releases by translating legal rules into outcome labels. It quantifies how severe arbitrariness can be and how to resolve it for high-stakes decisions.

entry.title: Massive Spikes in LLMs are Bias Vectors: Mechanistic Uncovering and Spike-Free Quantization

author.name: Yung-Chin Chen, Chung Peng Lee, Ze-Wei Liou, Naveen Verma
