entry.summary: This paper argues that massive activation spikes in LLMs are scalar intermediates of structural vector biases in spike-carrying tokens, driving attention sink and value-state drain mechanisms. It geometrically explains projection-weight coordination and proposes spike-free quantization.

entry.title: TabPrep: Closing the Feature Engineering Gap in Tabular Benchmarks

author.name: Andrej Tschalzev, Nick Erickson, Yuyang Wang, Huzefa Rangwala, Stefan L\"udtke, Heiner Stuckenschmidt, Christian Bartelt

entry.summary: Presents TabPrep, a lightweight feature-engineering preprocessing pipeline targeting structural data patterns that current tabular benchmarks ignore, achieving new peak performance on TabArena. Highlights an underexplored evaluation gap in tabular ML.

entry.title: Easy, robust approximate message passing for planted spike models

author.name: Misha Ivkov, Tselil Schramm

entry.summary: Presents a simple and efficient algorithm for robust approximate message passing in spiked matrix models that recovers near-AMP outputs despite adversarial corruption of a principal minor. Provides provable closeness guarantees.

entry.title: Manifold Diffusion for Structure Generation of Transition Metal Complexes

author.name: Luca Schaufelberger, Kjell Jorner

entry.summary: Introduces TMCgen, a manifold diffusion model that generates 3D geometries of transition metal complexes by diffusing over metal-ligand coordination angles plus torsional and rotational ligand degrees of freedom. Targets a hard structure-generation problem due to unconventional bonding.

entry.title: Generative Diffusion Priors for 3D Mapping of the Dark Universe

author.name: Brandon Zhao, Diana Scognamiglio, Olivier Dor\'e, Katherine L. Bouman

entry.summary: Uses generative diffusion priors trained on cosmological simulations to reconstruct the 3D dark matter distribution from single-line-of-sight weak-lensing observations, capturing non-Gaussian filamentary cosmic-web structure. Improves over handcrafted priors and neural ensembles for this ill-posed inverse problem.

entry.title: Observation, Not Prediction: Conversation-Level Disaggregated Scheduling for Agentic Serving

author.name: Jianru Ding, Ryien Hosseini, Pouya Mahdi Gholami, Mingyuan Xiang, Henry Hoffmann

entry.summary: Argues that the dependence on cost prediction in agentic LLM serving stems from using the turn as the scheduling unit, and shows that raising the unit to the whole conversation converts irregularity into a stable two-phase structure. This enables observation-based rather than prediction-based disaggregated scheduling.

entry.title: Provable Data Scaling Law for Meta Learning via Complexity Minimization

author.name: Kazuto Fukuchi, Ryuichiro Hataya, Kota Matsui

entry.summary: Introduces complexity minimization, a meta-representation learning framework that learns representations by minimizing worst-case downstream model complexity across source domains, to theoretically explain pre-training data scaling. It provides end-to-end analysis showing reduced downstream sample complexity as pre-training data grows.

entry.title: World-Task Factorization for Robot Learning

author.name: Eduardo Sebasti\'an, Adrian Pfisterer, Vito Mengers, Oliver Brock, Amanda Prorok

entry.summary: Studies the fundamental world-versus-task factorization in robot learning, investigating conditions under which separating embodiment/environment factors from task factors is principled and dictates what generalizes versus requires retraining. It offers a structural framework for policy design.

entry.title: Model-Based Quality Assessment for Massively Multilingual Parallel Data

author.name: Abdelaziz M. A. Ibrahim, Zihao Li, J\"org Tiedemann, Shaoxiong Ji

entry.summary: This paper decomposes quality assessment of massively multilingual parallel data into parallelism assessment via embeddings and reference-free quality estimation, benchmarking multiple models across thousands of translation directions. It finds no model is universally reliable and that naive ensembling dilutes strong signals.

entry.title: HypothesisMed: Inference-Time Answer Fusion and Structured Hypothesis-Space Reporting for Biomedical Question Answering

author.name: Md Motaleb Hossen Manik, Ge Wang

entry.summary: HypothesisMed is an inference-time reliability pipeline for biomedical multiple-choice QA that combines direct, chain-of-thought, and structured hypothesis-space prompting with answer fusion. It adds SPACE labels marking answer spaces as valid, incomplete, or contradicted to avoid confident incorrect commitments.

entry.title: When Is 0.1% Enough? Analyzing the Combined Effects of Dimensionality Reduction and Quantization on Text Embedding Compression

author.name: Riku Kisako, Hayato Tsukagoshi, Ryohei Sasano

entry.summary: This paper systematically examines combining dimensionality reduction and quantization for text embedding compression across four MTEB task families and four models. It shows the combination enables substantially stronger compression than either method alone.

entry.title: Efficient RAG with Intent-Aware Retrieval and Semantics-Preserving Chunking

author.name: Fachrina Dewi Puspitasari, Chaoning Zhang, Jiaquan Zhang, Zhicheng Wang, Hafiz Shakeel Ahmad Awan, Rizwan Qureshi, Jewon Lee, Tae-Ho Kim, Yang Yang

entry.summary: InSemRAG is a RAG framework addressing intent-agnostic retrieval and information fragmentation through an iterative retrieve-and-check mechanism with intention-aware retrieval and semantics-preserving chunking. It improves efficiency and relevance of retrieved knowledge.

entry.title: CARTE: A Benchmark for Mapping Language Model Knowledge Across France

author.name: Sarah Almeida Carneiro (X), Christos Xypolopoulos (X, NTUA), Xiao Fei (X), Yang Zhang (X), Michalis Vazirgiannis (X, MBZUAI)

entry.summary: CARTE is a multiple-choice benchmark evaluating LLMs on fine-grained regionally differentiated knowledge across the 13 metropolitan regions of France, with 2,431 questions across 14 thematic domains. It addresses the gap that prior benchmarks focus on national-level culture, ignoring intra-country variation.

entry.title: SentGuard: Sentence-Level Streaming Guardrails for Large Language Models

author.name: Jiaqi Yu, Xin Wang, Yixu Wang, Jie Li, Yan Teng, Xingjun Ma, Yingchun Wang

entry.summary: SentGuard proposes sentence-level streaming guardrails that moderate LLM output in parallel with generation, balancing the latency of full-response moderation against the instability of token-level checks. It uses a buffer that groups tokens into verified sentence chunks before release.

entry.title: K-BrowseComp: A Web Browsing Agent Benchmark Grounded in Korean Contexts

author.name: Nahyun Lee, Dongkeun Yoon, Guijin Son, Geewook Kim, Dayoon Ko, Jeonghun Park, Haneul Yoo, Jaewon Cho, Junghun Park, Changyoon Lee, Kyochul Jang, Jaeyeon Kim, Eunsu Kim, Woojin Cho, Seungone Kim

entry.summary: K-BrowseComp is a Korean-grounded web-browsing agent benchmark of 400 problems, with a manually validated 300-problem verified subset. Frontier models including GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro reach only 30-46%, and Korean-program LLMs score under 11%, revealing large agentic gaps in Korean contexts.

entry.title: Score-Control for Hallucination Reduction in Diffusion Models

author.name: Mahesh Bhosale, Naresh Kumar Devulapally, Abdul Wasi, Chau Pham, Vishnu Suresh Lokhande, David Doermann

entry.summary: This paper empirically confirms and formalizes that score smoothness causes hallucinations in diffusion models, linking hallucination probability mass to the Lipschitz constant of the learned score function. It introduces Variance-Guided Score Modulation to control the score Jacobian and reduce implausible samples.

entry.title: OptiWorld: Optimal Control for Video World Generation under Physical Constraints

author.name: Yu Yuan, Jianhao Yuan, Xijun Wang, Daiqing Li, Liu He, Lu Ling, Stanley H. Chan

entry.summary: OptiWorld brings classical optimal control into video world generation at inference time, extracting a compact world state, planning an optimal trajectory under physical constraints, and rendering video conditioned on it. It formulates planning as a geometric problem on a continuous manifold to produce safer, smoother, physically consistent motion.

entry.title: TextFake: Benchmarking AI-Generated Image Detection on Text-Rich Images

author.name: Yuning Zhang, Changtao Miao, Mingyu Liao, Tingyu Liu, Xinghao Wang, Tao Gong, Qi Chu, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: TextFake is a 20,000-image benchmark for detecting AI-generated text-rich images (fake screenshots, documents, news pages) across 28 languages and multiple scenarios, revealing that no existing detector or frontier VLM exceeds 80% accuracy. It exposes a major blind spot relevant to misinformation.

entry.title: Towards Interactive Video World Modeling: Frontiers, Challenges, Benchmarks, and Future Trends

author.name: Jiuming Liu, Chaojun Ni, Mengmeng Liu, Chensheng Peng, Fangjinhua Wang, Sitian Shen, Marc Pollefeys, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Ayush Tewari, Per Ola Kristensson

entry.summary: This survey systematically reviews interactive video world modeling, covering action-conditioned video and 3D generation, evaluation benchmarks, frontiers, challenges, and future trends. It synthesizes a rapidly growing field with applications in game engines, embodied AI, and autonomous driving.

entry.title: SafeGen-Bench: Benchmarking Safety in Image-Conditioned Text-to-Video Generation

author.name: Yingzi Ma, Xiaogeng Liu, Yawen Zheng, Chaowei Xiao

entry.summary: SafeGen-Bench benchmarks safety in image-conditioned text-to-video generation, focusing on the overlooked scenario where safe text and image inputs combine to produce harmful video content. It moves beyond prior benchmarks that test only malicious text prompts.

entry.title: Restoring Initial Noise Sensitivity in Text-to-Image Distillation via Geometric Alignment

author.name: Huayang Huang, Ruoyu Wang, Jinhui Zhao, Wei Deng, Daiguo Zhou, Jian Luan, Yu Wu, Ye Zhu

entry.summary: Identifies that text-to-image distillation methods lose sensitivity to initial noise, harming downstream noise-based control methods, and proposes a geometric alignment approach to restore the teacher's local geometric structure. Addresses an overlooked property in efficiency-focused distillation.

entry.title: Divide and Conquer: Reliable Multi-View Evidential Learning for Deepfake Detection

author.name: Xiaolu Kang, Zhongyuan Wang, Jikang Cheng, Baojin Huang, Zhanhe Lei, Gang Wu, Qin Zou, Qian Wang

entry.summary: Proposes DiCoME, a divide-and-conquer multi-view evidential learning framework for deepfake detection that addresses the Semantic Masking Effect where dominant semantic features overwhelm subtle artifact cues. Uses geometric view purification to decompose entangled representations.

entry.title: Residual Decoder Adapter: ID-Preserving Tokenizer Adaption for Autoregressive Text Rendering

author.name: Dongxing Mao, Jinpeng Wang, Jiahao Tang, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Linjie Li, Zhengyuan Yang, Lijuan Wang, Min Li, Jingru Tan

entry.summary: Proposes the Residual Decoder Adapter (RDA) to improve text rendering in visual autoregressive image models by upgrading an existing tokenizer post-hoc without retraining the tokenizer or AR model. Addresses blurry strokes and distorted letter shapes traced to tokenizer reconstruction limits.

entry.title: Unified Driving Tokens: Representation- and Geometry-Guided Discrete Tokenizer for Driving World Models and Planning

author.name: Ziyang Yao, Zeyu Zhu, YunCheng Jiang, Zibin Guo, Huijing Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes a representation-guided, geometry-enhanced discrete tokenizer for autonomous driving world models and planning, aligning the discrete bottleneck with frozen DINO features rather than optimizing only for pixel reconstruction. Aims to close the gap between easy-to-generate and useful-to-decode tokens.

entry.title: WebSpline: Structure-Informed Splines for Real-Time 3D Gaussians from Monocular Videos

author.name: Jongmin Park, Jeonghwan Yun, Minh-Quan Viet Bui, Munchurl Kim

entry.summary: Presents WebSpline, a dynamic 3D Gaussian framework for real-time reconstruction from monocular videos using Structure-Informed Splines (learnable cubic Hermite splines) organized by an auxiliary Structural Proxy Graph. Balances global structural coherence with local detail.

entry.title: Multimodal Action Diffusion for Robust End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jorge Daniel Rodr\'iguez-Vidal, Diego Porres, Gabriel Villalonga Pineda, Antonio M. L\'opez Pe\~na

entry.summary: Introduces the Action Diffusion Transformer (ADT), an anchor-free diffusion transformer for direct control-signal prediction (throttle, steer, brake) in end-to-end autonomous driving, arguing action multimodality is a key driver of performance and stability. Explores underexamined direct-control prediction.

entry.title: Ultra Diffusion Poser: Diffusion-Based Human Motion Tracking From Sparse Inertial Sensors and Ranging-Based Between-Sensor Distances

author.name: Dominik Hollidt, Tommaso Bendinelli, Christian Holz

entry.summary: Presents Ultra Diffusion Poser, a diffusion model for human motion tracking from sparse IMUs that explicitly uses UWB ranging-based inter-sensor distances as geometric constraints, including a module that analytically reconstructs the 3D sensor layout. Goes beyond using distances as mere input features.

entry.title: Chroma Clues: Leveraging Color Statistics to Detect Synthetic Images

author.name: Lea Uhlenbrock, Davide Cozzolino, Christian Riess

entry.summary: Exploits color statistics as a forensic cue for detecting synthetic images, observing that the LPIPS loss used in training generators is less sensitive to chrominance than luminance, leading to color discrepancies. Introduces hand-crafted and learned color transforms to expose generated images.

entry.title: TROPHIES: Temporal Reconstruction of Places, Humans, and Cameras from Multi-view Videos

author.name: Jinpeng Liu, Yukang Xu, Yutong Li, Xingyu Liu

entry.summary: Introduces TROPHIES, a unified framework for jointly reconstructing dynamic humans, static scenes, and camera poses in one global coordinate frame from multi-view videos. Addresses limitations of decoupled or single-view approaches that fail to recover coherent geometry and aligned trajectories.

entry.title: Places in the Wild: A Large, High-Resolution RAW Photograph Dataset for Ecologically Valid Vision Research

author.name: Michelle R. Greene

entry.summary: Releases Places in the Wild, a dataset of 67,574 high-resolution in-situ photographs across 810 locations and 260 scene categories, captured with a 45-megapixel camera in 14-bit RAW with dense 360-degree viewpoint sampling. Targets ecologically valid vision and neuroscience research with known capture conditions.

entry.title: Not All Points Are Equal: Uncertainty-Aware 4D LiDAR Scene Synthesis

author.name: Xiang Xu, Alan Liang, Youquan Liu, Xian Sun, Linfeng Li, Lingdong Kong, Ziwei Liu, Qingshan Liu

entry.summary: Proposes U4D, a 4D LiDAR scene synthesis framework that leverages per-point spatial uncertainty (Shannon entropy from a pretrained segmentor) to guide generation in a hard-to-easy schedule, synthesizing high-uncertainty regions first via unconditional diffusion. Addresses uniform modeling capacity ignoring varying perceptual difficulty.

entry.title: HumanNOVA: Photorealistic, Universal and Rapid 3D Human Avatar Modeling from a Single Image

author.name: Hezhen Hu, Wangbo Zhao, Lanqing Guo, Hanwen Jiang, Jonathan C. Liu, Zhiwen Fan, Kai Wang, Zhangyang Wang, Georgios Pavlakos

entry.summary: HumanNOVA generates photorealistic 3D human avatars from a single RGB image using a scalable 100k-asset data pipeline combining rigged assets and multi-camera fitting. Addresses data scarcity for generalizable avatar modeling.

entry.title: Belief Consistency Between Foundation-Model Evidence and Geometric Perception in Persistent Robotic Maps

author.name: Christoffer Heckman, Harel Biggie, Brendan Crowe, Nicholas Roy

entry.summary: Proposes an update operator with a calibrated commit gate and conflict-drop window to reconcile foundation-model semantic claims with geometric perception in persistent robotic maps. Flags contradictions between channels for more reliable mapping.

entry.title: Expanding Spatial and Temporal Context for Robotic Imitation Learning With Scene Graphs

author.name: Jianing Qian, Qinhe Peng, Emmanuel Panov, Leonor Fermoselle, Dinesh Jayaraman, Bernadette Bucher, Tarik Kelestemur

entry.summary: Uses dynamic scene graphs as structured explicit memory in robotic imitation learning to retain relevant historical context across long-horizon, partially observed tasks. Captures object-centric relationships and their temporal evolution.

entry.title: ActMVS: Active Scene Reconstruction with Monocular Multi-View Stereo

author.name: Guo Pu, Yixuan Han, Zhouhui Lian

entry.summary: ActMVS is presented as the first framework for monocular active scene reconstruction, delivering globally consistent dense depth at frame rates needed for robot/UAV navigation without depth sensors. Enables vision-only autonomous reconstruction.

entry.title: Dynamics and Representation Structure of Local Approximations to Gradient-Based Learning in Linear Recurrent Neural Networks

author.name: Ezekiel Williams, Alexandre Payeur, Guillaume Lajoie

entry.summary: Applies dynamical systems theory to compare local-approximation learning rules (RFLO, truncated BPTT) against full BPTT in linear RNNs, analyzing stationary solutions, stability, and convergence. Relevant to biologically plausible and neuromorphic learning.

entry.title: VLAMotor: Test-Guided Enhancement of Vision-Language-Action Models via Agent-BasedData Synthesis

author.name: Zeqin Liao, Peifan Ren, Zixu Gao, Hongyu Gong, Lianyu Hu, Wenbing Tang, Yuhong Nan, Zibin Zheng, Yang Liu

entry.summary: VLAMotor is presented as the first framework for VLA enhancement, integrating distance-aware model testing to expose failures and agent-based data synthesis to convert failures into supervisory data for finetuning. Goes beyond failure detection to model repair.

entry.title: ScaRF-SLAM: Scale-Consistent Reconstruction with Feed-Forward Models and Classical Visual SLAM

author.name: Yuhao Zhang, Yifu Tao, Frank Dellaert, Maurice Fallon

entry.summary: ScaRF-SLAM decouples classical feature-based visual SLAM for robust low-latency tracking from geometric foundation models used exclusively for mapping, anchoring mapping to SLAM poses and optimizing across depth scales. Achieves scale-consistent dense reconstruction.

entry.title: Dynamic Resilient Spatio-Semantic Memory with Hybrid Localization for Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Zhijie Yan, Shufei Li, Ze Zhang, Xin Liu, Yuhang Zheng, Zuoxu Wang

entry.summary: DREAM is a real-robot mobile manipulation framework that builds an online spatio-semantic voxel memory from RGB-D observations without a pre-built map, remaining geometrically consistent and semantically queryable as objects are relocated. Integrates perception, memory, localization, navigation, and manipulation.

entry.title: BEVIO: Efficient Bird's-Eye-View based Sparse-Update Visual-Inertial Odometry for Lunar Day-Night Navigation

author.name: Mohit Singh, Shehryar Khattak, Ashish Goel, Michael Paton, Kostas Alexis, Issa A. Nesnas

entry.summary: BEVIO enables reliable visual-inertial odometry with very sparse visual updates for lunar rovers via a bird's-eye-view image matching scheme robust to large inter-frame motion and difficult day-night self-illumination. Targets resource-constrained planetary navigation.

entry.title: RoboSemanticBench: Diagnosing Semantic Grounding in Action Prediction for VLA Models

author.name: Bin Yu, Yao Zhang, Haishan Liu, Shijie Lian, Yuliang Wei, Xiaopeng Lin, Zhaolong Shen, Changti Wu, Ruina Hu, Bailing Wang, Cong Huang, Kai Chen

entry.summary: RoboSemanticBench is a benchmark diagnosing whether VLA models genuinely use instruction semantics rather than visual or instruction-action shortcuts, requiring robots to answer embedded questions by grasping the correct answer block. It exposes weaknesses in semantic grounding of action prediction.

entry.title: Looking for backdoors in Jane Street LLMs

author.name: Cipolla

entry.summary: This post recounts the author's experience in the Jane Street LLM backdoor challenge, where they cracked some fine-tuned Qwen and DeepSeek-V3 models using white-box methods after prompting approaches failed. It shares partial results on finding hidden triggers in seemingly normal conversational models.

entry.title: Robust Shielding for Safe Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Edwin Hamel-De le Court, Thom Badings, Alessandro Abate, Francesco Belardinelli, Francesco Fabiano

entry.summary: This paper introduces a shielding framework for robust MDPs that guarantees safety under worst-case transition probabilities expressed as an LTL formula with a probability threshold, without assuming exact knowledge of safety-relevant dynamics. The shield is proven sound and optimal.

entry.title: Weak Critics Make Strong Learners: On-Policy Critique Distillation for Scalable Oversight

author.name: Can Jin, Jiakang Li, Rui Wu, Eddy Zhang, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: This work studies weak-critic strong oversight, using a weak model only to provide non-misleading revision directions rather than labels or judgments, and shows weak critiques can improve frozen strong models at inference time. It proposes progressive on-policy critique distillation for scalable oversight.

entry.title: SkillSmith: Co-Evolving Skills and Tools for Self-Improving Agent Systems

author.name: Yangbo Wei, Zhen Huang, Shaoqiang Lu, Junhong Qian, Qifan Wang, Chen Wu, Lei He

entry.summary: SkillSmith is a synergy-aware framework that co-evolves both skills and tools for self-improving agents, allowing tools to be wrapped, edited, composed, split, or retired when skill evolution reveals capability gaps. It uses an ecological utility model inspired by Lotka-Volterra dynamics to guide joint search.

entry.title: Characterization of Multi-Model Agentic AI Systems on General Tasks via Trace-Driven Simulation

author.name: Donghwan Kim, Prakhar Singh, Younghoon Min, Jongryool Kim, Jongse Park, Kiwan Maeng

entry.summary: GAIATrace introduces the first token-level trace dataset of two state-of-the-art agentic systems running the GAIA benchmark, capturing full reasoning tokens, task structures, and activities of participating LLMs for systems research. It enables trace-driven simulation to characterize multi-model agentic system behavior.

entry.title: TriAlign: Towards Universal Truth Consistency in Personalized LLM Alignment

author.name: Thi-Nhung Nguyen, Linhao Luo, Rollin Omari, Junae Kim, Thuy-Trang Vu, Dinh Phung

entry.summary: TriAlign studies truth-invariant alignment for personalized LLMs, ensuring universal truths remain consistent across social groups while preserving personalization, addressing the risk that some groups systematically receive less accurate answers. It proposes an offline multi-agent reinforcement learning framework.

entry.title: CAPF: Guiding Search-Agent Rollouts with Credit-Attenuated Privileged Feedback

author.name: Bin Chen, Xinye Liao, Yiming Liu, Xin Liao, Chonghan Liu

entry.summary: CAPF introduces Credit-Attenuated Privileged Feedback, a training-time mechanism that surfaces verifier-side information to guide search-agent rollouts on hard problems where end-to-end successful trajectories are rare. It provides feedback to identify errors and guide revision within the rollout under RLVR.

entry.title: WorldCoder-Bench: Benchmarking Physically Grounded 3D World Synthesis

author.name: Shuo Lu, Yinuo Xu, Kecheng Yu, Siru Jiang, Yongcan Yu, Yubin Wang, Haitao Yang, Yuxiang Zhang, Bin Wang, Ran He, Jian Liang

entry.summary: WorldCoder-Bench is a benchmark of 2,026 expert-curated tasks for autonomous physically grounded 3D world synthesis with Three.js, evaluating generated programs that must obey spatial and physical constraints and keep controls synchronized with hidden runtime state. It moves beyond pixel- or DOM-level evaluation into the opaque canvas.

entry.title: POIROT: Interrogating Agents for Failure Detection in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: I\~naki Dellibarda Varela, R. Sendra-Arranz, Pablo Romero-Sorozabal, J. M. Valverde-Garc\'ia, Annemarie F. Laudanski, \'Alvaro Guti\'errez, Eduardo Rocon, Manuel Cebrian

entry.summary: POIROT is a protocol that repurposes a multi-agent system's own agents as a distributed diagnostic layer for failure detection, leveraging existing epistemic diversity instead of centralized judgment. It outperforms single-LLM evaluator baselines with gains scaling with problem complexity.

entry.title: AgentPLM: Agentic Protein Language Models with Reasoning-Augmented Decoding for Protein Sequence Design

author.name: Sahil Rahman, Maxx Richard Rahman

entry.summary: AgentPLM equips a pretrained protein language model with reasoning-augmented decoding that interleaves generation with biophysical tool calls (ESMFold, FoldX, AutoDock Vina) and a trajectory-level preference optimization to learn when feedback is informative. It turns passive PLMs into active agentic designers.

entry.title: AGENTCL: Toward Rigorous Evaluation of Continual Learning in Language Agents

author.name: Yiheng Shu, Bernal Jim\'enez Guti\'errez, Saisri Padmaja Jonnalagedda, Yuguang Yao, Huan Sun, Yu Su

entry.summary: Presents AGENTCL, a benchmark for rigorously evaluating continual learning in language agents, addressing weaknesses of prior benchmarks that use naive task streams with limited cross-task relationship analysis. Aims to assess what agents actually learn and reuse over time.

entry.title: Foundation-Preserving Adaptation via Generalized Rayleigh-Quotient Optimization

author.name: Dongjun Kim, Adrian de Wynter, Huancheng Chen, Heasung Kim, Haris Vikalo

entry.summary: Proposes Foundation-Preserving LoRA (FoLoRA), which scores fine-tuning update directions by task utility per unit forgetting penalty using a generalized Rayleigh quotient. It actively regulates the adaptation-preservation trade-off during training rather than via fixed constraints.

entry.title: Persona Attack: Incremental Memory Injection Jailbreak Attack against Large Language Models

author.name: Junyoung Park, Seongyong Ju, Sunghwan Park, Jaewoo Lee

entry.summary: Proposes Persona Attack, an incremental memory-injection jailbreak that manipulates the model's context window step by step so accumulated injections override safety alignment. Shows increasing prioritization of injected instructions over internal safety mechanisms across widely used LLMs.

entry.title: BAGEN: Are LLM Agents Budget-Aware?

author.name: Yuxiang Lin, Zihan Wang, Mengyang Liu, Yuxuan Shan, Longju Bai, Junyao Zhang, Xing Jin, Boshan Chen, Jinyan Su, Xingyao Wang, Jiaxin Pei, Manling Li

entry.summary: Introduces BAGEN, a benchmark formalizing budget-awareness in LLM agents as progressive interval estimation of remaining internal and external budgets, with alerts when completion is unlikely. Finds consistent failure patterns across five frontier agents on four environments.

entry.title: Real2SAM2Real: Generative 3D Caches as Complementary Context for Video Diffusion

author.name: Jiayi Wu, Haoming Cai, Cornelia Fermuller, Christopher Metzler, Yiannis Aloimonos

entry.summary: Proposes Real2SAM2Real, leveraging 3D lifting models like SAM3D to extract an explicitly editable 3D cache that serves as a geometric scaffold for video diffusion models. It captures full 3D foreground volume to inject holistic spatial priors and enable precise camera/scene control.

entry.title: Drift Q-Learning

author.name: Anas Houssaini, Mohamad H. Danesh, Amin Abyaneh, Scott Fujimoto, Hsiu-Chin Lin, David Meger

entry.summary: Proposes DriftQL for offline RL, combining a drift-based behavioral regularizer with critic-driven policy improvement to bias the policy toward high-value data regions while attraction and repulsion prevent mode collapse. It avoids the iterative denoising and distillation required by diffusion/flow policies.

entry.title: Richer Representations for Neural Algorithmic Reasoning via Auxiliary Reconstruction

author.name: Jiafu Huang, Chao Peng, Chenyang Xu, Zhengfeng Yang, Kecheng Cai, Chenhao Zhang, Yi Wang, Yiwei Gong, Wanqin Zhou, Irene Zheng

entry.summary: This paper improves neural algorithmic reasoning by adding auxiliary reconstruction objectives to the encoder in encoder-processor-decoder architectures, where prior work focused mainly on the processor. Richer state representations improve replication of step-by-step algorithmic execution.

entry.title: GIRL-DETR: Gradient-Isolated Reinforcement Learning for Video Moment Retrieval

author.name: Shihang Zhang, Mingjin Kuai, Ye Wei, Zhen Zhang, Wei Ji

entry.summary: GIRL-DETR applies gradient-isolated reinforcement learning post-training to lightweight video moment retrieval DETR models, addressing misalignment between surrogate losses and non-differentiable metrics without disrupting fragile supervised features. It overcomes late-stage optimization stagnation.

entry.title: Certificates without Electrons? Theory and Evidence on Impacts from AI-Driven Power Demand

author.name: Dana Golden, Aruna Balasubramanian, Niranjan Balasubramanian

entry.summary: This paper develops a game-theoretic model of how data-center carbon-neutrality instruments (RECs, PPAs, colocation) affect grid reliability, prices, and emissions, identifying a timing wedge between consumption and credited renewable generation. It shows RECs covering 100% of consumption can still degrade outcomes.

entry.title: MLLM-Microscope: Unlocking Hidden Structure Within Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Ravil Mussabayev, Rustam Mussabayev

entry.summary: MLLM-Microscope analyzes hidden representations in multimodal LLMs by measuring linearity, intrinsic dimension, and anisotropy of multimodal token embeddings across layers, comparing LLaVA-NeXT and OmniFusion on ScienceQA. It finds highly linear behavior with model-specific differences in image-token properties.

entry.title: Beyond Task Success: Behavioral and Representational Diagnostics for WAM and VLA

author.name: Hung Mai, Bin Zhu, Tuan Do

entry.summary: Introduces a model-agnostic diagnostic framework comparing World-Action Models and vision-language-action policies via behavioral rollout analysis and sparse-autoencoder feature analysis. Asks whether future prediction in WAMs yields behaviorally meaningful improvements beyond task success.

entry.title: PSG-Nav: Probabilistic Scene Graph Navigation via Multiverse Decision Making

author.name: Rufeng Chen, Yue Chang, Xiaqiang Tang, Hechang Chen, Sihong Xie

entry.summary: Proposes PSG-Nav, building a 3D probabilistic scene graph with full semantic categorical distributions to handle perception uncertainty in open-vocabulary navigation, plus a Multiverse Decision mechanism that samples multiple likely worlds. Moves beyond local deterministic navigation decisions.

entry.title: UR-JEPA: Uniform Rectifiability as a Regularizer for Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures

author.name: Triet M. Le

entry.summary: Proposes UR-JEPA, which prevents representation collapse in joint-embedding predictive architectures by targeting a uniformly rectifiable measure respecting the manifold hypothesis, rather than LeJEPA's isotropic Gaussian target. Realized via a Carleson-type square function regularizer.

entry.title: TN-SHAP-G: Graph-Structured Tensor Network Surrogates for Shapley Values and Interactions

author.name: Farzaneh Heidari, Guillaume Rabusseau

entry.summary: TN-SHAP-G uses graph-structured tensor network surrogates to efficiently compute Shapley values and higher-order interactions for graph-structured inputs. It learns a compact multilinear surrogate mirroring the input graph topology, enabling deterministic recovery of interaction indices.

entry.title: AlphaToken: Decoupling Adaptation and Stability for Path-Aware Response Token Valuation in LLM Post-Training

author.name: Liu Qing, Ou Wu, Yi Du

entry.summary: AlphaToken is a response-token valuation framework for LLM post-training that decouples adaptation and stability, making each path-aware via local gradients and downstream causal signals. It approximates stability with a Fisher-drift proxy when retention data is unavailable.

entry.title: Order within Chaos: Capturing Intrinsic Energy Anomalies for AI-Manipulated Image Forgery Localization

author.name: Yiming Wang, Baiqi Wu, Qingming Li, Jiahao Chen, Tong Zhang, Shouling Ji

entry.summary: Proposes FLAME, a forgery localization framework that exploits a theoretically derived statistical energy gap—diffusion suppresses local high-frequency variance—to detect AI-manipulated image regions. Uses a LAD map plus a parameter-efficient SAM adapter for pixel-level localization.

entry.title: AutoForest: Automatically Generating Forest Plots from Biomedical Studies with End-to-End Evidence Extraction and Synthesis

author.name: Massimiliano Pronesti, Angelo Miculescu, Mohsin Kapdi, Paul Flanagan, Ois\'in Redmond, Joao Bettencourt-Silva, Gurdeep Mannu, Spiros Denaxas, Rui Bebiano Da Providencia E Costa, Anya Belz, Yufang Hou

entry.summary: Introduces AutoForest, claimed first end-to-end system automating the full pipeline from raw biomedical documents to synthesized forest plots, including data extraction, intervention/comparator definition, harmonization, and meta-analytic computation. Targets labor-intensive systematic reviews.

entry.title: Learning When to Translate for Multilingual Reasoning

author.name: Deokhyung Kang, Hyounghun Kim, Gary Geunbae Lee

entry.summary: Proposes Luar, a reinforcement learning framework that trains reasoning LLMs to selectively invoke English translation only when direct understanding of non-English input is unreliable. Addresses multilingual reasoning gaps without translating every query.

entry.title: FLaG: Fine-Grained Latent Grouping for Hallucination Detection

author.name: Wentao Ye, Liyao Li, Zhiqing Xiao, Muzhi Zhu, Jiaqi Hu, Zhanming Shen, Xiaomeng Hu, Sean Du, Haobo Wang

entry.summary: Proposes FLaG, a hallucination-detection framework that treats detection as mechanism-aware evidence aggregation, softly routing each instance to multiple latent evidence groups via energy-based routing and combining group-conditional reliability signals through log-marginal aggregation. Captures heterogeneous failure mechanisms a single global score misses.

entry.title: Perturbative methods for non-parametric instrumental variable

author.name: Wei Bu, Arthur Gretton

entry.summary: Introduces a perturbative approach inspired by physics for nonparametric instrumental variable estimation, extending kernel ridge methods with higher-order corrections that improve accuracy especially for ill-posed integral equations and high-dimensional regimes. Co-authored by Arthur Gretton.

entry.title: PE-means: Improved Differentially Private $k$-means Clustering through Private Evolution

author.name: Thomas Humphries, Zinan Lin, Sergey Yekhanin

entry.summary: Extends the private evolution algorithm to differentially private k-means clustering, computing a private histogram with constant sensitivity to guide evolution rather than summing private data with domain-proportional sensitivity. Reports ~20% average improvement in clustering loss over state-of-the-art.

entry.title: Saliency-Aware Model Merging

author.name: Jungin Park, Jiyoung Lee, Kwanghoon Sohn

entry.summary: Proposes SA-Merging, a data-free model merging method that uses connectivity-based saliency scores (extending SynFlow-style pruning) over task vectors plus merge-aware modulation to reduce task interference. Aims to scale model merging beyond simple parameter heuristics.

entry.title: Rethinking Bregman Divergences in Kronecker-Factored Optimizers

author.name: Bing Liu, Wenjie Zhou, Chengcheng Zhao

entry.summary: Analyzes how the choice of Bregman divergence in Kronecker-factored optimizers (Shampoo-style) affects approximation error when covariance is not exactly Kronecker-factored, studied through spectral properties. Provides theoretical insight into preconditioner design.

entry.title: LASER: Loss-Aware Singular-value Decomposition and Rank Allocation for Efficient Low-Precision Vision-Language Models

author.name: Haiyu Wang, Yutong Wang, Leshu Li, Yihui Ren, Sai Qian Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes LASER, a loss-aware SVD with curvature-weighted objectives and adaptive rank allocation across both attention and feed-forward layers for compressing low-precision vision-language models. Improves efficient VLM deployment.

entry.title: CUPID in the Model Zoo: Online Matchmaking for Selecting Your Dream LLM

author.name: Son Nguyen, Xinyuan Liu, Ransalu Senanayake

entry.summary: Proposes CUPID, an interaction-efficient active learning framework using a dueling bandit algorithm with a belief-aware UCB strategy to help users select the best LLM from a model zoo via pairwise feedback. Infers latent user preferences they may not articulate.

entry.title: Revisiting Neural Processes via Fourier Transform and Volterra Series

author.name: Peiman Mohseni, Nick Duffield, Raymond K. W. Wong

entry.summary: Revisits neural processes through Fourier transform and Volterra series, providing an interpretable function-class view of translation-equivariant NPs that avoids the local-receptive-field and uniform-grid limitations of convolutional designs. Improves interpretability and flexibility.

entry.title: Temporal Motif Signatures for Temporal Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Dylan Sandfelder, Mihai Cucuringu, Xiaowen Dong

entry.summary: Shows that short-horizon temporal motif patterns (repetition, reciprocity, star diversity, triadic flow) carry predictive structure that temporal GNNs often miss, and designs a compact leakage-safe 13-coordinate motif feature map. Demonstrates strong lift on MOOC interaction prediction.

entry.title: Ablating Archetypes: The Stability of Archetypal SAEs is an Artifact of Initialization and Metric Design

author.name: Micha{\l} Brzozowski, Neo Christopher Chung

entry.summary: This paper argues that the reported stability of Archetypal sparse autoencoders is an artifact of identical initialization across runs and metric design rather than a genuine property. It clarifies ambiguous notions of stability in mechanistic interpretability.

entry.title: Regularized Large Neighborhood Search

author.name: Germain Vivier-Ardisson, Laurent Demonet, Axel Parmentier, Mathieu Blondel

entry.summary: Regularized Large Neighborhood Search turns the LNS heuristic into an efficient MCMC sampler over feasible solutions by regularizing local subproblems, with associated Fenchel-Young losses. It bridges combinatorial optimization layers and neural networks without requiring exact global solutions.

entry.title: A Biconvex Formulation for Stable Transport of Mixture Models with a Unique Solution

author.name: Yeganeh Marghi, Kelly Jin, Uygar S\"umb\"ul

entry.summary: Proposes Optimal Mixture Transport, reformulating optimal transport between mixture models as a biconvex problem with a unique global minimizer and proven stability guarantees. Improves scalability and interpretability over pointwise transport plans.

entry.title: Stochastic Rounding Increases Small Singular Values

author.name: Linkai Ma, Tingzhou Yu, Petros Drineas

entry.summary: Sharpens theory showing stochastic rounding acts as an implicit regularizer by increasing small singular values, extending the effect beyond extreme aspect ratios to constant aspect ratio matrices. Deepens understanding of low-precision arithmetic in ML.

entry.title: Accelerating Min-Max Optimization via Power-Law Stepsizes

author.name: Yue Wu, Weiqiang Zheng, Yang Cai, Haipeng Luo

entry.summary: Provides the first positive result showing that deterministic power-law dynamic stepsizes alone accelerate Extragradient last-iterate convergence for biaffine min-max optimization to O(T^{-2}), beating the fixed-stepsize Theta(T^{-1/2}) rate. It draws on recent dynamic-stepsize advances for gradient descent.

entry.title: Learning Action-Conditional and Object-Centric Gaussian Splatting World Models for Rigid Objects

author.name: Jens U. Kreber, Lukas Mack, Joerg Stueckler

entry.summary: Introduces MRO-GWM, an action-conditional, object-centric Gaussian-splatting world model that predicts future rigid-body motion of multiple objects via a spatio-temporal transformer operating on canonical-frame Gaussians. It supports arbitrary shapes and multi-object scenes for agent prediction.

entry.title: From Empathy to Personalized Empathy: Adapting Empathetic Strategies to Individual Users

author.name: Wuqiang Zheng, Chengbing Wang, Yilin Yang, Junyi Cheng, Jianfei Xiao, Hu Sun, Yi Xie, Yangyang Li, Wenjie Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces personalized empathy, adapting empathetic strategies to individual user personality traits derived from interaction history. It contributes PersonaEmp, a dataset built from long-term user-AI interactions, and PereGRM, a reward modeling framework for personalization.

entry.title: From Outliers to Errors: Auditing Pali-to-English LLM Translations with Multi-Reference Adjudication

author.name: M\'at\'e Metzger, Nadnapang Phophichit, Hansa Dhammahaso

entry.summary: This paper audits Pali-to-English translations from four flagship LLMs using three human translations as a reference envelope rather than a single gold standard, with embedding drift triaging candidates for blinded adjudication. It addresses how single-score metrics conflate legitimate variation with error for classical languages.

entry.title: RoboTrustBench: Benchmarking the Trustworthiness of Video World Models for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Huiqiong Li, Jiayu Wang, Zhiting Mei, Anirudha Majumdar, Jingjing Chen, Bin Zhu

entry.summary: RoboTrustBench benchmarks the trustworthiness of video world models for robotic manipulation under Normal, Constraint-Sensitive, Counterfactual, and Adversarial scenarios. Built from real DROID episodes, it finds models produce coherent videos but fail at constraint reasoning, counterfactual grounding, and physical plausibility.

entry.title: Where to Look: Can Foundation Models Reach a Target Viewpoint Through Active Exploration?

author.name: Liyang Li, Muzhi Zhu, Zhiyue Zhao, Hengyu Zhao, Ke Liu, Linhao Zhong, Hao Chen, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: This work introduces Target Viewpoint Reproduction (TVR), an active task where an agent adjusts its viewpoint until matching a target image, plus TVRBench. Strong open and closed-source models achieve only 7.8% and 12.0% success, revealing major weaknesses in active spatial intelligence.

entry.title: PhyScene3D: Physically Consistent Interactive 3D Tabletop Scene Generation

author.name: Weixing Chen, Zhuoqian Feng, Yang Liu, Yexin Zhang, Yifan Wen, Yinghong Liao, Weichao Qiu, Guanbin Li, Liang Lin

entry.summary: Introduces PhyScene3D, a framework for generating physically consistent, collision-free 3D tabletop scenes for robotic learning by reformulating generation as a human-mimetic constructive process with a cognitive topological reasoning chain. Targets the gap between symbolic solvers and end-to-end regression that suffer from physical violations.

entry.title: Personalized 3D Myocardial Infarct Geometry Reconstruction from Cine MRI for Cardiac Digital Twins

author.name: Yilin Lyu, Mark YY Chan, Ching-Hui Sia, Lei Li

entry.summary: Proposes a geometry-motion embedded model to reconstruct personalized 3D myocardial infarct geometries directly from contrast-free cine MRI for cardiac digital twins, avoiding contrast agents needed in standard LGE MRI. Enables simulation-ready geometries for electrophysiology modeling.

entry.title: Polaris: Scaling Up Instruction-Guided Image Generation Towards Millions of Personalized Style Needs

author.name: Zhi-Kai Chen, Jun-Peng Jiang, Jun-Jie Tao, De-Chuan Zhan, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: Presents Polaris, a retrieval framework that systematically exploits an expanding ecosystem of fine-tuned modules and adapters to fulfill diverse personalized image generation needs without retraining new models. Scales instruction-guided generation toward millions of style requirements.

entry.title: Generalization Limits in Vehicle Re-Identification

author.name: Anis Yassine Ben Mabrouk (CB), Antoine Tadros (CB), Rafael Grompone von Gioi (CB), Gabriele Facciolo (CMLA, LIGM), Axel Davy (CB), Rodrigo Verschae

entry.summary: Critically examines vehicle re-identification benchmarks, showing that test sets contain near-identical vehicles from training, so memorization inflates scores while generalization fails. Proposes a new evaluation approach with view-based splits to measure true generalization.

entry.title: FocusDiT: Masking Queries in Diffusion Transformers for Fine-grained Image Generation

author.name: Xueji Fang, Liyuan Ma, Jianhao Zeng, Jinjin Cao, Mingyuan Zhou, Guo-Jun Qi

entry.summary: Proposes FocusDiT, which applies a masking scheme in diffusion transformers to focus computation on critical query tokens corresponding to complex details, treating the FFN as a key-value vocabulary for visual knowledge. Aims to improve fine-grained image generation.

entry.title: InsightVQA: High-Dimensional Emotion-Cognitive Visual Question Answering Benchmark

author.name: Shiyu Wang (East China Normal University, Shanghai, China), Ziyu Liu (East China Normal University, Shanghai, China), Chaoyi Yu (East China Normal University, Shanghai, China), Yujie Yin (East China Normal University, Shanghai, China), Zhongqian Mao (East China Normal University, Shanghai, China), Jing Chen (East China Normal University, Shanghai, China), Jiaqi Song (East China Normal University, Shanghai, China), Yunshi Lan (East China Normal University, Shanghai, China), Yan Wang (East China Normal University, Shanghai, China)

entry.summary: Introduces InsightVQA, a large-scale hierarchical visual question answering benchmark for emotion understanding and cognitive reasoning, with 138K curated images annotated at three levels (perception, grounded understanding, response-oriented). Moves beyond simple emotion recognition toward causal reasoning.

entry.title: PRIMA: Boosting Animal Mesh Recovery with Biological Priors and Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Xiaohang Yu, Ti Wang, Mackenzie Weygandt Mathis

entry.summary: Presents PRIMA, a framework for robust 3D quadruped mesh recovery under severe species and pose imbalance, incorporating BioCLIP biological priors and a test-time adaptation strategy to refine SMAL predictions. Improves generalization to underrepresented animals and rare articulations.

entry.title: Spatial-Temporal Decoupled Reference Conditioning for Identity-Preserving Text-to-Video Generation

author.name: Yuheng Chen, Teng Hu, Yuji Wang, Qingdong He, Lizhuang Ma, Jiangning Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces ST-DRC, a spatial-temporal decoupled reference conditioning framework for identity-preserving text-to-video generation that injects reference identity via video-VAE in-context concatenation while balancing semantic control and low-level identity fidelity. Avoids additional adapters for identity details.

entry.title: From Zero to Hero: Training-Free Custom Concept Spawning in World Models

author.name: Kiymet Akdemir, Pinar Yanardag

entry.summary: Presents a training-free method to inject user-specified custom concepts into autoregressive video world models at chosen locations, enabling controllable scene composition beyond base-model priors. Useful for gaming and interactive simulation.

entry.title: Single-Line Drawing Generation via Semantics-Driven Optimization

author.name: Tanguy Magne, Alexandre Binninger, Ruben Wiersma, Olga Sorkine-Hornung

entry.summary: Presents the first semantics-driven method for generating single continuous-line vector drawings from text or image prompts using score distillation sampling on B-spline curves. Provides control over detail level and artistic style.

entry.title: Whole-Body Inverse Kinematics with Graph Diffusion

author.name: Helong Huang, Kai Tan, Feng Wen, Guowei Huang, Xingyue Quan

entry.summary: GraphDiff-IK is a structure-aware graph diffusion framework for inverse kinematics that represents robots as kinematic graphs from URDF and formulates IK as conditional graph diffusion. Generalizes across morphologies and models multi-modal solutions.

entry.title: DriveAnchor: Progressive Anchor-based Flow Learning for Autonomous Driving Planning

author.name: Limin Yan, Haoyun Tang, Yutao Qiu, Hongqing Liu, Haoyu Xu

entry.summary: DriveAnchor is a three-stage flow-matching framework for autonomous driving planning that replaces Gaussian priors with a vocabulary of 2,398 trajectory shapes, adds corridor-based controllability via an energy field, and ensures safety. Composable behavioral diversity and control.

entry.title: Global-Local Attention Decomposition for Terrain Encoding in Humanoid Perceptive Locomotion

author.name: Shengcheng Fu, Yang Zhang, Zhanxiang Cao, Liyun Yan, Yizhi Chen, Yunpeng Yin, Yue Gao

entry.summary: GLAD decomposes terrain encoding into a global attention branch summarizing surrounding context and a state-conditioned local attention branch for precise foothold selection in humanoid perceptive locomotion. Improves performance on sparse-foothold terrain.

entry.title: Infeasible optimization problems and the hierarchical augmented Lagrangian method in imitation learning

author.name: Roland Andrews, Justin Carpentier, Ajay Sathya

entry.summary: Studies infeasible constrained imitation learning optimization problems and applies a hierarchical augmented Lagrangian method that drives policies toward the closest feasible constrained solution. Provides theoretical grounding for handling infeasible safety constraints.

entry.title: ImagineUAV: Aerial Vision-Language Navigation via World-Action Modeling and Kinodynamic Planning

author.name: Xuchen Liu, Jiawei Huang, Shihao Xia, Bingxi Liu, Jinqiang Cui, Jiankun Yang

entry.summary: ImagineUAV is an imagination-driven aerial vision-language navigation framework using a latent video diffusion model to generate instruction-conditioned future observations, from which 6-DoF motions are inferred and refined into collision-free trajectories by a kinodynamic planner. Addresses brittleness of VLA models from geometric inconsistency.

entry.title: Trans2Occ: Voxel Occupancy Estimation and Grasp for Transparent Objects from Simulation to Reality

author.name: Yixuan Yang, Sha Zhang, Rui Li, Zhenfei Yin, Xinzhu Ma, Yiran Qin, Lei Bai, Xudong Xu, Shilin Shan, Wangmeng Zuo, Yanyong Zhang, Wanli Ouyang, Feng Zheng, Shixiang Tang, Dongzhan Zhou

entry.summary: Trans2Occ predicts voxel-space occupancy directly from single-view RGB for transparent object grasping, avoiding unreliable depth from refraction and reflection, trained via a simulation pipeline generating paired RGB and voxel annotations across diverse materials and lighting. Enables sim-to-real transparent object manipulation.

entry.title: Intercepting the Future: Latent-Space Predictive World Model for Dynamic VLA Manipulation

author.name: Shahram Najam Syed, Arthur Jakobsson, Haoran Hao, Jeffrey Ichnowski

entry.summary: AHEAD augments a frozen VLA with a motion-aware latent world model that forecasts future feature tokens conditioned on per-token velocity and acceleration from optical flow, enabling manipulation of moving objects. It closes the latency gap that causes VLA failures on dynamic scenes.

entry.title: Monitoring computer-use agents in OSWorld-control

author.name: Chris Harig

entry.summary: This post builds a control setting for computer-use agents in OSWorld and studies monitoring setups, finding attackers can exploit tool-call opacity and screenshot-action gaps to exfiltrate data or access credentials without being caught. The results validate but do not comprehensively prove a monitoring evasion strategy.

entry.title: Open and closed models are on different exponentials

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert argues that open and closed AI models are on different economic exponentials, driven by whether users keep paying large premiums for top closed models, especially in coding agents. He predicts labs will protect their best models, delay API releases to avoid distillation, and that API businesses will decay.

entry.title: MindZero: Learning Online Mental Reasoning With Zero Annotations

author.name: Shunchi Zhang, Jin Lu, Chuanyang Jin, Yichao Zhou, Zhining Zhang, Tianmin Shu

entry.summary: MindZero is a self-supervised RL framework that trains multimodal LLMs for online Theory of Mind reasoning without ground-truth mental-state annotations, rewarding hypotheses that maximize the likelihood of observed actions. It supports efficient, uncertainty-aware online inference for real-time assistance.

entry.title: From Noise to Control: Parameterized Diffusion Policies

author.name: Renhao Zhang, Haotian Fu, Mingxi Jia, George Konidaris, Yilun Du, Bruno Castro da Silva

entry.summary: Parameterized Diffusion Policy conditions diffusion policies on low-dimensional continuous parameters embedded in a learned behavior manifold where distances reflect trajectory similarity, turning diffusion into a steerable optimization tool. It enables smooth interpolation between strategies and weight-free adaptation, validated on simulated and real robots.

entry.title: Hidden Thoughts Are Not Secret: Reasoning Trace Exposure in LLMs

author.name: Yu-An Lu, Ci-Yang Tsai, Yu-Lin Tsai, Raluca Ada Popa, Chia-Mu Yu

entry.summary: This paper studies whether hiding raw reasoning traces at the interface level prevents users from extracting useful reasoning supervision, introducing Reasoning Exposure Prompting that uses shadow-model demonstrations to elicit hidden traces. It suggests trace-hiding deployments do not fully protect proprietary reasoning behavior.

entry.title: DAG-MoE: From Simple Mixture to Structural Aggregation in Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Jiarui Feng, Hanqing Zeng, Karish Grover, Ruizhong Qiu, Yinglong Xia, Qiang Zhang, Qifan Wang, Ren Chen, Dongqi Fu, Jiayi Liu, Zhoukai Zhao, Xiangjun Fan, Benyu Zhang, Yixin Chen

entry.summary: DAG-MoE explores structural aggregation of expert outputs in Mixture-of-Experts as a complementary scaling axis, theoretically showing that replacing weighted summation with structural aggregation expands the expert-combination space without changing experts or router and enables multi-step reasoning within a single MoE layer. It addresses routing overhead bottlenecks of fine-grained experts.

entry.title: HomeFlow: A Data Flywheel for Smart Home Agent Training with Verifiable Simulation

author.name: Yi Gu, Huacan Wang, Shuo Zhang, Yuqing Hou, Lei Xue, Weipeng Ming, Chen Liu, Fangzhou Yu, Kuan Li, Ronghao Chen, Sen Hu, Xiaofeng Mou, Yi Xu

entry.summary: HomeFlow is a verifiable data flywheel for training smart home agents, using a simulation environment, procedural home generation, intent-to-success-condition compilation, and MCTS-based synthesis of verifiable multi-turn trajectories. It addresses the scarcity of high-quality training data for physical-world agents.

entry.title: Recognize Your Orchestrator: An Entropy Dynamics Perspective for LLM Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Junze Zhu, Weihao Chen, Xuanwang Zhang, Zhen Wu, Xinyu Dai

entry.summary: This work models LLM multi-agent orchestration as a mean-field entropy dynamics system governed by competing forces of task resolution and cumulative context loading, and introduces Inverse Workflow Generation to synthesize process-verifiable benchmarks. The entropy model fits empirical trajectories and yields interpretable stability parameters.

entry.title: Don't Ask the LLM to Track Freshness: A Deterministic Recipe for Memory Conflict Resolution

author.name: Vikas Reddy, Sumanth Challaram

entry.summary: This paper argues that LLM memory systems fail at temporal conflict resolution because the assembly step relies on LLM-mediated retrieval, and proposes a deterministic recipe for freshness tracking instead. It shows existing systems severely underperform on MemoryAgentBench's FactConsolidation task.

entry.title: Joint Agent Memory and Exploration Learning via Novelty Signals

author.name: Shizuo Tian, Xiaohong Weng, Rui Kong, Yuxuan Chen, Guohong Liu, Yuebing Song, Jiacheng Liu, Yuchen Li, Dawei Yin, Ting Cao, Yunxin Liu, Yuanchun Li

entry.summary: JAMEL jointly trains agentic latent memory and exploration policy through novelty-driven interaction, exploiting the mutual dependency where memory enables distinguishing exhausted behaviors and exploration generates supervisory signals. It addresses costly raw-history retention in long-horizon open-ended environments.

entry.title: Consistency evaluation of benchmarks used for causal discovery

author.name: Yuzhe Zhang, Chihui Chen, Lina Yao, Chen Wang

entry.summary: This work is the first to systematically study the quality of benchmark causal graphs, designing a pipeline that retrieves relevant research papers and prompts LLMs to check consistency between benchmark graphs and current literature. It highlights how misaligned domain knowledge affects evaluation of LLM-based causal discovery.

entry.title: Extreme Low-Bit Inference in Reasoning Models: Failure Modes and Targeted Recovery

author.name: Ekaterina Alimaskina, Darya Rudas, Denis Shveykin, Gleb Molodtsov, Pavel Vasiliev, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: This work shows that aggressive 2-bit quantization of large reasoning models can fail to deliver speedups because instability inflates token counts via repetitive loops and budget exhaustion, linking accuracy loss to process-level failures. It introduces lightweight controls including FP16 planning to recover performance.

entry.title: SIRI: Self-Internalizing Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Skills for LLM Agent Training

author.name: Zhongyu He, Yuanfan Li, Fei Huang, Tianyu Chen, Siyuan Chen, Xingyang Li, Meng Hsuan Yu, Xiangrong Liu, Leyi Wei, Lu Pan, Ke Zeng, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: SIRI is a three-phase RL framework that lets LLM agents discover, validate, and internalize reusable skills without external skill generators or inference-time skill banks, reducing engineering complexity and latency. It mines skills from the agent's own successful trajectories.

entry.title: A phenomenon of AI-conformity: how algorithms change human moral decision-making

author.name: Yana Venerina, Dmitry Koch, Nare Meloyan, Gerda Prutko, Valeriia Lelik, Victoria Taova, Andrey Kurpatov

entry.summary: Adapts the classic Asch conformity paradigm to study whether AI judgments shift human moral decision-making, finding evidence for algorithmic conformity across conditions with AI answers and explanations among 165 participants. Explores a poorly understood novel influence mechanism.

entry.title: BitsMoE: Efficient Spectral Energy-Guided Bit Allocation for MoE LLM Quantization

author.name: Jiayu Zhao, Zihan Teng, Minhao Fan, Tianrui Ma, Wentao Ren, Song Chen, Weichen Liu

entry.summary: BitsMoE is a spectral-energy-guided bit-allocation framework for Mixture-of-Experts LLM quantization that decomposes layers via SVD into a shared unquantized basis and expert-specific spectral factors, allocating bits by importance to enable ultra-low-bit compression. Addresses memory-intensive MoE deployment.

entry.title: Diffusion Image Generation with Explicit Modeling of Data Manifold Geometry

author.name: Duoduo Xue, Zhiyu Zhu, Junhui Hou

entry.summary: MIND is a diffusion image generation framework that explicitly models data-manifold geometry by integrating discrete patch tokenization into a continuous diffusion score function, enabled by a soft top-k aggregation for end-to-end differentiable training plus dual-branch high-frequency features. Combines discrete structural quantification with continuous generation flexibility.

entry.title: Diversity Over Frequency: Rethinking Tool Use in Visual Chain-of-Thought Agents

author.name: Dong-Hee Kim, Reuben Tan, Donghyun Kim

entry.summary: Investigates visual tool use in visual chain-of-thought agents beyond simple search, identifying a tool-use collapse phenomenon where models stop using tools while achieving higher accuracy, and finding eliminating tools degrades performance while incentivizing diverse tool use helps. Emphasizes diversity over frequency of tool use.

entry.title: StemBind: When MLLMs Get Lost Between Rules and Instances in Abstract Visual Reasoning

author.name: Xixiang He, Baiqi Wu, Xingming Li, Ao Cheng, Qiyao Sun, Xuanyu Ji, Qingyong Hu

entry.summary: Introduces StemBind, a shared-stem diagnostic benchmark for abstract visual reasoning that probes perception, rule induction, and answer selection separately on the same visual stem. It reveals that MLLMs often know the rule but still pick the wrong answer.

entry.title: DataShield: Safety-degrading Data Filtering for LLM Benign Instruction Fine-Tuning

author.name: Junbo Zhang, Qianli Zhou, Xinyang Deng, Wen Jiang, Jie Pan, Jinbiao Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes DataShield, an efficient method to identify safety-degrading samples within benign fine-tuning datasets by quantifying each sample's contribution to response compliance. It uses compliance vector extraction to assign safety-degradation scores without costly procedures.

entry.title: Interpretable Policy Distillation for Power Grid Topology Control

author.name: Aleksandra Dmitruka, Karlis Freivalds

entry.summary: This work distills a PPO agent for power grid topology control into compact decision trees and random forests, achieving comparable or better operational performance with interpretability and low compute. It uses stress-focused data collection on critical grid states.

entry.title: Benchmarks for Vision-Language Models in Urban Perception Should Be Reliability-Aware and Negotiated

author.name: Rashid Mushkani

entry.summary: This position-and-benchmark paper argues that VLM benchmarks for urban perception should treat annotator disagreement and abstention as measurement outcomes, report inter-annotator reliability, and treat label spaces as negotiable when informing governance. It grounds the argument in a Montreal street-scene benchmark.

entry.title: Leyline: KV Cache Directives for Agentic Inference

author.name: Bole Ma, Jan Eitzinger, Harald Koestler

entry.summary: Proposes KV cache directives for agentic inference, addressing the problem that agentic conversations involve policy-driven editing (retries, drops, pivots) that invalidate append-only cache assumptions. Focuses on actively removing or replacing cached spans.

entry.title: HASTE: Hardware-Aware Dynamic Sparse Training for Large Output Spaces

author.name: Nasib Ullah, Jinbin Zhang, Jean Lucien Randrianantenaina, Erik Schultheis, Rohit Babbar

entry.summary: Introduces group-shared fixed fan-in sparsity for extreme multi-label classification, where semantically related labels share a sparse input pattern while retaining independent weights. Achieves hardware-aware speedups by reducing irregular memory access in large output layers.

entry.title: CA-BED: Conversation-Aware Bayesian Experimental Design

author.name: Daniel Arnould, Rashad Aziz, Zixuan Kang, Tanav Changal, Kevin Zhu, Sunishchal Dev, Gabriel Grand, Shreyas Sunil Kulkarni

entry.summary: Proposes Conversation-Aware Bayesian Experimental Design, an inference-time framework integrating Bayesian experimental design with LLM likelihood estimation to optimize question selection over conversational turns. Maintains a belief distribution and anticipates ambiguous answers.

entry.title: TECCI: Tricky Edits of Collected and Curated Images

author.name: Aishwarya Agrawal, Roy Hirsch, Yasumasa Onoe, Sherry Ben, Jason Baldridge

entry.summary: Proposes TECCI, a new image-editing benchmark of curated images intentionally designed to target weaknesses of current text-guided editors on hard edits like position, motion, viewpoint, scale, and creative changes. Spans seven curated image categories.

entry.title: Understanding LLM Behavior in Multi-Target Cross-Lingual Summarization

author.name: Sangwon Ryu, Yihong Liu, Mingyang Wang, Yunsu Kim, Jungseul Ok, Gary Geunbae Lee, Hinrich Schuetze

entry.summary: Introduces MEA, a multi-target cross-lingual summarization benchmark covering 24 languages, and provides layer-wise analysis showing translation and summarization behaviors emerge jointly in later LLM layers. Finds MTXLS performance lags far behind English monolingual summarization.

entry.title: SkillAdaptor: Self-Adapting Skills for LLM Agents from Trajectories

author.name: Zhuoyun Yu, Xin Xie, Wuguannan Yao, Chenxi Wang, Lei Liang, Xiang Qi, Shumin Deng

entry.summary: Proposes SkillAdaptor, a training-free step-level skill adaptation framework for LLM agents that identifies the first actionable fault step in failed trajectories and applies targeted skill updates with acceptance checks. Enables fine-grained failure attribution while keeping the backbone frozen.

entry.title: Neural Network Compression by Approximate Differential Equivalence

author.name: Ravi Dhiman, Andrea Passarella, Mirco Tribastone, Lorenzo Valerio

entry.summary: Proposes compressing neural networks by aggregating neurons with similar functional behavior via an ODE-based lumping method (Approximate Forward Differential Equivalence) rather than removing weights. A single tolerance parameter controls the size-accuracy trade-off.

entry.title: On the Limits of Token Reduction for Efficient Unified Vision Language Training

author.name: Siyi Chen, Weiming Zhuang, Jingtao Li, Lingjuan Lv

entry.summary: This paper studies token-reduction acceleration for unified vision-language model training, uncovering an asymmetry where understanding tasks tolerate late-layer visual redundancy but generation tasks depend persistently on image tokens. It designs task-specific accelerators based on this insight.

entry.title: The Image Reconstruction Game: Drawing Common Ground Through Iterative Multimodal Dialogue

author.name: Sherzod Hakimov, Mattia D'Agostini, Ivan Samodelkin, David Schlangen

entry.summary: The Image Reconstruction Game is an automated benchmark where a vision-language describer issues corrective instructions to an image generator across turns, making accumulated common ground observable as a rendered image. It finds the describer dominates reconstruction quality while the generator determines whether refinement helps.

entry.title: A Structured Benchmark for Text-Guided Anomaly Detection: When Language Stops Conditioning the Decision

author.name: Stefano Samele, Eugenio Lomurno, Teodora Jovanovic, Sanjay Shivakumar Manohar, Alberto Crivellaro, Matteo Matteucci

entry.summary: TGAD is a structured benchmark for text-guided anomaly detection that progressively increases the functional role of language across scenarios, testing whether text actually conditions decisions versus relying on pretrained visual features. It challenges protocols that hold textual conditions constant.

entry.title: How Hard Can It Be? Hardness-Aware Multi-Objective Unlearning

author.name: Jiangwei Chen, Xinyuan Niu, Rachael Hwee Ling Sim, Zhengyuan Liu, Nancy F. Chen, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low

entry.summary: Proposes a hardness-aware, theoretically grounded constrained-optimization approach to machine unlearning that quantifies the difficulty of reconciling forget-quality and retain-utility objectives via data similarity. Aims to guarantee improvement of both objectives by specified amounts.

entry.title: On the Generalization in Topology Optimization via Sensitivity-Conditioned Bernoulli Flow Matching

author.name: Mohammad Rashed, Duarte F. Valoroso Madeira, Babak Gholami, Caglar Guerbuez, Yunjia Yang, Nils Thuerey

entry.summary: Studies OOD generalization of surrogate models for topology optimization, hypothesizing that performance depends on how much the conditioning signal preserves adjoint sensitivity information. Uses sensitivity-conditioned Bernoulli flow matching grounded in the Data Processing Inequality.

entry.title: Initialization is Half the Battle: Generating Diverse Images from a Guidance Potential Posterior

author.name: Xiang Li, Dianbo Liu, Kenji Kawaguchi

entry.summary: Identifies that standard Gaussian initialization in generative models causes trajectories to collapse into dominant modes, contributing to mode collapse. Proposes DivIn, which samples initial noise from a guidance-potential posterior via Langevin dynamics to enhance diversity.

entry.title: AdaCodec: A Predictive Visual Code for Video MLLMs

author.name: Haowen Hou, Zhen Huang, Zheming Liang, Qingyi Si, Chenglin Li, Shuai Dong, Kele Shao, Ruilin Li, Dianyi Wang, Nan Duan, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes AdaCodec, a predictive visual code for video MLLMs that sends a full reference frame only when the scene cannot be predicted from prior context and otherwise transmits compact inter-frame changes. Reduces redundant visual tokens caused by encoding each frame independently.

entry.title: Accurate Large-sample Uncertainty Quantification using Stochastic Gradient Markov Chain Monte Carlo

author.name: Yu Wang, Jie Ding, Jonathan H. Huggins

entry.summary: Proposes new discrete-time approximations to SGD and SGLD (with and without momentum) for accurate uncertainty quantification in large-batch and misspecified regimes where continuous-time theory fails. Provides quantitative, non-asymptotic predictions of stationary and iterate-average covariances.

entry.title: GLENS: Global Search via Learning from Solver Iterates with Diffusion Models

author.name: Anjian Li, Bartolomeo Stellato, Ryne Beeson

entry.summary: Proposes GLENS, a diffusion-model method that learns from solver iterates (not just final optima) to generate diverse, high-quality initial guesses for local minima of multimodal non-convex optimization problems. Leverages local-neighborhood information discarded by prior methods.

entry.title: How Much Orthogonalization Does Muon Need?

author.name: Hua Huang

entry.summary: Investigates how much orthogonalization the Muon optimizer actually requires, using a relaxed cubic Newton-Schulz schedule that uses fewer matrix multiplications than standard quintic iterations. Probes the relationship between polar accuracy, spectral shaping, and training quality.

entry.title: Variance-sensitive Thompson sampling for generalised linear bandits, revisited

author.name: Tom Perneczky, Marc Abeille, David Janz

entry.summary: Proves a variance-sensitive regret bound for Thompson sampling in generalized linear bandits using the Gaussian Poincare inequality after a warm-up phase, bypassing where prior optimism-based analyses fail. A focused theoretical contribution to bandit learning.

entry.title: The Assistant as a Privileged Persona: A canonical reference in cross-persona self-recognition

author.name: Asvin G

entry.summary: Investigates cross-persona self-recognition in Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, showing the Assistant persona acts as a privileged canonical reference for authorship judgments. Connects persona-vector distance to claim rates across diverse personas.

entry.title: Prior-Guided Multi-Omic Transformers for Single-Cell Gene Regulatory Network Inference

author.name: Tianyang Xu, Tianci Liu, Niraj Rayamajhi, Ryan Patrick, Kranthi Varala, Ying Li, Jing Gao

entry.summary: Presents EpiAwareNet, a prior-guided multi-omic transformer that reconstructs gene regulatory networks from paired single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin data using gene-peak cross-attention rather than fixed peak-to-gene links. Addresses scATAC sparsity with light biological priors.

entry.title: DistMatch: Adaptive Binning via Distribution Matching for Robust Sequential Conformal Prediction

author.name: Enver Menadjiev, Jihyeon Seong, Jisu Yeo, Jaesik Choi

entry.summary: Proposes DistMatch, a binning-based sequential conformal prediction method that recursively partitions residuals via a KS-statistic binary tree to induce approximately exchangeable leaves, avoiding reweighting under distribution shift. Provides theoretical and empirical support.

entry.title: RADE: Random Add-Drop Edge as a Regularizer

author.name: Danial Saber, Amirali Salehi-Abari

entry.summary: Proposes RADE, a stochastic graph augmentation that jointly adds and drops edges to simultaneously combat GNN overfitting and over-squashing while aligning training and inference distributions. Provides a regularizer that also supports long-range communication.

entry.title: COLLIE: Guiding Skill Discovery in Semantically Coherent Latent Space

author.name: Yao Luan, Ni Mu, Hanfei Ge, Yiqin Yang, Bo Xu, Qing-Shan Jia

entry.summary: Proposes COLLIE, a guided skill discovery framework that builds a semantically coherent skill latent space from dense unsupervised data, enabling reliable guidance from sparse online human feedback without training extra guidance models. Targets safer, task-relevant unsupervised skill discovery.

entry.title: Profiling Privacy Preservation Against Gradient Inversion Attacks in Tabular Federated Learning

author.name: Ivo Osterberg Nilsson, Maximilian Birr Engvall, Viktor Valadi, Teddy Lazebnik

entry.summary: Profiles privacy preservation against gradient inversion attacks in tabular federated learning across protocols, batch sizes, training stages, attacker assumptions, and task types using MIMIC-IV and other datasets. Characterizes when tabular FL leaks private data.

entry.title: Linear Strategic Classification with Endogenous Improvements

author.name: Siddharth Shrivastava, Mahvith Akshintala, B Vamsha Vardhan Reddy, Naresh Manwani, Sujit Gujar, Ganesh Ghalme

entry.summary: Studies linear strategic classification where strategic feature changes induce genuine outcome-relevant improvements rather than cosmetic gaming, under a single-index qualification model with linear-decomposable costs. Characterizes the strategic-optimal classifier when responses change true labels.

entry.title: Riemannian Optimization for Hadamard Products of Low-Rank Matrices

author.name: Pratik Jawanpuria, Ankish Chandresh, Bamdev Mishra

entry.summary: Formulates learning Hadamard products of low-rank matrices as optimization on a Riemannian quotient manifold, introducing a symmetry-invariant block-diagonal metric and a tuning-free Gauss-Newton Riemannian gradient descent that scales linearly in observed entries. Targets data with multiplicative structure.

entry.title: ATLAS: Agentic Test-time Learning-to-Allocate Scaling

author.name: Peijia Qin, Qi Cao, Pengtao Xie

entry.summary: ATLAS is an agentic test-time scaling framework where an LLM orchestrator owns the control loop, deciding when to gather evidence, stop, and synthesize answers through an extensible explore action. It moves orchestration from designer-engineered to model-controlled.

entry.title: A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms

author.name: Thomas Chen, Zhiyuan Li

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical framework for self-play theorem proving, formalizing theorems as a graph and analyzing the self-improvement of prover-conjecturer cooperating agents. It introduces primitive assumptions characterizing training guarantees.

entry.title: Randomized Least Squares Value Iteration itself is Joint Differentially Private

author.name: Haiyang Lu, Pratik Gajane, Shaojie Bai, Mohammad Sadegh Talebi

entry.summary: This paper shows that Randomized Least Squares Value Iteration, used for exploration in RL, is itself joint differentially private without additional noise mechanisms. It characterizes how exploration noise simultaneously provides privacy protection.

entry.title: IntraShuffler: A Privacy Preserving Framework for Heterogeneous DP Federated Learning

author.name: Farhin Farhad Riya, Olivera Kotevska, Jinyuan Stella Sun

entry.summary: Shows that epsilon-aware aggregation in heterogeneous differential privacy federated learning leaks information, allowing an honest-but-curious server to infer client data via gradient denoising. Proposes IntraShuffler to mitigate this privacy risk.

entry.title: HOIST: Humanoid Optimization with Imitation and Sample-efficient Tuning for Manipulating Suspended Loads

author.name: Songyang Liu, Shunyu Yao, Dingyuan Huang, Shuai Li

entry.summary: Proposes HOIST, combining imitation learning from VR teleoperation with sample-efficient batched RL to enable humanoid robots to manipulate underactuated suspended payloads through whole-body motion. Addresses safety and sample efficiency limitations of training from scratch.

entry.title: ERICA: Quantifying Replicability of Cluster Analysis

author.name: Siamak K. Sorooshyari, Manuel A. Rivas, Robert Tibshirani

entry.summary: Introduces ERICA, a framework for quantifying the replicability of clustering results via iterative cluster assignments, producing statistics and visualizations about cluster structure and outliers. Addresses the lack of quantitative scrutiny in widely used clustering.

entry.title: Cluster Analysis with Resampling for Validation and Exploration (CARVE)

author.name: Kai R. Wycik, Tiffany M. Tang, Tarek M. Zikry, Genevera I. Allen

entry.summary: Proposes CARVE, a resampling-based framework for validating and exploring clustering solutions that avoids geometric assumptions failing on heavy-tailed high-dimensional biomedical data. Grounded in clustering stability and generalizability.

entry.title: In-Expectation Convergence of Stochastic Gradient Methods under Heavy-Tailed Noise

author.name: Zijian Liu

entry.summary: Establishes new in-expectation convergence results for stochastic mirror descent and accelerated SGD under heavy-tailed noise with only finite p-th moments, extending recent findings that classical SGD can converge in such regimes. Strengthens theory of robust stochastic optimization.

entry.title: Tiny Recursive Models for Solving the J2-Perturbed Lambert Problem

author.name: Minduli Wijayatunga, Roberto Armellin

entry.summary: Presents TRM-PL, a Tiny Recursive Model that solves the J2-perturbed Lambert orbital problem via iterative latent refinement, unifying initial-guess generation and correction in an end-to-end differentiable architecture as a learned alternative to homotopy methods. Targets fast astrodynamics computation.

entry.title: Distribution-free changepoint localization after sequential change detection

author.name: Aytijhya Saha, Aaditya Ramdas

entry.summary: Proposes a distribution-free framework for localizing changepoints after sequential change detection, building post-detection confidence sets without distributional assumptions. It provides finite-sample coverage guarantees and bounds on confidence-set size.

entry.title: Convex Distance Operator Transport: A Convex and Geometry-Preserving Formulation

author.name: Junhyoung Chung, Euijong Song, Won Hwa Kim, Gunwoong Park

entry.summary: Introduces Convex Distance Operator Transport (CDOT), the first convex optimal transport framework aligning distributions across heterogeneous domains while jointly preserving feature correspondence and intrinsic geometry. It proves CDOT yields a valid pseudometric and relates it to Gromov-Wasserstein.

entry.title: The Ghost Couple: Correlated LLM Name Priors and Their Haunting of the Web and Academic Publishing

author.name: Micha{\l} Brzozowski, Neo Christopher Chung
