entry.title: Vision-language Models for Driver Monitoring Systems: A Driver Activity Description Dataset

author.name: David J. Lerch, Sarath Mulugurthi, Manuel Martin, Frederik Diederichs, Rainer Stiefelhagen

entry.summary: Creates a detailed natural-language description version of the Drive&Act dataset and benchmarks three VLMs on fine-grained driver activity description, showing current VLMs fail at subtle distinctions. Trains VLMs on the new description dataset with cross-dataset evaluation.

entry.title: Cross-Domain Dead Tree Detection via Knowledge Distillation in Aerial Imagery

author.name: Anis Ur Rahman, Mete Ahishali, Einari Heinaro, Samuli Junttila

entry.summary: Advances dead-tree detection in aerial imagery via knowledge distillation, adapting a model trained on Finnish data to Polish, German, and Estonian forest domains. Evaluates four KD variants against a fine-tuning baseline using tree-level IoU and F1 metrics.

entry.title: Question-Aware Evidence Ledgers for Video Relational Reasoning

author.name: Yilin Ou, Mengshi Qi, Huadong Ma

entry.summary: Presents a test-time reasoning pipeline for video relational reasoning (VRR-QA challenge) built around a GPT-5.5 video QA solver augmented with question-aware evidence ledgers that make targets, counts, reference frames, and temporal/spatial scope explicit. Uses external tools like detection and depth only when needed.

entry.title: NDPP-Grasp: Non-Differentiable Physical Plausibility Constraint-Guided Task-Oriented Dexterous Grasp Generation

author.name: Qiuchi Xiang, Haoxuan Qu, Hossein Rahmani, Jun Liu

entry.summary: NDPP-Grasp generates task-oriented dexterous grasps by injecting non-differentiable physical plausibility constraints directly into the diffusion generation trajectory, rather than relying on after-the-fact refinement. This produces grasps that are both functionally suitable and physically valid.

entry.title: Continuous Data Assimilation with Learned Surrogate Dynamics

author.name: Wenwen Li, Daniel Sanz-Alonso

entry.summary: This paper develops a finite-dimensional analysis of nudging-based continuous data assimilation that uses learned surrogate models of unknown dynamics. It establishes conditions guaranteeing accurate state tracking under model error in both noise-free and noisy settings.

entry.title: Agents on a Tree: Pathwise Coordination for Multi-Objective Molecular Optimization

author.name: Jia Zhang, Tengfei Ma, Tianle Li, Daojian Zeng, Xieping Gao, Xiangxiang Zeng

entry.summary: ATOM formulates multi-objective molecular optimization as a tree-structured multi-agent search where each node hosts an agent specialized for an objective and agents coordinate along paths rather than enforcing global consensus. This preserves diverse trade-off trajectories in vast chemical spaces.

entry.title: TIGER: Traceable Inference with Graph-Based Evidence Routing for Mitigating Hallucinations in Multimodal Generation

author.name: Kaixiang Zhao, Tianrun Yu, Shawn Huang, Porter Jenkins, Yushun Dong, Amanda Hughes

entry.summary: TIGER is an inference-time framework that mitigates hallucination in multimodal generation by independently extracting an observation graph from the input and a claim graph from the output, then assigning each claim a graph-conditioned risk score for localized fact-level repair. It avoids hallucinated claims biasing input interpretation.

entry.title: TAPS: Target-Aware Prefix Tree Selection for Diffusion-Drafted Speculative Decoding

author.name: Zhuoyu Wang, Junnan Huang, Xinyu Chen

entry.summary: TAPS proposes target-aware prefix-tree selection for diffusion-drafted speculative decoding, addressing that existing methods rank draft-tree nodes by marginal probability and waste verification on unreachable descendants of rejected prefixes. It conditions ranking on prefix reachability to improve acceptance per latency.

entry.title: Efficient Test-time Inference for Generative Planning Models

author.name: Robert Gieselmann, Mihai Samson, Federico Pecora, Jeremy L. Wyatt

entry.summary: This paper shows that a modified classical Open-Closed List search provides an efficient inference procedure for generative planning models, synergizing a learned generative rollout model with a learned heuristic for path prioritization. It offers a more efficient alternative to brute-force test-time compute scaling.

entry.title: Regularized Offline Policy Optimization with Posterior Hybrid Bayesian Belief

author.name: Hongqiang Lin, Pengfei Wang, Nenggan Zheng

entry.summary: This paper presents a regularized offline RL method using a posterior hybrid Bayesian belief over dynamics to unify sample-level and model-level epistemic uncertainty quantification. It addresses the computational intractability of policy optimization in Bayesian offline RL.

entry.title: Decoupled Behavioral Cloning for Scalable Inductive Generalization in RL from Specifications

author.name: Vignesh Subramanian, Subhajit Roy, Suguman Bansal

entry.summary: DIBS proposes a decoupled behavioral cloning approach for inductive generalization in RL from specifications, separating learning task-specific teacher policies from learning the policy-evolution function via behavioral cloning. It addresses poor training scalability when aggregated reward feedback becomes noisy across many tasks.

entry.title: AnyEdit++: Adaptive Long-Form Knowledge Editing via Bayesian Surprise

author.name: Bowen Tian, Caixue He, Jiemin Wu, Jingying Wang, Wenshuo Chen, Zexi Li, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: AnyEdit++ is a structure-aware long-form knowledge editing framework with Bayes-Chunk, an adaptive segmentation mechanism that identifies semantic boundaries via Bayesian surprise rather than fixed-window chunking. It is backed by theory on structural independence requiring orthogonal anchor keys to minimize cross-segment interference.

entry.title: "Skill issues'': data-centric optimization of lakehouse agents

author.name: Nicole Rose Schneider, Davide Ghilardi, Giacomo Piccinini, Jacopo Tagliabue

entry.summary: This work studies data-centric optimization of skill and environment files for coding agents operating on a branching lakehouse, reframing data-agent evaluation as a state-verification rather than output-matching problem. It presents a pipeline generating task-verifier pairs through executable lakehouse changes.

entry.title: Brain-Atlas-Guided Generative Counterfactual Attention for Explainable Cognitive Decline Diagnosis Using Multimodal Connectomes

author.name: Xiongri Shen, Jiaqi Wang, Zhenxi Song, Yi Zhong, Leilei Zhao, Xin He, Baiying Lei, Zhiguo Zhang

entry.summary: GCAN is an atlas-knowledge-guided generative counterfactual attention network for explainable diagnosis of cognitive decline using multimodal brain connectomes, framing diagnosis as source-to-target counterfactual generation. It aims to improve both classification and interpretability of connectivity changes.

entry.title: FlowTime: Towards Continuous Generative Watch Time Prediction via Flow-based Personalized Priors

author.name: Hongxu Ma, Han Zhou, Chenghou Jin, Jie Zhang, Xiaoyu Yang, Chunjie Chen, Jihong Guan, Shuigeng Zhou

entry.summary: FlowTime introduces a flow-based generative approach with personalized priors for continuous watch-time prediction in short-video recommenders, addressing mean-collapse, quantization, and latency limitations of existing paradigms. It revisits the problem from a causal perspective to capture multimodal interaction patterns.

entry.title: TERRA: Task-Embedded Reasoning and Representation Architecture for Cross-Domain Applications

author.name: Shayan Shokri

entry.summary: TERRA studies transfer of action-conditioned latent predictive representations across structurally analogous but unrelated domains such as driving scenes, robot workspaces, and financial order books. It gives a formal treatment of when representations or predictors learned in one structured-state domain carry over to another.

entry.title: Structure-Guided Adaptive Propagation for Protein-Protein Interaction Site Prediction

author.name: Enqiang Zhu, Yizi Liu, Yilong Luo, Yao Chen, Yu Zhang, Baoshan Ma

entry.summary: SGAP-PPIS is a structure-guided adaptive propagation model for protein-protein interaction site prediction that adapts information diffusion to local geometric environments rather than using fixed propagation schemes. It aims to distinguish true interaction sites from structurally similar non-interacting neighbors.

entry.title: Bayesian Spectral Emotion Transition Discovery from Multi-Annotator Disagreement

author.name: Keito Inoshita, Takato Ueno

entry.summary: BSETD is a two-stage Bayesian framework that discovers emotion-transition structure from multi-rater soft labels, using a hierarchical Dirichlet-Multinomial posterior built from outer products of soft labels to retain annotator-disagreement uncertainty. It avoids discarding the uncertainty lost by majority-vote hard labels.

entry.title: BADGER: Bridging Agentic and Deterministic Evaluation for Generative Enterprise Reasoning

author.name: Shannon Serrao, Soumitra Chatterjee, Dorina Strori, Abhishek Sharma, Nathan Miller

entry.summary: BADGER is a unified evaluation framework from Merkle integrating text-to-SQL assessment with agentic behavior evaluation into a production-grade pipeline calibrated against human expert judgment. It bridges execution-accuracy protocols and LLM-based assessment for enterprise reasoning.

entry.title: An Abstract Worlds Semantic Framework for Belief Change Operators

author.name: Daniel Grimaldi, M. Vanina Martinez, Ricardo O. Rodriguez

entry.summary: This paper proposes Abstract Worlds Semantics, a syntax-free set-theoretic framework for belief change inspired by Grove, treating worlds as primitive elements with world contraction and revision operators. It unifies classical and non-prioritized belief change models including AGM, KM, and Multiple Change.

entry.title: CSRP: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Chinese Text Correction via Reinforcement Learning with Efficiency-Aware Rewards

author.name: Wei Tian, Yuhao Zhou, Man Lan

entry.summary: CSRP is a three-stage framework for Chinese grammatical error correction combining continual pretraining, chain-of-thought SFT with explicit error reasoning, and GRPO with an efficiency-aware reward that penalizes unnecessary edits to reduce over-correction. Builds correction capability progressively.

entry.title: Update Opacity: Epistemic Accessibility and Governance Under AI System Change

author.name: Andrea Ferrario, Joshua Hatherley

entry.summary: Frames update opacity (users unable to understand why the same input now yields different outputs after model updates) as a diachronic failure of epistemic accessibility and a governance problem requiring selective disclosure. Argues against disclosing every update due to overload.

entry.title: Can Predicted Dynamics Exist in the Physical World?

author.name: Barak Or

entry.summary: Formulates physical admissibility as a prediction-control interface, arguing low RMSE does not guarantee physical executability, and evaluates decoded proposals against kinematic, dynamic, and horizon conditions to flag violations with component-level reasons. Demonstrated on the LeRobot PushT task.

entry.title: PEACE: A Planner-Executor Agent with Constraint Enforcement for UAVs

author.name: Erdem Uysal, Timo Kehrer, Sebastiano Panichella

entry.summary: Proposes PEACE, a planner-executor agent for PX4 drones that uses an LLM for single-pass mission planning while delegating low-level control to a structured ROS 2 tool-calling interface, reducing latency and hallucination risk. It builds a world model from modular detectors and depth projection for constrained UAV autonomy.

entry.title: Versatile Framework with Semantic and Structural guidance for Image Reconstruction from Brain Activity

author.name: Yizhuo Lu, Changde Du, Qiongyi Zhou, Liuyun Jiang, Huiguang He

entry.summary: Presents a framework for reconstructing visual stimuli from brain activity with both semantic and structural guidance, addressing prior methods' failure to preserve fine-grained spatial details like position and orientation. It improves controllability and interpretability of brain decoding.

entry.title: MyoSem: Aligning Electromyography to Natural-Language Action Semantics for Hand Action Understanding

author.name: Chiyue Wang, Dong She, Yang Gao, Zhanpeng Jin

entry.summary: Presents MyoSem, an EMG-to-action semantic alignment framework mapping low-level EMG signals into a shared semantic space built from multi-view action descriptions, enabling bidirectional EMG-text retrieval. It moves beyond fixed-label classification toward generalizable hand action understanding.

entry.title: Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems

author.name: Xiangyu Wang, Yawen He, Shivendra Pratap Singh, Han Huang, Mengtong Hu, Sharath Ciddu, Yi-Hsuan Hsieh, Erik Groving, Yi Ding, Jieming Di, Tony Wang, Min Yun, Xiaoyu Chen, Ling Leng, Rob Malkin

entry.summary: Introduces SCALR, a framework generating synthetic cross-domain user-item interaction events for large-scale recommendation, inspired by LLM synthetic data success. It decomposes cross-domain learning into translating source-domain events into a target domain to address sparsity and noisy feedback.

entry.title: Isolating LLM Lexical Bias: A Curation-Free Triangulated Metric for Preference-Stage Learning

author.name: Xiaoyang Ming, Jose Hernandez, Thomas Stephan Juzek

entry.summary: Proposes a curation-free triangulated metric to isolate LLM lexical bias introduced during preference-learning stages like RLHF, such as overuse of words like delve and furthermore. It addresses the reliance of prior research on manual curation to study preference-induced lexical misalignment.

entry.title: Short-form Text Rewriting with Phi Silica

author.name: Divya Tadimeti, Shawn Pan, Sameera Lanka, Chenghui Zhou, Sadid Hasan

entry.summary: This empirical study adapts the small Phi Silica model for short-form text rewriting via dataset curation, prompt distillation, and PEFT, using GPT-5-chat for supervision and judging. It shows fine-tuning improves semantic fidelity and hallucination robustness in this constrained setting.

entry.title: Dynamic Coordination Strategy Selection for Enterprise Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Thanh Luong Tuan

entry.summary: This paper evaluates whether enterprise multi-agent coordination strategy (consensus, debate, synthesis, or single-agent) should be selected dynamically by problem class, running a frozen matrix of enterprise tasks across multiple model arms. It finds a bounded but operationally useful result rather than the strong original hypothesis.

entry.title: RefDiffNet: Learning to Expose Subtle PCB Defects Before Detection

author.name: Vinay Edula, Nilesh Badwe, Priyanka Bagade

entry.summary: RefDiffNet is a lightweight plug-and-play input enhancement block that uses an aligned defect-free reference image to expose subtle PCB defects before detection, reviving a classical inspection idea in the deep learning era. It enhances images prior to the detector backbone.

entry.title: Temporally-Aligned Evaluation for Audio-Driven Talking Head Generation

author.name: Zhicheng Zhang, Lei Wang, Yu Zhang, Yongsheng Gao

entry.summary: Argues that audio-driven talking-head generation should be evaluated as a sequence-alignment problem rather than frame-wise comparison, since speech-driven motion has natural timing variations. Introduces a temporally-aligned evaluation reformulation.

entry.title: DiffuSent: Towards a Unified Diffusion Framework for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Shu Long, Yanglei Gan, Xuchuan Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes DiffuSent, a non-autoregressive diffusion framework that unifies all seven aspect-based sentiment analysis subtasks as boundary denoising diffusion processes with contrastive denoising training. Addresses boundary insensitivity in multi-word aspect and opinion terms.

entry.title: GJDNet: Robust Graph Neural Networks via Joint Disentangled Learning Against Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Canyixing Cui, Tao Wu, Xingping Xian, Xiao-Ke Xu, Mao Wang, Weina Niu

entry.summary: GJDNet defends graph neural networks against adversarial attacks by jointly disentangling node representations and decision spaces, targeting structure-feature mismatches caused by adversarial edge perturbations. It moves beyond fixed assortativity assumptions in prior defenses.

entry.title: Time-Aware Diffusion based on Preference Disentanglement for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Bangguo Zhu, Peng Huo, Yuanbo Zhao, Zhicheng Du, Jun Yin, Senzhang Wang

entry.summary: TDPM proposes time-aware diffusion with preference disentanglement for generative recommendation, addressing the limitation that diffusion processes apply uniformly across historical interactions. It models non-stationary, time-evolving user preferences over semantic indices.

entry.title: Breaking the Information Silo: Semantic Personas for Cross-Domain Recommendation

author.name: Jonathan Mayo, Moshe Unger, Konstantin Bauman

entry.summary: SPHERE enables cross-domain recommendation across strictly disjoint domains with no shared users or items by using semantic personas rather than identity or graph structure alignment. It overcomes the information-silo limitation of platforms.

entry.title: Boosting Multimodal Federated Learning via Chained Modality Optimization

author.name: Zixin Zhang, Fan Qi, Shuai Li, Xiaoshan Yang, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: FedMChain restructures multimodal federated learning as a chain of modality-wise phases to mitigate modality competition where dominant modalities suppress weaker ones. Each modality gets a dedicated optimization window with cross-modal error compensation.

entry.title: RadioMaster: Multi-Agent System for Autonomous Radio Signal Generation

author.name: Jiazhen Lei, Tianze Cao, Yuxin Sha, Sihan Wang, Bingbing Wang, Fengyuan Zhu, Zeming Yang, Xiaohua Tian

entry.summary: RadioMaster is a multi-agent system for autonomous radio signal generation, translating user intents into physical-layer signals. It addresses LLMs' domain ignorance and insensitivity to hardware constraints in wireless prototyping.

entry.title: Echo: A Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Speaker Diarization and Speech Recognition in a Shared Latent Space

author.name: Louis Mouchon

entry.summary: Echo is a proof-of-concept audio system built around a single 25M-parameter ViT encoder pretrained with a JEPA objective, carrying speaker identity, phonetic content, and source routing in one shared latent space. It handles diarization and source separation with light heads and no per-task fine-tuning.

entry.title: Repurposing Adversarial Perturbations for Continual Learning: From Defense to Active Alignment

author.name: Ran Liu, Min Yu, Mingqi Liu, Jianguo Jiang, Gang Li, Rongsheng Li, Ning Li, Zhen Xu, Weiqing Huang, Ming Liu

entry.summary: Proposes AdvCL, which repurposes adversarial perturbations as a geometric control signal for stable continual learning in LLMs via three plug-in modules promoting local smoothness, preventing over-alignment, and aligning toward prior-task prototypes. Reports gains in both performance and robustness.

entry.title: ODTQA-FoRe: An Open-Domain Tabular Question Answering Dataset for Future Data Forecasting and Reasoning

author.name: Zhensheng Wang, Xiaole Liu, Wenmian Yang, Kun Zhou, Yiquan Zhang, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: Introduces a new open-domain tabular QA task for future data forecasting and reasoning, with a real-estate dataset, plus TimeFore, an LLM-agent framework with Retriever, Forecaster, and reasoning roles. Targets future-oriented numerical prediction beyond retrieval-style table QA.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Multi-Task Graph Transformer for Trip-Level Transit Prediction

author.name: Oluwaleke Yusuf, Adil Rasheed, Frank Lindseth

entry.summary: Proposes SMT-GraphFormer, a spatiotemporal multi-task graph transformer that frames trip-level transit prediction as sequence-to-sequence boarding/alighting forecasting with delay and dwell as auxiliary tasks. Aims to capture within-trip evolution and network context.

entry.title: Conditioned free-energy density of proteins using unbalanced solutions to constraint satisfaction problems

author.name: Pratik Worah, Subhash Khot, Srinivasa Varadhan

entry.summary: This paper reduces the computation of free-energy for conditioned Curie-Weiss spin Hamiltonians to an unbalanced norm computation, designing a polynomial-time SDP algorithm with bounds. Applied to Ubiquitin, it explores backbone conformations and identifies flexible protein regions.

entry.title: Genotype-Conditioned Molecular Generation via Evidence-Grounded Multi-Objective Latent Perturbation in Diffusion Models

author.name: Brenda Nogueira, Gisela A. Gonzalez-Montiel, Nitesh V. Chawla, Nuno Moniz

entry.summary: This work optimizes a pretrained genotype-to-drug diffusion model via learnable latent perturbations to maximize a composite reward combining drug sensitivity, drug-likeness, and synthetic accessibility. It targets personalized anticancer drug generation conditioned on cancer genotypes.

entry.title: Fast Generalization after Interpolation via Critically Damped Momentum Optimization

author.name: Luca Muscarnera, Silas Ruhrberg Est\'evez, Yuanzhang Xiao, Mihaela Van der Schaar

entry.summary: GROKtimizer is a biphasic optimization schedule combining rapid convergence to interpolation with subsequent complexity minimization, motivated by two-regime risk minimization theory. It targets fast generalization in high-dimensional low-sample regimes.

entry.title: When Tabular Foundation Models Transfer Across Modalities: A Systematic Evaluation Across 95 Datasets, 7 Modalities, and Two Regimes

author.name: Julien Lafrance

entry.summary: This work systematically evaluates a single classification pipeline combining ETF preprocessing with a tabular foundation model for in-context inference across 95 datasets, 7 modalities, and two regimes. It carefully fixes the comparison against strong lightweight tuned baselines on the same frozen features.

entry.title: BlockGen: Flexible Blockwise Sequence Modeling with Hybrid Samplers

author.name: Justin Deschenaux, Caglar Gulcehre

entry.summary: BlockGen explores blockwise sequence modeling with hybrid samplers, investigating whether uniform-state diffusion models outperform masked diffusion when tokens are generated blockwise rather than full-sequence, with informed correctors targeting likely-wrong tokens. It addresses open questions about discrete diffusion paradigms.

entry.title: Entropy Minimization without Model Collapse: Mitigating Prediction Bias in Medical Imaging

author.name: Tim Nielen, Sameer Ambekar, Johannes Kiechle, Daniel M. Lang, Julia A. Schnabel

entry.summary: This work explains entropy minimization's model-collapse failure in test-time adaptation as distribution shifts merging class feature clusters while the decision boundary stays fixed, creating prediction bias. It shows EM amplifies this bias and proposes a mitigation for medical imaging.

entry.title: Guidance for Low-Level Perceptual Editing in Unconditional Diffusion Models

author.name: Shreyansh Modi, Akshat Tomar, Aarush Aggarwal

entry.summary: Presents a training-free framework for global low-level perceptual and aesthetic editing in unconditional diffusion models, using degradation concept vectors and bottleneck patching with classifier-free guidance. Addresses failure of standard h-space patching for global transformations.

entry.title: Statistical Testing on Directed Graphs by Surrogate Data Generation

author.name: Chun Hei Michael Chan, Alexandre Cionca, Dimitri Van De Ville

entry.summary: Extends surrogate-data-based non-parametric hypothesis testing from undirected to directed graphs by revisiting stationary graph signals via eigendecomposition of the directed graph shift operator. Enables statistical testing on directed graph signals.

entry.title: Efficient Approximation for Encoder--Decoder Neural Operators via Variation Spaces

author.name: Jia-Qi Yang, Lei Shi

entry.summary: Develops a variation-space function theory for encoder-decoder neural operators, establishing approximation bounds in Bochner L^q norm with constants independent of encoding dimension. It decomposes error into encoding and finite-width terms of order N^{-1/2}.

entry.title: On the Uncertainty Quantification Ability of Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Tyler R. Johnson, Kian Ben-Jacob, Nima Negarandeh, Oriol Vendrell-Gallart, Ramin Bostanabad

entry.summary: Empirically evaluates the uncertainty quantification ability of tabular foundation models (TabPFN v2.5) against Gaussian processes across regression problems of varying complexity. It assesses whether tabular FMs provide reliable UQ for scientific applications.

entry.title: Sensitivity as a Double-Edged Sword: A Trade-off Between Discriminability and Adversarial Robustness

author.name: Kai Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a trade-off where fully-connected classifiers' sensitivity makes them discriminative but adversarially vulnerable, while L2 distance-based classifiers are robust but less performant. It proposes a Hybrid Prototype Mixing reclassifier to retain discrimination with improved robustness.

entry.title: Error Bounds for a Diffusion Model-Based Drift Estimator

author.name: Ioar Casado-Telletxea, Omar Rivasplata

entry.summary: Provides theoretical error bounds for a recently proposed diffusion-model-based drift estimator for stochastic differential equations, treating drift estimation as a denoising/score-matching problem. It fills the gap of missing convergence guarantees using diffusion-model theory.

entry.title: ProbRes: Volatility Learning for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Tingting Wang, Yunyi Zhang, Benyou Wang

entry.summary: Presents ProbRes, a post-hoc probabilistic calibration method that explicitly learns conditional volatility dynamics for time-series forecasting and generates predictive distributions by resampling normalized residuals. It is architecture-agnostic and handles heteroskedastic financial data.

entry.title: Bayesian meta-learning for modeling Alzheimer's disease progression

author.name: Clara Hoffmann, Nadja Klein

entry.summary: Applies Bayesian meta-learning to predict distributions of discrete Alzheimer's disease progression scores conditional on current MRI volume and historical trajectories, addressing the challenge of few observations per individual. It captures individual-level correlation and nonlinear relationships without retraining.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Residuals for Adaptive Mesh Refinement in Finite-Difference PDE Solvers

author.name: Henry Kasumba, Ronald Katende

entry.summary: Studies a hybrid strategy using a physics-informed neural network not as the final solver but as an off-grid residual probe to guide adaptive mesh refinement for finite-difference PDE solvers. The PINN residual generates cellwise refinement indicators before the FD solver computes the final approximation.

entry.title: CRAFTQA: A Code-Driven Adaptive Framework for Complex Structured Data Reasoning

author.name: Chengtao Gan, Zhiqiang Liu, Long Jin, Yushan Zhu, Lei Liang, Wen Zhang

entry.summary: CRAFTQA is a code-driven adaptive framework for question answering over heterogeneous structured data like tables and knowledge graphs, overcoming the limitation of predefined function sets by generating code dynamically. It enables more complex reasoning across data types.

entry.title: DECK: A Consistency x Confidence Taxonomy of LLM Hallucinations

author.name: Mohit Singh Chauhan

entry.summary: DECK introduces a 2x2 taxonomy of LLM hallucinations organized by detectability signature (inter-sample consistency and token confidence) rather than error type. Each of its four regimes maps to a specific family of uncertainty scorers best suited to catch it.

entry.title: CRAM: Centroid-Routing and Adaptive MoE for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Jun-Tao Tang, Zhen-Hao Xie, Yu-Cheng Shi, Da-Wei Zhou

entry.summary: CRAM proposes centroid-routing with an adaptive mixture-of-experts for multimodal continual instruction tuning, isolating task-specific patterns into independent modules to balance anti-forgetting against parameter efficiency. It targets the dilemma between shared updates and isolated expansion.

entry.title: Transferable Self-Harm Surveillance from Emergency Department Triage Notes Using an Evidence-Augmented Machine Learning Approach

author.name: Liuliu Chen, Gowri Rajaram, Eleanor Bailey, Katrina Witt, Michelle Lamblin, Jo Robinson, Mike Conway, Vlada Rozova

entry.summary: This work develops a three-stage approach combining traditional ML with LLM-based screening and evidence extraction to detect self-harm in emergency department triage notes. It demonstrates strong transferability across three Australian hospitals with AUPRC around 0.88.

entry.title: InfoMerge: Information-aware Token Compression for Efficient Video Large Language Models

author.name: Xinxin Liu, Shiwei Gan, Xiao Liu, Yafeng Yin, Lei Xie, Sanglu Lu

entry.summary: InfoMerge is a training-free visual token compression method for video LLMs that uses robust redundancy estimation and content-aware budget allocation rather than local frame similarity or segment length. It captures non-uniform information distribution to cut computational overhead.

entry.title: LFA: Layer Feature Attention for Run-Time Introspection of 2D Object Detectors in Automated Driving

author.name: Mert Keser, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: Layer Feature Attention (LFA) is a lightweight introspection method for 2D object detectors in automated driving that aggregates features across multiple backbone layers via attention to predict detector failures. The key insight is that detection errors manifest differently across the feature hierarchy.

entry.title: 3D Segment Anything Model with Visual Mamba for Diagnosing Placenta Accreta Spectrum

author.name: Yuliang Zhang, Fang He, Lulu Peng, Tianyu Yan, Pingping Zhang, Ting Song, Lili Du, Dunjin Chen

entry.summary: 3DSAMba establishes the first MRI-based Placenta Accreta Spectrum dataset with segmentation and classification annotations, and proposes a feature learning framework combining a 3D Segment Anything Model with Visual Mamba for automatic PAS diagnosis. It targets accurate diagnosis in resource-limited hospitals.

entry.title: Through the PRISM: Principle-Aware, Interpretable, and Multi-Scale Evaluation of Visual Designs

author.name: Mona Gandhi, KJ Joseph, Srinivasan Parthasarathy, Sayan Nag

entry.summary: PRISM is a benchmark for principle-aware, interpretable evaluation of visual designs that systematically perturbs professional layouts along measurable design principles like readability, contrast, alignment, and coherence. It offers 100K training and 10K validation samples for diagnostic, multi-scale design assessment beyond single heuristic scores.

entry.title: VICR: Visual In-Context Restoration for Real-World Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Qichang Zhang, Hailong Wang, Baiang Li, Linhao Wang, Rong Fu, Erkang Cheng, Simon James Fong

entry.summary: VICR reformulates real-world image super-resolution as image completion using a Diffusion Transformer with decoupled local and global visual prior injection from the low-quality input. It aims to reduce structural drift and semantic inconsistency in generative Real-ISR.

entry.title: SWARD: Stochastic Window-Attention-Based Relational Distillation for Cross-Architectural Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Aditya Makineni, Qing Tian

entry.summary: SWARD is a cross-architectural knowledge distillation method using stochastic window-attention-based relational distillation to transfer from transformer foundation teachers to convolutional students for semantic segmentation. It bridges the representational gap between global and local receptive fields.

entry.title: Learning Neural Deformation Representation for 4D Dynamic Shape Generation

author.name: Gyojin Han, Jiwan Hur, Jaehyun Choi, Junmo Kim

entry.summary: This work proposes a neural deformation representation for 4D dynamic shape generation that separates motion from shape, improving temporal consistency and rendering speed over prior weight-generating methods like HyperDiffusion. It targets quality and efficiency in generating deforming 3D objects over time.

entry.title: Rank-Aware Quantile Activation for Motion-Robust Crop Segmentation in UAV Imagery

author.name: Abinav Kiran, Sravan Danda, Aditya Challa, Sougata Sen, Daya Sagar B S

entry.summary: This work proposes Dual Quantile Activation (QAct), a rank-aware activation block replacing magnitude gating with instance-level rank normalization to make UAV crop segmentation robust to motion blur. It delivers consistent mIoU gains, especially on rare texture-dependent classes.

entry.title: Exploiting In-Sensor Computing for Energy-Efficient Earth Observation

author.name: Luigi Capogrosso, Pietro Bonazzi, Loris Hoxhaj, Michele Magno

entry.summary: This work presents an end-to-end in-sensor computing framework for Earth observation, integrating TinyML with the Sony IMX500 intelligent vision sensor to shift processing to the sensor level and reduce downlink bandwidth bottlenecks. It targets energy-efficient onboard satellite processing.

entry.title: DeblurNVS: Geometric Latent Diffusion for Novel View Synthesis from Sparse Motion-Blurred Images

author.name: Changyue Shi, Wangbo Yu, Chaoran Feng, Li Yuan

entry.summary: DeblurNVS uses geometric latent diffusion for novel view synthesis from sparse motion-blurred images, modeling blur degradation while avoiding costly per-scene optimization for generalizable sparse-view synthesis. It handles blur that corrupts local details and multi-view correspondences.

entry.title: ForestMamba: Sparse Mamba with Geometry-guided Queries for 3D Forest Point Cloud Segmentation

author.name: Trung Thanh Nguyen, Tuan-Anh Vu, Duc Viet Le, Yasutomo Kawanishi, Takahiro Komamizu, Ichiro Ide, Teja Kattenborn

entry.summary: ForestMamba is a sparse Mamba architecture with geometry-guided queries for 3D forest point cloud segmentation, addressing the quadratic complexity of attention on large forest scenes and the lack of forest structural priors in generic models. It targets forest monitoring and biodiversity assessment.

entry.title: Paving the Way for Point Cloud Video Representation Learning Using A PDE Model

author.name: Zhuoxu Huang, Zhenkun Fan, Jungong Han, Josef Kittler

entry.summary: This work formulates point cloud video representation learning as solving a simplified Partial Differential Equation, regularizing spatial-temporal correlation learning to handle the unordered nature of sequential point clouds. It draws inspiration from fluid analysis to overcome flow-based methods' limitations.

entry.title: Exploiting Semantic and Pixel Representations for Ultra-Low Bitrate Image Compression

author.name: Hao Wei, Yanhui Zhou, Chenyang Ge, Saeed Anwar, Ajmal Mian

entry.summary: SPRDiff is a diffusion-based ultra-low bitrate image compression method that leverages both semantic and pixel representations to improve rate-distortion-perception trade-off, ensuring reconstructions remain pixel-faithful rather than only perceptually realistic. It targets compact yet semantically coherent representations.

entry.title: PillarDETR: YOLO-Backbone and RT-DETR Head for Real-Time 3D Object Detection

author.name: Smit Kadvani, Shriya Gumber, Kriti Faujdar, Harsh Dave

entry.summary: Proposes PillarDETR, a real-time 3D object detection architecture combining pillar-based LiDAR encoding with a YOLOv8-derived CSP backbone and an RT-DETR head. Aims to balance detection accuracy and inference speed for autonomous driving.

entry.title: Hierarchically Decoupled Mixture-of-Experts for Robust Traffic Sign Recognition in Complex Driving Scenarios

author.name: Mingxiao Wang, Xiaozhen Qu, Bolin Gao, Tong Wang, Lei He

entry.summary: Proposes CBDES MoE TSR, a hierarchically decoupled mixture-of-experts framework for robust traffic sign recognition that adapts to diverse scenarios like distant small targets and adverse weather. Departs from static globally-shared-parameter detection.

entry.title: SAVMap: Structure-Aided Visual Mapping of Large-Scale 2.5D Manhattan Wireframes from Panoramic Video

author.name: Howard Huang, Bharath Surianarayanan, Keifer Lee, Chenyu Wang, Chen Feng

entry.summary: Presents SAVMap, a method generating semantic wireframe maps of warehouse shelf and light structures from only panoramic video, using semantic segmentation and Manhattan-grid geometric constraints to track sparse structure points. Enables robot localization and digital twin generation in industrial settings.

entry.title: Reason-Then-Retrieve for CoVR-R with Structured Edit Prompts and Dense-Sparse Fusion

author.name: DongQing Liu, MengShi Qi, HongWei Ji

entry.summary: Builds a zero-shot reason-then-retrieve pipeline for reason-aware composed video retrieval around Qwen3.5-27B, generating structured descriptions and dense embeddings from token hidden states, with edit reasoning over reference videos. Addresses inferring undescribed targets from fine-grained changes.

entry.title: ToolFG: Towards Well-Grounded Fine-Grained Image Classification

author.name: Yu Xue, Haoxuan Qu, Zhuoling Li, Yihang Lou, Yan Bai, Hossein Rahmani, Jun Liu

entry.summary: Proposes GloResNet, a lightweight 3D CNN based on ResNet-10 pretrained on MedicalNet for predicting brain injury in preterm infants from T2-weighted MRI, using global manifold mapping and z-score normalization. Achieves 75% average accuracy in 5-fold cross-validation on the dHCP dataset.

entry.title: Simultaneous Model-Based Evolution of Constants and Expression Structure in GP-GOMEA for Symbolic Regression

author.name: Johannes Koch, Tanja Alderliesten, Peter A. N. Bosman

entry.summary: Adds simultaneous model-based constant optimization to GP-GOMEA for symbolic regression, improving accuracy by jointly evolving expression structure and real-valued constants. Builds on a leading evolutionary symbolic regression algorithm.

entry.title: Cuttlebot: a platform demonstration for complex, autonomous, bio-inspired swimmers

author.name: Alexander Nicholas White, Ang Leo Li, Alexander Yin, Derrick Roseman, Valeria Saro-Cortes, Hannah Wiswell, Aimy Wissa, Mihai Duduta

entry.summary: Demonstrates Cuttlebot, an autonomous cuttlefish-inspired robot driven by dielectric elastomer artificial muscles, swimming in 3D via undulatory fin locomotion on the CORE platform. Targets ecologically sensitive deep-sea operations.

entry.title: Series-Parallel Integrated Nonlinear Elastic Actuator applied to the lean motion of a bicycle simulator

author.name: Christina Kohler, Michiel Plooij, Nuria Pe\~na-Perez, Arend L. Schwab, Heike Vallery

entry.summary: Presents SPINEA, an actuator merging series and parallel elastic functions into a single elastic element via a nonlinear misaligned-axis transmission, applied to lean motion in a bicycle simulator. Provides both impedance decoupling and torque complementation.

entry.title: FAIR^2 Drones: An AI-Ready Standard for Cross-Domain Wildlife Drone Datasets

author.name: Jenna Kline, Kilian Meier, Vandita Shukla, Edouard G. A. Rolland, Elena Iannino, Lucie Laporte-Devylder, Constanza Andrea Molina Catricheo, Blair Costelloe, Elizabeth Campolongo, Henrik S. Midtiby, Devis Tuia, Benjamin Risse, Ulrik P. S. Lundquist, Anders Lyhne Christensen, Fabio Remondino, Thomas Richardson, Tanya Berger-Wolf

entry.summary: Proposes FAIR^2 Drones, a unified standard for cross-domain wildlife drone datasets bridging ecology, robotics, and computer vision with platform metadata, annotation specs, and open validation tools. Enables interdisciplinary dataset reuse.

entry.title: ROG-Grasp: Root-Oriented Geometry for Robotic Grasping and Placement

author.name: Zijian An, Augustus Sroka, Ran Yang, Bill Cai, Satoru Eto, Brian Poon, Kelvin Cai, Shijie Geng, Feng Liu, Yiming Feng, Lifeng Zhou

entry.summary: ROG-Grasp estimates produce orientation from root surface geometry using RGB-D perception, YOLO root detection, and point-cloud plane fitting for orientation-aware grasping and placement in agricultural processing. Outperforms VLA policies in reliability for this task.

entry.title: Adaptive PD Gains for Energy-Conscious Control in Physical Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Danyal Saqib, Francisco Andrade Chavez, Marie Charbonneau

entry.summary: Proposes an adaptive proportional-derivative gain scheme for energy-conscious safe physical human-robot interaction that limits mechanical energy without requiring force or torque sensors. Offers simpler implementation than existing energy-based approaches.

entry.title: Tether-Aware Dynamic Collision Avoidance for USV-HROV Systems

author.name: Yang Gu, Ziyang Hong, Xuanlin Chen, Hao Wei, Cheng Wang, Shujie Yang, Yulin Si

entry.summary: Proposes a tether-aware dynamic collision avoidance method for a USV tracking an HROV during subsea cable inspection, accounting for the submerged tether scraping passing vessels and the risk of tether tautness from evasive maneuvers. Balances collision avoidance with tracking constraints.

entry.title: A Kinetic Theory of Encounter-Based Information Propagation in Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: Alkesh K. Srivastava, Philip Dames

entry.summary: This paper develops a kinetic theory of encounter-based information propagation in multi-robot systems without persistent connectivity, identifying access, mixing, and freshness limits for target tracking. It treats information transport via physical encounters as a kinetic process affecting tracking error.

entry.title: Polar Depth for Potentially Heavy-Tailed Data

author.name: Stephan Clemen\c{c}on, Carlos Fern\'andes, Pavlo Mozharovskyi, Anne Sabourin

entry.summary: This paper introduces Polar Depth, a novel statistical depth notion expressed in polar coordinates suited for ordering extreme values of multivariate heavy-tailed distributions. It enables anomaly detection and proves properties of the depth of the largest observations.

entry.title: Robust inference for risk heterogeneity under group imbalance

author.name: Mengqi Xu, Subha Maity, Joel Dubin

entry.summary: This paper proposes a robust framework using Neyman orthogonality to infer risk heterogeneity between populations under group imbalance, yielding estimators insensitive to nuisance estimation error. It is motivated by biomedical applications like varying ICU mortality risk across ethnic groups.

entry.title: Dissolving the Deep Learning Sample Efficiency Gap

author.name: Samuel Knoche

entry.summary: This essay challenges the claim that deep learning is wildly sample inefficient compared to humans, arguing the apparent gap may dissolve under proper accounting and disputing interpretations like Byrnes's that better brain-like algorithms must exist. It reviews data-efficiency comparisons across language and games.

entry.title: Opus 4.8 Part 2: Model Welfare

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's analysis of Claude Opus 4.8 focuses on model welfare, examining Anthropic's attempts to fix Opus 4.7 issues around honesty, sycophancy, and Claude learning to tell evaluators what they want to hear. It argues these problems require integrated approaches rather than checklist whack-a-mole.

entry.title: Coupling Language Models with Physics-based Simulation for Synthesis of Inorganic Materials

author.name: Edward W. Staley, Tom Arbaugh, Michael Pekala, Alexander New, Christopher D. Stiles, Nam Q. Le, Gregory Bassen, Wyatt Bunstine, Tyrel McQueen

entry.summary: This paper introduces a hybrid framework that couples LLMs with thermodynamic databases and simplified kinetics models to evaluate inorganic synthesis planning, using the niobium-oxygen system as a case study. It compares LLM-generated synthesis routes against classical physics-based approaches.

entry.title: Threshold-Based Exclusive Batching for LLM Inference

author.name: Weifang Zhang, Yuzhou Nie, Bowen Pang, Guangrui Ma, Shining Wu

entry.summary: This paper shows that mixed batching of prefill and decode in LLM inference can inflate per-step cost above pure decode, with the crossover threshold depending heavily on GPU memory bandwidth. It derives a closed-form analysis to choose between mixed and exclusive batching based on hardware and workload.

entry.title: KACE: Knowledge-Adaptive Context Engineering for Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Jayant Parashar, Suchendra M. Bhandarkar

entry.summary: KACE introduces knowledge-adaptive context engineering for mathematical reasoning that separates knowledge storage from usage via difficulty- and domain-based organization, distilling training traces into an epistemic tree of typed cards. This avoids context bloat from accumulated feedback in a single growing prompt.

entry.title: SHARP: Sleep-based Hierarchical Accelerated Replay for Long Range Non-Stationary Temporal Pattern Recognition

author.name: Jayanta Dey, Shikhar Srivastava, Itamar Lerner, Christopher Kanan, Dhireesha Kudithipudi

entry.summary: SHARP is a sleep-inspired hierarchical accelerated replay framework for learning long-range non-stationary temporal patterns in strict streaming settings, decomposing learning into a memory module accumulating history and an accelerated replay mechanism. It targets credit assignment limits of RNNs and transformers in single-pass settings.

entry.title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Large Language Models Via Decoder Layer Skipping

author.name: Hanze Li, Jinhao You, Yichen Guo, Kai Tang, Shuangyang Xie, Xiande Huang

entry.summary: DeLask is a decoding framework that mitigates hallucinations by dynamically skipping decoder layers prone to producing them, based on a layer-wise analysis showing hallucinations originate in deeper layers and a theoretical view of forward computation as gradient-descent steps. It defines a drift signal to choose skipped layers.

entry.title: CAREAgent: Clinical Agent with Structured Reasoning and Tool-Integrated for Order Generation

author.name: Ruihui Hou, Ziyue Huai, Chennuo Zhang, Ziyan Liu, Siran Zhao, Yao Yu, Jie Zhai, Tong Ruan

entry.summary: CAREAgent is a clinical agent for fine-grained, executable order generation using structured reasoning and tool integration, supported by a two-stage agentic data-construction method that builds and filters verifiable reasoning trajectories aligned with realistic clinical tool usage. It addresses prior agents' focus on coarse decisions over executable orders.

entry.title: Self-Healing Agentic Orchestrators for Reliable Tool-Augmented Large Language Model Systems

author.name: Rahul Suresh Babu, Adarsh Agrawal

entry.summary: This paper presents a self-healing agentic orchestrator that treats reliability as a bounded runtime control problem, mapping observable failure signals to inferred failure classes and selecting budgeted recovery actions with verification and observability traces. It addresses orchestration-level failures beyond model errors.

entry.title: EVA-Net: Subject-Independent EEG Motor Decoding with Video-Derived Motor Priors

author.name: Ziyuan Li, Yueyu Sun, Yimeng Zhang

entry.summary: EVA-Net is a two-stage framework for subject-independent EEG motor decoding that uses action videos as semantic priors, aligning EEG and video features in a shared space via cross-modal and supervised contrastive objectives. It aims to disentangle motor semantics from subject-specific noise for minimal-calibration BCIs.

entry.title: TCAR-Gen: Temporal Graph Retrieval with Evidence Fusion for Knowledge-Grounded Generation

author.name: Sidra Nasir, Muhammad Noman Zahid, Rizwan Ahmed Khan

entry.summary: TCAR-Gen combines query-conditioned graph neural networks, temporal evidence fusion, and chain-of-trees reasoning to ground generation in retrieved evidence for temporal reasoning over historical criminal case narratives, outperforming several RAG baselines on a crime-diaries benchmark. Addresses temporal reasoning and evidence fusion gaps in RAG.

entry.title: Measuring and Mitigating Bias in Code Generated by Large Language Models

author.name: Yuxi Chen, Yutian Tang, Timothy Storer

entry.summary: Proposes a framework using code bias score and attribute change ratio to measure bias in code generated by GPT-4o and Gemini, examining the influence of protected attributes, prompts, and web search, plus four lightweight mitigation strategies. Quantifies bias prevalence in generated code.

entry.title: Beyond Text and Tables: Vision-Language Model Integration in ComProScanner for Extracting Materials Data from Scientific Figures with High Accuracy

author.name: Aritra Roy, Enrico Grisan, Chiara Gattinoni, John Buckeridge

entry.summary: Extends ComProScanner with a native vision-language model figure-extraction capability to mine quantitative materials composition-property data from scientific figures, adding a figure filter and graph extractor agent. Addresses data reported exclusively in figures rather than text or tables.

entry.title: Silent Failures in Physical AI: A Literature Review of Runtime Action Authorization for Autonomous Systems

author.name: Barak Or

entry.summary: A literature review of runtime action authorization for autonomous physical AI systems, framing silent failures where black-box models issue confident but physically unsafe actions due to sensor drift, occlusion, or hallucinated affordances. Distinguishes this from content moderation and classical robot safety.

entry.title: Interpreting FCDNNs via RG on Exponential Family

author.name: Fuzhou Gong, Zigeng Xia

entry.summary: Develops an interpretability theory connecting the renormalization group method from statistical physics to fully-connected DNN training, generalizing prior Ising-model results to continuous exponential-family input data. Proves correspondences between optimal network parameters and RG characteristic parameters.

entry.title: LP5X-PIM Sim: A High-Fidelity HW/SW Integrated Simulator for LPDDR5X-PIM

author.name: SangHoon Cha, Jaewan Choi, Byeongho Kim, Yoonah Paik, Sukhan Lee, Kyomin Sohn

entry.summary: This Samsung tech note describes a high-fidelity hardware/software integrated simulator for LPDDR5X processing-in-memory, modeling both data paths and control layers for performance and energy evaluation. It refines existing frameworks for behavioral accuracy against real hardware.

entry.title: FW-NKF: Frequency-Weighted Neural Kalman Filters

author.name: Adnan Harun Dogan, Berken Utku Demirel, Christian Holz

entry.summary: Introduces FW-NKF, a frequency-weighted neural Kalman filter that embeds a causal spectral-shaping operator into the measurement residual to suppress band-limited noise like sensor vibrations and interference. Jointly learns observation and transition networks for robust robotic state estimation.

entry.title: CHAM-net: A Contrastive Hierarchical Adaptive Meta-network for Robust Global Methane Flux Prediction

author.name: Rongchao Dong, Yiming Sun, Shuo Chen, Youmi Oh, Licheng Liu, Yiqun Xie, Xiaowei Jia

entry.summary: Proposes CHAM-net, a contrastive hierarchical adaptive meta-network for global methane flux prediction that explicitly learns site-specific dynamics and cross-year evolution from historical context. Addresses spatiotemporal heterogeneity overlooked by prior data-driven methods.

entry.title: Beyond the Simplex: Balanced Prototype Geometry for Scorer-Agnostic Open-Set Recognition

author.name: Mayank Sharma, Rohit Kumar Mourya

entry.summary: This paper gives a theoretical account of simplex-ratio open-set recognition that holds in all embedding dimensions including below C-1, centering on balanced equal-norm codes. It provides justification previously lacking for simplex-based OSR methods.

entry.title: TimeBlocks: Foundational and Continual Time-Series Blockbase -- Extended Version

author.name: David Campos, Bin Yang, Tung Kieu, Lei Chen, Chenjuan Guo, Christian S. Jensen

entry.summary: TimeBlocks is a foundational and continual time-series blockbase designed to be lightweight for real-time stream processing while handling multiple tasks, unlike large offline-only foundation models. It supports continual calibration for streaming data.

entry.title: ChWDTA: Channel-wise Wavelet-Domain Transformer Attention and Entropy Modeling for Learned Image Compression

author.name: Haisheng Fu, Runyu Yang, Feng Ding, Siyu Zhu, Jie Liang, Xiaoxiao Li, Zhenman Fang, Jingning Han

entry.summary: Introduces channel-wise wavelet-domain transformer attention and entropy modeling for learned image compression, computing attention on wavelet-transformed features to improve rate-distortion performance. Builds on hybrid CNN-transformer LIC backbones.

entry.title: Rethinking Amortized Neural Representations for High-Resolution Terrain Elevation Data

author.name: Haoan Feng, Xin Xu, Leila De Floriani

entry.summary: Rethinks amortized neural representations for high-resolution terrain elevation data, addressing scalability of fitting separate INRs per tile through a shared decoder with compact per-tile payloads. Adapts methods designed for natural images to heightfield terrain.

entry.title: Meta-Black-Box Optimization with Ensemble Surrogate Modeling for Robustness-Accuracy Trade-off within SAEA

author.name: Xiao Jin, Yongxiong Wang, Haobo Liu, Yudong Du, Yukun Du

entry.summary: Proposes a meta-black-box-optimization approach with ensemble surrogate modeling to jointly control multiple components of surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms, explicitly handling the robustness-accuracy trade-off in surrogate modeling. Extends MetaBBO beyond single-component control.

entry.title: Scalable Counterfactual Risk Estimation for Rare Events in Longitudinal Data

author.name: Xiaohui Yin, Avijit Mitra, Ying Zhou, Kun Chen, Hong Yu

entry.summary: Proposes a subsampling and reweighting strategy for scalable counterfactual risk estimation of time-varying treatments on rare survival outcomes in large longitudinal data. It addresses computational cost and class imbalance in g-formula/ICE estimators.

entry.title: Self-Regulating Annealing in Heavy-Tailed Diffusion Models

author.name: Keito Wakatsuki, Hideaki Shimazaki

entry.summary: Proposes an SDE-based sampler for heavy-tailed (Student's t) diffusion models with a state-dependent diffusion coefficient that induces a self-regulating annealing mechanism. It improves tail fidelity sampling for heavy-tailed datasets.

entry.title: Resonant Context Anchoring: Decoupling Attention Routing and Signal Gain at Inference Time

author.name: Mingkuan Zhao, Yide Gao, Wentao Hu, Suquan Chen, Tianchen Huang, Zhenhua An, Zetao Chang, Xiayu Sun, Yuheng Min

entry.summary: Proposes Resonant Context Anchoring, a lightweight inference-time intervention that addresses LLM contextual disregard by counteracting attenuation of external evidence in the residual stream. It aims to reduce factual hallucinations without expensive contrastive decoding.

entry.title: Non-Learning Low-Light Stereo Vision

author.name: Jason Wang, Lucas Nguyen, Hyunseung Eom, Wei Xu, Qi Guo

entry.summary: This work presents a non-learning stereo framework for disparity estimation from severely noisy images, using the Field of Junctions to retain noise-stable coarse features and boundary-aware Semi-Global Matching. It produces sparse disparity maps more accurate than recent learned stereo algorithms on unmasked pixels.

entry.title: A Systematic Benchmark of Intraoperative Ultrasound-to-MR Synthesis for Brain Tumour Surgery

author.name: Olga Esteban-Sinovas, Santiago Cepeda, Ignacio Arrese, Rosario Sarabia

entry.summary: This work presents a systematic benchmark of intraoperative ultrasound-to-MR synthesis for brain tumour surgery, spanning architectural paradigms, inference regimes, and downstream-task endpoints under a common protocol on the public ReMIND dataset. It aims to let MRI-based surgical infrastructure be reused intraoperatively without an extra scan.

entry.title: COLLAR: Cascaded Object-Level Latent Refinement for High-Fidelity Conditional Generation

author.name: Xinlong Zhang, Jia Wei, Xiaoyu Zhang, Teng Zhou, Chengyu Lin, Yongchuan Tang

entry.summary: COLLAR is a training-free framework for object-level controllable generation in Diffusion Transformers, progressively refining object features via field-of-view expansion and cross-scale semantic alignment. It targets artifact reduction and precise control in small regions.

entry.title: Boundary-Protection W8A8 HiFloat8 Quantization for Large-Scale Text-to-Video Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Yiming Zhao

entry.summary: This work presents W8A8 HiFloat8 post-training quantization for a 14B text-to-video diffusion transformer on Ascend NPUs, identifying that boundary transformer blocks have distinct activation statistics and retaining them in BF16 while quantizing middle blocks. It targets efficient large-scale video DiT deployment.

entry.title: Chameleon: Style-Content Disentangled Framework for Cross-Domain Object Compositing

author.name: Sukhun Ko, Soo Ye Kim, Jihyong Oh

entry.summary: Chameleon is a style-content disentangled framework for cross-domain object compositing that preserves a foreground object's identity while stylizing it to match a different-domain background. It addresses the lack of paired cross-domain compositing datasets that limits prior training-free methods.

entry.title: HiTokSR: A Coarse-to-Fine Tokenizer with Hierarchical Codebooks for High-Fidelity Real-World Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Mingxi Li

entry.summary: HiTokSR is a hierarchical token prediction framework for real-world image super-resolution that partitions the latent space along channels into frequency-aware groups, each quantized with an independent sub-codebook to disentangle low-frequency structure from high-frequency texture. It improves codebook utilization and representational capacity.

entry.title: Event-Based Vision in Space: Applications, Trends, and Future Directions

author.name: Luigi Capogrosso, Pietro Bonazzi, Michele Magno

entry.summary: This survey reviews event-based (neuromorphic) vision for space applications, covering applications, trends, and future directions, highlighting advantages over frame-based sensors in motion blur, power, and dynamic range. It consolidates a fragmented body of space-based literature.

entry.title: $\text{VG}^2$GT: Voxel-Gaussian Splatting Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer

author.name: Yibin Zhao, Yihan Pan, Jun Nan, Wenli Yang, Liwei Chen, Jianjun Yi

entry.summary: VG2GT is a voxel-Gaussian splatting visual geometry grounded transformer that leverages a frozen visual foundation model and a multi-scale differentiable voxel module to regress Gaussian primitives without accurate camera parameters or per-scene optimization. It reduces artifacts of pixel-aligned feed-forward methods.

entry.title: EIVE: End-to-End Instance-Specific Visual Explanations for Detection Transformers

author.name: Jianlin Xiang, Yanshan Li, Linhui Dai

entry.summary: EIVE generates end-to-end instance-specific visual explanations for DETR-like detectors by reformulating decoder cross-attention as a feature-attribution pathway, producing saliency maps in the forward pass without extra gradient computation or repeated inference. It improves explainability efficiency for multi-instance detection.

entry.title: Edge Prediction for Roof Wireframe Reconstruction with Transformers

author.name: Gustav Hanning, Ludvig Dill\'en, Jonathan Astermark, Johanna Lidholm, Viktor Larsson

entry.summary: Presents a Transformer encoder-decoder solution inspired by DETR for the S23DR Challenge 2026, reconstructing 3D house roof wireframes from sparse SfM point clouds and ground-level segmentation/depth. Uses semantic-priority subsampling and Gestalt/ADE20k feature augmentation.

entry.title: Rate-optimal neural boundary detection from unlabeled noisy images

author.name: Kyeongho Kim, Ilsang Ohn

entry.summary: This work proposes a continuous hinge-type surrogate loss for boundary detection in unlabeled noisy images without pixel annotations or parametric intensity models. It proves Fisher consistency and rate-optimality, combining the loss with deep networks for complex boundaries.

entry.title: Data-Automated Policy Learning for Nonlinear Welfare

author.name: Chunrong Ai, Zeqi Wu, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: This paper studies policy learning from observational data under a nonlinear welfare criterion that prioritizes specific population segments, with criterion and parameters depending on machine-learning-estimated propensity scores. It introduces a reweighting-based debiasing approach to correct ML estimation bias.

entry.title: AXIOM: A Trust-First Neuro-Symbolic Execution Architecture for Verifiable Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Alessio Bruno

entry.summary: AXIOM is a trust-first neuro-symbolic architecture where the LLM only canonicalizes natural-language math into a narrow schema consumed by a deterministic computer-algebra-system pipeline that derives, verifies, or abstains. It reports high verified correctness with zero confident-wrong errors via tight regex-prompt-handler routing.

entry.title: The Shape of Wisdom: Decision Trajectories in Language Models

author.name: Shailesh Rana

entry.summary: This single-author study analyzes 9,000 MMLU answer trajectories across three 7-8B instruct models, tracking how answer margins evolve layer-by-layer and finding that the largest group is unstable-correct rather than stable-correct. Attention contributions tend to point in the correct direction while MLP contributions do not.

entry.title: Community-Aware Assessment of Social Textual Engagement and Resonance: A Human-Centric Perspective on User-Generated Content Evaluation

author.name: Tianjiao Li, Kai Zhao, Xiang Li, Yang Liu, Huyang Sun

entry.summary: This work proposes CASTER, a human-centric task that evaluates whether user-generated content achieves positive community resonance based on multimodal attributes rather than aesthetic quality alone, and presents MEDEA with a Social Chain-of-Thought mechanism. It reframes video quality assessment toward social engagement dynamics.

entry.title: From Capability Models to Automated Planning: An AAS-Native Approach for Automatic PDDL Generation

author.name: Hamied Nabizada, Thomas Wirt, Luis Miguel Vieira da Silva, Felix Gehlhoff, Alexander Fay

entry.summary: This work shows that AAS capability models structured by four Industry 4.0 standards contain sufficient information to automatically generate PDDL planning problems, enabling production engineers to verify layout feasibility without planning expertise. It presents an AAS-native approach for automatic PDDL generation.

entry.title: Coordination Graphs for Constrained Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Santiago Amaya-Corredor, Miguel Calvo-Fullana, Anders Jonsson

entry.summary: Presents CG-CMARL, combining coordination graphs with Lagrangian duality to scale constrained multi-agent RL by decomposing the joint problem into pairwise regions with shared Q-functions, keeping model count independent of agent number. Uses Max-Sum message passing at execution time.

entry.title: RASER: Recoverability-Aware Selective Escalation Router for Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: Yuyang Li, Zihe Yan, Tobias K\"afer

entry.summary: RASER is a family of cheap routers built on one-shot RAG that decide whether to stop or escalate to expensive multi-hop retrieval, exploiting the finding that many multi-hop questions are already answered correctly by single-pass RAG. Saves token budget by avoiding unnecessary retrieval.

entry.title: AEyeDE: An Attention-Based Attribution Framework for AI-Generated Text Detection

author.name: Aria Nourbakhsh, Adelaide Danilov, Christoph Schommer, Salima Lamsiyah

entry.summary: AEyeDE detects AI-generated text using attention-based attribution matrices from a proxy Transformer fed into a lightweight CNN, outperforming text-only baselines especially in encoder-decoder translation settings. Aims to resist detectors that rely on surface statistics.

entry.title: VDSB-GWSyn: Diffusion Schr\"{o}dinger Bridge for Controllable and Anatomically Feasible Guidewire Synthesis in Coronary Angiography

author.name: Haoyuan Tang, Zhuo Zhang, Jialin Li, Shuai Xiao, Jiachen Yang

entry.summary: Proposes VDSB-GWSyn, a Diffusion Schrodinger Bridge framework for synthesizing controllable, anatomically feasible guidewire samples in coronary angiography to overcome scarce annotated data. It supports computer-assisted and robot-assisted PCI guidewire endpoint localization.

entry.title: Completion at the Boundary (CaB): Deployable Switching with Completion-Aware Control under Limited Calibration

author.name: Yusuke Sano, Takeshi Itoga

entry.summary: Studies completion detection for vision-language-action agents executing short composite instructions, proposing a deployable single globally-calibrated switching rule under limited calibration. It frames completion as a closed-loop intervention problem to avoid mistimed handoffs.

entry.title: SUPREME: A Multi-GPU Framework for Reproducible Image Unlearning Method Evaluation

author.name: Petros Andreou, Jamie Lanyon, Axel Finke, Georgina Cosma

entry.summary: Introduces SUPREME, an open-source multi-GPU framework for reproducible image unlearning evaluation that distributes training, unlearning, and evaluation across accelerators to enable many-seed assessment. It offers a registry-based design for adding methods, metrics, models, and scenarios.

entry.title: TabChange: Precise Attribute Changes in Tabular Data

author.name: Arjun Dahal, Yu Lei, Raghu N. Kacker, Richard Kuhn

entry.summary: TabChange generates minimally-changed yet natural counterfactual edits of attributes in tabular data by analyzing attribute relationships and avoiding unnecessary modifications. It addresses limitations of generative editing methods like CVAE that retain attribute info in latent space.

entry.title: SS-ZKR: Spatial-Semantic Zero-Knowledge Routing for Privacy-Preserving Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Hassan Touheed

entry.summary: Proposes a zero-knowledge routing protocol enabling content-based semantic routing of agent payloads across trust boundaries without intermediaries decrypting them, addressing GDPR/HIPAA compliance. Designed as a complementary layer atop A2A and MCP agent protocols.

entry.title: Soft-NBCE: Entropy-Weighted Chunk Fusion for Long-Context

author.name: Shihao Ji, Mingyu Li, Zihui Song

entry.summary: Proposes Soft-NBCE, replacing hard chunk selection in the Naive Bayes Cognitive Engine with soft entropy-weighted chunk fusion for long-context inference. Reduces semantic fragmentation from abrupt routing changes between tokens.

entry.title: Quantum Algorithm for Distributed Reduction of Entanglements (QADR): A Trainable and Simulation-Efficient QML Framework

author.name: Syed Farhan Ahmad, Gregory T. Byrd

entry.summary: Introduces QADR, a hybrid quantum-classical ML framework that decomposes a global n-qubit variational circuit into localized sub-circuits within causal light cones, reducing simulation memory scaling and mitigating barren plateaus. Targets trainability under NISQ constraints.

entry.title: On the Evaluation of Spiking Neural Network Configurations for Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Raj Patel, David Amebley, Taye Akinrele, Shaswata Mitra, Sayanton Dibbo, Shahram Rahimi

entry.summary: Conducts a controlled ablation evaluating 27 spiking neural network configurations (9 neuron models x 3 spike encodings) for network intrusion detection across four benchmark datasets. Characterizes the under-studied SNN design space for lightweight neuromorphic security deployment.

entry.title: LLM Consortium for Software Design Refinement: A Controlled Experiment on Multi-Agent Collaboration Topologies

author.name: Nagarjuna Kanamarlapudi, Praveen K

entry.summary: This controlled experiment evaluates 12 multi-agent LLM collaboration topologies for software architecture design using a factorial design across 520 runs. It finds structural adversarial and cross-model review topologies perform best.

entry.title: LayerRoute: Input-Conditioned Adaptive Layer Skipping via LoRA Fine-Tuning for Agentic Language Models

author.name: Prateek Kumar Sikdar

entry.summary: LayerRoute is a LoRA-based adapter that learns input-conditioned adaptive transformer-block skipping for agentic LLMs, exploiting the structural difference between short deterministic tool calls and long reasoning steps. It adds per-layer binary gating routers with straight-through estimators on Qwen2.5-0.5B.

entry.title: Train, Test, Re-evaluate: Schedule-Sensitive Evaluation of Generative Data for Hand Detection

author.name: Atmika Bhardwaj, Silvia Vock, Nico Steckhan

entry.summary: This paper shows that the apparent value of generative (synthetic) hand-detection data is highly sensitive to the training schedule used for re-evaluation, using inpainting to add accessories like gloves and jewelry. It tests YOLOv8n detectors under six training configurations on paired real and synthetic images.

entry.title: Agentic-J: An AI Agent for Biological Microscopy Image Analysis

author.name: Lukas Johanns, Marilin Moor, Davide Panzeri, Yu Zhou, Xinyi Chen, Nora F. K. Pauly, Zixuan Pan, Matthias Gunzer, Andreas M\"uller, Yiyu Shi, Hedi Peterson, Jianxu Chen

entry.summary: Presents Agentic-J, a containerized multi-agent assistant for biological microscopy analysis in ImageJ/Fiji that lets biologists specify tasks in natural language and generates reproducible, documented scripts. Specialized sub-agents handle plugin management, code generation, debugging, and statistical reporting.

entry.title: VLBM: Variational Latent Basis Modeling for OOD Robust Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Xudong Zhang, Jierui Lei, Jiacheng Li, Lingdong Shen, Jian Cui, Haina Tang

entry.summary: Proposes VLBM, a variational latent forecasting framework for multivariate time series that separates stable in-distribution dynamics from OOD-induced deviations via a shared low-rank latent basis. Targets reliability under rare but high-impact distribution shifts.

entry.title: AI-Guided Design and Optimization of Graphite-Based Anodes via Iterative Experimental Feedback

author.name: Qian Du, Mark M. Sullivan, James E. Saal, Florian Huber

entry.summary: Presents an iterative AI-guided sequential-learning workflow for graphite anode development using multi-objective inverse design on the Citrine Platform. Starting from noisy incomplete data, it improved formulation feasibility and process robustness to achieve 100% successful cell production.

entry.title: Mapping the evolution of small reservoirs in Brazil from 1984 to 2025 using deep learning

author.name: Kylen Solvik, Luis Gustavo Carvalho, Marcia N. Macedo

entry.summary: Trains a deep learning segmentation model to map small stream-fed reservoirs across Brazil from 1984 to 2025 using Landsat data, filling a gap in water resource datasets. Distinguishes artificial reservoirs from natural lakes at sub-square-kilometer scale.

entry.title: Turning Back Without Forgetting: Selective Backward Refinement for Parameter-Efficient Continual Learning

author.name: Anushka Tiwari, Kaiyi Ji

entry.summary: SABER enables controlled positive backward knowledge transfer in prompt-based continual learning without replay, using task-correlation criteria from prompt-gradient geometry. It selectively refines earlier tasks by restricting updates to non-interfering directions.

entry.title: CRePE: Convolution-aware Relative Importance in Post-training Pruning with Efficient Search

author.name: Cheonjun Park

entry.summary: CRePE improves post-training pruning of LLMs by incorporating 2D local neighborhood context and adaptive coefficients into relative importance scoring, extending the prior RIA method. It outperforms existing pruning methods across models and sparsity levels.

entry.title: Tree-Guided Identify-Then-Exploit: A Unified Framework of Best Arm Identification and Regret Minimization for Dueling Bandits

author.name: Pu Wang, Yao-Xiang Ding

entry.summary: TG-ITE is a unified framework for dueling bandits addressing best-arm identification, weak regret, and strong regret via a shared tree-guided identification stage with O(N) comparisons. It achieves O(N) sample complexity without stronger assumptions.

entry.title: Expressivity of congruence-based architectures for DNNs on positive-definite matrices

author.name: Antonin Oswald, Estelle Massart

entry.summary: Analyzes the expressivity of congruence-based layers for classifying symmetric positive-definite matrices, showing that orthogonality constraints can collapse architectures to a single hidden layer. Provides theoretical guidance for designing SPD neural networks.

entry.title: ReFLEX: Length-Generalizable CSI Denoising for MIMO-OFDM via Relative-Frequency Bias

author.name: Zhibin Zhang, Robert Potekhin, Ziwei Wan, Vladimir Lyashev, Zhen Gao

entry.summary: Presents ReFLEX, a length-generalizable transformer for CSI denoising in MIMO-OFDM using relative-frequency position bias, handling unseen resource-block lengths without retraining. Reports strong NMSE and BLER improvements in 3GPP channel simulations.

entry.title: Symmetric Hermite quadrature-based balanced truncation for learning linear dynamical systems from derivative data

author.name: Sean Reiter, Steffen W. R. Werner

entry.summary: Presents a symmetric Hermite quadrature-based balanced truncation method for learning reduced-order linear dynamical systems from transfer-function and derivative evaluations, preserving Hermiticity and asymptotic stability. Relevant to data-driven control design.

entry.title: Statistical Analysis of using the Shapley Value for Sensor Anomaly Localization with Accurate Classifiers

author.name: Xubin Fang, Rick S. Blum

entry.summary: Provides statistical analysis of using the Shapley value for sensor anomaly localization, proving that for independent observations an optimized Shapley test is equivalent to a single-term lower-complexity test with identical error probability. Examines dependent two-sensor cases as well.

entry.title: Semantic Retrieval for Product Search in E-Commerce

author.name: Nikhil Kothari, Saksham Samdani, Ritam Mallick, Praveen Gupta, Ankit Vijay, Surender Kumar

entry.summary: Presents a Siamese LLM dual-encoder for e-commerce semantic product retrieval, trained via contrastive learning with false-negative masking then a preference-optimization objective (ROAR) extending Bradley-Terry to graded relevance groups. It targets noisy colloquial queries over large catalogs.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Recurrent State-Space Neural Networks for Multi-Step Prediction

author.name: Ruiyuan Li, Ajay Seth, Manon Kok

entry.summary: Introduces PG-RSSNN, a physics-guided recurrent state-space neural network that uses recurrent structure to enable non-saturating activations for multi-step prediction, mitigating vanishing gradients and numerical divergence. It blends physical state-space knowledge with deep learning.

entry.title: Deep Learning for Remote Sensing to Improve Flood Inundation Mapping

author.name: Yogesh Bhattarai, Vijay Chaudhary, Wai Lim Kim, Sanjib Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces a cloud-removal framework for flood imagery using Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models with a Masked Diffusion Transformer to reconstruct optical satellite observations obscured by cloud during extreme precipitation. It improves flood inundation mapping over temporal compositing.

entry.title: Toward Responsible and Epistemically Grounded Multilingual LLMs for Computational Social Science and Humanities

author.name: Wajdi Zaghouani

entry.summary: This position paper reconceptualizes multilingual reasoning LLMs as hermeneutic instruments and proposes a theoretically grounded framework for evaluating them in social science and humanities contexts. It critiques existing task-based benchmarks for ignoring interpretive validity and cultural situatedness.

entry.title: On the Salience of Low-Probability Tokens for AI-Generated Text Detection: A Multiscale Uncertainty Perspective

author.name: Yikai Guo, Bin Wang, Xilai Fan, Wenjun Ke, Haoran Luo

entry.summary: This work proposes a multiscale uncertainty estimator for AI-generated text detection that focuses on informative low-probability tokens rather than boilerplate, improving robustness over brittle single-score detectors. It targets misinformation and academic misuse concerns.

entry.title: Beyond Isolated Behaviors: Hierarchical User Modeling for LLM Personalization

author.name: Liang Wang, Xinyi Mou, Xiaoyou Liu, Tiannan Wang, Yuqing Wang, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: PHF (Practice-Habitus-Field) draws on Bourdieu's sociological theory to model LLM personalization at three hierarchical levels: individual behaviors, accumulated dispositions, and shared regularities across similar users. It offers a structured alternative to flat behavioral aggregation.

entry.title: Local Diagnostics of Continuous Normalizing Flow for Out-of-Distribution Detection

author.name: Xinwei Cao, Mengxuan Lu, Torbj{\o}rn Svendsen, Giampiero Salvi

entry.summary: This work proposes a Lagrangian sub-flow framework using continuous normalizing flows for out-of-distribution detection of observations embedded in a data subspace. It addresses the likelihood paradox where deep generative models assign high likelihood to OOD samples, demonstrated on speech synthesis.

entry.title: Advances in Neural 3D Mesh Texturing: A Survey

author.name: Sai Raj Kishore Perla, Hao Zhang, Ali Mahdavi-Amiri

entry.summary: This survey comprehensively reviews recent advances in neural 3D mesh texturing, covering texture synthesis, transfer, and completion alongside foundations in mesh geometry, differentiable rendering, and neural generative models. It situates mesh texturing relative to NeRF and Gaussian Splatting approaches.

entry.title: Shape-Prior-Based Point Cloud Completion for Single-Stage Fully Sparse 3D Object Detection

author.name: Kaizheng Wang, Mingqian Ji, Jian Yang, Shanshan Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a shape-prior-based point cloud completion method tailored for single-stage fully sparse 3D detectors in autonomous driving, with an instance selection module and a two-step completion process. It addresses point cloud sparsity that limits detection performance.

entry.title: CR-JEPA: Cross-Modal Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for Remote Sensing Image Retrieval

author.name: Md Aminur Hossain, Ayush V. Patel, Nitant Dube, Biplab Banerjee

entry.summary: CR-JEPA applies a joint-embedding predictive architecture to cross-modal remote sensing image retrieval, using modality-specific stems, a shared transformer trunk, and JEPA-style masked latent prediction. It targets retrieval across heterogeneous sensing modalities.

entry.title: Automated Erythrocyte Detection and Tracking for Retinal Blood Flow Quantification in Erythrocyte-Mediated Angiography

author.name: Chiao-Yi Wang, Havish S Gadde, Yi-Ting Shen, Saige M. Oechsli, Osamah Saeedi, Yang Tao
