entry.title: When and How Long? The Readout-Mediator Angle in Temporal Reasoning

author.name: Shreyas Fadnavis, Praitayini Kanakaraj, Felix Wyss

entry.summary: This interpretability paper introduces the readout-mediator angle, showing that a linear probe can decode a feature (day-of-year) almost perfectly yet be orthogonal to the model's actual causal computation found via Distributed Alignment Search. It cautions that probe decodability does not imply causal relevance in temporal reasoning circuits.

entry.title: Provably Secure Agent Guardrail

author.name: Benlong Wu, Weiming Zhang, Kejiang Chen, Han Fang, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: Proposes a provably secure agent guardrail using a Proof-Constrained Action framework with neural-symbolic isolation, aiming for deterministic security lower bounds instead of probabilistic semantic guardrails. It targets agents with execution privileges facing decoupling attacks.

entry.title: OpenClawBench: Benchmarking Process-side Anomalies in Real-world Agent Execution Trajectories

author.name: Yibing Liu, Yangze Liu, Xiaolong Yin, Bin Wang, Chong Zhang, Hao Yin, Zhongyi Han

entry.summary: OpenClawBench is a large dataset of 31,264 annotated agent trajectories measuring process-side anomalies (the Outcome-Process Gap) that hide behind task success, such as unsafe writes and ignored errors. It enables supervision of agent process quality.

entry.title: PassNet: Scaling Large Language Models for Graph Compiler Pass Generation

author.name: Yiqun Liu, Yingsheng Wu, Ruqi Yang, Enrong Zheng, Honglei Qiu, Sijun He, Tai Liang, Jingjing Wu, Yuhan Zhou, Yiwei Zhang, Dongyan Chen, Weihan Yi, Xinqi Li, Siqi Bao

entry.summary: PassNet is a large-scale ecosystem for LLM-based compiler pass generation, where models author structured graph transformations integrating into compiler pipelines, with an 18K-graph dataset and 200-task benchmark. It targets long-tail workloads where default tensor compilation underperforms.

entry.title: How Coding Agents Fail Their Users: A Large-Scale Analysis of Developer-Agent Misalignment in 20,574 Real-World Sessions

author.name: Ningzhi Tang, Chaoran Chen, Gelei Xu, Yiyu Shi, Yu Huang, Collin McMillan, Tao Dong, Toby Jia-Jun Li

entry.summary: Presents a large-scale observational study of 20,574 real coding-agent sessions across 1,639 repositories, operationalizing misalignment through developer pushback and annotating episodes by form, cause, cost, and resolution. It finds most failures impose effort and trust costs and that visible resolutions remain costly, identifying seven recurring failure forms.

entry.title: M\=oLe-{\Lambda}: Learning the Coupled-Cluster Response State for Energies, Gradients, and Properties

author.name: Andreas Burger, Luca Thiede, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos-Gonzalez-Angulo, Alex Zook, J\'er\^ome Florian Gonthier, Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik

entry.summary: Introduces MoLe-Lambda, a machine learning method predicting the full ground-state CCSD response state by jointly learning right-hand T-amplitudes and left-hand Lambda-amplitudes from localized molecular orbitals. Enables fast access to coupled-cluster energies, gradients, and properties.

entry.title: Token Inflation: How Dishonest Providers Can Overcharge for Large Language Model Usage

author.name: Shahinul Hoque, Jinghuai Zhang, Jinyuan Sun, Fnu Suya

entry.summary: This security paper shows that per-token LLM billing is fundamentally hard to audit because providers control the model, tokenizer, and execution, creating a trust paradox where audits must rely on artifacts providers can manipulate. It demonstrates that three recent token-auditing frameworks can be systematically gamed to overcharge. It raises an important accountability concern for commercial LLM markets.

entry.title: Token-Level Generalization in LoRA Adapter Backdoors: Attack Characterization and Behavioral Detection

author.name: Travis Lelle

entry.summary: This paper shows LoRA adapters can be reliably backdoored via training data poisoning while preserving clean accuracy, with the backdoor generalizing at the token-feature level rather than structural pattern level. The asymmetry favors attackers since defenders cannot probe generically. Important security finding given LoRA's role as the dominant fine-tuned model distribution format.

entry.title: VideoFDB: Evaluating Full-Duplex Vision-Speech Capabilities in Conversational Agents

author.name: Amrita Mazumdar, Seonwook Park, Rajarshi Roy, Nikhil Srihari, Shengze Wang, Yuhao Zhou, Julia Wang, Koki Nagano, Shalini De Mello

entry.summary: VideoFDB is the first benchmark for full-duplex audio-visual conversational agents, with 237 dyadic clips spanning 11 nonverbal dynamics, a taxonomy separating perception from generation, and a rubric-based LM-as-judge evaluation. It extends full-duplex evaluation beyond speech to nonverbal cues like nods and smiles. Important for next-generation conversational agents from NVIDIA researchers.

entry.title: Digitally enriching a screening population for pancreatic cancer using routine blood-based measures and clinical histories

author.name: Chris Varghese, Leo Y. Li-Han, Richa Bisht, Ellen Larson, Frank Lee, Ryan M. Carr, Tanios S. Bekaii-Saab, Shounak Majumder, John D. Halamka, Mark Truty, Ajit H. Goenka, Hojjat Salehinejad, Cornelius A. Thiels

entry.summary: This work trains a transformer with multi-head attention on longitudinal coded diagnoses and blood test trajectories to predict pancreatic cancer risk with multi-year lead time, enabling digital enrichment of screening populations. The cohort included 6,017 cancer patients and 177,081 controls. Important clinical ML application for early cancer detection.

entry.title: Benchmarking Single-Factor Physical Video-to-Audio Generation

author.name: Tingle Li, Siddharth Gururani, Kevin J. Shih, Gantavya Bhatt, Sang-gil Lee, Zhifeng Kong, Arushi Goel, Gopala Anumanchipalli, Ming-Yu Liu

entry.summary: Introduces FlatSounds, a benchmark auditing whether video-to-audio models capture real physical processes using controlled counterfactual pairs that vary a single physical factor and single-video consistency tests. Evaluations of SOTA models (from a strong NVIDIA team) reveal they lean on text captions over the visual stream for physical inference.

entry.title: CalArena: A Large-Scale Post-Hoc Calibration Benchmark

author.name: Eug\`ene Berta, David Holzm\"uller, Francis Bach, Michael I. Jordan

entry.summary: CalArena is a large-scale standardized benchmark for post-hoc calibration covering nearly 2000 experiments across tabular and vision tasks with unified reproducible implementations of dozens of methods. It enables fair comparison of calibration approaches that have suffered from inconsistent small-scale evaluations.

entry.title: Masquerade: Learning from In-the-wild Human Videos using Data-Editing

author.name: Marion Lepert, Jiaying Fang, Jeannette Bohg

entry.summary: Masquerade edits in-the-wild egocentric human videos into robot demonstrations by estimating hand poses, inpainting arms, and overlaying a rendered robot, then pretrains a visual encoder to predict robot keypoints for policy learning. It addresses robot data scarcity by repurposing abundant human video.

entry.title: One Mask to Rule Them All: On Hidden Facts after Editing and How to Find Them

author.name: Ali Holmov, Paul Youssef, Nandi Schoots, Christin Seifert

entry.summary: This paper probes the internal mechanism of knowledge editing methods (ROME, MEMIT) and shows that diverse factual edits share a common functional structure that can be reversed by a single compact binary mask. The mask undoes the majority of edits by removing overattention in later layers, offering a mechanistic understanding of how edits persist.

entry.title: Large language models reorganize representational geometry during in-context learning

author.name: Hua-Dong Xiong, Li Ji-An, Robert C. Wilson, Kwonjoon Lee, Xue-Xin Wei

entry.summary: Investigates how the geometry of representation space shapes in-context learning, hypothesizing that ICL depends on online untangling of task-relevant representations analogous to neural classification. It connects mechanistic ICL work to a geometric, neuroscience-inspired account of representation reorganization.

entry.title: Mechanistic origins of catastrophic forgetting: why RL preserves circuits better than SFT?

author.name: Jeanmely Rojas Nunez, Viraj Sawant, Nathan Allen, Nomgondalai Amgalanbaatar, Yannis Zongo, Vasu Sharma, Maheep Chaudhary

entry.summary: Extends the behavioral finding that RL preserves prior capabilities better than SFT to the mechanistic level, introducing differential circuit vulnerability to measure head-level circuit degradation under fine-tuning. It finds a mechanistic trade-off where SFT adapts faster but damages internal circuits more than RL.

entry.title: Robust and Efficient Guardrails with Latent Reasoning

author.name: Siddharth Sai, Xiaofei Wen, Muhao Chen

entry.summary: COLAGUARD transfers multi-step safety reasoning into a continuous latent space via a stage-wise curriculum, enabling direct hidden-state propagation at inference for safety moderation without the latency of explicit reasoning. It improves macro-F1 across eight safety benchmarks while cutting token overhead.

entry.title: Knowledge Offloading: Decomposing LLMs into Sparse Backbones and Memory Modules

author.name: Karim Galliamov, Rochelle Choenni, Ivan Titov

entry.summary: KOFF (knowledge offloading) decomposes a pretrained LLM into a sparse shared backbone plus domain-specific external memory modules (LoRA adapters and learned KV caches) by jointly learning a structured pruning mask and recovery modules. It moves specialized knowledge out of the backbone with limited capability loss at ~12% sparsity.

entry.title: Eulerian Gaussian Splatting using Hashed Probability Pyramids

author.name: Mia Gaia Polansky, George Kopanas, Stephan Garbin, Todd Zickler, Dor Verbin

entry.summary: Eulerian Gaussian Splatting replaces heuristic densification in 3D Gaussian Splatting with gradient-based optimization of a learnable volumetric probability density, using a memory-efficient multi-scale hashed grid and an unbiased variance-reduced gradient estimator. It retains fast rasterization while enabling principled, end-to-end optimization.

entry.title: ReasonOps: Operator Segmentation for LLM Reasoning Traces

author.name: Daniel Lee, Owen Queen, James Zou

entry.summary: ReasonOps is an unsupervised, expressive method for annotating chain-of-thought traces with universal reasoning operators, applied to 44,662 traces from 12 thinking LLMs across 8 benchmarks. It discovers seven recurring discourse-level reasoning moves (e.g., backtracking, inferring, hypothesizing) shared across models.

entry.title: BlockBatch: Multi-Scale Consensus Decoding for Efficient Diffusion Language Model Inference

author.name: Xiaoyou Wu, Cheng-Jhih Shih, Binfei Ji, Yong Liu, Yingyan (Celine) Lin

entry.summary: BlockBatch accelerates diffusion language model inference by treating block size as a branching dimension and using multi-scale consensus decoding across shared KV-cache trajectories. It targets the granularity tradeoff that limits dLLM efficiency.

entry.title: Wait! There's a Way Out: A Decision Mechanism for Forecasting Conversational Derailment

author.name: Laerdon Kim, Vivian Nguyen, Cristian Danescu-Niculescu-Mizil

entry.summary: Proposes decoupling the decision to trigger an alert from derailment likelihood estimation in conversational derailment forecasting, accounting for possible recovery to reduce false positives. Authored by Danescu-Niculescu-Mizil's group, a leader in conversational analysis.

entry.title: LoopFM: Learning frOm HistOrical RePresentations of Foundation Model for Recommendation

author.name: Shali Jiang, Hua Zheng, Boyang Liu, Laming Chen, Kenny Lov, Chuanqi Xu, Lisang Ding, Qinghai Zhou, Can Cui, Xiaolong Liu, Xiaoyi Liu, Yasmine Badr, Xin Xu, Jiyan Yang, Ellie Dingqiao Wen, Gerard Jonathan Mugisha Akkerhuis, Chenxiao Guan, Rong Jin, Ruichao Qiu, Xian Chen, Shifu Xu, Zhehui Zhou, Ping Chen, Rui Yang, Haicheng Chen, Xiangge Meng, Song Zhou, Dharak Kharod, Shuyu Xu, Qiang Jin, Qiao Yang, Wankun Zhu, Qin Huang, Yuzhen Huang, Darren Liu, Parish Aggarwal, Hui Zhou, Erzhuo Wang, Shuo Chang, Xiaorui Gan, Wenlin Chen, Santanu Kolay, Huayu Li

entry.summary: LoopFM transfers richer knowledge from foundation models to compact vertical recommendation models by feeding FM intermediate embeddings as input features rather than distilling a single scalar, avoiding real-time FM inference at serving. Includes theoretical transfer-ratio analysis and large industry authorship (Meta).

entry.title: PatchBoard: Schema-Grounded State Mutation for Reliable and Auditable LLM Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Shuyu Zhang, Yaqi Shi, Lu Wang

entry.summary: PatchBoard replaces natural-language inter-agent dialogue with validated JSON Patch mutations over shared structured state, with a deterministic kernel enforcing schema and write contracts for auditable multi-agent collaboration. It shows large success-rate gains over LangGraph and Flock on ALFWorld.

entry.title: Reasoning-preserved Efficient Distillation of Large Language Models via Activation-aware Initialization

author.name: Junlin He, Yihong Tang, Tong Nie, Guilong Li, Binyu Yang, Jinxiao Du, Lijun Sun, Wei Ma

entry.summary: Identifies reasoning collapse in efficiently distilled LLMs caused by effective-rank collapse from width-reducing projection matrices, and proposes activation-aware initialization to preserve reasoning ability. It provides a geometric explanation and fix for distillation degradation.

entry.title: EarthShift: a benchmark for measuring robustness to real-world distribution shifts in Earth observation

author.name: Kelsey Doerksen, Hannah Kerner

entry.summary: EarthShift is the first public testbed for benchmarking robustness of Earth-observation models across realistic distribution shifts in time, geography, scale, and sensors. Experiments on 8 geospatial foundation models and 11 tasks reveal substantial out-of-distribution performance drops.

entry.title: How Much Is a Dataset Worth? Scaling Laws, the Vendi Score, and Matrix Spectral Functions

author.name: Jeff A. Bilmes and Gantavya Bhatt and Arnav M. Das

entry.summary: Connects neural scaling laws and the Vendi Score to submodular optimization, proving both are submodular and that the Vendi Score is a special case of a broader class of matrix spectral functions including DPP objectives. It introduces weakly matrix monotone functions and efficient secular-equation updates to avoid repeated eigendecompositions during greedy data appraisal.

entry.title: Minimal Prompt Perturbations Lead to Code Vulnerabilities: Prompt Fragility and Hidden-State Signals in Coding LLMs

author.name: Alexander Sternfeld, Andrei Kucharavy, Ljiljana Dolamic

entry.summary: Shows that minimal prompt perturbations, even single-character changes, can flip LLM-generated code from secure to vulnerable across three models and five languages, and that this fragility is partially encoded in hidden states. It highlights security risks of LLM coding assistants. Important for software supply-chain security awareness.

entry.title: Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes: Correlated Errors Undermine LLM Evaluation Panels

author.name: Guneet Kohli

entry.summary: Shows that LLM-as-a-judge panels suffer from correlated errors: a panel of 9 frontier judges from 7 families provides only about 2 independent votes' worth of information, with accuracy falling 8-22 points short of the independent-voting ideal because models make the same mistakes. It quantifies the lost informational value of ensembles. Important caution for LLM-based evaluation methodology.

entry.title: Audio Jailbreaks in Large Audio-Language Models: Taxonomy, Attack-Defense Analysis, and Cost-Aware Evaluation

author.name: Bo-Han Feng, Yu-Hsuan Li Liang, Chien-Feng Liu, You-Hsuan Chang, Yun-Nung Chen

entry.summary: This paper offers a unified taxonomy and controlled empirical evaluation of jailbreak attacks and defenses for large audio-language models, spanning semantic, acoustic, signal, and embedding-layer attacks. It also introduces cost-aware evaluation to compare attack practicality and defense utility. It consolidates a fragmented safety subfield.

entry.title: A Predictive Law for On-Policy Self-Distillation From World Feedback

author.name: Tommy He, Jerome Sieber, Matteo Saponati

entry.summary: This paper identifies a consistent linear correlation between the initial student-self-teacher performance gap and final improvement in on-policy self-distillation, offering a predictive law for OPSD outcomes without full training. The relationship holds across context types, model families, and scales. It provides empirical grounding for richer-than-scalar feedback RL post-training.

entry.title: UniSteer: Text-Guided Flow Matching in Activation Space for Versatile LLM Steering

author.name: Yingdong Shi, Ruiming Zhang, Changming Li, Zhiyu Yang, Kaixing Zhang, Jingyi Yu, Kan Ren

entry.summary: UniSteer is a text-guided activation flow-matching model that learns a universal conditional velocity field over residual-stream activations, enabling versatile LLM steering from natural-language conditions instead of fixed directions or per-task modules. It performs flow inversion at inference for fine-grained, compositional control. The unified steering formulation is the key advance.

entry.title: Unveiling the Visual Counting Bottleneck in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xingzhou Pang and Yifan Hou and Junling Wang and Mrinmaya Sachan

entry.summary: This paper deconstructs why VLMs fail at visual counting by separating individuation, magnitude awareness, and symbolic mapping, using synthetic Go boards and linear probes. It shows perceptual representations remain robust into extrapolation and pinpoints the failure to the symbolic mapping stage. A clean diagnostic contribution to understanding VLM generalization limits.

entry.title: Double-Edged Sword or Sharp Tool? Designing and Evaluating Triadic LLM-Teacher Collaboration for K-12 Writing at Scale

author.name: Canran Wang, Yuwen Yang, Zhen Wang, Ming Ma, Ding Yu, Chentai Wang, Keman Huang, Xiaoyong Du

entry.summary: This large-scale study designs and evaluates triadic LLM-teacher-student collaboration for K-12 writing using 57,954 essays from 10,195 students across 120 schools over two years. It finds the LLM as generative engine plus teacher as pedagogical gatekeeper improves writing quality through strategic labor division. Notable for its large real-world empirical scale.

entry.title: A Dual-Path Architecture for Scaling Compute and Capacity in LLMs

author.name: Markus Frey, Behzad Shomali, Joachim Koehler, Mehdi Ali

entry.summary: This paper proposes a dual-path transformer block that independently scales compute (a deep shared-parameter sublayer applied K times) and capacity (a wide sublayer applied once), combined via per-token gates. It surpasses iso-FLOP looped and baseline transformers while enabling per-token routing analysis. Relevant for efficient architecture scaling.

entry.title: When Should Models Change Their Minds? Contextual Belief Management in Large Language Models

author.name: Haoming Xu, Weihong Xu, Zongrui Li, Mengru Wang, Yunzhi Yao, Chiyu Wu, Jin Shang, Yu Gong, Shumin Deng

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Contextual Belief Management—when LLMs should update, preserve, or ignore accumulating information—via BeliefTrack, a closed-world benchmark with symbolic verifiers diagnosing Failed Stay, Failed Update, and Failed Isolation. It finds vanilla models fail severely, belief-tracking prompts help little, and RL helps. Relevant for long-horizon interaction reliability.

entry.title: Beyond 3D VQAs: Injecting 3D Spatial Priors into Vision-Language Models for Enhanced Geometric Reasoning

author.name: Chun-Hsiao Yeh, Shengyi Qian, Manchen Wang, Yi Ma, Joseph Tighe, Fanyi Xiao

entry.summary: GASP injects geometric-aware spatial priors directly into a VLM's transformer layers via a small correspondence head applied as deep supervision across all layers, trained with contrastive and geometry objectives from large-scale video scenes, rather than relying on 3D VQA fine-tuning or specialized encoders. It improves robust 3D spatial reasoning. Relevant for genuine geometric understanding in VLMs.

entry.title: A Heterogeneous Architecture for Robot RL Beyond GPU-Dominant Paradigms

author.name: Yufei Jia, Zhanxiang Cao, Mingrui Yu, Heng Zhang, Shenyu Chen, Dixuan Jiang, Meng Li, Xiaofan Li, Yiyang Liu, Junzhe Wu, Zheng Li, XiLin Fang, Tingyu Cui, Shengcheng Fu, Haoyang Li, Anqi Wang, Zifan Wang, Dongjie Zhu, Chenyu Cao, Zhenbiao Huang, Ziang Zheng, Jie Lu, Xin Ma, Zhengyang Wei, Xiang Zhao, Tianyue Zhan, Ye He, Yuxiang Chen, Yizhou Jiang, Yue Li, Haizhou Ge, Yuhang Dong, Fan Jia, Ziheng Zhang, Meng Zhang, Xiwa Deng, Zhixing Chen, Hanyang Shao, Chenxin Dong, Yixuan Li, Yizhi Chen, Bokui Chen, Kaifeng Zhang, Hanqing Cui, Yusen Qin, Ruqi Huang, Lei Han, Tiancai Wang, Xiang Li, Yue Gao, Guyue Zhou

entry.summary: UniLab is a heterogeneous CPU-simulation/GPU-learning architecture for robot RL that challenges the GPU-resident simulation default, decoupling CPU-parallel physics from GPU policy updates via a unified runtime. It argues the key is an efficient end-to-end loop rather than which processor runs physics. A systems contribution from a very large robotics team.

entry.title: Resolution Diagnostics for Paired LLM Evaluation

author.name: Anany Kotawala

entry.summary: This paper applies hypothesis-testing diagnostics to paired LLM evaluation, showing many displayed leaderboard rankings (e.g., 11 of 40 Open LLM Leaderboard v1 pairs, up to 6 of 9 MMLU-Pro pairs) are statistically unresolved under proper paired-test power analysis. It introduces a per-pair resolution ratio diagnostic and corrects a widely-used unpaired shortcut. Important methodological warning for LLM benchmarking.

entry.title: RoboWits: Unexpected Challenges for Robotic Creative Problem Solving

author.name: Chunru Lin, Hongxin Zhang, Fenghao Yu, Zhehuan Chen, Thomas L. Griffiths, Yejin Choi, David Held, Chuang Gan

entry.summary: RoboWits is a bi-manual robotic benchmark for evaluating cognitive reasoning, creative tool use, and robustness to unexpected conditions, built via an automated multi-agent task generation pipeline. It moves beyond skill-level execution to test creative problem solving. A valuable reasoning-centric robotics benchmark from a credible team.

entry.title: When, why, and how do diffusion posterior samplers fail? A finite-sample lens

author.name: Benjamin A. Burns, Sara Fridovich-Keil

entry.summary: Provides a finite-sample theoretical lens on why diffusion posterior samplers for imaging inverse problems fail, attributing errors to the inexact likelihood approximations used at intermediate timesteps. By approximating the posterior to arbitrary precision via training-set scaling, it clarifies when and how these approximations propagate to wrong posteriors.

entry.title: SchGen: PCB Schematic Generation with Semantic-Grounded Code Representations

author.name: Qinpei Luo, Ruichun Ma, Xinyu Zhang, Lili Qiu

entry.summary: Presents SchGen, described as the first LLM that generates editable PCB schematics from natural-language requests, using a semantically grounded code representation that encodes editing primitives with relative placement and pin-name-based wiring. It tackles the lack of an LLM-suitable representation and dataset for PCB design.

entry.title: NeuROK: Generative 4D Neural Object Kinematics

author.name: Chen Geng, Guangzhao He, Yue Gao, Yunzhi Zhang, Shangzhe Wu, Jiajun Wu

entry.summary: Proposes NeuROK, which learns a data-driven kinematic state parameterization and latent space for object-centric physical systems to generate realistic 4D temporal deformations of static objects under varying physical conditions. This avoids the predefined physical models and per-category system identification that limit prior 4D dynamics methods.

entry.title: Advice for making robust-to-training model organisms

author.name: SebastianP

entry.summary: Offers practical advice for building model organisms of misalignment that survive untargeted training, noting that common techniques produce fragile organisms which stop misbehaving after benign training like teaching pirate-speak. It identifies factors that make organisms more robust, which matters because fragile ones can't distinguish a strong removal technique from a weak organism.

entry.title: On Language Generation in the Limit with Bounded Memory

author.name: Jon Kleinberg, Anay Mehrotra, Amin Saberi, Grigoris Velegkas

entry.summary: This paper studies language generation in the limit under bounded memory, characterizing when memoryless and bounded-memory generators can output only new valid examples from an unknown language. It extends classical learning-theory results on memory constraints to the generation setting.

entry.title: Prompt-Level Reward Specifications for Open-Ended Post-Training

author.name: Zijun Weng, Xiaohui Hu, Shuangyong Song, Yongxiang Li, Kaidong Yu, and Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: Introduces a prompt-level reward specification framework for open-ended post-training that separates reward specification from computation, building reusable task-adaptive rubrics and hard-constraint checkers offline. It makes success criteria explicit before RL training.

entry.title: STAMP: Training Explicit Memory for Mobile GUI Agents in Controllable and Scalable Virtual Environments

author.name: Junyang Wang, Haiyang Xu, Xi Zhang, Zhaoqing Zhu, Ming Yan, Jieping Ye, Jitao Sang

entry.summary: STAMP trains explicit memory in mobile GUI agents using controllable virtual environments where deterministic memory variables are programmatically injected into synthesized tasks, teaching agents what and when to memorize. It addresses long-horizon failures from limited context windows.

entry.title: Latent Terms: Dense Retrievers Contain Trivially Extractable BM25-ready Zipfian Vocabularies

author.name: Benjamin Clavi\'e and Sean Lee and Aamir Shakir and Makoto P. Kato

entry.summary: Shows that dense retrievers' embeddings can be trivially decomposed by sparse autoencoders into a Zipfian latent vocabulary directly usable for BM25 scoring, with no retrieval-specific training. The method matches or beats single-vector and SPLADE baselines, bridging dense and sparse retrieval interpretably.

entry.title: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Temporal Logit Observability for LLM Safety Failures

author.name: Junyoung Park, Sunghwan Park, Seongyong Ju, Jaewoo Lee

entry.summary: Introduces Temporal Logit Observability (TLO), a training-free diagnostic that tracks a compliance-refusal margin during decoding to distinguish jailbreaks that succeed for different reasons, going beyond binary attack success rate. Places model-attack conditions on a calibrated 2D plane.

entry.title: Verifiable Rewards Beyond Math and Code: Lightweight Corpus-Grounded Process Supervision for Factual Question Answering

author.name: Shicheng Fan, Haochang Hao, Dehai Min, Weihao Liu, Philip S. Yu, Lu Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes CorVer, a lightweight corpus-grounded process reward using Wikipedia co-occurrence statistics to provide sentence-level credit for factual QA RL, replacing expensive neural verifiers. Extends verifiable rewards beyond math and code to factual accuracy, especially for rare-entity facts.

entry.title: Dial HEALTHDIAL for Advice: A Multilingual and Multi-Parallel Spoken Dialogue Dataset for Knowledge-Grounded Information Seeking

author.name: Songbo Hu, Yinhong Liu, Ej Zhou, Evgeniia Razumovskaia, Xiaobin Wang, Alexander Fraser, Ivan Vuli\'c, Anna Korhonen

entry.summary: HEALTHDIAL is a large-scale multilingual, multi-parallel spoken dialogue dataset with 6,000 WHO-grounded information-seeking dialogues and 163 hours of speech across Arabic, Chinese, English, and Spanish, with rich speaker demographic annotations. It supports development of RAG-based spoken dialogue systems for health. The multilingual parallel design is the key contribution.

entry.title: LamPO: A Lambda Style Policy Optimization for Reasoning Language Models

author.name: Redacted by arXiv

entry.summary: LamPO is a lambda-style policy optimization for reasoning LLMs that replaces scalar group advantages (as in GRPO) with a pairwise decomposed advantage aggregating reward gaps within response groups, improving credit assignment under sparse outcome rewards. It targets cases where solutions differ only subtly. The pairwise advantage is the key contribution.

entry.title: Faithful Embeddings of Irregular and Asynchronous Data for Online Log-NCDEs

author.name: Benjamin Walker and Alexandre Bloch and Lingyi Yang and Sam Morley and Terry Lyons

entry.summary: This paper shows that the interpolation/imputation step in continuous-time models for irregular asynchronous data is unnecessary, proving that compact-set universality transfers from input to data space under continuous injective embeddings. It introduces a faithful embedding for online Log-NCDEs. A theoretical contribution from the established Lyons signature group.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Robust Rubric Rewards

author.name: Ya-Qi Yu, Hao Wang, Fangyu Hong, Xiangyang Qu, Gaojie Wu, Qiaoyu Luo, Nuo Xu, Huixin Wang, Wuheng Xu, Yongxin Liao, Zihao Chen, Haonan Li, Ziming Li, Dezhi Peng, Minghui Liao, Jihao Wu, Haoyu Ren, Dandan Tu

entry.summary: RLR3 extends RLVR to partially verifiable vision-language tasks by routing instance-specific rubrics through deterministic verifiers and LLM-as-judge paths for criterion-level verification. It improves rubric execution accuracy during online RL. Relevant for fine-grained multi-criteria supervision in multimodal RL.

entry.title: How LoRA Remembers? A Parametric Memory Law for LLM Finetuning

author.name: Ziwen Xu, Haiwen Hong, Linsong Yu, Benglei Cui, Longtao Huang, Hui Xue, Ningyu Zhang

entry.summary: This paper uses LoRA as a controlled probe to quantify exact parametric memory in LLM fine-tuning, introducing a Parametric Memory Law—a power law linking loss reduction to effective parameters and sequence length—and revealing a deterministic token-level phase transition. It clarifies capacity limits of LoRA-based knowledge updates. Useful scaling-law insight for continual knowledge editing.

entry.title: Veda: Scalable Video Diffusion via Distilled Sparse Attention

author.name: Shihao Han, Hao Yang, Xinting Hu, Xiaofeng Mei, Yi Jiang, Xiaojuan Qi

entry.summary: Veda is a distilled sparse attention framework for video diffusion that formulates tile selection as an explicit reconstruction problem from full attention, finding quality depends on mask-geometry alignment rather than sparsity ratio. It uses statistics-aware tile scoring and a hardware-efficient tile-skipping kernel for practical speedups. Relevant for scaling high-resolution long video generation.

entry.title: REST3D: Reconstructing Physically Stable 3D Scenes from a Single Image

author.name: Xiaoxuan Ma, Jiashun Wang, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Yehonathan Litman, Kris Kitani

entry.summary: Presents REST3D, a single-image 3D scene reconstruction framework that produces physically stable, simulation-ready scenes without object floating or penetration, while staying faithful to the input image. It targets the gap between geometric plausibility and physical consistency in casual-image-to-asset pipelines.

entry.title: YoCausal: How Far is Video Generation from World Model? A Causality Perspective

author.name: You-Zhe Xie, Yu-Hsuan Li, Jie-Ying Lee, Kaipeng Zhang, Yu-Lun Liu, Zhixiang Wang

entry.summary: Introduces YoCausal, a benchmark testing whether video diffusion models truly understand causality versus overfitting temporal statistics, using temporally reversed real videos as zero-cost counterfactuals inspired by the Violation-of-Expectation paradigm. It proposes a Reverse Surprise Index and a VLM-driven Causality Cognition Index for stratified evaluation.

entry.title: AdaState: Self-Evolving Anchors for Streaming Video Generation

author.name: Yusuf Dalva and Pinar Yanardag

entry.summary: Identifies that autoregressive video diffusion models are structurally over-anchored to the first frame's KV representation, which dominates attention and suppresses motion and scene evolution toward static consistency. AdaState replaces this static anchor with a self-evolving adaptive state to restore dynamics in streaming generation.

entry.title: DynaFLIP: Rethinking Robotics Perception via Tri-Modal-Dynamics Guided Representation

author.name: Jusuk Lee, Seungjae Lee, Jonghun Shin, Hoseong Jung, Sungha Kim, Daesol Cho, H. Jin Kim, Jia-Bin Huang, Furong Huang

entry.summary: Introduces DynaFLIP, a dynamics-aware multimodal pretraining framework that pushes motion understanding into the visual encoder using image-language-3D-flow triplets from human and robot videos. It aligns the three modalities by encouraging them to span a small simplex volume in a shared hyperspherical space, improving action-relevant perception for manipulation.

entry.title: Optimal Gap-Dependent Regret for Private Stochastic Decision-Theoretic Online Learning

author.name: Tommaso Cesari, Roberto Colomboni

entry.summary: This paper resolves a COLT open problem by giving an optimal gap-dependent regret algorithm for stochastic decision-theoretic online learning under pure differential privacy, with a horizon-free explicit bound matching the known lower bound. It settles a clean theoretical question in private online learning.

entry.title: Diffusion Models Are Statistically Optimal for Learning Low-Dimensional Multi-Modal Distributions

author.name: Jingda Wu, Changxiao Cai

entry.summary: This paper proves that score-based diffusion models are statistically optimal for learning distributions supported on unions of low-dimensional subspaces, achieving near-minimax sample complexity that scales with intrinsic dimension under subgaussian assumptions. It strengthens theoretical understanding of why diffusion models succeed on structured high-dimensional data.

entry.title: Reasoning with Sampling: Cutting at Decision Points

author.name: Felix Zhou and Anay Mehrotra and Quanquan C. Liu

entry.summary: This paper improves training-free reasoning by sampling from a sharpened power distribution of a base LLM, proposing to cut at decision points rather than uniformly random positions to mix more efficiently to the target distribution. It makes training-free reasoning elicitation more practical without RL post-training.

entry.title: Converted, Not Equivalent: Benchmarking Codebase Conversion via Observational Equivalence

author.name: Linxin Song, Jiefeng Chen, Yue Huang, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Chi Wang, Jieyu Zhao, Jinsung Yoon, Tomas Pfister

entry.summary: T2J-Bench reformulates codebase conversion evaluation as transfer under a fixed equivalence contract verified semantically (e.g., gradients, optimizer behavior) rather than shallow outcome checks. It exposes how coding agents over-trust local validation and declare false success.

entry.title: Embodied3DBench: Benchmarking Low-Level Embodied Spatial Intelligence of Vision Language Models

author.name: Jiyao Zhang, Mingxu Zhang, Yitong Peng, Haoxuan Liu, Chenshuo Wang, Yuxing Long, Haoyang Huang, Dongjiang Li, Nan Duan, Hui Shen, Hao Dong

entry.summary: Embodied3DBench is a robot-centric benchmark for low-level embodied spatial intelligence of vision-language models, with six task categories spanning spatial structure understanding and interaction-oriented perception across 21k QA pairs. Evaluating 13 SOTA models reveals significant gaps in 3D embodied reasoning.

entry.title: GeRaF: Neural Geometry Reconstruction from Radio Frequency Signals

author.name: Jiachen Lu, Hailan Shanbhag, Haitham Al Hassanieh

entry.summary: GeRaF is presented as the first neural implicit method for near-range 3D geometry reconstruction from radio-frequency signals, introducing filter-based rendering, a physics-based RF volumetric rendering pipeline, and lensless sampling to handle RF's low resolution and specular reflections. It enables seeing through occlusions.

entry.title: PRO-CUA: Process-Reward Optimization for Computer Use Agents

author.name: Yifei He, Rui Yang, Hao Bai, Tong Zhang, Han Zhao

entry.summary: PRO-CUA is a process-reward optimization framework for computer-use agents that uses iterative step-level reinforcement learning, decoupling on-policy environment interaction from policy optimization to overcome sparse rewards and credit-assignment problems in long-horizon GUI tasks. It addresses imitation bottlenecks in filtered behavior cloning.

entry.title: The Confidence Shortcut: A Reasoning Failure Mode of Masked Diffusion Models

author.name: Dueun Kim, Albert No

entry.summary: This paper identifies a reasoning failure of masked diffusion language models where confidence-based decoding prematurely commits to locally easy tokens before resolving long-range dependencies, producing high-confidence errors, and shows confidence-aligned training entrenches the misalignment. It uses multi-digit addition as a concrete probe.

entry.title: When RL Suppresses Its Own Vocabulary: Recovering Reasoning Diversity in Puzzle-to-Math Transfer

author.name: Mayug Maniparambil, Arjun Karuvally, Terrence Sejnowski, Fergal Reid

entry.summary: This paper studies cross-domain RLVR transfer in a 7B model post-trained only on constraint-satisfaction puzzles, introducing a primitive-level framework that segments chain-of-thought into motifs to track how puzzle SFT induces a reasoning vocabulary that transfers to math. It also shows RL can suppress reasoning diversity and proposes recovering it.

entry.title: Guidance Contrastive Token Credit Assignment for Discrete Policy Optimization

author.name: Shufan Li, Konstantinos Kallidromitis, Akash Gokul Yusuke Kato, Kazuki Kozuka, Aditya Grover

entry.summary: GCPO enables per-token credit assignment in group-advantage RL methods like GRPO/DAPO by contrasting model predictions under positive versus negative prompts, assigning token-level advantages proportional to that difference rather than broadcasting uniform sample-level rewards. It improves fine-grained learning for math reasoning and text-to-image generation.

entry.title: BenchTrace: A Benchmark for Testing Reflection Ability and Controlled Evolution in LLM Agents

author.name: Jiahao Huang, Fei Cheng, Junfeng Jiang, Zefan Yu, Akiko Aizawa

entry.summary: BenchTrace is a benchmark of 1,821 annotated episodes for evaluating self-evolving agents' reflection quality and controlled evolution, separating reflection evaluation from evolution behavior. It addresses a real gap since existing evaluations only measure task scores rather than reflection ability.

entry.title: Compute Allocation in Evolutionary Search: From Depth-Breadth to Multi-Armed Bandits

author.name: Sixue Xing, Haoyu He, Kerui Wu, Zhuo Yang, Haozheng Luo, Tianfan Fu, Aarthy Nagarajan

entry.summary: Analyzes compute allocation in LLM-guided evolutionary search, identifying a fitness-compute envelope and depth-breadth scaling regularities, then proposes BaSE, a multi-armed bandit for allocating LLM calls. It improves reliability of single-run results in Evolve systems.

entry.title: Code-QA-Bench: Separating Code Reasoning from Documentation Memorization in Repository-Level QA

author.name: Jun Zhang, JianYing Qu, Hanwen Du, Zhongkai Sun, Yehua Yang, Qiao Zhao

entry.summary: Code-QA-Bench is an automated framework synthesizing repository-level code-understanding benchmarks that separate genuine code reasoning from documentation recall and memorization via an answer-first pipeline and three-condition design. It quantifies documentation utility and memorization.

entry.title: Accommodation Goes Both Ways: Studying Linguistic Convergence Between Humans and Language Models

author.name: Terra Blevins

entry.summary: A large-scale study on WildChat showing LLMs strongly overconverge toward user linguistic style across eight languages while humans converge at normal human-human rates, revealing asymmetric accommodation. It informs how AI may shape human language behavior.

entry.title: Entropy-KL Divergence-based Token Masking: A Novel Approach for Selective Fine-tuning of Large Language Models

author.name: Qi Liu, Mingdi Sun, Yongyi He, Zhi Zheng, Tong Xu, Yi Zheng, Zhefeng Wang, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes entropy-KL-divergence token masking for selective SFT, arguing low-data SFT should activate task-relevant capabilities rather than memorize, to prevent distribution shift that hurts subsequent RL exploration. It improves the SFT-then-RL post-training pipeline.

entry.title: FoRA: Fisher-orthogonal Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Juneyoung Park, Seongbae Lee, Han-Sang Lee, Kyuho Lee, Minjae Kim, Seungheon Hyeon, Kiduk Kwon, Seongwan Kim, Jaeho Lee

entry.summary: FoRA is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that reduces adapted layers rather than rank, selecting task-informative layers via a cheap Fisher score and training on the Stiefel manifold to preserve orthonormality. It outperforms LoRA and DoRA at half the parameter budget.

entry.title: FreeForm: Reduced-Order Deformable Simulation from Particle-Based Skinning Eigenmodes

author.name: Donglai Xiang, Vismay Modi, Rishit Dagli, Ty Trusty, Gilles Daviet, Anka He Chen, Nicholas Sharp, David I.W. Levin

entry.summary: FreeForm presents mesh-free reduced-order deformable simulation using a Reproducing Kernel Particle Method to build skinning eigenmodes from elastic-energy Hessians, achieving 40x training speedup over neural-field methods with lower error. It avoids meshing and per-shape optimization challenges.

entry.title: Draft-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Draft Models

author.name: Haodi Lei, Yafy Li, Haoran Zhang, Shunkai Zhang, Qianjia Cheng, Xiaoye Qu, Ganqu Cui, Bowen Zhou, Ning Ding, Yun Luo, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: Draft-OPD applies on-policy distillation to speculative decoding draft models, addressing the offline-to-inference mismatch where SFT-trained drafters plateau because they are evaluated on their own proposed states. It aims to extend acceptance length beyond SFT limits.

entry.title: LiteCoder-Terminal: Scaling Long-Horizon Terminal Environments for Learning Language Agents

author.name: Xiaoxuan Peng, Kaiqi Zhang, Xinyu Lu, Boxi Cao, Yaojie Lu, Hongyu Lin, Xianpei Han, Le Sun

entry.summary: Introduces LiteCoder-Terminal-Gen, a zero-dependency synthesis pipeline that autonomously generates verifiable terminal training environments, yielding 11k expert trajectories and 602 RL environments for training language agents. Addresses reliance on scraped repositories for agent training.

entry.title: Predicting Causal Effects from Natural Language Queries using Structured Representations

author.name: Giuliano Martinelli, Piriyakorn Piriyatamwong, Abelardo Carlos Martinez Lorenzo, Jasmin Baier, Riccardo Orlando, Satvik Garg, Sharif Kazemi, Linxi Wang, Arianna Legovini, Samuel Fraiberger

entry.summary: Introduces Query2Effect, a 72,000-question benchmark aligning natural language queries with experiment descriptions to test whether LLMs can forecast causal effect sizes from existing evidence. Varies query specificity across implicitness, abstraction, and ambiguity.

entry.title: Scaling Laws for Agent Harnesses via Effective Feedback Compute

author.name: Xuanliang Zhang, Dingzirui Wang, Keyan Xu, Qingfu Zhu, Wanxiang Che

entry.summary: Proposes Effective Feedback Compute (EFC), a trace-level scaling coordinate that credits only informative, valid, non-redundant, retained feedback when analyzing agent harness performance. It normalizes by task demand for cross-task comparison. This offers a more meaningful way to study test-time scaling in agents.

entry.title: Understanding Safety-Sensitive Expert Behavior in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs

author.name: Zhibo Zhang, Yuxi Li, Zhen Ouyang, Ling Shi, Kailong Wang

entry.summary: Investigates how safety alignment interacts with expert routing in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs, finding routing is largely topic-driven rather than refusal-specialized, and that safety can be altered while preserving routing. It introduces RASET, a red-teaming framework localizing safety in few experts. Relevant for MoE safety and robustness understanding.

entry.title: AfriScience-MT: Towards Decolonizing Science in Africa through Text Translation

author.name: Idris Abdulmumin, Tajuddeen Gwadabe, Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhammad, David Ifeoluwa Adelani, Nomonde Khalo, Ibrahim Said Ahmad, Abiodun Modupe, Anina Mumm, Sibusiso Biyela, Michelle Rabie, Johanna Havemann, Marek Rei, Jade Abbott, Vukosi Marivate

entry.summary: AfriScience-MT introduces a parallel corpus for six African languages across 11 scientific domains, created by professional translators who coined new scientific terms where none existed, and benchmarks MT systems and LLMs. It addresses the colonial-language dominance limiting African scientific access. An impactful low-resource and equity-focused contribution.

entry.title: AgentDoG 1.5: A Lightweight and Scalable Alignment Framework for AI Agent Safety and Security

author.name: Dongrui Liu, Yu Li, Zhonghao Yang, Peng Wang, Guanxu Chen, Yuejin Xie, Qinghua Mao, Wanying Qu, Yanxu Zhu, Tianyi Zhou, Leitao Yuan, Zhijie Zheng, Qihao Lin, Yimin Wang, Haoyu Luo, Shuai Shao, Chen Qian, Qingyu Liu, Ling Tang, Ruiyang Qin, Qihan Ren, Junxiao Yang, Kun Wang, Zhiheng Xi, Linfeng Zhang, Ranjie Duan, Bo Zhang, Wenjie Wang, Wen Shen, Qiaosheng Zhang, Yan Teng, Chaochao Lu, Rui Mei, Man Li, Jialing Tao, Xi Lin, Tianhang Zheng, Yong Liu, Quanshi Zhang, Lei Zhu, Xingjun Ma, Junhua Liu, Hui Xue, Xiaoxiang Zuo, Xiangnan He, Chao Shen, Xianglong Liu, Minlie Huang, Jing Shao, Xia Hu

entry.summary: AgentDoG 1.5 is a lightweight, scalable agent safety alignment framework updating the safety taxonomy for emergent open-world agent risks and using a taxonomy-guided data engine with influence-function purification to train small (0.8B-8B) guard models from ~1k samples, matching leading closed-source models. It targets practical agent deployment safety. A large-collaboration safety contribution.

entry.title: Latent Performance Profiling of Large Language Models

author.name: Tanmoy Chakraborty, Ayan Sengupta, Suparna Bhattacharya, Partha Pratim Chakrabarti, Amlan Chakrabarti, Supratik Chakraborty, Partha Pratim Das, Lipika Dey, Richa Singh and Mayank Vatsa

entry.summary: This position-and-method paper advocates moving beyond accuracy-centric benchmarks toward state-centered intrinsic assessment of LLMs, introducing Latent Performance Profiling to characterize how models process information and calibrate uncertainty. It addresses contamination and reliability shortcomings of leaderboards. The authors are an established group.

entry.title: RAISE: RAG Design as an Architecture Search Problem

author.name: Zhen Chen, Yibing Liu, Weihao Xie, Yu Liang, Peilin Chen, Shiqi Wang

entry.summary: RAISE reframes RAG pipeline design as an architecture search problem, providing a standardized framework and benchmark with 13 search algorithms across seven datasets. It aims to replace heuristic RAG configuration with systematic, reproducible optimization. This addresses reproducibility concerns in applied RAG.

entry.title: Towards Consistent Video Geometry Estimation

author.name: Zhu Yu, Jingnan Gao, Runmin Zhang, Lingteng Qiu, Zhengyi Zhao, Rui Peng, Yichao Yan, Kejie Qiu, Siyu Zhu, Si-Yuan Cao, Hui-Liang Shen

entry.summary: ViGeo is a feed-forward foundation model recovering spatially dense and temporally consistent geometry from video using a plain transformer with dynamic chunking attention that adapts between bidirectional and causal contexts at test time. It supports streaming, full-sequence, and long-video inference in one model. A completion-based data refinement framework improves supervision.

entry.title: PokerSkill: LLMs Can Play Expert-Level Poker without Training or Solvers

author.name: Boning Li and Baoxiang Wang and Longbo Huang

entry.summary: PokerSkill is a training-free, solver-free framework that gives LLMs expert-level poker play via a layered rule-based skill library accessed through a deterministic context engine that retrieves only relevant skill fragments. It bridges the gap between LLM poker knowledge and equilibrium-solver-level play without millions of core-hours. The skill-grounding interface is the key idea.

entry.title: How Reliable Are AI Attackers Against a Fixed Vulnerable Target? A 400-Run Empirical Study of LLM Penetration Testing Consistency

author.name: Galip Tolga Erdem

entry.summary: This empirical study runs 400 autonomous LLM penetration-testing trials (four models, 100 each) against an identical vulnerable honeypot to measure offensive behavior consistency. It finds no surviving content refusals and documents infrastructure-driven failures like Anthropic capacity errors truncating runs. It provides first-of-kind reliability measurement of AI attackers.

entry.title: Chess-World-Model: A 10M-Game Benchmark for Exact State Tracking from Chess Move Sequences

author.name: Benjamin Walker and Terry Lyons

entry.summary: Chess-World-Model is a 10-million-game benchmark testing whether models can exactly track board state from legal move sequences, including an out-of-distribution random-legal-play split to distinguish learned transition rules from human-position shortcuts. It provides a realistic, structured state-tracking test. It builds on prior findings that Transformers struggle with state tracking.

entry.title: SEAL: Can Saturated Benchmarks Be Revived by LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge?

author.name: Jiamin Chen, Yidi Wu, Qiexiang Wang, Qianben Chen, Yuchen Li, Yansen Zhang, Xiaokun Zhang, Wangchunshu Zhou, Chen Ma

entry.summary: SEAL is a self-improving evaluation protocol that revives saturated benchmarks via LLM-as-a-meta-judge, using single-elimination matches scored with task-level principles plus self-improving checklist criteria to extract latent ranking signal. It avoids building harder benchmarks by improving evaluation over existing outputs. It targets benchmark saturation among frontier models.

entry.title: PARCEL: Pool-Anchored Resampling with Conditioned Elastic Queries for Efficient Vision-Language Understanding

author.name: Selim Kuzucu, Alessio Tonioni, Vasile Lup, Bernt Schiele, Federico Tombari, Muhammad Ferjad Naeem

entry.summary: PARCEL combines pool-anchored resampling with conditioned elastic queries to compress visual tokens in large vision-language models across multiple budgets, resolving the conflict between spatial-only pooling (aliasing) and query-only resampling (poor grounding). It enables a single model to run at multiple token budgets under aggressive compression. The hybrid representation is the contribution. Authors are from Google and MPI.

entry.title: Overcoming Forgetting in LLM Fine-Tuning with Evolution Strategies

author.name: Kajetan Schweighofer, Conor F. Hayes, Roberto Dailey, Risto Miikkulainen, Xin Qiu

entry.summary: This paper shows that prior-task forgetting in evolution-strategies LLM fine-tuning is better characterized as recoverable performance drift than irreversible forgetting, and that it also arises in RL fine-tuning, attributing it to random-walk behavior in weakly constrained directions. It analyzes when and why drift occurs. Authors include Miikkulainen.

entry.title: RL2ML: Finite-Rollout Surrogate Objectives from Reinforcement Learning to Maximum Likelihood

author.name: Yifu Zheng

entry.summary: RL2ML develops a family of finite-rollout surrogate objectives with a closed-form, exactly unbiased gradient estimator that continuously connects standard RL, maximum-likelihood-like training, and beyond-MLE objectives under a fixed rollout budget. It introduces a group-level update scale revealing subcritical-supercritical update regimes. It clarifies the conflation between expected objectives and finite-rollout update geometry in RLVR.

entry.title: BioRefusalAudit: Auditing Biosecurity Refusal Depth Using General and Domain-Fine-Tuned Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Caleb DeLeeuw

entry.summary: This work audits whether LLM refusals on biosecurity-hazardous prompts are structurally robust or collapse under prompt reformatting, length caps, and formatting changes, testing five small models with sparse autoencoders. It finds refusals are brittle and inconsistent, with some models never genuinely refusing and others over-refusing benign biology. This matters for understanding the fragility of safety guardrails.

entry.title: HPO: Hysteretic Policy Optimization for Stable and Efficient Training under Sparse-Reward Regime

author.name: Mohamed Sana, Nicola Piovesan, Antonio De Domenico, Fadhel Ayed, Haozhe Zhang

entry.summary: HPO modifies GRPO-style RL for sparse verifiable rewards by reducing the weight of negative-advantage updates and using mean-length normalization, addressing a failure where early updates are dominated by negative advantages. Adaptive HPO sets the hysteretic weight from batch-level statistics, removing manual tuning. A practical RL training stability improvement.

entry.title: BORA: Bridging Offline Reinforcement Learning and Online Residual Adaptation for Real-World Dexterous VLA Models

author.name: Zhongxi Chen, Yifan Han, Yanming Shao, Huanming Liu, Congsheng Xu, Xiaoyu Chen, Yao Mu, Wenzhao Lian

entry.summary: BORA is an offline-to-online RL post-training framework for real-world dexterous vision-language-action models, building a critic in the offline phase and adding online residual adaptation to handle high-dimensional hand control and compounding errors safely. It addresses temporal inconsistency, sample inefficiency, and hardware risk. Relevant for practical dexterous robot manipulation.

entry.title: Anti Mode-Collapse in Mean-Field Transformer via Auxiliary Variables

author.name: Masaaki Imaizumi, Masanori Koyama, Noboru Isobe, Kohei Hayashi

entry.summary: This theoretical paper uses a mean-field transformer model to show that auxiliary variables like positional encoding act as a counterforce against self-attention mode collapse, where token distributions degenerate to a single point over many layers. It reconciles a known theoretical prediction with practical observations. A theory contribution on transformer dynamics.

entry.title: GRASP: Plan-Guided Graph Retrieval with Adaptive Fusion and Reranking on Semi-Structured Knowledge Bases

author.name: Yicheng Tao, Yiqun Wang, Xiangchen Song, Xin Luo, Kai Liu, Jie Liu

entry.summary: GRASP is a three-stage retrieval framework for semi-structured knowledge bases combining plan-based graph retrieval, plan-conditioned dense fusion, and a fine-tuned reranker. It substantially advances STaRK benchmarks, lifting average Hit@1 from 62.0 to 73.9. Relevant for product, academic, and precision-medicine search.

entry.title: CommunityFact: A Dynamic, Multilingual, Multi-domain Benchmark for Misinformation Detection in the Wild

author.name: Sahajpreet Singh, Insyirah Mujtahid, Min-Yen Kan, Kokil Jaidka

entry.summary: CommunityFact is a refreshable, multilingual, multi-domain benchmark for misinformation detection with 15,992 standalone claims across five languages, evaluating ten LLMs under thinking and web-search settings. It finds web access yields the largest gains but web-enabled source selection is misaligned with human Community Notes raters. Important for evaluating real-world fact-checking.

entry.title: MIRA: Mid-training Rubric Anchoring for Source-Aware Data Selection

author.name: Haowen Wang, Yaxin Du, Jian Yang, Jiajun Wu, Shukai Liu, Yuxuan Zhang, Pingjie Wang, Siheng Chen, Tuney Zheng, Ming Zhou, and Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: MIRA is a source-aware mid-training data selection framework using rubric anchoring to provide source-adaptive semantic criteria at near-pretraining scale, addressing the mismatch where existing methods assume fixed rubrics or standardized formats. It targets the distinct data selection problem of the mid-training stage. Relevant for modern LLM development pipelines.

entry.title: In-Context Reward Adaptation for Robust Preference Modeling

author.name: Zhenyu Sun, Zheng Xu, Ermin Wei

entry.summary: In-Context Reward Adaptation is a transformer-based framework that models diverse, unseen human preferences on the fly using in-context learning, adaptively inferring reward structure without costly retraining—addressing the brittleness of static single reward models in RLHF. It generalizes beyond fixed known preference domains. Relevant for robust pluralistic preference modeling.

entry.title: Demystifying Data Organization for Enhanced LLM Training

author.name: Yalun Dai, Yangyu Huang, Tongshen Yang, Yonghan Wang, Xin Zhang, Wenshan Wu, Qihao Zhao, Hao Li, Yuanyuan Gao, Kim-Hui Yap, Scarlett Li

entry.summary: Studies how the ordering/organization of training data (not just selection) affects single-epoch LLM pretraining, reusing precomputed sample scores to avoid extra compute. It formalizes four guidelines (boundary sharpening, cyclic scheduling, curriculum continuity, local diversity) and proposes two new data ordering methods.

entry.title: Uncertainty-driven 3D Gaussian Splatting Active Mapping via Anisotropic Visibility Field

author.name: Shangjie Xue, Jesse Dill, Dhruv Ahuja, Frank Dellaert, Panagiotis Tsiotras, Danfei Xu

entry.summary: Presents GAVIS, which quantifies uncertainty in 3D Gaussian Splatting by modeling each particle's anisotropic visibility with respect to training views using spherical harmonics, integrated into a Bayesian rasterizer for real-time (200 FPS) uncertainty estimates. This enables information-gain-driven active mapping.

entry.title: Physics Is All You Need? A Case Study in Physicist-Supervised AI Development of Scientific Software

author.name: Nhat-Minh Nguyen

entry.summary: A single-subject case study of a physicist supervising an AI coding agent (Claude Code with Sonnet/Opus) over 12 days to build a differentiable perturbation-theory module, classifying 15 supervision events by intervention level. It finds the agent autonomously fixed most issues but failed on three where it mistook symptom reduction for root-cause fixes that evaded oracle tests.

entry.title: How far behind are open models?

author.name: Håvard Tveit Ihle

entry.summary: Quantifies the capability gap between open-weight and closed-frontier models using 17 benchmarks (~110 datapoints), finding open models lag roughly 8-10 months on private benchmarks and 4-6 months on public ones. It also finds the gap was smallest around DeepSeek R1 (Jan 2025) and has since been growing, with code and data released for reproducibility.

entry.title: Attention as In-Context Empirical Bayes: A Two-Stage View via Particle Dynamics

author.name: Matthew Smart, Soumya Ganguly, Nilava Metya, Alexandre V. Morozov, Anirvan M. Sengupta

entry.summary: This paper interprets minimal attention-only transformers as performing two-stage empirical Bayes inference, where attention computes kernel-weighted posterior means, depth refines via particle dynamics, and skip connections carry the noisy query. It offers a statistical-physics-flavored theory of in-context denoising without explicit noise schedules.

entry.title: Indexing the Unreadable: LLM-Native Recursive Construction and Search of Service Taxonomies

author.name: Wei Zheng, Yang Yan, Yiyang Shao, Jinyang Li, Zeze Chang, Yukuang Jia, Qiming Mao, Chihyung Wang, Jingbin Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-native recursive method to construct and search service taxonomies for the Internet of Agents, addressing context-window limits and lost-in-the-middle problems when discovering thousands of MCP/A2A services. It frames service discovery as a context-management problem.

entry.title: ConMoE: Expert-Pool Consolidation via Prototype Reassignment for MoE Compression

author.name: Yilun Yao, Jiaming Pan, Elsie Dai, Peizhuang Cong, Yaoming Li, and Tong Yang

entry.summary: ConMoE compresses Mixture-of-Experts models by consolidating the expert pool into reusable prototypes and deterministically remapping expert references, preserving the router interface without training. It reduces memory cost of serving all experts.

entry.title: Offloading Score: Measuring AI Reliance Through Counterfactual Workflows

author.name: Vishakh Padmakumar, Lujain Ibrahim, Zora Zhiruo Wang, Jennifer Wang, Q. Vera Liao, Diyi Yang

entry.summary: Introduces an offloading score that quantifies how much cognitive effort users delegate to AI tools by simulating a counterfactual workflow without the tool and measuring steps saved. It is validated through metric checks and a controlled developer study under varied time pressure.

entry.title: GRASP: Gated Regression-Aware Skill Proposer for Self-Improving LLM Agents

author.name: Johannes Moll, Jean-Philippe Corbeil, Jiazhen Pan, Martin Hadamitzky, Daniel Rueckert, Lisa Adams, Keno Bressem

entry.summary: Proposes GRASP, a self-improving agent method that treats improvement as gated edits to a bounded skill library, admitting new skills only if they yield net improvement on a held-out probe under a hard regression budget. Evaluated on FHIR-based clinical benchmarks across five base models including GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek V4 Flash.

entry.title: When Do Graph Foundation Models Transfer? A Data-Centric Theory

author.name: Jiajun Zhu, Ying Chen, Peihao Wang, Yixuan He, Pan Li, Aditya Akella, Zhangyang Wang

entry.summary: Develops a data-centric theory for when graph foundation models transfer, using a graphon limit to decompose cross-domain output shift into finite-sample approximation terms and an intrinsic relabeling-invariant domain discrepancy, with positional-encoding stability as a key ingredient. It explains uneven and negative transfer. A theoretical advance for graph foundation models.

entry.title: Convergence Theory for Iterative LLM-Based Neural Architecture Search: A Parametric Cross-Entropy Framework with Closed-Form Proxy Reliability

author.name: Santosh Premi Adhikari, Radu Timofte, Dmitry Ignatov

entry.summary: This paper develops a convergence theory for iterative LLM-based neural architecture search by modeling it as a parametric cross-entropy method over executable programs, proving six results including monotonic quality improvement and geometric convergence of elite-set probability. It also shows delta-based generation outperforms full-code generation. It provides rare formal grounding for LLM-driven NAS.

entry.title: Meta-Cognitive Memory Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Ziyan Liu, Zhezheng Hao, Yeqiu Chen, Hong Wang, Jingren Hou, Ruiyi Ding, Yongkang Yang, Wence Ji, Wei Xia, Feng Liu

entry.summary: This paper argues memory-augmented LLM agents should optimize the clarity of beliefs induced by intermediate summaries rather than only trajectory-level success, introducing Belief Entropy as a self-supervised signal to localize where recursive summarization degrades. It addresses belief deviation that derails long-horizon reasoning. Meta-cognitive memory policy optimization is the framework.

entry.title: MarginGate: Sparse Margin-Triggered Verification for Batch-Invariant LLM Inference

author.name: Kexin Chu and Yang Zhou and Wei Zhang

entry.summary: MarginGate addresses non-reproducibility in temperature-zero BF16 LLM inference where the same request yields different tokens alone versus in a batch. It shows batch-induced token flips are sparse (0.3-1.3%) and predictable from low top-1/top-2 logit margins, applying expensive verification only to risky tokens. A practical efficiency-reproducibility contribution.

entry.title: Same Evidence, Different Answers: Canonical-Context On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Language Models

author.name: Zizhuo Lin, Quanling Liu, Jinsheng Quan, Chao Zhang, Yifan Zhu, Xing Shi, Jingtao Xu, Zhihui Li, and Yawei Luo

entry.summary: CCOPD addresses self-anchored drift, where LLMs reach different answers when the same evidence is revealed gradually across turns versus in one prompt. It uses on-policy distillation with a frozen full-prompt teacher guiding a student that receives evidence incrementally. Relevant for robust multi-turn conversational reasoning.

entry.title: PhyGenHOI: Physically-Aware 4D Generation of Dynamic Human-Object Interactions

author.name: Omer Benishu, Gal Fiebelman, Sagie Benaim

entry.summary: PhyGenHOI generates physically accurate and visually faithful 4D human-object interactions from a static 3D human and object as Gaussian Splats, coupling a Motion Diffusion Model for the human with Material Point Method simulation for the object via a unified differentiable Gaussian representation. It synthesizes dynamic actions like punching or kicking from text. A novel physics-aware 4D generation contribution.

entry.title: Conf-Gen: Conformal Uncertainty Quantification for Generative Models

author.name: Gabriel Loaiza-Ganem, Kevin Zhang, Wei Cui, Marc T. Law, Kin Kwan Leung

entry.summary: Conf-Gen adapts conformal risk control to generative models like LLMs and image generators, unifying prior conformal-for-LLM efforts and extending distribution-free uncertainty guarantees to new generative domains. It matters because mainstream conformal methods do not directly apply to unsupervised generation.

entry.title: On the Optimizer Dependence of Neural Scaling Laws

author.name: Vansh Ramani, Shourya Vir Jain

entry.summary: This work presents empirical evidence that the neural scaling-law exponent alpha is not fixed by architecture and data but depends systematically on the optimizer, with preconditioned methods yielding steeper scaling in random-feature regression. It challenges the common treatment of scaling exponents as constants.

entry.title: Conformal Certification of Reasoning Trace Prefixes

author.name: Matt Y. Cheung, Ashok Veeraraghavan, Hanjie Chen, Guha Balakrishnan

entry.summary: CROP provides a verifier-agnostic conformal calibration procedure that certifies the longest clean prefix of an LLM reasoning trace below a calibrated step-risk threshold, routing the uncertified suffix for review. It gives statistical guarantees on the retainable proportion of a reasoning chain rather than the whole answer.

entry.title: Spectral Guidance for Flexible and Efficient Control of Diffusion Models

author.name: Gabriel Moreira, Manuel Marques, Jo\~ao Paulo Costeira, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: Introduces Spectral Guidance, a framework that controls diffusion models by learning the singular functions of a conditional expectation operator and projecting arbitrary guidance signals onto the sampling trajectory. It enables stable, high-fidelity training-free control, reportedly improving conditional accuracy on CIFAR-10 by 37 points over the strongest training-free baseline.

entry.title: Reasoning that Travels: Dissecting How Chain-of-Thought Transfers Across Models

author.name: Xinyuan Cheng, Beiduo Chen, Philipp Mondorf, Barbara Plank

entry.summary: Studies cross-model chain-of-thought transfer using a controlled provider-receiver framework that compares force-answer with free-generation given increasingly longer reasoning-trace prefixes. It finds full traces often transfer but prefix trajectories behave differently, dissecting how provided CoT contributes to a receiver's answer.

entry.title: AIRGuard: Guarding Agent Actions with Runtime Authority Control

author.name: Suliu Qin, Haomin Zhuang, Yujun Zhou, Yufei Han, Xiangliang Zhang

entry.summary: Presents AIRGuard, a runtime guard that enforces least privilege as action-time authorization for tool-using agents, identifying authority confusion (untrusted context steering authorized actions) as a distinct failure mode from jailbreaks. It normalizes heterogeneous tool calls and tracks source and target trust to control side effects.

entry.title: Optimal Rates for Differentially Private Hypothesis Testing with E-values

author.name: Ben Jacobsen, Tomas Gonzales, Gavin Brown, Kassem Fawaz, Aaditya Ramdas

entry.summary: Characterizes the maximum achievable e-power for differentially private hypothesis testing between two distributions, providing an algorithm that matches the optimal rate and matching bounds on stopping times in the sequential setting. It connects anytime-valid inference via e-values with differential privacy guarantees.

entry.title: A Training-Time Diagnostic for Generalization via the Log-Alignment Ratio

author.name: Ali Shehper, Ashish Vaswani

entry.summary: Studies the log-alignment ratio (LAR), a measure of parameter-activation alignment, as a training-time diagnostic for generalization. It shows unembedding LAR tracks the memorization-to-generalization transition in grokking and the generalization gap in 3B-parameter pretraining.

entry.title: The Hamilton-Jacobi Theory of Deep Learning

author.name: Jose Marie Antonio Mi\~noza, Erika Fille T. Legara, Christopher P. Monterola

entry.summary: Identifies training a neural network exactly with a search through viscous Hamilton-Jacobi initial-value problems, where gradient steps select initial data and inference evaluates the Hopf-Cole solution. It shows residual networks, transformers, and recurrent architectures discretize the same class of HJ equations under a unifying deformation parameter.

entry.title: Label-Free Reinforcement Learning via Cross-Model Entropy

author.name: Matt Gorbett, Hossein Shirazi

entry.summary: Proposes Cross-Model Entropy (CME), a label-free RL reward signal defined as the mean log-likelihood of a generator's response under a separate verifier model, avoiding both ground-truth verifiers and human preference labels. It aims to mitigate the self-reinforcement of errors seen in self-referential label-free methods.

entry.title: Adopt $\neq$ Adapt: Longitudinal Analyses of LLM Conversations in the Wild

author.name: Rebecca M. M. Hicke, Kiran Tomlinson

entry.summary: Conducts a longitudinal analysis of how individual users change LLM behavior over time using ~12,000 Bing Copilot users compared with WildChat data, finding that while population-level trends exist, individual habits are overwhelmingly sticky. It also shows more active users have more successful, complex, professionally oriented conversations.

entry.title: Differentiable Belief-based Opponent Shaping

author.name: Aarav G Sane, Karthik Sivachandran, Rohan Paleja

entry.summary: D-BOS introduces a differentiable opponent-shaping method that treats other agents' beliefs as the manipulation target by differentiating through k-step softmax-Bayes belief dynamics, rather than relying on hard-coded deception objectives. It bridges opponent shaping and belief manipulation in multi-agent RL.

entry.title: Same Question, Different Source, Different Answer: Auditing Source-Dependence in Medical Multi-Source RAG

author.name: Yubo Li, Rema Padman, Ramayya Krishnan

entry.summary: This work audits source-dependence in multi-source medical RAG, showing systems give different answers depending on which institutional source is retrieved when sources disagree. It releases TransplantQA and a hierarchical retrieval/audit strategy, arguing source-dependence is a missing axis of NLP evaluation.

entry.title: OISD: On-Policy Internal Self-Distillation of Language Models

author.name: Xinyu Liu, Darryl Cherian Jacob, Yang Zhou, Jindong Wang, Pan He

entry.summary: OISD introduces on-policy internal self-distillation, where during GRPO RL post-training the final layer acts as a detached teacher to guide intermediate layers via logit alignment, transferring predictive reasoning signals into intermediate representations. It improves reasoning beyond sparse outcome rewards.

entry.title: Beyond Consensus: Trace-Level Synthesis in Mixture of Agents

author.name: Shreyas Fadnavis, Praitayini Kanakaraj, Felix Wyss

entry.summary: This paper shows that an LLM aggregator reading full reasoning traces from multiple agents recovers correct solutions even when agents unanimously agree, an aggregation paradox that majority voting cannot capture. It proposes Self-Consistent Mixture of Agents leveraging trace-level complementarity.

entry.title: Influence-Guided Symbolic Regression: Scientific Discovery via LLM-Driven Equation Search with Granular Feedback

author.name: Evgeny S. Saveliev, Samuel Holt, Nabeel Seedat, David L. Bentley, Jim Weatherall, Mihaela van der Schaar

entry.summary: Influence-Guided Symbolic Regression frames equation discovery as an LLM generating candidate basis functions evaluated with granular per-term influence scores rather than coarse scalar metrics, identifying which equation components drive performance or error. It improves LLM-driven scientific discovery efficiency.

entry.title: Tailoring the Curriculum: Student-Centered Reasoning Distillation via Dynamic Data-Model Compatibility

author.name: Jiahao Huang, Fei Cheng, Junfeng Jiang, Akiko Aizawa

entry.summary: Introduces a Data-Model Compatibility metric to select reasoning-distillation training data tailored to a specific student model, jointly weighing data quality, difficulty, and student capability. It improves distillation outcomes and offers a principled, student-centered curriculum approach.

entry.title: DenseSteer: Steering Small Language Models towards Dense Math Reasoning

author.name: Yang Ouyang, Shuhang Lin, and Jung-Eun Kim

entry.summary: DenseSteer is a training-free inference-time steering method that pushes small models toward dense reasoning (fewer steps, higher information density), improving math reasoning without increasing token-level loss. It exploits an empirical link between reasoning proficiency and density.

entry.title: DynSess: Dynamic Session-Level Evaluation and Optimization Framework for Role-Playing Agents

author.name: Rongsheng Zhang, Jiji Tang, Junnan Ren, Zuyi Bao, Weijie Chen, Ruofan Hu, Zhou Zhao, Tangjie Lv, Yan Zhang

entry.summary: DynSess is a session-level evaluation and optimization framework for role-playing agents, scoring full dialogue sessions and training characters via lookahead search with off-policy and on-policy RL variants. It addresses the gap left by turn-level methods.

entry.title: Diagnosing Harmful Continuation in Answer-Correct Long-CoT Training Traces

author.name: Chen He, Yuhao Wu, Lei Wang, Wenxuan Zhang, Fumin Shen

entry.summary: Identifies harmful post-conclusion continuation in answer-correct long chain-of-thought training traces and shows that deleting these continuations improves SFT outcomes for reasoning models. It offers a simple data-cleaning insight for reasoning SFT.

entry.title: EvoGM: Learning to Merge LLMs via Evolutionary Generative Optimization

author.name: Tao Jiang, Xinmeng Yu, Chenhao Yi, Yiling Wu, Yan Li, Ran Cheng, Dongmei Jiang, Jianguo Zhang

entry.summary: EvoGM uses a dual-generator architecture with cycle-consistent learning and winner-loser pairs to learn merging coefficients for LLM model merging, replacing hand-crafted evolutionary operators. It improves training-free model composition.

entry.title: MusTBENCH: Benchmarking and Advancing Temporal Grounding in Music LLMs

author.name: Daeyong Kwon, Qiyu Wu, Shinobu Kuriya, Junghyun Koo, Shuyang Cui, Zhi Zhong, Wei-Hsiang Liao, Hiromi Wakaki, Yuki Mitsufuji

entry.summary: MusTBENCH is a music-expert-validated benchmark for temporal grounding in large audio-language models, plus MusT, a four-stage optimization recipe to improve grounding of localized musical events. From Sony AI, it addresses whether music LLM answers are temporally accurate.

entry.title: Aligned but Fragile: Enhancing LLM Safety Robustness via Zeroth-Order Optimization

author.name: Zhihao Liu, Yifan Wu, Jian Lou, Di Wang, Yuxi Zhou, Yuke Hu

entry.summary: Studies safety-alignment fragility from the optimizer's perspective, arguing standard fine-tuning leaves alignment vulnerable to noise, quantization, and parameter perturbations. It proposes zeroth-order optimization to produce more robust alignment that resists lightweight post-alignment manipulations.

entry.title: GDSD: Reinforcement Learning as Guided Denoiser Self-Distillation for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Xiaohang Tang, Keyue Jiang, Che Liu, Qifang Zhao, Xiaoxiao Xu, Sangwoong Yoon, Ilija Bogunovic

entry.summary: Proposes GDSD, an RL method for diffusion language models that avoids the biased ELBO-as-likelihood surrogate by directly distilling the denoiser from an advantage-guided self-teacher derived from the closed-form optimum of reverse-KL-regularized RL. It matches denoiser logits to reduce training-inference mismatch.

entry.title: Rethinking Post-Training Recipes for Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Haoxin Liu, Yichen Zhou, Rajat Sen, B. Aditya Prakash, Abhimanyu Das

entry.summary: Proposes PostTime, a post-training recipe that teaches an LLM to act as a context-guided reviser over strong numerical time-series foundation model priors, deciding to revise, preserve, or ignore forecasts based on multimodal context. It combines supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards plus automated reasoning traces.

entry.title: PhoneWorld: Scaling Phone-Use Agent Environments

author.name: Zhengyang Tang, Yuxuan Liu, Xin Lai, Junyi Li, Pengyuan Lyu, Jason, Yiduo Guo, Zhengyao Fang, Yang Ding, Yi Zhang, Weinong Wang, Huawen Shen, Xingran Zhou, Liang Wu, Fei Tang, Sunqi Fan, Shangpin Peng, Zheng Ruan, Anran Zhang, Benyou Wang, Rui Yan, Ji-Rong Wen, Chengquan Zhang, Han Hu

entry.summary: Presents PhoneWorld, a reusable pipeline that converts real GUI trajectories and screenshots into controllable, reproducible phone-use agent environments with executable tasks, automatic verifiers, and training rollouts. Rather than hand-building one benchmark, it recovers screen connectivity, state-changing interactions, and verifiable goals from real traces to scale environment creation.

entry.title: On Asymmetric Optimization of Reasoning and Perception in Vision-Language Model Post-Training

author.name: Xueqing Wu, Yu-Chi Lin, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: Uses a controlled diagnostic framework with synthetic tasks to disentangle perception from reasoning in vision-language model post-training, revealing a consistent asymmetry where post-training improves reasoning more than perception. It traces this to token imbalance in chain-of-thought supervision and shows loss reweighting mitigates it for supervised fine-tuning.

entry.title: KBF: Knowledge Boundary as Fingerprint for Language Model and Black-Box API Auditing

author.name: Yijia Fang, Yiqing Feng, Bingyu Li, Mingxun Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces KBF, a low-cost black-box auditing protocol that fingerprints LLM APIs using stable numerical recall near the knowledge boundary to verify whether a claimed endpoint actually serves the advertised model. Across 16 production endpoints it flags all 155 economically relevant substitutions without false positives, detects partial mixed-routing attacks, and finds several reseller platform cells inconsistent with reference endpoints.

entry.title: The Complexity of Verifying Feedforward Neural Networks in Quantised Settings

author.name: Eric Alsmann, Martin Lange, Marco S\"alzer
