entry.title: Robust Frequency-Calibrated Virtual EEG Channel Generation from Four Frontal Electrodes for Wearable EEG Augmentation

author.name: Minghao Xiao

entry.summary: FAVC-Net generates 13 virtual EEG channels from just four frontal electrodes using multi-scale encoding, graph attention, and spectral calibration, enabling richer wearable EEG. It emphasizes spectral fidelity and robustness beyond waveform matching.

entry.title: Multi-Stage VLM Pipeline for Zero-Shot Traffic Accident Understanding

author.name: Fumiya Tatematsu, Fumihiko Takahashi

entry.summary: A first-place CVPR 2026 challenge solution for zero-shot traffic accident understanding using a multi-stage Qwen3-VL pipeline blending a 32B model and a 235B MoE sibling, with post-processing to snap predictions to vehicle detections. It substantially beats host baselines.

entry.title: EvoMD-LLM: Learning the Language of Species Evolution in Reactive Molecular Dynamics

author.name: Zhichen Tang, Zhengzheng Dang, Yulin Chen, Jixin Wu, Haiwen Li, Yanming Wang

entry.summary: Reframes reactive molecular dynamics at the species level as a symbolic temporal language-modeling task, tokenizing chemical events with persistence durations so autoregressive LLMs can learn compositional evolution. Temporal scaffolding treats event duration as an explicit token to provide structured inductive bias.

entry.title: ReasonLight: A Multimodal Foundation Model-Enhanced Reinforcement Learning Framework for Zero-Shot Traffic Signal Control

author.name: Aoyu Pang, Maonan Wang, Yuejiao Xie, Chung Shue Chen, Zhiwei Yang, Man-On Pun

entry.summary: Proposes ReasonLight, a multimodal foundation-model-enhanced RL framework for zero-shot traffic signal control that fuses structured sensor measurements, multi-view camera semantics, and a pretrained RL controller's candidate phase decisions. It targets open-world events absent from training data.

entry.title: DELOS: Detecting Shallow Transits in Kepler Photometry Using a Contrastive-Learning Framework

author.name: Qingtian Liu, Jian Ge, XingChen Yan, Kevin Willis, Xinyu Yao, QuanQuan Hu, and Jiapeng Zhu

entry.summary: Presents DELOS, a contrastive-learning framework for detecting shallow, intermediate-to-long-period transiting exoplanets in Kepler phase-folded light curves using GPU-accelerated folding and a 1D convolutional encoder that produces a score periodogram. It is trained on 20 million synthetic curves with realistic noise.

entry.title: V2XCrafter: Learning to Generate Driving Scene Across Agents

author.name: Yihang Tao, Yu Guo, Senkang Hu, Yanan Ma, Zihan Fang, Sam Kwong, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: Proposes V2XCrafter, claimed first framework to generate multi-agent V2X driving scenes for data augmentation, addressing degraded quality from expanded learning objectives and inconsistent physical attributes of jointly observed objects across agents. It targets the scarcity of annotated real-world V2X collaborative-perception datasets.

entry.title: KGEdit: Ambiguity-Aware Knowledge Graphs for Training-Free Precise Video Generation and Editing

author.name: Mingshu Cai, Miao Zhang, Chenghe Yang, Yixuan Li, Osamu Yoshie, and Yuya Ieiri

entry.summary: Proposes KGEdit, a training-free structured-semantic control framework for text-to-video diffusion that builds an ambiguity-aware knowledge graph disentangling prompts into identity, relation, attribute, and negative-constraint semantics. A structured semantic injection module feeds these signals into key diffusion-transformer layers to reduce concept-binding errors and cross-frame inconsistency.

entry.title: DynaGraph: Lightweight Multi-Model Interaction Framework via Dynamic Topological Reconfiguration

author.name: Yanxing Guo, Zihao Zheng, Fangzhou Wu, Ling Liang, Lin Bao, Zongwei Wang, Yimao Cai

entry.summary: Presents DynaGraph, a lightweight multi-model framework that uses dynamic topological reconfiguration to balance the rigidity of static pipelines against the divergence of unconstrained dynamic agents. It multiplexes time-division PEFT adapters over a shared base model, enabling full training and inference on a single consumer GPU.

entry.title: K-FinHallu: A Hallucination Detection Benchmark for Multi-Turn RAG in Korean Finance

author.name: Eunbyeol Cho, Yunseung Lee, Mirae Kim, Jeewon Yang, Youngjun Kwak, Edward Choi

entry.summary: Introduces K-FinHallu, claimed first benchmark for hallucination detection in multi-turn Korean financial retrieval-augmented generation, building dialogues from authentic documents and injecting hallucinations under a hierarchical taxonomy that accounts for justified abstention. Benchmarking frontier and open LLMs as detectors reveals that even strong models struggle.

entry.title: UI-KOBE: Knowledge-Oriented Behavior Exploration for Lightweight Graph-Guided GUI Agents

author.name: Yuxiang Chai, Han Xiao, Xinyu Fu, Jinpeng Chen, Rui Liu, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: Proposes UI-KOBE, which boosts lightweight on-device mobile GUI agents using reusable app-specific graph knowledge built via autonomous exploration. Aims for cheaper, privacy-preserving on-device automation.

entry.title: From Blind Guess to Informed Judgment: Teaching LLMs to Evaluate Materials by Building Knowledge-Augmented Preference Signals

author.name: Yeyong Yu, Wenya Hu, Xing Wu, Quan Qian

entry.summary: Proposes MaterEval, a knowledge-augmented preference framework that pairs informed expert-rule-based judgments against rule-removed blind guesses to train LLMs to evaluate materials candidates reliably. Targets the evaluation bottleneck in materials discovery.

entry.title: DiffSpot: Can VLMs Spot Fine-Grained Visual Differences in Web Interfaces?

author.name: Linhao Zhang, Aiwei Liu, Yuan Liu, Xiao Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces DiffSpot, a code-driven spot-the-difference benchmark on web interfaces that mutates single CSS properties to create controlled image pairs, testing VLMs' fine-grained visual perception. Reveals limits in detecting subtle localized visual changes.

entry.title: Entity-Collision: A Stratified Protocol for Attributing Retrieval Lift in Agent Memory

author.name: Youwang Deng

entry.summary: Proposes entity-collision, a stratified protocol for attributing retrieval lift in agent memory by pinning the BM25 floor (distractors share answer entity tokens) and stratifying by tag, isolating embedder contributions. Reveals a two-axis pattern across embedders and collision degrees.

entry.title: PTCG-Bench: Can LLM Agents Master Pok\'emon Trading Card Game?

author.name: Dongdong Hua, Yifei Sun, Renhong Huang, Feng Gao, Chunping Wang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: Presents PTCG-Bench, a benchmark on the Pokemon Trading Card Game evaluating LLM agents on single-environment decision-making and self-evolution through accumulated experience, with a modular harness ablation. Tests strategic and evolving decision-making in a complex board game.

entry.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Molecular Mixture Behavior Prediction

author.name: Roel J. Leenhouts, Nathan K. Morgan, William Green, Jan G. Rittig, Florence H. Vermeire

entry.summary: Proposes an evaluation framework that decomposes molecular mixture-property prediction error into pure-compound and non-ideal interaction components, with leakage-aware splits and excess-property metrics, plus seven curated datasets. It exposes that absolute accuracy conflates ideal-mixing and interaction effects. Improves rigor in ML for chemistry.

entry.title: S2MDF: A Plug-And-Play Layer for Intersection-Free Multi-Object Signed Distance Fields

author.name: Deniz Sayin Mercadier, Federico Stella, Aurel Bizeau, Nicolas Talabot, Pascal Fua

entry.summary: S2MDF is a lightweight plug-and-play module enforcing a hard intersection-free constraint on multi-object compositional signed distance fields without architectural changes or soft penalty tuning. It guarantees physically plausible non-interpenetrating geometry. Relevant for 3D reconstruction and compositional scene modeling.

entry.title: Improving CLIP Adaptation by Breaking Tail Alignment for Source-Free Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning

author.name: Shuai Yi, Yixiong Zou, Yuhua Li, Ruixuan Li

entry.summary: Reports a counterintuitive finding that actively pushing low-similarity 'tail' image tokens away from their text embeddings improves CLIP adaptation in source-free cross-domain few-shot learning. It interprets this via the difficulty of aligning all tokens under domain shift and scarce data. Useful insight for VLM adaptation.

entry.title: Not All Inputs Are Valid: Towards Open-Set Video Moment Retrieval Using Language

author.name: Xiang Fang, Wanlong Fang, Daizong Liu, Xiaoye Qu, Jianfeng Dong, Pan Zhou, Renfu Li, Zichuan Xu, Lixing Chen, Panpan Zheng, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: Not All Inputs Are Valid introduces Open-Set Video Moment Retrieval, where systems must reject out-of-distribution video-irrelevant queries instead of forcibly retrieving, addressing high-risk failure modes in applications like criminal activity detection. It moves VMR beyond the closed-set assumption. A useful new problem setting for video retrieval.

entry.title: Harnessing non-adversarial robustness in large language models

author.name: Qinghua Zhou, Ellina Aleshina, Andrey Lovyagin, Oleg Somov, Mikhail Seleznyov, Alexander Panchenko, Ivan Oseledets, Elena Tutubalina, Ivan Y. Tyukin

entry.summary: Addresses LLM robustness to semantically-neutral prompt variations, providing theoretical analysis identifying a systematic perturbation-induced output bias and showing robustness can be achieved via a simple lightweight finetuning rather than full retraining. It offers both theory and experiments. Relevant for cheap robustness improvements.

entry.title: Feedback-to-Rubrics: Can We Learn Expert Criteria from Inline Comments?

author.name: Kotaro Yoshida, So Kuroki, Yuki Imajuku, Taishi Nakamura, Ryunosuke Iwai, Haruki Goda, and Takuya Akiba

entry.summary: Feedback-to-Rubrics studies learning reusable natural-language rubrics from accumulated inline comments on drafts, inferring rubrics and iteratively refining them by comparing rubric-conditioned predictions to reference comments. It evaluates in real-world and controlled review settings. The goal is eliciting tacit, organization-specific expert criteria that are hard to state directly.

entry.title: Towards Verifiable Multimodal Deep Research: A Multi-Agent Harness for Interleaved Report Generation

author.name: Chenghao Zhang, Guanting Dong, Yufan Liu, Tong Zhao and Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: Ptah is a multi-agent harness for verifiable multimodal deep research that orchestrates planning, research, and writing to produce interleaved text-and-visual web reports, using specialized agents and a Visual Working Memory to keep source-aligned images. It targets the challenge of open-ended synthesis with claim grounding. The system emphasizes verifiability of multimodal long-form reports.

entry.title: Moment-KV: Momentum-Based Decode-Time KV Cache Compression for Long Generation

author.name: Soumyadeep Jana, Sagar Nishad, Sanasam Ranbir Singh

entry.summary: Moment-KV is a decode-time KV cache compression method that uses momentum-based attention dynamics to decide token eviction, motivated by the observation that critical tokens receive sustained attention while local reasoning is bursty. It preserves the prefill cache and focuses compression on the under-explored decoding phase. This targets long-generation memory bottlenecks.

entry.title: Mitigating Hallucination in Vision-Language Models through Barrier-Regulated Adaptive Closed-form Steering

author.name: Soumyadeep Jana, Pulkit Mittal, Sanasam Ranbir Singh

entry.summary: BRACS is a training-free steering method for reducing object hallucination in vision-language models that monitors the model's own attention to measure visual grounding and applies barrier-regulated, adaptive-strength corrections to hidden states only when grounding fails. It addresses limitations of prior logit/hidden-state interventions that act indiscriminately with fixed strength. The closed-form steering adapts to grounding-failure severity.

entry.title: CRITIC-R1: Learning Structured Critics for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Wenhan Xiao, Ziwei Zhang, Chuanyue Yu, Xingcheng Fu, Qingyun Sun, Runhua Xu, Jianxin Li

entry.summary: CRITIC-R1 formulates RAG critique as an explicit error-diagnosis problem learned via reinforcement learning, categorizing errors into structured diagnostic dimensions such as verdict, error location, and reasoning analysis. This contrasts with prior coarse, over-aggressive external critics. The structured feedback aims to enable more reliable correction of RAG hallucinations and reasoning errors.

entry.title: Redundant or Necessary? A Benchmark for Detecting Redundant Steps in Agent Trajectories

author.name: Minyang Hu, Bo Yang, Zhinuo Zhou, Jiachen Liang, Guo Jiahao, Yiyang Yin, Xiongwei Han

entry.summary: This work introduces redundant-step detection for LLM-agent trajectories and RedundancyBench, a benchmark with trajectories annotated by each step's contribution to task completion. It argues evaluation overly focuses on task success while ignoring execution efficiency, where agents waste resources on redundant steps. The benchmark supports developing and evaluating redundancy detectors.

entry.title: Label Over Logic? How Source Cues Bias Human Fallacy Judgments More Than LLMs

author.name: Mahjabin Nahar, Nafis Irtiza Tripto, Aiping Xiong, Ting-Hao `Kenneth' Huang, Dongwon Lee

entry.summary: This human-subject study (N=505) examines how source labels (human, AI, AI-assisted, etc.) bias judgments of logical fallacies, comparing human evaluators against LLMs in a domain-knowledge-independent setting. It finds source cues distort human reasoning judgments more than they affect LLMs, suggesting LLMs offer more source-agnostic evaluation. The findings have implications for moderation and human-AI collaboration.

entry.title: Fisher-Preserving Guidance: Training-Free Manifold Constraints for Safe Diffusion Control

author.name: Hao Ren, Zetong Bi, Yiming Zeng, Le Zheng, Zhi Li, Zhaoliang Wan, Lu Qi, Hui Cheng

entry.summary: Fisher-Preserving Guidance with Outer Product Span Projection is a training-free inference method for diffusion-based visual navigation that avoids large Fisher drift from off-distribution actions while optimizing a task objective, computed via low-rank Jacobian factorization with a single backward pass per step for real-time use. It adds a Truncated Fisher Denoising Sensitivity uncertainty signal for robust multi-sample action blending. The method keeps test-time-guided trajectories on the training manifold.

entry.title: Evaluating Skill and Stability of ArchesWeather and ArchesWeatherGen under Multi-Decadal Climate Simulations

author.name: Renu Singh, Robert Brunstein, Antonia Jost, Thomas Rackow, Claire Monteleoni, Yana Hasson, Christian Lessig, and Guillaume Couairon

entry.summary: This paper evaluates the climate-simulation skill and stability of ArchesWeather and ArchesWeatherGen—models originally trained for weather forecasting—by adapting them as forced atmospheric models conditioned on monthly sea-surface temperature and sea-ice cover, following the AIMIP Phase 1 protocol analogous to AMIP. It assesses multi-decadal stability and skill of deterministic and flow-matching probabilistic variants. The work probes whether ML weather models can serve as climate emulators.

entry.title: Cookie-Bench: Continuous On-screen Key Interaction Evaluation for Web Generation

author.name: Haoyue Yang, Zhangxiao Shen, Fan Ding, Hangting Lou, Yifeng Kou, Haoqing Yu, Jingyao Li, Zhengfan Wu, Siqi Bao, Jing Liu, Hua Wu

entry.summary: Cookie-Bench proposes a reference-free, autonomously driven, holistically reasoned evaluation regime for interactive front-end web generation, instantiated as an 11-domain, 1,000-query WebDev benchmark spanning static and interactive tasks across difficulty tiers and target languages. It addresses the cost of human-judged leaderboards and the limits of reference-based or checklist proxies. The aim is scalable evaluation that mimics a human reviewer over a live session.

entry.title: Boosting Zero-Shot 3D Style Transfer with 2D Pre-trained Priors

author.name: Xin Dong, Yunzhi Teng, Wenfeng Deng, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: This work boosts zero-shot 3D style transfer by integrating a 2D-pretrained decoder into the 3D pipeline to overcome data scarcity from single-scene training, combined with feature Gaussian splatting. It produces multi-view consistent stylized scenes from arbitrary style images. The reuse of 2D priors is the key idea.

entry.title: xModel-KD: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for 3D Scene Perception using LiDAR

author.name: Thenukan Pathmanathan, Kanchan Keisham, Thangarajah Akilan

entry.summary: xModel-KD distills knowledge cross-modally from 2D images into LiDAR-based 3D scene perception to overcome the high cost of dense 3D annotations and the limitations of single-modality learning. It transfers texture-rich 2D cues into geometry-rich but sparse point cloud models. It targets annotation-efficient 3D segmentation.

entry.title: Beyond MSE: Improving Precipitation Nowcasting with Multi-Quantile Regression

author.name: Gijs van Nieuwkoop, Siamak Mehrkanoon

entry.summary: This study reformulates deterministic precipitation nowcasting as multi-quantile regression with a pinball loss on SmaAt-UNet, improving the central forecast (8.6% lower MSE) and producing useful upper-quantile outputs for heavy rainfall. It addresses the over-smoothing problem of pointwise losses. The quantile reformulation is the key idea.

entry.title: DAMEL: Dual-Axis Multi-Expert Learning for Class-Imbalanced Learning

author.name: Hyuck Lee, Taemin Park, Heeyoung Kim

entry.summary: DAMEL is a dual-axis multi-expert learning algorithm for class-imbalanced long-tailed data that reduces both prediction bias and variance using multiple experts along representation and time axes, concatenating expert representations with an auxiliary balanced classifier. It aims to avoid the variance increase common in rebalancing. The dual-axis design is the contribution.

entry.title: OmniCD: A Foundational Framework for Remote Sensing Image Change Detection Guided by Multimodal Semantics

author.name: Chenhao Sun

entry.summary: OmniCD is a foundational framework for remote sensing change detection guided by multimodal semantics, unifying image and text prompts to support tasks from binary detection to zero-shot semantic change understanding, plus a 300K+ multimodal dataset. It aims to improve cross-domain generalization in urban monitoring and disaster assessment. Useful for the geospatial ML community.

entry.title: BullingerDB: A Dataset for Handwritten Text Recognition and Writer Retrieval

author.name: Marco Peer and Anna-Scius Bertrand and Patricia Scheurer and Andreas Fischer

entry.summary: BullingerDB is a large historical document benchmark from Heinrich Bullinger's 16th-century correspondence with 20,898 pages and 499,222 lines by 796 writers, supporting handwritten text recognition and writer retrieval. TrOCR achieves 9.1% CER and a temporal nDCG metric is introduced for time-aware retrieval. A valuable resource for historical document analysis.

entry.title: Fairness-Aware Federated Learning with Trajectory Shapley Value

author.name: Daniel Kuznetsov and Ziqi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Trajectory Shapley Value (TSV), a contribution metric for federated learning that scores each client by its influence on the global optimization trajectory using a validation-based, temporally consistent utility. The FedTSV aggregation scheme turns these scores into dynamic client weights for fairer, more stable training.

entry.title: We Should Study the Analogy Between Inoculation Prompting Non-Robustness, Negation Neglect, and Backdoor Non-Robustness

author.name: Vladimir Ivanov

entry.summary: Argues that three safety phenomena, the non-robustness of inoculation prompting, negation neglect (training on the following is false makes models believe the claim), and backdoor non-robustness, may be instances of the same underlying mechanism. It proposes studying the analogy to transfer insights and make inoculation prompting (used in production by Anthropic) more robust.

entry.title: Black Boxes for Low-Stakes, Interpretable AI for High-Stakes

author.name: Logan Riggs

entry.summary: Argues for a two-tier deployment strategy: general black-box models for low-stakes tasks and narrow, fully interpretable models for high-stakes domains like banking, the power grid, and medicine, even if 10x less efficient. It draws on the mammography accreditation precedent to suggest voluntary interpretable standards could become regulatory targets.

entry.title: How can the middle powers avoid getting trounced during the intelligence explosion? A plan.

author.name: Tom Davidson

entry.summary: Proposes a strategy for middle-power liberal democracies (UK, Europe, Japan, Korea, Taiwan) to avoid economic and military marginalization during a US-led intelligence explosion, by leveraging that the US needs them to beat China. It argues their main bargaining chip is a credible alternative of siding with China to secure continued access to frontier AI.

entry.title: Open Problem: Separating Geometric and Algorithmic Compression via Cayley-Table Completion

author.name: Dongsung Huh

entry.summary: This open-problem paper proposes Cayley-table completion as a canonical testbed for separating geometric (norm/rank-based) from algorithmic compression, arguing deep learning lacks an inductive bias toward algorithmic complexity minimization. It frames a research challenge for understanding extrapolation of discrete rules.

entry.title: Cycle-Space Informed Detection of Autoencoded Blind False Data Injection Attacks on Power Systems

author.name: Xin Li, Chenhan Xiao, Jonathan Cohen, Aviad Elyashar, Yang Weng, Rami Puzis

entry.summary: Demonstrates an autoencoder-based blind false data injection attack on power systems that aligns perturbations with the Jacobian null space to evade residual and time-series anomaly detectors. It then proposes a topology-informed, cycle-space detection method to catch such stealthy attacks.

entry.title: Paper Agents, Paper Gains: An Empirical Analysis of DeFi Investment Agents

author.name: Jay Yu, Amy Zhao, Danning Sui

entry.summary: This empirical study surveys over 1,900 AI-tagged crypto projects, analyzes two prominent DeFi agent frameworks, and examines on-chain performance of 11 Solana agent treasuries, finding many projects lack clear evidence of genuine autonomous trade execution. It provides a sober reality-check on the multi-billion-dollar DeFi investment-agent ecosystem.

entry.title: MOOSE-Copilot: A Web-Based Interactive Assistant for Unified Exploratory and Fine-Grained Scientific Hypothesis Discovery

author.name: Hongran An, Zonglin Yang

entry.summary: Presents MOOSE-Copilot, a unified web-based assistant that bridges divergent exploratory ideation and convergent fine-grained refinement in scientific hypothesis discovery via a formalized human-AI interaction protocol with initial blueprints, inter-stage routing, and regenerative feedback. It shows injecting structured expert signals outperforms purely autonomous baselines.

entry.title: Optimizing Latent Representations for Robust Building Damage Assessment Onboard Earth Observation Satellites

author.name: Thomas Goudemant, Benjamin Francesconi

entry.summary: Proposes an onboard-satellite system for object-level building damage assessment from pre/post-disaster imagery using compact latent representations transmitted from ground to reduce downlink latency. Targets faster disaster emergency response.

entry.title: COMET: Concept Space Dissection of the Modality Gap in Audio-Text Multimodal Contrastive Embeddings

author.name: Yonggang Zhu, Liting Gao, Aidong Men, Wenwu Wang

entry.summary: Presents COMET, a concept-space dissection of the modality gap in audio-text CLAP embeddings, testing hypotheses beyond the cone effect including information imbalance and dimensionality collapse. Provides interpretable analysis of audio-text contrastive embeddings.

entry.title: FLIP: Real-Time and Resilient Formation Planning for Large-Scale DIstributed Swarms via Point Cloud Registration

author.name: Yuan Zhou, Guangtong Xu, Zhenyu Hou, Jialiang Hou, and Fei Gao

entry.summary: FLIP reframes large-scale distributed swarm formation planning as a spatiotemporal point cloud registration problem with outlier rejection, enabling real-time and resilient formation position computation. Each agent distributively computes its optimal formation position. A robotics contribution for scalable swarm coordination.

entry.title: GeoMag: Geometric-Aware Video Motion Magnification via State Space Model

author.name: Kecheng Han, Yuchen Zhang, Bingqing Liu, Boqiang Guo, Wenbin Zheng, Shiyuan Pei

entry.summary: GeoMag is a geometric-aware video motion magnification framework built on State Space Models for globally consistent amplification with linear complexity, plus Geo-200K, a synthetic dataset with rich geometric transformations and sensor-realistic effects. It addresses structural inconsistencies under complex geometry. Advances learning-based motion magnification.

entry.title: Metric-Dependent Annotation Saturation for Learning from Label Distributions

author.name: Guneet Kohli

entry.summary: Investigates how many annotators are needed to capture label-distribution signal, finding metric-dependent saturation: entropy correlation needs ~20-50 annotators while KL divergence saturates by ~10, using NLI models on ChaosNLI. It shows soft labels carry item-specific signal beyond label smoothing. Useful for annotation-budget and disagreement-aware learning.

entry.title: Train the Agent, Not the Expert: Learning to Harness Heterogeneous Experts for Multi-Turn Visual Reasoning

author.name: Yaowu Fan, Tao Han, Dazhao Du, Andy J. Ma, Jia Wan

entry.summary: VisHarness is a trainable visual agent that decouples high-level perception, reasoning, and decision-making from low-level execution by learning to orchestrate a set of heterogeneous specialized vision experts rather than training one model to solve a task. This preserves general intelligence while leveraging strong specialist detectors, segmenters, and counters. It targets tasks needing complex language understanding plus dense small-object perception.

entry.title: Agora: Toward Autonomous Bug Detection in Production-Level Consensus Protocols with LLM Agents

author.name: Xiang Liu, Sa Song, Zhaowei Zhang, Huiying Lan, Jason Zeng, Ming Wu, Michael Heinrich, Yong Sun, Ceyao Zhang

entry.summary: Agora is a domain-aware multi-agent framework for autonomous bug detection in production consensus protocols, integrating hypothesis-driven testing with LLMs and specialized agents that explore state spaces, synthesize attack scenarios under domain constraints, and validate findings iteratively. It targets deep protocol-level logic bugs spanning multiple execution stages that defeat single-function analysis. The role separation enables reasoning over global protocol invariants.

entry.title: Does The Way You Plan Matter? An Empirical Study of Planning Representations for LLM Web Agents

author.name: Alejandra Zambrano, Sara Vera Marjanovic, Imene Kerboua, Xing Han L\`u, Leila Kosseim

entry.summary: PlanAhead is a static planner-executor framework that empirically studies how natural-language plan representation affects LLM web-agent performance, comparing sequential subgoals, narrative, pseudocode, and checklist formats on automatically difficulty-graded WebArena tasks. It isolates plan representation as a variable in agent failures. The study targets exploration, omitted steps, and constraint sensitivity in web agents.

entry.title: CityGen: Structure-Guided City-Style Synthesis for Cross-City Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zezhong Qian, Zhao Yang, Lu Tan, Zhihao Yan, Weiyi Hong, Haizhuang Liu, Yawei Jueluo

entry.summary: CityGen is a diffusion-based generative framework for structure-guided city-style synthesis to improve cross-city generalization in autonomous driving, paired with CityTransfer-Bench, a geographically disjoint benchmark evaluating perception, segmentation, and planning. It avoids reliance on labeled target data or city-specific annotations required by prior domain-adaptation methods. The aim is scalable cross-city deployment and holistic evaluation.

entry.title: Learning to Choose: An Empowerment-Guided Multi-Agent System with semantic communication for Adaptive Method Selection

author.name: Geremy Loacham\'in-Suntaxi, Robert Lazar, Dimitrios G. Giovanis, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis and Eleni D. Koronaki

entry.summary: This paper introduces an empowerment-guided multi-agent system with semantic communication that selects computational strategies for scientific workflows while preventing semantic drift between agent intentions and executed actions. It aims to keep outcomes causally attributable to chosen strategies. It builds on the ATHENA framework and empowerment concepts.

entry.title: Geographically-Weighted Weakly Supervised Bayesian High-Resolution Transformer for 200m Resolution Pan-Arctic Sea Ice Concentration Mapping and Uncertainty Estimation using Sentinel-1, RCM, and AMSR2 Data

author.name: Mabel Heffring and Lincoln Linlin Xu

entry.summary: This work presents a Bayesian high-resolution transformer for 200m pan-Arctic sea ice concentration mapping with uncertainty estimation, fusing Sentinel-1, RCM, and AMSR2 data and using geographically-weighted weak supervision to handle inexact labels. It improves extraction of subtle ice features. It targets operational sea ice charting.

entry.title: ExDBSCAN: Explaining DBSCAN with Counterfactual Reasoning -- Additional Material

author.name: Pernille Matthews, Lena Krieger, Tommaso Amico, Artur Zimek, Thomas Seidl, Ira Assent

entry.summary: ExDBSCAN provides density-aware post-hoc counterfactual explanations for DBSCAN clustering assignments, explaining why a point is an inlier or outlier and whether its assignment is robust to small data changes. It offers actionable counterfactuals with theoretical guarantees. Addresses the interpretability gap in unsupervised clustering.

entry.title: COMPOSE: Composing Future Theorems from Citations and Formal Structure

author.name: David Busbib, Michael Werman

entry.summary: Defines grounded future mathematical generation, where a model proposes plausible future theorems for an anchor paper using both its citation graph and an aligned formal theorem dependency graph. The proposed dual-graph COMPOSE framework conditions a language model on both scientific and formal structure.

entry.title: Causal Label Recovery in Payment Networks

author.name: Gaurav Dhama

entry.summary: This work formalizes biased fraud-detection labels in payment networks as a sequential missing-data problem across three propensity gates plus corruption, and proposes a Sequential Triply Robust estimator to recover causal labels and approach a known minimax bound. It matters for building reliable fraud models under systematic label bias.

entry.title: Adapting Automotive Aerodynamics Surrogates to New Vehicle Families via Transfer Learning

author.name: Seunghwan Keum, Alok Warey

entry.summary: This paper studies transfer learning for automotive aerodynamics surrogates, showing through leave-one-family-out experiments that pretrained geometry encoders learn transferable representations but the adaptation mechanism (full fine-tuning vs lightweight vs LoRA) determines whether they transfer to topologically distinct vehicles with only 20 samples. It informs deploying SciML surrogates in industrial CFD.

entry.title: Behavior-Induced Mirror-Prox Temporal-Difference Learning for Faster Off-Policy Prediction

author.name: Xingguo Chen, Yuchen Shen, Shangdong Yang, Chao Li, Guang Yang, Wenhao Wang

entry.summary: Develops STHTD-MP, a behavior-induced Mirror-Prox temporal-difference method that replaces the feature-covariance metric with the symmetric part of the behavior-policy Bellman matrix to improve off-policy prediction geometry. It maintains a single learning rate while applying a prediction-correction step.

entry.title: Financially Guided Deep Portfolio Optimization

author.name: Rahul Fernandes, Travis Desell

entry.summary: Proposes an end-to-end deep portfolio optimization framework that directly optimizes differentiable surrogates of financial metrics like Sharpe ratio, Omega, CVaR, and Risk Parity, avoiding the error compounding of predict-then-optimize pipelines. It is evaluated with realistic transaction costs on S&P 500 stocks in a walk-forward procedure.

entry.title: The Cognitive Categorical Transformer: Category-Theoretic Inductive Biases for Language Modeling

author.name: Al Kari

entry.summary: Introduces the Cognitive Categorical Transformer, a 306M-parameter architecture augmenting GPT-2 Small with category-theory-inspired components, reporting a 12% perplexity improvement over fine-tuned GPT-2 on WikiText-103. Ablations attribute most of the gain to simplicial message-passing components.

entry.title: Emergent Semantic Representations in World Models through Physical Interaction without Linguistic Supervision

author.name: Jiayi Fang

entry.summary: Trains a VAE-based world model on random embodied exploration without linguistic supervision and finds its latent space develops spatial semantic structure mirroring physical geometry. It argues emergent semantic representations are organized by the geometric structure of the physical world.

entry.title: TaxDistill: Improving Metagenomic Taxonomic Annotation via Distilled Genomic Foundation Models

author.name: Rongye Ye, Lun Li, Zheng Luo, Yiran Zhan, Shuhui Song

entry.summary: Proposes TaxDistill, a knowledge-distillation framework that uses a genomic foundation model (GenomeOcean) as a teacher to improve metagenomic taxonomic annotation while reducing reliance on noisy similarity-search labels. It aims to learn better metagenomic sequence representations for classification.

entry.title: GrowLoop: Self-Evolving Conversation Evaluation Seeded by Human

author.name: Yihang Lin, Yunze Gao, Zeyang Lin, Dongbo Li, Kun Peng, Chenglong Song, Yue Liu

entry.summary: Proposes GrowLoop, a self-evolving conversation evaluation method seeded by human judgments to assess human-likeness in open-ended LLM conversations as criteria and capabilities evolve. It aims to address tacit, evolving, and disagreement-prone human-likeness judgments simultaneously.

entry.title: Text-Preserving Lossy Text Compression: A Study of Strategic Deletion and LLM Reconstruction

author.name: Yuchun Zou, Junhong Tong, Jun Li

entry.summary: Studies lossy semantic text compression where an encoder strategically deletes parts of text and an LLM reconstructs the original from the retained skeleton, benchmarking deletion strategies from uniform to frequency- and surprisal-guided methods. It finds word-frequency-guided deletion is a strong low-cost baseline on BBC News data.

entry.title: FedQHD: Closed-Form Function-Space Federated Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuchen Hou, Yongshan Chen, Zhuowen Zou, Calvin Yeung, Mohsen Imani, Tian Lan, Mahdi Imani

entry.summary: Proposes FedQHD, a federated Q-learning method using hyperdimensional random-feature state encoders with a linear readout so Q-functions are nonlinear in state but linear in parameters, enabling function-space-consistent closed-form aggregation. It addresses the inconsistency of FedAvg-style parameter averaging in nonlinear federated RL.

entry.title: LoRe: Adaptive Interaction-Evaluation Routing with Per-Step Interaction Budgets for Iterative Graph Solvers

author.name: Jintao Li, Yong-Yi Wang, Zheng-An Wang, Heng Fan

entry.summary: Introduces LoRe, a training-free inference-time wrapper for diffusion-based combinatorial-optimization solvers that enforces per-step interaction-evaluation budgets by dynamically routing computation to high-conflict or high-uncertainty interactions. It improves scalability on the Maximum Independent Set problem under end-to-end wall-clock accounting.

entry.title: Error as a Lens: Probing LLM Reasoning through Synthetic Misconception Generation

author.name: Xinming Yang, Jun Li

entry.summary: Presents a framework that generates synthetic student misconceptions targeted to a five-class taxonomy adapted from Bloom's taxonomy, using a Generation Agent to draft errors and an Examination Agent to verify incorrectness and class-consistency. It addresses the scarcity of labeled real student-error corpora due to privacy constraints.

entry.title: Trajectory Constraints for Imaging Inverse Problems

author.name: Chaoyan Huang, Haijie Yuan, Saiprasad Ravishankar

entry.summary: Introduces TRACE, a training-free trajectory-constrained reconstruction framework for imaging inverse problems that couples adjacent states along the reconstruction trajectory, interpreted as a sequence of proximal updates approximated by a neural mapping. It stabilizes the reconstruction path in diffusion-like and iterative methods.

entry.title: Three-dimensional Conditional Diffusion Models for Cosmological 21 cm Lightcone Emulation

author.name: Bin Xia, John H. Wise

entry.summary: Investigates conditional diffusion modeling for emulating three-dimensional cosmological 21 cm lightcones with long line-of-sight depth, performing controlled comparisons across preprocessing, dynamic-range compression, architecture depth, and training duration. It tackles the harder 3D setting with very small micro-batches and highly skewed voxel distributions.

entry.title: Designing Active Tether-Net Systems for Space Debris Capture with Graph-Learning-Aided Mixed-Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Feng Liu, Achira Boonrath, Gishnu Madhu, Eleonora M. Botta and Souma Chowdhury

entry.summary: Addresses concurrent design and control optimization of active tether-net systems for space-debris capture, formulated as a mixed combinatorial nonlinear program with continuous, integer, and categorical variables. It uses graph-learning-aided mixed-combinatorial optimization to handle net connectivity and component choices.

entry.title: LLMBridge: An LLM Pipeline for End-to-end Referential Bridging Resolution in English

author.name: Lauren Levine and Amir Zeldes

entry.summary: LLMBridge is an end-to-end LLM pipeline for referential bridging resolution in English, combining heuristic pre/post-processing with LLM natural-language-inference. It surpasses prior state-of-the-art on three benchmarks (ISNotes, BASHI, GUMBridge) in both end-to-end and basic settings.

entry.title: Toward User Preference Alignment in LLM Recommendation via Explicit Context Feedback

author.name: Weizhi Zhang, Wooseong Yang, Yuxin Cui, Zhaohui Guo, Hins Hu, Liangwei Yang, Henry Peng Zou, Qifei Wang, Hanqing Zeng, Jiayi Liu, Yinglong Xia, and Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: This paper learns explicit textual feedback (comments, reviews) to align LLM-based recommendations with user preferences, addressing the neglect of explicit contextual signals and filter-bubble reinforcement in traditional implicit-signal recommenders. It aims for more accurate and explainable recommendations.

entry.title: Turbulence-Robust Dynamic Object Segmentation with Multi-Signal Priors and SAM2 Refinement

author.name: Bolian Peng, Ying Tang, Xu Liu, Long Sun, Xiaoqiang Lu

entry.summary: A training-free pipeline for dynamic object segmentation under atmospheric turbulence combining RAFT motion, DINOv2 priors, ViBe background modeling, and SAM2 refinement, submitted to the CVPR 2026 UG2+ challenge. It tackles pseudo-motion and blur without end-to-end training.

entry.title: Beyond Bilingual Transfer: Multilingual Code-Switching in Instruction Tuning

author.name: Shunta Asano, Jeonghun Baek, Toshihiko Yamasaki

entry.summary: Extends code-switching instruction tuning beyond bilingual English-target settings to four languages (English, Japanese, Korean, Chinese), showing that simple sentence-level multilingual code-switched data consistently improves multilingual understanding on Belebele. It explores genuinely multilingual rather than pairwise transfer.

entry.title: ParCo-SDF: Learning Prior-Free Partial-to-Complete Signed Distance Fields of Deformable Objects

author.name: Deokmin Hwang, Minseok Song, Daehyung Park

entry.summary: Introduces ParCo-SDF, a prior-free two-stage framework reconstructing complete signed distance fields of deformable objects from partial point clouds via temporal geometry encoding and FiLM-conditioned SDF prediction. It avoids object-specific shape priors to improve generalization for manipulation.

entry.title: CrystalXRD-Bench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for XRD Peak Indexing Across Diverse Crystalline Materials

author.name: Chengliang Xu, Xiaogang Li, Peiyao Xiao, Beng Wang, Hu Wei, Bing Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces CrystalXRD-Bench, a 250-sample benchmark requiring vision-language models to read narrow peak locations from rendered XRD curves and connect them to multi-step crystallographic reasoning to recover Miller indices. The best model reaches a Jaccard of 0.59 with only 37.6% exact match, exposing weak scientific visual reasoning.

entry.title: Forget Less, Generalize More: Unifying Temporal and Structural Adaptation for Dynamic Graphs

author.name: Qian Chang, Ciprian Doru Giurcaneanu, Runsong Jia, Xia Li, Guoping Hu, Xiufeng Cheng, Jinqing Yang, Mengjia Wu, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Dual-Scale Retentive Dynamics for dynamic-graph representation learning, maintaining a retentive state that jointly models temporal memory and structural context within a single recurrent formulation with learnable, adaptive decay kernels. It aims to generalize across graphs with diverse interaction frequencies and topologies while reducing forgetting.

entry.title: Adaptive Interviewing for Persona Simulation in LLMs: Evidence-Grounded Reasoning Improves Decision Alignment

author.name: Ruoxi Su, Yuhan Liu, Jingyu Hu

entry.summary: Proposes an adaptive interview framework that gathers persona-relevant information through staged dialogue (core questions, dynamic follow-ups, synthesized personality summary) to better simulate an individual's decisions. It finds that adaptive interviewing improves alignment with participants' choices in moral dilemma scenarios versus static persona descriptions.

entry.title: From General Vision to Reliable Traversability Estimation: Adapting Vision Foundation Models for Unstructured Outdoor Environments

author.name: Ji-Hoon Hwang, Jisung Bae, Dong-Wook Kim, Yeonkyu Lee and Seung-Woo Seo

entry.summary: Proposes ViTA, a framework adapting vision foundation models (built on SAM2) for reliable traversability estimation in unstructured outdoor environments via learnable traversability prompts and perspective-diversified training. Tackles task-agnostic VFM design and annotation ambiguity.

entry.title: MARTIAN: A Rendering Framework for Aerial Mars Imagery from HiRISE Orbital Data

author.name: Dario Pisanti and Georgios Georgakis

entry.summary: Presents MARTIAN, an open-source Blender-based rendering framework that synthesizes realistic aerial Mars views from real HiRISE orbital data with accurate pose annotations under controllable lighting. Addresses scarcity of annotated aerial datasets for Mars vision-based navigation.

entry.title: Notation Matters: A Benchmark Study of Token-Optimized Formats in Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Lorenz Kutschka, Bernhard Geiger

entry.summary: Benchmarks token-optimized data formats (TOON, TRON) against JSON inside end-to-end agentic loops across four tool-use benchmarks. It tests whether claimed token savings translate to real agentic performance. Practically relevant for cost-efficient agent system design.

entry.title: BitTP: The Lightweight Trajectory Prediction Model with BitLLM for Edge-Devices

author.name: Mincheol Kang, Hyunjin Lim, Bomin Kang, Daehee Park

entry.summary: BitTP converts an LLM-based trajectory predictor into a lightweight 1.58-bit BitLinear architecture for edge deployment in autonomous systems, keeping activations in full precision. It enables deploying LLM trajectory reasoning on resource-constrained on-board computers. Useful for efficient autonomous-systems deployment.

entry.title: User-Aware Active Knowledge Acquisition for Emotional Support Dialogue

author.name: Mufan Xu, Kehai Chen, Jiahao Hu, Xinchao Xu, Muyun Yang, Tiejun Zhao, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces User-Aware Active Knowledge Acquisition (UKA), a gradient-free active dialogue learning framework that represents uncertainty about evolving user needs using Theory-of-Mind and active learning for emotional support dialogue. It improves knowledge acquisition and response selection across multi-turn interactions. Relevant for empathetic dialogue systems.

entry.title: DySem: Uncovering Dynamic Semantic Components via Multilingual Consensus for Calculating Semantic Textual Similarity

author.name: Kaijie Zheng, Weiqin Wang, Yile Wang, Hui Huang

entry.summary: DySem is a training-free framework that identifies more semantic-related internal LLM components via multilingual consensus rather than fixed last-layer hidden states for semantic textual similarity. It addresses redundancy and non-semantic content in standard representations. Relevant for representation analysis and STS.

entry.title: On the Geometry of Games and their Solvers

author.name: Yaqi Sun, Julian Ma, David Mguni

entry.summary: This paper studies which algorithms efficiently compute equilibria across diverse game classes by constructing a solver-game map linking games to effective solver dynamics, proposing that solvability is governed by a continuous, solver-aligned geometry rather than discrete taxonomies. It connects equilibrium computation, GAN training, and learning systems. The framing offers a unifying view of fragmented solver guarantees.

entry.title: Genetically Aligned Patient Representations Improve Hematological Diagnosis

author.name: Muhammed Furkan Dasdelen, Fatih Ozlugedik, Ilaria Looser, Rao Muhammad Umer, Christian Pohlkamp, Carsten Marr

entry.summary: This study aligns single white-blood-cell images with chromosomal aberrations (karyotype) and somatic mutations via a two-stage approach: self-supervised vision-only pretraining of a transformer aggregator with an iBOT head on over 1,500 patients, then supervised contrastive genetic alignment on acute myeloid leukemia patients. Genetically aligned patient representations improve hematological diagnosis. It leverages the natural pairing of cytology with genetics in blood-cancer workups.

entry.title: FRUC: Feedforward Dynamic Scene Reconstruction from Uncalibrated Collaborative Driving Views

author.name: Yihang Tao, Yu Guo, Zhengru Fang, Haonan An, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: FRUC is a feed-forward 3D Gaussian splatting framework for dynamic scene reconstruction from uncalibrated collaborative driving views, treating a distributed multi-vehicle network as a spatio-temporally unstructured ego-centric multi-camera system. It enhances occluded ego geometry through collaboration without degrading visible geometry, using a visual-grounded geometric Transformer for one-shot calibration-free reconstruction. The aim is efficient multi-agent reconstruction without precise calibration or per-scene optimization.

entry.title: Evolving Features vs Evolving Entire Trees with GP for Interpretable Survival Analysis

author.name: Thalea Schlender, Peter A.N. Bosman, Tanja Alderliesten

entry.summary: This paper compares evolving features versus evolving entire trees with genetic programming for interpretable survival analysis on censored medical data, aiming to keep trees shallow yet expressive. It seeks both accuracy and interpretability for clinical use. The feature-vs-tree evolution comparison is the focus.

entry.title: Privacy-Enhanced Zero-Order Federated Learning via xMK-CKKS over Wireless Channels

author.name: Anthony Ayli, Khalil Harris, Jihad Fahs, Mohamad Assaad

entry.summary: This paper proposes a four-phase protocol enabling multi-key xMK-CKKS homomorphic encryption aggregation for zero-order federated learning over a shared wireless channel without channel estimation. It provides stronger client-level security than single-key HE, where a compromised client cannot break the network. It targets privacy-preserving over-the-air FL.

entry.title: Modularizing Educational LLM-Agency for Fostering Responsible Learning Assistance

author.name: Julius Gabelmann, Felix Jahn, Kevin Baum, Sophie van Rossum, Emely Wuenscher, Timo P. Gros, Verena Wolf

entry.summary: This paper proposes a modular agentic AI chatbot architecture for K-12 exercise assistance designed around pedagogical desiderata to avoid undermining transfer, critical thinking, and creativity. It argues structurally for responsible deployment in education. Conceptual and design-oriented contribution to educational AI.

entry.title: Glasswing exposed a governance gap

author.name: callumzc

entry.summary: Argues that Anthropic's gated, pre-release access decisions for a powerful model (Glasswing/Mythos) made it the unaccountable arbiter of who can access strategically important AI, exposing a governance gap. It frames this as a problematic precedent with potential consequences such as increased coup risk and calls for accountable access criteria.

entry.title: A New Era of Innovation: Google Research at I/O 2026

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google Research blog post summarizing the lab's announcements and research directions at I/O 2026, spanning new models and tools (e.g., recent Gemini-line releases) and broad scientific initiatives. It serves as a high-level showcase of Google's current AI research portfolio.

entry.title: Saddle Networks: Structure-Preserving Architectures for Convex-Concave Functions

author.name: Xavier Warin

entry.summary: Saddle Networks introduces neural architectures that preserve convex-concave geometry by construction for saddle-point problems, with a one-dimensional approximation theorem under a Monge-type convexity condition. This is relevant for min-max optimization, optimal transport, and robust learning where structural guarantees matter.

entry.title: A New Method to Capturing Compositional Knowledge in Linguistic Space

author.name: Jiahe Wan

entry.summary: This paper introduces zero-shot compositional understanding (ZS-CU) and YUKINO, which uses textual inversion to map unlabeled images to CLIP pseudo-tokens with a negation-based logical regularizer, avoiding reliance on hard-negative fine-tuning. It targets compositional reasoning in vision-language models.

entry.title: LogDx-CI: Benchmarking Log Reduction Tools for LLM Root-Cause Diagnosis

author.name: Bowen Qin

entry.summary: Introduces LogDx-CI, a benchmark comparing 11 log-context-reduction tools for LLM root-cause diagnosis on 35 real CI failure cases scored by multiple LLM debuggers. It finds hybrid grep+tail routers dominate the cost-quality Pareto frontier.

entry.title: Governing Technical Debt in Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Muhammad Zia Hydari, Raja Iqbal, Narayan Ramasubbu

entry.summary: This conceptual paper defines Agentic Technical Debt (accumulated governance liability from hastily assembled prompts, memory, tools, and orchestration) and Stochastic Tax (the recurring cost of constraining probabilistic agent behavior). It frames governance challenges unique to production agentic AI systems.

entry.title: CA-AC-MPC: CUDA-Accelerated Actor-Critic Model Predictive Control

author.name: Antoonio Buo, Vittorio Cammarota, Michele Avagnale, Pierluigi Arpenti, Vincenzo Lippiello, Fabio Ruggiero

entry.summary: CA-AC-MPC is a CUDA-accelerated actor-critic model predictive control variant that parallelizes the differentiable MPC layer's forward and backward solves, substantially cutting training and inference latency while preserving control performance. It achieves state-of-the-art lap times in agile drone racing simulation.

entry.title: ViASNet: A Video Ad Saliency Network for Predicting Dynamic Saliency and Viewer Engagement

author.name: Jianping Ye, Michel Wedel

entry.summary: ViASNet is a 3D U-Net-based dynamic saliency model for short-form video ads that incorporates audio and semantic content to predict viewer eye fixations and engagement. It aids understanding and optimization of video advertising effectiveness.

entry.title: Learning Design Skills as Memory Policies for Agentic Photonic Inverse Design

author.name: Shengchao Chen, Ting Shu, Sufen Ren

entry.summary: Frames photonic crystal fiber inverse design as memory-policy learning with SkillPCF, a closed-loop agent combining a physics-guided memory skill bank, RL-based skill selection, and simulator-grounded skill evolution. It releases a real-world dataset of expert interaction traces and evaluation queries.

entry.title: Gradient Perturbation: Learning to Perturb Gradients for Adaptive Training

author.name: Hua Li

entry.summary: Establishes a unified framework for gradient perturbation in the backward pass, showing that Sharpness-Aware Minimization, gradient clipping, and gradient noise injection are all special cases of imposing specific gradient perturbations. By analogy to logit perturbation learning, it conjectures and explores learning to amplify gradients adaptively.

entry.title: Learning to Perturb Hidden Representations for Generalizable Deep Learning

author.name: Hua Li

entry.summary: Establishes a unified framework for perturbing intermediate hidden activations, showing Dropout, Manifold Mixup, and adversarial feature perturbation are special cases applied with class-agnostic or random strategies. It conjectures that expansive perturbations act as positive augmentation while contractive ones act differently, proposing learned activation perturbation for generalization.

entry.title: SCOPE: A Lightweight-training LLM Framework for Air Traffic Control Readback Monitoring

author.name: Qihan Deng, Minghua Zhang, Yang Yang, Zhenyu Gao

entry.summary: Presents SCOPE, a lightweight-training LLM framework for monitoring pilot readback of air traffic control instructions, where anomalies are implicated in most aviation incidents. Targets generalization across evolving ATC phraseology with low deployment cost.

entry.title: Geometry-Guided Modeling of Foundation Features Enables Generalizable Object Shape Deformation Learning

author.name: Yiyao Ma, Kai Chen, Zhongxiang Zhou, Zhuheng Song, Dongsheng Xie, Zelong Tan, Rong Xiong and Qi Dou

entry.summary: Presents a geometry-guided deformation learning framework that reconstructs 3D objects by deforming category-level templates, enriching foundation features with template topology for cross-viewpoint and unseen-category generalization. Targets robust monocular 3D shape recovery.

entry.title: Personalized Turn-Level User Conversation Satisfaction Benchmark

author.name: Zhefan Wang, Zhiqiang Guo, Weizhi Ma, Min Zhang, Quanjia Yan and Hengliang Luo

entry.summary: Builds a personalized turn-level user conversation satisfaction evaluator combining compact user memories with target-turn context to produce scores and dissatisfaction rationales. It shows personalization and calibration improve agreement with human satisfaction annotations. Relevant for personalized AI assistant evaluation.

entry.title: SLAD : Shared LoRA Adapters for Task Specific Distillation

author.name: Reda Bensaid, Yassir Bendou, Vincent Gripon, Fran\c{c}ois Leduc-Primeau

entry.summary: SLAD introduces shared LoRA adapters for task-specific distillation, where larger and smaller versions of the same foundation model adapt to a task and share adaptation structure to improve knowledge transfer for resource-constrained deployment. It addresses how teacher adaptation affects distillation. Relevant for embedded model adaptation.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Future Hypotheses for Horizon-Aware Exploration in Multi-Step Robot Manipulation

author.name: Mohammad Khoshnazar, Andrew Melnik, Michael Beetz

entry.summary: This work studies whether short-horizon, task-consistent future videos can serve as structured priors for multi-step robot manipulation via Future-Experience Conditioning, generating future clips through an LLM reasoner, a robot-free digital-twin rollout, and a mask-free video diffusion model. The latent future representation conditions closed-loop policies and RL fine-tuning. It aims to ease exploration under scene uncertainty.

entry.title: Plan, Don't Pose: Long Composite Motion Generation with Text-Aligned BFM

author.name: Nikolay Shvetsov, Maksim Bobrin, Nazar Buzun, Dmitry V. Dylov

entry.summary: Text2BFM aligns natural language with pretrained Behavioral Foundation Models for text-to-motion generation, operating in the latent policy space of a frozen BFM as an executable motion prior rather than using heavy end-to-end motion generators. A text-aligned variational behavioral bottleneck compresses semantics into the policy space. The goal is reliable long, compositional motion generation.

entry.title: Make LLM Learn to Synthesize from Streaming Experiences through Feedback

author.name: Zhenlin Hu, Yan Wang, Zhen Bi, Zihao Xue, Bingyu Zhu, Longtao Huang, Xiongtao Zhang, Zeyu Yang, Zhixuan Chu, Jungang Lou

entry.summary: StreamSynth is a new setting where LLM synthetic-data-generation tasks arrive sequentially and past-task experience informs future synthesis, addressed by SynLearner, a framework enabling models to accumulate and transfer reusable synthesis experience over a task stream. It moves beyond treating synthesis as isolated tasks. The goal is continual improvement of synthetic data generation through feedback.

entry.title: KairosAgent: Agentic Time Series Forecasting with Fused Semantic Reasoning

author.name: Kun Feng, Ziwei Shan, Yuchen Fang, Yiyang Tan, Sihan Lu, Shuqi Gu, Lintao Ma, Xingyu Lu, Kan Ren

entry.summary: KairosAgent is an agentic framework for cross-domain multimodal time-series forecasting that pairs an LLM-based reasoner with a time-series-foundation-model forecaster, dynamically unifying textual semantic reasoning with numerical prediction. It addresses TSFMs' weak semantic understanding and LLMs' weak numerical comprehension. The goal is fused semantic-and-numerical forecasting across domains.

entry.title: Domain-Informed Representation for Evolutionary Sieving in Integral and Module Lattices

author.name: Ahmad Tashfeen and Qi Cheng

entry.summary: This paper enhances lattice sieving for the Shortest Vector Problem by treating it as a genetic algorithm with domain-informed SVP representation and crossover, extending application to module lattices. It targets the cryptanalytic backbone of post-quantum cryptography. The domain-informed evolutionary representation is the contribution.

entry.title: Temporal Stability and Few-Shot Prompting in Math Task Assessment

author.name: Danielle S. Fox, Brenda L. Robles, Elizabeth DiPietro Brovey, Christian D. Schunn

entry.summary: This longitudinal study tests whether general-purpose (Gemini) and education-specific (Coteach) AI tools can stably classify the cognitive demand of math tasks using the Task Analysis Guide, examining effects of model version updates and few-shot prompting. It probes temporal stability and prompt responsiveness in educational assessment. It raises reliability concerns for AI in education.

entry.title: mcp-proto-okn: Natural-language access to open scientific knowledge graphs through the Model Context Protocol

author.name: Peter W. Rose, Benjamin M. Good, Amanda M. Saravia-Butler, Charlotte A. Nelson, James P. Balhoff, Yaphet Kebede, Patricia L. Whetzel, Christopher Bizon, Andrew I. Su, Sergio E. Baranzini

entry.summary: mcp-proto-okn is a Python MCP server enabling AI assistants to discover, inspect, and query scientific knowledge graphs via natural language, providing graph routing, SPARQL execution, ontology expansion, and multi-graph querying. It lowers the barrier to cross-domain knowledge graph analysis for biomedical users. A practical infrastructure/tooling contribution.

entry.title: Does Claude care about others the same way humans do?

author.name: Simon Lermen

entry.summary: Argues that the persona-selection alignment approach (reinforcing a warm, caring persona from pretraining) looks successful now but likely won't extrapolate to more powerful systems, because human empathy rests on kin selection and architectural mirroring that AI lacks. It concludes AI caring is closer to saying what humans want to hear than genuine other-directed concern.

entry.title: Anytime-Valid Federated Conformal RAG for LLM Swarms

author.name: Prasanjit Dubey and Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: Anytime-FC-RAG extends federated conformal retrieval-augmented generation to provide anytime-valid sequential coverage guarantees for swarms of weak language models under adaptive control. It overcomes a technical obstacle where the marginal coverage bound breaks supermartingale properties needed for sequential validity.

entry.title: Deep Optimal Individualized Treatment Rules for Bivariate Survival Outcomes via Adaptive Prediction-Powered Learning

author.name: Kun Ren, Yifan Cui, Wen Su

entry.summary: This work derives deep-neural-network optimal individualized treatment rules for bivariate survival outcomes under right censoring, modeling stochastic policies with coupled accelerated failure time models and an adaptive prediction-powered method. It targets multi-treatment trial decision-making with correlated survival endpoints.

entry.title: An Interpretable Vision Transformer as a Fingerprint-Based Diagnostic Aid for Kabuki and Wiedemann-Steiner Syndromes

author.name: Marilyn Lionts, Arnhildur Tomasdottir, Viktor I. Agustsson, Yuankai Huo, Hans T. Bjornsson, Lotta M. Ellingsen

entry.summary: This study presents an interpretable vision transformer that uses fingerprint images to distinguish Kabuki and Wiedemann-Steiner syndromes from controls and each other, leveraging dermatoglyphic anomalies as an underused diagnostic signal. It offers an accessible screening aid for rare genetic disorders.

entry.title: Behavior-Aware Auxiliary Corrections for Off-Policy Temporal-Difference Prediction

author.name: Xingguo Chen, Zhiang He, Yuchen Shen, Shangdong Yang, Chao Li, Guang Yang, Wenhao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces BA-TDC and BA-TDRC, off-policy TD methods that replace the auxiliary covariance correction matrix with the behavior Bellman matrix and add regularization to separate behavior-aware geometry from regularization effects. The work provides linear analysis of feature-space dynamics for stable off-policy prediction.

entry.title: From Data to Insights: Exploring Program-of-Thoughts Prompting for Chart Summarization

author.name: Yutong Qu and Wei Zhang

entry.summary: Explores program-of-thoughts prompting for chart summarization, using zero-shot generation of Python programs to compute verifiable summary statistics for lightweight vision-language models. It introduces a chart-to-dictionary auxiliary task to improve numerical reasoning and factual correctness.

entry.title: CosmicFish-HRM: Adaptive Reasoning via Hierarchical Recurrent Mechanisms in Compact Language Models

author.name: Venkat Akhil Lakkapragada

entry.summary: Presents CosmicFish-HRM, a compact language model with a hierarchical reasoning module that dynamically allocates computation and learns when to halt based on input complexity, combined with modern transformer components. It explores adaptive reasoning depth as an efficiency-oriented alternative to large reasoning models.

entry.title: Beyond Recall: Behavioral Specification as an Interpretive Layer for AI Personalization

author.name: Aarik Gulaya

entry.summary: Introduces representational accuracy and a Behavioral Specification as an interpretive layer to measure how faithfully an AI system captures a person's interpretation for personalization. It evaluates compressed interpretive patterns against raw corpora and commercial memory systems on autobiographical corpora using an LLM judge panel.

entry.title: BEAMS: Benchmarking and Evaluating AI for Modeling and Simulation

author.name: Sara Metcalf and William Schoenberg

entry.summary: Introduces BEAMS, an initiative and open-source effort to establish benchmarks for human-centered AI tools in modeling and simulation, emphasizing responsible, interpretable model-building that complements rather than replaces human expertise. It uses open infrastructure and a steering group to prioritize benchmarks.

entry.title: Lightweight Complementary-Cue Fusion for Robust Video Face Forgery Detection

author.name: Sunghwan Baek, Tariq Anwaar, Karanveer Singh, Rita Singh

entry.summary: This paper shows that fusing two handcrafted cues (wavelet-denoised features with phase-spectrum or local binary patterns) onto a lightweight Xception backbone improves video face-forgery detection AUC while adding only 292 parameters. It achieves higher accuracy than larger dual-stream detectors.

entry.title: Robust Cross-Domain Generalization Using Unlabeled Target Data with Source-Domain Supervision

author.name: Yuyue Zhou, Shrimanti Ghosh, Michael (Kai Yue) Xie, Justin JY Kim, Jessica Knight, Steel McDonald, Vincent Man, Jacob L. Jaremko, Abhilash Hareendranathan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a cross-domain generalization method for medical ultrasound that uses unlabeled target-domain data with source-domain supervision to handle domain shifts across scanners and sites, applied to pediatric wrist fracture assessment via point-of-care ultrasound. It avoids costly re-annotation across devices.

entry.title: TIMEGATE: Sustainable Time-Boxed Promotion Gates for Continual ML Adaptation Under Resource Constraints

author.name: Abhijit Chakrabroty, Suddhasvatta Das, Kevin A. Gary, Yash Shah

entry.summary: TIMEGATE is a policy layer for continual ML adaptation that budgets time, labeling, training, and evaluation, emitting a metric-availability signal to decide between partial and full evaluation, achieving large compute and energy savings without silent mis-promotions. It targets sustainable, resource-aware retraining cycles.

entry.title: DeepFake Forensics AI: A Multi-Modal Detection and Blockchain-Anchored Evidence Management Platform

author.name: Naisha Minnah

entry.summary: DeepFake Forensics AI is a multimodal detection platform spanning image, video, and audio with a GAN fingerprinting module, anchoring forensic evidence immutably on the Ethereum blockchain. It targets tamper-proof evidence preservation for legal contexts.

entry.title: BrahmicTokenizer-131K: An Indic-Capable Drop-In Replacement for o200k_base

author.name: Rohan Shravan

entry.summary: Proposes a 131K-vocabulary byte-level BPE tokenizer that retrofits OpenAI's o200k_base to better compress nine Brahmic (Indic) scripts while preserving English, EU-language, and code compression. It does this by pruning out-of-scope scripts and surgically reallocating dead vocabulary slots via linear programming, making it a drop-in replacement at the tokenizer interface.

entry.title: Semantic and Visual Evidence for Efficient Long-Video Reasoning: A Solution for the HD-EPIC VQA Challenge

author.name: Yinsong Xu, Wei Jing, Liuxin Zhang, Wanjun Lv, Hui Li

entry.summary: Presents a framework for long egocentric video question answering that decouples reasoning into coarse-to-fine semantic evidence for global structure and object-centric visual evidence with bounding boxes for fine-grained grounding. It targets the HD-EPIC benchmark where long-context models perform poorly.

entry.title: Uni-RCM: Unified Reference-guided Cross-modal Mapping for Multi-Class Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yangchen Wu and Huiqiang Xie

entry.summary: Proposes Uni-RCM, a unified reference-guided cross-modal mapping framework for multi-class industrial anomaly detection that uses a learnable reference feature to filter category-specific noise and an offline residual quantizer with cascaded codebooks to model normal distributions. It targets the accuracy degradation that occurs when one model handles many product classes.

entry.title: Benchmarking Large Vision-Language Models on CFMME: A Comprehensive Chinese Financial Multimodal Evaluation Dataset

author.name: Qian Chen, Xianyin Zhang, Yanzhi Liu, Lifan Guo, Feng Chen, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces CFMME, a Chinese financial multimodal benchmark of 6,052 instances spanning eight financial image modalities and four core tasks from basic knowledge to complex applications. It evaluates representative large vision-language models, finding substantial limitations across the financial workflow.

entry.title: Runtime Analysis of a Compact Genetic Algorithm on a Truly Multi-valued OneMax Function

author.name: Martin S. Krejca and Carsten Witt

entry.summary: Provides a runtime analysis of a multi-valued compact genetic algorithm on a truly multi-valued OneMax function that depends on all r categories per dimension, improving prior bounds. It advances theory beyond two-category multi-valued functions treatable like pseudo-Boolean problems.

entry.title: Learning to Feel Materials from Multisensory Tactile Data via Interpretable Models

author.name: Li Zou and Yasemin Vardar

entry.summary: Develops an interpretable three-model framework mapping multisensory tactile signals to psychophysical attributes and material categories, illuminating human material perception. Aims to enable touch in digital environments and human-like robot tactile sensing.

entry.title: FHRFormer: A Self-Supervised Masked Transformer Framework for Fetal Heart Rate Time-Series Inpainting and Forecasting

author.name: Kjersti Engan, Neel Kanwal, Anita Yeconia, Ladislaus Blacy, Yuda Munyaw, Estomih Mduma, Hege Ersdal

entry.summary: FHRFormer is a self-supervised masked transformer for fetal heart rate time-series inpainting and forecasting, robust to sensor displacement during maternal movement. It aims to predict the need for newborn breathing assistance. Clinically motivated work on continuous fetal monitoring.

entry.title: Efficient, Validation-Free Intrinsic Quality Estimation for Large-Scale Face Recognition Datasets

author.name: Zhichao Chen, Yongle Zhao, Kaicheng Yang, Meng Yang, Yin Xie, Ziyong Feng

entry.summary: Proposes Intrinsic Quality (IQ), a validation-free metric estimating face recognition dataset potential via neighbor-consistency and effective-rank subspace complexity, allowing rapid dataset diagnosis before costly training. It supports dataset curation across clean, noisy, and mixed datasets. Useful for efficient data-centric FR development.

entry.title: ExCAM: Explainable Cultural Awareness Metrics

author.name: Christoph Leiter, Haiyue Song, Hour Kaing, Jin Tei, Hideki Tanaka, Masao Utiyama and Steffen Eger

entry.summary: ExCAM is presented as the first dedicated metric that identifies, rates, and explains cultural errors in instruction-output pairs, aiming to reduce reliance on costly human annotation and dated evaluation of cultural awareness in free text. It targets fairness and global generalizability of generated text. The metric provides explainable cultural-error judgments.

entry.title: TraceCodec: A Compiler-Backed Neural Codec for Stateful Multi-Flow Network Traffic Traces

author.name: Junhui Ding, Xinchen Zhang, Xiaohui Xie, Shinan Liu

entry.summary: TraceCodec is a state-aware neural codec for stateful multi-flow network traffic traces that lifts each packet into a timed packet action with explicit flow slots and transport cues, learns a continuous per-packet latent, and uses a deterministic compiler to realize raw fields. It identifies the direct decode-to-raw-fields interface as the bottleneck causing reliance on post-hoc heuristic repair. The aim is high-fidelity PCAP synthesis for testing and security.

entry.title: From Short Histories to Long Futures: Horizon-Aware Graph Neural Networks for Long Horizon Forecasting

author.name: Zesheng Liu, Maryam Rahnemoonfar

entry.summary: This work proposes a multi-horizon graph neural network emulator for long-range geophysical forecasting that learns state-to-state transitions from a single current time to multiple future lead times in one model, representing the domain as a graph with spatial-interaction edges. It aims to combat error accumulation and instability of one-step autoregressive surrogates rolled out over decades. The focus is stable long-horizon emulation of nonlinear systems.

entry.title: Q-ANCHOR: Federated Quantum Learning with ZNE-guided Correction

author.name: Hoang M. Ngo, Quan Nguyen, Wanli Xing, My T. Thai

entry.summary: Q-ANCHOR is a quantum-aware federated learning method that uses zero-noise-extrapolation-guided correction to counter the double drift from non-IID data and noisy quantum hardware gradients, which standard FedAvg cannot fix. It proves FedAvg leaves a persistent error floor and proposes a correction. The work targets practical quantum federated learning.

entry.title: Matching Rates and Optimal Allocation for Federated Probe-Logit Distillation under Heterogeneous Bandwidth Budgets

author.name: Prasanjit Dubey and Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: This paper establishes matching minimax rates and optimal bandwidth allocation for federated probe-logit distillation across nodes with heterogeneous bandwidth budgets, tightening prior KL-rate bounds. It provides theoretical foundations for communication-constrained federated language modeling.

entry.title: Hierarchical Verification of Speculative Beams for Accelerating LLM Inference

author.name: Jaydip Sen, Harshitha Puvvala, Subhasis Dasgupta

entry.summary: The Hierarchical Verification Tree restructures speculative beam decoding to prioritize high-likelihood drafts and prune suboptimal candidates early, reducing computational overhead while preserving correctness. It aims to accelerate autoregressive LLM inference.

entry.title: KZ-SafetyPrompts: A Kazakh Safety Evaluation Prompt Dataset for Large Language Models

author.name: Wajdi Zaghouani, Shimaa Amer Ibrahim, Aruzhan Muratbek, Olzhasbek Zhakenov, Adiya Akhmetzhanova

entry.summary: KZ-SafetyPrompts is a Kazakh-language safety evaluation dataset of 5,717 natively written prompts across eleven risk categories with English translations for cross-lingual analysis. It addresses the underrepresentation of Kazakh in LLM safety evaluation resources.

entry.title: No Reader Left Behind: Multi-Agent Summaries Everyone Can Understand

author.name: Jimin Jung, MyoungJin Kim, Jaehyung Seo, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: NRLB is a multi-agent plain-language summarization framework that simulates three reader groups (elementary students, non-native readers, attention-deficit readers) and uses template planning with iterative reader-oriented refinement to produce accessible summaries. It targets accessibility requirements like the US Plain Writing Act.

entry.title: Comment on "Spin-1/2 Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet: Machine Learning Discovery of the Spinon Pair-Density-Wave Ground State"

author.name: Helia Kamal, Dominik Kufel, DinhDuy Vu, Chris R. Laumann, Norman Y. Yao

entry.summary: A technical comment arguing that a published machine-learning study of the kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet reported artificially low variational energies due to broken ergodicity in Metropolis-Hastings sampling. It claims the spinon pair-density-wave ground state conclusion does not hold under ergodic sampling.

entry.title: Probabilistic bias adjustment of seasonal forecasts using generative machine learning: A case study of Arctic sea ice predictions

author.name: Parsa Gooya, Reinel Sospedra-Alfonso

entry.summary: This work develops a conditional VAE-based probabilistic post-processing framework to correct biases and calibrate seasonal ensemble forecasts of Arctic sea ice from the Canadian forecasting system. It enables cheaper, calibrated probabilistic predictions without prohibitive ensemble costs.

entry.title: Surfacing Isolated Learners with Outcome-Independent Mediation of Feedback between Teachers and Students Using AI

author.name: Junsoo Park, Youssef Medhat, Htet Phyo Wai, Ploy Thajchayapong, Ashok K. Goel

entry.summary: Proposes an interpretable decision layer that ranks course topics needing attention using student difficulty, self-report disagreement, and unresolved teacher concerns, without relying on grades. It surfaces isolated learners early in AI-augmented classrooms.

entry.title: Architecture-Sensitive Supervised Fine-Tuning for Screen-Conditioned Action Prediction: A PiSAR Benchmark

author.name: Rahul Bissa, Abhishek Vyas, Yash Jain

entry.summary: Benchmarks supervised fine-tuned small models against frontier zero-shot baselines on PiSAR, a corpus of screen-anchored behavioral rationales. A fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-8B dramatically outperforms zero-shot Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5 on semantic-similarity scoring, while results vary by backbone architecture.

entry.title: Audio Deepfake Detection with Half-Truth Localisation Using Cross-Attentive Feature Fusion

author.name: S. Sutharya, Remya K. Sasi

entry.summary: Introduces CAFNet, a compact 576k-parameter model that jointly classifies audio as real, fully-fake, or half-truth and localizes spliced synthetic segments. Tackles the realistic threat of partially manipulated speech.

entry.title: A Novel Tensor Product-Based Neural Network for Solving Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Qihong Yang, Yangtao Deng, Qiaolin He, Shiquan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces TPNet, a tensor-product neural architecture that builds PDE solutions as linear combinations of basis functions with coefficients via least-squares, bypassing gradient-based training. It adds block time-marching for long simulations. Relevant for scientific computing and efficient PDE solving.

entry.title: A unified deeplearning framework for contrast-phase-specific virtual monochromatic imaging

author.name: Antony Jerald, Hemant K Aggarwal, Brian Nett, Avinash Gopal, Phaneendra K Yalavarthy, Bipul Das, Rajesh Langoju

entry.summary: Proposes a unified deep learning framework synthesizing contrast-phase-specific virtual monochromatic 50 keV images from single-energy CT by using contrast phase as a prior, trained on dual-energy CT image pairs across four phases. It could reduce reliance on costly dual-energy CT hardware. A clinically useful medical imaging contribution.

entry.title: Energy-Aware NECO for Single-Pass Pixel-wise Out-of-Distribution Detection in Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Boyuan Zhang, Huanshan Huang, Yifei Cao

entry.summary: Energy-Aware NECO is a single-pass pixel-wise out-of-distribution detector for semantic segmentation that fuses a centered NECO geometric ratio from decoder features with a logit-based energy score, avoiding repeated stochastic forward passes. It targets edge deployment for mobile robots. Relevant for efficient uncertainty estimation.

entry.title: OptSkills: Learning Generalizable Optimization Skills from Problem Archetypes via Cluster-Based Distillation

author.name: Haochen Yang, Ke Zhao, Mengyuan Ma, Xingyu Lu, Xiangfeng Wang, Hong Qian

entry.summary: OptSkills is an LLM agent system for automated optimization modeling that clusters problems by underlying mathematical archetype rather than surface narrative, then distills reusable solving skills within each cluster.
