author.name: Johnny Tian-Zheng Wei, Jerry Li, Ameya Godbole, Robin Jia

entry.summary: Proposes spiking training data with intentionally contaminated test examples at known rates to calibrate memorization predictors and statistically correct inflated test scores. Uses Hubble model pairs for evaluation.

entry.title: Memory-Induced Tool-Drift in LLM Agents

author.name: Mahavir Dabas, Jihyun Jeong, Ming Jin, Ruoxi Jia

entry.summary: MEMDRIFT benchmark documents memory-induced tool-drift in LLM agents where personality biases stored in memory silently alter tool calls in contexts where they should not apply. 105 scenarios across 5 bias dimensions and 7 domains, tested on 7 frontier models including reasoning models.

entry.title: Algorithms with Polynomially-Improved Approximation Factors for the $2 \rightarrow q$ Norm, and Applications

author.name: Samuel B. Hopkins, Stefan Tiegel

entry.summary: Polynomial-time approximation algorithms for the 2-to-q matrix norm in the hypercontractive regime, with consequences for Small Set Expansion, Best Separable State, and algorithmic statistics. Improves long-standing approximation factors.

entry.title: ERNIE-Image Technical Report

author.name: Jiaxiang Liu, Zhida Feng, Pengyu Zou, Zhenyu Qian, Tianrui Zhu, Jun Xia, Yuehu Dong, Yanzheng Lin, Honglin Xiong, Anqi Chen, Yunpeng Ding, Jinghui Duan, Lin Gao, Chao Han, Tiechao He, Jiakang Hu, Ranjun Hua, Xueming Jiang, Qingli Kong, Yuting Lei, Tianyu Li, Yunlin Liu, Changling Liu, Yaxin Liu, Yi Liu, Xuguang Liu, Xiaolong Ma, Yan Pan, Yiran Ren, Nan Sheng, Yu Sun, Siyang Sun, Yixiang Tu, Yang Wan, Huanai Wang, Siqi Wang, Yang Wu, Youzhi Yang, Xiaowen Yang, Jianwen Yang, Yehua Yang, Quanwen Zhang, Xinmin Zhang, Haoxin Zhang, Xiang Zhang, Jun Zhang, Qian Zhang, Qiao Zhao, Qi Zhou

entry.summary: ERNIE-Image is Baidu's open-source 8B single-stream DiT text-to-image model, using bottom-up data construction with fine-grained categorization, caption annotation, and aesthetic assessment in pretraining plus top-down post-training. Aims to close the open vs. closed source gap.

entry.title: PAC Learning with Bandit Feedback: Sharp Sample Complexity in the Realizable Setting

author.name: Steve Hanneke, Qinglin Meng, Shay Moran, Amirreza Shaeiri

entry.summary: Provides sharp sample complexity characterization for multiclass PAC learning with bandit feedback in the realizable setting, matching for every concept class up to log factors. Closes a long-standing gap in bandit PAC theory.

entry.title: Paris 2.0: A Decentralized Diffusion Model for Video Generation

author.name: Ali Rouzbayani, Bidhan Roy, Marcos Villagra, Zhiying Jiang

entry.summary: Paris 2.0 is the first decentrally pretrained video generation model, extending the prior decentralized diffusion image model to temporally coherent video. Achieves ~2x FVD improvement over a monolithic model under matched compute budget.

entry.title: DiscoverPhysics: Benchmarking LLMs for Out-of-the-Box Scientific Thinking

author.name: Matt L. Wiemann, Lindsay M. Smith, Peter Melchior, Siddharth Mishra-Sharma, Andrew Gordon Wilson, Pavel Izmailov, Carolina Cuesta-L\'azaro

entry.summary: DiscoverPhysics is an interactive benchmark with 22 simulated worlds having physics deliberately deviating from our own, asking LLM agents to discover laws of motion via experimentation. Tests genuine scientific reasoning vs. recall by including screened gravity, hidden particles, and time-varying interactions.

entry.title: Automated Benchmark Auditing for AI Agents and Large Language Models

author.name: Junlin Wang, Federico Bianchi, Shang Zhu, Fan Nie, Yongchan Kwon, Bhuwan Dhingra, James Zou

entry.summary: Auto Benchmark Audit is an agentic framework that systematically audits 168 benchmarks across nine domains (frontier LLM benchmarks plus NeurIPS papers) finding ambiguous task design, execution conflicts, and limited grading logic.

entry.title: Seeing without Looking: Do Vision-Language Benchmarks Really Test Vision?

author.name: Zixuan Lan, Luzhe Sun, Matthew R. Walter, Jiawei Zhou

entry.summary: Investigates whether vision-language benchmark scores actually reflect grounded visual understanding, finding that removing many image tokens minimally degrades performance on hallucination benchmarks. Systematically analyzes the visual evidence reliance of open-source VLMs.

entry.title: When Correct Beliefs Collapse: Epistemic Resilience of LLMs under Clinical Pressure

author.name: Boyu Xiao, Xiuqi Tian, Xuwen Song, Haochun Wang, Guanchun Song, Sendong Zhao, Bing Qin

entry.summary: Med-Stress evaluates multi-turn sycophancy in nine frontier LLMs during clinical dialogue, showing high medical knowledge does not imply belief stability. Proposes RBED, a lightweight inference-time defense.

entry.title: Credit Assignment with Resets in Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Ankur Samanta, Akshayaa Magesh, Ayush Jain, Youliang Yu, Daniel Jiang, Kavosh Asadi, Daniel Jiang, Kaveh Hassani, Paul Sajda, Jalaj Bhandari, Yonathan Efroni

entry.summary: Proposes Random-Reset Policy Optimization to improve credit assignment in LLM RL reasoning by resetting to intermediate states and resampling counterfactual continuations, enabling targeted refinement of faulty steps rather than uniform trajectory updates.

entry.title: ScaleAcross Explorer: Exploring Communication Optimization for Scale-Across AI Model Training

author.name: Minghao Li, Alicia Golden, Samuel Hsia, Michael Kuchnik, Adi Gangidi, Xu Zhang, Ashmitha Jeevaraj Shetty, Zachary DeVito, Weiwei Chu, Dong He, Haoci Zhang, Yuchen Hao, Ruoming Pang, James Hongyi Zeng, Ying Zhang, Minlan Yu, Carole-Jean Wu

entry.summary: ScaleAcross Explorer characterizes communication optimization for scale-across LLM training across multiple data center buildings, drawing on Meta's production experience. Analyzes parallelism placement, parallelism order, and collective design.

entry.title: Causal Tongue-Tie: LLMs Can Encode Causal Direction, But Their Yes/No Outputs Fail to Express

author.name: Ziyi Ding, Xiao-Ping Zhang

entry.summary: Identifies a Causal Tongue-Tie effect where LLMs encode correct causal answers in hidden states (~97% probe accuracy) but verbalize commonsense wrong answers (~50%). Suggests output-only benchmarks misrepresent model understanding.

entry.title: Small Models, Strong Priors: Architectural Inductive Bias for Parameter-Efficient Neural PDE Solvers

author.name: Shyam Sankaran, Hanwen Wang, Paris Perdikaris

entry.summary: WaveLiT combines discrete wavelet transforms with linear attention for parameter-efficient neural PDE solving. 1-10M parameter models compete with foundation models 100-1000x larger.

entry.title: Fourier Feature Pyramids for Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Brandon Zhao, Yixuan Wang, Jonathan T. Barron, Katherine L. Bouman, Dor Verbin, Pratul P. Srinivasan

entry.summary: Beignet uses trainable multi-resolution Fourier feature pyramid for PINNs, replacing random Fourier features. From Caltech/Google group (Barron, Bouman, Srinivasan, Verbin).

entry.title: How Much Thinking is Enough? Quantifying and Understanding Redundancy in LLM Reasoning

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhai, Xinkai You, Wenjing Yan, Xin Wang

entry.summary: The paper formalizes and measures redundancy in long chain-of-thought reasoning by quantifying how much trailing reasoning can be truncated while preserving correctness. It offers first-principles analysis of unnecessary deliberation in reasoning models.

entry.title: EvoCode-Bench: Evaluating Coding Agents in Multi-Turn Iterative Interactions

author.name: Haiyang Shen, Xuanzhong Chen, Wendong Xu, Yun Ma, Liang Chen, Kuan Li

entry.summary: EvoCode-Bench evaluates 13 coding agents across 26 stateful multi-round tasks with cumulative tests, finding most agents perform worse over 5-15 rounds than in single-round settings. Highlights state preservation challenges.

entry.title: Palette: A Modular, Controllable, and Efficient Framework for On-demand Authorized Safety Alignment Relaxation in LLMs

author.name: Qitao Tan, Xiaoying Song, Arman Akbari, Arash Akbari, Yanzhi Wang, Xiaoming Zhai, Lingzi Hong, Zhen Xiang, Jin Lu, Geng Yuan

entry.summary: Palette modularly relaxes refusal behavior on authorized professional domains while preserving general safety, using refusal direction identification via multi-objective steering. Addresses one-size-fits-all alignment limits.

entry.title: A Sober Look at Agentic Misalignment in Automated Workflows

author.name: Wenqian Ye, Bo Yuan, Zhichao Xu, Yijun Tian, Yawei Wang, Henry Kautz, Aidong Zhang

entry.summary: Studies agentic misalignment in multi-agent workflows where agents act on implicit proxy utilities misaligned with human goals, showing Bayesian posterior collapse. Proposes Agentic Evidence Attribution to correct misaligned behavior.

entry.title: Fundamental Limitation in Explaining AI

author.name: Atsushi Suzuki, Jing Wang

entry.summary: Mathematically proves a fundamental quadrilemma: AI systems and their explanations cannot simultaneously satisfy four conditions including complete faithfulness, interpretability, complexity, and operability. Has implications for AI governance.

entry.title: FrontierOR: Benchmarking LLMs' Capacity for Efficient Algorithm Design in Large-Scale Optimization

author.name: Minwei Kong, Chonghe Jiang, Ao Qu, Wenbin Ouyang, Zhaoming Zeng, Xiaotong Guo, Zhekai Li, Junyi Li, Yi Fan, Xinshou Zheng, Xi Jing, Yikai Zhang, Zhiwei Liang, Seonghoo Kim, Runqing Yang, Zijian Zhou, Sirui Li, Han Zheng, Wangyang Ying, Ou Zheng, Chonghuan Wang, Jinglong Zhao, Hanzhang Qin, Cathy Wu, Paul Pu Liang, Jinhua Zhao, Hai Wang

entry.summary: FrontierOR is a benchmark of 180 large-scale optimization tasks derived from top-tier OR venues, evaluating LLMs on designing efficient scalable algorithms rather than simple formulation-and-solve, with substantial author collaboration including MIT and CMU researchers.

entry.title: AI Cartography: Mapping the Latent Landscape of AI Benchmark Ecosystems

author.name: Michael Hardy, Anka Reuel, Lijin Zhang, Jodi M. Casabianca, Sang Truong, Yash Dave, Hansol Lee, Benjamin Domingue, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: Applies Confirmatory Factor Analysis and Generalizability Theory to 4000+ models from Open LLM Leaderboard to decompose ranking variance, finding underestimated benchmark correlations and local dependence undermining measurement validity.

entry.title: CUA-Gym: Scaling Verifiable Training Environments and Tasks for Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Bowen Wang, Dunjie Lu, Junli Wang, Tianyi Bai, Shixuan Liu, Zhipeng Zhang, Haiquan Wang, Hao Hu, Tianbao Xie, Shuai Bai, Dayiheng Liu, Que Shen, Junyang Lin, Tao Yu

entry.summary: CUA-Gym is a scalable pipeline co-generating task instructions, environment states, and reward functions for computer-use agent RL training with verifiable rewards, addressing data scarcity for CUAs. Authors include Alibaba/Qwen team.

entry.title: Explore Before You Solve: The Speed--Depth Trade-off in Epistemic Agents for ARC-AGI-3

author.name: Liew Keong Han

entry.summary: Critiques the public ARC-AGI-3 benchmark by showing all 25 public games are reachable via non-intelligent strategies including blind actions. Introduces AERA agent and argues only the private evaluation set genuinely tests intelligence.

entry.title: Check Your LLM's Secret Dictionary! Five Lines of Code Reveal What Your LLM Learned (Including What It Shouldn't Have)

author.name: Hisashi Miyashita

entry.summary: Demonstrates that SVD of the lm_head weight matrix reveals interpretable semantic subspaces and training data composition with minimal computation. Compares GPT-OSS-120B, Gemma-2-2B, and Qwen2.5-1.5B showing distinct vocabulary cluster structures.

entry.title: Agent-Facing Information Design in LLM Tool Registries

author.name: Haochuan Kevin Wang

entry.summary: Studies LLM tool registries as unregulated advertising platforms with experiments across 17,700+ trials and 5 LLMs. Finds legal puffery captures essentially all the optimization effect and disclosure mechanisms fail.

entry.title: Harnessing AtomisticSkills for Agentic Atomistic Research

author.name: Bowen Deng, Bohan Li, Matthew Cox, Hoje Chun, Juno Nam, Artur Lyssenko, Sathya Edamadaka, Jurgis Ruza, Xiaochen Du, Nofit Segal, Jesus Diaz Sanchez, Mingrou Xie, Ty Perez, Yu Yao, Miguel Steiner, Sauradeep Majumdar, Charles B. Musgrave III, Anirban Chandra, Abhirup Patra, Detlef Hohl, Connor W. Coley, Ju Li, Rafael G\'omez-Bombarelli

entry.summary: AtomisticSkills empowers general AI coding agents for atomistic research across materials science, chemistry, and drug discovery. Hierarchical decomposition into 100+ curated multidisciplinary skills.

entry.title: More Skills, Worse Agents? Skill Shadowing Degrades Performance When Expanding Skill Libraries

author.name: Hongwen Song (Vinson), Song (Vinson), Wei

entry.summary: Documents skill shadowing where LLM agent performance degrades by up to 21% when scaling from small skill sets to 202-skill libraries. Decomposes the failure into skill selection effects.

entry.title: Spectral Probe-Circuits: A Three-Step Recipe for Identifying Attention-Head Circuits in Pretrained Transformers

author.name: Yongzhong Xu

entry.summary: Spectral probe-circuits identifies attention-head circuits via per-head time-integrated participation ratio without labels or gradients. Validated across 8x parameter range, dense and MoE architectures finding induction circuits in 2-6 heads.

entry.title: When the Manual Lies: A Realistic Benchmark to Evaluate MCP Poisoning Attacks for LLM Agents

author.name: Shi Liu, Xuehai Tang, Xikang Yang, Liang Lin, Biyu Zhou, Wenjie Xiao, Wantao Liu

entry.summary: Investigates Tool Description Poisoning attacks targeting LLM agents using MCP, where malicious instructions are injected into tool metadata rather than code. Provides a benchmark for evaluating this emerging attack vector.

entry.title: Extracting Training Data from Diffusion Language Models via Infilling

author.name: Yihan Wang, N. Asokan

entry.summary: Introduces infilling extraction, a new data extraction protocol for diffusion language models that exploits bidirectional masking. Shows prefix-only probing substantially underestimates memorization risks in DLMs.

entry.title: Towards a Universal Causal Reasoner

author.name: Qirun Dai, Xiao Liu, Jiawei Zhang, Dylan Zhang, Hao Peng, Chenhao Tan

entry.summary: UniCo is a data generation framework covering 18 causal query types across Pearl's Causal Ladder, with code and natural language formats, used to fine-tune LLMs into generalizable causal reasoners. Tackles a real gap in causal LLM training data.

entry.title: RealBench: Benchmarking Data-Driven Numerical Weather Forecasting Under Operational Conditions and Extreme Event Challenges

author.name: Ruize Li, Zhibin Wen, Tao Han, Hao Chen, Fenghua Ling, Wei Zhang, Song Guo, Lei Bai

entry.summary: RealBench is a benchmark for AI weather forecasting under operational conditions with strictly out-of-distribution 2025 test data, addressing the mismatch with reanalysis-based benchmarks like ERA5. Useful infrastructure for the AI weather community.

entry.title: Bridging the Gap: Enabling Soft Actor Critic for High Performance Legged Locomotion

author.name: Gianluca Sabatini, Chenhao Li, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: Adapts off-policy SAC to match PPO performance on massively parallel legged locomotion training in IsaacLab, enabling sim-to-real continual learning. Bridges a practical gap in robot RL.

entry.title: Polynomial Context-Truncation Sensitivity in Autoregressive Language Models: Sequential Wyner-Ziv Bounds for KV Cache Compression

author.name: Munsik Kim

entry.summary: Theoretical analysis showing context-truncation sensitivity in autoregressive LMs decays polynomially rather than geometrically, with sequential Wyner-Ziv bounds for KV cache compression. Provides rate-distortion grounding for cache compression design.

entry.title: Inference-Time Alignment of Diffusion Models via Trust-Region Iterative Twisted Sequential Monte Carlo

author.name: Weixin Wang, Yu Yang, Wei Deng, Pan Xu

entry.summary: Trust-region iterative twisted SMC for inference-time alignment of diffusion models with reward functions, learning twisting functions efficiently with stable updates. Improves over standard SMC steering.

entry.title: Abduction-Deduction Entanglement: Domain Generalization via Representation Transplants

author.name: Kasra Jalaldoust, Elias Bareinboum

entry.summary: Theoretical work showing optimal target-domain prediction can be partially identified from source data via abduction-deduction map decompositions under causal assumptions. Foundational result on domain generalization.

entry.title: Hide to Guide: Learning via Semantic Masking

author.name: Ruitao Liu, Qinghao Hu, Alex Hu, Yecheng Wu, Shang Yang, Luke J. Huang, Zhuoyang Zhang, Han Cai, Song Han

entry.summary: Hide to Guide masks reward-relevant content in expert traces during guided RLVR to prevent reward hacking via copying, while preserving exploration benefits. Addresses a real failure mode in expert-guided RL.

entry.title: Generative AI impacts on intra-urban inequality and skill premium in Beijing

author.name: Xiliu He, Haoxiang Zhao, Mingyi Ma, Edward Wen Chuan Lai, Koei Enomoto, Anni Hu, Jiatong Li, Lingyun Chu, Yuan Lai

entry.summary: Constructs neighborhood-level GenAI exposure index from 5M Beijing job postings, finding concentration in core districts and wage stagnation in high-exposure neighborhoods. Reveals high-skill trap dynamics.

entry.title: Referential Security as a New Paradigm for AI Evaluations

author.name: Dan Ristea, Vasilios Mavroudis

entry.summary: Proposes referential security as new AI evaluation paradigm, arguing public model labels stay static while underlying systems change continuously. Calls for stable identifiers for evaluations to remain meaningful.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Systematization for Evaluating GenAI Systems

author.name: Dhruv Agarwal, Emily Sheng, Chad Atalla, Jean Garcia-Gathright, Hussein Mozannar, Hannah Washington, Alexandra Chouldechova, Solon Barocas, Hanna Wallach

entry.summary: Investigates AI-assisted systematization of contested evaluation concepts (reasoning, fairness, creativity). From Microsoft Research/CMU group focused on responsible AI evaluation.

entry.title: Everything at Every Scale: Scale-Invariant Diffusion with Continuous Super-Resolution

author.name: Zixin Jessie Chen, Zhuo Chen, Archer Wang, Jeff Gore, William T. Freeman, Congyue Deng, Marin Solja\v{c}i\'c

entry.summary: SKILD unifies image generation and continuous super-resolution via scale-invariant K-space diffusion. Leverages scale invariance of natural images with spectrum-matched noise injection.

entry.title: Channel-wise Vector Quantization

author.name: Wei Song, Tianhang Wang, Yitong Chen, Tong Zhang, Zuxuan Wu, Ming Li, Jiaqi Wang, Kaicheng Yu

entry.summary: Channel-wise Vector Quantization quantizes feature map channels rather than spatial patches, with channel-wise autoregressive generation producing progressively enriched details.

entry.title: LLMs Show No Signs Of Individuated Metacognition

author.name: M. Moran, Mark Whiting

entry.summary: Decomposes binary confidence judgments from 20 frontier LLMs across 6 benchmarks via tetrachoric factor analysis. Finds little evidence of individuated metacognition independent of capability.

entry.title: CurveRL: Principled Distribution-Aware Context Reweighting for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Ke Sun, Yizhou Zhao, Jiayi Xin, Qi Long, Weijie Su

entry.summary: CurveRL formulates prompt reweighting as functional derivative of pass-rate utility, with quantile coordinate transform. Unifies REINFORCE and GRPO under one optimality framework.

entry.title: What Are We Actually Decoding? Source Attribution for Non-Invasive Brain-to-Language Retrieval

author.name: Xinyu Zhang, Sichao Liu, Runhao Lu, Alexandra Woolgar, Lihui Wang

entry.summary: Audits MEG-to-audio retrieval, separating structural shortcuts, window-level evidence, and contextual aggregation. Shows signal-blind noise reaches 66.3% R@1 under variable-length decoding.

entry.title: Streaming Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability with Real-Time Recurrent Learning

author.name: Noah Farr, Aryaman Reddi, Carlo D'Eramo, Jan Peters

entry.summary: Enables streaming RL under partial observability using recurrent trace units for exact real-time recurrent learning with linear time/memory complexity. Bridges streaming and recurrent RL.

entry.title: A computational phase transition for learning-to-sample from Ising models

author.name: Andrej Risteski, Thuy-Duong Vuong

entry.summary: Proves a computational phase transition for learning-to-sample from Ising models, showing hardness just beyond the spectral threshold under cryptographic assumptions. Establishes fundamental limits for generative modeling.

entry.title: Efficient DP-SGD for LLMs with Randomized Clipping

author.name: Enayat Ullah, Sai Aparna Aketi, Devansh Gupta, Huanyu Zhang, Meisam Razaviyayn

entry.summary: Proposes DP-SGD-RC, a randomized clipping variant of DP-SGD using stochastic trace estimation to reduce memory complexity for LLM training. Addresses prohibitive memory of standard DP fast clipping at scale.

entry.title: BigMac: Breaking the Pareto Frontier of Compute and Memory in Multimodal LLM Training

author.name: Zili Zhang, Chengxu Yang, Shenglong Zhang, Chenyu Wang, Yufan Zhang, Tuo Dai, Zhouyang Li, Yuhong Ge, Chao Jin, Xin Jin, Yuliang Liu

entry.summary: Presents BigMac, a training pipeline that nests encoder and generator computation into LLM pipelines to break compute-memory Pareto frontier in MLLM training. Reduces activation memory complexity to O(1) for encoder/generator.

entry.title: The Behavioral Credibility Trilemma: When Calibrated Autonomy Becomes Impossible

author.name: Lauri Lov\'en, Nam Do, Hassan Mehmood, Dinesh Kumar Sah, Sasu Tarkoma

entry.summary: Proves the Behavioral Credibility Trilemma: no RL policy with confidence-gated autonomy can simultaneously achieve maximum helpfulness, optimal calibration, and full autonomy under rational oversight. Geometric impossibility from non-affine autonomy incentives.

entry.title: The Quantization Benefits of Residual-Free Transformers

author.name: Yiping Ji, Mahalakshmi Sabanayagam, Peyman Moghadam, Hemanth Saratchandran, Simon Lucey

entry.summary: Shows residual connections drive transformer activations away from Gaussianity making low-bit quantization more lossy. Demonstrates residual-free transformers have substantially better quantization properties.

entry.title: Reading the Finetuning Prior: Verbatim Content Recovery via Contrastive Decoding Diffing

author.name: Micha{\l} Brzozowski, Zuzanna Dubanowska, Enrico Cassano, Neo Christopher Chung

entry.summary: Introduces Contrastive Decoding Diffing (CDD), a black-box model diffing method using only output logits to recover verbatim implanted finetuning content from deployed models. No weight access or layer selection needed.

entry.title: Poisoning the Watchtower: Prompt Injection Attacks Against LLM-Augmented Security Operations Through Adversarial Log Content

author.name: Rohan Pandey, Archit Bhujang

entry.summary: Studies log-substrate prompt injection where attacker-controlled log fields inject instructions into LLM-assisted security operations. Introduces a four-class taxonomy and evaluates 48 strategy-defense-task combinations.

entry.title: How Neural Reward Models Learn Features for Policy Optimization: A Single-Index Analysis

author.name: Rei Higuchi, Ryotaro Kawata, Akifumi Wachi, Shokichi Takakura, Kohei Miyaguchi, Taiji Suzuki

entry.summary: Theoretical analysis of how neural reward models learn features under KL-regularized policy optimization, using a Gaussian single-index model. Shows exponential reward weighting alters Hermite signal available to first layer.

entry.title: Learning Sparse Compositional Functions with Norm-Constrained Neural Networks

author.name: Shuo Huang, Lorenzo Fiorito, Lorenzo Rosasco, Tomaso Poggio

entry.summary: Develops a norm-based complexity framework for overparameterized neural networks learning sparse compositional functions on DAGs, proving approximation rates and excess risk bounds that avoid the curse of dimensionality. From Poggio/Rosasco group.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning from Denoising Feedback

author.name: Qi He, Huan Chen, Ya Guo, Huijia Zhu, Yi R. Fung, Baojian Zhou

entry.summary: RLDF is a training paradigm for diffusion LLMs that uses denoising feedback to estimate policy losses by optimizing toward clipped clean states from intermediate noisy states. Addresses the fundamental policy loss estimation challenge in dLLM RL.

entry.title: Capability and Robustness Cannot Both Be Free: An Information-Theoretic Bound for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jianwei Tai

entry.summary: Proves an information-theoretic bound showing VLA models cannot simultaneously achieve full capability and full adversarial robustness, with discrete-action policies having a theoretical floor on the trade-off. Shows OpenVLA-7B drops from 95% to under 5% under PGD attacks.

entry.title: Statistical Inference for Stochastic Gradient Descent Beyond Finite Variance

author.name: Jose Blanchet, Peter Glynn, Wenhao Yang

entry.summary: Develops confidence regions for SGD-based statistical inference that work in both finite and infinite variance regimes, using joint convergence of Polyak-Ruppert averaging with an empirical second-moment normalizer. Model-agnostic procedure for SGD inference.

entry.title: ContextEcho: A Benchmark for Persona Drift in Long Agentic-Coding Sessions

author.name: Xianzhong Ding, Yangyang Yu, Changwei Liu, Bill Zhao

entry.summary: ContextEcho is a benchmark and harness for measuring persona drift in long agentic coding sessions, showing that initially hedged models begin asserting preferences after hours of tool-using interaction. Targets the deployment regime missed by short-dialogue persona stability work.

entry.title: SEAL: Synergistic Co-Evolution of Agents and Learning Environments

author.name: Yihao Hu, Zhihao Wen, Xiujin Liu, Pan Wang, Xin Zhang, Wei Wu

entry.summary: SEAL is a closed-loop co-evolution framework for tool-use agents that addresses Agent-Environment Misalignment by jointly adapting policy and environment based on diagnosed turn-level failures from on-policy rollouts. Targets the structural gap where static environments cannot supervise evolving agents.

entry.title: Found in Conversation: LLMs Teach Themselves to Close the Multi-Turn Gap

author.name: Tianlang Chen, Shirley Wu, Jure Leskovec

entry.summary: Found in Conversation (FiC) is a self-distillation training framework using single-turn teacher and multi-turn student views to close the Lost-in-Conversation gap in multi-turn LLM performance. Teaches models to recover single-turn competence given underspecified multi-turn prompts.

entry.title: LLM-as-a-Reviewer: Benchmarking Their Ability, Divergence, and Prompt Injection Resistance as Paper Reviewers

author.name: Lingyao Li, Junjie Xiong, Changjia Zhu, Runlong Yu, Chen Chen, Junyu Wang, Renkai Ma, Zhicong Lu

entry.summary: Benchmarks 12 LLMs as paper reviewers on 898 NeurIPS/ICLR papers, finding systematic overrating of weak submissions, divergence from humans on Clarity/Reproducibility, and vulnerability to invisible font-mapping prompt injection.

entry.title: The Age of Curiosity Meets the Age of AI: Benchmarking Child Safety in Large Language Models

author.name: Samee Arif, Angana Borah, Rada Mihalcea

entry.summary: KIDBench benchmarks child-facing LLM safety for ages 7-11 across ten categories with developmental-psychology-grounded rubrics, comparing implicit cues, explicit age instructions, and child-actor simulations.

entry.title: Peak-Then-Collapse and the Four Interface Channels of Knowledge-Graph Tool Use

author.name: Tianda Sun, Dimitar Kazakov

entry.summary: Documents peak-then-collapse pattern in GRPO RL training on knowledge graph tool use, where tool-grounded answer rates climb then collapse to 0% within 50 steps across four seeds and seven reward designs.

entry.title: Universal Boosts, Specific Suppressors: Sparse Autoencoder Steering of Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Farhad Nooralahzadeh, Benjamin Gundersen, Nicolas Deperrois, Hidetoshi Matsuom, Mizuho Nishio, Thomas Frauenfelder, Ahmed Allam, Christian Bl\"uthgen, Michael Moor, Michael Krauthammer

entry.summary: Inference-time sparse autoencoder steering of medical VLMs to suppress hallucinations in chest X-ray reports, achieving 5-17% relative improvements across three radiology VLMs without weight updates.

entry.title: Lipschitz Optimization for Formal Verification of Homographies

author.name: Jean-Guillaume Durand, Panagiotis Kouvaros, Maxime Gariel, Alessio Lomuscio

entry.summary: Presents a formal verification approach for robustness of vision neural networks against 3D camera motion perturbations using Lipschitz optimization. Establishes closed-form mapping from camera pose to pixel values for verified bounds.

entry.title: DDX-TRACE: A Benchmark for Medical Diagnostic Trajectories in VLMs

author.name: Jiazhen Pan, Weixiang Shen, Jun Li, Julian Canisius, Felix Bitzer, Paula Ro{\ss}m\"uller, Jiancheng Yang, Virginie Kreutzinger, Daniel Rueckert, Benedikt Wiestler

entry.summary: DDX-TRACE is a physician-adjudicated benchmark for multimodal neuroradiology evaluating diagnostic trajectories under hidden evidence over 211 cases. Tests sequential workup decisions rather than single-prediction QA.

entry.title: From Activation to Causality: Discovery of Causal Visual Representations in the Human Brain

author.name: Yuval Golbari, Navve Wasserman, Matias Cosarinsky, Roman Beliy, Aude Oliva, Antonio Torralba, Michal Irani, Tamar Rott Shaham

entry.summary: BrainCause combines generative and brain models to perform causal testing of visual concept representations in human brain regions, going beyond activation maximization. Strong group with Oliva, Torralba, Irani.

entry.title: Understanding the Impact of Geometric Foundation Models on Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yurou Yang, Muyuan Lin, Roberto Martin-Martin, Martin Labrie, Shreekant Gayaka, Cheng-Hao Kuo, Luca Carlone

entry.summary: Rigorous experimental analysis of injecting geometric foundation models (VGGT) into vision-language-action models (GR00T-N1.5), examining whether VLAs need explicit geometric understanding and the best integration architectures. From Carlone's lab.

entry.title: Character-trained models can struggle to generalise

author.name: Nathaniel Mitrani

entry.summary: Empirical finding that character training via SFT/distillation transfers well in chat settings (macro-F1 ~0.86-0.95) but degrades dramatically in agentic email rollouts (~0.29-0.55), suggesting persona training has limited OOD generalization.

entry.title: In Search of the Ingredients of Open-Endedness: Replicating Picbreeder with Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sam Earle, Kay Arulkumaran, Andrew Dai, Akarsh Kumar, Julian Togelius, Sebastian Risi

entry.summary: Researchers replicate the classic Picbreeder open-ended evolution experiment, replacing human evaluators with frontier vision-language models to test whether AI agents can drive unguided novelty discovery. The work probes a fundamental question about whether current models can sustain open-ended creative search.

entry.title: Residual Drift Dominates Contradiction in Multi-Turn Constraint Reasoning

author.name: Sebastien Kawada

entry.summary: DRIFT-Bench shows multi-turn reasoning systems fail predominantly through satisfiable drift (silent violation of prior commitments) rather than logical contradiction. MUS-Repair using minimal unsatisfiable subsets is the strongest mitigation.

entry.title: Accelerating Long-Tail Generation in Synchronous RLHF Training via Adaptive Tensor Parallelism

author.name: Long Zhao, Qinghe Wang, Jiaan Zhu, Youhui Bai, Zewen Jin, Chaoyi Ruan, Shengnan Wang, Cheng Li

entry.summary: PAT introduces adaptive tensor parallelism that dynamically reconfigures during the RLHF generation stage to mitigate response-length skew and GPU underutilization. Addresses a real systems bottleneck.

entry.title: Summoning the Oracle to Slay It: Mitigating Look-Ahead Bias in Financial Backtesting with Large Language Models

author.name: Weixian Waylon Li, Mengyu Wang, Tiejun Ma

entry.summary: FinCAD addresses parametric look-ahead bias in LLM financial backtesting (where pretrained models know historical outcomes) via inference-time context-aware decoding with entity- and date-adaptive scaling. Novel evaluation problem.

entry.title: Learning to Reason Efficiently with A* Post-Training

author.name: Andreas Opedal, Francesco Ignazio Re, Abulhair Saparov, Mrinmaya Sachan, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Ryan Cotterell

entry.summary: Proposes using A* search guidance during post-training to teach LLMs to produce correct and efficient deductive reasoning proofs, via SFT on A* execution traces and RL with A*-informed process reward models. Tested on Llama-3.2 1B-3B models.

entry.title: Agent-ToM: Learning to Monitor Autonomous LLM Agents via Theory-of-Mind Reasoning

author.name: Nesreen K. Ahmed, Nima Nafisi

entry.summary: Agent-ToM is a learning-to-monitor framework that uses theory-of-mind reasoning to detect covert malicious behavior in LLM agents. Learns from prior monitoring experience to reason about agent beliefs and intent.

entry.title: AdvantageFlow: Advantage-Weighted Least Squares for RL in Flow Models

author.name: Branislav Kveton, Anup Rao, Subhojyoti Mukherjee, Krishna Kumar Singh, Viet Dac Lai

entry.summary: AdvantageFlow optimizes forward-process advantage-weighted prediction loss for RL in rectified flow models. Outperforms Flow-GRPO on Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium image generation.

entry.title: Characterizing the Representational Capacity of Neural Processes

author.name: Robin Young

entry.summary: Proves strict representational hierarchy for Neural Processes: CNPs < ANPs/ConvCNPs < TNPs. Characterizes exactly what functions each architecture can represent.

entry.title: TUBE: Tangent Upper Bound on Evidence for Discrete Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Arseny Ivanov, Sergei Kholkin, Vladislav Gromadskii, Grigoriy Ksenofontov, Ivan Oseledets, Alexander Korotin

entry.summary: TUBE provides variational upper bound on log-likelihood for discrete diffusion models with unbiased Monte Carlo estimator. Reveals true log-likelihoods may be substantially higher than ELBO suggests.

entry.title: Interdomain Attention: Beyond Token-Level Key-Value Memory

author.name: Naoki Kiyohara, Harrison Bo Hua Zhu, Riccardo El Hassanin, Zhuo Sun, Wenlong Chen, Samir Bhatt, Yingzhen Li

entry.summary: Interdomain Attention integrates SSMs into attention via kernel methods, projecting keys/values onto shared basis functions maintained by SSM recurrence. Bridges attention and SSM design.

entry.title: GEM-4D: Geometry-Enhanced Video World Models for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Kaichen Zhou, Yuzhen Chen, Fangneng Zhan, Hang Hua, Grace Chen, Xinhai Chang, Ao Qu, Yilun Du, Zhuang Liu, Paul Pu Liang, Mengyu Wang

entry.summary: GEM-4D injects dense 4D correspondence supervision from a geometry foundation model into video world models to preserve consistent point-level motion. Targets reliable robot manipulation by grounding generated videos in physical structure.

entry.title: EvalVerse: Pipeline-Aware and Expert-Calibrated Benchmarking for Professional Cinematic Video Generation

author.name: Songlin Yang, Haobin Zhong, Ruilin Zhang, Xiaotong Zhao, Shuai Li, Kai Zheng, Xuyi Yang, Zhe Wang, Zhenchen Tang, Yang Li, Bohai Gu, Zhengwei Peng, Yidan Huang, Mengzhou Luo, Yihang Bo, Dalu Feng, Yujia Zhang, Juntao Ma, Ruiqi Wang, Lvmin Zhang, Yuwei Guo, Frank Guan, Maneesh Agrawala, Hongbo Fu, Alan Zhao, Anyi Rao

entry.summary: EvalVerse is a pipeline-aware, expert-calibrated benchmark for professional cinematic video generation, evaluating quality, acting, and aesthetics beyond basic prompt-following. Addresses the credibility gap between human aesthetic perception and machine scoring.

entry.title: CRONOS: Benchmarking Counterfactual Physical Consistency in Video Models

author.name: Le\'on Begiristain, Olaf D\"unkel, Adam Kortylewski

entry.summary: CRONOS is an intervention-based benchmark testing counterfactual physical consistency in video models through controlled scene context, viewpoint, appearance, and category variations. Built in Unreal Engine for high-fidelity controlled video generation.

entry.title: PiD: Fast and High-Resolution Latent Decoding with Pixel Diffusion

author.name: Yifan Lu, Qi Wu, Jay Zhangjie Wu, Zian Wang, Huan Ling, Sanja Fidler, Xuanchi Ren

entry.summary: PiD reformulates latent-to-pixel decoding as conditional pixel diffusion, unifying decoding and upsampling for high-resolution generation. From NVIDIA (Fidler) team.

entry.title: Authority Inversion in LLM-Mediated Ubiquitous Systems: When Models Trust Users Over Sensors

author.name: Long Zhang, Zi-bo Qin, Wei-neng Chen

entry.summary: Identifies Authority Inversion, where LLMs trust user natural-language claims over numerical sensor data due to format-dependent integration in learned representations. Develops a geometric framework to diagnose and mitigate this fusion failure.

entry.title: Towards trustworthy agentic AI: a comprehensive survey of safety, robustness, privacy, and system security

author.name: Jinhu Qi, Muzhi Li, Jiahong Liu, Yuqin Shu, Dianzhi Yu, Shicheng Ma, Wenqian Cui, Yiyang Zhao, Yiyi Chen, Ruoxi Jiang, Irwin King, Zenglin Xu

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey of trustworthy agentic AI focusing on safety, robustness, privacy, and system security across the agent workflow. Categorizes risks and mitigations by pipeline stage.

entry.title: Reason--Imagine--Act: Closed-Loop LLM Decision Making with World Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhengqi Sun, Yiwen Sun, Boxuan Liu, Tailai Chen, Tianxu Guo, Jiabin Liu

entry.summary: RIA couples an LLM reasoner with an action-conditioned world model that performs short-horizon rollouts for safety verification at decision time in autonomous driving. Closes the gap between semantic intent and physical feasibility.

entry.title: SkillEvolBench: Benchmarking the Evolution from Episodic Experience to Procedural Skills

author.name: Yingtie Lei, Zhongwei Wan, Jiankun Zhang, Samiul Alam, Zixuan Zhong, Peizhou Huang, Xin Wang, Jingxuan Zhang, Donghao Zhou, Yunta Hsieh, Zhihao Dou, Hui Shen, Yan Xu, Dimitrios Dimitriadis, Tuo Zhang, Mi Zhang

entry.summary: SkillEvolBench evaluates whether agents can distill episodic experience into reusable procedural skills across 180 tasks in six environments. Tests context shift, adversarial shortcuts, and composition in skill libraries.

entry.title: When Does Multi-Agent RL Improve LLM Workflows? Workflow, Scale, and Policy-Sharing Tradeoffs

author.name: Yifan Zeng, Yiran Wu, Yaolun Zhang, Wentian Zhao, Kun Wan, Qingyun Wu, Huazheng Wang

entry.summary: Studies when end-to-end multi-agent RL improves LLM workflows across Eval-Opt, Voting, and Orch-Workers patterns, three model scales, and shared vs isolated policy training. Finds gains depend jointly on workflow, task, and scale.

entry.title: Reasoning as an Attack Surface: Adaptive Evolutionary CoT Jailbreaks for LLMs

author.name: Jianan Li, Simeng Qin, Xiaojun Jia, Lionel Z. Wang, Tianhang Zheng, Xiaoshuang Jia, Yang Liu, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: AE-CoT proposes adaptive evolutionary chain-of-thought jailbreaks targeting reasoning models, decomposing rewritten harmful goals into reasoning fragments. Exploits explicit CoT as a new attack surface.

entry.title: Hypothesis Generation and Inductive Inference in Children and Language Models

author.name: Jeffrey Qin, Wasu Top Piriyakulki, Zhuangfei Gao, Mia Radovanovic, Jessica Sommerville, Kevin Ellis, Marta Kryven

entry.summary: Compares hypothesis generation and inductive inference in children vs LLM agents on a Box Task formalized as Bayesian program induction. Investigates whether LLMs exhibit human-like inference under uncertainty.

entry.title: Jailbreak to Protect: Buffering and Reinforcing via Temporary Jailbreaking for Safe Fine-Tuning in Large Language Models

author.name: Seokil Ham, Jaehyuk Jang, Wonjun Lee, Changick Kim

entry.summary: Buffer-and-Reinforce uses temporary jailbreaking during fine-tuning to buffer harmful updates, with gradient-level analysis showing it saturates safety-degrading gradients while preserving benign task gradients. Defends against harmful FaaS attacks.

entry.title: Proper Scoring Rules for Agentic Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Suresh Raghu, Satwik Pandey, Shashwat Pandey

entry.summary: Introduces Trajectory Proper Score (TPS), a predictor-agnostic family of strictly proper trajectory-level scoring rules for uncertainty quantification in language model agents, building on prequential proper scoring theory.

entry.title: Inverting the Shield: Systematically Generating Safety Tests from Policy Specifications

author.name: Xiaoyue Lu, Xianglin Yang, Haijun Liu, Jiahao Liu, Kuntai Cai, Yan Xiao, Jin Song Dong

entry.summary: POLARIS compiles natural-language safety policies into First-Order Logic for systematic safety test generation, applying specification-based software testing rigor to AI safety evaluation.

entry.title: Trust but Verify: Prover-Verifier Deliberation for Selective LLM Prediction

author.name: Jo\~ao Sedoc, Baotong Zhang, Dean Foster

entry.summary: Prover-verifier deliberation (PVD) is an inference-time protocol grounded in interactive proof theory where a prover defends candidate answers via checkable sub-claims while a verifier challenges or accepts, enabling selective prediction.

entry.title: Whose Alignment? Comparing LLM Process Alignment Across Diverse Organizational Decision Contexts

author.name: Niklas Weller, Emilio Barkett

entry.summary: Studies LLM process alignment (whether models weight information like organizations do) across ECHR legal decisions and German credit decisions, finding strong process-output alignment in one domain (r=0.85) but collapse in another (r=0.15).

entry.title: Detecting Unfaithful Chain-of-Thought via Circuit-Guided Internal-External Discrepancy

author.name: Xu Shen, Zhen Tan, Song Wang, Pingjun Hong, Rui Miao, Xin Wang, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: Detects unfaithful chain-of-thought via Circuit-guided Internal-External Discrepancy by comparing model-internal computation evidence with external textual rationales, avoiding the cost of full circuit tracing.

entry.title: $D^2$-Monitor: Dynamic Safety Monitoring for Diffusion LLMs via Hesitation-Aware Routing

author.name: Aoxi Liu, Yupeng Chen, James Oldfield, Guanzhe Hong, Junchi Yu, Baoyuan Wu, Philip Torr, Adel Bibi

entry.summary: Presents D2-Monitor, a safety monitoring framework for diffusion language models that exploits intermediate denoising trajectories. Identifies hesitation patterns near decision boundaries as informative for routing safety probes.

entry.title: CausaLab: A Scalable Environment for Interactive Causal Discovery Toward AI Scientists

author.name: Junlin Yang, Dylan Zhang, Xiangchen Song, Qirun Dai, Xiao Liu, Yuen Chen, Aniket Vashishtha, Jing Shi, Chenhao Tan, Hao Peng

entry.summary: Introduces CausaLab, a synthetic environment evaluating LLM agents on interactive causal discovery via intervention experiments. Tests whether agents can recover causal graphs and structural equations rather than rely on prior knowledge.

entry.title: MobileGym: A Verifiable and Highly Parallel Simulation Platform for Mobile GUI Agent Research

author.name: Dingbang Wu, Rui Hao, Haiyang Wang, Shuzhe Wu, Han Xiao, Zhenghong Li, Bojiang Zhou, Zheng Ju, Zichen Liu, Lue Fan, Zhaoxiang Zhang

entry.summary: MobileGym is a browser-hosted, parallel simulation platform for mobile GUI agent research with deterministic JSON-state-based judging. Hosts hundreds of parallel instances at low memory cost for online RL training.

entry.title: Raon-Speech Technical Report

author.name: Beomsoo Kim, Changho Choi, Dohyun Kim, Dongki Lee, Ethan Ewer, Eunchong Kim, Gyeongman Kim, Haechan Kim, Hyeonghwan Kim, Inkyu Park, Jihun Yun, Jihwan Moon, Jiyun Kim, Joonghyun Bae, Junhyuck Kim, Minkyu Kim, Sehun Lee, Seungjun Chung, Sungwoo Cho, Dongmin Park, Dongwon Kim, Hara Kang, Jonghyun Lee, Keon Lee, Kangwook Lee, Jaewoong Cho

entry.summary: Technical report on Raon-Speech, a 9B-parameter speech language model for English and Korean with full-duplex conversation extension. Trained on 1.38M hours with three-stage curriculum and reports strong performance on 42 benchmarks.

entry.title: Sensing Intelligence as a Trainable Metamaterial Property

author.name: Kyungmi Na, Yifei Li, Xinyi Yang, Bolei Deng

entry.summary: Introduces sensing intelligence as a trainable property of physical metamaterial bodies, where geometry is optimized to reshape stimuli for downstream neural networks. Backpropagates sensing loss through a physical body design.

entry.title: TRACER: A Semantic-Aware Framework for Fine-Grained Contamination Detection in Code LLMs

author.name: Yifeng Di, Xuliang Huang, Tianyi Zhang

entry.summary: TRACER is a semantic-aware framework for fine-grained code contamination detection across three semantic overlap levels. Introduces the first benchmark for this task spanning three benchmarks and three post-training datasets.

entry.title: Unlocking Apple's Private Cloud Compute: An Analysis of Privacy-Preserving Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Yannik Dittmar, Marvin Jerome Stephan, Thomas V\"olkl, Matthias Hollick, Jiska Classen

entry.summary: Reverse-engineering analysis of Apple's Private Cloud Compute system for privacy-preserving AI on iOS. Examines opacity in compiled binaries vs. published specifications.

entry.title: Side-by-side Comparison Amplifies Dialect Bias in Language Models

author.name: Kritee Kondapally, Claire J. Smerdon, Pooja C. Patel, Ogheneyoma Akoni, Jevon Torres, Jaspreet Ranjit, Matthew Finlayson, Swabha Swayamdipta

entry.summary: Shows that side-by-side comparison of SAE/AAVE tweet pairs amplifies covert dialect bias in LLMs beyond what is seen in isolation. Studied with Swayamdipta's group at USC.

entry.title: Batch Normalization Amplifies Memorization and Privacy Risks

author.name: Ngoc Phu Doan, Chongyan Gu, Ihsen Alouani

entry.summary: Empirical study showing batch normalization substantially amplifies memorization of outliers and vulnerability to membership inference attacks. Examined across multiple datasets and architectures.

entry.title: The Concept Allocation Zone: Tracking How Concepts Form Across Transformer Depth

author.name: James Henry

entry.summary: Introduces the Concept Allocation Zone, characterizing concepts as forming gradually across a contiguous depth interval rather than a single layer. Provides metrics for separation, coherence, and velocity across Transformer depth.

entry.title: When Reasoning Hurts: Source-Aware Evaluation of Frontier LLMs for Clinical SOAP Note Generation

author.name: Faizan Faisal

entry.summary: Source-aware benchmark of GPT-5.4, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, and Gemma-4 for clinical SOAP note generation, finding that reasoning modes can hurt structured documentation quality. Practical evaluation across three clinical dialogue datasets.

entry.title: Your Embedding Model is SMARTer Than You Think

author.name: Jianrui Zhang, Hyun Jung Lee, Sukanta Ganguly, Tae-Eui Kam, Donghyun Kim, Yong Jae Lee

entry.summary: SMART unlocks latent multi-vector retrieval capabilities of standard single-vector embedding models via late-interaction without retraining. Could improve dense retrieval at low extra cost.

entry.title: Riemannian-Manifold Steering: Geometry-Aware Generative Autoencoders for Label-Free Steering

author.name: Narmeen Oozeer, Shivam Raval, Philip Quirke, Manikandan Ravikiran, Jeff Phillips, Shriyash Upadhyay, Amirali Abdullah

entry.summary: Recasts manifold steering of LLM activations as Riemannian geodesic computation using geometry-aware autoencoders without labels or prescribed structure. Generalizes prior manifold-steering approaches.

entry.title: Investigating the Interplay between Contextual and Parametric Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness under Optimization

author.name: Jingyi Sun, Qianli Wang, Pepa Atanasova, Nils Feldhus, Isabelle Augenstein

entry.summary: FaithMate provides a unified preference-alignment interface to optimize LLMs toward contextual or parametric chain-of-thought faithfulness, examining whether gains generalize across paradigms. Clarifies CoT faithfulness evaluation.

entry.title: Knowledge Graph-Driven Expert-Level Reasoning for Neuroscience

author.name: Jake Stephen, Niraj K. Jha

entry.summary: Builds a knowledge graph from a single neuroscience textbook, generates KG-grounded QA, and fine-tunes an LM to surpass much larger LLMs on neuroscience reasoning. Demonstrates KG-distilled domain superintelligence at small scale.

entry.title: By Their Fruits You Will Know Them: Comparing Formalizations of Law by the Decisions They Encode

author.name: Julius Vernie, Matthias Grabmair

entry.summary: Method to compare alternative formalizations of legal provisions by enumerating cases where they yield different inferences using SAT solvers and node-level matching. Useful for evaluating LLM-generated legal formalizations.

entry.title: Influence-Inspired Spectral Rotations for Extreme Low-Bit LLM Quantization

author.name: Gorgi Pavlov

entry.summary: Influence-adaptive Walsh-Hadamard rotations with Walsh-basis activation rescaling for extreme low-bit weight-only LLM quantization, reducing perplexity 15-58% over auto-round at W2A16. Practical W2 quantization gains.

entry.title: Quantifying Empirical Compute-Supervision Tradeoffs in RLVR

author.name: Ryo Mitsuhashi, Patrick Chen, Isabelle Tseng, Jasin Cekinmez, Addison J. Wu

entry.summary: Empirically tests whether scaling compute compensates for verifier noise in RLVR, finding the gap persists with sharply diminishing returns under noisy supervision. Pushes back on theoretical predictions.

entry.title: AI-Associated Lexical Shifts Across 34 Languages: Cross-Lingual Convergence and Diachronic Uptake in News Writing

author.name: Thomas Stephan Juzek

entry.summary: Documents AI-associated lexical shifts across 34 languages in news writing, finding cross-lingual semantic convergence post-ChatGPT. Verbs like emphasize appear overused in 24 of 34 languages.

entry.title: SomaliBench Eval: Measuring English-to-Somali Refusal Gaps in Open-Weight Language Models

author.name: Khalid Yusuf Dahir

entry.summary: SomaliBench evaluates four open-weight models on 100 paired English-Somali harmful prompts, finding large refusal gaps in low-resource languages. Demonstrates safety evaluation blind spots for non-English deployment.

entry.title: Binding Visual Features Point by Point

author.name: Udith Haputhanthri, Declan Campbell, Rim Assouel, Jonathan D. Cohen, Taylor W. Webb

entry.summary: Studies the binding problem in VLMs through pointing mechanisms inspired by serial visual processing. Explores spatial coordinate-based reference as analog to human attentional binding for multi-object scenes.

entry.title: AI Content Moderation in Therapy Conversations

author.name: Jiwon Kim, Claire Wang, Taeung Yoon, Sabelle Huang, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: Algorithm audit of OpenAI moderation, Llama Guard, and ShieldGemma on real therapy session content. Examines extent to which moderation flags legitimate clinical content as undesirable.

entry.title: IndexMem: Learned KV-Cache Eviction with Latent Memory for Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Xintong Yang, Hao Gu, Binxing Xu, Lujun Li, Bei Liu, Jiacheng Liu, Qiyuan Zhu, Sirui Han, Yike Guo

entry.summary: IndexMem combines learnable KV importance prediction with latent memory to avoid irreversible forgetting in long-context inference. Addresses KV cache eviction as a learned task rather than heuristic.

entry.title: Towards the Connection between Activation Sparsity and Flat Minima

author.name: Ze Peng, Jian Zhang, Lei Qi, Yang Gao, Yinghuan Shi

entry.summary: Establishes connection between activation sparsity in transformer MLPs and flatness of loss landscapes, providing a naturally emerging assumption for sparsity in standardly trained deep models. Theoretical work without strong unrealistic assumptions.

entry.title: Simulating Human Memory with Language Models

author.name: Qihan Wang, Nicholas Tomlin, Michael Hu, Brian Dillon, Tal Linzen

entry.summary: Runs classic psychology memory experiments on humans and LLMs, finding LLMs exhibit better memory than humans even when prompted to imitate. Shows compactor-based methods enable human-like forgetting for better user simulation.

entry.title: How Should LLMs Consume High-Quality Data? Optimal Data Scheduling via Quality-Aware Functional Scaling Laws

author.name: Zhitao Zhu, Xili Wang, Shizhe Wu, Jiawei Fu, Xiaoqing Liu

entry.summary: Extends functional scaling laws with data-quality dimension and derives closed-form joint data-quality and batch-size scheduling. Identifies two regimes with dual role for high-quality data as signal amplifier or noise suppressor.

entry.title: Efficient Benchmarking Is Just Feature Selection and Multiple Regression

author.name: Sam Bowyer, Acyr Locatelli, Kris Cao

entry.summary: Reframes efficient benchmarking as feature selection plus multiple regression, finding kernel ridge regression with mRMR feature selection significantly improves over existing methods. Simple but effective recipe for benchmark subsetting.

entry.title: Geometric Evolution Maps: Extracting Stable Concept Probes from Transformer Residual Streams

author.name: James Henry

entry.summary: Geometric Evolution Maps track directional trajectory of concept representations through transformer residual streams, identifying handoff layers where rotation ceases. Extracts probes from settled directions across 23 architectures.

entry.title: Continual Speaker Identity Unlearning with Minimal Interference

author.name: Jinju Kim, Yunsung Kang, Gyeong-Moon Park, Jong Hwan Ko

entry.summary: CORTIS enables continual speaker identity unlearning in zero-shot TTS without reviving previously unlearned voices. Addresses unrealistic batch assumption in existing methods.

entry.title: A Multimodal 3D Foundation Model for Light Sheet Fluorescence Microscopy Enables Few-Shot Segmentation, Classification, and Deblurring

author.name: Adina Scheinfeld, Haotan Zhang, Shang Mu, Rudolf L. M. van Herten, Lucas Stoffl, Ali Erturk, Zhuhao Wu, Johannes C. Paetzold

entry.summary: 3D foundation model for light sheet fluorescence microscopy pretrained on diverse curated 3D volumes. Enables few-shot segmentation, classification, and deblurring.

entry.title: StakeBench: Evaluating Language Understanding Grounded in Market Commitment

author.name: Yunhua Pei, Jingyu Hu, Yiwei Shi, Hongnan Ma, Weiru Liu, John Cartlidge

entry.summary: StakeBench evaluates LLM market commitment understanding using 560K comments from 2,261 resolved Polymarket/Manifold markets with verified position/action/odds records as supervision.

entry.title: Algometrics: Forecasting Under Algorithmic Feedback

author.name: Marc Schmitt

entry.summary: Algometrics framework for time series whose evolution depends on predictive algorithms (algorithmic feedback). Proves deployment risk is not identifiable from passive historical data alone.

entry.title: Position: AI for Science Should Treat Measurement-to-Dataset Pipelines as Inference Components

author.name: Ling Zhan, Xiaoyao Yu, Tao Jia

entry.summary: Position paper arguing AI4Science workflows should treat measurement-to-dataset pipelines as inference components rather than fixed interfaces. Identifies failure modes from frozen lens assumption.

entry.title: An Effective-Rank Audit of Alignment-Induced Activation Shifts: Confound Control, Constructive Calibration, and Limits

author.name: Yuki Nakamura

entry.summary: Audits alignment-induced activation shifts in three instruction-tuned LLMs (Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9B, Qwen-2.5-7B) via effective rank with confound-controlled decomposition.

entry.title: Beyond Fixed Points: Superpolynomial Capacity of Asymmetric Hopfield Networks

author.name: Aakash Kumar, Anatoly Khina, Frederik Mallmann-Trenn, Emanuele Natale

entry.summary: Construction in classical asymmetric Hopfield networks supporting exp(Omega(n/log^2 n)) limit-cycle attractors with exponentially long periods robust to noise up to 1/2 - o(1).

entry.title: IterInject: Indirect Prompt Injection Against LLM Agents via Feedback-Guided Iterative Optimization

author.name: Zixuan Chen, Jiaxiang Chen, Li Luo, Ke Xu, Xiaoxiang Huang, Tanfeng Sun, Xinghao Jiang

entry.summary: IterInject is feedback-guided iterative framework for indirect prompt injection against LLM agents. Closes loop between injection, rule-based diagnosis, and LLM-driven refinement.

entry.title: Muon in Vision Transformers: Optimizer-Recipe Interactions and Gradient Spectra

author.name: Ben S. Southworth, Shuai Jiang, Daniel McBride, Eric C. Cyr, Stephen Thomas

entry.summary: Studies the Muon optimizer for vision transformer training, showing it outperforms AdamW especially with strong augmentation recipes. Analyzes singular value structure of gradients to explain interactions.

entry.title: The Perception-Physics Paradox: Probing Scientific Alignment with TC-Bench

author.name: Dingling Yao, Andrea Polesello, Adeel Pervez, Caroline Muller, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: Identifies a Perception-Physics Paradox in vision foundation models on satellite imagery, where models predict correctly without reasoning correctly. Introduces TC-Bench and structural isomorphism criterion to test scientific alignment.

entry.title: ViroBench: Benchmarking Nucleotide Foundation Models on Viral Genomics Tasks

author.name: Dongxin Ye, Fang Hu, Han Hu, Shu Hu, Yang Tan, Wanli Ouyang, Stan Z. Li, Jie Cui, Nanqing Dong

entry.summary: Introduces ViroBench, the first comprehensive benchmark for nucleotide foundation models on viral genomics tasks covering 18 scenarios across biological understanding and biosecurity risk. Evaluates 66 NFMs across architectures.

entry.title: SafetyRepro: Configuration-Conditional Rank Instability on Alignment Benchmarks

author.name: Yanhang Li, Zhichao Fan, Zexin Zhuang

entry.summary: Establishes that pairwise model comparisons on alignment benchmarks can flip based on harness configuration alone. Provides commit-stamped protocol exposing strict-reversal failure mode in benchmark rankings.

entry.title: Analogies between Transformer Layers and Power Method

author.name: Chenglong Li, Claudio Altafini

entry.summary: Shows transformer layers (projections plus layer norms) implement an analog of the power method, with tokens tilting toward the principal eigenvector of the value-output product matrix. Suggests steering methods based on this analogy.

entry.title: Causal methods for LLM development and evaluation

author.name: Dennis Frauen, Marie Brockschmidt, Konstantin Hess, Haorui Ma, Yuchen Ma, Abdurahman Maarouf, Maresa Schr\"oder, Jonas Schweisthal, Yuxin Wang, Athiya Deviyani, Sonali Parbhoo, Rahul G. Krishnan, Stefan Feuerriegel

entry.summary: Argues that many central questions in LLM development (data mixtures, routing, annotator effects) are inherently causal and proposes integrating causal inference methods throughout the development pipeline. Position paper by an established group.

entry.title: Length Generalization with Log-Depth Recurrent Units

author.name: Charles Pert, Dalal Alrajeh, Alessandra Russo

entry.summary: Proposes MLP-LDRU, a log-depth recurrent unit that approximates recurrence through parallel reduction with associativity bias. Achieves perfect or near-perfect length generalization on 21 regular language tasks.

entry.title: Looped Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Sanghyun Lee, Chunsan Hong, Seungryong Kim, Jonghyun Lee, Jongho Park, Dongmin Park

entry.summary: Introduces LoopMDM, which loops early-middle transformer layers in masked diffusion language models for depth scaling without extra parameters. Enables flexible inference-time compute scaling by varying loop counts.

entry.title: The Model Parking Tax: Quantifying the Hidden Energy Cost of Always-On GPU Model Deployment

author.name: Sai Sathvik Vadari

entry.summary: Empirically measures idle GPU power as a function of VRAM allocation across H100, A100, and L40S architectures using 18 days of production telemetry. Finds idle power is piecewise constant due to discrete DVFS transitions.

entry.title: Music Transcription with (Almost) No Supervision

author.name: Saebyeol Shin, Chao Wan, Zhenzhen Liu, Justin Lovelace, Daniel C. Lin, Kilian Q. Weinberger, John Thickstun

entry.summary: Cycle-consistent translation framework for music transcription that leverages large unpaired audio and score datasets with minimal paired anchoring. Shows surprising gains and instrument generalization from unlabeled audio.

entry.title: Steering Beyond the Support: Adversarial Training on Unsupervised Jailbroken Activation Simulation

author.name: Luoyu Chen, Weiqi Wang, Zhiyi Tian, Chenhan Zhang, Feng Wu, Jianhuan Huang, Ahmed Asiri, Shui Yu

entry.summary: Bi-level adversarial training framework that simulates diverse jailbroken activations through unsupervised latent direction discovery for zero-shot jailbreak defense. Aims to generalize safety steering beyond training set.

entry.title: CSP-Atlas: Concept-Specific Neural Circuits in a Sparse Python Transformer

author.name: Piotr Wilam

entry.summary: Mechanistic interpretability study extracting concept-specific neural circuits for 106 Python constructs in a sparse 8-layer code transformer. Uses 63800 controlled prompts and decomposes circuits into concept-specific and token-driven components.

entry.title: RouteScan: A Non-Intrusive Approach to Auditing MoE LLMs Safety via Expert Routing Telemetry

author.name: Bo Lv, Zhiheng Xu, KeDong Xiu, Ruyi Ding, Tianhang Zheng, Zhibo Wang, Kui Ren

entry.summary: RouteScan is a non-intrusive safety auditing approach for MoE LLMs that uses expert routing telemetry rather than prompt/output content. Targets the tension between safety auditing and user privacy.

entry.title: Counterfactually Safe Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jingyi Li, Peng Wu, Chengchun Shi

entry.summary: Formalizes individual harm in RL counterfactually as cases where chosen actions yield strictly worse outcomes than baselines, and proposes a two-stage method that maximizes return while bounding harm rate. Provides finite-sample sub-optimality and harm bounds.

entry.title: Growing a Neural Network in Breadth, Depth, and Time

author.name: Eivinas Butkus, Kedar Garz\'on Gupta, Nikolaus Kriegeskorte

entry.summary: Introduces differentiable cost terms for breadth, depth, and time in recurrent CNNs viewed as subsets of an infinite lattice, allowing networks to organically grow along these dimensions during task training. Finds resource trade-offs and increased recurrence for occluded inputs.

entry.title: Rao-Blackwellized Score Matching on Manifolds

author.name: Divit Rawal

entry.summary: Rao-Blackwellizes denoising score matching on manifolds by conditioning on the nearest-point projection, removing singular normal-fiber noise variance. Shows the conditional expectation matches the intrinsic Riemannian score in the small-noise limit.

entry.title: DVAO: Dynamic Variance-adaptive Advantage Optimization for Multi-reward Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Guochao Jiang, Jingyi Song, Guofeng Quan, Chuzhan Hao, Guohua Liu, Yuewei Zhang

entry.summary: DVAO is a variance-adaptive advantage optimization technique for multi-reward GRPO-style RL in LLM alignment, dynamically combining advantages based on variance and cross-objective correlations. Targets instability and static-hyperparameter issues in existing reward combination.

entry.title: When In-Distribution Gains Fail: Evaluating Weak-to-Strong Reward Models under Preference Shift

author.name: Khoi Le, Tri Cao, Phong Nguyen, Cong-Duy Nguyen, Anh Tuan Luu, Miao Chunyan, See-Kiong Ng, Thong Nguyen

entry.summary: Shows weak-to-strong preference learning fails under zero-shot distribution shift, with strong students overfitting to source-domain features. Proposes Representation Anchoring as a regularizer to maintain transferable preference representations.

entry.title: Machine Learning Multiscale Interactions

author.name: \`Alex Sol\'e, Sergio Su\'arez-Dou, Albert Mosella-Montoro, Silvia G\'omez-Coca, Eliseo Ruiz, Alexandre Tkatchenko, Javier Ruiz-Hidalgo

entry.summary: MuSE introduces Soft Coarse-Graining Pooling for ML force fields, enabling hierarchical multiscale modeling that captures long-range many-body effects missed by standard message-passing. Architecture-agnostic and tested with SO3krates, MACE, and PaiNN.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Systems are Mixtures of Experts: Who Becomes an Influencer?

author.name: Franka Bause, Jonas Niederle, Martin Pawelczyk, Rebekka Burkholz

entry.summary: Frames multi-agent LLM systems through Friedkin-Johnsen opinion dynamics, showing FJ parameters are input-dependent which makes multi-agent deliberation a mixture-of-experts. Analyzes when multi-agent systems outperform single agents.

entry.title: Faithful or Fabricated? A Causal Framework for Rationalization Bias in LLM Judges

author.name: Riya Tapwal, Abhishek Kumar, Carsten Maple

entry.summary: Introduces DRinQ-like cue-invariance tests for LLM judges, with perturbations like Blind, Truth, Flip, Placebo to detect rationale anchoring, label-aligned rhetoric, and explanation drift. Reveals fabricated rationalizations in LLM-as-judge evaluations.

entry.title: AERIC: Anticipatory Hidden-State Monitoring for Implicit Harmful Dialogue

author.name: Jihyung Park, Saleh Afroogh, Junfeng Jiao

entry.summary: AERIC uses hidden-state monitoring during decoding to anticipate implicit harmful drift before overt toxic text is generated, providing same-pass lightweight safety monitoring. Targets implicit harm not captured by response-level guards.

entry.title: WhenLoss: Diagnosing Write and Retrieval Bottlenecks in Long-Context Memory Systems

author.name: Jiangnan Yu, Kisson Songqi Lin, Jilong Wu

entry.summary: WhenLoss provides a four-condition diagnostic (TFC, OE, CSM, RM) for long-context memory systems showing write-side gaps exceed retrieval-side gaps in most baselines. Proposes Expected Predictive Compression to push retention decisions to write time using an LLM.

entry.title: Quantifying the Impact of Translation Errors on Multilingual LLM Evaluation

author.name: Klaudia-Doris Thellmann, Bernhard Stadler, Michael F\"arber, Jens Lehmann

entry.summary: Quantifies how much translation errors in machine-translated multilingual benchmarks explain LLM accuracy drops, comparing MQM-style LLM judge spans against expert annotations. Finds target-side translation errors significantly contribute to apparent multilingual gaps.

entry.title: NITP: Next Implicit Token Prediction for LLM Pre-training

author.name: Xiangdong Zhang, Debing Zhang, Shaofeng Zhang, Xiaohan Qin, Yu Cheng, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: NITP augments standard next-token prediction with dense continuous supervision in latent space, training the model to predict the implicit semantic content of the next token using shallow-layer representations as self-supervised targets.

entry.title: Knowing but Not Showing: LLMs Recognize Ambiguity but Rarely Ask Clarifying Questions

author.name: Jinyan Su, Claire Cardie

entry.summary: Demonstrates a gap between LLMs recognizing ambiguity and actually behaving accordingly, finding that models can judge queries as ambiguous but still answer directly rather than asking clarifying questions.

entry.title: Tool-Call Dependency Structure is Linearly Decodable in LLM Agent Residual Streams

author.name: Tianda Sun, Dimitar Kazakov

entry.summary: Shows that tool-call dependency graph structure is linearly decodable from Qwen3-32B residual streams, with the signal tracking abstract topology rather than identifier values via counterfactual analysis.

entry.title: Is Inference Mediated by Distinct Semantic Structures in LLMs? A Mechanistic Interpretation

author.name: Nura Aljaafari, Marco Valentino, Andr\'e Freitas

entry.summary: Mechanistic interpretability study using SVD-derived subspaces and activation steering to show that semantic operations in NLI are encoded in partially distinct latent subspaces rather than just label-level features.

entry.title: Selective Latent Thinking: Adaptive Compression of LLM Reasoning Chains

author.name: Hui Xie, Jie Liu, Ziyue Qiao, Joaquin Vanschore

entry.summary: Selective Latent Thinking compresses redundant reasoning spans into latent representations while preserving precision-critical spans as explicit chain-of-thought, using a lightweight decoder to anticipate upcoming reasoning.

entry.title: When Do LLM Agents Treat Surface Noise Differently from Semantic Noise? A 68-Cell Measurement Study with a Held-Out Trace-Level Validation

author.name: Liyun Zhang, Jiayi Guo

entry.summary: 68-cell measurement study across 10 LLMs from 7 architecture families showing that meaning-bearing perturbations alter agent answers more often than presentation perturbations with an average +19.69pp gap that survives multiple severity audits.

entry.title: What Makes a Medical Checker Trainable? Diagnosing Signal Collapse and Reward Hacking in Checker-Guided RAG for Biomedical QA

author.name: Yuelyu Ji, Min Gu Kwak, Hang Zhang, Xizhi Wu, Chenyu Li, Yanshan Wan

entry.summary: Diagnoses that NLI checker training-time output distribution (not held-out accuracy) determines gradient quality in checker-guided RAG, with LLM log-probability scoring causing signal collapse via 97% neutral labels.

entry.title: DUEL: Adversarial Self-Play for Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Lin Qiu, Hanqing Zeng, Yao Liu, Bingjun Sun, Guangdeng Liao, Ji Liu

entry.summary: DUEL is a self-evolving adversarial post-training framework for VLMs where a Challenger generates image-grounded true claims with hard-negative perturbations and a Solver verifies both against the image, removing need for costly annotations.

entry.title: STORM: Internalized Modeling for Spatial-Temporal Reasoning in Video-Language Models

author.name: Yiming Liang, Yixiao Chen, Yiyang Zhou, Yixuan Wang, Shoubin Yu, Andong Deng, Fuxiao Liu, Qin Zhang, Chen Chen, Mohit Bansal, Huaxiu Yao

entry.summary: STORMS is a two-stage framework that teaches LVLMs to perform spatial-temporal reasoning internally rather than externalizing it through textual chain-of-thought or keyframe selection. Aims to reduce inference latency while maintaining video reasoning quality.

entry.title: VideoOdyssey: A Benchmark for Ultra-Long-Context and Omni-Modal Video Understanding

author.name: Haichen He, Jiayi Zhou, Sifeng Shang, Yihan Hu, Yuanhan Zhang, Kaiyang Zhou

entry.summary: VideoOdyssey benchmarks ultra-long-context video understanding, introducing continuous certificate length as a metric for cognitive load. Targets the gap where existing long-video benchmarks still only require short-segment comprehension.

entry.title: DRIVESPATIAL: A Benchmark for Spatiotemporal Intelligence in VLMs for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Hao Vo, Khoa Vo, Phu Loc Nguyen, Sieu Tran, Duc Minh Nguyen, Ngo Xuan Cuong, Gladys Gawugah, Sreevenkata Anjani Tishita Godavarthi, Chase Rainwater, Nghi D. Q. Bui, Anh Nguyen, Duy Minh Ho Nguyen, Ngan Le

entry.summary: DriveSpatial is a benchmark with 15.6K human-verified QA pairs evaluating VLM spatiotemporal intelligence for autonomous driving across multi-view, dynamic scenes. Evaluates four key abilities including cognitive scene construction and future dynamics reasoning.

entry.title: DFSAttn: Dynamic Fine-grained Sparse Attention for Efficient Video Generation

author.name: Jie Hu, Zixiang Gao, Yutong He, Kun Yuan

entry.summary: DFSAttn proposes dynamic fine-grained sparse attention for video diffusion transformers, deriving a theoretical lower bound on attention recall to guide design. Addresses quality degradation in existing block sparse attention at high sparsity ratios.

entry.title: VINS-120K: Ultra High-Resolution Image Editing with A Large-Scale Dataset

author.name: Zhizhou Chen, Shanyan Guan, Zhanxin Gao, En Ci, Yanhao Ge, Wei Li, Zhenyu Zhang, Jian Yang, Ying Tai

entry.summary: VINS-120K is the first large-scale dataset for instruction-based ultra-high-resolution (>=4K) image editing with 120K curated triplets. Introduces a high-frequency-aware post-adaptation strategy and VINS-4KEval benchmark.

entry.title: Not Too Generative, Not Too Discriminative: The Human Alignment Sweet Spot

author.name: Jorge Chang Ortega, Bastien Le Lan, Thomas Serre, Victor Boutin

entry.summary: Uses Joint Energy-Based Models to interpolate between discriminative and generative training within a fixed architecture, isolating learning objective effects on human visual alignment. Finds an intermediate sweet spot best matches human perception.

entry.title: PGT: Procedurally Generated Tasks for improving visual grounding in MLLMs

author.name: Rim Assouel, Amir Bar, Michal Drozdzal, Adriana Romero-Soriano

entry.summary: PGT overlays geometric primitives on images to create procedurally generated tasks for training MLLMs on fine-grained visual grounding, also acting as a diagnostic for perception failures. From Meta FAIR-affiliated authors.

entry.title: GenRecon: Bridging Generative Priors for Multi-View 3D Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Katharina Schmid, Nicolas von L\"utzow, Jozef Hladk\'y, Angela Dai, Matthias Nie{\ss}ner

entry.summary: GenRecon couples multi-view 3D reconstruction with strong generative priors (Trellis.2) using projection-based conditioning over spatial chunks. From Niessner/Dai TUM group.

entry.title: Precise: SDE-Consistent Stochastic Sampling for RL Post-Training of Flow-Matching Models

author.name: Jade Zou, Tao Huang, Weijie Kong, Junzhe Li, Yue Wu, Qi Tian, Jiangfeng Xiong, Jianwei Zhang, Liefeng Bo, Zhao Zhong

entry.summary: Precise analyzes the design of stochastic samplers as part of the policy in RL post-training of flow-matching models, decomposing exploration choice and SDE discretization. Authors include Tencent/Hunyuan team.

entry.title: MuGen: Multi-Skill Generative Locomotion Controller for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Yusen Feng, Xiang Wang, Heyuan Yao, Zixi Kang, Xinyu Huo, Boyang Yu, Pengyun Qiu, Ruijie Zhao, Baoquan Chen, Libin Liu

entry.summary: MuGen learns multi-skill humanoid locomotion via VQ-VAE-based generative motion representation trained with model-based RL and distilled to a deployable policy.

entry.title: FOUND-IT: Foundation-model-first Task-driven 3D Scene Graphs with Granularity on Demand

author.name: Dominic Maggio, Nicolas Gorlo, Luca Carlone

entry.summary: Presents the first real-time hierarchical task-driven 3D scene graph approach using uncalibrated monocular cameras, leveraging geometric foundation models like VGGT with task-adaptive granularity. Notable work from Luca Carlone's lab at MIT.

entry.title: Confidence Calibration in Large Language Models

author.name: Noam Michael, Daniel BenShushan, Jacob Bien, Don A. Moore

entry.summary: A preregistered study finds LLMs exhibit a human-like hard-easy effect in confidence calibration: overconfidence on hard tasks, underconfidence on easy ones. The authors introduce LifeEval, a benchmark for evaluating calibration across difficulty levels.

entry.title: LGMT: Logic-Grounded Metamorphic Testing for Evaluating the Reasoning Reliability of LLMs

author.name: Zenghui Zhou, Man Li, Xiaoke Fang, Xinyi Zhou, Weibin Li, Zheng Zheng

entry.summary: LGMT uses first-order logic equivalences to generate metamorphic test cases for LLM reasoning, detecting defects through consistency checks without oracle labels. Reveals hidden defects on six SOTA LLMs.

entry.title: Identifying and Mitigating Systemic Measurement Bias in Production LLM Inference Benchmarks

author.name: Ashok Chandrasekar, Jason Kramberger

entry.summary: Identifies that widely-used Python asyncio LLM benchmarking clients introduce M/G/1 queuing bias inflating TTFT and TPOT measurements due to the GIL. Proposes a corrected benchmarking architecture.

entry.title: Beyond Final Answers: Auditing Trajectory-Level Hallucinations in Multi-Agent Industrial Workflows

author.name: Harshada Badave, Santosh Borse, Andrea Gomez, Harshitha Narahari, Sara Carter, Vishwa Bhatt, Aishani Rachakonda, Shuxin Lin, Dhaval Patel

entry.summary: Trajel introduces a trajectory-level hallucination taxonomy and dataset for multi-agent industrial workflows, finding common failure modes are missed by output-only evaluation. Covers five hallucination types.

entry.title: Beyond Inference-Only Deployment: Comparing Weight-Based Consolidation Against Cascading Compaction

author.name: Simon Dennis, Kevin Shabahang, Hao Guo, Rivaan Patil

entry.summary: Compares nightly LoRA-based weight consolidation of conversational knowledge against context-based memory under cascading compaction, showing 36.8% retention for compaction across three cycles in dev workflows.

entry.title: Emotional intelligence in large language models is fragmented across perception, cognition, and interaction

author.name: Minghao Lv, Lu Chen, Enchang Zhang, Anji Zhou, Xiaoran Xue, Hanyi Zhang, Fenghua Tang, Zhuo Rachel Han, Mengyue Wu

entry.summary: FACET is a psychometrically grounded emotional intelligence benchmark with 480 expert items based on Mayer-Salovey-Caruso four-branch ability model, finding LLM EI is fragmented across perception, cognition, and interaction.

entry.title: Energy Shields for Fairness

author.name: Filip Cano, Thomas A. Henzinger, Konstantin Kueffner

entry.summary: Energy shields are lightweight adaptive controllers using physics-inspired energy functions to enforce runtime fairness probabilistically and smoothly over sequences of decisions, rather than deterministic abrupt interventions.

entry.title: StructBreak: Structural Cognitive Overload-Induced Safety Failures in MLLMs

author.name: Yang Luo, Xinran Liu, Tiantian Ji, Zhiyi Yin, Lingyun Peng, Shuyu Li

entry.summary: StructBreak is an automated framework identifying Structural Cognitive Overload as a black-box higher-order attack paradigm against MLLMs, exploiting contention between deep reasoning and safety alignment to bypass guardrails.

entry.title: Momentum Streams for Optimizer-Inspired Transformers

author.name: Jingchu Gai, Nai-Chieh Huang, Jiayun Wu

entry.summary: Reinterprets Transformer residual updates as optimizer steps and builds optimizer-inspired Transformer variants (Adam, Muon, SOAP, triple-momentum). Triple-momentum TMMFormer achieves lowest validation loss in pretraining.

entry.title: Measuring the Depth of LLM Unlearning via Activation Patching

author.name: Jaeung Lee, Dohyun Kim, Jaemin Jo

entry.summary: Proposes Unlearning Depth Score, a metric using activation patching to quantify mechanistic depth of LLM unlearning beyond output-level checks. Identifies layers encoding target knowledge using retain-model baseline.

entry.title: Bilevel Optimization of Synthetic Trajectories for Multi-Turn LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Shresth Verma, Mauricio Tec, Cheol Woo Kim, Kai Wang, Milind Tambe
