entry.summary: Presents OpenComputer, a framework for constructing verifiable software environments for computer-use agents. Covers 33 desktop applications with 1,000 tasks, app-specific state verifiers, self-evolving verification, and partial-credit evaluation.

entry.title: ReCrit: Transition-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Scientific Critic Reasoning

author.name: Wanghan Xu, Yuhao Zhou, Hengyuan Zhao, Shuo Li, Dianzhi Yu, Zhenfei Yin, Yaowen Hu, Fengli Xu, Wanli Ouyang, Wenlong Zhang, Lei Bai

entry.summary: Proposes ReCrit, a reinforcement learning framework that addresses sycophancy in LLMs by framing critic interaction as a correctness-transition problem. Rewards maintaining correct answers under criticism while allowing genuine corrections.

entry.title: PROWL: Prioritized Regret-Driven Optimization for World Model Learning

author.name: Ahmet H. G\"uzel, Jenny Seidenschwarz, Benjamin Graham, Jonathan Sadeghi, Jeffrey Hawke, Jack Parker-Holder, Ilija Bogunovic

entry.summary: Introduces PROWL, a KL-constrained adversarial curriculum for training world models where a policy actively seeks model failures while staying close to behavior distribution. The world model is fine-tuned on adversarially discovered trajectories.

entry.title: Transformers Linearly Represent Highly Structured World Models

author.name: Roman Kniazev, Nathana\"el Fijalkow

entry.summary: Trains a transformer on Sudoku solving traces and performs mechanistic analysis, finding the model builds a substructure world model organized around rows/columns/boxes rather than individual cells, and identifies a naked-single detection circuit.

entry.title: Stop Drawing Scientific Claims from LLM Social Simulations Without Robustness Audits

author.name: Jinyi Ye, Lei Cao, Ding Chen, Emilio Ferrara

entry.summary: Argues that scientific claims from LLM social simulations need robustness audits, showing that small implementation perturbations cascade into different macro-level outcomes through repeated interaction (butterfly effect in agent simulations).

entry.title: DMN: A Compositional Framework for Jailbreaking Multimodal LLMs with Multi-Image Inputs

author.name: Wenzhuo Xu, Zhipeng Wei, Zonghao Ying, Deyue Zhang, Dongdong Yang, Xiangzheng Zhang, Quanchen Zou

entry.summary: Proposes DMN, a compositional jailbreak framework for multimodal LLMs that exploits multi-image inputs by distributing harmful instructions across images, using multimodal evidence, and number chain tasks to distract models.

entry.title: Flash PD-SSM: Memory-Optimized Structured Sparse State-Space Models

author.name: Aleksandar Terzi\'c, Francesco Carzaniga, Nicolas Menet, Yannick Biehl, Michael Hersche, Thomas Hofmann, Abbas Rahimi

entry.summary: Proposes Flash PD-SSM, a structured sparse state-space model achieving comparable throughput to efficient SSMs while maintaining significantly better expressivity guarantees for modeling finite-state automata.

entry.title: Going PLACES: Participatory Localized Red Teaming for Text-to-Image Safety in the Global South

author.name: Charvi Rastogi, Mukul Bhutani, Minsuk Kahng, Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhammad, Evgeniia Razumovskaia, Priyanka Suresh, Ibrahim Said Ahmad, Charu Kalia, Yaaseen Mahomed, Madhurima Maji, Minjae Lee, Alicia Parrish, Jessica Quaye, Vijay Janapa Reddi, Aishwarya Verma, Lora Aroyo

entry.summary: Presents PLACES, a dataset of 26,000+ T2I model failure examples collected through participatory red teaming in the Global South, highlighting Western-centric safety biases in current models.

entry.title: Rebalancing Reference Frame Dominance to Improve Motion in Image-to-Video Models

author.name: Wooseok Jeon, Seungho Park, Seunghyun Shin, Sangeyl Lee, Hyeonho Jeong, Hae-Gon Jeon

entry.summary: Identifies 'reference-frame dominance' in image-to-video models where non-reference frames over-attend to reference frame tokens, suppressing motion. Proposes DyMoS, a training-free method that rebalances attention pathways to increase motion in generated videos without sacrificing image fidelity.

entry.title: Latent Laplace Diffusion for Irregular Multivariate Time Series

author.name: Zinuo You, Jin Zheng, John Cartlidge

entry.summary: Presents Latent Laplace Diffusion (LLapDiff) for irregular multivariate time series forecasting, modeling targets in Laplace domain via learnable complex-conjugate poles, enabling direct evaluation over irregular timestamps without step-by-step integration.

entry.title: Mega-ASR: Towards In-the-wild^2 Speech Recognition via Scaling up Real-world Acoustic Simulation

author.name: Zhifei Xie, Kaiyu Pang, Haobin Zhang, Deheng Ye, Xiaobin Hu, Shuicheng Yan, Chunyan Miao

entry.summary: Proposes Mega-ASR, a framework for robust speech recognition combining scalable compound-data construction (2M samples, 54 compound acoustic scenarios) with progressive acoustic-to-semantic optimization.

entry.title: A Case for Agentic Tuning: From Documentation to Action in PostgreSQL

author.name: Hongyu Lin, Mingyu Li, Weichen Zhang, Yihang Lou, Mingjie Xing, Yanjun Wu, Haibo Chen

entry.summary: Proposes PerfEvolve, translating expert database tuning methodologies into executable skills for LLM-based agents that perform version-consistency verification, workload-specific profiling, and multi-parameter optimization for PostgreSQL.

entry.title: BalanceRAG: Joint Risk Calibration for Cascaded Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Zijun Jia, Yuanchang Ye, Sen Jia, Yiyao Qian, Haoning Wang, Baojie Chen, Diyin Tang, Jinsong Yu, Zhiyuan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes BalanceRAG for jointly calibrating uncertainty thresholds in cascaded RAG systems, determining when to use LLM-only vs. RAG vs. abstaining, framed as a conformal prediction problem.

entry.title: Draft Less, Retrieve More: Hybrid Tree Construction for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Yuhao Shen, Tianyu Liu, Xinyi Hu, Quan Kong, Baolin Zhang, Jun Dai, Jun Zhang, Shuang Ge, Lei Chen, Yue Li, Mingcheng Wan, Cong Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Graft, a hybrid approach to speculative decoding that combines pruned draft trees with retrieval-based compensation to break the Pareto tradeoff between acceptance rate and computational overhead in LLM inference acceleration.

entry.title: Geometry-Lite: Interpretable Safety Probing via Layer-Wise Margin Geometry

author.name: Woo Seob Sim, Yu Rang Park

entry.summary: Introduces Geometry-Lite, a lightweight safety probe for LLMs that maps hidden-state representations to signed margins using centroid, local-neighborhood, and linear-boundary readouts to characterize how safety evidence forms across layers.

entry.title: GROW: Aligning GRPO with State-Action Modeling for Open-World VLM Agents

author.name: Xiongbin Wu, Zhihao Luo, Shanzhe Lei, Lechao Zhang, Xuhong Wang, Jie Yang, Zhonglong Zheng, Yuanjie Zheng, Xin Tan, Wei Liu

entry.summary: Proposes GROW, an RL framework for open-world VLM agents that decomposes collected trajectories into state-action samples to enable effective multi-turn GRPO training, avoiding the issues of excessively long contexts in standard GRPO.

entry.title: Conformal Selective Acting: Anytime-Valid Risk Control for RLVR-Trained LLMs

author.name: Hamed Khosravi, Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: Develops conformal prediction methods providing anytime-valid selective risk control for RLVR-trained LLMs deployed in regulated organizations, addressing limitations of existing methods under adaptive online-updated streams.

entry.title: Quant.npu: Enabling Efficient Mobile NPU Inference for on-device LLMs via Fully Static Quantization

author.name: Jinghe Zhang, Daliang Xu, Chenghua Wang, Weikai Xie, Tao Qi, Yun Ma, Mengwei Xu, Gang Huang

entry.summary: Proposes Quant.npu, a fully static quantization framework for LLMs on mobile NPUs with learnable quantization parameters and rotation matrices, enabling efficient on-device inference without runtime parameter recomputation.

entry.title: Mechanisms of Misgeneralization in Physical Sequence Modeling

author.name: Kento Nishi, Raphael Tang, Karun Kumar, Core Francisco Park, Hidenori Tanaka

entry.summary: Identifies 'physical misgeneralization' in sequence models for robotics/simulation where individual trajectories look plausible but aggregate distributions over physical quantities are wrong, analyzing mechanisms behind this failure mode.

entry.title: Hack-Verifiable Environments: Towards Evaluating Reward Hacking at Scale

author.name: Amit Roth, Ankur Samanta, Matan Halevy, Yoav Levine, Yonathan Efroni

entry.summary: Introduces hack-verifiable environments that embed detectable reward hacking opportunities directly into environments, enabling deterministic and automated measurement of whether agents exploit them.

entry.title: The Devil is in the Condition Numbers: Why is GLU Better than non-GLU Structure?

author.name: Xingyu Lyu, Qianqian Xu, Zhiyong Yang, Peisong Wen, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: Explains why GLU architectures outperform non-gated alternatives through NTK analysis: GLU reshapes the NTK spectrum to have smaller condition numbers, leading to faster convergence and characteristic loss-crossing behavior.

entry.title: Reasoning-Trace Collapse: Evaluating the Loss of Explicit Reasoning During Fine-Tuning

author.name: Lukas Twist, Helen Yannakoudakis, Jie M. Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that fine-tuning explicit reasoning models on instruction-response data without reasoning traces causes 'reasoning-trace collapse'—models produce answers but lose valid reasoning structure.

entry.title: OCTOPUS: Optimized KV Cache for Transformers via Octahedral Parametrization Under optimal Squared error quantization

author.name: Mark Boss, Vikram Voleti, Simon Donn\'e, Shimon Vainer

entry.summary: OCTOPUS advances KV cache compression by jointly quantizing rotated coordinate triplets using octahedral parameterization, achieving non-uniform bit allocation that improves upon prior rotation-preconditioned methods like TurboQuant and PolarQuant.

entry.title: From Circuit Evidence to Mechanistic Theory: An Inductive Logic Approach

author.name: Nura Aljaafari, Danilo S. Carvalho, Andre Freitas

entry.summary: Proposes treating circuit interpretation in mechanistic interpretability as inductive theory construction, with Causal Functional Signatures and architectural signatures learned by inductive logic programming to enable cumulative mechanistic science.

entry.title: Agent JIT Compilation for Latency-Optimizing Web Agent Planning and Scheduling

author.name: Caleb Winston, Ron Yifeng Wang, Azalia Mirhoseini, Christos Kozyrakis

entry.summary: Agent JIT compilation compiles web task descriptions into executable code with LLM calls and parallelization, replacing the sequential screenshot-execute loop in computer-use agents for faster and more reliable execution.

entry.title: Data Scaling as Progressive Coverage of a Predictive Contribution Spectrum

author.name: Zihui Song, Shihao Ji, Hongxi Li, Shuaizhi Cheng, Chunlin Huang

entry.summary: Investigates data scaling laws through a suffix-automaton representation of text, defining a predictive contribution spectrum that correlates with empirical scaling exponents and explains when scaling helps.

entry.title: Multi-Head Attention as Ensemble Nadaraya-Watson Estimation: Variance Reduction, Decorrelation, and Optimal Head Diversity

author.name: Ernest Fokou\'e

entry.summary: Develops a statistical theory of multi-head attention as an ensemble of Nadaraya-Watson kernel regression estimators, deriving Bias-Variance-Covariance decomposition showing variance reduction depends on head decorrelation via principal angles.

entry.title: NeuroQA: A Large-Scale Image-Grounded Benchmark for 3D Brain MRI Understanding

author.name: Mohammad H. Abbasi (Stanford University), Favour Nerrise (Stanford University), Shaurnav Ghosh (Stanford University), Ridvan Yesiloglu (Stanford University), Yuncong Mao (Stanford University), Bailey Trang (Stanford University), Mohammad Asadi (Stanford University), Merryn Daniel (Stanford University), Gustavo Chau Loo Kung (Stanford University), Ken Chang (Stanford University), Pavan Pinkesh Shah (Stanford University), Adam Turnbull (Stanford University), Kyan Younes (Stanford University), Seena Dehkharghani (Stanford University), Ehsan Adeli (Stanford University)

entry.summary: NeuroQA presents a large-scale benchmark with 56,953 QA pairs from 12,977 subjects for visual question answering on 3D brain MRI, spanning five clinical domains and evaluating 11 clinically grounded reasoning skills.

entry.title: Instant GPU Efficiency Visibility at Fleet Scale

author.name: Connor Pedersen, Dong H. Ahn, Michel Migdal, Collin Neale, Nik Konyuchenko

entry.summary: Presents Overall FLOP Utilization (OFU), a hardware-level GPU efficiency metric derived from two on-chip performance counters that works across GPU generations and numeric precisions without application instrumentation. Validated on 608 production jobs.

entry.title: Multimodal LLMs under Pairwise Modalities

author.name: Yan Li, Yunlong Deng, Yuewen Sun, Gongxu Luo, Kun Zhang, Guangyi Chen

entry.summary: Explores training multimodal LLMs using only pairwise modality data rather than jointly curated multi-way aligned datasets, providing theoretical conditions for representation identifiability and a practical framework.

entry.title: Auto-Dreamer: Learning Offline Memory Consolidation for Language Agents

author.name: Chongrui Ye, Yuxiang Liu, Yu Wang, Haofei Yu, Yining Zhao, Ge Liu, Julian McAuley, Jiaxuan You

entry.summary: Proposes Auto-Dreamer, an offline memory consolidation system for language agents inspired by complementary learning systems theory. Decouples fast per-session memory acquisition from slow cross-session consolidation to discover patterns and prune redundant memories.

entry.title: Thinking-while-speaking: A Controlled, Interleaved Reasoning Method for Real-Time Speech Generation

author.name: Xuan Du, Qiangyu Yan, Wenshuo Li, Borui Jiang, Changming Xiao, Han Shu, Xinghao Chen

entry.summary: Presents InterRS, a method for interleaving reasoning with speech generation in real-time, inserting reasoning steps only during natural pauses. Introduces novel training pipeline combining SFT with RL using timing-balance and linguistic quality rewards.

entry.title: Memory Grafting: Scaling Language Model Pre-training via Offline Conditional Memory

author.name: Runxi Cheng, Yuchen Guan, Yongxian Wei, Qianpu Sun, Qixiu Li, Sinan Du, Feng Xiong, Chun Yuan, Yan Lu, Yeyun Gong

entry.summary: Proposes Memory Grafting, which uses frozen hidden states from a separate model as conditional n-gram memory for language model pretraining, retrieved via exact longest-match suffix lookup. Cheaper than learning memory tables from scratch.

entry.title: LASH: Adaptive Semantic Hybridization for Black-Box Jailbreaking of Large Language Models

author.name: Abdullah Al Nomaan Nafi, Fnu Suya, Swarup Bhunia, Prabuddha Chakraborty

entry.summary: Introduces LASH, a black-box jailbreak framework that adaptively composes outputs from multiple base attacks as seed prompts, exploiting complementary strengths across different attack families for each target request.

entry.title: Mem-$\pi$: Adaptive Memory through Learning When and What to Generate

author.name: Xiaoqiang Wang, Chao Wang, Hadi Nekoei, Christopher Pal, Alexandre Lacoste, Spandana Gella, Bang Liu, Perouz Taslakian

entry.summary: Presents Mem-π, a framework where a separate model generates context-specific guidance for LLM agents on demand, jointly deciding when and what guidance to produce. Trained with decision-content decoupled reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Draw2Think: Harnessing Geometry Reasoning through Constraint Engine Interaction

author.name: Juncheng Hu, Jiawei Du, Xin Zhang, Joey Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: Presents Draw2Think, recasting geometric reasoning from latent inference into agentic interaction with the GeoGebra constraint engine. Uses a Propose-Draw-Verify loop where each reasoning step is constraint-checked algebraically.

entry.title: Can Vision Models Truly Forget? Mirage: Representation-Level Certification of Visual Unlearning

author.name: Zhenyu Yu, Yangchen Zeng, Chunlei Meng, Guangzhen Yao, Shuigeng Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Mirage, a representation-level auditing framework for machine unlearning in Vertical Federated Learning, revealing that methods passing output-level certification still retain substantial class structure in internal representations.

entry.title: Goodbye Drift: Anchored Tree Sampling for Long-Horizon Video-to-Video Generation

author.name: Matthew Bendel, Stephen W. Bailey, Mithilesh Vaidya, Sumukh Badam, Xingzhe He

entry.summary: Proposes Anchored Tree Sampling (ATS), a training-free inference-time scheduler for long-horizon video generation that replaces autoregressive rollout with sparse-to-dense anchor-bounded imputation organized as a tree, directly addressing drift.

entry.title: Finding the Correct Visual Evidence Without Forgetting: Mitigating Hallucination in LVLMs via Inter-Layer Visual Attention Discrepancy

author.name: Yutong Xie, Zhenglin Hua, Ran Wang, Wing W. Y. Ng, Xizhao Wang, Yuheng Jia

entry.summary: Identifies that LVLMs hallucinate when they pay insufficient attention to visual evidence and gradually forget it during generation. Proposes a hallucination mitigation method based on inter-layer visual attention discrepancy to enhance visual evidence at specific layers.

entry.title: CHOIR: Contact-aware 4D Hand-Object Interaction Reconstruction

author.name: Hao Xu, Yilin Liu, Yinqiao Wang, Chi-Wing Fu, Niloy J. Mitra

entry.summary: CHOIR reconstructs articulated hand motion, object shape with 6D pose, and contact information from monocular videos without assuming known objects. Uses contact as a key signal for alignment under challenging conditions like clutter and occlusion.

entry.title: Uni-Edit: Intelligent Editing Is A General Task For Unified Model Tuning

author.name: Dian Zheng, Manyuan Zhang, Hongyu Li, Hongbo Liu, Kai Zou, Kaituo Feng, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: Uni-Edit proposes that intelligent image editing can serve as a single general task for tuning Unified Multimodal Models, improving understanding, generation, and editing simultaneously without complex multi-task training pipelines.

entry.title: The Yes-Man Syndrome: Benchmarking Abstention in Embodied Robotic Agents

author.name: Doguhan Yeke, Elif Su Temirel, Ananth Shreekumar, Brandon Lee, Dongyan Xu, Z Berkay Celik

entry.summary: Introduces RoboAbstention, a taxonomy and scalable benchmark for evaluating when embodied robotic agents should abstain from executing instructions that are ambiguous, physically infeasible, or based on false premises.

entry.title: What and When to Distill: Selective Hindsight Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents

author.name: Xiaozhe Li, Tianyi Lyu, Yang Li, Yichuan Ma, Peiji Li, Linyang Li, Qipeng Guo, Dahua Lin, Kai Chen

entry.summary: Introduces SERL, a selective environment-reweighted learning framework for multi-turn LLM agents that leverages per-step environmental feedback (error messages, page changes, observations) to improve credit assignment in RL training. Systematically studies five feedback sources and two insertion granularities.

entry.title: DEFLECT: Delay-Robust Execution via Flow-matching Likelihood-Estimated Counterfactual Tuning for VLA Policies

author.name: Yixiang Zhu, Yonghao Chen, Rui Meng, Jingyu Guo, Jiaxiang Zou, Zijie Yang, Taowen Wang, Xinyu Chen

entry.summary: Introduces DEFLECT, a post-training refinement for VLA policies that addresses prediction-execution misalignment from asynchronous inference by converting latency into preference signals for offline training.

entry.title: DySink: Dynamic Frame Sinks for Autoregressive Long Video Generation

author.name: Bo Ye, Xinyu Cui, Jian Zhao, Tong Wei, Min-Ling Zhang

entry.summary: DySink proposes a retrieval-based framework for autoregressive long video generation that replaces fixed early-frame 'sinks' with dynamic memory, addressing content regression toward outdated anchors and 'sink collapse' caused by RoPE phase re-alignment.

entry.title: POLAR-Bench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Privacy-Utility Trade-offs in LLM Agents

author.name: Qiaoyuan Zheng, Yiqu Yang, Qi Gao, Imanol Schlag

entry.summary: Introduces POLAR-Bench evaluating privacy-utility tradeoffs when LLM agents interact with adversarial third-party systems. Tests across 10 domains with 7,852 samples, scoring both privacy protection and task utility under varying attack strategies.

entry.title: Probing Embodied LLMs: When Higher Observation Fidelity Hurts Problem Solving

author.name: Oussama Zenkri, Oliver Brock

entry.summary: Studies embodied LLM agents on a mechanical puzzle task, finding that agents counterintuitively perform best with raw RGB input and worst with perfect ground-truth symbolic observations. Suggests higher observation fidelity can hurt problem-solving.

entry.title: Not Every Rubric Teaches Equally: Policy-Aware Rubric Rewards for RLVR

author.name: Utkarsh Tyagi, Xingang Guo, MohammadHossein Rezaei, Daniel George, Anas Mahmoud, Jackson Lee, Bing Liu, Yunzhong He

entry.summary: Introduces POW3R, a policy-aware rubric reward method for RL with verifiable rewards that distinguishes human-assigned importance from current optimization signal usefulness. Shows static rubric aggregation fails when criteria are saturated or unreachable.

entry.title: Counterfactual Likelihood Tests for Indirect Influence in Private Reasoning Channels

author.name: Alexander Boesgaard Lorup (Openhagen)

entry.summary: Presents a counterfactual likelihood test for measuring influence between private reasoning channels in models, replacing unreliable textual probes with NLL shift measurements under donor block substitution.

entry.title: HalluWorld: A Controlled Benchmark for Hallucination via Reference World Models

author.name: Emmy Liu, Varun Gangal, Michael Yu, Zhuofu Tao, Karan Singh, Sachin Kumar, Steven Y. Feng

entry.summary: Introduces HalluWorld, an extensible benchmark grounded in explicit reference-world formulation for studying hallucination across settings (summarization, QA, RAG, agentic), providing controlled and reproducible evaluation.

entry.title: The Hidden Signal of Verifier Strictness: Controlling and Improving Step-Wise Verification via Selective Latent Steering

author.name: Yefan Zhou, Yilun Zhou, Austin Xu, Soroush Vosoughi, Shafiq Joty, Jiang Gui

entry.summary: Discovers that verifier strictness in step-wise verification is encoded in hidden states near verification paragraph boundaries, and shows hidden-state steering can modulate this to improve calibration.

entry.title: Do Vision--Language Models Understand 3D Scenes or Just Catalogue Objects?

author.name: Animesh Maheshwari, Divyansh Sahu, Nishit Verma

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark testing VLMs on 3D spatial understanding (occlusion, reflections, volumetric planning), finding a sharp dissociation: models plan rearrangements well (53-97%) but fail on occlusion (6-45%) and reflections (<7%).

entry.title: ParaVT: Taming the Tool Prior Paradox for Parallel Tool Use in Agentic Video Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zuhao Yang, Kaichen Zhang, Sudong Wang, Keming Wu, Zhongyu Yang, Bo Li, Xiaojuan Qi, Shijian Lu, Xingxuan Li, Lidong Bing

entry.summary: Introduces ParaVT, the first multi-agent RL framework for parallel video tool calling that dispatches multiple time-window crops in a single turn, addressing the 'Tool Prior Paradox' where pretrained models resist learning tool use through standard RL.

entry.title: Interference-Aware Multi-Task Unlearning

author.name: Ying-Hua Huang, Rui Fang, Hsi-Wen Chen, Ming-Syan Chen

entry.summary: Introduces multi-task unlearning addressing interference when removing data from shared-backbone multi-task models. Proposes full-task and partial-task unlearning settings and a method to handle task-level and instance-level interference from shared parameters.

entry.title: Attention-Guided Reward for Reinforcement Learning-based Jailbreak against Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Zheng Lin, Zhenxing Niu, Haoxuan Ji, Yuzhe Huang, Haichang Gao

entry.summary: Proposes an attention-guided reward for RL-based jailbreak attacks against Large Reasoning Models, showing attack success correlates with attention patterns on harmful tokens in input vs. reasoning content.

entry.title: From SGD to Muon: Adaptive Optimization via Schatten-p Norms

author.name: Thomas Massena (IRIT, DTIPG - SNCF, UT3), Corentin Friedrich (IRIT), Mathieu Serrurier (IRIT)

entry.summary: Introduces an adaptive optimization framework that dynamically selects between SGD and Muon-like updates per layer based on gradient and activation statistics. Uses a closed-form criterion derived from single-step random feature regression.

entry.title: PEEK: Context Map as an Orientation Cache for Long-Context LLM Agents

author.name: Zhuohan Gu, Qizheng Zhang, Omar Khattab, Samuel Madden

entry.summary: Introduces PEEK, a system that caches reusable orientation knowledge about recurring contexts as a 'context map' — a constant-sized artifact giving agents persistent understanding of what contexts contain and how they're organized.

entry.title: OmniGUI: Benchmarking GUI Agents in Omni-Modal Smartphone Environments

author.name: Felix Henry, Xiaochen Lin, Jiangyou Zhu, Yangfan, Bingqian Zhang, Min Chen, Shiyu Huang

entry.summary: Introduces OmniGUI, the first step-level benchmark for GUI agents requiring processing of continuous multimodal inputs (images, audio, video) at every action step. Covers 709 episodes across 29 applications with annotated multimodal dependency levels.

entry.title: Simply Stabilizing the Loop via Fully Looped Transformer

author.name: Rao Fu, Zixuan Yang, Jiankun Zhang, Jing Ma, Hechang Chen, Yu Li, Yi Chang

entry.summary: Identifies gradient oscillation and residual explosion as sources of instability in Looped Transformers, and proposes Fully Looped Transformer with stabilization techniques to enable more loop iterations without increasing parameters.

entry.title: The Growing Pains of Frontier Models: When Leaderboards Stop Separating and What to Measure Next

author.name: Adil Amin

entry.summary: Analyzes 34 frontier models from 10 labs (2024-2026) on SWE-bench and GPQA Diamond, finding capabilities cooperate (r=0.72) but with lab-specific patterns. Proposes h-field diagnostic for identifying what measurement is most informative next.

entry.title: When Individually Calibrated Models Become Collectively Miscalibrated

author.name: Zhaohui Wang

entry.summary: Proves that individually calibrated probabilistic models can become collectively miscalibrated when aggregated, showing this arises naturally from Brier-score-optimal local responses with correlated beliefs.

entry.title: DarkLLM: Learning Language-Driven Adversarial Attacks with Large Language Models

author.name: Ye Sun, Xin Wang, Jiaming Zhang, Yifeng Gao, Yixu Wang, Yifan Ding, Qixian Zhang, Henghui Ding, Xingjun Ma, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: Presents DarkLLM, an attack framework that trains an LLM to translate natural-language attack instructions into adversarial perturbations for vision/multimodal models, unifying multiple attack types through language.

entry.title: To Call or Not to Call: Diagnosing Intrinsic Over-Calling Bias in LLM Agents

author.name: Wei Shi, Ziheng Peng, Sihang Li, Xiting Wang, Xiang Wang, Mengnan Du, Na Zou

entry.summary: Diagnoses an intrinsic over-calling bias in LLM agents using sparse autoencoders, finding that models have an activation-independent offset favoring tool calls. Shows the bias exists across 6 models from 3 families.

entry.title: ESLD (External Surrogate Latent Defense): A Latent-Space Architecture for Faster, Stronger Prompt-Injection Defense

author.name: Yash Narendra

entry.summary: Proposes ESLD, a latent-space architecture for defending against prompt injection attacks in AI assistants. Uses an external surrogate model operating in latent space for faster and stronger detection of malicious inputs.

entry.title: Distilling Linearized Behavior for Effective Task Arithmetic

author.name: Thomas Sommariva, Francesca Morandi, Simone Calderara, Angelo Porrello

entry.summary: Proposes distilling linearized fine-tuning behavior into standard nonlinear models, bridging the gap between naturally disentangled linear task vectors and the expressivity of standard fine-tuning.

entry.title: EgoBabyVLM: Benchmarking Cross-Modal Learning from Naturalistic Egocentric Video Data

author.name: Dongyan Lin, Phillip Rust, Angel Villar Corrales, Alvin W. M. Tan, Mahi Luthra, Charles-\'Eric Saint-James, Rashel Moritz, Sheila Krogh-Jespersen, Vanessa Stark, Surya Parimi, Jiayi Shen, Youssef Benchekroun, Yosuke Higuchi, Martin Gleize, Tom Fizycki, Nicolas Hamilakis, Manel Khentout, Sho Tsuji, Bal\'azs K\'egl, Juan Pino, Michael C. Frank, Emmanuel Dupoux

entry.summary: Introduces EgoBabyVLM benchmark training VLMs on naturalistic infant and adult egocentric videos to study how models learn from sparse, weakly-aligned data streams similar to child language acquisition.

entry.title: COBALT: Crowdsourcing Robot Learning via Cloud-Based Teleoperation with Smartphones

author.name: Ayush Agarwal, Ansh Gandhi, Jeremy A. Collins, Omar Rayyan, Aryan Sarswat, Ranjani Koushik, Masoud Moghani, Ajay Mandlekar, Animesh Garg

entry.summary: Presents COBALT, a teleoperation platform for crowdsourcing robot demonstration data using smartphones, VR headsets, and other common devices, with scalable infrastructure supporting concurrent users on single GPU.

entry.title: Token by Token, Compromised: Backdoor Vulnerabilities in Unified Autoregressive Models

author.name: Tobias Braun, Jonas Henry Grebe, Hossein Shakibania, Anna Rohrbach, Marcus Rohrbach

entry.summary: Presents ToBAC, the first backdoor attack targeting unified autoregressive models (UAMs) that generate both text and images, showing that triggers can propagate malicious effects across output modalities.

entry.title: PhyWorld: Physics-Faithful World Model for Video Generation

author.name: Pu Zhao, Juyi Lin, Timothy Rupprecht, Arash Akbari, Chence Yang, Rahul Chowdhury, Elaheh Motamedi, Arman Akbari, Yumei He, Chen Wang, Geng Yuan, Weiwei Chen, Yanzhi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes PhyWorld, a video generation world model designed for physically faithful scene continuations through two-stage post-training that improves temporal coherence and physical consistency.

entry.title: Unlocking the Potential of Continual Model Merging: An ODE Perspective

author.name: Lihong Lin, Haidong Kang

entry.summary: Proposes an ODE-based perspective on continual model merging that provides explicit controllability over capacity allocation between old and new tasks. Addresses catastrophic forgetting in sequential model merging by treating task trajectories rather than isolated parameter points.

entry.title: Quantifying the Pre-training Dividend: Generative versus Latent Self-Supervised Learning for Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Noam Major, Kathy Razmadze, Yoli Shavit

entry.summary: Evaluates the 'pre-training dividend' of self-supervised learning for time series, comparing generative vs. latent alignment approaches. Introduces adaptations of LeJEPA and DINO for time series and finds the SSL benefit is highly asymmetric across task types.

entry.title: Investigating Cross-Modal Skill Injection: Scenarios, Methods, and Hyperparameters

author.name: Zhiyu Xu, Lean Wang, Yuanxin Liu, Lei Li, Hao Zhou, Fandong Meng, Jie Zhou, Xu Sun

entry.summary: Investigates cross-modal skill injection from LLMs to VLMs via model merging, studying scenarios, methods, and hyperparameters. Shows that model merging can transfer domain skills without additional training data.

entry.title: Spectral Integrated Gradients for Coarse-to-Fine Feature Attribution

author.name: Soyeon Kim, Seongwoo Lim, Kyowoon Lee, Jaesik Choi

entry.summary: Proposes Spectral Integrated Gradients (SIG), constructing integration paths via SVD of the baseline-to-input difference for feature attribution. Introduces global structure before fine-grained details in a coarse-to-fine progression.

entry.title: CriterAlign: Criterion-Centric Rationale Alignment for Code Preference Judging

author.name: Zhenyu Li, Aleksandar Cvejic, Zehui Chen, Peter Wonka

entry.summary: Proposes CriterAlign for pairwise code preference evaluation, showing that criterion-level pairwise judgments outperform standard pointwise scoring approaches. Introduces tie-driven criterion refinement for better discrimination.

entry.title: LIFT and PLACE: A Simple, Stable, and Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework for Lightweight Diffusion Models

author.name: Hyunsoo Han, Sangyeop Yeo, Jaejun Yoo

entry.summary: Proposes LIFT and PLACE for knowledge distillation of diffusion models, decomposing the objective into coarse alignment via linear fitting and fine refinement with locally adaptive coefficients to handle spatially non-uniform errors.

entry.title: FineBench: Benchmarking and Enhancing Vision-Language Models for Fine-grained Human Activity Understanding

author.name: Gueter Josmy Faure, Min-Hung Chen, Jia-Fong Yeh, Hung-Ting Su, Winston H. Hsu

entry.summary: Introduces FineBench, a large-scale human-centric video QA benchmark with 199K multiple-choice questions for evaluating fine-grained understanding of human activities including spatial/temporal grounding.

entry.title: Real-Time Parallel Counterfactual Regret Minimization

author.name: Boning Li, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: Presents Parallel CFR, the first parallelization framework for real-time depth-limited Counterfactual Regret Minimization, decomposing iterations into a 7-stage pipeline with two orthogonal dimensions of parallelism.

entry.title: World-Ego Modeling for Long-Horizon Evolution in Hybrid Embodied Tasks

author.name: Zuyao Lin, Jianhui Zhang, Peidong Jia, Xiaoguang Zhao, Shanghang Zhang, Xingyu Chen

entry.summary: Introduces World-Ego Modeling, decomposing future evolution predictions into world (scene regularities) and ego (robot-centric dynamics) components for long-horizon embodied tasks with interleaved navigation and manipulation.

entry.title: VL-DPO: Vision-Language-Guided Finetuning for Preference-Aligned Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhefan Xu, Ghassen Jerfel, Marina Haliem, Qi Zhao, Jeonhyung Kang, Khaled S. Refaat

entry.summary: Presents VL-DPO, using vision-language models as zero-shot reasoners to generate preference pairs for finetuning motion forecasting models in autonomous driving via DPO alignment.

entry.title: Neural Estimation of Pairwise Mutual Information in Masked Discrete Sequence Models

author.name: Jai Sharma, Yifan Wang, Bryan Li

entry.summary: Proposes a neural framework for estimating pairwise conditional mutual information from hidden states of masked diffusion models, enabling MI-guided parallel decoding by identifying conditionally independent variable subsets.

entry.title: Automated Kernel Discovery Towards Understanding High-dimensional Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Taeyoung Yun, Woocheol Shin, Inhyuck Song, Jaewoo Lee, Jinkyoo Park

entry.summary: Introduces Kernel Discovery, an LLM-driven evolutionary framework for automatically discovering GP kernels for high-dimensional Bayesian optimization, searching beyond predefined composition rules without conditioning on raw observations.

entry.title: Residual Paving: Diagnosing the Routing Bottleneck in Selective Refusal Editing

author.name: Bryce Hinkley, Peyman Najafirad

entry.summary: Introduces Residual Paving, a method for selective refusal editing in LLMs that separates routing decisions (whether to intervene) from edit capacity (what to apply), diagnosing the routing bottleneck in refusal editing.

entry.title: Closed-form predictive coding via hierarchical Gaussian filters

author.name: Aleksandrs Baskakovs, Sylvain Estebe, Kenneth Enevoldsen, Kristoffer Nielbo, Chris Mathys, Nicolas Legrand

entry.summary: Proposes closed-form predictive coding networks expressed as deep hierarchical Gaussian filters, restoring precision-weighted message passing that improves training speed and depth scaling compared to standard predictive coding.

entry.title: Spectral Unforgetting: Post-Hoc Recovery of Damaged Capabilities Without Retraining

author.name: Aarash Abro, Muhammad Tahir

entry.summary: Introduces DG-Hard, a post-hoc spectral repair method for catastrophic forgetting that operates only on the pretrained and fine-tuned checkpoints, treating the update as a low-rank signal and selectively repairing damaged capabilities.

entry.title: Decomposing MXFP4 quantization error for LLM reinforcement learning: reducible bias, recoverable deadzone, and an irreducible floor

author.name: Xiaocan Li, Shiliang Wu, Zheng Shen

entry.summary: Decomposes MXFP4 quantization error for LLM RL training into three components (scale bias, deadzone truncation, grid noise) and shows how each dominates different RL training pathways, enabling targeted mitigation.

entry.title: REFLECTOR: Internalizing Step-wise Reflection against Indirect Jailbreak

author.name: Jiachen Ma, Jiawen Zhang, Xiangtian Li, Bo Zou, Chaochao Lu, Chao Yang

entry.summary: Proposes REFLECTOR, a two-stage framework that internalizes step-wise self-reflection to defend against multi-step indirect jailbreak attacks on LLMs, using teacher-guided SFT followed by RL with outcome-driven rewards.

entry.title: Distributed Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Zhanhong Jiang

entry.summary: Provides the first convergence and time-complexity analysis of Direct Preference Optimization in distributed (federated and decentralized) settings with non-IID preference data across heterogeneous users.

entry.title: Correcting Stochastic Update Bias in Preconditioned Language Model Optimizers

author.name: Nikhil Nayak, Julia White, Urchade Zaratiana, Kelton Zhang, Henrijs Princis, Dhruv Atreja, Henry Fawcett, Matthew Thomas, George Hurn-Maloney, Ash Lewis

entry.summary: Identifies two finite-sample biases in preconditioned optimizers for LLM training: gradient-preconditioner coupling bias and nonlinear inversion bias. Proposes cross-fitted preconditioning and variance-corrected inversion.

entry.title: DASH: Fast Differentiable Architecture Search for Hybrid Attention in Minutes on a Single GPU

author.name: Weizhe Chen, Miao Zhang, Junpeng Jiang, Yaping Li, Weili Guan, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: Introduces DASH, a fast differentiable architecture search for hybrid attention (mixing different attention types across layers) that works in minutes on a single GPU, compared to Jet-Nemotron's 200B token search.

entry.title: Advantage Collapse in Group Relative Policy Optimization: Diagnosis and Mitigation

author.name: Xixiang He, Qiyao Sun, Ao Cheng, Xingming Li, Xuanyu Ji, Hailun Lu, Runke Huang, Qingyong Hu

entry.summary: Introduces Advantage Collapse Rate (ACR) as a diagnostic metric for GRPO training and proposes mitigation strategies. Shows ACR predicts training stagnation across 0.5B-14B parameter models.

entry.title: Behavior-Consistent Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Marcel Hussing, Liv G. d'Aliberti, Claas Voelcker, Benjamin Eysenbach, Eric Eaton

entry.summary: Addresses cross-run policy divergence in RL by formalizing behavior-consistent RL, proving that maximum-entropy RL with temperature proportional to Q-function disagreement bounds pairwise KL divergence between policies across training runs. This improves deployment reliability.

entry.title: A Mechanistic Study of Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Marin Bilo\v{s}, James T. Wilson, Anderson Schneider, Yuriy Nevmyvaka

entry.summary: Provides a mechanistic study of tabular foundation models, showing that different architectures realize qualitatively distinct similarity-based readouts through causal interventions, and that representation collapse is not a practical concern.

entry.title: Proximal State Nudging: Reducing Skill Atrophy from AI Assistance

author.name: Megha Srivastava, Jonathan Ouyang, Eric Zhou, Andrew Silva, Emily Sumner, Dorsa Sadigh, Yuchen Cui, Deepak Gopinath, Guy Rosman

entry.summary: Proximal State Nudging (PSN) is a shared autonomy algorithm that jointly optimizes skill development and task performance by nudging users toward learnable states, addressing skill atrophy from AI assistance.

entry.title: AgentAtlas: Beyond Outcome Leaderboards for LLM Agents

author.name: Parsa Mazaheri, Kasra Mazaheri

entry.summary: AgentAtlas proposes a comprehensive evaluation framework for LLM agents with a six-state control-decision taxonomy, nine-category trajectory-failure taxonomy, and multi-dimensional assessment beyond simple accuracy leaderboards.

entry.title: Sample Complexity of Transfer Learning: An Optimal Transport Approach

author.name: Haoyang Cao, Xin Guo, Wenpin Tang, Guan Wang

entry.summary: Provides rigorous analysis of transfer learning sample complexity using optimal transport theory, showing that when data dimension d>3, transfer learning achieves O(m^{-(α+1)/d}) sample complexity versus O(m^{-p/d}) without transfer.

entry.title: RoPeSLR: 3D RoPE-driven Sparse-LowRank Attention for Efficient Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Yuxi Liu, Zekun Zhang, Yixiang Cai, Renjia Deng, Yutong He, Kun Yuan

entry.summary: RoPeSLR addresses the 'RoPE Dilemma' in Diffusion Transformers for video generation by proposing a 3D RoPE-guided sparse-lowrank attention framework that preserves positional encoding structure while achieving efficient attention.

entry.title: DISC: Decoupling Instruction from State-Conditioned Control via Policy Generation

author.name: Hanxiang Ren, Pei Zhou, Xunzhe Zhou, Yanchao Yang

entry.summary: DISC uses a hypernetwork to generate entire visuomotor policy parameters from language instructions alone, structurally eliminating observation leakage where models learn scene-to-action shortcuts bypassing language grounding.

entry.title: Diagnosing Overhead in Dispatch Operations: Cross-architecture Observatory

author.name: Bole Ma, Jan Eitzinger, Harald Koestler, Gerhard Wellein

entry.summary: DODOCO instruments five MoE checkpoints across five sequence-mixer designs to test assumptions about AlltoAll dispatch in expert parallelism, finding that mock-token benchmarks may not faithfully represent production routing patterns.

entry.title: A Rigorous, Tractable Measure of Model Complexity

author.name: Oskar Allerbo, Thomas B. Sch\"on

entry.summary: Proposes a rigorous, easily computable model complexity measure based on gradient similarities across inputs, proving it generalizes specific measures like polynomial degree, kernel length scale, and number of neighbors.

entry.title: Federated LoRA Fine-Tuning for LLMs via Collaborative Alignment

author.name: Shuaida He, Liwen Chen, Long Feng

entry.summary: CLAIR proposes a contamination-aware federated LoRA fine-tuning framework that pools partial structure across heterogeneous clients while handling contaminated participants, applicable from linear regression to LLM modules.

entry.title: Frontier: Towards Comprehensive and Accurate LLM Inference Simulation

author.name: Yicheng Feng, Xin Tan, Yangtao Deng, Yimin Jiang, Yibo Zhu, Hong Xu

entry.summary: Frontier presents a discrete-event simulator for modern LLM inference serving that captures disaggregated architectures, complex parallelism, and stateful workloads including reasoning, agents, and RL rollouts.

entry.title: MedicalBench: Evaluating Large Language Models Toward Improved Medical Concept Extraction

author.name: Zhichao Yang, Gregory D. Lyng, Sanjit Singh Batra, Robert E. Tillman

entry.summary: Presents MedicalBench, a benchmark for medical concept extraction that specifically evaluates implicit medical reasoning - extracting concepts that are implied rather than explicitly stated in clinical narratives. Formulates extraction as a verification task with sentence-level evidence identification.

entry.title: Synchronization and Turn-Taking in Full-Duplex Speech Dialogue Models

author.name: Pablo Riera, Pablo Brusco, Cristina Kuo, Marcelo Sancinetti, S. R. K. Branavan

entry.summary: Studies synchronization and turn-taking in full-duplex spoken dialogue models by simulating conversations between two Moshi model instances. Measures representational synchronization via CKA and probes anticipatory turn-taking cues from internal activations.

entry.title: Mechanics of Bias and Reasoning: Interpreting the Impact of Chain-of-Thought Prompting on Gender Bias in LLMs

author.name: Edie Pearman, Sophia Osborne, Mira Kandlikar-Bloch, Mina Arzaghi, Florian Carichon, Golnoosh Farnadi

entry.summary: Investigates whether Chain-of-Thought prompting actually reduces gender bias in LLMs by combining benchmark evaluation with mechanistic interpretability and reasoning chain failure analysis. Finds CoT can reduce surface-level bias without changing underlying internal mechanisms.

entry.title: Direct Translation between Sign Languages

author.name: Zetian Wu, Bowen Xie, Wuyang Meng, Milan Gautam, Stefan Lee, Liang Huang

entry.summary: Proposes direct sign-to-sign language translation without going through text intermediary, addressing error propagation and information loss in cascade approaches. Aims to help 1.5 billion deaf/hard-of-hearing people communicate across language barriers.

entry.title: Distributional Alignment as a Criterion for Designing Task Vectors in In-Context Learning

author.name: Jihoon Kwon, Jiwon Choi, Jy-yong Sohn

entry.summary: Proposes that task vectors in in-context learning should be evaluated by their distributional alignment with full ICL inference, introducing d_NTP metric measuring next-token probability discrepancy. Uses this criterion to design better task vector extraction methods.

entry.title: PulseCol: Periodically Refreshed Column-Sparse Attention for Accelerating Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yanyi Lyu, Letian Chen, Futing Sun, Miao Zhang, Weili Guan, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: Introduces PulseCol, a periodically refreshed column-sparse attention method for diffusion language models that exploits reusable sparsity patterns to enable acceleration from earlier denoising iterations than block-sparse approaches.

entry.title: Cross-lingual robustness of LLM-brain alignment and its computational roots

author.name: Ni Yang, Rui He, Philipp Homan, Iris Sommer, Davide Staub, Wolfram Hinzen

entry.summary: Uses multilingual whole-brain encoding to examine brain-LLM alignment across Mandarin, English, and French during story listening. Finds distributed cortical-subcortical alignment across languages, with transformer depth paralleling neural hierarchy.

entry.title: "I didn't Make the Micro Decisions": Measuring, Inducing, and Exposing Goal-Level AI Contributions in Collaboration

author.name: Eunsu Kim, Jessica R. Mindel, Kyungjin Kim, Sherry Tongshuang Wu

entry.summary: Introduces CoTrace, a goal-level attribution framework for human-AI collaboration that traces how LLMs shape user goals through direct contributions and indirect influences. Finds models account for 11-26% of goal-shaping but more on initial formulation.

entry.title: Post-Hoc Understanding of Metaphor Processing in Decoder-Only Language Models via Conditional Scale Entropy

author.name: Lawhori Chakrabarti, Jennifer Johnson-Leung, Bert Baumgaertner, Aleksandar Vakanski, Min Xian, Boyu Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces conditional scale entropy (CSE), a wavelet-derived measure for analyzing how transformers process metaphors across layers. Proves CSE is invariant to update magnitude, finding metaphorical tokens produce higher spectral breadth than literal tokens.

entry.title: FullFlow: Upgrading Text-to-Image Flow Matching Models for Bidirectional Vision--Language Generation

author.name: Eric Tillmann Bill, Enis Simsar, Alessio Tonioni, Thomas Hofmann

entry.summary: Introduces FullFlow, a parameter-efficient method to upgrade pretrained text-to-image flow matching models into bidirectional vision-language generators by training only LoRA adapters and text heads, keeping images in continuous flow while adding discrete text insertion.

entry.title: How You Move Tells What You'll Do: Trajectory-Conditioned Egocentric Prediction

author.name: Sejoon Jun, Hai Nguyen-Truong, Luigi Seminara, Lorenzo Torresani

entry.summary: Shows that future camera trajectory serves as a powerful conditioning signal for egocentric video prediction (actions, plans, outcomes), substantially outperforming language conditioning by carrying operator intent that determines how actions unfold.

entry.title: FlowLong: Inference-time Long Video Generation via Manifold-constrained Tweedie Matching

author.name: Jangho Park, Geon Yeong Park, Gihyun Kwon, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: Proposes FlowLong for inference-time long video generation using manifold-constrained Tweedie matching between overlapping sliding windows, without additional training. Architecture-agnostic approach addressing both drift and repetitive motion.

entry.title: Focus-then-Context: Subject-Centric Progressive Visual Token Reduction for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yulin Zhao, Yun Wang, Dehua Zheng, Borui jiang, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: SPpruner proposes a subject-centric progressive visual token reduction method for VLMs that mimics human 'Focus-then-Context' perception, first identifying salient subjects then progressively expanding context. Reduces computational costs while preserving important visual relationships.

entry.title: Preserve, Reveal, Expand: Faithful 4D Video Editing with Region-Aware Conditioning

author.name: Zhangchi Hu, Wenzhang Sun, Xiangchen Yin, Jiahui Yuan, Chunfeng Wang, Hao Li, Kun Zhan, Xiaoyan Sun

entry.summary: PREX proposes a region-aware framework for faithful 4D video editing that decomposes target spatiotemporal volumes into Preserve, Reveal, and Expand roles based on observation support. Addresses the 'Evidence-Role Mismatch' problem in existing 4D-driven video diffusion models.

entry.title: DriveMA: Rethinking Language Interfaces in Driving VLAs with One-Step Meta-Actions

author.name: Weicheng Zheng, Yixin Huang, Qiao Sun, Derun Li, Hang zhao

entry.summary: DriveMA rethinks language interfaces in Driving VLAs, showing that concise one-step meta-actions are more effective than verbose reasoning chains. Meta-actions provide semantic grounding while being automatically derivable from expert trajectories.

entry.title: Reducing Object Hallucination in LVLMs via Emphasizing Image-negative Tokens

author.name: Meng Shen, Minghao Wu, Deepu Rajan

entry.summary: Proposes reducing object hallucination in LVLMs by identifying and emphasizing 'image-negative' tokens (those whose generation probability decreases with image context), revealing that most generated tokens are minimally influenced by image information.

entry.title: One-Step Distillation of Discrete Diffusion Image Generators via Fixed-Point Iteration

author.name: Chaoyang Wang, Yunhai Tong

entry.summary: Fixed-Point Distillation (FPD) distills discrete diffusion image generators into one-step models by corrupting the student's draft and refining with a single teacher step, using a multi-bandwidth drift loss in continuous feature space.

entry.title: TelePhysics: Physics-Grounded Multi-Object Scene Generation from a Single Image with Real-Time Interaction

author.name: Xin Zhang, Yabo Chen, Yijie Fang, Wanying Qu, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, Feng Xu, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: TelePhysics converts a single image into a physically consistent and controllable video through holistic scene-level 3D reconstruction with physics simulation, enabling real-time interaction without training.

entry.title: Verifiable Provenance and Watermarking for Generative AI: An Evidentiary Framework for International Operational Law and Domestic Courts

author.name: Gustav Olaf Yunus Laitinen-Fredriksson Lundstr\"om-Imanov, Nurana Abdullayeva

entry.summary: Presents a unified evidentiary framework mapping cryptographic content provenance, watermarking, and zero-knowledge attestation to legal proof requirements across international operational law, domestic procedure, and product regulation.

entry.title: Jointly Learning Predicates and Actions Enables Zero-Shot Skill Composition

author.name: Benedict Quartey, Sebastian Castro, Eric Rosen, Wil Thomason, George Konidaris, Stefanie Tellex

entry.summary: Introduces PACTS (Predicate Action Skills), which jointly model action trajectories and symbolic outcomes in visuomotor policies, enabling zero-shot composition of learned skills without retraining. Skills become composable because the model reasons about both actions and their symbolic effects.

entry.title: GaussianDream: A Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian World Model for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zijian Zhang, Yuqing Jiang, Qian Cheng, Si Liu, Ding Zhao, Ping Luo, Weitao Zhou, Haibao Yu

entry.summary: Introduces GaussianDream, a feed-forward 3D Gaussian world model that provides structured spatial-temporal supervision for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies. Couples current Gaussian reconstruction with future Gaussian prediction to provide explicit 3D geometry supervision during training.

entry.title: theory uplift differentially benefits safety & is underleveraged

author.name: Yudhister Kumar

entry.summary: Argues that near-superhuman math AI (expected by Q1 2027) will create a window where formal verification capabilities outpace capability development, benefiting safety research. Claims this opportunity is under-leveraged due to lack of infrastructure for turning compute into safety-relevant mathematical output.

entry.title: DOTRAG: Retrieval-Time Reasoning Along Paths

author.name: Larnell Moore, Naihao Deng, Rada Mihalcea, Farnaz Jahanbakhsh

entry.summary: Proposes DotRAG, a training-free GraphRAG framework that reformulates retrieval as reasoning over paths. Introduces Division of Thought (DOT) decomposing retrieval into query-conditioned constraints that guide graph exploration without explicit chain-of-thought reasoning.

entry.title: Robotics-Inspired Guardrails for Foundation Models in Socially Sensitive Domains

author.name: Rebecca Ramnauth, Drazen Brscic, Brian Scassellati

entry.summary: Proposes applying robotics-inspired formal constructs (runtime behavioral control, constraint enforcement) as guardrails for foundation models in socially sensitive domains. Introduces the Ground Control framework for trajectory-level safety guarantees.

entry.title: GeoX: Mastering Geospatial Reasoning Through Self-Play and Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Kyeongjin Ahn, Seungeon Lee, Krishna P. Gummadi, Meeyoung Cha

entry.summary: Proposes GeoX, a self-play framework for geospatial reasoning that uses executable programs yielding verifiable rewards. A single multimodal policy proposes and solves spatial problems across abduction, deduction, and induction modes without human-curated data.

entry.title: D-PACE: Dynamic Position-Aware Cross-Entropy for Parallel Speculative Drafting

author.name: Tianyu Wu, Yu Yao, Zhenting Qi, Han Zheng, Zhuohan Wang, Haoran Ma, Lawrence Liao, Himabindu Lakkaraju, Ju Li, Yilun Du

entry.summary: Proposes D-PACE for speculative decoding, deriving per-position training weights from a differentiable surrogate of expected accepted draft length, adapting weights dynamically rather than using fixed position-dependent schedules.

entry.title: Surviving the Unseen: Predictive Defense for Novel Multi-Turn Multimodal Attacks

author.name: Doohee You

entry.summary: Proposes TRIAD, a triple-tier anomaly defense framework that formulates MLLM safety verification as dynamic survival prediction, detecting progressive cross-modal attacks distributed across multi-turn conversations.

entry.title: Exploring and Developing a Pre-Model Safeguard with Draft Models

author.name: Hongyu Cai, Arjun Arunasalam, Yiming Liang, Antonio Bianchi, Z. Berkay Celik

entry.summary: Proposes using draft models (smaller LLMs) as pre-model safety guards to detect jailbreak attacks before invoking target models, leveraging transferability of attacks across model sizes.

entry.title: Stream3D: Sequential Multi-View 3D Generation via Evidential Memory

author.name: Kaichen Zhou, Zeyang Bai, Xinhai Chang, Mengyu Wang, Paul Liang, Fangneng Zhan

entry.summary: Stream3D is the first training-free streaming mechanism for turning frozen view-conditioned 3D generators into streaming generators using evidential memory that selectively caches informative historical frames based on evidence scores.

entry.title: Evaluating the Utility of Personal Health Records in Personalized Health AI

author.name: Rory Sayres, Kejia Chen, Ayush Jain, Matthew Thompson, Jonathan Richina, Xiang Yin, Jimmy Hu, Fan Zhang, Bob Lou, Mike Sanchez, Ines Mezerreg, Meredith Schreier, Hamsa Subramaniam, I-Ching Lee, Yugang Jia, Daniel Mcduff, Yossi Matias, Avinatan Hassidim, Dale Webster, Yun Liu, Jackie Barr, Quang Duong

entry.summary: Evaluates using Gemini 3.0 Flash with Personal Health Records (PHRs) to answer health queries, testing on 2,257 queries across different distributions. Assesses whether providing clinical data as context improves LLM health responses compared to without PHR context.

entry.title: DecisionBench: A Benchmark for Emergent Delegation in Long-Horizon Agentic Workflows

author.name: Yuxuan Gao, Megan Wang, Yi Ling Yu, Zijian Carl Ma, Ao Qu

entry.summary: Introduces DecisionBench, a benchmark for evaluating emergent delegation in multi-agent workflows where agents can call other models. Tests 11 models across 7 vendor families on delegation decisions, routing fidelity, vendor self-preference, and cost-latency tradeoffs.

entry.title: SceneCode: Executable World Programs for Editable Indoor Scenes with Articulated Objects

author.name: Puyi Wang, Yuhao Wang, Linjie Li, Zhengyuan Yang, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Yangguang Li, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: Presents SceneCode, a framework that compiles natural language prompts into executable code-driven indoor worlds with articulated objects. Enables physically interactable scene synthesis as programmatic world generation for embodied AI.

entry.title: Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification for Continuous AI Agent Evaluation

author.name: Yuxuan Gao, Megan Wang, Yi Ling Yu

entry.summary: Adapts conformal prediction and adaptive conformal inference for continuous AI agent evaluation, providing distribution-free coverage guarantees. Develops compositional uncertainty bounds for multi-agent pipelines and conformal abstention for pairwise rankings.

entry.title: Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model

author.name: Amin Sghaier, Ali Parviz, Alexia Jolicoeur-Martineau

entry.summary: Introduces Probabilistic TRM (PTRM), extending Tiny Recursive Models with stochastic Gaussian noise injection at each recursion step. Enables parallel trajectories exploring diverse solution basins as a task-agnostic test-time compute scaling method.

entry.title: ALDEN: Boosting Private Data Extraction from Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems via Active Learning and Distribution Estimation

author.name: Xingyu Lyu, Jianfeng He, Ning Wang, Yidan Hu, Tao Li, Danjue Chen, Shixiong Li, Yimin Chen

entry.summary: Proposes ALDEN, an attack that efficiently extracts private data from RAG systems using active learning to diversify malicious queries and distribution estimation to target high-value data. Demonstrates improved extraction rates over existing attacks.

entry.title: HELLoRA: Hot Experts Layer-Level Low-Rank Adaptation for Mixture-of-Experts Models

author.name: Jia Wei, Zhonghao Zhang, Ping Chen, Qianyang li, Yancheng Pan, Shaoxun Wang, Ziyi Qiu, Longxiang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes HELLoRA, which attaches LoRA modules only to the most frequently activated experts in MoE models at each layer. Reduces trainable parameters and FLOPs while improving performance through structured regularization.

entry.title: Metric-Gradient Projection for Stable Multi-Agent Policy Learning

author.name: Zuyuan Zhang, Sizhe Tang, Mahdi Imani, Tian Lan

entry.summary: Introduces HPML, which uses Hodge decomposition to separate the integrable (cooperative) component from the cyclic (adversarial) component in multi-agent learning update fields, projecting onto the metric-gradient component for stability.

entry.title: TwinRouterBench: Fast Static and Live Dynamic Evaluation for Realistic Agentic LLM Routing

author.name: Pei Yang, Wanyi Chen, Tongyun Yang, Pengbin Feng, Jiarong Xing, Wentao Guo, Yuhang Yao, Yuhang Han, Hanchen Li, Xu Wang, Zeyu Wang, Jie Xiao, Anjie Yang, Liang Tian, Lynn Ai, Eric Yang, Tianyu Shi

entry.summary: Introduces TwinRouterBench, a step-level routing benchmark for agentic LLM systems with static and live tracks, evaluating whether cheaper model substitution preserves downstream task success in multi-step agent workflows.

entry.title: From Sparsity to Simplicity: Enabling Simpler Sequential Replacements via Sparse Attention Distillation

author.name: Yuxin Ren, Maxwell D Collins, Miao Hu, Huanrui Yang

entry.summary: Proposes replacing attention layers with simpler sequential modules guided by observed sparsity patterns, using sparse attention distillation to identify which layers can be cheaply approximated.

entry.title: Lightweight and Fast Backdoor Model Detection

author.name: Yinbo Yu, Jing Fang, Xuewen Zhang, Chunwei Tian, Qi Zhu, Daoqiang Zhang, Jiajia Liu

entry.summary: Proposes DFBScanner, a lightweight static parameter inspection framework for fast backdoor detection in DNNs. Leverages the observation that backdoor-induced perturbations create anomalous parameter patterns detectable without clean samples.

entry.title: Shaping the Prior: How Synthetic Task Distributions Determine Tabular Foundation Model Quality

author.name: Mohamed Bouadi, Nassim Bouarour, Varun Kulkarni, Shivam Dubey, Aditya Tanna, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

entry.summary: Introduces O'Prior, a compositional realism prior for tabular foundation models that includes hierarchical SCM meta-generators, modular realism engines, stress modules, and curriculum scheduling to improve deployment robustness.

entry.title: FAGER: Factually Grounded Evaluation and Refinement of Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Youngsun Lim, Cusuh Ham, Pin-Yu Chen, Deepti Ghadiyaram

entry.summary: Proposes FAGER, an agentic framework for evaluating text-to-image models on factual correctness by constructing structured factual rubrics and verifying visually grounded facts implied by prompts.

entry.title: Be Kind, Rewrite: Benign Projections via Rewriting Defend Against LLM Data Poisoning Attacks

author.name: John T. Halloran, Noopur S. Bhatt

entry.summary: Proposes open-book benign rewriting (OBBR) as a proactive defense against LLM backdoor attacks, theoretically showing that rewriting with benign reference samples projects poisoned data to safe space.

entry.title: Diagnosing Multi-step Reasoning Failures in Black-box LLMs via Stepwise Confidence Attribution

author.name: Xiaoou Liu, Tiejin Chen, Dengjia Zhang, Yaqing Wang, Lu Cheng, Hua Wei

entry.summary: Introduces Stepwise Confidence Attribution (SCA) for diagnosing reasoning failures in black-box LLMs by assigning step-level confidence scores based on alignment with consensus structures across correct solutions.

entry.title: Inference-Time Scaling in Diffusion Models through Iterative Partial Refinement

author.name: Taegu Kang, Jaesik Yoon, Sungjin Ahn

entry.summary: Proposes Iterative Partial Refinement (IPR), an inference-time scaling method for sequential diffusion models that requires no external verifier, iteratively refining regions to improve generation quality.

entry.title: CaptchaMind: Training CAPTCHA Solvers via Reinforcement Learning with Explicit Reasoning Supervision

author.name: Pengcheng Wang, Haoxiang Liu, Yang Dai, Xiangxiang Zeng, Guanhua Chen, Baotian Hu, Longyue Wang, Weihua Luo

entry.summary: Introduces CaptchaBench (16K samples across 8 CAPTCHA types) and CaptchaMind, a reinforcement learning approach for training CAPTCHA solvers with explicit reasoning supervision. First training-based approach leveraging process-level annotations.

entry.title: EgoCoT-Bench: Benchmarking Grounded and Verifiable Operation-Centric Chain of Thought Reasoning for MLLMs

author.name: Yang Dai, Dian Jiao, Tianwei Lin, Wenqiao Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces EgoCoT-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating multimodal LLMs on fine-grained egocentric video understanding, specifically grounded chain-of-thought reasoning about hand-object interactions and operation sequences.

entry.title: Implicit Action Chunking for Smooth Continuous Control

author.name: Bosun Liang, Shuo Pei, Zirui Chen, Chuanzhi Fan, Chen Sun, Yuankai Wu, Huachun Tan, Yong Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Dual-Window Smoothing (DWS), an implicit action chunking framework that produces smooth control signals for physical deployment without expanding the action space dimension. Uses execution and planning windows for temporal coherence.

entry.title: Block-Sphere Vector Quantization

author.name: Heesang Ann, Joongkyu Lee, Min-hwan Oh

entry.summary: Provides unified theoretical comparison of rotation-based vector quantizers (EDEN, RabitQ, TurboQuant), showing their advantages are criterion-dependent. Proposes Block-Sphere VQ with new guarantees.

entry.title: Beyond Isotropy in JEPAs: Hamiltonian Geometry and Symplectic Prediction

author.name: Robert Jenkinson Alvarez

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis showing that isotropic regularization in Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) is suboptimal when downstream geometry is structured, deriving the minimax-optimal covariance and a closed-form 'price of isotropy'.

entry.title: CP-MoE: Consistency-Preserving Mixture-of-Experts for Continual Learning

author.name: Yang Liu, Toan Nguyen, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: Proposes CP-MoE, a continual learning framework using a transient expert mechanism with consistency-preserving routing bias to balance knowledge transfer and catastrophic forgetting in Mixture-of-Experts architectures.

entry.title: FBOS-RL: Feedback-Driven Bi-Objective Synergistic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xikai Zhang, Yongzhi Li, Likang Xiao, Yingze Zhang, Yanhua Cheng, Quan Chen, Peng Jiang, Wenjun Wu, Liu Liu

entry.summary: Proposes FBOS-RL, enhancing GRPO for reinforcement learning of LLMs by using feedback-driven sampling that adapts rollouts based on model capability, rather than always conditioning on the original prompt.

entry.title: Modality-Decoupled Online Recursive Editing

author.name: Siyuan Li, Youyuan Zhang, Fangming Liu, Jing Li

entry.summary: Proposes M-ORE, a modality-decoupled online recursive editor for multimodal LLMs that addresses cross-modal conflict and inter-edit interference during lifelong model editing with constant per-edit overhead.

entry.title: Weasel: Out-of-Domain Generalization for Web Agents via Importance-Diversity Data Selection

author.name: Fatemeh Pesaran zadeh, Seyeon Choi, Xing Han L\`u, Siva Reddy, Gunhee Kim

entry.summary: Proposes Weasel, a trajectory selection method for offline training of web agents that optimizes importance-diversity balance over states, websites, and interaction patterns to improve out-of-domain generalization.

entry.title: Neural Collapse by Design: Learning Class Prototypes on the Hypersphere

author.name: Panagiotis Koromilas, Theodoros Giannakopoulos, Mihalis A. Nicolaou, Yannis Panagakis

entry.summary: Shows that cross-entropy and supervised contrastive learning are different views of the same method (prototype contrast on the hypersphere), and proposes normalized losses that close the gap between them for achieving Neural Collapse.

entry.title: Fast Reconstruction of Exact Maxwell Dynamics from Sparse Data

author.name: Dan DeGenaro, Xin Li, Obed Amo, Michael Pokojovy, Sarah Adel Bargal, Markus Lange-Hegermann, Bogdan Rai\c{t}\u{a}

entry.summary: Introduces FLASH-MAX, a shallow neural network architecture for electromagnetic field prediction that satisfies Maxwell's equations by construction, achieving sub-1% error from ~1K observations in seconds with zero PDE residual.

entry.title: Latent Process Generator Matching

author.name: Lukas Billera, Hedwig Nora Nordlinder, Ben Murrell

entry.summary: Introduces latent process generator matching, a framework that treats observed generative state as a deterministic image of a tractable Markov process. Generalizes existing projection results for augmented-state flow matching and diffusion models.

entry.title: AVSD: Adaptive-View Self-Distillation by Balancing Consensus and Teacher-Specific Privileged Signals

author.name: Duy Nguyen, Hanqi Xiao, Archiki Prasad, Zaid Khan, Anirban Das, Austin Zhang, Sambit Sahu, Hyunji Lee, Elias Stengel-Eskin, Mohit Bansal

entry.summary: Proposes AVSD, a self-distillation framework for language models that balances consensus across multiple teacher views (solutions, demonstrations, feedback) while filtering view-specific information the student cannot access.

entry.title: Runtime-Certified Bounded-Error Quantized Attention

author.name: Dean Calver

entry.summary: Presents a tiered KV cache architecture with runtime-certified bounds on quantization error, using INT8 keys and INT4 values with FP16 fallback in system RAM for deterministic error recovery.

entry.title: PREFINE: Preference-Based Implicit Reward and Cost Fine-Tuning for Safety Alignment

author.name: Richa Verma, Bavish Kulur, Sanjay Chawla, Balaraman Ravindran

entry.summary: PREFINE fine-tunes a pre-trained RL policy for safety by incorporating cost constraints from trajectory-level preferences without retraining from scratch. Unlike standard RLHF, it works with trajectory-level preferences in continuous control environments.

entry.title: What Twelve LLM Agent Benchmark Papers Disclose About Themselves: A Pilot Audit and an Open Scoring Schema

author.name: Mahdi Naser Moghadasi (BrightMind AI, Texas Tech University), Faezeh Ghaderi (University of Texas at Arlington)

entry.summary: Audits twelve well-known LLM agent benchmark papers using a structured schema to assess reproducibility of evaluation details, finding significant gaps in reporting that prevent fair comparison across papers.

entry.title: EvoStruct: Bridging Evolutionary and Structural Priors for Antibody CDR Design via Protein Language Model Adaptation

author.name: Mansoor Ahmed, Sujin Lee, Umar Khayaz, Murray Patterson

entry.summary: EvoStruct bridges protein language models with 3D structural context via cross-attention adapters for antibody CDR design, addressing vocabulary collapse in GNN-based methods that over-predict few amino acids.

entry.title: The Economics of Model Collapse: Equilibrium, Welfare, and Optimal Provenance Subsidies in Synthetic Data Markets

author.name: Gustav Olaf Yunus Laitinen-Fredriksson Lundstr\"om-Imanov

entry.summary: Develops microeconomic theory of synthetic data markets under model collapse, proving existence/uniqueness of equilibrium, deriving welfare decomposition, and characterizing optimal provenance subsidies.

entry.title: Multi-agent Collaboration with State Management

author.name: Mengyang Liu, Taozhi Chen, Zhenhua Xu, Xue Jiang, Yihong Dong

entry.summary: STORM proposes state-oriented management for multi-agent code collaboration, mediating agent interactions with shared workspaces to detect and resolve conflicting edits in real-time rather than deferring to post-hoc merge steps.

entry.title: Llamas on the Web: Memory-Efficient, Performance-Portable, and Multi-Precision LLM Inference with WebGPU

author.name: Reese Levine, Rithik Sharma, Nikhil Jain, Abhijit Ramesh, Zheyuan Chen, Neha Abbas, James Contini, Tyler Sorensen

entry.summary: LlamaWeb presents a WebGPU backend for llama.cpp enabling memory-efficient LLM inference in browsers with static memory planning, tunable kernel library for cross-device variability, and support for numerous quantization formats.

entry.title: Conflict-Aware Additive Guidance for Flow Models under Compositional Rewards

author.name: Xuehui Yu, Fucheng Cai, Meiyi Wang, Xiaopeng Fan, Harold Soh

entry.summary: Identifies that gradient misalignment causes off-manifold drift when composing multiple constraints in guided diffusion/flow sampling, and proposes Conflict-Aware Additive Guidance to actively detect and resolve conflicting gradients.

entry.title: Linear-DPO: Linear Direct Preference Optimization for Diffusion and Flow-Matching Generative Models

author.name: Kesong Li, Yixuan Xu, Kuo-kun Tseng, Weiyi Lu, Kan Liu, Tao Lan

entry.summary: Linear-DPO derives a generalized DPO objective for both diffusion and flow-matching models via a unified reverse-time SDE framework, replacing sigmoid utility with linear utility for better text-to-image alignment.

entry.title: TextReg: Mitigating Prompt Distributional Overfitting via Regularized Text-Space Optimization

author.name: Lucheng Fu, Ye Yu, Yiyang Wang, Yiqiao Jin, Haibo Jin, B. Aditya Prakash, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: TextReg identifies prompt distributional overfitting in LLM prompt optimization (where prompts accumulate narrow rules and generalize poorly) and proposes regularized text-space optimization with a dual-factor inefficiency measure.

entry.title: Mind the Sim-to-Real Gap & Think Like a Scientist

author.name: Harsh Parikh, Gabriel Levin-Konigsberg, Dominique Perrault-Joncas, Alexander Volfovsky

entry.summary: Studies when and how a planner should supplement a pre-trained simulator with real experiments, providing decomposition of simulator error into identifiable calibration-deployment shift and irreducible parametric residual.

entry.title: Collocational bootstrapping: A hypothesis about the learning of subject-verb agreement in humans and neural networks

author.name: Claire Hobbs, R. Thomas McCoy

entry.summary: Proposes 'collocational bootstrapping' - a mechanism where statistical regularities in word co-occurrence help acquire syntax. Shows neural networks can learn subject-verb agreement from synthetic data with appropriate variability, matching patterns in child-directed language.

entry.title: Interpretable Discriminative Text Representations via Agreement and Label Disentanglement

author.name: Tong Wang, Yiqing Xu, Leo Yang Yang

entry.summary: Proposes operational criteria for interpretable text representations requiring both conceptual clarity (inter-annotator agreement) and label disentanglement (features shouldn't just paraphrase the target). Introduces concrete metrics for evaluating interpretability.

entry.title: Terminal-World: Scaling Terminal-Agent Environments via Agent Skills

author.name: Zihao Cheng, Hongru Wang, Zeming Liu, Xinyi Wang, Xiangrong Zhu, Yuhang Guo, Wei Lin, Jeff Z. Pan, Yunhong Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Terminal-World, an automated pipeline for generating training data for terminal agents using 'agent skills' as synthesis primitives that jointly encode tasks, preconditions, and environment states.

entry.title: Why Latent Actions Fail, and How to Prevent It

author.name: Jung Min Lee, Taehyun Cho, Li Zhao, Jungwoo Lee

entry.summary: Analyzes why latent action models fail due to exogenous state in videos, showing the standard reconstruction objective encodes exogenous information. Proposes learning in representation spaces focusing on endogenous components.

entry.title: ConceptSeg-R1: Segment Any Concept via Meta-Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuan Zhao, Youwei Pang, Jiaming Zuo, Wei Ji, Kailai Zhou, Bin Fan, Yunkang Cao, Lihe Zhang, Xiaofeng Liu, Huchuan Lu, Weisi Lin, Dacheng Tao, Xiaoqi Zhao

entry.summary: Formalizes generalized concept segmentation through a three-level taxonomy (context-independent, context-dependent, context-reasoning) and proposes ConceptSeg-R1 using Meta-GRPO, a meta-reinforcement learning approach for rule-induced concept grounding.

entry.title: VISTAQA: Benchmarking Joint Visual Question Answering and Pixel-Level Evidence

author.name: Mozhgan Nasr Azadani, Yimu Wang, Yongpeng Zhu, Lihong Chen, Milan Ganai, Sean Sedwards, Marco Pavone, Krzysztof Czarnecki

entry.summary: Introduces VISTAQA, a benchmark for jointly evaluating free-form answer correctness and pixel-level evidence grounding in VQA, with 1,157 expert-curated samples across six task types and six visual domains.

entry.title: What Semantics Survive the Connector? Diagnosing VLM-to-DiT Alignment in Video Editing

author.name: Hangyu Lin, Chao Wen, Chengming Xu, Jianxiong Gao, Jiangning Zhang, Xiaobin Hu, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: Investigates the semantic bottleneck between VLM connectors and DiT models in video editing, proposing a controlled diagnostic pipeline to identify what fine-grained semantics survive alignment versus what gets degraded.

entry.title: Bridging Structure and Language: Graph-Based Visual Reasoning for Autonomous Road Understanding

author.name: Lena Wild, Katie Z Luo, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: Introduces Combined Road Substrate (CRS), a graph-grounded framework bridging geometric road structure and open-vocabulary semantics for autonomous driving. Enables automatic generation of compositionally complex question-answer pairs for road understanding.

entry.title: DAMA: Disentangled Body-Anchored Gaussians for Controllable Multi-Layered Avatars

author.name: Daniel Eskandar, Berna Kabadayi, Garvita Tiwari, Gerard Pons-Moll

entry.summary: DAMA introduces a method for reconstructing physically plausible multi-layered clothed avatars using Gaussian splatting bound to SMPL-X with explicit garment disentanglement. Addresses the lack of geometric constraints in existing methods that leads to ambiguous garment boundaries.

entry.title: Q-ARVD: Quantizing Autoregressive Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Siao Tang, Xinyin Ma, Gongfan Fang, Xingyi Yang, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: Q-ARVD is the first systematic study of quantization for autoregressive video diffusion models, identifying two critical challenges specific to ARVDs that make standard quantization schemes suboptimal. Proposes tailored solutions for efficient deployment.

entry.title: SurgOnAir: Hierarchy-Aware Real-Time Surgical Video Commentary

author.name: Jingyi He, Yue Zhou, Long Bai, Kun Yuan, Nassir Navab, Yuan Bi

entry.summary: SurgOnAir is a streaming vision-language model for real-time surgical video commentary that processes frames sequentially without future access and generates narration tokens as visual input arrives, addressing the fundamental need for immediate reaction in the operating room.

entry.title: ProtoPathway: Biologically Structured Prototype-Pathway Fusion for Multimodal Cancer Survival Prediction

author.name: Amaya Gallagher-Syed, Costantino Pitzalis, Myles J. Lewis, Michael R. Barnes, Gregory Slabaugh

entry.summary: ProtoPathway introduces an interpretable multimodal framework for cancer survival prediction using learnable morphological prototypes for histopathology and pathway-structured graph networks for genomics, producing biologically grounded representations.

entry.title: Demo-JEPA: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for One-shot Cross-Embodiment Imitation

author.name: Jingyang He, Guangrun Li, Jieyu Zhang, Chengkai Hou, Zhengping Che, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Demo-JEPA, a cross-embodiment imitation framework using Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture that decouples demonstration intent from embodiment-specific execution.
